profile_epoch.rationale: Open Research in Depth by establishing which retained mechanisms support reliable endpoint search in the exchange-free L01 Anchor n-c55c3d520a2c. Its complete historical mean is 0.595670 with SD 0.026593; exchange removal gained 0.021326 on all three seed macros but lost four task/seed endpoints and increased dispersion. The original c-402ef46220 exchange grouping contains condition-dependent results: adding exchange under binary L01 in n-9edaa26007c3 gained 0.007397, whereas removing it under the count composition improved the current Anchor; the L16 removal n-cdac02dcd338 changed mean by only -0.000841 and is a contextual boundary, not transferable L01 evidence. Global family navigation separates predictive representation (f-200000000007), posterior allocation (f-100000000002) and graph transformation (f-100000000001), so this round isolates count features, residual influence, residual correlation and crossover rather than conflating them. The frozen catalog composition is reviewed, but its eight current contribution gaps remain experimental gaps. n-ae9cc6c2ca09 leaves correlation utility unresolved after a timeout; n-852bc7be4d7c and n-1faebb978a01 show substantial removal losses only under the earlier exchange-containing Parent; c-cf4ce43a7c contains duplicate count trajectories, not independent confirmation. Select batch size 10 to preserve the established feedback cadence and pool scale and avoid adding a second change while those composition questions are resolved. This is a comparability choice, not evidence that ten is optimal; smaller allowed batches would change feedback frequency and pool size and increase fitting frequency. The actual opening action is the mandatory fresh complete Anchor baseline under the protocol-owned Research in Depth profile. These four portfolio positions record the next contribution wave, to be reconsidered against that baseline before admission. No existing score is promoted to current-profile evidence and no scientific criterion is completed now.

research_direction.research_brief:
The current concern is limited productive exploration. The method learns from feedback and makes local improvements, but the runs examined show concentrated ancestry among top candidates, few offspring outperforming their best parent, and gains that are inconsistent across seeds. These observations suggest that the search may be repeatedly refining familiar structures without reliably discovering better alternatives.

Explore alternative GP kernels or tabular foundation model surrogates to improve candidate ranking and productive exploration.

method_proposal.differentiation: No closest bound lineage exists because context.bound_methods is empty. The closest catalogue method is Mol GA itself, with Graph GA supplying its graph operators; these are one method family, not distinct lineages created by parameter changes. Its identity is direct population evolution in molecular graph space, rather than a learned sequence policy or latent-space proposal distribution. The supplied Mechanism Cluster history is also empty, so there is no earlier refutation to reconcile.
method_proposal.first_improvement_direction: If the root succeeds but its observed offspring gains show that most oracle evaluations do not improve their breeding parents, first test posterior-sampling guidance for the existing graph search. Fit a fingerprint surrogate only to accepted observations from the current task, run the existing graph operators against sampled surrogate functions, and evaluate the generated sample maximizers. This is an inferred molecular transfer of the optimization specialization of [PS-BAX](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/file/f3c8bfcc9c2bc13a0f141cb58afc6e5a-Paper-Conference.pdf), where the target is the maximizer and posterior sampling reduces to Thompson sampling. Check chronological predictive usefulness and whether selected offspring produce more parent-beating scores; retain the change only if the protocol's final Top-1 evidence supports it. No campaign evidence currently establishes this bottleneck.
method_proposal.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_proposal.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

references.citation: Austin Tripp and José Miguel Hernández-Lobato. Genetic algorithms are strong baselines for molecule generation. arXiv:2310.09267, 2023. Sections 2–3 and Appendix A describe the anchor.

Chu Xin Cheng, Raul Astudillo, Thomas Desautels, and Yisong Yue. Practical Bayesian Algorithm Execution via Posterior Sampling. NeurIPS 2024. Section 3 describes posterior-sampled target sets and the maximization specialization motivating the conditional first improvement.

method_proposal.differentiation: The supplied context contains no bound methods and no mechanism clusters, so there is no existing lineage to name as the nearest comparator or campaign refutation to overcome. The nearest catalogue family is conventional latent BO, including InvBO: this proposal predicts scores in molecular structure space and generates by posterior-conditioned sampling, rather than optimizing a latent-space acquisition or repairing encoder-decoder inversion. Its proposal mechanism also differs from graph crossover and policy-gradient sequence generation. I fixed COWBOYS from the catalogue before opening its external paper. Published evidence is a nearby small-budget setting, not a replication of this benchmark's feedback schedule; learning an adequate prior within permitted preparation remains an empirical prerequisite.
method_proposal.first_improvement_direction: If the successful root shows batches with highly correlated GP predictions and few independent incumbent improvements, add one mechanism: covariance-aware selection among surplus molecules freshly generated by its existing MCMC sampler. Retain candidates with credible incumbent-improvement probability, then select subsequent batch members using posterior variance conditioned on already selected members. This imports the conditional-entropy batch selection idea from [PS-BAX, Appendix C](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/file/f3c8bfcc9c2bc13a0f141cb58afc6e5a-Paper-Conference.pdf), without adopting its finite-library experiments. The proposed transfer keeps the VAE, GP and MCMC target fixed and uses only transient de novo candidates. Test whether selected-batch conditional information increases and whether that translates into a higher final Top-1 mean; reduced correlation alone is not success. No root evidence exists yet, so this direction is conditional rather than an asserted observed bottleneck.
method_proposal.method_name: COWBOYS: GP-conditioned de novo latent sampling
method_proposal.method_thesis: Train a compact SELFIES VAE from the permitted unlabeled corpus during preparation, then freeze its decoder. Within each independent objective session, fit a Tanimoto-kernel GP directly to the observed molecular fingerprints and scores. Generate new molecules through preconditioned Crank-Nicolson MCMC targeting the Gaussian latent prior multiplied by the GP probability that the deterministically decoded molecule exceeds the observed incumbent. The molecule assessed by the surrogate must be the molecule submitted. Fill the protocol-announced batch with distinct generated structures and update the GP after feedback. The corpus supplies a generative prior, never a ranked molecule library. This follows the decoupled mechanism in [COWBOYS](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v267/moss25a.html). Our hypothesis is that structure-level prediction and immediate Bayesian conditioning can direct scarce labels toward a higher final observed maximum without fitting a reward-dependent neural generator. Success is measured by the benchmark's mean of independent final Top-1 scores.

method_proposal.differentiation: The supplied context.bound_methods is empty, so there is no most-similar bound lineage to name; context.evidence_view.clusters is also empty, with no earlier refutation to revisit. The closest catalogue family is REINVENT and its replay variants. This proposal anchors that policy-learning family through Augmented Hill-Climb, whose root learns only from current-batch elites. Its defining proposal mechanism is autoregressive generation from reward-updated parameters, distinct from graph crossover or mutation and from acquisition optimization through a frozen latent decoder. A different recurrent backbone or reward multiplier would remain this same lineage. All objective adaptation uses only observations from the current session.
method_proposal.first_improvement_direction: After the root succeeds, probe reuse of scored elites through randomized-SMILES experience replay. If the root logs show that high-reward molecules lose policy likelihood after later batches or that updates affect only their original serialization, retain a bounded elite memory and train on fresh equivalent SMILES views using the existing scores. Hold the prior, AHC loss, and generation rule fixed. Measure replayed-view count, policy likelihood on held-out equivalent views, and the rewards of subsequently evaluated new molecules; improvement must ultimately appear in final Top-1, not merely duplicates or validity. [Guo and Schwaller](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11200228/) provide direct molecular evidence for combining replay with SMILES augmentation. Mining the cross-domain catalogue suggests the related principle of exploiting known objective invariances: [Bardou et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.25051) study this through max kernels. Transferring that principle to equivalent SMILES training views is an inference; their GP kernel and reported optimization gains are not part of this proposal.
method_proposal.method_name: Augmented Hill-Climb with a corpus-trained SMILES policy
method_proposal.method_thesis: Train a compact autoregressive SMILES prior solely on the supplied unlabeled corpus, then initialize a fresh policy from that prior for each objective. Use the initial observations and each subsequent scored batch to update only its highest-reward sequences with the Augmented Hill-Climb loss: fit policy log likelihood to frozen-prior log likelihood plus scaled observed reward. Sample complete molecules token by token from the updated policy, canonicalize them, and refill invalid or duplicate proposals by further generation. The corpus supplies language training, never a ranked molecular pool. Elite-conditioned policy updates should shift generation toward new high-scoring molecular combinations quickly enough to improve the benchmark's mean final Top-1. This is a small-budget transfer hypothesis, not a claim that published larger-budget gains carry over. The root uses the current scored batch; randomized historical replay is reserved for the first improvement. The anchor's elite augmented-likelihood mechanism is described by [Thomas et al.](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13321-022-00646-z).

method_proposal.first_improvement_direction: If the successful root repeatedly selects the same prefix within a batch and those related completions yield few independent incumbent improvements, add pending-rollout counts to tree selection. Following [WU-UCT, Section 3.1](https://arxiv.org/html/1810.11755v5), count generated batch members awaiting feedback along their selected paths and include completed plus pending visits in the exploration term, while estimated rewards continue to use only real observations. Clear pending counts when feedback resolves each proposal. Keep the rollout prior, expansion rule and reward backup unchanged. This imports a delayed-feedback mechanism from game search into synchronous molecular batch construction; it does not require changing execution resources. Measure pending-count activation, the concentration of selected prefixes within batches, and incumbent improvements from subsequently evaluated completions. Broader branch coverage alone is insufficient: retention requires improved final Top-1 evidence. No current campaign observation establishes this bottleneck, so the direction is conditional.
method_proposal.method_name: ChemTS: UCT-guided SMILES prefix search with a frozen rollout prior
method_proposal.method_thesis: Anchor the root in [ChemTS](https://arxiv.org/html/1710.00616v1): train a compact autoregressive SMILES model solely on the supplied unlabeled corpus during preparation, then freeze it. For each independent objective, maintain a fresh prefix tree whose nodes hold visit counts and observed returns. Initialize its statistics from the supplied observations. Select prefixes through upper-confidence tree search, expand them using the frozen model's next-token distribution, and generate complete molecules by stochastic continuation. Backpropagate accepted oracle scores through the corresponding paths after feedback. Generate further continuations until the evaluator-announced batch contains distinct canonical structures. This is an expanding generative tree, with no corpus ranking or fixed molecular candidate set. The hypothesis is that sharing each scarce reward across its visited prefixes directs subsequent continuations toward promising molecular families quickly enough to improve the mean of independent final Top-1 scores. The root adapts tree statistics; it does not update neural parameters with rewards. The paper supports this search mechanism, but its larger, time-limited experiments do not establish performance under this benchmark's scarce feedback. Learning a useful rollout prior within permitted preparation remains an empirical prerequisite.

method_proposal.method_name: GenMol fragment remasking with a corpus-trained discrete denoiser
method_proposal.method_thesis: Anchor the method in GenMol's fragment-remasking mechanism: a bidirectional masked discrete diffusion model generates replacement fragments while retaining the surrounding molecular context. The anchor is described in [GenMol, Sections 4.1-4.2](https://arxiv.org/html/2501.06158v3). For this benchmark adaptation, train a compact denoiser solely on the permitted unlabeled corpus, then freeze it. Start each objective with a fresh archive of its supplied scored molecules. Select high-ranked observed whole molecules as contexts, replace a randomly chosen fragment with a variable-length mask chunk, iteratively sample the missing SAFE tokens, and decode the resulting complete molecule. Generate further completions until the evaluator-announced batch contains distinct canonical structures. Accepted feedback updates context selection and allows improving completions to become future contexts. This root uses the remasking core with observed whole-molecule contexts; the paper's corpus-derived fragment-vocabulary initialization and fragment-attaching stage are not required. The corpus trains the denoiser and supplies unlabeled length statistics, never a molecule pool for ranking or retrieval. The hypothesis is that contextual fragment replacement preserves useful structure while generating improving alternatives, raising the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Task-local selection can respond immediately to feedback without reward-dependent neural training, but useful conditional generation from the permitted preparation remains an empirical prerequisite.

method_proposal.first_improvement_direction: If the successful root reconstructs observations accurately but its latent GP repeatedly makes overconfident errors on subsequently evaluated proposals, first test a fully Bayesian tree-kernel surrogate using BARK. Replace the root GP's fixed covariance model with posterior samples of tree-agreement kernels and propagate uncertainty over both tree partitions and function values into its existing Thompson selection. Keep SeqFlow, token-adaptive proposals, trust regions and the de novo candidate stream fixed. [BARK, Sections 5-6](https://arxiv.org/html/2503.05574v2), found in the cross-domain catalogue, supports this covariance-uncertainty mechanism. Applying it to a discretely decoded molecular latent space is an inference; its engineering results do not establish molecular gains. The test is conditional because the supplied campaign observations do not yet demonstrate this bottleneck for NF-BO. Measure chronological predictive coverage, changes in which generated proposals are selected, and new incumbent improvements. Retain the change only with improved final Top-1 evidence, rather than treating calibration alone as success.
method_proposal.method_name: NF-BO: invertible sequence-flow search with token-adaptive latent proposals
method_proposal.method_thesis: Use NF-BO's SeqFlow mapping, exact left-inverse decoding, and token-adaptive trust-region search. Train a compact SELFIES flow on the permitted unlabeled corpus. Within each fresh objective session, adapt it using highly scored task-local sequences, re-encode all observations after updates, and fit a latent-space GP. Generate new latent proposals around scored observations by perturbing token blocks according to their estimated pointwise mutual information with the decoded sequence. Thompson sampling selects proposals for inverse-flow decoding. These mechanisms follow [NF-BO, Sections 4 and 5.3](https://arxiv.org/html/2504.14889v1). Regenerate as needed to fill the evaluator-announced batch with distinct canonical molecules; no corpus molecules are ranked or retrieved. The hypothesis is that score-directed local search around exactly reconstructable observations finds improving structures efficiently enough to raise the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Exact reconstruction alone is not the objective. Useful flow training and surrogate prediction under the permitted preparation and feedback remain empirical prerequisites.

method_proposal.method_name: Genetic GFN: reciprocal learning between a flow policy and graph search
method_proposal.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Genetic GFN: alternately generate molecules with a GFlowNet policy, refine the resulting scored population through graph crossover and mutation, and distill scored descendants back into the policy using rank-weighted off-policy replay. The policy uses trajectory balance with a learned log normalizer and regularization toward a frozen prior. [Kim et al., Section 3](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.05961v4) describe this mechanism. Train the prior only on the permitted unlabeled corpus. Each objective starts with clean policy adaptation, replay and population state initialized from its supplied observations. Use a positive terminal reward increasing with the observed maximization score. Schedule policy and genetic phases around the evaluator's announced feedback; both produce new molecules, and all reward-bearing training records come from accepted observations. Later policy samples must enter genetic populations, and accepted graph descendants must affect subsequent policy updates. Generate further valid, canonical-unique structures to fill announced batches, without corpus ranking or a fixed molecular library. The hypothesis is that learned global proposals propagate local discoveries into new promising regions and then support further graph refinement, raising the mean of five independent final Top-1 scores. Published larger-budget gains do not establish that this reciprocal learning becomes useful quickly enough here.

method_proposal.method_name: Simulated annealing through de novo molecular graph walks
method_proposal.method_thesis: Anchor the method in simulated annealing: randomly perturb a current configuration, accept improvements, sometimes accept deterioration, and gradually cool the acceptance rule. [Kirkpatrick, Gelatt and Vecchi](https://hedibert.org/wp-content/uploads/2013/12/1983KirkpatrickGelattVecchi.pdf) describe this mechanism for combinatorial optimization. Our molecular transfer maintains independent graph walks initialized from the current objective's supplied scored molecules. Each walk generates a new neighbor through atom or bond edits. After real feedback, accept a higher-scoring neighbor as the next working state; accept a lower-scoring neighbor with probability exp((new_score-current_score)/T), otherwise retain the source state. Subsequent edits follow the accepted working state, while a separate archive preserves the best observed molecule. Cool as feedback accumulates and distribute the evaluator-announced batch across walks with explicit proposal-to-source provenance. Regenerate invalid or already evaluated structures through further edits. Every submitted molecule is generated de novo; no corpus pool, learned prior or labeled source task is required. The hypothesis is that temporary score losses permit useful structural transitions whose later gains increase the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. This finite-budget optimizer does not claim equilibrium sampling or asymptotic convergence under molecular validity and novelty filtering.

method_proposal.method_name: DST: gradient-guided construction through relaxed scaffolding trees
method_proposal.method_thesis: Anchor the method in Differentiable Scaffolding Tree: relax molecular substructure identity and existence into continuous variables, ascend a structural surrogate, and sample discrete structures from the optimized variables. [Fu et al., Sections 3.1-3.3](https://wenhao-gao.github.io/assets/publications/2021_DST_ICLR/paper.pdf) describe this proposal mechanism. For our adaptation, derive an atom/ring token alphabet and train a compact graph encoder by masked-substructure reconstruction solely on the permitted unlabeled corpus. Freeze that encoder and fit a regularized linear scalar readout using only the current objective's accepted observations, updating the readout after feedback. Select scored molecules as local starting structures; hold their internal scaffold context fixed while optimizing relaxed leaf replacement, deletion and expansion variables through the surrogate. Keep surrogate parameters fixed during each structural optimization. Sample edited trees and compatible attachment choices stochastically, assemble new molecules, and repeat generation until the announced batch contains distinct valid structures. The token alphabet supports construction; complete corpus molecules are never retrieved or ranked, and attachment combinations are sampled rather than exhaustively enumerated. Accepted feedback updates both the scored archive and the readout. The hypothesis is that useful structural gradients concentrate new proposals toward real improvements quickly enough to increase the mean of independent final Top-1 scores. Reliable gradients from scarce labels and faithful transfer from relaxed to assembled structures are unproven prerequisites.

method_proposal.method_name: CMA-ES: covariance adaptation through a frozen molecular decoder
method_proposal.method_thesis: Anchor the optimizer in CMA-ES: sample a multivariate Gaussian, rank evaluated samples, move its mean by weighted recombination, and adapt covariance and step size using selected displacements and cumulative evolution paths. [Hansen, Sections 1-4](https://arxiv.org/html/1604.00772v2) describes this mechanism. For the molecular transfer, train a compact SELFIES VAE solely on the permitted unlabeled corpus and freeze its encoder and deterministic decoder. Each objective starts with fresh Gaussian and path state. Encodings of high-scoring supplied molecules may initialize geometric search locations, but their scores must not be assigned to nonidentical reconstructions. Generate latent samples, decode them into new molecules, and attach accepted oracle feedback to the exact latent sample that produced each submitted structure. Assemble scored generations while respecting the evaluator-announced batching, then update the Gaussian from descending observed-score ranks. Reject invalid or duplicate structures locally and continue de novo decoding. The corpus trains a generator and never supplies a ranked molecular library. The hypothesis is that learning correlated latent displacements directly from successful generations can uncover improving combinations without first estimating an objective surrogate, increasing the mean of independent final Top-1 scores. Useful decoder support and covariance adaptation within scarce feedback are empirical prerequisites; continuous-domain performance is not evidence that decoded molecular landscapes will behave similarly.

method_proposal.method_name: MAX-MIN Ant System over a molecular construction grammar
method_proposal.method_thesis: Anchor the method in MAX-MIN Ant System: construct solutions probabilistically from components, evaporate their pheromone weights, reinforce the iteration-best solution, and bound every pheromone weight away from zero and excessive dominance. [Stutzle and Hoos, Sections 2 and 4](https://www.cs.ubc.ca/~hoos/Publ/fgcs00.pdf) describe this mechanism. Our molecular adaptation constructs a fresh graph from an empty state through valence-aware atom, bond, ring-closure and termination actions. Choice probabilities combine a fixed chemical heuristic with task-local pheromones keyed by the local attachment context and action, allowing a useful action to transfer between different partial graphs. Preparation uses the permitted unlabeled corpus only for aggregate construction frequencies and stopping statistics. Initialize pheromones broadly, reconstruct valid construction traces for the supplied scored molecules, and use their best trace for the initial reinforcement. Generate the announced batch through complete new construction trajectories; only accepted whole-molecule feedback drives evaporation and reinforcement of that batch's best trace. Resample failed or duplicate constructions locally. There is no stored complete-molecule library, corpus ranking or fixed product enumeration. The hypothesis is that reusing successful local construction choices across new molecular combinations raises the mean of independent final Top-1 scores. Whether coarse construction contexts carry useful reward information quickly enough is unproven; pheromone concentration or validity alone is not success.

method_proposal.method_name: Molecule Swarm Optimization with persistent latent velocities
method_proposal.method_thesis: Anchor the method in Molecule Swarm Optimization: each particle keeps its latent position, velocity and best observed position, and moves through inertia plus independent stochastic attractions toward its personal best and the swarm's best. [Winter et al., Methods 2.2-2.4](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6836962/) describe this molecular use of particle swarm optimization. For our adaptation, train a compact SELFIES VAE solely on the permitted unlabeled corpus, freeze its encoder and deterministic decoder, and start each objective with clean swarm memories. Encodings of supplied molecules provide starting geometry; their scores initialize attractors only when decoding preserves canonical molecular identity. Otherwise establish scored attractors from actual generated evaluations, never from mislabeled reconstructions. Generate fresh latent positions through particle motion and decode new complete molecules. Locally retry stochastic motion for invalid or duplicate outcomes until the announced batch is filled. Match accepted feedback to the exact generating position before updating personal and shared bests; each batch uses only resolved memories. The corpus supplies a generator, never a molecule library for ranking or retrieval. The hypothesis is that persistent individual trajectories explore alternatives while shared successful locations redirect them quickly enough to improve the mean of independent final Top-1 scores. This uses the provided scalar objective directly, without additional desirability terms. Useful latent geometry and rapid transfer of discoveries between particles remain empirical prerequisites. The published model and evaluation scale do not establish those prerequisites under the permitted preparation and scarce feedback.

This changes action proposal and temporal credit assignment, not an acceptance constant. method_proposal.first_improvement_direction: If the successful root records delayed episode improvements but its exploration repeatedly changes direction through independent random actions, first add episode-consistent randomized value functions. Train independently initialized Q-heads with persistent bootstrap masks on accepted replay and head-specific target networks; select one head at episode start and keep its identity through that episode. Preserve graph operators, reward, horizon, replay records and the underlying double-Q update. [Osband et al., Sections 2-3](https://arxiv.org/html/1602.04621v2) supplies this temporally extended exploration mechanism. Mining the cross-domain catalogue also identifies the related principle in [PS-BAX, Algorithm 1](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/file/f3c8bfcc9c2bc13a0f141cb58afc6e5a-Paper-Conference.pdf): run an algorithm under one sampled function. method_proposal.method_name: MolDQN: Bellman-guided de novo graph-edit episodes
method_proposal.method_thesis: Anchor the root in MolDQN's value-based control of molecular edits: learn future action returns from scored transitions and choose subsequent graph modifications with a deep Q-network. [Zhou et al., Sections 2.1, 2.2 and 2.5](https://arxiv.org/html/1810.08678v3) describe finite molecular edit episodes, fingerprint features and double Q-learning. Our adaptation starts short episodes from task-local scored molecules and samples fresh valence-aware atom and bond edits at each state. A compact Q-network takes current and successor fingerprints, remaining episode depth and the episode's best observed score. Use a single Q-function with epsilon-greedy action selection in the root. Evaluate only selected new whole molecules; values assigned to unselected successors are predictions. Advance each trajectory after its matched feedback, even when the new molecule scores worse. For Top-1 alignment, use reward max(previous_episode_best, new_score) minus previous_episode_best and undiscounted finite-horizon backups: accumulated reward equals improvement in that episode's best score. This reward adaptation is our inference, not the paper's original reward. Train immediately from accepted transition replay using double-Q target selection and a lagged target network, with zero continuation value at episode termination. Retain all accepted intermediate molecules in the task incumbent archive. Interleave episodes according to announced batches, and generate further edits to replace invalid or duplicate proposals. Each decision samples an evolving neighborhood; no corpus pool, complete-molecule retrieval or fixed candidate enumeration is involved. No pretrained generator or external labels are required, and every objective starts with clean learning state. The hypothesis is that learned lookahead identifies useful edit sequences, including temporary score losses, quickly enough to raise the mean of independent final Top-1 scores. Learning useful continuation values from scarce transitions is unproven; the paper's much larger training regime does not establish this transfer.

Form a Gaussian coefficient posterior from accepted task-local observations with a posterior mean matching the root's ridge fit, draw one coefficient vector per construction, and optimize that sampled function with the existing graph program. Hold descriptors, context selection and chemical constraints fixed. This imports the optimization specialization of [PS-BAX, Section 3](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/file/f3c8bfcc9c2bc13a0f141cb58afc6e5a-Paper-Conference.pdf), identified in the cross-domain catalogue: execute the target optimizer under a posterior function draw. Retention requires improved final Top-1 evidence. method_proposal.method_name: Inverse-QSAR: mixed-integer de novo molecular construction
method_proposal.method_thesis: Anchor the method in inverse-QSAR through coupled linear regression and mixed-integer graph construction. [Zhu et al., Sections 1, 3 and 4](https://www.imrpress.com/journal/FBL/27/6/10.31083/j.fbl2706188) encode both a molecular descriptor function and a learned predictor in a program that constructs a graph satisfying structural specifications. Our benchmark adaptation fits a regularized linear score model only to the current objective's accepted observations, using atom-type, degree and typed-bond counts that can be represented exactly by integer constraints. For each proposal, take a scored molecule, choose a bounded editable peripheral region and retain its connected surrounding context. Represent replacement atom identities, bond orders and attachment choices as discrete variables, with connectivity, valence and descriptor-consistency constraints. Maximize the fitted scalar prediction over these variables instead of solving the paper's fixed target-interval problem. A feasible integer assignment supplies the new molecular graph directly. Validate the actual graph and recompute its descriptors before submission; exclude repeated assignments and retry construction when canonical identity is duplicate or invalid. Vary contexts and editable regions as feedback accumulates, and continue construction until the announced batch is filled. Use bounded subproblems and feasible solver incumbents rather than requiring a proof of global optimality for every proposal. The root needs no generative checkpoint or external labels. It constructs atom and bond combinations, without a corpus molecule pool, stored-fragment retrieval or the paper's subsequent isomer-enumeration stage. Each objective starts with clean scored and fitted state. The hypothesis is that jointly enforcing realizable structure while optimizing a task-local prediction concentrates evaluations on improving molecules and raises the mean of independent final Top-1 scores. Exact descriptor realization cannot compensate for an inaccurate predictor; both predictive usefulness and sufficient construction throughput remain unproven.

method_proposal.differentiation: Compared against all fourteen bound methods. 'Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution' uses evolutionary graph operators; this proposal makes its search region depend explicitly on negative examples. 'COWBOYS: GP-conditioned de novo latent sampling' uses posterior-conditioned latent sampling, whereas RACOS constructs categorical exclusion regions without a score-regression posterior. 'Augmented Hill-Climb with a corpus-trained SMILES policy' learns sequence likelihoods from elites; RACOS has no sequence-policy training. 'ChemTS: UCT-guided SMILES prefix search with a frozen rollout prior' maintains a prefix-search tree; this method samples complete frames from fresh classifiers. 'GenMol fragment remasking with a corpus-trained discrete denoiser' learns conditional fragment reconstruction; RACOS learns which coordinates must be fixed to exclude observed negatives and samples free coordinates directly. 'NF-BO: invertible sequence-flow search with token-adaptive latent proposals' requires a learned invertible latent mapping and Bayesian acquisition; neither mechanism is present here. 'Genetic GFN: reciprocal learning between a flow policy and graph search' couples trajectory-flow learning to evolutionary replay; RACOS has neither component. 'Simulated annealing through de novo molecular graph walks' advances chains through temperature-dependent acceptance; RACOS retains labeled examples and reconstructs a region for each proposal. 'DST: gradient-guided construction through relaxed scaffolding trees' differentiates a relaxed molecular objective; RACOS uses discrete classifications. 'CMA-ES: covariance adaptation through a frozen molecular decoder' learns a continuous Gaussian search distribution; RACOS has no learned latent geometry or covariance update. 'MAX-MIN Ant System over a molecular construction grammar' reinforces construction actions with pheromones; RACOS uses explicit negative-exclusion constraints. 'Molecule Swarm Optimization with persistent latent velocities' retains particle trajectories and personal/global attractors; RACOS has no particle motion. 'MolDQN: Bellman-guided de novo graph-edit episodes' learns multistep action values; RACOS directly classifies complete observed constructions. 'Inverse-QSAR: mixed-integer de novo molecular construction' optimizes a learned numerical objective through coupled integer constraints; RACOS samples categorical regions without a numerical predictor or combinatorial solver. method_proposal.method_thesis: The anchor is RACOS, selected before locating the primary source. Its categorical form chooses a positively labeled exemplar, randomly fixes coordinates to that exemplar until negative examples are excluded, further restricts the number of free coordinates, and samples the resulting region; a broader uniform component preserves exploration. Each proposal can use a newly randomized classifier. These are the mechanisms described by Yu, Qian and Hu in [Derivative-Free Optimization via Classification](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/10289/10148). My molecular adaptation applies this process directly to bounded categorical SELFIES frames, with removable padding that permits changes in molecular length. Preparation extracts only a construction-token alphabet from the permitted unlabeled corpus. There is no trained molecular encoder or decoder. Initial labeled molecules become exemplars only after encoding and decoding reproduce their canonical identity. For generated molecules, retain the actual sampled frame, its decoded canonical molecule, and the score actually returned for that molecule. Rank the current objective's observed molecules into a high-score positive group and a lower-score negative group; use these labels to construct exclusion regions. Free token positions are newly sampled and decoded into complete molecules, checked, canonicalized, and deduplicated. Rebuild a region or use the broad generation component when a region cannot provide a fresh molecule. These are online constructions from token primitives, not retrieval or enumeration of complete molecules. After each announced batch receives real feedback, refresh the labeled sets and incumbent; all pending proposals use only previously observed scores. Each objective starts with clean task-specific state and follows the protocol's supplied batch and resource limits. The hypothesis is that explicitly excluding observed poor token configurations will concentrate new molecular proposals around combinations that improve the incumbent with few labels. Success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Region exclusion, validity, or classification accuracy alone cannot establish that hypothesis. Positional token restrictions may have weak structural meaning, and multiple frames can decode to the same molecule; exact representation checks address score provenance but do not establish useful search geometry.

method_proposal.differentiation: The closest bound method is 'Simulated annealing through de novo molecular graph walks'. Its trajectory uses temperature-dependent probabilistic acceptance; tabu search uses explicit history-dependent structural prohibitions and chooses the best observed admissible neighbor even when all sampled neighbors are worse. This changes the search paradigm, rather than a cooling constant or graph-edit parameter. 'Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution' maintains breeding and survivor populations; this root follows a current-state trajectory with expiring move restrictions. 'MolDQN: Bellman-guided de novo graph-edit episodes' learns action values and multistep returns; tabu memory records recent structural moves without a Bellman model. 'RACOS: negative-exclusion sampling of de novo SELFIES regions' learns categorical regions from positive and negative score classes; tabu restrictions depend on recency and move reversals, not negative-example classification. 'MAX-MIN Ant System over a molecular construction grammar' reinforces reusable construction actions with pheromones; this root temporarily prohibits reversal attributes while walking from a complete graph. 'COWBOYS: GP-conditioned de novo latent sampling' and 'NF-BO: invertible sequence-flow search with token-adaptive latent proposals' generate through latent probabilistic models and Bayesian guidance; neither mechanism defines this root. 'CMA-ES: covariance adaptation through a frozen molecular decoder' and 'Molecule Swarm Optimization with persistent latent velocities' adapt continuous population motion through a decoder; this root has direct graph transitions and no latent geometry. 'Augmented Hill-Climb with a corpus-trained SMILES policy' updates a neural sequence policy, while 'Genetic GFN: reciprocal learning between a flow policy and graph search' couples learned flow probabilities with genetic refinement; tabu search has neither neural reward learning nor population exchange. 'ChemTS: UCT-guided SMILES prefix search with a frozen rollout prior' directs prefix-tree exploration, and 'GenMol fragment remasking with a corpus-trained discrete denoiser' reconstructs masked fragments; this root uses explicit structural edits and walk memory. 'DST: gradient-guided construction through relaxed scaffolding trees' and 'Inverse-QSAR: mixed-integer de novo molecular construction' generate by optimizing numerical surrogates under continuous or integer representations; this root evaluates sampled admissible neighbors directly. The supplied cluster history is empty, so no Mechanism Cluster refutes this family. Node n-4fa9546e559e reports that most graph offspring failed to beat their generating parents, motivating measurement of useful walk transitions without establishing a tabu-specific bottleneck. Node n-3ab6a944e3dd shows that frequent reuse of reinforced construction components need not produce incumbent gains; this reinforces the need to distinguish memory activation from actual Top-1 benefit. Neither observation proves that structural reversals are currently limiting search.

method_proposal.method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.

L01.method_thesis: The representative n-fc2c108a5253 is scored molecular-graph evolution with a task-local fingerprint Gaussian process that selects which freshly bred offspring receive oracle calls. Preparation writes deterministic operator and selector configuration only. Each objective process starts from its supplied scored molecules, keeps an all-accepted archive and a bounded score-ranked breeding population, fits the posterior to accepted labels, breeds a temporary surplus of connected novel graphs, computes their joint conditional distribution, and emits masked maximizers of independent correlated function draws. Accepted feedback both updates the archive and competes for survival, so admitted offspring can breed in the next batch. The implementation retains the root n-4fa9546e559e graph operators, parent quantiles and greedy survival; its added mechanism is learned selection before evaluation. The representative has complete seeds 0, 1 and 2 with macro mean 0.5443738005952443 and population SD 0.013310111166991866. Activation is confirmed, but only the original seed supplies a paired direct-parent comparison. Curate c-1e7b33da25 records replicated uncertainty-dependent choices without isolated evidence for uncertainty's marginal score contribution. Only 565 of 4350 selected offspring beat their generating best parent across the three runs. The blueprint therefore separates state, graph production, prediction and evaluation allocation, and closes by testing their interactions. The graph is a one-iteration data-dependency graph: accepted feedback from an emitted batch is an external input to the next iteration of feedback_memory, not a same-iteration cycle. Integration is a cross-cutting concern over that real closed loop. The frozen settings permit 24 Children in waves of four, hence six waves: one each for memory, posterior, allocation and integration, and two for graph production, whose coupled chemical edit and admissibility mechanisms have substantial documented headroom.

L03.method_thesis: Representative n-15499bde2e65 is an Augmented Hill-Climb molecular language policy with bounded historical elite replay. Preparation trains a recurrent next-token SMILES prior on the supplied unlabeled corpus, selects a checkpoint by a fixed unlabeled holdout and publishes only weights and metadata. Each objective clones an independent trainable policy from that verified frozen prior. Accepted observations retain their actual sampled serialization under a canonical molecular identity. Each nonempty batch contributes its highest-scoring half, joined by a uniform sample of earlier accepted elites from a score-ranked memory capped at 32. The policy fits each selected sequence toward frozen-prior log likelihood plus 60 times its accepted reward, using equal row weights and bounded clipped Adam updates. It then generates complete SMILES by ancestral token sampling; RDKit validation and canonical novelty checks refill a full announced batch directly from the policy. There is no surrogate, graph-edit generator, candidate-library ranking or randomized-SMILES training in this representative. The source comparison with current-only root n-4552e16d798a leaves preparation, model, sampler, ingestion and protocol functions unchanged; replay changes objective initialization and training membership/update accounting. The representative completes three seeds with macro mean 0.5075540530185733 and population SD 0.01151827890752029, but its paired root comparison remains seed 0 only. Curate c-a5a5c8a507 confirms replay gradient contributions in all 280 eligible new updates and reduced historical target error in 278; 328 of their 1400 historical exposures nevertheless have mathematically unattainable positive log-probability targets. The Layers therefore isolate prior learning, accepted-memory membership, reward-to-policy adaptation and direct generation/admission before integration. The dependency graph unrolls one learning-and-proposal iteration: evaluator feedback returns to accepted_elite_memory in the next iteration, not through a cyclic same-iteration edge. Memory commitment occurs after optimization in the implementation but depends on accepted elite records, not learned parameters. The frozen 24-Child cap and four-Child waves allow six waves: one each for prior, memory, generation and integration, with two for adaptation to address target attainability and productive current/history learning as separate possible mechanisms.

L07.method_thesis: The implemented method is a reciprocal neural/graph optimizer with posterior selection of graph offspring. Unlabeled SMILES train a recurrent prior; every objective starts a fresh adaptable copy and fresh accepted-only memory. After each feedback message, exact accepted molecular trajectories train the policy through trajectory balance, a learned log normalizer and categorical regularization toward the unchanged prior. The current cycle emits one ancestral policy batch directly, then two graph batches. Accepted policy molecules refresh the scored population; the first graph batch protects a real descendant of a fresh policy parent. Connected-fragment crossover and atom/bond edits produce a temporary novel offspring pool. A task-local Morgan/Tanimoto Gaussian posterior fits all earlier accepted labels, predicts the pool jointly, and an independent correlated function draw chooses each remaining evaluation slot. Only real accepted emissions enter survivors, replay and later posterior fits; unselected pool molecules remain unlabeled. Accepted graph descendants therefore influence subsequent policy sampling and later breeding. The current representative n-cc2d839e347b confirms both selection and reciprocal feedback across its complete replicas, while its supplied analysis leaves weak parent-beating yield, predictive calibration and chemically credible core coverage unresolved. Its direct-submission ancestor n-39550a3f15d7 supplies only the reported screening comparison; replicated component activation does not isolate a replicated score benefit. The six Layers below group preparation, neural learning, graph generation, conditional modeling, allocation and cross-component validation. Dependency edges describe the forward data dependencies within a feedback boundary and their development prerequisites. The runtime feedback loop is unrolled across boundaries: emitted molecules are scored outside the candidate, and the next accepted message becomes the next boundary input. Integration is a cross-cutting attribution Layer, not an extra molecular transformation.

L16.method_thesis: L16 is a task-local best-admissible-neighbor graph walk with short-term structural memory. The supplied representative n-9f7c7ec50039 prepares a fixed configuration without consuming a corpus or training a model, starts at the highest-scoring supplied molecular observation, and keeps separate current-state, best-observed, proposed-identity and pending-feedback records. From a Kekule representation of the current graph it samples atom substitutions, bond-order changes, path additions/deletions/insertions/contractions and ring opening/closure. Sanitization, connectivity, radical and atom-domain checks precede the repaired parse-and-reserialize identity normalization and canonical novelty check. For each valid fresh neighbor it computes signed occurrence changes of canonical rooted radius-one motifs. An active restriction vetoes the neighbor only when both inverse signs match restrictions carrying the same selected-transition provenance; one-sign and cross-transition-only matches remain admissible. The first complete announced batch of admissible neighbors is submitted directly, with no score predictor or acquisition model. Real accepted scores join the exact pending proposal. The highest-scoring accepted neighbor becomes the next current graph even on a worsening move; equal maxima currently use the canonical lexical tie rule. Every accepted observation also updates the independent best archive. A completed transition ages memory, expires entries and installs a bounded, sign-balanced selection of inverse attributes, with latest-transition overlap refresh. Documented generation obstruction can release the globally oldest live restriction; an empty accepted batch does not move or age the walk. The workflow graph below unrolls one proposal/feedback iteration. Its next current graph, seen set, archive and live-memory state return through the declared workflow boundary as inputs to the following iteration; these time-delayed feedback edges are not same-iteration dependency edges. Memory update operations belong to the memory component even when invoked after the feedback component emits its selected-transition event. The complete representative evidence and clusters c-c24599cabf and c-cfe57a29f0 establish real memory-dependent decisions and recovery of the recorded identity mismatch. They leave productive neighborhood chemistry, the score contribution of the surviving vetoes and plateau navigation unresolved. Reactive heteroatom bonds, unusual sulfur environments, dense closures and unspecified stereochemistry motivate chemistry-aware local research without supplying objective-specific answers. Passive alternative-batch traces are allocation diagnostics, not scored alternative trajectories. The identity repair remains a correctness invariant throughout Development.

approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from accepted scored molecules. It samples breeding parents from high-scoring population quantiles, applies connected-fragment crossover or successive local atom and bond edits, and fills a fresh surplus pool after graph validation, stable canonical identity checks and duplicate rejection. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled. A Gaussian process fitted to the complete task-local accepted archive uses integer-count Morgan features and generalized Tanimoto similarity. Correlated function draws choose distinct pool members for evaluation; real accepted scores then update the archive and a bounded score-greedy population.
approach.novelty: Remove the composite posterior selector's influence on successful emissions: take the first announced batch of valid unique pool members in generation order. Keep the complete inherited pool, model fitting, full covariance and original draws as passive controls. Earlier siblings removed counts, sampled residuals or their correlation while retaining predictive allocation. This test instead removes all predictive ranking at once at the existing pool boundary, treating the selector as one module. The independent sampled comparator records which identities would differ on each actual pool; it supplies no scores for unevaluated alternatives.

nodes.hypothesis: Remove all posterior-based influence on successful offspring allocation by selecting the first announced-batch-size valid unique candidates in inherited generation order from the fully generated pool, while retaining the complete accepted-only posterior computation and original draws passively.

finding_summary.headline: Generation-order allocation loses 0.124388 in mean endpoint score despite retaining full pool and model effort.
finding_summary.insights:
This closes a different question from the earlier count, residual and correlation controls: allocating evaluations using the complete predictive selector matters even when generation effort is held at the inherited full-pool boundary. The earlier selector addition also enlarged the pool and lacked a complete matched Parent panel, so it could not establish this conditional contrast. Local parent beats increased from 629 to 653, yet incumbent improvements fell from 258 to 163; adaptive local success is not a substitute for endpoint quality. The present loss does not apportion value among posterior means, counts, residual amplitude or correlation, and separate sibling losses cannot be added.

A plausible place to investigate the loss is how evaluation choices preserve useful chemical relationships across adaptive histories. The molecular report finds that generation-order output still reaches useful nitrile and aryl-amine alternatives, including both improved endpoints, while other streams move into densely connected heteroatom frameworks and miss strong Parent families. Reactive bonds, questionable ring geometry and unspecified stereochemistry persist. This concerns the evaluated distribution; it does not show that better alternatives were absent from the complete pools or identify a chemical mediator. Passive alternatives have no counterfactual scores.

Removing predictive influence is also different from removing computational cost: all surplus generation and model computations remain, and numerical failures would still use the inherited routes. No reduced-pool, compute-saving or optimizer-deletion conclusion follows. Actual recovery branches remain unexercised despite passing deterministic synthetic checks.
finding_summary.results:
All 435 successful batches evaluated the first ten members of a completed 160-member pool, with zero prefix-order violations or choices outside that prefix. The passive original sampler selected a different set in all 435 batches, and its sampled values strictly preferred another candidate on 4,317 of 4,350 generation-order masks. Thus the removal changed real evaluation choices under strong exposure. All 435 fits, full covariance factorizations and original normal arrays remained computed; the accepted-only feedback and identity-bound prediction joins passed. No natural numerical fallback or incomplete pool occurred.

Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.595670 to 0.471282, a paired change of -0.124388, well beyond the registered 0.002 loss scale. Seed macro changes were -0.134968, -0.105769 and -0.132426. All five task means declined. Thirteen of fifteen task-seed endpoints declined; zaleplon_mpo seeds zero and one improved by 0.019694 and 0.005802. Macro population deviation changed from 0.026593 to 0.014583. Correct removal and the predicted score loss support positive contribution from the composite selector in this exact full-pool search loop.

molecular.headline: Aromatic families remain, with useful nitrile and aryl-amine alternatives alongside peroxides, O-halogen bonds and difficult rings
molecular.overall_character: All supplied Child n-01b48dd09404 and published Parent n-62daf219c70a trajectories were read, with no missing paths or uncovered objectives. The brief reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true for Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2, with no profile mismatches. Each task has 900 Child trajectory records, including 870 optimizer records, and a complete matched Parent panel. The fixed initial molecules and their scores match within each paired task/seed. These trajectories describe accepted evaluated molecules; they do not enumerate every valid pool member, unselected candidate or rejected graph. The digest field proposed_by_optimizer and all chemistry frequencies below therefore concern recorded optimizer evaluations, not a census of the complete inherited generation pool. An emitted molecule, an accepted evaluation, and the highest observed retained endpoint are different observations. The digest final_molecules are late seed-2 evaluations, not every seed's retained incumbent; full trajectories supply the endpoint comparisons. The registered contrast removes posterior influence on successful allocation at full inherited pool effort while retaining posterior computation passively. This report does not audit activation, describe deletion of the optimizer, attribute chemistry to an individual posterior component, or infer pool reduction or compute savings. The output contains indole amides and ketones, nitrile-bearing biaryl amines attached to unsaturated ether/peroxide rings, linked aza-aromatic carbonyl systems, aryl tertiary amines, fused nitrogen diones, and both fluorinated aza-aromatics and densely oxygenated nonaromatic cages. Child ring-closure-string incidences are 0.9598, 0.9724, 0.9805, 0.9448 and 0.9437 in fixed task order; aromatic-string incidences are 0.9506, 0.9701, 0.9563, 0.9402 and 0.6609. These measure feature presence in molecular strings, not perceived ring counts or aromatic-atom fractions. The final stream includes a wholly nonaromatic seed family, so aromatic richness is not universal within every seed. Formal-charge and stereocentre-string incidences are 0.0 throughout. Available aliphatic amines and potentially stereogenic centres remain plainly present. Read-only RDKit perception of the exact trajectory graphs supports size, ring and functional-group descriptions; no new objective, affinity, feasibility or synthesis scores were calculated. The overall chemistry remains questionable in synthetic plausibility and weak in drug-likeness, with ordinary medicinal functional groups mixed with O-F/O-Cl bonds, peroxides, acyl fluoride, unusual carbon-sulfur triple bonds, strained unsaturation and unspecified stereochemistry. The relatively conventional tertiary-amine ketone and successful carbonyl-free nitrile family are important counterexamples: neither reactive bonds nor the Parent's exact scaffold families are universal necessities. Across-seed structural diversity is moderate, with narrower related series among each seed's leaders. No general absence of rings, amines or scaffold alternatives is demonstrated, especially in the unobserved pool. The original n-c55c3d520a2c report and its carry-forward in n-62daf219c70a were read through the fresh evidence index. The transferable gaps retain that provenance and are re-observed here under the current complete matched conditions; historical origin is not extra replication. Only Child SMILES from the digest or the trusted citation_trajectory_paths are quoted. Parent-only structures are described by published task/seed/evaluation. Read-only evidence and descriptors are in .slots/r0017-02-ablation-L01/molecular/trajectory_audit.json and inspected_records.json; history_molecular_sources.json preserves the original reports and source hashes. No structural association below assigns a reward to an unselected pool molecule or establishes which chemical change mediated the endpoint contrast.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-1 leader (evaluation 203) is a compact nitrile-bearing phenyl/pyridyl system connected through an NH group to an unsaturated oxygen ring containing an O-O bond and a fluoroethyl side chain. Related high-scoring members instead have a cyclic ether without peroxide. This family contains no carbonyl and no N-halogen bond. Seed 0 reaches a fused/bridged indole carboxanilide with methoxy, methyl and ordinary aryl fluorine substitution; seed 2 reaches an indole-linked aryl ketone with an additional O-CH2-N-containing ring. These leading molecules are compact, ring-rich and substantially aromatic. Mean Child SMILES length is 45.4, with a maximum of 95 and halogen-string incidence of 0.7609. The Parent leaders are an amino-substituted cumulene on an N-chloro indole (seed 0, evaluation 289), an N-hydroxy pyridyl amide with N-F (seed 1, 293), and an N-chloro indole vicinal diketone (seed 2, 294). The Child reaches higher retained endpoints in seeds 0 and 1 and a lower endpoint in seed 2, while avoiding N-halogen bonds in all these cited Child leaders. That is heterogeneous chemical change, not a uniform loss of useful chemistry.
liabilities: The seed-1 leader contains an O-O bond in an unsaturated ring. Its supplied score does not demonstrate stability or make the peroxide necessary; a cyclic ether relative also scores highly.

The other leaders have unusual fused/bridged connectivity or an O-CH2-N local environment and no stereochemical specification. Their conventional amide, ketone and aryl fluorine groups do not certify a route for the entire graph.
Very small fragments and much larger joined structures can both have negligible scores; molecular size is not a sufficient chemical quality rule.
missing_features: Consistent conventional alternatives preserving the favorable aromatic/polar organization are not established throughout the evaluated stream; the nonperoxide cyclic ether is already accessible and useful, so peroxide chemistry is not an unavoidable limitation.
Defined stereochemistry and conformational identity are absent for the fused/bridged saturated centres, while the unsaturated peroxide ring requires a distinct stability assessment.

The trajectory does not reveal an exact absent target pharmacophore. Both carbonyl-bearing and carbonyl-free leading frameworks exist, so the missing capability is reliable feasible alternatives rather than a prescribed carbonyl motif.

transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably retain useful molecular context while controlling fragmentation and excessive elaboration among evaluated proposals.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Use task-local feedback to preserve informative combinations of molecular regions while permitting simplification and scaffold replacement. Avoid turning a recurring functional group into a mandatory template or a size statistic into a fixed cutoff. The evaluated distribution cannot establish whether the full pool lacked better-sized alternatives, nor imply smaller pools, reduced generation effort, compute savings or a guaranteed score improvement.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The general concern originates in n-c55c3d520a2c and was carried by n-62daf219c70a. This re-observation is n-01b48dd09404 versus that published Parent on the complete matched Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2, 300 observations per objective, batch size 10 and the frozen Research-in-Depth epoch-1 profile with direct aromatic exchange disabled. Its registered condition is removal of posterior influence on successful allocation while retaining full inherited pool generation and passive posterior computation. The chemistry evidence covers accepted evaluations and their retained best values, not all unselected pool members; historical origin is not extra replication. Some streams remain among closely related halogen placements, short side chains or ring closures, and a compact Parent heterocyclic family is absent from the corresponding Child leading set. A current carbonyl-free nitrile family and a fused carboxanilide each exceed their matched Parent endpoint, and the flexible amine/ketone stream remains useful. Other streams instead retain a nonaromatic N/O/S cage or a crowded sulfone/diaminoalkene family. These counterexamples support uneven useful coverage, not global scaffold collapse, universal inferiority of new chemistry, or lack of those alternatives in unselected pools.
transferable_gaps.gap: Plausible useful scaffold alternatives are not consistently represented across evaluated seed streams, despite genuine successful changes of scaffold.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support feasible scaffold transformations that preserve or replace useful functional relationships learned from feedback, and judge their evaluated descendants rather than counting new strings alone. Use successes outside inherited scaffold families to constrain any proposed chemistry rule. This conditional coverage concern does not show which posterior component supplied useful allocation, label unselected molecules with rewards, attribute the outcome to pool effort, or establish that more diversity alone raises the endpoint.

nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

approach.method_basis: The Parent retains the highest-scoring accepted molecules as breeding parents and fits a fingerprint Gaussian process to every accepted label. It draws a preferred score band, chooses a molecule uniformly inside that band, breeds a fresh pool by graph crossover and mutation, and selects evaluations through correlated posterior draws. Feedback improves the archive, survivor population and posterior, but the parent sampler treats equally ranked eligible parents alike even when their evaluated offspring histories differ.
approach.novelty: Use the actual results of earlier offspring to allocate breeding opportunities within each existing score band. A parent gains credit when an accepted child surpasses the best molecule known before that child's batch; its smoothed historical success fraction determines its within-band sampling weight. This targets productive progress against the same batch incumbent instead of rewarding a child merely for beating a weak generating parent. The completed siblings tested equal core mass and core-diverse survival; this child keeps greedy survival and learns allocation from descendant outcomes.

nodes.hypothesis: Weight breeding-parent draws within each inherited score quantile by a smoothed fraction of that parent's earlier accepted offspring that beat their generation batch's pre-feedback incumbent.

finding_summary.headline: Parent-success weighting changed breeding and produced more small gains, but lowered final scores
finding_summary.insights: The historical fraction enriched the intended weight without identifying stronger absolute proposal quality. Its fixed smoothing prior gave untested parents substantial opportunity: their share of actual parent draws rose from 36.91% to 50.50%, while the share with an earlier incumbent-beating offspring fell from 14.51% to 13.39%. Thus much of the observed effect was trying parents with no evaluated offspring history. More progress events against the evolving incumbent did not imply a better search trajectory; their mean size fell from 0.02311 to 0.02068, and the search finished lower. Correctly freezing the reference within a batch removes feedback-order leakage but cannot make different runs' incumbent thresholds equally difficult. These results narrow the useful claim to executable, feedback-sensitive allocation, with negative transfer under this seed panel and budget. Credit is conditional on the posterior selector having chosen an offspring for evaluation, and crossover assigns the same outcome to both parents, so the selected outcome groups cannot establish a causal parent effect. The molecular assessment also found that the modest increase in core coverage retained strained rings, reactive heteroatom variants and oversized repeated assemblies. Parent-outcome credit alone supplied no demonstrated control over those chemical liabilities.
finding_summary.results: Historical credit changed parent selection on the recorded trajectories. Within-band probabilities differed from uniform in 101,614 of 109,053 draws (93.18%), and the selected parent differed from the passive uniform choice using the same random variate in 43,310 draws (39.71%). Selected parents had mean historical weight 0.3649, compared with 0.3037 under uniform selection over those same eligible lists. The accepted archive, score-ranked survival, offspring production and posterior selection retained their prescribed behavior. Among 4,350 scored offspring, strict improvements over the incumbent known before generation increased from 286 to 304, sequential incumbent improvements from 218 to 228, and strict best-parent beats from 565 to 578. These were smaller gains overall: cumulative incumbent improvement across the fifteen task/seed runs fell from 5.0382 to 4.7145. Mean generating-best-parent score fell from 0.4196 to 0.3840, and mean offspring score from 0.3192 to 0.2939. The three-seed final macro mean fell from 0.54437 to 0.52279, a paired mean change of -0.02158; the seed changes were -0.03001, -0.05149 and +0.01676. All five task means fell, with the largest loss on sitagliptin_mpo (-0.05863). The intended +0.002 mean improvement was not achieved.
