molecular.headline: Aromatic amides and amines coexist with strained small rings, repeated large assemblies and reactive heteroatom variants
molecular.overall_character: All supplied current and parent trajectories were read; every current task contains 900 molecules and 870 optimizer proposals. The output is strongly aromatic and ring-bearing, with aromatic-token rates from 0.9747 to 0.9874 and ring-closure rates from 0.9874 to 0.9931. Recognizable indole amides, quinoline-linked carbonyl rings and aryl amines coexist with highly constrained small rings, expanded nitrogen-containing diones, reactive nitrogen/oxygen substituents and oversized repeated molecular assemblies. The deco_hop proposal strings have mean length 97.6 and maximum 234, while all tasks also sample very small fragments. Many large products join recognizable fragments without retaining the useful scale or arrangement of the better molecules. All charged-token and stereocentre-token rates are 0.0; the first does not establish neutral solution forms for basic amines, and the second leaves stereogenic saturated frameworks undefined. Diversity is moderate across distinct seed families but locally narrow among the displayed leaders. Several high-scoring products have conventional bonding patterns, yet overall synthetic plausibility remains questionable because strained unsaturated rings, unusual ring connections, N-halogen groups, peroxides and reactive unsaturation persist.

per_task.generated_character: The strongest molecule is a compact bromoindole carboxamide with ethyl, methoxy and N-methyl fluoropyridyl substitution. This is a recognizable, synthetically plausible aromatic amide. Closely scoring relatives replace the indole ring by a benzene-annulated, highly unsaturated small carbon ring, retaining a bromo substituent and an N-methyl pyridyl amide. Other seeds give halogenated enaminone-like aryl compounds or fused aromatic amide frameworks. The low tail includes methane, fluorine, a small cyclic peroxide and a much larger assembly containing repeated aryl/enamide units. Thus the output spans both useful compact aromatic carbonyl chemistry and substantial chemical degeneration.
liabilities: Several near-leading structures contain a benzene-annulated, highly unsaturated small carbon ring with substantial strain and stability concerns.
N-F, N-Cl and alpha-halo carbonyl groups occur in another strong family; these are more reactive than ordinary aryl halogens.
Peroxide fragments, gross molecular duplication and undefined stereochemistry in later fused-ring products remain present.
missing_features: The lowest fragments and repeated large assemblies lack the compact aromatic carbonyl arrangement retained by the leading amides.

The displayed high-scoring series does not systematically preserve ordinary indole-like ring chemistry while varying the useful amide and pyridyl substitution; the best indole shows that a highly strained annulated ring is not necessary for a strong score here.
The N-halo enaminone series lacks a matched set of stable nitrogen substituents preserving the same carbonyl/aromatic arrangement. Equal halogen-swap scores do not establish a chemical requirement.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The bromoindole amide scores 0.4387992465191, while the small-ring aromatic amide relative reaches 0.438122145211641. A conventional indole framework therefore already supports the strongest observed score without requiring the more strained alternative. Adding thiol or amino substituents to the small-ring series gives 0.42853301243482195 or 0.42320968985939855. Separate alpha-halo carbonyl/N-halo enamine variants share 0.41048050866648705 despite swapping carbon-bound chlorine for fluorine or N-fluorine for N-chlorine. Those equal values do not demonstrate a need for the reactive bonds. The repeated aryl/enamide assembly scores 6.921499488854122e-25 and tiny fragments score 0.0. Compared with the parent, seed 1 reaches 0.4387992465191 versus 0.4126819838532174 with a sulfur-containing fused framework. Current seed 0 and seed 2 reach 0.41048050866648705 and 0.3918060951569304 versus parental 0.4463521672202675 and 0.4163503402962837.

per_task.generated_character: The displayed leaders connect an O/N-containing aromatic carbonyl heterocycle to a densely cross-connected polycyclic aza-aromatic framework. They carry fluorine, fluoroalkenyl, formate or aldehyde substitution and oxygen-linked terminal alkynes; some relatives replace the other alkyne with ethyl or methoxy. These are rigid and heavily aromatic, with crowded ring connections. Another seed produces smaller aryl-amino carbonyl/thiocarbonyl heterocycles, whereas seed 0 grows very large repeated dione, aryl and acylated nitrogen assemblies. Tiny fragments also remain in the proposal set. The leading fragments are recognizable, but the rigid topology and reactive appendages make the assembled chemistry less straightforward than simple heteroaryl substitution would suggest.
liabilities: Oxygen-linked alkynes, aryl formates, aldehydes and occasional reactive halogen connections complicate chemical stability.
Densely cross-connected aromatic frameworks can demand difficult ring topology even when SMILES parsing succeeds.
Very large repeated dione/acyl/aryl assemblies create a heavy size tail, and extra copies do not consistently improve the recorded score.
missing_features: The smallest fragments lack the connected aromatic and carbonyl/heteroatom organization of the better products.
The large repeated assemblies do not consistently preserve useful chemical scale; the current leaders show that extensive repetition is not necessary for a stronger observed score.

The displayed series incompletely covers ordinary ring topologies and stable substituents that retain the same aromatic polar-group arrangement. The equal-score ethyl/alkyne pair already provides one chemically simpler option.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The leading aza-aromatic compound scores 0.6175164849513612, compared with 0.6153329352045387 for a closely related structure with carbon at the corresponding aryl position. Replacing the latter's carbon-bound alkyne with ethyl preserves exactly 0.6153329352045387; an alternative more reduced ring arrangement also has that score. Thus the observed scores favor the overall aromatic heterocycle arrangement without demonstrating a need for all unsaturation. Small fragments score 0.5. The largest seed-0 repeated assemblies reach 0.5971495676310452, below the compact leading family, although this cross-family comparison does not isolate size as the only difference. The parent has best scores 0.6004556752278376, 0.6324703199409752 and 0.6083454583246726 across seeds, versus current 0.5971495676310452, 0.6175164849513612 and 0.6115618661257607. Current seed-1 leaders lack the parent's peroxide-chlorine appendage, but still have reactive alkynyl-oxygen and other difficult chemistry.

per_task.generated_character: The strongest family contains an aryl-substituted benzene-annulated small carbon ring, phenol, aryl fluorine, a methyl thioether and a saturated diaza ring with an aminomethyl substituent. These provide hydrophobic aromatic surfaces and several potentially basic nitrogen centres. Related molecules replace the aminomethyl connection with imine, enamine or cumulated imine functionality, or add another saturated nitrogen ring. The small carbon ring is strained but has conventional bonds; its multiple stereogenic relationships are unassigned. Low molecules are acid/amide/sulfonamide-rich compounds, small sulfur fragments or very large products combining multiple copies of the stronger frameworks.
liabilities: The benzene-annulated small ring and several substituted saturated centres create strain and stereochemical complexity.
Cumulated imines, cumulated sulfur-containing unsaturation and N-halogenated alternatives introduce reactive functionality.
Aminal-like nitrogen rings, alpha-fluoroamine environments and multiple potentially basic sites need more chemical definition than a neutral unlabelled SMILES provides.
missing_features: The lowest acid/amide/sulfonamide examples lack the accessible aliphatic amine arrangement of the high-scoring family.
The doubled assemblies lose the useful compact size and spacing of the individual aryl/amine framework.

Matched stable alternatives to cumulated imine or thione functionality are incomplete, although the leading aminomethyl molecule already shows that these groups are not essential to a strong observed score.
Relative and absolute configurations across the small carbon ring and substituted diaza ring are unspecified.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The aminomethyl-containing leader scores 0.9868145791586695, while its imine relative scores 0.9736699331433097. Several cumulated-imine or thione-containing relatives also score highly, but the strongest displayed molecule does not need those reactive unsaturations. Chlorine and fluorine variants at the saturated diaza ring share 0.973570128548226. Early acid/amide and sulfonamide structures score 0.000719339566735797 and 0.0008839899990958555. Large doubled versions of the aryl/amine framework score only 0.033524275750952556 and 0.03499409918861479. This associates the gradient with a compact aryl/aliphatic-amine arrangement and shows a clear loss when much larger assemblies are formed. Current per-seed maxima are 0.9606175719472576, 0.9250515635604988 and 0.9868145791586695, versus parental 0.9908331648929692, 0.9512348232667347 and 0.9914038363125457. Both generations retain aryl-rich amine chemistry, with different ring frameworks.

per_task.generated_character: The leading compounds connect an ethoxyquinoline-like aromatic group to an expanded nitrogen-rich dicarbonyl ring fused to a small unsaturated nitrogen ring. The latter ranges from an azetene-like connection to still smaller azirine-like alternatives. Carbonyls, NH and N-methyl substituents recur, and some relatives insert an alkylamino linker. Larger alternatives combine additional carbon rings and N/O-containing bridges around the same general aromatic/dicarbonyl motifs. The low tail contains methane, ethane, a hydrocarbon polyene and a small haloacetyl hydroxylamine. The leading compounds are of moderate size but have ring-strain and synthetic-access concerns despite their ordinary amide-like fragments.
liabilities: Small unsaturated nitrogen rings fused to larger carbonyl-containing rings raise strain and stability concerns.
Additional N-N connections, N/O bridges and dense ring closures add chemical complexity in alternative families.
Repeated assemblies and fragment-like products lose the useful organization without supplying a distinct better-performing chemical pattern.
missing_features: The low fragments lack the combined aromatic and dicarbonyl heterocycle arrangement of the stronger molecules.

The leading series lacks enough ordinary, less strained ring connections preserving that arrangement; near-equal scores across ring and linker changes do not establish a need for the smallest unsaturated nitrogen rings.
More elaborate fused alternatives leave possible stereogenic relationships unspecified, while the flatter leading structures still require a feasible constrained ring geometry.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The directly connected ethoxyquinoline/dicarbonyl polycycle scores 0.21529770451127778. Expanding a carbonyl-ring connection gives 0.21407917379021693, while a more contracted small nitrogen-ring arrangement gives 0.21194288404250966. Adding an ethylamino or aminomethyl connection yields 0.21138239979795584 or 0.21008596456279097, and a much larger elaborated polycycle scores 0.21052909287008859. These close values favor retention of the main aromatic/dicarbonyl organization, without showing a need for greater ring complexity or longer linkers. A repeated large final product scores 0.1509909661241802. Tiny fragments score 0.0 and a hydrocarbon polyene scores 0.007693218186208301. Current seed 2 reaches 0.21529770451127778 versus the parent's 0.21037674112349405 with a more expanded quinoline-linked dicarbonyl family; seed 0 and seed 1 reach 0.19245008972987526 and 0.20259185417308956 versus parental 0.22405709718343647 and 0.2133697489012744.

per_task.generated_character: The leading family contains an expanded nitrogen-rich dicarbonyl ring connected through several bonds to a phenolic aromatic system. Fluoromethyl, N-N-linked fluoromethyl or N-methylamino groups and ordinary methyl thioether substitution recur. This is a compact but unusual conjugated polycyclic framework, not a simple isolated dione. Other strong examples contain fluorinated small carbon rings, N-F bonds and N-S-H substituents. The lowest molecules join multiple aromatic dione units into large assemblies. Thus carbonyl and fluorine content are abundant, but their topology, bond type and chemical scale differ sharply across the score range.
liabilities: N-N substituents, direct N-F and N-S-H groups introduce labile or reactive chemistry.
Expanded conjugated nitrogen-rich rings and highly connected aromatic systems require synthetic and geometric scrutiny.
Repeated large dione assemblies and very strained fluorinated carbon-ring alternatives remain in the output.
missing_features: The low repeated assemblies lack the useful compact arrangement of polar groups and fluorinated substituents.
Some weaker close relatives fail to preserve the stronger examples' carbon-linked fluoromethyl organization, substituting direct N-F or additional fluorination instead.

The current displayed leaders do not cover the compact aryl-dione/aminomethyl arrangement of the stronger parent seed-1 molecule; this is a chemical coverage gap, not proof of a uniquely required target motif.
Stereogenic small-ring alternatives have no explicit configurations, while the conjugated expanded-ring leaders require feasible geometry and electronic structure beyond token-level aromaticity.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The fluoromethyl-rich phenolic dicarbonyl framework scores 0.5119423040474254; extending its N-N-linked fluorinated side chain gives 0.4904700558333632. A related N-N-linked fluoromethyl structure scores 0.47515676971860416 versus 0.44663453188929914 for its direct N-fluorinated relative. In another displayed pair, changing N-fluoromethyl to N-fluorination gives 0.4257652136908921 rather than 0.49995623590669624; changing it to difluoromethyl gives 0.20047296487227245. Fluorine placement and connection therefore matter more clearly than fluorine abundance. Repeated dione assemblies score as low as 2.9127834142160573e-62. Current seed 2 reaches 0.5119423040474254 versus parental 0.4071395189354175, but seed 0 and seed 1 reach 0.4269183152635783 and 0.352917314371487 versus parental 0.4759777345546235 and 0.5845583988949146. The stronger parent seed-1 family combined a compact aryl dione with carbon-bound aminomethyl and fluorinated substituents, rather than the present expanded ring framework.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The output includes a proposal-string maximum of 234 and mean of 97.6 in its most size-expanded task, alongside fragments such as methane or small halogen-containing species. A compact aryl/amine leader scores 0.9868145791586695, while doubled relatives score 0.033524275750952556 and 0.03499409918861479. Large repeated dione assemblies also occupy the lowest score tail.
transferable_gaps.gap: Useful local frameworks are still lost through molecular duplication or degeneration into tiny fragments.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve a useful molecular scale and the connected functional-group arrangement when changing structures. Offer meaningful scaffold and linker alternatives without making local variation depend on adding whole copies or deleting most of the framework.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A conventional indole amide scores 0.4387992465191 beside a highly unsaturated small-ring relative at 0.438122145211641. An aminomethyl-bearing structure scores 0.9868145791586695 versus 0.9736699331433097 for its imine relative. An ethyl/alkyne pair has the identical score 0.6153329352045387.
transferable_gaps.gap: Stable, less strained alternatives are not consistently retained despite strong observed examples.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Include matched simplifications that preserve useful aromatic, amine and carbonyl placement while replacing reactive unsaturation or strained ring connections. Distinguish ordinary medicinal bonds from N-halogen, peroxide and cumulated imine/thione functionality.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every task has stereocentre-token rate 0.0. Displayed products include substituted benzene-annulated small carbon rings, fluorinated saturated nitrogen rings, small unsaturated nitrogen rings and densely connected polycycles. Some leading flat structures are achiral, but their constrained topology still carries geometric requirements.
transferable_gaps.gap: Stereogenic products and constrained ring systems lack adequate geometric definition.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Represent feasible stereochemistry where it exists and preserve it through structural edits. Broaden access to ordinary ring sizes and less constrained connections rather than treating successful parsing or aromatic tokens as evidence of feasible three-dimensional chemistry.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Several close comparisons distinguish carbon-linked fluoromethyl from direct N-fluorination or additional fluorination, with scores ranging from 0.49995623590669624 to 0.20047296487227245 within a displayed family. Other leading aromatic/dicarbonyl relatives tolerate small linker or ring changes with little score difference, so simple heteroatom or halogen counts do not identify the useful arrangement.
transferable_gaps.gap: Matched placement of polar groups and fluorinated substituents remains incompletely covered.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Generate coherent matched series that vary linker length, attachment position, heteroatom identity and fluorine bond type while retaining the remaining framework. Let observed feedback identify which arrangements matter, without assuming that more heteroatoms, fluorines or rings improve a molecule.

approach.method_basis: The Parent maintains a live population of the best accepted molecular graphs, ordered by score and then admission serial. It breeds from three preferred score bands using fragment crossover and local mutations, with the inherited continuation and retry rules. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled. Stable molecular identity and novelty checks admit a full fresh proposal pool, and a count-fingerprint Gaussian process uses correlated posterior samples to allocate the evaluation batch. Every accepted score enters the complete model archive; high-scoring offspring can survive and breed later. At exactly tied scores the current serial ordering favors older records.
approach.novelty: Give newer accepted batches priority only when survivor scores are exactly equal, while preserving serial order within each batch. This changes the deterministic retention key and keeps the existing score-band sampler. The intended route is that equally scored recent offspring can survive or reach a preferred breeding band and expose useful future neighborhoods without sacrificing a strict score decision in that local contest. The frozen-initial-cohort test removed recursive reuse; the parallel uniform-parent control changes the draw law. This test retains both recursion and the original draw law. Historical size and distance preferences selected one walk state and provide counterexamples, not a transferred rule. Only one current-Parent test of this exact recency key is proposed; preserving current scores does not guarantee later gains.

nodes.hypothesis: Within score-greedy live-population retention, order records by descending raw accepted score, then descending origin_batch only at exact score equality, then ascending serial within each batch, retaining the original population cap and score-quantile parent sampler.

finding_summary.headline: Recent tied survivors reach real breeding, but preserving current scores still lowers the paired mean by 0.020779.
finding_summary.insights:
Most first changes in the search come from deterministic reordering rather than stronger sampling pressure: 14 of 15 first differing parent draws occur in states with unchanged first-parent probability maps. A fixed random index can select a different tied molecule even when its marginal probability is unchanged. Later band shifts do reach real breeders, so the result is not explained by absent exposure. However, the population-cutoff route remains unused, and the two evaluated products of newly supported parents both lose to their best parents. Local descendant wins and widespread later ancestry do not identify which part of the key change causes the endpoint loss.

Immediate score equality protects a local decision, not the usefulness of future neighborhoods. The molecular assessment finds chemically distinct exact ties, reactive bond environments, questionable ring geometry and unresolved stereochemistry alongside useful conventional amines and carbonyl frameworks. A newer record supplies no chemical-quality guarantee. The large loss in one decoration-hopping seed coexists with gains in its other two seeds; the very small first docking loss coexists with larger docking losses in the other seeds. These exceptions remain part of the complete result.

The single registered gain test ends with this negative conditional result. Earlier structural-retention and walk-tie failures remain separate counterexamples, and the two identical compactness panels count as one history. This experiment does not assign separate membership and ordering effects, establish chemical mediation, resolve the whole evolutionary foundation or combine with the other shared-Parent interventions.
finding_summary.results:
The new tie priority changes 3,504 of 4,350 local retained orders and 207 survivor sets while preserving every same-contest retained score vector and all 15 initial populations. At the 435 states actually used for generation, 136 first-parent probability maps and 46 support sets differ. Parents whose probability increases are used in 2,813 draws and participate in 126 evaluated products: 16 beat the best generating parent, nine tie and 101 lose. Seven raise the incumbent. All 145 records newly kept at the population cutoff remain outside later breeding support and never breed after that protection.

The mechanism activates, including real probability shifts and evaluated descendants, but the complete endpoint prediction fails. Mean final Top-1 falls from 0.595670 to 0.574891, a paired change of -0.020779 against the required +0.002. Seed changes are -0.041461, +0.001143 and -0.022017. Seven of fifteen endpoints improve and eight decline; four task means decline. Every supplied run completes and every proposal pool fills. Lower seed dispersion accompanies the lower mean.

molecular.headline: Aromatic heterocycles and aryl amines remain prominent; exact-score ties preserve reactive and geometrically doubtful chemistry
molecular.overall_character: All supplied Child n-03acfe1ba8af and published Parent n-62daf219c70a trajectories were present and read. The immutable brief independently reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true on Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2, with no profile mismatch or uncovered objective. Each task has 900 Child records, including 870 optimizer evaluations; each matched task/seed has the same ten fixed initial molecule/score records and 300 distinct accepted identities. Every Child retained best exceeds its fixed initial best. The observed chemistry therefore includes useful search even where its matched Parent endpoint is higher. The Child repeatedly produces substituted indole or benzothiophene amides, nitrogen-rich fused heterocycles, linked azaaryl systems, aryl/cyclic amines and carbonyl-rich bridged rings. There are multiple chemical families across seeds, with much narrower leading series within individual seeds. In fixed task order, ring-closure-string incidences are 0.9632, 0.9678, 0.9736, 0.9851 and 0.9678; aromatic-string incidences are 0.9621, 0.9655, 0.9632, 0.9805 and 0.9575. These are incidences of SMILES text features, not perceived ring counts or aromatic-atom fractions. Formal-charge and stereocentre-string incidences are 0.0 throughout. Distinct identities across the respective three-seed panels are 876, 876, 875, 875 and 873; cross-seed recurrence is separate from the 300 unique accepted identities within each run. Read-only RDKit perception of all supplied trajectories supports the chemical descriptions and size summaries. No objective, affinity or synthetic-feasibility score was calculated. Many molecules have recognizable medicinal-chemistry components, including ordinary aryl halides, amides, ethers and available amines. The weak drug-likeness and questionable synthetic-plausibility readings reflect recurrent N-halogen/O-halogen bonds, peroxides, cyanates, nitroso or thioformyl groups, unusual bridged rings and a cyclic cumulene, rather than an absence of rings or useful amines. Some high-scoring counterexamples avoid reactive heteroatom-halogen bonds or peroxides, and chemical plausibility does not consistently follow the supplied score gradient. The source difference is confined to recent origin_batch priority inside exact raw-score retention ties plus passive provenance diagnostics; cap, accepted archive, inherited quantile sampler and posterior/graph machinery remain present. Origin batch is an admission-history fact, not a chemical descriptor. The local contest is the actual live population plus the sequential newcomer, not the full archive. The read-only log audit joins each of the thirty task/seed trajectory leaders to its pooled, emitted and accepted records and actual scored generating parents. It also preserves representative local tie contests, actual parent draws and evaluated products. Initial records, retained population members, positive sampling support and actual selected parents are different sets. In one early equal-score indole pair, recency changes order while both first-parent probabilities remain equal; the recorded inserted-nitrogen product scores below its starting parent. Another exact tie changes a linked azaaryl parent's band probability while retaining the same local membership; its evaluated crossover product is larger and lower-scoring. A tied aryl-amine record crosses the positive-support boundary and actually participates in crossover, but the cited accepted product is the tiny fluorine molecule and is not admitted as a survivor. At a different cap contest, two equally scored methyl halides differ in retained membership while both have zero breeding probability and neither breeds later. Terminal retained-order changes have no later breeding opportunity. These deliberately selected examples distinguish order, membership, probability, support, actual breeding and accepted descendants; they are not frequencies of chemical success or activation verdicts. Passive legacy orders and probabilities in this audit reuse identical local Child contests. They are not scored alternative continuations, and local strict-score-vector preservation is not future-outcome preservation. All Child pool-size receipts show the inherited full pool; no reduced-pool or compute-saving interpretation follows. An unscored graph intermediate, a pooled offspring, an emitted proposal, an accepted scored molecule, a live survivor and a retained-best endpoint are separate observations. Chemical frequencies here describe accepted trajectories, not a census of unselected pool chemistry; unselected alternatives receive no invented labels or missing-chemistry inference. The digest final_molecules are late seed-2 evaluations, not the retained best of every seed. The original chemistry reports of n-c55c3d520a2c and its identical-trajectory carry-forward n-62daf219c70a were read through the fresh evidence index; historical reproduction supplies provenance, not independent replication. This is one complete same-Parent panel with adaptive histories. Shared baselines with round19 siblings are nonindependent; this report makes no compound, additive or interaction claim with another slot. Ancestry overlaps and crossover can have two scored parents; chemical association does not isolate rank versus membership effects, identify mediation, justify a blanket preference for younger molecules, or establish a whole-foundation contribution. The five per-task sections retain every seed endpoint and its chemistry exceptions. Audits are under .slots/r0019-03-improve-L01/molecular/, including trajectory_audit.json, inspected_records.json, leader_provenance.json, retention_examples.json, identity_scope_check.json and history_molecular_sources.json. No source or supplied trajectory/log path was missing. Only Child digest/trusted-trajectory SMILES are quoted; Parent-only structures are identified by published task, seed and evaluation.

nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

approach.method_basis: The Parent searches from one scored current molecule by sampling local atom, bond, path and ring edits, including a direct exchange of aromatic nitrogen and carbon that preserves molecular formula. It sanitizes and normalizes molecular identities, rejects duplicates and submits the first full batch allowed by its short-term inverse-motif memory. A fresh neighbor is blocked when opposite signed motif changes match restrictions from one earlier selected transition. The walk then moves to the highest-scoring accepted neighbor even after a worsening move, uses canonical order for exact ties and maintains a separate best archive. Selected transitions install bounded, sign-balanced restrictions with four-step tenure and latest-origin overlap refresh. Identity repair and the nitrogen-relocation menu are retained parts of this Parent.
approach.novelty: Remove active tabu rejection for one integration contribution probe. The same motif predicate and memory history will still be recorded, allowing every evaluated neighbor that the retained rule would have blocked to be identified. The evaluated batch will instead be the first full set of valid fresh graph neighbors. Earlier siblings relaxed matching, changed which transitions or motifs received credit, preserved overlapping origins or extended restriction lifetime; each kept an active tabu gate. This experiment tests the contribution of that entire admission gate after nitrogen-relocation development. The earlier relaxation losses motivate a predicted score decrease when the gate is removed.

nodes.hypothesis: Ablate enforcement of the retained same-transition bidirectional inverse-motif tabu gate: every graph-valid canonically fresh neighbor reaches the inherited first-full-batch admission path, while the unchanged Parent predicate and selected-transition memory lifecycle run only as passive diagnostics.

finding_summary.headline: Tabu removal admits 170 otherwise vetoed neighbors and lowers the mean score by 0.002275
finding_summary.insights: The active gate provides a small net endpoint benefit in this panel despite excluding some immediate improvements and even one molecule that becomes a Child task maximum. The result therefore rules out judging the gate solely by the quality of its excluded neighbors or by counts of local gains. Its effect develops through changed batch membership, random-stream consumption and later sources: every paired session first diverged at a common recorded neighbor vetoed by Parent and admitted by Child, but the next state sometimes stayed identical for several more batches. The effect is strongly seed- and task-dependent; the average loss is dominated by the second seed, especially sitagliptin_mpo, while two seeds improve. This is evidence for the entire gate in the tested panel, not universal necessity or an individual motif contribution. Removing restrictions also did not guarantee greater access to the retained nitrogen exchange: eligible source batches fell from 97 to 49 and accepted exchanges from ten to four; none of the four beat its source or was selected. Chemistry remained mixed. Similar typical size and ring counts conceal more peroxide and sulfur-triple-bond products alongside fewer nitrogen- and oxygen-halogen bonds; 80 of the 170 bypass admissions carry at least one defined concern marker. High labels do not establish stability or feasible geometry. Finally, all 135 affected Child batches stop with only six to nine observed retained-gate alternatives, so their unobserved replacements and alternative winners remain unknown.
finding_summary.results: Removal was exercised throughout the panel. All 435 batches contained the first ten valid fresh neighbors, with zero active tabu rejections, compared with 195 rejections in the Parent. The unchanged predicate identified 170 evaluated neighbors it would have vetoed on the actual Child history, spread over 135 batches and all 15 task sessions. Of these, 23 beat their source, 12 tied and 135 lost; nine strictly improved the archive and 29 became the next state. Across all proposals, source wins rose from 468 to 496 and strict archive updates from 238 to 269. Nevertheless, final macro mean fell from 0.521759 to 0.519484, a decrease of 0.002275 that narrowly meets the registered 0.002 prediction. Seed deltas were +0.021475, -0.037773 and +0.009471; their population deviation was 0.025574. Task mean changes were +0.006636 for zaleplon_mpo, -0.008325 for deco_hop, +0.039404 for drd2_docking, +0.007223 for median_2 and -0.056314 for sitagliptin_mpo. All runs completed with full validity. Raw generation attempts fell from 5303 to 5123, while recorded task runtime rose from 82.59 to 100.20 seconds.

molecular.headline: Aromatic ring families persist alongside peroxide bridges, reactive heteroatom halides and densely connected sulfur cages.
molecular.overall_character: Node n-045725e4628f was assessed against Parent n-abcd951ab7cc using the complete supplied seed panel: all fifteen trajectories per node, with 900 recorded molecules and 870 optimizer proposals per task. The digest lists no tasks without trajectories. The bounded best and final excerpts are not balanced across seeds, so the seed descriptions below also use the full trajectories. Every cited SMILES is from the authoritative digest. The generated chemistry is ring-rich, with substantial aromatic content, carbonyls, amines, ethers, halogens and sulfur. Every task has ring-closure and branch token rates of 1.0; aromatic-token rates range from 0.8414 to 1.0. These are molecule-level string-presence rates, not fractions of atoms or chemically proven aromatic rings. Passive RDKit reading of the Child proposals gives 21–52 heavy atoms and 1–10 perceived basis rings, with medians of 33 and 4. The Parent has corresponding ranges of 21–53 and 2–10, with the same medians. Distinct seed walks reach different frameworks, but the best excerpts often contain closely related variants of one framework. Chemical plausibility is mixed and often poor near the observed maxima. Under identical graph-marker definitions, Child versus Parent proposals containing an O–O single bond number 360 versus 55; sulfur triple bonds 187 versus 95; N–halogen bonds 383 versus 500; O–halogen bonds 189 versus 301; and hydrogen-bearing sulfur with total valence above two 1234 versus 1247. These overlapping markers describe structures, not measured reactivity. The O–O motif persists in 33 Child selected states versus no Parent selected states. Among the 170 accepted Child molecules tagged by the saved logs as retained-predicate would-veto admissions, 80 carry at least one of the defined concern markers; their median size and ring count are 32.5 heavy atoms and 4 basis rings. This subset is not chemically clean and does not establish an individual motif contribution. All task digests have charge and stereocentre-token rates of 0.0. RDKit identifies unassigned tetrahedral centres in 3318 of the 4350 Child proposals, while no proposal has a stored atom chiral tag. Formal neutrality does not mean that an amine could not protonate. Four accepted Child molecules are logged direct aromatic nitrogen positional exchanges, compared with ten in the Parent; this narrow subset does not characterize whole-walk chemistry. The passive audit and definitions are recorded in .slots/SPIRAL2.r0013-02-improve-L16.molecular-audit.json. No candidate execution, new molecule generation, scoring, conformer calculation or synthetic route assessment was performed. The observations support missing chemical controls and comparisons, not a known absent target pharmacophore.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 proposals contain 21–30 heavy atoms and 1–5 RDKit basis rings; the typical framework has three rings. Indole or benzothiophene cores carry an aryl carboxamide, with methoxy/ethoxy, methyl, amino, hydroxy or thiol substitutions. The seed-0 best is a 24-heavy-atom benzothiophene carboxamide with an aniline, methoxy group and chloromethyl substituent. The seed-1 best is a 23-heavy-atom indole carboxamide with ethoxy and aryl-thiol groups. The seed-2 best is a 26-heavy-atom benzothiophene hydrazide bearing N–Cl, chloromethyl, phenol and amino groups. These recognizable aromatic/carbonyl families coexist with late ring disruption and highly unusual sulfur bonding. The digest aromatic-token rate is 0.9655 and halogen-token rate 0.7575.
liabilities: The maximum contains an N–Cl hydrazide and a benzylic halide; the latter is a potential electrophilic site, while the N–Cl connection is a chemical-stability concern.

The digest also includes a ring-embedded C–S triple bond at hydrogen-bearing sulfur, hydroxylamine/hydrazine connections, disrupted aromatic rings and a strained small-ring aniline variant. Passing a molecular parser does not establish their synthetic feasibility.
missing_features: Stable, minimally substituted versions of the high-score aryl-carbonyl arrangement are not established for the N-chlorinated hydrazide maximum; the existing conventional amide examples show that ordinary linkages are accessible.
Late products do not consistently retain the compact aromatic geometry supported by the stronger observations. The data do not identify a particular absent target functional group.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial indole carboxamide scores 0.3051048083696145. The seed-0 benzothiophene amide reaches 0.40465559506276, while an early derivative that replaces the acyl linkage by a branched aminoalkyl connection scores 0.03343008011310944. Extending the seed-0 aromatic substituent into a longer oxygen/nitrogen-containing chain gives 0.05122719925570397. The visible gradient therefore favors a compact aromatic/carbonyl arrangement over these disrupted or extended alternatives. The seed-2 chloromethyl and bromomethyl hydrazides tie at 0.41885833432199493, so those observations do not establish a preference between those halogens. Parent best scores for seeds 0, 1 and 2 are 0.393567030299894, 0.39905049777278273 and 0.41003927643747895. Several later sulfur-triple-bond products still score around 0.398, so the label does not reliably reject chemically troubling bond environments.

The other seed walks include polyperoxide, N–Cl and unusual unsaturated sulfur or ring-bond environments. Long flexible branches and unassigned stereogenic sites add uncertainty about accessible conformations and practical synthesis.

nodes.method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
nodes.method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.

approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from real observations. It breeds from score-ranked groups of a greedy survivor population, uses its existing fragment crossover and local graph edits to build a fresh pool, and rejects invalid or previously evaluated identities. Its direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange route is disabled. Before each batch it fits a Gaussian process to the complete accepted archive using count fingerprints and a count-sensitive Tanimoto covariance. It draws correlated score functions over the pool and evaluates one still-available maximizer from each function. Real feedback then updates the archive, predictor, survivors and future breeders.
approach.novelty: Reserve only the final successful batch choice for the molecule with the greatest posterior variance remaining after accounting for the locations of the preceding choices and the inherited observation noise. Every preceding Thompson choice uses exactly the original draw and mask. This tests whether one deliberately information-seeking evaluation supplies useful later feedback. Earlier siblings removed sampled residuals or their correlation, froze later model learning, or optimized sampled immediate batch improvement; none establishes the value of this final variance choice. The older all-position conditioning experiment changed later random functions by assuming pending scores equaled their means. This proposal changes one acquisition objective, without assigning any score to a pending molecule.

nodes.hypothesis: Replace only the final successful posterior-selection position by the smallest-index maximizer of the original latent posterior variance conditional on earlier selected locations with the inherited observation noise, while preserving every preceding masked correlated Thompson choice and learning only from real accepted feedback.

finding_summary.headline: Variance-seeking labels changed predictions but never bred, and mean final score fell by 0.02279
finding_summary.insights: The missing benefit cannot be explained by a failure to select different molecules, accept their labels or update the predictor. This rule repeatedly spent its final evaluation on small, weak-scoring structures: 340 of 435 final choices had at most five heavy atoms, versus 18 in the Parent’s final positions. This accounts for most of the molecular assessment’s increase from 123 to 382 tiny accepted proposals overall. The winner’s mean variance fell only from 0.8596 before location conditioning to 0.8581 afterward, and conditioning changed the marginal-variance winner in just five batches. Thus the experiment mostly exposed uncertain molecules far from the selected prefix, rather than demonstrating a benefit from correcting within-batch redundancy. Their labels did provide measurable predictive information in the limited sense of fixed-history sensitivity and slightly lower observed next-query error; the omission contrast also changes normalization, and it does not establish calibrated uncertainty, information gain or endpoint mediation. Those modest predictive effects did not offset the unsuccessful final evaluations under this budget. The broader output still contains useful aromatic and heterocyclic families alongside reactive bonds, difficult ring geometry and unspecified stereochemistry; these chemical observations do not identify the cause of the endpoint loss. The negative contribution finding is conditional on this one-position rule, Parent composition and Search panel. It neither refutes ordinary accepted-label learning nor isolates the value of the covariance-conditioning term, and the registered complete exposed failure ends this rule without tuning its reserved count or schedule.
finding_summary.results: All 435 batches preserved the nine preceding Thompson choices on the same decision state. The final choice changed in 433 batches, always with a strict increase in remaining model variance; the other two choices coincided. Every final molecule was accepted. All 418 changed labels with a later fit opportunity altered next-batch predictions when compared with a passive fit omitting that row. Their next-query mean squared error fell slightly, from 0.0094934 with the row omitted to 0.0094283 with it included, although 89 of 418 next-batch comparisons worsened. None of the 435 final molecules beat its generating parent, improved the incumbent or was subsequently used for breeding. The Parent’s final positions produced 46 parent-beating molecules and 232 later-used breeders. Across the complete matched panel, mean final score fell from 0.595670 to 0.572880, a paired change of −0.022790 against the required +0.002. Seed changes were −0.045797, +0.011083 and −0.033656; 11 of 15 task/seed endpoints declined. Selection and later learning are confirmed; useful reserved-identity breeding and the performance prediction are not.

molecular.headline: Aromatic and heterocyclic families coexist with tiny fragments, reactive heteroatom-halogen bonds and difficult ring geometry
molecular.overall_character: Node n-062b351ccb52 produces substituted indole/azaindole amides, linked nitrogen heterocycles, aryl-alkyl and cyclic amines, quinoline-linked nitrogen-carbonyl rings, and fluorinated imino/carbonyl frameworks. All supplied Child and accepted published Parent n-62daf219c70a trajectory paths were present and read: each task has 900 observations across Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2, including 870 accepted optimizer proposals. No task is omitted and no comparison path is missing. The immutable request reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true, matched seeds 0, 1 and 2, and no profile-mismatched seeds. The present comparison is therefore a complete matched chemistry comparison under the supplied Research in Depth profile, batch size 10 and 300 observations per task. The published n-62daf219c70a report records exact reproduction of its same-code source n-c55c3d520a2c; its own historical profile mismatch is not a missing pairing for this Child. The original gaps below retain that source history, rather than treating the baseline reproduction as an independent chemical discovery. Digest ring-closure-string incidence is 0.9 to 0.9138 and aromatic-string incidence 0.8552 to 0.8977. These are molecule-level incidences of SMILES text features, not fractions of atoms or perceived ring counts. Formal-charge and stereocentre-string incidences are 0.0 on every task. A read-only CPU RDKit pass over the supplied trajectories supplies the explicitly labelled heavy-atom, bond and ring readings below; all accepted optimizer records parsed. Perceived cycles follow a graph ring-perception convention, not independent ring systems or proof of accessible three-dimensional geometry. The global aromatic abundance does not describe every leader: the leading seed-0 fluorinated imino/carbonyl molecule has no perceived aromatic atoms. Neutral strings also do not imply an absence of basic amines, and absent stereomarkers do not imply an absence of potentially stereogenic centres. The Child contains 382 accepted optimizer proposals with at most five heavy atoms, versus 123 in the Parent, with the Child count higher in every matched seed/task pair. These counts describe evaluated outputs; they do not identify which generator or acquisition component caused them. Rich ring chemistry coexists with N-halogen, O-halogen, peroxide and unconventional sulfur environments, strained-looking ring closures, and unspecified stereochemistry. Ordinary aryl fluorides, amines, amides and heterocycles also occur, so synthetic plausibility is questionable rather than uniformly impossible. Structural diversity is moderate across tasks and seeds, with much narrower families among nearby high-scoring records. Perceived graph differences, SMILES uniqueness and ring presence are not founder ancestry: no founder count, independent lineage count, component attribution or causal diversity benefit is inferred here. Scores quoted below are observed trajectory values, not new scores or measurements of synthesis, stability or biological activity. The digest final_molecules are late seed-2 proposals, not each seed's retained best molecule. nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

approach.method_basis: The Parent first trains a recurrent SMILES language model on an unlabeled molecular corpus. Each objective starts with a fresh policy copied from that prior, which then stays frozen. After each accepted batch, the policy fits the best-scoring half of the current molecules and a uniformly sampled group of earlier elites. Every target is the frozen prior log probability of the molecule's original accepted SMILES plus sixty times its real score, with equal weight for each training sequence. A memory keeps the thirty-two highest-scoring previously selected elites, preserving their original strings and scores. The updated policy directly samples complete SMILES, and chemical validation and canonical duplicate rejection fill the next batch.
approach.novelty: Replace uniform historical sampling with score-ordered replay: use the highest-scoring eligible historical molecules, keeping the same replay count. This makes the best accepted evidence already present in memory determine the historical training group. It leaves admission, retention and the learning rule intact. Earlier siblings explored the prior representation and training; the original replay experiment established that using history changes learning, but did not test whether preferentially selecting stronger history helps. A passive uniform draw on the same memory and a comparison of the two gradients will show whether this selection changes the evidence actually fitted. Concentration and useful novel molecules remain separate outcomes, because repeatedly choosing strong examples can also narrow exploration.

nodes.hypothesis: Replace uniform historical-elite replay membership with the highest accepted-score eligible records, ordered by descending score and canonical identity, while preserving the inherited replay count, original accepted sequence and reward provenance, memory admission/retention and equal-per-sequence online learning.

finding_summary.headline: Stronger historical replay changed learning, narrowed exploration and gave uneven score gains.
finding_summary.insights:
The experiment separates using replay from choosing its members. Historical replay already supplied measurable gradients in the Parent; selecting the strongest available history demonstrably changed both the reward distribution and the gradient of the loss actually optimized. The comparison uses the child's own memory and policy state, so it establishes the selection effect without inventing an alternative scored trajectory. Stronger reward did not mean a larger gradient: on changed updates, the mean actual combined-gradient norm was about 363 versus 493 for the passive uniform group. Repeatedly selected records were often already closer to their targets, and historical mean squared error moved only from 105.05 to 102.64 across the real updates; 834 of 2,100 historical row exposures nevertheless worsened.

The tradeoff is a narrower stream of accepted evidence and more repeated proposals. That concentration is visible in chemistry as well: the deco-hop proposal set fell from 529 to 392 distinct cores and the strongest neighborhoods repeatedly decorate related aromatic, amide, urea, amine or hydrazone families. Conventional connectivity remains dominant, but score ordering alone does not improve attachment chemistry, control oversized outliers or add missing stereochemical configurations. Positive augmented targets also persist in 595 of 2,100 historical exposures, despite being above the log-probability ceiling. The campaign now has evidence that reward enrichment can improve some endpoints while reducing novelty and producing inconsistent gains; preserving a broader supply of useful accepted evidence is an open question separate from whether this selector activates.
finding_summary.results:
The selection mechanism ran on the intended records. All 405 nonterminal updates with surplus eligible history changed replay membership and increased accepted replay reward relative to the passive uniform draw on that same memory. Across all 420 nonterminal historical updates, replay reward rose from the uniform comparator's 0.301506 to 0.376503; the fifteen no-surplus updates had no reward difference. Selected history exceeded the current elite mean in 370 updates, compared with 185 for the uniform comparator. All 405 changed selections also produced measurable changes in the actual training gradient at the registered tolerance. Original accepted strings, scores, chronological admission, top-32 retention, equal row weights and frozen priors were preserved.

The stronger replay was more concentrated: summing distinct replayed identities within the fifteen objective sessions gave 540 actual identities versus 1,103 under the passive comparator, and 335 versus 751 distinct Murcko cores. Actual replay was younger on average, at 4.47 batches versus 5.52, rather than simply older. In subsequent generation, raw validity increased from Parent 90.43% to 92.58%, while duplicate draws rose from 30.11% to 40.78% and novel yield fell from 60.31% to 51.81%. Forty-one batches needed additional sampling, versus five in the Parent. All fifteen tasks still completed the same 300-call budgets.

Mean final Top-1 increased from 0.507554 to 0.513272, a paired mean gain of 0.005718. The three paired changes were -0.012216, +0.009216 and +0.020155, so the benefit was uneven across replicas. Four task means increased; sitagliptin decreased. The final fifteen updates are excluded from the selection-to-proposal conclusions because no later proposals follow them.

The selection mechanism ran on the intended records. All 405 nonterminal updates with surplus eligible history changed replay membership and increased accepted replay reward relative to the passive uniform draw on that same memory. Across all 420 nonterminal historical updates, replay reward rose from the uniform comparator's 0.301506 to 0.376503; the fifteen no-surplus updates had no reward difference. Selected history exceeded the current elite mean in 370 updates, compared with 185 for the uniform comparator. All 405 changed selections also produced measurable changes in the actual training gradient at the registered tolerance. Original accepted strings, scores, chronological admission, top-32 retention, equal row weights and frozen priors were preserved.

The stronger replay was more concentrated: summing distinct replayed identities within the fifteen objective sessions gave 540 actual identities versus 1,103 under the passive comparator, and 335 versus 751 distinct Murcko cores. Actual replay was younger on average, at 4.47 batches versus 5.52, rather than simply older. In subsequent generation, raw validity increased from Parent 90.43% to 92.58%, while duplicate draws rose from 30.11% to 40.78% and novel yield fell from 60.31% to 51.81%. Forty-one batches needed additional sampling, versus five in the Parent. All fifteen tasks still completed the same 300-call budgets.

Mean final Top-1 increased from 0.507554 to 0.513272, a paired mean gain of 0.005718. The three paired changes were -0.012216, +0.009216 and +0.020155, so the benefit was uneven across replicas. Four task means increased; sitagliptin decreased. The final fifteen updates are excluded from the selection-to-proposal conclusions because no later proposals follow them.

The experiment separates using replay from choosing its members. Historical replay already supplied measurable gradients in the Parent; selecting the strongest available history demonstrably changed both the reward distribution and the gradient of the loss actually optimized. The comparison uses the child's own memory and policy state, so it establishes the selection effect without inventing an alternative scored trajectory. Stronger reward did not mean a larger gradient: on changed updates, the mean actual combined-gradient norm was about 363 versus 493 for the passive uniform group. Repeatedly selected records were often already closer to their targets, and historical mean squared error moved only from 105.05 to 102.64 across the real updates; 834 of 2,100 historical row exposures nevertheless worsened.

The tradeoff is a narrower stream of accepted evidence and more repeated proposals. That concentration is visible in chemistry as well: the deco-hop proposal set fell from 529 to 392 distinct cores and the strongest neighborhoods repeatedly decorate related aromatic, amide, urea, amine or hydrazone families. Conventional connectivity remains dominant, but score ordering alone does not improve attachment chemistry, control oversized outliers or add missing stereochemical configurations. Positive augmented targets also persist in 595 of 2,100 historical exposures, despite being above the log-probability ceiling. The campaign now has evidence that reward enrichment can improve some endpoints while reducing novelty and producing inconsistent gains; preserving a broader supply of useful accepted evidence is an open question separate from whether this selector activates.
