molecular.headline: Conventional aromatic medicinal chemistry spans many cores, with concentrated high-score families and no assigned stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: The supplied trajectories cover all five objectives and all three seeds: each task contains 900 evaluated molecules, including 870 optimizer proposals. All 4,350 optimizer-proposal SMILES parse with RDKit. This is predominantly recognizable medicinal chemistry: aromatic and heteroaromatic rings linked through amides, ureas, hydrazones, amines and sulfonamides. Proposal median heavy-atom counts are 24, 30, 28, 23 and 24 in the supplied task order; median ring counts are three throughout. Digest aromatic-token rates are 0.9586-0.9908 and ring-closure rates 0.9782-0.9977, so lack of rings or aromaticity is not the central deficit. Across individual tasks, 392-737 distinct nonchiral Murcko scaffolds occur among proposals, although the digest leaders repeatedly occupy close analogue families. Dominant structures have plausible conventional connectivity; occasional azides, peroxides, haloalkyl chains and very large products warrant separate scrutiny. These trajectories do not establish synthesis, stability, solubility or experimental activity. Relative to the parent, aromatic medicinal chemistry remains central, while the leading families change: pyrazole carboxamides and pyrrolylmethyl ureas replace prominent indole amides, flexible diamines join the strongest amine chemotypes, and acylhydrazones are more prominent in one otherwise weak-score session. No assigned stereocentres occur in optimizer proposals; molecules with unassigned stereocentres number 107, 76, 338, 201 and 286 in task order. Ring-rich generation therefore coexists with incomplete stereochemical specification.

per_task.generated_character: Proposals usually have a compact aromatic framework: median 24 heavy atoms and three aromatic rings. The leading approximately 0.470 family consists of N-aryl pyrazole carboxamides bearing an N-(1-arylethyl) amide substituent; the approximately 0.468 family comprises an N-methylpyrrolylmethyl group attached to a diaryl urea. Both are conventional three-ring medicinal-chemistry structures with carbonyl hydrogen-bonding groups and substantial aryl halogenation. An aza-fused aromatic hydroxy carboxamide also appears among the digest leaders. This differs from the parent leaders, which included substituted indole carboxamides. The low end includes long-chain ester elaboration and much larger, multiply linked ring systems, rather than an absence of valid or aromatic structures.
liabilities: Repeated aryl bromine and chlorine substitution can increase molecular mass without demonstrating a score benefit in the cited equal-score families.
Long alkyl tails and elaborate linked frameworks produce severe low-score outliers despite chemically recognizable bonding.
missing_features: Systematic exploration of alternative compact aromatic/carbonyl arrangements is underrepresented among the leading examples relative to repeated halogen variants; no specific unobserved target scaffold can be inferred.
The leading arylethyl carboxamides contain an unassigned stereogenic carbon, so the generated molecules do not specify which three-dimensional configuration is being proposed.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The supplied leaders associate moderate molecular size and organized aromatic/carbonyl substitution with scores near 0.47. Scores are identical within several halogen substitutions and positional variants, so these examples do not establish a reward for further halo decoration. Extending an indole ester with a very long alkyl chain gives about 3.14e-24, while an elaborate ring-and-linker-rich amide reaches about 9.07e-27. Those comparisons support size and arrangement sensitivity, but are not matched transformations isolating a single cause. Final pyrrolylmethyl urea analogues score about 0.423-0.436, showing that related heteroaromatic substitutions can retain appreciable score without reaching the listed maximum.

per_task.generated_character: This is the largest and most halogen-rich typical proposal set: median 30 heavy atoms, median molecular mass 437.343 and digest halogen rate 0.8701. The leading molecules have three aromatic six-membered rings, heavily fluorinated aryl groups, a substituted pyridine core, and aminomethyl, benzylamine or amide connections. A separate leading family contains diarylamino acylhydrazones. These are plausible synthetic motifs, although their dense fluorination and largely aromatic frameworks create substantial mass and polarity-distribution questions. Full trajectories contain 187 proposals matching an N-N=C connection. Compared with the parent, fluorinated aromatic and hydrazone chemistry persists, with the current leaders including less fused, three-ring pyridyl amine and amide architectures.
liabilities: Dense aryl fluorination and mostly aromatic frameworks can produce high molecular mass and limited three-dimensional shape; the trajectories contain no physical-property measurements.
Acylhydrazones and thiourea/imine variants introduce geometry, tautomerism and stability questions that a valid SMILES string does not settle.
Nine optimizer proposals exceed 50 heavy atoms; extending size is not itself supported as the useful structural feature.
missing_features: The leading repertoire supplies many fluorinated aromatic analogues but less evidence for chemically different architectures retaining the same useful spatial and electronic arrangement.
Hydrazone and imine examples do not specify C=N geometry; their displayed scores do not identify which configurational or tautomeric form would carry the implied interactions.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The top aminomethyl pyridyl structure scores 0.603953 and related amines or amides lie close to 0.60. A useful local contrast is the methylthio pyridyl amide at 0.599304 versus its methylsulfonyl counterpart at 0.343569: the rest of their displayed framework is the same, supporting sensitivity to sulfur oxidation state in that chemical context. It does not establish that sulfones are generally unfavorable. The small cyanophenyl sulfone scores 0.257003, whereas terminal aromatic thiourea/imine structures reach approximately 0.57-0.59. Size alone therefore does not explain the full gradient.

per_task.generated_character: The strongest displayed chemistry includes very flexible acyclic diamines: a tertiary nitrogen connects an N-butyl group, an arylbutyl group and a propyl secondary-benzylamine arm. Those molecules carry two halogenated aromatic rings and no saturated nitrogen ring. Another high-scoring family combines an arylpiperidine with an aminoethyl arylamine substituent. These are recognizable amine-rich medicinal-chemistry structures, with median proposal heavy-atom count 28 and median fraction of sp3 carbons about 0.529. Parent leaders instead prominently included arylpiperazine/indole combinations and fused aryl amines, so useful amine-plus-aromatic chemistry spans several topologies. Low-score examples are often amide-, sulfonamide- or acylhydrazone-rich aromatic structures with fewer clearly basic aliphatic amine sites.
liabilities: Long alkyl linkers, N-butyl or N-pentyl groups and heavy aryl halogens create substantial conformational freedom and mass; the leading chlorobromo diamine has molecular mass 465.907.
Several cited terminal molecules carry primary bromoalkyl or iodoalkyl groups, introducing possible electrophilic side-chain liabilities that the objective values do not characterize.
Ten proposals exceed 50 heavy atoms and the largest reaches 81, so the proposal distribution includes much larger structures than the leading compact ring/amine frameworks.
missing_features: No additional functional group can be inferred as necessary from near-ceiling scores; broader economical coverage of the observed amine/aromatic arrangements is the supported chemical coverage gap.
Three-dimensional specification remains incomplete across the full proposal set: 338 proposals contain an unassigned stereocentre, although the leading flexible diamine itself is achiral.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The flexible diamines reach 0.999998 and the arylpiperidine example 0.999994. Both retain accessible amine functionality and separated aromatic regions, supporting those shared features as a chemical association in this trajectory; a saturated nitrogen ring is not required by the leading examples. A compact nitro/acid heteroaromatic amide is near 1.86e-05 and a sulfonamide-substituted heteroaryl amide near 1.98e-05. In the final molecules, a tertiary amine with two bromobutyl arms and no aromatic ring scores 0.123770, while more extended molecules retaining a benzylamine-bearing aryl region score around 0.90 or above. These are contextual associations rather than measured binding or isolated substituent effects.

per_task.generated_character: Median proposals contain 23 heavy atoms and three rings, with 729 distinct nonchiral Murcko scaffolds among optimizer proposals. The leading family is arylsulfonylpiperazine chemistry: examples attach sulfonyl phenylpiperazine to a fused aza-lactam or chromanone-like framework, or attach N-methylpiperazine sulfonamide to substituted biphenyl systems. Those molecules combine aromatic surfaces, a saturated six-membered nitrogen ring, sulfonyl oxygens and sometimes an additional carbonyl. The parent also produced a leading N-methyl arylsulfonylpiperazine, alongside fused lactam and diaryl heterocyclic alternatives. The current leading structures are generally plausible synthetic chemotypes; the very low end includes carbon disulfide, allyl azide and small unusual or highly polar fragments.
liabilities: Small disconnected-from-the-leading-chemotype proposals include carbon disulfide and an organic azide, yielding little useful structural overlap with the higher-scoring multi-ring molecules.
Sulfonylation changes the electronic character of a ring nitrogen; counting every nitrogen as an interchangeable basic amine would misdescribe this family.
Some terminal proposals add multiple sulfur/nitrogen connections and tautomeric heterocycles without demonstrating improved placement of the leading polar groups.
missing_features: The output covers many core identities but supplies limited evidence for precise alternative placements of its useful aromatic, sulfonyl and amine regions beyond the leading analogue neighborhood.
Leading alternatives include an unspecified stereocentre in the chromanone-like example, and 201 proposals have an unassigned stereocentre; configurationally explicit versions are absent.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The fused aza-lactam sulfonylphenylpiperazine reaches 0.235468, a chromanone-like analogue 0.229568 and a methoxy biphenyl N-methylsulfonylpiperazine 0.222204. These support a combined multi-ring and polar-linker architecture in the observed neighborhood. Carbon disulfide and allyl azide score zero, while a heavily hydroxylated cyclic acid scores 0.013472: fragmentation or abundant oxygen alone does not reproduce the arrangement in the leaders. Other aromatic, carbonyl-containing terminal molecules remain near 0.10-0.15. The molecular evidence does not identify a single missing substituent capable of resolving the remaining low scores.

per_task.generated_character: The highest molecule is a compact N-methylbenzamide attached to a substituted fused azaheteroaromatic system bearing a hydroxyl group; it has 22 heavy atoms and three aromatic rings. Other leaders are substituted anisyl/pyridyl acylhydrazones, generally with two aromatic rings, and an aryl hydroxyethyl carboxamide attached to a pyrazole. These are recognizable, synthetically plausible chemical families rather than unusual-valence graphs. Full proposals have median 24 heavy atoms, three rings and 737 distinct nonchiral Murcko scaffolds. Relative to the parent leaders, which included sulfonamide/acyl heterocycles and fused imino carbonyl systems, the current digest is particularly concentrated in pyridyl acylhydrazones; N-N=C matches increase from 71 to 116 proposals. Worst examples include extremely large polycyclic, macrocyclic peptide-like or long-chain aromatic elaborations.
liabilities: Acylhydrazone enrichment brings possible E/Z, tautomeric and stability concerns that are not resolved by the objective scores.
Large aromatic appendages, long alkyl chains and oversized cyclic structures coincide with vanishing scores; six proposals exceed 50 heavy atoms.
The proposal set contains 286 molecules with an unassigned stereocentre and no assigned stereocentres, limiting interpretation of any geometry-dependent chemistry.
missing_features: Broader coverage of compact, correctly arranged polar heteroaromatic/carbonyl chemotypes is missing from the higher-score repertoire, which repeatedly returns close acylhydrazone analogues despite many proposed scaffolds.
The hydroxyethyl amide leader has an unassigned stereogenic alcohol carbon, while hydrazone leaders do not specify C=N geometry; these structures do not establish stereochemical adequacy.

The evidence supports no unique mandatory target-like group: the best displayed molecule is distinct from the repeated hydrazone family, so extrapolation should preserve access to alternative compact cores.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The compact benzamide/azaheteroaromatic structure scores 0.309504, the acetyl-substituted anisyl pyridyl acylhydrazone 0.281351, and the hydroxyethyl pyrazole carboxamide 0.274759. A dimethoxy aryl pyridyl acylhydrazone scores 0.233893, whereas the corresponding displayed acetyl hydrazone with the heteroaryl acyl region replaced scores 0.002010. Enlarging a methoxy substituent to a benzyl/CF3-bearing arm gives approximately 1.33e-09 despite retaining a pyridyl acylhydrazone. Thus functional-group placement and controlled size both appear relevant within the visible examples. The digest median is rounded to 0.0: the full 900-row trajectory median is approximately 3.19e-07 and only two rows are exactly zero. The displayed higher-score chemotypes occupy a sparse part of a mostly very low-score distribution.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A displayed pyridyl amide scores 0.599304 with a methylthio substituent and 0.343569 with the corresponding methylsulfonyl group. In another supplied session, a pyridyl acylhydrazone scores 0.233893 while the displayed acetyl hydrazone counterpart scores 0.002010. High-scoring amine-rich structures also differ chemically from lower-scoring amide and sulfonamide nitrogen environments. These examples show that heteroatom counts alone do not explain the observed gradient.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator covers many atoms and functional groups but does not consistently preserve their useful attachment and electronic context.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve access to chemically valid attachment-point and oxidation-state alternatives, and learn their value from observed feedback in their local structural context. Treat amines, amide nitrogens, sulfonamide nitrogens, thioethers and sulfones as different chemical environments rather than interchangeable token decorations.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Individual proposal sets contain 392-737 distinct nonchiral Murcko scaffolds, yet digest leaders cluster into pyrazole carboxamides, pyrrolylmethyl ureas, polyfluorinated pyridyl structures, flexible diamines, arylsulfonylpiperazines and acylhydrazones. Several halo-substitution or positional variants have identical displayed scores. Another session contains 737 scaffold identities while its full-trajectory median score is approximately 3.19e-07, showing that identity breadth is not sufficient chemical coverage of useful regions.
transferable_gaps.gap: Broad scaffold counts coexist with narrow high-score analogue families and repeated peripheral halogen variation.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support core and linker alternatives that preserve chemically meaningful arrangements already associated with reward, alongside local substitution. Assess useful chemical coverage from observed structural neighborhoods and feedback, without assuming that more unique strings or more halogen substitutions alone expands the productive repertoire.

transferable_gaps.evidence: No assigned stereocentres occur in the 4,350 optimizer proposals; the five sessions contain 107, 76, 338, 201 and 286 proposals with at least one unassigned stereocentre. Digest leaders include an arylethyl carboxamide, a chromanone-like ring and a benzylic alcohol whose stereocentres are unspecified. Acylhydrazone leaders also omit explicit C=N geometry. The leading flexible diamine is achiral, so stereochemical specification is a conditional need rather than a universal requirement.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator leaves stereogenic structures and configurationally ambiguous imine chemistry unspecified.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Represent and sample stereochemistry where a generated structure actually supports it, retaining chemically consistent configurations and bond geometry. Let feedback determine the usefulness of these alternatives, and keep achiral and configurationally explicit structures accessible without assuming an unobserved preferred stereoisomer.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Proposal median heavy-atom counts are 24, 30, 28, 23 and 24, but the numbers exceeding 50 heavy atoms are 1, 9, 10, 0 and 6. Cited low-score molecules include very long alkyl esters and oversized aromatic or macrocyclic structures. In a close hydrazone neighborhood, replacing a compact methoxy substituent with a benzyl/CF3-bearing extension accompanies a score near 1.33e-09. Conversely, flexible multi-amine chains can score near the ceiling, while some related proposals introduce primary bromoalkyl or iodoalkyl groups.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator lacks consistent context-sensitive control of molecular growth, flexible side chains and reactive appendages.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Maintain alternatives with controlled linker length, appendage size and functional-group reactivity, using local feedback to distinguish useful flexibility from destructive growth. A single global preference for small, rigid or ring-bound structures would discard demonstrated useful chemistry; the needed capability is contextual structural control and chemically informed handling of side-chain motifs.

nodes.method_name: Augmented Hill-Climb with a corpus-trained SMILES policy
nodes.method_thesis: Train a compact autoregressive SMILES prior solely on the supplied unlabeled corpus, then initialize a fresh policy from that prior for each objective. Use the initial observations and each subsequent scored batch to update only its highest-reward sequences with the Augmented Hill-Climb loss: fit policy log likelihood to frozen-prior log likelihood plus scaled observed reward. Sample complete molecules token by token from the updated policy, canonicalize them, and refill invalid or duplicate proposals by further generation. The corpus supplies language training, never a ranked molecular pool. Elite-conditioned policy updates should shift generation toward new high-scoring molecular combinations quickly enough to improve the benchmark's mean final Top-1. This is a small-budget transfer hypothesis, not a claim that published larger-budget gains carry over. The root uses the current scored batch; randomized historical replay is reserved for the first improvement. The anchor's elite augmented-likelihood mechanism is described by [Thomas et al.](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13321-022-00646-z).

approach.method_basis: The Parent trains a bidirectional masked denoiser on unlabeled molecular fragment sequences and freezes its neural weights. For each objective it ranks previously scored whole molecules, samples high-ranked ones as contexts, and replaces one fragment with a variable-length masked span. The model fills that span while retaining the surrounding fragments and attachment labels. Valid, connected, canonical new molecules are submitted in generation order; accepted scores update the archive and therefore the contexts used next. Parallel denoising usually produces more usable completions than fit in the announced batch, and the Parent discards that surplus.
approach.novelty: Add one mechanism: posterior-sampling selection among the fresh completions already produced by the Parent. A molecular-fingerprint Gaussian process fitted only to accepted scores represents uncertain objective values, and joint posterior draws select distinct completions for the batch. This is the first selector Child in this lineage; its only supplied sibling is the unmodified remasking root. The related graph-evolution experiment made a much larger offspring pool. Here the new selector uses the natural surplus of the existing denoising calls, so the experiment asks whether better use of those alternatives changes the search's best outcomes.

nodes.hypothesis: Replace generation-order submission with distinct maximizers of independent joint posterior function draws from an accepted-only, task-local Tanimoto fingerprint Gaussian process over the Parent's existing fresh surplus SAFE fragment completions.

finding_summary.headline: Posterior selection replicated: uncertainty redirected 68% of eligible choices, while final scores varied across seeds
finding_summary.insights: The experiment now rules out activation being peculiar to the first seed: accepted-only posterior updates, use of cross-candidate covariance, and uncertainty-driven changes to actual submissions all persisted across different prepared denoisers and search trajectories. The natural surplus was sufficient for selection in 285 of 290 new batches without increasing the inherited generation width or generating beyond the first sufficient call. Correct activation still leaves efficacy unresolved. Chronological GP prediction error beat the archive-mean predictor in nine of ten new task runs, but lost on seed-2 sitagliptin (RMSE 0.06228 versus 0.05839). The lower-scoring second replica had lower pooled prediction error and more completions beating their contexts than the first; neither diagnostic alone establishes better final best scores. Unsubmitted alternatives have no oracle labels, and there are no matched generation-order or greedy-mean control runs here. The molecular assessment further limits what the selector can accomplish: it reallocates calls among mostly related aromatic analogue families and inherits gaps in scaffold coverage, stereochemical specification and chemical plausibility. High scores and score ties across chemically different products do not by themselves show that reactive or questionable structures have been avoided. A matched selector ablation with the same prepared prior, together with inspection of the high-scoring chemistry, would separate the value of correlated uncertainty from prior quality and score permissiveness.
finding_summary.results: Both new replicas executed accepted-only GP conditioning and full-covariance posterior selection. Across their ten task runs, all 280 nonterminal feedback probes changed the posterior mean and variance on the same previously submitted molecules. Every one of 2,900 choices replayed as the maximum of its logged joint draw over the remaining pool. Selection changed the submitted generation-order set in 284 of 285 batches with surplus completions, replacing 1,304 prefix entries. Uncertainty changed 1,939 of 2,850 eligible choices (68.04%) relative to the posterior-mean maximizer of the identical remaining pool. The five batches without surplus were excluded from that uncertainty denominator; there were no numerical fallbacks, fingerprint collisions or exact choice ties. The same mechanism was already active in the supplied seed-0 baseline, where uncertainty changed 1,019 of 1,450 choices (70.28%). These are replications of activation, not new algorithm changes. The new macro scores were 0.50778 and 0.47068, alongside the original 0.50903. The three-seed mean was 0.49583 with population standard deviation 0.01779. Task means were 0.41036 for zaleplon, 0.59284 for scaffold hopping, 0.96337 for DRD2 docking, 0.20040 for median similarity and 0.31218 for sitagliptin. All tasks completed 300 oracle evaluations. The supplied comparison runs are the same selector on different seeds, so they do not establish a replicated score improvement over generation-order submission.

molecular.headline: Dense aromatic analogue families, with useful amines but repeated radical ions, reactive linkages and unspecified stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: The supplied trajectories cover seeds 1 and 2 of this Algorithm Node, with seed 0 of the same node as the comparison baseline. All five tasks are covered, each with 580 optimizer proposals among 600 evaluated records. The output contains recognizable indole carboxamides, benzothiazoles, pyrazoline thioureas, fused pyrimidinediones, arylpiperazines and more unusual cyclic polyamines. Related scaffolds recur with halogen, alkoxy, carbonyl and linker substitutions. Diversity is moderate across the combined output but much narrower within individual high-scoring families; distinct SMILES often represent close analogues. Every task has ring_closure_rate 1.0, and aromatic-atom indicator rates range from 0.9741 to 1.0. These indicate presence of ring digits and aromatic atoms, not that every ring is aromatic. Mean SMILES lengths range from 45.4 to 62.1, and the trajectories include both ordinary medicinal-sized frameworks and very long appended chains or macrocycles. The conventional cores support moderate drug-likeness, but overall synthetic plausibility is questionable because peripheral changes repeatedly introduce hydroperoxides, bare radical ions, unusual sulfur valence patterns and strained unsaturated rings. A syntactically accepted structure is not evidence of an isolable closed-shell compound. All stereocentre indicator rates are 0.0 despite visibly stereogenic aminals, branched arylalkyl chains and substituted saturated rings. The output therefore supplies substantial ring and aromatic chemistry while leaving chemical form, configuration and the stability of appended functionality unresolved. Several exact score ties between chemically different substituents make these omissions particularly visible.

per_task.generated_character: The main families are multiply substituted benzothiazoles with an anilinomethyl arm, methoxy/methylthio/acetyl substituents, and dimethoxyindole carboxamides or indole–oxadiazole combinations. A smaller acetyl-substituted pyrazoline thiourea is the best molecule. These are mostly medium-sized, ring-rich frameworks with plausible synthetic building blocks. Mean SMILES length is 45.4; ring and aromatic indicators are both 1.0, and halogen_rate is 0.7948. The low-scoring tail includes highly extended bridged-ring appendages and unusual boron or sulfur chemistry.
liabilities: The best molecule retains a thiourea, and the benzothiazole family frequently carries a thioether; their chemical reactivity and oxidation-state stability require assessment independent of the score.

The unusual hydrogen-bearing sulfur oxide linkage and the borane are chemically less straightforward than the conventional heteroaryl cores. Very large, densely connected ring appendages also create substantial synthetic complexity.
missing_features: Chemically controlled changes to the central heterocycle, linker and carbonyl pattern remain more informative than the repeated terminal F/Cl/Br substitutions that share a score; the high group is concentrated in close benzothiazole analogues.
The stereogenic carbon in the best substituted pyrazoline is unspecified. The trajectories do not show whether configuration affects this objective.
No uniquely missing target motif is established; the visible evidence favors a moderate-sized aromatic/polar arrangement already present in several different families.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The acetyl pyrazoline thiourea scores 0.41237650262954906, compared with 0.1501184006136499 for the initial hydroxyphenyl-substituted pyrazoline thiourea. This supports a favorable change in size and substituent balance within that broad family, without isolating a single causal property. The seed-0 best, another pyrazoline thiourea with an aldehyde-containing arm, scored 0.4443186615775074. The new benzothiazole methylthio series reaches 0.404945686740228 with F, Cl or Br on the terminal phenyl, giving exactly the same recorded score for those substitutions. The corresponding dimethoxy variants score 0.38519625255195356, while the diacetyl/methylthio example scores 0.4064265251651748. These local comparisons implicate the central substitution pattern more than terminal halogen identity. The initial indole carboxamide scores 0.3051048083696145; late indole–oxadiazole chemistry remains moderate at 0.2853198676066052. A massively extended indole derivative scores 1.7016180040499976e-35 and the small phenyl/hydroxymethyl borane scores 8.713153723578382e-09. The median is 0.196853, so neither indiscriminate extension nor drastic truncation is supported.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-1 high scorers largely retain a fused N-methyl pyrimidinedione connected to a substituted aryl group and a pyridyl or phenyl partner through a cyanamide-bearing aminal or N,O-acetal. Some carry long conjugated ketone side chains. Seed 2 also explores oxygen-rich medium-ring systems bearing aminomethyl heteroaryl and oxazole-like groups. These are larger and more elaborated than the simplest initial molecules: mean SMILES length is 62.1, with ring and aromatic indicators both 1.0 and halogen_rate 0.6776. The core heterocycles are recognizable, but several linkers and substituents make isolation and stability questionable.
liabilities: Cyanamide-bearing aminal and N,O-acetal connections raise hydrolytic-stability and chemical-form questions.
High-scoring examples encode terminal nitrogen radical anions; other examples contain extended conjugated ketones or an O–S(=O)2–S group ending in a very small unsaturated ring.
A late indole derivative contains a nitrosoalkyl substituent. These functionalities warrant specific chemical assessment, not an assumption of ordinary screening-library behavior.
missing_features: Stable, closed-shell alternatives to the recurrent cyanamide aminals, N,O-acetals and exotic appended fragments are insufficiently demonstrated around the same favorable aryl/heteroaryl arrangement.
The aminal stereocentre and geometries of conjugated unsaturated side chains are unspecified. Their effects cannot be inferred from the score ties.
A unique missing decoration is not identifiable from the available scalar scores; additional size or functional-group complexity is often tolerated without establishing a better chemical candidate.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The cyanamide-bearing aminal linking a pyridyl group to the aryl/fused-dione system scores 0.5974361625142148, above the initial fused-dione ester at 0.548381482770623. The seed-0 best, a different fused azaarene with an aminomethyl aryl arm and an ether chain, scored 0.5937687401188465. Both favor connected heteroaromatic/polar architectures, without specifying a unique scaffold. A particularly revealing series has the identical score 0.5900771267411073 for an N-methyl dione and variants with terminal bare [N-] groups. Graph interpretation of those terminal groups includes an unpaired electron; they are radical anions rather than ordinary protonation variants. The score therefore does not distinguish a conventional member of this series from those chemically problematic appendages. The worst proposal at 0.3047122074636306 introduces a sulfone joined to a large unsaturated carbocycle. Other digest low proposals lie around 0.527–0.531 and have simpler ester/carbonyl substitution or short indole amide arms. The median is 0.567667. A final medium-ring molecule with an O–S(=O)2–S linkage still scores 0.5873236733518856, again separating favorable numerical features from demonstrated chemical robustness.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-1 high group is a tightly related arylpiperazine family: an exposed aliphatic piperazine nitrogen connects through a branched alkyl chain to a second substituted aromatic ring. Methoxy, phenol and multiple F/Cl/I substitutions dominate. Seed 2 instead repeatedly combines substituted pyrrolidines and secondary amines with arylalkyl, biaryl or fused aromatic groups; some retain carboxylic acid or amide side chains. The recognizable amine/aryl frameworks are generally makeable, although unusual halogenated N-substituents occur. Mean SMILES length is 58.0, ring_closure_rate is 1.0, aromatic_atom_rate is 0.9828 and halogen_rate is 0.9845.
liabilities: Near-universal halogenation adds chemical mass and extensive aromatic substitution; neither the near-unity scores nor the exact ties establish improved experimental binding or acceptable physicochemical properties.
Some late N-substituents place fluorine, hydroxy or amino groups on the same carbon attached to ring nitrogen. The final N–C(O)(F)F group in particular requires chemical-form and stability scrutiny.
missing_features: Configurations are unspecified at the branched arylalkyl stereocentre and the substituted pyrrolidine/side-chain centres, even within the repeatedly high-scoring families.

Less heavily halogenated, chemically conservative alternatives retaining the favorable amine/aryl spacing are poorly represented; the observed score ties do not establish a requirement for iodine or any exact halogen pattern.
The trajectories do not provide a basis for naming an additional obligatory target interaction beyond the observed exposed-amine and aromatic arrangement.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The branched arylalkyl/arylpiperazine reaches 0.9999999869310162. The same score is recorded after replacing F with Cl on one ring, replacing iodine with chlorine, or changing a chlorine on the other ring to fluorine. The observed favorable arrangement is therefore clearer than any specific required halogen. The seed-0 best at 0.9640302775641455 was an arylcyclopropyl aminoalcohol linked to an N-substituted pyrrolidine, also retaining exposed aliphatic amines. The initial sulfonylated-pyrrolidine/amide/acid framework scores 0.01904115112334333; close early relatives remain low. A late molecule that preserves the branched arylalkyl region but replaces the piperazine region with a carbonyl-containing N-heterocycle and sulfone scores 0.007091365028079139. The contrast supports the importance of amine availability and its surrounding geometry, rather than nitrogen content alone. The median is 0.647607, and late seed-2 amine-containing structures score 0.7853743688684828 to 0.8786262267384644 in the cited examples. Acid-containing molecules can therefore remain favorable when the broader amine/aryl arrangement is retained.

per_task.generated_character: Seed 2 concentrates on aryl esters or alpha-ketoesters joined through a substituted ethyl unit to indole or benzodioxole and a methylated seven-membered triaza ring. That saturated ring has an adjacent N–N bond at its closure; it should not be described as an ordinary piperazine. Aldehyde, fluoro/chloro and occasional unusual sulfur substitutions diversify this family. Seed 1 stays mainly around aryl-substituted fused pyrimidinediones with small saturated-ring or ether decorations. Mean SMILES length is 60.8, with ring and aromatic indicators both 1.0. The combined population contains reasonable aromatic building blocks but chemically more complicated polyamines and occasional very large ring expansions.
liabilities: An aldehyde is present in the best molecule, and several neighbors carry alpha-ketoesters; their reactivity is a separate issue from the small differences in score.
The cyclic polyamine contains an N–N bond, while a later variant adds an N–O bond. Protonation, oxidation and chemical stability should not be assumed from the neutral SMILES.
A relatively high-scoring example includes an unusual sulfur oxide/ylide-like connection to a small ring; the low tail also contains hydrogen-bearing sulfur structures and enormous ring expansions.
missing_features: Stereochemical specification of the carbon connecting the aryl group, linker and cyclic polyamine is absent across the favorable series.
Alternative stable saturated linkers or nitrogen-ring arrangements that preserve the favorable aromatic spacing are insufficiently demonstrated outside the recurrent triaza-ring family.

The observed indole/benzodioxole contrast supports a local chemical preference, but it does not identify a uniquely missing target scaffold or prove that further aldehyde/carbonyl addition would help.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The benzodioxole/ester/aldehyde/triaza-ring molecule scores 0.21645935471676658. Its closely related indole counterpart scores 0.20125723423387007, making replacement of the fused heteroaromatic unit a more interpretable local contrast than a generic increase in ring content. An otherwise related fluoro-substituted benzodioxole compound scores 0.2147437190347249, showing that an aldehyde is not required for this favorable neighborhood. Alpha-ketoester analogues reach 0.21436521304349876. The seed-0 best was an indole/aryl-substituted fused dione at 0.1993252969257374, while the initial fused-dione ester scores 0.1678386594791329 and the new reported median is 0.171417. The chemistry moved toward a different polar aromatic/polyamine arrangement, but the high group remains a close analogue family. The lowest optimizer examples shown include a modified initial amide at 0.11074362710059762 and a highly extended macrocyclic structure at 0.12116074428058654. The digest span minimum of 0.01832842604508024 belongs to an initial molecule, not to an optimizer proposal.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-1 high family is an aryl ethyl ester linked to a fluorinated or chlorinated fused N-methyl pyrimidinedione. These compact, comparatively conventional carbonyl-rich heterocycles are closely related to the initial aryl/fused-dione ester. Seed 2 follows a markedly different family of multiply oxygenated nonaromatic cyclopentadienes bearing aryl amides or esters, alkoxyamine groups and frequent hydroperoxides. The latter family has substantially less convincing chemical robustness despite retaining aromatic substituents. Mean SMILES length is 47.2, ring_closure_rate is 1.0, aromatic_atom_rate is 0.9741 and halogen_rate is 0.7534.
liabilities: Hydroperoxides, alkoxyamine N–O bonds and a thiolate occur in the late output. These are chemically consequential functionalities, not ordinary methoxy or hydroxy substitutions.
A relatively high-scoring variant has an N–Br bond on a carbonyl-containing heterocycle. Such a halogenated nitrogen has different chemical reactivity from an aryl bromide.
The late bare [C+] and [N+] fragments also encode radical valence under graph interpretation. They are not established closed-shell protonation states of normal drug-like molecules.
Very long hydrophobic chains and large macrocycles add size and flexibility while losing the favorable score of the compact ring systems.
missing_features: The favorable compact ester/fused-dione arrangement has not been developed into clearly distinct, chemically robust families beyond repeated halogen and positional variants; the alternative oxygenated cyclopentadienes introduce substantial stability concerns.
Configurations at substituted nonaromatic ring carbons are unspecified. Ring closure and aromatic substituents do not supply stereochemical definition.

No missing basic amine or specific fluorinated fragment can be inferred as obligatory: the best family is dominated by carbonyl-bound and aromatic nitrogen, and the shown score ties leave several decoration choices unresolved.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best aryl ester/fused-dione molecule scores 0.343704064948769 and is the same molecule and score already present in the seed-0 baseline. A positional/halogen-placement variant has the same recorded score. Brominated close analogues score 0.33556413633387294. Relative to the initial phenolic, more extensively arylated fused-dione ester at 0.0020944534688323298, the favorable series preserves the polar dione and ester while simplifying an appended aryl group to a small halogen substituent and altering the aryl decoration. This is evidence of a restricted size/substitution balance, not a demonstrated need for a basic amine. The reported median is 0.007464. A huge hydrocarbon macrocycle scores 0.0, and long-chain acyl/alkoxy extensions score 2.4700785835147185e-67 and 5.3678001758351103e-67. Some chemically unusual late cyclopentadienes still score moderately: the cited alkoxyamine-containing structure scores 0.21776387859949217, and a hydroperoxide/thiolate combination scores 0.1402717223535657. Neither score establishes a stable molecular form or an attractive synthetic product.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The digest contains terminal nitrogen radical-anion variants with exactly the same score, 0.5900771267411073, as a conventional N-methyl relative. It also shows hydroperoxides, an N–Br heterocycle, a bare carbon cation with radical valence, and unusual hydrogen-bearing or multiply bonded sulfur linkages. Some of these remain among comparatively high-scoring or late proposals.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve closed-shell, chemically interpretable molecular forms during otherwise local changes.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide chemistry-aware control of hydrogen count, valence, charge and radical state, and stable alternatives to reactive linkages within the same scaffold families. Keep chemical form distinct from numerical score: observed objective values alone do not reject these changes. Do not equate every ordinary ionizable group with the bare radical-ion fragments shown here.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A benzothiazole series with F, Cl or Br shares score 0.404945686740228. Several differently halogenated arylpiperazines share 0.9999999869310162, and aryl ester/fused-dione positional variants share 0.343704064948769. The best groups repeatedly retain the same central ring and linker arrangements despite these peripheral changes.
transferable_gaps.gap: Repeated terminal substitutions produce distinct strings without demonstrating broader chemical capabilities around the favorable cores.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make chemically conservative changes to central ring topology, linker connectivity and functional-group arrangement accessible while retaining useful portions of observed molecules. Let task-local feedback determine whether those changes matter; repeated halogen swaps should not be treated as evidence that broad chemical neighborhoods have been explored.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every task reports stereocentre_rate 0.0 over 580 optimizer proposals. nodes.method_name: GenMol fragment remasking with a corpus-trained discrete denoiser
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the method in GenMol's fragment-remasking mechanism: a bidirectional masked discrete diffusion model generates replacement fragments while retaining the surrounding molecular context. The anchor is described in [GenMol, Sections 4.1-4.2](https://arxiv.org/html/2501.06158v3). For this benchmark adaptation, train a compact denoiser solely on the permitted unlabeled corpus, then freeze it. Start each objective with a fresh archive of its supplied scored molecules. Select high-ranked observed whole molecules as contexts, replace a randomly chosen fragment with a variable-length mask chunk, iteratively sample the missing SAFE tokens, and decode the resulting complete molecule. Generate further completions until the evaluator-announced batch contains distinct canonical structures. Accepted feedback updates context selection and allows improving completions to become future contexts. This root uses the remasking core with observed whole-molecule contexts; the paper's corpus-derived fragment-vocabulary initialization and fragment-attaching stage are not required. The corpus trains the denoiser and supplies unlabeled length statistics, never a molecule pool for ranking or retrieval. The hypothesis is that contextual fragment replacement preserves useful structure while generating improving alternatives, raising the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Task-local selection can respond immediately to feedback without reward-dependent neural training, but useful conditional generation from the permitted preparation remains an empirical prerequisite.

approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds molecules from score-ranked accepted survivors by connected-fragment crossover or local graph edits. It builds a fresh pool for each batch, fits a Tanimoto fingerprint Gaussian process to all earlier accepted observations, and selects molecules by correlated posterior function draws. One growth move appends a single atom to an available hydrogen-bearing site; that site can currently be carbon, nitrogen, oxygen, phosphorus or sulfur regardless of which element is added.
approach.novelty: Make halogen addition use carbon attachment sites. If the original growth draw would attach fluorine, chlorine or bromine to a heteroatom, redirect that same one-atom addition to an available carbon site; if none exists, let the existing bounded mutation retry continue. This preserves the source molecule's heavy-atom connections and the chosen halogen while changing its new bond context. Earlier siblings changed which accepted parents breed or survive. This Child instead changes one local growth channel, and uses explicit attachment chemistry rather than the corpus-occurrence rule tried in a different lineage.

nodes.hypothesis: Redirect halogen append mutations from heteroatom anchors to uniformly sampled eligible carbon anchors, preserving the selected halogen and single-atom growth.

finding_summary.headline: Carbon-directed halogen growth removed its reactive-bond channel, but final scores fell.
finding_summary.insights:
The experiment establishes that an attachment rule can remove a specific reactive-bond introduction while preserving the surrounding graph, without solving the broader chemistry problem. The rule changed a small evaluated channel: 22 of 4,350 proposals carried its redirected edit in their immediate breeding history. Meanwhile, 56 emitted N-halogen-containing molecules and 31 O-halogen-containing molecules had no such motif in either original generating parent, demonstrating introductions through the unchanged operators. Other products already had that motif available in their parents; their exact bond ancestry cannot be inferred from motif presence alone.

Carbon attachment itself remains chemically permissive. Four redirected pool products acquired a carbonyl-halide connection and three an imine-carbon-halide connection; none of those seven was evaluated. The full selected stream also contained more carbonyl/imine halides, while the molecular assessment still found strained small rings, reactive decorations, oversized repeated assemblies and unspecified stereochemistry. These observations narrow the next chemistry question to attachment environment and other introduction routes, rather than treating all carbon-bound halogens as robust alternatives. The simultaneous increase in core coverage and parent-beating events with a lower final best score also shows that these intermediate gains do not establish endpoint benefit. The altered stochastic search paths and posterior selection do not identify a causal score penalty for the removed, unscored attachment alternatives.
finding_summary.results:
The intended attachment change reached both pools and evaluation. All 489 halogen draws with a heteroatom anchor and available carbon support were redirected, sanitized and reconstructed as the same selected halogen attached by one new C-halogen bond. Every old heavy atom and bond was preserved, and all 489 direct products retained the source ring core. One further opportunity had no carbon site and correctly continued the bounded retry. The successful edits supplied 482 distinct pool descendants and 22 evaluated descendants; 19 of those ended with the append, while three underwent later edits.

The direct channel produced no new heteroatom-halogen bonds. The Parent’s single-append pool products had added 160 N-halogen, 55 O-halogen and 25 other heteroatom-halogen bonds; its emitted single-append products added 16 N-halogen and three other heteroatom-halogen bonds. Across all evaluated proposals, molecules containing N-halogen decreased from 572 to 535 and O-halogen from 441 to 173, but both remained common. Ring-core identities across the full emitted stream increased from 2,266 to 2,409; no explicit tetrahedral stereochemistry appeared.

All fifteen tasks completed the same 300-call budgets. Novel pool yield rose from 92.05% to 92.55%, and accepted molecules beating their best generating parent increased from 565 to 605. Among the 22 redirected descendants, two beat their best parent, one improved the incumbent and none was a final task/seed best. Mean final Top-1 nevertheless fell from 0.544374 to 0.539209, a paired change of -0.005165; seed changes were -0.011685, -0.020367 and +0.016558. The mechanism is confirmed, with negative and uneven endpoint utility.

molecular.headline: Aromatic polycycles and aryl amines coexist with reactive bonds, strained small rings, and oversized repeated assemblies
molecular.overall_character: The supplied current and parent trajectories cover every task and seed. Current proposals span compact aryl amides, saturated nitrogen rings, fused cyclic diones, and much larger repeated heteroaromatic assemblies. Ring and aromatic content are rich: the digest's ring-closure presence rates range from 0.9736 to 0.992, and aromatic-token presence rates from 0.9471 to 0.992. These are molecule-level SMILES readings, not aromatic atom fractions or evidence of feasible ring geometry. Halogen-token rates vary from 0.1655 to 0.9943, while explicit charge and tetrahedral stereolabel rates are zero throughout. Neutral drawings include potentially basic amines. The conventional aryl dione family shows that plausible medicinal chemistry is accessible, but other leaders carry acid chlorides, aldehydes, nitroso groups, direct nitrogen-halogen bonds, unusual sulfur valence, or highly unsaturated small rings. Distinct seed families provide moderate structural diversity; numerous unique strings also represent close decoration variants or duplication of existing ring systems. Relative to the parent, the chemistry moves between families without consistently removing these liabilities. The supplied scores establish structural associations, not a unique absent pharmacophore or synthetic feasibility.

per_task.generated_character: The leading molecules are compact, densely bridged aromatic systems carrying an N-methyl arylamide. The best contains benzene and pyridine rings, an oxygen/methylene/nitrogen bridge, and a sulfur-containing unsaturated ring; neighboring leaders exchange the aryl nitrogen, aryl halogen, bridge atom, or sulfur bond order. Other seeds produce more recognizable fused heteroaryl amides and benzene-annulated, highly unsaturated small rings. Thus there is abundant ring chemistry, rather than a shortage of molecular size: ring and aromatic presence rates are 0.9736 and 0.9713, with mean SMILES length 45.7. Ordinary amides and heteroaryl substituents look synthetically recognizable, but the multiply bridged connectivity and some unsaturated small-ring products need much more scrutiny.
liabilities: The sulfur cumulene with bracketed SH is an unusual chemical endpoint, despite its high supplied score.
Several final benzene-annulated unsaturated small rings have substantial geometric and electronic strain concerns.
Compact bridged topology does not by itself provide a credible synthesis, and late proposals still discard nearly all of the productive architecture.
missing_features: Matched simpler ring systems retaining the leading pyridylamide and heteroatom spacing are not established among the supplied leaders.
Stable sulfur and bridge alternatives are only partially represented; the near-leading cumulated sulfur structure leaves chemical stability unresolved.
Stereochemically specified versions of substituted bridge or ring variants are absent even when their connectivity can support stereoisomers.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The pyridyl N-methyl amide reaches 0.468900; the otherwise close fluorophenyl amide is 0.425708, and the unusual cumulated sulfur analogue is 0.457660. Within this local family, the aryl heteroatom arrangement matters and the unusual sulfur bonding does not improve the supplied score. Small fragments such as acetylene and methane score zero; the final methylfluoropyridine scores about 1.42e-11, so an aromatic ring alone is insufficient. A final indole-like arylamide scores 0.230346, whereas a different strained, annulated small-ring arylamide scores 0.388678; their multiple structural differences do not prove that strain is beneficial. The current seed-0 maximum is above the parent's 0.446352 and retains its compact bridged N/O-aromatic character while changing the carbonyl connection and sulfur content. Other current seed maxima are below their respective parent maxima, so the same chemical movement is not repeated across seeds.

per_task.generated_character: This is the largest molecular population by SMILES length, with mean 95.2 and maximum 227. Almost every proposal has aromatic and ring tokens, both at 0.992. One recurring family links several nitrogen-rich aromatic diones through substituted heteroaryl connections and unsaturated chains. The best molecule is more compact than those repeated assemblies but remains a complex fused aza/oxygen carbonyl system, connected through an N-O bond to a fluorinated heteroaromatic ring bearing a brominated thioether side chain and a carbon-bound bromonitroso substituent. Final molecules include repeated ester-linked azaaromatics, additional nitroso groups, and N-bromo acylated enamines. These are chemically elaborate structures with substantial route and stability questions.
liabilities: The leading bromonitroso substituent combines a reactive nitroso group with carbon-bound bromine; it should not be read as an ordinary nitro substituent.
Imidoyl halides, direct N-bromination, and N-O connections complicate stability and synthesis.
Repeated dione assemblies add size, unsaturated chains, and many connecting bonds without a consistent supplied-score advantage.
missing_features: Comparably connected but compact heteroaromatic carbonyl structures with stable peripheral bonds are insufficiently represented among the highest supplied scores.
Matched removal of nitroso, direct N-halogen, and imidoyl-halide functionality is not demonstrated while holding the main ring architecture constant.
Simple connecting groups that preserve the useful heteroaromatic arrangement without duplicating complete dione systems remain a visible gap.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The compact bromonitroso/thioether structure scores 0.608446. Several much larger repeated-dione molecules tie at 0.603906: exchanging an imidoyl chlorine for bromine, or shortening one unsaturated side chain to ethyl, does not change that supplied score. A final molecule joining substantial portions of two complex aromatic systems falls to 0.579001, while a smaller thioether/carbonyl heterocycle without the bromonitroso group scores 0.588747. These examples support complete heteroaromatic/carbonyl assemblies over isolated fragments, but do not establish a benefit from repeated growth or a requirement for the reactive groups. Methane and vinyl bromide both sit at the 0.5 floor. The parent's best seed-1 structure scored 0.632470 and also carried problematic oxygen-halogen chemistry; the current maximum is lower and replaces that particular chemistry with other liabilities rather than demonstrating their resolution.

per_task.generated_character: The high-scoring family combines methoxyfluorophenyl and chlorophenyl groups with potentially basic saturated nitrogen rings, including pyrrolidine, piperidine, and expanded diaza rings. Enamine or related unsaturated connections organize these groups, often alongside chloromethyl, aldehyde, or acid-chloride substituents. The leader additionally carries an aryl amino group. Other seeds generate bridged amine cages and oxygen-bridged aromatic structures with strongly constrained small-ring connectivity. Aromatic, ring, and halogen presence rates are 0.9851, 0.9908, and 0.9943; mean SMILES length is 68.7. The aryl-amine building blocks are recognizable, but the reactive appendages and some fused topology make the actual outputs substantially less straightforward than conventional aryl cyclic amines.
liabilities: Acid chlorides are reactive acylating functionalities, rather than routine stable amide or ketone decorations.
Enamines, aldehydes, and activated alkyl chlorides introduce stability or reactivity concerns despite high scores.
Late oxygen-bridged small rings and N-bromo analogues add separate geometry and bond-stability concerns.
Multiple neutral amine drawings do not establish a physiological protonation state, exposure, or useful binding geometry.
missing_features: Matched stable connecting groups preserving the aryl/basic-amine arrangement are not established alongside the acid-chloride, aldehyde, and chloromethyl leaders.
The potentially stereogenic saturated-ring connections have no explicit stereochemical specification.
Ordinary ring alternatives preserving the late oxygen-bridged aromatic substitution pattern are missing from the cited final series.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The aryl-amino pyrrolidine/enamine/chloromethyl molecule scores 0.993896; its analogue lacking the aryl amino group scores 0.986744. An aldehyde-containing diaza-ring analogue scores 0.993273, and an acid-chloride/piperidine analogue scores 0.992660. A chloromethyl diaza-ring structure without the linking enamine nitrogen still reaches 0.988417, so no single reactive linkage is established as necessary. Conversely, a shortened monoaryl enamine carrying a fluorinated amidine scores 0.001971, and a biaryl carboxylic acid/acetamide scores 0.000719. The observed association is with the assembled aryl/basic-ring architecture and its connections, not aromaticity, nitrogen, or halogen presence alone. The current seed-1 maximum exceeds the parent's 0.951235 while changing from a bridged cage/aldehyde family to linked cyclic amines; the parent already reached roughly 0.991 in other seeds with different aryl-amine structures.

per_task.generated_character: The strongest current family is comparatively conventional: an N-aryl fused pyrrolidine-like ring and a cyclic dione/ureide region carry an ethoxyphenyl substituent and an alkyl-substituted phenyl or pyridyl group. Carbonyl acceptors and an NH coexist with a partly saturated ring and substantial aromatic surface. Other seeds retain expanded nitrogen/carbonyl rings, annulated aromatic systems, and lactone-like connections; occasional outputs join two such large systems. Ring and aromatic presence rates are 0.992 and 0.9862, but the halogen rate is only 0.1655. Mean SMILES length is 59.2. The leading family is more apparently synthesizable than many other task leaders because it avoids direct N-halogen bonds and exotic small-ring unsaturation, although a route and stereochemical identity remain unspecified.
liabilities: Multiple aromatic groups and alkyl/ethoxy substitution create a sizable hydrophobic surface; the trajectories do not establish solubility.
Late structures still contain difficult expanded polycycles, N-O connections, or duplicated ring systems.
The substituted saturated ring in the otherwise plausible leading family has unspecified stereochemistry.
missing_features: More independent, compact aryl/carbonyl arrangements are underrepresented relative to decoration of the same fused dione family.
Stereochemically specified substituted saturated rings are absent.
Matched simplifications of extended or repeated polycycles that preserve useful carbonyl and aryl relationships are not demonstrated.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The alkylphenyl/ethoxyphenyl fused dione scores 0.229908; replacing one aryl carbon with nitrogen gives 0.229106, and expansion of the partly saturated ring gives 0.223627. Other changes to propyl, methyl, and ethoxy decoration produce nearby but lower scores, such as 0.221324 and 0.221171. This is a shallow preference among closely related complete aryl/carbonyl scaffolds. Methane, acetylene, and hydrogen peroxide score zero, while dimethyl ether scores 0.014932. A large doubled final polycycle scores 0.156670 versus 0.206435 for another, less repeated final polycycle; these are not matched structures, but size alone is plainly insufficient. The current seed-1 maximum exceeds the parent's 0.213370 and exchanges its N-fluorinated bridged dione for a more conventional fused dione. The parent's overall best was 0.224057 in a different expanded-ring family, so the current chemistry extends rather than resolves the modest score region.

per_task.generated_character: The leaders are compact nitrogen-rich fused aromatic or partly saturated carbonyl/imino systems, usually with phenolic oxygen, N-methyl or fluoromethyl substitution, and fluorinated unsaturated small rings. The best has a cyclobutadiene-like substituent containing two double bonds in a small carbon ring. Other high-scoring structures contain fluorinated cyclopropenes, fused unsaturated small nitrogen rings, or direct N-F bonds. These are substantial chemical feasibility concerns despite moderate molecular size. The lowest-scoring structures instead combine multiple large aromatic dione systems through esters, carbonyls, or ring-to-ring connections. Aromatic and ring presence rates are 0.9471 and 0.977, with mean SMILES length 53.9; neither scarcity of aromatic rings nor simple failure to grow molecules explains the observed output.
liabilities: Cyclobutadiene-like unsaturation brings severe strain and electronic instability concerns.
Fluorinated cyclopropenes and fused unsaturated small heterocycles further constrain feasible geometry and synthesis.
Direct N-F substitution is chemically distinct from routine carbon-bound fluorination and introduces a separate reactivity concern.
Large repeated aromatic carbonyl structures remain present even where their supplied scores are extremely small.
missing_features: Conventional ring replacements retaining the leading carbonyl/imino and fluorinated substituent arrangement are absent among the cited leaders.
Matched stable alternatives to direct N-F substitution and highly unsaturated small rings are not established.
Compact, independently connected alternatives are poorly represented relative to fused-ring rearrangements or duplication of existing aromatic dione systems.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The fluorinated fused imino/carbonyl leader scores 0.522447. Removing its aromatic fluorine while preserving the remaining depicted connectivity lowers the score to 0.486230, supporting a local substituent preference without demonstrating a general fluorination rule. Two different cyclopropene-bearing structures, one N-fluorinated and one bearing N-fluoromethyl, both score about 0.491792; their other topology differences prevent attributing the result solely to that substitution, and do not establish a need for N-F. Large repeated structures score as low as 3.48e-50, and a late joined fused-ring assembly scores 1.70e-12, indicating a strong observed disadvantage for those particular oversized combinations. The current seed-2 maximum exceeds the parent's 0.407140 while introducing more unsaturated small-ring chemistry. The parent's seed-1 maximum was higher, 0.584558, in an aryl dione/aminomethyl/fluoromethyl family without these cyclobutadiene-like substituents, so the current score does not justify interpreting strain as chemically necessary.

transferable_gaps.evidence: High-scoring outputs contain acid chlorides, aldehydes, alkyl halides, imidoyl halides, nitroso groups, direct nitrogen-halogen bonds, and unusual sulfur bonding. Other high-scoring structures omit individual liabilities, while the conventional aryl dione family demonstrates that reactive decorations are not universally required.
transferable_gaps.gap: Stable functional-group alternatives are incompletely explored around otherwise productive molecular architectures.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make chemically stable replacements and removals accessible while preserving the surrounding ring connections, aryl placement, and approximate molecular size. Evaluate those alternatives through the current objective's own feedback rather than treating reactive groups in a leading molecule as required chemistry.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The supplied molecules include cyclobutadiene-like substituents, fluorinated cyclopropenes, benzene-annulated unsaturated small rings, and tightly oxygen-bridged aromatic structures. Rich ring-token presence therefore coexists with substantial strain concerns; conventional fused diones and saturated amine rings are also available in the output.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring construction does not consistently preserve chemically credible unsaturation and geometry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide local changes to ring size, saturation, and fusion connectivity that preserve useful substituent relationships while allowing ordinary ring geometry. Ring closure and valence validity alone should not stand in for accessible chemistry.

transferable_gaps.evidence: One population has mean SMILES length 95.2 and maximum 227, with repeated dione assemblies. Several very large variants tie at 0.603906 despite shortening an unsaturated side chain, while other repeated assemblies have scores near zero. The same supplied trajectories also contain simple fragments after complete aromatic/carbonyl structures have been generated.
transferable_gaps.gap: Molecular size changes too often duplicate elaborate ring systems or remove most of the useful architecture.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support controlled simplification, removal of repeated units, and bounded connecting-group edits that retain a coherent molecular core. Let accepted structural comparisons determine useful size instead of assuming either growth or fragmentation is beneficial.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The digest reports zero explicit tetrahedral stereolabel presence on every proposal population. Cited substituted saturated nitrogen rings, brominated side chains, and partly saturated fused diones contain stereogenic connectivity whose configurations are not specified.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator leaves stereochemical identity unspecified even when it creates potentially stereogenic connections.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve known stereochemistry through structural edits and make valid local stereoisomer alternatives available when new centres arise. Use the current scoring feedback to determine whether stereochemical identity matters, without assuming that a label alone improves the score.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The leading aryl amides and diones have interpretable local analogues, including a near-tied phenyl/pyridyl pair and a lower-scoring sulfur-cumulene analogue. Elsewhere, changes simultaneously alter ring topology, heteroatom connection, reactive decoration, and size, leaving high scores attached to chemically questionable whole structures.
transferable_gaps.gap: Many nominally distinct molecules provide limited information about which stable structural feature is responsible for a score difference.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Expand matched local alternatives that isolate aryl position, heteroatom placement, carbonyl connection, and ring saturation while retaining the remainder of the molecule. Combine this with access to independently connected, synthetically credible scaffolds rather than only repeated decoration of the current ring family.

nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

branches: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
retained_mechanisms: Task-local scored molecular-graph population with score-ranked parent sampling across three high-ranked quantiles
De novo connected-fragment graph crossover
Local atom/bond mutation with inner operator retries and occasional multi-step graph walks
Chemical sanitization, canonical/isomeric identity rejection, and graph-based retries for complete novel pools; saturation-dependent retry branches retained but not exercised
Bounded greedy score-ranked survival and subsequent breeding from accepted offspring

Accepted-only task-local fingerprint Gaussian-process archive, exact joint posterior sampling over fresh offspring pools, masked batch selection, and feedback-driven posterior refitting; bounded numerical fallback retained but not exercised

Halogen append redirection from an originally heteroatom anchor to a uniformly chosen eligible carbon site, preserving the selected F/Cl/Br atom and original heavy-atom graph; empty carbon support uses inherited bounded retries.

approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves a greedy population of molecules using score-weighted breeding, connected-fragment crossover and ordinary atom/bond mutations, with direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange disabled. Each suggestion generates a fresh surplus pool. A Gaussian process learns from the full chronological archive of accepted task-local scores, using folded radius-two chirality-aware Morgan occurrence counts and dot-product count Tanimoto covariance. It normalizes scores with their current mean and population standard deviation, keeps fixed observation noise, and selects new offspring by correlated sampled functions with sequential duplicate masks. Actual accepted scores immediately update the archive and greedy survivors.
approach.novelty: Apply one fixed exponential covariance warp to the existing count similarity: exp(T−1). This retains occurrence information, molecular features and similarity order while adding a common covariance floor and changing conditional regression and sampled-function correlation. Earlier siblings removed multiplicity, unfolded coordinates, added an atom-pair channel, replaced the learner with trees, or projected sampled residuals; this warp changes none of those interfaces. The separate same-round alternatives change the overlap formula or distance geometry. The test asks whether this particular covariance law improves ranking of real evaluated offspring and useful exploration, then meets the complete endpoint criterion.

finding_summary.headline: Exponential covariance changes allocation but loses 0.03228 despite more local wins
finding_summary.insights: The fixed law clearly executed; missing exposure, broken Gaussian arithmetic, passive fit failure or altered random draws do not explain the endpoint loss. Better prediction on the actively selected stream and more wins against weaker parents did not translate into higher absolute search quality. Productive new typed cores rose only from 280 to 288 and generic cores from 190 to 191; more later breeding also failed to recover the lost endpoints. All 150 terminal offspring in each panel remain censored, and 73 Child versus 50 Parent offspring had later breeding support but were never drawn. The molecular assessment associates the lower results with extended and geometrically uncertain families alongside conventional high-scoring alternatives; fewer unusual local bonds do not establish chemical stability or explain covariance contribution. The experiment narrows the case against this exact lambda-one warp under the tested composition and budget. It cannot tell us whether covariance-floor smoothing, omitted candidate rewards or subsequent feedback caused the loss, and selected-stream diagnostics do not establish pool-wide ranking or calibration. The registered complete gain test ends this exact law; a materially different future law needs a sourced distinguishing experiment.
finding_summary.results: All 15 task/seed evaluations completed. Selected sets changed in 417 of 435 batches, with 1230 active selections outside the passive original set. On the actual Child emissions, MSE fell from 0.007744 with passive original predictions to 0.007064, pair-order accuracy rose from 66.48% to 67.19%, and mean within-batch Spearman rose from 0.4279 to 0.4417. These averages retain the losses: pair ordering worsened on every deco-hop seed and on one sitagliptin seed. Strict best-parent wins increased from 629 to 697 of 4350 offspring, and sequential incumbent advances from 258 to 273, but mean best-generating-parent score fell from 0.47046 to 0.44229; mean offspring score also fell slightly, from 0.38526 to 0.38235. Total incumbent gain fell from 5.80766 to 5.32350. Final macro score decreased from 0.59566965 to 0.56339196, a mean loss of 0.03227769 against the required gain of 0.002. Paired seed changes were −0.06839278, +0.00744768, −0.03588798; Child population SD was 0.00472367 versus 0.02659287. Median-2 improved in every seed, while deco-hop and docking lost in every seed. There were six task/seed wins and nine losses.
