approach.method_basis: The Parent walks from one scored molecule by drawing atom, bond, path and ring edits, normalizing their molecular identities, and directly evaluating the first full batch allowed by inverse-motif memory. Both inverse signs from the same selected transition must match to veto a fresh neighbor. The highest-scoring accepted neighbor becomes the next current graph even when its score is worse, and a separate archive retains the best score. The current deletion choices remove one leaf atom or contract one degree-two atom, so removal of a longer pendant substituent requires several separately evaluated transitions. Identity normalization, memory lifetime and accepted-score selection are already established parts of this Parent.
approach.novelty: Extend the existing deletion menu with a whole pendant-branch choice. When the deletion operator is drawn, it may remove an entire acyclic substituent attached through one single bond to a ring atom, while retaining every ring atom and the connections among retained atoms. Single-leaf choices remain in the same menu, and the operator keeps its existing allocation weight. This adds direct compact neighbors that no existing one-step removal can reach. The earlier sulfur sibling filtered local valence; this experiment changes the size of a permitted deletion and does not inherit or add that filter.

nodes.hypothesis: Extend the Parent's existing uniformly sampled leaf-deletion menu with whole multi-atom acyclic branches attached by one non-ring single bond directly to a ring atom, so the same deletion-operator allocation can emit a compact neighbor in one edit while retaining the complete ring framework.

finding_summary.headline: Whole-branch deletion produced compact neighbors, but every score replica regressed.
finding_summary.insights:
A lack of eligible branches was not the bottleneck: the Parent already had branch opportunities in 399 of 435 states, and the extension successfully turned such opportunities into new evaluated neighbors. The added prunings usually lost source score, rarely won their batch and were followed by regrowth whenever selected. Those observations help explain why immediate reductions of several atoms did not produce a lasting shift toward smaller sampled molecules under the unchanged accepted-score walk.

The experiment separates direct access to compact analogues from retaining useful score. Its complete method loses score in every seed, although that loss cannot be assigned solely to the pruned candidates because the changed menu also changes later sampling and trajectories. The molecular assessment remains dominated by sulfur-rich polycycles, reactive heteroatom bonds and unresolved ring geometry and stereochemistry. Ring-preserving removal alone does not resolve those chemical limitations.
finding_summary.results:
The expanded menu was available in 391 of 435 actual batch-start states. It selected 83 whole-branch edits, all graph-valid; after seven duplicate exclusions and seven tabu vetoes, 69 prunings reached evaluation. Each removed 2-14 heavy atoms in one step, averaging 3.75 atoms and 2.10 rotatable bonds, while retaining every ring atom and bond. The recorded menus, uniform selection, graph edits and identity joins passed the audit, including exact original behavior in all 55 deletion draws where no added branch was available.

Eight of the 69 evaluated prunings beat their source, and four became the next current state. All four later grew again. Typical emitted size remained essentially unchanged at 33.21 heavy atoms, compared with 33.20 for Parent. All three seeds completed their five 300-evaluation tasks; sampling cost was also similar at 12.14 versus 12.15 attempts per ten-member batch.

Mean macro final Top-1 fell from 0.520918 to 0.456635, a paired mean change of -0.064283. The three seed changes were -0.020009, -0.101316 and -0.071524. Every task mean declined, with the largest losses in DRD2 and sitagliptin. The intended neighborhood expansion and immediate size reduction occurred, while the score-retention hypothesis failed on the supplied panel.

molecular.headline: Sulfur-rich polycycles and reactive heteroatom bonds persist despite some recognizable aromatic amide families
molecular.overall_character: The current three-seed panel contains 900 entries and 870 optimizer proposals per task, with complete corresponding Parent n-9f7c7ec50039 trajectories. Ring-closure and branch presence are 1.0 throughout. Aromatic-token presence ranges from 0.7322 to 1.0, while charge and stereocentre token presence remain 0.0. These counters indicate SMILES features, not aromatic atom fractions, measured basicity or feasible stereochemistry. The output remains chemically close in broad character to the Parent: compact fused aromatic carbonyl compounds, large decorated nitrogen heterocycles, halogenated aromatic amine assemblies, bridged oxygen/nitrogen carbonyl systems and sulfur-rich cages. Several seeds change detailed scaffolds, giving moderate diversity across the panel, but each late trajectory mainly varies a related family. The more conventional indole or aza-indole amides coexist with multiply bonded hydrogen-bearing sulfur, sulfur-carbon triple bonds, N-Cl/N-F/O-F bonds, peroxides and extensive constrained ring closure. Overall synthetic plausibility remains poor and drug-like quality weak; recognizable fragments do not make these complete structures accessible. Score changes differ across seeds and do not consistently accompany a move toward more conventional chemistry.

per_task.generated_character: The best seed-1 family contains moderately sized fused aza-aromatic amides or thioesters, with ethyl/methyl groups, hydroxymethylthio or bromomethylthio substituents and N-Cl on the fused pyrrolic nitrogen. More conventional indole carboxamide and thioester relatives also score well. Other seeds move into bridged thione/amine systems or unsaturated sulfur-rich frameworks. Aromatic-token presence is 0.9678 and halogen presence is 0.8678. Compared with the Parent's indole, benzofuran N-chloroamide and aryl-ketone families, the current high region preserves compact fused aromatic/carbonyl arrangements while changing ring nitrogen and sulfur linkages. Whole-molecule plausibility is compromised by N-Cl, O-F, N-O and unusual sulfur chemistry.
liabilities: N-Cl, O-F, bromomethylthio and thioester groups create reactivity or stability concerns in otherwise recognizable aromatic scaffolds.
Late multiply bonded sulfur and dense bridged thione/amine structures have unresolved geometry and synthetic accessibility.
missing_features: Stable amide and thioester alternatives preserving the favorable fused aromatic arrangement are underrepresented relative to N-halogen, O-halogen and N-O substitutions.
Accessible alternatives to the late bridged or sulfur-rich ring systems and explicit configurations where stereocentres arise are absent from the shown high/final series.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best N-chloro aza-aromatic fluoroanilide scores 0.42749549733373915 versus the Parent seed-1 maximum of 0.39905049777278273. An indole thioester and corresponding amide score 0.404945686740228 and 0.39004142494831223, respectively, showing a favorable region without N-Cl on that indole. In contrast, disrupting the carbonyl into a hydroxyalkyl thioether gives 0.04016039186228654, and an expanded partially saturated ring system scores 0.016326676663027142. Compact aromatic/carbonyl placement appears favorable, while reactive N-Cl is not demonstrated to be universally necessary. The other current seeds do not improve over their paired Parent maxima.

per_task.generated_character: The strongest seed-2 molecules are very large substituted fused nitrogen diones linked to sulfur/nitrogen-rich heterocycles. They carry a long brominated polyene or imine-containing side chain, an alkyl-S-O-CH2 substituent, propyl and fluoroalkyl groups. Other seeds generate related diones with polyamines and N-Cl, or expanded nitrogen heterocycles with thioesters, imines and cyclic alkynes. Aromatic-token presence is 1.0 and mean SMILES length is 73.5, consistent with visibly extensive substitution but not itself a size descriptor. This resembles the Parent's heavily decorated heterocyclic chemistry; the latest structures remain difficult complete synthetic targets with labile heteroatom combinations and extensive flexibility.

Expanded or highly constrained heterocycles and unspecified fluoroalkyl stereochemistry reduce confidence in accessible molecular shape.
missing_features: Compact stable versions of the favorable heterocyclic arrangement are poorly represented among the late, extensively decorated molecules.
Conventional replacements for the alkyl-S-O linkage, reactive imine/haloalkene combinations and unusual heteroaromatic ring arrangements remain underexplored.

nodes.method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
nodes.method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.

approach.method_basis: The Parent alternates direct molecular sampling from a task-local neural flow policy with two rounds of graph crossover and mutation. It learns from the exact token trajectories and real scores of accepted molecules through trajectory balance, a jointly learned normalizer and regularization toward a frozen corpus-trained prior. Accepted graph discoveries re-enter the same replay archive. A fingerprint Gaussian posterior selects which fresh graph offspring receive evaluations while retaining the first fresh-policy handoff. Its reusable prior is chosen along the unchanged unlabeled training trajectory by fixed-noise valid, connected, unique molecular yield, with original holdout loss breaking ties. Online replay currently samples the full accepted archive by global score rank.
approach.novelty: Add a scaffold-balanced mixture to accepted trajectory replay: keep half of each trajectory's original rank probability and allocate the other half equally among available core families, preserving rank preference within each family. This changes which genuine accepted trajectories train the policy, with every accepted label and exact serialization retained. The lineage's other children changed prior preparation or graph posterior selection; none changed replay allocation. Other campaign experiments balanced breeding parents or survivor populations and lost score despite broader core use. This experiment tests a different path, the distribution of neural learning credit over the full accepted archive, and explicitly checks later policy behavior rather than treating extra scaffold counts as success.

nodes.hypothesis: Sample accepted trajectory-balance replay from an equal mixture of inherited score-rank probabilities and uniform scaffold-group mass with the inherited conditional rank probabilities preserved within each group.

finding_summary.headline: Scaffold-balanced replay broadened learning exposure and reached the policy, while completed-seed endpoints worsened
finding_summary.insights: Extra archive coverage did reach neural learning and subsequent sampling, so the result rules out a purely cosmetic entropy increase. It also exposes the allocation tradeoff: on the same accepted histories the mixture cuts expected graph-origin mass from 72.53% to 59.12% and reduces high-score rank emphasis, while giving much more replay to lower-ranked policy and initial records. Some transfer measures and average policy scores improve, yet those changes coexist with fewer novel raw candidates and weaker completed-seed best results. Broad replay therefore does not establish better endpoint search. The chemical assessment reinforces the distinction: plausible cyclic amines coexist with peroxide, N-halogen and constrained unsaturated-ring families, so family breadth does not certify useful functional context. The terminal failure is a separate inherited canonicalization weakness exposed by one emitted molecule; it explains the missing third formal score and does not explain the losses in the two successful seeds. A complete three-seed score-benefit conclusion remains unavailable.
finding_summary.results: The declared replay mixture ran in all 449 executed feedback states. Actual distinct scaffold groups per 32-member update rose from 17.87 to 23.26, with broader exposure in all fifteen task sessions. Graph-origin replay received less probability, but its average sampled trajectory log-probability increase rose slightly from 0.169 to 0.176 nats and more later policy emissions occupied previously trained graph families. Mean accepted policy-origin score increased from 0.205 to 0.238. This did not improve every output measure: raw valid-novel yield fell from 66.59% to 64.74%, duplicates increased, and emitted scaffold coverage narrowed slightly. Both formally successful seed endpoints fell, by 0.02618 and 0.06224. The third seed completed its oracle calls but failed on the final canonical-identity feedback join, leaving its formal macro score unavailable.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich output mixes plausible cyclic amines with peroxides, N-halogen bonds and severely constrained unsaturated rings
molecular.overall_character: All five supplied tasks cover all three seeds, with 900 trajectory rows and 870 optimizer proposals per task. All 4,350 optimizer proposals parse with RDKit, but their chemical plausibility varies substantially. The output is rich in rings and aromatic atoms: digest ring-closure rates range from 0.9782 to 0.9954 and aromatic-token rates from 0.9103 to 0.9759. Median proposal heavy-atom counts are 26, 35, 26, 32 and 25 in the fixed task order, with median ring counts of three, five, four, four and three. Conventional diaryl ethers, thioamides, aryl sulfonamides, heteroaromatic carbonyl systems, cyclic tertiary amines and arylpiperazines coexist with diaryl peroxides, N-chloro or N-fluoro groups, densely fused sulfur/nitrogen frameworks and small rings bearing cumulated carbon double bonds. Each task contains 529-717 distinct nonchiral Murcko scaffolds, but many digest leaders are variants within a few families; graph-level diversity does not establish accessible synthetic diversity. Relative to the parent, one leading repertoire becomes enriched in peroxides, another in small-ring allenes and N-halogen bonds, while the strongest cyclic-amine chemistry includes smaller, recognizable benzazepine-like structures. No assigned stereocentres occur among optimizer proposals, despite 273, 179, 562, 373 and 348 proposals containing an unassigned centre in task order. Synthetic plausibility is therefore questionable overall, with clear plausible subsets; the supplied scores do not establish stability, synthetic access or experimental activity.

per_task.generated_character: The leading family contains two methyl-substituted phenyl rings connected by an ether or peroxide, with an aryl thioamide attached to a diazine ring. The ether has 24 heavy atoms and the peroxide 25; both have three aromatic six-membered rings. Other leaders are compact fused azaaromatic ketones and a fused aromatic carbonyl/N-N heterocycle. Those carbonyl and thioamide frameworks are recognizable chemistry, but the peroxide, N-chloro amide/thioamide and unusual sulfur double-bond variants make part of the leading family chemically questionable as persistent drug-like molecules. The whole proposal set has median 26 heavy atoms and three aromatic rings. Compared with the parent, O-O single-bond proposals increase from 15 to 89 and N-halogen proposals from five to 27, so the new leading peroxide chemistry reflects a broader change in the sampled output.
liabilities: Diaryl O-O links and N-chloro or N-fluoro nitrogen sites introduce possible bond-cleavage and reactivity concerns; valid SMILES and objective values do not resolve those concerns.

The terminal sulfur-linked N-fluoro example and sulfur oxo/thioxo substitutions are chemically different from ordinary amides or sulfonamides and should not be interpreted as interchangeable polar linkers.
Nine proposals have at most three heavy atoms and four exceed 50, indicating occasional degeneration and overgrowth around an otherwise ring-rich population.
missing_features: The high-score neighborhood lacks demonstrated stable, conventional alternatives that retain the useful diaryl/polar arrangement while replacing its peroxide and N-halogen variants; the high-scoring ether shows such chemistry is already reachable.
Broader coverage of distinct compact aromatic carbonyl arrangements is less visible among the digest leaders than repeated changes around the same diaryl linker and thioamide family.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Replacing the diaryl ether link with an O-O link accompanies a score increase from 0.444319 to 0.455132 in a displayed local pair. Adding N-chlorination to the peroxide thioamide gives 0.439920, and the corresponding N-chloro carbonyl amide gives 0.438748. These observations show that the score tolerates the questionable bonds; they do not establish a benefit from N-chlorination or the chemical stability of a peroxide. Compact fused aromatic carbonyl structures also reach 0.436954 and 0.433013 without those particular bonds. At the low end, oxygen fluoride, methane and trifluoromethylamine score zero, while much larger, heavily elaborated molecules score about 1.05e-68 and 1.11e-62. The gradient therefore favors a structured intermediate-size aromatic/polar arrangement over both tiny fragments and overgrowth, while leaving some local chemical liabilities unpenalized.

per_task.generated_character: This is a large, highly aromatic, halogenated repertoire: median 35 heavy atoms, five rings, four aromatic rings and molecular mass 555.2495; the digest halogen rate is 0.8241. The highest molecule is a comparatively conventional three-ring aminoheteroaryl arylsulfonamide with methyl, fluoromethyl and aryl halogen substituents. Other leaders combine nitrogen/sulfur heteroaromatics with sulfonyl groups, carbonyls and heavily fused, iodine- or bromine-substituted ring systems. One displayed leader has eight rings and seven aromatic rings, and a terminal example contains selenium. The parent also contained large heteroaryl/sulfur frameworks and frequent peroxide or O-halogen connections. Current O-O single-bond proposals fall from 135 to five and O-halogen proposals from 93 to four, but substantial size and fusion remain: 146 current proposals exceed 50 heavy atoms.
liabilities: Large aromatic surfaces, iodine or bromine substitution and repeated ring fusion produce high molecular masses and little saturated shape in many leaders; no solubility or exposure measurements are supplied.

Some terminal molecules combine unusual nitrogen/oxygen/sulfur bonding or selenium heterocycles with already elaborate fused systems, increasing the uncertainty of interpreting them as ordinary medicinal chemistry.
The proposal distribution reaches 95 heavy atoms and 13 perceived rings; such overgrowth is not justified by the simpler structure at the highest displayed score.
missing_features: The output lacks consistent economical coverage of the productive aminoheteroaryl/sulfonamide arrangement: the highest displayed molecule is much simpler than several heavily fused alternatives.
Synthetic access and stable geometry are not established for the densely fused sulfur/nitrogen leaders; graph ring counts cannot substitute for chemically credible alternative ring systems.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The three-ring aminoheteroaryl sulfonamide scores 0.607553; a six-ring iodine-containing fused system scores 0.604646 and an eight-ring elaboration 0.598471. These examples do not support continually adding rings or heavy halogens as necessary for higher score. The low-scoring examples, around 0.265-0.292, also contain sulfones, carbonyls and sometimes several rings, but distribute them through more saturated or differently connected frameworks. Functional-group presence alone therefore fails to explain the gradient. A terminal small fluorinated diene scores 0.5 despite lacking the elaborate heteroaromatic architecture, so intermediate score itself is weak evidence of molecular completeness.

per_task.generated_character: The leading chemistry is substantially more conventional than the most unusual output elsewhere. The highest displayed molecule is a phenolic benzazepine-like structure: a seven-membered tertiary-amine ring fused to a benzene, with alkyl substituents, only 18 heavy atoms and molecular mass 247.382. A closely related leader has 17 heavy atoms. Another family is an arylpiperazine linked through a long alkyl chain to fluorinated naphthalene or aza-naphthalene rings; these examples have four rings and approximately 29-32 heavy atoms. The full set has median 26 heavy atoms and median sp3-carbon fraction 0.5. Parent leaders also included arylpiperazine chains and fused phenolic amines, but some were much more bridged or polycyclic; current median heavy-atom count falls from 30 to 26.
liabilities: Long alkyl chains in the arylpiperazine family increase conformational freedom, and extra halogenation increases mass, while the compact phenolic amine shows that neither feature is universally needed.
Some terminal structures add strained or partially dearomatized rings and duplicated arylpiperazine appendages; these are less straightforward chemical proposals than the leading conventional amines.
Thirty proposals contain an N-halogen bond, but the displayed highest-scoring conventional amines do not require that liability.
missing_features: No additional mandatory pharmacophoric group can be inferred from near-ceiling scores; the supported missing chemistry is configurationally specified coverage of the successful cyclic amines.

The compact leading phenolic amines have an unassigned stereogenic carbon. Across proposals, 562 molecules contain an unassigned centre and none has an assigned centre, leaving geometry-dependent interpretation unresolved.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Both the compact phenolic cyclic amine and the long-linker arylpiperazines reach scores above 0.999999. Their shared association is accessible tertiary-amine functionality presented with aromatic regions; extensive halogenation, multiple aromatic rings or one exact linker length is not required by all leading examples. An acetylated bis-sulfonamide aniline scores about 3.80e-05 and an aromatic carbamate about 9.56e-05, despite their heteroatoms and rings. The terminal shorter fluoroalkyl diazepane scores 0.036190, whereas related extended arylpiperazine architectures remain around 0.975-0.996. These observations indicate contextual amine/aromatic placement rather than generic nitrogen enrichment, and do not establish experimental receptor activity.

per_task.generated_character: The leading repertoire is dominated by fused azaaromatic systems with N-methylated cyclic amide carbonyls, supplemented by a bicyclic amine/ketone family carrying an N-ethoxy connection and an aromatic ether arm. The highest molecule has 30 heavy atoms, five rings and four aromatic rings; closely related N-alkyl variants occupy much of the digest. Several carbonyl-bearing rings are seven- or eight-membered within multiply fused frameworks, and another leader has a perceived nine-membered ring. These are complex rather than sparse ring systems. Full proposals have median 32 heavy atoms and four rings, with 668 nonchiral Murcko scaffolds. Parent leaders also included N-methyl cyclic carbonyl systems and aromatic assemblies, with additional sulfonylpiperazine chemistry; the current digest is more visibly concentrated in fused carbonyl/N-alkyl variants.
liabilities: Complex fused and bridged carbonyl frameworks may impose synthetic and conformational constraints that their accepted SMILES do not capture.
N-O bonds in the N-ethoxy family and unusual N/N/O ring arrangements deserve separate chemical scrutiny; their presence is not interchangeable with a conventional ether or amine.
Sixty proposals exceed 50 heavy atoms, and 373 contain an unassigned stereocentre, so size and geometry remain unresolved even though rings and carbonyls are plentiful.
missing_features: The leading set lacks broad chemically distinct alternatives that preserve the observed aromatic and cyclic-carbonyl arrangement; much of the visible variation changes N-alkyl groups or local ring closure.
No supplied evidence establishes stable conformations or accessible syntheses for the unusual fusion patterns, and the N-ethoxy bicyclic leader leaves a stereocentre unspecified.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The fused N-aryl carbonyl framework reaches 0.202215, the N-ethoxy bicyclic amine/ketone example 0.200010, and several nearby fused N-alkyl variants approximately 0.197-0.199. These small differences do not identify a unique missing substituent. The low end includes oxygen bonded to fluorine and chlorine at zero, bromopropane at 0.018950, ethyl acetate at 0.030544 and a small amino heterocycle at 0.041345. Those lack the combined aromatic/cyclic-carbonyl architecture of the leaders. A long-chain sulfur-rich cyclic molecule also scores only 0.031469, demonstrating that molecular size and heteroatom abundance alone are insufficient. Late, related N/O-rich fused carbonyl structures remain around 0.16-0.18 rather than establishing a different high-score chemotype.

per_task.generated_character: The highest family combines a fused nitrogen-rich dicarbonyl heterocycle, N-methyl and N-fluoro substituents, a hydroxylated azaaryl ring and a four-membered carbon ring. In the two highest displayed molecules that small ring contains a cumulated C=C=C unit; another leader contains a four-membered conjugated diene. These are severe ring-geometry liabilities, despite all SMILES parsing. Other leading families contain an N-acetyl arylsulfonamide with a sulfinamide substituent and unsaturated fluorinated five-membered rings, or hydrazone/polyene chains ending in a charged nitrogen/oxygen/sulfur group. Median proposal size is 25 heavy atoms and three rings. Compared with the parent, N-halogen proposals rise from five to 157, carbon-allene proposals from one to 113, and proposals with a carbon allene contained in a perceived ring of at most five atoms from zero to 93. The current chemistry is therefore not simply a conventional heteroaromatic analogue series.
liabilities: There are 93 proposals with a carbon allene in a perceived ring of at most five atoms, and 62 with a four-membered ring containing at least two double bonds. Their constrained unsaturation is a chemical-realizability concern that ordinary valence parsing does not test.

N-halogen bonds occur in 157 proposals, and the digest charged rate is 0.2471; the leading N-F and unusual charged sulfur/nitrogen forms require stronger chemical qualification than neutral carbonyl heterocycles.
Twenty-five proposals exceed 50 heavy atoms, while repeated small-ring or heterocycle duplication can produce vanishing scores without removing the original local liabilities.
missing_features: The leading neighborhood lacks demonstrated ordinary, geometrically credible ring alternatives preserving the useful carbonyl/azaaryl arrangement without a four-membered allene or diene.

Stable nitrogen substitution and sulfur/nitrogen electronic structures are not established for the N-fluoro and charged terminal-group families; the observed scores do not establish that these unusual bonds are required.
Configurationally explicit proposals are absent despite 348 molecules having an unassigned centre; the highest small-ring-allene examples also leave a stereogenic centre unspecified.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The N-fluoro dicarbonyl structures with a four-membered cyclic allene score 0.419765; the related four-membered diene scores 0.401915. A fluorinated five-membered diene sulfonamide scores 0.369632 and its cyclic-allene counterpart 0.366311. These values associate compact polar heterocycles and unsaturated substituent arrangements with higher score, but cannot establish stable realizable chemistry or a general benefit from cumulated bonds. The digest median is 0.001873, while eleven full-trajectory rows are exactly zero. Very large linked structures and long-chain polyamines populate that zero-score tail; duplicating the unusual N-halogen dicarbonyl framework in a terminal molecule gives approximately 1.63e-26. Compactness helps explain part of the visible gradient, while serious local bonding liabilities remain in the leaders.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A diaryl peroxide scores 0.455132 while the corresponding ether scores 0.444319, and N-chlorinated derivatives remain nearby. Another session has 157 N-halogen proposals, 113 carbon-allene proposals and 93 with an allene inside a perceived ring of at most five atoms; its highest structures carry both N-F and four-membered cumulated unsaturation. All proposals parse with RDKit, so these liabilities survive ordinary molecular-graph acceptance. Conventional aromatic carbonyl and cyclic-amine leaders elsewhere show that unusual bonds are not universally needed for appreciable reward.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably preserve ordinary bond chemistry and feasible ring geometry within productive structural neighborhoods.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The missing capability is reliable access to stable, geometrically credible alternatives that retain a useful arrangement of rings and polar groups. Chemical plausibility needs to distinguish ethers from peroxides, ordinary N-substitution from N-halogen bonds, and accessible unsaturated rings from extremely constrained cumulenes, independently of objective identity.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Median heavy-atom counts are 26, 35, 26, 32 and 25, but 4, 146, 7, 60 and 25 proposals respectively exceed 50 heavy atoms. Tiny fragments such as oxygen-halogen species or simple esters also occur at the low end. In one session the highest displayed aminoheteroaryl sulfonamide has three rings, whereas six- and eight-ring alternatives have slightly lower scores. In another, a phenolic tertiary amine with 18 heavy atoms reaches near-ceiling score alongside much larger arylpiperazines. Duplicating a polar heterocycle can coincide with a score around 1.63e-26.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator has inconsistent control of molecular size and topology around otherwise useful chemical arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Useful chemical coverage requires economical alternatives with controlled ring fusion, linker length and appendage size, while retaining demonstrated compact and extended chemotypes. A fixed preference for either very small molecules or maximal ring growth would miss the contextual structural relationships visible in the supplied feedback.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Across 4,350 optimizer proposals there are no assigned stereocentres. The five supplied sessions contain 273, 179, 562, 373 and 348 proposals with an unassigned centre. Digest leaders include a compact phenolic cyclic amine, an N-ethoxy bicyclic amine/ketone and fluorinated unsaturated rings with unspecified configurations. Ring richness therefore does not imply defined three-dimensional molecular proposals.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator emits stereogenic structures without specifying their configurations or resolving relevant bond geometry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The chemical representation needs to support explicit, internally consistent stereoisomers and bond geometries wherever those degrees of freedom exist. Their usefulness must remain determined by observed feedback, without assuming an unobserved preferred configuration or requiring stereochemistry in naturally achiral chemotypes.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Each session contains 529-717 nonchiral Murcko scaffolds, yet the displayed leaders repeatedly vary diaryl thioamide linkers, fused sulfonyl heterocycles, arylpiperazine chains, N-alkyl cyclic-carbonyl systems or N-fluoro dicarbonyl cores. Several nearby variants have identical or very similar scores. The leaders also demonstrate that nitrogen environments are not interchangeable: conventional tertiary amines, acylated nitrogens, sulfonamide nitrogens and N-halogen forms occupy very different chemical contexts.
transferable_gaps.gap: Many graph scaffolds do not translate into broad coverage of chemically distinct productive core arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The generator needs chemically meaningful alternatives in core connectivity and polar-group placement, beyond peripheral halogen changes, N-alkyl substitutions and new ring closures. Preserve the ability to explore different stable architectures that realize an observed useful arrangement, while distinguishing functional-group electronic context and avoiding any prescribed objective-specific scaffold.

nodes.method_name: Genetic GFN: reciprocal learning between a flow policy and graph search
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Genetic GFN: alternately generate molecules with a GFlowNet policy, refine the resulting scored population through graph crossover and mutation, and distill scored descendants back into the policy using rank-weighted off-policy replay. The policy uses trajectory balance with a learned log normalizer and regularization toward a frozen prior. [Kim et al., Section 3](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.05961v4) describe this mechanism. Train the prior only on the permitted unlabeled corpus. Each objective starts with clean policy adaptation, replay and population state initialized from its supplied observations. Use a positive terminal reward increasing with the observed maximization score. Schedule policy and genetic phases around the evaluator's announced feedback; both produce new molecules, and all reward-bearing training records come from accepted observations. Later policy samples must enter genetic populations, and accepted graph descendants must affect subsequent policy updates. Generate further valid, canonical-unique structures to fill announced batches, without corpus ranking or a fixed molecular library. The hypothesis is that learned global proposals propagate local discoveries into new promising regions and then support further graph refinement, raising the mean of five independent final Top-1 scores. Published larger-budget gains do not establish that this reciprocal learning becomes useful quickly enough here.

approach.method_basis: The Parent trains a recurrent SMILES prior on an unlabeled corpus and adapts a fresh policy independently for each objective. Each accepted batch supplies its best-scoring half for training, alongside a uniform sample of historical elites from the thirty-two highest-scoring retained identities. Original accepted strings and scores stay intact. The policy fits each sequence toward its frozen prior log probability plus sixty times the real accepted score, with equal weight per training row. After learning, current elites enter memory and the next novel molecules are sampled directly from the policy.
approach.novelty: Replay the retained examples that have waited longest since their last inclusion in training. Maintain one bounded timestamp per retained identity and refresh it when that identity joins the actual training group. The existing score and canonical order break ties. This spreads training opportunities over the same retained high-score memory while keeping original strings and targets. The sibling selector prioritizes score on every update, the retention sibling changes which families survive, and the view sibling changes how an accepted identity is written. This mechanism instead changes when the existing records are revisited. A passive uniform draw on the same memory will reveal whether waiting examples actually replace recently trained ones and change the learning gradient.

nodes.hypothesis: Select historical replay members by oldest last-training-membership batch, breaking ties by the inherited descending accepted-score/canonical order, while preserving the original accepted records, replay count, top-score memory retention and equal-row online learning.

finding_summary.headline: Replay shortened waiting gaps and changed learning, while the three-seed mean score fell
finding_summary.insights: More even access to retained records is now established, but it did not ensure that more of the available records were revisited before they disappeared. Across the actual trajectories, the mean largest waiting age in eligible memory fell from 9.898 to 4.486 updates and its observed maximum fell from 25 to 7. First historical reuse had a shorter tail, with its maximum falling from 23 to 6 updates, while its mean became later: 3.385 to 3.967. Of 1,602 identities with a usable replay opportunity, 556 never received one, compared with 540 of 1,562 in the parent. Among those 556 child identities, 401 had been evicted and 155 were still retained when the last useful replay opportunity ended. Scheduling the oldest records therefore improved waiting-time balance without resolving loss of access through retention turnover and the finite horizon. The actual selection had slightly higher reward than passive uniform on the same memory, by 0.003784 on average. Its poorer endpoint is therefore not explained by a general same-memory preference for weaker accepted scores. The adapted trajectories nevertheless supplied lower average rewards in both their historical and current elite groups. The fixed parent-stream schedule also shortened waits, but cannot predict which new molecules a changed policy would generate. Waiting time does not measure forgetting, and a larger learning gradient does not demonstrate useful transfer. The 480 positive log-probability targets among 2,100 nonterminal historical exposures remain mathematically unattainable. The supplied chemistry assessment describes broad, mostly conventional aryl amide and basic-amine chemistry, with incomplete local attachment and substitution comparisons, occasional uncontrolled growth and no explicit tetrahedral stereochemistry. Its scattered sitagliptin leaders do not establish a consistent productive local series. These findings, together with lower duplicate concentration and lower score, show that fitting retained strings more evenly is insufficient to preserve useful chemical relationships during exploration. Future tests need to connect refresh opportunities to retention lifetime, measured target error and the quality of subsequent novel molecules.
finding_summary.results: The scheduling and learning effects both occurred across all three seeds and five tasks. In the 390 nonterminal updates with surplus memory and unequal waiting ages, selected examples had waited 4.425 updates on average, versus 2.568 for the passive uniform choice on the identical memory and timestamp state: an increase of 1.856 updates. The increase was strict in 389 cases; in the remaining case both choices already selected five examples at the maximum waiting age. Refreshing the actual selection never left a larger pending maximum wait and reduced it in 286 of 420 comparisons. Replay memberships differed from uniform in 405 updates, and all 405 produced gradient changes above the registered numerical tolerance. Historical mean squared target error fell from 163.326 to 113.039, decreasing in 416 of 420 updates. These intermediate gains did not deliver the intended score gain. The three-seed mean final-best score was 0.495438, versus 0.507554 for the parent, a paired mean change of -0.012116. Population standard deviations were 0.022530 and 0.011518. Paired macro changes by seed were -0.029843, -0.035944 and +0.029439. Sitagliptin accounted for the main loss: its task mean fell from 0.297258 to 0.205390, with a decline in every seed. Zaleplon and median similarity gained 0.015642 and 0.015419 in task mean; scaffold hopping changed by -0.000575 and DRD2 by +0.000804. All 4,350 submitted policy proposals were valid and canonically novel within their sessions, and every task completed its 300 evaluations. Raw duplicate draws declined from 30.11% to 26.93%; all 435 child batches completed in one sampling call, whereas five parent batches needed another call.

molecular.headline: Mostly conventional aryl amides and basic amines; missing chemistry is better resolved local variation, not more exotic rings
molecular.overall_character: The full current and parent trajectories cover every task and seed; each current task has 900 observations and 870 optimizer proposals. The output is chemically broad and predominantly recognizable: aryl amides, ureas, sulfonamides, oxazoles, indoles, piperazines, ordinary fused-ring amines, and assorted polar or peptide-like structures. Ring-closure presence ranges from 0.9828 to 0.9943, and aromatic-token presence from 0.9483 to 0.9908. These molecule-level text counters are not aromatic atom fractions or proof of synthetic accessibility. Mean SMILES lengths range from 39.4 to 54.6, although occasional large hybrids and long alkyl chains remain. Leading ring systems usually have ordinary geometry and bond types; apparent synthetic plausibility is generally good, with compound-specific exceptions such as organoselenium, hydrazone, azide, nitrosamine, and very large polar structures. Charge-token rates range from 0.0299 to 0.3161, but several charged drawings are net-neutral nitro or heterocycle N-oxide representations, not evidence of a net ionic molecule. Explicit tetrahedral stereolabel rates are zero throughout. The parent also generated conventional medicinal chemistry, and the current outputs mainly change scaffold families and their substitution patterns rather than reveal a general shortage of rings, carbonyls, or basic amines.

per_task.generated_character: The leading molecule is a moderately sized benzamide carrying a terminal pyridyl amide and a benzylic ether linked to a methylpyridine. Other leaders include bicyclic aza-lactam carboxamides with benzyl or phenethyl substitution, N-methyl pyrrole carboxanilides with phenoxymethyl groups, a thioether-substituted azaaromatic amide, and an indole dicarboxamide. These are mostly conventional aromatic rings, ether or thioether connections, and standard amide bonds, with credible-looking synthetic building blocks. Aromatic and ring presence are 0.9885 and 0.9943, and mean SMILES length is 39.8. The low excerpt contains much larger polyaromatic/polyamine or amide-rich hybrids, including a permanently charged heteroaromatic structure, rather than a simple absence of ring chemistry.
liabilities: Large polyaromatic hybrids introduce substantial size and conformational complexity and appear among the lowest scores.
Benzylic ether, phenethyl, and related connections create flexibility and potential metabolic liabilities, although no stability measurements are supplied.
Some extreme low-scoring structures combine formal cationic centres, fluorinated groups, and several large aromatic fragments; their effects are not isolated by matched comparisons.
missing_features: More matched combinations of amide aryl identity, ether connection, and heteroatom position are needed to establish which parts of the leading arrangement transfer.
Compact alternative connections that retain the useful carbonyl/ether relationships are underrepresented relative to some late structures that discard them.
Large hybrid branches lack controlled simplification back to a coherent compact architecture.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The pyridyl/benzylic-ether benzamide reaches 0.511549; replacing its terminal pyridyl group with either of the cited chlorophenyl groups gives 0.432481. In a separate pyrrole-amide family, para-fluorophenyl and para-chlorophenyl variants tie at 0.433000, while the meta-chlorophenyl member gives 0.444319. This supports local heteroatom placement and connection geometry rather than a general halogen rule. A bicyclic aza-lactam carboxamide reaches 0.478654, showing another productive architecture. Large hybrids score as low as 1.12e-67. Conversely, a final arylalkene lacking the amide/ether arrangement scores 0.002927, and a simple formylbenzoic acid gives about 9.57e-10; reducing size while discarding functional relationships is also unproductive in these examples. The current seed-2 maximum exceeds the parent's 0.390070 sulfonamide-family maximum, but the parent's overall methoxyindole/benzyl carboxamide maximum was 0.528059. Both sets show accessible chemistry, without identifying one uniquely required scaffold.

per_task.generated_character: The strongest family comprises aryl sulfonamides connected to oxazoles and terminal phenyl or furyl groups, with extensive carbon-bound fluorination. The best is a largely aromatic, acceptor-rich sulfonamide with ordinary ring geometry. Nitro-substituted members and alternative furyl attachment patterns also appear near the top. Other seeds explore nitroaryl acylhydrazones, fluorinated aryl amidine-like compounds, and aminopyridine/nitrile systems. Ring and aromatic presence are 0.9931 and 0.9908; mean SMILES length is 54.6. The charge-token rate is 0.3161, but cited nitro leaders use internal N+/O- notation and are net neutral. These structures look broadly synthesizable, while their high aromatic surface, fluorination, and selected hydrazone/nitro groups leave physical-property and stability questions.
liabilities: Multiple aromatic rings and heavy fluorination create a substantial hydrophobic and low-flexibility surface; solubility and permeability are not measured.
Nitro and acylhydrazone-containing branches require their own chemical and metabolic assessment, even though charge-separated notation alone is not a liability.
Some larger alternatives add aromatic or polar groups without demonstrating a clearer local score advantage.
missing_features: Compact less fluorinated analogues preserving the strongest sulfonamide/heteroaryl connections are only partially represented.
Alternative ordinary connections and less aromatic scaffolds maintaining the observed donor/acceptor relationships are underrepresented among the leaders.
Matched stable alternatives around the nitroaryl acylhydrazone branch are insufficiently established.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The highly fluorinated phenyl/oxazole/sulfonamide scores 0.600929; a less fluorinated furyl analogue reaches 0.598891. Adding another fluorine to the sulfonyl phenyl ring in a matched mono-fluorophenyl series lowers 0.596372 to 0.595736, so more fluorination does not monotonically help. Related nitro analogues score 0.597042 and 0.596400, and changing remote heteroaryl attachment or substitution gives nearby scores. Low sulfone-containing structures score 0.266174-0.308334 despite substantial aromatic or amine content. These are not matched replacements of the leading sulfonamide/oxazole framework; they show that sulfonyl, aromatic, or basic groups alone are insufficient. The current maximum is below the parent's 0.611929 fluorinated azaaromatic/benzofuran family, while the current seed-2 maximum of 0.588776 exceeds its parent's 0.575867 in a different aryl amidine-like family. No unique requirement for extensive fluorination or nitro substitution follows.

per_task.generated_character: The leading chemotypes are simple and recognizable: N,N-dialkyl aminotetralins or related fused carbocycles, and arylpiperazines joined through a propoxy chain to another aromatic group. The best dipropyl aminotetralin has a basic tertiary amine and an ordinary benzene-fused saturated ring. Near-leading piperazines use phenyl, fluorophenyl, or bromophenyl groups; some add a second piperazine or a benzylamino substituent. Ring and aromatic presence are 0.9851 and 0.9724, with mean SMILES length 40.2. These are apparently plausible drug-like building blocks, without the need for exotic sulfur or highly strained aromatic closures. The substituted aminotetralin carbon has unspecified stereochemistry, and neutral free-base drawings do not establish the relevant protonation state.
liabilities: Long alkyl chains and extra aromatic/basic appendages increase size, lipophilicity, and conformational complexity without a necessary score gain.
Multiple potential protonation states and saturated-ring stereochemistry remain unspecified.
Near-unit supplied values do not distinguish the physical properties or stability of otherwise different high-scoring molecules.
missing_features: Defined stereoisomers of the substituted aminotetralins and related saturated rings are absent.
Systematic smaller, less hydrophobic peripheral variants are incomplete despite evidence that long-chain growth eventually lowers the score.
The near-upper score series does not establish a chemical need for additional aromatic groups, halogens, or repeated basic rings.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The dipropyl aminotetralin scores 0.999999969, and the fluorophenyl/phenoxypropyl piperazine scores 0.999999589. Smaller or expanded fused rings, modest alkyl changes, and several arylpiperazine decorations all remain near the same upper score region. Fluoro/bromo exchange in the extended piperazine series ties at 0.999998759. These tiny differences do not resolve a uniquely preferred chemical detail. In contrast, further lengthening a long N-alkyl chain in a matched benzylamino-substituted series lowers 0.933911 to 0.515659, supporting bounded peripheral growth. Low acid/amide/sulfonamide or nitro heteroaromatic structures score around 1.86e-5 to 4.11e-5; the observed association is with accessible basic amines arranged with hydrophobic groups, not nitrogen count alone. The parent also reached near-unit scores with arylpiperazines. The current output broadens that high-score chemistry to simpler aminotetralins, while its seed-0 maximum is lower than the parent's in another fused-amine family.

per_task.generated_character: The leading molecules combine aryl sulfonamides with N-methylpiperazine and either an indolyl anisole group or a substituted benzamide. Additional plausible leaders include a carbamate/benzodioxole piperazine sulfonamide and related aryl amino connections. These structures have ordinary aromatic and saturated heterocyclic rings, carbonyl or sulfonyl acceptors, and accessible NH or tertiary-amine functionality depending on substitution. Ring and aromatic presence are 0.9908 and 0.9506, with mean SMILES length 39.4. The lead series is synthetically recognizable. Low-scoring outliers instead include an acyclic azide, a nitrosamine, long lipid-like chains, a flexible amine/disulfide chain, and small nitro compounds; these should not be generalized to the main molecular population.

Additional piperidine-containing branches enlarge the molecule without improving the cited leading score.
Low-scoring azide and nitrosamine proposals carry separate reactivity or toxicological concerns.
Long lipid-like and flexible disulfide-containing outliers depart markedly from the productive compact aryl series.

Controlled simplification that retains the productive indole or benzamide relationship is incomplete.

per_task.score_gradient_reading: The indolyl anisole/N-methylpiperazine sulfonamide scores 0.247105; appending a piperidinyloxy group lowers it to 0.215431. per_task.generated_character: The modest-scoring leaders are chemically scattered. The best is an amino/methyl-substituted benzanilide carrying a cyanomethyl selenoether. Other leaders include a gem-difluoro carbonyl-containing nitrogen ring linked to an indole acetic acid, a formamidoaryl N-oxide heterocycle, a tertiary-amino thioether diacylhydrazine, a sulfonylhydrazone, and a simple methoxypyridyl/pyridylmethyl urea. These vary substantially in charge representation, ring topology, carbonyl connection, and heteroatom identity. Many are conventional in size and bonding; the selenium substituent and some hydrazone or N-oxide chemistry deserve individual scrutiny. The zero-scoring excerpt is dominated by much larger peptide-like, polyol-rich, lipid-like, or highly connected amine structures.

Hydrazone, diacylhydrazine, and N-oxide-containing leaders require individual stability assessment rather than one shared chemical explanation.
Very large peptide-like, polyol-rich, and lipid-like structures add many functional groups but remain at the observed floor.
Late small molecules can also lose the productive functional relationships, showing that generic simplification is insufficient.

The generator has not established a coherent compact arrangement that combines the useful carbonyl, donor, and heteroatom relationships across these otherwise diverse leaders.
Stable common-atom alternatives around the isolated organoselenium leader are not shown in a comparable series.

per_task.score_gradient_reading: The organoselenium benzanilide reaches 0.273727, the gem-difluoro acid/heterocycle 0.215065, the N-oxide/formamide 0.206590, and the diacylhydrazine/thioether 0.203133. The simple urea scores 0.170810. These are distinct scaffolds rather than a matched chemical gradient, so the selenium maximum does not demonstrate that selenium is beneficial or required. The median supplied score is zero, and large peptide/polyol hybrids score zero, but small final aryl amides, sulfonamides, or hydrazine-containing structures can also score poorly. Thus size reduction alone is insufficient. The current maximum is below the parent's 0.310866 compact imino/dicarbonyl heterocycle, and each current seed maximum is below its parent counterpart. transferable_gaps.evidence: Conventional arylamide, sulfonamide, and basic-amine leaders show interpretable local preferences, but another population's moderate leaders are unrelated selenium, fluorinated acid, N-oxide, hydrazine, and urea scaffolds. Those isolated structures do not identify which group actually contributes.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator lacks consistently controlled local variation around productive functional-group arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Generate matched alternatives that preserve the surrounding scaffold while varying one connection, substituent position, heteroatom, or carbonyl relationship. Build local evidence before carrying an isolated unusual group into many larger structures.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Large hybrid arylamides can score near zero, an added piperidinyloxy branch lowers 0.247105 to 0.215431, and further extension of a long N-alkyl chain lowers a matched score from 0.933911 to 0.515659. Yet modest additions to simpler aryl sulfonamides can help, so size alone is not a universal rule.
transferable_gaps.gap: Peripheral growth is not consistently bounded by the useful chemical architecture.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support controlled pruning and growth that retain the productive core and group spacing. Prefer comparisons that distinguish useful new functionality from repeated aromatic units, long alkyl chains, or unrelated polar fragments.

transferable_gaps.evidence: An organoselenium compound is a solitary moderate-scoring leader without a supplied sulfur or carbon analogue. Some branches contain hydrazones, nitro groups, azides, or nitrosamines, while most strong leaders use ordinary amides, sulfonamides, ethers, and amines.
transferable_gaps.gap: Stable common-atom alternatives are insufficiently tested around isolated unusual or reactive outputs.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make chemically conventional replacements accessible without disturbing the rest of the molecule, and evaluate them using current feedback. Do not infer that an unusual atom or bond is required merely because one molecule containing it scores well.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every digest population has zero explicit tetrahedral stereolabel presence. The aminotetralin leaders and substituted fluorinated nitrogen rings support stereochemical distinctions, and larger saturated or polyol structures can contain many unspecified centres.
transferable_gaps.gap: Stereochemical identity is missing despite access to credible saturated-ring chemistry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve existing stereochemical information and make valid local stereoisomers available when new centres arise. Use those defined molecules in local comparisons while retaining ordinary feasible ring geometry.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The leaders frequently combine multiple aromatic rings with fluorination, alkyl chains, sulfonamides, or basic amines. Closely related fluorination changes can be neutral or unfavorable, and extra amine-containing branches do not necessarily improve the supplied score. Broad overall molecular diversity does not resolve these local relationships.
transferable_gaps.gap: Alternative polar and hydrophobic arrangements are underexplored within the most successful aromatic families.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Vary aryl heteroatom position, linker polarity, carbonyl connection, and amine placement while holding size and the main topology reasonably steady. Let the current objective locate useful balance rather than assuming that more halogen, aromatic surface, or nitrogen is beneficial.

nodes.method_name: Augmented Hill-Climb with a corpus-trained SMILES policy
nodes.method_thesis: Train a compact autoregressive SMILES prior solely on the supplied unlabeled corpus, then initialize a fresh policy from that prior for each objective. Use the initial observations and each subsequent scored batch to update only its highest-reward sequences with the Augmented Hill-Climb loss: fit policy log likelihood to frozen-prior log likelihood plus scaled observed reward. Sample complete molecules token by token from the updated policy, canonicalize them, and refill invalid or duplicate proposals by further generation. The corpus supplies language training, never a ranked molecular pool. Elite-conditioned policy updates should shift generation toward new high-scoring molecular combinations quickly enough to improve the benchmark's mean final Top-1. This is a small-budget transfer hypothesis, not a claim that published larger-budget gains carry over. The root uses the current scored batch; randomized historical replay is reserved for the first improvement. The anchor's elite augmented-likelihood mechanism is described by [Thomas et al.](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13321-022-00646-z).

approach.method_basis: The Parent runs short molecular editing episodes from molecules that already have real scores. Several persistent lanes each propose one action per batch. At a decision, it generates a fresh neighborhood of valid single graph edits and usually selects the edit preferred by one neural estimate of future episode improvement, with occasional uniform random choices. Every accepted molecule becomes the lane's next state, including molecules that score worse. Rewards measure only increases in that episode's best score. A replay buffer of real accepted transitions trains the value network through double-Q backups: the current network chooses a continuation and a delayed copy evaluates that same continuation. This machinery was confirmed in the Parent, including learning that affected later actions, but its best molecules concentrated around one core per objective. All lanes use the same learned value function, and their explicit random exploration is sampled separately at each decision.
approach.novelty: Add episode-consistent exploration through bootstrapped value functions. Five independently initialized value networks learn from different persistent random subsets of the same accepted transitions, each with its own delayed target copy. Each lane samples one network when an episode begins and uses that network for the episode's exploitation decisions, including decisions after a temporary score loss. Keeping the network identity through a sequence gives different lanes different learned reasons to pursue edits over several steps; feedback can still update that network between batches. The proposed change is new within this lineage, whose supplied sibling history contains only the single-network Parent. It tests the exploration direction deferred by that Parent. The activation claim is that persistent, differently trained heads make different actual exploitation choices on the same available edits; broader search and better final scores are possible consequences to measure, not assumptions.

nodes.hypothesis: Replace the Parent's single acting Q-function with five independently initialized Q-functions trained on persistent Bernoulli bootstrap masks of accepted replay, each with its own lagged double-Q target, and select one head uniformly at episode start to control all exploitation decisions in that episode while retaining the Parent's epsilon branch.

finding_summary.headline: Learned episode heads diversify real choices and molecular distances, but lower the aggregate score
finding_summary.insights: Scarce feedback was sufficient to produce distinct learned head policies that changed real multistep search. The receipts rule out unused network copies, numerical value offsets alone, mask regeneration and broken feedback handling as explanations for this run. The exploration effect also appeared in average fingerprint distances, yet the large docking-score loss outweighed gains on three tasks. Greater policy and state diversity therefore did not deliver a higher aggregate score in this test. The molecular assessment still finds concentrated high-scoring families, reactive heteroatom motifs and demanding short bridges. The docking decline accompanies a different nitrogen, bridge and sulfur arrangement, which is an observed association rather than an identified causal structural defect. Broader fingerprint movement has not yet established broader coverage of useful, practical scaffold families. Further evidence is needed to separate the contributions of independent initialization, masked learning and persistent head identity, and to estimate score reliability across seeds. These results come from one paired screening seed; they do not establish a general score penalty or calibrated uncertainty.
finding_summary.results: The heads learned from different persistent transition subsets and kept their assigned identities through all 250 molecular editing episodes. Of 1070 exploitation decisions after learning, 710 strictly preferred an edit outside head zero’s maximizing choices; every episode offered multiple exploitation decisions under its persistent head. All 7250 head updates had nonzero parameter changes, and paired average learning residuals decreased for every task and head. Mean molecular fingerprint distance from episode starts rose from 0.443448 to 0.489426, and distance between contemporaneous lane states rose from 0.681615 to 0.733227. Later episode-best gains following losses increased from 123 to 145 events, although their mean positive increment fell from 0.015693 to 0.010788. The single-seed evaluator macro Top-1 score fell from 0.406693 to 0.350704, a change of -0.055989. Task Top-1 scores changed as follows: zaleplon_mpo 0.332184 to 0.438122 (+0.105938); deco_hop 0.614535 to 0.621204 (+0.006669); drd2_docking 0.753647 to 0.301684 (-0.451962); median_2 0.195125 to 0.184354 (-0.010772); sitagliptin_mpo 0.137973 to 0.208154 (+0.070181). All five tasks completed their 300-evaluation budgets with no invalid or duplicate proposals.

molecular.headline: Aromatic amides, heteroaryl lactones and dense bridged scaffolds coexist with peroxide chains and unusual sulfur chemistry
molecular.overall_character: The supplied seed-0 trajectories cover all five tasks, with 300 observed molecules and 290 optimizer proposals per task; there are no tasks without trajectories. These are mostly substantial, ring-rich organic graphs carrying aryl or heteroaryl groups, carbonyls, ethers, amines and halogens. The digest ring-closure rates are 0.9966 to 1.0 and aromatic-token presence is 0.9379 to 1.0. These are proportions of proposal strings containing the feature, not ring counts, aromatic atom fractions or evidence that the molecules are planar. Nonaromatic rings, bridges and saturated carbon centers are visibly present. Mean SMILES lengths range from 47.9 to 69.8 characters, a text-size indicator rather than molecular weight. The higher-scoring sets remain concentrated in a few related structural families, despite considerable peripheral and ring-connectivity variation. Ordinary medicinal chemistry is clearest in the hydroxyindole acetamide series. Elsewhere familiar lactones, diones and amines coexist with oxygen chains, oxygen-halogen bonds, unusual sulfur valence contexts, and very short bridges between separated positions on aromatic rings. Synthetic plausibility is therefore uneven and often questionable; a readable molecular graph does not establish an accessible synthesis or feasible geometry. All five charged-marker and stereocentre-marker rates are 0.0. Neutral drawings still contain ionizable groups, and several cited structures have unspecified stereogenic centers. The Parent trajectories show changes in the actual chemical families accompanying changes in observed scores, but these single-seed comparisons do not identify causal molecular features. The missing features below are inferred from the observed high/low contrasts; these data do not reveal an exact absent motif required by an objective.

per_task.generated_character: The best family is relatively compact: a hydroxyindole connected through an acetamide to a methylated aryl or azaaryl group, usually with an N-methyl amide and often an aryl halogen. The leading molecule combines a fused indole, a phenyl ring with separate fluoro and methyl substituents, a tertiary amide, phenol and pyrrolic NH; it is a conventional-looking synthetic target. Other high entries alter the amide into an unsaturated small lactam or imide-like linkage. The low end includes oxygen-rich saturated acetal frameworks and much larger diaryl ester/thioether chains. Proposal mean SMILES length is 47.9, ring-closure presence 1.0, aromatic-token presence 0.9793 and halogen presence 0.7862.
liabilities: The unsaturated four-membered lactam at evaluation 274 is much more strained and synthetically demanding than the leading acyclic amide; its score of 0.4178728841888079 does not establish practical accessibility.

Evaluation 298 contains an oxygen-chlorine bond on an aromatic oxygen and still scores 0.4163503402962837; evaluation 280 replaces a phenolic group with a hydroperoxide and scores 0.40297363075154996. These are reactive alternatives to an ordinary phenol.
Some ring-closed or branched analogues introduce unspecified stereogenic centers, although the leading acyclic amide itself has no such configurational requirement.
missing_features: The poor acetal and extended diaryl-chain products lack the compact combination of aromatic surface, intact amide linker and hydroxyindole seen in the better products; their additional functionality does not reproduce that arrangement.

The high end offers limited evidence of alternative uncomplicated scaffold/linker arrangements retaining those polar roles. Several alternatives instead introduce small strained rings, extra acylation or reactive oxygen substituents.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial methoxyindole carboxamide scores 0.3051048083696145; the hydroxyindole N-methyl aryl acetamide at evaluation 197 scores 0.438122145211641. The brominated relative at evaluation 268 scores 0.4272212457957658, while the bulky acetal at evaluation 65 scores 5.489053084697733e-11. The visible association is with a compact aryl/indole arrangement and a suitably placed carbonyl linker, rather than simply adding oxygen atoms or rings. The final fused lactam at evaluation 295 falls to 0.10121374680974261, and the final chloropyridyl amide at evaluation 300 scores 0.15456096577520334, showing sensitivity to connectivity and substitution within the general family. The Parent maximum was 0.33218372414937963 in a much more bridged, carbinolamine-containing indole family; the Child maximum is accompanied by a simpler, more conventional amide structure. This comparison does not isolate any single structural cause.

per_task.generated_character: The high-scoring family is an oxygen-substituted coumarin bearing an amino-linked pyrimidine or triazine and a further aryl ring. It is a largely aromatic, medium-to-large scaffold with a lactone carbonyl, ether substituents, ring-nitrogen acceptors and an NH linker. The top entries repeatedly terminate one aryl substituent in sulfur triple-bonded to nitrogen, an unusual sulfur group rather than a conventional carbon nitrile. Several also replace an ordinary alkoxy group with an oxygen chain or a chlorine-terminated oxygen chain. The low end contains aryl pyrazoline/thioamide-like families and extended diaryl ester chains. Mean proposal SMILES length is 57.6; ring and aromatic-token presence are both 1.0, with halogen presence 0.5897.
liabilities: Successive oxygen-oxygen bonds and chlorine-terminated oxygen chains occur among both the best and final molecules; these warrant major stability and handling concerns, rather than treatment as routine ether variations.

The aryl sulfur-nitrogen triple-bond group requires specific chemical justification. It should not be described as an ordinary nitrile or as automatically synthesizable because its valence can be represented.
Final molecules also contain oxygen-nitrogen linkers, thiocarbonyls and additional sulfur chains. The score does not consistently distinguish these from more conventional decorations.
missing_features: The lower-scoring families do not present the coumarin plus amino-azaaryl linkage seen repeatedly in the higher-scoring set.

The top set does not demonstrate a comparable range of chemically ordinary terminal polar groups: the unusual sulfur-nitrogen triple-bond motif persists across its better decorations. Stable alternative group/linker combinations preserving the favorable overall arrangement remain unshown.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The supplied diaryl-substituted dimethoxycoumarin scores 0.5418375031378128. Evaluation 193, with the amino-triazine connection and sulfur-nitrogen terminal group, scores 0.6157585507449115. transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Use chemical context when proposing changes to ethers, carbonyl groups and sulfur centers, with coherent alternatives in recognized bonding and oxidation-state contexts. Treat valence validity separately from stability and preparative plausibility. transferable_gaps.evidence: The leading multiaryl acid and fused-dione families contain very short carbon or ether bridges across separated aromatic positions. transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Offer ring and bridge changes with chemically feasible geometries, using contextual ring templates or task-independent geometric feasibility checks. Preserve access to ordinary saturated heterocycles and manageable ring-size alternatives while distinguishing them from severe short-bridge or crosslink strain. A higher ring count should not stand in for useful three-dimensional chemistry.

transferable_gaps.evidence: All five digest stereocentre-marker rates are 0.0. Cited products include benzylic amino/acid centers, substituted saturated heterocycles, acetal-bearing bridge carbons and potentially stereogenic sulfur environments, all without specified configuration. This does not imply that every molecule is chiral; the conventional leading hydroxyindole amide is a counterexample.
transferable_gaps.gap: New stereogenic connectivity is emitted without explicit configurational alternatives.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: When an edit creates or modifies a genuine stereogenic element, preserve valid existing stereochemistry and make chemically meaningful configurations accessible as explicit alternatives. Let observed task-local feedback determine their utility. The present trajectories do not establish a stereochemical score ceiling or a preferred unseen stereoisomer.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The higher-scoring excerpts recur around hydroxyindole acetamides, amino-azaaryl coumarins, halogenated multiaryl amine/acids and substituted fused diones. Many nearby products alter oxygen chains, single substituents or ring crosslinks; practical alternative core/linker arrangements retaining the useful functional roles are less evident. Different cores and saturated rings do occur, so the evidence supports concentrated high-end coverage rather than an absolute inability to leave a scaffold.
transferable_gaps.gap: Higher-scoring polar and aromatic arrangements are explored through a limited set of related scaffold families.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide coherent scaffold and linker alternatives that retain useful carbonyl, donor, acceptor and aromatic roles while changing their arrangement in manageable ways. Maintain chemically distinct alternatives using the observed scalar feedback, without prescribing a benchmark scaffold or assuming that any new core will score better.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every digest charged-marker rate is 0.0, yet the molecules include secondary and cyclic amines, azaaromatics, phenols and carboxylic acids. Several high products combine an acid with an amine in one molecule. This is a limitation of the emitted representations, not evidence that these compounds remain neutral in solution or that downstream processing ignores protonation.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ionizable structures are represented without explicit charge-state alternatives in the observed output.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Where the molecular interface permits distinct microstates, make chemically reasonable protonation and tautomer representations consistent with the generated functional groups. Avoid treating neutral SMILES as evidence of nonionizability. Any microstate exploration should be task-agnostic and evaluated rather than assumed beneficial.

nodes.method_name: MolDQN: Bellman-guided de novo graph-edit episodes
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in MolDQN's value-based control of molecular edits: learn future action returns from scored transitions and choose subsequent graph modifications with a deep Q-network. [Zhou et al., Sections 2.1, 2.2 and 2.5](https://arxiv.org/html/1810.08678v3) describe finite molecular edit episodes, fingerprint features and double Q-learning. Our adaptation starts short episodes from task-local scored molecules and samples fresh valence-aware atom and bond edits at each state. A compact Q-network takes current and successor fingerprints, remaining episode depth and the episode's best observed score. Use a single Q-function with epsilon-greedy action selection in the root. Evaluate only selected new whole molecules; values assigned to unselected successors are predictions. Advance each trajectory after its matched feedback, even when the new molecule scores worse. For Top-1 alignment, use reward max(previous_episode_best, new_score) minus previous_episode_best and undiscounted finite-horizon backups: accumulated reward equals improvement in that episode's best score. This reward adaptation is our inference, not the paper's original reward. Train immediately from accepted transition replay using double-Q target selection and a lagged target network, with zero continuation value at episode termination. Retain all accepted intermediate molecules in the task incumbent archive. Interleave episodes according to announced batches, and generate further edits to replace invalid or duplicate proposals. Each decision samples an evolving neighborhood; no corpus pool, complete-molecule retrieval or fixed candidate enumeration is involved. No pretrained generator or external labels are required, and every objective starts with clean learning state. The hypothesis is that learned lookahead identifies useful edit sequences, including temporary score losses, quickly enough to raise the mean of independent final Top-1 scores. Learning useful continuation values from scarce transitions is unproven; the paper's much larger training regime does not establish this transfer.
