molecular.headline: Conventional aromatic and cyclic-amine families, with missing stereochemistry and uneven control of size, connectivity and reactive substituents
molecular.overall_character: The supplied evidence covers seeds 1 and 2, using seed 0 of the same Algorithm Node as the baseline. All five tasks have trajectories, each containing 600 evaluated records including 580 optimizer proposals. The predominant chemistry is recognizable medicinal-chemistry material: indole carboxamides, anilino pyrimidines, aryl sulfonamides, piperazines and piperidines, fused carbonyl heterocycles and hydrazones. Related high-scoring series sit within a more diverse background. Structural diversity is moderate overall, with substantial scaffold variety on some tasks and concentration within a few favorable families on others. Ring-closure indicators span 0.9828–0.9983 and aromatic-atom indicators 0.9483–0.9966. These are fractions of SMILES containing those features, not aromatic atom fractions or measurements of three-dimensional shape. Mean SMILES lengths span 39.9–48.3, although the trajectories include much larger alkyl, peptide-like and densely fused structures. Most ordinary cores support plausible apparent makeability, but reactive variants and extreme size or polarity make overall drug-likeness moderate. Every stereocentre indicator is 0.0. This leaves configurations unspecified in substituted saturated rings, aminoaryl side chains and complex polycycles, despite those structures being represented. The output is not missing aromatic rings or basic amines as classes. Its gaps concern preserving favorable relationships between those features, controlling growth and polar-group additions, and producing defined, chemically tractable variants.

per_task.generated_character: The high group contains medium-sized ethyl/ethoxy indole carboxanilides, benzimidazole carboxamides with N-acyl saturated nitrogen rings, indole enone/sulfonamide compounds and diarylamine-linked aryl sulfonamides. These have conventional aromatic scaffolds and amide, sulfonamide, ether or trifluoromethyl substituents, with comparatively few strongly basic aliphatic centres. Mean SMILES length is 40.8, ring_closure_rate 0.9966 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.9862. The familiar building blocks make most upper examples plausible synthetic targets, while large fused or duplicated scaffolds and very long chains appear at the low end.
liabilities: The indole enone family contains a conjugated ketone electrophile with unspecified double-bond geometry. A favorable score does not establish its stability or selectivity.
Long hydrophobic chains, duplicated aromatic cores and densely fused, multiply functionalized structures create substantial size or synthetic complexity without preserving favorable scores.
missing_features: The current high group does not reproduce the favorable amide N-alkylation and aryl-linker arrangement observed in the baseline; comparable changes around the same core would be more informative than the score-tied halogen series.
Controlled addition of carbonyl or other polar groups without disrupting size and attachment patterns remains uneven, as the low-scoring dimethylcarboxamide-containing final example illustrates.
Configurations of substituted saturated nitrogen rings are unspecified, although these files do not establish stereochemical sensitivity of the objective.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The ethyl indole carboxanilide scores 0.4067656765249372 and its ethoxy relative 0.4064265251651748. The initial trimethoxy indole carboxamide scores 0.3051048083696145. The seed-0 best at 0.5280588545286916 retained the indole carboxamide but used an N-methyl benzyl-nitrile substituent instead of the current direct N-aryl attachment. This points to amide connectivity and substituent arrangement as an unresolved chemical difference; the comparison does not isolate a requirement for the nitrile. A second family of indole enone/sulfonamides has exactly the same score, 0.3949199041196016, for terminal Cl, Br or F. In the diarylamine/sulfonamide family, the compact example scores 0.3900700429110833, while adding a dimethylcarboxamide substituent in the last proposal gives 0.016846474583107045. Larger highly connected or long-chain examples fall to 6.104593358645627e-24 and 6.925504833777315e-22, but the small dichloroaminopyridine is also low at 1.496608667066175e-13. The median is 0.106506. These observations favor a bounded scaffold and polar-group arrangement rather than maximum aromaticity, minimum size or a particular terminal halogen.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-1 high family is dominated by anilino pyrimidines bearing aryl and trifluoromethyl or benzylamino substituents, attached to benzofuran, naphthalene or substituted phenyl systems. These are aromatic, nitrogen-containing screening-like frameworks with familiar amino and ether links. Seed 2 also explores aminoaryl esters, sulfonamides and more complex cyclic acetals. Mean SMILES length is 48.3, ring_closure_rate 0.9983, aromatic_atom_rate 0.9966 and halogen_rate 0.8483. The primary heteroaryl chemistry appears makeable, though extensive fluorination and linked aromatic rings give a large hydrophobic surface.
liabilities: The upper series can combine many aromatic rings and fluorinated substituents; solubility, conformational preferences and synthetic tractability are not given by the score.
A high acylhydrazone leaves hydrolytic stability and C=N geometry unresolved, and late N,O-acetal-like connections require chemical-form assessment.
Elemental fluorine is a reactive non-medicinal outlier despite its nonzero score.
missing_features: The connected anilino-azaaryl donor/acceptor arrangement is not consistently preserved when the output moves to aminoaryl esters, acetals or sulfone-containing alternatives.

Chemically comparable core and linker changes are needed to distinguish the favorable heteroaryl geometry from a general preference for highly fluorinated aromatic molecules; no unique required decoration is established.
The stereogenic aminoaryl side chains and cyclic acetals seen in the second trajectory lack configuration specification.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The fluorinated benzofuran/anilino-pyrimidine scores 0.61192894944948, and the methoxynaphthyl analogue scores 0.6067590497737556. Benzylamino-substituted relatives remain near this upper group. The seed-0 best at 0.5913471190523991 was an amino-linked quinoline-like system with a nitroaryl acylhydrazone, so the replication uses a different linker/core arrangement while retaining connected azaaryl and amino features. The initial fused-dione ester scores 0.548381482770623 and the median is 0.545366. Low examples include aromatic carbon-bonded sulfones at 0.2707003622563395 and 0.2713068181818182, plus a morpholine/imine/sulfone compound at 0.2801857585139319. Thus aromaticity, fluorination or a nitrogen ring alone does not explain the favorable anilino-azaaryl arrangement. A late sulfonamide-containing aminoaryl structure scores 0.5616122965172838, so sulfur oxidation itself is not sufficient to explain the low carbon-bonded sulfones. The isolated proposal FF scores 0.5; this is elemental fluorine, not a medicinal organic scaffold, and demonstrates that a middling numerical value cannot be read as chemical quality.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-1 high group is a coherent family of N-arylpiperazines connected by alkyl spacers to brominated indoles. Alkyl or alkoxy substitutions on the N-aryl ring and changes in spacer length occur repeatedly. These expose an aliphatic basic piperazine nitrogen in an aromatic environment. Seed 2 instead generates densely fused indole/aryl systems with tertiary cyclic or appended amines, sometimes including a ketone. Mean SMILES length is 44.0, ring_closure_rate 0.9879 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.9672. The flexible piperazine family is generally synthetically recognizable; the complex fused family entails substantially more stereochemical and synthetic complexity.
liabilities: The high-scoring bromomethyl-substituted member contains a benzyl bromide, an electrophilic alkylating handle, yet scores 0.9999999997416186. This is a concrete example of chemical reactivity not being ruled out by the objective.

Several upper examples retain long flexible chains between aromatic and amine regions, while the second trajectory creates densely fused polycycles. Both require conformational or stereochemical characterization.
Heavy aromatic bromination and extensive hydrophobic surface remain physicochemical questions, rather than established benefits of the near-ceiling score.
missing_features: The favorable exposed-amine/aromatic arrangement is already present. What is missing in the fused series is explicit stereochemical definition of its multiple saturated ring junctions and substituted carbons.

The near-ceiling family does not demonstrate which spacer or peripheral substituent gives a materially distinct chemical advantage; tractable alternatives need assessment beyond numerical closeness to the score ceiling.
No additional obligatory target interaction can be inferred from the shown molecules and scores alone.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The propyl-substituted arylpiperazine linked to a bromoindole scores 0.9999999999666845. Multiple linker, aromatic-substitution and bromine-position variants also have scores extremely close to 1. The baseline best at 0.9999917871646155 paired an indoline/aryl region with an ethyl-linked piperidine, retaining exposed aliphatic amines in a different framework. Both sets therefore support the same broad amine-plus-aromatic arrangement. By contrast, a nitroaryl acid/amide heterocycle scores 1.8588450134335675e-05, an aromatic ester/amide scores 2.8794410596630625e-05, and an acylated/sulfonylated nitrogen structure scores 3.8021829379963674e-05. A tertiary aniline-containing example is also low at 6.624810470904373e-05, showing that nitrogen presence alone is insufficient. The median is 0.707754, and late seed-2 fused amine structures remain high, including 0.9899704115532137. The chemical association is strong, but these near-ceiling scores do not determine an exact spacer length, halogen pattern, conformation or experimental affinity.

per_task.generated_character: The high group spans an indole-containing fused/bridged lactam-sulfonamide, a very simple N-methyl-N-sulfonyl piperazine, aryl sulfonamides bearing benzylpiperazines, cyclic diones and carbamate-containing heteroarenes. This is a substantial range of size and ring complexity rather than a single scaffold. Mean SMILES length is 39.9, ring_closure_rate 0.9879 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.9759. Most motifs are conventional, but the bridged high scorer and unusual sulfur or small reactive low-end fragments need more chemical scrutiny.
liabilities: The best fused/bridged scaffold requires stereochemical and synthetic-route definition, even though its component functional groups are familiar.
The low output includes a small organic azide, a highly halogenated electrophilic carbonyl fragment and an unusual nitrogen-oxide head group on a long chain.
A late piperazine carries a hydrogen-bearing sulfur oxide/hydroxy group whose chemical form is less straightforward than an ordinary sulfonamide.
missing_features: Consistent favorable placement of aromatic, carbonyl/sulfonyl and cyclic nitrogen groups remains unresolved across the many scaffolds; a simple piperazine already approaches the more elaborate upper structure.
The bridged lactam/sulfonamide high scorer has an unspecified stereogenic carbon. Configuration-sensitive alternatives are absent from the shown comparison.
The available scores do not identify a unique missing target-like ring system or justify adding rings indiscriminately.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The indole/lactam/cyclic-sulfonamide scores 0.21944544104637362, but the much simpler N-methyl-N-phenylsulfonyl piperazine already scores 0.20718664161756667. A larger aryl sulfonamide with benzylpiperazine scores 0.20289642340591482. Greater ring complexity is therefore not a general requirement. The seed-0 best at 0.20090425134085538 was an aryl/benzodioxole-substituted nitrogen heterocycle with a carbonyl, while the initial fused-dione ester scores 0.1678386594791329. The recurring favorable chemistry is an aromatic framework with a particular cyclic polar or sulfonamide/amine arrangement, not a single shared scaffold. At the low end, allyl azide scores 0.0, an N-hydroxy/trichloromethyl formamide scores 0.007693218186208301 and a small highly chlorinated enone scores 0.010594028769395466. A long fatty-acid-like nitrogen-oxide structure also scores only 0.019641313778463534. The median is 0.125545. Late charged heteroarenes and unusual sulfur-containing piperazines remain below the upper examples, showing that generic heteroatom, charge or nitrogen-ring addition is insufficient.

per_task.generated_character: The favorable structures include a compact N-rich fused bicyclic dicarbonyl heterocycle with an exocyclic imine, phenyl and benzyl groups, and dimethylaminoacetamide/furan-carboxamide-substituted anilines. Other upper examples use thiazole-fused diones, acylhydrazones and phenolic or methoxy aromatic groups. Mean SMILES length is 39.9, ring_closure_rate 0.9828 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.9483. These are mostly recognizable small-molecule functional-group combinations, but the full population also contains very large peptide-like, polyether, polyol and heavily decorated structures.
liabilities: The best imino/dione structure has tautomeric-form questions, and the hydrazones introduce hydrolytic-stability and C=N-geometry questions.

Peptide-like boronic acids, long polyethers and highly oxygenated chains depart sharply from the compact favorable molecules. These extremes add substantial polarity, flexibility or synthetic complexity.
Very large amide/aryl assemblies can retain chemically familiar fragments while losing nearly all score, so ordinary fragment identity is not evidence of a well-balanced whole molecule.
missing_features: The generator does not consistently retain a favorable balance of size, polar-group density and attachment pattern when extending the compact high-scoring cores.
Chemically defined tautomeric and double-bond forms of the imino/dione and hydrazone structures are not established by their SMILES scores.
A particular missing basic amine, fluorinated fragment or target-like connection cannot be specified from these diverse high scorers; the output already supplies multiple relevant functional classes.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The fused imino/dicarbonyl compound scores 0.3108657757276207 at the final evaluation. The para dimethylaminoacetamide/furan-carboxamide aniline scores 0.28770317918999355 and its meta positional isomer 0.28307300457324674. These close relatives show that linkage placement can be varied within a favorable compact polar/aromatic neighborhood. The seed-0 best at 0.2932061327730367 used an N-acyl sulfonamide attached to a fused azaarene, another different arrangement of moderate size and polar groups. The current best lacks an exposed aliphatic basic amine, while the dimethylamino series has one; neither basicity nor a particular fluorinated group is a universal visible requirement. At the low end, a peptide-like boronic acid scores 5.3426487496943955e-90, a large amidine/amide/aryl assembly scores 6.4760197316862265e-80, and a relatively small polyhydroxy acid scores 1.059041359266943e-68. Size alone therefore does not explain the gradient; polar-group density and topology matter as well. The reported median is 0.000002, and late hydrazone extensions remain extremely low before the final compact high scorer. A familiar ring or amide by itself is not enough.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every task reports stereocentre_rate 0.0 across 580 optimizer proposals. Digest examples include a bridged indole/lactam/sulfonamide, aminoaryl side chains, cyclic acetals and densely fused tertiary-amine polycycles with stereogenic carbons. The simpler flexible arylpiperazine high family is largely achiral, so the omission should be tied to eligible structures rather than attributed to every high scorer.
transferable_gaps.gap: Configurationally complex saturated scaffolds are emitted without explicit stereochemical specification.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Enable and preserve configurationally specified variants where stereocentres exist and evaluate them through current task-local observations. The files establish the omission but not its implementation cause or any objective-specific stereochemical sensitivity.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Mean SMILES lengths range from 39.9 to 48.3, while task maxima range from 84 to 107. Digest low examples include long hydrophobic chains, duplicated aromatic assemblies, a peptide-like boronic acid, an extended polyether and a polyhydroxy acid. A compact aryl sulfonamide scores 0.3900700429110833 while its dimethylcarboxamide-containing relative scores 0.016846474583107045; a small polyhydroxy acid also scores extremely poorly, showing that size reduction alone is insufficient.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently control appended size and polar-group density while retaining an otherwise favorable core.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support bounded changes to linker length, appendage size and polar-group count around observed useful molecules. Let local feedback select the appropriate balance; do not impose a universal preference for the smallest, least polar or least flexible compound, because favorable longer-spacer amine families are also present.

transferable_gaps.evidence: An indole enone/sulfonamide series has the same score, 0.3949199041196016, for Cl, Br and F. In contrast, the baseline indole N-methylbenzyl-nitrile amide at 0.5280588545286916 differs in attachment pattern from the current secondary arylamide family near 0.4068. Elsewhere, a simple N-methyl-N-sulfonyl piperazine at 0.20718664161756667 approaches a much more complex bridged structure at 0.21944544104637362. These examples do not support ring or heteroatom count alone as a useful chemical control.
transferable_gaps.gap: Peripheral analogue coverage is stronger than the demonstrated control of core attachment and nitrogen functional state across scaffold changes.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make controlled changes to amide N-substitution, aryl versus benzyl connection, cyclic nitrogen attachment and nearby carbonyl/sulfonyl placement available while retaining the surrounding core. Compare these chemical relationships using task-local observations rather than prescribing a particular amine state, terminal group or scaffold for all objectives.

transferable_gaps.evidence: An arylpiperazine/indole molecule containing a benzyl bromide scores 0.9999999997416186. The digest also includes elemental fluorine at 0.5, high-scoring conjugated enones or acylhydrazones, and late unusual sulfur oxide forms. These show that ordinary scaffold chemistry and a favorable numerical value can coexist with reactive or non-medicinal fragments.
transferable_gaps.gap: Numerically favorable refinement is not consistently accompanied by chemically conservative substituents and molecular forms.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Offer tractable alternatives to reactive handles and preserve coherent hydrogen, valence and charge states within related scaffold families. Treat chemical-form plausibility separately from the scalar score, while avoiding blanket removal of all electrophilic, sulfur-containing or ionizable groups.

nodes.method_name: Augmented Hill-Climb with a corpus-trained SMILES policy
nodes.method_thesis: Train a compact autoregressive SMILES prior solely on the supplied unlabeled corpus, then initialize a fresh policy from that prior for each objective. Use the initial observations and each subsequent scored batch to update only its highest-reward sequences with the Augmented Hill-Climb loss: fit policy log likelihood to frozen-prior log likelihood plus scaled observed reward. Sample complete molecules token by token from the updated policy, canonicalize them, and refill invalid or duplicate proposals by further generation. The corpus supplies language training, never a ranked molecular pool. Elite-conditioned policy updates should shift generation toward new high-scoring molecular combinations quickly enough to improve the benchmark's mean final Top-1. This is a small-budget transfer hypothesis, not a claim that published larger-budget gains carry over. The root uses the current scored batch; randomized historical replay is reserved for the first improvement. The anchor's elite augmented-likelihood mechanism is described by [Thomas et al.](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13321-022-00646-z).

approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from accepted scored molecules. It chooses parents from high-scoring population quantiles and fills a surplus pool using connected-fragment crossover or successive local mutations, with bounded retries and saturation recovery. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled. Stable canonical identities and duplicate rejection govern pool admission. A Gaussian posterior trained on the full accepted archive uses integer-count Morgan fingerprints and generalized Tanimoto similarity; correlated score draws select distinct candidates from the pool. Accepted feedback updates the archive and a bounded population of the best observed molecules.
approach.novelty: Add a narrow sulfur-environment introduction gate at final pool admission. It preserves the source experiment's neutral sulfur envelope and exact local signatures, including permitted terminal carbon-sulfur double bonds. For a one-parent proposal, outside-envelope signature counts may not exceed that parent's counts. For crossover, each signature may not exceed its largest count in either actual generating parent. Rejected products trigger the existing bounded refill loop. The new question is transfer from a single-source tabu walk to two-parent graph pools with posterior selection. Completed siblings altered crossover or posterior components; pending siblings alter donor construction or ordinary continuation. This Child retains those Parent mechanisms and tests only the sulfur admission rule.

nodes.hypothesis: Reject a final valid canonically novel offspring before pool admission exactly when an outside-envelope sulfur local signature has greater multiplicity than its maximum across the actual accepted scored generating parents, using the fixed neutral-sulfur envelope and exact signature from n-93cd9a000278, then continue the inherited bounded pool-generation loop.

finding_summary.headline: The sulfur gate contains new violations and retains the mean, but misses the performance-gain goal
finding_summary.insights: The narrow admission rule transfers from a single-source walk to scored-parent pools and can preserve the panel mean without establishing a useful endpoint gain. Its real exposure is sparse and uneven, and the Parent included one targeted introduction that improved its incumbent, so rejecting this chemistry is not synonymous with removing only unproductive paths. The exact per-signature maximum is validated separately from a parental sum; synthetic boundary cases are not search evidence. The relative rule would still allow inherited signatures within their reference counts: an inherited outside-envelope Parent offspring became the deco_hop incumbent at 0.617802. Zero absolute violations here therefore does not establish universal cleanliness. The emitted chemistry retains permitted thiocarbonyls, thioethers and oxides, but also 93 sulfur-halogen observations and unresolved non-sulfur reactivity, ring geometry and stereochemistry. Conventional thioether and sulfur-free improving alternatives constrain those concerns without proving a broader filter would help. The earlier source gate still has its favorable mean alongside a losing seed and greater dispersion; this new result neither pools nor rewrites that evidence.
finding_summary.results: The gate rejects exactly 130 of 69730 valid novel pool candidates with positive sulfur-signature excess. All 69,600 admitted members and 4,350 evaluated offspring have zero excess against their actual scored parents. Rejections affect 81 batches containing 810 real accepted evaluations; every pool and announced batch completes. 3 sessions have no positive exposure and reproduce their Parent trajectories. Absolute outside-envelope sulfur also falls from seven Parent emissions to zero Child emissions under these clean inherited states, while sulfur remains in 1100 Child observations versus 935 Parent observations. Mean endpoint score rises from 0.595670 to 0.596453, a change of only +0.000783. That meets the registered -0.002 noninferiority boundary but misses the separate +0.002 gain goal. Seed changes are +0.017686, +0.002307 and -0.017643; six task-seed endpoints improve, six decline and three tie. Macro population dispersion rises from 0.026593 to 0.033970.

molecular.headline: Sulfur stays inside the narrow envelope; aromatic leaders still carry reactive attachments and difficult ring geometry
molecular.overall_character: Node n-1744a1494180 emits compact aromatic amides and sulfur/carbonyl analogues, linked nitrogen-rich heterocycles, aryl-substituted aliphatic amines, quinoline-linked nitrogen/carbonyl rings, and fluorinated imino/carbonyl systems. There is substantial ring and aromatic chemistry, with narrower leader families within seeds. Digest ring-closure-string incidence ranges from 0.9598 to 0.9897 and aromatic-string incidence from 0.9517 to 0.9782. Those are molecule-level text incidences, not perceived ring counts or aromatic-atom fractions. Formal-charge and stereocentre-string incidences are 0.0 throughout, although aliphatic amines and potentially stereogenic centres are plainly present. All 15 Child and 15 published Parent trajectory paths were present and read, covering all five objectives and issued Search seeds 0, 1 and 2. Each node has 900 records per objective, including 870 accepted optimizer observations. No path, task or paired seed comparison is missing. context.comparison reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true with no profile mismatch; the baseline is the published current-profile n-62daf219c70a. The full records, not only the digest late seed-2 proposals, establish the seed endpoints. The entire 300-record sessions for zaleplon_mpo seed 1, deco_hop seed 0 and median_2 seed 1 reproduce Parent evaluation/source/SMILES/score/best_so_far records exactly. Other sessions diverge chemically; exact endpoint ties alone were not used to claim identity. Read-only RDKit 2023.09.6 classification using the brief's declared neutral sulfur cases finds no absolute outside-envelope sulfur centres in the initial molecules or any of the 4350 Child optimizer observations. Parent has seven such optimizer observations, all in seed 2: three terminal nitrogen-sulfur-double cases in deco_hop, two unusual sulfur-valence cases in drd2_docking, and two in median_2. This is an absolute output description, not a reconstruction of parent-relative excess, rejection decisions or mechanism activation. The declared relative rule permits inherited outside-envelope signatures within their reference multiplicities; zero observed here is conditional on these trajectories and cannot be generalized to other starting populations. Sulfur is not removed: 1100 Child optimizer observations contain sulfur versus 935 Parent observations. Child sulfur centre counts are 734 divalent/hydrogen-bearing, 11 aromatic, 299 terminal carbon-double, 71 one-oxo and 86 two-oxo. These correspond respectively to 688, 11, 291, 71 and 77 molecule observations; a molecule can contain several centres or classes. The envelope permits sulfur-halogen bonds, N-S connections and thiocarbonyl groups, and constrains no non-sulfur atom. It establishes neither universal plausibility nor stability, safety, synthesis, pharmacology or geometry. Reactive local bonding, small-ring/bridged unsaturation and unspecified stereochemistry therefore keep overall synthetic plausibility questionable and drug-likeness weak, despite recognizable high-scoring azaaryl amides and cyclic aryl amines. Molecular sizes, motif counts and path hashes are documented in .slots/r0016-03-improve-L01/molecular/trajectory_chemistry_audit.json. All quoted complete SMILES are in the Child digest or trusted Child trajectories. Parent descriptions use its published trajectories and original molecular assessment. The score gradients are descriptive associations, not sulfur-specific effects, component attribution, or scores for rejected alternatives. Recurring gaps retain provenance in n-c55c3d520a2c through n-62daf219c70a; the n-93cd9a000278 envelope is a declared source condition, not pooled efficacy evidence.

per_task.generated_character: Leaders have 24-25 heavy atoms and three perceived rings. Seed 0 favors a divinyl/methyl-substituted azaindole-like fused system with an N-hydroxy aryl amide, no sulfur and no halogens. Seed 1 reproduces the Parent indole/pyridyl N-hydroxy amide with ring N-F and aryl chlorine. Seed 2 gives an N-H indole joined through adjacent thiocarbonyl/carbonyl groups to a pyridyl ring, plus methylamino and hydroxymethyl substituents. Sulfur remains present in 251 of 870 optimizer observations, versus Parent 150, predominantly divalent/H-bearing or terminal carbon-double forms. The leading sulfur-free azaaryl amide is comparatively recognizable chemistry, whereas N-halogen, N-S and adjacent thiocarbonyl/carbonyl variants require distinct local assessments. Median heavy-atom count is Child 24 versus Parent 25.
liabilities: N-F/N-Cl/N-Br ring substitution and halomethyl ethers remain outside the sulfur constraint. The N-hydroxy amide is recognizable chemistry and must not be conflated with the separate N-halogen bond.

nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

approach.method_basis: The Parent walks from one scored current molecule by sampling local graph edits, including a direct exchange of aromatic nitrogen and carbon that preserves molecular formula. It normalizes identities, rejects duplicates and fills each batch with the first neighbors admitted by its inverse-motif memory. The highest-scoring accepted neighbor becomes current even when its score is worse, while an independent archive retains the best observations. Memory blocks only qualifying two-sign reversals from one selected transition; partial reversals can remain admissible. When accepted neighbors tie for the maximum score, canonical spelling currently decides which becomes the next source.
approach.novelty: Among equally best accepted neighbors, prefer the one that undoes the fewest motif-occurrence changes from the immediately previous selected transition, then use canonical order if that comparison also ties. This gives the most recent structural direction a chance to persist at the same accepted score. Earlier tie-selection siblings preferred fewer heavy atoms or greater distance from the current molecule. This rule instead compares the directions and magnitudes of two consecutive moves; it can prefer less structural displacement and does not reward compactness. The existing proposal generator and memory restrictions remain the Parent's.

nodes.hypothesis: Among exact accepted-score batch maxima, select the neighbor with the smallest capped inverse motif-occurrence overlap with the immediately previous selected transition, then use canonical lexical order for any remaining tie.

finding_summary.headline: Five tied choices reduced immediate motif overlap, but the predicted score gain did not appear
finding_summary.insights: This rules out failure to execute the tie rule as the explanation for the absent score gain. Reducing immediate motif-count reversal can change the search without shortening its plateaus or improving its aggregate endpoint. The five choices overlap within only two task/seed continuations, so the later deco_hop improvement cannot be credited independently to each of its four changed ties. The count statistic also has a narrower chemical meaning than preserving the last physical edit: it can penalize extending an ethyl group to propyl, or match a motif lost on one ring to a motif introduced on another. One changed choice preserves a C#S-O group by extending an unrelated N-alkyl chain, while another replaces a carbonyl carbon with sulfur. The molecular assessment finds that the altered paths retain or add questionable sulfur, oxygen-oxygen and sulfur-halogen connections, with no change to the pooled highest-scoring molecule on any task. Lower overlap therefore supplies no evidence of improved feasibility or more useful chemistry. Whether a comparison tied to actual edited sites or chemically useful arrangements would improve these choices remains open.
finding_summary.results: The rule changed five of 26 tied maximum decisions across two of fifteen task/seed sessions. Each change kept the same accepted score and reduced overlap with the previous move to zero; the corresponding lexical choices would have reversed eight motif occurrences in total. All five choices had later evaluations. Across the complete walks, inverse overlap during score plateaus fell from 26 to 14 occurrences, yet plateau transitions increased from 49 to 52. The three-seed macro mean was 0.52169764, compared with 0.52175912 for the parent: a paired change of -0.00006147, below the predeclared +0.002 improvement. The changed deco_hop continuation finished at 0.61072664 versus 0.60921826, while median_2 finished at 0.18849201 versus 0.19092251. The other thirteen full molecule/score trajectories were identical. The local mechanism is confirmed; the predicted score benefit is refuted.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic and carbonyl families repeatedly acquire unusual sulfur, reactive attachments and dense cages with unspecified stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character: Node n-1aba3c4825a4 produces medium-sized to large, heavily substituted ring systems: recognizable indole/benzofuran carboxamides, aryl ketones, fused nitrogen heterocycles, cyclic amines and lactams coexist with much less conventional sulfur-rich cages. Each supplied task digest covers 900 evaluated rows, including 870 optimizer proposals over seeds 0, 1 and 2. Ring-closure-token presence is 1.0 in every proposal set. Aromatic-token presence in the fixed task order is 0.9563, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0 and 0.7184; these are molecule-presence rates, not fractions of aromatic atoms. Every task has charged-token and stereocentre-token rates of 0.0. The neutral spelling does not imply absence of potentially basic amines. Passive RDKit reading of the full supplied trajectories confirms ring and aromatic content and graph parseability, but does not establish conformational feasibility, chemical stability or synthesis. Structural diversity is moderate: different seeds reach different ring families, while the displayed score leaders often cluster around one heavily modified framework. Direct Child/Parent comparison finds identical molecule/score records in thirteen of fifteen task/seed trajectories. The differences are confined to deco_hop seed 2 and median_2 seed 1; the highest-scoring molecule pooled over seeds remains identical to the Parent on every task. The changed trajectories introduce different chemistry without resolving the recurring liabilities. All five objectives have trajectories. Size, bond-prevalence and Parent comparisons below are passive counts from those files, recorded in .slots/SPIRAL2.r0012-09-improve-L16.molecular-audit.json. Score readings describe observed molecular associations and do not infer an unseen target structure, activity mechanism or score for an unobserved analogue.

per_task.generated_character: The optimizer proposals contain 21-29 heavy atoms and 2-6 RDKit-perceived rings. The displayed leaders are relatively compact fused heteroaromatic/phenyl carbonyl compounds. The seed-1 indole carboxamide at evaluation 61 has ethoxy, methyl and thiol substituents and scores 0.39905049777278273; its indole/anilide connectivity is comparatively recognizable synthetic chemistry. The overall leader at seed 2 evaluation 133, score 0.41003927643747895, is a benzofuran carboxamide carrying an aminophenyl group, an N-chloro amide, methyl substituents, a thiol and a carbon bearing both amino and chloro substituents. The seed-0 leader is a benzothiophene aryl ketone with an aminomethyl ether and chloromethyl group, score 0.393567030299894. Later products also include bridged unsaturated rings and substituted sulfur. All three complete molecule/score trajectories match the Parent, so these recognizable motifs and the less plausible derivatives are inherited output chemistry.
liabilities: The leading N-chloro amide and carbon bearing both amino and chloro substituents are chemically less reassuring than the ordinary anilide; thiol and chloromethyl groups also introduce reactivity concerns.

Other cited molecules contain N-F/N-O or N-N connections, and late unsaturated sulfur bridges require structural and synthetic scrutiny. These concerns do not apply indiscriminately to normal thiophene or amide functionality.
Ring-rich low scorers show that adding or distorting rings does not by itself preserve the favorable chemical arrangement.
missing_features: Consistent retention of the compact fused-aromatic/carbonyl/phenyl arrangement during scaffold changes: several lower-scoring products disrupt aromaticity or the carbonyl connection.

Broader coverage of conventional, less reactive variants of the same successful aryl-carbonyl arrangements; ordinary indole amide chemistry already appears among the leaders, but reactive N-halogen and benzylic attachments recur.
Defined stereochemical identities for the substituted saturated and bridged products. The records establish absent specification, not a demonstrated score reward for adding it.

nodes.method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
nodes.method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.

approach.method_basis: The Parent trains a recurrent prior on the original unlabeled molecular strings, samples training rows uniformly within length buckets, and keeps the checkpoint with the lowest ordinary heldout token loss. Each objective starts an adaptable copy while the prior stays fixed. Neural batches refresh a scored graph population; the first following graph batch protects a descendant of a fresh neural parent. A fingerprint posterior fit to accepted scores selects other offspring from temporary pools, and accepted graph trajectories feed trajectory-balance policy learning. This existing reciprocal search, including its posterior selection, receives the changed prior but is otherwise preserved.
approach.novelty: Give original training molecules carrying less frequent token contexts a bounded increase in sampling probability while retaining a uniform component for every row. Rarity is learned only from the unlabeled training split and is capped so isolated unusual contexts cannot dominate allocation. Unlike the earlier siblings, this intervention neither creates alternative strings nor selects checkpoints with a generative probe. It tests whether allocating more learning opportunities to underrepresented original contexts broadens usable prior support without changing online search.

nodes.hypothesis: Reallocate unlabeled prior-training rows within each inherited length bucket using an equal mixture of uniform sampling and capped inverse-document-frequency context-rarity weighting, while retaining original strings and the ordinary holdout checkpoint rule.

finding_summary.headline: Rare-context learning improved, but later validity fell and one replica ended early.
finding_summary.insights:
This establishes that extra exposure to existing rare token contexts can improve their heldout likelihood without improving average likelihood or adapted generation validity. The conditional result concerns only 306 rare-context targets across the three holdouts, about 0.052% of all heldout targets; there are no heldout contexts absent from training. It therefore supports learning of underrepresented existing syntax, while broad chemical support and unseen-context generalization remain open. Common contexts slightly deteriorated in every seed, and all update caps were reached, ruling out fewer training updates as the explanation for that tradeoff.

The molecular evidence further limits what the higher completed-replica scores mean. Conventional aromatic/amine and carbonyl families coexist with high-scoring peroxide/O–halogen variants, hydroxyallenes and strained closures; favorable scores do not show that those liabilities are necessary, since more conventional alternatives also score highly. The changed training distribution did not supply missing stereochemical examples. The early termination exposes a separate fragility in inherited graph canonicalization, whose source was unchanged; it does not invalidate the verified training allocation, but it prevents a complete reliability claim. A useful next question is how to retain the observed rare-context learning while preserving common-context performance and chemically credible generation, with the identity failure addressed as a separate online mechanism.
finding_summary.results:
Training consumed the intended redistribution in every seed: all 89,226 minibatches changed row membership, and mean capped rarity rose from 2.25875 under the paired uniform reference to 2.38357, a 5.53% increase. Rarity rose in all seven length buckets in every seed. Exposures to contexts below the training-frequency median increased about 1.86-fold. Independent evaluation of the selected checkpoints on identical holdout rows found lower rare-context token loss in all three seeds: pooled Parent loss 2.25659 fell to 1.85778. Common-context loss increased from 0.56370 to 0.56435; the recorded ordinary mean holdout loss increased slightly from 0.56458 to 0.56501. All preparations completed 29,742 steps, with mean preparation time rising from 259.5 to 368.4 seconds. Original strings, ordinary checkpoint selection and online search interfaces remained intact.

The generation outcome was less favorable. Across matched complete tasks, raw policy validity fell from 70.04% to 62.77%, although candidate-side duplicate rejection also fell. First-batch validity was 91.17% in the Parent and 89.67% in the child; later batches were substantially less valid and already reflected task feedback. The two fully completed replicas increased mean final Top-1 from 0.522200 to 0.576765, with paired gains of 0.035148 and 0.073981. Gains centered on sitagliptin and one deco-hop replica, while other task comparisons were mixed. The third zaleplon task stopped after 120 of 300 evaluations when repeated canonicalization of a ring-closure offspring alternated aromatic representations and tripped the inherited trajectory-identity check. Fourteen of fifteen tasks completed, so no complete three-seed child macro result is available.

molecular.headline: Rich ring chemistry includes hydroxyallenes, bridged amines, thionoesters, and high-scoring peroxide/O–F and strained ring variants.
molecular.overall_character: All available trajectories were read: 4,320 child rows, including 4,170 optimizer proposals, and 4,500 Parent rows, including 4,350 proposals. Coverage is incomplete for zaleplon_mpo: child seeds 0 and 1 have 300 rows each, while seed 2 ends at evaluation 120 and its supplied summary is buggy. Its molecular description therefore covers 720 rows and 690 optimizer proposals, compared with 900 and 870 in the Parent; nothing is inferred about the missing 180 evaluations. The other four tasks each supply all 900 rows and 870 proposals. Every observed child optimizer SMILES parses in the supplied RDKit environment. The repertoire is ring-rich, with aromatic and partly saturated heterocycles, aryl amines, carbonyl groups, bridged amines and sulfur-containing groups. Digest ring-closure rates are 0.9812–0.9908 and aromatic-marker rates 0.8333–0.9805; these are string-presence counters rather than atom fractions or guarantees of credible ring geometry. Read-only RDKit median heavy-atom counts are 24.5, 38, 30, 32 and 25 in the supplied task order. Conventional motifs coexist with hydroxyallenes, O–F bonds, peroxide/peroxyhalogen groups, short closures across aromatic frameworks and highly elaborated linked molecules. All digest stereocentre rates are 0.0; unassigned tetrahedral centres occur in 196 of 690 first-task proposals and 180, 608, 501 and 441 of the 870 proposals in the remaining tasks, with assigned centres in none. These output observations support mixed chemical plausibility and uneven useful-core coverage; they do not establish the cause of the incomplete execution or whether any algorithmic mechanism activated.

per_task.generated_character: This assessment covers the 720 observed rows, including only 120 rows from seed 2. Seed 0 favors a benzofuran-like aromatic core attached to pyridyl and saturated diaza-ring groups, with a hydroxyallene side chain in the leader. That molecule has 24 heavy atoms and four rings, three perceived as aromatic. Other high neighbors contain an aminocyclopentyl substituent and a carboxylic acid on a fused or rearranged ring framework. The observed seed-2 family is more conventional acetyl/dimethyl indole carboxamide chemistry with a fluorophenyl or chlorophenyl amide. Thus aromatic nitrogen, amines, carbonyls and ring diversity are present. Parent leaders included biaryl pyrazole/acetanilide and quinoline/urea structures, with an indole-amide branch as well. The child median is 24.5 heavy atoms and three rings, but its raw scaffold and feature counts cannot be treated as complete three-seed coverage because the Parent supplied more observations.
liabilities: The leader contains a hydroxyallene, and its neighbors include sulfur- or fluorine-substituted cumulenes. The digest cumulated-double-bond marker rate is 0.0594; actual persistence and reactivity of these proposed forms are unmeasured.
Some favorable acid/amine structures use a contracted four-membered ring or other rearranged fused connectivity. Parseability does not establish low strain or a practical synthesis.
The low tail includes a small cyclic peroxide and very large polyene or polar assemblies; these depart substantially from the moderate-sized high families.
missing_features: Chemically ordinary alternatives that retain the favorable aryl/amine/oxygen-ring arrangement while varying the hydroxyallene or rearranged ring geometry are not established as a coherent high-level series. The conventional indole-amide examples show that unusual cumulene chemistry is not the only productive observed family.
Explicit configurations are absent from substituted saturated-ring and fused-ring variants. No preferred stereoisomer is identified by the available rows.
Complete chemical coverage of the third replica is unavailable. Any conclusion about absent core families or final chemistry must remain limited to its first 120 evaluations.

An aminocyclopentyl/carboxylic-acid structure scores 0.43351949803907636 and a related oxygen-ring structure 0.432935295928208. per_task.generated_character: The pooled leaders are seed-1 aminoquinazoline-like structures bearing an oxygen-fluorine substituent and peroxide, peroxyhalogen or oxygen/sulfur attachments. Their aryl partner contains an extra short closure across the nominal aromatic framework; RDKit identifies two four-membered rings in the leading 23-heavy-atom molecule, alongside the two six-membered aza-aromatic rings. This is not an ordinary phenyl-substituted quinazoline despite the familiar-looking aromatic SMILES. A separate high example has a more conventional substituted aminoquinazoline/aryl-ether framework with a thiophene-linked oxime ether. Other seeds explore larger nitro-containing heteroaromatic assemblies. The child median is 38 heavy atoms and five rings, compared with 36 and four in the Parent, and 177 of 870 proposals exceed 50 heavy atoms versus 128 Parent proposals. Parent high families also combined aminoheteroaromatics and carbonyl/imine linkers, but the new leading neighborhood prominently exhibits peroxide/O–F and short-ring chemistry.
liabilities: O–O single bonds occur in 66 of 870 child proposals versus five Parent proposals; O–halogen bonds occur in 54 versus seven. Leading cited molecules directly contain O–F and O–O–halogen connections.

The high family with two four-membered rings formed by a short aromatic-framework closure has major geometric and synthetic questions. Ring-closure markers alone do not establish conventional aromatic ring systems.

The full set includes very large linked molecules, reaching 114 heavy atoms. Their extensive aromatic/heteroaromatic assembly and charged groups leave physical-property balance and synthesis unestablished.
missing_features: Matched, synthetically credible alternatives preserving the useful aza-aromatic/donor/aryl arrangement are not established for the leading peroxide/short-ring family. A different conventional high example shows that the upper score region is not restricted to that problematic connectivity.
Controlled independent changes to linker geometry, ring size and peripheral oxygen functionality are underrepresented among the near-identical leaders.

The output does not demonstrate a uniquely missing target functional group. Its visible limitation is chemically credible realization of useful arrangements, rather than a general shortage of heteroaromatics.

per_task.generated_character: The leading family contains a diaryl fused nitrogen/carbonyl framework whose dicarbonyl-ring nitrogen is connected through an N–N bond to N-methylpiperazine. Methoxy, isopropyl, aldehyde and extra ring-fusion variants decorate the aromatic portion. The leader has 37 heavy atoms and five rings, including a seven-membered carbonyl-containing ring. per_task.generated_character: Two quite different families occupy the upper digest. Seed 1 produces an N-methylaminomethyl-substituted azetidine attached through its nitrogen to a fluorinated, partly saturated fused oxygen/nitrogen heterocyclic network; the leader has 25 heavy atoms, five perceived rings and three unassigned tetrahedral centres. transferable_gaps.evidence: Cited structures near 0.8796240145542753 combine O–F, peroxide or peroxyhalogen functionality with a useful aminoaza-aromatic framework; a more conventional oxime-ether/aryl-ether example reaches 0.8713274281080406. Elsewhere, high families include hydroxyallenes, dicarbonyl N–N attachments and multiple thionoesters. C=S functionality occurs in 209 of 870 proposals in one set versus 32 Parent proposals. Favorable observations thus coexist with chemically sensitive alternatives, without establishing those alternatives as necessary.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably preserve chemically credible functional-group bonding within favorable molecular neighborhoods.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide chemically coherent functional-group alternatives that preserve useful surrounding aryl, donor, acceptor and amine relationships. Distinguish carbonyl from thionocarbonyl, ordinary ether from peroxide or O–halogen, and carbon-linked amines from N–N or N–O attachments. Use current-session accepted feedback to compare actual alternatives rather than equating parser validity or a high score with chemical persistence.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The cited aminoaza-aromatic leader contains two four-membered rings produced by a short closure across its aryl partner. Other high examples include an azetidine with a fluorinated polyheterocyclic attachment, a bridged pyrrole/tertiary-amine core and rearranged carbonyl-ring systems. Every digest gives stereocentre_rate 0.0; unassigned centres occur in 196 of 690 observed first-task proposals and 180, 608, 501 and 441 of 870 proposals in the remaining sets, with assigned centres in none.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring topology and stereochemical representation do not provide adequate control of the geometry of complex output.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support credible ring closure, expansion and contraction together with explicit configurations for existing stereogenic centres. Keep geometry, saturation and connectivity changes distinguishable so accepted feedback can evaluate defined chemical alternatives. The current absence of specification does not establish a benefit for any chosen configuration.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The cited low tails include methane, dihalogen/peroxide fragments, a cyclic peroxide and long polyene or polar assemblies. One complete set has 177 of 870 proposals above 50 heavy atoms versus 128 Parent proposals and reaches 114 heavy atoms. Yet smaller carbonyl/piperazine examples can sit near much larger relatives in another upper tail, and some larger heteroaromatics are favorable. The evidence therefore supports context-dependent useful size rather than a universal small-molecule rule.
transferable_gaps.gap: Some size-changing proposals fragment away or overbuild useful connected molecular arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Enable growth, contraction and linker changes that preserve a coherent accepted core and its useful local polar-group arrangement. Avoid relying on tiny fragments or repeated assembly of whole motifs, and let accepted observations determine the appropriate complexity for the current session.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The digest repeatedly revisits hydroxyallene/heteroaryl amines, aminoaza-aromatic peroxide/short-ring variants, bridged aryl amines, dicarbonyl/piperazine assemblies and aminomethyl or thionoester-rich heterocycles. Different seeds access different families, but much of each upper neighborhood changes peripheral atoms or ring closures. Nonchiral Murcko counts in the four fully covered child sets are 713, 523, 702 and 545; such graph counts include local edits and highly elaborated assemblies, and the partially observed first set cannot be treated as full-panel coverage.
transferable_gaps.gap: Useful core diversity remains uneven within the leading neighborhoods despite a varied overall ring repertoire.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Maintain access to multiple accepted chemical families and enable core replacements that retain useful spatial and electronic relationships among aromatic groups, amines, donors and acceptors. Assess core and functional-group diversity directly rather than relying on a new string, peripheral decoration or an additional ring closure as evidence of a useful new family.

nodes.method_name: Genetic GFN: reciprocal learning between a flow policy and graph search
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Genetic GFN: alternately generate molecules with a GFlowNet policy, refine the resulting scored population through graph crossover and mutation, and distill scored descendants back into the policy using rank-weighted off-policy replay. The policy uses trajectory balance with a learned log normalizer and regularization toward a frozen prior. [Kim et al., Section 3](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.05961v4) describe this mechanism. Train the prior only on the permitted unlabeled corpus. Each objective starts with clean policy adaptation, replay and population state initialized from its supplied observations. Use a positive terminal reward increasing with the observed maximization score. Schedule policy and genetic phases around the evaluator's announced feedback; both produce new molecules, and all reward-bearing training records come from accepted observations. Later policy samples must enter genetic populations, and accepted graph descendants must affect subsequent policy updates. Generate further valid, canonical-unique structures to fill announced batches, without corpus ranking or a fixed molecular library. The hypothesis is that learned global proposals propagate local discoveries into new promising regions and then support further graph refinement, raising the mean of five independent final Top-1 scores. Published larger-budget gains do not establish that this reciprocal learning becomes useful quickly enough here.

approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from a bounded population of accepted high-scoring molecules. It draws breeding sources from score bands, recombines connected fragments from two sources, and applies local atom, bond and ring edits. Ordinary mutation can continue for several steps, and a successful crossover can receive a finishing mutation. Stable canonical identity checks admit a fresh surplus pool. A Gaussian process trained on the complete chronological archive of accepted scores uses counts of local molecular environments and generalized Tanimoto similarity; correlated posterior draws choose the molecules that receive evaluation. Accepted offspring update both the predictor and the score-ranked breeding population. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled. Its bond-change primitive currently changes one existing bond's order; it has no coordinated, degree-preserving connectivity rearrangement.
approach.novelty: Add one optional two-single-bond rewiring move: cut two disjoint single bonds in one source and reconnect their four endpoints in a different matching, conserving the source atoms, each atom's heavy degree and bond-order sum, and the molecular formula. The move can reach a complete arrangement without requiring a valid sequence of separate one-edge changes. The first bond keeps its inherited random choice; only that selected bond gains an equally weighted choice between the old bond-order path and uniform eligible rewiring descriptors. Earlier siblings moved a pendant branch along an aromatic ring or assembled rings from two parents; neither supplied this single-source, degree-conserving neighborhood, and both lost endpoint score despite real downstream use. The ring-without-finishing combination also lost. This experiment retains ordinary continuation and the supported finishing branch. Conservation and wider connectivity are hypotheses about access, while actual accepted improvements, later use and the complete endpoint comparison determine whether that access helps.

nodes.hypothesis: Add an optional single-source two-single-bond rewiring mode inside change_bond that replaces two vertex-disjoint nonaromatic single bonds by an alternative perfect matching of their four endpoints, conserving atom attributes, per-atom heavy degree, bond-order sum and molecular formula under the fixed selected-first-bond sampling law.

finding_summary.headline: Rewiring yields clean, reused improvements but lowers the complete-panel mean by 0.03953
finding_summary.insights: Lack of valid products, failed delivery and complete absence of productive reuse are ruled out as explanations for this route’s loss. Local improvements were real, but they were insufficient: over the whole search, parent wins rose from 629 to 709 while mean offspring score fell from 0.38526 to 0.35259 and the mean best-parent reference fell from 0.47046 to 0.42528. There were more incumbent improvements, but their summed magnitudes fell from 5.80766 to 5.21465. Thus easier parent comparisons and more reuse can coexist with worse endpoints. The chemical review likewise shows that alternative ring arrangements can retain reactive bonds and unresolved geometry or stereochemistry; conservation does not establish feasible or useful chemistry. Four unevaluated pool products also changed aromatic representation after passing the registered conservation witness, so exact attribute preservation cannot be extended across every canonical reparse. The complete result supports an adverse effect of adding this fixed route in this composition, including its displaced legacy opportunities and changed adaptive history. It does not identify a chemical mediator or the value of the whole graph-search foundation.
finding_summary.results: The route executed throughout the panel: 3,141 switches were sampled, 74 failed the sanitation conservation gate, and 3,067 passed, including 2,861 immediate identity changes. It supplied 178 evaluated offspring. Of 124 clean rewrites of a scored source, 26 beat that source and 24 of those winners later bred; one unused winner still had a later opportunity, while one was born in the final batch. Across all route offspring there were 38 wins, 32 ties and 108 losses, and 126 were actually reused. Nevertheless, mean final Top-1 fell from 0.595670 to 0.556135, a complete paired loss of 0.039534 against the required gain of 0.002. All three seed averages declined; four of fifteen endpoints improved and eleven declined. The standard deviation of seed averages fell from 0.026593 to 0.020758, which does not offset the lower score.

molecular.headline: Aromatic and amine-rich molecules explore new ring arrangements while retaining reactive bonds and unresolved geometry and stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: The output contains compact fused nitrogen heterocycles, linked aza-aromatics, flexible and cyclic aryl amines, bridged nitrogen-carbonyl frameworks, and fluorinated imino/carbonyl systems. Ring and aromatic chemistry are abundant: the digest ring-closure-string incidence ranges from 0.9575 to 0.9828 and aromatic-string incidence from 0.8575 to 0.977. These are incidences of SMILES text features among molecules, not ring counts or aromatic-atom fractions. Formal-charge and stereocentre-string incidences are 0.0 on every task, despite visible protonatable amines and potentially stereogenic centres. Synthetic plausibility is questionable and drug-likeness weak overall because recognizable medicinal chemistry coexists with N-halogen/O-halogen bonds, reactive peripheral groups and difficult ring arrangements. Diversity is moderate across seeds and tasks, with narrower families among a seed's leaders; the nonaromatic medium-ring family is a counterexample to universal aromatic convergence. All 15 Child and 15 published Parent search trajectory files were read, covering 9000 records; each Child task has 900 records including 870 optimizer proposals. No paths or task comparisons are missing. The immutable context reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true, with matched seeds 0, 1 and 2 and no profile-mismatched seeds. The Parent's older same-code comparison had different profile conditions; that historical limitation does not negate the complete current pairing and supplies no component attribution. The digest final_molecules are late seed-2 proposals, not all seed incumbents. Sizes, bond environments and ring descriptions below were read from the supplied graphs with RDKit; perceived ring-basis sizes do not establish accessible conformations, stability or synthetic routes. The complete record-level audit and path hashes are in /projects/standard/adeshwal/shared/zhou2577/SPIRAL/.slots/round-0024-slot-0/molecular_trajectory_audit.json. Topology contrasts concern observed accepted outputs. Trajectories alone do not join those structures to a particular edit, distinguish clean rewrites from mixed histories, or establish physical atom conservation, activation, reuse or chemical mediation. Conserved formula and degree would not by themselves certify useful functional arrangements or remove undesirable chemistry; route-specific conservation must be established separately. The transferable gaps retain the provenance recorded by the indexed Parent report and the conditions of this new observation.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-0 leader has 25 heavy atoms: an aromatic fused framework bearing methoxy, methyl and acetyl groups, an N-brominated diarylamine, and an additional fused four-membered N-N/C=N ring. Seed 1 instead reaches a 24-heavy-atom annulated imine/indole framework with methoxy groups and carbon-bound aryl fluorine; it has no N-halogen or O-halogen bond. The 25-heavy-atom seed-2 leader retains an indole carboxamide, but connects its ring nitrogen to an N-fluoro anilino group and carries a chloromethyl ether. The Parent leaders instead comprise an indole-associated cumulene, a pyridyl N-hydroxy amide, and an indole-aryl diketone. Thus the Child changes the leading annulation and linker arrangements while remaining in compact aromatic-rich chemistry. Indole amides, ketones and aryl ethers are recognizable synthetic motifs; the additional unsaturated small ring and N-halogen attachments make the strongest examples questionable targets.
liabilities: N-Br on a diarylamine and N-F on an N-N-linked anilino group have different reactivity from ordinary aryl C-Br or C-F; the chloromethyl ether is another potentially labile environment.
The fused four-membered N-N/C=N ring raises strain and electronic-structure concerns. Annulation and aromatic notation are not evidence of isolability.
Large linked derivatives and tiny inorganic fragments are still evaluated even though their observed scores are negligible.
missing_features: The best seed-0 and seed-2 examples do not demonstrate comparably rewarded conventional nitrogen substitution while retaining their favorable aromatic/polar organization; the seed-1 leader is a real counterexample to any claim that such chemistry is wholly absent.
Accessible geometry and electronic structure of the extra fused unsaturated four-membered ring are not established by its valid SMILES.
The trajectories do not identify an exact absent target pharmacophore or a universal requirement for an amide, a particular halogen, or additional rings.

nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from accepted high-scoring molecules. A bounded population supplies score-quantile breeding parents; fresh candidates come from connected-fragment crossover or local atom and bond mutation walks, including the retained formula-preserving aromatic nitrogen-position exchange. Stable canonical identity admission builds a surplus pool. A Gaussian process trained on all earlier accepted scores uses local-environment occurrence counts and generalized Tanimoto covariance, and correlated posterior draws choose the evaluated batch. Accepted offspring update the full prediction archive and compete for survival and later breeding.
approach.novelty: Remove two-parent fragment crossover and let the existing single-parent mutation walks supply every fresh pool. This tests whether recombination still contributes after the retained nitrogen-position move and count-sensitive posterior are combined. Earlier siblings changed which partners cross or which first-parent ring cores survive a cut; both retained crossover and lost mean score. This ablation removes that route completely, preserving the current mutation operators and learned selector, to test whether a simpler composition can preserve the Parent's performance.

nodes.hypothesis: Remove two-parent connected-fragment crossover from fresh-pool production, routing every proposal through the inherited single-parent local-mutation walk while retaining the count-based posterior and correlated batch allocation.

finding_summary.headline: Crossover removal lowers mean score by 0.02886 despite more local improvements
finding_summary.insights:
The complete-loop ablation supplies evidence that crossover still contributes to this integrated method on the supplied panel. Its lower observed parent-beating rate was an inadequate argument for removal. That rate compared crossover products with the better of two parents, and both route cohorts had already been shaped by population history and posterior selection. The simpler route makes many small local advances on lower-scoring search paths; more improvements and more survivor reuse do not guarantee stronger endpoints. Removing crossover also changes the opportunities seen by the retained nitrogen move: valid exchange steps increase from 435 to 658, while accepted walks containing an exchange fall from 46 to 27. Local availability therefore does not establish useful allocation after the search distribution changes.

The coverage evidence narrows, but does not settle, the explanation. Evaluated scaffolds distinguished by atom and bond types increase from 1,806 to 1,898, while generic topologies decrease. This is consistent with more chemical variation within a narrower set of shapes. Even the number of generic cores producing incumbent gains rises, so broad exploration loss alone is insufficient to explain the lower endpoint quality. The molecular assessment shows a tighter size range, 21–44 heavy atoms instead of 1–120, alongside an increased median, 33 instead of 29. N–halogen structures and unspecified stereochemistry become more frequent, and bridged or strained heterocyclic families remain. Compactness has not supplied chemical control. Which recombination opportunities preserve productive scaffold relationships, and how their changed populations interact with posterior allocation, remain open. The result does not show that crossover is useful in every generator or that any individual omitted recombinant would have scored well.
finding_summary.results:
Crossover is absent from all 73,389 eligible breeding attempts, all 69,600 pooled candidates and all 4,350 evaluated offspring. All 15 task-and-seed evaluations complete, and the inherited mutation operators, nitrogen-position exchange, accepted-score archive and correlated posterior selector remain active. The three-seed mean final score falls from 0.57434 to 0.54548, a loss of 0.02886 against the registered 0.002 non-inferiority threshold. Every seed mean declines: by 0.06136, 0.00445 and 0.02078. Mean task scores fall by 0.11996 for sitagliptin, 0.01804 for DRD2 and 0.01126 for decoration hopping; they rise by 0.00327 for median similarity and 0.00167 for zaleplon. Seed dispersion increases for every task.

Mutation-only search makes more strict improvements over its generating parent: 713 versus 624 among 4,350 offspring. It also records 286 versus 241 incumbent improvements and reuses 2,606 versus 2,455 nonterminal offspring as later parents. Yet mean absolute offspring score falls from 0.38664 to 0.34884. Generic scaffold coverage contracts from 13,420 to 9,655 in the pools and from 1,059 to 984 among evaluated molecules. Pools need fewer attempts, and internal invalid graphs fall from 536 to two, but there is no isolated generation-speed measurement: the large total runtime reduction comes mainly from recorded oracle time.
