molecular.headline: Ring-rich heteroaromatics and cyclic amines have a tighter size range, but unusual bonding and unspecified stereochemistry persist.
molecular.overall_character: The complete seed panel was read for n-1faebb978a01 and Parent n-559d25e9c9c7: all five tasks, seeds 0, 1 and 2, with 900 trajectory entries and 870 optimizer proposals per task. No tasks lack trajectories. The Child produces connected, branched molecules with substantial ring chemistry, rather than isolated small fragments. Every task has digest ring_closure_rate 1.0; aromatic_atom_rate ranges from 0.8943 to 1.0. These text counters indicate presence, not chemically achievable ring geometry. Passive RDKit 2023.09.6 inspection finds 21–44 heavy atoms per Child proposal, median 33, versus Parent 1–120, median 29; mean sizes are 31.7763 and 32.9570 respectively. The Child removes size extremes while retaining sizable molecules. Its 984 generic Murcko cores versus Parent 1059 show real topological exploration, but upper-score cohorts repeatedly concentrate on closely related families. All 4350 Child proposals parse as single connected structures with zero formal charge. Potentially protonatable amines are nevertheless present. The main quality deficit is chemical control: 887/4350 Child proposals contain an N–halogen bond, compared with 745/4350 Parent proposals. Oxygen–oxygen bonds decline from 236 to 38, so the liability mix changes rather than disappearing. Potential unassigned tetrahedral centres occur in 2818/4350 Child and 2284/4350 Parent proposals; neither panel contains an assigned centre. Conventional aryl ketones, ethers, amides, imides and cyclic amines coexist with N-fluoro/N-bromo groups, sulfenamides, unusual sulfur valences, strained rings and crowded heteroatom chains. This supports questionable synthetic plausibility and weak overall medicinal-chemistry quality, despite recognizable useful fragments. All scores below are supplied observations, rounded where stated. A score association identifies a local chemical trend; it cannot establish the desirability of an unseen pharmacophore. The passive audit, input hashes, descriptor definitions and digest-only structure drawing are in .slots/SPIRAL2.r0013-03-improve-L01.molecular-audit.json, the adjacent .py and .png. SMARTS bond counts are structural flags, not measured reactivity or synthetic success.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 proposals are compact, 21–28 heavy atoms with median 25, and overwhelmingly retain an indole-like fused aromatic unit plus another aromatic partner. The digest has ring and aromatic presence rates 1.0. Seed 0 emphasizes N-halogenated aryl amides/amidines and N–O or N–S substitution on the fused ring; its cited seed 0/evaluation 257 molecule has a methoxy group, fluoromethyl substituent, aniline and N-bromoamide. Seed 1 reaches a methoxy/methyl indole–pyridyl ketone carrying an allenylamino substituent. Seed 2 reaches a related pyridyl ketone with an annulated N,O-acetal ring and ethyl substituent. The latter contains 23 heavy atoms and three aromatic rings plus the acetal ring, so ordinary compact heteroaryl chemistry is accessible. The allenyl and N-halogenated families are less straightforward synthetic endpoints than that ring/ketone framework.
liabilities: N–halogen bonds occur in 201/870 proposals. The cited N-bromoamide and ring N–S attachment warrant chemical scrutiny; acceptance of their SMILES is not evidence of storage stability or an available synthesis.

The allene in the highest supplied molecule is a concrete cumulated-bond liability to examine. The digest cumulated_double_bond_rate is 0.0609; aromatic bridges and ring-opened polyenes also occur among low-score structures.
Local scaffold concentration is strong: all 30 highest supplied scores within seed 0 share one generic Murcko core. Diverse text substitutions can therefore leave the core chemistry almost unchanged.
missing_features: The favorable intact pyridyl-ketone and compact heteroaromatic arrangement is not consistently represented across seed families; one upper-score family instead relies on N-halogenated amides and another on an allenylamine. A stable, varied set preserving the favorable ring and heteroatom arrangement is missing from these upper examples.

The panel gives no basis for declaring a particular unseen target scaffold or nitrile mandatory. The supported deficit is control of aromatic connectivity and substituent placement while changing functional groups.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxy indole carboxanilide at seed 0/evaluation 9 scores 0.305105. Upper digest molecules favor a less oxygenated, intact aromatic framework: the allenylamino pyridyl ketone scores 0.457265 and the annulated pyridyl ketone 0.456219. Moving the pyridine nitrogen within the latter family gives 0.456219 at evaluations 242 and 263, versus 0.444908 at 256. Ring disruption, extended imine/polyene substitution or abnormal aromatic bridges occur among the lower examples: seed 1/evaluation 47 scores 0.034295, seed 1/evaluation 189 0.024368, and the highly cyclized seed 2/evaluation 31 0.079887. More rings or nitrogen alone therefore do not describe the gradient. Even within the late annulated series, replacing ethyl with methoxy gives 0.262943 at evaluation 299 and an isopropyl analogue gives 0.356118 at 300. Child seed maxima, in seed order, are 0.439907/0.457265/0.456219 versus Parent 0.457660/0.442313/0.448414. The Parent also centers on compact substituted indole-like amides; the Child has additional ketone/acetal chemistry, not a universal change of molecular class.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 proposals span 22–42 heavy atoms, median 35; all have ring and aromatic text features. The upper molecules are nitrogen-rich, highly substituted heteroaromatic assemblies. Seed 0/evaluation 296 has 37 heavy atoms, seven nitrogens, imine/amidine-like links, a tertiary amide and chlorinated carbon substituents. Its ostensibly aromatic bicyclic unit has a bridged topology; RDKit aromaticity does not establish that this geometry is realistic. Seed 2/evaluation 287 has 38 heavy atoms and nine nitrogens, combining pyrazole, triazine and a fused heteroaryl lactone with an N-fluorohydrazine chain and S–Cl group. The complete seed 1 trajectory, whose incumbent is absent from the bounded digest, instead ends in a substituted fused dione/heteroaryl family with an N-bromo side chain; its evaluation 291 incumbent additionally contains an oxygen–oxygen–fluorine chain. These are chemically elaborate, often reactive graphs, with recognizable heteroaromatic fragments embedded in questionable whole molecules.
liabilities: N–halogen bonds occur in 404/870 proposals and S–halogen bonds in 26/870. Seed 2/evaluation 287 explicitly combines N–F, N–N, chloromethyl and S–Cl features in one molecule.

The aromatic bridge in seed 0/evaluation 296 and the cumulated ring double bonds in seed 1/evaluation 20 are distinct geometric concerns; a high ring counter is not proof of a conventional aromatic scaffold.

High-scoring seed 2 molecules carry many acceptor sites but no hydrogen-bond donor in the cited fluorohydrazine family. Dense polar functionality and multiple reactive handles make apparent synthetic plausibility questionable; the supplied scores do not measure those liabilities.
Potential tetrahedral stereocentres are unassigned in 362/870 proposals; the entire digest has stereocentre_rate 0.0.
missing_features: A varied set of stable linkages presenting the favorable nitrogen-rich aromatic environments is missing from the upper digest: imines, N-halogenated hydrazines and chlorosulfur substituents dominate those alternatives.

Nitrile-bearing heteroaromatics occur prominently in a higher-scoring Parent seed family but scarcely in the Child: only 4/870 Child proposals have a nitrile. That marks an underexplored chemical family, not evidence that adding a nitrile itself increases this objective.
The cited bridged aromatic core lacks demonstrated realizable geometry. The molecules provide no route or conformational evidence supporting that particular aromatic assignment.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The supplied initial fused dione at seed 0/evaluation 7 scores 0.548381. Lower optimizer examples include the chromone/polyene/cyclopentadiene-nitrile structure at seed 2/evaluation 11, 0.515327, and a distorted nitrogen-rich polycycle at evaluation 59, 0.517390. Across all three seeds, the higher-score cohorts contain larger and more nitrogen-rich structures than the lower cohorts, but the examples do not isolate one beneficial heterocycle. Seed 0/evaluations 296 and 282 reach 0.614194 and 0.614070 despite the strained aromatic topology. The seed 2 N-fluorohydrazine/triazine family reaches 0.611063; several methylation, halogen and lactone-ring variants tie at 0.609062, while a rearranged, less aromatic triazine-derived ring at evaluation 298 falls to 0.584198. Thus the score tolerates substantial peripheral reactivity. Child maxima are 0.614194/0.587219/0.611063 versus Parent 0.609280/0.619982/0.616992. Parent seed 0 contains very large repeated aromatic assemblies, whereas Parent seeds 1 and 2 include nitrile-bearing heteroaryl and aminoether/heteroaryl families. The Child narrows size markedly without resolving the reactive chemistry.

per_task.generated_character: These 870 molecules have 25–44 heavy atoms, median 36. Rings are universal and aromatic and halogen text-presence rates are both 0.9977. The upper family in seed 1 is recognizably amine-centered: an azetidine or pyrrolidine, an aminoethyl branch, a fluorinated arylalkyl segment and a chloropyridyl terminus connected through sulfenamide, aminoxy or aminoether links. The highest digest molecule, seed 1/evaluation 287, has 31 heavy atoms, a pyrrolidine and two aromatic rings. Seed 0 instead develops fused sulfur-containing cyclic amines with exocyclic amino groups; seed 2 develops bridged amines with thioether and unusual tetravalent sulfur representations. Cyclic amines and arylalkyl substituents look like ordinary medicinal-chemistry building blocks, but the accessory bonding and undefined three-dimensional arrangements make whole-molecule plausibility uneven.
liabilities: Upper molecules include sulfenamides and aminoxy bonds; sulfur-containing final seed 2 molecules additionally show nonstandard tetravalent sulfur written with a carbon–sulfur double bond and two carbon substituents. These need chemical interpretation beyond valence sanitization.

The highest digest molecule has three potential unassigned tetrahedral centres; the fused seed 0/evaluation 300 structure has five. Arbitrarily unspecified stereoisomers are a substantive identity and geometry gap here.

Halogenation is almost universal, and some fluorine atoms sit on saturated linker carbons. Higher score does not itself establish chemical stability, favorable physical properties or a realizable synthesis.
missing_features: The useful amine centres are already present. What is absent is assigned stereochemistry and a controlled spatial presentation of these centres relative to the aromatic groups: every one of the 870 proposals has at least one potential unassigned tetrahedral centre.

Clean alternative connections between the amine and aromatic fragments are only sparsely represented among the upper digest. The tied N–S and N–O examples, and the nearby aminoether example, do not establish a need for the reactive N–S connection.

The strings contain no formal charge assignments despite potentially protonatable amines. They do not resolve protonation or tautomeric alternatives, and the observed scores cannot identify an unshown preferred state.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The strong observable trend is loss of the initial bulky acid/amide/sulfonamide architecture and acquisition of non-amide cyclic and side-chain amines. The 39-heavy-atom acid/amide analogue at seed 1/evaluation 12 scores 0.008243; the polyoxygenated cage at seed 2/evaluation 20 scores 0.011637. In contrast the 31-heavy-atom pyrrolidine/polyamine at seed 1/evaluation 287 scores 0.994023. Its azetidine analogue scores 0.988534 at evaluation 233, and the corresponding N–O-linked variant also scores 0.988534 at 242. An aminoether variant reaches 0.982352 at 277. Across all seeds the 30 upper-score structures retain a saturated non-amide amine according to the conservative structural query and contain no carboxylic acid; the lower cohorts commonly retain acids and carbonyl-rich links. This supports accessible amine/aryl geometry and reduced acid/carbonyl burden as local associations, not a required sulfur bond. Child maxima are 0.982195/0.994023/0.953346 versus Parent 0.995949/0.996455/0.991289. Both panels reach amine/aryl-rich chemistry, while the Child seed 2 endpoint remains concentrated on a distinct bridged sulfur family.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 proposals are relatively large but size-concentrated, at 29–39 heavy atoms with median 35. Ring text-presence is 1.0 and aromatic presence 0.9989, whereas halogen presence is only 0.1379. Seed 0 upper molecules attach a propyl/ethoxy-substituted phenyl and an indole/indazole-like unit to a nitrogen-containing medium ring with imide carbonyls and methylated amines. Seed 0/evaluation 286 has 36 heavy atoms and a 10-member ring; nearby digest examples have 9-member rings. Seed 1 combines an extended fused aromatic/ether framework with an 11-member nitrogen-rich carbonyl ring. Seed 2 ends in more extensively fused aromatic lactam/urea-like assemblies, exemplified by the six-ring structure at evaluation 297. Medium-ring lactams/imides are plausible chemical classes, but these particular crowded, hydrazine-bearing or N–O-substituted ring systems have no demonstrated synthesis.
liabilities: Unusual single N–N and N–O bonds occur in 309/870 and 143/870 proposals respectively. The seed 0 incumbent has an N-amino substituent, and the seed 1 incumbent combines neighboring nitrogens with an N-methoxy group.

A ring of at least nine atoms occurs in 384/870 proposals. These rings are not automatically unsynthesizable, but their conformational and cyclization demands are real; apparent makeability cannot be inferred from ring closure syntax.
Potential tetrahedral centres are unassigned in 699/870 proposals. Low-score polyenes add further unresolved alkene geometry and less controlled conformational freedom.
missing_features: The upper molecules lack a well-separated set of conventional cyclic amine–carbonyl architectures that keeps the favorable aromatic/alkyl/ether arrangement while avoiding hydrazine or N–O additions. The high-scoring simpler ring at seed 0/evaluation 288 demonstrates some access, but most cited upper variants revisit the same medium-ring family.

Assigned stereochemistry and justified medium-ring conformations are absent. The supplied scalar scores do not reveal a missing named target scaffold or uniquely preferred side group; several chemically different substituents tie.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The supplied initial aryl fused dione at seed 0/evaluation 7 scores 0.167839. Lower optimizer examples such as seed 1/evaluation 27, 0.127558, and seed 0/evaluation 12, 0.138853, carry extended unsaturated chains attached to the retained dione/heteroaryl skeleton. Higher molecules combine alkyl/ether-substituted aromatics with reorganized cyclic amine–carbonyl connectivity: seed 0/evaluation 286 scores 0.245134 and its shorter-ring neighbour at 291 0.244694. A related ring without the terminal N-amino group reaches 0.243262 at 288, so that reactive appendage is not necessary to reach the same neighborhood. The 30 highest supplied scores within each of seeds 0 and 1 all have a ring of at least nine atoms, whereas only one of each corresponding lower cohort does. This is an observed association with a cyclic polar framework, not evidence that enlarging any ring helps. Thiol-, amino- and methyl-substituted variants at seed 0/evaluations 242, 248 and 252 all score 0.239636. Child maxima are 0.245134/0.240689/0.220274 versus Parent 0.222706/0.243215/0.230352. Both retain aryl/ether/alkyl plus cyclic carbonyl motifs; the Child explores more nitrogen-rich medium rings without a consistent per-seed endpoint shift.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 proposals span only 25–32 heavy atoms, median 29, with universal rings, aromatic text-presence 0.8943 and halogen presence 0.8678. The seeds reach visibly different chemotypes. Seed 0 produces fluorinated phenolic/aldehydic aryl groups attached to a fused or bridged cyclic imide cage. Seed 1 upper examples have an N-linked urea/formamide unit, a pyrazole, a fluorocyclopropene and an unsaturated four-member lactone. Seed 2 concentrates on an imino pyrrolopyrimidinone-like core carrying N–F, a fluorinated sulfur ring and a bridged sulfur-containing lactone. Its cited evaluation 225 molecule has 29 heavy atoms, five rings, three fluorines and two sulfurs. These are compact, heteroatom-rich ring systems, but the N-halogen chemistry, strained rings and unassigned stereochemistry make synthetic plausibility questionable.
liabilities: N–halogen bonds occur in 248/870 proposals. The highest digest molecule contains an N–F bond adjacent to imino/carbonyl functionality, in addition to the carbon-bound fluorines.

Seed 1/evaluation 280 combines a cyclopropene with an unsaturated four-member lactone. Seed 2 adds bridged lactones and reduced sulfur rings; evaluation 300 further adds an S–S chain and scores only 0.115908.
Potential tetrahedral centres are unassigned in 768/870 proposals. Ordinary aromatic-ring and atom-count summaries substantially understate this family’s geometric and stereochemical complexity.
missing_features: The observed favorable fluorine and imino/carbonyl arrangement is not reproduced across a broad set of stable, ordinary ring systems. Upper examples depend either on N-halogenated sulfur/lactone polycycles or on a cyclopropene and a strained four-member lactone.

Defined stereochemical versions of the bridged and fluorinated ring systems are absent. The seed 2 highest molecule has five potential unassigned tetrahedral centres, so its apparent compactness does not specify one realizable three-dimensional molecule.
These trajectories do not identify an absent named pharmacophore as necessary. They show that preserving useful fluorine placement while changing the surrounding skeleton remains poorly covered.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl fused dione at seed 0/evaluation 7 scores 0.002094. The unfluorinated aryl/dione/lactone structure at seed 2/evaluation 23 scores 5.789136455227341e-13. Higher families redistribute the aromatic framework and concentrate fluorine while retaining carbonyl and nitrogen functionality. The seed 2 saturated fluorinated sulfur-ring analogue at evaluation 225 scores 0.544777, compared with 0.508038 for the related unsaturated ring at 203. Replacing that carbon-bound fluorine by chlorine in evaluation 296 gives 0.364462, showing that halogen count alone is insufficient. Replacing N–F by N-fluoromethyl gives 0.480746 at evaluation 247, while an N-bromomethyl variant scores 0.168520 at 299. The imino-to-oxo analogue with fluoromethyl scores 0.476491 at 252. These examples support a narrow local fluorine/heteroatom-placement gradient, while the reactive N–F bond itself is not proof of good chemistry. Seed 1/evaluation 280 reaches 0.487517 with a different, sulfur-free but strained ring arrangement. Child maxima are 0.348389/0.487517/0.544777 versus Parent 0.651021/0.487006/0.602525. The Parent upper molecules are mainly aryl-substituted N-fluoro imino heterocycles with fluorinated carbon side chains; the Child adds substantially more bridged sulfur/lactone chemistry in seed 2. That chemical change is descriptive, without assigning the score differences to one feature.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The complete Child panel contains 887/4350 N–halogen structures. Digest upper-score examples include an N-bromoamide, an N-fluorohydrazine with an S–Cl substituent, sulfenamide-linked cyclic amines and an N-fluoro imino heterocycle. Nearby upper-score aminoether and less decorated cyclic-carbonyl examples show that some more ordinary connections are accessible. Bond flags identify chemical patterns rather than measured instability.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably keep favorable ring and heteroatom environments while supplying conventional, stable peripheral bonds.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide chemically conventional alternatives for the same attachment environments, with explicit bond-context handling around nitrogen, oxygen, sulfur and halogens. Preserve useful ring connectivity and let observed feedback compare those alternatives. RDKit-valid valence and a high supplied score alone do not supply a chemical-plausibility constraint.

transferable_gaps.evidence: All task digests have stereocentre_rate 0.0. Passive inspection finds potential unassigned tetrahedral centres in 2818/4350 Child proposals, including three in the highest-scoring cyclic-amine digest example and five in the bridged fluorinated sulfur/lactone example. Formally aromatic bridged subgraphs and strained small rings add geometry concerns that a ring-closure counter cannot express.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not produce stereochemically resolved versions of its saturated and bridged ring systems.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make stereochemical identity an explicit, graph-derived part of generating and comparing candidates where stereocentres exist, and preserve it through subsequent edits. Treat ring size, bridgehead unsaturation and feasible geometry as structural properties to examine independently of task identity; the present trajectories do not supply preferred configurations.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The Child has 984 generic Murcko cores across 4350 proposals, yet some per-seed upper cohorts collapse to one generic core for all 30 molecules. The digest repeatedly shows halogen, imino/oxo, ring-size or terminal-substituent variants at identical or very close supplied scores. Its overall size range is 21–44 heavy atoms versus Parent 1–120; the tighter range coexists with narrow upper families rather than demonstrating broader useful chemistry.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator explores many topologies but does not consistently maintain several chemically distinct alternatives within its favorable score regions.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Seek alternative connected scaffolds and attachment arrangements that retain locally favorable functional-group relationships, and track their coverage separately from distinct SMILES. Maintain multiple chemistry families using accepted feedback, while avoiding a diversity objective that is satisfied merely by ring damage, reactive substitutions or extreme molecular size.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Only 5/4350 Child proposals contain a nitrile versus 261/4350 Parent proposals, while N–halogen bonds occur in 887/4350 Child proposals. The visible upper-score families repeatedly place nitrogen in crowded imino, hydrazine or N-halogen environments. This is an observed coverage imbalance; it does not establish that a nitrile or any one replacement is universally beneficial.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator represents stable heteroatom-bearing functional-group families very unevenly.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Broaden task-independent access to stable nitrogen and other heteroatom environments at existing attachment sites, including underrepresented functional-group families, and let the same accepted-score feedback determine their usefulness. Match ring placement and size where possible so that functional-group variation is interpretable without a hidden objective template.

nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

retained_mechanisms: Task-local population of previously accepted scored molecular graphs, sampled through the inherited three score-ranked parent quantiles.

Single-parent atom/bond mutation with unchanged operator weights, bounded inner retries and one/two/three-step walks; saturation-driven longer walks and exhaustion limits remain present but unexercised.
Formula-preserving C/N positional exchange within the same eligible six-member aromatic ring, retaining per-site choice, invariant gates and actual mutation-sequence receipts.
Connected graph sanitization, stable canonical/isomeric admission with graph-equivalent alias verification, initial/emitted/pending/pool novelty exclusions and bounded fresh-pool construction.
Bounded greedy score-ranked survival with admission-order tie breaking and subsequent breeding from accepted descendants.
Full accepted-only task-local Gaussian-process archive, ordered admission history, archive-mean centering, population-SD scaling with floor and fixed observation noise.
Integer-count Morgan environments in the inherited hashed radius-two vocabulary, squared-norm generalized Tanimoto covariance and shared pool/next-fit conditional prediction.
Joint correlated posterior draws over each fresh pool, masked batch maximization, accepted-feedback refitting and next-fit probes; bounded numerical fallback remains present but unexercised.
Disabled connected-fragment crossover, partner selection within that route and optional post-crossover mutation remain as unreachable source code; none executes in this panel.

approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs using only accepted scores from the current task. It keeps the best 64 accepted molecules, ordered by score with earlier serials breaking exact ties, and draws breeding parents from the preferred upper half through three weighted score bands. Connected-fragment crossover and bounded chains of atom and bond edits generate a fresh pool. A Gaussian-process model using count fingerprints learns from the complete accepted archive, including discarded survivors, and selects the requested batch through correlated posterior score samples. Canonical identity checks and duplicate rejection connect accepted feedback back to the population. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchanges remain disabled.
approach.novelty: Remove only the survivor-capacity truncation: retain every usable accepted molecule in the same score order, then let the original weighted score bands operate on that larger population. This isolates the total contribution of the cap under its existing consumer, including the resulting changes in support and probabilities. Earlier siblings changed recency priority, core competition, recursive breeding, uniform parent allocation, or a recency/uniform combination; none tested this capacity-only removal. We will trace records that the old cap would discard through eligibility, actual breeding and accepted descendants before interpreting the matched endpoint contrast.

nodes.hypothesis: Remove only live accepted-population capacity truncation, retaining every usable canonical unique finite-scored accepted record in inherited descending score and ascending serial order for the unchanged score-quantile breeder.

finding_summary.headline: The survivor cap contributed: its removal broadened actual breeding but lowered mean endpoint score by 0.023495
finding_summary.insights:
This answers the narrow capacity question: bounded live membership adds conditional endpoint value when the original weighted score bands, recursive breeding and full-archive predictor remain active. Retained lower-ranked molecules really reached breeding and accepted reuse, so their failure to improve the aggregate cannot be explained by storage without access. The higher parent-win count is not evidence of better search: it accompanies weaker parent references, lower absolute offspring scores and fewer incumbent gains. Evictee-derived products were not uniformly useless—one became its session’s final leader and three improved an incumbent—but those local successes did not offset the total loss.

The audit also identifies the access boundary: merely exceeding 64 live records was insufficient; the original upper-half sampler first exposed discarded ranks when the archive reached 130. This separates the evictee route from earlier probability shifts among shared records. Their individual causal contributions remain unresolved. The frozen molecular assessment found mixed chemistry, with fewer direct nitrogen-halogen bonds but more oxygen-halogen and peroxide bonds, and persistent ring-geometry and stereochemical gaps. Broader breeding therefore did not demonstrate consistently more credible chemistry, nor does that association explain the endpoint loss causally. Whole-loop contribution, chemical mediation, transfer beyond this three-seed profile and any additive relationship to earlier controls remain open; the exact capacity control is answered without a cap sweep.
finding_summary.results:
The removal ran as intended in all fifteen task/seed sessions. Every accepted molecule stayed live, and 1,632 records that the old cap would discard were actually used in 5,005 parent draws. They produced 120 accepted direct offspring; 56 of those later bred and 20 produced another 47 accepted descendants. Eligibility did not guarantee delivery: 289 supported records were never drawn while beyond the old cap, and many batches drew them without accepting an offspring. Probability changes among records already inside the capped population also had substantial exposure, so this is the total capacity effect under the inherited sampler.

Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.595670 to 0.572175, a paired change of -0.023495, beyond the registered 0.002 descriptive scale. All three seed macros declined; twelve of fifteen task/seed endpoints declined and three improved. Seed population SD fell from 0.026593 to 0.011713, which does not itself establish reliability. Across accepted proposals, mean absolute score fell from 0.385256 to 0.370365 and the mean best-parent reference fell from 0.470456 to 0.449157. Strict parent wins rose from 629 to 773, while incumbent improvements fell from 258 to 229. All formal sessions completed their full oracle budget.

molecular.headline: Aromatic amides, heterocycles and aryl amines remain rich, but reactive heteroatom bonds, difficult rings and unspecified stereochemistry persist
molecular.overall_character: The full Child n-1fdd6af786dc and published Parent n-62daf219c70a Search trajectories were read for every supplied task and seed. All 30 paths exist and contain 300 sequential records, comprising 10 initial and 290 accepted optimizer molecules per task/seed: 4,500 records and 4,350 accepted optimizer proposals per node. All accepted identities are unique within their session, all records parse with RDKit 2023.09.6, and the summaries report no invalid or duplicate emitted attempts. Each initial best, final best, accepted count and terminal best_so_far reconciles with its summary. Regeneration reproduces the immutable Child molecular_digest exactly, including its string counters and excerpts. context.comparison reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true with matched seeds 0,1,2 and no profile mismatch. There are no missing trajectory paths, omitted objectives, or absent Child/Parent task/seed chemistry comparisons. These observations describe accepted outputs; unselected fresh-pool proposals and their unobserved rewards are not part of this chemical denominator. The digest final_molecules are the last proposals in its concatenated seed-2 stream, not each seed's best molecule; all per-seed leaders and late streams were inspected separately. Initial molecules are identified as supplied initial observations, not credited as new output. The output contains indole carboxamides, linked carbonyl/thione heteroaromatics, aryl- and cyclic-amine frameworks, quinoline-linked nitrogen/carbonyl rings, and fluorinated imino/carbonyl heterocycles. The Child has perceived rings in 4,211/4,350 accepted proposals and aromatic atoms in 4,183/4,350. The digest ring-closure incidences range from 0.9529 to 0.9862 and aromatic-string incidences from 0.9437 to 0.9793; these are molecule-level text incidences, not ring counts or aromatic-atom fractions. Ring and aromatic chemistry are rich. Recognizable medicinal-chemistry fragments coexist with direct N-halogen bonds in 775/4,350 proposals, O-halogen bonds in 557/4,350 and O-O bonds in 431/4,350, versus 1,042, 278 and 273 in the equally sized Parent output. These overlapping counts do not define a validated synthetic-feasibility score. N-halogen incidence falls while O-halogen and peroxide incidence rise; this is a mixed chemical difference. Conventional carbon-bound halogens and useful nonamide amines are clearly present. RDKit identifies unassigned tetrahedral centres in 2,098/4,350 Child molecules, versus 2,408/4,350 Parent molecules; no Child molecule has a specified tetrahedral centre or a formally charged atom. Neutral representation does not mean absence of protonatable nitrogen, and no pKa, stereoisomer activity, conformer, synthesis route or stability measurement is supplied. Synthetic plausibility is therefore questionable and drug-likeness weak overall, despite more plausible individual members. Structural diversity is moderate: many typed and generic graph cores occur, but leading chemistry often stays within related seed-specific families. Typed Murcko cores preserve atom and bond types; generic cores replace atoms by carbon and bonds by single bonds, retaining the extracted graph topology. Their counts neither certify independent pharmacophores nor measure synthetic accessibility. In fixed task order, exact containment of any nonempty initial typed core occurs in 263,5,15,22,18 of 870 Child proposals, while generic-core containment occurs in 533,221,200,163,85. These are subgraph tests, not founder reachability, mapped atom retention or the number of atoms physically conserved through an edit history. Actual atom conservation and multigeneration ancestry are not established by these unmapped trajectory records; they are deliberately not inferred from core overlap. Likewise, chemistry/score associations here do not identify activation, causal chemical mediation or the contribution of the changed population interface. Descriptor definitions, complete row-level measurements, chronological batch summaries, both nodes' per-seed extremes and trajectory/summary SHA256 values are in /projects/standard/adeshwal/shared/zhou2577/SPIRAL/.slots/L01-resume-20260928/r22-slot2-molecular/audit.json and /projects/standard/adeshwal/shared/zhou2577/SPIRAL/.slots/L01-resume-20260928/r22-slot2-molecular/measured_rows.jsonl. Every cited_smiles entry is an exact Child string from its named task in the immutable request's trusted paths; Parent comparisons use published source coordinates. The highest/lowest decile comparisons below each use 29 of the 290 accepted records per seed, with observed-score ties broken by evaluation order. The prior gap provenance was checked in the indexed published molecular reports for n-c55c3d520a2c and n-62daf219c70a; this report adds the present paired observations without turning those historical conditions into new component evidence.

per_task.generated_character: All 870 accepted Child proposals were read. RDKit heavy-atom counts span 1-39 (median 25); perceived ring counts span 0-6 (median 3), with median 3 aromatic rings. Nonempty typed/generic Murcko core counts are 247/91 in the Child and 294/123 in the published Parent. The leading families are compact, mostly three-aromatic-ring indole carboxamides connecting a methoxy/alkyl-substituted fused ring to phenyl or pyridyl groups. Seed 0/evaluation 291 is a 24-heavy-atom vinyl/methoxy indole anilide with indole N-F; seed 1/evaluation 273 is a 25-heavy-atom ethyl/methyl/methoxy analogue bearing both amide N-F and indole N-Br; seed 2/evaluation 104 is a 24-heavy-atom indole anilide with an additional five-member oxygen ring and methylamino substituent. The latter has four perceived rings and no N/O-halogen, peroxide or cyclic-cumulene flag. These are chemically recognizable frameworks, but the halogenated nitrogen variants are not ordinary stable substitution patterns. Across the full Child stream, 289/870 contain N-halogen bonds, 11 O-halogen, 10 O-O and 13 a carbon-centred cyclic cumulene. The respective Parent counts are 445,13,5,0. Thus fewer N-halogen structures do not mean all liabilities disappear. In the 29 highest-scoring records per Child seed, nonempty typed/generic cores number 4/1, 4/2 and 8/6; the corresponding Parent counts are 9/6, 2/2 and 9/3. This is real seed variation within closely related leading families, not global scaffold collapse.
liabilities: Indole N-F/N-Br and amide N-F/N-Br replace ordinary nitrogen environments in highly scored molecules; an identical score across F/Br variants does not certify their comparable stability or preparation.

The full stream also contains cyclic peroxides, cyclic cumulenes and very small fragments; 34/870 accepted proposals have at most five heavy atoms. Repeated aromatic substitution dominates many leaders, though chemically less problematic NH amides are present.
missing_features: The high-scoring aromatic-carbonyl/second-aryl arrangement is present. What remains poorly demonstrated is a wider set of chemically credible alternative connectivities that preserves that arrangement; the highest seed-1 family still relies on reactive nitrogen substitution. Seed-0 and seed-2 nonhalogenated relatives are explicit counterexamples to an absolute inability.

The records do not identify a particular absent target pharmacophore or prove a stereochemical requirement. Realizable local bond chemistry and coherent alternative scaffolds are missing assurances, not unobserved objective components that can be named from these scores.

The supplied starting indole amide scores 0.3051048083696145. Child seed 0/evaluation 211 keeps an ordinary indole NH and pyridyl amide and scores 0.4239904333396317, close to its seed's 0.4254027310763201 N-F leader. Seed 2's nonhalogenated leader scores 0.4188539082916955. High score therefore does not uniformly require N-halogen bonds. Seed 1/evaluations 273 and 286 exchange amide N-F for N-Br yet share exactly 0.4828171386373609; the score does not distinguish their different bond chemistry. High-decile median heavy-atom counts are 24,26,24 versus 10,8,18 in the low deciles. Small fragments such as seed 1/evaluation 234 cyclic peroxide C1COO1 score 0.0, while the 39-heavy-atom doubled indole at seed 0/evaluation 42 scores 3.861219282660785e-08. The observed gradient is compatible with retaining a compact aromatic-carbonyl/second-ring arrangement, not simply maximizing size or ring count. Late proposals can remain below their earlier best: seed 2/evaluation 300 is an aza-aryl relative at 0.3037868548718482. The Parent seed-0 leader is an N-chloro indole linked through a cumulene/amino segment, seed 1 retains N-F on an indole hydroxylated amide, and seed 2 uses an N-chloro indole diketone; these paired structural differences do not isolate which substituent caused the score differences.

per_task.generated_character: All 870 accepted Child proposals were read. RDKit heavy-atom counts span 1-117 (median 34); perceived ring counts span 0-19 (median 4), with median 4 aromatic rings. Nonempty typed/generic Murcko core counts are 447/308 in the Child and 403/276 in the published Parent. The three seeds develop different N/O-rich aromatic families. Seed 0/evaluation 284 is a 29-heavy-atom, four-ring pair of linked fused nitrogen heteroaromatics with carbonyl, thione, N-alkyl and carbon-bound halogen groups. Seed 1/evaluation 295 is a 36-heavy-atom, five-ring ether-linked heteroaromatic/nitrile framework; RDKit assigns all five rings aromatic, but a triple bond lies in a perceived six-member ring. Seed 2/evaluation 248 is a 35-heavy-atom assembly of methoxy aromatic and aza-aryl units joined through a fluorinated N/O-substituted carbon, carrying a C-S-O-O-F arm and a fused three-member ring. The full output has 25/870 N-halogen, 211 O-halogen, 273 O-O and 44 small-ring alkyne incidences, versus 30,89,218,17 in the Parent. The liabilities are strongly seed-dependent: all 29 highest-decile seed-2 molecules have O-O, 26 have O-halogen, while neither bond occurs in the seed-0 or seed-1 high deciles. The 117-heavy-atom extreme is a highly repeated heteroaromatic/ether construction, not evidence that larger products are better chemistry.
liabilities: The leading seed-1 graph contains a triple bond inside a six-member ring and a bromomethyl ether; aromatic flags and valence acceptance do not establish a persistent, readily preparable compound.

Seed-2 leaders repeatedly contain S-O-O-F/O-O-F or longer oxygen chains, an N/O-substituted fluorinated carbon and fused small-ring geometry. Their local reactivity, stereochemistry and stability are unresolved; 343/870 molecules have RDKit-unassigned centres.

Repeated heteroaromatic elaboration reaches 117 heavy atoms without a corresponding high score, while 25/870 accepted proposals contain at most five heavy atoms. Neither extreme supplies controlled functional context.
missing_features: Linked aromatic nitrogen, oxygen and carbonyl regions are already abundant. The missing demonstrated capability is to preserve useful multi-ring attachment relationships in consistently credible bond and ring environments; the almost equal nonalkyne seed-1 relative shows that at least one such local alternative is reachable.

No Child example reproduces the high observed Parent seed-0 range, but the trajectories do not reveal which unobserved decoration pattern would do so. A specific target-required substructure cannot be inferred from this score gap; source-associated scaffold differences are not evidence for atom conservation or for a causal missing feature.

The best supplied initial molecule scores 0.548381482770623. Tiny optimizer structures such as seed 0/evaluation 295 FCCl have the observed floor score 0.5; linked, heteroatom-rich aromatic arrangements attain the higher values. Seed 1/evaluation 275 scores 0.6201180588921683 using a four-ring aza-aryl/ether framework without a cyclic alkyne, almost the same as the six-member-ring-alkyne leader at 0.6205019253751162. transferable_gaps.evidence: Original gap source: n-c55c3d520a2c, carried into its same-code current-profile baseline n-62daf219c70a; re-observed in n-1fdd6af786dc on the supplied complete epoch-1 Search panel, seeds 0,1,2, batch 10 and 300 observations per session. Among 4,350 accepted proposals, direct N-halogen, O-halogen and O-O bonds occur in 775,557,431 records versus 1,042,278,273 in the equally sized Parent output. The shifts are mixed and counts overlap. Some leaders contain N-Br, N-N(F)F or O-O-F arms; other high-scoring molecules contain ordinary carbon-bound halogens and no such bonds. One fluoromethyl-ether imino/carbonyl leader has no direct N/O-halogen or peroxide, and one complete set of high deciles lacks all three bond types. The gap is conditional local chemistry, not a universal absence of plausible products.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator still does not consistently preserve ordinary heteroatom bond environments while modifying otherwise useful aromatic, amine and carbonyl frameworks.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator would need bond-environment-aware alternatives that retain the functional context supported by its own accepted feedback. Distinguish carbon-bound halogens and useful amines from direct heteroatom-halogen and oxygen-chain additions. Evaluate whether chemically ordinary alternatives remain useful rather than assuming a universal filter improves the supplied objective; these structural associations do not attribute the liability to a particular component.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Original gap source: n-c55c3d520a2c, carried into its same-code current-profile baseline n-62daf219c70a; re-observed in n-1fdd6af786dc on the supplied complete epoch-1 Search panel, seeds 0,1,2, batch 10 and 300 observations per session. The Child has rings in 4,211/4,350 proposals, 35 records with a carbon-centred cyclic cumulene and 44 with a triple bond in an RDKit perceived ring of at most eight atoms. A leader contains a triple bond in a six-member ring; other leaders contain a fused three-member ring, a four-member imine or larger bridged nitrogen rings. A closely scored nonalkyne relative and high-scoring noncumulated structures are present, so unusual geometry is neither universal nor demonstrated to be necessary. Ring/aromatic perception is a graph property, not a conformation measurement.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator can create many ring graphs without establishing credible cyclic unsaturation, bridge geometry or accessible conformations.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Task-agnostic ring transformations need to preserve plausible relationships between ring size, bond order and bridge connectivity while offering alternative arrangements of feedback-supported functional groups. Any geometry check should distinguish ordinary small or fused rings from the particular unsupported unsaturation pattern. No conformer calculations, synthetic routes or score benefit from such a change were established here.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Original gap source: n-c55c3d520a2c, carried into its same-code current-profile baseline n-62daf219c70a; re-observed in n-1fdd6af786dc on the supplied complete epoch-1 Search panel, seeds 0,1,2, batch 10 and 300 observations per session. RDKit finds unassigned tetrahedral centres in 2,098/4,350 Child proposals and specified centres in none; all supplied stereo-marker and formal-charge string incidences are zero. Individual aryl/polyamine, bridged peroxide and fluorinated cyclic-imine leaders have multiple unassigned centres. Other leaders are achiral by this test. Abundant structural aliphatic amine proxies show that neutral SMILES are not evidence of missing protonatable nitrogen, and a ring or substructure match does not resolve these identities.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output leaves potentially stereogenic molecular identity unspecified after constructing saturated and bridged centres.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Representation and transformations would need to preserve or deliberately resolve stereochemical identity when the generated chemistry requires it, with appropriate handling of achiral or configurationally unstable cases. Treat protonation and tautomerism separately. The record establishes an identity gap, not a measured stereochemical reward penalty or a component-specific cause.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Original gap source: n-c55c3d520a2c, carried into its same-code current-profile baseline n-62daf219c70a; re-observed in n-1fdd6af786dc on the supplied complete epoch-1 Search panel, seeds 0,1,2, batch 10 and 300 observations per session. The Child emits 140/4,350 accepted proposals with at most five heavy atoms, versus 123/4,350 in the Parent; small fragments still appear late in every supplied objective stream. Large repeated structures also score poorly: the observed 117-heavy-atom example scores 0.5630252100840336, the 68-heavy-atom example 0.1202735457465673, and the 45-heavy-atom doubled imino/carbonyl example 9.038074984387526e-16 within their separate sessions. Compact multi-region structures outperform both extremes in those same streams, while useful open-chain amines and simpler nonreactive relatives demonstrate that simplification is already possible. Cross-session numerical scales are not pooled into a chemical quality score.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently retain useful functional context when fragmenting molecules or expanding related ring systems.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Use task-local accepted feedback to distinguish context-preserving edits from fragment loss and redundant elaboration, keeping enough of the learned functional arrangement while allowing productive simplification. This supports neither a universal minimum size nor a preference for larger molecules. Absence of mapped atom provenance means the needed context cannot be inferred merely from ancestral membership or a retained-core label.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Original gap source: n-c55c3d520a2c, carried into its same-code current-profile baseline n-62daf219c70a; re-observed in n-1fdd6af786dc on the supplied complete epoch-1 Search panel, seeds 0,1,2, batch 10 and 300 observations per session. Per supplied stream, nonempty typed/generic core counts range from 230-547 and 87-372 across 870 Child accepted proposals. Within individual highest deciles they range from 2-22 typed cores and 1-17 generic cores, and several leaders remain close indole-amide or fused imino/carbonyl variants. There are also aryl/amine and nitrogen/carbonyl high deciles with many distinct generic cores, plus different families across seeds: global collapse is false. Relative to the Parent, typed core coverage increases in some streams and decreases in others, while generic coverage can change in a different direction. Exact initial-core subgraphs, generic topology, full-molecule identity, multigeneration ancestry and actual retained atoms are different observations; the latter two are not measured in this molecular audit.
transferable_gaps.gap: Many graph identities do not yet establish a broad set of independent, chemically credible alternatives to the leading family within each search.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Seek chemically plausible scaffold rearrangements that preserve feedback-supported functional relationships and assess useful alternatives beyond peripheral substitutions. Track typed and generic core coverage separately and validate geometry and local chemistry rather than rewarding string novelty alone. Use atom-mapped edit evidence for any future retention claim; neither founder reachability nor core overlap supplies it. These observations motivate a coverage question, not a claim that diversity necessarily improves scores or that the changed population rule caused the gap.

nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

approach.method_basis: The Parent constructs fresh graph-edited offspring from accepted scored parents, then uses an accepted-feedback fingerprint Gaussian process and correlated posterior draws to select each batch. Candidate strings also serve as the keys for temporary uniqueness, emitted exclusions and matching later scores. Its graph checker returns a reparsed molecule with the spelling produced just before that parse, which can leave the stored graph and its identity key out of step.
approach.novelty: Require a stable molecular identity before a candidate enters the pool. Keep already consistent identities, normalize a changing spelling only when the new spelling survives confirmation and still describes the original checked graph, and reject representations that remain inconsistent through the existing bounded generation loop. Earlier siblings altered chemical edits or parent allocation. This change leaves the generated graph and selector intact and extends an earlier identity-repair idea to the newly observed case of alternating representations.

nodes.hypothesis: Admit generated pool candidates only under a parse-and-serialize-stable canonical identity, normalizing stable aliases and rejecting representations that remain inconsistent on confirmation.

finding_summary.headline: Two pool identities stabilized; every evaluated molecule and score stayed unchanged
finding_summary.insights: This establishes a correction at the pool interface that preserves the represented graphs and the search trajectory under the installed parser. Its demonstrated benefit is stable bookkeeping: the only corrected entries were unselected, and their fingerprints were unchanged. A separate read-only replay rejected all 59 unstable representations recorded in the sibling with carbonyl preservation, including one that sibling had emitted. Five of those unstable representations retained the same fingerprint after another parse, showing why fingerprint equality cannot substitute for the registered identity test. The child itself produced no unstable candidate and never evaluated a renamed identity, so empirical failure prevention and accepted feedback under a changed key remain open. Its unchanged emitted chemistry still contains reactive heteroatom-halogen and peroxide bonds, concentrated aromatic ring families and unspecified stereochemistry. Identity consistency does not resolve those chemical limitations.
finding_summary.results: Both known stable aliases were normalized, reducing disagreements between stored pool identities and their molecules from two to zero. Across 75,484 otherwise valid checked attempts, 75,482 identities stayed unchanged and two received confirmed spellings of the same graphs. Independent checks found no admitted identity instability, graph modification, new identity collision or feedback mismatch. Neither corrected pool member was selected. All 435 pools reached 160 candidates, and all 4,350 generated evaluations retained the parent’s exact molecule and score order. Mean final-best score across three seeds remained 0.544374, with population standard deviation 0.013310; every paired task and seed score difference was zero, within the supplied 0.002 non-inferiority allowance. The offspring parent-beating rate also stayed at 565 of 4,350, or 12.99%. Identity checks consumed 7.28 seconds in aggregate, and the added receipts increased diagnostic log size from 98.24 MB to 147.13 MB. Recorded total wall time was lower, but these historical runs do not isolate the incremental runtime cost.

molecular.headline: Parent chemistry persists: aromatic polycycles, halogenated amines and carbonyl heterocycles, with reactive bonds and unspecified stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character: The evaluated molecule/score order matches Parent n-fc2c108a5253 in every supplied task/seed trajectory. The emitted chemistry therefore remains the same. All objectives have trajectories; each digest covers 900 molecules, including 870 optimizer proposals. This is a ring-rich, mostly aromatic output with several distinct seed-dependent families: compact bridged heterocycles, linked carbonyl heteroaromatics, aryl-substituted saturated amines, and larger aza rings. The digest ring-closure rates range from 0.9736 to 0.9943 and aromatic-atom presence rates from 0.9414 to 0.9885. These are fractions of SMILES containing the indicated text features, not fractions of atoms or measured ring counts. Both the charged and stereocentre text rates are 0.0 throughout. Neutral SMILES still contain potentially basic amines, and the lack of stereochemical labels does not mean the graphs are achiral. Recognizable medicinal chemistry fragments coexist with oxygen-halogen bonds, nitrogen-halogen bonds, peroxide chains, crowded aminal centres, unusual ring junctions, and occasional very small or extensively concatenated products. Structural diversity is moderate across the full panel but much narrower within the highest-scoring excerpts. Synthetic plausibility is questionable rather than uniformly absent: familiar substructures are present, while complete routes, stability, and stereochemical control are not established. The score-gradient statements below describe associations in the supplied molecules and scores; they do not establish an unseen target structure, experimentally measured activity, or an intrinsic score benefit from repairing a chemical liability.

per_task.generated_character: The higher-scoring products are compact but densely fused or bridged aromatic heterocycles carrying an aryl/heteroaryl carbonyl appendage and small alkyl substituents. The leading structure has an ethyl/methyl-substituted nitrogen-containing polycycle with an O-methylene bridge and a ketone connected through methylene to fluoropyridine. Other high examples replace that connection with an aroyl group or a thioester. The initial methoxy-rich indole carboxanilide is recognizable conventional chemistry; later structures also include N-fluoro amides and fused N-N or N-O rings. Mean proposal SMILES length is 44.5, with ring-closure rate 0.9736, aromatic presence 0.9724, and halogen presence 0.869. These are mostly substantial multi-ring molecules, with small fragment outliers. The leading ketone is more chemically interpretable than some heteroatom-rich variants, but its unusual bridged core would still need a credible synthesis and structural assignment. Chemistry and associated scores are unchanged from the Parent.
liabilities: N-fluoro amides, N-N/N-O ring linkages, and a thioester introduce different reactivity or stability concerns; they should not be treated as interchangeable examples of ordinary aryl fluorination or amide chemistry.
Unusual short bridges and ring junctions complicate synthetic planning and geometry, while the SMILES provide no explicit stereochemical specification.
Ethene and the N-chloro imine demonstrate loss of essentially the entire multi-ring feature combination even late in the trajectory.
missing_features: The low-scoring fragment products lack the aromatic/heteroaromatic surfaces and carbonyl-bearing connection jointly present in the higher-scoring molecules.

The output does not establish broad, synthetically routine alternative cores that retain this compact feature arrangement; the best excerpt stays close to an unusual bridged family. An additional unseen target-specific group cannot be inferred from the observed scores.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial methoxy-rich indole carboxanilide scores 0.3051048083696145; the leading bridged heterocycle/fluoropyridyl ketone scores 0.4463521672202675. The high aroyl analogue scores 0.4349635367667153, and the thioester analogue still scores 0.4238198477630873. The common observed association is a compact aromatic carbonyl-bearing assembly with small substituents, not one uniquely established linker chemistry. The late N-fluoro-amide/N-N-ring product scores 0.3630045684864706, whereas the final ethene and the N-chloro imine fragment score 0.0. Ring-free fragments do not express the combination retained by the better molecules. These comparisons do not establish that added bridges, thioesters, or N-halogen bonds are independently beneficial.

per_task.generated_character: The higher-scoring molecules join carbonyl-bearing O/N heteroaromatic ring systems through an NH connection. The leading family also carries an aryl cyanate substituent, a short annulated carbon bridge, an aryl halogen, and an O-O-Cl chain. The final excerpt contains still more nitrogen-rich fused/linked dicarbonyl heterocycles, including N-F, N-Cl, and oxygen-chlorine substituents. Mean proposal SMILES length is 94.4 and the maximum is 248: the full trajectories include much larger concatenated aromatic assemblies than the leading compact representatives. Ring-closure and aromatic presence are both 0.9885; halogen presence is 0.7851. The familiar carbonyl heterocycles and NH linkage are embedded in molecules whose reactive substituents and complex annulation make overall synthetic plausibility questionable. The Parent has the same chemistry and score order.
liabilities: O-O-Cl and O-O-F chains combine peroxide and oxygen-halogen bonds; these are chemical reactivity liabilities despite their high objective scores.
Late N-halogenated dicarbonyl heterocycles and oxygen-halogen substituents raise further stability and synthetic-handling concerns.
Short annulated bridges, extensively repeated heterocyclic units, and large aromatic surfaces complicate synthesis and molecular properties; SMILES validity alone does not resolve those concerns.
missing_features: The tiny low-scoring molecules lack the linked aromatic surfaces, NH connection, and distributed carbonyl/heteroatom acceptors present in the higher-scoring family.

The highest excerpt poorly covers chemically ordinary replacements for the unusual peripheral bonds while preserving the same compact core geometry. The fluoromethyl example shows one such alternative; the scores do not identify a required unvisited scaffold.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted dicarbonyl heterocycle scores 0.548381482770623, compared with 0.6324703199409752 for the leading linked heteroaromatic product. Small methylamine and molecular chlorine examples both score 0.5, so that floor does not demonstrate useful molecular features. Within a closely related high-scoring core, the O-O-Cl-bearing structure scores 0.6300605077662029 and the fluoromethyl replacement scores 0.6293992623616929. Replacing its aryl bromine with methyl retains 0.6300605077662029. Thus the observed score is compatible with the linked heteroaromatic/carbonyl arrangement while distinguishing these reactive or halogen substituents only weakly. It does not establish a need for peroxide-halogen chemistry or increasing molecular size.

per_task.generated_character: The better products are medium-sized aryl-rich amines with saturated nitrogen-containing rings and flexible benzylic or alkenyl connections. One high-scoring family contains a saturated diaza ring with a crowded aminal centre, an exocyclic amine, an N-alkyl substituent, and substituted aromatic ends. Another has spiro-connected aza rings, halogenated aryl groups, and an aryl thiol. Mean proposal SMILES length is 60.2; ring-closure presence is 0.9851, aromatic presence 0.9782, and halogen presence 0.9874. These molecules already contain basic-amine opportunities; a lack of ring nitrogens is not their general limitation. Some spiro-amine frameworks are recognizable medicinal chemistry, while the crowded aminals, occasional O-Cl groups, chloromethyl substituents and undefined stereochemistry make the full products less routine. The same structures and scores occur in the Parent.
liabilities: Crowded aminal centres, including a carbon bearing an exocyclic amino group and both ring nitrogens, require scrutiny for stability and synthetic accessibility.
Aryl thiols, O-Cl substituents, and N-chloromethyl groups occur alongside otherwise recognizable amine frameworks; high scores do not establish their suitability.
No explicit charge or stereochemical labels are present. Potentially basic nitrogens are encoded neutrally, so the emitted strings do not document a protonation-state or stereoisomer exploration.
missing_features: Low-scoring aryl fragments and the final truncated aminal fail to retain the aromatic-appendage/amine/geometry combination expressed by the better molecules.

The spiro and substituted saturated-ring products lack stereochemical specification. Their graphs can encode different spatial arrangements, but the trajectories do not test whether a particular stereoisomer improves this objective.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The leading aminal/aryl/amine assembly scores 0.9914038363125457 and the spiro-amine/aryl-thiol example 0.9908331648929692. A small halogenated aromatic fragment scores 0.001421581552029289. A particularly useful local comparison retains the aryl ends and enamine-linked core: the ring N-methyl analogue scores 0.981088217863691, while its N-formyl analogue scores 0.48797702544581545. That change alters nitrogen electronics and hydrogen-bonding capacity. The final smaller product retaining the diaza ring and fluorinated aromatic end but losing the other aromatic appendage scores 0.011495655106721757. The visible gradient favors the combined aromatic surface, amine character, and connecting geometry. It does not imply that every amine, extra halogen, or additional nitrogen independently helps.

per_task.generated_character: The higher-scoring products are medium-to-large cyclic assemblies containing alkyl-substituted pyridyl or quinolyl groups, a benzofused carbonyl heterocycle, and N-methylated aza rings or macrocyclic connections. Carbonyls, aromatic nitrogens, tertiary amines or amidic nitrogens recur; oxygen and sulfur substitutions appear among neighboring products. The final excerpt includes unsaturated, nitrogen-rich larger rings bearing quinoline-like appendages. Mean proposal SMILES length is 55.9; ring-closure presence is 0.9943, aromatic presence 0.9885, and halogen presence only 0.269. This family is much less dependent on halogen decoration than the others. The individual functional groups are often familiar, but constructing the complete fused/bridged larger-ring arrangements would require deliberate synthetic planning and stereochemical control. Chemistry and its score trajectory remain identical to the Parent.
liabilities: Large and sometimes bridged aza rings create conformational and ring-closure challenges; their existence as valid graphs is not a synthesis.
Serial changes interconvert tertiary amines, amides and urea-like connections, changing basicity and donor/acceptor patterns along with ring geometry.
Bulky repeated aromatic appendages and unspecified stereochemistry add uncertainty even though this family has fewer obvious heteroatom-halogen liabilities than several other outputs.
missing_features: Low-scoring chains lack the coupled heteroaromatic/carbonyl/cyclic-nitrogen arrangement that is present in the better products.

The highest excerpt provides limited alternative, synthetically straightforward ring topologies retaining that feature arrangement, and it does not specify stereochemistry at newly substituted or bridged centres. The observed scores do not identify a particular missing target scaffold.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted dicarbonyl heterocycle scores 0.1678386594791329, whereas the leading pyridyl/benzofused dicarbonyl/aza-ring assembly scores 0.22405709718343647. A related analogue without the extra methylene between the N-methyl nitrogen and carbonyl scores 0.21884002370946612; this changes both ring size and amine-versus-amidic character, so those effects cannot be separated. Ethane scores 0.012461119656980673 and the small acyclic amide 0.025605696979529788. The common higher-scoring feature set is the combined aromatic heterocycle, nitrogen-rich ring and carbonyl arrangement, rather than amide presence alone. The larger final molecule carrying repeated quinoline-like appendages scores 0.1754730092490373, below the more compact final dicarbonyl aza-ring example at 0.21037674112349405; repetition and size alone do not ensure higher score.

per_task.generated_character: The leading family consists of compact fluorinated aryl compounds attached to an N-alkylated fused dicarbonyl heterocycle, with aminomethyl or aminoethyl substituents. The top example has a free primary amine, aryl fluorine and fluoromethyl groups, and the carbonyl-bearing heterocycle; neighboring examples include N-F substitution. Another seed finishes with more extensively fused heteroaromatics bearing thiol/hydroxyl groups and small fluorinated carbocycles, without the same pendant primary amine. The leading aminomethyl compound contains comparatively conventional functional groups; N-fluoro congeners, very large repeated cores and unsaturated small rings elsewhere are less straightforward. The Parent emits the same chemistry with the same scores.

Small unsaturated carbocycles, thiol substituents and cumulated-double-bond examples require chemical scrutiny; these are not evidence of an intrinsically inaccessible whole output.
Large repeated heterocyclic/aromatic assemblies show that the emitted chemistry does not reliably remain within the compact size and feature balance seen in the better family.

The output lacks a broad set of chemically stable scaffold alternatives preserving that arrangement. Where small saturated carbocycles create stereochemical choices, these are unspecified; a stereochemical score benefit has not been demonstrated.

Its close aryl-chloro analogue scores 0.5064928497454653: replacing that aryl chlorine with fluoromethyl accompanies an increase within this particular family. Let observed feedback determine which combinations matter without assigning task identity.

transferable_gaps.evidence: One proposal set has mean SMILES length 94.4 and maximum 248. Other supplied records include the very large repeated-core molecule Cn1c(=O)c2c(-c3ccccc3)n(-c3cc4cc(c3O)C(n3c(=O)c5c(-c6ccccc6)n(-c6cc(C(=O)OCCl)ccc6O)cc5n(C)c3=O)OC4=O)cc2n(C)c1=O at 1.6758614448245604e-53, and the final fragment C=C at 0.0. nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

retained_mechanisms: Task-local scored molecular-graph population with score-ranked parent sampling across three high-ranked quantiles
De novo connected-fragment graph crossover
Local atom/bond mutation with inner operator retries and occasional multi-step graph walks
Chemical sanitization, canonical/isomeric identity rejection, and graph-based retries for complete novel pools; saturation-dependent retry branches retained but not exercised
Bounded greedy score-ranked survival and subsequent breeding from accepted offspring

approach.method_basis: The Parent trains a SELFIES variational autoencoder on the permitted unlabeled corpus and freezes it. A complete Gaussian state contains both the semantic latent and the variables that determine categorical decoding, so each state produces one reproducible molecule. During an objective, a Gaussian process learns from the fingerprints and scores of that session's accepted molecules. Parallel pCN chains sample the Gaussian prior weighted by the GP probability of beating the best observed score. The Parent randomly takes a novel batch from retained chain states and submits the exact molecules used for prediction.
approach.novelty: Add empirical elite-threshold conditioning: after each feedback message, use the 90th percentile of accepted scores as the probability threshold. This asks whether a molecule can enter the observed upper score region even when an isolated record lies far above the decoder's predicted scores. The proposed causal change is a less extreme threshold that changes which pCN transitions are accepted. This lineage has only its root so far; its incumbent threshold is the direct comparator, and no sibling has tried an elite-percentile threshold.

nodes.hypothesis: Replace the observed-maximum threshold in the Parent's GP-probability pCN target with the linearly interpolated empirical 90th percentile of unique accepted current-session scores, so the same prior-preserving sampler conditions on entering an observed elite score region instead of exceeding an isolated incumbent.

finding_summary.headline: Elite conditioning changed sampling but lowered the single-seed mean score to 0.391
finding_summary.insights:
An extreme incumbent tail can be relaxed enough to materially redirect sampling without improving record discovery. The paired receipts rule out an inactive cutoff, unaccepted labels or prediction/submission mismatch as explanations for this score result. Lowering the cutoff changed relative preferences: it accepted 5,401 moves the incumbent rule would reject, and rejected 1,103 moves that rule would accept. The effect therefore includes which molecular transitions are preferred, as well as the overall acceptance rate.

On the two sessions that motivated the intervention, the elite target became permissive: mean retained-minus-prior log elite probability was only 0.087 for drd2_docking and 0.021 for sitagliptin_mpo. Their scores moved in opposite directions. This narrows the next question to how much record-seeking pressure is useful, and whether the GP can distinguish useful molecular arrangements within the decoder's reachable space. The molecular assessment finds abundant rings and familiar medicinal fragments, but inconsistent whole-molecule assembly and control of functional-group placement in both runs; threshold relaxation leaves those generator limitations open. These chemistry observations suggest further hypotheses, not a proven cause of the score loss. One seed establishes the logged behavioral effect but cannot establish the reliability of the score tradeoff, GP calibration or equilibrium mixing.
finding_summary.results:
The intended threshold and sampling effects occurred. All 145 fitted cutoffs exactly matched the accepted-score 90th percentile and lay below the incumbent. On 4,640 identical prior probes, the mean standardized threshold deficit fell from 5.193 to 1.057, and the fraction more than three posterior standard deviations below the cutoff fell from 66.49% to 0.43%. Retained states showed the same direction in every round. Replaying both rules with the same proposals and random draws changed 6,504 of 36,800 accept/reject decisions (17.67%); every actual update followed the elite rule. All 1,450 submitted molecules retained exact prediction identity and filled the budget.

The seed-0 mean final-best score fell from 0.433167 to 0.390832, a decrease of 0.042335. The largest change was drd2_docking, which fell from 0.867722 to 0.572905. median_2 fell from 0.171784 to 0.167839. Gains on zaleplon_mpo (0.340635 to 0.375713), deco_hop (0.573265 to 0.574331) and sitagliptin_mpo (0.212429 to 0.263373) did not offset those losses. This is confirmed mechanism activation with a negative score result on the one available seed.
