molecular.headline: Ring-rich carbonyl and amine families retain reactive N-halogen bonds, small constrained rings and oversized heterocycles
molecular.overall_character: All supplied child and parent trajectories were read, and every requested task is covered. Each task contains 900 recorded molecules, including 870 optimizer proposals. The proposal ring-closure-token rates are 0.9644-0.9839 and aromatic-token rates are 0.9138-0.9828. The tiny fragments in the worst-molecule excerpts therefore represent a small low-score tail, not an absence of ring or aromatic chemistry in the overall output. Mean SMILES lengths range from 42.2 to 87.8. The main families are indole-like aryl amides, large repeated aza-carbonyl assemblies, aryl polyamines, fused nitrogen/carbonyl polycycles and fluorinated imino heterocycles. Families differ across seeds, but the strongest excerpts usually cluster around closely related frameworks. Relative to parent n-559d25e9c9c7, the output retains those broad themes while changing the prevalence of reactive heteroatom bonds and small rings. Ordinary amides, ethers and amines coexist with N-F/N-Cl/N-Br bonds, imines, N-N/N-O connections, aziridines, and some unusually substituted sulfur. All charged-token and stereocentre-token rates are 0.0. Neutral SMILES do not establish solution protonation, and substituted rings are frequently stereochemically unresolved. Size, small-ring and configuration counts below are passive RDKit readings of the supplied SMILES; the digest counters themselves are string-level presence readings. No new oracle scores, synthesis scores or conformational feasibility results were generated. The chemistry is questionable because of these local bonding and geometry issues, not because medicinal fragments are missing altogether.

per_task.generated_character: The proposal median is 25 heavy atoms. The leading molecules contain 24-26 heavy atoms and combine an indole-like fused aromatic system with an aryl or pyridyl carboxamide, vinyl groups and methyl, methoxy, thioether or methylamino substituents. The highest observed example has both an N-chloro amide and a fluorinated ring nitrogen. Many other leaders have N-fluoro or N-bromo amides. A strong alternative contains an ordinary N-H amide linking a fused N/O ring framework to a methylpyridyl group. The weakest excerpt consists of tiny molecules such as an interhalogen, acetylene, short hydrocarbons and a small sulfur/oxygen ring. The main aromatic-amide scaffolds are recognizable chemistry, but direct halogenation of their nitrogens creates much less convincing stable medicinal compounds.
liabilities: N-halogen amides and fluorinated aromatic ring nitrogen are distinct reactive-bond concerns from ordinary carbon-bound halogens.
Vinyl groups, thioethers and fused N/O connections complicate stability or synthesis in some variants.
Tiny hydrocarbon, interhalogen and heterocyclic fragments discard the useful larger molecular arrangement.

nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds fresh molecular graphs from accepted, score-ranked survivors using fragment crossover and local atom or bond edits. A fingerprint Gaussian process learned from all earlier accepted scores selects each evaluation batch by correlated posterior draws over the fresh pool. The Parent also verifies stable canonical identities before pool admission, normalizing confirmed aliases without replacing the checked graph. Its bond-change move alters bond order; it has no direct move that shifts an intact side group to a neighboring aromatic position while keeping the whole molecule's composition.
approach.novelty: Add intact pendant-branch relocation to the existing bond-change menu: detach an acyclic side group from an aromatic carbon and reconnect that same group to an adjacent aromatic carbon bearing a hydrogen. This exposes substitution-position alternatives while preserving the group, ring framework and formula. Earlier siblings changed parent allocation or survival, protected all first-parent rings, redirected halogen growth, protected carbonyl atoms, or stabilized identity keys. None tested this positional move in their fresh graph pools. A different graph-walk lineage evaluated ten such moves but retained none; this experiment tests whether the Parent's existing learned pool selection can put a useful positional alternative into accepted breeding ancestry.

nodes.hypothesis: Extend the existing change_bond menu with relocation of an intact single-attachment acyclic branch from an aromatic carbon to an adjacent hydrogen-bearing aromatic carbon, exposing positional isomers to the inherited fresh-pool selector while preserving the branch, ring framework and molecular formula.

finding_summary.headline: Positional moves reached useful breeding ancestry, but the panel score fell slightly
finding_summary.insights:
The fresh-pool selector and accepted-survivor breeder can carry a useful positional edit into later ancestry, resolving the earlier graph-walk experiment's absence of retained relocation winners. The demonstrated benefit is narrow: two of 13 evaluated one-atom moves improved their parents, while none of seven evaluated multi-atom moves did. Keeping a larger branch intact therefore establishes access to positional alternatives without establishing better scores. A score-neutral methyl relocation also entered extensive later ancestry, so immediate parent improvement and later usefulness are different observations.

Two final-best molecules have recorded relocation ancestry, but subsequent edits and crossover prevent assigning their endpoint gains to a conserved moved group. Changing the option menu also changes the search path, so the paired panel measures the complete method; it supplies no scores for unselected alternatives. The molecular assessment still finds concentrated aromatic polycycles, reactive heteroatom bonds, strained ring arrangements and unspecified stereochemistry. Local formula and ring conservation did not resolve those chemical limitations, and the panel loss leaves the registered score-benefit expectation refuted even though construction, evaluated positional access and useful breeding ancestry are confirmed.
finding_summary.results:
All 368 sampled branch reconnections preserved the registered atom and bond counts, molecular formula, branch composition and aromatic ring framework. Of the 365 moves that changed molecular identity, 362 reached pools and 20 were evaluated with the relocated attachment still present. The evaluated set contained 13 one-atom and seven multi-atom branches. Two moves beat their generating parents; both moved fluorine. Sixteen evaluated products survived their batch, and 14 were chosen as breeding parents 979 times across 972 later attempts. One fluorine shift increased its source score from 0.382775 to 0.394039, raised the incumbent, and was reused in 444 attempts with 85 later accepted descendants. Every evaluated multi-atom move scored below its best generating parent.

Mean final-best score across three seeds was 0.542797, versus 0.544374 for the Parent: a paired change of -0.001577, which misses the required +0.002 gain. Seed variation decreased from a population standard deviation of 0.013310 to 0.004718, but the paired seed changes were mixed. All 435 pools filled to 160 candidates and all 4,350 proposed evaluations were accepted. Stable identity bookkeeping was preserved; its inherited guard rejected seven unstable representations before pool admission.

molecular.headline: Aromatic polycycles and halogenated amines dominate; reactive bonds, strained ring closures and unspecified stereochemistry persist.
molecular.overall_character: All supplied current and Parent trajectories were read; no objective lacks trajectories. Each current task digest covers 900 recorded molecules, including 870 optimizer proposals. The output contains substantial aromatic and heteroaromatic ring systems, carbonyl-rich aza rings, halogenated aryl groups, saturated amines, and seed-dependent fused or bridged families. Ring-closure text rates range from 0.9736 to 0.9931 and aromatic-atom presence rates from 0.8966 to 0.9862. These are fractions of proposal strings containing those features, not atom fractions or measured ring counts. Charged and stereocentre text rates are 0.0 throughout. Neutral strings nevertheless contain potentially basic amines, and graph inspection identifies unassigned stereocentres in several leading products. There is moderate diversity across the complete panel, with much narrower families within individual seeds and their high-scoring excerpts. Familiar medicinal fragments coexist with heteroatom-halogen bonds, peroxide or N-O linkages, unusual small ring annulations, crowded aminal centres, and occasional extensive duplication of ring systems. Compared with Parent n-213e85380e04, the leading chemotypes have changed, but these broad chemical liabilities remain. nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves a population of scored molecular graphs. It keeps the highest-scoring survivors, favors their upper score bands when choosing parents, and generates offspring with mutation chains and connected-fragment crossover. Accepted offspring can become later parents. Every accepted score also enters a complete archive used by a count-fingerprint Gaussian process to select each evaluation batch from a larger fresh candidate pool through correlated posterior draws. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled, while ordinary graph edits, stable molecular identity checks, duplicate rejection and bounded fallbacks remain active.
approach.novelty: Test one registered combination linking survivor retention to its breeding consumer: keep the incumbent and newest other live records, then draw parents uniformly from every eligible live survivor. The recency-only sibling stored extra records that never bred; the uniform-live sibling used otherwise unsupported parents under greedy retention. Both lowered the mean. This exact joint implementation supplies the missing fourth treatment, follows protected records into actual use and scored descendants, and measures the total interaction. It differs from recent-score-tie priority and core-based retention, and makes no separate component-benefit or performance-rescue claim.

nodes.hypothesis: Jointly replace nonincumbent greedy survivor membership with the exact incumbent-preserving newest-serial rule from n-8fa256ded991 and replace rank-preferred live-parent choice with the exact all-eligible-live uniform law from n-a56491c332aa, on the single code Parent n-62daf219c70a, to connect directly protected survivors to their breeding consumer.

finding_summary.headline: Protected records reached scored offspring, but the joint mean fell and the interaction was negative
finding_summary.insights:
Changing the consumer removed the storage-without-use obstruction observed with recency alone, but making protected alternatives breed did not recover endpoint performance. This is a resolved negative result for the exact joint intervention and its matched-panel interaction. It does not assign the loss to either component separately or settle the value of the wider graph-evolution foundation. The original losses from both single controls remain.

Participation and productive search separated sharply: the joint run produced 1,060 strict generating-parent wins versus 629 for the Parent, against weaker generating parents, while sequential incumbent advances fell from 258 to 201. Protected ancestry reached 525 accepted records and twelve incumbent advances, but only one final leader; overlapping ancestry is not proof that a retained structure mediated the endpoint. More perceived molecular cores likewise did not establish useful chemical diversity: the molecular assessment found 2,005 typed and 1,327 generic cores versus 1,850 and 1,117 for the Parent, alongside 299 tiny products versus 99 and continuing unusual ring bonds and unspecified stereochemistry. Recognizable cyclic amines and carbonyl frameworks remain counterexamples to treating every product as implausible. Neither core counts nor founder reachability measures retained atoms or synthetic feasibility.

The fixed combination has an exposed, complete answer without rescue tuning. Why particular trajectories lose, which chemistry would be useful, and how the broader foundation contributes remain open; this shared-Parent panel supplies neither independent replication nor reliability beyond the issued seeds.
finding_summary.results:
The access mechanism worked. Of 196 records retained against a local greedy eviction, 182 reached a later live population and all 182 were subsequently sampled, in 3,736 parent draws. The other 14 had no later opportunity. Those parents produced 155 accepted offspring, of which 151 later bred. Only two immediately advanced the incumbent. The stricter group still directly protected at the consumed retention contest produced 61 accepted offspring and no immediate incumbent gains. In median_2 seed 2, protected parents were drawn 140 times but produced no accepted offspring. All fifteen joint task runs completed.

Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.595670 to 0.530508, a paired loss of 0.065161. All three seed macros and all five task means declined; three of fifteen task-seed endpoints improved. The joint mean was also 0.053355 below recency alone and 0.019163 below uniform-live sampling alone. The four-treatment interaction, joint minus recency minus uniform plus the Parent, was −0.007357, beyond the registered 0.002 descriptive scale. Its seed values were +0.025676, −0.057736 and +0.009990, with population deviation 0.036194, so the negative mean does not describe every seed.

molecular.headline: Aromatic carbonyl and aryl-amine families persist, alongside more tiny fragments, unusual ring bonds and unspecified stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character:
All supplied Child and published Parent trajectories were read for all five objectives and Search seeds 0, 1 and 2. The brief reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true, with all seeds matched and no profile mismatches. The indexed published recency-only n-8fa256ded991 and uniform-live-only n-a56491c332aa trajectories were also read descriptively: 60 files and 18,000 observations in total, with no missing paths. Each node contributes 4,500 observations, including 4,350 optimizer products and 150 fixed initial records; each task contributes 870 optimizer products. No task was omitted. Only accepted evaluated products and initial observations are visible in these trajectories; unselected candidate pools have no invented scores or inferred chemistry coverage. The digest final_molecules are the tail of seed 2, not every seed's best molecule. All seed leaders and selected low and final examples below come from the full trajectories. Original indexed molecular reports for the Parent and both component comparators were read to preserve the source and conditions of recurring gaps.

The Child produces recognizable annulated aryl carboxamides and ketones, azaarene/carbonyl assemblies, biaryl cyclic amines, cyclic urea/imide-like systems, fluorinated carbocycles and thiourea/hydrazone structures. Optimizer median heavy-atom counts, in fixed task order, are 24, 34, 32, 31 and 26, versus Parent 25, 33, 31, 30 and 27. Across the Child, the range is one to 113 heavy atoms and the median is 28 heavy atoms with four RDKit-perceived rings. Ring and aromatic chemistry are abundant: digest ring-digit incidences range from 0.8621 to 0.9517, and aromatic-text incidences from 0.6425 to 0.9253. These are the fraction of molecule strings containing the feature, not the fraction of atoms aromatic, physical ring feasibility or scaffold counts. The chemically recognizable families and conventional cyclic-amine leaders are meaningful counterexamples to calling every output implausible. Nevertheless, reactive-looking local bonds, constrained unsaturation, complex bridges and many unspecified configurations justify questionable synthetic plausibility and weak overall medicinal-chemistry quality; none is a synthesis or activity measurement.

The distinction between identities, perceived cores and ancestry matters. Over the evaluated optimizer records the Child has 4,138 distinct exact SMILES and 2,005 nonempty typed / 1,327 generic Murcko cores; Parent has 4,286 strings and 1,850 / 1,117 cores. The component comparators have 1,782 / 1,055 and 2,060 / 1,403 cores, respectively. Generic cores replace atom types and bond orders, and all core counting omits stereochemistry; empty acyclic cores are excluded. This shows substantial perceived topology variation, while recurring leading families within seeds support moderate rather than collapsed chemical diversity. It does not show independent plausible pharmacophores, useful diversity or atoms retained from a founder. Trajectory files do not map atoms or provide actual-parent ancestry; founder reachability, if supplied by a separate provenance audit, remains graph ancestry rather than conserved scaffold chemistry. No protected-record, component-activation or chemical-mediation conclusion is drawn here.

The Child includes 299 products with at most three heavy atoms, versus Parent 99, recency-only 105 and uniform-live-only 134; 425 Child products are acyclic versus Parent 129. Conversely, direct N-halogen / O-halogen / O-O bond-bearing record counts are 489 / 145 / 114 for Child, 1,042 / 278 / 273 for Parent, 897 / 456 / 319 for recency-only and 483 / 247 / 157 for uniform-live-only. These overlapping counts are whole-record occurrences, not distinct bonds or a combined quality score. Ring-triple-bond and ring-cumulated-carbon flags occur in 41 and 61 Child products, versus 17 and 42 in Parent. Fewer heteroatom-halogen flags therefore do not establish general chemical improvement. RDKit identifies possible unassigned tetrahedral centres in 2,446 Child products versus 2,408 Parent products, while all Child digest stereocentre and charge-string incidences are zero. Neutral tertiary amines remain plainly present, so absence of charge notation does not mean absence of basic sites. Potential centres are structural flags, not proof of configurational stability.

The per-seed endpoint scores below are existing trajectory observations, not newly assigned scores. Their structural associations do not identify why a score changed, the objective's full desired chemistry, or separate effects of the two jointly changed decisions. The current comparison has one code Parent, and the published component trajectories remain their own adaptive histories. No additive chemical contribution, significance, unseen-seed reliability or whole-foundation value follows. Read-only CPU descriptor definitions, original trajectory hashes and all records are in .slots/L01-resume-20260928/r21-slot3-molecular/trajectory_descriptors.json and molecule_records.jsonl; describe.py reproduces them without candidate or oracle execution.

The earlier n-c55c3d520a2c source provenance is historical: its profile boundary is not converted into a matched comparison here. Current complete pairing refers specifically to n-62daf219c70a.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 evaluated optimizer products range from one to 39 heavy atoms, median 24, with median three perceived rings. Ring-digit and aromatic-text incidences are 0.8897 and 0.8678. All three seed leaders have 25 heavy atoms but different local ring chemistry. Seed 0 evaluation 291, score 0.42762099872850584, is a methoxy/methyl arene fused to a partially unsaturated nitrogen ring, with an amino-bearing saturated centre and an N-fluoro aryl carboxamide. Seed 1 evaluation 190, 0.4163503402962837, carries a fused seven-membered N-N ring, a carbon-bound chloride, hydroxymethyl group and fluoropyridyl ketone; it has no N-halogen bond. Seed 2 evaluation 299, 0.45555627303128626, is an ethynyl/methoxy/methyl N-methyl indole-like carboxamide whose amide nitrogen bears fluorine and a pyridyl substituent. The observed makeability ranges from recognizable aromatic amide chemistry to unusual nitrogen substitution and uncertain cyclic geometry. The seed-2 evaluation-253 benzofuran-like N-methyl pyridyl carboxamide, 0.4272212457957658, is a relatively conventional counterexample with carbon-bound fluorine and no direct N/O-halogen or peroxide bond.
liabilities: N-F carboxamides occur in the seed-0 and seed-2 leaders; N-hydroxy and N-N alternatives require their own stability and synthetic assessment rather than being treated as automatically ordinary.
A seed-1 near-leader at evaluation 278 scores 0.41605207864642335 despite cyclic cumulated double bonds. High score and a parseable SMILES do not establish feasible ring geometry.
There are 72 products with at most three heavy atoms, and late tiny proposals coexist with developed multiring structures.
missing_features: The leading set does not consistently combine its useful aromatic-carbonyl organization with ordinary amide nitrogen substitution and credible ring geometry. Such alternatives are partially present, including the benzofuran-like tertiary amide, so this is incomplete coverage rather than an inability to make aromatic rings or amides.

Configuration is unspecified at saturated ring centres in the seed-0 and seed-1 leaders. These trajectories contain no matched stereoisomer comparison and do not establish that specifying one would improve the score.
No unique missing target motif can be inferred from these records: both fused aromatic and partially reduced N-ring series reach the upper observed range.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxy indole aryl amide at evaluation 9 scores 0.3051048083696145. Higher examples retain an organized aromatic/polar carbonyl framework while altering methoxy content, side chains, ring constitution and nitrogen environment. The score does not require N-F: the seed-1 leader lacks it, and the seed-2 N-hydroxy carboxamide at evaluation 262 scores 0.44989726212142783. Late fragmentation remains costly: seed-2 evaluation 298, OCF, scores 8.28920643387263e-20, while evaluated elemental or tiny unsaturated fragments reach zero. These comparisons support molecular context rather than an isolated functional-group prescription. Parent leaders for seeds 0/1/2 score 0.39405142067435733 / 0.47411701813450596 / 0.438972502037081 and remain substituted fused aromatic N systems with N-halogen groups. The Child therefore has both higher and lower seed endpoints, without a consistent gain from a particular ring or halogen change. The component-comparator leaders also preserve carbonyl/aromatic families, including halogen-free examples and larger or spiro ring variants; neither explains the joint output by itself.

per_task.generated_character: The evaluated set ranges from one to 113 heavy atoms, median 34, with median four perceived rings; ring-digit and aromatic-text incidences are 0.8621 and 0.8425. The seed-0 leader at evaluation 299 scores 0.6034633506581824 and contains 45 heavy atoms: linked pyrazole/aryl/azaaryl regions, substituted urea and formamide carbonyls, conjugated imino functionality, halogens, and a triple bond in a six-membered oxygen-containing ring. The seed-1 leader at evaluation 295 scores 0.5990766677041187 and contains 38 heavy atoms, with an imino aryl group, linked or annulated N heterocycles, carbonyl/ester side chains and direct O-F. The terminal seed-2 leader at evaluation 300 scores 0.6115618661257607 and has 49 heavy atoms, six perceived rings, azaaromatic/nitrile and cyclic-carbonyl regions, methoxy/acetal substituents and O-Cl. This is bulky, largely aromatic and heteroatom-rich output with serious local bond and geometry questions. Recognizable carbonyl and azaarene components do not by themselves make the assembled structures synthetically persuasive.
liabilities: The seed-0 leader contains a cyclic triple bond despite aromatic labels. The task set contains 41 ring-triple-bond-bearing products; graph perception does not validate their geometry.
Direct O-F and O-Cl in the other seed leaders raise context-dependent reactivity and makeability concerns. They are distinct from carbon-bound aromatic fluorine or chloride.

Large appended or coupled modules, flexible oxygenated side chains and imino groups add complexity without proving useful functional organization; 70 products are at most three heavy atoms at the other extreme.
The seed-2 best is terminal. Its structure and observed score say nothing about later descendants or retained atom provenance.
missing_features: The observed Child leaders do not demonstrate the compact, strongly scoring heteroatom/carbonyl organization seen in the Parent seed-0 leader. This is an observed coverage difference, not a prescription to reproduce that molecule or its reactive bonds.

Credible alternatives to constrained cyclic triple bonds and direct O-halogen substitution are not consistently combined with the upper observed scores. Near-scoring alternatives lacking those particular bonds do exist, and may retain other liabilities.
No unique rewarded scaffold can be identified from the trajectories; decorated size and ring count are inadequate proxies for the favorable connected arrangement.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial best, evaluation 7, scores 0.548381482770623. Very small optimizer products such as seed-0 evaluation 48, dimethyl ether, score 0.5. The 37-heavy-atom seed-2 evaluation-69 sulfone/polyene/carbonyl-N assembly scores 0.2888457269700333, showing that size and aromatic complexity alone are insufficient. The seed-2 43-heavy-atom nitrile/carbonyl-thione alternative at evaluation 272 scores 0.6023391812865497 without O-Cl, and seed-1 evaluation 296 scores 0.5923490233391169 with an O-formyl group instead of O-F but also other structural differences; neither is a controlled single-bond replacement. The visible gradient is consistent with particular connected heteroaromatic/carbonyl arrangements, not simply more rings or more halogen. Parent seed leaders score 0.8561477222467935 / 0.6248206599713055 / 0.6178024026512013. Its strongest leader has 30 heavy atoms and compact fused N/carbonyl/thione and azaaryl chemistry, but also O-F and a chloromethyl ether; the Child's larger leaders do not reproduce its upper score range. Recency-only leaders span 0.6030158256195879 to 0.6431665876937657 and uniform-live-only leaders 0.5983092961702587 to 0.6077243572172578, with their own hypohalite, peroxide, nitrogen and ring liabilities. These are comparator chemistries, not evidence that either component supplied or removed a required fragment.

per_task.generated_character: The products range from one to 90 heavy atoms, median 32, with median three rings and two aromatic rings; ring-digit and aromatic-text incidences are 0.9437 and 0.9253. The seed-0 leader at evaluation 242, score 0.9999886694484911, is a 26-heavy-atom N-propyl azetidine linked through an alkyl chain to a fluorinated/methylated biphenyl with a fluoromethyl substituent. The seed-2 leader at evaluation 293, 0.9636142513873031, is a 27-heavy-atom substituted N-methyl pyrrolidine joining two fluorinated aromatic regions, with a methoxy-bearing benzylic centre and phenol. Both contain recognizable basic aliphatic amines and carbon-bound fluorine without the flagged N/O-halogen or peroxide bonds. Seed 1 diverges: evaluation 295, 0.7437807598425547, is a 30-heavy-atom halogenated diaryl cyclohexene with a methoxy-thiol-type O-CH2-SH substituent and no nitrogen atom. Its crowded substituted carbon ring and sulfur terminus warrant more scrutiny than the simpler cyclic-amine series. Plausible medicinal-chemistry motifs therefore exist, but the whole output is neither uniform nor uniformly persuasive.
liabilities: The leading aryl-amine structures are heavily hydrophobic and halogenated by inspection, with uncertain balance of polar and nonpolar groups; no measured solubility, exposure or biological activity is supplied.
Seed-1 evaluation 263 and its final product contain acid chloride functionality, and the leader retains an unusual oxygen/sulfur terminus. High score does not certify stability or synthesis.
RDKit detects possible unassigned centres in 807 of 870 optimizer records. Ordinary azetidines and pyrrolidines are counterexamples to any blanket objection to small saturated N rings.
missing_features: The seed-1 leading series lacks the available aliphatic amine-and-aromatic organization repeatedly present in the higher-scoring seed-0, seed-2 and Parent leaders. The generator already makes such amines elsewhere, and nitrogen-containing seed-1 relatives show that merely adding nitrogen is not sufficient.
The cyclic-amine leaders leave stereochemical relationships at substituted saturated and benzylic centres unspecified; no enantiomer or diastereomer preference can be inferred.
The score record supplies no protonation or binding-pose information. Zero charge-string incidence cannot be interpreted as a lack of protonatable chemistry.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial best is 0.01904115112334333. Very low optimizer products include seed-0 evaluation 25, an N-sulfonyl pyrrolidine ester at 0.00016747245492913543, and seed-1 evaluation 33, a sulfonamide-bearing pyrrolidine/amide-acid fragment at 0.0006926945710016989. In contrast, the seed-0 and seed-2 upper range accompanies a nonacylated cyclic tertiary amine positioned between or near hydrophobic aromatic regions. This is a repeated association, not a measured binding mode or proof that an amine is sufficient: seed 1's nitrogen-free leader is well above its early lows, its nitrogen-containing acid-chloride relative at evaluation 263 scores 0.731564594156626, and the seed-2 final sulfur/amine-rich product scores 0.3544714456182126. Parent leaders score 0.9999989177995104 / 0.9969753164881906 / 0.9999934235240012 and all retain available aliphatic amines on flexible, cyclic or fused aryl arrangements. The corresponding recency-only leaders also retain aryl/amine combinations; the uniform-live-only seed-0 leader is an ordinary biaryl azetidine, while its other leaders are more complex ring systems. The Child seed-1 absence of a basic nitrogen among its leading constitution is a descriptive chemical difference, not proof that either retention or sampling caused its lower endpoint.

per_task.generated_character: The evaluated products range from one to 71 heavy atoms, median 31, with median five perceived rings and two aromatic rings; ring-digit and aromatic-text incidences are 0.9517 and 0.9253. The seed-0 leader at evaluation 233, score 0.18867027068276818, is a 23-heavy-atom annulated aromatic N system connected to a nine-membered N-alkyl dicarbonyl ring. Seed 1 evaluation 175, 0.18753249934291275, has 33 heavy atoms and six perceived rings: a quinoline-like aromatic ether region connected to a densely bridged amine/lactam/urea-like cage with an acetyl group. Seed 2 evaluation 241, 0.21177936240075523, has 27 heavy atoms, alkyl substituents, an aromatic-labelled N-containing annulated system and a cyclic N-methyl dicarbonyl group; RDKit perceives rings of sizes six, seven and nine. The enlarged aromatic-labelled ring is a geometry/aromaticity question rather than proof of a conventional aromatic scaffold. All three leaders are free of direct N/O-halogen and O-O bonds. Their local carbonyl/amine chemistry is recognizable, but the medium-ring and cage connectivities leave synthetic plausibility uncertain.
liabilities: Medium rings, cross-links and dense ring junctions complicate conformational and synthetic interpretation. The seed-2 nine-membered aromatic-labelled N ring deserves explicit scrutiny.
The 51-heavy-atom terminal coupled product has duplicated carbonyl/N-rich regions and is worse-scoring than the compact leader; larger size is not evidence of useful chemical coverage.
The leading examples demonstrate that direct heteroatom-halogen bonds are not necessary for the upper observed scores here, although such bonds occur elsewhere in the evaluated set.
missing_features: The Child does not consistently recover the upper observed aromatic/carbonyl/amine organization of the Parent across its seeds. These features themselves are present; their productive arrangement and alternatives are the coverage gap.
The cage and enlarged-ring families lack independent geometric or synthetic support. Straightforward functional groups embedded in a parseable graph do not establish a feasible complete molecule.
The seed-1 cage leaves its potentially stereogenic junctions unspecified; the trajectories cannot assign a score penalty to that omission.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial fused N-dicarbonyl/arene molecule at evaluation 7 scores 0.1678386594791329. The upper range retains combined aromatic and carbonyl/nitrogen organization; it is only modestly separated from this initial example. Tiny proposals including seed-0 evaluation 265, water, and seed-1 evaluation 197, hydrazine, score zero. More elaboration is not uniformly favorable: the seed-2 final 51-heavy-atom coupled assembly scores 0.15510900536560693, below its 27-heavy-atom leader. Replacing a leader carbonyl environment by an imino environment in seed-2 evaluation 274 gives 0.20115274729832738; this illustrates tolerated local variation without proving a unique required group. Parent leaders score 0.2258403994203931 / 0.2214095461892601 / 0.22600312875247064, and retain alkylated aromatic N systems linked to cyclic carbonyl/amine frameworks at 34, 32 and 29 heavy atoms. Recency-only leaders occupy related medium-ring aromatic/carbonyl families; uniform-live-only leaders also include enlarged or caged variants. All three Child endpoints are lower than their matched Parent observations despite many perceived cores. The record supports sensitivity to connectivity and functional-group arrangement, not ring abundance alone.

per_task.generated_character: The products range from one to 50 heavy atoms, median 26, with median four perceived rings but only one aromatic ring. Ring-digit incidence is 0.8644 and aromatic-text incidence 0.6425, so this set is substantially less uniformly aromatic than the other tasks; it is not ring-poor. Seed 0 evaluation 194, score 0.49469115575536243, is a 28-heavy-atom N-rich fused dione with a fluorinated cyclopropyl group and fluoroethyl substituent, including a constrained fused four-membered connection. Seed 1 evaluation 188, 0.4987766923969328, is a 25-heavy-atom wholly nonaromatic thiourea/hydrazone-like assembly with a partially unsaturated hydroxy carbocycle, a fluorohydroxy cyclopropene and a fluorinated small imine-containing N ring. Seed 2 evaluation 280, 0.5551603988142229, is a 25-heavy-atom bridged or annulated amino carbocycle/N-dicarbonyl system with carbon-bound fluorine and two N-F bonds; the perceived ring sizes are five, seven, seven and eight. This is distinct seed chemistry rather than a single aromatic family, but the constrained unsaturation, unusual N bonds and stereochemical omissions make the leaders questionable synthesis targets.
liabilities: The seed-2 leader has two N-F bonds, while seed-0 and seed-1 leaders instead expose small constrained ring connections or unsaturation. Removing one bond flag alone would not resolve all chemistry concerns.

There are 43 molecules with a ring carbon carrying two double bonds, and the supplied cumulated-double-bond string incidence is 0.0552; these different graph and text definitions must not be conflated.

The set includes 86 products with at most three heavy atoms, and 573 products with possible unassigned tetrahedral centres. Neither a high ring count nor RDKit parsing establishes stability, stereochemical identity or synthesis.
missing_features: The Child does not consistently reach the higher observed compact fluorinated polar-group arrangements of the Parent, but fluorination, carbonyls, amines and N heterocycles are already available. The records do not identify a unique missing group.

Plausible ring geometry is not consistently combined with the favored local polar/fluorinated environments. Carbon-bound fluorine without N-F is present in strong examples, so direct N-fluorination cannot be treated as a chemical necessity.
The multiple fluorinated ring centres and junctions lack stereochemical specification, and no matched stereoisomer or molecular-state comparison is available.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial best, evaluation 7, scores 0.0020944534688323298; the shared initial thiourea/hydrazone example at evaluation 3 is only 4.620656635650526e-15. The upper observed range accompanies compact fluorinated N/O/S-containing ring frameworks rather than isolated halogens or unrestricted molecular growth. Seed-1 evaluation 153, F, scores 1.1043196211273875e-26, while the seed-0 50-heavy-atom doubled carbonyl/N-ring assembly at evaluation 56 scores 2.1720424118142743e-25. Seed-0's final four-heavy-atom unsaturated oxygen ring scores 5.554325974994788e-20. Aromaticity and N-F are not universal requirements: the seed-1 leader has no perceived aromatic ring and neither seed-0 nor seed-1 leader has N-F. Parent leaders score 0.6510211907030741 / 0.4870057305679067 / 0.7208853668418119 and are fluorinated imino/carbonyl N systems; the strongest Parent example lacks N-F but contains problematic cyclic cumulation and an enlarged aromatic-labelled ring. The Child seed-1 observation is higher than its Parent, while the other two are lower. Recency-only leaders retain fluorinated imino/carbonyl families; uniform-live-only includes a carbon-bound-fluorinated dione without N-F at 0.6054403589897509 and an N-fluorinated thiourea/hydrazone at 0.4438102388357315. These mixed counterexamples prevent a target motif or aromaticity prescription based on one seed.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This gap was recorded in n-c55c3d520a2c, reproduced by n-62daf219c70a and remains in n-2e9e08198747 on the matched epoch-1 Search panel, seeds 0, 1 and 2, with 300 observations per objective and ten-member batches. Direct N-halogen / O-halogen / O-O record counts are 489 / 145 / 114 in the current 4,350 products versus 1,042 / 278 / 273 in the Parent. Current leaders include N-F carboxamides, O-F and O-Cl groups, while conventional carbon-bound-fluorine cyclic amines, a tertiary aromatic carboxamide and halogen-free carbonyl leaders are counterexamples. The original component comparators have their own different flag counts and leaders; a lower aggregate flag count does not establish improved chemistry or score.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve conventional local bond environments within otherwise recognizable aromatic, carbonyl and amine frameworks.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide environment-aware local alternatives that preserve functional relationships supported by accepted task-local feedback. Distinguish carbon-bound halogens from direct N/O-halogen bonds, and assess N-O, N-N and sulfur groups in their actual environment. These are candidate chemical capabilities to test, not evidence for blanket filtering, a guaranteed score benefit or attribution to either changed component.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The geometry gap originates in n-c55c3d520a2c through n-62daf219c70a and is re-observed under the current complete matched panel. Current products include 41 ring-triple-bond-bearing molecules and 61 with a ring carbon carrying two double bonds, versus Parent 17 and 42. Leaders include cyclic triple bonds, an enlarged aromatic-labelled N ring, small unsaturated rings and dense bridges. Ordinary azetidine and pyrrolidine aryl amines also score highly, and near-scoring alternatives lack some flagged bonds; small rings or fused systems are therefore not uniformly problematic.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently distinguish a valid ring graph from a geometrically and synthetically credible ring construction.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make local unsaturation, ring size, bridge connectivity and molecular state available to a task-agnostic assessment of proposed topology changes. Explore feasible alternatives preserving feedback-supported polar and aromatic relationships. Ring digits, aromatic labels, generic core counts and founder reachability supply no physical geometry evidence; neither a blanket ring ban nor component-specific causality follows.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This source gap was present in n-c55c3d520a2c and the reproduced n-62daf219c70a baseline, and is directly re-observed in n-2e9e08198747 at the matched current budget. The current evaluated stream spans one to 113 heavy atoms, with 299 products at most three heavy atoms versus Parent 99, recency-only 105 and uniform-live-only 134. A terminal 51-heavy-atom coupled assembly scores 0.15510900536560693 below its 27-heavy-atom leader at 0.21177936240075523. Tiny products reach near-zero or zero scores in several objective sessions, but a small ether scores 0.5 in another, so the meaning of fragmentation depends on feedback. Compact conventional aryl amines remain strong counterexamples to a universal demand for larger structures.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator lacks consistent control of molecular-context loss and excessive elaboration while producing chemical alternatives.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Use accepted local feedback to preserve useful connected functional-group context through deletion, growth and replacement. Evaluate both simplifying and scaffold-changing alternatives without a universal minimum size or a preference for growth. These observations concern evaluated output only; they do not establish that useful unselected alternatives were unavailable, identify a retention or sampling mediator, or authorize rescue tuning of the ended fixed combination.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This identity gap was recorded for n-c55c3d520a2c, reproduced by n-62daf219c70a and persists across the current matched Search seeds and profile. All current task digest stereocentre incidences are 0.0, and no stereo markers occur in the read trajectories. RDKit identifies possible unassigned tetrahedral centres in 2,446 of 4,350 current optimizer products versus 2,408 Parent products, including substituted cyclic amines, fluorinated carbocycles and bridged junctions. Available neutral amines are present despite zero charge incidence. No matched stereoisomer comparison or configurational-stability assessment is supplied.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator leaves many potentially stereogenic constitutions without an explicit stereochemical identity.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve or deliberately resolve stereochemical state when the generated constitution requires it, with explicit exceptions for achiral or configurationally unstable cases. Treat protonation, alkene geometry and tautomerism separately. The evidence establishes incomplete specification, not an objective-specific preferred state, a measured score penalty or the contribution of a particular algorithm component.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The conditional leading-family coverage gap was recorded in n-c55c3d520a2c and its n-62daf219c70a baseline and remains qualified rather than absolute in n-2e9e08198747. Current evaluated products have 2,005 typed and 1,327 generic nonempty Murcko cores, versus Parent 1,850 and 1,117; recency-only has 1,782 and 1,055, and uniform-live-only 2,060 and 1,403. Recurrent aromatic-carbonyl, cyclic-amine and fluorinated heterocyclic leaders coexist with real seed-family differences, tiny fragments, unusual aromatic-labelled rings and highly elaborated structures. These descriptors show perceived topology coverage, not retained founder atoms, chemical independence, feasibility or a mediator of endpoint differences.
transferable_gaps.gap: Many distinct graph topologies do not translate into consistently demonstrated plausible alternatives to the leading chemical family.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Judge alternative scaffolds by preserved functional relationships, credible connectivity and actual accepted feedback, rather than string novelty, founder-union size or generic-core novelty alone. The generator already changes ring topology; the missing capability is reliable useful and plausible coverage. Preserve the original node/profile conditions and counterexamples when transferring this gap, and do not split the joint output into separate component value.

nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

approach.method_basis: The Parent learns a recurrent molecular prior and chooses its prepared checkpoint by fixed-noise ancestral valid, connected, distinct molecular yield, with heldout token loss breaking ties. Each objective starts an adaptable copy of that prior and an accepted-only archive; trajectory-balance updates with a learned normalizer and fixed-prior regularization transfer real graph feedback into later neural sampling. One direct neural batch alternates with two graph batches. Accepted neural molecules refresh a score-ranked breeding population and supply a protected descendant at the first graph handoff. Connected-fragment crossover and atom/bond mutations construct temporary novel offspring pools, and accepted-score fingerprint posterior function draws choose the remaining evaluations. The atom-replacement mutation currently changes one element at one site, so moving a ring nitrogen while retaining composition requires multiple separately sampled substitutions.
approach.novelty: Extend the existing atom-replacement menu with a direct positional exchange between a pyridine-like nitrogen and a hydrogen-bearing carbon in the same aromatic six-member ring. The exchange moves the nitrogen while preserving the formula, ring connectivity and substituent attachment positions, making a new local arrangement available in one edit. Earlier Children in this lineage changed prior preparation, replay, flow credit or neural sampling. This Child changes graph generation. A previous graph-walk experiment established that this exchange can yield scored positional isomers but exposed very few of them and missed its score target; the new question is whether the Parent's larger temporary pools and posterior selection turn that same positional channel into useful accepted descendants.

nodes.hypothesis: Extend the existing graph replace_atom option menu with a direct formula-preserving exchange of a neutral aromatic nitrogen and a hydrogen-bearing aromatic carbon in the same six-member ring, retaining the ring connectivity and substituent attachment framework.

finding_summary.headline: Nitrogen exchange yields 20 evaluated positional isomers; endpoint scores rise while direct yield stays weak
finding_summary.insights:
Larger temporary pools successfully expose this conserved-composition channel to real evaluation, but they do not establish that the posterior favors it: 19 of 315 positional alternatives were selected, or 6.03%, compared with the overall pool allocation of 6.25%. Most constructed alternatives therefore remain unscored. The clean cases show that moving a nitrogen can improve a particular accepted molecule, while their negative average and the nearly unchanged total parent-beating count rule out a general improvement in direct offspring yield in this panel. The registered parent-relative yield prediction is contradicted even though physical activation and the endpoint score target are established.

The endpoint gain cannot be assigned to those five local wins. Expanded menus change stochastic search paths and pool competition, and accepted descendants can subsequently breed and train the policy. The evidence does not separate those continuing effects from the immediate nitrogen relocation. The molecular assessment also places a limit on the chemical interpretation: useful ring and functional-group arrangements coexist with reactive peripheral groups, unusual ring geometry and unspecified stereochemistry. Preserving formula and attachments can preserve those liabilities as well. The remaining question is which local positional contexts merit evaluation; neither a universally favorable nitrogen position nor improved synthetic plausibility is demonstrated.
finding_summary.results:
The exchange ran 397 times. Every construction preserved molecular formula, bond connectivity and the qualifying aromatic ring; 341 products were different positional isomers and 56 were symmetry-equivalent to their immediate source. Ordinary novelty checks admitted 315 distinct positional alternatives to temporary pools and reserved one for a protected handoff. The posterior selected 19 of those 315 alternatives, and the protected product was also evaluated, establishing 20 accepted positional isomers. One further evaluated molecule contained a symmetry-equivalent exchange after crossover and is excluded from that activation count. All 150 protected handoffs and every announced batch remained valid.

Fourteen evaluated positional isomers came from an accepted parent followed by exactly one exchange. Five beat that parent and nine lost, with a mean score change of -0.030970. All fourteen entered the immediate survivor population, twelve later served as generating parents, and one increased the running best score by 0.000290. The six positional isomers produced after crossover all scored below their best recorded generating parent; their immediate crossed sources were unscored. Across the entire graph channel, strict parent-beating descendants slipped from 452 to 449 of 2,850, and mean child-minus-best-parent score worsened from -0.089170 to -0.103903.

Despite that weak direct yield, the complete three-seed endpoint mean rose from 0.550198 to 0.587094. Paired gains were 0.052557, 0.021169 and 0.036962, giving a mean gain of 0.036896, above the registered 0.002 target. Deco hop, median and sitagliptin means increased; zaleplon and DRD2 means decreased slightly. All 4,350 generated submissions were accepted within the supplied 4,500-evaluation panel.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich medicinal scaffolds coexist with reactive heteroatom bonds, unusual ring geometry and unspecified stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: All five objectives have complete supplied trajectories, with 900 records and 870 optimizer proposals per objective. The molecules include linked and fused heteroaromatics, saturated cyclic amines, aryl sulfonamides, lactams, ethers, imidates and fluorinated urea/hydrazine chains. This is broad chemical exploration with concentrated upper-score families, rather than a shortage of rings or nitrogen. In the fixed objective order, the digest ring-closure presence rates are 0.9874, 0.9885, 0.992, 0.9943 and 0.9874; aromatic-token presence rates are 0.9782, 0.977, 0.9655, 0.9667 and 0.8437. These are fractions of proposal strings containing the markers, not fractions of their atoms that are aromatic. Read-only RDKit perception of the full optimizer trajectories gives median heavy-atom counts of 25, 31, 30, 33 and 25, and median ring counts of 3, 4, 4, 4 and 2. The corresponding Parent medians are 25, 36, 30, 32 and 24 heavy atoms, and 3, 4, 4, 4 and 3 rings. Nonchiral Murcko scaffold counts in the current proposals are 655, 600, 588, 641 and 532, although many represent local ring edits or enlarged assemblies rather than independent useful core families. Conventional makeable-looking fragments coexist with N-Cl bonds, O-O bonds, imines, hydrazine-derived linkages, strained small rings, conjugated enlarged rings and highly charged oxygen environments. The digest stereocentre-marker rate is 0.0 on every objective; graph perception finds potential tetrahedral centres in 232, 363, 601, 280 and 493 optimizer proposals respectively. Thus unspecified stereochemistry is a real representational gap, rather than evidence that the molecules are all achiral. Synthetic plausibility and drug likeness are mixed. The recorded scores support chemical associations within these samples; they do not establish a synthesis, a binding pose, or a causal contribution from any particular generator edit.

per_task.generated_character: The dominant upper family has a phenyl ring joining a diazine bearing an imidate or imine to a conjugated seven-member oxygen ring. The two highest digest examples each have 24 heavy atoms, two aromatic six-member rings and one nonaromatic seven-member oxepin-like ring. Other high entries replace the imidate with an amidine-containing aryl ether, change diazine nitrogen positions, or use a methoxyindole-carbonyl-imidazole-pyridyl assembly. These are moderately sized, largely unsaturated molecules, with polar groups placed on an extended ring framework. Their functional groups are chemically recognizable, but the imidates, imines and conjugated enol-ether ring make stability and synthetic handling less routine than for ordinary aryl amides. The full proposal median is 25 heavy atoms and three rings; tiny fragments and much larger branched structures also occur. Compared with the Parent, the upper chemistry shifts from fused aza-ring/amide and unusual sulfur-containing families toward linked diazine/oxygen-ring imidates. The median aromatic-ring count falls from three in the Parent to two here, while median total ring count stays at three.
liabilities: The leading imidate/imine and conjugated oxygen-ring combinations warrant scrutiny for hydrolysis, tautomerism and chemical stability; their recorded scores do not measure these properties.

Late examples introduce ring expansion, a small imine-containing ring or thiol substitution without retaining the highest recorded scores. Increased ring or heteroatom complexity is not itself evidence of improved chemistry.
The full proposals include N-Cl and O-O bonds, and the large low-score assemblies can contain multiple unspecified stereocentres.
missing_features: The lowest fragments lack the connected aromatic framework and polar handles shared by the upper families; the largest poor examples lack their moderate size and limited elaboration. Those features are not preserved consistently across the output.

The upper excerpt shows conventional carbonyl chemistry mainly in a separate indole family, while the dominant linked-ring series relies on imidates, imines and amidines. Equally favorable, chemically varied polar-group arrangements within that same linked framework are not established by the shown molecules.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The digest span is 0.0 to 0.49065338146265813, with median 0.163735. The two cited diazine nitrogen positional isomers tie at 0.49065338146265813, so these examples do not show a universal preference for relocating a ring nitrogen. The analogous imine scores 0.4786541264696099, and the alternate diazine imidate scores 0.4789131426105757. Contracting the oxygen ring gives 0.46746448265590934; the cited less-unsaturated seven-member version gives 0.38212123769975087. The separate indole-carbonyl family reaches 0.4586023950591373. Together these observations favor a moderate molecular size and particular ring/polar-group arrangements, with both heteroatom placement and saturation mattering locally. Methane scores 0.0, whereas a 50-heavy-atom multiring amide/ether assembly scores 2.2628488414681176e-49. Neither minimal fragments nor accumulation of rings and polar groups reproduces the upper-score chemistry.

per_task.generated_character: The upper excerpt is concentrated on an anilinoquinazoline-like scaffold: a fused aromatic diazine/benzene system linked through NH to a substituted phenyl ring. Methoxy or other alkoxy groups, halogens and a terminal aryl formaldimine recur. The highest example has 28 heavy atoms and three aromatic six-member rings, but also an O-N(Cl)-ethyl substituent containing both N-O and N-Cl bonds. A simpler dimethoxy member has 24 heavy atoms. The fused aza core, arylamine link and ordinary ethers are plausible synthetic building blocks; the N-chlorinated hydroxylamine ether and formaldimine are less conventional final medicinal functionality. Another trajectory ends with nitrogen-dense fused systems, small fused rings and multiple explicitly negative oxygens. The current full median is 31 heavy atoms and four rings, compared with 36 heavy atoms and four rings in the Parent. The Parent upper chemistry included larger linked quinazoline-like systems and carbonyl-bearing piperazine derivatives, so the current prominent family is a smaller connected aza-aromatic arrangement, not newly acquired aromaticity.

Some final structures combine heavily fused small rings with alkoxide-like and N-O anions; the cited multiply negative molecule has no accompanying counterion in its SMILES. Charge and valence validity do not establish a plausible dominant chemical state.

transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make candidate construction sensitive to complete local functional-group environments, including the atoms bonded to nitrogen, oxygen, sulfur and halogens. Retain access to conventional stable alternatives when varying an accepted core, so exploration does not depend on adding reactive heteroatom-halogen or heteroatom-heteroatom bonds. Learn any objective-value tradeoff from accepted feedback; these chemical concerns alone do not establish that blanket exclusions would improve scores.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every digest stereocentre-marker rate is 0.0. Direct graph perception finds potential tetrahedral centres in 232, 363, 601, 280 and 493 optimizer proposals in the fixed objective order. The cited compact amino-substituted tricycle, aziridine-containing polycycle and leading fluorinated urea/hydrazine chain all contain unspecified tetrahedral centres.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not express stereochemical alternatives for the many potentially chiral structures it emits.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Represent and preserve stereochemical assignments when constructing or changing potentially stereogenic centres, and make chemically feasible configurations available as distinct alternatives where the evaluation interface distinguishes them. Changes in configuration should be separable from changes in connectivity. The supplied observations establish missing specification, not a preferred stereoisomer or a guaranteed score benefit.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The quoted upper molecules include a ten-member conjugated aza-lactam marked aromatic by graph perception, a seven-member cyclic cumulene, aziridine-containing polycycles and several heavily fused small-ring systems. Ring-token presence is already close to universal, and normal phenyl, heteroaryl and cyclic-amine motifs are also present. The missing property is control over ring geometry, not the ability to close rings.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring construction does not consistently constrain conjugation and ring geometry to chemically credible alternatives.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Explore ring size, fusion, bond order and saturation with attention to the resulting geometry and functional-group compatibility. Keep conventional ring alternatives available while preserving useful attachment positions, and distinguish changes in ring topology from peripheral decoration. Aromatic notation and valence sanitization should not be treated as proof of a feasible conformation or easy synthesis.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A fluorinated urea/hydrazine pair has the same C14H17F3IN3O3 formula but scores 0.49702898037063575 and 0.42289529223448297 when fluorine is distributed differently between chain and aryl ring. Adding a consecutive nitrogen to a related chain gives 0.1359300194081745 instead of 0.4779789711749196. Elsewhere, two ring-nitrogen positional isomers tie at 0.49065338146265813. The upper amine/aromatic series repeatedly differs from low amide-, sulfonamide- or pyrrole-nitrogen examples in nitrogen accessibility and bonding context. These observations support context-dependent placement, not a universal benefit from another heteroatom or any single relocation.
transferable_gaps.gap: Useful functional-group position and electronic context are not reliably retained across molecular edits.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide coordinated alternatives for functional-group orientation, linker position and heteroatom placement while retaining a coherent core and comparable molecular scale. Distinguish accessible amines from amide, sulfonamide, aromatic and hydrazine nitrogen rather than treating element count as the relevant chemical property. Allow current-session observations to determine which local arrangements matter, without encoding a named target or fixed target-specific functional-group recipe.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The zero-score excerpts include methane, acetylene, a 25-heavy-atom acyclic polyamine and 70- or 83-heavy-atom multigroup assemblies. A 50-heavy-atom multiring amide/ether assembly receives 2.2628488414681176e-49. In contrast, quoted upper families include a 23-heavy-atom amine tricycle, a 24-heavy-atom fluorinated polar chain and a 37-heavy-atom sulfonylpiperazine/aza-lactam. These different useful sizes show that neither universal shrinking nor multiplying whole favorable motifs is an adequate chemical rule.
transferable_gaps.gap: Size-changing moves do not consistently preserve a useful connected arrangement of rings, linkers and polar groups.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make growth, contraction and linker changes preserve a recognizable connected core and the relationships among its aromatic, amine and carbonyl groups. Maintain alternatives at multiple chemically coherent scales, with current accepted observations determining the useful size range. Treat fragmentation to tiny pieces and wholesale concatenation as distinct chemistry from controlled local elaboration.

nodes.method_name: Genetic GFN: reciprocal learning between a flow policy and graph search
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Genetic GFN: alternately generate molecules with a GFlowNet policy, refine the resulting scored population through graph crossover and mutation, and distill scored descendants back into the policy using rank-weighted off-policy replay. The policy uses trajectory balance with a learned log normalizer and regularization toward a frozen prior. [Kim et al., Section 3](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.05961v4) describe this mechanism. Train the prior only on the permitted unlabeled corpus. Each objective starts with clean policy adaptation, replay and population state initialized from its supplied observations. Use a positive terminal reward increasing with the observed maximization score. Schedule policy and genetic phases around the evaluator's announced feedback; both produce new molecules, and all reward-bearing training records come from accepted observations. Later policy samples must enter genetic populations, and accepted graph descendants must affect subsequent policy updates. Generate further valid, canonical-unique structures to fill announced batches, without corpus ranking or a fixed molecular library. The hypothesis is that learned global proposals propagate local discoveries into new promising regions and then support further graph refinement, raising the mean of five independent final Top-1 scores. Published larger-budget gains do not establish that this reciprocal learning becomes useful quickly enough here.

approach.method_basis: The Parent trains a recurrent SMILES language model on an unlabeled molecular corpus and starts each objective with a fresh policy copied from that frozen prior. Each accepted batch supplies its highest-scoring half, joined by the strongest eligible original strings from a memory of thirty-two earlier elites. Historical fitting weights decrease with previous training exposure while current and historical groups retain their total loss shares. The policy fits weighted squared error toward frozen-prior sequence log likelihood plus sixty times accepted reward, projecting each positive target independently to zero, using bounded clipped Adam updates and retaining the final policy. It then samples complete SMILES directly from the adapted policy and submits the first valid, canonically novel identities in sample order, refilling when necessary and discarding surplus draws.
approach.novelty: Add progressive spacing of repeated molecular cores during admission. The first new molecule with a ring-and-linker core is admitted immediately. Once that core occupies k places in the current batch, its next admission requires k+1 further distinct valid draws of that core; intervening draws are discarded. Other newly encountered cores can therefore reach the same batch, while a dominant core remains admissible and no randomness is added. Earlier siblings diversified retained training memory or balanced choices of breeding parents. This change acts directly on fresh policy samples before oracle submission, leaving both training membership rules and token generation intact. Same-stream admission receipts will show whether additional cores actually reach evaluation. The earlier diversity experiments also warn that spacing a productive family can weaken exploitation.

nodes.hypothesis: Deterministically thin repeated atom/bond-typed Murcko cores within each suggestion: after k molecules of a core have been emitted, admit its next member only on the (k+1)-th distinct valid canonical-novel draw of that core since its preceding emission, resetting that per-core interval after admission; first occurrences and identity-keyed acyclic or extraction-fallback draws pass immediately.

finding_summary.headline: Core thinning delivered broader molecular batches, but final Top-1 fell despite higher AUC.
finding_summary.insights:
The experiment resolves the delivery question: additional cores already present in fresh policy samples can reach the oracle without losing the first-come batch's core support. That delivery was often unproductive. Of the 242 additional core representatives, only six improved the actual incumbent: four on zaleplon and two on docking. Deco-hop received 116 additional core representatives without an incumbent improvement from any of them. Its previously dominant phenyl/anilinoquinazoline core was evaluated 54 times instead of 160 and reached a lower best score. This is compatible with diluted exploitation, although unscored discarded molecules cannot identify the value of any particular forgone proposal.

Coverage is also a poor predictor of the magnitude of the final change. Sitagliptin gained only seven batch-level cores yet had the largest mean endpoint loss. Admission changes alter later feedback and therefore later generated streams; a same-stream comparison isolates immediate delivery, not the complete search that would have followed different admissions. The higher AUC and lower endpoint further separate earlier progress from the final objective.

The chemical assessment narrows what broader coverage did not repair. Productive functional-group attachment arrangements remain inconsistently preserved, and the many structures with potential stereochemistry still have no specified configurations. Those are open chemical capabilities, not established causes of this score loss. Useful next evidence would need to show that broader admission preserves productive local series or transfers their attachment chemistry, rather than using core count as a proxy for usefulness. The utility claim is rejected while the admission and delivery mechanism is confirmed.
finding_summary.results:
The admission mechanism ran correctly and changed which constitutional cores reached evaluation. Across 435 batches, it rejected 436 eligible repeated-core draws in 167 batches. Comparing each recorded stream with its first ten valid novel structures, actual batches gained cores 159 times and never lost a previously represented core. Mean core count increased from 9.106 to 9.662, delivering 242 additional batch-level core representatives and changing 304 canonical output identities. Mean core concentration fell from 0.133 to 0.110. All state transitions, original-string provenance and paired behavior before the first intervention passed the passive audit.

All fifteen task sessions completed their budgets. Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.522705 to 0.508247, a paired change of -0.014458 against the required +0.002 increase. Seed changes were +0.009826, -0.032176 and -0.021023; population dispersion across seed scores changed from 0.020072 to 0.019593. Task mean changes were -0.014692 for zaleplon, -0.014459 for deco-hop, -0.005454 for median-2 and -0.037685 for sitagliptin; docking decreased by only 0.000000211 near its ceiling. Recorded mean AUC nevertheless rose from 0.405593 to 0.430066, chiefly through earlier progress on docking and zaleplon.

Broader batches required more work. Raw draws increased from 35,568 to 36,880, and batches needing extra sampling increased from 16 to 28. Raw duplication rose from 32.21% to 34.50%, while validity fell from 91.79% to 91.11%. No generation limit was exhausted. Recorded generation time rose from 24.75 to 37.90 seconds across the panel, including 10.38 seconds for core extraction and 0.52 seconds for receipts; the interval gate itself took 0.009 seconds.
