molecular.headline: Ring-rich medicinal scaffolds with closed-shell atom assignments, but undefined stereochemistry, fragile handles and uneven appendage growth.
molecular.overall_character: The complete seeds 0, 1 and 2 were read for every objective in the supplied order; tasks_without_trajectories is empty. Each task contributes 900 accepted records, including 870 optimizer appearances. The digest initial excerpt shows seed 0 and its final excerpt shows seed 2; those excerpts are not the whole seed panel. All Child and Parent trajectory files were inspected passively. Across 4,350 Child optimizer appearances, RDKit 2023.09.6 perceives a median of 26 heavy atoms and three rings, with a heavy-atom range of 4 to 90. The digest ring-closure rates run from 0.9805 to 0.9977 and aromatic-text occurrence rates from 0.9460 to 0.9966; these are fractions of SMILES containing those features, not fractions of atoms that are aromatic. Aromatic amides, quinazolines, piperazines and other cyclic amines, sulfones/sulfonamides, ethers and halogenated aryl groups are prominent. Nonaromatic rings occur in 1,841 appearances, so this is not exclusively flat aromatic chemistry. The medicinal motifs make many individual structures apparently makeable, but the whole output also contains overgrown chains, repeated polar groups and reactive or form-sensitive attachments. That supports questionable synthetic plausibility and moderate drug-likeness for the collection, without asserting a synthetic route or experimental property. The 2,811 distinct nonempty atom/bond-typed Murcko cores indicate broad overall graph exploration; enrichment of the strongest molecules in narrower families remains visible. Core counts retain linker and heteroatom distinctions and do not measure diversity of biological activity. The Child has zero positive RDKit radical-electron assignments versus six Parent appearances, while 315 Child appearances contain formal atomic charges and 1,058 contain sulfur. This is a molecular-representation observation only. All tasks have a stereocentre-text rate of 0.0; passive perception nevertheless finds 870 Child appearances with at least one unassigned carbon stereocentre, and no explicit tetrahedral or bond-stereochemical text. Eleven complete task/seed molecular-score sequences match the Parent exactly; four differ, with unchanged endpoint identities in two of those. No mechanism-activation or score-utility decision is made. The reproducible passive counts, digest-to-trajectory checks, file hashes and per-seed comparisons are in r0012-08-improve-L03-molecular.audit.py and r0012-08-improve-L03-molecular.audit.json beside this report.

per_task.generated_character: Mostly medium-sized aromatic amides: optimizer heavy atoms have median 24 and range 4-90, with median three rings. The ring/aromatic text rates are 0.9908/0.9839. The strongest digest structure, O=C(NCc1ccccn1)c1cccc(Cn2ccccc2=O)c1, is a three-ring benzamide joining a pyridylmethyl group and an N-substituted pyridone. Other strong molecules include acetamido-indole carboxamides, anilinopyridine carboxamides, sulfinamides and an O-benzyl hydroxamate. These are recognizable medicinal motifs, although their exact molecular forms and synthesis have not been demonstrated. Seed 0 retains the indole-amide endpoint at 0.43351949803907636 and seed 1 the pyridone-containing benzamide at 0.4767312946227961. Both full streams match the Parent. Seed 2 ends with a best value of 0.39128611874634317 in a substituted diarylamide/urea family, whereas the Parent reached 0.5 with a compact heteroaryl-ether carboxanilide. That Parent structure is described from its trajectory rather than quoted because it is absent from this digest. The Child contains a much larger long-chain tail: 15 optimizer strings have an uninterrupted C run of at least 10, versus one in the Parent.
liabilities: Long hydrocarbon tails inflate size and flexibility; the worst set includes a very long-chain sulfonium species as well as long neutral amides. Closed-shell atom assignments do not resolve these liabilities.

The high-scoring sulfinamide/imidic-acid representations and hydroxamate show unresolved form-sensitive chemistry. Their presence is not evidence that all such bonds are unstable or synthetically inaccessible.
missing_features: Reliable retention of compact aryl/heteroaryl carbonyl arrangements during appendage changes is missing from much of the stream, especially the seed-2 long-chain excursion. The examples do not identify a unique absent target scaffold.

Defined configurations are missing for eligible stereogenic variants: 118 optimizer appearances have an unassigned carbon centre. Their scores do not establish that configuration assignment alone would improve this objective.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The observed gradient favors compact, organized aromatic carbonyl/heteroatom arrangements over indiscriminate chain growth. The best benzamide scores 0.4767312946227961; adding the digest phenol substituent gives 0.44383095403034933, so additional hydrogen-bond functionality is not automatically rewarded. The final decanoyl diarylamide scores 0.000005647693002104746, while the neighboring shorter branched-acyl analogues score 0.34072682485201594 and 0.34977917230128097; the halogen differences make these associations rather than a fully controlled series. The extremely long-chain amides in the worst excerpt score 0.0. The O-benzyl hydroxamate still reaches 0.4629100498862757 and the sulfinamide 0.4531317717091581, so the evidence does not justify removing every N-O bond or sulfur-containing group. The digest median is 0.076866.

per_task.generated_character: This panel is especially aromatic and heavily decorated: median 32 heavy atoms, median four rings, and ring/aromatic text rates 0.9977/0.9966. Halogens occur in 0.7207 of optimizer SMILES. All twelve best digest entries are seed-2 anilinoquinazoline analogues with methoxy groups, fluorinated phenyl substituents and variable alkyl, alkoxy, amino, nitrile or extra aryl appendages. These cores are apparently plausible medicinal chemistry, with substantial flat aromatic surface. The full other seeds also sample different nitrogen-rich aromatic and hydrazone families. Seed-0 and seed-1 recorded endpoints remain 0.5998615059406662 and 0.6263699396108253 with their Parent endpoint identities. Seed 2 reaches 0.6861742139310967 versus the Parent 0.6669492630755185. Its endpoint has 28 heavy atoms and three aromatic rings, whereas the Parent endpoint, also present in the Child digest, has 35 heavy atoms and four aromatic rings. Across the task, 353 distinct typed Murcko cores versus the Parent 355 show substantial exploration despite concentration among the best examples.
liabilities: Large aromatic surfaces and frequent halogens can create a solubility and lipophilicity burden; those properties were not measured here. The 90-heavy-atom extreme shows that overgrowth remains possible.
N-rich imine/hydrazone and other reactive-handle chemistry persists in the broader stream. Familiar ring systems and nonradical assignments alone do not establish a stable, tractable molecular form.
missing_features: The best excerpt does not demonstrate comparable success after replacing the anilinoquinazoline architecture with another ring topology; most of its high-score variation is decoration of that family. Broader raw core availability already exists.

The output lacks consistent control of appendage size and aromatic surface while keeping its useful heteroatom arrangement. No exact unobserved scaffold or pharmacophore can be inferred from this score landscape.
Explicit configurations are absent from the 103 appearances with perceived unassigned carbon stereocentres; the strongest pentan-3-yl example itself has no such carbon centre.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The trajectory supports anilino-fused diazine geometry with tuned peripheral decoration. CCC(CC)c1cc2c(Nc3ccc(F)c(F)c3)ncnc2c(OC)c1OC scores 0.6861742139310967; its trifluorophenyl analogue scores 0.6856617647058824. Adding a phenyl group to the latter core lowers the recorded value to 0.6695813460519343. The corresponding difluoro butoxy pair gives 0.6840559232542575 without the extra phenyl and 0.6666996765035981 with it. These close structural comparisons support restraint in aryl growth within this family, not a universal smaller-is-better rule. In contrast, the worst diaryl-quinoline sulfone/acid scores 0.28535067873303166 and an indole aryl ketone/sulfone scores 0.28799019607843135. Small dichlorostyrene and methyl isothiocyanate remain near 0.5, which also warns against reading that baseline as medicinal quality. The digest median is 0.5748.

per_task.generated_character: The strongest molecules combine several aryl surfaces with unacylated cyclic amines and alkyl linkers. Median size is 28 heavy atoms and three rings; ring/aromatic text rates are 0.9874/0.969. Seed 0 emphasizes aryl/benzyl piperazines, seed 1 benzofused cyclic amines and arylpiperazines connected to benzyl phenol/anisole groups, and seed 2 aryl ketones carrying a propoxy-piperidine appendage. In contrast with an absence-of-basic-nitrogen diagnosis, 490 optimizer appearances have an unacylated saturated ring-nitrogen structural proxy. The common amine, aryl and ketone/ether motifs are apparently makeable, although large flexible compounds and unusual side chains remain. All three complete molecular-score streams match the Parent. Their recorded endpoint values are 0.9999997933663268, 0.9999997851052089 and 0.9999991526291698.
liabilities: The O-CH2-Cl group is an electrophilic, potentially labile attachment rather than an ordinary aryl chloride. It occurs in four emitted appearances and remains present in a near-ceiling digest example.

Several strong molecules have long flexible linkers, multiple potentially protonatable amines and substantial hydrophobic aryl surface. Their SMILES are mostly formally neutral; that is not evidence that they remain neutral in solution.
missing_features: What is uneven is preservation of the favorable cyclic-amine/aryl attachment relationship, not availability of cyclic amines. Much of the lower-score stream acylates or sulfonylates nitrogen or changes that relationship.
Conservative attachment chemistry is missing even among the best-scoring molecules, as the chloromethyl ether demonstrates. Near-ceiling scores do not establish a stable medicinal form.
Stereochemical definition is absent for 190 appearances with perceived unassigned carbon centres. The cited endpoint structures do not require treating every molecule as tetrahedrally stereogenic.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best aryl/benzyl piperazine scores 0.9999997933663268, and the benzofused cyclic-amine/benzyl-phenol compound 0.9999997851052089. Poorer molecules often place nitrogen in amide or sulfonamide environments or fail to present the same amine/aryl relationship: the N-acylated piperidine carboxamide scores 0.000026715842904959654 and the sulfonyl-piperidine heteroaryl amide 0.000019828327575562915. The final structure retaining the propoxy-piperidine arm scores 0.999988872643426, whereas a smaller amino ketone without that arm scores 0.0035116287191461495; these also differ in linker constitution, so the arm is an association rather than an isolated causal feature. A longer ether/amide linker gives 0.5728095677025575, while multiple ordinary alkyl linker lengths are already close to the ceiling. Crucially, the chloromethyl-ether-bearing arylpiperazine still scores 0.9999994163676008. The reported score therefore does not itself screen out that reactive attachment. The digest median is 0.049032.

per_task.generated_character: Medium-sized, varied heterocyclic chemistry has median 24 heavy atoms and three rings, with ring/aromatic text rates 0.9908/0.9632. Piperazines, aryl sulfonamides, quinoline-like fused aromatics, benzodioxoles, ethers and lactam/carbonyl groups recur. The strongest digest molecule joins a methylquinoline sulfonyl group and a benzodioxole sulfonyl group across piperazine; its five perceived rings include three aromatic rings. Both piperazine nitrogens are sulfonylated, so calling this molecule a free basic piperazine would be wrong. Many conventional sulfonamide/piperazine connections look synthetically plausible, while the N-rich unsaturated ring and form-sensitive outliers require individual assessment. The task retains 732 typed Murcko cores, the same as the Parent. All three endpoint identities and values remain unchanged: 0.2125118592516207, 0.20428349275442803 and 0.2588686674995393; only the late seed-2 molecular sequence differs.
liabilities: Sulfonamide multiplication changes nitrogen basicity and adds substantial polar functionality. It can coexist with the best observed score here, so the concern must be evaluated in molecular context.

Azide, N-O-bearing and form-sensitive N-rich fragments remain among poorer molecules. The tiny fragments and long hydrophobic charged species are chemically unlike the better organized multi-ring compounds.
missing_features: The stream does not reliably assemble complementary ring and aryl-linker features into the organized arrangements found among its strongest molecules. Hundreds of distinct cores already exist, so a simple claim of missing ring diversity is unsupported.
No unique absent reference scaffold can be diagnosed from these modest scores. The supported gap is productive attachment organization rather than a prescribed nitrogen charge state.
The 187 optimizer appearances with unassigned carbon stereocentres lack explicit configuration, without evidence here of which configuration would help.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Organized combinations of cyclic nitrogen and aryl/sulfonyl anchors outperform isolated small polar or reactive fragments. The bis-sulfonyl piperazine scores 0.2588686674995393, compared with 0.2272296156064184 for the related quinoline-sulfonyl N-methylpiperazine. An N-methylpiperazine joined through an aminoethyl sulfonamide to benzodioxole scores 0.2229480268629566, so alternative attachment arrangements can also be useful. A simpler N-methylpiperazine/pyrrolylmethyl final molecule scores 0.13091966785799863: having the ring alone is insufficient. The small alkyl azide scores 0.0, sulfamic acid 0.02668612498071339, and the small sulfur-linked diacid 0.02095188685475281. Sulfur and polarity are therefore context-dependent, and the best structure explicitly contradicts a universal demand for an unsulfonylated basic nitrogen. The digest median is 0.127565.

per_task.generated_character: This is a broad mixture rather than convergence on one scaffold: median 24 heavy atoms, median three rings, and 774 distinct typed Murcko cores. Ring/aromatic text rates are 0.9805/0.9460. The top seed-2 structure is a single fluorinated/trifluoromethyl phenyl ring bearing an N-acylsulfonamide and a butyl-substituted secondary aminoacetyl arm. Other strong molecules include branched oxalamides, aryl-sulfonyl imidazolines with an ester, a guanidino benzofused N ring, and a quinolinone-linked thiourea/thiophene assembly. Conventional amide and sulfonamide connections appear makeable, but the full set also includes overgrown peptide-like chains, lipid-like tails and complicated tautomer-sensitive heterocycles. All three complete streams match the Parent exactly. Seed endpoints remain 0.2711448282680827, 0.26424211308214746 and 0.32609684308650033. The digest median displays 0.0; this rounded display is not evidence that half the exact scores equal zero.
liabilities: Long aliphatic tails and repeated amide/carbonyl growth produce large flexible or strongly polar outliers. These are present despite ring-rich chemistry elsewhere in the same stream.

Several structures combine acidic and basic groups or tautomer-sensitive C=N/C=S chemistry. Such structures require contextual form assessment; the absence of an assigned radical is insufficient to establish stability or synthetic feasibility.
missing_features: The generator lacks consistent compact organization of polar functions and aryl substituents across its proposals. The highest-scoring features appear intermittently while larger peptide-like and heteroatom-heavy combinations remain common possibilities.

Explicit stereochemical choices are missing for the branched oxalamide, the guanidino benzofused-ring example and other eligible structures. Passive perception finds 272 optimizer appearances with an unassigned carbon centre; no stereoisomer comparison was evaluated here.

Uniformly coherent ionization and tautomeric presentation is not demonstrated across amino N-acylsulfonamides, guanidines, imidates and thioureas. The observed scores alone do not identify a preferred solution-state form.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Compact placement of carbonyl/nitrogen groups with suitable aryl substitution is associated with the best observed values. CCCCNCC(=O)NS(=O)(=O)c1cc(C(F)(F)F)ccc1F scores 0.32609684308650033, and the branched fluorinated oxalamide 0.3085499097640706. In a close aryl-sulfonyl imidazoline pair, the fluorophenyl compound scores 0.3034617343186778 versus 0.24905607529893223 without that fluorine. Replacing the ester by its imidate representation in the fluorinated example gives 0.2795168707513844. By contrast, the long peptide-like and lipid-like digest structures score 0.0; another heavily carbonylated and nitrogen-rich structure scores 3.540513082254524e-90. The final repeated-carbonyl heterocycle scores 2.6445959326166367e-17. Neither adding more polar groups nor simply adding amines and rings is sufficient. Because several unrelated compact families score better, these records do not reveal a unique missing target pharmacophore.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every task has a digest stereocentre-text rate of 0.0. Passive RDKit perception finds an unassigned carbon stereocentre in 870 of 4,350 optimizer appearances, with no assigned centres or explicit bond-stereochemical text. The digest oxalamide CCC(CC(=O)Nc1cc(C(F)(F)F)ccc1F)NC(=O)C(=O)N(C)C contains a carbon centre whose configuration is unspecified. Many other leading structures are achiral, so the gap applies only where the graph supports stereochemistry.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not explicitly specify configurations for the stereogenic structures it emits.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator would need to recognize eligible stereogenic elements and generate explicit configurations while preserving connectivity and useful attachment relationships. Configuration coverage should be demonstrated on actual emitted identities; these records do not establish a score benefit for any stereoisomer.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The digest includes zero-scoring long-chain amides and peptide-like repeats. CCCCCCCCCC(=O)Nc1ccc(C(=O)Nc2cccc(F)c2)cc1 scores 0.000005647693002104746, whereas its shorter branched-acyl relatives score much higher. Conversely, useful molecules already include ordinary extended alkyl linkers. The full proposal panel spans 4-90 heavy atoms; extreme size is an observed output property, not a required property of its better structures.
transferable_gaps.gap: Appendage growth is not reliably coordinated with the existing scaffold and polar-group load.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The generator needs scaffold-context-dependent control of linker length, substituent extent and repeated polar functions while retaining learned attachment patterns. This evidence supports coherent growth from observed feedback, not a universal preference for short, nonpolar or minimally substituted molecules.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Strong emitted families include unacylated aryl/benzyl piperazines and linked cyclic amines, while a ring-N-acylated piperidine carboxamide is near the low end of its own observed score span. Yet Cc1cc(S(=O)(=O)N2CCN(S(=O)(=O)c3ccc4c(c3)OCO4)CC2)c2ccccc2n1 is the strongest molecule in another supplied span even though both piperazine nitrogens are sulfonylated. The full output already contains 1,003 appearances of an unacylated saturated ring-nitrogen proxy; there is no general absence of that chemistry.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve the chemical role of ring nitrogen when it changes attachments.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The generator needs to distinguish amine, amide, sulfonamide and conjugated nitrogen attachment contexts while exploring new structures. Preserve or deliberately vary the role learned from accepted molecules instead of treating nitrogen count, ring presence or a universally basic piperazine as the objective.

transferable_gaps.evidence: All 4,350 emitted optimizer appearances have zero RDKit-assigned radical electrons, but Fc1ccc(N2CCN(CCCCNCc3ccc(OCCl)cc3)CC2)cc1F still scores 0.9999994163676008 and contains a chloromethyl ether. O=S(Nc1cc(C(O)=NCc2ccccc2Cl)ccn1)c1ccccc1 retains imidic-acid/sulfinamide form sensitivity at 0.42730032301881693. Other strong molecules contain ordinary sulfur chemistry or an N-O linkage, so a blanket heteroatom or bond ban would discard chemistry already associated with good observed values.
transferable_gaps.gap: Closed-shell atom assignments leave reactive attachment chemistry and uncertain molecular forms unresolved.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The generator needs context-aware treatment of electrophilic attachments and tautomer/ionization forms beyond parse validity and radical count. Any future change should distinguish a specific molecular-form concern from ordinary aryl halides, charges, sulfur or N-O chemistry, without equating a structural filter with demonstrated experimental stability.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The output has 2,811 nonempty atom/bond-typed Murcko cores, but all twelve highest entries in one digest are decorated anilinoquinazolines from a single seed. Another panel has 732 distinct typed cores while its strongest structure is an organized bis-sulfonyl piperazine. Thus neither complete scaffold collapse nor a general lack of rings explains the remaining chemistry; many different graphs are available but useful combinations are uneven.
transferable_gaps.gap: Broad graph novelty has not established reliable diversification of the attachment patterns in the strongest families.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The generator needs to explore altered ring topology, saturation and substituent vectors while retaining the functional-group relationships supported by its own accepted molecules. Evidence should track actual productive structural families, since additional canonical identities or core counts alone do not establish better chemistry.

nodes.method_name: Augmented Hill-Climb with a corpus-trained SMILES policy
nodes.method_thesis: Train a compact autoregressive SMILES prior solely on the supplied unlabeled corpus, then initialize a fresh policy from that prior for each objective. Use the initial observations and each subsequent scored batch to update only its highest-reward sequences with the Augmented Hill-Climb loss: fit policy log likelihood to frozen-prior log likelihood plus scaled observed reward. Sample complete molecules token by token from the updated policy, canonicalize them, and refill invalid or duplicate proposals by further generation. The corpus supplies language training, never a ranked molecular pool. Elite-conditioned policy updates should shift generation toward new high-scoring molecular combinations quickly enough to improve the benchmark's mean final Top-1. This is a small-budget transfer hypothesis, not a claim that published larger-budget gains carry over. The root uses the current scored batch; randomized historical replay is reserved for the first improvement. The anchor's elite augmented-likelihood mechanism is described by [Thomas et al.](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13321-022-00646-z).

approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves a score-ranked population of molecular graphs using quantile-based parent draws, connected-fragment crossover and ordinary graph mutations. It creates fresh surplus pools, rejects unstable or duplicate identities, and admits a novel candidate only when its sulfur signatures do not exceed the largest corresponding count in its original scored generating parents. A Gaussian process learns from the complete chronological archive of accepted task-local scores using folded integer Morgan occurrence counts and dot-product count-Tanimoto covariance. It normalizes scores by the archive mean and population standard deviation, then uses correlated posterior function draws with stable masked choices to allocate each announced batch. Greedy survival and real accepted feedback drive later breeding; direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange remains disabled.
approach.novelty: I replace the covariance by the fixed square of the Parent's count-Tanimoto similarity. This one zero-preserving integer-power sharpening weakens partial similarity while retaining count magnitude information, unit self-similarity and exact fingerprint aliases. It may improve ranking and productive exploration, but may also fragment useful extrapolation. No completed same-Parent sibling is supplied. The concurrent exponential mean and residual-path experiments examine a different law at separate output boundaries; this experiment coherently changes the complete train, cross and pool covariance. Earlier min/max overlap, normalized Matérn, unfolded counts, added atom-pair information and exponential covariance failures remain specific counterexamples, not evidence that squaring will work.

nodes.hypothesis: Replace the original dot-product count-Tanimoto covariance T_DP by the fixed squared law K(x,y)=T_DP(x,y)**2 on unchanged folded Morgan integer occurrence rows, coherently in every GP Gram block while preserving inherited zero/unit conventions and exact T_DP=1 aliases.

finding_summary.headline: Squared covariance changes real exploration but loses endpoint score despite modest ranking and core-reuse gains
finding_summary.insights: This exposed test separates genuine allocation and discovery-to-reuse delivery from useful final optimization. Weakening partial covariance while preserving zeros and count magnitude can produce more productive new cores and modestly better selected-stream ordering, yet still reduce absolute incumbent progress and endpoints. The exact fixed exponent-two route has exhausted its registered test; more novelty, narrower dispersion and ranking gains do not rescue it. Exact count aliases remain, so the route does not resolve representation collisions. The chemistry report finds recognizable amides and aryl cyclic amines alongside reactive nitrogen-halogen bonds, cyanate/acyl-fluoride or cumulated unsaturation, unresolved ring geometry and unspecified states; stronger Parent structures also have liabilities. Neither core novelty nor those differences identify chemical mediation. Passive alternatives have no labels or continued ancestry, and shared descendants do not prove independent scaffold contribution. Current composition review, whole-foundation and constituent coverage, full-current-condition and joint interactions, chemical mediation, full-history processing and partial lineage composition remain open. The distinct concurrent exponential output-path probes and historical kernel failures cannot be pooled into a covariance-floor, mean/residual or universal kernel conclusion.
finding_summary.results: The squared covariance ran throughout all three seeds and five tasks, changed 1,442 accepted choices relative to original preferences on the same masks, and added 1,209 accepted records outside the passive original sets. On those actual accepted labels, pair accuracy rose from 0.73967 to 0.74039 and mean batch Spearman from 0.59327 to 0.59635, but MSE worsened from 0.0092124 to 0.0094384. Productive new typed/generic cores increased from 262/163 to 287/197, and later-used sources with useful accepted descendants from 146/91 to 176/121. This did not produce stronger overall progress: sequential incumbent gains fell from 255 to 242 and their summed magnitude from 5.81942 to 5.15234. Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.596453 to 0.551982, a paired loss of 0.044472 against the required +0.002. All three seed macros fell; fourteen of fifteen task/seed endpoints fell. Macro dispersion narrowed from 0.033970 to 0.016362.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic families retain reactive bonds and unresolved geometry, alongside recognizable amides and cyclic amines
molecular.overall_character:
Node n-36a7bb9883ec generates compact fused azaaryl carbonyl/thione systems, linked nitrogen-rich carbonyl heterocycles, aryl-substituted aliphatic amines, quinoline-linked nitrogen/carbonyl rings, and fluorinated dione/imino systems. Rings and aromatic regions are abundant: digest ring-closure incidence ranges from 0.9494 to 0.9782 and aromatic-string incidence from 0.9299 to 0.9724. These are molecule-level text incidences, not ring counts or aromatic-atom fractions; some unusual aromatic SMILES labels do not survive RDKit aromatic-ring perception. All charged and stereocentre-string incidences are 0.0, although potentially basic aliphatic nitrogen and unassigned tetrahedral centres are present. Global diversity is moderate, with distinct seed families but repeated close substitutions within leaders. Recognizable medicinal fragments coexist with direct N-halogen bonds, O-halogen attachments, cumulated unsaturation, N/O/S linkages and dense or small connected rings. Parsing is not evidence of synthetic access, geometry, stability or pharmacology. The inherited sulfur condition cannot certify those properties, and this assessment does not reconstruct gate decisions or certify absolute envelope compliance.

All 15 Child and 15 published n-1744a1494180 Parent trajectories were present and read, spanning five tasks and Search seeds 0, 1 and 2. Each side has 900 records per task, including 870 optimizer records; every Child digest counter, count and excerpt molecule/score/evaluation join matches. No task, path or paired seed is absent. context.comparison states child_complete=true and paired_complete=true without profile mismatch. The comparison uses the published current Parent, not older n-62daf219c70a endpoints. Digest final_molecules are late seed-2 proposals, not final Top-1 molecules; all seed endpoints below come from the full chronology. Child cited_smiles are supported by its digest or the request's trusted Child trajectory list; Parent structures are described from published comparison paths, which are not additional citation authority. CPU-only offline RDKit descriptors and path hashes are recorded in .slots/round-0027-slot-2/molecular_evidence_audit.json.

The Parent's full original molecular assessment was read through context.evidence_index. Recurring local-bond, geometry, unspecified-state, context-preservation and plausible-alternative gaps originated in n-c55c3d520a2c, continued through n-62daf219c70a and n-1744a1494180, and remain conditional output associations in this Child at 300 observations per task on the issued Search panel. The exact declared neutral sulfur envelope from n-93cd9a000278 remains a source condition; older numerical effects are not pooled or transferred. These molecules neither identify the component causing a liability nor establish chemical mediation of a score difference. The pinned current composition remains needs_review pending scheduled catalog_review at round27 close under v-17b4d64669a7955c8e61ca7e. This chemistry report closes none of the whole-foundation m-4fa9546e559e, constituent, full-current-condition, joint-interaction, chemical-mediation, full-history-processing or partial L07 composition gaps.

per_task.generated_character: The leading molecules are compact 24-25-heavy-atom fused indole/azaindole-like systems linked to pyridyl regions by amide, thioamide or ketone connections. Seed 0 has an additional carbon bridge/ring and an N-hydroxy thioamide; seed 1 has an ordinary pyridyl amide but direct ring N-F; seed 2 has an N-H indole, vinyl group and pyridyl ketone. Methoxy, short alkyl and aryl halogen substituents recur. The optimizer median size is 25 heavy atoms versus Parent 24. Familiar azaaryl carbonyl chemistry is present, but the bridged thioamide and N-halogen variants have uncertain routine synthetic access.
liabilities: Direct N-F/N-Br substitution on an indole-like nitrogen is distinct from ordinary carbon-bound aryl halogen substitution and keeps synthetic plausibility questionable.
The N-hydroxy thioamide and additional bridged ring require local stability and geometry assessment; sulfur membership alone cannot answer it.
missing_features: Plausible independent realizations of the favorable compact aromatic/carbonyl arrangement remain limited among leaders; the Parent supplies a conventional halogen-free alternative that this Child's leaders do not reproduce.
Consistently conventional local bonding around ring nitrogen and the carbonyl/thione link is unresolved; the observed gradient supplies no exact missing target pharmacophore.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxyindole anilide scores 0.3051048083696145; Child seed endpoints are 0.4369542269692598, 0.4387992465191 and 0.4254027310763201. Small molecules such as methane and SBr score 0.0. Labels therefore associate with complete compact aromatic/carbonyl organization rather than isolated fragments. A tied leading series exchanges aryl F/Br/Cl and ring N-F/N-Br while retaining 0.4387992465191, so peripheral halogen identity is not uniquely established as the favorable feature. Parent reaches 0.4593573492521118 with a sulfur-free, halogen-free divinyl azaaryl N-hydroxy amide; its other endpoints are 0.47411701813450596 and 0.4369542269692598. The Child offers different thione/ketone arrangements without demonstrating a chemical reason for the paired label changes.

per_task.generated_character: This set contains the largest molecules, with a 36-heavy-atom optimizer median versus Parent 31. Child endpoints range from a 28-heavy-atom N-rich fused dione/thioimidate-like linked-ring system to a 46-heavy-atom linked heterocyclic framework bearing cumulated diene ether arms. Seed 1 instead has a 37-heavy-atom azaaryl/carbonyl/ether structure carrying O-C#N, a cyanate rather than an ordinary carbon-linked nitrile. Ring-closure and aromatic-string incidences are high, but the seed-0 leader has only one RDKit-perceived aromatic ring and the unusual seed-2 leader none: lowercase text is not proof of conventional aromatic stabilization. Dense small closures, unusual unsaturation and reactive peripheral groups make synthesis questionable.
liabilities: Cumulated double bonds are present at string incidence 0.0391, including the highest-label structure; extended ether-linked unsaturation raises local stability and synthesis questions.
Aromatic text labels span small fused closures and unusual ring bonding; no conformer or ring-strain evidence validates these graphs.
O-linked cyanate and azoalkene fragments require assessment separate from ordinary nitriles or amides.
missing_features: Geometrically credible, synthetically plausible alternatives preserving the successful heterocyclic relationship are not established among leading labels; the Parent's stronger example is itself chemically questionable.
Stable ordinary peripheral groups replacing cyanate, cumulene ether or azo functionality are not consistently represented in leaders. Their necessity is not established by these observations.

The initial linked aryl dione scores 0.548381482770623. The association favors particular connected heterocyclic arrangements over fragments, but tolerates cumulenes and dense ring topology. Parent endpoints are 0.8561477222467935, 0.6204376881838878 and 0.6442339647723496: its strongest compact linked carbonyl/thione family also has O-F and halomethyl ether liabilities. The Child's larger seed-0 structure does not reach that label, so increased ring-rich mass and changed liabilities are not evidence of improved chemistry or objective fit.

nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

Connected-fragment crossover, optional finishing mutation, ordinary mutation continuation and all seven atom/bond/ring operation families with unchanged probabilities and bounded saturation/retry behavior.
Disabled direct aromatic C/N exchange, stable canonical/isomeric identity and original-graph reuse, initial/emitted and temporary-pool duplicate rejection.

Unchanged radius-two/chiral/2048 folded Morgan integer counts/cache, complete accepted-archive GP normalization/noise/factors; coherent fixed squared count-Tanimoto kernel, original correlated residual allocation and stable masked choices. Unsquared original GP retained solely as isolated unscored same-state diagnostics.

The added narrow sulfur rule permits source-inherited signatures and the listed ordinary sulfur classes; it adds no tabu walk, corpus vocabulary, operator change, global blacklist or whole-molecule validity test.

approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds molecular graphs from a bounded population of high-scoring accepted molecules, using connected-fragment crossover and ordinary mutations. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled. Before each batch it fits a Gaussian process to every accepted observation, using count-Morgan fingerprints and generalized Tanimoto similarity, fixed observation noise, and archive-based score normalization. It generates a larger pool of fresh valid unique offspring, draws correlated posterior functions over that pool, and emits the available maximum of each draw. Accepted scores update the archive and score-greedy survivor population. The residual amplitude currently comes entirely from the fitted posterior and inherited normalization; earlier forecast errors do not adjust its influence on selection.
approach.novelty: Add one task-local feedback rule for the amplitude of those existing correlated residuals. Save the prediction and raw allocation uncertainty before scoring each emitted molecule, then use only earlier accepted errors to estimate a bounded common multiplier, shrunk toward the inherited value of one. Large standardized errors receive a capped contribution to this estimator while remaining fully visible in diagnostics. The same multiplier scales the whole next draw without changing the fitted means or correlations. Completed siblings removed residual influence, correlation, count multiplicity, or crossover; this experiment retains them and tests whether their existing residual amplitude can usefully adapt. Historical noise-fitting controls changed GP regularization and lost endpoint score despite better prediction diagnostics, so complete endpoint comparisons remain decisive.

nodes.hypothesis: Scale the existing correlated allocation residual by one bounded task-local multiplier learned from earlier accepted, pre-feedback standardized squared prediction errors, with shrinkage toward inherited amplitude one and no change to fitted count-GP means or cross-candidate correlation.

finding_summary.headline: Accepted-error scaling changes choices and intervals but lowers the matched endpoint mean by 0.038141
finding_summary.insights: This feedback-amplitude variant is an executed but unsuccessful endpoint intervention; it does not overturn the separate evidence for retaining nonzero correlated residuals. Changing interval coverage and many selected identities is insufficient to establish useful search or calibration away from the acquired stream. Shrinkage and capped contributions preserve bounded adaptation, but 382 large errors remain in the Child diagnostics, and a common multiplier cannot anticipate a first unseen surprise. One shared first-batch miss is 253 raw allocation SDs from its prediction while the multiplier is still one. Which changed choices produce the losses remains unresolved. Molecular evidence preserves conventional alternatives and some larger improving ring families alongside reactive bond environments, crowded geometry, excessive elaboration and fragments. Those mixed examples rule out a universal size, ring or heteroatom rule as the explanation for the score loss. The next scientific question is which conditions make amplitude changes useful; these results do not justify re-tuning the preregistered constants after seeing the panel or combining sibling effects.
finding_summary.results: The fixed feedback recurrence reconstructs for all 4,350 accepted emitted predictions and excludes the 150 initial observations. Emission multipliers range from 0.586 to 2.849, preserving the raw fitted model and cross-candidate correlation. Scaling changes 377 of 435 same-pool selected sets and creates 1703 strict same-mask winner disagreements. On the actual Child stream, nominal 95% coverage moves from 77.91% using raw jittered allocation SD to 90.69% using its prospectively scaled SD; the same saved means give identical MSE 0.011318. Coverage gains are not uniform. Mean endpoint score falls from 0.595670 to 0.557528, a paired loss of 0.038141 instead of the required gain of at least 0.002. All seed macros fall (-0.044258, -0.005456 and -0.064710), while eight task-seed endpoints improve and seven decline. The largest losses are deco_hop seed 0 (-0.248112) and sitagliptin_mpo seed 2 (-0.344354); median_2 improves in every seed.

molecular.headline: Aromatic heterocycles and bridged amines persist, with reactive substitutions, crowded rings and unspecified stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: This assessment reads all 4,500 Child observations, including 4,350 optimizer proposals, and all 4,500 observations in the fifteen published Parent trajectories named by the immutable request. Every supplied task and Search Seed 0, 1 and 2 is covered; no listed path is missing. The brief reports complete Child evaluation and complete profile-matched pairing to n-62daf219c70a under the Research in Depth epoch-1 profile, 300 observations per task and batches of ten. The chemistry spans aryl carbonyl and thiocarbonyl systems, methoxy-substituted cyclic hydrazones, nitroso-substituted azaarenes, bridged aryl amines, large nitrogen/carbonyl ring assemblies, and fluorinated imino/carbonyl heterocycles. Small fragments and overgrown assemblies coexist with these leading families. Structural diversity is moderate across seeds and tasks, with substantial elaboration of a recurring family within individual trajectories; this is not global scaffold collapse. Proposal aromatic-string incidence ranges from 0.8391 to 0.9931 and ring-digit incidence from 0.8690 to 0.9943. These support abundant ring-containing and aromatic-labelled output, but do not measure aromatic stability, independent scaffolds or feasible three-dimensional geometry. Every task has charge-string and stereocentre-string incidence 0.0, despite visible aliphatic amines and potentially stereogenic ring junctions. Recognizable medicinal functional groups coexist with direct heteroatom-halogen bonds, halomethyl groups, unusual sulfur environments, small unsaturated rings and crowded bridges; makeability and overall drug-likeness therefore remain questionable and weak, respectively, rather than uniformly absent. Sizes below are heavy-atom-token counts read from the supplied SMILES, not computed conformational, synthesis or property measurements. Parent endpoint and chemical comparisons are descriptive; they neither identify activation of residual-scale calibration nor attribute a chemical liability to that component. The last emitted molecule is distinguished from the retained highest-scoring observation.

per_task.generated_character: The three seed leaders contain 25, 26 and 24 heavy-atom tokens. Seed 0 combines an N-fluorinated pyrrolic ring and a pyridyl ketone/imine region with a small, multiply unsaturated carbocycle. Seed 1 instead makes a methoxy-substituted cyclic hydrazone carrying a thiourea-like carbonyl analogue, an N-chloromethyl substituent and a fluorophenyl group, with a crowded spiro/bridged unsaturated carbocyclic extension. Its chlorine is attached to carbon in the chloromethyl group, not directly to nitrogen. Seed 2 uses an arene annulated to small nitrogen rings, an N-ethyl substituent, methoxy substitution and an N-fluoro carboxanilide. Conventional indole carboxanilides are present among the initial observations. The proposal halogen-string incidence is 0.9241 and mean SMILES length 43.3, but many late leaders replace conventional connectivity with strained-looking ring arrangements or reactive substitutions.
liabilities: Direct N-F and N-Cl bonds occur in some families; the seed-1 leader instead carries N-chloromethyl functionality and a crowded carbocyclic bridge. These are distinct chemical concerns.
Multiple unsaturated small-ring junctions raise strain and synthetic-accessibility questions that SMILES validity and aromatic labels do not answer.
Potential stereogenic saturated junctions lack explicit stereochemical identity.
missing_features: The favored aryl/polar organization is present, but stereochemically defined and geometrically credible alternatives to the crowded spiro, bridged and small unsaturated ring arrangements are not demonstrated at the leading scores.

Conventional bond environments are not preserved consistently around the nitrogen and carbonyl regions; the observed nonfluorinated amide counterpart shows that the local N-F bond is dispensable in one scored context.
Independent plausible alternatives within each leading family remain limited, although the distinct families across seeds rule out an inability to change scaffolds.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial indole carboxanilide scores 0.3051048083696145. The seed-0, seed-1 and seed-2 leaders reach 0.4443186615775074, 0.4565130794320982 and 0.44049061101245846. Intact aryl/polar-ring organization is associated with useful scores: sulfur alone scores 0.0, while a much larger, multiply linked aryl ketone assembly at seed 0/evaluation 205 scores only 5.051687510283091e-18. Neither fragmentation nor general enlargement reproduces the leaders. transferable_gaps.evidence: This gap is inherited from n-c55c3d520a2c through the identical-chemistry baseline n-62daf219c70a, and is re-observed in n-38bcd7569cce on Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2, 300 observations per task and batches of ten. transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve conventional bond environments while retaining favorable aromatic and heterocyclic organization.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Transformations should distinguish bond environment from element identity and offer conventional local alternatives while preserving useful relationships learned from accepted task-local scores. Retain ordinary carbon-bound halogens and available amines where appropriate. The missing capability is reliable context-sensitive chemistry, not a universal prohibition of nitrogen, sulfur, halogens or all reactive groups; no blanket filter's score benefit is established.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This geometry gap originates in the n-c55c3d520a2c assessment reproduced by n-62daf219c70a; the current complete, matched three-seed panel supplies new spiro/bridged hydrazones, multiply unsaturated small carbocycles, densely connected aryl amines, extended aromatic-labelled systems and large nitrogen/carbonyl ring closures. Counterexamples include conventional initial aromatic carboxamides and recognizable amine, lactam and lactone motifs. Some current more elaborate nitrogen/carbonyl ring families exceed their matched Parent endpoints, and a bridged amine nearly reaches the supplied score ceiling. Thus the concern is unresolved feasibility, not proof that bridges, ring richness or elaboration always reduce score.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently distinguish ring graphs that can be written from geometrically credible fused, bridged and unsaturated structures.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring transformations need sensitivity to size, bridge connectivity and unsaturation geometry, together with alternative feasible connectivities preserving learned favorable functional arrangements. A chemically credible alternative should be evaluated in its own task-local context. Ring counts, aromatic labels and high objective scores alone cannot establish synthesis or conformational plausibility; this assessment supplies no causal score benefit for a geometry rule.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This identity gap was recorded for n-c55c3d520a2c and reproduced in n-62daf219c70a; it persists in the current matched Search panel at the same observation budget and cadence. Stereocentre-string incidence is 0.0 for every task despite substituted saturated, spiro and bridged environments in the cited leaders. transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not specify stereochemical identity when new potentially stereogenic saturated centres and ring junctions are generated.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve or explicitly resolve stereochemistry when a generated constitution requires it, with appropriate exceptions for achiral or configurationally unstable cases. Treat protonation, tautomerism and alkene geometry as separate state questions. No particular stereoisomer, charge state, objective-specific structure or component-specific failure is justified by the available scores.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This context-control gap is inherited from n-c55c3d520a2c via n-62daf219c70a and has fresh evidence in the current three-seed, 300-observation panel. Tiny halogen or hydrocarbon proposals reach observed floors, including late proposals, while some large duplicated aryl/heterocyclic assemblies score far below more compact leaders. A 44-atom decorated family barely exceeds its 32-atom matched Parent leader. The counterexamples matter: all three leading nitrogen/carbonyl ring assemblies are larger than their matched Parents and have higher endpoints, while several compact amine families already score highly. Neither universal shrinking nor universal growth follows from these observations.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably preserve useful functional-group context while controlling fragmentation and excessive scaffold elaboration.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Use task-local feedback to retain useful combinations of aromatic, amine and carbonyl regions while offering controlled simplification, replacement and independent feasible scaffold alternatives. The capability gap is consistent preservation of productive molecular context, not inability to make small or large molecules. Avoid a fixed size floor, a universal growth preference or claims that additional diversity must improve score; chemistry associations do not isolate the residual-scale intervention.

nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

retained_mechanisms: Accepted-only task-local archive, bounded greedy survivors and score-quantile parent selection.

Connected-fragment crossover, optional post-crossover mutation, ordinary mutation continuation and all seven ordinary atom/bond/ring operations with fixed probabilities and bounded retry/saturation rules.
Disabled direct aromatic C/N exchange with passive opportunity tracing; stable canonical/isomeric identity, original graph reuse and both duplicate scopes.
Count-Morgan shared features and cache, generalized Tanimoto GP, original normalization and observation noise, full joint covariance, full Cholesky/jitter and raw next-fit probes.
Nonzero correlated residual allocation with inherited base normals, stable masks/ties and identity-bound saved predictions, now under one positive accepted-error amplitude multiplier.
Fixed surplus pools, batches, budget/profile, fresh task state, finite guards and original valid-pool numerical fallback.

approach.method_basis: The reference is Genetic GFN, published by Kim and colleagues, a two-phase generator that keeps handing work between a learned sampler and ordinary graph editing. A sequence model that writes molecules one token at a time is first trained on a large unlabeled corpus of drug-like structures, then adapted separately for each objective so that the chance of it finishing any particular molecule rises with the score that molecule actually received. Molecules it samples are dropped into a small scored population, which is then improved by ordinary genetic operations on the molecular graph: crossover between two parents, and single atom, bond and ring edits. The scored offspring are turned back into training targets for the sequence model, drawn preferentially from the high-scoring end of the archive, so the network proposes globally, the graph operators refine locally, and the refined results reshape what the network proposes next. A learned scaling term lets the model fit that reward-proportional target without knowing the total reward in advance, and a pull back toward the frozen corpus-trained model keeps it from collapsing onto whatever it found first.
approach.novelty: This is a root, so everything concrete here is a choice the implementation makes rather than something inherited from a parent. It fixes the alternation as one neural batch followed by two graph batches of ten molecules each, so roughly two thirds of the evaluation budget goes to graph refinement rather than to the network. It forces neural output into the breeding population at every cycle boundary instead of letting the population close over itself. It caps the scored population at sixty-four members. It sets the training reward as an exponential in the raw score, so a small score difference becomes a large difference in training weight. It draws replay targets with a probability that falls off as one over rank, so top molecules are revisited without the rest of the archive being starved. And it trains the corpus model only on unlabeled data, keeping every reward-bearing update local to one objective, so nothing learned from one objective can leak into another.

nodes.hypothesis: Alternate de novo sampling from a task-local GFlowNet SMILES policy with graph crossover and mutation of its refreshed scored population, then distill accepted graph descendants back into the policy through rank-weighted off-policy trajectory-balance replay with a learned log normalizer and regularization toward a frozen corpus-trained prior.

finding_summary.headline: Best of the thirteen Discovery roots at 0.5103, but the lead rests on one near-saturated objective
finding_summary.insights: The reciprocal loop demonstrably ran, and the node running it leads a field of thirteen roots whose scores span 0.2331 to 0.5103. What the run does not show is that the coupling produced the lead. Most graph offspring still fell below their generating parent, which is exactly the limitation this lineage was framed to address, so the advantage may come from the corpus-trained prior supplying realistic starting chemistry rather than from the feedback cycle itself. The per-objective spread is the sharper message: the same optimizer that nearly saturates one objective returns roughly 0.20 on another, so the campaign's current ranking is driven mostly by how well a method's proposal distribution happens to overlap each objective's answer, not by uniform competence, and a macro mean over five objectives will reward a method that wins one of them outright. With one seed and no parent this is not a reliability claim. What stays open is whether the lead survives more seeds, and whether being selective about which descendants get evaluated would convert the four-fifths of offspring that currently degrade their parent into usable gains.
finding_summary.results: Macro mean 0.510250764298028 on the single screening seed, the highest of the thirteen roots. Per objective the run returned 0.989650581855642 on the docking objective, 0.6290937996820349 on the decoration objective, then 0.46331566856387824, 0.27137962936984883 and 0.19781414201873615 on the remaining three, so one near-saturated result plus one strong result carry most of the lead while three objectives sit low. Every pre-registered observable activated and the falsifier did not trigger. The corpus-only prior cut held-out token loss from 4.560865074576297 to 0.5625432162352548 over 29742 steps on 1268755 sequences, and 150 later integrity checks found zero changes to it. Five hundred policy-generated molecules were admitted across 50 population refreshes, and 2958 complete graph-to-policy-to-sample-to-breeding chains were reconstructed through 106 distinct policy bridges. All 76800 replay draws came from accepted observations, with realized top-rank enrichment 0.2551173919195906 above the 0.5 uniform reference. Trajectory-balance residual fell from 27.86439877950252 to 22.643096844616046 across 2400 updates, 2381 of which reduced it, and all 2240 graph-bearing updates produced nonzero graph-derived gradients over 54110 draws. Of 1450 unique proposals, 500 came from the policy and 950 from graph operators, but only 173 descendants (18.2 percent) strictly beat their best generating parent, and the mean child-minus-best-parent change was -0.09497708681416797.

molecular.headline: Real medicinal chemistry with hard per-objective motif lock-in, and not one defined stereocentre
molecular.overall_character: Across all five objectives the generator emits ring-rich, heavily aromatic, well-branched molecules of ordinary size: ring closure appears in 95 to 99 percent of proposals, aromatic atoms in 87 to 97 percent, mean SMILES length runs 43 to 59, and cumulated double bonds are essentially absent at under one percent. The chemistry is recognisably drawn from a drug-like corpus, with indoles, pyridines, oxazoles, methoxyaryls, amides and benzylamines recurring. Two things are uniformly missing. No proposal in any objective carries a defined stereocentre. And within each objective the top of the ranking collapses onto a single decorated scaffold that is then permuted one atom at a time, so the twelve best molecules are usually variants of one structure rather than twelve independent answers.

per_task.generated_character: Genuine dopaminergic pharmacophore. A tryptamine-like indole carrying a primary or secondary amine, joined through a single methylene to a brominated tetrahydroisoquinoline. These are molecules a medicinal chemist would recognise on sight, and they reach 0.989650581855642 from starting material at 0.019.
liabilities: heavy reliance on aryl bromide, which reads as a synthetic handle rather than a finished substituent
aminal-like N-CH2-N fragments appearing in several of the top-scoring entries
the single best entry stacks two bromides on one ring plus a fused diazepane, an unusually greasy strained core
missing_features: defined stereochemistry at the ring-fusion and benzylic centres these scaffolds genuinely possess
conformationally constrained linkers other than the single methylene bridge used everywhere
aryl substitution beyond bromide and chloride on the tetrahydroisoquinoline ring
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Score tracks one triad: free basic amine, indole, and a halogenated benzylamine partner. Everything above 0.97 has all three; the bottom of the trajectory is amine-free heteroaryl chemistry such as triazine ethers and thiourea-adjacent amides, scoring four orders of magnitude lower.

per_task.generated_character: One motif, repeated. A 1,3-oxazol-5-yl group hung off an aminopyridine that is fused or linked to a lactone or lactam ring, with a second oxazole carried on an exocyclic alkene. Eleven of the twelve best entries are one- or two-atom permutations of each other.
liabilities: hemiaminal and enol fragments written NC(O)=C, which are tautomer artefacts rather than isolable species
an exocyclic C(=C) alkene conjugated to a ring carbonyl in nearly every top molecule, a Michael acceptor
trivial fragments such as CC and CCCN entering the trajectory at all, which wastes evaluations
missing_features: saturated or partly saturated ring systems to break the flat all-heteroaryl character
any defined stereocentre, despite several sp3 ring-fusion carbons being present
substituent chemistry beyond methyl, isopropyl and anilino on the central pyridine
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The scoring band is extremely compressed: best 0.6290937996820349 against a starting set already at 0.5, and everything above 0.62 carries the paired-oxazole plus aminopyridine arrangement. The worst entries are either oversized sulfone and bisphosphonate adducts or trivial fragments that still score exactly 0.5, so the objective floors small molecules rather than punishing them.

per_task.generated_character: Two families sharing one tail. A clean one, a methoxyphenyl ether of a pyridine carboxamide with a picolylamide cap, which is ordinary amide chemistry. And a dominant one built around an acryl-aldehyde enol ether, O=CC=C(O-aryl), capped by a non-aromatic 2H-pyrrole ring.
liabilities: O=CC=C(O-aryl) is a conjugated aldehyde and a Michael acceptor, and it is in most of the top twelve
C1C=CC=N1 2H-pyrrole rings are tautomerically unstable and not isolable as drawn
N=C(S) thioimidate and OOC peroxy-methyl fragments appear in mid-ranked entries
missing_features: a stable connectivity that reproduces what the acryl-aldehyde enol ether is contributing
aromatic five-membered rings in place of the non-aromatic 2H-pyrroles the generator keeps emitting
defined stereochemistry at the sp3 ring carbons of the pyrrolines it builds
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The 2-pyridylmethyl group is the recurring feature of everything above 0.37. The stable amide family and the reactive enol-ether family reach almost the same score, so the objective is not discriminating between them. The very bottom is occupied both by fragments and by overlong multi-ring adducts, both scoring effectively zero, so size is punished at both ends.

per_task.generated_character: A single scaffold explored exhaustively. A 1,3-dimethyl hydantoin-dione ring joined by an exocyclic double bond to a benzylic carbon that also carries a phenyl and an alkyl-aryl ether. All twelve best entries are that same molecule with the alkyl decoration and ring size varied.
liabilities: the exocyclic alkene sits between two ring carbonyls, making it a strong Michael acceptor in every top entry
late proposals introduce an O-O peroxy linkage and an N-hydroxy hydantoin, both degradation-prone
one late proposal carries a fully conjugated triene tail, which is not a stable substituent
missing_features: a second distinct scaffold family, to test whether the plateau is the objective's ceiling or the search's
polar functionality on the phenoxy ring beyond a single hydroxyl
defined stereochemistry at the benzylic and hydantoin sp3 centres
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Scores are banded between 0.184 and 0.198 for the whole top twelve, and the only gradient is small alkyl decoration: adding an ethyl or propyl on the phenoxy ring, or fusing a cyclobutane onto it, moves the score by thousandths. The floor is trivial fragments, so the objective rewards mere presence of the motif far more than any refinement of it.

per_task.generated_character: Nitro-substituted cyclohexadiene rings carrying a pyridin-2-ylmethyl hydrazone. The charged-fragment rate here is 0.3655, far above the 0.01 to 0.03 seen on the other objectives, and that charge is almost entirely the nitro group the generator has latched onto.
liabilities: malformed nitro groups written [N+][O-] without the second oxygen appear inside the top twelve
hydrazones are hydrolytically labile and are the single load-bearing feature of the whole top set
nitroalkene fragments, both reactive and toxicophoric, recur across the highest-scoring molecules
missing_features: the fluorinated aryl and fused triazole chemistry a chemist would reach for on this kind of target
any defined stereocentre, though this objective family is built around configuration
aromatic carbocycles in place of the non-aromatic cyclohexadiene rings that dominate the top set
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Every entry above 0.19 pairs a hydrazone C=NN with a 2-pyridyl or picolyl group, with the nitro group added on top. The worst molecules are large polyfunctional adducts scoring down to 1e-87, so this objective punishes size ferociously and the search responded by shrinking rather than by getting the chemistry right.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The stereocentre rate is exactly 0.0 in all five trajectory sets, across 1450 proposals, even though the molecules routinely contain sp3 ring-fusion and benzylic carbons that are genuine stereocentres.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator never emits a defined stereocentre.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Configuration is outside the proposal alphabet as built. A generator aimed at shape-dependent properties would need stereo tags in its token vocabulary and stereo-aware graph edits, plus feedback able to distinguish two configurations of the same skeleton, otherwise half of the accessible chemistry is unreachable by construction.

transferable_gaps.evidence: In every trajectory the twelve best molecules are one- or two-atom permutations of the same core, the winning family is reached early and then only decorated, and the score spread across those twelve is often under 0.02.
transferable_gaps.gap: Within any one objective the search collapses onto a single decorated scaffold.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Reward-weighted replay concentrates the proposal distribution faster than local graph edits can leave it. A generator would need something that explicitly keeps distinct cores alive, such as similarity-penalised replay or budget reserved for proposals sampled far from the current archive, rather than relying on random atom edits to escape a basin they helped dig.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Conjugated aldehyde enol ethers, exocyclic alkenes flanked by ring carbonyls, hemiaminal NC(O)=C fragments, 2H-pyrroles and nitro groups written with only one oxygen all appear in the top-scoring sets, not merely in the discarded tail.
transferable_gaps.gap: Reactive electrophiles and tautomer artefacts are proposed as if they were finished molecules.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Nothing in the loop distinguishes a scoreable string from a makeable compound, so a reactive motif that happens to score can become the load-bearing feature of the archive and then be amplified by replay. A structural-alert and valence-sanity screen applied before a proposal spends an evaluation would stop that amplification.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Only 173 of 950 graph descendants strictly beat their best generating parent, an 18.2 percent rate, and the mean child-minus-best-parent score change across the run was -0.09497708681416797.
transferable_gaps.gap: Local graph edits usually make their parent worse.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Descendants are being evaluated indiscriminately, so four fifths of the graph budget buys degradation. A generator would gain from a cheap internal ranking over candidate descendants before real evaluations are spent, so the budget goes to the offspring most likely to exceed the parent they came from.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The aromatic-atom rate runs 0.87 to 0.97 across every set, the recurring rings are five- and six-membered heteroaromatics, and the few sp3 rings present are small carbocycles bolted on as peripheral substituents.
transferable_gaps.gap: Saturated three-dimensional ring systems are almost absent.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The proposal distribution has inherited the flat, heteroaryl-dense character of its pretraining corpus. A generator would need edit operations that build and fuse saturated rings, and a prior whose sampling does not collapse onto planar aromatic frameworks, before it can offer any three-dimensional shape at all.

nodes.method_name: Genetic GFN: reciprocal learning between a flow policy and graph search
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Genetic GFN: alternately generate molecules with a GFlowNet policy, refine the resulting scored population through graph crossover and mutation, and distill scored descendants back into the policy using rank-weighted off-policy replay. The policy uses trajectory balance with a learned log normalizer and regularization toward a frozen prior. [Kim et al., Section 3](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.05961v4) describe this mechanism. Train the prior only on the permitted unlabeled corpus. Each objective starts with clean policy adaptation, replay and population state initialized from its supplied observations. Use a positive terminal reward increasing with the observed maximization score. Schedule policy and genetic phases around the evaluator's announced feedback; both produce new molecules, and all reward-bearing training records come from accepted observations. Later policy samples must enter genetic populations, and accepted graph descendants must affect subsequent policy updates. Generate further valid, canonical-unique structures to fill announced batches, without corpus ranking or a fixed molecular library. The hypothesis is that learned global proposals propagate local discoveries into new promising regions and then support further graph refinement, raising the mean of five independent final Top-1 scores. Published larger-budget gains do not establish that this reciprocal learning becomes useful quickly enough here.

Fresh task-local adaptable policy, learned log normalizer and Adam state
Accepted-only replay with exact trajectory retention and positive rank-weighted sampling

approach.method_basis: The Parent keeps independent molecular graph walks, each starting from a supplied scored molecule. It proposes random atom or bond edits from each current state, evaluates one neighbor per scheduled walk, accepts improvements, and sometimes accepts a loss using a temperature that falls as feedback arrives. An accepted worse molecule remains the source of that walk's next edit, while a separate archive preserves the best observed score. Its eight edit operators check molecular parsing, connectivity, canonical identity and novelty, but have no reference for whether a new local chemical environment occurs in ordinary molecular data.
approach.novelty: Add one frozen local chemistry support gate to the existing edit proposals. A small vocabulary extracted from unlabeled corpus molecules will identify supported atom environments; a proposed neighbor must not introduce or multiply an unsupported environment relative to its generating state. This addresses the observed drift into unusual ring atoms and bonds while allowing existing unusual environments to remain or disappear. This lineage has only its root, so no sibling has tested a corpus-derived support gate. The experiment asks whether restricting local chemical changes makes the same annealed walks more productive.

nodes.hypothesis: Condition the Parent's existing graph-edit proposal distribution on a frozen unlabeled-corpus vocabulary of local atom environments, rejecting an otherwise valid novel neighbor whenever it introduces or increases the multiplicity of an unsupported environment relative to that walk's scored source state.

finding_summary.headline: New unsupported environments fell to zero; the one-seed mean score rose from 0.233 to 0.268
finding_summary.insights:
The parent really was entering local environments absent or rare in the corpus: roughly one proposal in five increased their multiplicity. Supported alternatives were available with little extra retry work, so that behavior was avoidable without changing annealing or sacrificing evaluation budget. The same-run rejection traces establish this intermediate effect directly; the mixed score response leaves open whether removing these environments is broadly useful or primarily changes which stochastic paths are reached. The gain exceeds the declared 0.002 mean-score target on this seed, but one improving objective and one declining objective do not show a universal advantage or isolate which blocked chemistry caused either change.

Complete local support still allowed the chemistry assessment to find hydroperoxides, peracids, crowded bridges and N-Cl bonds. The N-Cl center environment itself occurred in eight sampled corpus molecules, so its survival follows the declared threshold rather than exposing a bypass. The improved drd2_docking maximum also retains a hydroperoxide and crowded ring topology. Local empirical support therefore narrows chemical drift but does not certify whole-molecule geometry, stability or synthetic plausibility. Coherent ring and functional-group changes remain worth investigating with rules shared across objectives. All starting and working child molecules were locally supported here, so preservation or removal of inherited unsupported environments remains an untested use case.
finding_summary.results:
The intended mechanism happened on all five objectives. Using the same frozen vocabulary for both runs, 298 of 1,450 parent proposals introduced or multiplied an unsupported atom environment (20.55%); none of the 1,450 child proposals did. The mean number of introduced unsupported environments fell from 0.311 per proposal to exactly zero. The gate rejected 235 otherwise valid novel candidates and redirected 205 proposal requests to supported alternatives from the same unchanged scored source. All batches remained full, and attempts per emitted molecule rose modestly from 1.165 to 1.364. Every Metropolis decision, cooling value, working-state update and archive check agreed with the inherited rules.

On the sole evaluated seed, the mean of the five best scores rose from 0.233114 to 0.268497 (+0.035383). The improvement came from drd2_docking, which rose from 0.044776 to 0.280588. Zaleplon_mpo fell from 0.381715 to 0.322816; deco_hop stayed at 0.557517, median_2 at 0.167839, and sitagliptin_mpo at 0.013725. All 1,450 child proposals were evaluated without invalid or duplicate entries. These are single-seed results and do not establish repeatability.
