approach.method_basis: The Parent trains a recurrent SMILES prior on the supplied unlabeled strings, then chooses a checkpoint with a fixed holdout. Each objective receives a fresh policy copy and a frozen reference prior. Its best current observations train together with a uniform sample from the thirty-two strongest earlier accepted elites, preserving their original strings and accepted scores. A fixed prior-likelihood-plus-reward target drives bounded policy updates, and ancestral sampling generates complete new molecules that pass chemical and duplicate checks. Every unlabeled molecule is always presented in the same supplied traversal, so alternative starts and attachment contexts of that molecule receive no direct training exposure.
approach.novelty: Add equivalent rooted-SMILES views only during unlabeled prior training. For each selected training molecule, choose between its original string and one cached alternate traversal rooted at a reproducibly selected atom. Verify that the alternate has exactly the same canonical molecular identity and fits the existing token interface before using it. This lets the same molecular connections appear in different sequence contexts while preserving the original fixed holdout and all online learning rules. The earlier sibling grouped bracket characters into atom units; this experiment retains the Parent tokenizer and instead tests invariance to molecular traversal. Any improved language coverage must still transfer to valid novel chemistry to count as useful search.

nodes.hypothesis: During unlabeled prior training, mix each selected molecule's supplied SMILES with one cached, deterministic atom-rooted SMILES view whose canonical/isomeric molecular identity is verified, exposing the unchanged recurrent model to equivalent attachment contexts while keeping online learning and sampling unchanged.

finding_summary.headline: Rooted views learned equivalent traversals, but validity fell and one replica stopped early
finding_summary.insights: Equivalent traversal exposure reached the training loss and transferred to held-out alternative strings. The smaller serialization preference is supported by improved alternate likelihood, while the loss on the supplied strings makes the tradeoff visible. This narrows the bottleneck: adding sequence contexts can improve traversal coverage without delivering reliable chemical search improvement. Lower duplicate rates did not translate into broader accepted scaffold coverage; invalid draws increased and late chemical families became more concentrated. The chemistry still favors conventional aromatic amine and carbonyl families, with unresolved attachment placement, extreme-size tails and reactive outliers. No missing stereochemical information was recovered. The available score changes are mixed and the completed-seed mean gain is below the registered 0.002 effect; the failed third task prevents the full intended score comparison. The specific canonicalization key mismatch identifies a separate robustness gap in the inherited feedback interface. Preparation stayed within the existing deadline and retained the same number of training batches, so lost training steps do not explain this outcome. Whether improved equivalent-string likelihood can preserve original-string quality and improve useful chemical coverage remains open.
finding_summary.results: Across three preparations, changed equivalent views appeared 10,938,511 times and contributed 553,572,420 target tokens to real training batches. Reconstructing all 3,629,346 cached row/view pairs and every training tensor receipt found no identity, token round-trip, length, or holdout-membership violation. The fixed panels contained 11,774 changed views. Their alternate NLL fell from 4.5739 to 0.7043 nats per alternate token. Under the same independent checkpoint comparison, alternate NLL improved from the parent's 1.6256 to 0.7043, while original-string NLL worsened from 0.5638 to 0.6004. The alternate-minus-original full-sequence NLL gap narrowed from 55.16 to 6.61 nats per changed molecule. Each preparation finished 29,742 training batches; mean preparation time rose from 243.5 to 902.0 seconds, with a 401.8 MiB temporary cache. On the same 14 completed tasks, raw validity fell from 90.24% to 86.55%, duplicates fell from 29.22% to 23.47%, and novel draws rose from 61.01% to 63.08%. Mean accepted scaffold counts stayed similar (218.4 to 217.2), while late scaffold concentration increased. The two completed paired seeds scored 0.51444 versus 0.51394, a mean change of +0.00050; their individual changes were -0.00199 and +0.00300. The third DRD2 run stopped at 170 evaluations because an emitted aromatic string changed canonical form when reparsed, activating the unchanged feedback-provenance guard. Its incomplete task leaves the three-seed macro score unavailable. All logged online updates preserve the frozen prior and original accepted replay strings.

molecular.headline: Conventional aromatic amines and carbonyl heterocycles dominate, with size extremes and an anomalous oxygen cation
molecular.overall_character: The output spans many recognizable medicinal-chemistry families: diarylamino heteroarenes, substituted quinazolines and pyrimidinones, indole-linked piperazines, sulfonamides, hydantoins, ureas and small saturated rings. Most leading molecules are medium-sized and have conventional bonds, with plausible synthetic entry points through amide formation, amine substitution or aromatic coupling. The full trajectories are structurally broad, although individual late families become much narrower. The supplied digest contains 900 molecules and 870 optimizer proposals per task except drd2_docking, which has 770 molecules and 740 proposals; that task's seed-2 trajectory ends at evaluation 170, so no later molecules are inferred. Ring-closure rates range from 0.9816 to 0.9977 and aromatic-token rates from 0.9483 to 0.9966. Mean SMILES lengths range from 39.2 to 50.1, but long polyaryl assemblies, lipids, peptides and highly polar nucleotide-like structures create an extreme-size tail. Charged-token rates range from 0.023 to 0.1207; many charges belong to recognizable nitro or N-oxide groups, while a leading molecule contains a chemically anomalous terminal positive oxygen. All stereocentre-token rates are 0.0, as in the supplied parent strings. The overall chemistry is mostly plausible and moderately drug-like, with isolated severe exceptions and no evidence that all stereogenic products represent defined stereoisomers.

per_task.generated_character: The displayed leading family consists of fairly compact diarylamino pyrimidines or a related pyridine, decorated with methoxy, ethoxy, methyl, phenol and aryl halogen groups. These are aromatic, largely flat molecules with exocyclic NH connections and heteroaromatic acceptors. Most of this family has ordinary, synthetically plausible bonding. The best-scoring entry is an exception: its terminal positive oxygen is singly attached to an aryl carbon and has an open-shell valence representation, rather than an ordinary phenol or ether. Other seeds contain acylurea and hydrazone-related aromatic families. The lowest examples are much larger polyaryl assemblies, elaborate fused polycycles or long unsaturated chains with multiple carbonyl groups.
liabilities: The singly bound terminal positive oxygen in the nominal best entry is an unusual open-shell species and cannot be treated as an ordinary stable medicinal substituent.
Multiple aromatic rings and aryl NH links yield predominantly flat structures, while the extreme tail adds excessive ring and linker complexity.
Hydrazone-related and heavily elaborated low-scoring molecules introduce additional configurational or chemical ambiguity without resolving the observed structural fit.
missing_features: The large low-scoring structures lack the compact aromatic and polar-group arrangement retained by the neutral diarylamino heteroarene leaders.
Matched neutral, closed-shell alternatives around the best oxygen-cation entry are not fully established by the displayed examples, although closely scoring ordinary phenolic relatives already exist.

The current leading set does not recover the substituted indole-carboxamide arrangement of the stronger parent seed-0 molecule; this is a missing well-performing chemical family among the displayed leaders, not proof that a particular group is universally required.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The unusual oxygen-cation structure scores 0.42762099872850584, while ordinary phenol/methoxy/methyl diarylamino pyrimidines with either meta aryl chlorine or fluorine score 0.42408253349563446. Ethoxy analogues score 0.42036761694214836 for either halogen, so the chemical family is supported without relying on the anomalous oxygen. Moving chlorine from the meta to para position in the displayed phenol-containing series gives 0.3925552460025089; the para-hydroxy relative scores 0.342125381162771. The largest multiaryl example scores 8.434866188027838e-50. This favors a compact arrangement of aromatic rings, amino links and selected substituent positions, rather than indiscriminate aromatic growth. Parent seed 0 reached 0.5280588545286916 with a compact substituted indole carboxamide; current seed 0 reaches 0.40822403535979507 with an acylurea-like family. Current seed 2 instead reaches 0.42762099872850584 versus the parent's 0.3900700429110833 with an aryl sulfonamide family. These different frameworks leave no unique missing pharmacophore established.

per_task.generated_character: The leading molecules are moderately sized to bulky, aromatic and heteroaromatic structures with methoxy-rich phenyl or fused aza-aromatic systems. Quinazoline-like cores carry amidine, amide or aryl connections; another strong family consists of amino pyrimidinones connecting a methoxylated aryl group to a fluorinated aryl or pyridyl group. The amide, amidine, amino and ether functionality is mostly conventional and synthetically plausible. Some other high examples link several nitrogen-rich heterocycles, increasing aromatic density. The lows include a small acyclic polyether, simple dimethoxybenzene, a small bicyclic lactam and sulfur-oxidized aromatic compounds.
liabilities: Repeated aromatic and methoxy-rich substitution creates fairly flat, heavily decorated structures with limited saturated shape diversity in the leading series.
Amidine protonation and the ionization of nitrogen-rich heterocycles are not characterized by their mostly neutral drawn forms.
Large multiheteroaryl extensions and occasional reactive or charged structures in the wider trajectory add chemistry outside the relatively conventional leading families.

The present highest family retains that broad chemistry with different decoration. The observed seed-2 endpoint scores 0.9999887250097366; its shorter trajectory is not treated as a complete three-seed endpoint comparison.

transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve chemically appropriate valence, hydrogen count and electronic state when changing atom identity or charge. Supply stable closed-shell alternatives around useful molecular frameworks without excluding legitimate charged functional groups.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The cited low tail includes giant multiaryl assemblies, long hydrocarbon chains, peptide-like molecules, phosphate-rich nucleotide-like structures and small polar fragments lacking the aromatic and linker organization of the stronger examples. transferable_gaps.gap: The generator still emits extreme sizes and polarities that lose the organization found in its better molecules.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Offer changes that preserve a useful scale and local functional-group balance while varying molecular shape. Avoid making a local chemical change depend on large scaffold accretion, long-chain growth or removal of most of the relevant framework.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Moving an aryl substituent changes a displayed aromatic-amine score from 0.42408253349563446 to 0.3925552460025089. transferable_gaps.gap: Coverage of matched functional-group positions and linker geometry remains incomplete despite clear local score differences.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Generate chemically coherent matched series that vary substituent position, linker length, heteroaromatic nitrogen placement and ring shape while retaining the other useful fragments. Let observed scores determine which arrangements matter.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every task has stereocentre-token rate 0.0. The cited hydantoins, cyclobutanol derivative, polyols and complex spiro or fused alternatives contain possible stereogenic relationships, whereas many leading flat heteroarenes and simple piperazines are naturally achiral.
transferable_gaps.gap: Stereogenic saturated-ring products lack explicit stereochemical identities.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Represent and preserve feasible absolute and relative configurations where stereochemistry exists, and generate matched stereoisomers when relevant. nodes.method_name: Augmented Hill-Climb with a corpus-trained SMILES policy
nodes.method_thesis: Train a compact autoregressive SMILES prior solely on the supplied unlabeled corpus, then initialize a fresh policy from that prior for each objective. Use the initial observations and each subsequent scored batch to update only its highest-reward sequences with the Augmented Hill-Climb loss: fit policy log likelihood to frozen-prior log likelihood plus scaled observed reward. Sample complete molecules token by token from the updated policy, canonicalize them, and refill invalid or duplicate proposals by further generation. The corpus supplies language training, never a ranked molecular pool. Elite-conditioned policy updates should shift generation toward new high-scoring molecular combinations quickly enough to improve the benchmark's mean final Top-1. This is a small-budget transfer hypothesis, not a claim that published larger-budget gains carry over. The root uses the current scored batch; randomized historical replay is reserved for the first improvement. The anchor's elite augmented-likelihood mechanism is described by [Thomas et al.](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13321-022-00646-z).

approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves a bounded population of molecules scored in the current task. It favors high score quantiles when choosing the first parent and a distinct crossover partner, generates fresh graphs through crossover and ordinary atom/bond edits, and admits stable canonical identities. A Gaussian-process predictor trained on the complete accepted-score archive uses count fingerprints and correlated posterior samples to select the next evaluation batch from a larger fresh pool. Each accepted offspring immediately enters score/serial-ordered survivor competition and can breed at the next suggestion; all accepted labels also enter the next fit, including records that do not survive. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled.
approach.novelty: This ablation removes just the newest accepted cohort's immediate breeding opportunity. First-parent and partner selection use the ordinary bounded population as it stood before the most recent nonempty accepted feedback cohort, while current survival and full predictor learning still update immediately. The next real nonempty cohort releases the preceding cohort to this breeding snapshot if it survived ordinary retention. Earlier siblings froze breeders to the initial molecules, changed survivor capacity or recency, or changed source probabilities and draw scheduling. None isolated this single-cohort consumer delay. The test asks whether prompt recursive use adds value beyond later recursive use.

nodes.hypothesis: Remove only immediate access of the newest nonempty accepted observe cohort to both breeding-parent consumers by using the original bounded greedy population from immediately before that cohort; release a cohort after the next real nonempty accepted cohort, while ordinary current survival and full accepted-archive GP learning remain immediate.

finding_summary.headline: One-cohort breeding delay preserves recursion but lowers mean final Top-1 by 0.052370.
finding_summary.insights:
Prompt reuse contributes beyond simply allowing accepted offspring to breed eventually, under this fixed optimizer, feedback cadence and evaluation budget. Full learning from new scores remained immediate, so withholding those labels from the predictor does not explain this contrast. The previous static-initial experiment established the value of recursive access overall; this result adds a narrower timing answer while preserving that earlier finding.

More local parent wins are compatible with worse search when breeding sources themselves have lower scores. Similar numbers of distinct reused offspring also conceal shallower scored ancestry: maximum depth fell from 23 to 14. These observations narrow the explanations, but do not establish that ancestry depth, source quality or molecular age caused the endpoint loss. Support, ranks, sampling probabilities, random consumption and subsequent adaptive histories all changed together.

The molecular assessment found rich ring systems, useful amine and carbonyl arrangements, and seed-dependent scaffold families in both runs, alongside recurring reactive heteroatom-halogen bonds, difficult ring geometries and unspecified stereochemistry. Chemically mixed alternatives and task-specific improvements remain visible. The timing contrast identifies no chemical mediator or general shortage of rings or functional groups. Whole-foundation value, interaction with the separate learner control, and reliability beyond these three matched seeds remain open.
finding_summary.results:
The delay operated in all fifteen task/seed runs. None of 110,134 parent draws used the newest accepted cohort, although 2,522 newly accepted molecules had positive support under the immediate current-population law. Later recursion remained active: 2,409 accepted offspring eventually bred, producing 4,031 accepted products with generated parents. All 435 full-archive predictor fits and all 435 fresh pools completed. Maturity did not guarantee use: 841 retained offspring never received positive support and another 56 supported offspring were never drawn. The final 150 offspring lacked a future maturation event; the preceding 150 matured only at terminal feedback and had no subsequent breeding opportunity.

Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.595670 to 0.543300, a paired change of -0.052370 against the registered 0.002 scale. Seed macro changes were -0.115073, -0.011259 and -0.030776. Ten task/seed endpoints declined and five improved: the exceptions were two zaleplon runs, two median-similarity runs and one decoration-hopping run. Docking and sitagliptin declined in every seed. Seed macro population SD decreased slightly, from 0.026593 to 0.024744.

Strict offspring-versus-best-parent wins increased from 629 to 877, but mean absolute offspring scores fell from 0.385256 to 0.321667 and mean best-generating-parent scores fell from 0.470456 to 0.384678. Incumbent advances fell from 258 to 219, with total increment magnitude decreasing from 5.807663 to 5.022119 across the fifteen searches.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich heterocycles and aryl amines vary by seed, with reactive heteroatom halides, difficult ring geometry and unspecified stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character: This assessment of n-4a649366619a reads every row in the 15 supplied Child trajectories and the 15 published search trajectories of code Parent n-62daf219c70a. Each task has 900 Child observations across Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2, including 870 optimizer observations. No requested trajectory path is missing, no task is omitted, and context.comparison separately confirms child_complete=true and paired_complete=true with the same three matched seeds and no profile mismatch. The bounded digest pools seeds: its final excerpt is from seed 2, so it is not treated as a representative terminal molecule for every seed. The output is predominantly medium-sized to large, branched, aromatic and heterocyclic; it includes recognizable amides, lactams, esters, phenols, ethers and available aliphatic amines. The digest ring-closure incidences range from 0.9494 to 0.9862 and aromatic-token incidences from 0.9310 to 0.9782; these measure the presence of string features, not aromatic atom fractions or geometric feasibility. Different seeds reach distinct families, while their high-scoring neighborhoods repeatedly modify the same frameworks. This supports moderate structural diversity with local concentration, not global scaffold collapse. Drug-like functional arrangements coexist with N-halogen and O-halogen bonds, dense bridges, small unsaturated rings, cyclic cumulenes, very large elaborations and occasional tiny fragments. RDKit perception from the actual trajectories finds no parsing failures among the 4,350 Child optimizer records, but this is only graph validation. It identifies unassigned tetrahedral centers in 2,035 of those records, while the digest reports stereocentre-string and charge-string incidences of 0.0 for every task. Neutral notation does not imply absence of protonatable amines. Size, ring counts and motif counts below are deterministic readings of the observed molecules, not new oracle scores or synthesis predictions. Plausibility judgments concern apparent chemical environments; routes, stability, conformations and protonation have not been demonstrated. Full source hashes, per-seed descriptors, exact score values and initial/best/worst/final records are in .slots/round-0025-slot-2/molecular_audit.json, generated by molecular_audit.py using RDKit 2023.09.6. All report cited_smiles are actual Child strings authorized by the immutable request. Parent comparisons use its published trajectories through the supplied evidence index; the indexed Parent molecular report supplies historical gap provenance. These chemical associations do not attribute an effect to the breeder delay, establish activation, identify a chemical mediator, or decide contribution.

per_task.generated_character: The optimizer records have a median of 25 heavy atoms and three perceived rings, usually with extensive aromatic character; the digest aromatic-token incidence is 0.9667. The three seed leaders each have 24 heavy atoms but differ substantially. Seed 0, evaluation 262, has a benzene-fused four-member unsaturated ring, a methoxy group and an N-fluorinated amidine linked to fluoropyridine. Seed 1, evaluation 270, is an alkyl/vinyloxy-substituted indole-like aromatic system with an N-Cl bond and a pyridyl ketone. Seed 2, evaluation 179, has a methylthio substituent, an N-methyl-N-phenyl amide and a fused N/O-containing ring system; RDKit perceives a four-member ring containing aromatic-labelled atoms. Thus the output can supply compact aromatic carbonyl arrangements, but even the halogen-free seed-2 leader needs a ring-geometry assessment. Other seed-2 high records contain N-hydroxy amides or ring-bound cumulated double bonds. These are more complex and chemically questionable than a uniform collection of ordinary aryl amides. The Parent also favors compact aryl/heteroaryl carbonyl or imino structures, with N-halogen substitution in its seed leaders.
liabilities: Direct N-halogen bonds occur in 376 of 870 Child optimizer records, compared with 445 of 870 Parent records; ordinary carbon-bound halogen substitution is chemically distinct. These frequencies do not establish the effect of removing the bonds.

The seed-2 aromatic-labelled four-member N/O ring and cyclic-cumulene relatives raise geometric and synthetic concerns. N-hydroxy amides and methylthio groups require their own environment-specific assessment and are not automatically equivalent to the more reactive N-halogen examples.
missing_features: Consistently conventional bond environments around the favorable compact aromatic/carbonyl arrangement are missing from the leading set: the seed-0 and seed-1 leaders use N-halogen bonds, while the halogen-free seed-2 leader has an unusual small aromatic-labelled ring.

Geometrically credible alternatives to the small fused rings and endocyclic cumulated bonds are not established at the same scores. The record does not identify an absent target motif that could be supplied simply by adding another ring or nitrogen.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The common initial aryl amide at evaluation 9 scores 0.3051048083696145. Child seed-0/1/2 leaders score 0.4175635604843711, 0.4597940970593737 and 0.45766047024715; the paired Parent leaders score 0.39405142067435733, 0.47411701813450596 and 0.438972502037081. The direction therefore differs by seed. Seed 1 evaluation 201 retains an alkyl/methoxy/N-chloro aromatic core but lacks the substantial carbonyl-linked aromatic region and scores only 0.00184649918126606; seed 0 evaluation 282 is ethene at 0.0. The visible association favors an organized, moderately sized aromatic plus carbonyl/imino arrangement over fragments or an isolated decorated core. This is not an isolated proof of any one functional-group requirement. Seed 2 evaluation 190 reaches 0.4491253474628456 with a fused N-heterocycle/N-hydroxy aryl amide and no halogen, countering a universal halogen requirement. Its cyclic-cumulene/N-bromo-amide relative at evaluation 253 reaches 0.4514335070299504, so high scores do not exclude difficult chemistry. The seed-2 last proposal at evaluation 300 scores 0.3995736468848427; it is not that seed's best molecule.

per_task.generated_character: The pooled optimizer records have a median of 33 heavy atoms and five perceived rings, with ring-closure-string incidence 0.9747. The seed-0 leader at evaluation 286 has 29 heavy atoms and four aromatic rings: a nitrogen-rich fused dione joined through an N-N-containing linkage to an aza-aromatic bicyclic region, with methyl, fluoromethyl and carbon-bound chlorine groups. The seed-1 leader at evaluation 296 has 33 heavy atoms and four aromatic rings, linked aza-aromatic/carbonyl/ether regions, aryl Br/F, chloromethyl and chloromethyl-ether substituents. Seed 2 instead favors a 37-heavy-atom, three-aromatic-ring biheteroaryl/anilino system with carbon-bound fluorines and multiple ester groups, including a vinyl ester. These ester-bearing graphs are more conventional locally than the reactive substituents in some other seeds, although their size, flexibility and synthetic route remain concerns. At the extreme, an evaluated proposal has 112 heavy atoms; this is not the size of the leaders. The Parent seed-0 leader has a different compact fused/bridged carbonyl-thione organization, including O-F and a halomethyl ether, while its other seeds retain distinct linked aromatic families.
liabilities: The seed-1 leader contains a chloromethyl ether and other halogenated termini; the seed-0 leader contains an N-N linkage. These deserve local reactivity assessment, without treating ordinary aryl halides or every N-N bond as inherently unmakeable.

Multiple ester groups, broad aromatic surfaces and large outlier elaborations add flexibility or synthetic burden. The seed-2 conventional ester family is a counterexample to universal heteroatom-halide dependence, but no route or stability record is supplied.
missing_features: Reliable coverage of alternative connected heterocyclic arrangements is not demonstrated within each seed: the Child does not recover the Parent seed-0 leading organization at its observed score, while its seed-2 family exceeds the paired Parent. No common absent atom or decoration explains both cases.

Less reactive peripheral alternatives that retain useful aromatic connectivity need chemical feasibility evidence. The tied ester/ether/thiono variants show that peripheral chemical identity can change without an observed score improvement, rather than establishing a specific required substituent.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The common initial aryl-substituted fused dione scores 0.548381482770623. Child seed-0/1/2 leaders score 0.6297226207556194, 0.617581553779641 and 0.6379551820728291, versus Parent values 0.8561477222467935, 0.6248206599713055 and 0.6178024026512013. The large seed-0 separation coexists with a seed-2 reversal; it cannot be summarized as one missing ring class. A smaller fused nitrogen-carbonyl fragment in Child seed 0 evaluation 138 scores 0.5183568573060292, and methane at evaluation 278 has the observed 0.5 floor. The higher records preserve combined, connected heteroaromatic regions and substituent context. Seed 0 evaluation 261 is a 32-heavy-atom secondary cyclic amine with a seven-member unsaturated N-ring, an aryl amide, phenol, methoxy and carbon-bound halogens. Seed 1 evaluation 299 is a 31-heavy-atom flexible diaryl chain carrying a primary amine and an N-methyl six-member diazinane-like cyclic aminal, plus phenol and methoxy groups. Seed 2 evaluation 300 has 33 heavy atoms, a related saturated two-nitrogen ring, an amide, an aniline, hydroxymethyl and a chroman-like fused ether ring. The three leaders have two aromatic rings each and recognizable medicinal-chemistry handles, without direct N-halogen or O-halogen bonds. RDKit identifies unassigned tetrahedral centers in 845 of 870 Child optimizer records. Neutral SMILES and absent stereotags leave chemical identity under-specified; they do not imply that the structures are achiral or nonbasic.

Cumulated carbon double-bond centers occur in 41 Child optimizer records, including 37 with the center in a perceived ring of at most seven atoms, but none of the ten highest-score records in each Child seed has one. Protonation and local aminal stability are unresolved despite abundant available amines. The missing evidence is a chemically defined, feasible presentation of those centers; recommending the addition of a basic ring nitrogen would misdescribe the existing output.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The indexed n-62daf219c70a molecular report attributes this gap to n-c55c3d520a2c and its repeated Search evidence. It is re-observed here in n-4a649366619a relative to n-62daf219c70a under the frozen Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2, batch size 10 and 300 observations per objective. The 4,350 Child optimizer records include 813 with direct N-halogen bonds and 77 with direct O-halogen bonds; these counts overlap and are not a count of distinct affected records. Leaders also include a chloromethyl ether and N-S functionality. Counterexamples are substantial: aryl/aliphatic-amine leaders and the ester-rich linked aromatic family have ordinary carbon-bound halogens without N/O-halogen bonds, and a halogen-free aromatic amide scores highly within its own history. The deficiency concerns local environments, not a general inability to form useful amines, heterocycles or carbon-halogen bonds.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve conventional local bond environments while retaining useful aromatic and heterocyclic arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Task-agnostic graph transformations could distinguish bond environments and offer chemically plausible alternatives while preserving favorable relationships learned from local feedback. The record motivates testing that capability; it does not show that blanket halogen removal or a fixed reactivity filter improves scores. The inherited gap keeps its original source and frozen observation conditions, and this assessment attributes it to no individual component or timing change.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This gap is carried from n-c55c3d520a2c through the indexed n-62daf219c70a report and re-observed in n-4a649366619a on the same frozen three Search Seeds at 300 observations per objective. The Child emits a high-score four-member N/O ring represented with aromatic atoms, dense bridged dicarbonyl systems, and cyclic cumulenes including a four-member-ring example. All 4,350 evaluated Child optimizer graphs parse in RDKit, showing that parsing does not resolve these questions. Ordinary saturated-ring amines and noncumulated high-score alternatives are also present; this is not a universal defect of ring formation or a requirement for exotic unsaturation.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently separate a valid ring graph from a geometrically credible pattern of fusion, bridging and unsaturation.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring edits could account for ring size, feasible bond geometry and bridge connectivity while proposing alternative frameworks that preserve learned functional arrangements. Lowercase aromatic notation, ring counts and successful valence checks cannot substitute for this information. The evidence supports assessing local geometry, not banning all small rings or bridges, and establishes no score benefit or component-specific cause.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The indexed Parent report records the same gap for n-c55c3d520a2c and n-62daf219c70a. In n-4a649366619a under the frozen three-seed Search panel, every digest stereocentre-string incidence is 0.0, while RDKit identifies unassigned tetrahedral centers in 2,035 of 4,350 optimizer records. Examples include aryl-substituted cyclic amines, fluorinated unsaturated rings and bridged carbonyl systems. Other leading aromatic molecules are achiral under this perception, so not every record requires a stereotag. Formal-charge-string incidence is also 0.0, but available amine motifs are plainly present.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not specify stereochemical identity when graph edits create potentially stereogenic saturated and bridged centers.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The representation and transformations could preserve or explicitly resolve stereochemical identity where applicable, distinguishing stable centers from achiral or configurationally unstable environments. Protonation and tautomerism need separate treatment. These observations identify incomplete chemical specification; they do not demonstrate a stereochemical score penalty, justify an objective-specific state rule, or attribute the omission to a particular component.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This gap is inherited from the n-c55c3d520a2c observations recorded in the n-62daf219c70a molecular report and recurs in n-4a649366619a at the frozen Search budget and batch size. The Child evaluates 87 structures with at most three heavy atoms, including late low-score hydrocarbon or halogen fragments, alongside very large repeated or appended ring systems whose observed scores can be low. Higher values generally preserve organized combinations of aromatic, carbonyl and available amine regions. A 21-heavy-atom single-aryl cyclic amine still has a high recorded score in its own history, providing a counterexample to the idea that useful molecules must always be larger or more polyaromatic.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably retain useful functional-group context while controlling fragmentation and excessive elaboration.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Task-local feedback could guide edits that preserve useful chemical context while simplifying or replacing dispensable regions. The missing consistency does not justify a fixed minimum size, automatic growth preference, or removal of every fragment proposal. The evidence describes evaluated outcomes only and does not attribute them to a component or establish that restricting these moves would improve the final result.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The n-62daf219c70a report traces this conditional coverage gap to n-c55c3d520a2c. The current n-4a649366619a Search panel again shows repeated peripheral substitutions and local ring-segment changes around each seed's favored aromatic amide, linked heterocycle, aryl-amine or bridged dicarbonyl family. Different seeds nevertheless reach distinct families, and some Child families exceed their paired Parent values while others do not. Ring and aromatic-string incidences are high throughout. These facts support local concentration and chemically mixed alternatives, not global collapse or an inability to invent rings; structural resemblance alone does not establish ancestry.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently supply independent, plausible scaffold alternatives within each seed's high-score neighborhood.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator could propose feasible alternative connectivities that retain relationships supported by its own observations and evaluate whether those alternatives remain useful. Distinct strings do not establish meaningful scaffold coverage, and more diversity alone is not a demonstrated benefit. The original source, frozen Search conditions and seed-dependent counterexamples must remain attached when this gap is transferred; it is not an attribution to breeder timing or any retained component.

nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds molecular graphs from a score-ranked survivor population. It samples preferred score quantiles, uses connected-fragment crossover and ordinary local mutation walks to fill a fresh surplus pool, then checks molecular validity, stable canonical identity and duplicates. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled. An active Gaussian process uses count-Morgan features and every real accepted score from the current task; correlated posterior draws allocate the announced evaluation batch. Accepted offspring enter the full model archive and compete for the bounded greedy survivor population, so later breeding can build on earlier generated molecules.
approach.novelty: Freeze only the breeder to its ordinary initial usable, score-ranked cohort. Every later graph proposal still uses the inherited parent-draw and graph-edit rules, and the posterior continues learning from all real accepted offspring. Updated survivors remain available for incumbent tracking and reporting but cannot become breeding parents. Earlier controls removed crossover, ordinary continuation or predictive allocation; this probe preserves those mechanisms and cuts the accepted-offspring-to-breeder feedback path. It measures that recursive feedback within the current optimizer, while leaving the broader whole-optimizer question open.

nodes.hypothesis: Sever recursive accepted-offspring breeding feedback by fixing every breeding-parent draw and breeding-cohort availability check to an immutable copy of the ordinary initial usable score-ranked population, while preserving active posterior learning from all real accepted observations and the live survivor updates used for tracking and reporting.

finding_summary.headline: Recursive breeding feedback contributes: fixing initial parents lowers every matched endpoint and the mean by 0.260206.
finding_summary.insights:
These complete, exposed results establish positive conditional contribution of recursive offspring-to-breeder feedback within the current optimizer, even while accepted-label posterior learning remains active. The initial cohort contains ten molecules, but only five have positive support under the inherited unexcluded quantile law. Fixing that breeder holds membership, ordering and cohort size together; this experiment cannot apportion their effects or isolate the survivor rule. It also leaves the broader whole-foundation question open. Separate component removals and shared-Parent siblings cannot be added into a joint value estimate.

The local success counts illustrate why ancestry and endpoint quality must be kept separate. Beating an initial molecule becomes more common, and prediction errors are smaller on the changed evaluated distribution, yet the search makes fewer incumbent gains and ends lower. Every Child endpoint still exceeds its initial best. The molecular assessment finds useful available amines, ring closures and scaffold rearrangements alongside recurring initial amide, nitrile/carbonyl and dione organizations. Some lower-scoring Child leaders have more familiar local chemistry than the higher-scoring Parent leaders. The deficit therefore does not establish an absence of chemical novelty, require reactive motifs, or identify a chemical mediator. Scored ancestry depth one also allows unscored multistep edits and crossover finishing.

The fixed neighborhoods remained productive enough to fill all full pools under inherited bounds, although they required more attempts. No rescue from live survivors was used. Exhaustion and recovery semantics passed source and synthetic checks but were not naturally exercised. Three matched Search seeds support this descriptive conditional result; they do not establish universal reliability or value for unobserved descendants.
finding_summary.results:
Every one of 122,044 Child parent draws came from the unchanged initial cohort; no accepted offspring became a breeding parent. The Parent used accepted offspring in 105,073 of 110,295 draws. All fifteen task/seed sessions matched through their first complete batch, then diverged at the first parent, pool member and evaluated molecule of batch two. Generated offspring still entered the live survivors and the full score archive. All 435 accepted-label posterior fits and original sampled-maximum allocations remained active. All pools filled, all three seeds completed, and no natural fallback or exhaustion occurred.

Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.595670 to 0.335464, a paired change of -0.260206 against the registered 0.002 loss scale. Seed macro changes were -0.306557, -0.273839 and -0.200221. Every one of fifteen task-seed endpoints and all five task means declined. Population deviation across seed macros rose from 0.026593 to 0.047795. Local parent beats increased from 629 to 2,007 against the easier fixed initial comparators, while incumbent improvements fell from 258 to 84. Generation also encountered more duplicate proposals: 14,385 versus 6,358.

All audits are read-only with respect to candidate/framework/policy/evaluation artifacts; no oracle, new formal evaluation, hidden Confirmation data, eligibility decision or finalization is performed.

molecular.headline: Conventional amides and aromatic frameworks recur; useful free amines emerge, but alternative useful arrangements remain uneven
molecular.overall_character: All supplied Child n-4d4b5eafa8b3 and published Parent n-62daf219c70a trajectories were present and read. The brief independently reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true for Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2, with no profile mismatch and no uncovered objective. Each task contributes 900 Child records, including 870 optimizer evaluations, with complete matched Parent trajectories and identical fixed initial molecule/score records. Every Child retained best exceeds its fixed initial best, while every matched Parent endpoint remains higher. This is not an absence of chemical improvement over the initial observations. The evaluated Child molecules repeatedly retain recognizable indole carboxamide, polyaryl nitrile/carbonyl, pyrrolidine acid/amide and nitrogen-dione motifs. Useful scaffold rearrangements and available amines also occur, and many leaders avoid the Parent leaders' reactive N-halogen or cyclic-cumulene environments. Child ring-closure-string incidences are 0.9517, 0.9552, 0.9034, 0.9736 and 0.8391 in fixed task order; aromatic-string incidences are 0.9437, 0.9506, 0.8471, 0.9678 and 0.731. These are incidences of text features, not perceived ring counts or aromatic-atom fractions. Formal-charge and stereocentre-string incidences are 0.0 throughout, despite available amines and potentially stereogenic saturated centres. The digest reports 639, 782, 783, 702 and 765 distinct identities across the respective Child panels. A separate check confirms 300 distinct accepted identities within every task/seed, so cross-seed recurrence is not within-run duplicate evaluation or a failure of the budget ledger. Diversity is moderate across the recognizable molecular families and narrower among repeated leading series. The moderate drug-likeness judgement reflects familiar amide, ether, carbonyl and amine chemistry in the leaders, not strong biological performance or proved synthesis. Synthetic plausibility remains questionable for parts of the evaluated stream because of N-O/N-N ring connections, unusual sulfur or halogen environments, enlarged joined frameworks and unspecified stereochemistry. The strongest Child leaders do not universally have those liabilities; conventional-looking molecules can still have substantially lower supplied scores than questionable Parent molecules. Read-only RDKit perception supports size and functional-group descriptions; no new objective, feasibility or affinity scores were calculated. The initial observations, the frozen usable breeding cohort, and the subset actually selected as scored parents are distinct. For each retained task/seed leader, the audit joins its pool, emission and accepted-observation records and the recorded scored starting parents. The registered condition fixes initial-cohort breeding sources while retaining real accepted-label posterior allocation and live survivor updates. Source excerpts were read to interpret those records; this report does not decide activation or isolation. An unscored mutation intermediate or crossover product is not a newly scored breeding parent. A product can differ substantially from its initial sources through crossover and successive graph edits; fixed scored ancestry does not imply one atom edit or conservation of an initial scaffold. A pool member, an emitted offspring, an accepted scored molecule, a live survivor and the retained best endpoint are also different observations. The digest and chemical frequencies describe accepted trajectories, not every pool member or rejected graph. The digest final_molecules are late seed-2 evaluations, not the best molecule of every seed. No absence from the evaluated leaders is promoted into absence from the full pool, and unselected alternatives receive no invented labels. The original n-c55c3d520a2c chemistry report and its carry-forward in n-62daf219c70a were read through the fresh evidence index. Each transferable gap retains its original provenance and current conditions. Only digest/trusted-trajectory Child SMILES are quoted; Parent-only molecules are described by published task/seed/evaluation. Audits under .slots/r0018-02-ablation-L01/molecular/ include trajectory_audit.json, inspected_records.json, leader_provenance.json with log/source hashes, identity_scope_check.json and history_molecular_sources.json. No source or trajectory path was missing. Chemical resemblance and leader ancestry do not isolate the effect of a particular edit, membership/rank/size change or survival rule, identify mediation, or establish the contribution of the entire graph-evolution foundation. The retained predictive learning channel and live survivors prevent interpreting this condition as deletion of all feedback or the full optimizer.

per_task.generated_character: The leading molecules in all Child seeds are compact N-H indole carboxanilides with ordinary aryl fluorine, methoxy, methyl and sometimes methylthio substituents. They retain the recognizable aromatic/amide organization of the initial trimethoxyindole anilide, while replacing or relocating peripheral methoxy groups. A separate useful family is a phenyl/heteroaryl pyrazoline bearing a thioacyl group; the output is therefore not restricted to the indole skeleton. Mean Child SMILES length is 40.3, with a maximum of 63 and halogen-string incidence 0.754. These leading indole amides have relatively conventional bonds and no N-halogen or peroxide motif. The Parent leaders instead include an amino-substituted cumulene on N-chloro indole (seed 0, evaluation 289), an N-hydroxy pyridyl amide with N-F (seed 1, 293), and an N-chloro indole vicinal diketone (seed 2, 294). The Child leaders look chemically more familiar locally, while all matched retained scores are lower. That contrast does not establish that the Parent liabilities are required.
liabilities: The leading indole amides have conventional local bonding; their limitations concern repetitive leading chemistry and unverified overall properties rather than a universal reactive-bond defect.
Thioacyl, methylthio and thiolmethyl variants require environment-specific stability assessment, while enlarged acetal-bearing or ring-opened relatives introduce additional conformational complexity.
Conventional small rings and tiny stable molecules can still score zero when the combined molecular context is absent; that is a score observation, not chemical invalidity.
missing_features: The leading set does not consistently explore distinct compact arrangements beyond variants of the initial indole amide; the useful pyrazoline family is a real exception, so there is no global inability to change scaffold.

Conventional alternative frameworks expressing the stronger Parent score associations are not demonstrated at comparable scores, but the observed ordering does not identify an exact absent pharmacophore or justify requiring N-halogen bonds.
Stereochemical identity is unresolved in the saturated pyrazoline and more complex relatives, although the flat leading indole amides themselves do not require a stereocentre assignment.

A dimethoxy/methyl relative scores 0.36371550417720466, while a methoxy/dimethyl leader reaches 0.38277504802042894; another positional isomer shares 0.38277504802042894. The methylthio-containing seed-1 and seed-2 leaders score 0.38236359684532834 and 0.38236359684532834. The pyrazoline thioacyl example reaches 0.37402294333585284, compared with 0.1501184006136499 for the related initial pyrazoline/thioamide framework. Inserting a methylene between indole and its amide gives 0.22116953418646673, a large acetal-bearing aryl substituent gives 4.874557967239721e-07, and isolated oxetane scores 0.0. These observations favor a compact connected aromatic/polar arrangement and particular peripheral composition; they do not support merely adding rings or heteroatoms. Structurally nearby evaluated examples are comparisons, not a demonstrated scored ancestor chain. Matched retained best scores, Child / Parent, are seed 0: 0.38277504802042894 / 0.39405142067435733; seed 1: 0.38236359684532834 / 0.47411701813450596; seed 2: 0.38236359684532834 / 0.438972502037081. per_task.generated_character: The seed-1 leader (evaluation 15) is a methoxy/methyl-substituted benzofused N/O carbonyl heterocycle linked to a fluorinated biaryl nitrile. Seed 0 instead reaches an extended chromenone-like polyaryl nitrile bearing an additional fused diaza-aromatic unit. Seed 2 joins a related aryl/pyridyl nitrile carbonyl system to an aryl-substituted fused nitrogen dione. These are medium-sized to extended aromatic assemblies with recognizable nitrile, ether and carbonyl groups. Mean Child SMILES length is 61.4, maximum 130, and halogen-string incidence 0.3874. The leaders avoid the O-F, peroxide and N=S chemistry in the Parent seed-0 and seed-2 leaders, but some Child examples are much larger and more aryl-rich. Leader receipts link the current examples to initial aryl nitrile/carbonyl, dione or quinoline-containing sources; the seed-1 leader records successive graph edits, so a fixed scored source is not a one-edit neighbourhood. The Parent compact linked carbonyl-thione leader (seed 0, evaluation 281) and other Parent leaders (seeds 1 and 2, evaluation 296) remain higher-scoring. Their reactive local groups do not make them validated chemical targets.
liabilities: Extended polyaryl surfaces and numerous linked ring systems create size, conformation and synthetic-route concerns even when their local bonds are conventional.
Some lower-scoring evaluated recombinations introduce unusual carbonyl/sulfone connections; similar-looking aromatic richness does not preserve the useful functional arrangement automatically.

The largest joined molecules add considerable connectivity without consistently exceeding the smaller leaders. A molecular graph and a score do not establish accessibility or useful physical properties.
missing_features: The Child evaluated leaders do not recover the compact Parent seed-0 heterocyclic organization. This is a missing high-scoring arrangement in the evaluated set, not proof that similar chemistry is absent from the generated pool.

Reliable compact alternatives to the extended polyaryl combinations are not established throughout the leading set; the comparatively compact seed-1 leader shows that less molecular bulk can already be useful.
No exact missing target motif follows from these scalar scores, and the useful Child nitriles and ordinary ethers argue against a requirement for the Parent peroxide or O-F groups.

per_task.generated_character: Much of the evaluated Child material retains the initial fluoromethoxy-biaryl carboxylic-acid/amide/pyrrolidine framework and its aryl-sulfonyl region. The seed-0 leader (evaluation 294) adds an aryl methyl and places a methylene between pyrrolidine nitrogen and the aryl sulfone, leaving an available tertiary amine. The seed-1 leader instead has an expanded partially unsaturated nitrogen ring and an enamine-like linkage while retaining the bulky acid/sulfonamide context. The strongest Child example, seed 2 evaluation 121, is smaller: an aryl carboxylic acid linked through a secondary amine/methylene to N-methylpyrrolidine, with the aryl sulfone and amide carbonyl absent. Mean Child SMILES length is 67.4, maximum 135, and halogen-string incidence 0.8851. The bulky acid/amide/sulfone assemblies coexist with that more recognizable available-amine derivative. The Parent leaders are a flexible aryl tertiary amine (seed 0, evaluation 284), an aminoalkyl pyrrolidine/aryl ether (seed 1, 261), and a pyrrolidine/fused thioether/biaryl framework (seed 2, 241). The Child therefore does produce useful available amines, but does not consistently reach the Parent's stronger aryl-amine arrangements across evaluated seeds.
liabilities: Several leading or late evaluated examples remain bulky and multifunctional, with large halogenated aryl surfaces plus acid, amide and sulfone regions; their combined physical properties and synthesis are untested.

Unassigned stereochemistry and different amine/amide/sulfonamide environments prevent treating all nitrogen-containing variants as equivalent pharmacological objects.
missing_features: Available aliphatic amines in a useful aryl environment are not consistently realized across the evaluated seed leaders, despite a clear successful example. Basic amines are not absent from the chemistry or from the initial observations.

The output does not consistently disentangle useful aryl/amine relationships from bulky acid/amide/sulfone or acetal material. The acid-retaining leader is an explicit limit on any recommendation to remove all acidic groups.

The N-methylpyrrolidine amide relative scores 0.11854231818713744 and the corresponding amine/methylene-linked example 0.6832960028134325. per_task.generated_character: The Child seed-0 and seed-2 leaders are small N-alkyl trimethoxyindole carboxamides; seed 2 also has an indole methyl substituent. The seed-1 leader is a hydroxy/methyl azaaryl group linked to an aryl-substituted fused nitrogen dione. These leading molecules are unfluorinated and use conventional amide or dione chemistry. Large joined structures and oxygen-rich acetal frameworks add substantial complexity while scoring extremely poorly in this record. Their poor values do not reveal which individual region is responsible.
Some evaluated proposals still introduce peroxide or N-Cl chemistry, but these do not define the leading Child family and cannot be assigned as mediators of the overall paired loss.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The general chemistry concern originates in n-c55c3d520a2c and was carried by n-62daf219c70a. It is assessed here in n-4d4b5eafa8b3 versus that published Parent on complete matched Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2, 300 observations per objective, batch size 10 and the frozen Research-in-Depth epoch-1 profile with direct aromatic exchange disabled. The current condition fixes initial usable scored breeding sources while retaining real accepted-label posterior allocation, graph intermediates and live survivor updates. Evidence concerns accepted evaluated molecules and their leaders; it is not a census of unselected pool chemistry, a total-foundation deletion test or additional historical replication. Leading output repeatedly retains indole carboxamides, aryl nitrile/carbonyl systems, pyrrolidine acid/amide material and nitrogen diones. Identical or closely related evaluated molecules recur across seeds, while the stronger Parent leading arrangements are often absent from the corresponding Child leaders. Counterexamples include a useful pyrazoline thioacyl family, linked heteroaromatic recombinations, new carbonyl-ring closures and a substantially improved available-amine derivative. Every current retained best exceeds its fixed initial best, so the finding is limited useful coverage rather than absence of molecular novelty or useful search.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently provide independent useful arrangements beyond recurring initial functional-group and scaffold combinations in evaluated output.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support chemically coherent alternatives that reorganize learned useful relationships under the legal task-local source and feedback rules, and assess their actual evaluated descendants. Do not equate new strings or one-edit distances with meaningful scaffold coverage. These observations cannot prescribe a benchmark-specific scaffold, show that missing chemistry was unavailable in the pool, or attribute an endpoint effect separately to membership, rank, cohort size, survival or the entire optimizer.

Conversely, another initial molecule already has an available cyclic amine but scores poorly, and tiny fragments or large joined acetal/aryl systems also perform poorly. Differentiate amine, amide and sulfonamide environments instead of treating nitrogen count as basicity. A fixed molecular-size cutoff or universal polar-group deletion is not supported, and structurally near evaluated examples must not be mistaken for scored ancestor/descendant steps.

nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

approach.method_basis: The Parent searches a tree of partial SMILES strings. It initializes each objective's tree from the supplied scored molecules, chooses token branches using their average accepted return and an upper confidence exploration bonus, and expands branches supported by a corpus-trained language model. That model remains frozen and completes selected prefixes into whole molecules. Accepted scores update the generating paths. To fill a proposal batch, the Parent selects a block of rollout paths before generating their completions, using the same completed-observation counts for every selection in that block.
approach.novelty: Add pending-path counts to UCT so each selected rollout reserves its path before the next path is chosen. The exploration bonus then accounts for both completed and outstanding work, while average rewards continue to use accepted observations. Reservations disappear when a rollout is discarded or its feedback arrives. This tests whether acknowledging work already assigned reduces repeated sampling from one prefix during a batch. This lineage currently contains only the Parent; no sibling has tested pending-aware selection.

nodes.hypothesis: Reserve each selected rollout along its prefix path and include completed plus pending counts in UCT's exploration term, while retaining accepted-only empirical reward means; release each reservation when the rollout is discarded or its observation resolves.

finding_summary.headline: Reservations spread evaluated rollouts across prefixes; the screening score falls
finding_summary.insights: Delayed-feedback concentration is controllable with the existing frozen generator and accepted-only reward estimates. The controlled replay establishes that outstanding work changes actual choices, and the emitted-molecule analysis establishes that the added branch coverage survives invalid, duplicate and surplus filtering. However, almost complete dispersion across ten starting prefixes did not produce a better overall best molecule within the screening budget. This leaves the useful balance between branch reuse and wider allocation open; the score losses do not establish that reservations are generally harmful. The molecular assessment found broadly diverse ring chemistry comparable to the Parent, with useful amine and heteroaromatic motifs already reachable but inconsistent control of their arrangement and whole-molecule growth. That narrows the unresolved problem to obtaining and refining useful chemical combinations: a larger count of distinct SMILES prefixes alone does not establish better chemical coverage. These structural observations suggest an explanation to investigate, not a demonstrated cause of the score decrease. One seed supports activation and a mixed score outcome, without establishing reproducibility or which degree of allocation spread would improve final Top-1.
finding_summary.results: On the single paired screening seed, pending work changed 4,361 of 5,834 branch decisions with a choice between eligible children (74.75%). Of these changes, 3,961 came from altered UCT rankings among completed children; another 400 involved priority for children without completed observations. All 2,900 reservations resolved exactly once, without negative counts, leaks or changes to completed reward statistics. Mean concentration of evaluated rollout-start prefixes fell from 0.809379 to 0.117517 across 145 batches, and distinct prefixes per ten-molecule batch rose from 1.73 to 9.54. Single-prefix batches fell from 76 of 145 to zero, with lower concentration on all five objectives and every paired batch. Both runs delivered all 1,450 valid, unique optimizer proposals within the same oracle budget and retained identical frozen prior weights. The macro final Top-1 score nevertheless fell from 0.479189 to 0.473468, a decrease of 0.005720. Final scores rose for zaleplon_mpo (0.394920 to 0.409811), drd2_docking (0.977922 to 0.999998), and median_2 (0.179942 to 0.180094), while deco_hop fell from 0.606003 to 0.580076 and sitagliptin_mpo from 0.237157 to 0.197364. The proposed allocation mechanism is confirmed; its expected positive score effect was not observed.

molecular.headline: Diverse aromatic and saturated ring chemistry; missing stereochemical specification and consistent control of useful motif arrangements.
molecular.overall_character: All five supplied seed-0 trajectories and their Parent counterparts were read; no task lacks a trajectory. Each current trajectory contains 300 unique molecules, including 290 optimizer proposals. Evaluation numbers below refer to these current trajectories unless explicitly marked Parent. The proposals are predominantly ring-containing medicinal-chemistry-like structures: linked phenyl and aza-aromatic rings, fused heterocycles, piperidines, piperazines, amides, sulfonamides, ethers, phenols and occasional highly elaborate polycycles. The digest ring-closure occurrence rates are 0.9897 to 1.0 and aromatic-token occurrence rates are 0.9517 to 0.9862; these are fractions of proposal strings containing the relevant tokens, not aromatic-atom fractions or perceived ring counts. Mean SMILES lengths are 37.6 to 39.8 characters, with task maxima from 70 to 87 characters; these are size proxies, not molecular weights. Structural breadth is real and comparable to the Parent, including both aromatic and saturated ring families. Basic cyclic amines are clearly present and must not be called globally missing. Every task has stereocentre_rate 0.0, even though some structures contain potentially stereogenic saturated frameworks. The major deficits are unassigned stereochemistry, inconsistent arrangement of already available polar and aromatic motifs, and excursions into oversized or chemically awkward assemblies. Common scaffolds look makeable in principle, but the peroxyester, unusual imine/imidic-acid representations, densely substituted fused systems and very large appendages justify a questionable overall synthesis reading. This is a structural assessment of the supplied seed, not a synthetic-route validation or an activation judgement.

per_task.generated_character: Ring-rich aromatic and heteroaromatic molecules dominate: ring_closure_rate 0.9966, aromatic_atom_rate 0.9586 and mean SMILES length 39.3. Evaluation 64 is a fused sulfur/nitrogen heterocycle with an oxo group, hydroxymethyl substituent and aminomethyl-linked biphenyl; evaluation 89 is an aminomethyl biphenyl bearing a fluorobenzamide; evaluation 264 is an N-acylated, partly saturated fused nitrogen ring system. The initial indole carboxamide at evaluation 9 already combines a compact aromatic framework with amide and methoxy groups. These are recognisable small-molecule scaffold combinations, although fused-core preparation and substitution selectivity would need examination. The low end includes a long-chain phosphorus-acid/thioether assembly, a large polyaryl polyamine and a tiny nitrotriazole. Rings and functional-group variety are abundant; stereochemical assignments are absent.
liabilities: Evaluation 15 couples extensive hydrocarbon growth to multiple phosphorus-acid oxygens, while evaluation 183 combines large aromatic bulk with several amine-containing appendages; both illustrate poor control of whole-molecule size and polarity.

The dibrominated, multiply substituted cyclopentene at evaluation 38 and the elaborate fused systems raise substitution-selectivity and stereochemical preparation questions even though their graphs were accepted.
missing_features: Most weak examples lack the balanced, intermediate-sized aromatic-plus-polar arrangement visible in the stronger examples: some are too small and sparsely decorated, while others carry long chains or excessive appended ring systems.

A controlled set of close variants preserving a promising ring arrangement while adjusting heteroatom position, linker length or polar substituents is not demonstrated by the cited high and final examples. Their diversity does not identify one additional mandatory functional group.

Explicit stereochemical specification is missing from the substituted saturated frameworks, including evaluation 38. The supplied scores do not establish whether specifying it would improve this objective.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Evaluation 64 scores 0.409810651230724, evaluation 89 scores 0.4020361505269851 and the initial indole amide scores 0.3051048083696145. In contrast, the long-chain phosphorus-containing evaluation 15 scores 0.0, the bulky polyamine at evaluation 183 scores 2.20671388958451e-47, and the small nitrotriazole at evaluation 77 scores 9.100886676973802e-15. The visible association is with an intermediate-sized aromatic framework carrying a restrained arrangement of polar substituents, rather than with simply adding rings, nitrogen or charge. It is not a universal amide requirement: some other high scorers lack an amide. The late piperazine/sulfonamide/piperidine assembly at evaluation 299 scores only 1.7564413240447329e-06, despite having familiar medicinal groups; the digest median is 0.007587. Parent evaluation 272 reached 0.3949199041196016 with an aryl nitrile/pyridyl/furyl thiourea assembly. The current best changes the particular scaffold while retaining the broad combination of aromatic bulk and short polar functions; it does not reveal a new globally absent ring class.

per_task.generated_character: The output spans ordinary aromatic amides and heterocycles through saturated amine-rich, multi-ring molecules. Ring_closure_rate is 0.9931, aromatic_atom_rate 0.9828 and mean SMILES length 37.7. per_task.generated_character: A broad mixture of multi-ring nitrogen heterocycles, aromatic amides, sulfonamides, piperazines and methoxy/methylenedioxy aromatics appears. Mean SMILES length is 39.8, ring_closure_rate 0.9897 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.969. Evaluation 73 is an iodinated aminocarbazole with pyridyl and N-methylpiperidyl appendages. Evaluation 218 combines an ethyl sulfonamide, piperazine amide and methylenedioxyaryl unsaturated acyl group; evaluation 188 is a fused aromatic lactam bearing methoxy groups and a tertiary sulfonamide. These are chemically distinct polar aromatic assemblies, not a collapsed scaffold family. Their components are familiar medicinal chemistry, but heavily substituted fused systems and dense halogenation add preparation and physical-property concerns. Small nonaromatic sulfur compounds, an adamantane-derived guanidine-like structure and a chlorinated peroxyester populate the lower end.
liabilities: Evaluation 289 contains a peroxyester O-O linkage in a multiply chlorinated unsaturated chain, a chemical-stability and preparation liability rather than ordinary drug-like decoration.
The iodocarbazole at evaluation 73 and the multiply halogenated aromatic piperazine at evaluation 19 add heavy aromatic/halogen burden; such bulk is not itself evidence of better chemistry.

The conjugated unsaturated amide at evaluation 218 and the exocyclic unsaturated carbonyl system at evaluation 120 merit reactivity scrutiny; their existence does not establish that the objective rewards covalent reactivity.
missing_features: Small sulfur-containing and minimally decorated ring molecules lack the combined aromatic framework and distributed carbonyl, sulfonamide or amino functionality seen in the stronger examples. No single one of those groups is shared by every strong example.

A convincing, locally varied arrangement of these features is not demonstrated: chemically remote aromatic assemblies attain similar modest scores. The evidence supports a missing combination of features, not a specific reference scaffold or mandatory halogen.

per_task.generated_character: Every proposal has a ring-closure token, aromatic_atom_rate is 0.9862 and mean SMILES length is 39.0, but the longest string reaches 87 characters. Stronger examples are relatively compact nitrogen-rich heteroaromatics with exposed donor/acceptor sites: evaluation 291 joins an N-methylimino N/N/S heterocycle to a hydroxylated methylindole; evaluation 68 joins an aminocyclopentyl indole to a triazole; evaluation 42 combines a phenolic oxygen-containing fused ring, diazine and pyrrolidine. liabilities: The zero-scoring glycoside and triterpenoid-like oxime-ether ester are elaborate, densely functionalised structures with unspecified stereochemistry and substantial synthetic complexity.

The exocyclic imino heterocycle at evaluation 291, the aryl imine at evaluation 55 and the imidic-acid representation at evaluation 300 raise tautomer, hydrolysis or configurational questions that are not resolved by the recorded score.

The stronger compact heterocyclic combinations are not accompanied in the digest by a coherent series that preserves their arrangement while varying one substituent. The missing capability is precise co-arrangement, not globally absent fluorine, amines or heterocycles.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The digest stereocentre_rate is 0.0 on every supplied task, as in the Parent. The emitted aminocyclopentyl structure NC1CCC(c2c[nH]c3ccc(-n4cnnc4)cc23)C1 and substituted cyclopentene OCC1CC(n2cncn2)=C(c2cc(Br)cc(O)c2Br)C1c1ccccc1 contain saturated substitution patterns whose stereochemical alternatives are not specified. This establishes an output representation gap, not a measured score gain from stereochemistry.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not emit explicit stereochemical identities for its saturated and potentially stereogenic structures.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make stereochemical specification available in de novo generation and preserve it through identity handling. Let accepted observations from the current session determine whether particular configurations are useful; do not assume every objective distinguishes them.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The structure c1ccc2c(c1)CCCN2CCCN1CCC(c2noc3ccccc23)CC1 scores 0.999998249672007, while the later amine-containing c1ccc(N2CCN(C(Cn3cccn3)c3ccncc3)CC2)cc1 scores 0.19802005266210823. In another supplied trajectory, O=S(=O)(Nc1ccc(-n2ccnc2)cc1)c1cccc2cnccc12 scores 0.5732259891576988 but O=S(=O)(CCNCCOc1ccc(Br)cc1)c1ccc(F)cc1 scores 0.2715410107705054. Both comparisons retain broad functional-group categories while changing connectivity and environment; they are observational contrasts, not matched molecular pairs. The output already contains cyclic amines and sulfur chemistry, so adding those categories alone would not address the gap.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not demonstrate controlled variation of linker geometry and nitrogen environment while preserving a promising ring arrangement.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support de novo conditional variations that can retain a locally promising ring framework while changing linker length, attachment position or a nitrogen functional state separately. Derive any retained arrangement only from accepted observations within the current session, without a task-specific motif library.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Task mean SMILES lengths stay between 37.6 and 39.8 characters, but long and elaborate tails remain. The long-chain phosphorus-acid structure O=P(O)(O)OP(=O)(O)c1cncc(CCCC#CCCCCCCC(O)CSCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCO)c1 scores 0.0, as do the bulky oxime-ether ester and glycoside cited above. A large polar guanidine/sulfonamide assembly and a large hydrophobic polyaryl amine score 2.1621778663534096e-63 and 4.5515839886258796e-63 in the same trajectory, while its compact heterocyclic examples reach 0.19736413136179395 and 0.18901307662677713. Conversely, a tiny nitrotriazole in another trajectory also scores poorly, so indiscriminate shortening is unsupported.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably control whole-molecule size and polar appendage growth around useful chemical arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Allow de novo generation to adjust scaffold extent, branch growth and polar substitution separately, preserving enough context to learn which combinations the current accepted observations favor. Use adaptive chemical size control rather than treating SMILES length as molecular weight or imposing a universal small-molecule cutoff.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The emitted chlorinated peroxyester C=C(Cl)C(Cl)C(Cl)CCOOC(C)=O scores 0.02101192765437668 and the activated nitroalkene/sulfone C=C([N+](=O)[O-])S(=O)(=O)c1ccccc1 scores 9.203194082858293e-05. Other cited structures contain imidic-acid representations, dense halogen substitution and elaborate unassigned polycycles. In contrast, some common amide, ether and cyclic-amine combinations score well. transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently distinguish a valid molecular graph from a chemically ordinary, plausibly preparable arrangement.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Expose chemical-stability, tautomer and synthetic-complexity context during generation or candidate review, so accepted feedback can distinguish useful diversity from awkward assemblies. Prefer coherent chemistry learned from the permitted unlabeled corpus; avoid blanket bans on heteroatoms, formal charge or all uncommon groups.

nodes.method_name: ChemTS: UCT-guided SMILES prefix search with a frozen rollout prior
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in [ChemTS](https://arxiv.org/html/1710.00616v1): train a compact autoregressive SMILES model solely on the supplied unlabeled corpus during preparation, then freeze it. For each independent objective, maintain a fresh prefix tree whose nodes hold visit counts and observed returns. Initialize its statistics from the supplied observations. Select prefixes through upper-confidence tree search, expand them using the frozen model's next-token distribution, and generate complete molecules by stochastic continuation. Backpropagate accepted oracle scores through the corresponding paths after feedback. Generate further continuations until the evaluator-announced batch contains distinct canonical structures. This is an expanding generative tree, with no corpus ranking or fixed molecular candidate set. The hypothesis is that sharing each scarce reward across its visited prefixes directs subsequent continuations toward promising molecular families quickly enough to improve the mean of independent final Top-1 scores. The root adapts tree statistics; it does not update neural parameters with rewards. The paper supports this search mechanism, but its larger, time-limited experiments do not establish performance under this benchmark's scarce feedback. Learning a useful rollout prior within permitted preparation remains an empirical prerequisite.
