approach.method_basis: A genetic algorithm run directly on molecular graphs. It keeps a population of molecules that have already been scored by the objective, samples breeding parents from the high-scoring end of that population, and builds new candidates by cutting two parents apart and recombining connected fragments, and by making small local edits to atoms and bonds. Everything generated is sanitised, canonicalised and sent straight to the oracle; whatever comes back with a good score is merged into the population and the weakest members are dropped. There is no surrogate model, no pretrained network, no library of catalogue molecules to rank, and no cross-task memory: the only thing that steers the search is the scores of the molecules this run has itself already paid for.
approach.novelty: The method statement leaves the selection pressure, the population bookkeeping and the failure handling open, and this implementation fixes all three. Parents are drawn from three declared high-ranked score bands rather than from a single elite cut, so breeding stays broad while still being score-directed. Survival is greedy on a bounded population of sixty-four, seeded only from the ten scored molecules supplied at the start, with accepted offspring merged the moment their scores arrive so the very next batch already breeds from them. Proposals that come back invalid or already-seen are replaced by generating more molecules from the same operators, never by falling back to a fixed reserve list. Seven distinct atom and bond mutation operators sit alongside fragment crossover, and every breeding event logs its parent ranks, operator provenance and parent-beating outcome so the selection pressure can be checked after the fact rather than assumed.

nodes.hypothesis: Evolve a task-local population of scored molecular graphs by sampling breeding parents across high-ranked score quantiles, generating de novo offspring with graph crossover and atom/bond mutation, and greedily retaining the highest-scoring observed survivors after each feedback batch.

finding_summary.headline: Plain graph evolution with no learned model ranks third of thirteen Discovery roots, and every intended behaviour activated
finding_summary.insights: The campaign now has a strong, cheap baseline. Against the thirteen Discovery roots on this seed, which span 0.2331 to 0.5103, this root sits third at 0.4917, within 0.019 of the best method in the round, and it did that with no pretraining, no corpus-trained generator, no surrogate and no learned policy. That reframes what the more elaborate lineages have to justify: any learned component now has to earn its place against direct selection on task-local scores, not against a naive baseline. The interesting tension is that activation was clean while efficiency was not. Roughly six in seven oracle calls went to molecules that did not beat the parent that made them, and the mean offspring was worse than its parent, so the strong result comes from occasionally getting lucky at scale rather than from reliably climbing. That is precisely the bottleneck a proposal-filtering mechanism would attack, and it is the most concrete Development target this root produces. What is still open: one seed only, so no reliability claim and no anchor decision; no paired comparison against any other algorithm; and the retry machinery was never stressed, since the longest rejection streak was two, so behaviour on an exhausted or hostile neighbourhood is untested.
finding_summary.results: Macro mean 0.4917 on the single screening seed, with per-task finals of 0.5989 on deco_hop, 0.9051 on drd2_docking, 0.2083 on median_2, 0.3315 on sitagliptin_mpo and 0.4145 on zaleplon_mpo. All four pre-registered observables moved in the intended direction and the falsifier was not triggered. Parent selection was strongly score-directed: across 2225 breeding selections the mean topness percentile was 0.883 against a uniform baseline of 0.5, an enrichment of +0.383, and all three declared quantile bands were used on every task. Both operator families produced offspring on every task, with crossover behind 0.439 and atom/bond mutation behind 0.743 of the 1450 emitted molecules; 74 outer retries were needed for 1524 attempts. Feedback demonstrably changed the search: 1025 offspring were admitted to the population immediately, 432 distinct admitted offspring were later chosen as parents 2084 times, and reuse began in batch 2 on every task. Final population best rose above initialization everywhere, most sharply on drd2_docking (0.0190 to 0.9051) and sitagliptin_mpo (0.0021 to 0.3315). The one weak number is local improvement: only 201 of 1450 offspring, or 13.9 percent, strictly beat their best breeding parent, and the mean child-minus-best-parent difference was -0.084.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich, aromatic, entirely achiral molecules that converge hard onto one inherited scaffold per run, with an unstable-motif tail
molecular.overall_character: Across all five runs the generator emits ring-heavy, strongly aromatic molecules: ring-closure rate 0.92 to 0.99 and aromatic-atom rate 0.89 to 0.96 in every run, with essentially no cumulated double bonds (0.000 to 0.007). Mean SMILES length varies widely by run, from 38.8 to 70.2, which shows the graph operators do grow and shrink molecules in response to feedback. What each run converges on is recognisably a decorated descendant of one of the ten molecules it started with: the top twelve structures in a run typically share a complete skeleton and differ only in single-atom substituent swaps. Two systematic absences stand out. Stereocentre rate is exactly 0.000 in all five runs, so the generator never writes a stereochemical assignment even when it builds tetrahedral ring-fusion carbons. Charged-atom rate is also exactly 0.000 everywhere, so no ionised or zwitterionic forms are ever proposed. Alongside the plausible majority there is a persistent tail of chemistry a bench chemist would reject outright: peroxide and trioxide chains, N-hypofluorite groups, S-O-N linkages, and degenerate one- and two-atom fragments that still consume oracle calls.

per_task.generated_character: Almost every proposal is a 6-5 fused bicyclic heteroaromatic carrying an aryl carboxamide. The entire top of the run is one indole or azaindole 2-carboxamide anilide skeleton rewritten with methyl, ethyl, methoxy, fluoromethyl and halogen swaps, and that skeleton is visibly a decorated version of the best molecule the run was handed at the start.
liabilities: Peroxide O-O linkages introduced by crossover between two aromatic cores
Bare one- and two-atom fragments such as elemental halides submitted as candidates
Thioamide substitution of the amide carbonyl, giving a metabolically unstable analogue
missing_features: No ring systems beyond the inherited bicycle - no bridged, spiro or tricyclic cores are ever built
No stereodefined sp3 centres anywhere in the run
No basic or ionizable side chain to balance the neutral amide core
No ring-size variation, since every new ring closed is five- or six-membered
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Score tracks how completely the inherited skeleton survives. The three structures tied at 0.4145 all keep the fused bicycle, the ring NH, the exocyclic amide and the 4-fluoroanilide intact and differ only at one substituent. The zero tail is either a one- or two-atom fragment or an oversized crossover product that fused two whole copies of the scaffold together, so the objective gives no partial credit for half a scaffold.

per_task.generated_character: The run settles on the xanthine, or purine-2,6-dione, core carried in from the starting set. It is N-aminated with a halogenated aminopyridine and decorated with a second aryl or heteroaryl ring, and most of the top structures also hang a conjugated polyene or enamine tail off the core. Mean SMILES length reaches 56.6, so molecules here grow substantially larger than their parents.
liabilities: N-hypofluorite groups written on the imide nitrogen, which is not a real functional group
Long conjugated polyene tails built by repeated mutation at the same site
Peroxide and N-N-O chains formed by blind heteroatom substitution
missing_features: No saturated or partially saturated linker to place the decoration out of the core plane
No stereochemistry on the sp3 centres it does create
No ring systems beyond fused five- and six-membered rings and simple biaryl links
No acidic or basic ionizable group anywhere in the run
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The objective barely separates anything: the whole run lies between 0.500 and 0.599, and the starting molecules already scored 0.500 to 0.548, so the entire 29-batch search bought about 0.05. Everything sitting exactly at the 0.500 floor is a one- to three-heavy-atom fragment, which means the score behaves mostly as a has-any-structure indicator with a small decoration bonus on top.

per_task.generated_character: This is the one run whose winners look like a real receptor-ligand series. The strongest structures pair a 2-aryl-pyridine with an N-alkyl pyrrolidine or piperidine basic amine, several carrying a free carboxylic acid on the connecting carbon. Molecules are the largest of the five runs at mean length 70.2, and the ring-closure rate is the highest at 0.986.
liabilities: Aryl thiol substituents on the biaryl tail, which would oxidise readily
S-O-N chains produced by heteroatom substitution on the aromatic ring
Free aldehyde groups retained on high-scoring structures
missing_features: No stereochemistry, despite genuine tetrahedral centres in the winning series
No explicit protonated ammonium form of the basic amines
No conformationally constrained bicyclic amine head groups
No aromatic ring systems larger than a single biaryl pair
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Score rises steeply with the presence of a protonatable N-alkyl saturated amine attached to a biaryl tail. The 0.905 and 0.884 structures both carry exactly that pair, whereas the 0.0004 to 0.002 tail retains the aromatic halves and has lost the basic nitrogen entirely. Adding halogen and thiol decoration to the tail while keeping the amine moves the score only within the 0.72 to 0.91 band, so the amine is the discontinuity and the decoration is fine-tuning.

per_task.generated_character: One fused polycyclic aminal-plus-cyclic-urea cage bearing an ethoxy-substituted aryl arm dominates the entire top of the run. The twelve best differ only in whether individual ring carbonyls are C=O or C=N, whether the aryl arm is propyl or butanoyl, and whether an extra amino group is present. Halogen rate is 0.145, the lowest of the five runs, so the generator essentially stopped using halogens here.
liabilities: Aminal N-CH2-N motifs at the heart of every top structure, which would hydrolyse readily
Cumulated allene-type double bonds appearing in a small fraction of proposals
Enamine C=C linkages conjugated into the ring carbonyls
missing_features: No aromatic variation beyond an unsubstituted or amino-substituted phenyl ring
No halogen substitution anywhere on the winning series
No stereochemistry on the several sp3 ring-fusion atoms in the cage
No alternative cage topology - the same fused system is reused for the whole run
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The band is extremely narrow, 0.2008 to 0.2083 across the whole top twelve, while the losing tail is trivially small - a single carbon, acetonitrile, ethanol, isopropyl chloride. So the gradient rewards keeping the complete cage plus arm assembled and is almost flat once that assembly exists, which is why the search plateaued at 0.2038 for batches 14 through 21.

per_task.generated_character: Compact, heavily oxygenated fused polycyclics: a methoxylated benzene fused to an imidazole and to a dioxole or dioxane ring, usually with one fluorine sitting on a ketal-like carbon. Mean SMILES length is 38.8, the shortest of the five runs, and the aromatic rate drops to 0.886, so this run built more saturated ring content than the others.
liabilities: Peroxide and trioxide chains such as O-O-O-C appearing in the zero-scoring tail
Orthoester and ketal carbons carrying both a fluorine and two alkoxy groups
One- and two-atom fragments submitted as candidates and consuming oracle calls
missing_features: No trifluoromethyl or polyfluorinated aliphatic groups
No primary aliphatic amine or amide nitrogen chain
No stereochemistry, although the chemistry this objective rewards is stereodefined
No open-chain flexible backbone - almost everything proposed is caged
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The 0.331 winner and its 0.271, 0.250 and 0.238 followers are the same tetracyclic ketal-imidazole with the fluorine and methoxy positions permuted, so the run is a single-scaffold decoration search. Everything at zero is either a single atom, a diatomic, or an oversized dimer built by crossover, and the median score of 0.031 against a best of 0.331 shows how sharply the objective drops away from that one cage.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The stereocentre rate is exactly 0.000 in all five independent runs, across 1450 proposed molecules, even though the winning series in several runs contain genuine tetrahedral carbons - a substituted pyrrolidine attached to a biaryl, ring-fusion carbons in a fused aminal cage - where configuration would change the chemistry entirely.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator has no concept of stereochemistry at all
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The operator set writes only flat connectivity. A generator that can address three-dimensional chemistry needs mutation operators that set, invert and permute tetrahedral and double-bond configuration as first-class edits, and a novelty check that treats two configurations of the same skeleton as distinct molecules rather than as a duplicate to reject.

transferable_gaps.evidence: In every run the entire top twelve share a complete ring skeleton that is visibly present in one of the ten molecules the run was handed at the start, and successive improvements only swap single substituents on it. Where a new ring does appear it comes from fusing two copies of an existing core together, which produced oversized dimers that scored zero.
transferable_gaps.gap: Rings are inherited and decorated, never invented
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Fragment recombination plus atom and bond edits can decorate a skeleton but cannot construct an unseen ring system, so the reachable chemistry is bounded by whatever ring systems the starting molecules happen to contain. A generator would need ring-construction and ring-breaking operators, or a fragment source outside the current population, to reach scaffolds not present at initialization.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Bare one- and two-atom species - a chlorine atom, a diatomic interhalogen, a single carbon, acetonitrile, ethanol - were emitted as candidates and consumed oracle evaluations, scoring zero every time. At the other extreme, crossover produced dimers well over 140 characters that also scored zero. Both extremes appear in the worst-scoring set of multiple runs.
transferable_gaps.gap: No control over what counts as a submittable molecule
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Validity is being checked only as chemical sanitisation, which a lone halogen passes. A generator spending a fixed evaluation budget needs a size and complexity floor and ceiling on emitted structures, so that operator accidents are rejected and regenerated locally instead of being paid for at the oracle.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Peroxide and trioxide chains linking two aromatic rings, N-hypofluorite groups written onto an imide nitrogen, and S-O-N chains on an aromatic ring all appear among the proposed molecules, in some cases inside otherwise reasonable structures. These are products of substituting one heteroatom for another without any check on the resulting local environment.
transferable_gaps.gap: Blind heteroatom substitution creates motifs that cannot exist as stable compounds
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The mutation alphabet treats all heteroatom swaps as equivalent. A generator would need a substructure-level plausibility screen applied after each edit, rejecting known-unstable local environments before the molecule is proposed, which costs nothing at the oracle and removes a systematic slice of wasted budget.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Within each run the twelve best molecules differ from one another by single-atom substituent swaps, and the population best plateaus for long stretches - fifteen consecutive batches with no improvement in one run, eight in another - while the population mean keeps creeping up. The search is refining a single basin rather than testing alternatives.
transferable_gaps.gap: Selection collapses onto one skeleton and cannot recover breadth
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Greedy score-ranked survival on a bounded population removes structural variety faster than the operators can regenerate it, so the population converges to near-duplicates and breeding produces near-duplicates in turn. A generator needs an explicit diversity term in survival, a similarity cap on the retained population, or a restart mechanism, so that budget spent after a plateau is spent somewhere new.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The charged-atom rate is exactly 0.000 in all five runs. Carboxylic acids and basic amines do appear, but always drawn in their neutral forms, and no quaternary, zwitterionic or explicitly ionised species is generated anywhere in 1450 molecules.
transferable_gaps.gap: No ionizable or charged chemistry is ever proposed
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The operators never place a formal charge, so a whole region of chemistry - permanently charged head groups, zwitterions, salt forms - is unreachable regardless of how the objective scores. A generator intended to cover ordinary medicinal chemistry needs charge-setting edits and a canonicalisation policy that preserves them.

nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

approach.method_basis: The failed NF-BO Parent searches around already scored molecules using an injective SELFIES sequence flow. It learns the flow density from unlabeled molecules, adapts the same flow to high-scoring observations within each independent objective, and re-encodes every observation before fitting its latent Gaussian process. It generates fresh trust-region proposals by perturbing whole token blocks according to estimated sequence-level pointwise mutual information, ranks them with correlated Thompson samples, and decodes through the explicit inverse flow. Canonical validity and novelty checks refill each announced batch. This recovery retains that algorithm and every bound mechanism.
approach.novelty: This is a numerical recovery of the failed Parent, not a new research mechanism. Execute the loaded task-local flow, recurrent states, and its continuous latent path in double precision so that rounding drift is less likely to cross a token-decoding boundary after adaptation. Preserve the strict equality check for every token, including termination and padding, and retain every adaptation step. The proposed precision repair is not yet verified; success requires the original reconstruction checks and complete task execution.

nodes.hypothesis: Recover the recorded post-adaptation left-inverse crash by promoting the loaded task-local sequence flow and its continuous recurrent forward/inverse latent calculations from float32 to float64, with dtype-compatible probe assignment and unchanged strict token reconstruction checks.

finding_summary.headline: Double precision restores exact reconstruction and completes all five tasks; recorded best scores stay unchanged.
finding_summary.insights: The result supports finite-precision recurrent inverse drift as a recoverable implementation bottleneck: strict equality survives without omitting padding, dropping observations, or skipping adaptation. It does not identify the original mismatched token positions, so a padding-only explanation remains unproven. Numerical recovery also leaves the main search-quality questions intact. Nominal 95% GP intervals cover only 466 of 1,450 outcomes (32.1%); coverage on the 1,240 shared predictions is unchanged at 444 outcomes, and only 22 of the 210 added predictions are covered. In addition, 97.6% of examined decodes reproduce their generating center. The molecular assessment finds the same narrow high-scoring families and recurring unusual charged heteroatoms and chain growth, with weak chemical plausibility. These findings make surrogate calibration and useful, chemically credible local variation worth probing independently. Recovery is demonstrated for this seed and checkpoint under the existing budget; continuous inverse error still reaches 0.004864 in one successful check, so exact reconstruction here does not establish stability for arbitrary future histories.
finding_summary.results: On the screening seed, all five objectives complete 300 evaluations. The two sessions that previously stopped at 150 and 240 evaluations now finish, bringing the total from 1,290 to 1,500. All 300 reconstruction checks preserve the full padded token sequence and canonical molecule: 46,500 of 46,500 observation-check instances match exactly. At the former failure points, maximum continuous inverse error falls from 0.405526 to 0.000005301 on drd2_docking and from 0.404005 to 0.00000001510 on median_2. Preparation produces the identical checkpoint. All 150 online adaptations execute their original 24 steps, every GP fit uses freshly encoded observations, PMI still favors informative token blocks, and posterior uncertainty still affects selection. Every emitted batch contains ten valid novel molecules. The completed macro score is 0.419751565. All 1,290 shared trajectory records match the parent exactly, and the additional 210 evaluations produce no new task best. Because the parent lacks a complete macro score, these results establish numerical recovery without establishing a paired macro-score gain.

Preparation produces the identical checkpoint. All 150 online adaptations execute their original 24 steps, every GP fit uses freshly encoded observations, PMI still favors informative token blocks, and posterior uncertainty still affects selection. Every emitted batch contains ten valid novel molecules. The completed macro score is 0.419751565. All 1,290 shared trajectory records match the parent exactly, and the additional 210 evaluations produce no new task best. Because the parent lacks a complete macro score, these results establish numerical recovery without establishing a paired macro-score gain.

The result supports finite-precision recurrent inverse drift as a recoverable implementation bottleneck: strict equality survives without omitting padding, dropping observations, or skipping adaptation. It does not identify the original mismatched token positions, so a padding-only explanation remains unproven. Numerical recovery also leaves the main search-quality questions intact. Nominal 95% GP intervals cover only 466 of 1,450 outcomes (32.1%); coverage on the 1,240 shared predictions is unchanged at 444 outcomes, and only 22 of the 210 added predictions are covered. In addition, 97.6% of examined decodes reproduce their generating center. The molecular assessment finds the same narrow high-scoring families and recurring unusual charged heteroatoms and chain growth, with weak chemical plausibility. These findings make surrogate calibration and useful, chemically credible local variation worth probing independently. Recovery is demonstrated for this seed and checkpoint under the existing budget; continuous inverse error still reaches 0.004864 in one successful check, so exact reconstruction here does not establish stability for arbitrary future histories.

molecular.headline: Recognizable aryl and nitrogen heterocycles persist among the high scorers, amid unusual charged heteroatoms and unsaturated chains.
molecular.overall_character: Node n-50bccbe8104b produces recognizable aryl amides, diaryl nitrogen linkers, pyrrolidines and carbonyl-rich heterocycles, together with extensive ring opening, unusual heteroatom substitutions and chain growth. The seed-0 digest covers 300 records per task, including 290 optimizer proposals and 10 supplied initial molecules. Rings are frequent: the per-task ring-closure rates range from 0.631 to 0.9828, while aromatic-marker rates range from 0.3103 to 0.6517. These are fractions of SMILES containing text markers, not perceived ring counts or aromatic-atom fractions. The output is therefore neither ring-free nor uniformly aromatic. Its most recognizable higher-scoring series remain concentrated around a few aryl and nitrogen-containing frameworks, despite 300 unique recorded molecules per task. The collection has weak medicinal-chemistry plausibility because ordinary fragments are repeatedly connected through undercoordinated charged atoms, unusual multiply bonded boron, phosphorus or sulfur, labile-looking nitrogen/oxygen linkages, or long unsaturated tails. The synthetic-plausibility judgment concerns these specific combinations; it does not assert that all organoboron, organophosphorus, charged molecules or cumulenes are impossible. No synthesis or stability evidence is supplied, and no measured binding interpretation is inferred from a scalar score. Compared with Parent n-77c41c9bc036, every shared trajectory record is identical in molecule, score and evaluation order. Three full trajectories are unchanged; the other two extend identical prefixes from 150 and 240 records to 300. Every task retains the same recorded best score. The added chemistry continues the same structural families and liabilities. All score-gradient readings below describe associations within these supplied molecules, without assigning unseen objective requirements.

nodes.method_name: NF-BO: invertible sequence-flow search with token-adaptive latent proposals
nodes.method_thesis: Use NF-BO's SeqFlow mapping, exact left-inverse decoding, and token-adaptive trust-region search. Train a compact SELFIES flow on the permitted unlabeled corpus. Within each fresh objective session, adapt it using highly scored task-local sequences, re-encode all observations after updates, and fit a latent-space GP. Generate new latent proposals around scored observations by perturbing token blocks according to their estimated pointwise mutual information with the decoded sequence. Thompson sampling selects proposals for inverse-flow decoding. These mechanisms follow [NF-BO, Sections 4 and 5.3](https://arxiv.org/html/2504.14889v1). Regenerate as needed to fill the evaluator-announced batch with distinct canonical molecules; no corpus molecules are ranked or retrieved. The hypothesis is that score-directed local search around exactly reconstructable observations finds improving structures efficiently enough to raise the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Exact reconstruction alone is not the objective. Useful flow training and surrogate prediction under the permitted preparation and feedback remain empirical prerequisites.

approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds fresh molecular graphs from accepted high-scoring molecules using score-quantile parent sampling, connected-fragment crossover and local edits, including its retained formula-preserving aromatic nitrogen-position exchange. Stable canonical identity checks admit a surplus pool. A Gaussian process trained on the complete accepted archive uses counts of local molecular environments and generalized Tanimoto covariance to predict that pool. It currently fills the evaluation batch with independent correlated posterior draws, removing each chosen identity before the next draw. Accepted scores update both the breeding population and prediction archive.
approach.novelty: Make later batch choices account for uncertainty already represented by earlier pending selections. After choosing a molecule, condition the remaining draw residuals on that molecule taking its current posterior mean. This reduces shared random excursions without changing the fitted model or its predicted means. Earlier siblings changed breeding state, molecular edits, fingerprint representation or fitted noise; none coordinated the pending choices through this within-batch conditioning. The test asks whether that coordination improves the use of the existing pool, with changed selections and conditional variance measured separately from score.

nodes.hypothesis: Condition later within-batch posterior draw residuals on earlier selected pool molecules taking their current posterior means, so pending selections remove shared sampling uncertainty before subsequent masked maximization.

finding_summary.headline: Conditioning changes 287 batches, but the mean score falls slightly
finding_summary.insights:
The experiment establishes a real allocation effect and narrows its value: removing some shared posterior variation is insufficient by itself to improve the final best score on this panel. The intervention reaches a modest typical redundancy opportunity, with a larger tail, and still permits related high-mean molecules to occupy the same batch. Even on identical pools, average count-fingerprint similarity increased slightly while posterior correlation decreased. Lower model correlation therefore cannot substitute for chemical diversity or score evidence. More parent-beating offspring and more incremental incumbent improvements also proved insufficient as proxies for the final endpoint.

The lower MSE describes a changed adaptive search stream; the fitted prediction model and its means remained unchanged on shared inputs. Mean conditioning supplied no new labels and did not repair the already poor uncertainty coverage. Whether real pending outcomes would support these zero-innovation constraints remains open, and unobserved counterfactual choices cannot answer it. The molecular assessment further limits the small core-coverage gain: smaller assemblies now contain many more small or tightly bridged rings, while reactive bonds and unspecified stereochemistry persist. Graph-core novelty is not evidence of feasible chemistry. A stronger test of useful batch coordination would need to connect model redundancy to actual score dependence or chemically meaningful alternatives; this run rules out treating the measured contraction alone as evidence of that connection.
finding_summary.results:
All 3,915 within-batch projections executed correctly. On identical Child pools and random draws, they preserved all 435 first choices but changed 600 of 4,350 selection positions and 287 of 435 batch sets. Later selected molecules lost an average 3.30% of their original sampling variance; the median reduction was 0.81%. Mean absolute within-batch posterior correlation fell from 0.04721 to 0.04571, and mean nonempty molecular-core coverage rose slightly from 7.06 to 7.14 cores per ten-molecule batch. Neither consequence was universal. All batches and evaluations completed.

The three-seed macro mean fell from 0.57434 to 0.57250, a change of -0.00184 against the registered +0.002 minimum. One seed improved and two declined. Mean final scores rose for sitagliptin by 0.01151 and zaleplon by 0.00714, while DRD2 fell by 0.01705, median similarity by 0.00706 and decoration hopping by 0.00376. Strict improvements over the best generating parent increased from 624 to 677 out of 4,350 offspring, and incumbent improvements rose from 241 to 278. On their respective scored streams, prediction MSE fell from 0.011269 to 0.009821, but mean within-batch rank correlation fell from 0.550 to 0.534 and nominal 95% latent-interval coverage fell from 76.9% to 76.1%. Correct conditioning and better local improvement counts did not deliver the intended final-score gain.

nodes.finding:
All 3,915 within-batch projections executed correctly. On identical Child pools and random draws, they preserved all 435 first choices but changed 600 of 4,350 selection positions and 287 of 435 batch sets. Later selected molecules lost an average 3.30% of their original sampling variance; the median reduction was 0.81%. Mean absolute within-batch posterior correlation fell from 0.04721 to 0.04571, and mean nonempty molecular-core coverage rose slightly from 7.06 to 7.14 cores per ten-molecule batch. Neither consequence was universal. All batches and evaluations completed.

The three-seed macro mean fell from 0.57434 to 0.57250, a change of -0.00184 against the registered +0.002 minimum. One seed improved and two declined. Mean final scores rose for sitagliptin by 0.01151 and zaleplon by 0.00714, while DRD2 fell by 0.01705, median similarity by 0.00706 and decoration hopping by 0.00376. Strict improvements over the best generating parent increased from 624 to 677 out of 4,350 offspring, and incumbent improvements rose from 241 to 278. On their respective scored streams, prediction MSE fell from 0.011269 to 0.009821, but mean within-batch rank correlation fell from 0.550 to 0.534 and nominal 95% latent-interval coverage fell from 76.9% to 76.1%. Correct conditioning and better local improvement counts did not deliver the intended final-score gain.

The experiment establishes a real allocation effect and narrows its value: removing some shared posterior variation is insufficient by itself to improve the final best score on this panel. The intervention reaches a modest typical redundancy opportunity, with a larger tail, and still permits related high-mean molecules to occupy the same batch. Even on identical pools, average count-fingerprint similarity increased slightly while posterior correlation decreased. Lower model correlation therefore cannot substitute for chemical diversity or score evidence. More parent-beating offspring and more incremental incumbent improvements also proved insufficient as proxies for the final endpoint.

The lower MSE describes a changed adaptive search stream; the fitted prediction model and its means remained unchanged on shared inputs. Mean conditioning supplied no new labels and did not repair the already poor uncertainty coverage. Whether real pending outcomes would support these zero-innovation constraints remains open, and unobserved counterfactual choices cannot answer it. The molecular assessment further limits the small core-coverage gain: smaller assemblies now contain many more small or tightly bridged rings, while reactive bonds and unspecified stereochemistry persist. Graph-core novelty is not evidence of feasible chemistry. A stronger test of useful batch coordination would need to connect model redundancy to actual score dependence or chemically meaningful alternatives; this run rules out treating the measured contraction alone as evidence of that connection.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich families retain reactive bonds and unresolved stereochemistry; smaller assemblies now carry many more small rings.
molecular.overall_character:
Node n-521f362b3777 produces substantial organic molecules with aromatic and saturated heterocycles, carbonyls, tertiary amines and frequent halogens, together with a small tail of molecular fragments. All five supplied objectives have trajectories; tasks_without_trajectories is empty. Each task contains 900 recorded evaluations, including 870 optimizer proposals across the supplied seeds. Digest ring-closure rates range from 0.9609 to 0.9839 and aromatic-SMILES rates from 0.8667 to 0.9759; these are fractions of proposal strings containing those features, not ring counts or fractions of aromatic atoms. Explicit charge and stereocentre string rates are zero throughout. Ring systems and aromatic chemistry are rich, synthetic plausibility is questionable, and drug-likeness is moderate because ordinary medicinal motifs coexist with reactive functionalities and implausible topologies. Structural diversity is moderate: numerous core identities coexist with strong concentration around individual high-scoring families.

A passive RDKit 2023.09.6 reading of every supplied Child and Parent trajectory finds all 4,350 optimizer occurrences in each corpus parseable. Child molecules have median heavy-atom counts of 25, 38, 32, 33 and 27 in the fixed task order. Compared with Parent n-559d25e9c9c7, occurrences above 50 heavy atoms fall from 313 to 100, while occurrences with a perceived three- or four-membered ring rise from 268 to 1,372. Small rings alone do not establish a liability; the concerning examples include a ring-embedded alkyne, highly bridged aromatic graphs and substituted aziridines. RDKit identifies unspecified tetrahedral centres in 2,631 Child proposals versus 2,284 Parent proposals, with no explicitly assigned centres in either. The output therefore explores substantial three-dimensional connectivity without specifying stereoisomers. Neutral SMILES also contain many potentially basic amines; zero formal charge must not be read as absence of ionizable nitrogen.

Observed scores below are the supplied scores, and comparisons describe associated chemistry without assigning mechanism activation, biological activity, synthetic accessibility or a new quality score. No particular missing target pharmacophore can be identified solely from these trajectories. Full passive counts, motif definitions, descriptor calculations and path/seed/evaluation references are recorded in /projects/standard/adeshwal/shared/zhou2577/SPIRAL/runs/SPIRAL2/policy/responses/r0012-01-improve-L01-molecular.audit.json; its companion .audit.py reproduces the audit. Aggregate chemical counts include optimizer occurrences, and perceived ring/core counts do not establish distinct feasible synthetic scaffolds.

nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

approach.method_basis: The Parent walks from one scored current molecule by sampling local atom, bond, path and ring edits, including direct formula-preserving exchanges of aromatic nitrogen and carbon positions. It sanitizes and normalizes each molecular identity, rejects duplicates, and submits the first full batch permitted by short-lived inverse-motif memory. It moves to the highest-scoring accepted neighbor even after a worsening move and keeps its best observation separately. A veto needs opposite signed motif matches from one earlier selected transition, but a recurring signed motif currently transfers its sole memory entry to the newest transition.
approach.novelty: Preserve overlapping transition provenance: let the same inverse motif retain a separate, independently expiring entry for each recent selected transition that installed it. A newer use can then coexist with an older pair through the older pair's original lifetime. This tests whether preserving coherent short-term protection redirects evaluations usefully. Earlier siblings withheld credit after nonimproving moves or required a complete signature match; this change retains unconditional credit and the existing two-sign predicate while changing only how overlapping origins survive.

nodes.hypothesis: Retain a separate inverse-motif restriction for every still-live selected-transition provenance when signed motif keys overlap, so later installations do not overwrite older provenance and the unchanged same-transition bidirectional veto can use each origin until its own original expiry or documented oldest-entry release.

finding_summary.headline: Older motif provenance changed one evaluated batch and its winner, but the final score fell
finding_summary.insights: Premature overwrite can remove a restriction that later matters to an admission decision, so preserving origins does more than increase table occupancy. Yet the opportunities were sparse: 47 collision pairings across 36 installation events yielded only one changed complete batch. The parent and child each recorded 195 vetoes in total, showing why whole-run veto counts alone would have missed this activation. The newly available replacement was locally better and won its batch, but its subsequent walk ended worse. Immediate source or archive gains therefore do not establish useful long-term redirection, and the later loss cannot be treated as the isolated value of the excluded molecule. This narrows the result to coherent short-term provenance protection; it does not establish that shared local motifs identify reversal of an entire edit or that broader retention improves search. The molecular assessment also finds the inherited aromatic and ring-rich families, unusual sulfur bonding, reactive decorations and unspecified stereochemistry largely intact, with no demonstrated chemistry improvement explaining the redirection. The benefit under histories with more overlap-dependent candidates remains open. No obstruction release occurred, so behavior after a release was not tested.
finding_summary.results: Across the 15 task-and-seed sessions, 45 older restrictions survived overlapping installations without losing their original provenance or expiry. They preserved four bidirectional transition groups that the latest-origin rule would have broken. On the same accepted histories, this produced one additional veto among 4,545 valid novel candidate tests; two other tests gained an older qualifying origin but were already vetoed. The extra veto changed one complete ten-molecule batch in deco_hop seed 1. Its replacement was evaluated, beat the source by 0.004805, became the next state and immediately raised the best observed score by 0.002352. Nevertheless, this seed finished at 0.594191 versus the parent's 0.605140. All 14 other trajectories were unchanged. The three-seed macro mean was 0.521029 versus 0.521759, a paired change of -0.000730 against the required +0.002. Across all 4,350 accepted proposals, the source-beating frequency fell from 10.759% to 10.621%, and strict archive improvements fell from 238 to 232. Provenance retention and evaluation redirection are confirmed; the specified score-benefit claim is refuted.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic families persist, with unusual sulfur bonding, reactive decorations and unresolved stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: The generated set spans moderately sized fused heteroaryl amides and ketones, larger decorated nitrogenous heterocycles, aminoalkyl polycycles, and densely connected sulfur-containing cages. Every covered task has 870 optimizer proposals and ring_closure_rate 1.0. Aromatic-atom presence rates range from 0.7184 to 1.0; these are fractions of strings containing aromatic notation, not aromatic atom fractions or perceived ring counts. Mean SMILES lengths range from 46.2 to 69.9 and describe textual complexity, not molecular weight. Conventional aromatic/carbonyl substructures remain recognizable, but many higher-scoring molecules combine them with heteroatom-halogen bonds, unusual multiply bonded sulfur, or elaborate bridges. Thus synthetic plausibility is questionable overall, although the simpler indole carboxamides look substantially more conventional than the sulfur cages. Structural diversity is moderate across the observed families, with close analogues concentrated within each seed; numerous unique strings do not establish broad useful scaffold coverage. All panels report stereocentre_rate 0.0 and charged_rate 0.0. This shows absent explicit stereochemical and charge notation; it does not show absent stereogenic atoms or absent basic amines. All supplied Child and Parent trajectory records agree outside deco_hop seed 1. The chemistry therefore largely persists from Parent n-abcd951ab7cc. All objectives listed in the brief have trajectories; tasks_without_trajectories is empty. The readings below concern observed molecular-score associations and apparent chemistry, without assigning biological activity, synthetic routes, objective components, or mechanism activation.

per_task.generated_character: Moderately sized, substituted fused heteroaromatics predominate: indole carboxanilides, benzofuran carboxanilides and benzothiophene aryl ketones, carrying alkoxy, methyl, amino, thiol and halogen-containing substituents. The later stream also contains enlarged, partly dearomatized bridged rings. Mean SMILES length is 46.2, aromatic_atom_rate 0.9563 and halogen_rate 0.7552. The ethoxy/methyl/thiol indole carboxanilide at seed 1 evaluation 61 is a recognizable medicinal-chemistry framework; the seed 2 best adds an N-chloroamide and an amino/chloro-substituted benzylic carbon, making its plausibility more doubtful. All trajectories and best structures match the Parent.
liabilities: N-chloroamide, N-fluoro/N-hydroxy amine and benzylic halide motifs introduce apparent reactivity concerns beyond the ordinary heteroaryl amide framework.
Dense partly dearomatized bridges and multiply bonded sulfur appear in late molecules without stereochemical specification or evidence of a feasible synthesis.
missing_features: Consistent preservation of the favorable compact aromatic-carbonyl arrangement is missing from low-scoring ring-expansion and carbonyl-disruption proposals.

A demonstrated set of conventional analogues retaining the best benzofuran substitution pattern while replacing its N-chloroamide and amino/chloro carbon is missing; the scores do not establish those reactive decorations as necessary.
The shown gradient does not identify a particular unobserved target-specific functional group as the missing answer.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial methoxy-substituted indole carboxanilide scores 0.3051048083696145, compared with 0.39905049777278273 for the ethoxy/methyl/thiol analogue and 0.41003927643747895 for the substituted benzofuran N-chloroamide. The benzothiophene aryl ketone also reaches 0.393567030299894. In contrast, the indole derivative in which the carbonyl linkage is replaced by a substituted saturated amino linkage scores 0.03343008011310944; a much less aromatic enlarged-ring ketone scores 0.021532846118034143. These comparisons associate the better region with intact fused aromatic/carbonyl/aryl arrangements and selective peripheral changes. They do not isolate a benefit from N-chlorination, thiols or any single substituent. The dense later ring systems can retain appreciable scores, so neither maximum aromaticity nor simple synthetic appearance is a sufficient explanation.

per_task.generated_character: These are large, heavily decorated nitrogen-rich aromatic heterocycles with carbonyl or thiocarbonyl groups. The strongest seed 0 family carries a substituted phenyl group, exocyclic imines, an amino/fluoro carbon linker, and an extended ether/thioether/acetal-like appendage attached through unusual multiply bonded sulfur. Late seed 2 examples retain a fused dicarbonyl heterocycle with polyenyl and bulky alkoxy substituents. Mean SMILES length is 69.3, maximum length 95, and aromatic_atom_rate 1.0. The conventional heterocyclic cores are recognizable, but the accumulated decorations make the complete structures synthetically questionable. Only seed 1 differs from the Parent: its observed best is an expanded nitrogen-rich carbonyl/imine heterocycle with an alkenyl side chain and an aryl thioacyl group, while the Parent best has heteroaryl-linked amidine and thioester functionality. Neither family establishes a cleaner chemical solution.
liabilities: The best family combines terminal imines, N-bromination, unusual sulfur bonding and long heteroatom-rich appendages; nearby leaders also carry sulfur-chlorine bonds.
Flexible ether/thioether/acetal-like chains and crowded substituent patterns increase synthetic and conformational uncertainty. No synthesis or stability evidence accompanies these scores.
missing_features: A demonstrated economical representation of the higher-scoring heterocyclic arrangement is missing: closely related enlarged appendages receive identical scores, leaving the minimal useful attachment pattern unresolved.
Conventional, tractable replacements for the multiply bonded sulfur linkage and reactive terminal groups are not established among the leading examples.
The lower-scoring changed seed does not establish which lost or relocated heteroaryl feature caused the decrease, because its scaffold and substituents changed together.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted fused dicarbonyl heterocycle scores 0.548381482770623. A lower optimizer example with a reorganized nonaromatic fused nitrogen ring scores 0.526081691583997, whereas the elaborated seed 0 thione/oxo family reaches 0.6161710037174721. Several cited decorated analogues share exactly 0.6155070237050044 despite changes in alkyl length, sulfur substitution or N-bromination. The local plateau therefore supplies no evidence that each added decoration contributes. The changed seed 1 trajectory ends at best_so_far 0.5941905687894993 versus Parent 0.605139548855754; these seed-specific best structures are described from the full trajectories and are not quoted because they are outside the supplied digest. The observed gradient favors particular reorganizations and decorations of the inherited heterocyclic family, but it does not reveal the unseen structural requirement of the objective.

per_task.generated_character: Large halogenated aromatic/polycyclic molecules evolve from carboxylic-acid, amide and sulfonamide-rich starting chemistry toward unacylated cyclic amines, aminomethyl substituents, phenols and aryl groups linked through unusual sulfur-containing rings. The best seed 2 structure combines a phenolic aryl group, a chlorophenyl group, an aminomethyl-substituted N/S ring and a bridged amine-containing sulfur framework. Seed 0 leaders include small saturated aza rings and sulfur-rich aryl linkages. Mean SMILES length is 69.9, aromatic_atom_rate 1.0 and halogen_rate 0.9966. Free amine centres are present despite charged_rate 0.0. The aromatic/amine functionality is medicinally recognizable, but sulfur-sulfur multiple bonding and dense asymmetric ring systems make the full structures questionable. Every trajectory matches the Parent.
liabilities: Multiply bonded sulfur with explicit sulfur hydrogens, sulfur-sulfur multiple bonds and cumulated heteroatom bonding appear in high-scoring structures, raising strong synthetic plausibility questions.
Halogen-heavy aromatic regions, crowded aza rings and unspecified stereochemistry complicate interpretation of the proposed shapes and functional-group presentation.
missing_features: Conventional analogues preserving the favorable amine-to-aromatic connectivity and spacer geometry without unusual sulfur-sulfur or carbon-sulfur multiple bonding are not demonstrated.

Explicit stereochemical alternatives and plausible charge-state representations are absent despite asymmetric saturated rings and free amines; their effect on this score cannot be inferred from the shown molecules.
Lower-scoring proposals fail to preserve the specific aminoalkyl attachment and distal aromatic structure that the local comparisons support.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: An early acid/amide/sulfonamide-containing optimizer molecule scores 0.007468397818197266, while the phenolic aminoalkyl sulfur polycycle reaches 0.9148143511682032. A closely related aminomethyl-containing structure scores 0.8663008496126992; replacing one aminomethyl branch with an aminooxy branch gives 0.5308080684367313, removing a methylene between a ring nitrogen and the sulfur-containing ring gives 0.3331237338421948, and disrupting its distal chlorophenyl ring with sulfur gives 0.04252669549740123. These local comparisons support sensitivity to aminoalkyl connectivity, linker spacing and an intact distal aromatic group. They do not show that adding more nitrogen is uniformly beneficial or that the exotic sulfur framework is required. The high recorded score is not direct evidence of binding, selectivity, stability or synthesizability.

per_task.generated_character: Medium-to-large aryl/heteroaryl polycycles carry tertiary lactam or related carbonyl groups, alkyl substituents and bridged nitrogen/oxygen linkages. The best excerpt is concentrated on an azaaryl/aryl unsaturated bridged scaffold containing an N-O bond and a cyclic carbonyl-containing chain. Other seeds explore brominated aryl/thioester families and later sulfur-rich bridged carbonyl structures. Mean SMILES length is 61.0 and aromatic_atom_rate 1.0. Aromatic rings and carbonyl functionality are abundant; the unusual bridges and heteroatom bonds make the overall chemistry questionable rather than obviously tractable. The complete trajectories match the Parent.
liabilities: N-O and N-N bridges, including a peroxide-containing high-scoring analogue, give uncertain stability and synthesis compared with ordinary lactam scaffolds.
Other proposals carry oxygen-bromine bonds and unusual sulfur substituents; late sulfur-rich cages retain scores without resolving these chemical concerns.
Asymmetric bridged structures have no explicit stereochemical specification.
missing_features: Several independent, conventional ring/linker arrangements reproducing the favorable aryl, heteroaryl and carbonyl placement are not established; the leading digest remains concentrated on a bridged N-O family.
A demonstrated compact and tractable alternative to the elaborate bridges is missing. Additional rings alone are not the missing chemistry, because ring closure is already universal.
The shown scores do not establish which unobserved functional group would satisfy the objective beyond the local topology and substituent associations.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial fused dicarbonyl heterocycle scores 0.1678386594791329. Ring-opened derivatives bearing pendant amino/carbonyl chains score 0.12467972074136988 and 0.1263981386214515, while the bridged azaaryl/aryl lactam family reaches 0.21196904390980506. A close ring-expanded/phenyl analogue scores 0.2108231310031427, and a peroxide-containing related bridge remains at 0.20647766243219587. The gradient is consistent with a particular constrained aryl/heteroatom/carbonyl arrangement and tolerates substantial changes in the tether chemistry. The modest separation from the median 0.17833 does not identify an unseen target motif, and near-top tolerance of the peroxide bridge does not endorse its chemical quality.

per_task.generated_character: Compact but highly connected heteroatom-rich polycycles replace much of the initial peripheral aryl chemistry. The leading seed 1 molecules retain a nitrogenous dicarbonyl/[nH] region embedded in dense sulfur-containing fused and bridged rings, with carbon-fluorine substituents and a sulfur-linked fluorinated alcohol branch. Other seeds reach sulfur-rich carbonyl cages carrying an acyl fluoride, or an aldehyde and N-fluoro imino functionality. Mean SMILES length is 62.8, aromatic_atom_rate 0.7184 and halogen_rate 0.7. This is rich ring chemistry with less persistent aromatic notation than the other panels, not an absence of rings. The tightly interlocked sulfur frameworks look particularly difficult to realize as conventional stable molecules. All trajectories match the Parent.
liabilities: Dense ring intersections and multiple unusual carbon-sulfur and sulfur-sulfur bond environments make synthetic plausibility especially weak for the leading cages.

The seed 0 leading excerpt contains an acyl fluoride; late seed 2 examples contain N-F functionality, an aldehyde, and a sulfur-chlorine acyl derivative. These are apparent reactivity liabilities, not evidence of a stable medicinal scaffold.
No explicit stereochemistry resolves the asymmetric saturated ring junctions or substituted fluorinated carbons.
missing_features: Conventional heterocyclic or partially saturated scaffolds presenting the favorable compact fluorinated carbonyl/donor arrangement without the elaborate sulfur network are not demonstrated among the leaders.
Specified stereochemistry is missing from highly asymmetric fluorinated cages; neither a preferred stereoisomer nor a score benefit from assigning one can be inferred.
The demonstrated gradient concerns compactness and heteroatom placement within unusual cages; it does not justify prescribing an unobserved objective-specific group.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted fused dicarbonyl heterocycle scores 0.0020944534688323298, and an early expanded carbonyl-containing derivative scores 7.590554525032884e-10. The compact fluorinated sulfur cage reaches 0.5903526424693334. In the late seed 2 series, a compact sulfur/carbonyl cage scores 0.4484554129767839, whereas an analogue with expanded carbon paths scores 0.01685401516576383. Within these observed families the better region is associated with compact connectivity, fluorination and reorganized heteroatom/carbonyl placement. Several features change together, and low-scoring sulfur-rich examples show that sulfur addition alone is insufficient. The observations do not identify a required reference-like pharmacophore or establish any reward for chemical stability.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Higher-scoring digest molecules contain N-chloroamides, N-brominated heterocycles, N-F groups, multiply bonded sulfur with explicit sulfur hydrogens, and sulfur-sulfur multiple bonds. Recognizable aromatic, carbonyl and amine fragments coexist with these liabilities. Some chemically more conventional analogues score well, so none of these liabilities is demonstrated to be universally necessary.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably preserve conventional local chemical environments while varying favorable ring and linker arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator could expose alternatives with conventional bond environments while preserving the surrounding attachments, using local chemical context rather than atom valence alone. Evaluate such alternatives through the existing score interface; a plausibility preference is a hypothesis to test, not an assumed score improvement or a blanket exclusion of sulfur.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The leading examples concentrate on close analogues of fused heteroaryl carbonyls, N-O bridged azaaryl lactams, aminoalkyl sulfur polycycles and dense fluorinated cages. Low-scoring counterparts often disrupt an aromatic ring, carbonyl linkage or aminoalkyl spacer; the output does not establish that elaborate bridges are required to retain the favorable arrangement.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output lacks demonstrated simple scaffold and linker alternatives that retain favorable functional-group placement.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Expose chemically coherent ring/linker replacements or simplifications that retain attachment points and recognizable donor, acceptor and aromatic arrangements. Such proposals would test whether the same useful local features can be expressed in more conventional frameworks, using only the current molecule and observed feedback.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every task digest reports stereocentre_rate 0.0, while the quoted molecules contain crowded substituted aza rings, fluorinated saturated carbons and bridged cages. The observed structural diversity therefore leaves configuration unresolved; the supplied scores do not establish whether assigning configuration would be recognized or rewarded.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not demonstrate stereochemically specified alternatives for its asymmetric ring and substituent chemistry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Where a generated graph permits stereoisomers, expose chemically consistent stereochemical alternatives and determine through the existing identity and evaluation interfaces whether they remain distinct and score-sensitive. Treat this as missing representation coverage, not evidence that one particular configuration is favorable.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every task digest reports charged_rate 0.0, yet higher-scoring molecules include unacylated cyclic amines and aminomethyl branches. Formal charge is unspecified or neutral in these strings; this observation neither removes their potential basicity nor establishes their state under any experimental condition.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not demonstrate charge-state coverage for the free amines it already emits.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic representation could consider chemically appropriate ionization alternatives where the protocol permits them, while checking whether normalization and scoring distinguish those states. No objective identity or presumed assay condition should be used to choose a charge state.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Several leading large heterocyclic molecules share the recorded score 0.6155070237050044 despite changes in alkyl length, sulfur substitution and N-bromination. Long ether/thioether appendages and crowded substitutions persist, while other leading families similarly contain many close variants of elaborate ring systems.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not establish which bulky peripheral decorations are dispensable within a high-scoring family.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Offer controlled peripheral shortening or branch replacement that keeps the central attachment framework intact. Observed ties can motivate testing simpler molecules, but do not prove that an unevaluated deletion will preserve the score; retain ordinary feedback-based comparison.

nodes.method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
nodes.method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.

approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves scored molecular graphs. It draws breeding parents from ranked quantiles of a greedy survivor population, applies graph mutation walks or connected-fragment crossover, and admits fresh, canonically distinct offspring only if they do not introduce excess outside-envelope sulfur signatures relative to their original scored parents. For each fresh surplus pool it fits a Gaussian process to the full chronological accepted archive using chirality-aware Morgan occurrence counts and generalized Tanimoto covariance. It normalizes scores by the archive mean and population standard deviation, samples correlated functions over the pool, and evaluates sequential distinct sample maximizers. Real accepted feedback updates both the archive and survivors.
approach.novelty: Replace the covariance with one fixed inner product of unit-normalized count vectors. This asks whether agreement in relative local-environment composition supplies a more useful predictive and exploration geometry. It preserves the count vocabulary and correlated sampling but deliberately removes overall count magnitude: proportional count rows alias. The siblings tested squared Tanimoto, exponential mean or residual substitutions, and removal of active selection; none tested this linear count-direction law. Earlier normalized-count Matern used Euclidean distance and a positive disjoint-covariance floor, whereas this law gives zero to disjoint nonzero rows and has no lengthscale or fitted parameter.

nodes.hypothesis: Replace only the inherited GP covariance with the fixed normalized-count inner product K(x,y)=(x dot y)/(sqrt(sum(x*x))*sqrt(sum(y*y))) for nonzero raw inherited Morgan count rows, with empty/empty=1 and exactly one empty=0, coherently in every training, cross, pool and probe Gram block; preserve the complete correlated posterior-sampling allocator and all noncovariance interfaces.

finding_summary.headline: Real selection changes worsen ranking and lower endpoint mean by 0.07723
finding_summary.insights:
The changed geometry and delivered choices happened, but the predicted ranking and productive-exploration benefits did not. This rules out rescuing the tested fixed law with its lower dispersion or slightly higher scaffold-win counts under this composition and profile. New-core local wins arose from weaker absolute sources and did not turn into stronger actual continuation. molecular.overall_character:
Node n-52bd6c308406 emits ring-rich aromatic amide/imino series, linked azaheterocycles, aryl/cyclic amines, fused nitrogen/carbonyl systems and fluorinated bridged rings. nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from a bounded, score-ranked population of accepted molecules. Each first parent is sampled through weighted score bands; crossover samples a different accepted partner through the same band rule, while ordinary mutation uses only the first source. Connected-fragment recombination, optional finishing mutations and local graph walks produce a surplus pool of new canonical identities. A Gaussian process trained on all earlier accepted scores uses counts of molecular environments and generalized Tanimoto similarity; correlated posterior draws select the announced batch. Accepted results immediately enter learning and greedy survival. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange remains disabled.
approach.novelty: Change only how the two crossover sources are paired. A minimum-similarity transport coupling keeps each molecule's original prospective probability in the first role and in the partner role, and never allows an originally forbidden pair, while moving joint probability toward less similar accepted partners. Some formerly possible pairs may disappear. Earlier siblings changed score weighting, source access, first-draw scheduling, survivor retention or product lifetime; the older affinity and core-balancing rules also changed marginal allocation. This test instead changes dependence between the two source roles. Lower similarity, productive complete offspring and improved final scores are separate predictions, and the first does not establish either of the others.

nodes.hypothesis: Replace only the conditional crossover-partner sampler with a certified deterministic minimum-count-Tanimoto transportation coupling of the original two-role joint law, preserving both original prospective role marginals and every original zero-pair restriction while retaining the exact first-parent sampler and distinct source identities.

finding_summary.headline: Less-similar pairs reached accepted offspring, but the matched mean fell by 0.0371
finding_summary.insights: Preserving each role’s score exposure at a fixed population did not preserve the joint best-parent threshold or the quality of later adaptive populations. Expected best-parent score moved upward in 282 states and downward in 153 despite the fixed marginals. The Child recorded more parent-beating offspring (745 versus 629) and more incumbent advances (277 versus 258), but accepted offspring had lower absolute mean scores (0.37150 versus 0.38526), their actual best-parent references were weaker (0.44047 versus 0.47046), and positive incumbent increments were smaller on average (0.01896 versus 0.02251). Thus the extra local wins and reuse do not establish more productive exploration. Changed pairs did reach real complete products and feedback, so lack of downstream exposure does not explain the failed score prediction. The chemistry still spans many ring frameworks and includes recognizable aryl cyclic amines, alongside reactive attachments, questionable bridges and unresolved stereochemistry; the evidence does not identify any of these as the cause of the score loss. Lower count-feature similarity controls source dependence, but this fixed objective did not reliably produce better complete molecular arrangements under the tested conditions. The contribution of the retained graph-evolution foundation and the chemical or RNG-mediated cause of the loss remain open.
finding_summary.results: The coupling worked as intended in all 435 encountered population states. At each fixed state it preserved each source’s original probability in both parent roles and every forbidden pair, while expected pair similarity fell from 0.7591 to 0.7029. Actual partner identity changed in 30,333 of 34,407 crossovers. Those changed pairs produced 1,277 accepted complete molecules; 683 later served as breeding sources. There were no solver fallbacks or incomplete evaluations. Nevertheless, final Top-1 macro mean fell from 0.59567 to 0.55854: a paired change of -0.03713, failing the registered +0.002 criterion. Six of fifteen task/seed cells improved and nine declined. Seed changes were -0.07451, +0.00075 and -0.03761. The largest losses were decoration hopping in seed 0 and the sitagliptin objective in seed 2. Seed dispersion fell from 0.02659 to 0.00544, which does not establish reliable improvement.
