molecular.headline: Aromatic amides, cyclic amines and fluorinated heterocycles coexist with reactive attachments and unresolved ring geometry
molecular.overall_character: Node n-5449c5ae9486 produces compact aromatic amides and ketones, nitrogen-rich linked heterocycles, aryl cyclic amines, medium-ring nitrogen/carbonyl frameworks, and fluorinated diones or imino-amides. The brief reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true against code Parent n-62daf219c70a: all supplied Child and published Parent trajectories for Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2 were present and read. Each task has 900 Child records, including 870 optimizer proposals; there are no missing task trajectories, missing Parent paths, or absent matched seed comparisons. The supplied ring-closure-string incidences are 0.9609 to 0.9851 and aromatic-string incidences 0.931 to 0.9782. These measure the proportion of proposal strings containing a feature, not aromatic-atom fractions or scaffold diversity. Ring and aromatic chemistry are plainly available. Both formal-charge and stereocentre-string incidences are 0.0 on every task, although the molecules include protonatable amines and potential stereogenic centres. Synthetic plausibility is questionable because several leaders combine recognizable functional groups with N-halogen or O-F bonds, peroxides, short bridges across aromatic rings, unusual aromatic-labelled medium rings, or reactive halomethyl attachments. The conventional aryl piperidine leader is an important exception; these concerns are not universal. Overall drug-likeness is weak across the full output, with more recognizable medicinal chemistry in the cyclic-amine families. Diversity is moderate across seeds and tasks, while leaders within individual seeds repeatedly revisit related arrangements; many different graph scaffolds do occur, so this is not global structural collapse. The digest final excerpts are late seed-2 proposals, not the retained best molecule of every seed. Per-task comparisons below use each complete trajectory and its recorded scores; displayed decimal scores are rounded. Heavy-atom counts and ring descriptions are offline RDKit readings of the supplied SMILES, documented with source hashes in .slots/round-0025-slot-0/molecular_audit.json and molecular_features.jsonl. Graph validity, aromatic perception and a high oracle label do not establish stability, synthesis or geometry. The inherited gaps originated in the Development-profile report for n-c55c3d520a2c and were carried into n-62daf219c70a; their current re-observation preserves that provenance. The present complete Parent pairing does not turn that earlier profile into an independent current-profile comparison. Chemistry associations here do not attribute liabilities, inherited fragments or endpoint changes to a particular algorithm component.

per_task.generated_character: All three seed leaders have 25 heavy atoms, but their chemistry differs. Seed 0 produces an azaindole carboxamide with methoxy, methylthio and vinyl substituents and an N-fluoro anilide. Seed 1 instead leads with an N-methyl benzimidazole/pyridyl ketone carrying both a benzylic chloride and a chloromethyl ether. Seed 2 favors an N-N-bridged, partially unsaturated aryl framework bearing a tertiary N-methyl anilide, methoxy group and vinyl thioether; its graph has four perceived rings, including the pendant phenyl. These are compact, aromatic, carbonyl-containing molecules rather than simple chains. Mean proposal SMILES length is 42.2; ring-closure and aromatic-string incidences are 0.9724 and 0.9701. Familiar amide, ketone and heteroaryl chemistry coexists with environment-specific reactivity or bridge-geometry questions. Parent leaders instead include N-halogenated indole-like amide, diketone or cumulated-unsaturation families; the Child changes these arrangements without eliminating the chemistry concerns.
liabilities: N-F or N-Cl on an amide nitrogen and the chloromethyl/benzylic chloride attachments need local chemical-stability assessment; they should not be equated with ordinary aryl halogens.
The N-N bridge and unsaturation constrain the seed-2 topology; its representable graph and favorable label do not establish a feasible synthesis or conformation.
Late tiny proposals lose the aromatic and carbonyl context entirely, while late larger relatives can still score below the retained incumbent.
missing_features: The leading records do not establish conventional, less reactive replacements for the N-halogen amide, chloromethyl ether or benzylic chloride that preserve each family's score. The seed-2 non-N-halogen leader is a counterexample to an absolute need for that bond.

The bridged leader lacks an explicitly specified stereochemical identity and demonstrated accessible ring geometry. The record identifies no exact unseen target motif that can legitimately be prescribed.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxyindole anilide scores 0.305104808. The Child seed-0, seed-1 and seed-2 leaders score 0.420740853, 0.436818201 and 0.468683683, respectively; the corresponding published Parent leaders score 0.394051421, 0.474117018 and 0.438972502. Thus the seed-1 chemistry does not share the other seeds' direction. In a particularly close Child contrast, the seed-2 vinyl thioether at evaluation 258 scores 0.468683683, while replacing that linking sulfur with carbon to give the allyl analogue at evaluation 297 gives 0.338344080 with the rest of the recorded framework unchanged. This supports a local sulfur-environment association, not a universal sulfur requirement. The seed-0 N-F and N-Cl amide variants at evaluations 257 and 265 have the identical score 0.420740853, while the seed-2 leader contains no N-halogen bond. Isolated F at seed-0 evaluation 248 scores 0.0. The visible gradient favors contextual aromatic/carbonyl arrangements and particular substitutions; heteroatom or halogen presence alone is insufficient.

per_task.generated_character: The seeds diverge strongly. Seed 0 expands to a 55-heavy-atom leader containing several linked/fused nitrogen-rich aromatic dione units, N-O connectivity, an unsaturated linker and a brominated ether-bearing tail. Seed 1 instead has a 29-heavy-atom compact, densely cross-linked nitrogen/sulfur aromatic framework with an N-N link and a cyclic peroxide; short sulfur bridges create four-membered cycles across aromatic nitrogen-containing segments. Seed 2 leads with a 46-heavy-atom indane-like/heteroaryl dione assembly, aminopyridyl and imino linkages, a polyunsaturated tail and two O-F bonds. These are not interchangeable examples of one scaffold. Mean SMILES length is 81.2 and the maximum is 234, with ring-closure incidence 0.9793 and aromatic incidence 0.9782. Ring richness and extensive heteroatom functionality coexist with substantial synthetic and stability questions. The published Parent seed-0 leader is a much more compact linked fused heterocycle with carbonyl/thione, O-F and halomethyl-ether chemistry; Parent seeds 1 and 2 use different heteroaryl or peroxide-containing families.
liabilities: The O-F bonds, cyclic peroxide and brominated ether-bearing tail raise different local reactivity questions; a single generic halogen or oxygen count would obscure them.
Seed-1 short sulfur bridges across aromatic segments and dense cross-linking are geometrically questionable even though its heavy-atom count is modest.

Large repeated heterocyclic units and long unsaturated appendages add synthetic complexity without a consistent observed score advantage; tiny hydrocarbon outputs show the opposite loss of useful molecular context.
missing_features: The output does not establish robust, simpler, chemically credible alternatives preserving favorable linked heteroaryl/carbonyl relationships across seeds; a compact but strained peroxide/sulfur-bridge molecule is not evidence that compactness alone solves feasibility.

Conventional local alternatives to O-F, cyclic peroxide and short aromatic-spanning sulfur bridges are not demonstrated at each leader's score. The exact missing feature behind the stronger Parent seed-0 label is not identifiable from these unmatched scaffolds.
The polyunsaturated and imino tails lack explicit geometric-isomer identity. Their score benefit relative to specified isomers was not measured.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Child seed-0, seed-1 and seed-2 leaders score 0.597950492, 0.617519320 and 0.620471918; the matched Parent values are 0.856147722, 0.624820660 and 0.617802403. In particular, the large seed-0 dione assembly does not recover the Parent's compact leading arrangement. The initial aryl-substituted fused dione scores 0.548381483, whereas acetylene at seed-0 evaluation 163 scores the observed floor of 0.5. Within the seed-2 linked heterocycle family, the distinct tail variants at evaluations 289 and 292 both score 0.619537418 despite different size and unsaturation. The favorable association is with retained complex aromatic/heterocyclic organization; neither adding more atoms nor preserving every distal tail detail has a demonstrated general benefit. The small positive seed-2 Parent difference and the other seeds' lower labels must remain separate; no single required missing decoration follows from these records.

per_task.generated_character: The leaders already contain available amines with substantial aromatic surface. Seed 0 gives a 25-heavy-atom bridged N-aryl cyclic-amine/polyamine framework with an aryl thiol and carbon-bound fluorine. Seed 1 gives a recognizable 26-heavy-atom aryl piperidine with methoxy, aryl fluorine and fluoromethyl-substituted phenyl groups. Seed 2 gives a 26-heavy-atom N-propyl azetidine joined through an ethyl segment to a brominated phenolic biaryl; one aryl ring also carries a fused four-membered O/CH2 ring. The azetidine is an ordinary saturated small-ring motif, whereas the fused oxygen ring poses a separate strain question. Mean SMILES length is 59.6 and halogen-string incidence 0.9839. Parent leaders include flexible tertiary aryl amines and pyrrolidine-containing fused-ring molecules, also with unassigned stereochemistry. The seed-1 piperidine is a more conventional synthetic framework than several of the other task leaders and is an important positive chemical counterexample.
liabilities: Seed-2 ring strain must be distinguished from the conventional azetidine; counting all small rings as equally problematic would be chemically misleading.
Some relatives add benzylic halides or N-Cl bonds, including the final seed-2 proposal, but the seed-1 and seed-2 leaders do not need such attachments.
Substantial aromatic/halogen content and unresolved configurations leave physical-property and stereochemical questions that the supplied labels do not answer.
missing_features: Explicit stereochemical identity is missing for the substituted cyclic amines and benzylic centres. A basic amine is not missing, and the absence of a formal charge symbol does not establish lack of protonatability.

A geometrically credible replacement for the seed-2 fused oxygen four-membered ring at its exact label is not established. The high-scoring seed-1 piperidine shows that this topology is not a universal requirement.

The near-ceiling labels do not identify a further absent receptor-binding feature; the demonstrable gaps concern molecular identity and feasibility rather than an inferred target-specific pharmacophore.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Child seed-0, seed-1 and seed-2 leaders score 0.972085158, 0.996155819 and 0.999991691 against Parent values 0.999998918, 0.996975316 and 0.999993424. In contrast, the simple aryl methyl sulfone at seed-1 evaluation 13 scores 0.000321412 and an N-sulfonyl pyrrolidine/carbonyl fragment at seed-0 evaluation 17 scores 0.000438413. These are contextual comparisons, not controlled amine-removal experiments, but they associate the high labels with accessible aliphatic amines organized beside aromatic regions, rather than nitrogen or halogen count alone. The shorter 26-heavy-atom seed-2 leader scores 0.999991691; its 30-heavy-atom amino/fluorinated linker analogue at evaluation 250 scores 0.999989984. Extra linker atoms are therefore not necessary for a near-ceiling label. The conventional seed-1 piperidine also scores highly without an N-halogen bond or the fused oxygen four-membered ring. These oracle labels do not measure experimental binding, selectivity or chemical accessibility.

per_task.generated_character: Seed 0 leads with a 31-heavy-atom diaryl ether/tertiary-amine medium-ring framework bearing a saturated dicarbonyl nitrogen ring. Seed 1 reaches a 34-heavy-atom propyl/ethoxy-substituted polycyclic aryl framework containing adjacent ring nitrogens, a methylated amine, and ketone/lactam carbonyls. Seed 2 gives a 34-heavy-atom bridged diaryl ether with N-N connectivity and carbonyl-containing nitrogen-ring segments. The perceived cycle sizes include medium and large rings; the seed-1 graph includes an aromatic-labelled nine-membered nitrogen-containing cycle, whose notation does not establish a stable aromatic conformation. Mean SMILES length is 53.9, ring-closure incidence 0.9828, aromatic incidence 0.9759, and halogen incidence only 0.1. This chemistry supplies aromatic surfaces, nitrogen centres and carbonyl groups without relying on abundant halogens. Parent leaders also combine aryl/quinoline regions with nitrogen/carbonyl medium-ring or bridged systems, but with different connectivities.
liabilities: Dense bridges, medium-ring closures and constrained unsaturation make synthesis and conformation uncertain despite moderate heavy-atom counts.
N-N or N-O variants need assessment in their actual ring and carbonyl environments; the presence of an N-N bond alone is not a blanket instability verdict.
Ring richness and small local score gains coexist with unresolved geometry, so these quantities cannot serve as chemical-feasibility certificates.
missing_features: The leaders do not establish simpler, geometrically supported connectivities that retain the favorable aromatic/nitrogen/carbonyl organization at the same labels.
The bridged and medium-ring products lack defined stereochemical/conformational identity; aromatic atom flags on a large cycle do not supply that information.
Several different frameworks occur across seeds, but within each leading family the record does not establish broad coverage of chemically independent, demonstrably feasible alternatives.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted fused dione scores 0.167838659. Child seed-0, seed-1 and seed-2 leaders score 0.218217890, 0.237568874 and 0.231120084; the published Parent leaders score 0.225840399, 0.221409546 and 0.226003129. The seed-0 result therefore differs in direction from the other seeds. In seed 1, the leader at evaluation 256 scores 0.237568874 and the related structure with the ketone position reduced to a methylene at evaluation 264 still scores 0.232556132. In seed 2, insertion of a methylene into the N-N-containing ring segment changes 0.231120084 to 0.229673071. These nearby labels favor the broad aromatic/nitrogen/carbonyl arrangement without making one ring size or carbonyl count uniquely sufficient. Methane at seed-1 evaluation 197 scores 0.0. The remaining score gap cannot be assigned to a missing named target motif from these trajectories.

per_task.generated_character: Seed 0 leads with a 26-heavy-atom fused nitrogen dione carrying N-F, a fluorinated cyclopentene, and an enol/imine-containing fluoroalkyl side chain. Seed 1 leads with a 30-heavy-atom fused nitrogen dione bearing two N-F bonds, a fluorocyclopropyl substituent and a fluorinated thiol-bearing lactam fused to an unsaturated larger ring. Seed 2 instead reaches a 23-heavy-atom single-benzene imino-amide with methoxy, methylamino and carbon-bound fluorine substituents, plus an N-amino alkynyl-amide segment extending into a fluoroalkene. It has neither the fused dione core nor an N-F bond. Mean proposal SMILES length is 47.5, aromatic incidence 0.931, ring-closure incidence 0.9609 and halogen incidence 0.8115. Compact fluorinated polar chemistry is present, but its local connectivity is frequently unconventional. The Parent's strongest seed-2 example had a small cyclic cumulene and a large aromatic-labelled nitrogen ring; the current leaders use different chemistry, while N-F attachments recur in seeds 0 and 1.
liabilities: N-F on carbonyl-containing heterocycles, the N-amino alkynyl-amide segment and enol/imine tails require environment-specific stability and synthesis assessment; none is validated by the score.
Fluorinated saturated centres and alkene/imine arrangements are stereochemically unspecified. The thiol-bearing lactam and unsaturated ring geometry add separate local questions.
The current leaders avoid the Parent's leading cyclic cumulene, but this change alone does not establish better overall feasibility or explain the recorded score differences.
missing_features: The molecules do not establish consistently conventional fluorinated/polar arrangements with resolved tautomeric and geometric identity at the leaders' scores. The single-ring, non-N-F seed-2 leader is a real alternative family, not proof that fused rings or N-F are required.
Stereochemically specified saturated-ring products and stable local alternatives to the N-fluorinated diones are not demonstrated. Any score benefit from specifying them remains unmeasured.

The evidence does not identify an exact absent drug-like target scaffold or pharmacophore. Adding nitrogen, fluorine or rings indiscriminately would ignore the very low labels of the large initial/early molecules and tiny fragments.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Child seed-0, seed-1 and seed-2 leaders score 0.545501720, 0.520017184 and 0.495324126, versus Parent values 0.651021191, 0.487005731 and 0.720885367. Thus seed 1 rises while seeds 0 and 2 do not. The initial aryl-substituted dione scores 0.002094453, and the oversized 54-heavy-atom acetal/dione assembly at seed-1 evaluation 13 scores 2.192995343284275e-43. In seed 0, adding one methylene between the leading heterocycle and cyclopentene changes 0.545501720 to 0.492534554. This supports a context-specific fluorine/size association, not a universal fluorination prescription or need for N-F. The single-ring seed-2 leader and the close seed-1 benzenoid lactam relative scoring 0.518998130 also prevent treating the most elaborate ring system as required. The changed scaffold families do not isolate why the Parent's seed-2 label was higher.

Conversely, a conventional aryl piperidine and a single-ring imino-amide with carbon-bound fluorine are high-scoring within their own records without N-halogen bonds. transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Task-agnostic transformations need chemically appropriate substituent alternatives that preserve favorable functional-group relationships learned from accepted feedback. Distinguish heteroatom-halogen and activated benzylic environments from ordinary carbon-bound halogens, and assess N-N or peroxide bonds in their actual context. transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Representations and transformations need to preserve or explicitly resolve stereochemical identity where chemically meaningful, while distinguishing achiral or configurationally unstable cases. transferable_gaps.evidence: The gap originates in Development-profile n-c55c3d520a2c and is carried by n-62daf219c70a; it recurs in n-5449c5ae9486 under Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2, 300 observations per task and batch size 10. nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from accepted, scored molecules. It samples breeding parents from high-scoring bands of a bounded population, combines connected fragments, and applies ordinary local mutations and short mutation walks. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchanges are already disabled. Stable canonical identity checks admit a fresh surplus pool. A Gaussian process fitted to all earlier accepted scores uses counts of local molecular environments and generalized Tanimoto similarity to predict that pool jointly. Each batch position chooses the remaining maximizer of a fresh correlated score draw; accepted offspring then update both the prediction archive and the breeding population.
approach.novelty: Remove only cross-candidate residual correlation from allocation, giving each candidate an independent Gaussian excursion with its existing jittered marginal variance. The fitted joint model and nonzero random exploration remain. No completed sibling of this current baseline is supplied. An earlier correlation-only control changed decisions but left one task unfinished, and its Parent still allowed direct aromatic exchanges. This experiment reuses that precise control on the exchange-free Parent and seeks a complete comparison under the current profile. It tests whether the search can avoid a material endpoint loss when dependence is removed; it adds neither a new acquisition objective nor a chemical diversity rule.

nodes.hypothesis: Remove cross-candidate dependence from allocation residual draws by sampling independent Gaussian residuals with the Parent's unchanged jittered marginal variances, while retaining the fitted count-based joint posterior.

finding_summary.headline: Correlation removal executes correctly but lowers the complete matched mean by 0.018447
finding_summary.insights: The isolated reverse control supports a positive contribution of correlated allocation residuals in the current exchange-free search, with substantial seed and task dependence. Independent draws do not guarantee diverse selections: on the same Child pools they raise mean absolute fitted-model correlation from 0.05063 to 0.05465 and slightly reduce nonempty typed and generic core counts. Strict local parent beats increase from 629 to 661 and incumbent gains from 258 to 273, yet the endpoint mean falls, so these local measures do not explain the benefit. Molecular evidence preserves compact conventional alternatives and some larger improving families alongside reactive bond environments, repeated large assemblies and destructive fragments; no single chemistry or size rule accounts for the score. Which adaptive choices mediate the benefit remains open. The earlier correlation-removal panel still lacks its timed-out seed-0 endpoint, and its two-seed gain under a different Parent and profile remains separate evidence. This complete comparison answers the current component question without repairing or reinterpreting that historical record.
finding_summary.results: All 435 allocations remove analytic residual cross-covariance while preserving the original jittered marginal variances. Every sampled value and selected identity reconstructs. Replaying correlated draws on the same Child inputs changes 422 of 435 selected sets; thirteen sets coincide, and residuals still move 3,747 of 4,350 choices away from the available mean maximum. Mean final score falls from 0.595670 to 0.577222, a paired loss of 0.018447 against the registered 0.002 scale. The no-material-loss prediction is therefore contradicted, although the removal itself is confirmed. Seed macro changes are -0.066439, +0.035503 and -0.024407: ten task-seed endpoints fall and five rise. The strongest loss is deco_hop seed 0 (-0.253234); the strongest gain is sitagliptin_mpo seed 1 (+0.158750). All tasks complete under the matched profile.

molecular.headline: Aromatic amides, aryl amines and crowded nitrogen rings coexist with large repeated assemblies and reactive difluoroamino groups
molecular.overall_character: This report concerns the fresh complete panel for n-54adc6a641e8. All fifteen Child and fifteen published Parent trajectory files were present and read. Each task has 900 records and 870 optimizer proposals across Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2; no task lacks trajectories. The brief reports complete Child evaluation and complete current-profile pairing with code Parent n-62daf219c70a, with no profile-mismatched seeds. Chemistry comparisons below use those published Parent trajectories, not an older incomplete correlation experiment. The report does not decide activation, rank algorithms or attribute a chemical change to residual correlation. The output is ring-rich and largely aromatic: ring-closure-string incidence spans 0.9586 to 0.9828 and aromatic-string incidence 0.9552 to 0.9736. These are molecule-level text incidences, not ring counts, aromatic-atom fractions or proof of geometric aromaticity. Families include compact benzofused azaaromatic amides, substituted indole/amidine systems, linked nitrogen/oxygen carbonyl heterocycles, flexible and bridged aryl amines, crowded nitrogen-dicarbonyl rings and fluorinated nitrogen-rich heterocycles. Some trajectories also produce very large repeated carbonyl/aryl assemblies and small poor-scoring fragments. Families differ across seeds, but within-seed leaders often remain close relatives, supporting moderate overall diversity. Synthetic plausibility remains questionable and overall drug-likeness weak. Reactive N-halogen, peroxide, O-F, imino-fluoride and thioaldehyde environments coexist with recognizable amides, carbonyls, amines and ethers. The strongest fluorinated family has two difluoroaminomethyl groups, with fluorines attached to nitrogen; those are not ordinary fluoromethyl substituents. Its lack of cumulated double bonds removes one specific Parent concern without establishing a chemically stable molecule. Counterexamples to uniform chemical failure include a high-scoring N-hydroxy azaaromatic amide and a comparatively conventional flexible aryl tertiary amine. Other gains involve larger or more crowded rings, so higher score is not synonymous with better synthetic plausibility. Formal-charge and stereocentre-string incidences are 0.0 for every task despite visible protonatable amines and potential stereogenic centres. Sizes below count heavy-atom tokens in cited trajectory SMILES; no synthesis, physical-property or conformational validation was performed. The digest final excerpts are late seed-2 proposals, not each seed's best retained molecule. Parent comparisons rely on its published trajectories; cited_smiles contains only current molecules authorized by the digest or trusted current trajectory list.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-1 leader has 25 heavy atoms: an ethyl/dimethyl-substituted benzofused azaaromatic ring linked through an N-chloro amide to a chloropyridyl ring. A nearby leader uses N-hydroxy amide chemistry and an additional carbon-bound chlorine. Seed 2 retains a 25-heavy-atom methoxy/methyl indole-like amidine family with halogen substitution on both ring and linker nitrogen. Seed 0 instead reaches a 25-heavy-atom partly dearomatized, expanded unsaturated N-fluorinated ring system attached to a fluoropyridyl imine. Mean proposal SMILES length is 43.2, with halogen incidence 0.9678. Compact aromatic and carbonyl/imine organization is plentiful, but reactive nitrogen substitution and atypical unsaturation remain prominent.
liabilities: N-Cl amides, N-F ring nitrogens and N-halogen amidines differ chemically from ordinary carbon-bound halogens.
The N-hydroxy amide is recognizable chemistry but does not validate every neighbouring N-halogen variant; the partly dearomatized unsaturated structures require separate assessment.
Late small fragments can lose the combined ring/linker context while retaining an imine or halogen.
missing_features: Conventional local alternatives preserving the favorable azaaromatic/linker arrangement are not consistently established at the leading score; the near-leading N-hydroxy amide is a counterexample to obligatory N-chlorination.
The expanded unsaturated and N-halogenated families lack demonstrated stable geometry, configuration and synthesis.
The observed gradients do not identify an absent exact target pharmacophore, and additional rings, nitrogen or halogens are not a general inferred solution.

The benzofused azaaromatic N-chloro amide reaches 0.47189631731668286; its methoxy-substituted relative scores 0.47127110791377924. An N-hydroxy analogue with altered carbon-bound chlorination scores 0.4624615253670981, showing useful reward without an N-halogen bond, though the comparison changes more than that one bond. The Child seed-1 result is close to but below Parent 0.47411701813450596. Seed 0 reaches 0.39347683285969637 versus Parent 0.39405142067435733, and seed 2 reaches 0.42762099872850584 versus Parent 0.438972502037081. Isolated fluorine scores 0.0, while a late small vinyl/imino pyridyl fragment scores 1.214856075093651e-06. The favorable association concerns a compact combined ring/linker organization, not halogen presence or one azaaromatic fragment alone.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-1 leader has 46 heavy atoms and combines linked heteroaromatic/carbonyl regions with branched fluorinated ether/acetal groups, an imidate-like connection, a carbon-linked nitrile and an O-linked cyanate. Its compact terminal aromatic-labelled fragment contains extra short ring closures whose realistic geometry is not established. Seed 0 reaches an 80-heavy-atom multiheteroaryl assembly with repeated dione units, carbonyls, polyene/imine chains, peroxide and N/O-halogen environments. Seed 2 reaches a 44-heavy-atom extensively linked/annulated azaaromatic dione bearing formyl/urea-like and vinyl substitution. Mean proposal SMILES length is 119.5, with a maximum of 236. Large repeated assemblies therefore form a substantial part of the visible output, while the leading seed-1 family still has a distinct more compact organization.
liabilities: O-linked cyanate is distinct from the carbon-linked nitrile present elsewhere. Fluorinated acetal/ether centres require assessment without conflating their carbon-bound fluorine with direct O-F.
The large seed-0 leader contains peroxide, direct O-F and N-Cl environments alongside repeated diones and conjugated chains.
Dense short ring closures and extensive annulation may satisfy graph notation without demonstrating a stable aromatic or three-dimensional geometry.
missing_features: Stable independent arrangements preserving the favorable combined heterocyclic features are not consistently represented across seeds; very large repeated assemblies do not recover the stronger compact Parent organization.
The short aromatic-labelled ring closures, imidate-like linkages and highly substituted acetal centres lack demonstrated accessible geometry and chemical stability.
Conventional alternatives to cyanate, peroxide and heteroatom-halogen functionality are not established at comparable scores; the data do not identify one required target decoration.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted dione scores 0.548381482770623. The seed-1 leader reaches 0.633657779658626, while two related decorated molecules score 0.630172470325923 and 0.6302100372963424. nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

retained_mechanisms: Accepted-only task-local archive, bounded greedy survivor population and score-quantile breeding selection.
Connected-fragment crossover, optional post-crossover mutation and ordinary one-/two-/three-call continuation with bounded retries and saturation rules.
All seven ordinary atom/bond/ring mutation families, fixed weights/atom bounds and disabled direct aromatic C/N exchange with passive opportunity tracing.
Sanitization, stable canonical isomeric identity and original-graph provenance, initial/emitted and temporary-pool duplicate rejection, fixed surplus pools and announced batches.

approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from a bounded population of accepted high-scoring molecules. It uses score-quantile parent sampling, connected-fragment crossover and local graph mutations, including its retained formula-preserving aromatic nitrogen-position exchange. Stable identity admission checks each fresh candidate before a surplus pool is formed. A Gaussian process trained on all earlier accepted scores uses binary local-environment fingerprints to predict that pool, and correlated posterior draws choose the molecules submitted for evaluation. Accepted feedback updates both the breeding population and the full prediction archive.
approach.novelty: Make the posterior sensitive to how many times each local molecular environment occurs. Replace binary fingerprint presence with integer environment counts and the corresponding generalized Tanimoto covariance. Repeated ring or substituent environments can then change similarity even when their presence is already recorded. Earlier siblings changed survivor or parent allocation, graph edits and identity admission; they have not changed the posterior to retain environment multiplicity. This mechanism supplies quantitative representation to the existing learned selector. Its usefulness must be established through prospective prediction and the paired search results.

nodes.hypothesis: Replace binary Morgan-presence covariance with generalized Tanimoto covariance on integer counts of the same hashed local molecular environments, so the accepted-feedback Gaussian process conditions on environment multiplicity.

finding_summary.headline: Environment counts change selection and lift mean score by 0.0226, but uncertainty coverage worsens
finding_summary.insights:
The useful change comes from reweighting ordinary similarity relationships, not from splitting exact fingerprint ties: the only binary-equivalent pair in the Child pools remained count-equivalent. Counts usually increased archive-to-pool similarity and reduced posterior uncertainty, but neither direction was universal. Their prediction advantage was much larger when passively applied to the Parent's selected stream than on their own selected stream, showing why historical prediction gains need to be checked after selection adapts. Sitagliptin supplies the largest score gain even though its paired MSE worsens and its latent intervals cover only one third of scored emissions. Improved mean prediction therefore does not fully explain the whole-search gain; the contribution of changed uncertainty to allocation remains open. Uncertainty calibration is now a concrete issue to probe separately.

The molecular assessment finds smaller families in several streams, yet oversized assemblies, unusual heteroatom bonds, constrained rings and unspecified stereochemistry remain. Counts preserve the same local environment vocabulary and many hashing collisions; they supply neither a demonstrated size penalty nor evidence of synthetic or geometric feasibility. These results establish count-sensitive posterior execution and utility on the supplied panel, while leaving broader chemical usefulness and transfer to other search distributions unresolved.
finding_summary.results:
Environment multiplicity changed the similarity matrices and posterior distribution in all 435 fits. On identical archives and pools, 69,570 of 69,600 predicted means changed; replaying the same random draws changed 434 of 435 selected batches. The three-seed macro mean rose from 0.55177 to 0.57434, a gain of 0.02257 above the registered 0.002 minimum. Two seed means improved and one fell. Mean final scores rose for sitagliptin by 0.06213, median similarity by 0.02333, DRD2 by 0.02056 and decoration hopping by 0.00911, while zaleplon fell by 0.00228. All evaluations completed; strict improvements over the best generating parent rose from 593 to 624 out of 4,350 offspring.

On the Child's identical scored molecules, the count model reduced prediction MSE from a passive binary model's 0.011797 to 0.011269, about 4.5%, and raised mean within-batch rank correlation from 0.469 to 0.550. The archive-mean baseline MSE was 0.042504. However, mean latent interval width shrank from 0.263 to 0.168, and nominal 95% coverage fell from 85.6% to 76.9%; including observation noise only raised count-model coverage to 77.2%. This is evidence for better average prediction and search outcomes on this panel, alongside worse uncertainty coverage.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich families become smaller in several streams, but unusual heteroatom bonds and unspecified ring stereochemistry persist
molecular.overall_character: All supplied tasks and their Parent trajectories were read. Each current task contains 900 records, including 870 optimizer proposals. Ring-closure text presence ranges from 0.9575 to 0.9851 and aromatic-text presence from 0.9517 to 0.9747; these are fractions of proposal strings containing the relevant syntax, not fractions of atoms. The products include indole carboxamides, linked nitrogen/oxygen heteroaromatics, aryl-bearing cyclic amines, medium-ring aza-dicarbonyl assemblies, and fluorinated imino/carbonyl heterocycles. Distinct families occur across seeds, while leading excerpts concentrate on related members within a family. Several streams are smaller on average than Parent n-9edaa26007c3, but small size does not remove N-F, N-S, unusual sulfur bonding, unsaturated small rings or difficult polycyclic connectivity. Every task has charged_rate and stereocentre_rate 0.0. Neutral strings still contain potentially basic amines; the strings do not establish solution or evaluator protonation states. Structural counts below are passive RDKit readings of the supplied trajectories, recorded in .slots/SPIRAL2.r0011-02-improve-L01.molecular-audit.json. Parsing establishes connectivity, without establishing a feasible conformation, stability or synthetic route.

per_task.generated_character: The main high-scoring family comprises medium-sized, heavily substituted indole carboxamides attached to phenyl or pyridyl rings. Methoxy or vinyl-ether groups, methyl/vinyl substituents, an indole NH and an amide carbonyl recur; many leading amides carry N-F or N-Cl. A conventional secondary-amide member has 24 heavy atoms and three rings. The highest observed molecule instead has a compact bridged nitrogen-containing core, a phenyl carboxamide with an N-S bond, and 24 heavy atoms. The indole/aryl amide components are familiar synthetic building blocks, whereas the N-halogen, N-sulfanyl and bridged variants are less routine endpoints. Mean proposal SMILES length is 42.2 versus Parent 44.7; halogen presence falls from the Parent digest 0.9609 to 0.623. The Parent highest observed record was an N-fluoro indole/pyridyl carboxamide at 0.46092619585962435. The current chemistry retains that broad family while increasing vinyl substitution and changing the leading bridged core.
liabilities: The leading N-F and N-Cl bonds are on amide nitrogen, rather than carbon-bound aromatic halogens; the highest molecule also has an N-S bond. These require separate chemical scrutiny from ordinary aryl carboxamides.
Vinyl ethers and the compact bridged nitrogen-containing core add reactivity or geometric questions. The bridged product has a potential stereochemical choice that its string does not specify.
missing_features: The low-end fragments lack the integrated fused-aromatic, carbonyl and aryl/heteroaryl arrangement expressed by the stronger molecules; some late substitutions also fail to retain its favorable balance.

Conventional amide substitution is demonstrated near the leading scores, but an equally strong family with both ordinary bond chemistry and straightforward alternative core connectivity is not established. The observations do not identify an unseen target-specific group that must be added.

The cited divinyl/methoxy pyridyl secondary amide scores 0.4330127018922193; replacing its amide hydrogen with either Cl or F gives 0.4423126980074005 in both cases. The N-fluoro phenyl/vinyl-ether congener reaches 0.4484138510190879, and the bridged N-S-containing product reaches 0.45766047024715. Methane scores 0.0. nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from previously accepted scored molecules. Score-band parent draws feed connected-fragment crossover and ordinary local mutations, while direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled. Its graph checker sanitizes and reparses each offspring. A second admission step verifies a stable canonical identity, normalizes confirmed graph-equivalent aliases and rejects unstable identities before duplicate checks build the surplus pool. A Gaussian process fitted to all earlier accepted scores uses folded counts of local molecular environments; correlated posterior draws allocate the announced evaluation batch. Real accepted feedback updates the prediction archive and the greedy breeding population.
approach.novelty: Remove the active stable-identity admission step while keeping its original checks as passive diagnostics. The original checked graph and its returned string will pass directly to the existing novelty, pool and emission bookkeeping. This isolates the retained identity component; the other current siblings change the count representation, donor construction or posterior allocation. An older identity control only normalized two unselected aliases, whereas the current Parent rejects one unstable representation. The new control follows any affected candidate through pool entry, selection and actual evaluator feedback. A natural identity failure remains evidence, and only complete exposed matched runs can answer the endpoint-contribution question.

nodes.hypothesis: Remove active stable-canonical pool normalization and rejection after the inherited graph checker, routing its original checked molecular object and raw returned identity through existing novelty, pool, emission and pending interfaces while retaining the original stable-admission helper only as a passive comparator.

finding_summary.headline: Removing stable identity admission changes seven evaluations but leaves every endpoint unchanged
finding_summary.insights:
An unselected pool member can still change which other molecules receive evaluations. Here the pool substitution and index shift changed the correlated allocation, so equal endpoints do not mean identical search behavior. This supplies current downstream exposure that the older two unselected stable aliases lacked. The zero endpoint effect is nevertheless narrow: the sole opportunity occurred in the last batch, after the existing best score was already reached. The changed labels did not train another model or seed further breeding.

The experiment does not establish that an unstable key is safe to emit. That boundary was never naturally exercised, and the missing-provenance guard still raises in an explicitly synthetic control using real archived feedback. Nor does admission removal establish better chemistry: the altered final choices include both a high-scoring halogen-free amine and retained reactive substituents, while the broader ring-geometry and stereochemical limitations remain. Earlier identity exposure, actual selection of an unstable representation and other parser conventions remain open. The observed component result does not establish universal dispensability or effects of combining sibling changes.
finding_summary.results:
The removal had a real admission effect. Among 75,958 checked Child attempts, one candidate had an alternating identity string that the Parent rejected. The Child admitted its original checked graph and raw key into the final docking pool. The candidate itself was never selected, emitted or scored, and its two spellings were not shown to be graph-equivalent. Its admission substituted one pool member and shifted 104 shared positions. With the same recorded random-normal draws and unchanged marginal predictions for shared candidates, the final allocation evaluated seven different molecules. Four of those new alternatives remained in the final population; none improved the incumbent. Fourteen of fifteen complete task/seed trajectories were identical.

All fifteen task runs completed with valid unique batches, successful feedback joins and no external rejection or identity exception. Every paired final score and every best-so-far sequence stayed unchanged. Mean endpoint score was 0.595670 in both nodes, with seed population SD 0.026593; all three paired seed changes were exactly zero, within the registered 0.002 allowance. The active bypass was confirmed and the complete exposed comparison supports a conditional no-material-effect endpoint contribution for the admission component.

All common identities retain their recorded scores, all fifteen best_so_far sequences are identical, and the final best molecules are shared. The output consists of substituted indole amides and diketones, linked fused nitrogen heterocycles, flexible and cyclic aryl amines, bridged nitrogen-carbonyl systems, and fluorinated imino/carbonyl heterocycles. nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from previously accepted, scored molecules. It retains at most 64 survivors by score, draws parents from favored score bands, and either recombines connected fragments from two parents or makes a short sequence of ordinary single-parent mutations. A successful crossover receives an additional random finishing mutation with probability 35 percent before it reaches the candidate pool. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled. Valid, unique proposals fill a fresh surplus pool; a Gaussian process fitted to all earlier accepted scores uses counts of local molecular environments and correlated posterior draws to choose the announced evaluation batch. Accepted offspring update both the model archive and the breeding population.
approach.novelty: Remove only the optional finishing mutation after a successful crossover, retaining its original random gate draw. The immediate recombinant must still pass the ordinary validity, identity and duplicate gates. Earlier siblings removed whole crossover or ordinary single-parent continuation; others changed recombination, parent scheduling or proposal lifetime. None isolates this finishing branch. Finishing can disrupt a completed structure, but the Parent also evaluates useful finished products and breeds from them, so the registered contribution prediction is a score decrease on removal. A complete contrary or negligible result would answer the same narrow question. This finishing-only treatment also supplies the separate control needed to interpret the parallel ring-recombination interaction.

nodes.hypothesis: Remove optional post-crossover finishing mutation by setting its existing probability from 0.35 to 0.0 while retaining exactly one original gate draw after every successful ordinary crossover, so its immediate product reaches the unchanged admission pipeline without a finishing call; retain ordinary single-parent continuation and every other active Parent rule.

finding_summary.headline: Finishing contributes to endpoint search: its removal lowers the mean despite more local wins
finding_summary.insights:
The complete exposed removal supports a positive contribution from optional finishing in this exact exchange-disabled search composition. Earlier whole-crossover and ordinary-continuation controls did not answer this boundary. Preserving immediate recombinants clearly delivered useful evaluated and breeding products, yet that delivery was insufficient to preserve final search quality. More local wins were measured against weaker generating parents; they cannot substitute for the endpoint comparison. The result remains conditional: the gain in one seed and seven task/seed cells rules out a uniform benefit claim.

The molecules also do not support a simple chemical-preservation explanation. Mean size and ring count increased, but distinct typed core count decreased from 1,851 to 1,749. Tiny fragments and cumulenes became less frequent, while reactive heteroatom-halogen bonds, difficult ring geometries and unspecified stereochemistry persisted alongside useful conventional alternatives. Those are observed changes, not identified causes of the endpoint loss. Observed wall time increased from about 579 to 2,868 seconds, largely alongside higher oracle time on changed molecules, so fewer finishing calls do not establish a compute saving. The separate roles of missing finishing products, altered admission and random streams, and later adaptive feedback remain unresolved. This finding closes the exact finishing contribution question under the tested conditions; it does not establish whole-foundation value or the pending ring-by-finishing interaction.
finding_summary.results:
Finishing was absent at all 35,049 successful crossover opportunities, with 12,346 retained gate draws below the old threshold. Of those exposed immediate products, 9,907 entered candidate pools and 515 reached real evaluation. All 501 nonterminal accepted products entered the next model fit; 297 later bred. Fourteen births were terminal, and 204 other accepted products had later opportunities but were never reused.

All fifteen task/seed comparisons completed. Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.595670 to 0.559427, a paired change of -0.036243 against the registered 0.002 loss threshold. Seed changes were -0.059007, +0.020922 and -0.070644; eight task/seed endpoints declined and seven improved. Decoration hopping and docking had the largest mean losses, while zaleplon and median-2 means improved. Seed population dispersion fell from 0.026593 to 0.021675 around the lower mean. Across all accepted offspring, strict parent wins rose from 629 to 689 and incumbent gains from 258 to 264, but absolute offspring and parent scores were lower and the average positive incumbent step fell from 0.022510 to 0.019939.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic amides, cyclic amines and nitrogen-carbonyl polycycles retain reactive bonds and unspecified stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: Assessed Algorithm Node n-5a357a2ac96f against published Parent n-62daf219c70a. All 15 Child and 15 published Parent trajectory files were present and read in full: 9000 records altogether, including 4350 evaluated optimizer proposals on each side. Every task has 900 records, including 870 optimizer proposals, across Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2; tasks_without_trajectories is empty. The immutable brief reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true, with all supplied seeds matched and no profile-mismatched seeds. There are no missing paths or absent task/seed comparisons. The final_molecules digest excerpt contains late seed-2 proposals, not every seed incumbent; seed-specific bests and terminal proposals were read from the full files. The output consists of substituted indole/benzimidazole amides and strained arene-fused analogues, linked aza/oxygen polycycles, aryl cyclic amines, medium-ring nitrogen-carbonyl systems, and fluorinated imino/carbonyl heterocycles. Across tasks, supplied ring-closure-string incidence is 0.9724 to 0.9931 and aromatic-string incidence is 0.969 to 0.9839. These measure whether a molecule contains the text feature, not its ring count or fraction of aromatic atoms. Halogen-string incidence ranges from 0.2069 to 0.9713. Formal-charge and stereocentre-string incidence are 0.0 throughout; neutral strings nevertheless contain recognizable protonatable amines. A read-only RDKit 2023.09.6 audit of the trajectory SMILES parsed every evaluated optimizer proposal on both sides. Child heavy-atom counts have median 29 and mean 32.55, versus Parent median 28 and mean 28.71. Child mean perceived ring count is 4.49 versus 3.79, while the median is 4 on both sides. This is substantial cyclic and aromatic chemistry, with saturated nitrogen rings also present. Structural diversity is moderate across seeds and tasks but narrower among leading relatives within a seed; different strings and perceived ring counts do not establish independent useful scaffolds. The same audit finds N-halogen bonds in 1092 Child versus 1042 Parent optimizer records, O-halogen bonds in 545 versus 278, and O-O bonds in 272 versus 273. These are overlapping record-level incidences, not counts of distinct molecules or measurements of reactivity. Carbon-centred cumulated double bonds occur in 6 Child versus 52 Parent records, and proposals with at most 4 heavy atoms number 70 versus 119. Thus several liabilities persist while cumulenes and tiny-fragment exposure are less frequent. No emitted optimizer SMILES on either side contains an explicit tetrahedral or double-bond stereochemical marker; RDKit finds at least one unassigned potential tetrahedral centre in 2214 Child records. Perceived potential stereochemistry does not establish configurational stability. Ordinary aromatic halogens, amides, ethers, lactams and tertiary amines coexist with N-F/N-Cl, O-halogen, peroxide, strained-ring and unusual sulfur environments. Drug-likeness is weak overall and synthesis questionable, although individual conventional functional groups and some leaders are credible starting points for chemistry review. Valid SMILES and high oracle scores do not establish synthesis, stability, conformation or biological activity. The original gap reports for n-c55c3d520a2c and the baseline reproduction n-62daf219c70a were read through context.evidence_index; recurring gaps below preserve that provenance and are newly conditioned on this Child panel. Their recurrence or attenuation does not identify a responsible component, establish chemical mediation, or label any unobserved alternative molecule. Descriptor definitions, complete source-path hashes, per-seed examples and record-level derived chemistry are in .slots/round-0023-slot-0/molecular/chemistry_audit.json, trajectory_chemistry.jsonl and audit_chemistry.py. These are audit artifacts; this response is the only molecular_report. Parent molecules are described from their published trajectories, while every cited_smiles entry is verified against the Child digest or immutable-request trusted Child trajectory paths.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This gap was recorded for n-c55c3d520a2c and reproduced in n-62daf219c70a; it recurs in n-5a357a2ac96f on the complete matched Search Seed panel at 300 observations per task. The present evaluated optimizer records include 1092 with N-halogen bonds, 545 with O-halogen bonds and 272 with O-O bonds, versus 1042, 278 and 273 in the published Parent. The absent capability is reliable environment control, not an inability to make conventional heterocycles, amines or carbon-bound halogens.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve conventional local bond environments when retaining otherwise useful molecular frameworks.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Task-agnostic transformations need to distinguish heteroatom-halogen, peroxide and unusual sulfur environments from conventional substitutions, and offer chemically plausible alternatives while retaining relationships supported by accepted local feedback. Preserve the counterexamples: neither a universal halogen ban nor an automatic reward for replacing every flagged bond follows from these observations. This recurring chemistry gap has no identified component attribution or measured replacement benefit.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This extends the ring-feasibility gap recorded for n-c55c3d520a2c and reproduced in n-62daf219c70a, with narrower current conditions. Conventional pyrrolidine and fluorinated small carbocycles also appear, including at high scores. More rings and valid aromatic SMILES therefore do not by themselves resolve geometry, while the reduced cumulene count prevents treating the historical pattern as unchanged.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently resolve the geometric feasibility of fused small rings, medium-ring bridges and aromatic-labelled larger heterocycles.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring transformations need ring-size, unsaturation and junction-aware feasibility assessment together with alternative connectivities that retain useful functional-group arrangements. Distinguish ordinary small carbocycles from difficult fused unsaturation and bridges; do not infer a blanket prohibition of small rings or aromatic heterocycles. The observed changes in chemistry do not establish endpoint mediation or a score benefit from any proposed geometry constraint.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This gap originates in n-c55c3d520a2c, recurs in n-62daf219c70a, and remains in n-5a357a2ac96f under the complete matched Search conditions. Every supplied Child task has stereocentre-string incidence 0.0, and none of the 4350 evaluated optimizer SMILES contains an explicit tetrahedral or double-bond stereochemical marker. RDKit identifies at least one unassigned potential tetrahedral centre in 2214 of those records, including substituted cyclic amines, fluorinated carbocycles, bridged frameworks and sulfoxide-containing molecules. Potential-centre perception does not establish configurational stability. Zero formal-charge-string incidence is a separate observation and coexists with clearly protonatable amines.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generated molecular identities remain stereochemically unspecified even when their saturated or sulfur-containing environments admit potential stereochemistry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic representation and its transformations need to preserve or deliberately resolve stereochemical identity where physically meaningful, while recognizing achiral or configurationally unstable cases. Assess protonation and tautomerism separately. These records show incomplete molecular definition; they do not demonstrate a stereochemical score penalty, a missing basic centre, or responsibility of any particular search component.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This was recorded for n-c55c3d520a2c and reproduced in n-62daf219c70a; the n-5a357a2ac96f matched Search panel shows persistence with counterexamples. There are 70 evaluated optimizer proposals with at most 4 heavy atoms versus Parent 119, so small-fragment exposure has declined. Some isolated halogen or small reagent-like proposals still receive floor scores, while a late amino/sulfoxide/aryl fragment loses the cyclic context and scores 0.007925811229838719 against 0.7672225298102587 for that seed leader. At the other extreme, a 120-heavy-atom assembly scores 0.57781217750258, below a 41-heavy-atom linked-polycycle leader at 0.6563896336014299 in another seed of the same objective. A 21-heavy-atom cyclic amine approaches its observed score ceiling elsewhere. These are conditional structural associations across actual records, not a matched causal size experiment.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably retain useful functional-group context while avoiding both tiny fragments and excessive molecular elaboration.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Task-local feedback should support context-preserving simplification and replacements while detecting when fragmentation removes the useful arrangement. The missing capability is consistent control of context and elaboration; neither a fixed minimum size nor a universal preference for smaller or larger molecules is justified. Keep chemically informative small high-scoring structures as counterexamples, and assess proposed alternatives through the allowed local feedback.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This conditional coverage gap was recorded for n-c55c3d520a2c and reproduced in n-62daf219c70a. It is re-observed in n-5a357a2ac96f at the supplied Search Seeds and observation budget: leaders repeatedly alter halogen location, short side chains, imino/carbonyl identity or ring segments within retained aromatic-amide, aryl-cyclic-amine and nitrogen-carbonyl families. Several peripheral variants have equal or very close scores. Different seeds reach distinct families, including a flexible aryl/pyridyl assembly and a fused aza/oxygen polycycle, so the full output is not globally collapsed and the generator plainly forms rings. The missing coverage concerns feasible alternatives among useful leading molecules, not raw SMILES variety.
transferable_gaps.gap: The leading outputs do not consistently include chemically independent plausible alternatives to a successful framework within each seed.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Task-agnostic structural transformations need to offer chemically independent connectivities that retain favorable functional and spatial relationships supported by current accepted feedback. Evaluate whether the resulting alternatives remain useful and chemically credible; new strings, more rings or greater core variety alone cannot establish improvement. Preserve the original source and these conditions when transferring the gap, rather than attributing convergence to a particular component or assuming that diversity necessarily raises the objective.

nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

retained_mechanisms: Accepted-score graph evolution and recursive accepted-offspring breeding, original score-quantile first-parent and excluded-partner allocation, greedy score/serial survival capped at 64, and the full chronological real-label archive.
Ordinary connected-fragment crossover remains active; its single post-success gate random draw remains, while the optional finishing mutation body is retained but unreachable at probability zero.
All seven ordinary mutation families, internally bounded retries and one/two/three-call ordinary continuation remain active; saturation and exhaustion laws are unchanged but unexposed.
Sanitization, exact stable canonical identity verification, initial/emitted and temporary-pool duplicate rejection, original atom cap, bounded outer retries and fresh 160-member pools.
Integer-count Morgan local-environment features, generalized Tanimoto GP, accepted-only full-archive fitting, adaptive score normalization, fixed noise/jitter and full covariance.

approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves a population of scored molecular graphs. It samples a first parent from score-ranked bands, then either mutates that graph or samples a different scored identity and joins connected fragments from the two parents. Crossover may receive a finishing mutation, and ordinary mutation may continue for several steps. Valid, canonically unique products fill a fresh surplus pool. A Gaussian process fitted to every accepted task-local score, using count fingerprints and a Tanimoto kernel, supplies correlated posterior draws that choose the announced evaluation batch. New real scores update both the complete learning archive and bounded greedy survivors, so accepted offspring can become future breeders. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled in this Parent.
approach.novelty: Remove only the rule that forbids drawing the first parent again as its crossover partner. The original score-ranked partner sampler can then draw the same accepted identity twice, and the existing fragment construction, finishing mutation and duplicate checks decide what happens. Earlier siblings removed crossover, flattened partner rank weights or changed donor cuts; none isolated this identity-exclusion rule. Self recombination could form a different graph, reproduce a rejected parent, or change retry and pool competition. Measuring those outcomes tests whether forced distinct-parent mating contributes under the current complete method.

nodes.hypothesis: Remove only the selected first canonical identity exclusion from actual crossover-partner sampling, allowing ordinary self-pair draws under the original score-quantile band and member law while preserving all first-parent behavior and unchanged crossover, finishing and admission.

finding_summary.headline: Distinct-parent exclusion contributes: removal lowers the mean by 0.03199 despite productive self offspring
finding_summary.insights:
Enforcing distinct source identities contributes positively under this complete method and evaluation profile, even though self recombination can produce useful, subsequently reused molecules. The tested contribution includes both permitting self-pairs and redistributing probability among other partners, followed by their different random draws and feedback histories. These data do not separate those channels or establish a diversity mechanism.

The extra local wins are especially informative: total parent wins rose from 629 to 673 and incumbent advances from 258 to 265, yet mean accepted-offspring score fell from 0.385256 to 0.371429 and mean best-parent score from 0.470456 to 0.448955. The advances were more numerous but added less total improvement. Thus easier parent comparisons and lower dispersion can accompany weaker endpoints. The molecular assessment also finds different leading aromatic families across seeds alongside recurring questionable attachments and unspecified stereochemistry; those concerns persist in the Parent and do not identify the exclusion rule as their cause. Individual channel contributions, chemical mediation and reliability beyond the measured panel remain unresolved. This result answers the distinct-partner boundary within the retained foundation, without attributing an entire foundation or combining sibling effects.
finding_summary.results:
The removal ran as specified and lowered the complete mean from 0.595670 to 0.563677, a decrease of 0.031992 against the registered 0.002 scale. Ten of the 15 task/seed endpoints fell and five improved. Seed-macro changes were -0.092144, +0.012064 and -0.015897; macro dispersion also fell, from 0.026593 to 0.022045. The largest losses were the seed-0 deco-hop and sitagliptin endpoints, while the zaleplon task mean improved.

There were 2,851 actual self-pairs. They produced 359 immediate copies, 2,489 different graphs and three construction failures. Finishing changed 135 copies into different final identities; 224 remained rejected copies. The self channel reached 2,454 fresh pool entries and 155 real evaluations, including 27 parent wins and 14 incumbent advances. Eighty-seven accepted self products later bred, and 41 had accepted children. Separately, replay from identical sampler states found 6,283 changed choices among nonself partners, which reached 346 accepted evaluations. All 15 full cells had evaluated self products, but 310 individual batches had self draws without a self evaluation; these zeros and terminally censored products remain in the comparison.

molecular.headline: Aromatic families vary across seeds, but reactive attachments, awkward ring closures and unspecified stereochemistry persist
molecular.overall_character: For n-60350f969287, every supplied Child trajectory and every published code-Parent n-62daf219c70a trajectory was read: all five tasks on Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2, with 300 observations in each file. Each task has 900 Child observations, including 870 optimizer proposals. There are no missing trajectory paths or uncovered tasks. The immutable brief reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true, all supplied seeds matched, and no profile-mismatched seeds. This is a complete chemistry comparison under the frozen Research in Depth epoch-1 profile with feedback batches of 10; the paired endpoints below are copied from observed trajectory maxima and are descriptive. No activation or component-contribution verdict is made. These evaluated structures do not identify which chemistry came from equal-source crossover, ordinary mutation, subsequent finishing, or adaptive selection. The output contains compact fused aromatic ketones, esters and N-amino amides; linked heteroaryl assemblies, including very large repeated structures; diaryl aliphatic amines; bridged nitrogen-carbonyl systems; and fluorinated diones and polycycles. Recognizable medicinal chemistry coexists with N-halogen bonds, sulfur-fluoride attachments, unusually cross-linked aromatic-labelled graphs, and unspecified stereochemistry. Different seeds produce different families, while the strongest molecules within a seed often remain close relatives: structural diversity is moderate overall, not global collapse, but independent plausible alternatives among leaders are limited. Ring-closure-string incidence spans 0.9598 to 0.9793, and aromatic-string incidence spans 0.9483 to 0.9782. Those are molecule-level text incidences from the digest, not ring counts or aromatic-atom fractions. All tasks have charged_rate=0.0 and stereocentre_rate=0.0. The neutral strings nevertheless include clearly protonatable amines. Heavy-atom counts and ring descriptions below were read from the actual trajectory graphs with RDKit 2023.09.6; successful parsing is not evidence of stability, accessible geometry, synthesis or biological activity. The digest final_molecules are late seed-2 observations, not each seed's retained best, so each full seed trajectory was inspected. Parent evidence was read through the supplied evidence_index, including the full Molecular assessments for n-62daf219c70a and original gap source n-c55c3d520a2c. Their original chemical concerns and counterexamples remain conditional historical evidence; present examples are re-observations, not unchanged structures or independent mechanistic replication. The complete path/hash manifest, descriptor readings and Parent history are in /projects/standard/adeshwal/shared/zhou2577/SPIRAL/.slots/round-0024-slot-3/molecular-audit.json, with row-level provenance in molecular-records.jsonl in the same directory. per_task.generated_character: The strongest molecules are compact aromatic/carbonyl assemblies. Seed 0 reaches a 24-heavy-atom benzimidazole-like fused heteroaromatic ketone joined to phenyl, with vinyl, ethyl, methoxy and N-F substitution. Seed 1 reaches a 24-heavy-atom partially unsaturated fused nitrogen ring carrying a pyridyl ester, methyl/vinyl substituents and N-F or N-Br. Seed 2 reaches a 25-heavy-atom indole-like N-amino anilide: a fused aromatic system linked through carbonyl to nitrogen bearing both aryl and terminal amino substitution, with N-halogen on the fused ring. The latter therefore contains a genuine N-N bond, not simply an ordinary anilide. Mean optimizer SMILES length is 41.6, ring-string incidence 0.9632, aromatic-string incidence 0.9586 and halogen-string incidence 0.8943. These are not ring-deficient molecules. Parent leaders instead include an aromatic cumulene/imine in seed 0, an N-hydroxy pyridyl amide in seed 1 and an aryl vicinal diketone in seed 2; the broad aromatic territory persists while the detailed linkages differ.
liabilities: N-F, N-Br and N-Cl attachments to ring nitrogen differ chemically from ordinary carbon-bound aryl halogens; their appearance among leaders is not stability evidence.

The seed-2 N-amino amide introduces N-N chemistry, and nearby molecules alter N-O or N-S environments. Familiar amide-like connectivity does not establish synthetic accessibility of the whole molecule.
Vinyl groups, hydrazine-like substitution and unassigned saturated stereochemistry need molecule-specific assessment; the scores do not justify declaring every such group forbidden.
