The seed-2 top molecule avoids the Parent cyclic cumulene and N-F, so those liabilities cannot be treated as unavoidable generator outputs.

Potential stereogenic fluorinated carbons, ring junctions and amino-bearing centres lack explicit stereochemical identity; the trajectories do not identify a preferred tautomer, conformer or stereoisomer.

The higher reward for a particular dione/fluorine/amino arrangement does not reveal an absent exact pharmacophore. Extra amino substitution and a thione replacement provide strong counterexamples to simplistic functional-group prescriptions.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted dione scores 0.0020944534688323298. Child best values are 0.42248772984058786, 0.5959013456438182 and 0.6464670514720593 in seeds 0, 1 and 2. In seed 0, extending the saturated oxygen ring by one carbon lowers 0.42248772984058786 to 0.21435073283939884. In seed 1, the close relative with an extra fluoromethyl carbon scores 0.47818630139536483, below the 0.5959013456438182 leader. In seed 2, changing one dione oxygen to sulfur gives 0.00021901608523897876; changing one carbon-bound fluorine to amino gives 0.001778564838545041. Those close counterexamples support sensitivity to the complete polar-group composition and placement, not a general benefit from more donors or arbitrary heteroatom replacement. The less-bridged N-fluoro diene analogue still scores 0.6368477634260005, so the leading bridge is not established as essential to a useful score. Isolated fluorine scores 1.1043196211273875e-26, and the final seed-2 vinylamine proposal scores 2.365058330274635e-17: fluorine or amine functionality alone does not recreate the successful context. Observed Child versus matched Parent best values are: seed 0, 0.42248772984058786 versus 0.6510211907030741; seed 1, 0.5959013456438182 versus 0.4870057305679067; seed 2, 0.6464670514720593 versus 0.7208853668418119. The seed-1 improvement and seed-0/seed-2 losses retain their opposite directions; they do not show that one topology or N-F status universally controls reward.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source and conditions: this gap was recorded for n-c55c3d520a2c and reproduced in Parent n-62daf219c70a; it recurs in n-60350f969287 under the epoch-1 profile, Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2, 300 observations per task and feedback batches of 10. Current leaders include N-F/N-Br/N-Cl aromatic or cyclic nitrogen, N-amino amides, and unoxidized S-F attachments. Counterexamples are essential: an earlier conventional diarylmethylamino/pyrrolidine reaches 0.9999817933180638, the fluorinated dione leader at 0.6464670514720593 contains no N-F, and changing one peripheral S-F to S-methyl accompanies a slightly higher observed value. The problem is inconsistent environment control, not inability to emit useful amines, carbon-bound halogens or conventional sulfur chemistry.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve conventional local bond environments while modifying otherwise useful aromatic, amine and carbonyl frameworks.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Task-agnostic transformations need chemically meaningful local alternatives that preserve favorable complete scaffold relationships learned from real feedback, while distinguishing carbon-bound halogens, N-halogen bonds, ordinary thioethers/sulfoxides and unoxidized sulfur fluorides. These examples motivate assessing bond environments; they do not establish that a universal halogen or heteroatom filter raises reward, or that any particular search component caused the liability.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source and conditions: n-c55c3d520a2c and its same-output Parent baseline n-62daf219c70a established this chemical concern on the supplied Search panel. It is re-observed in n-60350f969287 under epoch 1 at the same Search seeds, observation budget and batch size. The current evidence is not an unchanged Parent cyclic-cumulene leader: it includes short internal cross-links in aromatic-labelled fragments, nitrogen-rich medium-ring bridges and crowded fluorinated diene polycycles. Conversely, conventional saturated cyclic amines and a less-bridged diene analogue at 0.6368477634260005 remain strongly scored. Successful graph parsing, many ring digits and aromatic labels do not demonstrate an accessible three-dimensional structure.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently distinguish representable ring connectivity from credible geometry and synthetically accessible topology.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring transformations need awareness of ring size, unsaturation, bridge connectivity and plausible conformational alternatives while retaining favorable functional relationships. Distinguish ordinary small rings from unsupported aromatic cross-links or constrained unsaturation. The chemical concern is conditional; a blanket ban on small rings, all bridges or ring formation is not supported, and chemistry association does not identify mechanism contribution.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source and conditions: the same representation gap was recorded for n-c55c3d520a2c and n-62daf219c70a and persists for n-60350f969287 across the complete supplied Search panel under epoch 1. Every current task has stereocentre-string incidence 0.0 despite amino-ether methines, substituted small rings, fluorinated bridgeheads and a sulfoxide among the observed molecules. Charged-string incidence is also 0.0, but accessible aliphatic amines are visibly present. No stereochemical penalty, protonation failure or preferred isomer is established by these scalar scores.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not specify stereochemical identity after generating potentially stereogenic saturated, bridged and sulfur-containing environments.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Representations and transformations need to preserve or explicitly resolve configurational identity when the resulting chemistry requires it, with separate handling of achiral and configurationally unstable cases. Protonation and tautomerism are separate state questions. The absent specification is directly observed; a score benefit from resolving it and attribution to any component remain unmeasured.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source and conditions: this conditional gap originates in n-c55c3d520a2c, is preserved in n-62daf219c70a, and recurs in n-60350f969287 at the supplied epoch-1 Search budget. Late tiny halogen or hydrocarbon observations reach recorded floors; a final vinylamine is also extremely low. At the other extreme, an 80-heavy-atom elaboration scores 0.6038062283737025, below the related 45-heavy-atom best at 0.6042806936682606. Yet compact aryl amines score highly, and smaller complete heteroaryl arrangements are already generated. The evidence concerns retention of a whole useful arrangement, not a universal minimum or maximum size.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably retain useful functional-group context while avoiding unhelpful fragmentation and repeated structural elaboration.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Task-local feedback should support transformations that preserve enough chemical context to test the learned arrangement while allowing meaningful simplification or replacement. Check whether elaboration retains useful relationships rather than merely adding repeated rings, and whether fragmentation leaves a viable whole candidate. No fixed size cutoff or guaranteed benefit from greater size follows from these observations.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source and conditions: leading-family concentration was documented for n-c55c3d520a2c and n-62daf219c70a and remains a conditional coverage concern for n-60350f969287 under the complete epoch-1 Search panel. Leaders repeatedly vary alkyl, halogen, carbonyl-adjacent or short ring segments on a retained family. The strongest aromatic/carbonyl family differs across seeds, as do compact heteroaryl, very large repeated heteroaryl, aryl-amine and fluorinated-polycycle arrangements; this is not global structural collapse or lack of ring generation. Close counterexamples show that more nitrogen, more carbon or a sulfur-for-oxygen replacement can lower score, so merely changing atoms is not reliable useful scaffold breadth.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently supply chemically independent, plausible alternatives to the leading scaffold family within each seed.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Scaffold-level alternatives need to preserve feedback-supported whole functional and spatial relationships in chemically distinct, feasible connectivities, with usefulness judged from subsequent real labels. Distinct strings, ring counts and global diversity do not certify useful alternatives. These chemical coverage observations neither establish that more diversity improves the objective nor attribute the observed concentration to the removed source-identity exclusion.

nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves task-local molecular graphs from scored observations, draws ranked breeding parents from greedy survivors, and constructs a complete surplus pool through crossover and ordinary graph mutations. Stable molecular identity and a final sulfur-signature gate admit only fresh unique offspring whose outside-envelope signatures do not exceed the per-signature maximum in their original scored generating parents. A Gaussian process on folded Morgan occurrence counts learns every earlier accepted raw score with adaptive normalization. Joint posterior function draws then choose the announced evaluation batch, and real accepted feedback immediately updates both survivors and the chronological learning archive.
approach.novelty: This full-pool generation-order control removes the composite posterior selector’s influence on successful evaluation choices while retaining its original computation and the sulfur gate. The first admitted members receive evaluation in their inherited generation order. The older control tested ungated pools; this tests the selector after sulfur admission changed the pool and ancestry. The pending siblings change predictive means or residual laws while retaining active predictive allocation, so they answer different questions.

finding_summary.headline: Posterior selection remains valuable after sulfur admission: removal loses 0.128 mean Top-1
finding_summary.insights:
The joint posterior allocation still contributes substantially after sulfur admission changes the available pool and later ancestry. This is now measured under the current gated conditions, with exposure in every task and seed; the earlier ungated loss alone could not establish that. More novel cores, more new parent-beating cores and easier selected-stream prediction did not preserve absolute source quality or incumbent improvement. This rules out treating those local proxies, or the narrower seed-average dispersion, as sufficient evidence of useful exploration. The result concerns the whole successful allocation consumer and its total adaptive effect. It does not isolate a mean, fingerprint, normalization or residual constituent, show a sulfur interaction, or attribute the whole graph foundation.

Chemistry remains mixed. Fewer N-halogen structures coexist with more O-halogen and peroxide structures, while useful conventional ether/ketone and methoxy alternatives and useful permitted sulfur remain. Some of the highest labels still belong to chemically doubtful output, including the cyclic-peroxide family in the sole improving endpoint. Those examples preserve exceptions without proving a chemical mediator, a universal liability penalty or a benefit from broader filtering. Passive alternatives have no new labels or continued ancestry. Current composition review, separate constituent and joint-interaction evidence, chemical mediation, partial alternative-lineage composition and full-history coverage remain open.
finding_summary.results:
All fifteen matched task/seed runs completed with the full budget. Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.596453 to 0.468270, a paired loss of 0.128183. All three seed averages fell, by 0.20602, 0.07253 and 0.10599. Fourteen endpoints fell; the sole gain was zaleplon seed 1, from 0.474117 to 0.479919. The control emitted exactly the first ten admitted molecules from every one of 435 complete 160-member pools. The passive original selector chose a different set in every batch and strictly preferred another identity in 4321 of 4350 same-mask selections. There were no natural fallback, incomplete-pool or factorization failures. The entire original GP computation and sulfur rule remained present.

The control produced 634 parent-beating offspring versus 648, but only 155 sequential incumbent advances versus 255. Its average offspring score was 0.22594 versus 0.37205, and average best-generating-parent score 0.31170 versus 0.45530. It created more new typed/generic cores (2366/1815 versus 1820/1117), including more new parent-beating cores (325/229 versus 262/163). Fewer accepted sources later entered breeding (2038 versus 2469). Final-batch sources were censored for later reuse. Prospective prediction accuracy on the control's own accepted stream was better: unequal-label pair accuracy 0.771 versus 0.710 and mean within-batch Spearman 0.666 versus 0.526. Those are different selected streams; at the same actual identity the passive original mean is unchanged and its MSE contrast is zero.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic families retain reactive bonds, difficult connectivity and unspecified stereochemistry across divergent seed histories
molecular.overall_character: Node n-605c7a785b51 produces linked nitrile/azaaryl amines, fused aryl amides, large azaaryl/dicarbonyl assemblies, aryl cyclic amines and sulfoxides, connected nitrogen/dione rings, and fluorinated imino/carbonyl systems. Whole-trajectory diversity is moderate, with much narrower repeated leader families within seeds; distinct strings are not evidence of independent useful scaffolds. Digest ring-closure-string incidence spans 0.9437-0.9747 and aromatic-string incidence 0.6609-0.9724. These are fractions of molecules exhibiting text features, not ring counts or aromatic-atom fractions. Charged and stereocentre-string incidences are 0.0 on all five objectives. This does not mean basic amines or potentially stereogenic graphs are absent. Read-only RDKit 2023.09.6 finds unassigned tetrahedral centres in 2112 of 4350 Child optimizer observations, compared with 2455 Parent observations. Child has 397 observations with O-O bonds, 172 with N-halogen bonds, 517 with O-halogen bonds and 27 with S-halogen bonds; Parent counts are respectively 128, 786, 217 and 93. These classes overlap and are chemical flags, not measured stability. Lower N-halogen incidence coexists with higher O-halogen and peroxide incidence, so no global chemistry improvement follows. Sulfur-containing observations remain 1108 Child versus 1100 Parent; permitted local sulfur chemistry is not a whole-molecule plausibility guarantee. Synthetic plausibility is questionable and drug-likeness weak because recognizable medicinal motifs coexist with reactive local attachments, difficult ring geometry, tiny fragments and overgrown structures. All 15 Child and 15 authoritative published Parent trajectories were read completely. Each side has 900 records per objective, including 870 accepted optimizer observations; no path, task or paired seed is missing. All digest counters, counts, extreme scores and digest molecule/score/evaluation/source/seed tuples match the Child files. context.comparison has child_complete=true and paired_complete=true, matched seeds 0/1/2 and no profile mismatch. Full trajectories establish seed endpoints; digest final_molecules are late proposals, not incumbents. Parent baseline is n-1744a1494180 under the supplied Research in Depth epoch-1 profile, 300 observations including ten initial and announced batches of ten. The measured macro values are Child 0.4682702139687083 and Parent 0.59645311428869, with paired delta -0.12818290031998167. Chemistry differences are own-stream descriptive associations under divergent feedback histories, not selector activation, a selector constituent contribution, a sulfur contribution or chemical mediation. Unlabelled passive pool alternatives have no invented score or ancestry here. The frozen catalog composition_status=needs_review at v-17b4d64669a7955c8e61ca7e remains unresolved by this report; whole-foundation, constituent, joint-interaction, mediation, partial L07 composition and full-history-processing gaps remain separate. Prior transferable gaps retain their original n-c55c3d520a2c/n-62daf219c70a and n-1744a1494180 conditions, rather than becoming unconditional efficacy evidence. Complete paths, hashes, descriptor counts and cited example audits are in .slots/round-0027-slot-3/molecular/trajectory_chemistry_audit.json. All cited complete SMILES are digest or trusted Child-search molecules; Parent chemistry is described from its published trajectories and original report.

nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

approach.method_basis: The Parent searches from one scored current molecule. It samples local atom, bond, path and ring edits, including a direct exchange of aromatic nitrogen and carbon that preserves the molecular formula. After graph checks, identity normalization and duplicate rejection, it evaluates the first full batch allowed by short-term inverse-motif memory. The highest-scoring accepted neighbor becomes the next state even after a worsening move, and an independent archive keeps the best observation. Each selected transition installs a small, sign-balanced set of changed local motifs, ranked by whole-molecule count change and canonical description. A later neighbor is blocked when opposite inverse signs match the same stored transition.
approach.novelty: Prioritize memory for motifs rooted at the atoms and bond endpoints directly edited by the selected transition. A local motif can change merely because an adjacent atom's environment changed; the current count-based ranking can give that surrounding motif a scarce slot while omitting a motif at the actual edit site. The new ranking puts changes supported at those sites first, then uses the Parent's existing ordering. Earlier siblings changed count turnover, occurrence boundaries, ring annotations, score-based credit, matching coverage or overlap retention. None used the concrete edit's atom correspondence to allocate the existing memory slots.

nodes.hypothesis: Prioritize a selected transition's globally changed motifs whose signed occurrence changes are supported among the atoms and bond endpoints directly edited by that transition, using this binary site-support priority ahead of the Parent's existing rank within its unchanged bounded sign-balanced inverse-motif installation.

finding_summary.headline: Direct-site credit redirected 80 evaluations but slightly reduced the panel score
finding_summary.insights: Direct edit provenance can redirect scarce memory slots and real evaluations. The unresolved issue is whether the resulting motif restrictions protect useful search behavior. Of the 373 keys added by site priority, 230 later matched a fresh molecule and 60 participated in a bidirectional veto; 105 of the 314 that expired had never matched. Full-stream source improvements increased from 468 to 475 and archive improvements from 238 to 254, while their mean positive gains fell from 0.024350 to 0.022872 and from 0.019744 to 0.018437, respectively. More locally supported credit and more small improvements therefore did not establish the registered panel benefit. A newly admitted sulfur-free aryl-amine molecule reached the DRD2 maximum of 0.949238, showing that useful conventional chemistry was accessible. The records identify 590 later scored descendants of the 11 changed selected states, but they cannot assign those descendant scores to one credited motif or supply the missing scores and proposals of an alternative walk.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich molecules retain aromatic and polar frameworks, but unusual sulfur, reactive bonds and undefined stereochemistry persist
molecular.overall_character: All supplied tasks have trajectories. Each digest covers 900 recorded molecules, including 870 optimizer proposals. Every proposal set has ring_closure_rate 1.0 and branch_rate 1.0; aromatic-token occurrence rates, in the supplied task order, are 0.9609, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0 and 0.7747. These are fractions of SMILES containing those tokens, not fractions of aromatic atoms or proof of feasible ring geometry. The molecules span compact fused aromatic carboxamides, extensively decorated nitrogen heterocycles, aryl-linked amines, bridged lactams and sulfur-rich cages. There is real variation across replicas and tasks, but many high-scoring examples are close relatives within these families; molecular uniqueness does not establish broad scaffold exploration. Ordinary amides, ethers, aromatic heterocycles and amines coexist with heteroatom-halogen bonds, peroxide bonds, unusual sulfur coordination and highly constrained ring networks. No task has explicit charge or stereocentre tokens in optimizer proposals. Neutral SMILES can still contain basic amines; absent charge notation does not mean absent ionizability. The Parent comparison shows changes within these families and a notable sulfur-free aryl-amine maximum, without a general resolution of synthetic plausibility. Sizes and structural descriptions below come from passive parsing of the supplied trajectories; scores are recorded observations, not new calculations. The supporting audit, including input hashes and perceived structural descriptors, is .slots/SPIRAL2.r0011-07-improve-L16.molecular-audit.json. Parsing and ring perception do not establish synthesis, stability, binding or realizable stereochemistry.

per_task.generated_character: The optimizer proposals have 21-29 heavy atoms and mean SMILES length 46.4. Much of the chemistry retains an indole, benzofuran or benzothiophene-like framework connected through a carbonyl to a second aromatic ring, with alkoxy, methyl, amino, hydroxymethyl, thiol and halogen substituents. The ethoxy/methyl/thiol indole carboxanilide at 0.39905049777278273 has a recognizable synthetic framework. The maximum at 0.41003927643747895 is instead a benzofuran carboxamide carrying an N-chloro amide, an aminophenyl group, a thiol and an amino/chloro carbon. Other high observations and the final digest include bridged, partly unsaturated ring systems. The Parent has the same maxima in seeds 1 and 2; seed 0 changes from an aromatic sulfur-ring ketone at 0.393567030299894 to the bridged sulfur-containing ketone at 0.40196779766986834. The chemistry remains aromatic/carbonyl-centered, with substantial variation in ring feasibility and substituent reactivity.
liabilities: N-chloro amides, N-fluoro groups in low-scoring descendants, thiols and benzylic halides introduce reactivity concerns beyond the ordinary aromatic/carbonyl framework.
Dense closures and partially dearomatized enlarged rings create uncertain geometry and demanding synthesis; successful parsing is insufficient evidence of accessibility.
missing_features: Coverage of conventional matched carbonyl linkers and substituent patterns remains incomplete around the retained aromatic frameworks; the strong ordinary amide shows that reactive amide chlorination is not required for a high observation.
The bridged and amino/halogen-substituted products lack specified stereochemical identities. The trajectories do not show which configurations, if any, preserve the favorable arrangement.
No unseen optimal scaffold or exact missing target feature can be inferred from these comparisons alone.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxy indole carboxanilide scores 0.3051048083696145, whereas the ethoxy/methyl/thiol analogue reaches 0.39905049777278273. The enlarged, partly dearomatized nitrogen-ring example scores 0.03167521481852009. Together these observations support preserving a compact aromatic-carbonyl arrangement while varying substituent placement; they do not isolate any one substituent as causal. The conventional amide already approaches the N-chloro maximum, so these observations do not establish a need for the reactive N-Cl bond. transferable_gaps.evidence: A sulfur-centered connection and its carbon analogue both score 0.9341451805829589, and a sulfur-free aryl-amine structure reaches 0.9492384404345239. An ordinary indole carboxamide reaches 0.39905049777278273 near an N-chloro carboxamide at 0.41003927643747895. transferable_gaps.gap: The generator reaches useful aromatic and polar arrangements without consistently supplying conventional matched alternatives to unusual sulfur and reactive heteroatom connections.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Broaden graph-local access to matched conventional connections while retaining the surrounding attachment arrangement. Compare actual feedback for those alternatives; the generator should not require unusual sulfur, peroxide or heteroatom-halogen bonds to reach nearby configurations of its useful fragments. This is an accessibility gap, not evidence for a universal sulfur ban or an unobserved score benefit.

transferable_gaps.evidence: An aromatic amide series reaches 0.39905049777278273 while a related carbonyl-deleted connection scores 0.03343008011310944. Ring-opened carbonyl-chain examples score 0.12467972074136988 and 0.1263981386214515 below constrained aromatic/carbonyl examples. A methylene-linked amine/sulfur-ring structure scores 0.9441493227693659, whereas its direct-link analogue scores 0.907358519207774. All proposal sets already have ring_closure_rate 1.0.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently retain useful aromaticity, carbonyl placement and amine spacing when it changes ring or linker topology.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide coherent matched ring and linker alternatives that preserve other observed useful connections while testing one geometric or attachment change. Access to feasible topology matters more than simply adding rings; local score comparisons should determine which arrangements to retain.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Several variants differing in alkyl extension, chain branching and terminal unsaturation share 0.6155070237050044. Other side-chain and ether/thioether variants share 0.6161710037174721. The most decorated maximum has 54 heavy atoms, long oxygen/sulfur chains and densely substituted aromatic groups. These ties do not show that the additional flexible appendages are necessary.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator incompletely explores simpler members of score-indistinguishable decoration families.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Include matched shortening and simplification moves around an already scored framework, with preserved core attachments and feedback-based comparison. The missing capability is reliable access to simpler nearby structures; the evidence does not establish that smaller molecules will always score better.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every task has stereocentre-token rate 0.0. The supplied high molecules include substituted saturated nitrogen rings, amino/halogen-bearing carbons, bridged lactams and densely fused sulfur cages. Some high variants have the same elemental formula but different bond placement and recorded scores.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator leaves stereochemical identity and geometric feasibility unresolved for constrained and substituted products.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Represent and preserve feasible configurations when structural changes create or alter stereogenic relationships, and retain access to less strained topology alternatives. Do not equate a valid SMILES or a perceived ring with a realizable three-dimensional molecule. No benefit from a particular configuration is established by the current unassigned examples.

nodes.method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
nodes.method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.

Direct neutral aromatic C-H/pyridine-like N exchange within a perceived aromatic six-member ring, appended at both sites to the inherited change_atom menu, preserving formula and the full attachment framework

Binary direct-edit-root support from exact selected-edit replay and temporary atom correspondence on copies, prioritized before the original bounded sign-balanced inverse-motif ranking, with explicit legacy fallback and descriptive support provenance

approach.method_basis: The reference is MolDQN, published by Zhou and colleagues, which applies value-based reinforcement learning directly to molecular graphs, with no generative model in between. It starts from a molecule that already has a real score and then runs a short episode of single edits: add or remove an atom, add or remove a bond, change a bond order, always within what valence allows. At each step it draws a bounded set of legal successor molecules and asks a small neural network which one is worth taking, where the network is given fingerprints of the current molecule and the candidate, how many edits are left in the episode, and the best score the episode has seen so far. Selection is epsilon-greedy, so most of the time it takes the network's favourite and occasionally it takes a random legal edit. The reward is not the new molecule's score but the amount by which that score raises the episode's running best, so an edit that makes things worse earns nothing and is still taken as the next state to build from. That is the point of the method: a molecule can be walked downhill deliberately if the network expects a payoff a few edits later. Because there is no discounting and rewards are increments of a running maximum, an episode's total return is exactly the improvement it achieved. The network learns by double Q-learning from a replay buffer of edits that actually received oracle scores: an online network picks the best continuation from the successor state, a lagged copy of that network supplies its value, and the difference between that target and the online prediction drives the update.
approach.novelty: The commitments this root makes go well beyond the method statement. The reward definition is the largest: rewarding the increment to the episode's running best, undiscounted, is an adaptation chosen so that the quantity the agent maximises telescopes into exactly the best-score improvement the benchmark cares about, rather than the original formulation's terminal-property reward. Episodes are deliberately short, six edits, with ten independent lanes interleaved so that each ten-proposal batch contains exactly one pending action per lane and no lane ever influences another mid-batch. Candidate actions are drawn fresh every time, forty at each decision and eight for each replay continuation, and crucially the continuations used to form learning targets are re-sampled at training time rather than stored, so the action set is never allowed to harden into a fixed candidate library. Value predictions for candidates that were not selected stay predictions: only edits the oracle actually scored enter replay, and a rejected action leaves the lane's state and remaining depth untouched. The root uses one Q-head with a declared epsilon schedule falling from 0.4 toward roughly 0.16, explicitly no ensemble and no episode-fixed randomised value function, so that any exploration benefit later observed can be attributed. Each objective restarts weights, target copy, optimizer, replay and archive from nothing, and preparation stores no learned artifact and no molecule pool at all.

nodes.hypothesis: Select fresh molecular graph edits with a single epsilon-greedy continuation-value network, advance persistent finite-horizon episodes through every matched accepted successor, and learn from accepted transitions using undiscounted episode-best improvement rewards and double-Q Bellman backups through a lagged target network.

finding_summary.headline: Graph-edit Q-learning activated in full but scored 0.4067, eighth of thirteen Discovery roots
finding_summary.insights: The campaign now has a clean answer to a question it could not previously separate: correct temporal-credit machinery is not by itself worth a score. Every part of the Bellman construction was audited and held, including the exact double-Q target, the detached lagged network, reward telescoping, and the use of updated weights in subsequent decisions, and the result still lands in the lower half of the roots and below the frozen-latent swarm root that carries no learning at all. Two mechanisms explain that. The learning signal is thin, because four fifths of transitions carry zero reward under a running-best definition, so most gradient comes from the zero mass and the mean continuation term of 0.014 sits at the same scale as the residual error the network still has, which is also why nearly three thousand continuation values came out negative when the true quantity cannot be. And the search collapses: the molecules produced show that exploitation, once it finds a good core, spends its remaining budget swapping single atoms on that core, which is precisely the behaviour a value function would need a long-horizon reason to escape. For method choice this argues that direct graph editing is the right way to stay in makeable chemistry, but that pairing it with a value-learning controller adds machinery whose payoff is not visible at this feedback scale; the effort is better spent on the exploration and diversity side than on the credit-assignment side. Still open: this is a single seed with no parent and no paired comparison, so the ranking is indicative; the 216 recovered-loss links and 123 later episode-best gains after temporary losses are descriptive and do not isolate learned lookahead from ordinary hill-climbing; and whether episode-consistent randomised exploration would change the picture was deliberately left untested here.
finding_summary.results: One screening seed, macro mean 0.406692671573943, eighth among the campaign's thirteen Discovery roots on a spread running 0.2331 to 0.5103. Per objective the means were 0.7536466193285815 on the docking task, 0.6145349727054742 on the decoration-hop task, 0.33218372414937963 on the zaleplon task, 0.19512536527753646 on the median task and 0.13797267640874414 on the sitagliptin task. Every registered observable moved as intended. The graph sampler filled all 1450 acting neighbourhoods with 40 valid novel candidates each and all 20215 replay continuation neighbourhoods with eight, emitting exactly 29 batches of ten unique molecules per objective with zero invalid, duplicate or rejected proposals; an independent re-execution of 17026 distinct edit receipts reproduced every one. The temporal machinery worked: 250 episode starts, 1200 multistep continuations, and 800 accepted transitions that strictly lowered the score yet still advanced their lane, of which 666 went on to be the source of a later edit. Reward telescoping held to a maximum residual of 5.551115123125783e-17 with gamma exactly one. Of 22900 replay targets, 2685 were horizon terminals equal to reward and all 20215 nonterminal continuation terms were nonzero, mean 0.013847408184662015, so the targets genuinely differed from reward-only regression. Learning registered: mean paired Huber loss fell from 6.10635587187527e-05 to 5.3964929417511364e-05 and mean absolute temporal-difference error from 0.004401601105964189 to 0.004148056249060887, decreasing on every objective, with 1242 of 1450 individual steps improving. The learned values then drove behaviour: 1095 exploitation choices against 355 random ones, every neighbourhood showing nonconstant values, and a fixed sixteen-candidate diagnostic probe changing its preferred molecule 30 times over training. The counterweight is the sparsity of signal: 1179 of 1450 accepted transitions carried zero reward, only 271 were positive, and 2880 of the sampled continuations were predicted negative even though a true remaining episode-best gain can never be below zero.

molecular.headline: Drug-like fused aromatic scaffolds inherited from the seeds, decorated with impossible bonds and collapsed onto one core per objective
molecular.overall_character: Because every molecule is one legal edit away from a molecule that was already there, this node's output looks far more like real medicinal chemistry than a decoder's would. Ring closures appear in 99 to 100 percent of emitted molecules and aromatic atoms in 94 to 100 percent; the sets are full of genuine fused heterocycles, indoles, coumarins, xanthines, benzodioxoles and aminopyridines, carrying amides, sulfonamides and basic amines at sensible positions. The two problems are structural rather than cosmetic. First, the edit operators are constrained only by valence and connectivity, so they cheerfully form bonds that no chemist would draw: oxygen-fluorine, oxygen-chlorine and oxygen-bromine hypohalites, nitrogen-sulfur and nitrogen-chlorine bonds on imide nitrogens, NON(O)O chains, peroxides, hemiaminals, and three-membered oxygen rings fused straight onto an arene. Second, the search converges hard: within any objective the twelve highest-scoring molecules are one- and two-atom variants of a single core, several sharing scores to four decimal places, so what reads as optimisation is largely relabelling. Stereochemistry is absent everywhere and no molecule carries a formal charge.

per_task.generated_character: Two families only. One is a methoxy- or ethoxy-substituted fused indole bearing a carbinolamine and an N-linked fluorinated bicycle, repeated with single-atom substitutions across almost the entire best list. The other is the supplied dimethoxyindole carboxamide with one atom changed. Ring closure and aromatic rates are both at or near 1.0, and the halogen rate of 0.86 comes almost entirely from a single inherited aryl fluoride.
liabilities: carbinolamine and aminal centres of the C(O)N type, which are hydrolytically unstable
sulfur attached directly to an amide or ring nitrogen as a bare SH
a bridged bicyclic alkene written across ring-closure pairs that would be anti-Bredt
a cumulated allene fragment surviving in the low-scoring set
missing_features: no pyrazolopyrimidine or comparable fused bicyclic nitrogen core is ever constructed
no nitrile group appears despite it being a common feature of this chemotype
no N,N-dialkyl acetamide is built onto the aryl ring
no stereochemistry on the sp3 carbinolamine centre the scaffold creates
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The top eleven molecules occupy a band from 0.317 to 0.332 and differ from each other by a methyl versus ethyl, a hydroxyl versus methoxy, or the position of one substituent, so score is essentially flat across the whole exploited core. The zero-scoring tail is composed entirely of the supplied starting molecules and their immediate first edits, which means the improvement came in one jump and was then elaborated rather than extended.

per_task.generated_character: A single scaffold, elaborated exhaustively: a methoxy-substituted coumarin or benzoxazinone fused to a three-membered oxygen ring, bearing an aminopyridine that in turn carries a second heteroaryl with sulfur and oxygen substituents. Aromatic atoms appear in 100 percent of molecules and rings in 100 percent, and the mean length of 56 characters is stable across the run, which is what a converged edit search looks like.
liabilities: sulfenic acid substituents written as SO and OS directly on an aromatic ring
a three-membered oxygen ring fused across two adjacent aromatic carbons, an arene oxide
an NON(O)O chain built onto a fused heteroaromatic
an O-bromo substituent on a lactone carbon, which is a hypobromite
missing_features: no sulfonamide is ever formed, only lower sulfur oxidation states
no saturated ring is added anywhere on the periphery
no basic amine or other solubilising handle is introduced
no stereochemistry, even where the fused three-membered ring creates defined faces
per_task.score_gradient_reading: All twelve best molecules fall between 0.594 and 0.615, separated only by whether a given position carries SO, OS, O, S, Br or SC, and by whether the fused ring is a five- or six-membered lactone. The worst molecules, at 0.52 to 0.53, are the supplied starting molecules with a single atom changed. The objective evidently rewards the scaffold much more than the decoration, and the search extracted that in the first few batches and then plateaued.

per_task.generated_character: The most convincing output of the run and the longest, averaging 72 SMILES characters. Almost every high scorer is a dichlorophenyl sulfur group on a methylated diazepane or piperazine, connected through a benzylic tertiary amine to a pyridine bearing a fluorophenol and an acetic acid arm. These are recognisable ligand-shaped molecules assembled by editing the supplied sulfonamide reference, with a halogen rate of 0.92.
liabilities: a sulfilimine-oxide written as C=S(=O)(N), which is not a preparable functional group
an aryl hypofluorite O-F substituent standing in for a fluorine
an S-chloro substituent on an aromatic ring
an aminal nitrogen placed alpha to a ring nitrogen in the diamine
missing_features: the inherited sulfonamide is never rebuilt at full oxidation state once degraded
no stereochemistry on either the benzylic or the ring sp3 centre, both of which a real ligand would define
no alternative aromatic core is ever explored beyond the one inherited from the seed
no amide linker is offered as a replacement for the sulfur-nitrogen hinge
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Score tracks how much of that assembled pharmacophore survives. The 0.65 to 0.75 band keeps all four pieces, the dichloroaryl sulfur, the cyclic diamine, the basic benzylic amine and the fluorophenol-pyridine; the 0.23 to 0.46 band loses one, usually by swapping a hydroxyl onto the dichloroaryl or replacing fluorine with an O-F. The near-zero tail is small aziridine and bromoalkane fragments produced early before the core was found.

per_task.generated_character: One core and nothing else: an N,N-dimethyl xanthine fused to a benzofuran, carrying an alkoxyphenyl on the ring-fusion nitrogen. Every one of the twelve best molecules is that scaffold with one substituent moved or relabelled, and the aromatic and ring rates are both exactly 1.0. It is inherited almost intact from the strongest supplied starting molecule.
liabilities: an N-chloro imide nitrogen, which is an oxidising and unstable group
a peroxide written into an alkoxy substituent as CCOOC
an ynol ether, an alkyne bonded directly to an aromatic oxygen
an epoxide appended by atom insertion onto a heteroaromatic ring
missing_features: no scaffold departure at all from the inherited xanthine-benzofuran system
no aliphatic or saturated ring is ever introduced into the molecule
no ionisable acid or base handle is added anywhere
no stereochemistry, though several edits create sp3 ring carbons
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best band spans 0.189 to 0.195, a range of six thousandths across twelve molecules, and the two top entries share the same score to six decimal places while differing by an ether position. The worst molecules at 0.106 to 0.117 are edits of the other supplied starting molecules that never reached this core. So the entire gain over the supplied incumbent of 0.168 is a small decoration effect on a scaffold the search was handed rather than found.

per_task.generated_character: The node's weakest objective. Output is a single purinone or pyrazolo-fused bicyclic core carrying two aryl rings, a fluorine on one of them, a hydroxymethyl on the imide nitrogen and a bare sulfur on the ring nitrogen, repeated with tiny variations. Aromatic atoms are present in 94 percent of molecules and rings in 100 percent, so this is a flat, fully unsaturated set.
liabilities: a bare SH substituent on an imide nitrogen, which is a sulfenamide with no stability
N-hydroxymethyl hemiaminal groups on both imide nitrogens
a benzylic hypofluorite written as COF on an aromatic ring
a thiocarboxylic acid formed by substituting sulfur into a carboxyl
missing_features: no trifluoromethyl group is ever assembled, only single fluorine substituents
no saturated fused ring or piperazine-like system is constructed
no primary aliphatic amine beta to a carbonyl
no defined stereochemistry, which for a target defined by one configuration caps the score outright
no polyfluorinated aromatic ring
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Scores are compressed between 0.110 and 0.138, with five of the twelve best sharing 0.115357 exactly while differing only in where the fluorine and hydroxymethyl sit on their respective rings. The zero tail is edits of the supplied starting molecules. There is no readable gradient here at all: the search found one core early, and moving substituents around it changes almost nothing.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Emitted molecules carry oxygen-fluorine, oxygen-chlorine and oxygen-bromine bonds (OF, OCl, OBr substituents), nitrogen-sulfur and nitrogen-chlorine bonds on imide nitrogens, NON(O)O chains, and a sulfilimine-oxide written C=S(=O)(N). Every one of these passed sanitisation, reparsing and an independent structural re-execution.
transferable_gaps.gap: Edit operators form element pairings that valence permits but chemistry forbids
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Legality checks on valence and connectivity are not sufficient to keep a graph editor inside makeable chemistry. The proposal step needs an element-pair and functional-group context filter, so that a heteroatom-heteroatom bond is only formed where such a bond is actually known, applied before a molecule consumes an oracle call.

transferable_gaps.evidence: In every objective the twelve highest-scoring molecules are one- or two-atom variants of a single fused scaffold, with score bands as narrow as six thousandths across all twelve, and five molecules in one set sharing an identical score to six decimal places. Late-run output is indistinguishable from mid-run output apart from substituent position.
transferable_gaps.gap: The search collapses onto one core and then relabels single atoms
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Sampling a local neighbourhood and taking its best member cannot leave a basin once it is in one, no matter how good the value estimate is, because every legal move is one atom wide. A generator needs a scaffold-level move, an explicit novelty or diversity pressure across lanes, or forced restarts from unrelated regions, or it will spend the majority of its budget confirming a structure it already has.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Sulfonamides present in the starting molecules are degraded to sulfinamides and then to sulfilimine-oxide forms, and sulfur substituents appear across the range from thioether to sulfenic acid within a single best list, purely as the by-product of adding and deleting oxygen atoms.
transferable_gaps.gap: Functional-group oxidation state is edited as if it were a free variable
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Treating a functional group as an arbitrary collection of atoms lets the editor wander through oxidation states that are not isolable. Groups should be manipulated as units with a declared set of allowed states, so that an oxygen deletion either produces a real lower oxidation state or is not offered at all.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Ring-closure rates of 0.99 to 1.00 sit alongside aromatic-atom rates of 0.94 to 1.00, and no emitted molecule introduces a new aliphatic ring: rings that appear are either inherited flat heteroaromatics or accidental three-membered oxygen rings fused onto an arene.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator builds no saturated or three-dimensional structure
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Atom and bond edits on an aromatic template can decorate but cannot saturate, so the whole sp3-rich half of drug-like space is unreachable. Ring-forming operators that close aliphatic rings, and operators that reduce aromatic systems, are needed for a generator to explore three-dimensional shape.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The stereocentre rate is exactly 0.0 across every emitted molecule, including the many products bearing sp3 ring carbons with four distinct substituents and the benzylic amine centres the operators construct.
transferable_gaps.gap: No stereochemistry is set even where the edits create defined centres
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: An edit vocabulary that changes atoms and bonds but never sets configuration cannot address any property that depends on it, and worse, it silently produces racemic answers to questions whose answer is a single enantiomer. Stereo-setting operators and stereo-aware features are a prerequisite, not a refinement.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Inserting a single oxygen produced peroxides such as the CCOOC ether chain, inserting oxygen next to nitrogen produced carbinolamine and hemiaminal centres of the C(O)N type, and inserting carbon next to an aromatic oxygen produced an ynol ether. None of these were rejected.
transferable_gaps.gap: Atom insertion creates unstable linkages as an unnoticed by-product
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Single-atom insertion is the operator most likely to build a group nobody intended, because the atom lands between two existing heteroatoms. A proposal-time substructure blocklist covering peroxides, hemiaminals, strained fused small rings and heteroatom-heteroatom chains would remove most of this class at no cost to reach.

nodes.method_name: MolDQN: Bellman-guided de novo graph-edit episodes
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in MolDQN's value-based control of molecular edits: learn future action returns from scored transitions and choose subsequent graph modifications with a deep Q-network. [Zhou et al., Sections 2.1, 2.2 and 2.5](https://arxiv.org/html/1810.08678v3) describe finite molecular edit episodes, fingerprint features and double Q-learning. Our adaptation starts short episodes from task-local scored molecules and samples fresh valence-aware atom and bond edits at each state. A compact Q-network takes current and successor fingerprints, remaining episode depth and the episode's best observed score. Use a single Q-function with epsilon-greedy action selection in the root. Evaluate only selected new whole molecules; values assigned to unselected successors are predictions. Advance each trajectory after its matched feedback, even when the new molecule scores worse. For Top-1 alignment, use reward max(previous_episode_best, new_score) minus previous_episode_best and undiscounted finite-horizon backups: accumulated reward equals improvement in that episode's best score. This reward adaptation is our inference, not the paper's original reward. Train immediately from accepted transition replay using double-Q target selection and a lagged target network, with zero continuation value at episode termination. Retain all accepted intermediate molecules in the task incumbent archive. Interleave episodes according to announced batches, and generate further edits to replace invalid or duplicate proposals. Each decision samples an evolving neighborhood; no corpus pool, complete-molecule retrieval or fixed candidate enumeration is involved. No pretrained generator or external labels are required, and every objective starts with clean learning state. The hypothesis is that learned lookahead identifies useful edit sequences, including temporary score losses, quickly enough to raise the mean of independent final Top-1 scores. Learning useful continuation values from scarce transitions is unproven; the paper's much larger training regime does not establish this transfer.

approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from a bounded population of accepted high-scoring molecules. It samples breeding parents by score band, recombines connected fragments and applies local graph mutations. Its retained special move exchanges a nitrogen and a carbon within one aromatic six-member ring, preserving formula and connectivity while changing nitrogen placement. Stable identity admission forms a fresh surplus pool. A Gaussian process trained on all earlier accepted scores uses counts of local molecular environments and generalized Tanimoto similarity; correlated score draws choose which pool members receive evaluations. Accepted offspring update both the prediction archive and the breeding population.
approach.novelty: Remove only the direct aromatic nitrogen-position exchange from the atom-replacement menu and measure its contribution to the complete feedback loop. The ordinary element substitutions, crossover, other mutations and count-based posterior remain. Earlier evidence established useful positional edits before the posterior learned environment counts, and a later integration sibling removed crossover. None of the supplied siblings isolates whether this particular two-atom move still adds useful search paths under the retained count-based selector. Because some current exchange products improve incumbents and later breed, the registered prediction is a score decrease when the move is removed. The experiment tests that contribution rather than assuming sparse use makes the move dispensable.

nodes.hypothesis: Remove the direct formula-preserving aromatic C/N positional-exchange options from the inherited atom-replacement menu, leaving only its original single-atom element substitutions while retaining all other graph, feedback and posterior mechanisms.

finding_summary.headline: The same-code baseline reproduces all trajectories and the 0.595670 mean
finding_summary.insights: The campaign now has a complete baseline under the opening Research in Depth profile, with the exchange-free implementation and its feedback chain verified. Repeating the same seeds reproduced the same search histories; this adds execution and profile-baseline evidence without adding independent search trajectories or isolating any retained component’s value. The earlier finding that removing direct exchanges improved the mean remains a historical counterexample to the predicted loss, and is not retested here. The chemistry also reproduces the earlier limits: useful aromatic/carbonyl and aryl-amine arrangements coexist with reactive heteroatom–halogen bonds, doubtful ring geometry and unspecified stereochemistry. Those liabilities and uneven task dispersion persist at the reproduced score. Current-profile component interventions are still needed to determine which retained mechanisms support that score and whether useful chemistry can be preserved while improving reliability.
finding_summary.results: All fifteen task runs completed. Final Top-1 macro mean was 0.595670, with seed population SD 0.026593; the three seed macros were 0.625412, 0.560866 and 0.600731. Every endpoint and every molecular trajectory reproduced the historical Anchor. Direct exchanges remained absent despite 904 eligible selected-site menus with 1,276 withheld partners. Accepted-only learning, crossover and correlated posterior selection all executed. The 4,350 accepted offspring produced 629 best-parent beats, 258 incumbent improvements and 2,401 later-used breeding molecules, exactly as before. The historical seeds are all profile-mismatched, so the protocol provides no paired effect estimate.

nodes.finding:
