molecular.headline: The baseline reproduces aromatic heterocycles and aryl amines, including reactive halogen bonds and doubtful ring geometry
molecular.overall_character: This is the same-code profile baseline of Parent n-c55c3d520a2c, not a new chemical intervention. All supplied current and published Parent trajectory paths were present and read. Across all fifteen task/seed files, evaluation, source, SMILES, score and best_so_far records are identical to the Parent. The brief reports child_complete=true but paired_complete=false, no matched seeds, and profile-mismatched Parent seeds 0, 1 and 2. Thus the available historical chemistry comparison is exact reproduction; it is not a complete profile-matched Parent comparison, an independent chemistry sample, or evidence for any component contribution. The gaps below retain their original source in n-c55c3d520a2c and are re-observed in this baseline under its supplied Search Seeds and frozen profile. All five tasks are covered, each with 900 trajectory records and 870 optimizer proposals; no task lacks trajectories. The output comprises substituted indole amides and diketones, linked fused nitrogen heterocycles, flexible and cyclic aryl amines, bridged nitrogen-carbonyl systems, and fluorinated imino/carbonyl heterocycles. Ring-closure-string rates are 0.9632 to 0.9828 and aromatic-string rates are 0.954 to 0.9736. These are molecule-level incidences of text features, not perceived ring counts or aromatic-atom fractions. Formal-charge and stereocentre-string rates are 0.0 throughout, although protonatable aliphatic amines and potentially stereogenic saturated centres are visibly present. Ring chemistry and aromaticity are rich, but synthetic plausibility remains questionable and overall drug-likeness weak because recognizable functional groups coexist with N-halogen and O-F bonds, peroxides, problematic cyclic unsaturation and difficult bridges. Structural diversity is moderate across seeds and tasks, with much narrower families among leaders within a seed; distinct SMILES alone do not establish independent scaffold coverage. Sizes below count heavy-atom tokens in the cited trajectory SMILES; SMILES lengths are the supplied digest counters. Neither those readings nor the supplied scores establish synthesis, stability, protonation, conformation or biological activity. The digest final_molecules are late seed-2 proposals, not the best retained molecule of every seed; the full trajectories were used to inspect other seed endpoints.

per_task.generated_character: The leading seed-1 molecule has 25 heavy atoms: an ethyl/dimethyl/chloro-substituted indole linked through an N-hydroxy amide to a pyridyl ring, with fluorine attached to the indole nitrogen. Nearby leaders keep the fused aromatic/amide/azaaryl organization while changing N-S, N-halogen or halomethyl substituents. Seed 2 develops an indole-aryl vicinal-diketone family with aminomethyl substitution; seed 0 also reaches an amino-substituted cumulene attached to a fused aromatic system. Mean proposal SMILES length is 42.1 and halogen-string incidence is 0.8805. These are mostly compact aromatic frameworks rather than ring-deficient fragments, but their local nitrogen and halogen environments make apparently familiar skeletons questionable synthetic targets. The same families and exact scores occur in the published Parent.
liabilities: Leading N-F, N-Cl and N-Br attachments to indole nitrogen are chemically different from ordinary carbon-bound aromatic halogens; N-S substitution and halomethyl ethers also raise local reactivity concerns.
The N-hydroxy amide is a recognizable functional group but does not resolve the separate N-halogen liability on its scaffold.
The vicinal-dicarbonyl family has potentially reactive carbonyl chemistry, while the seed-0 leader contains a cumulated-double-bond segment; the scores do not demonstrate their stability.
missing_features: The leading examples do not establish conventional stable nitrogen substitution that preserves the favorable aromatic/carbonyl/azaaryl arrangement at the same score; an ordinary N-H indole amide is already present initially, so the generator is not incapable of that chemistry.
Chemically independent compact frameworks expressing the favorable functional-group arrangement are scarce among the leading examples; most vary substitutions on retained aromatic families.
The observed score ordering does not identify an exact missing pharmacophore, and does not establish that adding more donors, rings or halogens would help.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxyindole anilide scores 0.3051048083696145, while the N-hydroxy pyridyl-amide leader reaches 0.47411701813450596. Retaining only an N-fluoro amide on the trimethoxyindole, without its pendant aryl group, gives 0.0038788336708218928; ClCl reaches 0.0. The visible positive association therefore concerns the combined compact aromatic and carbonyl organization, not halogen presence alone. Two N-halogen/halomethyl variants share 0.4478476056206344 despite different peripheral placements. The seed-2 diketone leader scores 0.438972502037081, whereas a more substituted late relative scores 0.2537139094300773; extra polar substitution is not uniformly rewarded. The seed-0 cumulene leader scores 0.39405142067435733. These comparisons do not isolate a required reactive bond or an absent target-specific motif.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-0 leader has 30 heavy atoms and links a quinazoline-like fused aromatic region to a dense nitrogen-rich fused/bridged carbonyl-thione core. It bears aryl chlorine, an O-F group, and a fluorinated chloromethyl-ether side chain. An analogue replaces that side chain with difluoromethyl. Seed 1 favors linked aza-aromatic and oxygen-containing carbonyl rings with a carbon-linked nitrile and an O-linked cyanate. Seed 2 instead reaches aryl/heteroaryl assemblies bearing peroxide, nitrite and N=S functionalities. Mean proposal SMILES length is 59.1, with a maximum of 191, so compact leaders coexist with much larger proposals. The recognizable fused heterocycles do not make their reactive attachments or dense ring junctions synthetically routine. These are the same output families as the Parent, with no baseline-specific change in size or chemistry.
liabilities: The leader contains an aryl O-F bond, not an aryl C-F bond, and a chloromethyl ether; these require a different reactivity assessment from ordinary aromatic halogen substitution.
Thione functionality and crowded nitrogen-ring connectivity coexist with unspecified stereochemical possibilities; a graph and score do not establish a synthetic route.

Other high-scoring seed families retain O-linked cyanates, peroxide links, nitrite and N=S groups. These are specific local chemistry concerns, not proof that all heterocycles or nitriles are undesirable.
missing_features: Stable peripheral alternatives that preserve the favorable linked heterocyclic arrangement are not established among the best examples; local substituent ties leave room for alternatives without identifying one as better.
The dense fused/bridged core lacks demonstrated accessible geometry and stereochemical identity; higher ring count alone does not recover the favorable arrangement.

The compact leading family appears in one seed while other seeds retain different reactive families; the observed record does not demonstrate reliable coverage of that favorable chemical organization across seeds.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted fused dione scores 0.548381482770623, a smaller nitrogen-carbonyl ring fragment scores 0.5093370681605975, and ethene sits at 0.5. The linked nitrogen-rich leader and its difluoromethyl analogue both reach 0.8561477222467935. A nearby connectivity variant reaches 0.8467276542724114, while the more extensively cross-linked final seed-0 structure falls to 0.564499484004128. This favors a particular combined heterocyclic arrangement in this sample, rather than simply adding rings, atoms or fluorine. Other seed leaders reach 0.6248206599713055 and 0.6178024026512013 in different families. The tied peripheral variants do not show that an O-F bond is required, and the floor score should not be interpreted as evidence of useful chemistry.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-0 leader is a 30-heavy-atom flexible tertiary amine connecting aromatic regions through alkyl chains, with phenol, methoxy, ethyl and propyl groups, a benzylic chloride and aromatic bromines. Seed 2 produces recognizable pyrrolidine-substituted dihydrobenzothiophene/biaryl frameworks with phenol or thiol and carbon-bound fluorine. Seed 1 favors an aminoethyl-substituted pyrrolidine attached to a fluorinated cyclic aryl-ether region with another aminomethyl group. Mean proposal SMILES length is 53.8 and halogen-string incidence is 0.9851. Accessible aliphatic amines and substantial aromatic surface are already present. These frameworks offer more recognizable synthetic handles than several other leading families, but heavy halogen substitution, flexible chains and unassigned stereochemistry remain concerns. The Parent contains the identical examples.
liabilities: The flexible leader combines a potentially reactive benzylic chloride with substantial bromine/chlorine mass and long hydrophobic alkyl segments; solubility, stability and selectivity are not characterized.
Some near-leading relatives introduce large ring closures or a cyclic cumulated-double-bond segment, whose feasibility is not established by their high scores.
The pyrrolidine and fused thioether skeletons are recognizable, but their unspecified stereochemistry prevents a fully defined molecular identity.
missing_features: Stereochemically specified forms of the successful saturated-ring and benzylic arrangements are absent, despite visible potential stereogenic centres.
A comparably evaluated stable replacement for the leading benzylic chloride is not established at its exact score; other high-scoring cyclic-amine families show that this liability is not universal.

Protonation states are not explicitly resolved in the neutral SMILES, but a lack of formal charge does not imply a lack of basic centres. The chemistry does not support a recommendation simply to add an amine.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: An N-sulfonyl cyclic amine scores 0.00021169315013374197; the flexible tertiary amine reaches 0.9999989177995104 and the fused-thioether/pyrrolidine analogue 0.9999934235240012. A further aminoalkyl cyclic-amine leader reaches 0.9969753164881906. The visible association is the presentation of available aliphatic amines together with aromatic regions, rather than nitrogen or halogen count alone. A smaller final fused-thioether amine still scores 0.9947190867301007, so all aromatic appendages and maximal size are not required in this record. Flexible, cyclic and even cyclic-cumulene variants can approach the score ceiling. These are supplied oracle scores, not measurements of affinity, selectivity or geometric accessibility.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-2 leader has 29 heavy atoms and joins a propyl-substituted quinoline to a partially unsaturated, bridged nitrogen/oxygen ring system with N-methyl groups and carbonyls. Seed 1 uses related quinoline-linked amino/ether rings and dicarbonyl nitrogen rings; seed 0 reaches a densely bridged diaryl lactam containing an N-O bridge. Thus aromatic surfaces, saturated nitrogen centres and carbonyl acceptors are all represented. Mean proposal SMILES length is 52.6 and halogen-string incidence is 0.1241, much lower than in the other supplied families. Recognizable functional groups coexist with medium-ring bridges and difficult connectivity, so atom-count compactness alone does not establish an accessible synthesis. The same structures and gradients are already present in the Parent.
liabilities: Medium-ring closures, bridges and ring-bound unsaturation create synthesis and geometry questions despite moderate heavy-atom counts.

The diaryl leader contains an N-O bridge, and nearby variants introduce further N-O or N-N functionality; these require environment-specific assessment rather than treating all nitrogen substitutions as equivalent.
Stereocentre-string incidence is 0.0, so potential stereogenic saturated centres in these connected ring systems remain unspecified.
missing_features: The leading families do not demonstrate simpler, accessible connectivities that preserve the favorable arrangement of aromatic, nitrogen and carbonyl regions at the same score.
Stereochemical and conformational identity of the saturated bridges and medium rings is unresolved.
Chemically independent alternatives are limited among leaders within each seed, although the different seed families prevent a claim of total scaffold collapse.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted fused dione scores 0.1678386594791329 and the leading quinoline/bridged-dicarbonyl structure reaches 0.22600312875247064. Extending its oxygen-containing ring segment gives 0.2243673789386108; a corresponding carbon-containing segment gives 0.22237557923837944. A different diaryl bridged lactam reaches 0.2258403994203931. These nearby values associate reward with the combined aromatic and nitrogen-carbonyl organization more than with a unique local atom. Methane scores 0.0. The final seed-2 bridged relative scores 0.20735848908965118, while its retained incumbent remains higher. The record supplies no exact missing target motif and no evidence that increasing general ring or heteroatom richness will solve the remaining gap.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-2 leader has 26 heavy atoms. It contains an aromatic-labelled nine-membered nitrogen ring bearing imino and carbonyl groups, N-fluoroalkyl substituents, and a fluorinated five-membered carbocycle with an enolic hydroxyl and a cumulated sequence of double bonds. This leader has carbon-bound fluorine rather than an N-F bond, but its cyclic cumulene raises a substantial geometric concern. Seed 0 instead retains N-fluorinated fused imino/carbonyl heterocycles attached to anisole and a small unsaturated nitrogen ring. Seed 1 retains a related fused dione with phenol and fluorinated alkenyl substituents. Mean proposal SMILES length is 46.6; the cumulated-double-bond-string incidence is 0.0517. Compact size and abundant nitrogen do not resolve the difficult ring geometry or reactive substitutions. All of this chemistry is reproduced from the Parent.
liabilities: The cumulated sequence forced into a five-membered ring raises severe strain and synthetic-accessibility concerns.

Other leaders retain N-F bonds and small unsaturated nitrogen rings. The top molecule's lack of N-F is a real counterexample to a universal N-F requirement, not evidence that local reactivity is controlled throughout the output.
A sharp local score change can occur while the doubtful core remains unchanged; score sensitivity therefore cannot certify that core's chemical feasibility.
missing_features: Geometrically credible alternatives preserving the compact fluorinated/polar organization are not established at the leading score; the high-scoring noncumulated relative is an important counterexample to any claim that reward requires the cyclic cumulene.

The large aromatic-labelled nitrogen ring and enolic representation lack demonstrated conformational and tautomeric identity; lowercase aromatic notation is not evidence of a stable aromatic conformation.
Explicit stereochemical identity of substituted saturated centres is absent, and the scores do not identify an exact missing target pharmacophore or justify importing one.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted fused dione scores 0.0020944534688323298. The cyclic-cumulene leader reaches 0.7208853668418119, while a related noncumulated carbocycle with changed nitrogen substitution reaches 0.6725143757617169. This is not an isolated cumulene comparison and does not show that the cumulene is required. The strongest close contrast changes the leader's N-fluoromethyl substituent to N-hydroxymethyl with the rest of the cited framework unchanged: the score falls to 0.006653135242129762. The observed sensitivity is to that local substitution within that scaffold, not a universal requirement for fluorine. Seed-0 and seed-1 leaders score 0.6510211907030741 and 0.4870057305679067 in other families. Isolated F and FF score 1.1043196211273875e-26 and 4.97400031457045e-24, respectively, so fluorination without molecular context is insufficient.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This gap originates in n-c55c3d520a2c and is reproduced identically in n-62daf219c70a on Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2 at 300 observations per task. Leaders contain N-F, N-Cl, N-Br, O-F, halomethyl ethers or benzylic chloride; other seed leaders contain peroxide and cyanate groups. Conventional carbon-bound halogens and recognizable tertiary or cyclic amines also occur at high scores, and one fluorinated leader contains no N-F bond. The problem is environment-specific, not an absence of heterocycles, amines or stable halogen chemistry.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve conventional bond environments when modifying otherwise useful aromatic and heterocyclic frameworks.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator needs bond-environment-aware transformations and plausible local alternatives that retain favorable scaffold and functional-group relationships learned from feedback. Preserve ordinary carbon-bound halogens and useful nitrogen centres where supported. These structural associations do not establish that a universal filter or replacement raises the benchmark score, and the same-code baseline does not attribute the liability to a particular retained component.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This gap originates in n-c55c3d520a2c and is reproduced identically in n-62daf219c70a on the supplied Search Seeds at 300 observations per task. The fluorinated imino/carbonyl leader combines a small cyclic cumulene with a large aromatic-labelled nitrogen ring; other leaders contain medium-ring bridges, and an aryl-amine relative contains cyclic cumulated double bonds. A noncumulated fluorinated relative and conventional saturated cyclic amines also have high scores, so neither unusual unsaturation nor difficult bridges are universal requirements.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently distinguish a representable ring graph from a geometrically credible unsaturation pattern or bridged topology.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring construction needs sensitivity to ring size, bond geometry and bridge connectivity, together with alternative topologies that preserve learned favorable functional arrangements. Ring counts and aromatic labels cannot supply this missing feasibility information. The observed families motivate assessing geometry, not a blanket prohibition of small rings, fused systems or ring formation; no causal score benefit is established here.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This gap was present in n-c55c3d520a2c and recurs without change in n-62daf219c70a across the supplied Search Seeds and observation budget. Every task has stereocentre-string incidence 0.0, while the cited aryl/cyclic amines, fluorinated ring centres and bridged frameworks contain potentially stereogenic environments. Formal-charge-string incidence is also 0.0, but clearly protonatable amines are present; that is a separate representation question.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not specify stereochemical identity after generating potentially stereogenic saturated and bridged centres.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Representations and transformations need to preserve or explicitly resolve stereochemistry when a generated structure requires it, with appropriate treatment of achiral or configurationally unstable cases. Protonation and tautomerism should be assessed separately rather than inferred from the lack of charge markers. These records establish unspecified identity, not a measured stereochemical score penalty or a component-specific failure.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This gap originates in n-c55c3d520a2c and is reproduced identically in n-62daf219c70a on the supplied Search Seeds at 300 observations per task. Tiny halogen and hydrocarbon proposals reach observed floors, including late proposals, while useful scores occur for combinations of aromatic, carbonyl and amine regions. A more cross-linked final fused heterocycle scores below its compact leader. Conversely, a smaller fused-thioether amine retains a high score, so useful simplification is already possible and lower size is not intrinsically bad.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably retain enough functional-group context while avoiding unhelpful fragmentation and excessive elaboration.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Task-local feedback can inform transformations that preserve useful chemical context while simplifying or replacing dispensable portions. The missing capability is consistent control of context loss and elaboration, not an inability to make small molecules. Neither a fixed minimum molecular size nor an automatic preference for larger structures follows from these condition-dependent observations.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This gap was recorded for n-c55c3d520a2c and is re-observed in the identical n-62daf219c70a Search trajectories at the supplied budget. Leaders repeatedly alter halogen placement, short side chains, carbonyl-adjacent groups or ring segments on retained aromatic amide, fused heterocycle, aryl-amine and bridged dicarbonyl frameworks. Different seeds do produce different families, and ring-string incidence is high throughout, so the evidence supports limited leading-family alternatives rather than global structural collapse or inability to form rings.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently produce chemically independent plausible alternatives to the leading scaffold family within each seed.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Scaffold transformations should preserve learned favorable spatial and functional-group relationships while offering chemically independent, feasible connectivities. Evaluate whether such alternatives remain useful under task-local feedback; distinct strings alone do not establish useful scaffold coverage. This is a conditional chemical coverage gap, not evidence that any specific search component caused convergence or that more diversity necessarily improves the objective.

nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

retained_mechanisms: Score-quantile parent allocation, previously accepted scored parents, bounded greedy survival and the full accepted-score archive.
Connected-fragment crossover with unchanged post-crossover mutation probability and multi-parent opportunities.
Ordinary single-atom replacement plus append, delete, insert, bond-change, ring-open and ring-close mutations, with inherited walk and saturation laws.
Sanitization, stable canonical identity admission, initial/emitted and temporary-pool duplicate rejection, bounded retries and fixed surplus pools.
Integer-count Morgan features, generalized Tanimoto kernel, accepted-only chronological GP fitting, unchanged normalization/noise/jitter and full posterior covariance.
Correlated posterior score draws with masks, exact pool-to-emission predictions, pending identity joins and next-fit feedback probes.
Passive aromatic-pair enumeration and the unreachable direct-exchange implementation retained for controlled attribution.
Fresh objective-local state, deterministic prepared settings, ten-member announced batches and protocol-owned budgets/resources.

approach.method_basis: The Parent trains a recurrent SMILES language model on an unlabeled molecular corpus and starts each objective with a fresh policy copied from that frozen prior. Each accepted batch contributes its highest-scoring half. A memory retains the thirty-two strongest earlier elites, and its strongest eligible records join the current examples with their original accepted strings and rewards. Historical examples receive smaller relative weights when earlier fitting batches have used them more often, while total current and historical loss shares stay fixed. Each target is frozen-prior sequence log likelihood plus sixty times accepted reward, projected individually to zero if positive. The policy fits squared residuals with bounded clipped Adam updates and keeps the final iterate. It directly samples complete SMILES and refills each batch using chemical validation and canonical duplicate rejection.
approach.novelty: Remove inverse-exposure weighting within selected history and give every selected current or historical sequence the same loss coefficient. This probes the contribution of diminishing historical influence after the Parent acquired individual target ceilings. Earlier siblings added exposure weighting under uncapped targets, changed replay membership, or shifted total current/history shares; none supplied this ceiling-preserving removal result. The probe restores equal influence across already selected historical examples without changing their membership or targets. Its activation claim is increased effective historical row count and a changed learning direction on unequal-count opportunities. Its utility hypothesis is that the simpler weighting remains non-inferior; more even influence alone does not establish useful molecular progress.

nodes.hypothesis: Remove inverse-prior-fitting-count weighting within the selected historical replay group, using the plain mean of squared individually ceiling-projected target residuals over the unchanged selected current and historical sequences while preserving their membership and total current/history shares.

finding_summary.headline: Equal historical influence changed learning but lost final score, despite better progress earlier in the budget.
finding_summary.insights:
Individual target ceilings did not make exposure weighting dispensable on this panel. The paired controls narrow the change to its intended intervention: loaded priors matched, the first thirty accepted records matched in all fifteen sessions, and proposals diverged only after the first unequal-count update. Two seeds improved modestly, so the evidence supports a useful aggregate endpoint contribution from the removed rule under this composition, with substantial variation across seeds. It does not establish a universal benefit.

A larger effective number of weighted rows is not the same as broader molecular exploration. Giving repeatedly fitted records more influence coincided with more duplicate draws, fewer observed scaffolds and stronger concentration in some analogue families. The molecular assessment still finds rich aromatic and cyclic-amine chemistry, with uneven attachment and size control and no assigned stereochemistry; those limitations persisted despite even replay influence. This is compatible with redundant concentration, but the records do not isolate a particular remembered molecule or chemical feature as the cause.

The retained ceilings also leave a coupled feasibility problem: 235 of 420 prospective historical updates had projected target probability mass above one, and 42 set all ten selected targets to zero. Equal coefficients cannot recover distinctions erased by those ceilings. Fewer historical residual regressions than the parent’s 905 coexisted with a worse endpoint, ruling out that count as a sufficient utility measure. Passive gradient comparisons identify the local learning intervention; they supply no alternative Adam trajectory or alternative molecules. The remaining question is how the altered exploitation pattern produces better early progress but a large endpoint loss in one seed.

molecular.headline: Rich aromatic and cyclic-amine chemistry, but uneven attachment and size control, concentrated analogue families and no specified stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character: Node n-644bbf90f05f generates recognizable aromatic amides, fused nitrogen heterocycles, aryl ethers, piperazines, aryl sulfonamides and hydrazones. These are substantial organic scaffolds, not a ring-deficient output stream. The digest contains 870 optimizer proposals per task; ring-closure-presence rates are 0.9851 to 0.9966 and aromatic-atom-presence rates are 0.9575 to 0.9931. Those are fractions of SMILES containing the relevant text features, not fractions of aromatic atoms or perceived ring counts. Passive RDKit inspection of every supplied trajectory gives median heavy-atom counts of 24, 31, 27, 23 and 25 in the supplied task order, with median perceived ring counts of 3, 4, 3, 3 and 3. All 4,350 accepted optimizer appearances parse. Constitutional coverage is broad: atom-typed Murcko scaffold counts are 449, 344, 500, 729 and 756, although this definition distinguishes linker and ring-atom changes and is not a measure of useful diversity. Stronger subsets often concentrate on close analogues, while lower and late proposals include fragments, excessive alkyl growth, specialized reactive groups and elaborate structures without a demonstrated synthesis. Routine connections make many leaders plausibly makeable, but the whole stream merits questionable synthetic plausibility and moderate medicinal character. Every digest stereocentre_rate is 0.0; RDKit identifies 960 optimizer appearances with an unassigned potential tetrahedral centre and none with an assigned centre. The Parent already had the main functional classes; this node changes their topology, substitution and family concentration without filling the stereochemical gap. All five task trajectories and their Parent counterparts were read; tasks_without_trajectories is empty. Final digest examples are the last displayed seed-2 proposals, not the best retained molecules or a summary of every seed. Chemical score readings below are associations in accepted records, not definitions of hidden objectives, experimental activity claims or mechanism-activation judgements. Descriptor definitions, input hashes and paired trajectory receipts are in runs/SPIRAL2/policy/responses/r0013-04-improve-L03-molecular.audit.json; perception used RDKit 2026.03.3.

per_task.generated_character: The stream is dominated by medium-sized aromatic carboxamides; its median is 24 heavy atoms and three perceived rings. The digest leaders are hydroxy-substituted fused azaarenes bearing methyl/ethyl groups and an N-phenyl or N-benzyl carboxamide. The leading fused diazaarene anilide has 23 heavy atoms, three aromatic rings and molecular weight 307.353. These amide and heteroaromatic connections are recognizable synthetic chemistry. Late seed-2 examples instead join substituted phenyl rings through benzamide bonds and attach an additional amide to a saturated diazacycle; the six-membered diazacycle has a different nitrogen arrangement from piperazine. Relative to the Parent, aromatic amides remain central but their arrangements change. Seed 1 moves from a pyridone/pyridylmethyl benzamide at 0.4767312946227961 to the fused azaarene anilide at 0.4809720776848348. Seed 2 moves from an ether-linked heteroaromatic anilide at 0.5 to the diazacyclic bis-amide family, whose recorded best is 0.4126819838532174.
liabilities: Several low proposals carry long hydrocarbon appendages or multiply linked aromatic amides, adding flexibility and synthetic burden without a corresponding recorded score benefit.
The fused phenol/aza-arene leaders have extensive planar aromatic surface; the trajectories provide no solubility or tautomer-state measurements.
Small halogenated fragments pass molecular validity but do not constitute the organized chemistry associated with the higher scores.
missing_features: Reliable preservation of a compact aromatic carboxamide arrangement during exploration: low proposals either lose it or bury it inside much larger structures.

More consistent control of heteroaromatic nitrogen position, amide attachment and substituent size within the observed useful composition range. The classes themselves are already present; the unresolved feature is their arrangement, not a general absence of rings or amides.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Compact, organized aromatic amides separate the higher scores from both fragmentation and excessive growth. The leading anilide scores 0.4809720776848348, whereas the small halomethane scores 0.0 and the long-chain ether scores 7.215371679253266e-38. The enlarged fused-azaarene/benzyl multi-amide scores 9.527824512419634e-21 despite retaining recognizable ring and amide motifs. Within the leading core, adding a meta bromine to the N-phenyl ring changes 0.4809720776848348 to 0.4531365599537262; more halogen is not automatically rewarded. The late fluorochloro bis-amide scores 0.4126819838532174, showing another viable arrangement, but neither these associations nor ring abundance identify a unique missing target scaffold.

per_task.generated_character: The stronger molecules are heavily aromatic, decorated 4-anilino-2-phenylquinazolines with fluorines and an alkoxy substituent. The leader has 31 heavy atoms, four aromatic rings, seven rotatable bonds and molecular weight 423.438. Its butoxy group is attached through oxygen directly to the fused aromatic core. The digest leaders vary halogens on the phenyl group and interchange alkoxy, alkoxymethyl, alkyl and alkylamino attachments around that core. These aryl-amino and aryl-ether connections look makeable, although the dense substitution adds route complexity. Full trajectories also show acylhydrazone/heteroaromatic families in other seeds. The weaker sulfonyl-conjugated ester and late imine represent potentially reactive or condition-sensitive connections that need individual chemical assessment.
A nitrate representation receives 0.5004402958788305 despite lacking an organic scaffold; the observed score baseline is not evidence of medicinal plausibility.
missing_features: Consistent retention of the favorable aryl-oxygen attachment while varying peripheral groups; many adjacent proposals replace its connectivity and score lower.

Evidence for comparably strong alternative central topologies is limited in the digest, whose leaders all retain the same decorated quinazoline. This is a local family-coverage gap, not a claim that the generator cannot make other rings.

Low examples include an N-sulfonyl piperidine at 1.9828327575562915e-05 and an aromatic nitro acylhydrazone at 4.1105044111594925e-05. Thus nitrogen presence alone is insufficient: retaining an unacylated amine and its aryl spacing is associated with stronger records. This is not a matched-pair demonstration of an amine effect. per_task.generated_character: The stream is chemically broad, with a median of 23 heavy atoms and three perceived rings, but its stronger subset repeatedly combines aryl sulfonamides and piperazine. The leader is a methylquinazolinone bearing an N-phenylpiperazine sulfonamide: 27 heavy atoms, four perceived rings and molecular weight 384.461. Other leaders replace the fused lactam system with a cyclic ether/ketone, a substituted biaryl, or a more elaborate nitrogen ring assembly. These aryl sulfonamide and heterocycle connections are generally recognizable makeable chemistry. The whole-stream audit finds 729 distinct atom-typed Murcko scaffolds, so low overall scores cannot be described as a total collapse onto one core. The Parent shared the sulfonyl-piperazine theme. Seed 0 changes from a methoxychlorophenyl sulfonamide at 0.2125118592516207 to the fused quinazolinone at 0.2354681799202668, whereas the Parent seed-2 bis-sulfonyl piperazine at 0.2588686674995393 is replaced by a different ring/sulfonamide arrangement whose best is 0.22841141193470538.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Closely related aromatic leaders score 0.6817985456116351 with a direct aryl-oxygen linkage, 0.6608516590255653 with an alkoxymethyl linkage and 0.6584621764113501 with an aryl-NH linkage. In another series, unacylated cyclic-amine/aryl molecules score near the recorded ceiling while a sulfonylated piperidine is a low example. Sulfonylated piperazine is nevertheless productive elsewhere, so there is no universally preferred nitrogen role.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator can emit useful functional classes but does not reliably preserve their attachment chemistry and chemical roles while varying a scaffold.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Task-agnostic generation needs control over connection site, bond order and nitrogen substitution, allowing feedback to distinguish and preserve useful arrangements. A ring or functional-group inventory alone cannot express that chemical distinction; no particular linkage should be imposed across all objectives.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Compact aromatic amides and heteroaryl compounds coexist with zero-scoring fragments and very weak long-chain or multiply linked assemblies. A compact fused heteroaryl benzamide scores 0.30950439639437716, whereas a large alkyl/heteroaryl/sulfonamide assembly scores 2.103895097704417e-113. Other long-chain diamines still score above 0.99, demonstrating that both size sensitivity and chemical acceptability depend on the observed family rather than a universal size cutoff.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently maintain the size and structural organization of its own stronger molecules during continued exploration.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Generation should be able to vary size, linker length and heteroatom composition locally around feedback-supported families while retaining access to alternatives. Chemical growth should remain interpretable and coherent; a global demand for larger, smaller, more aromatic or more highly aminated molecules is not supported.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every digest stereocentre_rate is 0.0. Passive perception of the supplied optimizer trajectories identifies 960 appearances with unassigned potential tetrahedral centres and none with an assigned centre. The cited leading bridged ether, cyclic ether/ketone and benzylic alcohol illustrate the gap; the acylhydrazone series also lacks explicit C=N geometry.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator produces potentially stereogenic structures without specifying their stereochemical state.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic representation and proposal process would need to express stereochemical alternatives when it generates stereogenic atoms or geometrically distinct double bonds, retaining that information through molecular identity handling. This is a demonstrated coverage gap, not evidence that assigning a particular stereoisomer would increase the recorded scores.

transferable_gaps.evidence: All 4,350 accepted optimizer appearances parse in the passive structural audit, yet the digest includes an organic azide, trichloromethyl N-hydroxyformamide, sulfonyl-linked nitrogen chain, nitrate and carbon disulfide alongside conventional amides, aryl ethers and cyclic amines. Validity therefore admits both ordinary medicinal scaffolds and specialized, reactive or trivial species.
transferable_gaps.gap: Syntactic molecular validity is accompanied by uneven control of chemical stability and routine synthetic plausibility.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator needs to distinguish coherent makeable connections and plausible molecular states from merely valid strings, without assuming that every unusual functional group is forbidden or that score alone certifies chemistry. The supplied structures support scrutiny of connection stability and synthetic context; they do not provide actual routes or experimental stability measurements.

nodes.method_name: Augmented Hill-Climb with a corpus-trained SMILES policy
nodes.method_thesis: Train a compact autoregressive SMILES prior solely on the supplied unlabeled corpus, then initialize a fresh policy from that prior for each objective. Use the initial observations and each subsequent scored batch to update only its highest-reward sequences with the Augmented Hill-Climb loss: fit policy log likelihood to frozen-prior log likelihood plus scaled observed reward. Sample complete molecules token by token from the updated policy, canonicalize them, and refill invalid or duplicate proposals by further generation. The corpus supplies language training, never a ranked molecular pool. Elite-conditioned policy updates should shift generation toward new high-scoring molecular combinations quickly enough to improve the benchmark's mean final Top-1. This is a small-budget transfer hypothesis, not a claim that published larger-budget gains carry over. The root uses the current scored batch; randomized historical replay is reserved for the first improvement. The anchor's elite augmented-likelihood mechanism is described by [Thomas et al.](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13321-022-00646-z).

approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds molecular graphs from a population of at most sixty-four accepted molecules, kept in descending score order. It chooses a high-ranking score band and then a molecule uniformly within that band, produces a fresh surplus of crossover and mutation offspring, and uses correlated draws from a fingerprint Gaussian process to choose which offspring to evaluate. Every accepted score trains the posterior, even if its molecule leaves the breeding population. This loop reliably learns and selects, but most evaluated offspring do not improve on their generating parents, and successful molecular cores accumulate many close relatives.
approach.novelty: Give each represented molecular core equal breeding probability within the already selected score band. A core with many surviving analogues will share its probability among those analogues, while a less represented accepted core gains an opportunity to breed. The existing preference for high-scoring bands remains intact. The lineage's earlier child changed how generated offspring are selected for evaluation; this child changes only which accepted parents produce those offspring. Neither recorded sibling nor a supplied mechanism cluster has tested this conditional correction for core multiplicity.

nodes.hypothesis: Within each inherited score quantile, sample accepted breeding parents with probability inversely proportional to the number of eligible survivors sharing their Murcko core, so every represented core has equal conditional mass.

finding_summary.headline: Core-balanced breeding broadened core use and raised parent-beating yield, but lowered final scores.
finding_summary.insights:
Equalizing core probability can reduce repeated use of abundant families without improving the best molecules found. The clearest coverage expansions were in decoration hopping and DRD2, yet their parent-beating counts and final-score means fell. Zaleplon breeding became more concentrated despite correct balancing within each selected band, showing that changing the conditional draw does not guarantee broader realized coverage once the evolving survivor population is considered.

The modest parent-beating gain also uses a weaker reference: mean best-generating-parent score fell from 0.419645 to 0.395720, while mean evaluated-offspring score fell from 0.319152 to 0.301731. This relative yield gain therefore does not establish stronger offspring production. The number of admitted offspring later reused for breeding stayed almost unchanged, at 2,163 versus 2,167, and incumbent gains did not increase. The evidence narrows the problem to allocating toward productive surviving families rather than simply reducing their multiplicity imbalance; discarded or ineligible cores still receive no opportunity. The molecular assessment also shows that broader structural coverage continues to include repeated heterocycle growth, tiny fragments, reactive nitrogen-halogen/peroxide groups and strained fused rings. Murcko-core coverage alone does not resolve those quality limitations. Passive comparisons supply probabilities and parent identities, with no scores for alternate offspring or an alternate search trajectory.
finding_summary.results:
The allocation change executed correctly in all three replicas. Of 111,246 parent draws, 86,634 had unequal core multiplicities; every logged probability vector and inverse-CDF choice matched the intended rule. On the same eligible states and logged uniform variates, 36,398 selected parent ranks and 29,554 selected cores differed from the passive uniform comparator. Mean represented cores used per breeding batch rose from 12.98 to 14.60, and mean concentration of breeding uses fell from 0.299 to 0.189, measured as the sum of squared core-use shares. Coverage rose in 10 of 15 task/seed sessions; the effect was not universal. All accepted-state, survivor and pending-provenance checks passed, and both panels completed all 4,500 oracle evaluations.

Strict best-parent beats increased from 565/4,350 (12.99%) to 600/4,350 (13.79%), and mean child-minus-best-parent score improved from -0.100493 to -0.093989. Incumbent improvements were nearly unchanged, at 216 versus 218. Mean final-best score across tasks and seeds fell from 0.544374 to 0.524118, a paired change of -0.020256. Seed changes were -0.052822, -0.023812 and +0.015865; all five task means declined. Thus the intended allocation mechanism is confirmed, while the intended score increase was not observed.

molecular.headline: Repeated heterocycle growth and tiny fragments coexist with reactive, highly fused leading molecules
molecular.overall_character: The current panel contains 900 recorded entries and 870 optimizer proposals per task, with complete three-seed Parent n-fc2c108a5253 trajectories. Aromatic-token presence ranges from 0.9425 to 0.9931 and ring-closure presence from 0.977 to 0.9931; charge and stereocentre token presence are 0.0 throughout. These are string-presence measurements, not aromatic atom fractions, ionization measurements or evidence of feasible stereochemistry. The output is ring-rich and often extensively aromatic: fused nitrogen carbonyl systems, aromatic amine/aminal frameworks and halogenated unsaturated heterocycles dominate the leaders. Chemical scale varies from tiny fragments to large assemblies of repeated heterocycles. This is particularly pronounced in deco_hop, whose mean SMILES length is 115.4 and maximum is 235; its seed-2 final molecules visibly repeat nitrogen-dione units. The Parent also produced reactive and extensively connected structures. Current leaders retain N-halogen bonds, peroxide or hypohalite motifs, tight ring fusion and unspecified configurations. Overall synthetic plausibility is questionable, with strongly implausible individual small-ring or growth outliers, and drug-like quality remains weak. Across-seed diversity is moderate; many late streams mainly elaborate a common core.

per_task.generated_character: The best seed-2 molecules are moderately sized fused unsaturated nitrogen heterocycles bearing fluoroaryl carboxamides, alkyl/alkoxy substituents and hydroxymethyl or aminomethyl groups. Amide N-Br/N-Cl/N-F and fused-ring N-F are frequent in the leaders. Seed 0 reaches pyrazole thioamides with phenolic, cyclopentadienyl and cyclobutenyl groups; seed 1 reaches an aryl ketone with N-O/N-N functionality. Aromatic-token presence is 0.9782 and halogen presence is 0.7149. Relative to the Parent aromatic ketone, amide and thioheterocyclic families, the compact aromatic/carbonyl theme persists, with reactive nitrogen substitution and unusual ring geometry.
liabilities: N-Br, N-Cl and N-F bonds add reactivity to amide and ring nitrogens; N-O/N-N variants add compatibility concerns.
Unusual unsaturated small rings, scaffold doubling and very small fragment products reduce the chemical coherence of the output.
missing_features: Stable nonhalogenated nitrogen alternatives preserving the successful aromatic/carbonyl arrangement are poorly represented among the leading amide series.

Accessible fused-ring alternatives and explicit configurations or alkene geometry are absent for many unusual partially saturated and bridged products; a unique target pharmacophore cannot be inferred.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best N-bromoamide/N-fluoro heterocycle scores 0.4294168350924388 versus 0.4163503402962837 for the paired Parent seed 2; other paired seeds change in different directions. N-Cl, N-F and N-Br amide variants share 0.41885833432199493, so their reactivity is not distinguished. A halogen-free pyrazole thioamide reaches 0.4220190409118175, showing N-halogen chemistry is not universally required in this region. Tiny peroxide or halogen compounds score 0.0, and an isolated fluoro-carbamoyl fragment scores 9.818532642967522e-13. The complete ring/carbonyl arrangement matters more than a reactive group in a tiny fragment.

per_task.generated_character: The best seed-1 family is a relatively compact fused aza-heteroaromatic carbonyl system joined to fluorinated nitrogen heteroaryl rings. It bears a cyclic peroxide bridge and alkyl, vinyl or ethynyl substituents. In contrast, seed 0 and especially seed 2 produce large structures with repeated nitrogen-dione/heteroaryl modules, ester/ketone connections and many aromatic rings; some final products also contain N-Br. Aromatic and ring-closure presence are 0.9931 and halogen presence is 0.8575. The Parent also favored reactive fused heterocycles and expanded dione assemblies. Here the highest score occurs in the more compact seed-1 family rather than the large repeated assemblies.
liabilities: Cyclic peroxide, N-halogen and reactive linker motifs complicate stability and synthesis.
Very large repeated heterocycle assemblies create substantial size, aromaticity, flexibility and synthetic-complexity liabilities.
missing_features: Compact stable alternatives preserving the favorable heteroaryl/carbonyl arrangement are underrepresented relative to peroxide-bearing or repeatedly expanded structures.
The late growth families lack a demonstrated need for repeated dione units, extra aromatic attachments and ester-linked duplication.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best peroxide-containing fused heterocycle scores 0.616390401531925, compared with the Parent seed-1 maximum of 0.6324703199409752. Vinyl, ethynyl and methyl derivatives tie at 0.6152337858220212. Removing a peroxide oxygen from the vinyl compound gives 0.6151026837099413, demonstrating a near-equivalent nonperoxide alternative. Much larger seed-2 assemblies remain around 0.59, with a maximum of 0.5995098039215686, while tiny fluorine or hydrocarbon fragments score 0.5. The recurring nitrogen/carbonyl/heteroaryl arrangement appears favorable, without evidence that repeated growth or peroxide functionality is necessary.

per_task.generated_character: The leaders combine halogenated aromatic rings with nitrogen-rich saturated rings, secondary methylamino groups and compact fused aminal frameworks. The best seed-2 family contains a small diazetidine-like unit and aryl N-Cl; seed 1 also gives sulfinamide-linked bicyclic diamines or densely fused carbon/nitrogen rings. Fluoromethoxy groups have carbon-bound fluorine, while other members carry the distinct reactive aryl O-F motif. Aromatic-token presence is 0.9839 and halogen presence is 0.992. The Parent similarly produced aromatic amines with constrained rings. Current synthesis remains questionable because of tight junctions and reactive substituents.
liabilities: Tight small-ring aminal fusion and unspecified configurations create substantial geometric and synthetic uncertainty.
Aryl N-Cl and O-F bonds, occasional unusual sulfur bonding and bulky aromatic substitution remain chemical or physicochemical liabilities.
missing_features: Accessible less constrained cyclic-amine and aminal geometries preserving the favorable aromatic spacing are underrepresented among the leaders.
Defined stereochemistry at fused junctions and sulfinamide sulfur, together with relevant protonation alternatives, is absent from the displayed comparisons.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best N-chloro fused aromatic aminal scores 0.9557660498629175 versus 0.9914038363125457 for the paired Parent seed 2. A sulfinamide/bicyclic-diamine member reaches 0.9490309869379135 without N-Cl or O-F, while a less connected aromatic aminal without N-Cl scores 0.9252905395110519. Early acidic amide derivatives score as low as 0.000719339566735797, and a small sulfur/N-Cl fragment scores 0.0017478706282521514. These observations favor the complete aromatic/amine arrangement rather than reactive halogen bonding alone. All current paired maxima are below their Parent counterparts.

per_task.generated_character: The leaders are densely fused aromatic nitrogen polycycles with ethoxy, amino or alkyl substituents and attached or bridged lactam/dione regions. Some have N-O-containing rings or additional saturated bridges. Aromatic-token presence is 0.9816 and ring-closure presence is 0.9851; numerous fused aromatic rings are visible in the leaders. Sulfur and halogens are not major features of the best series. Relative to the Parent cyclic carbonyl, aryl-aza and amine frameworks, current output often contains more condensed fused aromatic connectivity, increasing planarity and synthetic complexity without a clear score advantage.
liabilities: Large fused aromatic surfaces create solubility and nonspecific-interaction concerns, while extensive ring connectivity complicates synthesis.
Bridge stereochemistry, unusual N-O/N-N connectivity in some variants and fragment-sized proposals remain unresolved quality issues.
missing_features: Simpler accessible frameworks preserving the favorable aromatic and carbonyl/nitrogen attachment pattern are underrepresented relative to condensed polycyclic growth.
Configurations are unspecified for saturated bridges and junctions, and the evidence does not show that additional fusion is needed over more flexible alternatives.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best amino/ethoxy fused polycyclic dione scores 0.21165206225960834 versus the Parent seed-0 maximum of 0.22405709718343647; the other paired current maxima are also lower. Removing a carbonyl in a close late relative retains 0.2106565294702053. Another fused aryl/aza-lactam family reaches 0.20845479592460323. Tiny hydrocarbon or peroxide fragments score 0.0, while several more elaborate final variants remain below the leaders. The evidence favors an intact aromatic/polar-ring arrangement but does not identify a required single carbonyl or unique target fragment.

per_task.generated_character: Higher-scoring seed-2 compounds are moderately sized nitrogen-rich cyclic diones with imine-containing N-substituents, carbon-bound fluorine, N-F and a chlorofluorinated fused small-ring hydrocarbon partner. The best nitrogen dione has an expanded aromatic ring rather than a conventional small heterocycle. Seed 1 includes an activated ester attached to a cyclobutadiene-like ring and a fluorinated fused dione; other members contain lactones. Aromatic-token presence is 0.9425 and halogen presence is 0.8517. Large doubled or repeated dione/aryl assemblies occupy the low tail. The Parent also had favorable compact fluorinated carbonyl/nitrogen arrangements, but current N-F and strained-ring chemistry still limit plausibility.
liabilities: N-F, O-F, imine and activated unsaturated ester motifs introduce reactivity; the cyclobutadiene-like ring raises strong stability concerns.
Expanded nitrogen-rich aromatic rings, fused small-ring geometry and repeated dione growth lack established synthetic accessibility and stereochemical definition.
missing_features: Stable accessible alternatives retaining the favorable nitrogen/carbonyl/fluorinated arrangement without N-F or strained unsaturated small rings are not demonstrated among the leaders.
Configurations at fused hydrocarbon junctions and hydroxyl/fluoro-bearing sites are absent, while late doubled structures lose the compact favorable arrangement.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The seed-2 maximum is 0.5197936759696083 versus 0.4071395189354175 for its Parent; the current maxima for the other seeds are lower. Adding a nitrogen within a close final dione ring lowers the score to 0.0839454186797069, showing sensitivity to local ring composition rather than nitrogen count. The cyclobutadiene-like ester scores 0.4852949787500649. Large coupled aromatic/dione products score as low as 1.6758614448245604e-53. Bounded size and particular carbonyl/nitrogen/fluorinated-ring placement appear favorable, but the observations do not establish reactive N-F or strained rings as chemically desirable solutions.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Digest extremes include elemental or small hydrocarbon/peroxide molecules and repeated nitrogen-dione/heteroaryl assemblies. One proposal set has mean SMILES length 115.4 and maximum 235, while its highest score comes from a much smaller fused heterocycle.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve a useful molecular scale between tiny fragments and repeated large assemblies.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make fragment retention, compact recombination and removal of repeated modules available while preserving useful attachment geometry. Repeated aromatic or carbonyl units should not dominate alternatives to an intact favorable scaffold.

transferable_gaps.evidence: High-scoring molecules contain N-Br/N-Cl/N-F, O-F and cyclic peroxide motifs. N-halogen variants tie at 0.41885833432199493; a peroxide-containing vinyl heterocycle at 0.6152337858220212 has a nonperoxide relative at 0.6151026837099413.
transferable_gaps.gap: Reactive halogen and peroxide bonds remain frequent substitutes for stable heteroatom chemistry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide stable matched nitrogen and oxygen bonding alternatives around the same cores, and represent functional-group compatibility independently of scalar feedback. Some reactive bonds are demonstrably unnecessary to retain the observed favorable arrangement.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Leaders include tightly fused aminal rings, extensive aromatic condensation, expanded nitrogen diones and a cyclobutadiene-like motif. Stereocentre-token presence is 0.0 throughout despite saturated ring junctions and sulfur centres requiring configurational consideration.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring-rich generation is not matched by reliable ring geometry or stereochemical specification.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Distinguish accessible small and fused rings from strongly strained unsaturation or incompatible junctions, and support configuration assignment and stereoisomer variation. Current trajectories do not establish stereochemical score sensitivity.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A less connected aromatic aminal retains 0.9252905395110519, a fused relative with a removed carbonyl retains 0.2106565294702053, and methyl/vinyl/ethynyl heterocycle variants share 0.6152337858220212. Larger repeated or more fused products do not consistently improve scores.
transferable_gaps.gap: High-scoring regions contain too few simple alternatives relative to the fusion and decoration explored.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Expand simpler linker, ring and substituent variants around recurring aromatic, carbonyl and amine arrangements. Score-tolerant regions could then contain more accessible and chemically interpretable molecules.

nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

approach.method_basis: Simulated annealing keeps one current configuration, perturbs it randomly, and always accepts an improvement while accepting a deterioration with a probability that falls as a temperature parameter cools. Early on the walk can move downhill and escape a local optimum; late on it behaves almost greedily. Applied to molecules, the configuration is a graph, the perturbation is an atom or bond edit, and the acceptance test uses the observed score returned by the oracle.
approach.novelty: This root runs many independent walks in parallel rather than one, with at most one outstanding proposal per walk, so the oracle batch is filled by different points in the space instead of by one trajectory. It ties the cooling schedule to accumulated feedback rather than wall time, seeds the initial temperature from the spread of the initial scores, and keeps a separate best-observed archive so that accepting a downhill move never loses the incumbent.

nodes.hypothesis: Maintain independent task-local molecular graph walks, generate de novo atom or bond edits from each current working state, accept nondecreasing observed scores and accept decreases with probability exp((new_score-current_score)/T), and cool T as accepted feedback accumulates while preserving a separate best-observed archive.

finding_summary.headline: The annealing machinery was exact in every respect and produced the round's lowest score, 0.233
finding_summary.insights: This node isolates the round's most important lesson. The search algorithm is provably correct and the search still failed, so what separates the field is not the optimizer but the proposal distribution it draws from. Aromatic content here is 50 to 67 percent against 87 to 100 percent for every root above 0.4, and the graph edits repeatedly produce aromatic phosphorus rings and hypervalent centres that are not real chemistry. Any future work on this lineage belongs in the edit operator set, not in the acceptance rule or the cooling schedule. One seed only, and its deco_hop result shows the walk does work where the initial molecules are already close.

molecular.headline: Aromatic phosphorus rings and hypervalent centres: a correct search over chemistry that does not exist
molecular.overall_character: Ring closure is high at 97 percent on every objective, but only half to two thirds of proposals contain any ordinary aromatic atom, the lowest of any root that completed. The gap is filled by exotic ring systems the graph editor is willing to construct: phosphinine rings written with aromatic phosphorus, hypervalent phosphorus and sulfur centres, and nitrogen-halogen bonds. nodes.method_name: Simulated annealing through de novo molecular graph walks
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the method in simulated annealing: randomly perturb a current configuration, accept improvements, sometimes accept deterioration, and gradually cool the acceptance rule. [Kirkpatrick, Gelatt and Vecchi](https://hedibert.org/wp-content/uploads/2013/12/1983KirkpatrickGelattVecchi.pdf) describe this mechanism for combinatorial optimization. Our molecular transfer maintains independent graph walks initialized from the current objective's supplied scored molecules. Each walk generates a new neighbor through atom or bond edits. After real feedback, accept a higher-scoring neighbor as the next working state; accept a lower-scoring neighbor with probability exp((new_score-current_score)/T), otherwise retain the source state. Subsequent edits follow the accepted working state, while a separate archive preserves the best observed molecule. Cool as feedback accumulates and distribute the evaluator-announced batch across walks with explicit proposal-to-source provenance. Regenerate invalid or already evaluated structures through further edits. Every submitted molecule is generated de novo; no corpus pool, learned prior or labeled source task is required. The hypothesis is that temporary score losses permit useful structural transitions whose later gains increase the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. This finite-budget optimizer does not claim equilibrium sampling or asymptotic convergence under molecular validity and novelty filtering.

approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from previously evaluated molecules. It retains a bounded population by score, draws breeding parents from preferred score bands, and generates a surplus pool through connected-fragment crossover or ordinary one-parent mutation walks. A successful crossover has a separate 35% chance of one finishing mutation before validity and duplicate checks. The Parent already excludes the direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen positional exchange. Its Gaussian process learns from the complete chronological archive of accepted task-local scores, using counts of local molecular environments and generalized Tanimoto similarity. Correlated posterior draws choose the molecules to evaluate; accepted offspring update both the model archive and the score-ranked breeding population.
approach.novelty: Test the interaction between the already evaluated two-cut ring construction and removal of crossover finishing. Reuse the ring construction exactly: when both actual parents support it, it can join complete components cut from two parental rings at two endpoints under the original uniform choices. Disable the finishing branch for every successful crossover while retaining its random draw. This sends the immediate recombinants to ordinary admission without another edit at that boundary. The earlier ring-only sibling built and evaluated new rings but lost score; some of its finished products also lost the new ring pattern. Neither that result nor earlier donor-conditioning siblings tested this joint treatment. The concurrent finishing-only control completes the four-treatment comparison needed to distinguish an interaction from the general effect of removing finishing. Structural persistence may help search, but greater persistence alone cannot establish an endpoint gain.

nodes.hypothesis: Combine the exact optional two-cut ring-segment crossover of n-870ed6964d46 with removal of post-crossover finishing on code Parent n-62daf219c70a: set only post_crossover_mutation_probability from 0.35 to 0.0 while retaining its existing random draw after every successful ordinary or ring-mode crossover.

finding_summary.headline: Intact ring products reached breeding; a positive but uneven interaction did not recover the Anchor score
finding_summary.insights:
Finishing is a real conditional boundary for this exact construction: the four matched conditions show that its total effect changes when ring mode is present. Correct construction, intact evaluated rings and later breeding rule out a globally broken delivery mechanism, but they do not restore the required endpoint performance. The apparent benefit is concentrated in seed 2, especially docking, and the ring-without-finishing contrast itself is negative in two of three seed macros. Those shared controls are dependent evidence, so the positive mean interaction does not establish a reliable general benefit or independent component replication.

Structural preservation alone is insufficient as an explanation. All three median-2 endpoints improve despite no evaluated ring-mode descendant, and one zaleplon gain occurs with no selected ring construction at all. Eligible mode draws, unselected pool competitors and changed adaptive histories can still change those searches. The joint run produces more local best-parent wins overall (768 versus 629), but mean generating-parent score falls from 0.470456 to 0.403872, mean offspring score from 0.385256 to 0.341961, and the average positive incumbent step from 0.022510 to 0.017312. That separates frequent small local gains from stronger final search.

The chemistry further limits the claim. Ring-rich aromatic and nitrogen/carbonyl families coexist with reactive attachments, difficult bridges or small-ring unsaturation and unresolved stereochemistry. Distinct typed and generic cores fall even as ring-only graph diversity rises; nearby high-scoring conventional examples show that the questionable attachments are not universally needed. Preserving a typed cycle therefore proves neither useful geometry nor feasible synthesis. The present evidence answers the fixed joint contribution question and rejects its separate performance prediction. Which preserved products, lost finishing products, random-stream changes or later feedback paths explain the interaction remains open; no unselected alternative received a score, and no chemical mediation claim follows.
finding_summary.results:
All 35,061 successful crossovers retained their original gate draw and skipped finishing; 12,487 draws fell below the former 35% threshold. Ring mode made 5,283 valid two-attachment products. All 169 evaluated noncopy descendants retained the new typed cycle and both selected component patterns, versus 167 of 179 and 151 of 179 in the ring-only treatment. The evaluated noncopy count nevertheless fell from 179 to 169. All 161 nonterminal ring births entered the next model fit, 103 later bred, 41 beat their best parent and 12 improved the incumbent. Eight terminal births were censored; nine task/seed cells evaluated no ring descendant.

The complete four-condition comparison gives a mean interaction of +0.047285, with seed interactions -0.004750, +0.009258 and +0.137346 (population SD 0.063939). Removing finishing improves the ring-only mean by +0.011042, while removing it without ring mode lowers the mean by -0.036243. This is a heterogeneous interaction: ten task/seed interactions are positive, three negative and two unchanged. The joint mean remains 0.561665 versus the Anchor’s 0.595670, a loss of -0.034004 against the required +0.002 gain. Six endpoints improve and nine decline; seed macro changes are -0.078161, +0.010125 and -0.033978. Seed population SD falls from 0.026593 to 0.010338 around the lower mean.

nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from accepted task-local observations. It draws breeding parents from score-ranked quantiles, applies connected-fragment crossover and ordinary atom, bond and ring mutations, and keeps a bounded greedy survivor population. Before evaluation it builds a fresh surplus pool, verifies canonical identities and rejects newly introduced outside-envelope sulfur signatures relative to their maximum multiplicity in the actual scored generating parents. A Gaussian process fitted to the full chronological accepted archive uses folded Morgan integer counts and dot-product count Tanimoto covariance. Its correlated function draws select the announced batch; only real accepted feedback changes survivors and the next fit.
approach.novelty: Replace the allocation residual law by the conditional covariance of the fixed exponential count-Tanimoto model, while keeping the original model's predictive mean. This changes residual variances and dependence together, allowing exploration to move without changing same-state mean ranking. The Parent has no completed direct siblings in the brief. The deliberately complementary parallel test changes the mean while retaining original residuals; the earlier full exponential substitution changed both outputs on an ungated Parent and lost endpoint score. This hybrid has not been evaluated and does not identify a factorial interaction.

nodes.hypothesis: Modify only the allocation residual output law on sulfur-gated Parent n-1744a1494180: retain the exact original dot-product count-Tanimoto raw mean mu_DP and replace its standardized latent conditional residual covariance C_DP with C_E from the fixed kernel K_E=exp(T_DP-1). Actual draws are mu_DP[None,:] + score_scale * (Z @ chol(C_E + active_jitter*I).T), using the one original batch-by-pool standard-normal array Z and inherited sequential masks/first-index ties. Active marginal SD is score_scale*sqrt(clamp_min(diag(C_E),0)); original means and truthful exponential SDs reach emission and next-fit probe diagnostics. This is one hybrid Gaussian allocation law replacing residual variance and dependence together, not a correlation-only change or the posterior of a single GP kernel.

finding_summary.headline: Residual exploration changed choices but lost 0.02971 in mean endpoint score
finding_summary.insights: The residual substitution was exposed strongly enough to test the route: its loss cannot be explained by an unchanged allocator, an incorrect mean path, missing feedback or a timeout. This narrows the uncertainty: more local wins and genuinely new productive cores can arise from lower-quality sources and still yield smaller total progress and worse endpoints. Later use did not repair that problem. All 2,519 positively supported Child sources were distinguished from 1,681 nonterminal sources without support; 52 supported sources were never drawn, and the 150 terminal records had no later opportunity. These are opportunity and use observations, not independent ancestral credit. The molecular assessment finds diverse ring-rich families rather than global scaffold collapse, but sulfur-halogen incidence fell from 93 to 8 while nitrogen-halogen incidence rose from 786 to 938, oxygen-halogen from 217 to 262 and carbon allenes from 11 to 148. Questionable attachments, difficult closures and unspecified stereochemistry persist among high scores. Those associations help explain why novelty and a narrow sulfur admission gate cannot certify chemical quality; they do not prove chemical mediation of the endpoint loss. The exact residual route ends under its registered rule. The passive exponential-mean diagnostic does not license choosing a post-result hybrid. The old full exponential experiment used an ungated Parent, so this test and its complementary sibling do not establish a current-Parent factorial interaction, component additivity or transfer. Current Parent composition remains awaiting catalog review, and broader foundation, constituent, joint-interaction, chemical-mediation, partial-lineage-composition and full-history gaps remain open.
finding_summary.results: All 15 task/seed runs completed with 300 observations each. Across 435 decision pools, the residual covariance and sample values changed while the original predictive mean stayed intact; 318 selected sets and 326 orders changed, with 626 strict original-law disagreements under the actual masks. All 4,350 offspring joined real prelabel predictions, feedback and accepted archives; 4,200 later reached another fit/probe and 150 final-batch observations were censored. Original-mean ranking/MSE on those same labels remained unchanged. On their different actual streams, Child pair accuracy was 0.69951 versus Parent 0.70955, mean batch Spearman 0.50187 versus 0.52551, and MSE 0.009780 versus 0.011213. The passive exponential mean scored better on the Child labeled stream (accuracy 0.70623, MSE 0.008191); it supplied no active means or extra rewards. Parent beats rose from 648 to 659, sequential incumbent events from 255 to 262, and new productive typed/generic cores from 262/163 to 294/197. But absolute offspring means fell from 0.372050 to 0.370888, best generating-parent means from 0.455304 to 0.445316, and summed incumbent gain from 5.819415 to 5.373764. Productive-source descendant edges fell from 485 to 477 and their average score from 0.360034 to 0.348999. Final macro score was 0.566743 versus 0.596453: paired gain -0.029710 against the required +0.002. Seven task/seed endpoints improved and eight worsened. Seed gains were -0.083275, +0.020415 and -0.026271; Child population dispersion was 0.011974 versus 0.033970. All positive/adverse endpoints and AUC results are retained.
