molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic families retain reactive heteroatom-halogen bonds, difficult closures and unspecified stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: Node n-6ebafca203bf produces recognizable azaaryl amides, linked nitrogen-rich heterocycles, aromatic regions combined with aliphatic amines, nitrogen/carbonyl medium rings, and fluorinated imino/carbonyl systems. Different seeds reach different families, but leaders within a seed commonly differ only in halogen attachments, short chains or local ring closures. The chemistry is neither acyclic nor globally collapsed. Digest ring-closure-string incidences range from 0.9713 to 0.9885 and aromatic-string incidences from 0.9632 to 0.9828; these measure molecule-level text presence, not aromatic atom fraction or perceived ring counts. Formal-charge and stereocentre-string incidences are zero on every task. Perceived generated median heavy-atom counts in fixed task order are 25, 35, 29, 29 and 27, versus Parent 24, 31, 29, 31 and 27. All 15 Child and 15 published accepted Parent trajectories were read, each containing 300 observations including ten initial records. There are 4350 generated observations per node. No paths, tasks or paired seeds are absent. context.comparison independently states child_complete=true, paired_complete=true and no profile mismatches; Parent is n-1744a1494180. RDKit parses every generated record, which establishes representability only. Counts over those records find direct N-halogen bonds in Child 938 versus Parent 786, O-halogen bonds in 262 versus 217, and carbon allenes in 148 versus 11. Sulfur-halogen bonds decrease from 93 to 8; that does not make the residual nitrogen/oxygen attachments or ring geometry conventional. Unassigned perceived tetrahedral centres occur in 2015 Child records versus 2455 Parent records, with no explicit @ notation in either. This count excludes axial alkene/allene identity and does not establish stable configurations. Sixty-nine Child records versus 82 Parent records have at most three heavy atoms. Local-bond and geometry flags are observations, not synthesis, toxicity or stability measurements. Scores remain evaluator labels and the complete paired molecular contrasts are descriptive. Passive choices, rejected candidates and their hypothetical continued chemistry have no labels here. The inherited sulfur admission condition constrains a narrow local representation and can permit inherited exceptions; this report does not reconstruct its reference multiplicities or attribute chemistry to that gate or to either predictor output. Its activation belongs to analyze. Current Anchor composition remains needs_review pending prescribed catalog review. Whole-foundation m-4fa9546e559e, constituent, joint-interaction, chemical-mediation, partial L07 composition and incomplete full-history gaps remain unresolved. Published earlier molecular assessments were read through the legal evidence_index for gap provenance, not pooled as additional matched trials. Counts, score strata, path hashes and source hashes are in .slots/round-0027-slot-1/molecular/chemistry_measurements.json and source_provenance.json.

per_task.generated_character: Compact fused indole/azaindole-like aromatic regions linked through an amide to pyridyl groups dominate. Generated median size is 25 heavy atoms and three perceived rings, with three aromatic rings; most have alkyl/alkenyl and ether substitution. Seed-0 and seed-1 leaders each have 25 heavy atoms and three rings. Both carry an N-halogen amide, while seed 1 also puts fluorine directly on the fused ring nitrogen. Seed 2 reaches a 24-heavy-atom carbon-bridged fused framework with pyridyl amide, methoxy and isopropenyl groups; RDKit perceives five rings including dependent closures, not five independent aromatic systems. Its bridge geometry and unassigned centre require examination. Final seed-2 proposals keep this family but alter carbonyl, nitrogen and halogen attachments. These are medicinally recognizable arrangements with questionable local substitutions and dense closure variants, not a demonstrated synthesis.
liabilities: Direct N-Cl/N-Br at the amide and N-F/N-Br/N-Cl at ring nitrogen are distinct from ordinary aryl halides and merit environment-specific reactivity assessment.
The non-N-halogen alternative introduces carbon bridges and unspecified stereochemistry; removing one suspicious bond does not establish credible whole-molecule geometry.
missing_features: Conventional local nitrogen substitution is not consistently retained at the leading labels, despite a high-scoring non-N-halogen amide counterexample.

Independent plausible realizations of the favorable aromatic/carbonyl arrangement are limited among close leaders; ring and carbonyl abundance are already present. No exact missing target pharmacophore is inferable from this record.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The seed-1 leader and its ring N-Br and N-Cl relatives all score 0.4828171386373609 while retaining an amide N-Br. This equality does not establish a need for any of those reactive attachments. The non-N-halogen seed-2 bridged amide scores 0.4692371322034651. Initial trimethoxyindole anilide scores 0.3051048083696145. Tiny C=CF scores 0.0; a substantial doubled aromatic amide system scores only 4.199543746961361e-07. Compact aromatic/carbonyl organization is favored over fragmentation or indiscriminate aromatic growth. In the 217-record high-score generated quartile, 155 contain N-halogen bonds, compared with 74 in the low quartile; this association is conditional on the searched scaffolds and cannot establish causality. Child seed endpoints 0/1/2 are 0.4588069837338257, 0.4828171386373609, 0.4692371322034651; published Parent endpoints are 0.4593573492521118, 0.47411701813450596, 0.4369542269692598.

per_task.generated_character: Larger linked heterocyclic molecules dominate: median 35 heavy atoms, four perceived rings and three aromatic rings, versus Parent 31 heavy atoms and four aromatic rings. Seed 0 builds a nitrogen-rich densely fused/bridged system with ester/ketone, propyl and tert-butyl regions; its 32-heavy-atom leader has six perceived rings including a four-membered closure. Seed 1 builds a 35-heavy-atom, three-azaaryl arrangement with an O-CH2-N=CH linkage, nitrile and thiocyanate groups, aryl bromine, formate ester and a four-membered oxygen-containing fused closure. Carbon-linked nitrile and sulfur-linked thiocyanate are different groups. Seed 2 instead retains an allene/vinyl-substituted nitrogen-rich dione connected by N-N to an aminoaryl region bearing haloalkyl thioether and thioester groups. The last six digest proposals reflect only that late seed-2 family. Allene presence is 115 of 870 generated records versus Parent 1; large concatenations extend to 119 heavy atoms. Linked aromatic heterocycles are recognizable, but the highly elaborated closures and chemically labile attachments keep synthesis questionable.
liabilities: O-CH2-N=CH imine-containing linkage, formate ester and sulfur-linked thiocyanate require separate hydrolytic/reactivity assessments; none is proven unstable from its SMILES alone.
O-Cl/O-Br alternatives, halogenated thioesters, N-N connections and substituted allenes survive alongside stronger labels. The inherited sulfur envelope is not a whole-molecule stability test.
Size extends far beyond the compact leaders; the 230-character digest maximum is string length, not a synthetic accessibility measure.
missing_features: Stable conventional linkages preserving the linked azaaryl/nitrile arrangement are not consistently demonstrated at the leading label; the record does not reveal a uniquely required scaffold.

Conformational and synthetic access to the fused four-membered closures and large concatenated systems is unverified. The output already contains substantial heterocyclic variety, so more rings alone is not a supported need.
Allene axial configuration and haloalkyl stereochemistry are unspecified when meaningful; the observed labels do not establish their importance.

per_task.generated_character: Aromatic regions associated with available aliphatic nitrogen centres dominate the strongest labels. Generated median size is 29 heavy atoms with three perceived rings and two aromatic rings. Seed 0 ends at a 23-heavy-atom aryl imine joined to another aryl region through methylene, with allylic/propyl groups and a fused four-membered carbon ring. Seed 1 gives a 29-heavy-atom diaryl diaza ring with exocyclic alkene and a sulfoxide-containing side chain; the shared N-C-N carbon is an aminal-like environment, and both carbon and sulfoxide stereogenicity are unspecified. Seed 2 gives a 27-heavy-atom N-propyl pyrrolidine attached to a fluorinated bridged biaryl carbon system with primary aminopropyl and aryl bromide groups. Its five perceived rings include redundant closures. This is recognizably amine-containing medicinal chemistry with separate imine, aminal, stereochemical and geometric concerns. Basic nitrogen generation is clearly an existing capability despite entirely neutral notation.
liabilities: The imine-containing seed-0 family, aminal-like diaza ring, sulfoxide configuration and densely closed fluorinated biaryl framework pose different chemistry questions and should not be treated as one liability.
Unassigned centres occur in 820 of 870 Child generated records versus Parent 839. Decreased small-unsaturated-ring flags, 3 versus 171, do not constitute a geometry or synthesis validation.
missing_features: Defined stereochemical identities and demonstrated conformations are absent for the successful saturated/bridged amines: 213 of 217 high-score generated records have perceived unassigned centres.

Consistently conventional and accessible realizations of the aromatic/available-nitrogen arrangement remain unresolved. There is no supported missing capability to generate basic amines or aromatic rings.
An exact absent target pharmacophore cannot be identified from these scores; neutral SMILES also do not establish the evaluated protonation state.

per_task.generated_character: Nitrogen/carbonyl rings linked to aromatic or azaaromatic regions dominate. Median generated size is 29 heavy atoms, four perceived rings and two aromatic rings. The seed-1 30-heavy-atom leader links ethoxyphenyl to a fused heterocycle containing cyclic carbamate, lactam and N-methyl/N-propyl nitrogen segments. Seed 0 makes an indazole-like aromatic region attached to an unsaturated medium nitrogen ring with dicarbonyl, alkyl and amino functionality. Conventional amide/carbamate fragments coexist with unusual connected ring geometry, so their complete synthesis remains uncertain.
liabilities: Dense fusion, unsaturated medium rings, and N-N-containing alternatives require whole-ring evaluation; recognizable carbonyl fragments do not validate their geometry.

Small-unsaturated-ring SMARTS flags occur in 76 Child records versus Parent 46, and N-N presence falls from 301 to 131. These describe motif redistribution, not a uniform improvement in chemical plausibility.

Conformation and synthetic access to unsaturated connected medium rings remain unverified; there is no shortage of rings, amides or nitrogen.

Some leading arrangements require stereo specification while the strongest seed-1 leader has no perceived tetrahedral centre; this gap is conditional, not universal. No exact missing target motif is supported.

per_task.generated_character: Compact fluorinated nitrogen-rich imino/carbonyl systems dominate, with generated median 27 heavy atoms, three perceived rings and two aromatic rings. Seed 0 has a phenol-linked aromatic-labelled nine-membered nitrogen ring bearing imino/carbonyl, N-F and fluorinated alkenyl substitution. transferable_gaps.evidence: Originally reported for n-c55c3d520a2c, carried through n-62daf219c70a and the published n-1744a1494180 molecular assessment, and re-observed in n-6ebafca203bf under the current profile, Search seeds 0/1/2, 300 observations including ten initial per objective and matched sulfur-gated Parent. These are conditional output associations; the hybrid residual law, original mean and inherited gate are not separately attributed. Across 4350 generated observations, direct N-halogen presence is Child 938 versus Parent 786 and O-halogen presence 262 versus 217. Sulfur-halogen presence falls from 93 to 8, while N-halogen amides, ring N-F and O-Cl/O-Br alternatives remain among stronger labels. Non-N-halogen amides and near-ceiling aryl amines provide counterexamples to universal dependence on the suspicious attachment.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably preserve conventional local functional-group environments while modifying productive aromatic and heterocyclic arrangements.

nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

approach.method_basis: The Parent alternates neural proposals with two graph refinement phases, learns from exact accepted molecular trajectories using rank-weighted trajectory balance and a joint normalizer, and regularizes the adapting policy toward a frozen corpus-trained prior. A fingerprint Gaussian posterior chooses graph offspring for evaluation while preserving the first fresh-policy handoff. The reusable prior is selected along unchanged unlabeled training by valid, connected, unique generation yield, with original holdout loss breaking ties. During a neural phase the current sampler uses only the adapted policy distribution; the frozen reference influences learning but does not directly participate in token selection.
approach.novelty: Anchor each neural token draw to the frozen reference by using the normalized geometric mean of the adapted-policy and prior probabilities at the same generated prefix. This keeps both the learned score preference and the reference in the actual sampling distribution. The earlier children changed prior preparation, replay allocation, KL direction or trajectory-balance credit; this one preserves the Parent learning stack and changes only ancestral generation. Lower reference divergence is tested directly on the sampled prefixes, while novel molecular yield, graph-feedback transfer and endpoint score remain separate empirical questions.

nodes.hypothesis: Generate neural proposals ancestrally from the normalized geometric mean of the adapted-policy and frozen-prior next-token distributions at each shared generated prefix, with equal fixed exponents and unchanged accepted-score learning.

finding_summary.headline: Geometric anchoring improved valid-novel yield but weakened neural scores and missed the mean-score gain
finding_summary.insights: Direct reference anchoring can substantially improve syntactic and novelty yield at generated prefixes while attenuating useful accepted-score adaptation. The effect was strongest after the first adapted-policy batch: later valid-novel yield rose from 64.00% to 85.42%, while later accepted neural mean score fell from 0.211885 to 0.160124. Graph feedback continued to train the policy: all 6,480 nonterminal graph-bearing replay steps had nonzero graph-only gradients, and exact accepted graph log likelihood increased by 0.180643 on average per training exposure. The weaker downstream family overlap and scores therefore occurred despite active graph learning. Ring-core overlap is a descriptive connection, not proof of causal or functional transfer. The extra raw yield did not expand the evaluated neural stream under this sampler. Both runs emitted exactly 1,500 neural molecules from 150 calls and needed no additional sampling call. The valid surplus discarded after filling a batch increased from 6,491 to 8,819. Mean active sequence length shortened from 59.409 to 48.290 draws including EOS, but measured neural-phase generation time rose from 14.608 to 27.896 seconds across the runs, including diagnostic overhead. This narrows the result: improved parser/novelty yield alone was not a limiting resource for these full batches. The supplied chemistry assessment describes broad ring-rich output with ordinary medicinal motifs alongside reactive bonds, unusual heteroatom bonding, uncontrolled growth and absent stereochemical specification. Those combined neural/graph outputs do not establish that the extra unscored valid draws preserve useful functional context. The experiment supports the conditional distribution effect and higher raw yield, while leaving useful molecular transfer and search advantage unsupported. It does not show that the adapted weights stayed closer to the prior; the KL comparison holds the generated prefix fixed and compares two sampling distributions at that prefix.
finding_summary.results: The intended sampling mechanism activated. Across 12,000 raw neural sequences and 579,478 active token prefixes, the recorded behavior distribution differed from the adapted policy. On those same prefixes, mean KL divergence to the frozen prior fell from 0.182477 for the adapted-policy endpoint to 0.040980 for behavior; mean behavior/policy L1 distance was 0.144892. Every raw sequence had lower average behavior-to-prior divergence. All 150 saved audit prefixes reconstruct the registered geometric midpoint. Valid-novel raw yield rose from 7,991/12,000 (66.59%) to 10,319/12,000 (85.99%), improving in all three seeds and all five tasks. Invalid draws fell from 3,807 to 1,680, unterminated draws from 37 to zero and duplicates from 165 to one. However, mean accepted neural score fell from 0.204941 to 0.158382. Among 1,350 later neural emissions, exact ring-core overlap with previously trained graph molecules fell from 53 to 39. The three-seed mean final-best score was 0.542371 versus the parent's 0.550198, a paired change of -0.007826; population standard deviations were 0.030347 and 0.021738. Paired macro changes were +0.009185, -0.078386 and +0.045722. Task-mean changes were -0.020870 for zaleplon, -0.052561 for scaffold hopping, -0.012984 for DRD2, -0.004175 for median similarity and +0.051459 for sitagliptin. Every task completed all 300 evaluations.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich medicinal motifs coexist with reactive bonds, difficult polycycles and absent stereochemical specification.
molecular.overall_character: The evaluated proposals cover aromatic ethers, azaheterocycles, amines, amides, sulfones, fluorinated heterocycles and densely fused or bridged rings. Each task digest contains 900 evaluated molecules, including 870 optimizer proposals. Across the task digests, ring-closure rates run from 0.9747 to 0.9966 and aromatic-presence rates from 0.9448 to 0.9839; these are fractions of proposal SMILES containing the relevant text, not ring counts or aromatic atom fractions. Mean SMILES lengths range from 43.7 to 65.4, with some much larger assemblies. Every stereocentre_rate is 0.0, despite structures with stereogenic ring junctions and substituted saturated atoms. The overall chemical vocabulary is broad, while the digest high-scoring sets repeatedly concentrate in particular scaffold families and seeds. Ordinary medicinal functional groups coexist with peroxides, terminal imines, unusual sulfur bonding, phosphines, N-fluorinated rings and small strained heterocycles. Compared with Parent n-dd7b8aa31113, the prominent families change, but neither chemical plausibility nor stereochemical completeness is consistently established. These are assessments of the evaluated molecular outputs; their trajectory source labels do not separate neural proposals from graph descendants, and they do not establish raw-generation validity or mechanism activation.

per_task.generated_character: The strongest digest family consists of moderately sized pyridine/phenyl aromatic assemblies joined by a biaryl bond and a benzyl ether, with ethoxy or methoxy substituents and frequent halogens. CCOc1ccc(-c2ccccc2COc2cc(Cl)ccn2)cn1 has recognizable aryl-ether chemistry, aromatic nitrogen acceptors and no strongly basic aliphatic amine or carbonyl. Some close relatives add an amino group or close additional rings. Other seeds also explore substituted indole carboxamides and more elaborate fused heterocycles. The low end includes very large polyamide/polyamine assemblies, polyhydroxylated carbohydrate-like structures and a long-chain phosphorus/quaternary-ammonium/silicon compound. The optimizer ring-closure rate is 0.9885, aromatic-presence rate 0.9759 and mean SMILES length 43.7. The leading ether structures appear substantially more synthetically conventional than the oversized and unusually fused excursions.
liabilities: Aromatic-heavy structures and peripheral halogen/linker edits dominate the leading family; the output does not establish solubility, conformational preference or a synthesis route.
Large fragment combinations add long chains, numerous polar groups or unusual phosphorus/silicon/charge combinations while losing the favorable score range.
missing_features: The low-scoring large structures fail to retain the economical aromatic/acceptor arrangement and limited side-chain size seen in the stronger ether family.
The leading family shows little saturated stereodefined shape variation; whether such alternatives would improve this objective is unmeasured, rather than an established requirement.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The digest spans 0.0 to 0.475614712250357, with median 0.151051. The leading aromatic ether scores 0.475614712250357, whereas the long-chain charged phosphorus/silicon structure scores 0.0 and the large polyamine/amide assembly scores 2.5085649778800826e-59. A close local comparison changes only ethoxy to propoxy on the chlorinated biaryl ether: 0.46457806514522626 becomes 0.3189563030428961. This supports a preference for a specific modest-size substitution pattern rather than indiscriminate chain growth. In the matched Parent seed-2 trajectory, the best molecule was a carbonyl- and nitrile-bearing bicyclic nitrogen scaffold at 0.46457806514522626; the Child seed-2 ether family reaches 0.475614712250357. Different functional-group families can therefore occupy a similar score range, and these data do not establish an obligatory missing amide, nitrile or particular unseen pharmacophore.

per_task.generated_character: The leading digest family is a medium-to-large aromatic anilino-thienopyrimidine series, bearing phenyl or heteroaryl substituents, methoxy, methyl and halogens. Its ring nitrogens and anilino NH provide an organized acceptor/donor pattern, but many leading members also contain a terminal methylene imine or an aryl methyl peroxide. The simpler aryloxy members have familiar medicinal-chemistry connectivity. Other seeds develop much larger fused azaaromatic, urea/formamide and repeated polycyclic assemblies, including the long final seed-2 molecule cited here. The low end instead includes cyclic sulfones, sulfonamides, acids and flexible sulfone-linked aromatic structures. Ring-closure rate is 0.9908, aromatic-presence rate 0.9839 and mean SMILES length 65.4; the maximum is 187 characters. The scaffold vocabulary is plausible, but the peroxide/imine substitutions and complex final assemblies make overall synthetic plausibility questionable.
liabilities: The terminal methylene imines and explicit O-O bonds deserve chemical stability and synthetic scrutiny; no such verification accompanies their scores.
Large fused and repeated azaaromatic assemblies accumulate difficult ring connections and densely substituted nitrogen chemistry without a correspondingly decisive score advantage.
missing_features: The weaker cyclic-sulfone and flexible-chain proposals lack the organized fused azaaromatic/anilino donor-acceptor context shared by the stronger Child family.

Chemically conventional substituent alternatives are not comparably developed across the leading family: high-scoring termini often become imines or peroxides. Their chemical replacement is a quality gap; an objective-score benefit is not established.

The leading Child digest does not reproduce the Parent high-scoring quinazoline/piperazinone arrangement, so the observed family coverage is incomplete rather than demonstrably missing one required atom or group.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The leading imine-bearing anilino-thienopyrimidine scores 0.6720445459737293; its otherwise matching pendant phenyl analogue without fluorine scores 0.6441828361070634. The peroxide analogue scores 0.629303689979929, and a conventional phenoxy analogue scores 0.6254953764861295. Thus high scores coexist with both conventional and chemically concerning substituents; the small numerical differences do not prove the concerning groups are necessary. The cyclic sulfone/carboxylic acid at the low end scores 0.2596495291029798, whereas a very large final azaaromatic assembly still scores 0.594488188976378. The observed gradient emphasizes the particular aromatic nitrogen-rich context more clearly than it enforces simplicity or ordinary peripheral chemistry. Parent seed-1 reached 0.8301591128254581 in a quinazoline/piperazinone-rich family, while Child seed-1 reaches 0.6720445459737293 in the thienopyrimidine series. This is a change in explored high-scoring chemistry, not evidence that adding a particular parent fragment would reproduce its score.

per_task.generated_character: The strongest molecules combine hydrophobic chlorinated aromatic groups with accessible aliphatic amines. They include a flexible aminated tertiary organophosphine, dichlorophenylpiperazines with alkyl chains and unusual C=S(=O) sulfur centers, and larger fused heteroaromatic/aryl amine structures. The seed-2 family combines an arylpiperazine, a secondary amine linker, an aminophenol ring and a halogenated fused heterocycle. These are recognizably amine-rich rather than nitrogen-deficient outputs. The low end instead contains acylated/sulfonylated nitrogens, nitro hydrazones and neutral carbonyl-rich aromatics without the same exposed aliphatic amine context. Ring-closure rate is 0.9747, aromatic-presence rate 0.9448, halogen rate 0.7241 and mean SMILES length 47.9. The charged rate of 0.0126 concerns written formal charges and does not measure how often the neutral amines could protonate.
liabilities: The aminophosphines and C=S(=O)-bearing sulfur structures require more chemical justification than an accepted score provides. Long flexible alkyl branches and alkyl chlorides add further chemical liabilities.
Small N-N ring closures can radically change strain, basicity and geometry. A formal parser-accepted ring does not establish that the intended cyclic-amine chemistry has been preserved.
missing_features: The low-scoring carbonyl/sulfonyl-rich structures lack the exposed non-amide aliphatic amine context present in the strongest molecules; the generator as a whole clearly can produce that context.

Reliable preservation of favorable cyclic-amine topology is missing: the close piperazine-to-small-N-N-ring comparison loses the stronger score despite retaining the surrounding aryl and linker features.
Explicit configurations are absent at substituted saturated centers and ring junctions; no stereochemical preference can be inferred from these unassigned SMILES.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The aminophosphine scores 0.9957613133842727 and the sulfur-bearing arylpiperazine 0.9941946146870084, while the acylated/sulfonylated nitrogen structure scores 3.8021829379963674e-05. This supports accessible aliphatic amine plus hydrophobic aromatic context within the sampled structures, without identifying a binding pose or proving a contribution from phosphorus or unusual sulfur. A particularly informative pair preserves the rest of the seed-2 scaffold: its piperazine-containing molecule scores 0.9889622948332054, but contraction to the small N-N-containing ring in the final digest scores 0.4586415097801264. Correct local ring connectivity and amine spacing matter more than merely retaining nitrogen atoms. The Parent also produced arylpiperazines and bridged basic amines; its seed-2 arylpiperazine reached 0.9999999657062248 without the Child seed-0 phosphine or unusual sulfur motif. Those motifs are therefore not established as missing requirements.

per_task.generated_character: The leading family contains fairly large but compact multicyclic indole-containing scaffolds with fused/bridged saturated or unsaturated ketone rings and an aryl sulfone or sulfonamide linked to benzodioxole. nodes.method_name: Genetic GFN: reciprocal learning between a flow policy and graph search
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Genetic GFN: alternately generate molecules with a GFlowNet policy, refine the resulting scored population through graph crossover and mutation, and distill scored descendants back into the policy using rank-weighted off-policy replay. The policy uses trajectory balance with a learned log normalizer and regularization toward a frozen prior. [Kim et al., Section 3](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.05961v4) describe this mechanism. Train the prior only on the permitted unlabeled corpus. Each objective starts with clean policy adaptation, replay and population state initialized from its supplied observations. Use a positive terminal reward increasing with the observed maximization score. Schedule policy and genetic phases around the evaluator's announced feedback; both produce new molecules, and all reward-bearing training records come from accepted observations. Later policy samples must enter genetic populations, and accepted graph descendants must affect subsequent policy updates. Generate further valid, canonical-unique structures to fill announced batches, without corpus ranking or a fixed molecular library. The hypothesis is that learned global proposals propagate local discoveries into new promising regions and then support further graph refinement, raising the mean of five independent final Top-1 scores. Published larger-budget gains do not establish that this reciprocal learning becomes useful quickly enough here.

approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from a population ranked by real accepted scores. It samples breeding parents across favored score quantiles, uses crossover and successive atom or bond mutations to fill a fresh pool, and checks molecular identity and novelty before admission. A Gaussian process fitted to all accepted task-local labels uses count fingerprints and correlated function draws to choose a unique evaluation batch. Real feedback updates the full training archive and greedily retained breeding population. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled. Each pool is currently discarded after its decision, including every valid molecule that was not selected.
approach.novelty: Give an unselected final molecule one more decision opportunity after real feedback, while generating the entire usual fresh pool first. Append eligible unselected molecules from only the preceding fresh pool in their original order, and let the existing selector decide over the union. Fresh occurrences win duplicate joins; older deferred molecules cannot be carried again. This tests proposal lifetime. The earlier prefix-harvesting sibling instead added intermediate products inside a fixed pool and reduced independent generation attempts; selector-removal, frozen-training and incumbent-targeting siblings changed different consumers. No unselected molecule becomes a label or a breeding parent.

nodes.hypothesis: Extend each valid unselected fresh final proposal to exactly one later suggestion by appending the immediately preceding fresh pool's surviving unselected records after a fully generated current fresh pool, then apply the unchanged current accepted-only correlated posterior selector to that ordered union.

finding_summary.headline: One-round reconsideration produced local gains and descendants but lowered all three seed averages
finding_summary.insights: The result rules out missing exposure, failed revaluation and curtailed fresh output as explanations for the failed endpoint prediction. Useful delayed molecules and extensive descendant ancestry were insufficient to improve the full objective: most delayed evaluations still lost to their original best parent, and one task/seed had no delayed incumbent gain. The matched contrast rejects this fixed one-round lifetime rule under the tested composition; it does not isolate the cost of deferred competition from wider joint draws and the later adaptive trajectories. The passive fresh-only choices have no separately observed outcomes. The chemistry assessment likewise found more distinct core graphs without consistently better leading families: aromatic heterocycles and aryl amines remained prominent, and the strongest Parent arrangements were not reproduced in the tasks with the largest losses. Reactive local bonds, difficult ring geometry and undefined stereochemistry persist alongside more conventional high-scoring examples. Graph diversity and ancestor reachability therefore cannot stand in for reliable endpoint progress or plausible independent chemistry.
finding_summary.results: The lifetime mechanism ran with full fresh generation intact: all 435 decisions first produced 160 fresh proposals. Of 62,105 admitted deferred occurrences, every prediction changed after ten new real labels and 1,315 were evaluated. They produced 46 incumbent improvements; 593 later became breeders, and 2,797 accepted molecules had a delayed ancestor. Yet the complete mean final Top-1 fell from 0.595670 to 0.548956, a paired change of -0.046714 against the required +0.002 gain. All three seed averages were lower; nine of fifteen task/seed endpoints fell and six improved. The largest task-mean losses were sitagliptin_mpo (-0.147107) and deco_hop (-0.080214), while median_2 improved by 0.005534. Seed dispersion decreased from 0.026593 to 0.012479, around a lower mean. All formal evaluations completed within the unchanged budget and limits.

molecular.headline: Aromatic heterocycles and aryl amines span many ring graphs, but reactive bonds, difficult topology and undefined stereochemistry persist
molecular.overall_character: All supplied Child and published Parent trajectories were read: each of the five objectives has 900 Child records, including 870 optimizer records across Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2. No task or supplied trajectory path is missing. The immutable request reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true against n-62daf219c70a, with the same Search Seeds and no profile-mismatched seeds. This supports a complete descriptive chemistry comparison under the frozen Research-in-Depth epoch-1 profile, batch size 10 and 300 observations per task; it does not establish a component contribution or mechanism activation. The authoritative Parent artifacts are the published runs/SPIRAL2/nodes/n-62daf219c70a/seed-*/trajectories files, reached through the supplied artifact list and evidence index. The trusted citation list contains Child trajectories only, so cited_smiles below quote Child records; Parent examples are described with their published seed/evaluation references. The digest final_molecules excerpt is late seed-2 output, not every seed endpoint or every retained incumbent. Full trajectories supply the other seeds. The Child makes indole/pyridine ketones and thioamides, partially saturated aryl amides, linked nitrogen/carbonyl heterocycles, fluorinated amino-enones, cyclic and bridged aryl amines, and fluorinated imino/dione rings. The digest ring-closure-string incidences are 0.9598, 0.9701, 0.9724, 0.9828 and 0.9448 in the fixed task order; aromatic-string incidences are 0.9552, 0.9701, 0.9644, 0.9736 and 0.9356. These are molecule-level text incidences, not ring counts, aromatic-atom fractions or synthetic-feasibility measures. All charged-string and stereocentre-string incidences are 0.0, despite visible protonatable amines and potential stereogenic centres. Bounded CPU RDKit inspection of the supplied graphs confirms substantial ring/topology variation: nonempty typed/generic Murcko scaffold counts in fixed task order are Child 300/146, 470/339, 431/293, 602/421 and 252/114; Parent counts are 294/123, 403/276, 390/258, 583/405 and 207/92. These graph descriptors count changed atom identities and ring connections, including questionable structures; they do not establish independent plausible chemical families. Per-seed high-score neighborhoods remain much narrower than the entire proposal set, while different seed families prevent a claim of global scaffold collapse. Accepted-parent reachability was separately traced in the supplied Child and published Parent logs without missing joins: visibly different aryl-amine leaders in the Child all reach the initial sulfonylated aryl/amide founder, for example. Such genealogical reachability does not prove atom retention, conserved scaffold identity, founder contribution or independent rediscovery. The descriptor and reachability audits are under .slots/L01-resume-20260928/r21-slot0-molecular/. Recognizable medicinal-chemistry frameworks coexist with N-halogen and O-halogen bonds, peroxides, terminal imines, unusual sulfur bonding and complicated unsaturated/bridged rings. Overall plausibility is therefore questionable rather than uniformly implausible: high-scoring conventional amine-containing and liability-free local-bond counterexamples exist. Scores and graph validity do not establish synthesis, stability, conformation, protonation state or biological activity. Historical gaps below retain their source in n-c55c3d520a2c through the n-62daf219c70a baseline; historical profile boundaries are not treated as new matched-effect evidence.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-0 leader at evaluation 281 has 26 heavy atoms and three aromatic rings: a dimethoxy substituted indole-like core connects through a methylene/thioamide segment to pyridine, with both an N-F bond and an N-Br thioamide nitrogen. Seed 1 instead reaches a 24-heavy-atom partially saturated quinoline-like carboxamide with a fluoropyridyl amide, hydroxymethyl group and two aromatic rings at evaluation 293; its other favored family is a diaryl pyrazoline carbothioamide. Current higher-scoring families include N-F/N-Br bonds, N-O-F, peroxides, terminal imines and an unusual C#S-C segment. transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve conventional local bond environments while exploring otherwise useful aromatic, carbonyl and amine arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator would need environment-aware local transformations and conventional bonding alternatives that preserve favorable structural relationships learned from its own accepted feedback. Evaluate such alternatives rather than prescribing a target motif or assuming a blanket functional-group filter improves scores. These output associations do not identify which retained component caused the liabilities or whether proposal lifetime changes their frequency causally.

transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring transformations need a way to preserve useful relationships while accounting for ring size, unsaturation, bridge connectivity and accessible conformation. Plausible alternative connectivities would test this gap without a blanket prohibition on small rings, fusion or ring formation. nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

Connected-fragment crossover with unchanged post-crossover mutation probability and multi-parent opportunities.
Ordinary single-atom replacement plus append, delete, insert, bond-change, ring-open and ring-close mutations, with inherited walk and saturation laws.

approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs using accepted task-local scores. A bounded population supplies parents from high-scoring bands. It generates fresh candidates either by joining connected fragments from two parents or by applying local mutation walks to one parent; direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is already disabled. Stable canonical identity checks and duplicate rejection form a surplus pool. A Gaussian process trained on all earlier accepted scores uses counts of local molecular environments and generalized Tanimoto similarity, and correlated posterior draws choose the evaluated batch. Accepted offspring update both the full prediction archive and the breeding population.
approach.novelty: Remove connected-fragment crossover so that every proposal follows the existing single-parent mutation walk. Ordinary mutation continuation, saturation handling and correlated posterior allocation remain. No completed child of this current baseline is supplied; the parallel children change allocation residuals, while this child changes the generating route. An earlier crossover removal lost endpoint score under a Parent that still allowed direct aromatic exchanges. Reusing that isolated removal on the exchange-free Parent tests whether recombination still contributes after the generator composition changed. The registered prediction is a material score loss, with a complete contrary result also answering the component question.

nodes.hypothesis: Remove two-parent connected-fragment crossover from fresh-pool production, routing every proposal through the inherited single-parent local-mutation walk while retaining the count-based posterior and correlated batch allocation.

finding_summary.headline: Removing crossover lowers the matched mean by 0.054937 despite more local improvements
finding_summary.insights: This complete isolated removal supports a positive contribution of connected-fragment crossover in the current exchange-free search composition. That conclusion concerns the whole adaptive rerouting experiment, including changed ancestors and proposal histories; it does not assign value to an individual fragment or recombinant. A simple diversity-collapse explanation is inadequate: typed emitted cores increase from 1,851 to 1,924 while generic cores decrease from 1,118 to 1,009, and every Child emission retains a ring. Mean molecular size increases even though the extreme size range narrows. Molecular evidence likewise shows rich annulated amide, amine and heterocyclic families, with high-scoring conventional alternatives and persistent reactive bonds, difficult geometry and unspecified stereochemistry. More local wins or more typed cores therefore cannot substitute for the complete endpoint comparison or establish chemical feasibility. Which useful arrangements crossover helps search reach, and how that benefit interacts with the retained posterior and mutation continuation, remain open.
finding_summary.results: Crossover disappears from every one of 73,611 breeding attempts, even though a distinct eligible partner was available each time. The Parent used crossover on 34,334 attempts and evaluated 1,492 crossover offspring. The retained one-parent walks, all seven ordinary mutation families, accepted feedback and correlated posterior selection continue to operate. All three seeds complete. Mean final score falls from 0.595670 to 0.540732, a paired loss of 0.054937 against the registered 0.002 material-loss threshold. Seed losses are 0.112917, 0.004694 and 0.047200. Twelve of fifteen task-seed endpoints fall; median_2 and sitagliptin_mpo improve on seed 1, and zaleplon_mpo improves on seed 2. Population dispersion across seed macros falls from 0.026593 to 0.019996, so the lower dispersion accompanies lower scores. Strict local parent beats nevertheless rise from 629 to 726 and incumbent gains from 258 to 282; those local counts do not predict the endpoint result.

molecular.headline: Rich ring chemistry persists: annulated amides, aryl amines and larger nitrogen rings coexist with reactive bonds and difficult geometry
molecular.overall_character: All fifteen Child and fifteen published Parent trajectory files were present and read. Each task has 900 records, including 870 optimizer proposals, across Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2; no task lacks trajectories. The brief reports complete Child evaluation and complete profile-matched pairing with code Parent n-62daf219c70a, with no profile-mismatched seeds. Comparisons below use those published Parent trajectories. This is an assessment of molecular output under the crossover-removal ticket, not a judgement of mechanism activation or a chemical attribution of the intervention's effect. Every proposal has ring-closure notation, and aromatic-string incidence ranges from 0.9977 to 1.0. These molecule-level text incidences do not measure ring diversity or establish aromatic geometry. The output contains compact indole/annulated aryl amides, extended nitrogen-dione and imine systems, aryl-containing aliphatic amines, large nitrogen-carbonyl rings and sulfur-containing fused or bridged heterocycles. It retains a variety of families across seeds, with narrower variations among leaders within a seed. Removing the named route has not made the observed output ring-deficient or uniformly small; these structures alone cannot identify which route created them. Synthetic plausibility remains questionable and overall drug-likeness weak because familiar amides, amines, ethers and thioethers coexist with N-halogen and O-F bonds, ketenimine or other cumulated unsaturation, peroxides, unusual sulfur bonding and crowded bridges. Important counterexamples are the high-scoring halogen-free annulated amide, the strongest aryl-amine leader without an N-halogen or O-F bond, and larger nitrogen-ring frameworks that outperform some matched Parent examples. Thus neither reactive groups nor smaller size are universal requirements of the observed score gradient. Stereocentre-string incidence is 0.0 throughout despite saturated and bridged potential stereogenic centres. Formal-charge-string incidence is 0.0011 for one task and 0.0103 for another, and 0.0 for the remaining tasks; inspected charged examples are charge-separated diazo groups, not evidence of systematic amine protonation treatment. Ring-bearing molecules also populate the low-scoring tail, so the Parent's tiny-fragment diagnosis cannot be carried over as the principal current chemistry gap. Sizes below are heavy-atom counts from cited trajectory SMILES tokens. No synthesis, physical-property, stereochemical or conformational validation was performed. Digest final excerpts are late seed-2 proposals; full trajectories establish each seed's actual incumbent and endpoint.

Seed 2 reaches a 24-heavy-atom annulated aza-aromatic carboxanilide bearing methoxy and vinyl substituents, with no halogen at all. Mean proposal SMILES length is 43.9, and every proposal has rings and aromatic text. These are compact, recognizable aromatic amide/amidine families, but N-halogen linkers, ring rearrangements and reactive peripheral groups prevent a blanket claim of ordinary synthetic plausibility.
liabilities: N-F amides and N-Cl amidines occur among leaders, and some nearby structures add N-N connections. These require different assessment from ordinary carbon-bound aryl halogens.

The vinyl ether and unusual annulation deserve stability and synthetic-route assessment, while the rare charge-separated diazo proposal is an additional reactive environment rather than a resolved protonation state.
missing_features: Conventional linker alternatives at the leading score are not consistently represented across seeds, although the high-scoring halogen-free annulated amide proves that reactive halogen attachment is not inevitable.

Independent compact frameworks preserving the favorable aromatic/linker organization are less evident among leaders than local ring and substituent variants; the output is not globally scaffold-collapsed.
Configuration and chemical stability of amidine, N-halogen and rearranged nitrogen-ring variants are not specified by the supplied graphs.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Observed in n-767d2ce08797 on Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2 at 300 observations per task, with complete current-profile Parent n-62daf219c70a. The earlier environment gap, sourced to n-c55c3d520a2c and retained in that Parent, persists as N-halogen bonds, O-F, ketenimine and diazo groups, peroxides, acyl fluoride and unusual sulfur-carbon multiple bonding. Counterexamples include a high-scoring halogen-free annulated amide and an aryl-amine leader without N-halogen or O-F. The deficiency is conditional on bond environment, not a failure to produce amides, amines or conventional sulfur chemistry.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve conventional local bond environments while exploring otherwise useful ring and functional-group arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Task-agnostic transformations need plausible local alternatives that preserve favorable relationships learned from feedback while distinguishing ordinary ethers, thioethers and carbon-bound halogens from reactive environments. Preserve the observed conventional alternatives. The records do not establish that a universal filter improves score or identify a particular search component as the chemical cause.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-767d2ce08797, under the supplied Search profile and budget with complete Parent n-62daf219c70a pairing. Current leaders include extended annulations, crowded amine bridges, a large nitrogen-carbonyl ring and a sulfur-containing bridged lactone; ring-closure-string incidence is 1.0 throughout. The geometric concern was already present in the historical n-c55c3d520a2c chemistry, but its particular strongest cyclic cumulene is not the current leader. transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring transformations need geometry-sensitive assessment of connectivity, unsaturation and conformational constraints, alongside alternative topologies preserving learned functional relationships. transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-767d2ce08797 on the supplied three Search Seeds and observation budget, compared with n-62daf219c70a. transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-767d2ce08797 across all supplied Search Seeds at 300 observations per task, continuing the identity gap recorded for n-c55c3d520a2c and n-62daf219c70a. Assess protonation, tautomerism and imine/alkene geometry separately rather than equating formal-charge notation with available basic centres. This is an incompleteness of chemical identity, not an observed stereochemical score penalty or a component attribution.

nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

approach.method_basis: The Parent searches from one scored current molecule. It samples local atom, bond, path and ring edits, including a direct exchange of aromatic nitrogen and carbon that preserves molecular formula. It normalizes molecular identities, rejects duplicates and submits the first complete batch allowed by its short-term memory of inverse local structural changes. After receiving real scores, it moves to the highest-scoring accepted neighbor even when that move is worse than the current state. Exact score ties currently go to the lexically first canonical identity. A separate best-observed archive keeps its own score and canonical tie rule.
approach.novelty: Choose the molecule with the fewest heavy atoms when several accepted neighbors share the exact maximum score, then use the existing canonical ordering if sizes also tie. This lets the walk avoid some neutral graph growth without surrendering the best score available in that accepted batch. Earlier siblings changed edit generation or structural memory; the whole-branch deletion child exposed smaller proposals but often lost score and later regrew. This mechanism instead acts on an already scored tie set. It adds no deletion operator, chemistry filter or size preference outside exact maximum ties.

nodes.hypothesis: Resolve exact ties at the maximum accepted batch score by choosing the candidate with the fewest heavy atoms, then the lexicographically smallest canonical identity, while leaving every non-tied accepted maximum and the independent best archive unchanged.

finding_summary.headline: Six compact tie choices preserved immediate scores, but the panel mean fell
finding_summary.insights: Equal immediate scores do not make tied molecules equivalent starting points for the remaining search. The rule reached smaller real states and preserved the independent archive, so the missing score benefit cannot be explained by a tie implementation failure or an immediate sacrifice in accepted score. The two affected walks ended smaller than their parents yet found lower best scores, narrowing the claim: this size preference controls some neutral growth, but has not identified better future neighborhoods. The chemistry assessment reinforces the distinction between atom count and useful simplification: deco_hop proposals had slightly fewer atoms on average but greater molecular mass and more nitrogen-halogen bonds, while unusual sulfur chemistry persisted. A compact winner can also be a bond change or element substitution. Local chemical organization or neighborhood quality therefore remains a more informative open question than size alone. Six interventions in two overlapping walks do not isolate the contribution of each choice, and the sparse activation does not establish how the rule would behave on other tasks.
finding_summary.results: Six of 28 exact maximum-score ties selected a different molecule, all on deco_hop plateaus in two seeds. Every changed choice preserved the accepted maximum score and used one or two fewer heavy atoms than the lexical winner, saving ten atoms across those decisions. Three choices kept the source size and three reduced it by one atom. All 407 unique maxima retained the same choice on the same accepted batch, and the identity, archive and transition audits passed. Descendants exceeded the compact selected size after five of the six changes; the remaining case finished at that size after five further steps. Later archive improvements occurred, but the complete three-seed macro mean fell from 0.521759 to 0.520655, a paired loss of 0.001104 against the required gain of 0.002. Both affected seeds declined; all four other tasks and the third seed retained exactly the parent's molecule/score sequences.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich, often aromatic molecules with recurrent unusual sulfur, reactive halogen bonds and unresolved stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character: Node n-770a3cefca6a covers every task in the supplied digest; tasks_without_trajectories is empty. The digest contains 900 evaluated molecules and 870 optimizer proposals per task. Its proposal ring_closure_rate is 1.0 throughout; aromatic_atom_rate ranges from 0.7184 to 1.0 and describes the presence of aromatic SMILES tokens, not the fraction of atoms that are aromatic. These are substantial heterocyclic and polycyclic graphs, not small acyclic fragments. Passive RDKit 2023.09.6 parsing of all 4350 proposals succeeds: they contain 21-49 heavy atoms, with median 33, and 2-10 perceived rings, with median 4. Graph parsing does not establish energetic stability or a synthesis. Relatively conventional indole carboxamides coexist with heavily decorated nitrogen heterocycles, sulfur-rich cages, medium-ring bridges, heteroatom-halogen bonds and unusual neutral sulfur multiple bonding. Some individual structures are plausible, but repeated problematic chemistry among the reported high scorers and late proposals supports the overall implausible/weak reading. Diversity is moderate at the graph level across the panel; high scorers within a task frequently remain closely related members of a local family. All proposal charged_rate and stereocentre_rate counters are 0.0. This means no explicit charge or stereochemical labels, not an absence of ionizable atoms or stereogenic graphs: 3432 proposals have potential unassigned stereocentres in the passive audit. Against Parent n-abcd951ab7cc, all molecule/score sequences match exactly on four tasks; only deco_hop seeds 0 and 2 differ. The chemistry comparison below concerns those observed outputs and makes no activation finding. All descriptor counts and parent comparisons are reproducible in .slots/SPIRAL2.r0012-03-improve-L16.molecular-audit.json; they describe proposal occurrences, and perceived ring counts can include overlapping rings in bridged systems. The digest final_molecules are the last proposal records from seed 2, not a selected endpoint or the best archive.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The cited high-score molecules include carbon-sulfur-carbon connectivity with sulfur triple-bonded on both sides, neutral sulfur-sulfur multiple bonds and hydrogen-bearing sulfur in multiply connected ring systems. These occur in graphs that parse successfully, including a recorded 0.6145389662714401 plateau that does not distinguish markedly different sulfur bond orders. The issue is the local bonding environment, not every sulfur-containing group.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator lacks reliable control of chemically conventional sulfur bonding while exploring otherwise useful heteroatom patterns.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Expand access to conventional heteroatom and linker alternatives while retaining the surrounding scaffold, and distinguish unusual sulfur environments from ordinary thioethers, thiocarbonyls and oxidized sulfur groups. Chemical validity needs information beyond successful graph sanitization; the same chemical criterion must apply to every supplied objective.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Passive graph reading finds N-halogen bonds in 628 proposals, O-halogen bonds in 301 and S-halogen bonds in 333 out of 4350 proposals; these categories can overlap. Digest exemplars show N-chloroamides, N-brominated carbonyl heterocycles, O-brominated aryl substituents and sulfenyl chlorides. Some of these liabilities coexist with the highest recorded scores.
transferable_gaps.gap: Halogen placement is insufficiently selective for stable medicinal substituents rather than reactive heteroatom-halogen bonds.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Represent halogen edits with their attachment chemistry intact, and offer matched conventional carbon-bound substitutions or replacements for reactive heteroatom attachments. Use the observed local scores to explore those alternatives without assuming that generic halogen presence is beneficial.

transferable_gaps.evidence: In the changed proposal family, parent-to-child mean heavy atoms decrease from 38.90344827586207 to 38.60344827586207 while calculated mean molecular weight increases from 597.9077586206896 to 618.5739229885057. Elsewhere, a cited 30-heavy-atom high scorer carries five sulfur atoms and six perceived rings, and a 31-heavy-atom high scorer has a network of seven overlapping perceived rings. The recorded chemistry decouples small atom count from tractability.
transferable_gaps.gap: Compact graph size does not reliably produce lower molecular mass, simpler ring topology or easier synthesis.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide chemically complete simplifications and scaffold alternatives that can reduce heavy-element burden, bridge congestion or flexible decoration while retaining observed aromatic, carbonyl and amine relationships. Evaluate chemical simplicity independently of heavy-atom count; no supplied comparison establishes a score gain from a blanket size preference.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every digest reports stereocentre_rate 0.0. Passive perception nevertheless identifies potential unassigned stereocentres in 3432 of 4350 proposals. Cited high-score molecules include graphs with four and seven potential unassigned centres, and a cited final cage has eleven. Thus the missing labels are a molecular-definition gap, not evidence that the search only makes achiral molecules.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not specify stereochemistry for many graphs with potential stereogenic centres.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve or explicitly represent stereochemical choices when edits create, retain or remove stereogenic centres, using only task-independent molecular information and the permitted identity rules. This would improve the specificity of the output; the observed trajectories do not establish a score advantage for stereoisomer enumeration.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The cited comparisons include a compact carbonyl-linked fused aromatic family above enlarged or carbonyl-disrupted variants, and an amine-rich aryl framework whose ring-dearomatized sulfur analogue scores much lower. The top exemplars repeatedly remain within one local structural family, often adding unusual sulfur bonds or bridge congestion. Rings and aliphatic amine centres are already present; their stable arrangement in alternative scaffolds is the incomplete capability.
transferable_gaps.gap: Useful aromatic, carbonyl and amine relationships are insufficiently explored through diverse conventional scaffold alternatives.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Offer scaffold and linker changes that preserve chemically interpretable arrangements of aromatic surfaces, carbonyls and nonacylated amines while changing ring topology or attachment geometry. Let real feedback determine where those arrangements matter; the evidence supports richer conventional alternatives, not a universal pharmacophore or a task-specific motif prescription.

nodes.method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
nodes.method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.

approach.method_basis: NF-BO does Bayesian optimization in a latent space that is exactly invertible. A normalizing flow maps molecular sequences to continuous latents and back with no reconstruction error, so a point chosen in latent space decodes to a definite molecule rather than an approximation. A Gaussian process is fitted over the scored latents, Thompson sampling picks promising directions, and proposals are made by perturbing selected token blocks within a trust region before decoding back through the inverse flow.
approach.novelty: This root commits to choosing which token blocks to perturb by an estimated sequence-level pointwise mutual information rather than uniformly, so the perturbation concentrates on positions the flow considers informative. It also adapts the flow to high-scoring task-local sequences mid-session and re-encodes every observation after each adaptation, which keeps the latent geometry aligned with the current objective instead of frozen at corpus statistics.

nodes.hypothesis: Search around scored task-local molecules in an injective SELFIES SeqFlow latent space, adapt the flow to high-scoring observations, and use a latent GP with Thompson sampling to select fresh trust-region proposals whose perturbed token blocks are chosen from estimated sequence-level PMI before exact inverse-flow decoding.

finding_summary.headline: The only root to fail: the flow adaptation aborted mid-run and two objectives never finished
finding_summary.insights: The failure is not in the idea but in adapting the flow while a session is live. Re-encoding every observation after each adaptation is what makes the latent geometry stay useful, and it is also what puts a failure-prone training step inside the oracle loop, where an abort costs the remaining budget on that objective. The partial results that did land are suggestive, with 0.652 on drd2_docking from only 140 calls, so the approach is not obviously weak. The molecules also show a distinct problem: perturbing token blocks in a SELFIES-based latent produces boron, phosphorus and cumulated-double-bond structures at very high rates. A repair should move adaptation to a batch boundary with a guarded fallback before this lineage is judged on score.
finding_summary.results: The node is recorded buggy with no macro score, and its mechanism is refuted. Three objectives completed their full 290 proposals, but drd2_docking stopped at 140 accepted molecules and median_2 at 230, in both cases when a flow adaptation aborted. Of 129 adaptation attempts only 127 completed. The components that did run checked out: corpus pretraining moved held-out token loss from 15.283 to -3.877, exact left-inverse decoding held with a maximum error of 7.7e-07 at the selected checkpoint, all 840 pointwise mutual information estimates were nondegenerate, and every one of the 124 completed batches emitted exactly the announced ten valid novel molecules.

molecular.headline: Boron, phosphorus and cumulated double bonds: latent perturbation decodes to chemistry that does not exist
molecular.overall_character: This is the most chemically implausible output in the round. Cumulated double bonds, essentially absent from every other root, appear in 42 percent of proposals on one objective and 95 percent on another. Boron appears as a terminal double-bonded atom, phosphorus appears as cationic chains, and charged species reach 88 percent on one objective. Aromatic content runs 31 to 66 percent, and one proposal reaches 239 characters. nodes.method_name: NF-BO: invertible sequence-flow search with token-adaptive latent proposals
nodes.method_thesis: Use NF-BO's SeqFlow mapping, exact left-inverse decoding, and token-adaptive trust-region search. Train a compact SELFIES flow on the permitted unlabeled corpus. Within each fresh objective session, adapt it using highly scored task-local sequences, re-encode all observations after updates, and fit a latent-space GP. Generate new latent proposals around scored observations by perturbing token blocks according to their estimated pointwise mutual information with the decoded sequence. Thompson sampling selects proposals for inverse-flow decoding. These mechanisms follow [NF-BO, Sections 4 and 5.3](https://arxiv.org/html/2504.14889v1). Regenerate as needed to fill the evaluator-announced batch with distinct canonical molecules; no corpus molecules are ranked or retrieved. The hypothesis is that score-directed local search around exactly reconstructable observations finds improving structures efficiently enough to raise the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Exact reconstruction alone is not the objective. Useful flow training and surrogate prediction under the permitted preparation and feedback remain empirical prerequisites.

approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds molecular graphs from a score-ranked population, using crossover and mutation with stable canonical identity checks. It keeps every accepted raw score, refits a Gaussian process on local molecular environment counts, and draws whole prediction functions over a fresh surplus pool. Each requested evaluation goes to the best still-available candidate under one function draw. Accepted outcomes update the archive, raw-score survivors and future breeding population.
approach.novelty: Replace that learner and its sampled functions together with a fixed ensemble of bootstrapped regression trees on exactly the same count vectors. Refit all trees from accepted labels, then choose each evaluation using one uniformly sampled tree over the full pool. This tests a different nonlinear response law after kernel, target, residual-scale and acquisition variants failed. The trees can disagree, but bounded leaf averages and exact ties can also limit exploration; both are measured rather than repaired during the test.

nodes.hypothesis: Replace the active accepted-only count-GP learner and Gaussian function distribution jointly with 128 fixed bootstrapped CART response trees on unchanged Morgan counts, allocating each batch position by the maximum of one uniformly sampled tree function with replacement and original-index exact ties.

finding_summary.headline: Tree functions changed every selected batch, but the paired endpoint mean fell by 0.060977
finding_summary.insights:
Distinct fitted functions and changed evaluation choices were not sufficient for endpoint benefit. Selected-stream mean squared error improved from 0.012718 to 0.010939, while ordering correlation fell from 0.5322 to 0.4474. Every median_2 error improved even though all its endpoints declined. These are different adaptive evaluation streams, so neither the lower error nor the empirical tree spread establishes calibration or explains the total loss. Exact ties, leaf-average support and later search history remain possible contributors whose individual effects were not isolated.

The inherited inputs still merge some distinct molecules: nineteen current alias pairs were observed, but only one pair had both members scored, at an equal value. Trees additionally give equal predictions to many unequal count vectors. Neither representation aliases nor shared leaves prove chemical identity or independent scaffold coverage. Conventional compact indole amides, carbon-bound halogens and available amines coexist with giant linked-ring structures, reactive bonds and difficult bridges. Useful conventional counterexamples rule out a universal need for those liabilities; they do not establish a chemical cause of the score loss.

This result concerns the joint fixed learner and sampled-function law. It does not reverse the useful GP boundary or its conditional component findings, and it does not identify separate effects of trees, bootstrapping, ties or uncertainty. The large runtime spread is preserved: all replicas completed under identical resources, with much of the observed elapsed variation in deco_hop oracle time. Changed molecules and nested instrumentation prevent an isolated learner-speed or chemistry attribution.
finding_summary.results:
All 435 accepted-archive refits and all 55,680 native tree structures reproduced. Every pool contained 128 distinct functions with 7 to 47 distinct first maximizers, and all 435 selected sets differed from both ensemble-mean and generation-order controls. Selection still relied heavily on pool order: 4,092 of 4,350 sampled-function maxima were exact ties. One unselected tree was constant; no entire batch lacked functional exposure. Real feedback remained intact, with 581 parent wins and 252 incumbent advances, compared with 629 and 258 for the Parent.

The complete three-seed mean fell from 0.595670 to 0.534693, a paired loss of 0.060977 against the required gain of 0.002. Seed changes were −0.082304, +0.000169 and −0.100795. Five task/seed endpoints improved: deco_hop seeds 1 and 2, drd2 seed 1, sitagliptin seed 1 and zaleplon seed 2. Ten declined; all five task means and all three median_2 endpoints were lower. The implemented mechanism is confirmed and its endpoint-benefit prediction is falsified.
