molecular.headline: Compact aromatic amides and amines coexist with giant linked heterocycles, reactive heteroatom bonds and difficult bridges
molecular.overall_character: All fifteen Child and fifteen published Parent task/seed trajectories were read: 4,500 observations per arm, including 4,350 evaluated optimizer offspring per arm. All five tasks and issued Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2 are covered; context.comparison reports complete Child evaluation and complete matched Parent pairing with n-62daf219c70a. No required trajectory or comparison is absent. The output contains indole anilides, aza-aromatic ketones and thioamides, repeated nitrogen-dione systems, extended polyaryl lactones, cyclic aryl amines, bridged nitrogen-carbonyl frameworks and fluorinated imino/enol heterocycles. There is abundant ring chemistry: digest ring-closure incidence is 0.9977 to 1.0 and aromatic-text incidence 0.9839 to 1.0 across evaluated optimizer proposals. These are incidences of SMILES text features, not perceived ring counts or aromatic-atom fractions. Compact leaders with 23 to 35 heavy-atom tokens coexist with two linked-heterocycle leaders with 104 and 115 tokens. Size statements count heavy-atom tokens in actual SMILES; no conformation or synthesis calculation was performed. Ring systems and aromaticity are rich, synthetic plausibility is questionable and drug-likeness weak overall. Recognizable amides, carbon-bound halogens, ethers and amines provide favorable conventional counterexamples, but other high-scoring structures retain N-halogen or O-Cl bonds, unusual sulfur valence, very short bridges, crowded unsaturation or enormous repeated aromatic regions. Diversity is moderate across tasks and seeds, with narrower related families among leaders within a seed; distinct strings, folded fingerprints and tree predictions do not establish independent scaffold coverage. Every task has zero stereocentre and formal-charge text incidence. Potentially stereogenic and protonatable structures nevertheless occur; unspecified identity is not evidence of absent amines or a measured protonation/stereochemical penalty. The accepted-provenance audit joins each of the 4,350 observed offspring to its same-batch emitted identity, sampled function selection and earlier real breeding-parent observations. All fifteen first endpoint leaders were immediately admitted to survival. Immediate admission is not a claim about every later population. Initial molecules are identified separately; trajectory final rows are late evaluations, not necessarily retained leaders. The selector is the joint replacement of the learner and function-sampling law by 128 native bootstrap CART trees on inherited folded Morgan occurrence counts, with one uniformly sampled fitted tree function per batch position. Predictions are in raw-score units; logged spread is empirical tree-population dispersion, not Gaussian posterior uncertainty or established calibration. The raw accepted scores and endpoint definition remain unchanged. In the current logs, 4,092 of 4,350 selected available maxima are tied and are resolved by original pool order. This is descriptive selection provenance, not evidence that tied molecules are identical or that order, bagging or any isolated constituent caused endpoint behavior. Count aliases can persist, and different count vectors can also share tree leaves. Unselected pool candidates, passive mean choices and alternative tree choices have no counterfactual oracle labels or independent rollout here. The inherited breeding, ordinary mutation/crossover, identity rules and raw-score survival remain relevant to the observed families. A matched whole-node Parent comparison does not isolate the chemical contribution of the learner, bootstrap, function law or inherited components. Published Parent chemistry is the comparison baseline; its carried gaps originated in n-c55c3d520a2c and were reproduced by the same-code n-62daf219c70a baseline, not independently rediscovered there. The current panel supplies new conditional chemistry observations without rewriting that history. The successful resource receipt records 6 CPUs, one A40 and 16,000 MB for each replica, with elapsed times 00:41:07, 00:05:05 and 00:49:55. Their spread is retained as execution context without chemical or computational causal attribution. Scores and structural associations below do not establish synthesis, stability, conformation, biological activity, mechanism activation or eligibility. Evidence and reproducible audits are in .slots/r0020-01-improve-L01/molecular/trajectory_audit.json and accepted_provenance_audit.json; source hashes include the immutable brief, current logs, Parent evidence and resource receipt.

per_task.generated_character: All 870 evaluated optimizer proposals contain ring-closure and aromatic text; halogen incidence is 0.9586. Seed 0 evaluation 203 is a compact 23-token dimethyl/hydroxymethyl N-H indole anilide with carbon-bound fluorine and an ordinary secondary amide. This is a comparatively plausible conventional counterexample to a universal reactive-bond requirement. Seed 1 evaluation 299 is another 23-token structure, an aza-aromatic fused/partially unsaturated system bearing a ketone-linked fluoroethylpyridyl group rather than an amide. Seed 2 evaluation 292 has 26 tokens, vinyl/alkyl substitution, an N-hydroxy fused nitrogen ring and an N-chloroamide linked to fluoropyridine. missing_features: The panel does not consistently reproduce favorable aryl/amine arrangements in independently plausible ring geometries and ordinary sulfur environments across seeds; useful amine functionality itself is already present.
Potentially stereogenic amine-adjacent and bridged centres remain unspecified, and neither the text nor the scores establish protonation state or bound conformation.

The seed-2 sulfur/amine leader reaches 0.7053251580843446. Its later O-N/S-connected relative at evaluation 296 scores 0.07492752058572245, and a much larger fused aromatic/amine variant at evaluation 297 scores 0.47675345676884856. The N-sulfonyl pyrrolidinemethanol at seed 2 evaluation 25 scores only 0.0002239457302601391. Favorable structures often retain aryl regions and available aliphatic nitrogen, but the initial conventional amine-containing molecule at seed 0 evaluation 6 scores 0.0003786988088202195, so amine presence alone is insufficient. Matched seed 0/1/2 final Top-1 values are Child 0.9950567809473136, 0.9999948312113772, 0.7053251580843446 versus Parent 0.9999989177995104, 0.9969753164881906, 0.9999934235240012. per_task.generated_character: Ring, aromatic and branch text each occur in 0.9989 of evaluated optimizer proposals, whereas halogen incidence is only 0.2011. The first leaders have 31, 35 and 34 heavy-atom tokens in seeds 0, 1 and 2. Seed 0 evaluation 264 combines two aromatic regions, propyl/ethoxy substitution, a tertiary nitrogen-containing fused/bridged ring system and one ketone; it is not a dicarbonyl leader. Seed 1 evaluation 298 contains an N-N-linked medium dicarbonyl ring connected through an aminoalkene to a diaryl O/N-bridged framework. Seed 2 evaluation 233 retains a nitrogen-dione region and an O-C-O bridge in a crowded diaryl system. Recognizable ether, carbonyl and amine groups are present, but their global ring arrangement is more questionable than these local groups. The first leaders follow logged insert-atom, append-atom and insert-atom events respectively, on real accepted relatives, and were admitted to survival.
liabilities: Crowded fused/bridged unsaturation and N-N-containing medium rings make graph-level validity an inadequate proxy for synthetic plausibility.
Both context-poor fragments and large duplicated frameworks receive low scores; a fixed preference for small or large molecules is unsupported.
missing_features: Coverage is incomplete for simpler, independently plausible connectivities that preserve the favorable multi-region aromatic/nitrogen/carbonyl context without accumulating difficult bridges or dimer-like growth.
The records leave bridge stereochemistry and geometric feasibility unresolved, and do not isolate a single missing functional group shared by all seed endpoints.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The seed-0 ketone leader scores 0.22421360157322032 versus 0.22283778663202786 for its one-carbon-contracted accepted parent at evaluation 201 and 0.22109504077434303 for the N-N-containing relative at evaluation 263. These nearby scores show several ring arrangements retain some favorable context, not that one nitrogen substitution is universally required. Seed-1 and seed-2 leaders score 0.21645935471676658 and 0.20920617393575747. per_task.generated_character: Evaluated optimizer proposals are predominantly aromatic and ring-containing, with incidences 0.9839 and 0.9977; halogen incidence is 0.7954 and cumulated-double-bond text incidence 0.023. Seed 0 evaluation 262 has 24 heavy-atom tokens: an imidazole-like aromatic ring, conjugated aminoalkene region, N-methylamide, fluorinated alcohol side chain and N-F bond. Its ring-opening lineage connects it to the accepted fused-ring parent at evaluation 250. Seed 1 evaluation 282 has 28 tokens: fused sulfur/nitrogen carbonyl rings, exocyclic imine/enol-like groups, N-Br, a fluorinated hydroxyl-bearing centre and carbon-bound bromine/fluorine; it was observed after crossover plus atom replacement. Seed 2 evaluation 282 has 29 tokens: a crowded fused nitrogen-dione/amine framework with unsaturated small rings and enol/imino groups. Its fluorines are carbon-bound, an important counterexample to a universal N-F requirement, though its topology remains questionable. It follows crossover of accepted parents. All three first leaders were immediately admitted to survival.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This gap originated in n-c55c3d520a2c and was carried by the same-code n-62daf219c70a Parent. In the new n-7922cfd1903a panel, high-scoring accepted and retained structures include N-F, N-Cl, N-Br, O-Cl and unusual doubly carbon-unsaturated sulfur environments. Conventional secondary amide and carbon-bound-halogen leaders also occur; one compact O-Cl-free structure ties an O-Cl relative, and another fluorinated leader has only carbon-bound fluorine. These current Search-Seed observations at 300 evaluations per task establish conditional local liabilities, not a universal need to remove halogens or heteroatoms.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve conventional local bond environments while adapting favorable aromatic, amine and carbonyl frameworks.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide bond-environment-aware alternatives that preserve useful relationships learned from real local feedback, including ordinary carbon-bound halogens and available nitrogen centres. Evaluate plausible substitutions through the same authorized feedback, without assuming a blanket filter improves scores. The chemistry association neither identifies a responsible learner constituent nor transfers an earlier component finding to the joint tree selector.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The Parent inherited a geometry gap from n-c55c3d520a2c. Current accepted leaders again include very short carbon or oxygen bridges, crowded nitrogen/carbonyl ring systems and small unsaturated rings; low-scoring later relatives include cyclic cumulation and ring reorganizations. A compact conventional indole amide also remains favorable, and the Parent has a high-scoring unusual cyclic-cumulene exception. Thus strained-looking graphs are neither universally necessary nor uniformly penalized by the observed objectives.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generated ring graphs do not consistently establish credible bridge geometry, unsaturation or stereochemical identity.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring transformations need size-, bridge- and bond-geometry awareness and feasible alternative connectivities that retain learned functional context. Preserve access to ordinary fused and saturated rings. Structural feasibility needs its own check; neither SMILES validity nor a high score establishes it, and these observations do not prove a score gain from any particular restriction.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This representation gap was recorded in n-c55c3d520a2c and its same-code Parent. Every current task again has stereocentre and formal-charge text incidence 0.0 across its 870 evaluated optimizer proposals, although saturated fluorinated centres, bridged centres and recognizable protonatable amines occur. The current score records do not compare stereoisomers or establish protonation or tautomer populations.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output leaves potentially stereogenic centres unspecified and does not establish the chemical microstates represented by neutral text.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve or resolve stereochemical identity where chemically meaningful, treating achiral and configurationally unstable cases appropriately. Assess protonation and tautomer identity separately from charge-marker absence; do not infer that neutral strings lack basic nitrogen. This is an identity/coverage limitation with no measured score penalty or isolated model attribution.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The original n-c55c3d520a2c gap, reproduced in n-62daf219c70a, included both fragmentation and overgrowth. The current panel changes its emphasis: two endpoint leaders contain 104 and 115 heavy-atom tokens, and a 120-token relative exactly ties the latter, while a 31-token leader in the same objective is also favorable. Elsewhere 48-, 51-, 59- and 64-token linked structures score poorly compared with compact leaders. Rings and aromatic text are almost universal in this panel, so the older tiny-fragment observation must not be generalized into a current absence of aromatic context.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably control excessive elaboration while retaining the functional context of useful compact molecules.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Use real feedback to preserve useful multi-region context while offering simplifications and nonduplicative replacements. The missing capability is consistent context-sensitive control, not the ability to make either small molecules or large rings. Do not infer a universal size cutoff, score advantage for compactness, or causal responsibility of bootstrap trees from these whole-node observations.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The coverage gap originated in n-c55c3d520a2c and was repeated in the same-code Parent. Current leaders within a seed often vary side-chain length, halogen identity, one ring atom or bridge connectivity; several distinct structures tie raw endpoints. Across seeds there are nevertheless compact amides, linked thioamides, very large polyaryl systems, cyclic amines and nitrogen-carbonyl frameworks, so global structural collapse is unsupported. The accepted provenance shows real exposure and survival for the quoted leaders, not a catalogue of all unselected pool chemistry or independent efficacies.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently supply chemically independent, plausible alternatives within each leading family.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Develop feasible scaffold replacements that retain task-local favorable chemical relationships, then assess their real accepted outcomes. Distinct SMILES, finite folded-count identities, equal predictions or shared tree leaves are not measures of chemically independent coverage. Unscored mean or alternative-tree choices cannot supply a counterfactual chemistry benefit; keep the original source and these applicability conditions with this gap.

nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds a live population of scored molecular graphs. It samples parents from high-scoring bands, generates offspring through crossover or short sequences of atom and bond mutations, and fills a fresh pool with valid, novel identities. Only the final product of each ordinary mutation sequence is offered to that pool. A Gaussian-process predictor fitted to all real accepted scores uses folded local count fingerprints and correlated posterior draws to select the evaluation batch. Newly accepted offspring enter the full score archive and compete for the score-greedy survivor population, allowing useful descendants to become later parents. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled; identity checks, continuation, retries and crossover finishing mutation remain active.
approach.novelty: Make successful intermediate products of ordinary mutation sequences available to the existing pool selector. Finish the entire original sequence, offer its final product first, then offer earlier successful products from latest to earliest under the same validity and novelty gates. This preserves continuation while exposing molecules it currently passes over. It differs from shortening mutation sequences, adding a new graph move, changing breeding preference or rewarding unscored intermediates. Intermediate products occupy some slots that would otherwise require independent final proposals, so increased path coverage can help or hurt the complete search.

nodes.hypothesis: After each complete inherited ordinary single-parent mutation chain, offer its original final product first and then its proper successful graph snapshots in reverse chronological order to the same bounded novel-candidate pool, without shortening or extending the chain.

finding_summary.headline: Harvested prefixes reached real feedback and breeding, but the paired mean endpoint fell by 0.040930
finding_summary.insights:
Making earlier products visible can expose useful molecules without improving the overall search. Among 49 same-attempt pairs where both prefix and final were actually scored, prefixes won 34, lost ten and tied five. These selected, dependent comparisons do not describe all intermediates. The only prefix that first attained a session endpoint was a zaleplon product whose original final remained unscored; that session still finished below its matched Parent. Across the whole Child, parent wins rose from 629 to 722 and incumbent advances from 258 to 306, yet the complete endpoint mean declined. The retained GP also had lower error on its changed evaluated stream, which cannot establish a better model or explain the loss.

The result applies to this one final-first/reverse-prefix collection rule. Prefix occupancy, fewer independent attempts and later adaptive histories changed together, so their separate effects remain unresolved. It does not reverse the earlier positive contribution of retaining ordinary continuation or justify assuming shallower products are better. Chemical counterexamples reinforce that boundary: a higher-scoring prefix retains an acyl fluoride, while another oxygen-ring prefix loses substantially to its sulfur-ring final. Conventional indole amides and useful aryl amines coexist with reactive bonds, excessive elaboration, difficult rings and unspecified stereochemistry. Extra path coverage did not establish chemical feasibility or independent scaffold coverage. Higher-floor recovery and mutation-call exhaustion were tested only in isolated controls, not naturally exercised here.
finding_summary.results: The full inherited mutation chains ran, and 7,287 proper intermediate products entered the fixed pools. Of 461 evaluated prefixes, 78 beat their generating parent, 353 lost and 30 tied; 29 advanced the incumbent. After feedback, 370 survived their batch and 294 later bred in 10,630 actual parent draws. All 435 pools filled. Multiple admissions reduced independent generation attempts from 75,961 to 67,373, without shortening any completed chain. All three matched replicas completed. Mean final score fell from 0.595670 to 0.554740, a paired loss of 0.040930 against the required gain of 0.002. Seed changes were −0.089537, +0.003553 and −0.036805. Four task/seed endpoints improved—zaleplon seed 0, drd2 and sitagliptin seed 1, and median_2 seed 2—while eleven declined. The mechanism is confirmed and its endpoint-benefit prediction is falsified.

molecular.headline: Indole amides and aryl amines coexist with reactive halogens, oversized heterocycles and unspecified stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: All fifteen Child and fifteen published Parent trajectory files were read, covering Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2 with 300 observations per task/seed. The fresh brief marks complete Child evaluation and complete matched pairing to n-62daf219c70a, with no profile mismatch or missing trajectory. Each task has 900 records, including 870 evaluated optimizer proposals. The digest counters describe those evaluated proposals, not every unscored pool molecule or intermediate graph. Their ring-closure text incidence is 0.9655 to 0.9862 and aromatic-text incidence 0.9598 to 0.9816; charge and stereocentre text incidence are zero throughout. These incidences do not count perceived rings, aromatic-atom fractions, stereoisomers or protonation states. Sizes below are heavy-atom-token counts from the actual SMILES. The output includes compact indole amides, amidines, aryl aminoalkyl compounds, medium nitrogen rings, crowded fused nitrogen-carbonyl systems and extensively linked ester/imine/heterocyclic assemblies. Ring chemistry and aromaticity are rich. Synthetic plausibility is questionable and overall drug-likeness weak because recognizable compounds coexist with N-halogen, O-F/O-Cl, acyl-halide, peroxide and unusual sulfur multiple-bond environments, difficult bridges and excessive elaboration. Diversity is moderate across tasks/seeds and narrower among each seed's leaders; there is no basis to equate extra path positions with independent scaffold diversity. Every accepted offspring was joined by session, batch and emitted identity to its actual pool role and earlier scored parents: 4,350 joins comprise 2,429 ordinary finals, 1,460 crossover finals and 461 proper prefixes. Full ordinary effort comes only from 37,238 ordinary_mutation_chain records: 44,942 mutate calls and 56,618 inner attempts. Per-product traces overlap or truncate these chains and must not be summed as additional effort. There are 7,704 successful proper intermediate positions from 6,620 chains; 7,287 enter the fixed pools, while 362 are duplicates, 3 invalid and 52 overflow. Only 461 pool-admitted prefixes are evaluated. Among them, 374 have immediate survivor-admission receipts, 78 beat their generating parent and 29 advance the incumbent. Later accepted-descendant records reuse 157 as parents; this is observed-parent reuse, not an exhaustive count of all breeding draws. Immediate admission is not permanent retention. The earliest molecule attaining each final session-best score is a crossover final in seven sessions, ordinary final in seven and proper prefix in one. Later tied endpoint molecules can have different roles, including a proper-prefix amidine. No natural higher-floor ordinary chain or stopped-on-failure chain appears in the audited panel; synthetic implementation controls are not outcome evidence for those cases. There are 49 same-attempt prefix/final pairings where both products received real labels: 34 prefixes score higher, 10 lower and 5 tie. These selected, dependent pairings are not an estimate over all intermediates and do not identify the overall intervention's benefit. The per-task examples retain both directions. Unselected intermediate or final products have no counterfactual score here. A successful graph step, admission, parent win or ancestry is not proof of chemical improvement. One prior snapshot's checked serialization differs from its later admitted text; the audit retains that distinction and joins the stable normalized admission, emission and accepted identity instead of treating raw text difference as a new molecule. The extra path products share scored generating parents; unscored intermediates are not assigned parent labels. The matched Parent already expresses the inherited chemistry gaps originating in n-c55c3d520a2c. This Child's pool composition, ordinary generation effort and later adaptive history change together; chemical observations do not separate these effects. The earlier continuation-removal first products described by the immutable brief belong to that different history and provide no labels for current or Parent-unselected prefixes. nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

approach.method_basis: The Parent learns a recurrent SMILES prior from unlabeled molecules and chooses its checkpoint by the yield of valid, connected, distinct ancestral samples, with heldout likelihood breaking ties. Each objective receives a fresh adaptable copy and a frozen reference. Accepted molecular trajectories train the adaptable policy through trajectory balance, a learned normalizer and prior regularization. The online cycle emits one neural batch followed by two graph batches. Accepted neural molecules refresh the scored breeding population and supply a protected first graph descendant. The graph operator independently cuts the two selected parents, usually retains the larger first fragment and smaller second fragment, and joins their exposed atoms with a single bond. Atom and bond mutations may follow. An accepted-score fingerprint posterior chooses the remaining evaluations from a temporary offspring pool, and accepted graph descendants return to neural replay. The join currently requires molecular validity but does not check whether either attachment resembles the bond environment it replaces.
approach.novelty: Add reciprocal cut-endpoint context matching to crossover: a retained endpoint may replace the opposite parent's discarded endpoint only when their local typed neighborhoods agree. This makes the actual attachment sites, rather than whole-molecule resemblance or complete-ring retention, the unit of compatibility. The lineage's previous siblings changed prior preparation or accepted-score neural behavior; related campaign experiments favored similar parents or preserved complete ring cores while leaving attachment compatibility unresolved. This experiment changes only the admissibility of the already sampled two-cut graft. A mismatch returns to the Parent's existing mutation path, and crossover involving its whole-fragment hydrogen-attachment fallback remains explicitly outside the gate.

nodes.hypothesis: Gate two-cut graph crossover by reciprocal equality of the retained and opposite discarded endpoint contexts, preserving the Parent fragment draws and routing mismatches through its existing mutation fallback.

finding_summary.headline: Attachment matching worked, but crossover nearly vanished and one replica failed
finding_summary.insights: Exact local attachment matching can suppress genuinely available mismatched grafts while preserving a small usable crossover channel. Its dominant effect here was to replace crossover with first-parent mutation: 23 of the 27 later-mutated crossover emissions had reproduced a parent before mutation, and only six evaluated emissions had a changed immediate recombination product. Better overall graph yield therefore does not establish better recombination. Mutation work rose from about 149 to 192 attempts per graph request, and scaffold variety within individual task/seed pools narrowed even though every pool filled. The rule also preserves unusual chemistry already accepted in a source: both pure crossover emissions retained N–F bonds, and the broader output still contained N–O and N–N environments and unspecified stereochemistry. The strong sitagliptin score increase cannot be read as improved synthetic quality. The completion failure is separately explained by an inherited molecule reader alternating between two aromatic SMILES representations after a protected ring-closing mutation; it does not erase the measured gate activation. Full three-seed utility and a useful contribution from compatible recombination remain unresolved.
finding_summary.results: The gate rejected 18,963 otherwise valid joins, including 18,158 that were also novel and encodable. Every one of the 847 surviving applicable joins satisfied both independently reconstructed endpoint matches. The channel remained usable, but barely: only two changed pure crossovers reached evaluation, alongside 27 crossovers followed by mutation. Crossover evaluations fell from 1,133 to 29, and their best-parent beats fell from 121 to two. Overall graph yield improved from 452/2,850 to 541/2,710 best-parent beats; on the same observed batch prefixes, the Parent had 437/2,710. All 271 reached graph batches were full, and all 143 reserved first descendants had real current policy ancestry. However, a feedback identity error stopped one task at 90 of 300 evaluations, so the panel used 4,290 of 4,500 calls and has no complete three-seed score. The two completed seed macro scores rose from 0.542383 to 0.565620 and from 0.579854 to 0.586448. Across complete three-seed task endpoints, sitagliptin rose by 0.163068 and deco_hop by 0.010448, while median_2 fell by 0.020074 and drd2 by 0.002229. Zaleplon fell by 0.006004 over the two completed seeds.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich ureas, azaarenes and cyclic amines coexist with unusual N–O, N–N and N–F chemistry and unspecified stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character: The supplied output of n-7ba291681388 spans recognizable medicinal scaffolds and chemically questionable derivatives. Aromatic and saturated heterocycles are abundant; ring supply is not the missing capability. The digest ring-closure rates range from 0.9851 to 0.9977 and aromatic-atom-presence rates from 0.8379 to 0.9818. These are fractions of SMILES containing the respective notation, not ring counts or fractions of aromatic atoms. Every task has a stereocentre-notation rate of 0.0. Overall exploration includes several scaffold families, but the highest-scoring excerpts mostly contain close relatives within seed-specific families. Compared with parent n-dd7b8aa31113, the observed chemistry changes substantially without eliminating unusual heteroatom connections: compact ureas replace some exotic fused aromatic derivatives, smaller azaaryl assemblies retain N–O chemistry, and other trajectories concentrate on nitrogen chains or covalent N–F bonds. No synthesis, stability, protonation or biological mechanism is established by these scores. All listed tasks have trajectories. The supplied zaleplon_mpo seed-2 trajectory ends at evaluation 90, with 80 optimizer proposals; its digest contains 660 optimizer proposals across seeds. The other supplied task/seed trajectories reach evaluation 300, giving 870 optimizer proposals per task. nodes.method_name: Genetic GFN: reciprocal learning between a flow policy and graph search
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Genetic GFN: alternately generate molecules with a GFlowNet policy, refine the resulting scored population through graph crossover and mutation, and distill scored descendants back into the policy using rank-weighted off-policy replay. The policy uses trajectory balance with a learned log normalizer and regularization toward a frozen prior. [Kim et al., Section 3](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.05961v4) describe this mechanism. Train the prior only on the permitted unlabeled corpus. Each objective starts with clean policy adaptation, replay and population state initialized from its supplied observations. Use a positive terminal reward increasing with the observed maximization score. Schedule policy and genetic phases around the evaluator's announced feedback; both produce new molecules, and all reward-bearing training records come from accepted observations. Later policy samples must enter genetic populations, and accepted graph descendants must affect subsequent policy updates. Generate further valid, canonical-unique structures to fill announced batches, without corpus ranking or a fixed molecular library. The hypothesis is that learned global proposals propagate local discoveries into new promising regions and then support further graph refinement, raising the mean of five independent final Top-1 scores. Published larger-budget gains do not establish that this reciprocal learning becomes useful quickly enough here.

approach.method_basis: The Parent walks from one scored molecular graph. It samples local atom and bond edits, including direct exchanges of an aromatic nitrogen and a hydrogen-bearing carbon in the same six-member ring. Valid, canonically fresh neighbors pass through a short-lived inverse-motif memory before filling the announced batch. The walk moves to the highest-scoring accepted neighbor even when that score is worse than its source, breaks exact score ties by canonical spelling, and keeps a separate best archive. Each selected transition installs at most four inverse local-motif restrictions. Installation first reserves up to two slots for each sign, then fills any remaining slots by occurrence-change magnitude and canonical motif order. A candidate is vetoed only if it matches both inverse signs from the same selected transition. Overlapping keys take the latest provenance and deadline, entries expire after four completed steps, and a documented oldest-entry release handles generation obstruction. Normalized canonical identities preserve the proposal-to-feedback join.
approach.novelty: Remove the sign reservation from the four-slot installation choice. Select the four highest-ranked changed motifs using the Parent's existing magnitude and canonical ordering, irrespective of how many have each sign. Keep insertion order unchanged whenever the selected keys agree with the Parent. This isolates the contribution of sign-balanced memory allocation to a veto that already requires both signs. Earlier siblings changed which motifs rank first while retaining the sign reservation, changed matching or memory lifetime, or removed the whole veto or nitrogen-relocation menu. None removed this reservation alone. The Parent trace suggests that most changed selections would still retain both signs, so the utility prediction is non-inferiority, not stronger chemical credit or a guaranteed reduction in vetoes. Actual memory and admission changes will establish execution; complete scored trajectories will test that prediction.

nodes.hypothesis: Remove the per-sign reservation from bounded inverse-motif installation: select up to the inherited four changed motifs by the Parent's global descending absolute occurrence-change and canonical-motif rank without sign quotas, preserving inherited insertion order on coincident selections and retaining the same-transition bidirectional veto and memory lifecycle.

finding_summary.headline: Removing sign balance changed search and lost 0.01185 in mean endpoint score
finding_summary.insights: Keeping both signs available is not enough to preserve the contribution of balanced memory allocation. Which motif representatives inherit each transition’s provenance matters even when capacity, magnitude ranking, veto logic and memory lifetime stay fixed. Ten relaxed admissions produced only one source improvement, one tie and eight losses, with no immediate archive gains; most changed the batch cutoff without becoming the next state. Conversely, one added veto enabled an oxygen-deletion refill that did improve the zaleplon archive. These opposing local effects show why fewer vetoes cannot stand in for better search. The loss supports retaining the quota in the developed method on this panel, while leaving the responsible individual replacements unresolved: ten conditional comparison batches lack a tenth recorded member, and passive memories do not define independently evolved walks or scores. Chemistry remained in the same aromatic/carbonyl, aryl-amine and sulfur-cage families, with nearly unchanged size and persistent reactive heteroatom bonds and unspecified stereochemistry. The observed score tradeoff therefore does not establish improved chemical feasibility.
finding_summary.results: The removal executed exactly and changed 116 of 420 memory installations that could affect later proposals. Most still retained both signs: 414 of 420, while total selected motif-change magnitude increased by only one count. On the Child’s recorded history, restoring balanced selection would change twelve gate decisions: ten candidates were newly admitted by the removal and two were newly vetoed. This reached actual scored allocation and selected states. Eight of fifteen task/seed trajectories changed; all fifteen finished. The three-seed mean final Top-1 score fell from 0.521759 to 0.509908, a paired loss of 0.011851 that exceeds the allowed 0.002 decline. Seed effects were +0.009516, -0.041309 and -0.003760. Sitagliptin supplied the largest loss, especially seed 1 at -0.195597, and DRD2 also declined; zaleplon improved. Mean recorded AUC fell from 0.393354 to 0.391556. The mechanism is confirmed, and the non-inferiority prediction is rejected.

molecular.headline: Aromatic carbonyls and aryl amines persist, with reactive N/O bonds, unusual sulfur coordination and densely fused cages
molecular.overall_character: Every supplied child and parent trajectory was read, and all requested tasks are covered. Each task contains 900 recorded molecules, including 870 optimizer proposals. The proposal ring-closure-token rate is 1.0 throughout, aromatic-token rates range from 0.7977 to 1.0, and mean SMILES lengths range from 46.3 to 70.1. These are molecular string readings rather than fractions of aromatic atoms or tests of chemical stability. The output consists of substantial ring-bearing compounds: indole/benzofuran amides and aryl ketones, bulky decorated aza-heterocycles, halogenated aryl amines, bridged nitrogen/carbonyl systems and highly fused sulfur cages. Distinct seed families give moderate structural diversity, while the strongest excerpts remain concentrated in closely related frameworks. Typical heavy-atom sizes are unchanged from parent n-abcd951ab7cc, and 7 of the 15 task/seed trajectories are identical. Changed trajectories retain the same broad chemistry and its unresolved liabilities rather than showing uniformly more conventional structures. Ordinary amides, amines, ethers and carbonyls coexist with N-halogen and O-halogen bonds, N-N/N-O bridges, peroxides, sulfur-halogen bonds and multiply bonded sulfur with additional substituents or hydrogen. All charged-token and stereocentre-token rates are 0.0. Neutral strings do not establish solution protonation, and unassigned configurations do not imply achiral structures. Size and structural counts below are passive RDKit readings of supplied SMILES; no new oracle score, synthesis score or geometric-feasibility result was generated. Local score associations do not reveal an unseen required scaffold or prove that chemically questionable bonds are necessary.

nodes.method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
nodes.method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.

approach.method_basis: The Parent starts from the best supplied molecule and walks through batches of fresh local graph edits, including direct formula-preserving exchanges of aromatic nitrogen and carbon positions. It sanitizes each graph, repairs its canonical identity before duplicate checks, and submits the first full batch allowed by short-term inverse-motif memory. A selected transition installs at most four signed local attributes for four completed steps, with overlapping attributes refreshed to the latest transition. The current veto needs only one positive and one negative inverse match from the same transition. The highest-scoring accepted neighbor becomes the next current state even after a worsening move; equal maxima use the canonical lexical order, and an independent archive retains the best observed molecule.
approach.novelty: Require a candidate to match every currently live inverse attribute belonging to one selected transition before that transition can veto it, while still requiring both inverse signs. This makes the veto respond to a complete retained signature instead of any two opposite-sign fragments. Earlier memory siblings changed single-attribute matching to a two-sign rule or withheld memory credit from nonimproving moves. This experiment keeps credit for every selected move and changes only how completely a candidate must match the stored signature; the neighborhood extensions already present in the Parent remain in place.

nodes.hypothesis: Veto a valid novel neighbor only when its signed motif changes match every currently live inverse restriction of at least one selected-transition provenance group and that complete group contains both inverse signs, replacing the Parent's one-match-per-sign criterion without changing memory credit or lifecycle.

finding_summary.headline: Complete-signature memory admitted 113 scored neighbors, but lowered every seed's macro score
finding_summary.insights: Incomplete motif matches do exclude some useful variations: newly admitted methyl addition, ring opening and aryl substitution produced real archive gains. A newly admitted phenol-oxygen deletion was selected despite a score loss, then a newly admitted hydroxymethyl addition in the next batch produced the strongest observed DRD2 molecule. Those concrete successes did not rescue the overall score claim. The checks rule out an unexercised predicate, missing feedback, loss of unconditional memory credit, altered expiry or restored historical signatures as explanations for the negative panel result. Requiring full motif coverage reduces exclusions as intended, but this panel shows that greater matching specificity is not sufficient to identify restrictions that can be removed beneficially. Whether the partial-signature vetoes help diversification remains open: once batch membership changes, later source graphs and random-stream consumption change, and ancestry alone cannot assign the final score difference to one admitted edit. The chemistry assessment also finds persistent reactive heteroatom bonds, unusual sulfur environments, difficult ring geometry and absent stereochemical assignments alongside recognizable aromatic/carbonyl and amine families. The stronger individual molecules therefore do not establish improved chemical feasibility or broader useful scaffold coverage.
finding_summary.results: On the Child's actual source states and live memory tables, the inherited rule would veto 178 fresh draws; the complete-signature rule vetoed 65 and admitted the other 113. Every new admission was evaluated, affecting 96 batches across all fifteen task sessions, and twenty became next states. Fifteen improved on their source, five tied and 93 worsened it; five produced immediate archive gains. Complete signatures still vetoed 63 distinct fresh molecular identities, including a two-attribute group left after overlap replacement. Memory credit, four-step tenure and overlap handling were preserved. All budgets and batches completed, using 5209 generation attempts versus the Parent's 5303. The three-seed macro mean fell from 0.521759 to 0.482572, a paired change of -0.039187 against the required +0.002. All three seed means declined. Four task means fell; median_2 rose by 0.002696. The largest task-mean losses were sitagliptin (-0.104268) and DRD2 (-0.075446). Across all accepted proposals, source improvements fell from 468 to 436, and strict archive improvements changed from 238 to 237 while their total magnitude fell from 4.699005 to 4.111202.

molecular.headline: Aromatic carbonyl families, amine-bearing bridged cores and sulfur-heavy polycycles lack consistent stability and stereochemical control
molecular.overall_character: All five tasks and all supplied parent trajectories were read. Each task digest covers 900 evaluated molecules, including 870 optimizer proposals. The output is richly cyclic and usually aromatic: ring_closure_rate and branch_rate are 1.0 throughout; aromatic_atom_rate is 0.908, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0 and 0.9437 in the supplied task order. These are molecule-level SMILES-text counters, not aromatic atom fractions or measures of feasible ring geometry. There are recognizable indole carboxanilides, nitrogen-rich carbonyl heterocycles, aryl-linked amines and cyclic amide/ketone systems, together with extensive reactive heteroatom attachments and densely connected sulfur-containing cages. The ordinary members make an across-the-board judgement of chemical impossibility inappropriate, but the recurrent liabilities justify questionable synthetic plausibility and weak overall drug-likeness. Distinct identities and several scaffold families support moderate diversity; the upper excerpts nevertheless repeatedly reuse particular cores and vary their appendages. charged_rate and stereocentre_rate are both 0.0 for every task. Free amines and potentially stereogenic ring junctions are visibly present, so these zeros mean absent charge/configuration notation, not absent ionization or stereochemistry. Heavy-atom ranges below were counted directly with RDKit from every supplied optimizer trajectory; no property oracle or new molecule was evaluated. The parent has the same broad chemical families and liabilities. The comparisons below describe observed chemistry and recorded scores, without attributing changes to the algorithm mechanism. Missing-feature statements distinguish gaps in chemical coverage from a required pharmacophore, which these trajectories alone cannot establish. There are no tasks without trajectories.

per_task.generated_character: The optimizer products contain 21–29 heavy atoms. All contain rings and most contain aromatic atoms, with ring_closure_rate 1.0 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.908. The upper excerpt includes relatively ordinary ethoxy/methyl/thiol-substituted indole carboxanilides and amino-substituted benzothiophene carbonyl derivatives. The seed-0 leader instead links an aminopyridine through a ketone to a bridged, partly aromatic thiophene-containing core bearing amino and hydroxymethyl groups. Later molecules retain similar size but accumulate partially reduced rings, extra closures, aminated carbon centres and halogenated side chains. The simple aromatic amides look more approachable synthetically than those multiply connected late polycycles.
liabilities: Cited upper members include free thiols, chloromethyl substituents and thioesters; later upper members also contain N–F bonds on heavily substituted side chains. These are chemical handling or stability concerns that the score does not resolve.
Late products combine small ring junctions with unsaturation and unassigned stereocentres. Ring-closure notation establishes connectivity, not a feasible conformation or synthesis.
missing_features: The useful compact aromatic/carbonyl arrangement is not consistently preserved in the later molecules. Coverage of conventional alternative heteroaryl carbonyl frameworks is limited relative to the many reductions and extra ring connections.

Defined configurations and tractable geometric alternatives for the bridged analogues are absent. The visible gradient does not identify an additional obligatory functional group that all these molecules lack.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The supplied trimethoxy indole carboxanilide scores 0.3051048083696145; the ethoxy/methyl/thiol analogue at seed 1, evaluation 61 scores 0.39905049777278273. The bridged aminopyridyl ketone at seed 0, evaluation 170 scores 0.40196779766986834. A modified indole whose carbonyl linker has become a substituted saturated carbon at seed 0, evaluation 42 scores 0.03343008011310944, and the N-chlorinated, partly reduced ring system at seed 1, evaluation 234 scores 0.010020601872687556. Together these observations favour preservation of a compact carbonyl-linked aromatic/heteroaromatic arrangement within the shown series; neither more rings nor more heteroatoms alone explains the scores. The parent has the identical seed-1 leader, while its seed-2 leader is an N-chloro benzofuran carboxanilide scoring 0.41003927643747895; this node instead retains a thiol-bearing indole carboxanilide as the seed-2 best at 0.3748218641899741. Thus the chemical comparison includes a more conventional amide at a lower recorded endpoint, rather than evidence that the objective reliably rewards synthetic plausibility.

per_task.generated_character: These are the largest products by heavy-atom range, 30–49, with mean SMILES length 70.0 and ring_closure_rate and aromatic_atom_rate both 1.0. The leading excerpt repeatedly retains a fused nitrogen-containing dicarbonyl heterocycle with two pyridyl appendages, an amino linker, ethers and a dimethylaminomethyl ether side chain. The same structures also carry an oxygen–fluorine bond and an imide nitrogen–chlorine bond. Terminal chains vary between alkyl, alkenyl, alkynyl and cumulated-double-bond forms. cumulated_double_bond_rate is 0.1839 across proposals. The cited carbon cumulenes and sulfur cumulene share the upper score with more conventional chains, so the visible objective does not separate their chemical plausibility.
Substantial appendage growth, flexible chains and unassigned centres complicate an already large scaffold; formal graph validity does not supply a practical route.

There is limited upper-excerpt coverage of distinct core frameworks that reproduce the polar attachment pattern. Tied tail variants do not identify a further required functional group or demonstrate broader scaffold coverage.

A lower optimizer product with altered carbonyl/unsaturation around that core scores 0.5286081645773063. The low optimizer examples retain the initial biaryl carboxylic acid, amide and N-sulfonyl pyrrolidine pattern, whose conventional functional groups are synthetically more familiar than the later sulfur networks.

The final seed-2 examples include carbon–sulfur triple bonds, multiple hydrogen-bearing multivalent sulfur centres, sulfur–sulfur connectivity and densely overlapping rings. Their synthesis and stable three-dimensional realization are especially questionable.

A particular named amine ring is not established as a missing requirement.

Assigned configurations and realistic conformational alternatives for the bridged cores are absent. charged_rate 0.0 does not mean the free amines cannot protonate, and the submitted strings do not reveal any protonation treatment used during scoring.

per_task.generated_character: These products span 28–43 heavy atoms, with ring_closure_rate and aromatic_atom_rate both 1.0. The leading seed-2 family combines phenyl and propyl-substituted oxygen-bridged arene groups with a partially saturated nitrogen heterocycle fused to a larger ring containing a ketone, an N-methyl amide, another amine and a methoxy-bearing amino carbon. Nearby high-scoring products contain unusual sulfur-hydride environments or N–S bonds. Lower members also retain O–Br groups and N–N connections; their presence is not evidence of a useful or stable pharmacophore.

Configuration-defined aminoether and ring-junction variants, together with route-consistent alternatives to the larger ring closures, are absent from the shown output.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted fused dicarbonyl heterocycle scores 0.1678386594791329, and the current seed-2 leader scores 0.20992737768880673. An opened carbonyl-containing side-chain analogue scores 0.12467972074136988. Late variants that contract the phenyl ring to a nonaromatic diene or remove a carbonyl score 0.1890295187081868 and 0.19855299930894993 respectively. The visible association is with cyclic presentation of the aryl and carbonyl groups, rather than aromaticity or molecular size alone. Sulfur is not required by the upper excerpt: the sulfur-free leader sits alongside related sulfur-bearing molecules at 0.2078390661284897 and 0.20641345956774915. The parent seed-2 best at 0.20185639717998205 is a larger aryl-substituted cyclic carbonyl/amine framework; the present seed-2 upper family retains that broad architecture with different ring connections and decoration. The parent seed-0 best at 0.21196904390980506 also belongs to an aryl/cyclic amide family, so the supplied chemistry does not demonstrate departure into unrelated high-scoring scaffolds.

per_task.generated_character: The products contain 26–37 heavy atoms but frequently pack them into dense fused and bridged sulfur-rich systems. ring_closure_rate is 1.0 and aromatic_atom_rate is 0.9437 across proposals; nevertheless, the leading seed-2 molecule and its closely related ring-contracted analogue have no aromatic atoms in their parsed graphs. The leader has six sulfur atoms, an imine, an ester ring, a sulfur–oxygen double bond, N–S connections, carbon-bound fluorine and multiple unusual sulfur-hydride/double-bond environments. Other upper members retain carbonyl/imino nitrogen heterocycles, acyl fluoride or N-fluorinated groups within highly connected cages. These are compact by atom count, but their bonding and topology make their synthetic plausibility particularly poor.
liabilities: Hydrogen-bearing multivalent sulfur, carbon–sulfur multiple bonds, sulfur–sulfur single-bond connections, N–S attachments and dense ring intersections present substantial stability, geometry and synthesis concerns.

Cited upper members include acyl fluoride and N–F bonds as well as free sulfur-containing terminal groups. Formal parsing and high recorded scores do not establish that these are stable medicinal compounds.
No stereochemistry is assigned despite complex junctions and potentially stereogenic sulfur or carbon environments.
missing_features: A chemically conventional realization of the compact polar-atom and fluorine arrangement associated with the upper scores is not established; the current realization is dominated by unusual sulfur bonding.

Alternative frameworks with regular ring geometry and assigned configurations are absent from the leading excerpt. The supplied scores do not identify a required amine class or another particular absent functional group.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aromatic dicarbonyl scaffold scores 0.0020944534688323298, and an expanded carbonyl heterocycle at seed 2, evaluation 17 scores 7.590554525032884e-10. The sulfur-rich, partly imino leader at evaluation 284 scores 0.44981689162204463. Close late variants score 0.3717269599472881 after shortening a bridge, 0.2831350668795932 after removing the imine methyl, 0.0847360681405348 after inserting an amino-containing linker, and 0.40618640040890686 after contracting the ester-containing ring. The observable gradient is sensitive to the particular compact topology, substitution and polar-atom arrangement. Neither aromaticity nor simply adding sulfur explains it; other sulfur-rich structures in the low excerpt also have extremely small scores. The parent already produced similarly unusual sulfur-containing cages, with seed-0 and seed-1 best scores 0.48118636011729826 and 0.5903526424693334. The current upper chemistry preserves that problematic family rather than supplying a conventional structural interpretation of the objective.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Upper-excerpt molecules include oxygen–fluorine and nitrogen–chlorine bonds, sulfur cumulenes, acyl fluoride, N–F groups and dense sulfur-hydride networks. A carbon connector and an unusual sulfur counterpart share the recorded score 0.9341451805829589; conventional tails and cumulene tails also share 0.6118152178904348. These observed ties show that chemical plausibility cannot be inferred from the available scalar score.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output lacks consistent control of reactive heteroatom attachments and unusual sulfur bonding.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator would need bond-context-aware alternatives that distinguish ordinary aromatic sulfur, thioethers and carbonyl chemistry from reactive heteroatom–halogen connections and unusual multivalent sulfur. Coherent replacements should preserve useful attachment patterns so their value can be measured through actual feedback; the evidence does not justify rejecting every sulfur-containing molecule.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every proposal set has ring_closure_rate 1.0 and stereocentre_rate 0.0. The cited leaders and late molecules include bridged polycycles, small ring intersections, aminoether centres and unusual sulfur junctions that can require configurations and constrained geometry. Thus missing ring formation is not the gap; the missing coverage is chemically coherent realizations of those connections.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring connectivity is abundant, but realistic geometry and explicit stereochemical coverage remain weak.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Introduce task-independent ring-topology and bond-geometry awareness, together with configuration-defined alternatives when the existing graph permits them. Preserve ordinary aromatic and polar motifs while exploring realizable closures. The effect of assigning configurations or restricting closures must be measured, since the current score records establish no stereochemical preference.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Distinct molecules and several ring families are present, but the upper excerpts repeatedly retain the same fused dicarbonyl core, enlarged aryl-substituted carbonyl ring, bridged aryl amine core or sulfur-rich cage. The entire 0.6118152178904348 excerpt varies decorations on one framework, including chemically very different terminal unsaturation. This supports moderate output diversity without demonstrating broad coverage of chemically distinct upper-score scaffolds.
transferable_gaps.gap: High-scoring structural variety is concentrated in reused scaffold families with changing appendages.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The generator would need coherent replacements of ring frameworks and linkers that preserve generic aryl, donor and acceptor attachment relationships while changing the underlying scaffold. Evaluate those alternatives with task-local feedback, without naming a desired target or reference compound. Merely creating another canonical identity is insufficient evidence of new chemical coverage.

transferable_gaps.evidence: An upper-excerpt molecule with a free secondary amine, aryl amino group and hydroxymethyl substituent scores 0.9492384404345239, while a shown acid/amide/sulfonamide structure scores 0.007468397818197266. Many other features differ, and analogues without the linker secondary amine still score 0.9214072921127627 and 0.9265115835486502. The charged_rate of 0.0 throughout describes neutral notation; it does not indicate that the generator lacks ionizable nitrogen.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not systematically vary accessible amine presentation independently of dense scaffold changes.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide chemically coherent ring and side-chain alternatives that vary whether nitrogen is acylated, its accessibility and its distance from aromatic groups while limiting other scaffold changes. The generator should let observed feedback determine where those properties matter, without mandating one amine ring or inferring a required charge state from the submitted strings.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The upper excerpts contain compact aromatic carbonyl systems, whereas the cited saturated replacement of a carbonyl linker scores 0.03343008011310944. Elsewhere an opened carbonyl side-chain analogue scores 0.12467972074136988, and late aryl contraction or carbonyl removal accompanies lower recorded scores within the same visible family. These are local structural associations, not proof that every carbonyl must be retained.
transferable_gaps.gap: Useful carbonyl and aromatic arrangements are not consistently preserved during structural diversification.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Add coherent whole-functional-group and linker replacements that can retain carbonyl orientation and aryl attachment geometry while exploring composition or ring context. Such proposals would test more interpretable chemical alternatives than accumulating disconnected changes to a functional group. Preserve task-agnostic feedback as the criterion for which alternatives prove useful.

nodes.method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
nodes.method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.

approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves scored molecular graphs with crossover and mutation, draws breeding parents from high-scoring bands of its current survivor population, and keeps a full archive of accepted scores. Before each new proposal batch, a Gaussian process fits every accepted record using local molecular count fingerprints. It evaluates a fresh pool of offspring through correlated sampled functions and selects their available maxima. Real offspring scores update both this predictor and the score-greedy breeding population. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled, while continuation, crossover finishing mutation, stable identity admission and bounded numerical fallbacks remain active.
approach.novelty: Control the ongoing-learning path by fitting the same active Gaussian process only to immutable copies of the original usable initial observations at every suggestion. Its initial training membership, labels and normalization stay fixed together. Later accepted scores still enter the full archive and determine live survivors and breeding parents. This differs from removing predictive selection or fixing breeding parents: current offspring still receive correlated GP predictions and evaluation choices, but generated labels cannot teach that predictor. The experiment asks what this one feedback path contributes, rather than proposing that a static predictor is a better optimizer.

nodes.hypothesis: Freeze the active count-Tanimoto GP training dataset to immutable copies of the original usable initial accepted archive in its original order for every inherited fit, jointly freezing its empirical label normalization while retaining full real-archive feedback for live graph breeding and the original correlated posterior allocation on fresh pools.

finding_summary.headline: Continued GP conditioning contributes: initial-only training lowers every matched endpoint and the mean by 0.151856.
finding_summary.insights:
Ongoing conditioning on generated accepted observations adds value beyond an initially fitted predictor in this optimizer, even when real-label survival, recursive breeding and posterior selection remain active. The experiment therefore answers a narrower question than removing the whole selector or freezing the breeding cohort. Training membership, later label information and empirical normalization were held together: their individual effects, and their interaction with survival, remain unassigned. All sitagliptin fits retain the initial scale floor, but this exposure alone does not establish that the floor causes its endpoint losses.

Useful local search persists under the frozen predictor. It produces 580 best-parent wins and 125 incumbent advances, and every endpoint exceeds its initial best. The molecular assessment finds recognizable amide and aromatic-carbonyl families, useful available amines, changed linkers and ring closures. Some lower-scoring Child leaders have more conventional local chemistry than their Parent counterparts; other outputs retain reactive bonds, doubtful ring geometry and unresolved stereochemistry. The loss does not establish absent chemical novelty, require reactive motifs or identify a chemical mediator. Three leaders arrive in the final batch and cannot show later feedback effects.

The lower selected-stream prediction error is measured on different molecules and cannot establish better calibration or replace the endpoint contrast. Likewise, passive full-archive calculations change all 420 later selected sets on the actual Child pools, but do not supply alternative rewards or future histories. This complete exposed result ends the registered initial-cohort control. Shared-Parent sibling experiments and historical repeated trajectories are dependent evidence, so their effects cannot be added or treated as independent replications.
finding_summary.results:

molecular.headline: Familiar aromatic amides and carbonyl heterocycles persist, with useful amines but incomplete context control and reactive ring chemistry
molecular.overall_character: All supplied Child n-7de8feaf821f and published Parent n-62daf219c70a trajectories were present and read. The brief independently reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true for Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2, with no profile mismatch or uncovered objective. Each task contributes 900 Child records, including 870 optimizer evaluations; all matched task/seed initial molecule and score records agree. Every Child retained best exceeds its fixed initial best, while all fifteen matched Parent endpoints remain higher. The seed-0 indole-amide comparison is nearly matched, whereas several available-amine and fluorinated-heterocycle comparisons differ substantially. The Child produces recurrent indole carboxamides, aryl-linked nitrogen/carbonyl systems, amide and sulfonamide material with available amines, and bridged or fused nitrogen rings. Many recognizable initial functional-group arrangements remain visible in leading output, but actual recursive breeding also produces changed linkers, new ring closures and useful simplifications. There is moderate chemical diversity across families and seeds, with narrower useful leading neighborhoods; this is not global structural collapse or an inability to produce rings. In fixed task order the digest ring-closure-string incidences are 0.9931, 0.9471, 0.969, 0.9828 and 0.954, and aromatic-string incidences are 0.9931, 0.9425, 0.9575, 0.9586 and 0.9241. These are text-feature incidences, not perceived ring counts or aromatic-atom fractions. Formal-charge and stereocentre-string incidences are 0.0 throughout. The respective cross-seed distinct-identity counts are 841, 870, 876, 874 and 870; each task/seed still has 300 distinct accepted identities. Cross-seed recurrence is not within-run duplicate evaluation. The moderate drug-likeness reading reflects familiar amides, ethers, carbonyl heterocycles and available amines in many leaders. It does not imply confirmed activity or easy synthesis. Synthetic plausibility remains questionable because other accepted molecules carry N-F or O-Cl bonds, peroxide/peracid groups, unusual imines and four-membered or bridged closures, and because very large joined products recur. Several conventional Child indole-amide and amine leaders avoid reactive bonds found in their Parent counterparts, so lower observed scores do not uniformly mean worse chemical plausibility. Read-only RDKit descriptors were calculated from the supplied trajectories; no objective, affinity or synthesis score was generated. The authorized source and receipts distinguish the immutable original usable accepted GP cohort from the complete real observation archive and the live score-ranked breeding population. Across the recorded Child fits, the initial ten training records and their label mean/scale remain the training basis, while final real archives contain all 300 accepted records. The later accepted leaders have genuine raw scores, enter the real archive and survive by the inherited score law; their absence from GP training is not rejection or loss of genetic feedback. For example, the seed-0 amine/amide leader appears in the next context as a live rank-0 survivor and archived observation but not a training member, and later actually breeds a high-scoring accepted analogue. The same distinction holds for a leading pyridyl indole amide whose later accepted descendant loses useful context and scores poorly. These are molecular provenance examples, not an activation verdict. The full-pool receipts retain the inherited pool size, and current molecules still receive current predictions and correlated selection draws. A fixed training cohort does not mean constant predictions for different molecules, frozen pools, static initial breeders or removal of the selector. The inherited archive_mean prediction field is explicitly scoped in these receipts to the initial training mean; its name does not make it the current complete-archive mean. Training membership, later-label information and empirical normalization are held together in this control; their separate effects, whole-selector contribution and whole-foundation contribution are not identified here. All thirty Child/Parent task/seed leaders were joined to actual pooled, emitted and accepted records and their generating scored parents. Initial-source molecules, unscored graph intermediates, pooled offspring, emitted proposals, accepted observations, live survivors, actual breeders and retained-best endpoints remain distinct. Some late leaders have no later feedback opportunity; another recorded leader breeds a chlorinated pooled analogue with no accepted label. No score or chemical benefit is imputed to that unqueried molecule. Chemical frequencies and missing-feature statements concern accepted trajectories and leaders, not a census of the full unselected pool. The digest final_molecules are late seed-2 observations, not all seeds' retained best. The original gap reports in n-c55c3d520a2c and their identical-trajectory carry-forward in n-62daf219c70a were read through the fresh legal evidence index. Historical reproduction is provenance, not independent replication. This single complete matched panel shares a Parent baseline with other current routes and has adaptive histories; no independent-replication, combined, additive or interaction claim follows. Chemical association and overlapping ancestry do not establish mediation or separate predictive from survival contributions. All supplied source, trajectory and log paths were present. Audits under .slots/r0020-03-ablation-L01/molecular/ preserve trajectory descriptors, source/log hashes, leader_training_provenance.json, original gap provenance and citation joins. Only Child digest/trusted-trajectory SMILES are quoted; Parent-only molecules are identified by their published task, seed and evaluation.

All three are recognizable compact aromatic amides without N-halogen bonds or carbon cumulenes. The vinyl ether and free thiol still pose local stability questions, but these leaders are more conventional than many Parent leaders. The Parent endpoints at seed 0/evaluation 289, seed 1/evaluation 293 and seed 2/evaluation 294 instead include an N-chloroindole cumulene, an N-fluoro/N-hydroxy pyridyl amide and an N-chloroindole aryl diketone. nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
