approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds from score-ranked accepted molecules and recombines a fragment from each of two selected parents. For the first parent it usually keeps the larger side of a random bridge cut, then joins that piece to a donor fragment and may apply a local mutation. A Gaussian process trained on all accepted observations selects a batch from the resulting fresh pool. The random cut can separate ring systems or discard part of a strong first parent's core before the selector sees the product.
approach.novelty: Preserve the first parent's complete ring core during fragment crossover. Choose only pendant cuts whose retained side contains every source ring atom and the paths connecting them, then attach the donor fragment through the existing crossover. This changes the physical fragment retained, whereas earlier siblings changed parent allocation, survival or similarity-based pairing. It also differs from the separate whole-branch pruning experiment: donor replacement and learned pool selection already belong to this Parent, so the new question is whether preserving its core improves recombination.

nodes.hypothesis: When forming a crossover's first-parent fragment, sample only pendant single-bond cuts and retain the side containing every source ring atom and its connecting linkers.

finding_summary.headline: First-parent ring cores survived crossover, but final scores fell on all three seeds
finding_summary.insights: Physical inheritance of the first parent’s complete ring system worked and reached evaluation, but the full-core restriction did not improve the complete method. The crossover cohort produced more parent-beating descendants while the complete search ended at lower scores, so that local diagnostic is insufficient to establish improved optimization. It rules out failed cutting or lack of exposure to the selector as the explanation for the negative utility result. Keeping every ring can also keep a large or unproductive framework, while the donor adds more structure and useful peripheral functional relationships can still be removed. Optional mutation can then undo the protected structure. The supplied chemistry is consistent with this limit: conventional arylamide and sulfinamide leaders coexist with duplicated frameworks, dense bridges, reactive substituents and unspecified stereochemistry. The next useful distinction is which core and attachment relationships deserve preservation, and when replacement or simplification is beneficial; this result does not establish that all rings should always survive. The observed crossover subgroups differ in parents and later edits, and the changed random-call schedule alters subsequent search history. Neither the subgroup score difference nor molecular size identifies an individual protected cut’s causal value, and unused candidates have no oracle counterfactual labels.
finding_summary.results: Across 34,564 informative first-parent fragment calls, the inherited rule would retain the complete source ring/linker core with mean probability 55.968%; the applied pendant-cut rule made that probability one. All 33,626 sanitized protected crossovers preserved the original core atoms and bonds before canonicalization. Protected crossovers reached 28,875 novel pool descendants and 1,714 actual evaluated descendants; 1,587 of those emissions followed an immediate crossover that changed the first parent’s identity. Of 600 evaluated crossover descendants with a later mutation, 224 no longer contained the original typed ring/linker core. One additional unselected immediate-only pool product changed aromatic representation during the inherited canonicalization step. Mean emitted size rose from 33.39 to 40.90 heavy atoms, and 938 attempted products exceeded the unchanged 120-atom limit. The protected crossover cohort had 210/1,714 strict best-parent beats and mean child-minus-best-parent score -0.112347, compared with 172/1,679 and -0.156871 in the Parent’s crossover cohort. All fifteen Child task/seed runs completed. Mean final score fell from 0.544374 to 0.529067, a paired change of -0.015307; all three paired seeds declined (-0.014873, -0.022309, -0.008738). The mean DRD2 change was -0.090254, despite gains on three other tasks.

molecular.headline: Compact arylamide and sulfinamide leaders coexist with repeated large frameworks, dense bridges, and reactive substituents
molecular.overall_character: Every supplied current and parent trajectory was read; all tasks and seeds are covered. Each current task contains 900 observations and 870 optimizer proposals. The current proposals are consistently substantial molecules: ring-closure and branch presence are 1.0 throughout, and aromatic-token presence ranges from 0.9931 to 1.0. These text counters indicate whether a SMILES contains the relevant token, not aromatic atom fractions or feasible three-dimensional rings. Small fragments are not the visible limiting chemistry. Instead, the low-scoring excerpts repeatedly join complete arylamide or dione systems, and one population has mean SMILES length 130.8. More compact leaders include ordinary N-methyl arylamides and a recognizable tertiary-amine/cyclobutane/sulfinamide series. Other families use densely bridged nitrogen/carbonyl rings or N-fluorinated enol/thiol-containing structures. Drug-like functional groups are therefore present, but synthetic plausibility and stability are uneven. Explicit tetrahedral stereolabel rates are zero throughout; formal charge tokens are rare, appearing at rate 0.0034 in the arylamide population and zero elsewhere. Neutral drawings can still contain basic amines. Several seed families provide moderate structural diversity, while much nominal variety comes from decoration, repeated units, or additional bridges. Relative to the parent, some leading chemistry becomes more conventional, but size, topology, and reactive bond liabilities remain.

per_task.generated_character: The best current family consists of compact fused/bridged heteroaromatics carrying an ordinary N-methyl phenylamide, methoxy or methylamino substitution, small alkyl groups, and a carbon-bound fluorine on a ring bridge. Nearby leaders replace phenyl with pyridyl or use sulfur/nitrogen ring connections. The leading molecule avoids the direct amide N-F bond seen in the parent's seed-2 leader, although other current seeds still produce N-fluorinated or N-chlorinated heteroaromatic amides. Ring presence is 1.0, aromatic presence 0.9989, and mean SMILES length 47.2. The compact leading architecture and standard amide are recognizable, but ring-bridge geometry and stereochemical identity still require assessment. The low excerpt instead contains duplicated, often heavily decorated arylamide systems connected through N/O/S or carbon linkages.
liabilities: Fluorinated bridge connectivity and dense fusion make accessible geometry and stereoisomer identity uncertain.
Bromomethyl and chloromethoxy variants add potential reactivity without establishing a general score advantage.
Other seed families retain direct N-F/N-Cl or additional N-N connections.
Joining complete arylamide systems sharply enlarges the molecules and appears repeatedly among the lowest supplied scores.
missing_features: Matched simpler bridge connections retaining the leading N-methyl arylamide and substituent relationships are insufficiently represented.
The substituted fluorinated bridge has no explicit stereochemical identity.
Stable compact alternatives are still incompletely represented across seeds, where direct N-halogen bonds and duplicated arylamides remain.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The methoxy/methyl/fluorinated-bridge N-methyl phenylamide reaches 0.459794. Replacing phenyl with pyridyl lowers the score to 0.442564; replacing the aryl methyl with fluoromethyl gives 0.441920. In that fluoromethyl series, replacing methoxy with methylamino gives 0.458807, and fluoromethyl-to-bromomethyl exchange ties at 0.458807. Extending methylamino to ethylamino then lowers a closely related final structure to 0.299139. These local changes reveal specific substituent preferences, not a general benefit from adding fluorine, nitrogen, or size. Repeated arylamide assemblies score as low as 3.62e-22 despite retaining the apparent core functionality. The current seed-2 maximum exceeds the parent's 0.416350 while replacing an N-fluoroamide with N-methyl amide chemistry and a different bridged core. The parent's overall maximum was 0.446352 in another bridged N/O-carbonyl family. This is evidence of a different productive molecular arrangement, not proof that any individual bridge or fluorine position is required.

per_task.generated_character: This population is dominated by large, extensively linked aromatic structures. The leading family contains a benzopyranone-like carbonyl core, biaryl connections, a terminal ethynyl group, and repeated pyridyl/diazine-type rings linked through ethers. Carbon-bound fluorine, chlorine, methyl, and methoxy substituents decorate the extended framework. Its ring sizes and bond types are more recognizable than the unusual heteroatom-halogen chemistry in some parent leaders, but the overall assembly is very large and rich in aromatic acceptors with little donor functionality. Other seeds make still larger mixtures of repeated carbonyl heterocycles, imine/enol-ether connections, and unsaturated chains. Mean SMILES length is 130.8 and maximum 232, with aromatic and ring presence both 1.0. Synthetic assembly and physical properties are major unresolved issues even where individual substructures are ordinary.
liabilities: The large aromatic surface and many connecting bonds create unresolved solubility, permeability, and synthesis concerns; none is measured here.
Repeated azaaryl-ether units add considerable molecular size without a monotonic supplied-score gain.
Some neighboring molecules introduce ethynyl ethers, imines, cumulated bonds, thiocarbonyls, or other labile unsaturated connections.
Extensive late ring closure and appendage growth increase synthetic complexity while remaining near the same score region.
missing_features: More compact frameworks retaining the useful heteroaryl and carbonyl relationships are underrepresented.
Matched removal of remote repeated rings is only partially demonstrated, despite the favorable methoxy simplification.
Balanced polar functionality and fewer aromatic connections are not established within the leading high-acceptor, low-donor series.
Stable short alternatives to the imine/enol-ether appendages remain insufficiently represented.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The terminal-methoxy version of the extended heteroaryl-ether framework scores 0.611490. Replacing that small group with an additional heteroaryloxy appendage gives 0.608641; much longer unsaturated appendages score 0.608404-0.610960. The smaller peripheral arrangement therefore does at least as well within the supplied family. Several different changes tie at 0.608641, including chlorine/methyl exchange on a remote ring, ether-to-thioether substitution, and carbonyl-to-thiocarbonyl substitution in related molecules. These ties provide no evidence that extra remote size or sulfur is needed. Low optimizer molecules already contain substantial aryl/carbonyl frameworks at 0.523237-0.527966, showing that rings and heteroatoms alone are insufficient. The current maximum is slightly above the parent's seed-2 value of 0.608345 but below the parent's overall 0.632470. Its leading chemistry replaces the parent's linked N-halogenated diones with long heteroaryl ethers; other current seed maxima are lower than their parent counterparts and remain very large.

per_task.generated_character: The leading family is chemically recognizable: an N-propyl tertiary amine connects a substituted cyclobutane/anisyl group to a branched chain bearing an aryl sulfinamide. The sulfinamide contains a single S=O group, and the other aromatic ring is a chlorinated pyridine. Related molecules exchange carbon-bound halogens, fluorinate alkyl groups, or modify methoxy/thioether substitution. These structures contain a potentially basic tertiary amine, a sulfinamide NH, an oxidized sulfur acceptor, and hydrophobic aromatic groups. Ring presence is 1.0, aromatic presence 0.9977, halogen presence 1.0, and mean SMILES length 75.6. The ordinary sulfinamide and cyclobutane are not inherently evidence of implausible chemistry, but several carbon and sulfur stereochemical distinctions are unspecified. Other seeds produce more bridged aryl amines or larger amide-linked cages, including unusual combined S=N/S=S sulfur functionality.
liabilities: The leading sulfinamide and substituted saturated carbons can generate stereoisomers with different geometry, but no configuration is specified.
Chloromethyl and extended halogenated alkyl variants introduce additional reactivity or size concerns.
Some late cages combine imino and thiocarbonyl bonding at sulfur with difficult polycyclic topology.
Large amide-linked cage assemblies retain considerable hydrophobic surface and connecting-group complexity at lower supplied scores.
missing_features: Stereochemically defined sulfinamide sulfur, branched carbon, and substituted cyclobutane arrangements are absent.
Matched simpler side-chain and aryl substitution alternatives preserving the useful tertiary-amine relationship are incompletely represented.
More ordinary connections are missing within the lower-scoring, highly bridged sulfur-cage branch.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The dichloropyridyl sulfinamide/tertiary-amine leader scores 0.981641; exchanging one pyridyl chlorine for fluorine gives exactly the same score. Replacing the branched ethyl portion with fluoromethyl gives 0.972794, while longer halogenated alkoxy decorations reach 0.963293. These observations favor the complete aryl/amine/sulfinamide arrangement and show no universal advantage from additional fluorination or peripheral growth. Low molecules include an aryl acid/amide/N-sulfonyl cyclic-amine assembly at 0.007264 and a protected polyol-rich amine-containing structure at 0.011436. Nitrogen or ring presence alone is therefore insufficient. The current seed-0 maximum is below the parent's 0.990833 spiro-amine maximum, while changing to a more open sulfinamide/cyclobutane series. Current seed-1 reaches 0.962141 in another aryl-amine family, but seed-2 peaks at 0.718928 in a much more complex amide-linked sulfur cage. The high-scoring ordinary sulfinamide series demonstrates that exotic sulfur bonding is not universally needed.

per_task.generated_character: The strongest family consists of densely bridged polycycles carrying alkyl/ethoxy-substituted aromatic rings, partly saturated nitrogen rings, and an N-methyl carbonyl-rich ring. The leader contains an N-N connection within the carbonyl-containing ring closure; nearby analogues replace that connection with carbon or alter bridge length and saturation. Other seed families include large fused aromatic diones and linked aryl/N-methyl lactams, some with tightly oxygen-bridged azaaromatic fragments. Ring presence is 1.0, aromatic presence 0.9977, and mean SMILES length 61.8. Halogen presence is only 0.0989. The functional groups provide recognizable carbonyl and aromatic chemistry, but the crowded bridge network is synthetically demanding and its conformations are unspecified.
liabilities: Overlapping bridges and unsaturated ring connections make synthesis and accessible conformation uncertain.
The leading N-N connection and related N-O or peroxide structures introduce additional bond-stability questions.
Some linked aryl/lactam molecules contain strongly constrained oxygen/azaaromatic small-ring closures.
Duplicated carbonyl/aromatic systems substantially increase size while appearing among the lowest supplied scores.
missing_features: Less bridged alternatives retaining the aryl and carbonyl arrangement are insufficiently represented near the leading scores.
Matched removal of the N-N connection and controlled bridge simplification are only partially demonstrated.
Stereochemically specified bridgehead and substituted saturated-ring identities are missing.
Compact alternatives to joining entire aromatic dione or lactam systems remain underrepresented.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The N-N-containing bridged leader scores 0.231463. Its carbon-connected ring analogue scores 0.225320, while other bridge and saturation variants cluster at 0.221185-0.228396. The modest local differences do not establish that the most complex bridge network is necessary. A different linked aryl/lactam family reaches 0.222716. Low optimizer examples instead duplicate or join large aromatic dione systems through ester, anhydride, peroxide, or N/O connections, scoring 0.112181-0.117809. A late doubled structure likewise drops to 0.152283, below simpler final members around 0.21. The current seed-0 maximum is above the parent's 0.224057 expanded nitrogen/carbonyl-ring maximum, while changing to a more extensively bridged cage. The current seed-2 maximum also exceeds its parent's 0.210377, but introduces constrained oxygen-containing ring connections. Neither comparison establishes synthetic ease or resolves the limited score region.

per_task.generated_character: The leading family contains an expanded cyclic dione with direct N-F substitution, fused to a partly unsaturated nitrogen ring bearing pyrrolyl or pyridyl and substituted enol/thiol groups. The best attaches a fluoromethyl/fluorine-substituted cyclobutenol carrying a vinylic thiol; a near-leader instead uses a fluoropyridyl group and a larger cyclopentenol/thiol substituent. An open-chain enol/thiol relative is also shown. These are compact carbonyl/heteroaryl molecules, but direct N-fluorination, tautomeric enol/thiol functionality, and strained unsaturated small rings make apparent stability and synthesis questionable. Ring presence is 1.0, aromatic presence 0.9931, and mean SMILES length 58.0. The low excerpt contains large hybrid or repeated dione systems, not a lack of molecular architecture.
liabilities: Direct N-F bonds on the carbonyl-containing ring introduce a distinct reactivity concern.
Cyclobutenol strain and enol/thiol tautomerism complicate stability, synthesis, and interpretation of the drawn structure.
Fluorinated, hydroxylated, and thiolated saturated carbons have unspecified stereochemistry.
Joining complete dione systems yields very large molecules with extremely low supplied scores.
missing_features: Matched ordinary N-substitution alternatives retaining the leading dione and enol/thiol arrangement are missing.
Stable replacements for the tautomeric and potentially reactive thiol/enol region have not been established without changing the rest of the molecule.
Less strained saturated or open-chain connections are only partially represented around the useful heteroaryl/carbonyl relationships.
Explicit stereochemical identities of the fluorinated substituted rings are absent.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The pyrrolyl/fluorinated-cyclobutenol-thiol leader scores 0.576998; its analogue replacing the saturated ring fluorine with thiol gives 0.555217. The fluoropyridyl/cyclopentenol family reaches 0.571115, versus 0.526837 without that aromatic fluorine and 0.531910 after replacing its saturated ring fluorine with thiol. Within a methyl-substituted cyclobutenol series, replacing the vinylic thiol with hydroxyl causes a particularly large change, from 0.532883 to 0.032767. This is a specific observed functional-group preference, not evidence that all sulfur or fluorine additions help. An open-chain enol/thiol analogue still reaches 0.530545, so a strained small ring is not established as essential. A late doubled molecule scores 1.66e-21, and a large early hybrid scores 2.88e-57. The current seed-2 maximum exceeds its parent's 0.407140 but remains below the parent's overall 0.584558 aryl dione/aminomethyl/fluoromethyl maximum, which had different and more conventional peripheral chemistry.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Low-scoring excerpts repeatedly duplicate arylamides or diones, with supplied scores as small as 3.62e-22 and 1.66e-21. One proposal population has mean SMILES length 130.8. Within its leading family, replacing a remote heteroaryloxy appendage with methoxy raises the supplied score from 0.608641 to 0.611490.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator too often joins complete molecular systems instead of preserving a compact productive core.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide controlled removal of repeated units and simplification of remote appendages while preserving the informative core and key group relationships. Use accepted local comparisons to determine useful size instead of assuming that retaining two complete parent-like architectures is beneficial.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The cited molecules include fluorinated aromatic bridges, densely overlapping nitrogen/carbonyl cages, constrained oxygen/azaaromatic closures, and unsaturated small rings. Ring-closure presence is already 1.0 throughout, while simpler sulfinamide/cyclobutane chemistry and an open-chain enol/thiol analogue also achieve high local scores.
transferable_gaps.gap: Geometric and synthetic feasibility remain unresolved as ring systems acquire additional bridges.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make bridge opening, alternative connection points, ring expansion, and saturation changes accessible while preserving useful functional-group spacing. Treat valence-valid closure as incomplete evidence of accessible geometry or a credible synthesis.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Several families retain direct N-F or N-Cl bonds, N-N connections, enol/thiol groups, or labile unsaturated appendages. Ordinary N-methyl arylamide and sulfinamide leaders demonstrate access to more conventional bonding. A thiol-to-hydroxyl change can sharply reduce a supplied score, so simple blanket removal of every reactive group would also discard locally useful chemical distinctions.
transferable_gaps.gap: Stable functional-group alternatives are not explored systematically around reactive high-scoring structures.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Offer matched stable substitutions that preserve the surrounding scaffold, polarity pattern, and approximate size, then let current score feedback evaluate them. Distinguish the chemical role of a group from its incidental reactivity instead of copying it uncritically or removing an entire functional class.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every digest population has zero explicit tetrahedral stereolabel presence. The leading sulfinamide has stereogenic sulfur and substituted carbon connections, while bridged amides and fluorinated enol/thiol rings introduce additional stereochemical distinctions.
transferable_gaps.gap: Stereochemical identity is left unspecified even in families with clear carbon and sulfur stereochemistry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve stereochemical information through structural changes and make valid local stereoisomers available when new centres arise. Combine this with credible ring geometry and current scoring feedback so that one unspecified connectivity is not treated as a fully defined accessible molecule.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Chlorine/fluorine exchange in a sulfinamide series ties at 0.981641, several remote ether/thioether or carbonyl/thiocarbonyl changes tie at 0.608641, and methylamino-to-ethylamino extension lowers another local score from 0.458807 to 0.299139. Elsewhere, multiple simultaneous ring and connecting-group changes obscure which chemical feature matters.
transferable_gaps.gap: Chemically local alternatives are too sparse to separate useful functionality from incidental growth and topology.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Expand matched changes to substituent position, carbonyl connection, heteroatom identity, amine spacing, and bridge geometry while keeping the remaining structure fixed. Include independently connected, synthetically credible alternatives rather than relying mainly on large rearrangements or repeated units.

nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

branches: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
retained_mechanisms: Task-local scored graph population with score-ranked parent sampling from three high-ranked quantiles
Connected-fragment graph crossover with inherited donor cut/side selection and single-bond attachment
First-parent pendant cut selection that retains every original ring atom and its connecting linkers, with deterministic component metadata caching
Local atom/bond mutation, bounded inner retries, occasional multistep graph walks and optional post-crossover mutation
Sanitization, canonical/isomeric identity checks, temporary-pool uniqueness and bounded fresh-pool generation; saturation-dependent retry branches retained
Bounded greedy score-ranked survivor retention and subsequent breeding from accepted offspring

Accepted-only fingerprint Gaussian-process archive, exact joint posterior function sampling over fresh offspring pools, masked batch selection and feedback-driven refitting; bounded numerical fallback retained

approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds molecular graphs from a bounded population of accepted high-scoring molecules. It samples parents from score quantiles, combines connected fragments and applies local edits, including its retained formula-preserving aromatic nitrogen-position exchange. Stable canonical identity checks admit a fresh surplus pool. A Gaussian process trained on every earlier accepted score represents molecules by counts of local environments and uses generalized Tanimoto covariance to predict the pool. Independent correlated posterior draws currently choose each batch member, removing its identity before the next draw. Real accepted feedback updates both the breeding population and the prediction archive.
approach.novelty: Remove sampled uncertainty from the choice rule: submit the molecules with the highest posterior means, using pool order to break exact ties. Keep the learned model and the original draws, with those draws serving only as passive comparisons. Earlier siblings coordinated pending uncertainty or optimized a predicted batch maximum; both retained uncertainty in their decisions and neither improved the final mean score. This is the first supplied sibling to test mean-only allocation on the current Parent. It asks whether concentrating evaluations on predicted quality helps, while measuring the loss of uncertainty exposure and molecular-core coverage that the Parent-pool replay predicts.

nodes.hypothesis: Select each successful batch by stable descending posterior mean on the existing fresh pool, removing sampled uncertainty from the identity-allocation rule while retaining the learned count-based posterior.

finding_summary.headline: Mean-only selection executed, narrowed chemical coverage, and reduced final macro score by 0.0404
finding_summary.insights:
This removal experiment supplies negative utility evidence for treating the sampled excursions as wasted evaluations. The learned mean remains informative against its own archive-mean baseline, but concentrating on its highest predictions produced more local improvements along a search that ended lower. Parent-beating yield and lower selected-stream prediction error therefore remain poor substitutes for final search quality. The model itself was frozen: lower SD exposure and lower error describe the selected molecules and their subsequent feedback, not improved uncertainty calibration.

Lost breadth is a plausible explanation to investigate. The chemistry assessment found fewer distinct cores in 14 of 15 paired streams, consistent with the matched-pool coverage loss. It also found persistent unusual bonds, burdensome decorations and unspecified stereochemistry, so more selective allocation did not establish better chemical feasibility. The result narrows the next question to which exploratory choices or independent molecular families help preserve useful search paths. It does not identify a particular discarded molecule as the missing winner: alternate choices have no counterfactual oracle outcomes, and the downstream histories differ. Transfer beyond this Parent and supplied panel remains open.
finding_summary.results:
All 4,350 successful choices followed the stable highest-mean order, with zero violations. On the same 435 Child pools, the inherited sampled rule would have selected a different set in every batch. Mean-only selection raised average predicted quality from 0.357917 to 0.390251 and reduced original prediction SD from 0.038134 to 0.020556. Mean absolute within-batch posterior correlation rose from 0.054704 to 0.064071, count-fingerprint similarity rose from 0.5810 to 0.8211, and distinct nonempty chemical cores fell from 6.503 to 4.437 per ten molecules. These are comparisons on identical pools and model distributions.

The completed search scored worse. Three-seed final macro mean fell from 0.574344 to 0.533937, a paired change of -0.040407 against the required +0.002. All three macro replicas declined. Task mean changes were -0.104061 for sitagliptin_mpo, -0.043769 for drd2_docking, -0.036782 for zaleplon_mpo, -0.018368 for deco_hop, and +0.000944 for median_2. This occurred despite strict parent-beating offspring increasing from 624 to 707 out of 4,350 and batches improving the incumbent increasing from 182 to 197. Mean accepted batch-best fell from 0.487313 to 0.437676. Selected-stream prediction MSE fell from 0.011269 to 0.004397, while within-batch rank correlation fell from 0.550 to 0.316. Nominal 95% latent intervals covered only 77.24% of Child scores, versus 76.92% for the Parent. All batches were complete and accepted, with no numerical fallback.

molecular.headline: Aromatic families narrow around ordinary drug-like cores, but unusual bonds, oversized decorations and unspecified stereochemistry persist
molecular.overall_character:
Read all supplied trajectories for node n-852bc7be4d7c and Parent n-559d25e9c9c7: each covers the five tasks at seeds 0, 1 and 2, with 900 scored rows per task, including 870 optimizer proposals. No task lacks trajectories. The digest pools seeds: its leading indole, amine-rich and polycyclic-dione examples come from seed 2, and its leading heavily decorated and fluorinated diones come from seed 1. The other seed families are included below from their full trajectories. Scores quoted here are recorded values; displayed endpoint decimals are rounded.

The output consists of connected, ring-rich molecules carrying aromatic or heteroaromatic cores, amide/lactam carbonyls, ethers, variable nitrogen functionality and frequent halogens. These are not predominantly tiny fragments. The digest ring-closure rate is 1.0 for every task; its aromatic-atom presence rate is 1.0 except 0.9989 for the fluorinated-dione task. These are molecule-presence counters, not aromatic atom fractions. All task counters show zero explicit charge and zero stereocentre markers.

Passive RDKit 2023.09.6 inspection of the supplied optimizer rows finds all 4350 recorded Child optimizer proposals parse, while 1768 have at least one graph-perceived unassigned chiral centre and none has an assigned one. Parsing does not establish stability, a realizable stereoisomer or a synthesis. Some indole carboxamides have recognizable medicinal chemistry; other leading families contain highly decorated halogenated acetals, peroxide/polysulfide tethers, sulfur doubly bonded to two carbons, or complicated ring closures. The weak drug-likeness judgement reflects these recurring liabilities and large structures, not an absence of medicinal-chemistry motifs.

Distinct nonempty atom-and-bond Murcko core counts fall in 14 of 15 paired streams; the exception rises from 41 to 47. This supports narrow within-stream coverage, although the pooled panel contains several distinct families and genuine ring edits. Core counts retain heteroatom and bond-order changes and are not counts of independent synthetic scaffold families. The passive audit, including trajectory hashes, descriptor definitions and per-seed high/low summaries, is .slots/SPIRAL2.r0012-10-improve-L01.molecular-audit.json. No oracle, biological validation or synthesis-route calculation was performed.

per_task.generated_character: Compact indole-like aromatic families dominate all seeds. Optimizer median heavy-atom counts are 25, 25 and 24 in seed order; each has a median of three aromatic rings. The digest leader is a neutral indole carboxamide linked to a pyridyl ring, with methyl/vinyl and methoxy or vinyl-ether substituents: 24 heavy atoms, molecular weight 319.36 Da and three aromatic rings. Its secondary amide and indole NH provide donors, with carbonyl/ether/pyridyl acceptor sites. Full trajectories show seed 0 also favouring N-hydroxy hydrazide-like links, and seed 1 favouring bromomethylated N-amino/imine variants. Thus the clean pyridyl amide leader does not represent all emitted chemistry. The ordinary amide family is plausibly approachable; the heteroatom-linker variants are less routine. Parent and Child retain similar typical size, but pooled distinct Murcko cores contract from 276 to 103.
liabilities: The leading vinyl ether and pendant alkenes introduce stability/reactivity questions; they are not themselves evidence that the molecules are unmakeable.

Acyl fluoride, bromomethyl, N-O/N-N and O-S-O variants broaden the graph vocabulary without demonstrated handling of their functional-group chemistry. The digest halogen-presence rate is 0.8632 even though its highest-scoring examples are halogen-free.
missing_features: Alternative compact heteroaromatic core architectures preserving the useful amide and donor/acceptor arrangement are poorly represented among leaders; existing pyridyl positional variation is present and should not be mistaken for a missing capability.

The cleaner pyridyl amide arrangement is not reproduced among the other seeds' leading families, which instead alter the polar link through hydrazide/imine chemistry. A tractable route to varying this arrangement without those link changes remains unshown.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The cited initial trimethoxy, fluorophenyl indole carboxamide scores 0.3051048083696145. The leading pyridyl, vinyl/ether variants reach 0.4330127018922193; pyridyl position and placement of the unsaturated substituents can change without changing this top value. A smaller dihalobenzene scores 2.2064040954992307e-13, an expanded heteroaromatic assembly with bromomethyl groups scores 1.389263800640293e-08, and an indole acyl fluoride scores 0.0012711582014672507. This supports a bounded-size, intact aromatic/polar arrangement rather than arbitrary aromatic content or growth. Late replacement of the ether with an O-S-O-containing tether gives 0.38171497280435657. These are multi-feature associations; the data do not establish an obligatory missing target group. In seed order 0, 1, 2, Parent-to-Child best accepted scores are 0.457660 to 0.416350, 0.442313 to 0.388678, 0.448414 to 0.433013.

per_task.generated_character: Large, multiply substituted nitrogen heteroaromatic diones dominate. Median optimizer heavy-atom counts are 45, 46 and 45 across seeds, with corresponding median ring counts of seven, five and five. Seed 1 keeps an N-alkylated fused dione core and several aryl/azaaryl rings, then adds fluorinated/chlorinated alkyl groups, an imidate-like side chain and an O-C-O-C(Cl)-N-containing acetal/aminal-like tether. Its cited leader has 54 heavy atoms, five aromatic rings and molecular weight 811.09 Da; another near-top example has 63 heavy atoms and weighs 969.64 Da. Seed 0 instead develops a more cyclized azaaromatic assembly and long oxygen chains: 269 of its 290 optimizer molecules contain an O-O bond. Seed 2 retains the dione/azaaryl ester assembly and develops sulfur-containing tails, visible in the cited final molecules. These are coherent families but demanding synthetic proposals. Relative to Parent, the seed-0 median shrinks from 91 to 45 heavy atoms while seed 2 grows from 31 to 45; a single overall size-change description would be misleading.
liabilities: High molecular weight, many aromatic rings and flexible substituted tails create a substantial physical-property and synthesis burden. Chlorinated acetal/aminal-like centres and imidates require chemistry beyond ordinary alkyl decoration.

The passive audit finds O-O bonds in 325 and S-S bonds in 72 of this task's 870 Child proposals. Peroxide and polysulfide chains need stability and compatibility assessment; their scores provide none.
Stereogenic substituted side chains are left unspecified. The 63-heavy-atom cited analogue has five graph-perceived unassigned chiral centres.
missing_features: Compact, independently varied decorations that retain useful heteroaromatic and polar environments without accumulating long heteroatom chains are missing among the Child leaders. The stronger compact Parent example supports keeping this possibility open, without establishing a matched causal comparison.

The leaders do not demonstrate a route-plausible range of ether, amine and carbonyl substituents at similar size and attachment geometry; a few families account for extensive local decoration. Pooled nonempty Murcko cores fall from 415 in Parent to 105 in Child.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial ester/phenol dione scores 0.548381482770623. A compact bis-pyridyl dione scores 0.5385026737967915, and simple hydroxyl or partially dearomatized analogues remain around 0.5427-0.5447. More elaborate heteroaryl substitution and longer heteroatom/alkyl decorations accompany the 0.6014791881664947 leader. Added size alone is insufficient: the cited 63-heavy-atom analogue scores slightly less, 0.6011334766464725. Sulfur-rich late seed-2 products remain near 0.595, despite O-S-S-S-containing and related tethers. This gradient tolerates chemically questionable decoration; it does not validate it. The Parent seed-2 leader reached 0.616992140985949 with 30 heavy atoms, further showing that a much larger assembly is not demonstrably required. In seed order 0, 1, 2, Parent-to-Child best accepted scores are 0.609280 to 0.593697, 0.619982 to 0.601479, 0.616992 to 0.595975.

per_task.generated_character: Halogenated aryl groups are combined with increasingly accessible amine functionality and partially saturated rings. Median heavy-atom counts are 32, 33 and 32 across seeds, with median aromatic-ring counts of two throughout. Seed 0 concentrates on a substituted cyclopentadiene joining aryl and amino-bearing sulfinamide chemistry; seed 1 develops an amine/amidine-rich fused and bridged polycycle. Seed 2, which supplies all digest leaders, joins two substituted aryl groups to a seven-membered diaza ring and an additional secondary amine. The first cited leader has 31 heavy atoms, three rings, molecular weight 467.05 Da, a phenol and an aniline, and sulfur doubly bonded to two terminal methylene carbons. That sulfur connectivity is graph-valid but far removed from the original sulfonamide chemistry. There is no shortage of amine centres in the successful products. Every Child optimizer molecule in this task has a graph-perceived unassigned chiral centre.
liabilities: Sulfur doubly bonded to two carbons occurs in 226 of 290 seed-2 proposals, including its leaders. RDKit acceptance is not evidence that this unusual sulfur functionality is stable or synthetically accessible.

The other seeds carry their own unresolved chemistry: densely fused amine/amidine rings, sulfenamide-like N-S connectivity or substituted cyclopentadiene systems. Their different chemistry should not be hidden behind the pooled best example.
All 870 proposals contain halogens and all 870 have unassigned graph-perceived chirality; size and binding scores alone do not settle chemical quality.
missing_features: Ordinary, tractable linkers that preserve the observed aryl-to-amine arrangement without the double-methylene sulfur centre are not demonstrated among the seed-2 leaders. The useful amine motif is already present; its chemical setting is the gap.

Defined stereoisomers and checked ring/side-chain geometry are absent despite the saturated, multiply substituted structures. Explicit charge states are also absent, so the visible neutral amines do not establish their protonation during scoring.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial acidic amide/sulfonamide assembly scores 0.01904115112334333; cited related early products score 0.009976648048984032-0.014368314381838294. They contain multiple carbonyl/acid groups and nitrogen tied into amide or sulfonamide environments. Higher products remove much of this acidic/carbonyl burden and expose amine-like nitrogen alongside aryl surfaces; the leading diaza-ring example reaches 0.9655637585918335. A primary-amine-containing analogue reaches 0.9588401522964047. The high-versus-low comparison in every seed supports this polar-functionality change, with reduced size also evident in the high-score groups. It cannot isolate the contribution of the unusual sulfur centre, predict protonation, or establish a binding mechanism. The full Parent trajectories reached their best values in amine-containing families without the Child's double-carbon sulfur motif. In seed order 0, 1, 2, Parent-to-Child best accepted scores are 0.995949 to 0.945006, 0.996455 to 0.941817, 0.991289 to 0.965564.

per_task.generated_character: Medium-sized aryl/dione families undergo ring closure and partial saturation rather than extensive size growth. Median heavy-atom counts are 34, 33 and 35 for seeds 0, 1 and 2. Seed 0 develops fused oxygen-containing aryl systems and expanded dione rings; seed 1 stays more aromatic with ether/acetal bridges. Seed 2 produces the digest leaders: propyl- and ethoxy-substituted aryl groups, lactam carbonyls and a tertiary amine embedded in a fused/bridged polycycle. Its top cited structure has 35 heavy atoms, molecular weight 473.62 Da and five RDKit rings, of which two are aromatic; its perceived ring sizes include a four-membered ring and a ten-membered ring. Another near-top connectivity has five rings with smallest/largest perceived sizes five and eight. These are structurally varied ring systems, but their geometry and preparation remain unverified. The more aromatic seeds explain why the pooled median still has four aromatic rings.
liabilities: Small rings combined with larger bridged/fused cycles and unsaturation can impose substantial geometric and synthetic constraints. The recorded scores and ring perception do not prove that these conformations are realizable.

Late products also introduce N-O or N-S links within already complicated architectures. The score for the cited N-S-containing final example is 0.2262793367697775; this is not evidence for improved chemical tractability.
missing_features: Independent, geometrically credible arrangements of the aryl, ether, lactam and amine environments are underrepresented relative to repeated variants of a few ring frameworks. No exact missing target substructure follows from these scalar scores.

Specified relative and absolute stereochemistry is missing from the partially saturated polycycles. The leading structure has two graph-perceived unassigned centres; its near-top alternative has three.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl ester/phenol fused dione scores 0.1678386594791329, and cited early fluoro/chloro/amino aryl variants score 0.15402959422966314-0.15625847779496568. Replacing these decorations with propyl/ethoxy groups, changing carbonyl-ring connectivity and adding partially saturated cyclic/amine environments accompanies the leader at 0.2386887674913355. A different bridged-ring topology scores 0.2380664345096624. Seed-2 high-score products have fewer aromatic rings than its early low-score products, so simply adding aromaticity is not the observed direction. Both aromatic and less aromatic solutions remain in the other streams, and the multi-feature edits do not identify one required ring closure. Pooled Parent-to-Child Murcko coverage decreases from 566 to 224, while endpoint changes are mixed. In seed order 0, 1, 2, Parent-to-Child best accepted scores are 0.222706 to 0.232446, 0.243215 to 0.227970, 0.230352 to 0.238689.

per_task.generated_character: Compact fluorinated derivatives of the N-alkylated fused dione replace the bulky initial decoration. Median heavy-atom counts are 28, 28 and 25 across seeds. Seed 0 develops cyclopropene, imine/oxime-like and N-F variants. Seed 1, which supplies the best digest examples, joins the dione to a fluorinated aryl ring fused to an N/O-containing ring; substituents include fluoromethoxy or fluoroethoxy groups. Its leader has 29 heavy atoms, molecular weight 414.32 Da and four rings, three aromatic, with a ring NH and an N-C-O-containing saturated segment. A different equal-scoring leader has an N-O bond. Seed 2 instead uses fluorinated alkyl substitutions and a seven-membered unsaturated oxygen ring bearing an OH; its cited leader has 27 heavy atoms, molecular weight 383.33 Da and three rings, two aromatic. These are distinct seed-specific products despite the common dione core.
liabilities: Direct N-F bonds, N-O connectivity, cyclopropene rings and cumulated double bonds appear in the full proposal stream. The digest cumulated-double-bond presence rate is 0.054 and its halogen-presence rate is 0.9023. These observations warrant structure-specific chemistry checks, not a claim that every member is unstable.

The fluorinated cyclic N/O products contain unspecified stereogenic carbons. Carbon-bound fluorine in an ordinary ether or alkyl group should be distinguished from direct N-fluorination; the scalar scores do not validate either synthetic route.
missing_features: Controlled alternatives placing comparable carbon-bound fluorine and ordinary nitrogen/oxygen functions on different compact cores are poorly represented among leaders; both small fragments and oversized analogues miss the observed balance.

Defined stereochemistry for the fused N/O-ring family is absent. The equal best values for differing N-C-O versus N-O connectivity also leave the preferred polar geometry unresolved; a task-specific pharmacophore cannot be inferred.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial ester/phenol dione scores 0.0020944534688323298. A larger cited aryl-extended ester analogue scores 2.861477157288716e-20, while a fluorobiphenyl fragment scores 1.5914126699678847e-18. The seed-1 N/O-ring leaders reach 0.5102212569858039 and the seed-2 fluorinated oxygen-ring example reaches 0.49929611529456036. The visible gradient therefore favours a bounded-size, fluorinated nitrogen/oxygen-containing assembly; neither fluorination alone nor growth suffices. Seed-1 N-C-O and N-O ring arrangements can share the same best score, so the data do not establish that an N-O bond is required. Late dione/fluoroalkyl edits range widely, including the cumulated-double-bond example at 0.37521555493964914 and an N-F/N-O-containing aryl product at 0.2227500990669383. Their multiple simultaneous changes preclude assigning these differences to one bond. In seed order 0, 1, 2, Parent-to-Child best accepted scores are 0.651021 to 0.418851, 0.487006 to 0.510221, 0.602525 to 0.499296.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Distinct nonempty atom-and-bond Murcko core counts fall in 14 of 15 paired streams. The compact indole family contracts from 276 to 103 pooled cores and the heavily decorated dione family from 415 to 105. Several best-molecule excerpts contain positional or peripheral variants of one seed-specific framework. These are observed output restrictions, not proof that the generator is absolutely incapable of another scaffold.
transferable_gaps.gap: The emitted search does not sustain a broad range of chemical cores around productive local motifs.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Create and retain independent core arrangements that preserve observed useful polar groups, approximate size and attachment relationships. Let accepted scalar feedback distinguish these alternatives. Further peripheral substitution alone does not demonstrate this missing breadth.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every recorded Child optimizer molecule parses, yet the leading amine-rich family contains sulfur doubly bonded to two carbons, present in 226 proposals. The decorated dione family contains O-O bonds in 325 proposals and S-S bonds in 72; its cited finals include extended sulfur/oxygen tethers. The fluorinated dione leaders include equal-scoring N-C-O and N-O ring alternatives, so unusual bonding is not uniformly required by the visible high scores.
transferable_gaps.gap: Graph validity does not reliably preserve conventional bonding or manageable functional-group chemistry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide chemically interpretable alternatives for changing heteroatom functionality while preserving useful connections. Assess unusual sulfur valence, long heteroatom chains and direct nitrogen-halogen edits separately from ordinary ethers, amides and carbon-bound halogens. Neither parsing nor a high scalar score is a chemical-feasibility check.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A leading decorated dione has 54 heavy atoms and molecular weight 811.09 Da; a near-top analogue has 63 heavy atoms and weighs 969.64 Da while scoring slightly lower. The corresponding Parent stream also contains a stronger 30-heavy-atom endpoint. Other compact families lose score both on fragmentation and on excessive extension, so the panel does not support a universal smaller-is-better rule.
transferable_gaps.gap: Decoration growth is not accompanied by reliable control of molecular size and synthetic burden.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support subtractive and size-preserving structural changes alongside growth, keeping useful functional-group relationships intact. Explore the empirically useful size region with simpler substituent chemistry rather than allowing chain length or repeated decoration to stand in for improved molecular design.

transferable_gaps.evidence: All digest stereocentre-marker rates are zero. Passive graph inspection finds unassigned chiral centres in 1768 of 4350 Child optimizer rows and no assigned centres. The leading bridged dione combines small and large rings, while a near-top topology differs in ring sizes and has more unassigned centres; neither has a demonstrated realizable stereoisomer.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output leaves stereochemistry and the geometry of newly created ring systems unresolved.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve, specify and validate stereochemical relationships when edits create saturated centres or ring junctions. Check geometric feasibility of constrained ring connectivity and distinguish graph-perceived possible chirality from realizable stereoisomers. The present scores do not establish a score gain from this capability.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Low-scoring acidic amide/sulfonamide assemblies evolve into much higher-scoring aryl/amine families while size, rings and sulfur connectivity also change. Compact indole leaders preserve an amide but alter aryl nitrogen and unsaturation; fluorinated dione leaders alter ring topology and heteroatom bonding together. These contrasts reveal promising environments without identifying the causal contribution of one group.
transferable_gaps.gap: Useful polar-functionality changes are often entangled with several unrelated chemical changes.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Generate local alternatives that vary donor/acceptor or amine connectivity while holding more of the surrounding framework and size fixed. Preserve explicit functional-group meanings and distinguish neutral amines from amide-bound nitrogen; derive any preference from observed feedback rather than assuming an objective-specific pharmacophore.

nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from accepted scored observations. It retains a bounded score-ranked breeding population, samples parents from favored score bands, and generates a fresh surplus pool through connected-fragment crossover and local mutation walks. Its crossover normally cuts one non-ring single bond in each parent and joins the retained fragments with one bond; where no such cut exists, it can attach a whole molecule at an available hydrogen site. Optional finishing mutation follows crossover. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled. Stable canonical identity checks reject invalid or duplicate proposals. A Gaussian process trained on all earlier accepted scores uses counts of local molecular environments and generalized Tanimoto similarity; correlated sampled score functions choose which fresh pool members receive evaluation. Accepted feedback updates both the model archive and the greedy breeding population.
approach.novelty: Add one two-cut ring-segment construction option to the existing crossover. When both actual scored parents have an eligible isolated nonaromatic ring, give the original crossover and the new option equal probability. The new option takes a connected ring segment, with all its attached subgraphs, from each parent and reconnects their two open ends into a ring. This supplies direct access to alternative two-attachment ring connectivities while keeping the original route available. Earlier siblings changed donor compatibility or excluded parent copies, and an older experiment protected every first-parent ring; those exposed changes lost score. This experiment changes which ring products can be constructed, without imposing those restrictions or assuming that distinct strings or preserved rings are useful. Its value depends on the new products surviving ordinary checks, receiving evaluations and improving the complete search.

nodes.hypothesis: Extend the inherited two-parent crossover with an equally weighted two-cut ring-segment mode only when both actual scored parents have eligible isolated nonaromatic-ring descriptors, joining one complete retained component from each parent by two single bonds while preserving the ordinary single-cut route and its no-support random law.

finding_summary.headline: Ring recombination reached evaluation and later breeding, but every seed mean fell
finding_summary.insights:
Failed construction and a globally blocked evaluation route do not explain this result: the new two-attachment products were built correctly, evaluated and reused. The complete exposed loss therefore supports a negative total contribution from this particular extension under the tested search composition, while leaving the separate evidence for ordinary crossover intact. Greater local win frequency is misleading here because the generating-parent references also became weaker. One positive endpoint even occurred in a run that never selected ring mode; its eligible mode draw changed the subsequent random stream, so that gain cannot be assigned to a new ring product.

The chemistry narrows the remaining limitation. The search now reaches medium and large nitrogen/carbonyl rings, including 72 accepted proposals with rings of at least twelve atoms, yet access to those graphs does not establish useful arrangements or feasible geometry. Finishing mutation also matters: the new typed ring pattern survives in all 124 pure evaluated recombinants but only 43 of the 55 finished ones. Aromatic, amine and carbonyl families remain well represented, alongside reactive bonds, difficult sulfur and small-ring structures, and unspecified stereochemistry. More scaffold identities and fewer molecules in a limited bond-alert screen coexist with lower scores. The unresolved question is which altered ancestors, pool competition and accepted feedback paths produced the endpoint loss; the observed cohorts do not supply scores for unselected alternatives or isolate an individual ring segment’s causal value. This complete failure closes the registered test without a ring-size, mode-weight or donor-preference sweep.
finding_summary.results:
Ring mode was selected on 5,498 of 10,982 jointly eligible opportunities. All 5,496 products constructed below the atom limit conserved the selected source components and made the intended two attachments; two selected choices exceeded the inherited atom limit before construction. There were 4,957 immediate products distinct from both parents and 539 parent copies. The route delivered 179 evaluated descendants of nonidentical constructions: 124 pure crossovers and 55 with finishing mutation. Another 11 evaluations gained novelty only by mutating a parent copy. All 174 nonidentical descendants with a later opportunity entered the next model fit, 96 later bred, 35 beat their best generating parent and 15 improved the incumbent. Exposure was uneven: none of the six zaleplon and decoration-hop runs evaluated a ring-mode descendant.

All fifteen Child task runs completed. Mean final Top-1 score fell from 0.595670 to 0.550623, a paired change of -0.045046 against the required +0.002. Seed macro changes were -0.014404, -0.020055 and -0.100680; ten task-seed endpoints declined, two improved and three were unchanged. Seed population SD increased from 0.026593 to 0.045826. The largest losses were docking seed 2 (-0.309828) and sitagliptin seeds 0 and 2 (-0.113615 and -0.189390). Across the entire search, local parent beats nevertheless rose from 629 to 652 and incumbent increases from 258 to 266.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic output includes cyclic amines and macrocyclic dicarbonyls, but also reactive bonds and doubtful ring geometry
molecular.overall_character:
Assessed n-870ed6964d46 against published code Parent n-62daf219c70a using every supplied actual Search trajectory: all five tasks, seeds 0, 1 and 2, and all 30 Child/Parent files. All paths exist; each file has 300 consecutive finite-score observations, comprising 10 initial molecules and 290 accepted optimizer proposals. The complete Child molecular digest is exactly reproduced from those files, including every excerpt, score span, unique count and string counter; all task summary endpoints and paired differences reconcile. Both context.comparison.child_complete and paired_complete are true, with no profile-mismatched seed or missing comparison. The fixed initial molecules and scores agree in every pairing. The complete molecular identity/score trajectories are identical for zaleplon_mpo seed 2 and deco_hop seeds 0 and 2. Those null cells are retained explicitly. Digest final_molecules are the last pooled proposals from seed 2, not per-seed incumbents; score_span includes initial observations, whereas best_molecules and worst_molecules describe optimizer proposals. All quantities below use actual accepted molecules and existing scores; no unselected pool alternative is scored or characterized as if evaluated.

The Child makes substituted indole amides, imides and vicinal diketones; dense linked nitrogen heterocycles; flexible and cyclic aryl amines; sulfur-rich cages; nitrogen/carbonyl macrocycles; and fluorinated, partially unsaturated ring systems. Its 4,350 accepted proposals have 1–120 heavy atoms, median 28; 4,244 contain a perceived ring and 4,177 an aromatic atom. The digest's taskwise ring-closure-string incidence is 0.9655–0.9851 and aromatic-string incidence 0.9184–0.9770; these are molecule-level text incidences, not aromatic-atom fractions. RDKit detects nonaromatic rings in 2,971 proposals, compared with 2,757 in Parent, and saturated rings in 1,610 versus 1,266. Rich ring chemistry therefore coexists with much narrower leading families within individual seeds. There are 1,977/1,851 distinct Child/Parent typed Murcko cores, 1,172/1,118 generic Murcko cores and 655/631 generic ring-only graphs across the whole panel. Per-task and per-seed changes are mixed. Seventy-two Child proposals have a perceived ring of at least 12 atoms, all within the nitrogen/carbonyl macrocycle stream; this count is 9, 1 and 62 by seed, versus zero in each matching Parent cell. The largest Child perceived ring has 23 atoms. These counts establish access to varied graphs, not useful topology, geometric feasibility or synthesis.

Local chemical liabilities remain substantial but are not universal: 634 Child proposals have an N–halogen bond, 123 O–halogen, 294 O–O and 12 halogen–halogen; 1,010 have at least one of these motifs, versus 1,490 in Parent. Those overlapping motif counts form a limited structural screen, not a complete reactivity or safety model. Several near-leading flexible or piperidine-containing amines have none of these bonds; conversely, an alert-free sulfur cage and small unsaturated ring graphs remain chemically questionable. RDKit flags potential tetrahedral centres in 2,534 Child proposals versus 2,408 Parent proposals, yet all are unassigned, and there are no explicitly assigned atom chiral tags or double-bond stereo tags in either accepted stream. All atoms also have zero formal charge. Neutral aliphatic amines are visibly present, so this does not mean an absence of basic centres or establish a physical protonation state. Synthetic plausibility is a cautious structural reading: recognizable amides, aryl groups, piperidines, sulfoxides and macrocyclic motifs coexist with N–halogen/O–halogen chemistry, peroxides, complex bridges and small-ring unsaturation. No conformer, stability measurement or synthetic route was supplied, and graph sanitation is not such evidence.

Audit definitions: RDKit 2023.09.6 parsed all 9,000 trajectory rows. Reported rings are its perceived atom rings. Typed cores use GetScaffoldForMol; generic cores use MakeScaffoldGeneric on that scaffold; both omit stereochemistry and map every empty scaffold to one <acyclic> sentinel. The separate generic ring-only graph retains only perceived ring bonds and their incident atoms, removes exocyclic atoms and inter-ring linkers, then makes atoms carbon and bonds single, preserving disconnected-ring multiplicity. Ten highest-scoring proposals per cell are ordered by the existing score and then evaluation number; this is a descriptive chemistry stratum. The aliphatic-amine proxy requires neutral, nonaromatic trivalent N with single bonds to carbon only, excluding aromatic carbon neighbors and carbons double-bonded to N/O/S; it is not a measured basicity or protonation rule. Ring labels, exact core identity and substructure similarity are structural observations. Pedigree ancestry requires its own accepted-parent receipts; literal retained source atoms require source-indexed maps at construction and separate post-edit mapping. These trajectories carry neither, and this report makes no ancestry, atom-conservation or component-contribution inference from scaffold coverage. Reproducible full-panel measurements and file hashes are in .slots/L01-resume-20260928/r22-slot0-molecular/audit.json. Inherited chemical gaps retain their first-recorded n-c55c3d520a2c origin and original profile boundary, their published n-62daf219c70a recurrence, and the present current-profile recurrence; no historical effect estimates are pooled.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 accepted proposals span 1–38 heavy atoms, median 24; 840 contain perceived rings and 838 contain aromatic atoms. Seed 0's 25-heavy-atom leader at evaluation 196 is an ethyl/methyl/methoxy-substituted indole carboxamide linked to chloropyridine, with fluorine bonded directly to the indole nitrogen. Seed 1's 25-heavy-atom leader at evaluation 275 has an N-aminomethyl indole joined through an acyclic imide to fluoropyridine; it contains carbon-bound halogen and no N–halogen bond. Seed 2's 24-heavy-atom leader at evaluation 294 keeps an N-chloroindole–aryl vicinal diketone with an aminomethyl substituent. All three leaders have three perceived rings, with sizes 5, 6 and 6. These retain compact fused aromatic/carbonyl organization rather than lacking rings. N–halogen-containing proposals are 132, 14 and 25 by seed, compared with 190, 230 and 25 in Parent. Seed 2 is molecularly identical to Parent; seeds 0 and 1 change family details in different directions. Top-ten generic-core counts are 2, 4 and 2, compared with Parent 3, 1 and 2, so neither total collapse nor uniform diversification is supported. Across all 870 accepted proposals, Child/Parent distinct typed Murcko cores are 256/295, generic Murcko cores 107/124, and generic ring-only graphs 57/70. These are different structural coverage measurements under the fixed acyclic convention, not independent chemical families or atom-provenance counts.
liabilities: N–F, N–Cl and N–Br substitutions on an indole nitrogen are not interchangeable with ordinary aryl carbon–halogen bonds; their local reactivity requires assessment.
Vicinal diketones, acyclic imides and N-aminomethyl substitution introduce context-dependent reactivity or stability questions; recognized group names are not a synthetic route.
Tiny late fragments lose the composite framework, while additional polar branches can also lower score. Neither liability supports a universal size or heteroatom rule.
missing_features: The favorable aromatic/carbonyl organization is demonstrated, but a consistently conventional local nitrogen environment at the same leading score is not; the high-scoring N–C imide and N–H diketone are real counterexamples to any claim that ordinary nitrogen substitution is inaccessible.

Independent, chemically credible alternatives to indole-centered leading families remain incompletely demonstrated. Generic-core and ring-graph variation measures cannot establish that the alternatives have suitable geometry or synthesis.
The trajectory does not reveal an exact missing pharmacophore, and it does not support simply adding rings, nitrogen or fluorine.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxyindole anilide (seed 0, evaluation 9) scores 0.3051048083696145. The seed-0 N-fluoro/pyridyl-amide leader reaches 0.4387992465191, and seed 1's imide with ordinary N–C substitution reaches 0.4279555137322127. Seed 2's diketone reaches 0.438972502037081, while its N–H indole/azaaryl diketone at evaluation 220 reaches 0.4259670894318899 without N–halogen. Thus the observed reward accompanies a combined aromatic and carbonyl arrangement, not a demonstrated requirement for a reactive nitrogen substituent. A more elaborated seed-2 relative at evaluation 297 scores 0.2537139094300773; extra aminoalkyl substitution is not uniformly rewarded. Removing most of the framework leaves seed 0's final pyridyl acetamide at 6.9339977595548645e-09, and acetylene at evaluation 279 scores 0.0. The ten lowest-scoring proposals in seeds 0 and 1 are all acyclic small graphs. These contrasts do not identify an exact absent target motif. Existing Child/Parent final Top-1 values are seed 0: 0.4387992465/0.3940514207 (difference +0.0447478258); seed 1: 0.4279555137/0.4741170181 (difference -0.0461615044); seed 2: 0.4389725020/0.4389725020 (difference +0.0000000000). These are descriptive paired outcomes, not scores assigned by this report.

per_task.generated_character: Accepted proposals span 1–100 heavy atoms, median 33; 850/870 contain rings and 849 aromatic atoms. Seed 0's 30-heavy-atom leader at evaluation 281 has five perceived rings: a quinazoline-like aromatic region joined to a densely fused/bridged nitrogen/carbonyl/thione region, with aryl chlorine, O–F and a fluorinated chloromethyl-ether appendage. Seed 1's 38-heavy-atom leader at evaluation 287 has six perceived rings, a linked aza/oxygen heterocycle-carbonyl assembly, a carbon-bound aryl fluoride, a chlorinated alkynyl side chain and an O–O-containing ring region. Its 35-heavy-atom counterpart at evaluation 276 keeps six rings, a carbon-linked nitrile and ether-linked heterocycles without O–O or heteroatom–halogen bonds. Seed 2's 37-heavy-atom leader at evaluation 296 instead joins substituted aryl/azaaryl regions through peroxide-containing and nitrogen-containing connections, including nitrite and N=S functionality. Seeds 0 and 2 reproduce Parent's complete molecular trajectories. Only seed 1 changes: its nonaromatic-ring incidence is 251/290 versus Parent 40/290, and O–O incidence 37/290 versus 4/290. Familiar aromatic and carbonyl groups coexist with difficult ring junctions and local substituents; the very large proposals are not representative of every leader. Across all 870 accepted proposals, Child/Parent distinct typed Murcko cores are 436/404, generic Murcko cores 317/277, and generic ring-only graphs 194/144. These are different structural coverage measurements under the fixed acyclic convention, not independent chemical families or atom-provenance counts.
liabilities: O–F on an aromatic oxygen, a halomethyl ether, thione, and crowded ring junctions make the seed-0 graph a questionable synthetic target despite its recognizable heterocyclic portions.

O–O bonds occur in 251/870 Child proposals, including ring and linker contexts; other leaders retain nitrite and N=S groups. These are distinct local chemistry issues, not an objection to all ethers, heterocycles or nitriles.
No synthesis, stable tautomer or conformation is demonstrated for the complex aromatic-labelled O–O ring region or the additional cross-linked products.
missing_features: Reliable access to conventional peripheral chemistry around the favorable linked heterocyclic arrangements is not demonstrated at the strongest score. The close no-peroxide seed-1 example is a useful counterexample to a universal need for the peroxide-containing region.

nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

retained_mechanisms: Task-local finite accepted-score archive, a score/serial ordered 64-member greedy breeding population, and favored score-quantile sampling with exclusion of the first parent from the second draw.

The original non-ring single-cut/whole-fragment crossover route, plus the conditional equally weighted physical two-cut ring-segment variant with deterministic full-component descriptors and two endpoint pairings.
The inherited 0.45 crossover opportunity, obstruction multiplier, 0.35 optional finishing mutation and ordinary one-/two-/three-step continuation with saturation laws.

Ordinary atom replacement, append, delete, insert, bond change, ring closure and ring opening; direct aromatic C/N exchange remains disabled, with its passive enumeration and unreachable implementation retained.
Connected sanitation, stable canonical identity admission, initial/emitted and temporary-pool duplicate rejection, bounded retry handling and full 160-member fresh surplus pools.

Integer-count Morgan fingerprints, generalized Tanimoto similarity, full chronological accepted-archive GP fitting, raw-score mean/scale normalization, fixed noise/jitter and full posterior covariance.
Correlated masked posterior function draws, pool-index/fit-version emission receipts, pending accepted-identity joins and next-fit prediction probes.

Task-local source-index snapshots and descriptor memoization keyed by the exact atom/bond representation, plus passive mutation/crossover/identity diagnostics; no product library, extra scored selector or learned external model.
Fresh objective state and the inherited deterministic prepared settings, protocol-announced batch size, evaluation procedure and resource/budget interface.

approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs using accepted task-local scores. It keeps a bounded score-ranked breeding population, draws parents from high-scoring rank bands, and produces either connected-fragment crossovers with optional finishing mutation or ordinary mutation walks. Ordinary walks usually make one edit call and sometimes two or three; obstruction can force longer walks. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled. At each suggestion the Parent fits its count-fingerprint Gaussian process to the complete accepted archive, generates a fresh surplus pool containing only final products, and uses correlated posterior draws to choose the announced evaluation batch. Real accepted scores then update both breeding survivors and the next model fit. The model is already fitted when a mutation walk starts, but does not guide its intermediate steps.
approach.novelty: Add two-arm posterior-mean guidance to optional ordinary continuation. After the unchanged first mutation, each requested second or third step at the ordinary saturation floor tries two fresh mutations from the same current intermediate and continues with the higher predicted raw score. Only the chosen path's final product can enter the original pool. Earlier siblings removed continuation, admitted intermediate products into finite pool slots, or changed predictive fitting and final allocation. This variant preserves the continuation schedule, independent final-product slots and correlated final selector while changing one decision inside the walk. It tests whether an existing useful predictor can guide the next graph step; a predicted arm advantage is evidence of that decision, not measured score improvement.

nodes.hypothesis: Modify optional ordinary second/third mutation continuation at saturation floor one by drawing exactly two fresh arms from the same current intermediate and continuing with the valid arm of greatest raw-score posterior mean from the existing suggestion-entry accepted-label count GP, with first-arm exact ties and bounded inherited fallbacks, while retaining the full final-product pool and correlated final selector.

finding_summary.headline: Two-arm choices reached evaluation and later breeding, but mean Top-1 fell by 0.048083
finding_summary.insights: This result rules out lack of execution, absent evaluated delivery, lost feedback, zero cohort-level recursion and reduced final-pool capacity as explanations for the failure of this fixed rule. The model successfully imposed its preferences without producing better search. Across all accepted offspring, mean raw score fell from 0.385256 to 0.326704 while mean best-generating-parent score fell from 0.470456 to 0.395280. Parent-beating counts rose from 629 to 690 and incumbent-update counts from 258 to 261, yet total incumbent increments fell from 5.807663 to 5.086425. More local wins therefore coexist with weaker sources and less endpoint progress. Selected-stream prediction MSE fell from 0.012718 to 0.007832, but the labels being predicted changed and recorded 1.96-standard-deviation coverage fell from 76.28% to 74.60%; this does not establish better transferable calibration. Chemistry inspection likewise finds both recognizable aromatic amides and amines and persistent questionable bond environments, ring geometries and unresolved stereochemistry. The largest deficits include failure to reproduce a compact high-scoring heterocyclic combination, but neither missing rings/amines nor a specific chemical mediator is established. Most unchosen arms remain unscored, and no alternate continuation future was executed. The evidence supports a negative total contribution of this exact fixed guidance rule under these conditions; it leaves the separate roles of local prediction preferences, extra random draws and later adaptive history unresolved, and does not reverse the value of ordinary continuation itself.
finding_summary.results: The continuation rule executed 8,640 two-arm decisions. Independently reconstructed predictions confirm 4,266 strict choices of a different second-arm identity; 44 exact ties chose the first arm. Those changed paths delivered 237 distinct evaluated finals. All 230 with another suggestion remaining entered the next model fit, and 120 later served as breeding parents. The audit also retains 110 nonterminal finals with no later use and seven terminal births; one task/seed had six affected accepted finals and no later breeding. Final proposal capacity stayed at 160 products per suggestion. Nevertheless, mean final Top-1 fell from 0.595670 to 0.547587, a paired change of -0.048083 against the required +0.002. All three seed macros and all five task means decreased; four of the 15 individual task/seed cells improved. Macro population SD declined from 0.026593 to 0.017941, but the gain criterion failed.
