molecular.headline: Aromatic amides and aryl amines coexist with enlarged heterocycles, reactive bonds and unresolved stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: Node n-87c89dda7e3b produces substituted indole amides, azaaromatic methylamines, compressed ring systems, linked nitrogen-rich carbonyl/thione assemblies, flexible and cyclic aryl amines, medium-ring lactams and fluorinated imino/dione heterocycles. Ordinary medicinal-chemistry groups are present, but many outputs also contain unusual heteroatom bonds, large repeated assemblies or unresolved ring geometry. Some leaders are appreciably more conventional than their close high-scoring relatives; neither universal implausibility nor a general absence of rings, amines or heterocycles fits the evidence. Structural diversity is moderate across seeds and tasks, with recurring leading families within individual streams. The weak drug-likeness judgement concerns the mixed output and its liabilities, not a claim that every compound is unsuitable. No synthesis, stability, protonation, conformation or biological activity has been established by this inspection. The digest was read before all 15 Child and 15 published Parent trajectory files. All paths exist; all 9,000 records were read, covering every task and Search Seed 0, 1 and 2. Each task has 900 Child records, including 870 evaluated optimizer proposals. There are no tasks without trajectories. The immutable comparison reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true, matched seeds 0, 1 and 2, and no profile mismatch. This is therefore a complete descriptive chemistry comparison with n-62daf219c70a, not an absent or partial Parent comparison. The profile is the supplied Research in Depth profile, 300 observations per task and feedback batch size 10, with direct aromatic C/N exchange disabled. The Parent source of record is runs/SPIRAL2/nodes/n-62daf219c70a/seed-{0,1,2}/trajectories; its full Molecular report and the original n-c55c3d520a2c gap report were read through the supplied evidence index. Current gaps retain that historical provenance while describing changed current molecules. In fixed task order, digest ring-closure-string incidences are 0.9655, 0.9747, 0.9862, 0.9839 and 0.9517; aromatic-atom-string incidences are 0.9644, 0.9736, 0.9839, 0.9747 and 0.9506. These are molecule-level SMILES-text incidences, not aromatic atom fractions or ring counts. Every task has charged-string and stereocentre-string incidence 0.0. Neutral strings nevertheless contain readily recognizable ionizable amines. Independent RDKit readings of evaluated optimizer molecules give median heavy-atom counts 25, 43, 33, 32 and 27; no optimizer row failed parsing. Parsing does not certify chemical feasibility. All counts and molecule descriptors below derive from these supplied trajectories; the audit and annotated row provenance are in .slots/round-0024-slot-1/molecular_chemistry_audit_slot1.json and molecular_annotated_trajectories_slot1.jsonl. Scores are the recorded labels, never recomputed. Last emissions are distinguished from retained best molecules. Unchosen continuation arms have no labels here and receive no chemical outcome credit. Changed chemical families, alert counts or high-score associations do not identify activation, component contribution, mediation, or the cause of any endpoint difference.

per_task.generated_character: Evaluated proposals have median 25 heavy atoms, range 1-41, and predominantly aromatic ring systems. Seed 2 reaches a 24-heavy-atom ethynyl/dimethyl/methoxy indole carboxamide attached to pyridine: a recognizable three-ring heteroaryl amide without a halogen or sulfur triple bond. Seed 0 instead reaches a 25-heavy-atom dimethoxy azaaromatic bicyclic region joined through methylene and an N-chloro or N-bromo aniline nitrogen to a fluorophenyl ring; this leading family has no carbonyl. Seed 1 reaches a 24-heavy-atom oxygenated, tightly connected ring framework carrying an imine, a ketone and an amino/pyridyl side chain; RDKit perceives four-membered closures and an unassigned centre. The stream can therefore make conventional aromatic amides, but it also explores strained connectivities and carbon-sulfur triple-bond strings. Such sulfur bonds occur in 95 of 870 Child optimizer rows versus none of the matched Parent rows for this task. N-halogen bonds occur in 314 Child rows versus 445 Parent rows, so one liability declines while another appears.
liabilities: N-Cl and N-Br substitution occurs on amine or amide nitrogen in strong examples; the carbon-sulfur triple-bond strings are particularly unusual synthetic targets.
Dense small-ring connectivity in seed 1 and its unspecified stereochemical centre leave geometry and molecular identity unresolved.
Tiny floor-scoring molecules are still evaluated late, including the seed-0 NCl and seed-1 oxetane at evaluation 286.
missing_features: Consistent conventional bond environments around the favorable compact aromatic/polar arrangement are missing across the emitted set, although the leading seed-2 indole amide is an explicit counterexample to universal chemical implausibility.
Independent feasible replacements for the compressed seed-1 topology are not demonstrated at its leading score; a ring-rich string alone does not establish a geometrically accessible scaffold.

The observed scores do not identify a unique absent target pharmacophore. Amide, carbonyl-free azaaromatic and constrained families all score above the initial best, so no single functional group can be prescribed from this panel.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxyindole anilide scores 0.3051048083696145. The conventional ethynyl indole amide at seed 2 evaluation 256 reaches 0.447213595499958; the sulfur-triple-bond relative at evaluation 208 scores 0.4357560621547693. These differ at several substituents and do not isolate a sulfur-bond effect, but the best observed score plainly does not require that unusual bond. The seed-0 N-Cl and N-Br analogues at evaluations 241 and 282 tie at 0.436818201428663, while the compressed seed-1 framework reaches 0.40282869817021466. NCl, methane and oxetane each score 0.0 in the cited rows: isolated groups or ring presence alone do not reproduce the reward. The visible association is with a compact combined aromatic/polar arrangement; an amide is useful in one family but absent from another leader. Matched Parent best scores in seed order are 0.39405142067435733, 0.47411701813450596, 0.438972502037081; Child values are 0.436818201428663, 0.40282869817021466, 0.447213595499958. Thus the changed families include both favorable and adverse seed comparisons. Parent leaders also retain N-halogen or cumulene liabilities, so those comparisons are not a chemical-quality standard.

per_task.generated_character: This is the most enlarged output family: median 43 heavy atoms and maximum 120, compared with 33 and 100 in the Parent. Digest mean SMILES length is 85.6. The seed-2 leader has 50 heavy atoms and joins nitrogen heteroaromatics to a carbonyl/thione-containing aromatic-labelled nine-membered ring, with an enyne/diyne appendage, chloromethyl and bromoethyl-ester groups. A near-leading 37-heavy-atom relative instead has a conventional fused five/six-membered heterocyclic region. Seed 0 favors a 37-heavy-atom linked aminopyridine/azole assembly with N-acyl, vinyl, ketone and aldehyde functionality. Seed 1 reaches a 62-heavy-atom repeated fused nitrogen-dione assembly; nearby examples use peroxide linkages and N-halogen bonds. These are rich ring graphs, but their repeated units, numerous heteroatoms and reactive attachments make straightforward synthesis and ordinary drug-like size doubtful.
liabilities: Oversized repeated heterocycles carry many carbonyl and heteroatom groups while giving only modest changes within the observed score band.
Strong examples include peroxides, N-halogen bonds, haloalkyl esters, chloromethyl groups and cumulene chains; these raise environment-specific reactivity and synthesis concerns.

Aromatic notation on a nine-membered heterocycle does not establish an accessible planar aromatic state. The near-tied smaller fused-ring relative shows that this unusual topology is not universally required.
missing_features: Compact alternatives retaining the favorable linked nitrogen/carbonyl/thione organization are not consistently delivered at the stronger Parent score. Compactness is already possible in the Child and is not itself a demonstrated causal remedy.
Conventional, synthetically credible substitutes for the repeated peroxide/N-halogen assemblies and haloalkynyl appendages are not established at their recorded scores.

The larger aromatic-labelled ring lacks demonstrated conformational and tautomeric identity; no exact missing objective-specific arrangement can be inferred solely from the Parent/Child family difference.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl fused dione scores 0.548381482770623. Child seed leaders score 0.6010870669511328, 0.5968277867192773, 0.6097957431147641; matched Parent leaders score 0.8561477222467935, 0.6248206599713055, 0.6178024026512013. The Parent seed-0 leader is a compact 30-heavy-atom linked fused nitrogen/carbonyl/thione system, although it too contains reactive oxygen/halogen and ether substituents. The Child does not reproduce that high-scoring combination in its leading output. Within Child seed 2, the 50-heavy-atom evaluation-289 leader scores 0.6097957431147641 and the smaller 37-heavy-atom evaluation-296 relative scores 0.6095356709459028. Several larger variants, including differing cumulated side chains at evaluations 261 and 299, share 0.6077788191190253. The 120-heavy-atom assembly at evaluation 57 scores only 0.565359477124183. Size, repeated rings and extra unsaturation therefore do not uniformly buy reward. Hydrazine and an isolated haloalkyne sit at 0.5; that floor is not evidence of useful chemistry. The observed gradient concerns particular combined heterocyclic arrangements, with considerable peripheral indifference, rather than a general demand for more rings or atoms.

per_task.generated_character: Proposals have median 33 heavy atoms, range 1-107. The seed-0 leader is a relatively conventional 25-heavy-atom molecule with two alkyl-linked phenyl rings, two primary amines, two phenols and carbon-bound fluorine. Seed 2 builds fluorinated/chlorinated aryl groups and a dimethylaminophenol around saturated five-membered diamine or piperazine rings, connected through flexible carbon or thioether-containing chains. The 30-heavy-atom seed-2 leader has a five-membered diamine. Seed 1 instead retains an unusual hydrogen-bearing sulfur centre written with oxo, hydroxyl, aryl and nitrogen bonds, along with a four-membered nitrogen ring, pyrrolidine, chloromethyl and fluorinated aryl groups; its leader has 33 heavy atoms. Accessible aliphatic amines and saturated nitrogen rings are plainly present. Conventional examples have recognizable synthetic handles, while the sulfur-rich and small-ring variants are less convincing. RDKit finds unassigned potential atom centres in 848 of 870 optimizer rows, with none assigned.
liabilities: The seed-1 hydrogen-bearing hypervalent sulfur environment, small nitrogen rings and chloromethyl group warrant chemical scrutiny; representability is not proof of an ordinary stable sulfur functional group.
Flexible multiply aminated chains, phenols, thioethers and occasional N-O or O-Cl substituents leave stability, oxidation and solution-state behaviour unresolved.
The neutral SMILES omit stereochemical assignments even where the parsed structures contain potential centres; neutral notation does not mean the amines are nonionizable.
missing_features: The missing capability is reliable presentation of the already present aromatic/available-amine organization in conventional, resolved structures; neither basic nitrogen nor saturated nitrogen rings are absent.

Specified stereochemical identity is absent for the branched chains, fluorinated centres and substituted nitrogen rings. Actual protonation and conformational preferences are unmeasured by this audit.

No observed matched molecular comparison identifies a unique additional pharmacophore needed to recover the Parent values. The seed-0 conventional amines are a counterexample to a claim that all strong outputs require unusual sulfur or nitrogen-halogen chemistry.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial best shown scores 0.01904115112334333. N-sulfonyl pyrrolidine/amide fragments at seed 2 evaluations 18 and 17 score 0.00016650955053713697 and 0.0002562175393167918. The two-primary-amine/diaryl phenol leader reaches 0.9939842754428707. Its O-amino relative at seed 0 evaluation 271 scores 0.9898084892495691, so the extra N-O bond is not needed for the stronger observed result. The five-membered diamine leader reaches 0.977819851459075 and a piperazine relative reaches 0.9725770376635565. These examples associate accessible aliphatic nitrogen plus aromatic surfaces with high labels; they do not isolate a pKa, amine count or specific binding interaction. The 107-heavy-atom early assembly scores 0.02885837683273389, showing that aromatic bulk alone is insufficient. The lower seed-1 Child stream retains the unusual sulfur/small-ring family, but that association does not establish that this chemistry caused its deficit. These are oracle labels, not measured affinity, selectivity or verified docking geometry.

per_task.generated_character: Proposals have median 32 heavy atoms, range 1-62, with substantially less halogen incidence than the other streams: the digest halogen-string rate is 0.177. The seed-1 leader has 33 heavy atoms and links a substituted quinoline through methylene ether to an aryl-fused 11-membered lactam ring containing additional N-methyl amines. Seed 0 has 34-heavy-atom diaryl ether/amine frameworks joined through an exocyclic alkene to a bridged nitrogen dicarbonyl system with a four-membered ring. Seed 2 has a 30-heavy-atom quinoline linked to nitrogen-containing seven-membered ring paths and two carbonyl groups. These combine recognizable ethers, amines, lactams and aromatic surfaces, but the bridges and medium rings create substantial route and conformational questions. They are not ring-deficient or heteroatom-deficient fragments. The Parent shows related quinoline/dicarbonyl and bridged diaryl families, rather than an entirely separate chemical regime.
liabilities: Dense four-membered/medium-ring junctions and exocyclic unsaturation complicate geometric feasibility and synthesis even when all atoms have accepted valence.
The macrocyclic-lactam family is not intrinsically impossible, but no route or populated conformation is demonstrated; larger ring count is not evidence of richer useful chemistry.
Peripheral N-O insertion and further elaboration can reduce the score while retaining the same difficult framework; neither complexity nor heteroatom count is monotonically rewarded.
missing_features: Chemically independent, geometrically characterized alternatives preserving the favorable aromatic/amine/carbonyl relationship are not established; current leaders repeatedly retain medium-ring or bridged connectivity.

Explicit stereochemical identity is missing in the bridged and saturated examples, although the leading seed-1 macrocyclic graph has no RDKit-enumerated unassigned atom centre and still has unmeasured conformational preferences.
No unique absent target motif is resolved by the small differences among the leading families. Conventional nitrogen, oxygen, carbonyl and aromatic functions already occur together.

Seed-1 evaluation 264, the quinoline/macrocyclic-lactam leader, scores 0.22653939982357355; its methyl-for-ethyl relative at evaluation 194 scores 0.2240284446102978. Enlarging the lactam closure with an N-O connection at evaluation 294 gives 0.22271156434457534. The seed-0 evaluation-254 and evaluation-288 molecules tie at 0.22427840319352513 despite a nitrogen-to-carbon ring-site difference. This supports tolerance of more than one local nitrogen arrangement, not an exact missing heteroatom prescription. A 62-heavy-atom repeated early assembly scores 0.1273277339340891, below the initial best. The combined aromatic/amine/carbonyl organization matters more visibly than simply increasing size or ring count. Child seed leaders are 0.22427840319352513, 0.22653939982357355, 0.21763406411564537; matched Parent leaders are 0.2258403994203931, 0.2214095461892601, 0.22600312875247064. The seed-1 improvement and seed-0/seed-2 decreases coexist. The final seed-2 emission scores 0.2044644469050835, below its retained 0.21763406411564537 leader; it is not the endpoint incumbent.

per_task.generated_character: Proposals have median 27 heavy atoms, range 1-61. The seed-0 leader is a 27-heavy-atom fused five/six-membered nitrogen dione carrying an imidoyl-fluoride group, N-alkoxymethyl substitution and a fluorinated alkenyl chain. Its fluorines are carbon-bound, not N-F. Seed 1 instead joins a hydroxypyridine to an aromatic-labelled nine-membered nitrogen-dione ring with N-fluorine, alkyl and haloalkyl groups; a close high-scoring relative replaces N-F with N-fluoroalkyl substitution. Seed 2 reaches a 28-heavy-atom framework with two perceived nine-membered aromatic rings, carbonyls and a fluorinated thiol-containing ketone side chain. The smaller fused core is more conventional than the large aromatic-labelled rings, but the imidoyl fluoride, unsaturated substitution and solution-state identities still require scrutiny. Child N-halogen incidence is 251 of 870 optimizer rows versus 476 in the Parent; digest cumulated-double-bond-string incidence is only 0.0011. Those reductions do not remove the large-ring or other local bonding concerns.
liabilities: The imidoyl-fluoride substituent is an unusual electrophilic motif, while some other leaders retain N-F bonds or haloalkyl groups. Carbon-bound fluorination itself is not a blanket liability.
Two nine-membered rings labelled aromatic, or a single expanded nitrogen-dione ring, require geometry and tautomer checks beyond SMILES acceptance.
Tiny fluorine-containing emissions remain late in the stream, while early repeated assemblies are extremely low scoring; both loss of context and excessive elaboration are visible.
missing_features: A conventional, geometrically credible alternative to the large aromatic-labelled rings is not demonstrated at those seeds' leading scores. The seed-0 fused core shows that large rings and N-F bonds are not universal requirements.

The favorable compact fluorinated/polar organization is not consistently expressed with ordinary stable functional groups; imidoyl fluoride, N-F and unusual ring representations remain among strong outputs.

Stereochemical identity of the fluorinated saturated seed-2 chain and the tautomeric, imine/alkene and conformational identities of the heterocycles are unresolved. The trajectory does not identify an exact absent target pharmacophore.

Seed 2 reaches 0.47065134047819507, whereas its more fluorinated final emission scores 0.34837829103775814. The exact group context matters, but none of these labels establishes feasibility. The Parent seed-2 leader contains a small cyclic cumulene of doubtful geometry. Its stronger label does not make that motif a required or chemically credible answer.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source: the gap was recorded for n-c55c3d520a2c and retained by the identical-trajectory baseline n-62daf219c70a; it is re-observed in changed outputs of n-87c89dda7e3b on Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2 under the supplied 300-observation, batch-10 profile with direct aromatic C/N exchange disabled. Strong emitted examples include N-halogen bonds, peroxide links, an imidoyl fluoride, an unusual hydrogen-bearing sulfur environment and carbon-sulfur triple-bond strings. One current aromatic-amide stream has 95 sulfur-triple-bond outputs versus none in its matched Parent stream, yet its best molecule contains an ordinary terminal alkyne instead. Conventional indole amides, primary arylalkyl amines and saturated diamine rings are counterexamples to a universal inability to generate plausible groups.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve conventional local bond environments while retaining otherwise useful aromatic and polar structures.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Task-agnostic transformations need awareness of the bonding environment and the ability to offer conventional alternatives while preserving combinations supported by local accepted feedback. Ordinary carbon-bound halogens and useful amines must remain distinguishable from unusual heteroatom bonds. These observations justify a chemical capability gap, not a universal filter, a guaranteed score gain, or attribution to the current continuation decision.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source: the gap was recorded for n-c55c3d520a2c and retained by the identical-trajectory baseline n-62daf219c70a; it is re-observed in changed outputs of n-87c89dda7e3b on Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2 under the supplied 300-observation, batch-10 profile with direct aromatic C/N exchange disabled. Current leading families include compressed four-membered closures, medium-ring bridged carbonyl systems and aromatic-labelled nine-membered heterocycles. Historical Parent cyclic-cumulene concerns remain source-specific; the current best fused fluorinated dione does not require a cyclic cumulene. Conventional fused indoles and saturated diamines are present, and a smaller fused heterocycle nearly ties a larger expanded-ring relative. Ring richness is therefore real, but reliable geometric credibility is not established.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably distinguish a valid ring graph from a credible ring geometry and unsaturation pattern.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring construction and scaffold changes need ring-size, bridge-connectivity and unsaturation awareness, together with feasible alternative connectivities that retain learned functional relationships. Aromatic labels and ring counts cannot supply that information. This is not a ban on small or medium rings, nor evidence that geometric scrutiny would itself improve the recorded objective.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source: the gap was recorded for n-c55c3d520a2c and retained by the identical-trajectory baseline n-62daf219c70a; it is re-observed in changed outputs of n-87c89dda7e3b on Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2 under the supplied 300-observation, batch-10 profile with direct aromatic C/N exchange disabled. Every digest task has stereocentre-string incidence 0.0. Parsed current arylalkyl amines, substituted diamines, bridged carbonyl frameworks and fluorinated chains contain unassigned potential atom centres; one emitted aryl-amine stream has such centres in 848 of 870 optimizer rows, with none assigned. Some compact aromatic leaders have no enumerated atom centre, so this gap applies when a structure actually requires specification. Charge-string incidence is also 0.0, but recognizable ionizable amines are already present.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not resolve stereochemical identity after generating potentially stereogenic saturated and bridged centres.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Representation and transformations need to preserve or deliberately resolve stereochemistry when relevant, while keeping achiral and configurationally unstable cases distinct. Protonation, tautomerism and conformational identity are separate questions. This evidence establishes unspecified chemical identity, not a measured stereochemical score penalty or a missing basic-amine capability.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source: the gap was recorded for n-c55c3d520a2c and retained by the identical-trajectory baseline n-62daf219c70a; it is re-observed in changed outputs of n-87c89dda7e3b on Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2 under the supplied 300-observation, batch-10 profile with direct aromatic C/N exchange disabled. Current evaluated streams contain tiny floor-scoring fragments late in search and repeated heterocyclic assemblies up to 120 heavy atoms. A 37-heavy-atom heterocycle nearly ties a 50-heavy-atom relative; other enlarged repeated assemblies score below their initial useful context. Conversely, compact indole amides and arylalkyl amines score strongly, showing that simplification and useful small structures are possible. Neither smallness nor bigness is intrinsically rewarded across these records.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently retain useful molecular context while controlling fragmentation and redundant elaboration.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Proposals need feedback-informed ways to preserve functional-group relationships while simplifying, replacing or expanding dispensable portions. The capability gap is consistent context control, not an inability to add atoms or form rings. A fixed minimum size, automatic growth preference or universal fragmentation prohibition does not follow, and the observed molecule associations do not identify which retained component produced them.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source: the gap was recorded for n-c55c3d520a2c and retained by the identical-trajectory baseline n-62daf219c70a; it is re-observed in changed outputs of n-87c89dda7e3b on Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2 under the supplied 300-observation, batch-10 profile with direct aromatic C/N exchange disabled. Strong excerpts repeatedly alter short chains, halogen placement, ether length, local nitrogen sites or ring segments within retained aromatic-amide, linked heterocycle, aryl-amine, macrocyclic-lactam and fluorinated-dione families. The Child and Parent do show different families across seeds, including conventional counterexamples, so global structural collapse is not supported. Many distinct SMILES and high ring-string incidence do not establish broad useful feasible scaffold coverage within an individual adaptive stream.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently furnish chemically independent plausible alternatives to each seed's leading family.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Scaffold-level proposals need to reorganize locally supported functional relationships into chemically independent, credible connectivities. Actual accepted labels and chemical plausibility must distinguish useful alternatives from merely distinct graph strings. This conditional coverage gap neither identifies a target-specific scaffold nor proves that more diversity, or any particular search component, would improve the endpoint.

nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves scored molecular graphs. It samples breeding parents from high-score population groups, applies its existing crossover and mutations, and builds a surplus pool of fresh valid identities. A Gaussian process trained on all accepted raw scores uses count fingerprints and a Tanimoto kernel. For each evaluation slot it draws a correlated score function across that pool and picks the best still-available molecule. Real accepted outcomes alone update the model archive and score-ranked survivors. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is already disabled; ordinary mutations and their continuation remain active.
approach.novelty: Add incumbent-referenced expected batch improvement: reuse one fixed panel of joint posterior scenarios, begin every scenario at the best raw score already accepted, and choose each molecule for its remaining positive contribution to that batch improvement. This targets progress beyond the current best while accounting for score peaks covered by earlier batch choices. Earlier shared-panel and antithetic experiments maximized an unthresholded batch maximum under an older Parent. Current siblings have tested representation, predictive targets, generation, feedback and selector removals; none supplies a formally evaluated current-Parent unthresholded shared-panel control. This experiment therefore tests the complete new allocation rule against the Parent. The same-panel unthresholded comparison explains decision differences without claiming an isolated endpoint effect of the threshold.

nodes.hypothesis: Replace successful independent-row posterior allocation with greedy incumbent-referenced expected batch improvement over one fixed 128-or-announced-batch-size shared joint posterior panel, using only the best previously accepted raw score and exact smallest-index ties.

finding_summary.headline: Incumbent targeting raises sampled batch utility, but smaller real gains lower all three seed means
finding_summary.insights:
The experiment exposes a failure of the complete incumbent-referenced allocation rule under this Parent: correct positive-improvement targeting and higher sampled utility did not deliver larger real advances. More update events again accompanied smaller increments. The mean realized batch-improvement contrast telescopes to the final-score contrast on these equal-length streams, so those two failures should not be counted as independent endpoint evidence. The result supports a negative contribution from this whole rule under the tested composition. A threshold-only endpoint effect remains unresolved because the current unthresholded comparison has no separately evaluated future trajectory.

Finite-panel zero gain also failed to identify unproductive molecules. Fourteen zero-gain choices beat their frozen real incumbent, eleven made sequential incumbent updates, 205 were later bred and 119 survived to the final populations. Two became session leaders. Every one of those fourteen real wins had no sampled scenario above the incumbent. The chemical report includes a ring-free urea/enamide/thiocarbonyl leader and a distinct aza-dicarbonyl leader in this group. These are concrete limits of the sampled improvement support; they do not establish whether model error, finite tail sampling, myopic selection or later breeding caused the overall loss.

Selected-stream MSE and interval coverage improved while within-batch ordering weakened, but the selected molecules and histories changed. Those diagnostics do not establish repaired uncertainty or improved chemistry. Familiar amines and lactams still coexist with reactive bonds, difficult rings, large assemblies and unspecified stereochemistry. The older unthresholded and antithetic failures retain their exchange-containing Parent conditions, and shared-Parent siblings supply no isolated threshold, additive or joint-component effect. The complete exposed endpoint failure supplies the registered approach-review evidence without authorizing acquisition tuning.
finding_summary.results:
The allocation mechanism executed and changed real decisions. All 435 frozen incumbents, 128-row posterior panels and 4,350 exact greedy choices passed independent reconstruction. There were 3,681 positive-gain choices and 669 exact-zero choices; 23 complete batches had zero sampled improvement from their first position. Every zero choice followed the registered smallest-index tie rule without a fallback. All 435 selected sets differed from the Parent rule on the same panels. Mean sampled batch-improvement utility rose by 0.005726: 371 batches improved, 64 tied and none declined. Against the unthresholded shared-panel rule, 343 sets changed and mean utility rose by 0.000256, with fifteen contrary losses.

Real progress moved the other way. Average realized batch improvement fell from 0.013351 to 0.011410. Advancing batches rose from 202 to 204 and sequential incumbent updates from 258 to 270, but mean positive batch gain fell from 0.028751 to 0.024331. Mean accepted offspring score also fell, from 0.385256 to 0.351177. All evaluations completed, yet final mean score fell from 0.595670 to 0.539394, a paired change of -0.056276 against the required +0.002. Seed changes were -0.092867, -0.016706 and -0.059254. Nine task-seed endpoints declined and six improved, including all three median-similarity endpoints.

molecular.headline: Aryl amines and bridged lactams persist; an acyclic sulfur/urea chain leads one task despite zero sampled marginal gain
molecular.overall_character: All five objectives and all three issued Search seeds were inspected for Child n-8a62df15e51f and code Parent n-62daf219c70a. Each node has 4,500 evaluated records, including 4,350 optimizer products; every task contributes 900 records and 870 optimizer products. context.comparison establishes both complete Child evaluation and complete matched Parent pairing, with no profile mismatch or missing trajectory. All fifteen paired trajectories differ; common molecular identities retain consistent recorded scores. The actual resource receipt records three completed replicas with six CPUs, 16,000 MB and one A40 each. The supplied full-panel mean is 0.5393940797230263 versus 0.5956696497334577, with paired seed changes -0.09286669965406602,-0.016705653920698005 and -0.05925435645652999. All three median-similarity endpoints improve, while several other endpoints fall; these contrary cases remain in the per-task comparisons. These are recorded evaluation outcomes, not an activation, eligibility or component-contribution decision. The molecules remain rich in aromatic and heterocyclic frameworks: indole carboxamides, linked halogenated heteroaryls, cyclic and macrocyclic amines, ether/lactam bridges and aza-dicarbonyl cores. A conspicuous exception is an acyclic urea/enamide/ketone/thioaldehyde leader. Median heavy-atom counts in fixed task order are 25,37,29,31,26, versus Parent 25,33,31,30,27. The overall median is four perceived rings and two aromatic rings. Digest ring-string presence ranges from 0.8931 to 0.9862 and aromatic-string presence from 0.8034 to 0.9782; these are molecule-level text counters, not geometry or aromatic atom fractions. The lowest aromatic fraction belongs to the population containing the acyclic leader, so its ring-free chemistry must not be hidden by the overall ring-rich description. Within-seed upper-score neighborhoods are usually much narrower than the complete panel. Familiar functional groups coexist with chemical liabilities. Counts of optimizer molecules with N-halogen/O-halogen/O-O bonds are 437/109/75 for the Child versus 1,042/278/273 for the Parent. This decrease in specific motifs does not establish a global feasibility improvement: the Child has 147 molecules containing a ring carbon with at least two double bonds, versus 42 in the Parent, and also produces aryl cyanates, terminal C=S groups, N-S substitution, crowded aminals, short unsaturated rings and dense bridges. Not every carbon with two double bonds is the same kind of cumulene; the concrete cyclic carbon-chain examples are identified below. No Child evaluated molecule has a ring triple bond, but that is not evidence of its absence from unscored pools or the unchanged generator's support. There are 124 products with at most three heavy atoms versus Parent 99, alongside evaluated structures as large as 120 heavy atoms. All digest stereocentre-marker rates are zero, while RDKit identifies unassigned tetrahedral centres in 2,391 Child and 2,408 Parent optimizer rows. Ring perception, sanitization and a score do not establish a synthesis, stability, accessible conformation, safety or a preferred stereoisomer. Actual molecule provenance was joined through pool identity, emitted prediction, accepted score, survivor population and later parent reuse in all thirty logs. The Child and Parent each construct 69,600 pool records and evaluate 4,350 optimizer products. Every one of the 435 Child suggestions freezes its incumbent from the complete preceding accepted raw-score archive; all exact tied records and the smallest-serial representative match that history. The representative is an initial molecule in 17 batches and an earlier accepted offspring in 418; 53 batches have multiple incumbent ties. It is neither the generating-parent score nor a posterior prediction or future observation. The fixed recorded panel has 128 joint function-value rows in each batch. All active marginal vectors, masks, chosen identities and exact tie choices were checked against that panel without generating new draws or scores. The prediction mean and standard deviation remain raw-score moments; posterior_sample is a passive panel-row value, separate from the optimizing marginal increment. There are 3,681 positive-marginal and 669 exact-zero-marginal evaluated choices. The latter occur in 96 batches, including 23 wholly zero batches, and select the smallest remaining original pool index. This is normal finite-panel saturation, not numerical fallback; no fallback occurred. The zero cohort contains 70 acyclic products and 24 tiny fragments, but also substantial useful-scoring molecules: 59 beat their best generating parent, 14 exceed the batch's frozen incumbent, 11 update the running incumbent, 355 survive their batch, 119 remain in the final population and 205 are later bred. Only four of these zero-marginal choices have any panel row above the original incumbent; later marginal saturation can also occur after earlier choices already cover those rows. Zero finite-panel utility therefore does not show chemical absence or lack of real improvement potential. Two session leaders come from zero-marginal ties. The acyclic leader in seed 1 of the final task is evaluation 194, position 3/pool index 3 in wholly saturated batch 19. Its frozen incumbent is the earlier accepted evaluation 143 at 0.3487520004285424, drawn from 190 preceding accepted records; its generating parent is a different molecule at 0.2624259366847637. The leader scores 0.43419030554852406 after an append and ring opening. Seed 2/evaluation 158 is likewise a zero choice, scoring 0.4189666353060081 after a fluorine append to a small-ring dicarbonyl family. Both are molecular counterexamples to treating zero sampled marginal gain as useless chemistry, but neither identifies a beneficial causal contribution from the tie rule or the acquisition threshold. All 435 same-panel passive controls are available. The unthresholded rule changes its batch set relative to the actual choices in 343 batches; the independent-row rule changes all 435. Their complete sequences were checked on their own masks, separately from same-active-prefix diagnostics. Unevaluated alternatives receive no labels, chemical-outcome claims or hypothetical future histories. The actual scored Child has 632 best-parent beats and 270 incumbent updates versus Parent 629 and 258, while mean realized improvement over the frozen batch incumbent is 0.011410412713128188 versus 0.013350949610039598. Counts of local wins, internal panel utilities and selected chemistry are different observations; none alone explains the lower complete endpoints. Historical unthresholded n-9c0f6fa601f8 and antithetic n-0db88abff519 retain their original exchange-containing Parent n-559d25e9c9c7 and paired means -0.0003646022443066406 and -0.016104112533858978. Both had opposing seed effects; the antithetic variant also used a different zero-gain mean-completion rule. They are conditional counterexamples, not independent tests on the present exchange-free Parent. Current rank-target n-ae12ccae8c7b and magnitude-credit n-9d0376974738 likewise retain their negative endpoint results despite favorable local progress measurements. There is no formally evaluated current-Parent unthresholded sibling: this comparison concerns the complete incumbent-referenced shared-panel rule versus independent-row allocation, and cannot split the threshold from the changed panel/batch law. Shared-Parent contrasts and later breeding ancestry do not establish additive efficacy or chemical mediation of terminal scores. Full trajectory chemistry is in trajectory_chemistry_audit.json; allocation_exposure_audit.json joins actual history, choices and retained molecules; selected_chemistry_audit.json links positive/zero cohorts and leader provenance; historical_evidence_extract.json preserves the original sources and conditions. per_task.generated_character: Better products are compact indole carboxamides with a separate phenyl or pyridyl surface and methoxy, methyl or vinyl substituents. The top fifty have 23-26 heavy atoms and three aromatic rings. Seed 0's leader has an N-amino indole, bromomethyl group and fluorophenyl amide. Seed 1 has a vinyl/methoxy indole with an N-S-substituted pyridyl amide. Seed 2's 24-heavy-atom leader carries an enol-like vinyl alcohol and an amide nitrogen/methylene bridge spanning a pyridyl ring; its five perceived rings do not make this bridge a routine saturated amine. N-halogen bonds are much less prevalent than in the Parent: 128 versus 445 optimizer products, although still present in 19 of the highest fifty. Parent leaders used related aromatic carbonyl frameworks, including N-fluoro, N-hydroxyamide and diketone chemistry. The shift changes local liabilities without eliminating them.
liabilities: Bromomethyl substitution, N-amino indole, N-S-substituted amide and residual N-Cl/N-Br amides warrant distinct chemical scrutiny; they are not interchangeable with ordinary aryl halogenation.
The short amide-N/methylene bridge across a pyridyl ring constrains geometry. The leader’s enol-like group adds a tautomeric question that is not resolved by its recorded score.
missing_features: The small poor products lack the combined aromatic surfaces and compact carbonyl connection found in better molecules. The leading excerpt offers limited routine alternatives preserving that spacing without short pyridyl-spanning bridges, N-S/N-N substitution or halomethyl groups.

All 870 optimizer choices have positive sampled marginal gain on this task, yet only some improve their real parent or incumbent. All three matched endpoints increase modestly; these gains remain alongside the full-panel losses. Recorded seed maxima, Child versus matched Parent in seed order 0/1/2, are 0.234809 versus 0.225840; 0.224985 versus 0.221410; 0.226526 versus 0.226003 (rounded to six decimals).

per_task.generated_character: This population spans chemically different solutions. Seed 0 leads with an N-S-substituted dicarbonyl bicyclic core, a fluorinated five-member imine ring and a fluoromethyl cyclopentadienol. Seed 2 leads with pyridyl and difluoro/aminoaryl groups on a dicarbonyl heterocycle fused to an unsaturated four-member nitrogen ring. Seed 1's highest product is entirely acyclic: a 24-heavy-atom chain containing substituted urea, ketone, enamide, terminal C=S, fluoropropyl acyl and an N-bound fluoro/chloromethyl centre. This ring-free leader is a real exception to the abundant cyclic output. The whole-panel median is 26 heavy atoms and one aromatic ring versus Parent 27 and three aromatic rings. N-halogen occurrence falls to 39 from Parent 476, but N-S chemistry, thiocarbonyl/enamide chains, small-ring strain and unspecified geometry remain. Parent leaders included N-F carbonyl/imino rings and a highly scored but difficult cyclic-cumulene family.
liabilities: The acyclic leader has a terminal thioaldehyde-like C=S and conjugated carbonyl/enamide chain, with unspecified alkene geometry and an unassigned fluoro/chloro carbon centre.

The cyclic leaders retain N-S substitution, imine/enol chemistry or an unsaturated four-member nitrogen ring. Fewer N-halogen bonds than the Parent do not by themselves establish improved stability or synthetic feasibility.
missing_features: Tiny fragments and enlarged repeated frameworks fail to reproduce the moderate-sized distribution of carbonyl, nitrogen and peripheral substituents found in better products. The acyclic leader prevents interpreting the observed gap as a universal need for additional rings.

The evaluated upper sample lacks chemically routine, stereochemically and geometrically defined alternatives spanning these same functional arrangements without terminal C=S, N-S or short unsaturated-ring liabilities. Their absence here does not establish absence from unscored pool support.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The three Child maxima are 0.431372, 0.434190 and 0.418967. The bulky repeated dicarbonyl assembly at seed 0/evaluation 82 scores only 7.721662777993149e-34, and atomic F at seed 2/ evaluation 253 scores 1.1043196211273875e-26. Thus moderate size and a distributed functional-group arrangement matter within these samples; neither ring abundance nor fluorine alone is sufficient. The acyclic leader at seed 1/evaluation 194 follows append_atom plus open_ring from the accepted aromatic precursor at evaluation 156 (0.262426). It is selected at exactly zero marginal gain in wholly saturated batch 19, whose real frozen incumbent is evaluation 143 (0.348752), not that generating parent. Its predictive mean is -0.037001, distinct from its observed 0.434190 score. Seed 2/evaluation 158 is another zero choice: an F append to evaluation 144 (0.339428) exceeds the frozen incumbent from evaluation 73 (0.401281). There are 601 zero-marginal choices on this task, including these two retained session leaders. These counterexamples do not make zero ties or ring opening universally favorable, and every matched seed endpoint remains below its Parent. Recorded seed maxima, Child versus matched Parent in seed order 0/1/2, are 0.431372 versus 0.651021; 0.434190 versus 0.487006; 0.418967 versus 0.720885 (rounded to six decimals).

transferable_gaps.evidence: In the current complete panel, 669 actual evaluated choices have zero marginal gain; 14 exceed their frozen accepted incumbent and 205 are later bred. Two session leaders are zero choices, including an acyclic urea/enamide/thiocarbonyl product made by appending and opening a ring. Its accepted precursor and the distinct earlier incumbent are exactly joined. This narrows the output limitation to a mismatch between some observed molecular transformations and their sampled improvement support. The historic n-9c0f6fa601f8 and n-0db88abff519 results remain conditional on their exchange-containing Parent and different allocation laws; no current-Parent unthresholded scored sibling isolates the threshold here.
transferable_gaps.gap: Chemically informative accepted molecules can lie outside all positive finite-panel improvement scenarios, so zero sampled value does not identify unproductive chemistry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Retain chemical provenance and real feedback for novel transformations even when the finite panel assigns zero marginal value. Distinguish ring opening that retains a distributed polar framework from destructive fragmentation; neither a new chemistry ban nor a claim about unscored alternatives follows from the zero class. Any future allocation interpretation must preserve the complete-law and historical comparison limits.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The n-c55c3d520a2c chemistry gap, reproduced by Parent n-62daf219c70a, remains with a changed balance: N-X/O-X/O-O occurrences decrease to 437/109/75, while ring carbons with at least two double bonds occur in 147 evaluated products versus Parent 42. Aryl cyanates, N-S substitution, terminal thiocarbonyl chains, short unsaturated rings and dense bridges coexist with recognizable amines, amides and ethers. Some ordinary high-value products avoid these motifs, so they are not required in every productive family. These structural counts describe selected output, not relative chemical outcomes of passive alternative batches.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably separate conventional whole-molecule alternatives from reactive substituents and difficult ring geometry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Expand chemically conventional alternatives preserving accepted molecules’ ring, amine and carbonyl relationships, with task-agnostic feedback assessing their value. Track explicit reactive bonds and ring geometry separately from graph validity and descriptor similarity; a lower count of one liability is not a universal feasibility gain.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The current evaluated stream includes 124 molecules with at most three heavy atoms versus Parent 99 and extends to 120 heavy atoms. Tiny examples often score at or near the observed floor, while a large repeated heterocyclic product scores 7.721662777993149e-34. In contrast, one ring-free 24-heavy-atom product leads its session and several compact amine or carbonyl frameworks score well. The evidence therefore concerns maintenance of a useful distributed architecture, not a universal ring-retention or size-minimization rule. This refines the existing n-c55c3d520a2c and n-62daf219c70a whole-molecule plausibility gap without assigning an endpoint effect to any edit.
transferable_gaps.gap: Scaffold size and functional-group relationships are not consistently preserved across fragmentation, ring edits and molecular enlargement.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support controlled changes of connectivity while retaining and contrasting complete accepted functional-group arrangements. Separate useful ring opening from collapse and avoid equating repeated motifs with useful added chemistry. Validate the actual resulting molecules through authorized feedback; unselected pool outcomes remain unknown.

transferable_gaps.evidence: As in n-c55c3d520a2c and n-62daf219c70a, every current digest stereocentre-marker rate is zero. RDKit nevertheless finds unassigned tetrahedral centres in 2,391 of 4,350 optimizer products, including every molecule in two highest-fifty excerpts and both saturated/cyclobutene and bridged lactam leaders. The acyclic thiocarbonyl leader also lacks specified alkene geometry. These are observations about evaluated representations, not proof that all potential configurations are stable or absent from every unscored generated structure.
transferable_gaps.gap: Evaluated stereochemical and geometric alternatives remain unspecified despite abundant saturated, bridged and heteroatom-adjacent centres.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Represent and preserve meaningful stereochemical and alkene-geometric distinctions where the actual graph supports them, then use allowed feedback to assess their value. Do not infer achirality, accessible geometry or a preferred configuration from unspecified strings and scalar scores.

nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

approach.method_basis: The Parent is an ant colony optimizer that builds each molecular graph from an empty state. At each step it chooses a starting atom, attaches an atom to an existing site, closes a ring bond, or stops. Fixed aggregate frequencies from an unlabeled molecular corpus supply chemical preferences, including attachment, ring-closure and stopping weights. A separate table of task-local pheromones multiplies those preferences. The Parent identifies a reusable attachment component by the central atom's identity, charge, explicit hydrogens, degree, used bond order and ring membership, together with the proposed bond and new atom. Ring-closure components use both endpoint descriptions and their path length. Initial reinforcement comes from an exact reconstruction of the best supported starting observation. After feedback, all pheromones evaporate and only the highest-scoring accepted molecule in that batch deposits credit on its actual construction trace, once per distinct key. Positive lower and upper bounds preserve exploration. Later ants share the credited local components even when they occur inside different partial molecules.
approach.novelty: I add neighborhood-resolved pheromone credit: an attachment site also carries a sorted description of its directly bonded neighbors, and a ring closure carries this description at both endpoints. A move that was rewarded beside one arrangement of atoms and bonds will therefore share that reward only with the same bounded neighborhood. For example, the same central carbon description can acquire different credit when its neighboring atom is oxygen instead of carbon. This tests the Parent's observed loss of selectivity, where almost every accepted ant reused reinforcement but very few improved the incumbent. The lineage currently contains only the original ant colony root, so no sibling has tested a finer pheromone key. The corpus-derived heuristic still uses its original contexts; the new distinction acts specifically through which construction decisions share accepted winner credit.

nodes.hypothesis: Refine only the Parent's attachment and ring-closure pheromone keys with fixed, permutation-invariant one-bond neighborhood descriptors so accepted winner reinforcement transfers between matching local neighborhoods instead of all sites sharing the Parent's coarser endpoint description.

finding_summary.headline: Neighborhood credit localized and lifted the screening mean, but successful molecules remained rare
finding_summary.insights: This experiment separates local credit discrimination from productive molecular search. Different neighborhoods really were being collapsed by the old keys, and the new keys distinguish them without changing the legal chemistry or fixed heuristic weights. Matching neighborhoods also recur often enough to transfer credit across different partial molecules, so the refinement did not eliminate transfer through excessive sparsity. Yet most ants still inherit some online credit, and only 5.84% of the observed split-menu groups carried unequal refined pheromones. More precise keys therefore changed specific decisions without making successful whole molecules common. The chemistry explains why the modest mean gain should not be read as a broadly improved generator. The molecular assessment found a compact acyclic urea behind the strongest score increase, but long unsaturated chains and unconventional ring assemblies still dominate. Mean atom count fell slightly, while ring-closure actions fell sharply and terminations at the 64-atom ceiling became more frequent. In every task the late molecules were larger than the early molecules. Local credit refinement alone did not produce sustained access to compact, organized, functionalized chemistry. The result supports the implementation and shows a descriptive gain on this seed; it does not establish a reliable oracle-score benefit of selective credit. Larger changes in different objectives nearly cancel, some counted gains are near numerical ties, and the same-menu probability comparisons do not score unsubmitted alternatives. Whether broader molecular constraints or a better size and termination prior can make the now-demonstrated local discrimination useful remains open, as does its reliability across seeds.
finding_summary.results: The intended credit localization happened. Across the five task-specific tables, 3,027 attachment keys and 6,522 ring-closure keys separated previously shared neighborhoods. All 145 online winner updates withheld deposits from other neighborhoods when opportunities existed, totaling 75,964 alternative/update pairs. Every one of 10,719 mixed-neighborhood update probes increased the winner neighborhoods' conditional probability mass. Later construction contained 18,485 selected moves whose conditional probabilities changed and whose exact neighborhoods traced to earlier accepted online winners. The optimization gain was much smaller than the amount of activity. Among accepted ants that reused online credit, 7 of 1,396 beat their pre-batch incumbent, compared with 3 of 1,399 for the Parent; reuse still reached about 96% of accepted ants. All strict incumbent beaters increased from 8 to 12, but three of the new online-reusing docking beaters were steps of at most 0.00000044 along a low score plateau. The single screening seed's mean final Top-1 rose from 0.2523 to 0.2579. The sitagliptin multi-property score rose from 0.0980 to 0.2392, while dopamine-receptor docking fell from 0.1371 to 0.0289 and decoration hopping fell from 0.5534 to 0.5484. The zaleplon and median-molecule scores stayed at 0.3051 and 0.1678. No generated molecule beat the supplied starting incumbent on three of the five objectives. All 1,450 submitted molecules were accepted; one additional local construction repeated a molecule and was replaced before submission.

molecular.headline: Long polyene chains dominate; occasional polar cages and a compact urea score better, but conventional scaffold chemistry remains sparse.
molecular.overall_character: All five supplied task trajectories and their Parent counterparts were read for seed 0. Each contains 290 optimizer proposals plus 10 initial observations. The generated population consists mainly of long, repeatedly unsaturated carbon chains, interrupted by amines, enamines, occasional imines, ethers and carbonyls. Rings are substantial in amount but often unconventional in arrangement: partially unsaturated carbocycles and dense fused or bridged assemblies occur alongside isolated aryl segments. The digest ring-closure rates range from 0.3966 to 0.8966, while aromatic-text rates range from 0.1241 to 0.5690; these are fractions of strings carrying a feature, not aromatic atom fractions or assessments of ring quality. Mean SMILES lengths range from 60.1 to 76.5. Direct atom counts from the trajectories show that shorter strings than the Parent frequently reflect fewer closures and branches rather than a substantial size reduction. The emitted structures have no explicit tetrahedral stereochemistry, and inspection also found no specified alkene geometry. All supplied generated SMILES parsed with RDKit, which establishes readable molecular graphs, not stability or synthetic accessibility. The quality labels describe substantial ring occurrence, sparse aromatic organization, questionable preparative chemistry, weak resemblance to ordinary medicinal chemistry and recurrent polyene motifs despite distinct molecular identities. Atom and functional-group counts below are direct structural readings of the supplied SMILES; all scores are the recorded evaluator values. Digest medians displayed as 0.0 are rounded and must not be interpreted as a majority of exactly zero observations.

per_task.generated_character: Mean SMILES length is 73.6; direct heavy-atom counts average 47.46 and reach 64. Ring-closure and aromatic-text rates are 0.8966 and 0.5690. Much of this ring content is a carbocycle or aryl segment embedded in a long polyene, rather than a compact aromatic scaffold. Evaluation 11, the best generated structure, is a compact, densely bridged nitrogen-containing polycycle bearing a nitrile, chlorine and cyclic ketones. Other higher examples include a partially unsaturated N/O polycycle and a nitrogen-free aryl-containing enone/aldehyde chain. Late structures are predominantly long hydrocarbon-rich polyenes, sometimes with ketones, aldehydes or a nitrile. Conventional fragments are recognizable, but their extended unsaturation and crowded ring combinations make synthesis and isolation questionable.
liabilities: Long polyenes and conjugated carbonyl chains create numerous unspecified alkene geometries and potential chemical-stability burdens.
Dense bridged rings with extensive unsaturation and unassigned stereochemistry need geometric and synthetic scrutiny; successful SMILES parsing does not resolve those concerns.
missing_features: Repeated production of compact, conventionally substituted aromatic NH heterocycles with an attached amide, as seen in the best supplied initial molecule; generated aromatic content is frequently carried on long unsaturated extensions.

Sustained access to the compact polar arrangements found among the higher generated examples. The final proposals mostly lose their concentrated nitrogen/carbonyl organization; the data do not identify one mandatory heteroatom motif.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The 24-heavy-atom bridged nitrile at evaluation 11 scores 0.19324099086270913; the 21-heavy-atom N/O polycycle at evaluation 65 scores 0.17464941125558517. The nitrogen-free, shorter carbonyl-containing structure at evaluation 176 still scores 0.13915472870419515, so nitrogen alone cannot explain the gradient. Long final polyenes score zero or near zero; evaluation 300 has 64 heavy atoms and score 0.0. Exactly 130 of the 290 generated proposals score zero. The clearest association is with compactness and functional-group arrangement, not simply having a ring: many zero-scoring chains also contain rings. The supplied indole carboxamide at evaluation 9 remains best overall at 0.3051048083696145. Compared with Parent n-3ab6a944e3dd, ring-closure/aromatic-text rates rise from 0.6103/0.2172 to 0.8966/0.5690 and the generated maximum moves from 0.1775836262122333 to 0.19324099086270913, while that initial overall best remains unchanged.

per_task.generated_character: Mean SMILES length is 75.3 and direct heavy-atom count averages 50.05. Ring-closure rate is 0.8345, but aromatic-text rate is only 0.2655. The best generated molecule at evaluation 223 combines aryl-containing fused ring units, amide groups and nitrogen-containing linkers with a very long alkenyl appendage. Evaluation 26 is smaller and contains a fused N/O ring assembly, an amino substituent and an imine/N-N-containing chain. Other proposals distribute amines, enamines, imines, ethers and amides through long unsaturated backbones. The late molecules retain scattered rings and polar groups but look like extended polyene constructs; their synthesis is considerably less straightforward than the supplied conventionally substituted aromatic starting molecules.
liabilities: Extended polyenes with repeated amine/enamine and occasional imine or hydrazone-like functionality impose stability and stereochemical complexity.
Some highly fused N/O assemblies and densely unsaturated ring junctions have questionable preparative accessibility despite acceptable formal valence.
missing_features: Reliable production of clearly substituted aryl and carbonyl-bearing nitrogen heterocycle arrangements like those present in the stronger initial observations; such organization is diluted by unsaturated tails in much of the generated set.

Compact variants that preserve a polar ring system while varying its substituents. The two leading generated examples show that both compact and large structures can reach the upper observed band, but no clean analogue series identifies the decisive arrangement.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The generated maximum is 0.5468883205456095 at evaluation 223, versus the observed floor of 0.5 for hydrocarbon-rich chains and sparsely functionalized carbocycles. An aromatic/N/O-rich 29-heavy-atom molecule at evaluation 26 scores 0.5441609421000981, close to the 64-heavy-atom generated maximum. Thus ring-associated polar functionality and aromatic organization distinguish the higher band more consistently than size alone; neither a universal growth benefit nor a universal small-molecule preference follows. The final cited proposals range from 0.500866325911808 to 0.5162088883649651. The best supplied initial molecule scores 0.548381482770623 and remains best overall. The Parent generated maximum was 0.5533540672422114; its ring-closure/aromatic-text rates were 0.9448/0.4241. The current products have less ring and aromatic occurrence while retaining almost the same mean atom count.

per_task.generated_character: Mean SMILES length is 76.5 and direct heavy-atom count averages 51.10. Ring-closure and aromatic-text rates are 0.5345 and 0.1241. The upper observed score band is dominated by very long, mostly nonaromatic polyenes with chain amines or enamines and occasional partially unsaturated carbocycles or N-containing rings. Acyclic and cyclic structures occur at the identical maximum. Smaller low-scoring examples include propene, aldehyde/imine-containing structures, an acyl chloride and an unusual three-membered cyclic dicarbonyl graph. The extended chains and unusual reactive or constrained outliers support questionable synthetic plausibility; the score plateau is not evidence that these are convincing receptor ligands.
liabilities: Long chains with many unassigned double-bond geometries provide poorly specified three-dimensional structures and substantial hydrophobic bulk.
Low-scoring proposals include an acyl chloride, unusual sulfur bonding and a very small cyclic dicarbonyl; these raise direct reactivity or strain concerns.
missing_features: Compact scaffold coverage comparable to the Parent structures that received scores above the present plateau. The current high band mainly samples long unsaturated chains rather than demonstrating an improved compact binding arrangement.

Conventional aromatic and saturated nitrogen-ring arrangements are underrepresented, not absent. Their independent benefit and any receptor-specific missing pharmacophore cannot be established from these tied scores.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Exactly 111 generated molecules share the maximum 0.02885837683273086. Evaluation 96 has 60 heavy atoms and an N-containing ring, while evaluation 123 is an acyclic 53-heavy-atom amine/polyene at that same score. Propene scores 0.004764078329913475 and the three-membered cyclic dicarbonyl scores 0.003770354034741671. The observed progression toward larger chains ends in a repeated plateau, which cannot distinguish a favored ring system, amine placement or binding geometry. The best initial observation is 0.01904115112334333; another initial molecule already contains an N-methyl saturated amine ring yet scores only 0.0003786988088202195, so simply adding such an amine is unsupported guidance. The Parent had a compact fused, nitrogen-substituted polycyclic outlier at 0.13712669868003655, above this plateau. Its ring-closure/aromatic-text rates were 0.9724/0.2897, versus the current 0.5345/0.1241. Those differences describe a loss of ring-rich output, without establishing why the docking scores differ.

per_task.generated_character: Mean SMILES length is 73.1 and direct heavy-atom count averages 50.47. Ring-closure rate is 0.8552 and aromatic-text rate is 0.4310. The best generated molecule at evaluation 62 is a large, partly aromatic N-rich fused assembly with carbonyl functionality, a fluoro-substituted unsaturated linker, an aryl amine connection, a tertiary amide and an amino-ether tail. Other higher examples are densely bridged nitrogen cages with nitriles and ketones, or complex heteroaromatic/carbonyl-containing systems. The lower band contains acyclic amino-polyenes of both small and very large size. The ring-rich structures have more differentiated functionality, but their congested topology and long tails leave synthetic plausibility questionable.
liabilities: Congested fused and bridged unsaturated rings, together with unspecified stereochemistry, complicate three-dimensional feasibility and route planning.
Long amino-polyene and aldehyde-containing tails add unsaturation and reactive functionality without consistently retaining the organized polar scaffold of the better examples.
missing_features: Routine access to conventionally linked aromatic and nitrogen/carbonyl heterocyclic units like those in the stronger supplied starting molecules, without converting the whole structure into a bridged cage or a long polyene.

Controlled substitution around a retained compact ring system, which would help separate the observed contributions of ring identity, carbonyl placement and heteroatom arrangement; the present examples change several of these together.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The generated maximum is 0.12097167578182677 at evaluation 62; the bridged nitrile/ketone cage at evaluation 11 scores 0.1000061734111242. The short amino-polyene at evaluation 32 scores 0.0, and the 64-heavy-atom acyclic nitrogen-containing chain at evaluation 226 scores 0.006228601608634516. Thus the distinction is not simply small versus large: organized rings and associated functionality separate the higher band from chain-only structures. The best supplied initial aromatic, carbonyl-rich heterocycle remains best overall at 0.1678386594791329. The Parent generated maximum was 0.13095077916237702. Aromatic-text occurrence increases from 0.3069 to 0.4310, while ring-closure occurrence falls from 0.9517 to 0.8552 and the overall best remains the same initial molecule. More aromatic text alone therefore does not establish better scaffold organization.

per_task.generated_character: Mean SMILES length is 60.1 and direct heavy-atom count averages 39.66. Ring-closure and aromatic-text rates are 0.3966 and 0.1379, so most generated structures are acyclic and nonaromatic. The best generated molecule at evaluation 62 is a 19-heavy-atom substituted urea with unsaturated arms ending in an aldehyde and an imine. Other higher examples include a complex N/O fused carbonyl-containing structure, an acyclic imine/vinyl-ether-rich molecule and a short amino-polyenone. Later proposals are predominantly hydrocarbon polyenes with occasional amines or terminal aldehydes. The urea itself is a conventional linkage, but its unsaturated imine/aldehyde substituents and the broader polyene population raise stability and synthesis concerns.
liabilities: The best-scoring molecule still combines multiple unsaturated bonds with terminal imine and aldehyde functionality; its score does not establish stability or a practical route.
The dominant late polyenes have extensive unspecified alkene geometry, low polar-group density and frequent terminal carbonyl reactivity.
missing_features: Consistent regeneration of compact molecules with concentrated carbonyl and nitrogen functionality. The best urea is an isolated example, while late products mostly return to extended unsaturated chains.

Chemically stable variants of the compact polar arrangements already receiving higher scores, with less reliance on imines, enamines and aldehydes. Improved stability is a chemical need here, not an independently demonstrated scoring requirement.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The compact acyclic urea scores 0.23921423452807236. The N/O fused structure at evaluation 20 scores 0.0814995806289838 and the acyclic heteroatom-rich structure at evaluation 43 scores 0.04838092252183626. The long final aldehyde/polyene at evaluation 299 has 64 heavy atoms and score 0.0; exactly 108 of the 290 optimizer proposals score zero. The higher examples favor compactness and concentrated polar functionality relative to long hydrocarbon-rich chains, but they do not establish that a ring, fluorination or a particular named heterocycle is required: the best example has none of those features. The initial maximum was 0.0020944534688323298. The Parent maximum was 0.09799523162987753 for a cyclic amino-polycarbonyl/lactone structure; the present best instead uses an acyclic urea arrangement. Ring-closure/aromatic-text occurrence falls from the Parent values 0.5483/0.1966 to 0.3966/0.1379. The higher best score therefore does not correspond to more aromatic or cyclic chemistry.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Mean heavy-atom counts from the generated trajectories range from 39.66 to 51.10, against 28.40 for the shared initial set. In each trajectory the final 50 proposals have a higher mean atom count than the first 50. The compact 19-heavy-atom urea at score 0.23921423452807236 and the 24-heavy-atom nitrile cage at 0.19324099086270913 contrast with long final polyenes scoring zero. A different upper-band example has 64 heavy atoms, so the evidence does not justify a universal preference for the smallest possible molecule.
transferable_gaps.gap: Compact functionalized molecules are reached occasionally but are not sustained as a substantial output regime.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide a corpus-grounded size and termination prior that keeps compact functionalized structures readily reachable while retaining multiple size classes. Measure size with atom counts and unsaturated-chain extent; shorter SMILES alone can reflect lost ring structure.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Digest ring-closure rates span 0.3966 to 0.8966, while aromatic-text rates span 0.1241 to 0.5690. The examples include isolated rings embedded in long chains, highly bridged unsaturated cages and an unusual three-membered cyclic dicarbonyl. Direct ring inspection finds only 6 to 10 proposals per 290 with a saturated nitrogen-containing ring, including rings inside cages; this is a deficit of conventional scaffold coverage, not an inability to close any ring.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring closure is common, but conventional aromatic and saturated heterocyclic organization is poorly represented.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make common aromatic rings, saturated heterocycles and supported fusion patterns reliably available with controlled substitution and attachment geometry. Corpus-derived ring-environment support or coherent ring motifs could supply this capability without identifying the objective.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The generated examples contain amines, enamines, imines, ethers and carbonyls, so heteroatoms are not absent. Higher examples include a compact urea, nitrile/carbonyl ring assemblies and aromatic amide-containing initial molecules, but many later proposals consist mainly of carbon chains with scattered nitrogen or terminal aldehydes. Direct inspection finds only 4 to 10 generated molecules per trajectory carrying an aromatic nitrogen atom.
transferable_gaps.gap: Polar groups are often dispersed through unsaturated chains instead of organized into compact, chemically distinct environments.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Represent and preserve the bond-order and neighboring-group context that distinguishes an amine, enamine, imine, amide, urea or heteroaromatic nitrogen. Enable compact variants of observed polar arrangements and controlled changes around those arrangements so scalar feedback can compare related chemistry.

transferable_gaps.evidence: All supplied optimizer SMILES parse, yet the cited structures include dense unsaturated bridges, a very small cyclic dicarbonyl, acyl chloride functionality and repeated enal/enone or imine-containing chains. Some of these motifs appear in higher-scoring examples, so recorded reward alone does not establish an isolable or readily synthesizable product.
transferable_gaps.gap: Readable valence-consistent graphs still include chemically questionable ring and reactive-group combinations.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Use corpus support for complete ring/fusion environments and reactive-group co-occurrences when weighting or validating constructions. Track geometric and functional-group compatibility separately from formal valence, while retaining supported polyene and polycyclic chemistry.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The digest stereocentre rate is 0.0 on every trajectory, and the full generated strings contain no explicit alkene-geometry markers. Long polyenes and multiply bridged ring systems therefore reach evaluation without their potential stereochemical alternatives being explicitly distinguished. These observations establish missing output specification, not that any particular objective necessarily rewards one isomer.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not specify stereochemistry even when its unsaturation and ring topology create isomeric choices.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Allow feasible tetrahedral and alkene stereochemistry to be assigned, retained through canonicalization and explored as part of molecular identity. Constrain assignments using the actual ring geometry and local bonding rather than an objective-specific stereochemical template.

nodes.method_name: MAX-MIN Ant System over a molecular construction grammar
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the method in MAX-MIN Ant System: construct solutions probabilistically from components, evaporate their pheromone weights, reinforce the iteration-best solution, and bound every pheromone weight away from zero and excessive dominance. [Stutzle and Hoos, Sections 2 and 4](https://www.cs.ubc.ca/~hoos/Publ/fgcs00.pdf) describe this mechanism. Our molecular adaptation constructs a fresh graph from an empty state through valence-aware atom, bond, ring-closure and termination actions. Choice probabilities combine a fixed chemical heuristic with task-local pheromones keyed by the local attachment context and action, allowing a useful action to transfer between different partial graphs. Preparation uses the permitted unlabeled corpus only for aggregate construction frequencies and stopping statistics. Initialize pheromones broadly, reconstruct valid construction traces for the supplied scored molecules, and use their best trace for the initial reinforcement. Generate the announced batch through complete new construction trajectories; only accepted whole-molecule feedback drives evaporation and reinforcement of that batch's best trace. Resample failed or duplicate constructions locally. There is no stored complete-molecule library, corpus ranking or fixed product enumeration. The hypothesis is that reusing successful local construction choices across new molecular combinations raises the mean of independent final Top-1 scores. Whether coarse construction contexts carry useful reward information quickly enough is unproven; pheromone concentration or validity alone is not success.
