branches: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
retained_mechanisms: Task-local scored molecular-graph population with score-ranked parent sampling across three high-ranked quantiles
De novo connected-fragment graph crossover
Local atom/bond mutation with inner operator retries and occasional multi-step graph walks
Chemical sanitization, canonical/isomeric identity rejection, and graph-based retries for complete novel pools; saturation-dependent retry branches retained but not exercised
Bounded greedy score-ranked survival and subsequent breeding from accepted offspring

Accepted-only task-local fingerprint Gaussian-process archive, exact joint posterior sampling over fresh offspring pools, masked batch selection, and feedback-driven posterior refitting; bounded numerical fallback retained but not exercised

Carbonyl-preserving atom-replacement target support: exclude exactly existing C=O endpoints, retain the inherited conditional element law, and expose fixed-source/inner-retry traces through pool and evaluated-descendant provenance

approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds molecular graphs from a bounded population of accepted high-scoring molecules, using score-quantile parent sampling, connected-fragment crossover and local graph mutations. Its retained mutations include formula-preserving relocation of aromatic nitrogen, and stable identity checks admit a surplus pool of novel candidates. A Gaussian process trained on all earlier accepted scores uses integer counts of local molecular environments and generalized Tanimoto similarity to predict that pool jointly. The Parent chooses each evaluation by taking a fresh correlated posterior draw's highest available candidate, then admits accepted feedback to its prediction archive and breeding population.
approach.novelty: Add explicit batch-best allocation. Build one shared panel of posterior function draws and choose each next molecule by how much it raises the panel's average best score among the molecules already selected. This lets the remaining evaluations cover high-outcome possibilities that the current batch has not captured. Earlier siblings changed survival, parent allocation, graph production, identity admission or posterior features and noise; they have not optimized the utility of the selected batch as a set. The new rule retains the Parent's count posterior and tests a different use of its predictions, with a fixed 128-path numerical panel and separately measured real search outcomes.

nodes.hypothesis: Allocate the announced batch by greedy maximization of a shared Monte Carlo estimate of the posterior expected maximum over the selected pool members, so each added molecule is valued by its incremental contribution to the batch's predicted best outcome.

finding_summary.headline: Batch utility changes selection and raises offspring yield, but final mean score does not improve
finding_summary.insights:
The missing batch-set objective was a real decision difference, but correcting it did not supply the registered final-score benefit. This rules out lack of allocation opportunities or a nonexecuting selector as explanations for the result. It also shows why more parent-beating offspring and more incumbent updates are insufficient evidence of stronger final solutions: they can be more frequent increments along a weaker search history. Here the absolute batch-best scores declined even as those counts rose.

The higher internal objective describes the same finite posterior panel used to choose the batch. It does not reveal the real scores of the unevaluated alternatives. The posterior model itself is unchanged; the lower prediction MSE reflects a changed selected stream and feedback history, and does not establish repaired uncertainty. Coverage remains especially poor on sitagliptin, at 37.4%. Model error, limited tail sampling and the objective’s focus on the next batch rather than future breeding remain plausible limits. Those explanations need separate evidence; the current paired panel does not identify their individual contributions. Greedy maximization is also approximate: on the Parent’s original ten-path panels, its existing batches already captured every path maximum and a passive greedy replacement sometimes lost internal utility.

The molecular assessment finds recognizable ring-rich families alongside recurrent reactive heteroatom bonds, unusual ring closures and unassigned stereochemistry. The slightly narrower core coverage and higher same-pool correlation show that batch-best complementarity need not mean broader or cleaner chemistry. Valid graphs and higher posterior batch utility therefore leave chemical feasibility unresolved. The supported finding is successful allocation activation with no demonstrated final-score gain on these three seeds; transfer to different posterior quality, chemical families or batch sizes remains open.
finding_summary.results:
The batch objective changed the selected set in 434 of 435 batches when compared with the Parent rule on the same candidate pools and posterior draws. Among 3,765 later positions with a distinct positive-gain winner, 3,440 choices differed from the corresponding raw-draw winner under the same mask. Every emitted choice matched the registered acquisition. The internal estimate of the batch maximum rose by 0.00597 on average against the Parent comparator: 418 batches improved, 17 tied and none declined. The finite panel still saturated: 150 later positions across 45 batches had exactly zero gain and followed the declared index tie rule.

On the actual scored searches, strict improvements over the best generating parent rose from 624 to 688 out of 4,350 offspring, and incumbent improvements rose from 241 to 298. Yet the average accepted batch-best score fell from 0.48731 to 0.46096. The three-seed final macro mean was 0.57398 versus 0.57434 for the Parent, a change of -0.00036, below the required +0.002 improvement. One seed improved and two fell; seven of fifteen task/seed endpoints improved. Mean endpoints rose for sitagliptin and median similarity, while decoration hopping, DRD2 and zaleplon declined. Every session completed with valid, novel emissions and no numerical fallback.

Selected-stream prediction MSE fell from 0.01127 to 0.00980, while mean within-batch rank correlation fell from 0.550 to 0.515. Nominal 95% latent intervals covered only 77.6% of outcomes, versus 76.9% for the Parent. On identical Child pools, the changed rule selected slightly more uncertainty than the Parent rule, but average conditional correlation increased slightly and distinct molecular cores fell from 7.17 to 7.06 per batch.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic families with cyclic amines and amides, but recurrent reactive bonds, unusual ring closures and unassigned stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character: All five objectives have complete supplied trajectories; the brief lists no tasks_without_trajectories. The output contains compact methoxyaryl heterocycles, extensively decorated nitrogen heterocycles, flexible diaryl cyclic amines, medium-ring polyamides, and fluorinated carbonyl-rich heterocycles. These are predominantly connected ring-containing molecules, with occasional tiny fragments. The digest ring-closure rates range from 0.9506 to 0.9793 and aromatic-token rates from 0.9333 to 0.9747; these are fractions of proposal strings containing those features, not aromatic atom fractions or evidence of conventional ring geometry. All 4350 optimizer occurrences parse as single connected molecules in passive RDKit 2023.09.6 checks. This establishes graph validity only. Many accepted graphs contain nitrogen-halogen or oxygen-halogen bonds, peroxide links, dense thione chemistry, or short bridges across aromatic systems. Useful ordinary medicinal-chemistry motifs are present, especially non-acylated cyclic amines, aryl ethers and amides, but their coexistence with these liabilities makes overall synthetic plausibility questionable and drug-likeness weak. Structural diversity is moderate across the supplied seeds and objectives, with recognizable families dominating the high-score excerpts; high string uniqueness does not establish broad chemically plausible scaffold coverage. Every task has a zero digest stereocentre rate, although passive perception finds unassigned tetrahedral centres in many proposed graphs. Compared with parent n-559d25e9c9c7, the families remain recognizable while ring topology and heteroatom attachments change; the task entries describe those chemical differences alongside existing recorded scores without attributing activation or assigning new scores. All passive sizes, bond counts and perceived ring sizes below come from the supplied trajectories and are recorded in the accompanying molecular.audit.json. Digest best examples are pooled across seeds, whereas its final examples are the last listed seed-2 evaluations; those final examples are proposals, not a claim that the incumbent was lost.

per_task.generated_character: The optimizer mainly produces compact aromatic nitrogen compounds: median 25 heavy atoms, with a digest mean SMILES length of 41.5 and ring/aromatic-token rates of 0.9506/0.9437. The initial methoxyindole arylamide scores 0.3051048083696145. One high-score family retains indole-like rings and an arylamide but attaches fluorine to the amide nitrogen and halogen to the pyrrolic nitrogen. The pooled best molecule instead has 26 heavy atoms, two benzene rings, a benzene-fused four-member nitrogen ring, methoxy groups, a nitrile, a formamidine-like substituent and an N-chloro aryl enamine; its perceived ring sizes are 4, 6 and 6. This is ordinary fragment vocabulary assembled into a chemically unusual architecture. Relative to the parent, the median heavy-atom count remains 25, but nitrogen-halogen-containing proposals increase from 102/870 to 500/870. The parent endpoints are mainly indole/arylcarboxamide variants and a more extensively closed arylamide system; the child adds the nitrile-bearing small-ring family. The corresponding recorded parent-to-child endpoints, in seed order, are 0.45766047024715 to 0.43299980873877003, 0.4423126980074005 to 0.4519753205796759, and 0.4484138510190879 to 0.4586023950591373.
liabilities: N-F, N-Cl and N-Br attachment is recurrent, including halogenated amide and pyrrolic nitrogens; these are reagent-like bond environments rather than an established stable analogue series.

The best scaffold combines a benzene-fused four-member nitrogen ring with an enamine and formamidine-like group. Feasible synthesis and persistence of this assembly are not established by sanitization.
The final O-Br example adds a reactive oxygen-halogen bond while scoring substantially below its methoxy relative.
missing_features: The favorable nitrile/ring-nitrogen/methoxy combination is not preserved consistently in late proposals; the cited amino, ring-carbon and O-Br changes lose score.

A comparably scoring realization of that compact aromatic and polar arrangement with conventional, non-halogenated nitrogen bonding is not demonstrated by the pooled best excerpt. Its score benefit remains untested.
The best small-ring scaffold contains an unassigned tetrahedral centre. No configuration-resolved alternatives are supplied, so stereochemical preference cannot be inferred.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Small fragments such as the cited ethene and dibromine have score 0.0, whereas the connected aromatic heterocycles reach 0.4586023950591373. There are informative close comparisons: the best N-chloro, N-bromo and N-fluoro congeners all have exactly that score, so halogen identity within this set is not a demonstrated preference. Replacing the nitrile by an amino group in the cited N-bromo scaffold gives 0.2933971259571244. Replacing its embedded ring nitrogen by carbon in the N-chloro scaffold gives 0.4005880245850623. In the related saturated side-chain scaffold, replacing a methoxy group by O-Br gives 0.23618327637050734 versus 0.457118710172062 for the methoxy analogue. These comparisons support retaining the particular nitrile, ring-nitrogen and methoxy arrangement within this family; they do not establish that N-halogen reactivity is necessary.

per_task.generated_character: This is the largest and most heavily decorated output family: median 43 heavy atoms, mean SMILES length 90.8, and ring/aromatic-token rates of 0.9713/0.9678. The pooled best example has 39 heavy atoms and perceived ring sizes 4, 4, 6, 6, 6 and 6. It combines an aromatic core and an adjacent-nitrogen heteroaromatic ring with an N-rich thione heterocycle, exocyclic unsaturation, fluorinated amino substituents and strained annulations. The final seed-2 family instead contains linked nitrogen heteroaromatics, a benzene-fused lactone, carbamate/formamide groups and oxygen-rich chains carrying aldehydes, peroxides or O-F attachments. Across the full child stream, 224/870 proposals have an oxygen-halogen bond, 110/870 have an O-O bond, and 240/870 have a perceived three- or four-member ring. The parent already had large decorated assemblies and reactive oxygen chains; its corresponding counts were 113/870, 164/870 and 18/870. The mean heavy-atom count changes from 51.13333333333333 to 48.57011494252873 while the median changes from 41 to 43, so this is not a uniform shift toward compact molecules. Recorded parent-to-child endpoints are 0.6092799188640974 to 0.616571018651363, 0.6199818405862896 to 0.5942318675042833, and 0.616992140985949 to 0.6074025115664243. The parent seed-2 endpoint had 30 heavy atoms; the child seed-2 endpoint has 48 and an O-O-containing appendage.
liabilities: The best structure combines multiple thiones, a fluorinated carbon attached to several nitrogens, imine/enamine-like groups and small fused rings; the combination warrants a substantially stronger feasibility argument than its valid graph provides.
The final family carries O-O, O-F, aldehyde and nitroso functionality in highly decorated molecules. These are structural reactivity concerns; no stability or toxicity measurement is supplied.
Size remains poorly bounded chemically: the optimizer reaches 119 heavy atoms, and its seed-1 endpoint contains 81 heavy atoms with extensive unsaturated decoration.
missing_features: Compact, chemically conservative alternatives that preserve the favorable connected heteroaromatic arrangement are poorly represented in the best child excerpt; the parent seed-2 endpoint demonstrates that a smaller architecture can receive a comparable recorded score.

The excerpt does not resolve which peripheral donor, acceptor and ring substitutions matter: many differently decorated structures share the same recorded score. Stable replacements for peroxide, oxygen-halogen and densely unsaturated appendages are an untested chemical capability, not an inferred objective requirement.
Configuration-defined versions of the fluorinated and annulated structures are absent; no stereochemical reward can be read from these trajectories.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The cited fluorine, interhalogen and small carbonyl examples sit at the observed floor of 0.5. The initial fused heterocycle/aryl ester scores 0.548381482770623, and the decorated ring-rich products reach 0.616571018651363. This supports a preference for some connected heteroaromatic architecture over tiny fragments, but does not identify a unique decoration requirement. The digest contains many chemically different side-chain and annulation variants tied at 0.616019768563163. The final peroxide/O-F structure still scores 0.606951871657754, and the nitroso/peroxide example scores 0.6036414565826331. Those observations show that chemically consequential appendages can be tolerated within a narrow score band; they do not establish useful reactivity or synthetic viability. The lower endpoint of the much larger seed-2 child also gives no support for indiscriminate growth as a favorable feature.

per_task.generated_character: The high-score family consists of substituted diaryl molecules joined through flexible aliphatic chains and non-acylated cyclic amines. The optimizer median is 32 heavy atoms; digest mean SMILES length is 58.0, and ring/aromatic-token rates are 0.9644/0.9632. The best example has 31 heavy atoms, two benzene rings, a tertiary azetidine nitrogen, methoxy and O-NH2 groups, aromatic halogens and a benzylic chloride. Its perceived rings are 4, 6 and 6; it is not a piperazine scaffold. Nearby high scorers exchange the O-NH2 group for methoxy or O-Br, or add a primary amine. The final seed-2 family contains bridged saturated diamines, aryl thiols and frequently a sulfur centre bearing both C=S and S=S double-bond representations. The parent likewise reached diaryl non-acylated amines, including more conventionally sized saturated rings. Child versus parent counts are 454/870 versus 9/870 for perceived three- or four-member rings and 204/870 versus 86/870 for oxygen-halogen bonds. Recorded parent-to-child endpoints are 0.9959491085611949 to 0.9974355450101015, 0.9964552366323939 to 0.9913558178631674, and 0.9912887882944748 to 0.9895007716676499. The high-score amine/diaryl arrangement persists while the ring and appendage chemistry changes.
liabilities: The leading series combines long rotatable linkers, heavy aryl substitution and a benzylic chloride; graph validity alone does not establish useful exposure or stability.
O-Br and N-Br variants occur among high scorers, while final structures add aryl thiols and highly unusual multiply double-bonded sulfur environments.

Azetidines can be synthetically legitimate, but the frequent small and bridged ring assemblies require individual geometric and synthetic assessment. Their presence alone is not a blanket failure criterion.
missing_features: The useful non-acylated cyclic amine is already present; a claim that this generator lacks basic ring nitrogens would contradict the molecules. What is missing is consistent preservation of that arrangement in conventional, well-defined ring systems without questionable appendages.

The high-score diaryl amines are not configuration-defined: the best structure has three unassigned tetrahedral centres, and 833/870 optimizer proposals have an unassigned centre. No stereochemical preference can be inferred.

No reliable score requirement for O-Br, O-NH2 or the unusual sulfur centre is demonstrated; cleaner versions retaining the diaryl/amine geometry remain a transferable chemical direction rather than a target-specific prescription.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The cited low-score ketone/sulfonamide has a sulfonyl-bound ring nitrogen and scores 0.00021169315013374197; the small fluorinated aromatic ether scores 0.0018635782899060198. Neither has the high-score combination of two aryl regions and a freely substituted saturated amine. The initial large acidic sulfonamide scores 0.01904115112334333, so aromatic size or halogenation alone is insufficient in the shown molecules. The ordinary dimethoxy diaryl azetidine reaches 0.9969241385274472; its O-Br relative is 0.9972659759311256 and its O-NH2 relative is 0.9974355450101015. Thus the diaryl/non-acylated-amine arrangement is the strongest visible common feature, while these small differences do not establish a need for reactive oxygen substitution. The final diamine lacking the unusual sulfur double-bond assembly still scores 0.981013411741664. Basicity and protonation are chemical interpretations of nitrogen environment here, not measured pKa values or evidence of a particular binding pose.

per_task.generated_character: The output concentrates on aryl-substituted nitrogen/carbonyl rings with alkyl and ether decoration. The optimizer median is 32 heavy atoms, mean SMILES length is 55.2, and ring/aromatic-token rates are 0.9793/0.9747; halogen-token rate is only 0.108. The best example has 33 heavy atoms and a propyl/ethoxy-substituted phenyl group attached to a ten-member nitrogen ring containing two N-methyl amide carbonyls. Its other aromatic substituent is a nonstandard compact bridged aza/[nH] system: RDKit perceives two five-member cycles sharing a bridging path, not an ordinary fused azaindole. The next cited example replaces that part by an even more constrained aromatic bridge with perceived four-member cycles, alongside a nine-member polyamide ring. A separate high-score family combines a short aryl-oxygen bridge, a phenyl-bearing lactam region and an eight-member nitrogen ring. The parent already produced alkoxyaryl cyclic urea/lactam and polyamide architectures. The child has 409/870 proposals with perceived three- or four-member rings versus 102/870 in the parent, and 431/870 with rings of at least eight atoms versus 393/870. Recorded parent-to-child endpoints are 0.22270606177144964 to 0.2395714363708875, 0.24321515648721753 to 0.21628057414063917, and 0.23035161967494103 to 0.2451042931779277.
liabilities: Short bridges across aromatic systems can sanitize without establishing a realistic geometry. The two five-member perceived cycles in the best terminal heteroaromatic group should not be described as a conventional fused aromatic scaffold.
Medium-ring polyamides and multiply bridged lactams may be makeable individually, but the supplied graphs provide no ring-closure route or conformational feasibility evidence.
The high-score N-O replacement changes ordinary amide bonding without a visible score penalty, illustrating that score similarity does not establish interchangeable chemical stability.
missing_features: The best excerpt does not supply a conventional aromatic ring architecture carrying the same favorable aryl/polyamide arrangement without short, geometrically unusual aromatic bridges. Such chemically conservative alternatives are not established as score improvements.
The favorable ether, alkylaryl and amide connectivity is not retained consistently during ring and bond substitutions; late examples include altered amide environments and aromaticity.
Configuration-defined forms of the medium-ring and bridged products are absent: 779/870 proposed graphs contain an unassigned tetrahedral centre.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The cited methane, difluoromethane and acetylene fragments score 0.0. The initial fused heterocycle/aryl ester scores 0.1678386594791329, while the aryl/medium-ring polyamide assembly reaches 0.2451042931779277. Repeated amide carbonyls, alkyl-substituted aryl groups and appropriately linked nitrogen rings coexist in the higher-score family; this does not mean that adding any amide or ring is favorable. The ten-member polyamide example scores 0.2451042931779277 and the closely related ring-expanded example scores 0.2420342333201952. The N-O-containing replacement also scores 0.2420342333201952 despite changed bond chemistry. The final structure with a contracted nonaromatic carbocycle and changed attachment scores 0.2123251450326003. Together these observations favor retention of the connected aryl/carbonyl/nitrogen arrangement over fragmentation or some topology changes, but do not identify the hidden objective references or prove that the unusual aromatic bridge is chemically necessary.

per_task.generated_character: The dominant output is compact fluorinated nitrogen/carbonyl chemistry derived from fused heterocyclic diones and related ring-reorganized systems. The optimizer median is 28 heavy atoms, mean SMILES length is 51.0, and ring/aromatic-token rates are 0.9517/0.9333. The best example has 27 heavy atoms and formula C16H14F3N5O3. It contains an N-fluorinated nitrogen-rich dione ring, an exocyclic double bond, a bridged aromatic/lactam assembly, carbon-bound fluorines and N-methyl groups; only its benzene ring is perceived as an aromatic ring. Another leading family contains a fluorinated azetidine, a fluorinated heterocyclic dione, a hydroxylated unsaturated carbocycle and a thiol. The best seed-2 excerpt instead uses a more flexible amide/enol-ether-like chain and an S-F bond. The parent was already rich in N-fluorinated dione/imino heterocycles. Its median heavy-atom count is 27 versus 28 in the child; its median aromatic-atom count is 15 versus 9, consistent with the child exploring more nonaromatic ring-reorganized chemistry. Nitrogen-halogen proposals number 534/870 in the parent and 593/870 in the child. Recorded parent-to-child endpoints are 0.6510211907030741 to 0.5980589738951324, 0.4870057305679067 to 0.600551289906133, and 0.6025252354500499 to 0.5700483900567853.
liabilities: N-fluorinated diones/imides dominate much of the proposal stream. These are chemically distinct from carbon-fluorinated medicinal scaffolds and may behave as reactive fluorinating motifs.
The best families add strained azetidines, unusual aromatic bridges, enol/enamine-like unsaturation, thiols or S-F groups. Their synthetic and solution behavior is not established.
Repeated large fused-dione/aryl assemblies consume proposals despite extremely low recorded scores, while substantial local connectivity changes can destroy score even near the favorable size range.
missing_features: The compact carbonyl/nitrogen/fluorine balance visible in the high-score family is not preserved consistently: the stream still produces repeated oversized heterocycles and nearby small molecules with very different recorded scores.

Comparable high-score fluorinated architectures using conventional carbon-fluorine placement and stable nitrogen/oxygen connectivity are not demonstrated by the best excerpt; the observed scores do not establish a need for N-F or S-F bonding.

No configuration-resolved versions of the fluorinated saturated and bridged products are shown. Unassigned tetrahedral centres occur in 529/870 child proposals, and their effect on the objective is unknown.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The large repeated heterocycle/aryl product in the worst excerpt has 59 heavy atoms and scores 5.725865957926842e-51. The initial aryl/fused-dione ester scores 0.0020944534688323298. The leading compact fluorinated products reach 0.600551289906133 and 0.5980589738951324, supporting a strong preference in these trajectories for a bounded heteroatom/fluorine arrangement over repeated large heteroaromatic assemblies. Size alone is not sufficient: the cited late 28-heavy-atom carbon-linked chain scores 0.19196886149180178, and the 29-heavy-atom saturated nitrogen-ring variant scores 0.02741443602854399. The best lactam-containing assembly scores 0.600551289906133, whereas insertion of a carbon between that carbonyl and its ring nitrogen gives 0.5926816636813125. That is a local indication that the carbonyl/nitrogen connectivity matters. Neither the preference for carbon-bound versus nitrogen-bound fluorine nor an exact desired pharmacophore is isolated by these multi-feature comparisons.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Nitrogen-halogen bonds occur in 500/870 proposals in one compact aromatic family and 593/870 in a compact fluorinated family. Another ring-rich family contains oxygen-halogen bonds in 224/870 and O-O bonds in 110/870 proposals. High-score excerpts contain N-F/N-Cl/N-Br analogues with identical recorded scores, and a clean diaryl amine analogue remains near its O-Br relative in score. Thus reactive attachments recur without evidence that every such attachment supplies the favorable chemistry.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably preserve favorable molecular architectures while keeping heteroatoms in conventional, chemically persistent bond environments.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide chemically conservative alternatives that retain the connected aromatic, amine and carbonyl architecture while varying substituents within appropriate bond environments. Explore conventional carbon-bound halogens and stable nitrogen/oxygen functionality using task-local observed feedback, without assuming that a high recorded score certifies stability or that all heteroatom-halogen chemistry must be forbidden.

transferable_gaps.evidence: One high-score compact aromatic structure contains a benzene-fused four-member nitrogen ring. Another high-score polyamide contains two perceived five-member aromatic cycles sharing a bridging path; its nearby congener has perceived four-member aromatic cycles. A diaryl amine stream has 454/870 proposals with perceived three- or four-member rings versus 9/870 in the parent, while the polyamide stream has 409/870 versus 102/870. These are changes in ring architecture, not evidence of failed valence parsing.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring generation does not distinguish ordinary accessible ring chemistry from short aromatic bridges and densely constrained closures that merely form valid graphs.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make ring construction sensitive to ring size, bridge placement and a plausible embedding of aromatic atoms, while retaining legitimate small saturated rings. Offer less strained topologies that preserve observed favorable substituent relationships; use actual feedback to discover which alternatives matter rather than imposing an objective-specific scaffold.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The digest stereocentre rate is 0.0 on every supplied proposal set. Passive perception finds unassigned centres in 833/870 proposals in a diaryl cyclic-amine family, 779/870 in a polyamide family and 529/870 in a fluorinated heterocycle family. The leading diaryl amine alone has three unassigned centres. No configuration-resolved score comparison is present.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator supplies constitutionally varied molecules but no explicitly assigned tetrahedral configurations for the stereogenic structures it creates.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Add the ability to construct and preserve explicit configurations at stereogenic centres when generating or changing molecular graphs. Treat configuration exploration as an untested capability and let available feedback determine its utility; do not infer a preferred stereoisomer from unspecified structures.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The decorated heterocycle stream reaches 119 heavy atoms and ends one seed at 81 heavy atoms. A repeated heterocycle/aryl structure with 59 heavy atoms scores 5.725865957926842e-51, whereas compact 27- and 28-heavy-atom structures in its trajectory receive much larger recorded scores. Yet nearby small structures can also score poorly, and other high-score families contain medium rings and extensive decoration. The favorable property is therefore not a universal small-molecule rule.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output lacks consistent control of size and repeated decoration while retaining the particular functional-group connectivity supported by accepted scores.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support contraction and removal of redundant decoration while preserving the local carbonyl, nitrogen, aromatic and substituent relationships associated with observed score. Maintain access to larger architectures where feedback supports them; the needed capability is controlled simplification and size exploration, not an objective-named size target.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A nitrile-to-amino substitution changes a recorded score from 0.4586023950591373 to 0.2933971259571244, an embedded nitrogen-to-carbon change gives 0.4005880245850623, and methoxy-to-O-Br replacement changes 0.457118710172062 to 0.23618327637050734. Elsewhere, freely substituted saturated amines recur in high-score diaryl structures while a sulfonyl-bound ring nitrogen occurs in the lowest-score excerpt. These observations distinguish nitrogen and oxygen environments rather than merely their presence.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator often changes a useful functional-group role while making nearby graph edits, and the output does not reliably retain the favorable local arrangement.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Offer transformations that can retain nitrile, ether, non-acylated amine and amide roles, as well as controlled alternatives that change one such role. Use observed same-process feedback to discover which local relationships deserve preservation; do not hard-code a role or motif for an unnamed objective.

nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

retained_mechanisms: Task-local scored molecular-graph population with score-ranked parent sampling across three high-ranked quantiles
De novo connected-fragment graph crossover
Local atom/bond mutation, inner retries and occasional multi-step graph walks
Direct formula-preserving same-six-member-aromatic-ring C/N positional exchange in the inherited per-site replacement menu, including its invariant gates and passive mutation-sequence receipts
Chemical sanitization, stable canonical/isomeric identity admission with graph-equivalent alias confirmation, novelty rejection and bounded graph-based retries for complete pools
Bounded greedy score-ranked survival and subsequent breeding from accepted offspring
Accepted-only task-local Gaussian-process archive with full ordered accepted history, archive-mean centering, population-SD scaling and fixed observation noise
Integer-count Morgan environment representation in the inherited hashed radius-two vocabulary, generalized squared-norm Tanimoto covariance, and consistent pool/next-fit conditional predictions

approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds molecular graphs from accepted high-scoring molecules selected by score band. It either joins connected fragments from two parents, sometimes followed by mutation, or makes an ordinary mutation walk. Each mutation call retries the same seven primitive edit families with fixed weights until a valid product is found or its bound is reached. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled. Stable identity and duplicate checks form fresh surplus pools. A Gaussian process trained on all earlier accepted scores uses counts of local molecular environments and generalized Tanimoto similarity; correlated posterior draws choose the evaluated offspring. Accepted raw scores update the archive and greedy survivor population.
approach.novelty: Add magnitude-sensitive feedback to the existing mutation-operator lottery. Only an evaluated, accepted ordinary product with exactly one mutation call supplies credit to its uniquely successful primitive. Its nonnegative improvement over its actual generating source is scaled by the accepted archive available before emission and converted to a bounded reward. Smoothed accumulated rewards reweight the unchanged operator repertoire once per suggestion. Earlier operator-success weighting increased local win frequency while reducing gain size and final scores; this variant tests a different credit statistic under selective evaluation. It retains all composite generation and continuation, unlike removing those routes to simplify attribution. The current siblings test other proposal, representation, identity or selector boundaries, not this accepted single-call magnitude-credit law.

nodes.hypothesis: At each real suggestion boundary, reweight the unchanged mutation-operator mixture by smoothed bounded gain-magnitude credit from exactly joined earlier accepted ordinary single-call offspring, freezing positive weights throughout that suggestion and preserving every inherited generation route.

finding_summary.headline: Magnitude credit raises simple-source gains, but incumbent progress and endpoint mean fall
finding_summary.insights:
Magnitude-sensitive allocation improved the selected simple-source gain measurements without preserving stronger search progress. This narrows the motivating frequency-versus-size question: the eligible gain-size prediction succeeded, but it did not protect absolute candidate quality, incumbent advances or endpoints. Sources and archive scales were also lower, and the GP selected which outcomes could teach the weights. The result therefore supports a negative contribution from this particular added allocation rule under the tested composition; it does not establish that magnitude credit is worse than binary credit or that any primitive is causally ineffective.

The learned rule also affected failed inner trials, ordinary continuation and crossover finishing, none of which supplies its own credit. A successful one-call output after inner retries can still train its uniquely successful operator. Historical reward enrichment in those choices is an allocation result, not evidence that credit transfers as future efficacy. Rare operators retain optimistic smoothing, and invalid attempts remain invisible to the accepted-only reward. The preserved continuation and crossover channels, as well as terminal survivors, continue to produce useful outcomes outside consumed credit.

The chemical assessment still finds useful compact amines, lactams and aromatic alternatives alongside large repeated assemblies, unusual peripheral bonds, difficult rings and unspecified stereochemistry. A positive source gain or retained descendant can preserve those liabilities. Neither the credit labels nor lineage counts isolate a chemical explanation for the endpoint loss. The experiment supplies an exposed complete score failure under the registered review condition; changing provenance, suppressing composite routes or retuning the reward would be a new intervention.
finding_summary.results:
The credit and allocation mechanism executed as registered. Of 2,567 eligible accepted one-call outputs, 2,473 were consumed at a later real suggestion; 94 terminal outputs remained unused for allocation. Failed internal retries did not become extra credit trials, and composite outcomes remained uncredited raw observations. All 435 frozen weight calculations and 83,314 recorded primitive choices passed independent checks. The first fifteen suggestions matched the Parent, while all 420 later laws changed. Fixed-weight replay on the same recorded random states changed 36,657 primitive choices. These reached 1,700 accepted descendants; 917 later served as parents and 400 remained in final populations.

Within the eligible cohort, source wins rose from 403 to 452 and mean positive gain rose from 0.023041 to 0.025333. Positive gain per eligible observation also rose, from 0.003661 to 0.004461. Yet mean absolute offspring score fell from 0.404728 to 0.374110, and eligible incumbent advances fell from 164 to 147. Across the whole search, wins rose from 629 to 708 while mean positive-win size slipped from 0.024527 to 0.024071 and incumbent advances fell from 258 to 243.

All fifteen task runs completed. Mean final score fell from 0.595670 to 0.566674, a paired change of -0.028996 against the required +0.002. Seed changes were -0.086822, +0.053583 and -0.053749; nine of fifteen task-seed endpoints declined and six improved. Seed population SD rose from 0.026593 to 0.033955. Every pool and announced batch completed, although primitive validity decreased and one call exhausted its twelve internal attempts.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This gap originates in n-c55c3d520a2c and is reproduced in n-62daf219c70a; it recurs in n-9d0376974738 on complete matched Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2 at 300 observations per objective under the frozen profile. Evaluated or retained leaders carry N-halogen, N-S, N-O, O-S, cyanate and halomethyl chemistry. Credited positive-gain outputs can retain those groups. Strong aza-aromatic alkenes without N-halogen/amide groups and simpler high-scoring pyrrolidine/O,N-ring examples are counterexamples to a universal need for them.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve conventional bond environments while retaining favorable scaffold relationships.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Offer bond-environment-aware alternatives that preserve useful local scaffold and functional-group relationships learned from feedback. Distinguish ordinary carbon-bound halogens and familiar amine, amide or thioether environments from unusual attachments. Operator credit, canonical validity and positive gain do not establish synthetic accessibility or a universal filtering benefit.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The gap was recorded for n-c55c3d520a2c and n-62daf219c70a and remains in the current n-9d0376974738 matched three-seed panel. Structures include a three-membered heteroatom-containing ring motif, crowded brominated O/N bridges, small fused oxygen/carbocyclic rings, medium-ring polyamine lactams and large aromatic-labelled nitrogen rings. The strongest fluorinated leader lacks a cyclic cumulene, and simpler conventional-looking cyclic-amine alternatives score highly, so the most difficult motifs are not universal requirements.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently distinguish a representable ring graph from credible unsaturation, aromaticity or bridge geometry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide alternative ring topologies sensitive to ring size, bond geometry, heteroatom arrangement and bridge connectivity while preserving useful chemical context. Do not equate ring counts, aromatic labels, a close-ring gain or a canonical string with feasible geometry. These observations do not support banning every small, fused or medium ring or assigning one edit a causal endpoint value.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Previously observed in n-c55c3d520a2c and n-62daf219c70a; all five n-9d0376974738 tasks again have zero stereocentre-string incidence under the matched three-seed observation budget. Cited molecules include multiply fluorinated cyclopentyl centres, substituted pyrrolidines, bridged O/N systems and unspecified alkene/imine arrangements. The lone charge-marked small nitrile oxide does not provide systematic protonation coverage, while basic amines already occur in neutral notation.
transferable_gaps.gap: Emitted molecules lack specified stereochemical identity where saturated, bridged or geometrically isomeric features require it.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve or resolve stereochemical identity when warranted, distinguishing achiral and configurationally unstable cases. Treat protonation and tautomerism separately. Accepted identity joins and normalization provenance preserve the strings supplied; they cannot restore missing stereochemical content or demonstrate a stereochemical score penalty.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Context-retention limitations were present in n-c55c3d520a2c and n-62daf219c70a and recur in n-9d0376974738 under complete matched Search conditions. Small hydrocarbon, halogen, peroxide and nitrile-oxide outputs reach observed floors. One seed instead produces a 76-heavy-atom hydrazone/urea-like leader and repeated larger relatives without recreating the Parent's favorable compact family. Compact aryl amines and aza-aromatics remain high-scoring, and simpler local alternatives can approach more crowded leaders.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve useful molecular context while controlling fragmentation and repeated assembly.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Keep coherent functional-group context when simplifying or recombining structures, and distinguish useful elaboration from repetition. These conditional observations justify neither a fixed minimum size nor automatic preference for larger molecules. The presence of credited delete/append edits and uncredited continuation or crossover products does not identify which route caused the size distribution.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-9d0376974738 compared with complete n-62daf219c70a Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2 at 300 observations per objective. A credited single-call fluorine append improves its source while retaining N-F bonds and an unusual nitrogen ring; other leaders remain local amide, aryl-amine or lactam variants. Different seeds do reach different families, so this is not global structural collapse. Terminal eligible leaders, continuation products and crossover leaders demonstrate useful chemistry outside consumed credit. Historical n-9ab62999124d and n-030a6ccbba7c remain failed more-but-smaller-gain counterexamples under different mechanisms and conditions.
transferable_gaps.gap: Local source improvements can preserve a narrow chemically questionable family without supplying independent plausible alternatives.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Assess coverage through complete molecular arrangements and feasible alternatives, rather than gain events or operator names alone. Preserve the distinction between credit-eligible observations, actual weighted exposure, unlabelled pool options and later retained chemistry. The current fixed-weight comparison cannot isolate magnitude from binary credit; shared-Parent siblings and descendant ancestry do not identify additive or causal chemical effects.

nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves a bounded population of scored molecular graphs. It keeps the highest accepted scores, draws breeding sources from preferred score bands, and builds fresh molecules by mutation or connected-fragment crossover with a different partner identity. Accepted offspring can breed in later batches. A Gaussian-process predictor learns from the complete task-local accepted archive using count fingerprints and adaptive score normalization; correlated posterior samples select evaluations from a full pool of fresh graph proposals. Ordinary mutation continuation, crossover finishing and canonical identity checks remain active, while direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen positional exchange is disabled.
approach.novelty: This control removes nonincumbent access only from the first-parent role: every mutation starting source and crossover first source becomes the current accepted incumbent. It still consumes the original first-parent draws as passive references, keeps the full survivor population, and draws crossover partners by the original ranked law excluding the actual first identity. Earlier siblings flattened rank weights, expanded live membership, or changed survivor retention; none tested whether alternatives beyond the best first source contribute while population and partner diversity remain available. The question is the conditional value of that access, with useful, harmful and negligible contributions all informative.

nodes.hypothesis: Remove access to nonincumbent first-parent sources by executing the original quantile-group and member draws passively in their original order for every first-parent request, then using the current population[0] accepted record as the actual first parent, while retaining the complete ordinary live population and original score-quantile crossover-partner law with exclusion of that actual first identity.

finding_summary.headline: Removing nonincumbent first sources lowered the matched mean despite more incumbent improvements
finding_summary.insights: Access to alternative first sources has positive conditional value under this exact graph-search composition and evaluation profile. Choosing the best current score at every first-parent call raised source quality on each actual state, yet the resulting search histories had lower absolute generating-parent and offspring scores and smaller incumbent gains. More improvement events, continued partner diversity and extensive descendant reach therefore do not establish better endpoint search. The effect is uneven: all three median_2 endpoints improved slightly, while the largest losses were in two sitagliptin seeds and one deco_hop seed. The molecular assessment likewise found distinct leading families and a strongly enlarged series in one seed, rather than a universal loss of chemical variety; that enlarged series slightly improved its matched endpoint. Reactive local bonds, difficult ring connections and unspecified stereochemistry remain in the output, but these observations do not identify the chemical cause of the mean loss. The result answers only the conditional value of permitting nonincumbent first sources, including its changes to source probabilities, partner exclusions, graph randomness and feedback. It does not establish the contribution of the entire evolutionary foundation, separate mutation from crossover first-source effects, or combine this intervention with the partner-exclusion sibling.
finding_summary.results: Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.595670 to 0.539853, a paired change of -0.055816 across the three Search seeds. Ten of fifteen task/seed endpoints fell and five rose; seed mean changes were -0.106272, +0.009419 and -0.070597. The restriction executed on every first-parent call: 80,056 of 90,891 passive draws changed identity, and 3,829 accepted products came from those changed draws. Population survival, the original excluded-partner rule, learning and all 435 full proposal pools remained intact. Incumbent improvements increased from 258 to 287, but their mean positive size fell from 0.022510 to 0.017319 and their summed gain fell from 5.807663 to 4.970416. Mean accepted offspring score fell from 0.385256 to 0.334168. The changed products did reach later breeding: 2,037 were used again and 823 produced an accepted immediate descendant; products admitted at the end or superseded within a feedback batch were counted separately as censored.

molecular.headline: Aromatic amides, aryl amines and dense heterocycles recur, with reactive bonds, difficult ring connections and occasional size expansion
molecular.overall_character: Node n-9da98b015a09 produces substituted indole amides and aryl ketones, linked aza-aromatics, amine-bearing aromatic frameworks, densely bridged nitrogen/carbonyl systems, and fluorinated imino heterocycles. All fifteen Child and fifteen published Parent n-62daf219c70a search trajectory files were present and read: 9000 total records, including 900 records and 870 optimizer proposals per task in each panel. No trajectory path or task comparison is missing. The immutable comparison reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true, matched Search seeds 0, 1 and 2, and no profile-mismatched seeds. These are complete matched chemistry observations under the supplied epoch-1 profile, budget 300 and feedback batch 10; chemistry associations do not establish activation, mechanism contribution, chemical mediation, or reliability on unseen seeds. Published Parent trajectories, rather than a prior report alone, supply the comparisons below. The indexed Parent report and its source report in n-c55c3d520a2c were also read to preserve gap provenance; the historical source profile is not pooled with the current matched panel. Across Child tasks the digest ring-closure-string incidence is 0.946 to 0.9793 and aromatic-string incidence 0.9356 to 0.9793. These are molecule-level text-feature incidences, not aromatic atom fractions or perceived ring counts. Formal-charge and stereocentre-string incidence is 0.0 throughout. Available aliphatic amines and potentially stereogenic centres are nevertheless present. RDKit parsing of all supplied records succeeded; heavy-atom counts and ring-connectivity readings below were derived from those records, separately from the digest counters. Parseability does not certify stability, geometry, synthesis or biological activity. Recognizable medicinal-chemistry groups coexist with N-halogen and O-halogen bonds, N-N/N-O links, sulfur variants, strained-looking bridges and unspecified stereochemistry. Some ordinary indole amides and cyclic amines score well, so these liabilities are not universal. Diversity is moderate across all seeds and tasks but much narrower among leaders within a seed; neither high unique-SMILES counts nor ring presence establish broad useful scaffold coverage. A very large aza-aromatic series in one seed precludes describing the output as uniformly compact. Digest final_molecules are late seed-2 proposals, not every seed incumbent; all reported seed maxima and final examples were checked against full trajectories. The audit and citation validation are recorded under .slots/round-0024-slot-2/.

per_task.generated_character: The leading molecules in all three seeds retain a fused indole region plus a pendant aromatic ring, with carbonyl, methoxy and short carbon/nitrogen substituents. Each seed leader has 25 heavy atoms. Seed 0 favors amino-substituted indole aryl ketones, including an alpha-chloro ketone. Seed 1 favors an indole carboxanilide with an N-halogen amide and a brominated aminomethyl substituent. Seed 2 retains a vinyl/methoxy/methyl-substituted indole anilide, with terminal sulfur attached to the indole nitrogen in the final leading series. These mostly compact aromatic frameworks have recognizable synthetic handles, but their particular reactive substituents need scrutiny. Mean proposal SMILES length is 43.4, and halogen-string incidence is 0.9425. In seed order 0/1/2, Child maxima are 0.39347683285969637/0.4387992465191/0.40497388700123543 versus Parent 0.39405142067435733/0.47411701813450596/0.438972502037081. The Parent leaders instead include an amino-substituted cumulene, a pyridyl N-hydroxy amide, and an aryl vicinal diketone. Thus related aromatic/carbonyl chemistry persists with different local arrangements; the Child does not uniformly lose rings or amines.
liabilities: The seed-1 leaders place F, Cl or Br on amide nitrogen and combine that with a benzylic carbon bearing both amino and bromine substituents; these are different chemical environments from ordinary aryl C-halogen bonds.

The seed-0 alpha-halo ketone and seed-2 N-S attachment raise local stability and reactivity questions. The ordinary methylene ketone and N-H amide counterexamples prevent treating those bonds as necessary.
Unspecified saturated-centre stereochemistry and poor scores for both fragmentation and excessive elaboration remain despite a familiar indole skeleton.
missing_features: Consistently conventional substitution at the highest-scoring aromatic/carbonyl arrangements is not demonstrated. Ordinary N-H indole amides already score well, so stable amide chemistry is available rather than absent.
Stereochemical identity is unspecified at the alpha-halo ketone and brominated amino-bearing carbon centres; the supplied scores do not show whether resolving it would change the objective.
Chemically independent plausible alternatives are sparse among the leading within-seed series. No exact absent target pharmacophore follows from these trajectories.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxyindole anilide scores 0.3051048083696145. The seed-1 N-fluoro and N-chloro amides both reach 0.4387992465191, so their tie does not identify a specific N-halogen requirement. The seed-0 alpha-chloro ketone and a relative with an ordinary methylene ketone and an extra aromatic fluorine both score 0.39347683285969637; that comparison changes halogen position and does not isolate one bond. An ordinary N-H indole/N-H anilide in seed 2 reaches 0.40196779766986834, close to its N-S relative at 0.40497388700123543. Removing the pendant aromatic halogen still gives 0.3996288825296233 in that N-S series, whereas inserting an additional carbonyl/nitrogen unit into the amide linkage gives 0.2623347145996688. The visible association concerns a compact combined aromatic/carbonyl arrangement and substitution pattern, not halogen presence, greater size or reactive bonds alone.

per_task.generated_character: The seeds produce sharply different chemistry. Seed 0 leads with a 29-heavy-atom linked azaaryl/aminomethyl assembly carrying a hydrazone, an N-fluoro acetamide, aryl fluorine/bromine and an oxygen bridge across the aza-aromatic region. The bridge creates a four-membered ring path. Seed 1 reaches a 38-heavy-atom carbonyl/thione-rich fused nitrogen heterocycle linked to halogenated aromatic rings; it has seven chlorines, including O-Cl and chloromethyl environments, an N-N linkage and an O-S-O-Cl segment. Seed 2 expands into very large nitrogen-rich aryl/azaaryl assemblies with carbonyl, imine and alkenyl linkers: its earliest maximal molecule has 89 heavy atoms, and a proposal reaches 118. liabilities: The hydrazone/N-N chain, N-halogen amide and short oxygen bridge in seed 0 warrant local reactivity and geometry assessment.
Seed 1 combines O-Cl bonds, chloromethyl substitution, sulfur/oxygen links and a thione. Counting these as ordinary aromatic halogen substitutions would conceal their different chemistry.

Seed 2 carries many linked ring regions, imines and extended unsaturation in molecules much larger than the compact leaders. Such elaboration raises synthesis and physicochemical concerns without demonstrating a proportionate score improvement.
The floor value 0.5 for tiny fragments and toluene is an observed score property, not evidence of useful chemical function.

The small arene-spanning oxygen bridge and densely linked aza-aromatic systems lack demonstrated conformational and synthetic feasibility; aromatic notation cannot supply those properties.
Conventional peripheral alternatives at comparable leading scores are insufficiently established. The data do not justify prescribing more rings, more halogens or a particular named scaffold.

A 31-heavy-atom aminomethyl-linked azaaryl/dione proposal scores 0.5856408137025302 before the compact hydrazone family reaches 0.6310924369747899 with an N-fluoromethyl acetamide and 0.6338675004885675 with an N-fluoro acetamide. Seed 0 leads with a 31-heavy-atom N-ethyl pyrrolidine linked through a substituted chain to hydroxyl/chloropyridyl and halogenated phenyl regions, with a primary amine and sulfoxide. Seed 1 leads with a 29-heavy-atom spiro small-ring tertiary amine adjacent to an imine and benzylic chloride, plus a fluorinated biaryl/ethylamine region. Conventional cyclic amines and amides provide plausible chemistry, but some small-ring connectivity, unsaturation and stereochemical identity remain questionable. Both panels therefore reach aromatic amine chemistry; the contrast is not presence versus absence of a basic centre.

Several otherwise recognizable amine-rich products are structurally underspecified at potentially stereogenic atoms, including sulfur in the sulfoxide series.
Very large early products retain numerous aromatic and polar groups but low scores, so bulk alone is not evidence of favorable molecular organization.

Geometrically credible alternatives to the short arene-spanning nitrogen bridge are not established at its leading score. Ordinary cyclic amines and amide-linked relatives already score well, so a general inability to generate medicinal-chemistry amines is contradicted.

The trajectories do not identify an exact missing receptor-binding feature or justify adding basic centres indiscriminately; the remaining difference from Parent endpoints is not chemically decomposed.

The seed-1 spiroamine leader scores 0.9942738952920857 and its ethylamine-to-methylamine relative 0.9940479100596546. Seed 0 gives 0.9763374487514358 for both the sulfoxide and S=S analogue, while an ordinary amide-linked relative scores 0.9746153453426508. The seed-2 aryl ether and aryl sulfide tie at 0.9741097936653909. A 119-heavy-atom early product rich in aromatic rings, amides, sulfonamides and protected oxygen functions scores only 0.028858376832814066. The observed association concerns the presentation of available amines with aromatic regions, not nitrogen count, size or one sulfur/oxygen link. These oracle scores are not measured affinity, selectivity, protonation or conformational accessibility.

per_task.generated_character: The leading structures are aromatic nitrogen/carbonyl assemblies with dense bridges and medium rings. Seed 0 has a 37-heavy-atom diaryl framework containing a propyl/ethoxy-substituted phenyl region, N-methyl lactam groups and an N-N link. Seed 1 has a 31-heavy-atom aryl-O-N-linked fused nitrogen heterocycle with an N-methyl aminoalkyl bridge and carbonyl. Seed 2 has a 37-heavy-atom diaryl bridged system combining ethers, secondary and tertiary nitrogen environments, an N-N link and carbonyl-containing nitrogen rings. transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve conventional local bond environments while modifying useful aromatic and heterocyclic frameworks.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator would need environment-aware transformations that offer conventional local alternatives while preserving favorable arrangements learned from its own accepted feedback. Their observation does not establish that blanket filtering, a particular replacement, or any specific component change improves scores; stability and synthetic access remain unmeasured.

nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

approach.method_basis: The Parent walks from one scored molecule by sampling local graph edits, including direct exchanges of an aromatic nitrogen and a carbon within the same six-member ring. It normalizes molecular identities, rejects duplicates and submits the first full batch permitted by short-term inverse-motif memory. It then moves to the highest-scoring accepted neighbor even after a loss, while keeping a separate best archive. Memory records signed changes in rooted one-bond environments, keeps up to four inverse attributes from each selected transition, and vetoes a proposal when both signs match one live transition. These environments record atom properties and bond order but omit whether a bond belongs to a ring.
approach.novelty: Make inverse memory distinguish cyclic and acyclic versions of the same local environment by adding a binary ring-membership flag to every bond in its rooted motif. Ring and chain occurrences will then receive separate signed counts and restriction keys. The original motif description remains the ordering prefix, so the addition preserves priority between existing motif families. Earlier memory siblings changed sign coverage, score-based credit, count-based ranking, overlap retention or occurrence boundaries; they retained the same pooled structural descriptions. This experiment changes the topological context of the remembered attribute. It keeps the Parent's graph generation and nitrogen relocation mechanism.

nodes.hypothesis: Refine each rooted radius-one motif with binary cycle membership of its root-to-neighbor bonds, so signed occurrence counts and inverse tabu restrictions distinguish cyclic from acyclic instances of an otherwise identical local environment.

finding_summary.headline: Separating ring and chain motifs changed 20 evaluated neighbors, but all three seeds lost score
finding_summary.insights: The result rules out lack of structural activation or lack of evaluated exposure as the explanation for the missing score benefit. The original labels really did pool ring and chain occurrences, and the refined labels still transferred restrictions between distinct molecules during a live memory window. That additional topological distinction alone did not improve this search. It also did more than remove vetoes: resolving opposite changes that previously canceled changed which motif families were retained in nine transitions and created one extra veto. The largely unfavorable outcomes of the newly allocated neighbors show why passive admissions cannot be treated as evidence of useful search. The full trajectories also change when a batch stops on a different draw, so the large final losses do not identify the causal score contribution of any single annotation or unscored alternative. The supplied molecular assessment still finds aromatic and carbonyl arrangements alongside reactive heteroatom bonds, unusual sulfur cages and undefined stereochemistry. Binary cycle membership does not describe ring size, geometry, strain or chemical stability; those limitations remain open after this experiment.
finding_summary.results: The observed graphs contained 834 old motif families with multiple cycle contexts, and those distinctions reached live restrictions and scored proposals. A separate unannotated memory replay on the same sources and accepted history shows that 19 evaluated molecules were newly admitted and one evaluated molecule replaced a newly vetoed ring opening, changing 20 of 435 actual batches. Only one of these 20 molecules improved its source, by 0.001295; 19 worsened it and none tied. None immediately improved the best archive. One worsening ring closure became the next walk state, but its 20 later evaluated descendants added no archive gain. The three-seed mean final score fell from 0.521759 to 0.476854, a paired loss of 0.044906 instead of the required gain of 0.002. All three seeds declined. DRD2 and sitagliptin accounted for the largest task losses; zaleplon improved slightly on average.

molecular.headline: Aromatic carbonyl scaffolds persist, but high scores also accompany reactive decorations, sulfur cages and undefined stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: Node n-9dc03aaf234b produces medium-sized to large, heavily branched ring systems: recognizable indole/benzofuran/benzothiophene carbonyl compounds, decorated nitrogen heterocycles, aryl-linked cyclic amines, bridged amides and sulfur-dense cages. All five tasks are covered. Each digest contains 900 evaluated molecules, including 870 optimizer proposals, across seeds 0, 1 and 2. Every proposal set has ring_closure_rate 1.0 and branch_rate 1.0. Aromatic-token presence is 0.9057, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0 and 0.7264 in the supplied task order; these are fractions of strings containing aromatic tokens, not aromatic-atom fractions or evidence that every leading molecule is aromatic. Every set has charged_rate 0.0 and stereocentre_rate 0.0. Neutral SMILES can contain basic amines, and these records do not reveal protonation or stereochemical processing inside an evaluator. There is meaningful variation between seeds and tasks, but high-scoring excerpts commonly comprise close relatives of a few frameworks. An ordinary indole carboxamide is reasonably recognizable synthetic chemistry; many other leaders combine unusual sulfur coordination, heteroatom-halogen bonds or tightly connected bridges whose makeability is questionable. These coexist with useful-looking aromatic and carbonyl arrangements. The chemistry remains broadly similar to Parent n-abcd951ab7cc even where particular structures and recorded scores differ. All supplied child and parent trajectories were read passively. Structural sizes below are atom counts derived from their saved SMILES; scores are copied from those trajectories or the digest. The audit at .slots/SPIRAL2.r0011-04-improve-L16.molecular-audit.json records input hashes, graph readings and exact digest-to-trajectory matches. The digest final_molecules entries are the last evaluated neighbors of seed 2, not the best archive or all seeds combined. Missing features below distinguish absent chemical quality from demonstrated score requirements: these data cannot identify an unseen target pharmacophore, prove synthesis or establish biological activity.

per_task.generated_character: The optimizer proposals contain 21-29 heavy atoms. Compact fused aromatic heterocycles linked through an amide or ketone to a phenyl ring are prominent: the 0.39905049777278273 indole carboxamide has ethoxy, methyl and thiol substituents, while the 0.41003927643747895 benzofuran relative carries an anilide, an aminochloromethyl group, an aniline nitrogen and an N-chloro amide. Other strong examples replace the heteroaromatic core with bridged unsaturated O/N/S rings. The 0.3984261621341843 ketone is a considerably more entangled sulfur-containing polycycle. Ordinary aryl amides are plausible starting chemistry; the chlorinated nitrogen and unusual bridged sulfur products are much less convincing synthetic endpoints. Ring-token presence is universal and aromatic-token presence is 0.9057; this is not a ring-poor search.
liabilities: The highest displayed benzofuran compound includes an N-chloro amide and an aminochloromethyl substituent; these are chemical reactivity concerns distinct from ordinary carbon-bound aryl chlorine.
Thiols, unusual multiply bonded sulfur, highly bridged unsaturated frameworks and the cyclic alkyne-containing low example raise stability or geometric concerns.
Potential configurations in the aminochloromethyl and bridged products are unspecified; the proposal stereocentre-token rate is 0.0.
missing_features: Consistent preservation of the useful aromatic-carbonyl connection through late structural changes; some low neighbors lose it while retaining many rings and heteroatoms.

A wider set of stable matched versions of the compact heteroaromatic carbonyl framework without N-halogen substitution or unusual sulfur bridges. Conventional indole amides already occur, so the missing capability is sustained chemically coherent variation, not access to aromatic rings or amides.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial methoxy-rich indole carboxamide scores 0.3051048083696145. Its higher-scoring relatives retain a relatively compact aromatic/carbonyl arrangement. Low examples with a tetrahedral aminoalkyl linkage instead of the intact amide carbonyl score 0.03343008011310944 and 0.04832573556546499. The 0.0083275363022723 low example combines disrupted fused-ring chemistry, a small nitrogen ring and a cyclic alkyne-containing sulfur appendage. These comparisons support preservation of carbonyl connectivity and a coherent aromatic framework, although several substitutions change together. They do not establish that N-chlorination, a thiol or a sulfur bridge is required. Parent and child share the displayed 0.39905049777278273 and 0.41003927643747895 leaders. In seed 0 the recorded peak changes from the 0.393567030299894 benzothiophene ketone to the 0.3984261621341843 bridged ketone; that structural change does not itself demonstrate better makeability. The displayed final sulfur-cage neighbors still include a low 0.11267802872031613 example.

nodes.method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
nodes.method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.
