approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds molecular graphs from a greedy population of accepted high-scoring molecules using connected-fragment crossover and local atom or bond edits. It builds a fresh surplus pool, then a fingerprint Gaussian process trained on all accepted labels selects evaluations through correlated posterior draws. Its retained identity-admission repair confirms stable canonical keys before pool insertion. Atom replacement currently changes one element at a time; occasional multistep walks can combine substitutions, but there is no direct move that relocates a ring nitrogen while preserving composition.
approach.novelty: Extend the existing atom-replacement menu with one coordinated nitrogen positional exchange: swap a neutral aromatic nitrogen and a hydrogen-bearing aromatic carbon in the same six-member ring. This changes nitrogen placement while retaining formula, connectivity and substituent attachments. The earlier siblings protected carbonyl atoms or whole ring cores, redirected halogen growth, or changed parent allocation. This adds a local alternative without those restrictions. A different lineage exposed only ten such exchanges and missed its score target; here the larger fresh pool and inherited learned selector provide different conditions for testing the same chemical move.

nodes.hypothesis: Extend the inherited per-site atom-replacement menu with a direct exchange of a neutral aromatic nitrogen and a hydrogen-bearing aromatic carbon in the same six-member ring, preserving molecular formula and connectivity while changing nitrogen placement.

finding_summary.headline: Nitrogen exchanges reached 30 evaluations and one new task best; mean score rose 0.007397
finding_summary.insights: This establishes a useful local alternative under the existing pool generator and learned selector, including an observed incumbent gain, while narrowing the utility claim to particular molecular families. Pure exchanges were often neutral or harmful, and all eight evaluated descendants that also contained other edits lost to their best generating parent. Evaluated exposure was concentrated in zaleplon, decoration and median; neither DRD2 nor sitagliptin evaluated an exchange. The sitagliptin score gain therefore cannot be credited to a directly scored positional isomer, and the aggregate trajectory difference does not isolate the contribution of each swap. Three later reversals were correctly rejected as duplicates, demonstrating why operation counts alone overstate retained alternatives. Formula and connectivity preservation also leave the larger chemical limitations intact: the successful nitrogen relocation retained a reactive N-F substituent, the overall emitted stream grew in mean size, and explicit stereochemistry remained absent. The evidence supports testing nitrogen position as a local chemical variable; it does not establish broader ring-topology coverage, synthetic feasibility, or a uniformly favorable exchange neighborhood.
finding_summary.results: The intended positional edit executed correctly. All 536 sampled exchanges preserved formula and connectivity; 435 changed molecular identity and 101 were symmetry identities. Changed exchanges reached 404 pool entries and 30 evaluated molecules. Twenty-nine evaluations retained the exact immediate isomer; one also changed another atom later, while retaining the exchanged nitrogen placement and aromatic ring. The 22 evaluations containing only the exchange gave five source improvements, nine ties and eight losses. One pyridyl nitrogen relocation raised an accepted score from 0.438799 to 0.460926 and established a new final task best. Across all three seeds, mean final-best score increased from 0.544374 to 0.551771, a gain of 0.007397 above the registered 0.002 threshold; population standard deviation decreased from 0.013310 to 0.008223. Two seed macros improved and one declined. Zaleplon and sitagliptin task means rose, while decoration, DRD2 and median means fell. Every task completed its budget, all pools filled, and all admitted identities and feedback joins remained consistent. Recorded total wall time rose from 2,391 to 4,705 seconds, with both greater oracle time and substantially larger diagnostic logs.

molecular.headline: Aromatic and ring-rich products include oversized repeats, reactive substituents, short arene bridges and unspecified stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: All supplied tasks were read, including their Parent trajectories. Each child task contains 900 records, including 870 optimizer proposals. Ring-closure presence ranges from 0.9805 to 0.9908 and aromatic-text presence from 0.9471 to 0.9874; these are fractions of SMILES containing the relevant syntax, not fractions of atoms. The output contains recognizable indole carboxamides, heteroaromatic carbonyl systems, aryl-substituted cyclic amines and complex aza/carbonyl ring assemblies. Across seeds these are distinct families, but leading excerpts repeatedly decorate a limited family within a session. Some products are compact and chemically recognizable; others have repeated aromatic assemblies, unusual heteroatom bonds or severe ring-geometry concerns. Every digest has charged_rate and stereocentre_rate 0.0. Read-only RDKit perception of the supplied SMILES supports the structural descriptions and atom counts below; no synthetic route or three-dimensional feasibility is established by that parsing. Relative to Parent n-213e85380e04, chemistry changes unevenly: one stream grows substantially, another gains cyclic cumulenes, and another contains fewer halogenated products. These are observations of output, not a judgment of mechanism activation.

per_task.generated_character: The leading family consists of medium-sized, alkyl- and methoxy-substituted indole carboxamides connected to pyridyl rings. The first cited product has 25 heavy atoms and three rings, with an indole NH, an amide carbonyl, a pyridyl nitrogen and an N-F bond on the amide. Closely related products change aromatic halogens or nitrogen placement; another high-scoring cited product contains an N-O-Cl appendage on the indole nitrogen. Mean proposal SMILES length is 44.7, ring-closure presence 0.9805, aromatic presence 0.9782 and halogen presence 0.9609. Ordinary aryl carboxamide chemistry is recognizable, but its N-halogen and N-O-Cl variants are less routine synthetic endpoints. The Parent had similar mean length, 44.5, but lower halogen presence, 0.869, and its highest observed record was a bridged carbonyl/heteroaryl assembly at 0.4463521672202675. The child leading family is less topologically elaborate while retaining the same broad aromatic/carbonyl emphasis.
liabilities: N-F on an amide and N-O-Cl on a ring nitrogen are chemically different from ordinary carbon-bound halogens and raise reactivity and handling concerns.

Peripheral variation remains concentrated around one aromatic family; increased aromatic or halogen content alone does not preserve the favorable feature balance, as the duplicated late product shows.
missing_features: The tiny fragments and large repeated-core tail fail to retain the bounded fused-aromatic/carbonyl/heteroaryl arrangement expressed by the leaders.

The highest excerpt offers limited conventional amide N-substitution and alternative core chemistry at the same observed score. Whether removing the reactive substituents can retain that score is unresolved; the data do not identify an additional unseen target pharmacophore.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The supplied initial indole carboxamide scores 0.3051048083696145, while the leading pyridyl N-fluoroamide scores 0.46092619585962435. Within the leading framework, the three cited aromatic F, Cl and Br congeners all receive 0.46092619585962435. The cited alternative pyridyl nitrogen position receives 0.4387992465191 with the rest of that F-bearing framework retained. Thus attachment-relative heteroaromatic nitrogen placement is distinguishable in these observed products, while the particular aromatic halogen is not distinguished in this comparison. Methane receives 0.0, and the late repeated indole/amide assembly receives 9.929836687250678e-11. The visible gradient favors a bounded combination of aromatic surface, carbonyl linkage and heteroaryl placement over fragmentation or wholesale duplication. It does not establish that the chemically unusual N-F bond is generally desirable.

per_task.generated_character: The highest child excerpt contains very large repeated assemblies of aryl and pyridyl rings and conjugated oxygen/nitrogen carbonyl heterocycles. Ethoxy groups, chloromethyl ethers, imine and alkene connectors, cyanates and, in some congeners, aryl nitriles decorate those assemblies. The first two cited products have 91 and 113 heavy atoms, respectively. The final seed-2 excerpt instead contains smaller linked or annulated N-methyl dicarbonyl heterocycles, often bearing N-F, N-Cl or O-Cl groups. Mean proposal SMILES length is 125.3, versus 94.4 in the Parent; child ring and aromatic presence are both 0.9874. This is abundant ring chemistry with substantial repeated-core growth, not broad evidence of ordinary medicinal scaffolds. The complete multi-ring products have difficult synthesis and geometry questions even where their component groups are familiar.

nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

A candidate is vetoed only when its signed radius-one motif changes match both inverse signs from the same active source transition. finding_summary.headline: The repaired walk completes all three seeds while preserving the recorded search behavior.
finding_summary.insights:
The new evidence closes the specific uncertainty left by the recovery run: the identity fix supports the full previously failing seed, beyond the ten batches that could be replayed earlier. Exact preservation of all available successful histories narrows the earlier interruption to proposal-to-feedback identity bookkeeping. The original executable has no completed continuation for the failed task, so this establishes operational recovery and a complete score estimate without establishing a new search advantage. The seed-0 comparison supplied with this replication is the same repaired algorithm, not a separate intervention.

The small spread in macro score also hides task variation: sitagliptin final scores range from 0.4484554129767839 to 0.5903526424693334 across the three seeds. The molecular assessment finds different ring frameworks across the added seeds but persistent reactive heteroatoms, dense cages and unspecified stereochemistry, with late trajectories concentrated within related families. Successful identity handling and stable macro performance therefore leave chemical feasibility and useful scaffold coverage unresolved.
finding_summary.results:
The previously failing seed-2 feedback now reaches the correct pending proposal. The repaired walk processes all ten scores in that batch and continues to the full 300-evaluation task budget. Both added seeds complete all five tasks: 3,000 evaluations, 2,900 optimizer outcomes and 290 completed walk steps, with no invalid evaluations, duplicates or unresolved feedback. Replaying the original source still reproduces the exact identity-lookup exception, while the repaired replay matches the formal continuation.

The comparison preserves every one of the 4,310 previously recorded molecule/score entries in normalized order. All fourteen complete task logs are identical to the original runs; the failed prefix differs only in the spelling of one molecular identity, whose returned graph is unchanged. The inherited tabu behavior remains active in the two new seeds: 132 of 3,032 valid novel attempts are vetoed, while 1,577 partial inverse matches reach evaluation and supply 153 selected next states.

Macro final Top-1 is 0.518077929779343 for seed 0, 0.527798815337278 for seed 1 and 0.516876739241218 for seed 2. The complete three-seed mean is 0.5209178281192797, with population standard deviation 0.004890242222897396. The previously incomplete zaleplon task finishes at 0.41003927643747895. These are formal evaluation results; the diagnostic replay makes no oracle calls.

molecular.headline: Additional seeds vary the ring frameworks but retain reactive heteroatoms, dense cages and unspecified stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: This report covers seeds 1 and 2 of n-9f7c7ec50039. The supplied parent comparison is the same node's existing seed-0 chemistry, not a new parent-to-child chemical intervention. All current tasks have 600 recorded entries and 580 optimizer proposals. Ring-closure and branch presence rates are 1.0 throughout; aromatic-token presence ranges from 0.719 to 1.0, and charge and stereocentre token presence are 0.0 throughout. These counters describe SMILES-token presence, not aromatic atom fractions, basicity or stereochemical feasibility. The added seeds span recognizable indole/benzofuran amides, large nitrogen-rich diones, halogenated aromatic amine assemblies, bridged lactams and sulfur-rich cages. This gives moderate diversity across seeds and tasks, although each late trajectory remains concentrated in a related family. Several conventional medicinal fragments are retained, but many high-scoring complete structures have unusual sulfur valence, N-halogen or O-halogen bonds, highly constrained ring junctions or extensive flexible substitution. Rings and aromatic content are abundant; reliable synthetic accessibility and explicit stereochemistry remain the clearer gaps. The more conventional members should not be conflated with the implausible sulfur-rich and densely bridged leaders.

per_task.generated_character: Moderately sized aromatic carboxamides are prominent: seed 1 has ethoxy-, methyl- and thiol-substituted indole anilides, while seed 2 reaches an amino/chloro-substituted benzofuran N-chloroanilide. Later seed-2 molecules replace the fused aromatic core by bridged unsaturated oxygen or sulfur frameworks, retaining an aryl carbonyl-containing linkage. nodes.method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
nodes.method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.

approach.method_basis: COWBOYS separates the generative model from the surrogate entirely. A variational autoencoder is trained on the unlabeled corpus and its decoder is frozen, giving a latent space with a known Gaussian prior. A Gaussian process is then fitted not in that latent space but directly on molecular fingerprints and their scores. Generation samples the latent prior tilted by the probability that the molecule it decodes to would beat the current incumbent, using a Markov chain that preserves the prior. The result is that the surrogate steers sampling without ever having to model the latent geometry.
approach.novelty: This root commits to a Tanimoto-kernel Gaussian process on fingerprints as the tilt, and to preconditioned Crank-Nicolson transitions, which is the specific choice that keeps the latent prior invariant no matter how strong the tilt becomes. It requires the same deterministically decoded molecule to be used both for the probability estimate and for submission, so the surrogate is never consulted about a molecule different from the one that gets scored.

nodes.hypothesis: A corpus-trained frozen SELFIES VAE generates de novo molecules through prior-preserving pCN MCMC whose latent target is the standard Gaussian prior multiplied by a task-local fingerprint Tanimoto GP's probability of exceeding the observed incumbent, with the same deterministic decoded molecule used for prediction and submission.

finding_summary.headline: Decoupling the surrogate from the latent space reached 0.433, sixth of thirteen
finding_summary.insights: The design goal is met: the surrogate genuinely steers sampling and the prediction-submission identity never breaks, which is a real integrity property that several latent methods in this round cannot claim. The acceptance rate near 54 percent indicates the chain is mixing rather than sticking. What limits it is that a fingerprint Gaussian process fitted to at most 290 points has to generalise across a space the decoder can reach, and its probability estimates flatten out where the incumbent is already high, which shows as a median score of exactly zero on the hardest objective. Whether a different kernel or an incumbent-relaxation would help is untested, on one seed.
finding_summary.results: The macro mean of 0.433 places this sixth. It reached 0.868 on drd2_docking, 0.573 on deco_hop and 0.341 on zaleplon_mpo, with 0.212 on sitagliptin_mpo and 0.172 on median_2. Corpus pretraining cut held-out reconstruction loss from 4.225 to 0.161. Every session initialized a fresh Gaussian process on exactly ten scored structures and grew it in steps of ten to 290. Across the five sessions the sampler attempted 36,800 transitions and accepted 19,938, all 145 rounds had nonconstant posterior probabilities, and all 1,450 submitted molecules matched the recorded prediction identity exactly, so no molecule was ever scored that the surrogate had not itself evaluated.

molecular.overall_character: Ring closure is high and consistent at 98 to 99 percent on every objective, and aromatic content runs 67 to 91 percent, so the population sits in real chemical space more often than not. Molecules are moderate at forty-four to forty-seven characters and cumulated double bonds are near zero. nodes.method_name: COWBOYS: GP-conditioned de novo latent sampling
nodes.method_thesis: Train a compact SELFIES VAE from the permitted unlabeled corpus during preparation, then freeze its decoder. Within each independent objective session, fit a Tanimoto-kernel GP directly to the observed molecular fingerprints and scores. Generate new molecules through preconditioned Crank-Nicolson MCMC targeting the Gaussian latent prior multiplied by the GP probability that the deterministically decoded molecule exceeds the observed incumbent. The molecule assessed by the surrogate must be the molecule submitted. Fill the protocol-announced batch with distinct generated structures and update the GP after feedback. The corpus supplies a generative prior, never a ranked molecule library. This follows the decoupled mechanism in [COWBOYS](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v267/moss25a.html). Our hypothesis is that structure-level prediction and immediate Bayesian conditioning can direct scarce labels toward a higher final observed maximum without fitting a reward-dependent neural generator. Success is measured by the benchmark's mean of independent final Top-1 scores.

approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds fresh molecular graphs from a greedy population of accepted high-scoring molecules. Both mutation sources and crossover partners are drawn from preferred score bands, with uniform choice inside each band and exclusion of the first parent when choosing its partner. A fingerprint Gaussian process trained on every accepted label then selects which generated offspring are evaluated. The implementation already favors strong individual parents, but it does not use molecular similarity when deciding which two parents to recombine.
approach.novelty: Condition the crossover partner choice on similarity to the already selected first parent, using the same fingerprint definition that the Parent already declares. More similar eligible partners receive more of the chosen score band's probability, while the first-parent rule and score-band preference remain intact. This tests whether recombining related high-scoring molecules preserves useful local structure more often. The completed siblings altered core balance and survivor diversity; this experiment changes compatibility of a parent pair without replacing survivors or changing crossover chemistry.

nodes.hypothesis: Within the inherited selected score band, sample a crossover partner with probability proportional to its accepted-molecule fingerprint Tanimoto similarity to the already selected first parent.

finding_summary.headline: More similar crossover partners produced more local gains, but lower final scores
finding_summary.insights: The experiment separates selecting related molecules from obtaining more productive chemistry. Similarity enrichment and changed pairings are established, but the smaller parent-relative deficit partly accompanies a weaker reference parent and does not demonstrate stronger absolute offspring. Crossover contributed more local incumbent gains while the inherited mutation stream contributed fewer; mutation is not an unaffected control because new pairings change the accepted population and subsequent random trajectory. Much of the final-score loss came from the second seed's sitagliptin run, so this panel supports negative mean transfer rather than a universal failure of related-parent crossover. Fingerprint relatedness also did not preserve a common core more often: the share of evaluated crossover offspring reusing a generating parent's core fell from 34.25% to 33.00%, while survivor core coverage broadened. The molecular assessment still found repeated large assemblies, reactive halogen connections and strained rings; larger repeated products often offered little score separation from smaller relatives. Thus shared fingerprint features alone did not ensure that the unchanged fragment crossover preserved useful attachment relationships or chemical scale. The conditional-law comparison establishes allocation, but supplies no score for an unchosen partner and no causal attribution for either member of a pair.
finding_summary.results: The intended pairing mechanism changed actual breeding. Of 34,123 partner draws, 33,350 had unequal similarities and used the registered weights; 7,967 choices (23.35%) differed from the passive uniform choice on the same eligible partners and random variate. On nondegenerate states, expected Tanimoto similarity rose from 0.48313 under uniform selection to 0.51979 under the applied law. Actual mean pair similarity rose from the Parent's 0.48309 to 0.51650. The first-parent rule, greedy survival, graph operators and posterior selection remained unchanged. Both runs evaluated 1,679 crossover and 2,671 mutation offspring. Crossover best-parent beats rose from 172 to 176 and sequential incumbent improvements from 75 to 84. Its mean parent-relative deficit narrowed from -0.15687 to -0.13737, but the mean best generating-parent score also fell from 0.43361 to 0.40325, and absolute crossover-offspring score fell from 0.27674 to 0.26587. Raw invalid crossover attempts increased from 123 to 326. Mutation incumbent improvements fell from 143 to 130, leaving fewer total improvements (214 versus 218). The three-seed macro mean fell from 0.54437 to 0.52840, a paired change of -0.01597; seed changes were -0.00054, -0.06139 and +0.01401. All five task means declined, with the largest mean loss on sitagliptin (-0.06334). Every formal task still completed its full evaluation budget.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic carbonyl and amine families carry reactive halogens, strained connections and repeated large assemblies
molecular.overall_character: All current and parent trajectories were read. Each current task has 900 recorded molecules and 870 optimizer proposals. The output is predominantly aromatic and ring-bearing: aromatic-token rates range from 0.9701 to 0.9874 and ring-closure rates from 0.9805 to 0.9908. Compact fused heteroaromatic amides, aryl-linked saturated amines and quinoline/pyrrole/lactam combinations coexist with very large repeated dione, ester and carbonate assemblies. The most size-expanded task has mean SMILES length 108.2 and maximum 253, while tiny fragments also occur throughout the trajectories. All charged-token and stereocentre-token rates are 0.0. This leaves potentially basic nitrogen centres drawn without a solution ionization state and stereogenic bridged or substituted rings without configurations. Diversity is moderate across seed families but often narrow within a leading series. Familiar medicinal fragments are present, yet overall synthetic plausibility is questionable because N-halogen and acyl-halide groups, N-N and N-O connections, strained small rings, peroxides and reactive unsaturation persist.

per_task.generated_character: The leaders are compact fused and bridged aza-aromatic systems with an aryl amide or aryl ketone. Alkyl and ether substitution decorate the ring framework; several leading amides are directly N-fluorinated. A related family contains a conventional N-H amide and a thiophenol substituent, while another has an ordinary sulfur bridge and aryl ketone. Other seeds produce N-chloro amides or cumulated unsaturation in larger heterocycles. The lowest proposals are tiny imine or halogen-containing fragments, and a late elaborated amide product adds another ring/carbonyl connection with a much lower score. Conventional carbonyl fragments are recognizable, but the bridged topology and reactive nitrogen substituents limit synthetic confidence.
liabilities: N-F and N-Cl amides are reactive functionality rather than ordinary aryl halogenation.
Some relatives add thiols, O-Br groups or unusual unsaturation, including a cumulated-double-bond string rate of 0.0816.
Bridged ring arrangements and appended carbonyl rings increase geometric and synthetic complexity.
missing_features: The lowest fragments and over-elaborated products lose the compact aromatic/carbonyl arrangement retained by the stronger molecules.

Matched stable nitrogen substituents and ordinary ring connections around the leading framework are incomplete; the N-H amide and conventional sulfide/ketone relatives already show viable alternative chemistry.
Configurations at substituted bridge atoms are unspecified, and cumulated unsaturation in other relatives lacks a demonstrated feasible geometry.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The methyl-substituted fused N-fluoroamide scores 0.44941366017785356 with either para aryl bromine or chlorine. Replacing a ring methyl by methylthio gives 0.4166419114047398 for the same halogen pair, so sulfur addition is not rewarded in that local comparison. A conventional N-H amide relative reaches 0.4254027310763201 and an aryl ketone/sulfide relative reaches 0.42570769607214154; N-fluorination is therefore not universal among the stronger outputs. The more elaborated final amide structure scores 0.015332630870835013, and tiny fragments score 0.0. Current seed 2 reaches 0.44941366017785356 versus parental 0.4163503402962837 with a different N-fluoro carbonyl framework. Current seed 0 and seed 1 reach 0.4163503402962837 and 0.40143692941489145 versus parental 0.4463521672202675 and 0.4126819838532174. These observations favor a compact aromatic carbonyl arrangement without isolating one universally required heteroatom bond.

per_task.generated_character: The leading seed-2 family contains N-methylated heteroaromatic diones, substituted aza-aromatic ester groups and imine-containing unsaturated side chains with oxygen-linked alkynes. Some members join multiple copies of these motifs through branched carbon or ether-containing connections. Additional variants contain a chlorinated oxime ether connection, cyanate-like substitution or direct N-chlorination. Seed 0 produces very large multiaryl ester/carbonate assemblies with several nitriles; seed 1 develops fused carbonyl-rich heterocycles. The low tail includes simple hydrocarbons and an extremely strained small cyclic alkyne. The output has abundant polar and aromatic fragments, but repeated growth and reactive appendages dominate practical synthesis concerns.
liabilities: Oxygen-linked alkynes, imines, chlorinated oxime ethers, direct N-Cl and O-Cl variants introduce reactive chemistry.
Repeated dione/aryl/ester units and many ester or carbonate connections add size, flexibility and hydrolysis-sensitive bonds.
The small cyclic alkyne in the low tail is a particularly clear example of graph validity not establishing a plausible molecular geometry.
missing_features: Small isolated fragments lack the connected aromatic and carbonyl arrangement of the stronger products.
The leading set incompletely represents stable, less repetitive structures that retain the useful core; the smaller example already has a score close to much larger relatives.
Imine/alkene geometry and configurations of branched linkers are unassigned, while some small-ring alternatives require extreme geometric distortion.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The leading decorated dione/ester structure scores 0.6071971741156846. A substantially smaller member retaining a single dione/aza-aromatic core reaches 0.6060752169720347; extending an alkyl substituent or replacing N-methyl by N-chloro preserves exactly that score. Larger linked variants reach 0.606951871657754 or 0.6065327120947389, offering little separation from the smaller framework. Multiaryl ester/carbonate variants both score 0.6061163101604278 despite a change in peripheral nitrile substitution. Tiny or isolated reactive fragments score 0.5. The molecular evidence favors retention of the organized aromatic/carbonyl framework but does not show a strong need for its repeated appendages. Current per-seed maxima are 0.6061163101604278, 0.6025580572910527 and 0.6071971741156846, versus parental 0.6004556752278376, 0.6324703199409752 and 0.6083454583246726.

per_task.generated_character: The leading seed-2 molecules combine diarylmethyl aromatic groups with primary aryl amino and N-fluoroamino substituents, an available saturated-ring amine and a fluoroethyl-substituted pyrrolidine. Linker and ring topology vary between relatively open amine chains, small nitrogen rings and spiro or bridged arrangements. A similarly strong seed-0 family instead has chlorinated anisyl groups, a carbinolamine-like connection and a constrained bicyclic saturated amine, without direct N-F. Other seed-1 products contain unusually coordinated sulfur. The low examples are acid/amide/sulfonamide derivatives or isolated halogenated carbonyl/alcohol fragments. Recognizable aryl-amine chemistry is present, but N-halogen groups, unstable connection types and undefined configurations remain common.
liabilities: Direct N-F groups and alpha-haloamine or carbinolamine-like connections can be reactive or chemically labile.
Small nitrogen rings, cyclopropane-fused saturated amines and spiro systems create strain and configurational complexity.
More elaborate relatives combine multiple basic centres and hydrophobic aromatic groups, and occasional unusual sulfur bonding persists in another seed.
missing_features: The low acid/amide/sulfonamide and small fragment products lack the integrated aromatic and accessible aliphatic-amine arrangement found in stronger molecules.
Stable matched replacements for N-fluoroamino and carbinolamine-like connections are incomplete, although different high-scoring families show that no single reactive connection is universal.
Stereochemistry at substituted saturated rings and bridge atoms is absent; the scores do not establish a preferred configuration.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The N-fluoroaryl/diarylmethyl/saturated-amine leader scores 0.9862523132425369. The seed-0 carbinolamine/bicyclic-amine compound reaches 0.9860539690682922 and a less constrained amine-chain relative scores 0.9829644103093601. Thus strong observed scores occur across distinct aryl/amine frameworks and do not establish a need for direct N-F or maximal ring constraint. A related open amine chain in seed 2 reaches 0.9790824394553618. An expanded, partly dearomatized version of the substituted aryl group scores 0.18447496826975118, while the low acid/amide/sulfonamide example scores 0.0005876222816323224. A small anisyl alcohol/chloromethyl fragment scores 0.0015965585288304303. These observations support the combined aromatic/aliphatic-amine arrangement rather than either fragment alone. Current seed maxima are 0.9860539690682922, 0.9538130524845956 and 0.9862523132425369, versus parental 0.9908331648929692, 0.9512348232667347 and 0.9914038363125457.

per_task.generated_character: The leading family combines an alkylquinoline ether, a pyrrole ring and a nitrogen-rich cyclic carbonyl framework. The latter varies between expanded lactam/hydrazine-like rings, fused carbonyl heterocycles and N-O-containing connections. Alkylamino and acetyl substituents recur. Other seeds produce larger fused ester/carbamate structures or peroxide-containing cyclic diones. The very low examples are small molecules such as methane, water, acetylene and hydroxymethyl fragments that lack the leading framework. The principal fragments are recognizable, but N-N and N-O bonds, peroxide alternatives and expanded fused rings make the assembled structures less conventional.
liabilities: N-N, N-O and peroxide connections introduce chemical lability in otherwise recognizable carbonyl-ring families.
Additional ring fusions and expanded heterocycles add synthetic and conformational complexity without a clear local score advantage.
Repeated structures and tiny fragments still appear alongside the useful aromatic/carbonyl organization.
missing_features: The lowest fragments lack the integrated aromatic and carbonyl-containing nitrogen framework of the stronger molecules.

The displayed series incompletely covers ordinary stable carbon/nitrogen ring connections preserving the same fragment placement; closely scoring variants do not establish a need for N-O or hydrazine-like bonds.
Expanded ring conformations and stereogenic alternative frameworks remain undefined, and no single unseen functional group is established as the missing objective feature.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The quinoline-ether/pyrrole/cyclic nitrogen-carbonyl leader scores 0.21843931889797025, while a related acetyl/carbonyl framework reaches 0.21821789023599233. Several nitrogen-, oxygen- or carbon-linked variants remain close: 0.21505649253221687, 0.21387513707167027 and 0.2133697489012744. A methylene insertion into the aryl-ether connection gives 0.2120637831740049. These comparisons support the overall quinoline/pyrrole/carbonyl organization more clearly than a unique N-N or N-O connection. Tiny fragments score 0.0, and additional fused-ring elaboration in final molecules remains around 0.2000100007500625 to 0.2030079876549599. Current seed 2 reaches 0.21843931889797025 versus parental 0.21037674112349405 with a different quinoline-linked expanded dicarbonyl framework. Current seed 0 and seed 1 reach 0.2088465157016203 and 0.2118805753879094 versus parental 0.22405709718343647 and 0.2133697489012744.

per_task.generated_character: The strongest family combines a nitrogen-containing fused dione bearing direct N-F substituents, a small unsaturated carbon ring and a methylamino-substituted cyclopentadiene-like ring carrying an acyl fluoride. Free thiol or sulfur-linked ring closures occur in relatives. A second family has a more fused carbonyl-rich aza framework with carbon-bound fluorine and an aryl acyl fluoride, while another seed produces aldehyde-bearing sulfur/nitrogen heterocycles. These are moderate-sized but chemically reactive structures. The low tail is dominated by large coupled dione units or highly elaborated sugar/aryl assemblies, including examples that already carry acyl fluorides.
liabilities: Acyl fluoride and direct N-F are reactive bonds and should not be conflated with ordinary stable carbon fluorination.
Small unsaturated rings, free thiols, sulfur-linked cages and aldehydes add stability or strain concerns.
Large coupled diones and complex sugar/aryl assemblies create severe size and topology deviations from the stronger molecules.
missing_features: The low repeated assemblies lack the useful compact arrangement despite carrying some of the same dione or fluorinated groups.

The displayed leaders lack a matched series retaining the carbonyl and fluorinated-group geometry while replacing acyl fluoride and direct N-F with stable alternatives. Their presence in stronger molecules does not establish chemical necessity.
The stronger parental aminomethyl/fluorinated-aryl dione arrangement is not recovered among the current leading families.
Configurations of substituted small rings and unsaturated-ring geometries remain unspecified.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The leading acyl-fluoride/N-fluorinated dione scores 0.5176146979065886. Adding fluorine to its small carbon ring gives 0.5099566511392558, while chlorine there gives 0.4470674757352588. A more bridged sulfur-containing relative scores 0.4780400812140165, so additional ring closure does not improve that comparison. The second fused family reaches 0.44237693944672385 with fluoromethyl substitution, and related carbon-bound fluorine arrangements score 0.4337016156471047 or 0.4333617268342616. These observations associate stronger scores with a compact carbonyl-rich framework and specific fluorinated-group placement, not maximal fluorine count. Large repeated dione assemblies score as low as 1.7287338239402662e-48; some contain acyl fluoride too, showing that this group alone is insufficient. Current seed 0 and seed 2 reach 0.5176146979065886 and 0.44237693944672385 versus parental 0.4759777345546235 and 0.4071395189354175. Current seed 1 reaches 0.3176770239241658 versus parental 0.5845583988949146 with a more conventional aminomethyl/fluorinated-aryl dione family.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The cited output includes N-F and N-Cl groups, acyl fluorides, N-O and N-N connections, peroxides and oxygen-linked alkynes. Strong alternatives with conventional N-H amide or sulfide/ketone connections reach 0.4254027310763201 and 0.42570769607214154, and distinct aryl/amine families reach similar scores with different reactive groups.
transferable_gaps.gap: Reactive bond types remain entangled with useful aromatic, carbonyl and amine arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide matched stable substitutions that preserve useful fragment placement. Distinguish ordinary amides, amines, thioethers and carbon-bound halogens from acyl-halide, heteroatom-halogen and other labile connections.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The most size-expanded proposal set has mean SMILES length 108.2 and maximum 253. A smaller dione/aza-aromatic member scores 0.6060752169720347, close to much larger relatives at 0.606951871657754, while tiny fragments sit at low baselines and large repeated dione assemblies can score 1.7287338239402662e-48.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator still produces excessive repetition and tiny fragments instead of consistently preserving useful molecular scale.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Expand chemical variety through coherent changes in scaffold, substitution and linker geometry while preserving the useful core size. Include simplifications that remove whole repeated units or unnecessary appendages without destroying the principal functional-group arrangement.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every task has stereocentre-token rate 0.0. The cited molecules contain substituted bridges, small nitrogen rings, cyclopropane-fused amines, unsaturated small carbon rings and an extremely strained small cyclic alkyne. Other structures add expanded rings and imine geometry that cannot be judged from aromatic or closure tokens alone.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring geometry and stereochemical identity remain unresolved for constrained or unsaturated products.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Offer ordinary ring topologies and feasible configurations, preserve stereochemical assignments when structures change, and compare matched alternatives with different constraints. Successful parsing should not substitute for chemically plausible geometry.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Aryl bromine and chlorine relatives share 0.44941366017785356, while replacing a methylthio substituent by methyl raises the displayed pair to that value from 0.4166419114047398. Several alkyl or N-chloro substitutions leave another family at 0.6060752169720347, and multiple carbon/nitrogen/oxygen connection variants retain closely similar scores.
transferable_gaps.gap: Matched local simplifications are incomplete where additional complexity has little demonstrated score value.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Generate matched changes that remove unnecessary substitution, unstable bonds or extra ring connections while holding the useful aromatic and polar fragments fixed. Let observed feedback distinguish necessary geometry from tolerated embellishment.

nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

approach.method_basis: The Parent starts from the best supplied molecule and samples local atom, bond, path and ring edits, including a direct exchange of aromatic nitrogen and carbon that preserves molecular formula. It normalizes molecular identities, rejects duplicates and submits the first full batch admitted by its structural memory. The highest-scoring accepted neighbor becomes the next current molecule even after a tie or loss, while a separate archive keeps the best observation. Every selected transition currently installs short-lived inverse motif restrictions, regardless of whether that transition improved its source. A later neighbor is vetoed when opposite signed restrictions match the same earlier transition.
approach.novelty: Give new memory credit only to a selected transition that strictly improves its actual source score. Tied and worsening winners still become current and age existing memory, but install or refresh no restrictions. This tests whether protecting locally unsuccessful moves unnecessarily blocks fresh variations that reverse their motifs. Earlier siblings refined which motif matches cause a veto, repaired identity bookkeeping, changed local chemistry or reweighted edit operators; none conditioned restriction installation on the individual selected winner's observed gain. The Parent's aromatic nitrogen exchange remains part of the tested method.

nodes.hypothesis: Install and refresh inverse-motif restrictions only when the selected actually accepted neighbor has a strictly higher score than its recorded source; tied and worsening selected transitions still move and age the walk but receive no new memory credit.

finding_summary.headline: Selective memory credit admitted 74 scored neighbors, but lowered the panel mean
finding_summary.insights: The experiment establishes that protecting nonimproving moves can block useful fresh variations: newly admitted methyl removal and aryl-fluorine removal both produced immediate archive gains. It also rules out an unexercised gate, missing feedback or changed restriction tenure as explanations for the negative panel result. Those useful cases were sparse, and overall source-improvement frequency and positive-gain magnitude fell. The archive improved slightly more often, but its total improvement was smaller. This narrows the question to the search value of the restrictions: withholding credit based on one move's local gain does not reliably identify protection that is expendable on this panel. Whether protecting nonimproving moves helps diversification remains unresolved because the passive comparison cannot reproduce an alternative walk or score excluded candidates. Preserved overlap provenance matters in practice: an older improving pair survived a skipped refresh and blocked a candidate that unconditional credit would admit. Thus the gate does not create a universal admissibility superset. The supplied molecular assessment still finds reactive heteroatom bonds, unusual sulfur connections and dense ring systems alongside recognizable aromatic/carbonyl and amine families; the changed allocation supplies no evidence that chemical feasibility improved.
finding_summary.results: All 184 tied or worsening selected moves skipped memory installation, omitting 719 attributes while retaining 984 attributes from improving moves. On the Child's recorded history, unconditional credit would veto 188 novel draws; the actual gate vetoed 115. This admitted 74 candidates across all fifteen task sessions, while preserved older provenance caused one additional veto in the opposite direction. Twenty newly admitted candidates became next states. Fourteen improved their source score, thirteen tied and forty-seven worsened it; only two immediately improved the archive. The three-seed macro mean fell from 0.521759 to 0.501486, a paired change of -0.020273, against the registered requirement of +0.002. Two seeds declined and one improved. Task means improved for zaleplon and median_2, but declined for deco_hop, DRD2 and sitagliptin, with the largest loss in DRD2. All runs completed their full budgets and batches.

It also rules out an unexercised gate, missing feedback or changed restriction tenure as explanations for the negative panel result. Those useful cases were sparse, and overall source-improvement frequency and positive-gain magnitude fell. The archive improved slightly more often, but its total improvement was smaller. This narrows the question to the search value of the restrictions: withholding credit based on one move's local gain does not reliably identify protection that is expendable on this panel. Whether protecting nonimproving moves helps diversification remains unresolved because the passive comparison cannot reproduce an alternative walk or score excluded candidates. Preserved overlap provenance matters in practice: an older improving pair survived a skipped refresh and blocked a candidate that unconditional credit would admit. Thus the gate does not create a universal admissibility superset. The supplied molecular assessment still finds reactive heteroatom bonds, unusual sulfur connections and dense ring systems alongside recognizable aromatic/carbonyl and amine families; the changed allocation supplies no evidence that chemical feasibility improved.

molecular.headline: Aromatic carbonyl and amine families persist, with small fused rings, reactive heteroatom bonds and sulfur-rich cages
molecular.overall_character: All supplied Child and Parent trajectory files were read; all five objectives are covered. Each Child task contains 900 recorded molecules, including 870 optimizer proposals. Ring-closure and branch-token rates are 1.0 throughout. Aromatic-token rates are 0.9793, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0 and 0.7839 in the supplied task order; mean SMILES lengths are 45.9, 68.6, 68.6, 61.8 and 63.4. These are substantial connected ring-bearing compounds, ranging from comparatively compact indole/carbonyl derivatives to bulky decorated aza-heterocycles, aryl polyamines, expanded heterocycles and densely connected sulfur cages. The token rates describe strings containing those features, not aromatic atom fractions or chemically perceived ring counts. Diversity is moderate across seeds and frameworks, but many leading examples are close local analogues. The chemistry changes relative to Parent n-abcd951ab7cc without resolving its recurring feasibility problems. Ordinary amides, ethers, amines and aromatic rings coexist with N-halogen and O-halogen bonds, peroxide connections, unusual sulfur-sulfur multiple bonds and demanding ring junctions. Every task has charge-token and stereocentre-token rates of 0.0; this leaves stereogenic relationships unspecified and does not imply that the amines cannot protonate. Apparent synthesis and medicinal quality are therefore questionable despite recognizable useful fragments. Score comparisons below are observations from the provided trajectories, not new scores, binding-mode assignments or claims about hidden objective requirements.

The strongest seed-2 example is a benzofuran-like system fused to a small saturated carbocycle bearing a primary amine, with a methyl group and an arylmethyl ketone whose terminal ring carries an N-chloro amino group. Seed 0 instead produces an ethoxy/methyl aromatic framework fused to small carbocycles, linked through an ordinary amide to an aminoaryl group; nearby variants contain benzothiophene or aza-aromatic rings and hydroxylamine functionality. Seed 1 retains an ethoxy/methyl/thiol indole carboxanilide. The latter has recognizable conventional synthetic connections, whereas the small fused rings and reactive substituents complicate other leaders. Lower examples replace the carbonyl connection with a saturated heteroatom-rich carbon, disrupt aromaticity or join a thioester to an expanded unsaturated sulfur ring. Late molecules retain the carbonyl families while adding further sulfur and N-O chemistry.

nodes.method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
nodes.method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.

approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from task-local accepted scores. It keeps the best 64 scored survivors, draws breeding parents from three preferred score bands, and generates fresh molecules with fragment crossover and local graph mutations, including the inherited continuation and retry rules. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled. Candidate identity checks reject invalid, unstable or duplicate proposals. For each evaluation batch it builds a full pool and uses a Gaussian process with count-based molecular fingerprints and correlated posterior samples to choose which candidates receive scores. Every accepted score enters the complete model archive; the best surviving offspring can become parents of later generations.
approach.novelty: This control makes every eligible live survivor equally likely to breed. It keeps the original band draw as a passive diagnostic, then uses the existing member draw over the full eligible live population. The earlier frozen initial-cohort experiment stopped accepted descendants from becoming breeders. Here those descendants continue to breed under the original survival rule, so the new contrast tests the complete inherited score-quantile preference. I expect broader rank use and weaker generating parents to lower final scores, but only complete matched endpoints can establish that contribution. Support restrictions and probability weights change together; their separate effects and the value of the entire optimizer remain unresolved.

nodes.hypothesis: Replace the inherited score-quantile preference with uniform draws over every eligible member of the current live score-greedy survivor population, retaining the original band construction and band-choice draw passively, the existing member-choice call and partner-exclusion fallback, recursive accepted-offspring breeding, and active accepted-label count-GP allocation.

finding_summary.headline: Score-quantile preference contributes: uniform live breeding lowers mean final Top-1 by 0.045998.
finding_summary.insights:
This establishes positive conditional contribution of the inherited score-quantile preference while recursive feedback, greedy survival and the predictive selector remain active. It does not separate the value of restricting support from the value of weighting supported ranks. It also does not repeat the earlier fixed-initial-parent experiment or settle the value of the whole graph-evolution foundation.

The contrast separates participation from productive progress. Previously unsupported parents contributed to 1,427 evaluated offspring, of which 928 later bred. Yet strict generating-parent beats increased from 629 to 1,055 against weaker sources, while sequential incumbent gains fell from 258 to 203. Predictions also had lower error and higher within-batch ordering correlation on the changed evaluated distribution, despite worse endpoints. None of these selected associations establishes a causal mediator or a transferable surrogate-quality gain.

The molecular assessment finds recognizable biaryl amines and useful aromatic/carbonyl combinations alongside inherited reactive bonds, crowded rings and unspecified stereochemistry. The halogen-free carboxamide improvement and a strong carbon-bound-fluorine leader prevent treating unusual bonds or blanket chemical exclusions as the explanation. Broader parent participation therefore did not resolve chemical feasibility or ensure better endpoint search. Terminal admissions and unselected alternatives provide no unobserved descendant outcomes.
finding_summary.results:
All 106,858 Child breeding draws followed the uniform law over eligible current survivors, including partner exclusion. 53,199 draws used ranks that the inherited score bands could never choose, and 92,549 lay outside the passively drawn band. Mean selected topness was 0.500066, close to the exclusion-conditioned uniform expectation of 0.499988, versus 0.884073 under the original law on those same states. Accepted offspring continued to enter survivors and breed: 3,254 distinct offspring were later used, versus 2,401 for the Parent. molecular.headline: Aryl amines and compact carbonyl rings coexist with peroxide, N-halogen and strained-ring chemistry under live-parent sampling
molecular.overall_character:
All fifteen Child and fifteen published Parent trajectories were read: 4,500 observations per node, including 4,350 optimizer proposals per node. Every supplied task and Search Seed 0, 1 and 2 is covered, with no missing listed path. The brief reports complete profile-matched pairing to n-62daf219c70a at 300 observations per task and ten-member batches. The molecules include annulated pyrrole carboxamides, a halogen-free spiro N/O-ring carboxamide, linked azaarenes and carbonyl-rich heterocycles, peroxide/azo/hypochlorite assemblies, recognizable biaryl cyclic amines, sulfur-containing polycycles, nitrogen/carbonyl cages and fluorinated dione or thiourea/hydrazone systems. Proposal ring-digit incidence spans 0.9287 to 0.9782 and aromatic-string incidence 0.8701 to 0.9621. Those are presence counters in SMILES, not counts of independent scaffolds or validation of geometry. Diversity is moderate across evaluated seed families, with substantial local series within seeds. Recognizable amines, amides, phenols and carbonyl rings are present, but unusual bond environments and crowded topology leave overall makeability questionable and drug-likeness weak. Every task has stereocentre-string and charge-string incidence 0.0 despite saturated stereogenic environments and available basic amines. Sizes below are heavy-atom-token counts, not computed physical properties. Raw trajectory scores are used throughout; initial observations, optimizer proposals, observed leaders, immediate survivor admissions and later reuse are distinguished.

The read-only log audit joins all 4,350 accepted offspring through pooled identity, actual posterior selection, emission and feedback to real earlier accepted parents. It checks parent score, serial, rank and identity against the corresponding live-population snapshot. Across 106,858 recorded actual parent draws, 96,539 use generated offspring. On 92,549 draws the chosen rank is outside the passively sampled legacy group, and 53,199 draws have zero recorded probability under the legacy law. Actual bands are reconstructed from actual ranks independently of passive band labels. These are participation diagnostics, not an activation or causal-mediation verdict, and passive bands are not counterfactual executed parents. The audit finds 3,254 accepted offspring later used as actual parents, distinguishing immediate admission, next-batch membership and terminal records without a later opportunity. This is the stated uniform draw over current live survivors; it is not the previous frozen-initial-cohort control or removal of the graph foundation. Retained score-greedy survival and GP allocation remain part of the stated comparison, without attribution of chemical changes to either. Direct-generation examples below do not characterize every ancestral choice, and parent beats are not substituted for matched endpoint gains. No oracle score is assigned to unselected alternatives, and fingerprint equivalence is not inferred from structural resemblance or score ties.

per_task.generated_character: The three seed leaders contain 24, 25 and 24 heavy-atom tokens. Seed 0 has an annulated pyrrolic carboxanilide with a larger unsaturated carbocycle, an O-F substituent and an N-S substituent. Its earlier N-H relative retains the same O-F liability. Seed 1 instead uses an N-H pyrrolic carboxamide, a fluorinated or brominated pyridyl group and a fluoromethyl ether on an unsaturated annulated ring; that ether has O-C-F connectivity, not O-F. Seed 2 reaches a halogen-free N-methyl carboxanilide with methylthio substitution and a spiro four-membered N/O ring written C2(N=CO2), fused into the annulated pyrrole region. The ordinary aryl amide motif is retained, but the small N/O ring and annulated unsaturation have unresolved geometry. Mean proposal SMILES length is 42.1, aromatic-string incidence 0.9425 and halogen incidence 0.8805. The halogen-free leader is a counterexample to universal halogen dependence.
liabilities: Direct O-F and N-S bonds in one seed differ chemically from the carbon-bound fluorine in another seed's fluoromethyl ether.
The halogen-free leader still contains a crowded four-membered N/O ring; removing a halogen does not establish synthetic feasibility.
Large coupled relatives and expanded ring variants can lose useful score while retaining many of the same functional groups.
missing_features: The favored aryl/carboxamide context is present, but stable local alternatives to O-F and N-S chemistry are not consistently established at each leading score.
Credible geometry and specified stereochemistry for the spiro N/O ring and unsaturated annulated frameworks remain unestablished.
The highest-score fluorine deletion shows that further halogenation is not a universal missing capability; no exact absent target motif follows from the observed scores.

The seed-1 fluoro/bromo pyridyl variants tie exactly; that does not establish shared fingerprints. A 35-atom overgrown seed-2 relative scores 3.747882018472857e-08 and isolated O scores 0.0, so aromatic expansion or heteroatoms without the right context are insufficient. transferable_gaps.evidence: This gap originates in n-c55c3d520a2c through the reproduced n-62daf219c70a baseline and is re-observed in n-a56491c332aa on Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2 at 300 observations per task and ten-member batches. Accepted leaders and relatives contain O-F, O-Cl, N-F, N-S, N-nitroso, peroxide and unusual hydrogen-bearing sulfur environments. Direct accepted-parent joins show that such structures can be admitted and reused. Counterexamples include an ordinary biaryl cyclic amine, a halogen-free carboxamide whose fluorinated parent scores lower, a strong carbon-bound-only fluorinated dione, and a near-scoring aryl chloride alternative to O-Cl that still retains other liabilities. The chemistry is context-dependent, not uniformly reactive or uniformly conventional.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve conventional local bond environments within useful aromatic and polar frameworks.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Offer conventional local alternatives while preserving favorable functional relationships learned from real task-local feedback. Distinguish direct heteroatom-halogen bonds, carbon-bound halogens, N-O-C groups and peroxide links. Admission, reuse or a parent beat does not establish chemical desirability or guarantee a score benefit from filtering; these observations do not attribute the liability to uniform parent allocation.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The geometry gap is inherited from n-c55c3d520a2c via n-62daf219c70a and persists in the current matched panel as a four-membered N/O spiro ring, an unsaturated four-membered nitrogen ring, cross-linked aromatic-labelled fragments, nitrogen cages and larger lactone or N/S ring assemblies. High ring-digit incidence does not establish feasibility. Recognizable azetidine/biaryl amines and saturated fluorocyclobutyl groups are important counterexamples to a blanket claim that small rings are invalid. Some complex leaders beat their actual generating parents but remain below the matched Parent endpoint, separating local progress from benchmark outcome.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently pair representable rings with credible unsaturation geometry and feasible fused, spiro or bridged connectivity.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Assess ring size, bridge connectivity, unsaturation and molecular state in context while retaining access to ordinary small, fused and saturated rings. Explore feasible alternative connectivities preserving useful functional arrangements. Ring counts, aromatic labels and high raw scores cannot supply missing physical information; no general ring ban or causal mediation claim follows.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This identity gap was recorded for n-c55c3d520a2c, reproduced by n-62daf219c70a and remains in the current complete panel. Every task has stereocentre-string incidence 0.0 despite substituted azetidines, benzylic centres, spiro rings, fluorinated carbocycles and cages. Charge-string incidence is also 0.0, but available amines are present. These observations establish unspecified identity, not a measured penalty for any particular stereoisomer or protonation state.
transferable_gaps.gap: Potentially stereogenic saturated centres and ring junctions remain without explicit stereochemical identity in the output.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve or resolve stereochemistry when the generated constitution requires it, with exceptions for achiral or configurationally unstable cases. Treat protonation, alkene geometry and tautomerism separately. No objective-specific state prescription follows, and equal raw scores or fingerprint features do not certify complete molecular identity.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This gap is inherited from n-c55c3d520a2c through n-62daf219c70a and has fresh evaluated and accepted-lineage evidence under the current budget. Tiny fragments and some enlarged coupled structures score poorly, while compact combinations of aromatic, amine and carbonyl regions can score well. The two positive matched endpoint exceptions coexist with decreases elsewhere; direct parent-band exposure and strict parent beats do not track endpoint sign uniformly. Distinct evaluated seed families prevent a claim of global scaffold collapse. Immediate admission, next-batch membership and later reuse are separately recorded, and terminal children have no subsequent draw opportunity.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably preserve productive molecular context while controlling fragmentation, elaboration and dependence on close scaffold relatives.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Use accepted task-local evidence to preserve favorable relationships during simplification, growth and chemically independent scaffold replacement. Evaluate alternatives for both useful score and plausible chemistry without a fixed size rule. Keep active live-population choices separate from passive sampled bands, and distinguish accepted ancestry from unrealized counterfactuals. Broader parent participation or more descendants cannot by itself establish useful chemical coverage or a causal mediator of endpoint change.

nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from a bounded population of accepted, scored molecules. It samples breeding parents from high-score bands, recombines connected fragments, and applies ordinary graph mutations and continuation walks; direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled. Stable canonical admission creates a fresh surplus pool. A Gaussian process fitted to every earlier accepted score uses counts of local molecular environments and generalized Tanimoto similarity. It draws one correlated score function for each announced batch position and takes each masked maximum, without conditioning later draws on earlier selections. Only real accepted feedback updates its prediction archive and score-ranked breeding population.
approach.novelty: Add the previously tested mean-fantasy residual projection to this exchange-free Parent. After each choice, project later random residuals as if that pending molecule equaled its current predicted mean, keeping the means and fitted model unchanged. This is an exact transfer of an existing rule, not a new conditioning formula or a demonstrated improvement: its earlier trial under an exchange-containing Parent changed many batches but slightly lowered the final mean. Current siblings have removed residual correlation, optimized a shared sampled batch maximum, or reserved the last position for conditional variance. None tests this unchanged zero-innovation projection in the present composition. The experiment asks whether its changed later choices now help complete search outcomes; contraction, local parent wins and accepted reuse alone cannot answer that.

nodes.hypothesis: Add the exact archived mean-fantasy within-batch residual projection to the exchange-disabled Parent: condition future sampled residual rows on each earlier selected molecule taking its unchanged posterior mean, using the original jittered sampling covariance and zero innovations only for batch allocation.

finding_summary.headline: Projection changed batch choices, but endpoint score fell on all three seeds
finding_summary.insights: The result rules out nonactivation, missing accepted feedback or numerical fallback as explanations for the failed endpoint prediction. Lower average model correlation, selected-stream prediction error and seed dispersion were insufficient to improve search. The slightly larger count of parent wins partly accompanies weaker generating parents, so it does not establish higher absolute quality. Downstream opportunity also had limits: three newly selected nonterminal molecules had positive breeding support but were never drawn; four task/seed cohorts of new selections produced no positive direct-descendant incumbent increment, while terminal selections had no later opportunity. The earlier trial under an exchange-containing Parent was also adverse; this complete loss ends the registered fixed transfer without parameter rescue. The molecular assessment still finds chemically varied aromatic and heterocyclic outputs, alongside reactive halogen bonds, difficult ring geometry and unspecified stereochemistry. Those liabilities and inconsistent useful family coverage remain relevant gaps, but these data do not identify chemical mediation, an exchange interaction or the contribution of the retained graph-evolution foundation.
finding_summary.results: All 3,915 projections executed correctly and preserved every first choice. They changed 657 later positions and 295 of 435 batch sets, replacing 493 selected memberships. Later selected sampling variance fell by 3.28% on average. These choices entered real feedback: all 482 nonterminal newly selected molecules entered later fits, and 296 of the 493 new selections later bred. Yet the final mean fell from 0.595670 to 0.553927, a paired loss of 0.041742 against the required gain of 0.002. All three seed macros fell; six task/seed endpoints improved and nine declined. Strict parent wins rose from 629 to 642, while absolute offspring mean fell from 0.385256 to 0.359834 and total incumbent improvement fell from 5.807663 to 5.181529. The largest endpoint losses were deco_hop in seed 0 and sitagliptin_mpo in seed 2; median_2 improved in two seeds but fell in the third.
