molecular.headline: Ring-rich medicinal scaffolds, narrow leading families, uneven size and attachment chemistry, and no specified stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character: All five objectives have trajectories. The assessment reads every accepted record in the child and Parent n-c2ef5c1d5a78 trajectories, with initial molecules distinguished from optimizer proposals. Each child task contributes 870 accepted optimizer proposals. These are predominantly connected, branched, aromatic molecules carrying amides, sulfonamides, ethers, heteroaromatics and saturated nitrogen rings. The digest ring-closure rates range from 0.9805 to 0.9977 and aromatic-token presence rates from 0.946 to 0.9954; these are fractions of SMILES containing those features, not fractions of atoms or perceived ring counts. RDKit readings of the accepted trajectories give median heavy-atom counts of 24, 29, 27, 24 and 24 in the supplied task order, and 505, 439, 599, 732 and 774 distinct nonempty Murcko cores. This supports broad overall scaffold coverage alongside much narrower leading families. Most leading connections look chemically conventional, but tiny fragments, repeated bulky substructures, heavily decorated aromatics and unusual reactive groups make the full set less consistently credible than its best examples. Synthetic plausibility is therefore marked questionable for the complete output, not because the leading compounds are necessarily unmakeable. No synthesis routes or experimental properties were supplied. All digest stereocentre rates are 0.0; the full accepted strings contain neither tetrahedral nor double-bond stereochemical annotations. Some graphs nevertheless have potential stereocentres. The final excerpt is the last seed-2 proposals, not an aggregate incumbent list. Molecular associations below do not establish a hidden target structure, binding pose or mechanism activation.

per_task.generated_character: The leading molecules are moderately sized heteroaryl amides. The best, O=C(NCCc1ccccn1)c1cccc(Oc2cccnc2)c1, has 24 heavy atoms and three aromatic rings: a benzamide, pyridyl-ethyl substituent and pyridyl ether. A second family joins an azaindole carboxamide to N-acyl tetrahydroisoquinoline; COc1nccc2[nH]c(C(=O)N3CCc4ccccc4C3)cc12 exemplifies its fused aromatic rings and partially saturated ring. These contain meaningful donor/acceptor arrangements, not merely carbon-rich rings; the acylated ring nitrogen is an amide rather than a free basic amine. Amide formation and aryl-ether connectivity look synthetically ordinary. The full proposal set has median 24 heavy atoms and three rings. Compared with the Parent, seed 0 moves from an acetamido indole/benzylamide leader to an azaindole/cyclic-amide leader, seed 1 retains a heteroaryl-benzamide theme with different attachments, and seed 2 turns toward amidine-containing aryl compounds. Distinct nonempty cores decrease from 539 to 505.
liabilities: Repeated fused-ring amide fragments produce bulky, highly aromatic tails with very poor recorded scores.
The final amidine-rich examples alter ionization and donor character substantially; merely retaining nitrogen or an amide does not preserve the leading chemistry.
Stereo annotations remain absent where the wider trajectory introduces asymmetric carbon centres.
missing_features: Consistent preservation of the intermediate-size aromatic amide arrangement: lower-scoring proposals often retain isolated amidine or ring fragments, or repeat whole substructures, without the attachment pattern found in the leaders.

Reliable placement of aromatic nitrogen acceptors alongside the amide/ether connections is incompletely explored across families. The observed scores do not identify a unique absent target scaffold or justify prescribing one.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The leading heteroaryl benzamide scores 0.4861724348043977 and the azaindole cyclic amide 0.46525423631337554, versus 0.3051048083696145 for the initial trimethoxy indole anilide. This associates useful scores with a bounded aromatic/amide assembly and its nitrogen placement. Duplicating related indole/cyclic-amide fragments gives a 49-heavy-atom, eight-ring molecule scoring 1.4993141975019237e-30; the tiny [N-]=C=S fragment scores 5.670115669739515e-23. Size and attachment balance matter in both directions. The final seed-2 benzamidine alone scores 2.673918678015723e-09, while its brominated cyclic-amide derivative reaches 0.28620461684558623. Parent/child best observed scores are 0.43351949803907636/0.46525423631337554 in seed 0, 0.4767312946227961/0.4861724348043977 in seed 1, and 0.5/0.39970285249856186 in seed 2. The changed chemistry is heterogeneous across seeds.

per_task.generated_character: All twelve digest leaders are seed-2 nitropyrimidines bearing an arylamino arm and an aryloxy arm, with dense fluoro/chloro substitution; the best also carries an aryl nitrile. N#Cc1cc(F)c(F)cc1Nc1ncc([N+](=O)[O-])c(Oc2ccc(F)c(F)c2)n1 has 29 heavy atoms and three aromatic rings. These are relatively flat, highly decorated heteroaromatics with conventional aryl-N and aryl-O connections. Their nitro charge-separated notation should not be mistaken for evidence that the whole molecule is a salt or a protonated amine. Full trajectories also show bulky methoxy-rich polyaryl heterocycles in seed 0 and arylguanidine/benzodioxole families in seed 1. The child has median 29 heavy atoms and four rings, versus Parent medians of 33 heavy atoms and four rings; median aromatic-ring count changes from four to three. The Parent seed-2 leaders are decorated anilino/phenyl quinazolines rather than this nitropyrimidine series. Both sets look makeable in principle, with greater synthetic and physical-property uncertainty in the very large decorated tails.
liabilities: Nitroheteroarenes and densely halogenated aromatic surfaces recur throughout the leading series; their reactivity and physical-property consequences are not measured by these trajectories.
Several seed-0 outputs accumulate methoxy-substituted aryl rings, raising size, conformational and synthetic complexity without recovering the Parent leading score.
The digest charged rate of 0.2103 includes nitro resonance notation and is not a measure of useful ionizable centres.
missing_features: The high-scoring subset offers little core or connection diversity beyond a single nitropyrimidine/arylamino/aryloxy architecture. The wider search contains other cores but does not reproduce the Parent leading quinazoline arrangement at its recorded score.

Controlled ways to vary the relative positions and linkage chemistry of the aromatic arms remain underdeveloped compared with repeated halogen decoration or excessive polyaryl expansion. No unique unseen optimal core follows from these records.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best nitropyrimidine scores 0.6214761999075724; closely related halogen variants score 0.6212041367498847 and 0.620870265914585. Isolated trimethoxybenzene scores 0.5013149820285789, and a fluorodichlorobenzene scores 0.5017638239703678, so aromaticity and halogens alone do not reproduce the assembled heteroaryl architecture. The lowest digest example is a three-aryl vinyl nitrile/sulfone at 0.2797517851071064, showing that even similar ring abundance can accompany much lower score. The final expanded polyaryl nitropyrimidine scores 0.6052882830318782 rather than exceeding the compact leader. Parent/child seed-2 best observed scores are 0.6669492630755185/0.6214761999075724 with the changed core family. Distinct nonempty cores increase from 355 to 439, while each child seed has a lower recorded best than its Parent; broader core coverage alone therefore does not explain productive chemistry.

per_task.generated_character: The leading seed-0 series consists of aryl-substituted piperidines whose tertiary nitrogen carries an arylbutyl chain. Oc1cccc(C2CCN(CCCCc3ccc(F)cc3)CC2)c1 has 24 heavy atoms, two aromatic rings, one saturated piperidine and a phenol. Related leaders vary methoxy, methyl, vinyl, fluoro and linker amine groups; a pyrrolidine variant also appears. These are recognizable, plausibly synthesizable aromatic cyclic amines with flexible spacers. The full set has median 27 heavy atoms and four rings. Seed 1 instead reaches substituted quinoline/piperazine/piperidine assemblies, and seed 2 emphasizes quinoline/aryl ethers or thioethers linked to cyclic amines. Parent leaders also combine aromatic surfaces and exposed aliphatic amines, but use different arylpiperazine, fused-ring amine and aminoketone arrangements. Thus basic cyclic-amine chemistry is already a demonstrated capability, although it is not retained in every proposal.
liabilities: Several strong molecules combine substantial aromatic surface with long flexible alkyl linkers or extra amines; the supplied scores do not establish solubility, selectivity or the preferred protonation state.
Neutral SMILES notation conceals the distinction between potentially protonatable tertiary amines and nonbasic amide/sulfonamide nitrogens if judged only by token counts.
The wider trajectory includes asymmetric saturated-ring substitutions without specified stereochemistry.
missing_features: Low-scoring proposals often lack the exposed aliphatic amine and appropriate aromatic-linker arrangement seen in the leaders, despite retaining a nitrogen-containing ring. The generator has this chemistry but does not preserve its functional role reliably.
No missing pharmacophore can be inferred for the near-ceiling leaders. Conformationally constrained or stereochemically specified alternatives are not established as rewarded by the supplied scores.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The phenol, methoxy and methyl arylpiperidines score 0.9999999627983533, 0.9999999476834859 and 0.999999917451054: all are effectively at the observed upper end, so these differences do not establish a meaningful substituent preference. By contrast, the amide/thiadiazole/sulfonyl-piperidine example scores 1.9828327575562915e-05 and the N-acyl piperidine carboxamide 2.6715842904959654e-05. These low examples still have rings and nitrogen, but the cyclic nitrogen is acylated or sulfonylated rather than an exposed aliphatic amine. The dominant visible gradient concerns nitrogen function and its connection to aromatic groups, not the mere presence of nitrogen or rings. The child seed-2 best is 0.9901614972653325 versus the Parent 0.9999991526291698, while the leading seed-0 family remains near the score ceiling. These are score/structure associations, not evidence of a docking pose or experimental activity.

per_task.generated_character: This output combines aromatic sulfonyl groups with piperazines and fused heteroaromatics. The leader, Cc1cc(S(=O)(=O)N2CCN(S(=O)(=O)c3ccc4c(c3)OCO4)CC2)c2ccccc2n1, has 32 heavy atoms and five rings: a quinoline, piperazine and benzodioxole system. Both piperazine nitrogens are sulfonylated, so this leader should not be described as carrying two free basic amines. Other leaders use N-methyl or N-aryl piperazines, aryl sulfonamides and benzodioxole-containing side chains. The full set has median 24 heavy atoms and three rings, with 732 nonempty Murcko cores; chemically diverse exploration coexists with only a few strong combinations. These sulfonamide and cyclic-amine connections generally look synthetically plausible, although the multiply decorated and unusual heterocyclic variants are less straightforward. All accepted molecular identities, scores and evaluation positions in each seed match the Parent trajectories exactly.
liabilities: Extra sulfonyl-piperazine branches add size, acceptors and synthetic steps without a corresponding increase over the leading combination.
Nitrogen counts obscure markedly different amine and sulfonamide functions; the strongest bis-sulfonyl example has both piperazine nitrogens deactivated as bases.
The low-scoring tail includes reactive azide or unusual N-O/chlorinated functionality and highly flexible acyclic material.
missing_features: Consistent assembly of complementary aromatic and sulfonyl-piperazine fragments is missing from most proposals even though the fragments themselves are available; the strongest combination is not reproduced by simply adding more of them.

A compact range of alternative linkages and attachment positions around those combined motifs is incompletely represented among the leaders. The modest scores do not reveal a uniquely missing reference scaffold.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The bis-sulfonyl piperazine connecting quinoline and benzodioxole scores 0.2588686674995393. Its smaller quinoline-sulfonyl N-methylpiperazine relative scores 0.2272296156064184. A larger, 41-heavy-atom example with an extra sulfonyl-piperazine branch scores 0.2301209791058402, so further motif multiplication is not uniformly rewarded. The initial aromatic heterocycles already provide modest scores, whereas the acyclic allyl azide scores 0.0 and the trichloromethyl N-hydroxyformamide 0.007693218186208301. The observed gradient favors specific combinations of cyclic/aromatic fragments and sulfonyl connections over small acyclic fragments; it does not establish that free basic nitrogen is universally required. The unchanged Parent trajectories show the same chemical coverage and limitations.

per_task.generated_character: The leaders span several families rather than a single close series. The best, CCCCNCC(=O)NS(=O)(=O)c1cc(C(F)(F)F)ccc1F, is a 23-heavy-atom, single-aryl N-butylamino acylsulfonamide with fluoro and trifluoromethyl groups. Another strong single-aryl compound combines an amide with an oxalamide side chain and an unspecified asymmetric carbon. Other leaders include arylsulfonyl imidazolines with ester or imidate substituents, a guanidino saturated-ring compound, a quinolone/acylthiourea and a sulfonyl lactam. The full set has median 24 heavy atoms and three rings, and 774 nonempty Murcko cores. Ordinary amide/sulfonamide/ester connections make many leaders look synthetically plausible; imines, hydrazones, unusual ring junctions and unspecified stereochemistry complicate others. All accepted molecular identities, scores and evaluation positions match the Parent for every seed.
liabilities: Acylsulfonamide, guanidine, imidazoline, hydrazone and acylthiourea alternatives have different ionization and tautomeric behavior, which the observed scores do not disentangle.
Peptide-like, long-chain lipid-like and bulky polyaryl tails carry substantial flexibility or size and include the weakest observed scores.
Late proposals can lose the chemistry of earlier strong examples rather than remaining close useful analogues.
missing_features: Reliable retention of the moderate-size polar/aromatic balance found in the leaders is missing from much of the output; long lipids, peptides and multiply decorated aromatics explore very different compositions with little recorded reward.

The high-scoring amide-oxalamide graph contains an unspecified stereocentre, and none of the proposal strings encode tetrahedral stereochemistry. This is missing stereochemical coverage, although the trajectories cannot establish that assigning an isomer would improve this objective.
A common unseen target scaffold cannot be inferred from these heterogeneous leaders; prescribing one from the task name would go beyond the supplied molecular evidence.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The amino acylsulfonamide scores 0.32609684308650033 and the fluoro/trifluoromethyl aryl amide-oxalamide 0.3085499097640706. Within the imidazoline family, the fluorophenyl methyl-ester compound scores 0.3034617343186778 versus 0.24905607529893223 for its nonfluorinated phenyl counterpart. This is evidence for a local substitution association, not a universal halogen requirement: other strong families lack that arrangement. Large polyaryl, lipid-like and peptide-like examples score 0.0; the cited peptide has 61 heavy atoms and many flexible connections. Balanced size and connection of polar groups are more consistent with the leaders than indiscriminate growth. The digest displays a median score of 0.0, which is a rounded summary rather than proof that half the exact scores equal zero. Every molecule in the final seed-2 excerpt is below 0.001 despite earlier stronger examples. Broad coverage has not produced consistent proposals retaining the useful combinations.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A leading aromatic amide has 24 heavy atoms and score 0.4861724348043977, whereas duplication of related indole/cyclic-amide fragments produces a 49-heavy-atom, eight-ring example at 1.4993141975019237e-30. In another panel a 23-heavy-atom amino acylsulfonamide scores 0.32609684308650033 while the cited 40-heavy-atom lipid-like and 61-heavy-atom peptide-like outputs score 0.0. Tiny fragments also fail, so neither universal shrinking nor adding ring fragments is supported.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve useful molecular size and attachment balance while varying a scaffold.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator needs ways to change connections and substituents while retaining an objective-local, feedback-supported range of size and functional-group composition. Repeated whole-fragment growth and severe truncation should be distinguishable from coherent local chemical variation; no fixed task-specific size or scaffold rule follows from these examples.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Near-ceiling aromatic cyclic-amine leaders contain exposed tertiary nitrogen, while ring nitrogens tied into amides or sulfonamides occur in very low-scoring molecules of comparable ring abundance. Conversely, a leading bis-sulfonyl piperazine scores 0.2588686674995393 with both piperazine nitrogens sulfonylated. The nitro-rich leading series also contributes formal charge tokens without establishing a net ionic or basic centre.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably distinguish the chemical function of a heteroatom from merely retaining its element or ring.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve and vary amine, amide, sulfonamide, aromatic-nitrogen and charge-separated functional contexts explicitly enough that local feedback can distinguish them. The needed capability is context-sensitive chemical variation, not a universal requirement to add basic nitrogen, charge or more heteroatoms.

transferable_gaps.evidence: One panel contains 439 distinct nonempty Murcko cores, yet all twelve digest leaders share a nitropyrimidine with arylamino and aryloxy arms. Another has 599 cores but its digest leaders concentrate on closely related aromatic cyclic amines. The nitropyrimidine panel has more observed cores than the Parent while every seed has a lower recorded best. Positional and halogen variants are plentiful; coherent high-scoring changes of the core or its attachments are less evident.
transferable_gaps.gap: Broad overall scaffold coverage does not translate into broad productive alternatives around the strongest molecular families.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The generator needs to maintain plausible alternatives for ring topology and attachment geometry around feedback-supported families, in addition to peripheral substitutions and distant low-scoring structures. Such variation must be learned from the current objective-local observations without hidden task identity or a prescribed benchmark scaffold.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every digest stereocentre rate is 0.0 and the full child proposal strings contain no tetrahedral or directional double-bond annotations. The aryl amide-oxalamide scoring 0.3085499097640706 has an unassigned tetrahedral centre; asymmetric saturated-ring and peptide-like proposals provide further examples. This is absent specification, not proof that the graphs are achiral.
transferable_gaps.gap: The accepted output does not encode stereochemical alternatives even when the molecular graph contains asymmetric centres.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator would need to represent and retain explicit stereochemical choices when generating asymmetric graphs, so accepted feedback could distinguish those choices where the oracle is sensitive. The supplied evidence establishes the coverage gap but does not establish a score benefit from any particular stereoisomer.

nodes.method_name: Augmented Hill-Climb with a corpus-trained SMILES policy
nodes.method_thesis: Train a compact autoregressive SMILES prior solely on the supplied unlabeled corpus, then initialize a fresh policy from that prior for each objective. Use the initial observations and each subsequent scored batch to update only its highest-reward sequences with the Augmented Hill-Climb loss: fit policy log likelihood to frozen-prior log likelihood plus scaled observed reward. Sample complete molecules token by token from the updated policy, canonicalize them, and refill invalid or duplicate proposals by further generation. The corpus supplies language training, never a ranked molecular pool. Elite-conditioned policy updates should shift generation toward new high-scoring molecular combinations quickly enough to improve the benchmark's mean final Top-1. This is a small-budget transfer hypothesis, not a claim that published larger-budget gains carry over. The root uses the current scored batch; randomized historical replay is reserved for the first improvement. The anchor's elite augmented-likelihood mechanism is described by [Thomas et al.](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13321-022-00646-z).

Fresh independent objective policy and persistent Adam initialization from the verified frozen prior
Current scored-batch top-half elite selection with original accepted strings and frozen-prior log likelihood plus sixty times accepted reward
Individual zero-ceiling projection retained for current elites, with exact preservation of nonpositive targets
Historical-only removal of the individual ceiling, restoring raw historical targets without changing current targets or selected membership
Task-local canonical top-32 accepted-elite memory with original-sequence replay and fixed current/history loss shares
Descending accepted-score/canonical historical selection and inherited passive uniform membership draw
Once-per-executed-update identity fitting counts and inverse-one-plus-count weighting within history, including exact equal-count mean-loss controls

approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds molecular graphs by connected-fragment crossover and ordinary mutation from a bounded high-scoring population; direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled. It retains every accepted score in a task-local archive and fits a Gaussian process using radius-two, chirality-aware Morgan environment counts folded into 2,048 coordinates. Generalized count-Tanimoto similarity supplies the training and joint pool covariance. Fixed noise and archive score normalization define the fitted posterior. Each batch selects available maxima from correlated posterior function draws over a larger pool of fresh valid unique offspring. Accepted feedback updates the archive and score-greedy survivors.
approach.novelty: Remove only the final folding of environment identifiers into 2,048 bins. Keep the same local environments and their occurrence counts, but align them by the native environment hash identifiers when calculating the same count-Tanimoto kernel. This separates distinct identifiers that previously shared a modulo bin and can change similarity weights, posterior means and covariance, then the identities selected by the existing allocator. Unlike the count-removal sibling, multiplicity remains; unlike the failed residual-scaling variant, allocation amplitude is unchanged. This does not make fingerprints unique: finite native hashes and identical local-environment multisets still alias. The current audit exposes kernel and choice changes without establishing endpoint benefit.

nodes.hypothesis: Replace fixed-width folded Morgan count coordinates with occurrence counts keyed by the corresponding native unfolded environment hash identifiers, using the same generalized count-Tanimoto covariance so distinct modulo-bin aliases no longer mix in posterior similarities.

finding_summary.headline: Unfolding changes covariance and selection but lowers every seed’s macro score
finding_summary.insights: The experiment rules out insufficient representation or allocation exposure as an explanation for the missing gain. Removing folding changes ordinary similarity relationships and adaptive choices, but it does not reliably help the retained optimizer. On the same Child selected molecules, prediction MSE improves only slightly, from 0.007847 to 0.007808, and interval coverage rises from 75.36% to 75.82%; those diagnostics do not rescue the endpoint result. All three median_2 streams worsen in prediction MSE while improving at the endpoint, further limiting a simple prediction-to-search explanation. Exact native-count ties remain, as do finite-hash and local-environment limits. The molecular output retains useful aromatic, amine, urea and carbonyl organization alongside reactive bonds, crowded rings and unspecified stereochemistry; neither the losses nor the median_2 gains establish a universal size or chemical-feasibility rule. This is a negative result for the incremental unfolding variant on this composition, not a reversal of the earlier evidence for retaining occurrence counts. Changed means and covariance, adaptive graph paths and possible lost accidental regularization remain unresolved mediators.
finding_summary.results: Native counts preserve multiplicity and remove modulo-bin mixing on 41,278 of 69,600 pool occurrences. All 435 pool kernels change against their folded controls, changing 392 selected sets while 43 sets remain identical. Nine distinct-molecule pairs still share native count vectors. Every active fit and choice reconstructs, and every evaluation completes. Mean endpoint score falls from 0.595670 to 0.547507, a decrease of 0.048163 rather than the required 0.002 increase. Seed macro changes are -0.077453, -0.013541 and -0.053495. Six task-seed endpoints improve and nine decline; all three median_2 endpoints improve. Macro dispersion drops from 0.026593 to 0.000322 around the lower mean.

nodes.finding:
Native counts preserve multiplicity and remove modulo-bin mixing on 41,278 of 69,600 pool occurrences. All 435 pool kernels change against their folded controls, changing 392 selected sets while 43 sets remain identical. Nine distinct-molecule pairs still share native count vectors. Every active fit and choice reconstructs, and every evaluation completes. Mean endpoint score falls from 0.595670 to 0.547507, a decrease of 0.048163 rather than the required 0.002 increase. Seed macro changes are -0.077453, -0.013541 and -0.053495. Six task-seed endpoints improve and nine decline; all three median_2 endpoints improve. Macro dispersion drops from 0.026593 to 0.000322 around the lower mean.

The experiment rules out insufficient representation or allocation exposure as an explanation for the missing gain. Removing folding changes ordinary similarity relationships and adaptive choices, but it does not reliably help the retained optimizer. On the same Child selected molecules, prediction MSE improves only slightly, from 0.007847 to 0.007808, and interval coverage rises from 75.36% to 75.82%; those diagnostics do not rescue the endpoint result. All three median_2 streams worsen in prediction MSE while improving at the endpoint, further limiting a simple prediction-to-search explanation. Exact native-count ties remain, as do finite-hash and local-environment limits. The molecular output retains useful aromatic, amine, urea and carbonyl organization alongside reactive bonds, crowded rings and unspecified stereochemistry; neither the losses nor the median_2 gains establish a universal size or chemical-feasibility rule. This is a negative result for the incremental unfolding variant on this composition, not a reversal of the earlier evidence for retaining occurrence counts. Changed means and covariance, adaptive graph paths and possible lost accidental regularization remain unresolved mediators.

molecular.headline: Aryl ureas, nitrogen/carbonyl rings and sulfur-rich amines coexist with oversized heterocycles, acyl halides and uncertain geometry
molecular.overall_character: All fifteen Child trajectories and fifteen published Parent trajectories named by the immutable brief were read: 4,500 observations per node, including 4,350 optimizer proposals per node. All five tasks and Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2 are covered; no listed path is missing. The brief reports complete, profile-matched pairing to n-62daf219c70a at 300 observations per task and ten-member batches under the Research in Depth profile. The generated chemistry includes compact halogen-free aryl ureas, N-amino indole-like carbonyl systems, small unsaturated carbocycles, repeated azaheterocyclic carbonyl assemblies, imine-rich azaarenes, aryl amines carrying unusual sulfur environments, biphenyl or quinoline-linked nitrogen/dicarbonyl rings, and fluorinated imino/carbonyl heterocycles. Molecular size and chemical character vary markedly across seeds. Rings and aromatic-labelled atoms are abundant: proposal ring-digit incidence ranges from 0.9621 to 0.9862 and aromatic-string incidence from 0.9586 to 0.9816. Those are string-level readings, not demonstrations of stable aromaticity, feasible conformations or independent scaffold coverage. Structural diversity is moderate across the panel, with recurring leading series within seeds; the familiar urea, amide, lactam and amine groups rule out an absence of medicinal chemistry, while reactive acyl halides, unusual sulfur bonding and crowded ring topology make overall plausibility questionable and drug-likeness weak. Every task has stereocentre-string and charge-string incidence 0.0. Basic amines nevertheless occur, and potentially stereogenic ring centres remain unspecified. Sizes below are heavy-atom-token counts from the supplied SMILES. Only evaluated output is assessed: these trajectories cannot establish unselected-pool exposure or the chemical alternatives a pool contained. The stated folded-bin alias-removal intervention is distinct from native-hash or count-vector equivalence; native Morgan identifiers or equal count vectors do not certify molecular identity, and this report does not measure those equivalences. Equal scores likewise do not identify shared fingerprints. Chemical and paired-score associations below do not establish component activation or attribution. The reproducible read-only audit records all trajectory hashes, row counts and digest-extrema checks.

per_task.generated_character: The three seed leaders contain 24, 23 and 25 heavy-atom tokens. Seed 0 produces an N-amino indole-like bicyclic arene with methoxy, vinyl, chloromethyl and benzoyl substituents. Seed 1 instead reaches a halogen-free bridged aryl/unsaturated nitrogen ring bearing a methoxy group and an N-pyridyl urea. A tied 23-atom relative moves the oxygen into the ring connectivity. These leaders use recognizable carbonyl/urea chemistry, although their bridge geometry is not established. Seed 2 uses a benzene-fused four-membered unsaturated carbocycle carrying an anilide, methoxy and methylamino groups, plus a ketenimine side chain. Thus aromatic and polar functionality is present, but some connectivity is much less conventional than the initial indole carboxanilide. Mean proposal SMILES length is 41.1, halogen-string incidence 0.6701 and cumulated-double-bond incidence 0.0333. The high-scoring halogen-free seed-1 series is a substantive counterexample to universal halogen dependence.
liabilities: N-amino aromatic nitrogens, chloromethyl substituents and occasional N-F amides introduce context-specific reactivity concerns.
The benzene-fused four-membered unsaturated ring and ketenimine side chain raise geometric and stability concerns; their presence is not justified by SMILES validity alone.
The recognizable urea functionality does not by itself establish the feasibility or stereochemistry of its bridged core.
missing_features: The favorable aryl/polar organization is present, but consistently accessible alternatives to the bridged and small unsaturated ring connectivities are not established at the leading scores.
Specified stereochemical identity is missing in the saturated bridge environment, and the ketenimine-containing series lacks demonstrated geometric and stability characterization.

Local bond environments are not controlled consistently: the scored nonfluorinated amide counterpart and halogen-free urea show that direct N-halogen chemistry is not necessary throughout this output.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial indole carboxanilide scores 0.3051048083696145; the three seed leaders score 0.4254027310763201, 0.46746448265590934 and 0.40826532672592236. Isolated Br scores 0.0. Useful scores associate with retained aromatic/carbonyl organization, not halogen presence alone. Local comparisons are conditional: removing an amide N-F bond changes 0.4038761425223417 to 0.40650757542526167. In one seed-2 series, anilide-to-aryl-thioester replacement lowers 0.40196779766986834 to 0.3250152096349864; in a related N-amino-substituted series, the corresponding replacement raises 0.3900685872822928 to 0.40497388700123543. Neither amide nor thioester is universally favored. The two different seed-1 oxygen placements both score 0.46746448265590934, which does not establish fingerprint equivalence. Matched Parent endpoints are 0.39405142067435733, 0.47411701813450596 and 0.438972502037081. Seed 0 improves while seeds 1 and 2 decrease; the Child's compact halogen-free urea remains a chemical counterexample to treating all strong output as reactive halogen chemistry. No exact absent target motif is identifiable from these observations.

per_task.generated_character: The three seed leaders contain 44, 63 and 34 heavy-atom tokens. Seed 0 joins two carbonyl-rich nitrogen rings through an N-N bond and carries exocyclic unsaturation, an azaaromatic fragment, an aldehyde-containing side chain, and both an acyl chloride and an acyl fluoride. A tied relative replaces the acyl chloride with an acyl bromide. These are reactive acyl halides, not ordinary carbon-bound aryl halogens. Seed 1 is a large repeated azaheterocyclic carbonyl/oxygen-ring assembly with carbonate esters, allyloxy substitution, a nitrile-containing cumulated chain and a small fused oxygen-containing ring. Seed 2 instead links multiple azaarenes through imine/amidine-like segments and includes an N-chlorinated imino terminus with carbon-bound chlorine. Mean proposal SMILES length is 81.5, aromatic-string incidence 0.9690 and ring-digit incidence 0.9690. The set is ring-rich and often substantially elaborated; stable, compact heteroaromatic chemistry is not the dominant appearance of these particular leaders.
liabilities: Acyl chloride, bromide and fluoride groups, N-N connectivity, conjugated aldehyde-containing chains and N-chlorinated imines create substantial stability and handling questions.
Large repeated heterocyclic units and multiple ester/carbonate or imine linkages increase structural and synthetic complexity without a uniform score advantage.
Cumulated unsaturation and small fused rings require geometric assessment; lowercase aromatic notation does not resolve it.
missing_features: The output does not demonstrate consistently stable replacements for acyl halides, N-chlorinated imines and other reactive decorations while preserving the favorable heteroaromatic organization.
Compact, chemically independent alternatives to repeated heterocyclic assemblies remain limited among the evaluated leading series; this is not a statement about unselected pools.
Feasible geometry and defined stereochemical or imine configurations are not demonstrated for the fused and highly unsaturated assemblies.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted fused dione scores 0.548381482770623. An early peroxide-substituted quinoline scores 0.5100965759438103, while isolated Br scores the observed floor of 0.5. The three leaders reach 0.6235001463271876, 0.6170880178893099 and 0.6205348735011614. In the seed-0 leader, acyl chloride-to-bromide substitution leaves 0.6235001463271876 unchanged; this does not establish molecular or fingerprint equivalence and supplies no evidence that either reactive group is synthetically desirable. A ring-opened 44-atom final relative scores 0.5832761524546192, so atom count alone does not preserve reward. The seed-2 50-atom elaborated relative scores 0.619688253850436, below its 34-atom leader. Parent endpoints are 0.8561477222467935, 0.6248206599713055 and 0.6178024026512013, with 30-, 32- and 37-atom leaders. The Child loses in seeds 0 and 1 despite substantial enlargement; seed 2 improves with a smaller leader in a different imine-rich family. The Parent's stronger seed-0 thione/O-F/halomethyl family also had liabilities, so lower Child score cannot be read as either improved or worsened makeability in isolation.

per_task.generated_character: The three seed leaders contain 31, 27 and 30 heavy-atom tokens. Seed 0 links a halophenol/imine region through an aminoalkyl chain to an unusual ring-bound sulfur centre with S=O, S=C and S-N connections, and also carries a chloroalkyl side chain. Seed 1 has two substituted aryl regions, a saturated cyclic diamine, phenol/methoxy groups and a sulfur centre double-bonded to an exocyclic methylene while also attached to aryl carbon and nitrogen. These sulfur environments are not ordinary sulfonamides. Seed 2 joins a chloropyrrole and a small saturated nitrogen ring to a tertiary amine and fluorinated, chlorinated tetralin-like region; its ring nitrogen bears a terminal sulfur group written N[SH]=O. A close leading family uses bridged cyclic sulfur-oxide connectivity instead. Available aliphatic amines are clearly present throughout these leaders. Mean proposal SMILES length is 60.9 and halogen-string incidence 0.9897. Aryl amine organization is recognizable, but unusual sulfur bonding and connected ring geometry weaken confidence in ordinary medicinal-chemistry plausibility.
liabilities: S=C/S=O/S-N combinations and terminal hydrogen-bearing sulfur-oxide groups require environment-specific valence and stability scrutiny.
Small nitrogen rings, multiply connected sulfur-containing rings and unspecified saturated stereocentres raise synthesis and geometry questions.
Chloroalkyl groups, aryl halides and sizable aromatic surfaces coexist, but the trajectory scores do not characterize stability, solubility or selectivity.
missing_features: Conventional bond environments are not consistently maintained around sulfur while successful aryl/amine relationships are explored; strong sulfur-free relatives show that sulfur is not an indispensable universal component.
Explicit stereochemistry and conformational identity are absent for substituted tetralin-like centres, saturated nitrogen rings and bridged junctions.
The neutral SMILES do not resolve protonation states, although potentially basic centres are abundant; the records do not justify simply adding another amine.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: An N-sulfonyl cyclic amine scores 0.00021169315013374197; an early amide/carboxylate/sulfonamide assembly scores 0.0006269216484658979. The three seed leaders reach 0.9410969690840454, 0.9209804791284083 and 0.9766949967449473. Available aliphatic amines together with aromatic regions associate with higher scores, but this is not a nitrogen-count or sulfur requirement: a sulfur-free seed-0 aryl/amine assembly scores only 0.24375714718505176, whereas sulfur-free seed-2 carbonyl and hydroxylamine-substituted bridged variants score 0.9487092468687838 and 0.96818782227592. Their differing structures preclude attributing the values to sulfur removal alone. The sulfur-oxide bridged relative scores 0.9723252692687101. All three matched Parent endpoints are higher, at 0.9999989177995104, 0.9969753164881906 and 0.9999934235240012, in flexible or cyclic aryl-amine families; the Parent includes high-scoring ordinary sulfur-free amines. The observed gradient therefore supports functional-group presentation in context, not a need for unusual sulfur valence. These oracle values do not establish binding selectivity or physical accessibility.

per_task.generated_character: All three seed leaders contain 33 heavy-atom tokens. Seed 0 attaches an ethoxy/methyl biphenyl to a bridged nitrogen/dicarbonyl system with an enolic hydroxyl and an N-N ring closure. Seed 1 uses a propyl/ethoxy biphenyl attached to a partially unsaturated fused nitrogen/dicarbonyl ring system containing N-methyl lactam groups and a saturated amine. This seed-1 family is a comparatively recognizable combination of ordinary aryl, amide and amine chemistry. Seed 2 combines a propylquinoline, a pyrrole and an aminomethyl-linked bridged dicarbonyl/tertiary-amine ring. The Parent leaders contain 34, 32 and 29 atoms, so Child size change is not uniform. Proposal aromatic-string incidence is 0.9816, ring-digit incidence 0.9862 and mean SMILES length 56.4; halogen-string incidence is only 0.1184. These families supply a useful counterexample to the heavily halogenated output elsewhere. Geometry and stereochemical definition remain concerns, but not every leading ring system is equally exotic.
liabilities: The seed-0 N-N ring closure and enolic representation require local stability and tautomer assessment.
Bridged and partially unsaturated nitrogen/carbonyl rings can be synthetically demanding; higher score does not validate their routes or conformations.
Strong scores occur without substantial halogen decoration, so halogenation is not a general missing capability in these families.
missing_features: Stereochemical and conformational identity of the saturated bridges and ring junctions remains unresolved.

The favored aromatic/nitrogen/carbonyl organization is present, but consistent access to simpler feasible connectivities at the same leading scores is not established; the near-leading contracted ring is a useful partial counterexample.
Independent plausible evaluated alternatives within each leading family are limited, although the different biphenyl and quinoline/pyrrole families prevent a claim of global scaffold collapse.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted fused dione scores 0.1678386594791329. A 15-atom nitrogen/dicarbonyl ring lacking the larger aromatic region scores 0.08411963849598328; the final 21-atom quinoline/pyrrole product lacking the leader's nitrogen/carbonyl appendage scores 0.16922282244532988. A 56-atom duplicated heterocyclic assembly scores 0.11780871699819487 and ethene scores 0.0. Together these examples associate useful reward with combined aromatic and polar-ring context rather than simple growth, fragmentation or either region alone. The three leaders reach 0.23115033995213558, 0.24300288424853 and 0.22923668265172575, each above the matched Parent endpoint of 0.2258403994203931, 0.2214095461892601 and 0.22600312875247064. This all-seed gain must be preserved despite chemical concerns elsewhere. Deleting a ring nitrogen and contracting the seed-1 leader's ring gives a 32-atom relative scoring 0.24150836237182322, showing that the precise larger nitrogen ring is not uniquely necessary for a similar score. The record does not reveal a single missing target motif or a universal requirement for further ring elaboration.

per_task.generated_character: The three seed leaders contain 28, 27 and 25 heavy-atom tokens. Seed 0 has a fused imino/carbonyl nitrogen heterocycle carrying N-methyl and N-F groups, a fluoroethyl substituent and a fluorinated aryl fluoromethyl ester. That ester contains O-C-F connectivity, not an O-F bond. Seed 1 uses a large aromatic-labelled nitrogen/dicarbonyl ring bearing N-F, an enolic fluorinated cyclopentadiene and a fluorinated cyclohexadiene substituent. Its aromatic notation does not establish a stable planar aromatic ring. Seed 2 makes a multiply connected aryl/nitrogen heterocycle with two imino groups, a saturated fluorinated ring centre and an aryl acyl fluoride; the latter is C(=O)F, chemically distinct from fluoroalkyl substitution. Mean proposal SMILES length is 49.3. Aromatic-string and ring-digit incidences are 0.9586 and 0.9621, while cumulated-double-bond incidence is only 0.0011. The current leaders do not require the small cyclic cumulene seen in the Parent seed-2 leader, but other geometric and bond-environment liabilities remain.
liabilities: Direct N-F bonds and acyl fluoride functionality create different stability concerns; carbon-bound fluorine and O-C-F ester connectivity must not be conflated with them.
Large aromatic-labelled nitrogen rings, crowded fused/bridged connectivity and fluorinated enolic carbocycles require physical geometry and tautomer assessment.
More elaborate duplicated heterocycles can lose useful molecular context, while absence of a cyclic cumulene does not establish that a replacement topology is feasible.
missing_features: Stable bond environments and credible ring geometry are not consistently combined with the favorable compact fluorinated/polar organization.
Explicit saturated-centre and alkene stereochemistry, together with established enol/imino tautomeric identity, is missing from the cited representations.

The evaluated series do not establish stable local replacements for acyl fluoride or N-F at their exact leading scores; near-leading N-F-free chemistry and opposite local score responses require context-sensitive interpretation.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted fused dione scores 0.0020944534688323298; a 48-atom highly connected duplicated heterocycle scores 1.3307726692355508e-17 and isolated F scores 1.1043196211273875e-26. The three leaders reach 0.5186463461539925, 0.4880863339901072 and 0.5014496282827379. Reward associates with compact fluorinated/polar organization, not fluorine count or heterocycle multiplication alone. Moving one fluorine between the aryl and fused-ring regions in the seed-0 leading family changes 0.5186463461539925 to 0.5011774408284522. In other close seed-0 comparisons, an N-F-to-N-methyl change lowers 0.46148604570485713 to 0.3534091128637756, and replacing fluoromethyl ester with methyl ester lowers 0.4326345826918735 to 0.30121868572054644. These local counterexamples limit any claim that removing a reactive or fluorinated group always helps. Conversely, a differently connected seed-1 relative without direct N-F scores 0.4836905232399345, close to its seed leader; it is not an isolated N-F comparison. Parent endpoints are 0.6510211907030741, 0.4870057305679067 and 0.7208853668418119. The small seed-1 gain coexists with decreases in seeds 0 and 2, whose Parent families also had unresolved geometry or N-F liabilities. No exact absent pharmacophore can be inferred from these records.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This gap originates in the n-c55c3d520a2c assessment reproduced by n-62daf219c70a and is newly observed in n-b14daceabbeb on Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2 at 300 observations per task and batches of ten. Current leading families include acyl halides, direct N-F, N-chlorinated imines and unusual S=C/S=O/S-N environments. Counterexamples are essential: a halogen-free urea scores 0.46746448265590934; removal of amide N-F changes 0.4038761425223417 to 0.40650757542526167; and a sulfur-free bridged amine scores 0.96818782227592. In another context N-F-to-N-methyl replacement lowers 0.46148604570485713 to 0.3534091128637756. These are conditional chemical associations, not uniform substitution rules or attribution to the covariance change.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve conventional local bond environments within otherwise useful aromatic and polar frameworks.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Offer conventional local alternatives that preserve favorable functional-group organization learned from accepted task-local feedback, distinguishing acyl halides, heteroatom-bound halogens and ordinary carbon-bound halogens. Treat sulfur by its full bond environment. The missing capability is reliable chemical context control, not a universal element ban or proof that a plausibility filter raises objective scores.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The geometry gap is inherited from n-c55c3d520a2c through n-62daf219c70a and recurs in this complete matched panel as benzene-fused small unsaturated rings, crowded aryl bridges, large aromatic-labelled nitrogen rings and imine-rich or cumulated side chains. High ring-digit and aromatic-string incidence do not establish stable conformations. The current leaders need not reproduce the Parent's cyclic-cumulene motif, and comparatively conventional urea and fused amide/amine families also score well. All three aromatic/nitrogen/dicarbonyl families improve over their matched Parent endpoints, so elaboration or ring formation is not uniformly score-worsening.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not reliably combine representable ring connectivity with demonstrably credible geometry and unsaturation patterns.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring transformations need attention to ring size, bridge connections, unsaturation and geometric compatibility, while maintaining access to ordinary fused and saturated ring chemistry. Assess feasible alternative connectivities using task-local feedback. Neither string validity nor a high score resolves this limitation, and the evidence does not support banning ring formation or assigning the issue to folded versus native hash representation.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This identity gap was recorded for n-c55c3d520a2c and reproduced by n-62daf219c70a; it persists in the current supplied three-seed panel. Every task's stereocentre-string incidence is 0.0, despite bridged urea cores, substituted nitrogen rings and fluorinated saturated centres in the cited leaders. Charge-string incidence is also 0.0, but available amines are present. The data establish unspecified identity, not a measured stereochemical or protonation-related score penalty.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator leaves potentially stereogenic saturated centres and ring junctions without specified stereochemical identity.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve or explicitly resolve stereochemistry where generated constitution requires it, with appropriate exceptions for achiral and configurationally unstable structures. Treat protonation, alkene geometry and tautomer identity separately. No particular stereoisomer, charge state or objective-specific structure is justified by these scores, and the chemical gap is not evidence of native-hash uniqueness or equivalence.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This gap is inherited from n-c55c3d520a2c via n-62daf219c70a and has new evaluated-output evidence in the current matched panel. Tiny late hydrocarbon/halogen products reach observed floors; some large duplicated heterocycles score far below compact leading frameworks. One 63-atom repeated heterocyclic leader remains below its 32-atom matched Parent leader, while a 34-atom alternative exceeds its 37-atom Parent. Counterexamples prevent a size rule: the three nitrogen/dicarbonyl leaders all contain 33 atoms and all improve despite Parent sizes of 34, 32 and 29; a contracted 32-atom relative remains close to its 33-atom leader. Different seed families show actual evaluated variation, but not the contents or exposure of unselected pools.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently retain productive functional-group context while avoiding unhelpful fragmentation or repeated scaffold expansion.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Use accepted task-local evidence to preserve useful aromatic, amine and carbonyl relationships during simplification, growth and chemically independent scaffold replacement. Evaluate whether new alternatives retain useful scores and plausible chemistry. Avoid a fixed size floor, automatic growth preference or an assumption that distinct native hash identifiers imply independent molecular scaffolds; the current evidence supports neither a pool-coverage claim nor a causal benefit for more diversity.

nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

branches: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
retained_mechanisms: Score-quantile parent allocation, previously accepted scored parents, bounded greedy survival and the full accepted-score archive.
Connected-fragment crossover with unchanged post-crossover mutation probability and multi-parent opportunities.
Ordinary single-atom replacement plus append, delete, insert, bond-change, ring-open and ring-close mutations, with inherited walk and saturation laws.
Sanitization, stable canonical identity admission, initial/emitted and temporary-pool duplicate rejection, bounded retries and fixed surplus pools.

Native integer-count Morgan environments and exact generalized count-Tanimoto covariance; accepted-only chronological GP fitting, unchanged normalization/noise/jitter and full posterior covariance. Multiplicity is retained while fixed-width folding is removed only from active coordinates.
Correlated posterior score draws with masks, exact pool-to-emission predictions, pending identity joins and next-fit feedback probes.
Passive aromatic-pair enumeration and the unreachable direct-exchange implementation retained for controlled attribution.
Fresh objective-local state, deterministic prepared settings, ten-member announced batches and protocol-owned budgets/resources.

approach.method_basis: The Parent walks from one scored molecular graph by sampling local atom and bond edits, including direct exchanges of aromatic carbon and nitrogen that preserve the molecular formula. It validates each product, rejects previously seen canonical identities, and applies a short memory of signed changes in local molecular motifs. A candidate is excluded only when it matches both inverse signs from the same earlier selected transition. After each accepted batch, the walk moves to its highest-scoring neighbor, even when that move worsens the current score, with canonical spelling breaking exact ties. A separate archive preserves the best observation. Each selected move requests at most four inverse restrictions. They last four completed moves, but a repeated signed motif currently replaces its live entry with the latest transition and restarts its expiry.
approach.novelty: Remove replacement and lifetime refresh when a selected move requests a signed motif that already has a live restriction. Keep that existing entry unchanged until its original expiry or ordinary obstruction release; install a new entry normally once the key is absent. Earlier siblings kept several overlapping origins, extended exercised restrictions, or removed the entire tabu gate. This probe retains one original live entry per signed motif and leaves the gate active. It tests whether repeated reassignment and renewed protection are necessary after neighborhood development. The immediate claim is zero overlap refreshes with preserved original provenance and deadlines; later admission and score effects must be measured. The utility hypothesis is that removing this refresh remains non-inferior.

nodes.hypothesis: Remove latest-transition refresh of an already-live signed inverse-motif restriction: preserve its original entry and expiry unchanged, treating repeated selected-transition credit for that signed key as a no-op until ordinary expiry or release makes the key absent.

finding_summary.headline: Keeping old restrictions changed five admissions and failed the non-inferiority test
finding_summary.insights: Latest-origin refresh affects both how long a restriction survives and which signed changes belong to one transition. Preserving an older origin restored one veto against an aromatic nitrogen positional isomer, yet removed four others by splitting newer groups or letting an older entry expire. None of the four newly admitted molecules was selected or improved the best archive, although two beat their current source. Each affected session initially kept the same batch winner; the two endpoint losses emerged only after later trajectories diverged. This rules out treating refresh removal as a harmless storage simplification in this evaluation, without assigning the losses to any single excluded or admitted molecule. The chemistry remains concentrated in the same broad scaffold families, including unusual sulfur bonding, difficult bridges and unresolved stereochemistry, so these admission differences do not demonstrate a chemical-quality benefit. Three passive replacement prefixes stop one molecule short; they support the observed decision differences, not scores for unobserved alternative trajectories.
finding_summary.results: All 48 overlapping requests preserved the original restriction and its deadline, with zero refreshes or backfilled credit slots. On the recorded search history, this changed five candidate decisions across four batches: four vetoes disappeared and one was added. All fifteen task–seed runs completed. Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.521759 to 0.518794, a paired decline of 0.002965 that exceeds the 0.002 non-inferiority margin; population SD rose from 0.006329 to 0.008617. The loss comes from drd2 seed 0 (-0.035615) and deco_hop seed 2 (-0.008861); the other thirteen task–seed scores tie. Mean recorded AUC also fell slightly, from 0.393354 to 0.392994. The mechanism therefore executed, while its utility hypothesis was falsified.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich scaffolds drift into unusual sulfur bonding and dense bridges, with no stereochemical definition
molecular.overall_character: This node produces substituted fused aromatics, aryl amines and nitrogen-carbonyl heterocycles, but much of the late chemistry contains unusual sulfur valences, sulfur-containing cages, reactive heteroatom bonds and complicated closures. All proposal sets have ring-closure-string rate 1.0. Aromatic-string rates are 0.9563 for zaleplon_mpo, 1.0 for deco_hop, drd2_docking and median_2, and 0.7184 for sitagliptin_mpo; these measure presence in a SMILES, not the aromatic fraction of its atoms. Formal-charge and stereocentre-string rates are 0.0 throughout. Recognizable amine, amide and heteroaromatic motifs coexist with structures that are implausible as routine synthetic targets, particularly the dense sulfur-rich leaders. Diversity is moderate across seeds, while each leading excerpt is concentrated on related frameworks. All five objectives have complete supplied trajectories: each has 900 molecules, including 870 optimizer proposals. Parent comparison uses n-abcd951ab7cc. Ordered optimizer SMILES and scores coincide in 12 of the 15 matched task/seed streams; differences occur in deco_hop seeds 1 and 2 and drd2_docking seed 0. This is an observation about output overlap, not a mechanism-activation judgment. Heavy-atom counts, molecular weights and ring descriptions below were derived with RDKit from the supplied trajectory SMILES. Potential stereogenic centres are not necessarily configurationally stable, and their identification does not establish accessible geometry. Digest final excerpts are late seed-2 proposals, not each seed's incumbent.

per_task.generated_character: The best molecule is a 26-heavy-atom benzofuran carboxanilide with methyl groups, an aryl thiol, an aminated benzylic chloride and an N-chloro amide. A more conventional 23-heavy-atom ethoxy/methyl/thiol-substituted indole carboxanilide scores almost as highly; another seed favors benzothiophene-linked aryl ketones. Thus the useful chemistry is compact fused aromatic rings joined to a second aryl group through a carbonyl-containing connection. Late molecules also contain partially dearomatized bridged rings and unusual sulfur double bonds. Mean proposal SMILES length is 46.2. All three complete molecular streams, including their best structures and scores, coincide with the Parent.
liabilities: The best molecule combines an N-chloro amide, a benzylic carbon bearing both amino and chloro groups, an aryl thiol and unspecified stereochemistry.
Later proposals introduce dense bridges, partially lost aromaticity, N-N bonds or unusual sulfur double bonds. Their graph validity does not establish stability or makeability.
The presence of a relatively conventional indole near the top argues against describing every sulfur-containing molecule as intrinsically implausible; the concern is the local bonding environment.
missing_features: Consistent preservation of compact aromatic carbonyl-linked arrangements is missing from many later proposals, despite the relatively high scores of conventional indole and benzothiophene frameworks.
Stable versions of the leading benzofuran substitution pattern, avoiding N-chloro and aminated benzylic-chloride functionality, are not established among the best examples.
The scores do not identify an absent exact pharmacophore; broader stable arrangements of the observed favorable functions remain unexplored in the leading excerpt.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The leading benzofuran amide scores 0.41003927643747895, the conventional indole amide 0.39905049777278273, and the benzothiophene ketone 0.393567030299894. The initial trimethoxyindole amide scores 0.3051048083696145. A similarly sized, more open/dearomatized nitrogen-containing ring structure in the worst proposal excerpt scores 0.021532846118034143. This supports compact aromatic organization and carbonyl placement rather than molecular size alone. The final densely bridged sulfur-containing proposal reaches 0.3852230774700024, so unusual closures can still score moderately; neither sulfur insertion nor N-chlorination has a demonstrated universal advantage.

per_task.generated_character: The best excerpt is a large substituted aryl/fused nitrogen-heterocycle family with a carbonyl and thione, imines, N-alkyl groups, a fluoro-substituted amine linkage and a long mixed ether/thioether chain. The best molecule has 51 heavy atoms and calculated molecular weight 870.8, including bromine, chlorine and sulfur. It has recognizable aromatic rings but a highly unusual substituted carbon-sulfur double-bond environment, and an N-bromo ring nitrogen. The seed-2 final excerpt instead combines a fused dione and aza-aromatic cyclic ether with unsaturated hydrocarbon arms and O-S substituents. Mean proposal SMILES length is 68.9. The best seed-0 and seed-1 molecules coincide with the Parent. The changed seed-2 leader has 42 heavy atoms and score 0.6003577106518283, versus the Parent's 47-heavy-atom leader at 0.6092182584436399; neither set establishes ordinary synthetic plausibility.
liabilities: The leader combines high molecular weight, a long flexible mixed-heteroatom chain, imines, unusual sulfur bonding and N-Br substitution.
The late seed-2 structures contain O-S linkages and multiply unsaturated hydrocarbon substituents without stereochemical definition.
Repeated similar scores among closely related elaborate structures provide little evidence that their growing chemical complexity is useful.
missing_features: Compact conventional substitutes for the successful heteroaromatic/carbonyl arrangement are not demonstrated among the strongest examples; high scores coexist with substantial side-chain and heavy-element burden.
Stable sulfur and nitrogen bonding environments are not consistently preserved when the favorable fused core is elaborated.

The observed gradient does not establish that an unseen decoration or target scaffold would be rewarded; the clear missing capability is chemically controlled elaboration of the structures already favored.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted fused dione scores 0.548381482770623. A rearranged small-ring variant among the worst proposals scores 0.526081691583997, whereas the large substituted leading family reaches 0.6161710037174721. In seed 2, the cited aromatic fused-dione proposal scores 0.5999120578463943, while its more saturated or sulfur-reorganized fused-core variants score 0.541765876888247 and 0.5450350272434115. This indicates sensitivity to retained heteroaromatic/carbonyl organization. Numerous leader variants share 0.6155070237050044 despite changes to alkyl arms or N-bromination, giving no evidence that every additional substituent contributes useful chemistry.

per_task.generated_character: The leading molecules carry aromatic hydrophobic regions and primary/tertiary amine centres, but embed these recognizable functions in unusual sulfur-containing ring systems. The best molecule has 32 heavy atoms, phenol and chlorophenyl groups, an aminomethyl substituent, a tertiary ring nitrogen and a sulfur-sulfur double-bond environment involving explicitly hydrogen-bearing sulfur. Other seeds produce small sulfur/amine rings or densely bridged aryl systems containing cumulene-like nitrogen/carbon/sulfur connectivity. Mean proposal SMILES length is 70.0, halogen-string rate is 0.9966, and cumulated-double-bond-string rate is 0.0598. Parent and Child seed-1 and seed-2 streams coincide. The changed seed-0 best falls from the Parent's 0.8856242185485628 to 0.8500094650652374, with unusual sulfur chemistry and constrained rings present in both.
liabilities: Leading examples contain unusual sulfur-sulfur or carbon-sulfur double bonds and hydrogen-bearing sulfur environments rather than only ordinary sulfides or sulfonamides.
Some successful examples combine small rings, dense bridges, halogen-rich aromatics and unassigned potential stereogenic centres.
The higher score does not establish that the apparent sulfur cage can be made, isolated or adopt a favorable conformation.
missing_features: Stable and geometrically credible versions of the favorable aryl/basic-amine arrangement are not demonstrated among the leaders; basic amine centres themselves are present.
The leading rigid and small-ring structures lack assigned stereochemical configurations, leaving the actual spatial presentation of aromatic and amine functions unresolved.
Neutral SMILES do not establish the relevant protonation state of these amines; the zero charge-string rate should not be interpreted as absence of basic chemistry.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best aryl-amine/sulfur-ring structure scores 0.9148143511682032. A low-scoring early acid/amide/N-sulfonyl-amine molecule scores 0.007468397818197266. Later leaders have more exposed aliphatic amine functionality and reorganized aromatic linkages, consistent with a preference for their combined presentation; this comparison does not isolate any single group. A late analogue that replaces the chlorophenyl region with a sulfur-containing nonaromatic ring scores only 0.04252669549740123. Sulfur-rich structures occur at both ends, so sulfur count or unusual valence alone does not explain reward. The benchmark score does not establish measured receptor binding.

per_task.generated_character: The best family is a densely bridged 31-heavy-atom system combining propyl-substituted pyridine, phenyl, an alkene, an N-methyl lactam and an N-O-containing bridge. Perceived cycles include eight- and nine-membered rings; these overlapping cycles do not imply independent simple rings. Other seeds carry larger nitrogen-carbonyl ring systems, thioesters, O-Br groups or unusual sulfur-containing bridges. Mean proposal SMILES length is 61.0. Every proposal contains ring-closure and aromatic text. All three complete molecular streams and their best molecules coincide with the Parent, so the same structural limitations persist.
liabilities: The leading scaffold has multiple overlapping medium-ring bridges and N-O connectivity; synthesis and accessible geometry are unresolved.
Related proposals introduce a peroxide bridge or O-Br substituents, and late molecules retain unusual sulfur valences.
The output lacks stereo markers despite potential stereogenic centres in the leading and late structures.
missing_features: Alternative simpler connectivities preserving the favorable aryl/nitrogen-carbonyl organization are not demonstrated among the best examples.
Stereochemical and conformational definition of the dense bridges is absent.
The leading excerpt remains concentrated on a single bridged family rather than distinct frameworks testing the same functional-group arrangement.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted fused dione scores 0.1678386594791329. The best bridged aryl/pyridyl lactam scores 0.21196904390980506, while an opened carbonyl/hydrazine-bearing proposal scores 0.12467972074136988. The observed gain accompanies a particular cyclic arrangement of aromatic and nitrogen-carbonyl functions, rather than simply more heteroatoms. Closely related N-O-bridged and peroxide-extended variants score 0.20775769309691736 and 0.20647766243219587. A late sulfur-rich cage scores 0.18814867381840605. The score differences do not show a reliable preference for ordinary stable bonding or identify an absent exact pharmacophore.

per_task.generated_character: The leading molecules are compact in atom count but chemically extreme sulfur-rich cages. The best has 30 heavy atoms, five sulfur atoms and calculated molecular weight 513.64. It combines a nitrogen-heterocyclic dione with carbon-bound fluorines, a hydroxyfluoromethyl thioether substituent, sulfur double bonds, hydrogen-bearing sulfur and dense bridged rings including a three-membered cycle. The best molecule retains only a small aromatic heterocyclic region; other high-scoring seeds have no aromatic atoms under RDKit perception. Thus the overall aromatic-string rate of 0.7184 should not be mistaken for uniformly aromatic leaders. Late seed-2 molecules are nonaromatic sulfur cages with aldehyde and N-fluoro amidine-like functions. Mean proposal SMILES length is 62.8. All complete molecular streams coincide with the Parent.
liabilities: Dense sulfur-rich polycycles contain unconventional sulfur valences, sulfur-sulfur bonds and very small rings. Familiar dione and fluorinated groups do not make the overall cages routine synthetic targets.
Late structures add N-F functionality, aldehydes or a sulfur-chlorine-containing acyl substituent, with no demonstrated stability control.
Atom-count compactness conceals substantial heavy-element burden and complex unresolved stereochemistry.
missing_features: Conventional stable frameworks retaining the favorable compact polar/fluorinated arrangement are not demonstrated among the strongest examples.
The many potential stereogenic centres and constrained closures lack assigned configurations or evidence of accessible geometry.
The observed molecules do not identify a missing exact target motif; chemically independent alternatives to the sulfur-cage family remain absent from the leading excerpt.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best cage scores 0.5903526424693334, while the initial aryl-substituted fused dione scores 0.0020944534688323298 and an early expanded dione proposal scores 7.590554525032884e-10. The later high scores accompany changed compact topology, fluorine placement and sulfur-rich composition, but simultaneous changes prevent attribution to a single desired group. Seed-2 final structures range from 0.004199910554494925 to 0.4484554129767839 despite sharing dense sulfur cages; shortening and reconnecting the carbonyl-containing segment in two cited late ring systems accompanies scores of 0.2536619453071564 and 0.4484554129767839. The score therefore distinguishes exact connectivity within these families, without demonstrating synthetic realism or a general preference for greater sulfur content.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Leading and late molecules include sulfur-sulfur double-bond environments, hydrogen-bearing sulfur in unsaturated cages and heavily substituted sulfur connected through double bonds. Conventional benzothiophene and thiol-containing structures also occur, so sulfur presence alone is not the problem.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not control sulfur bonding environments well enough to keep familiar scaffolds chemically credible.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Task-agnostic generation needs bond-environment awareness that distinguishes ordinary sulfides, thiophenes and other established sulfur groups from unsupported local valence/topology combinations. Stable alternatives should be compared within the same learned structural context rather than banning the element or assuming a score benefit.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Cited molecules contain N-Cl, N-Br, N-F, O-Br, N-O and peroxide connections, together with benzylic amino/chloro substitution. Some remain near the top of their observed score ranges, so reward is not a demonstrated chemical-stability filter.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output lacks control over reactive heteroatom-halogen and heteroatom-heteroatom connections.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic proposal process would need to preserve useful functional-group placement while providing chemically conventional bond alternatives. Any admissibility or reactivity constraint must distinguish local environments and be evaluated rather than inferred from graph validity.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every task has ring-closure-string rate 1.0 and stereocentre-string rate 0.0. Leaders include dense medium-ring bridges and sulfur cages with small rings and unassigned potential stereogenic centres.
transferable_gaps.gap: Abundant ring closure is not accompanied by demonstrated geometric feasibility or stereochemical definition.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring construction needs task-agnostic topology and conformational checks, with deliberate handling of stereochemical identity where relevant. Counting rings or accepting a valence-valid graph cannot establish makeability, and not every small ring should be treated as invalid.

transferable_gaps.evidence: One leader has 51 heavy atoms and calculated molecular weight 870.8 with a long mixed ether/thioether chain; another has only 30 heavy atoms but five sulfurs and calculated molecular weight 513.64. Several elaborate close variants share exactly the same score.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently control heavy-element burden and flexible elaboration while preserving favorable scaffolds.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Task-agnostic structural simplification needs to consider elemental composition, side-chain redundancy and flexibility as well as atom count. The data motivate testing compact conventional alternatives, without establishing a universal size cutoff or a benefit from deleting every substituent.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The best excerpts recur as fused aromatic carbonyl compounds, elaborated fused diones, sulfur-containing aryl amines, one bridged lactam family and dense sulfur cages. Distinct SMILES often change a side chain or local atom without escaping the same difficult framework.
transferable_gaps.gap: Leading chemistry remains concentrated in related frameworks instead of chemically independent solutions.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Scaffold-level changes should reorganize learned favorable functional-group relationships into different plausible frameworks. Meaningful diversity needs evidence from the chemistry of scored descendants rather than identity counts alone.

nodes.method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
nodes.method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.
