approach.method_basis: The Parent builds molecules by differentiating through a soft version of their structure. It represents each scored molecule as a graph of whole rings and individual atoms, preserves the interior, and makes the identities and presence of selected terminal units and expansion sites adjustable probabilities. A graph encoder learned from unlabeled molecules stays frozen, while a ridge readout is refitted on the current objective's accepted scores. Starting molecules are sampled with a preference for high score rank. The Parent takes bounded gradient steps that increase this readout's predicted value, retains the best relaxed state, then samples structural decisions and compatible attachments to assemble valid, distinct molecules. Accepted products enter the archive and can become later starting structures. The observed limitation is that increasing this point prediction often fails to produce a better assembled molecule.
approach.novelty: The added mechanism is ascent of a lower confidence bound on structural gain. A Gaussian posterior over the existing ridge coefficients estimates how uncertain a proposed change in the frozen graph features is. Structural ascent subtracts one posterior standard deviation of that gain, so a promising but poorly supported direction receives a smaller gradient contribution. The fitted mean remains the Parent's ridge prediction, and the resulting probabilities still drive its existing sampling and assembly process. This lineage contains only its root so far; no sibling has tested coefficient uncertainty inside structural ascent. The experiment asks whether that uncertainty changes the structural updates before sampling, and whether the resulting proposals transfer more reliably to actual improvements.

nodes.hypothesis: Replace point-estimate structural ascent with ascent of a numerically smoothed lower confidence bound on relaxed structural gain, subtracting one standard deviation computed from the full Gaussian coefficient posterior associated with the Parent's accepted-only ridge readout and differentiating that uncertainty through the frozen graph encoder.

finding_summary.headline: Uncertainty changed every relaxation, but the mean score fell from 0.3619 to 0.3079
finding_summary.insights:
This experiment establishes that coefficient uncertainty can change structural search before sampling and survive every downstream assembly step. It also shows that correcting this particular source of uncertainty is insufficient to remove prediction optimism or preserve the best final score. The strongest illustration is DRD2: 188 of 290 proposals beat their source, yet the search settled around a much lower score. The molecular assessment describes increasingly crowded polyacetals with late scores near 0.028858, while the Parent's stronger products belonged to a different biaryl/amine series. Repeated small improvements inside a weak chemical family can therefore make source-beating rates look favorable while valuable regions remain unreached.

The evidence leaves open whether the uncertainty penalty restricted productive exploration, whether early stochastic differences redirected the search, or whether structural information missing from the frozen features dominated the remaining errors. The posterior covers coefficient uncertainty conditional on an empirical noise estimate; it does not cover attachment choices, stereochemistry or the gap between a relaxed state and its assembled molecule. The generated structures still exhibit the reactive attachments and unspecified configurations identified by the molecular assessment. Preserving access to alternative core families and representing attachment environments remain worth testing. One paired seed cannot establish the repeatability of the four gains or the DRD2 loss.
finding_summary.results:
The intended mechanism ran throughout this screening replica. All 150 accepted-score posterior fits were valid, all 145 feedback updates changed the full coefficient covariance, and all 152 structural optimizations changed their retained categorical distributions relative to the same starting state's mean-only ascent. Every one of the 1,450 emitted proposals used those changed distributions. All eligible nonzero uncertainty corrections reduced the raw gradient's uncertainty directional derivative, and every optimization retained a positive confidence gain; none needed a fallback.

On the single supplied seed, macro Top-1 fell from 0.361872 to 0.307903, a loss of 0.053969. Four objectives improved: zaleplon_mpo from 0.380139 to 0.394051, deco_hop from 0.589062 to 0.602445, median_2 from 0.180051 to 0.183284, and sitagliptin_mpo from 0.234090 to 0.330875. The loss came from drd2_docking, which fell from 0.426020 to 0.028858. Both runs completed all five 300-evaluation tasks with valid, distinct batches.

Local improvement became more frequent: 447 of 1,450 proposals beat their generating molecule, compared with 380 for the Parent. Predicted improvements were realized 41.1% of the time, up from 32.4%. Their average actual score change nevertheless worsened from -0.025853 to -0.031192, and average overstatement of assembled source-relative gains rose from 0.023479 to 0.034251. Better local hit rates did not produce a better overall search result.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich scaffold series with reactive attachments; the largest products are crowded polyacetals with undefined stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: For n-b3517f183781, the supplied seed-0 trajectories each contain 300 distinct recorded molecules, including 290 optimizer proposals. Every proposal set has ring_closure_rate 1.0 and branch_rate 1.0. The main products are dihydropyrazole-thioureas, extended heteroaryl-substituted indoles, quinoline ethers linked to substituted piperidines, silylmethyl-substituted indole carboxamides, and heavily elaborated polyacetals. Rings, heteroatoms, aromatic groups and saturated amine rings are readily represented. Aromatic-atom presence rates are 1.0 for zaleplon_mpo, deco_hop and median_2, 0.9828 for sitagliptin_mpo, and 0.3379 for the predominantly saturated drd2_docking series. These are presence readings from SMILES text, not aromatic atom fractions or perceived ring counts. The output has many distinct decorations but narrow core families within each trajectory. Ordinary medicinal scaffolds coexist with O-F and N-F bonds, peroxides, chloromethyl ethers, sulfenyl chlorides, primary hydrosilanes and, in a late polyacetal, an explicit carbanion. The most congested polyacetals are difficult to regard as routine synthetic targets. All proposal sets have stereocentre_rate 0.0: configurations are unspecified even where the connectivity implies stereogenic carbons. This does not mean the molecules are achiral. The qualitative quality labels describe the recorded structures; no synthesis, conformer, docking-pose or new property calculation was performed. All supplied objectives are covered. The score readings below are associations in these trajectories and the Parent comparison, not proof of individual substituent effects or a missing target-specific pharmacophore.

per_task.generated_character: Mostly compact to moderately sized aryl-substituted dihydropyrazoles carrying a thiourea linkage. The leading series has two aryl arms, phenols, methyl substitution and small fluorinated groups; the best molecule at evaluation 277 has an N-methylated aryl-thiourea, an aryl fluoride and a fluoromethyl ether. The fluoromethyl ether has a carbon between oxygen and fluorine. Other high and late examples instead contain hydroperoxides, O-O-S or O-S attachments and aryl thiols. Mean SMILES length is 44.5, with maximum 67; aromatic and ring presence rates are both 1.0 and halogen presence is 0.6517. The core is recognizably makeable organic chemistry, while several terminal attachments have questionable stability. Relative to Parent n-0e1f7686dea8, the leading chemistry remains a dihydropyrazole family but retains the thiourea and phenolic aryl groups, where the Parent leaders used an aminomethyl-pyridyl cap and a furyloxyphenyl arm.
liabilities: Evaluation 59 contains an aryl hydroperoxide, and the final molecule contains an O-O-S chain. These introduce reactive oxygen-oxygen bonds into otherwise familiar scaffolds.
Evaluation 289 carries an aryl sulfenyl chloride. Such an S-Cl attachment is a materially different stability concern from the ordinary carbon-bound fluorine in the best molecule.

Some lower-scoring products crowd extra saturated or heteroaromatic rings around the same core. The individual fragments are familiar, but the complete attachment patterns are less convincing synthetic targets.
missing_features: Comparably successful alternative core connectivities that retain the compact polar/aromatic arrangement are not demonstrated among the leading molecules; the highest-scoring set stays with the dihydropyrazole-thiourea family.
Defined configurations at the substituted dihydropyrazole carbons are absent. The supplied records contain no comparison from which a stereochemical score preference could be inferred.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The polyacetal population has mean SMILES length 100.7 and maximum 175, with many pendant heterocycles, charged nitrogen environments and an SiH3 group. Its late reported scores lie close to 0.028858 despite substantial appendage changes. Elsewhere, compact indole and dihydropyrazole variants coexist with much lower-scoring derivatives carrying extra rings.

transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide molecule-level contraction and rearrangement options as well as expansion, so a smaller scaffold can present a similar set of polar and ionizable groups. transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make alternative central ring connectivities and linker geometries accessible while preserving favorable functional relationships observed in accepted molecules. transferable_gaps.evidence: Every proposal set has stereocentre_rate 0.0. The cited substituted dihydropyrazoles, fluorinated benzylic amines, substituted piperidines and crowded polyacetals nevertheless contain stereogenic connectivity. transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not express defined stereochemical products even when its connectivity creates stereogenic centers.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support explicit configuration and its preservation through structural changes so that emitted identities can denote individual stereoisomers. nodes.method_name: DST: gradient-guided construction through relaxed scaffolding trees
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the method in Differentiable Scaffolding Tree: relax molecular substructure identity and existence into continuous variables, ascend a structural surrogate, and sample discrete structures from the optimized variables. [Fu et al., Sections 3.1-3.3](https://wenhao-gao.github.io/assets/publications/2021_DST_ICLR/paper.pdf) describe this proposal mechanism. For our adaptation, derive an atom/ring token alphabet and train a compact graph encoder by masked-substructure reconstruction solely on the permitted unlabeled corpus. Freeze that encoder and fit a regularized linear scalar readout using only the current objective's accepted observations, updating the readout after feedback. Select scored molecules as local starting structures; hold their internal scaffold context fixed while optimizing relaxed leaf replacement, deletion and expansion variables through the surrogate. Keep surrogate parameters fixed during each structural optimization. Sample edited trees and compatible attachment choices stochastically, assemble new molecules, and repeat generation until the announced batch contains distinct valid structures. The token alphabet supports construction; complete corpus molecules are never retrieved or ranked, and attachment combinations are sampled rather than exhaustively enumerated. Accepted feedback updates both the scored archive and the readout. The hypothesis is that useful structural gradients concentrate new proposals toward real improvements quickly enough to increase the mean of independent final Top-1 scores. Reliable gradients from scarce labels and faithful transfer from relaxed to assembled structures are unproven prerequisites.

method_references.title: Tianfan Fu, Wenhao Gao, Cao Xiao, Jacob Yasonik, Connor W. Coley, and Jimeng Sun. Differentiable Scaffolding Tree for Molecular Optimization. ICLR 2022. Sections 3.1-3.3 describe the anchor; Section 4 reports the larger labeled-training prerequisite that this adaptation must replace.

approach.method_basis: The Parent learns a recurrent SMILES prior from an unlabeled corpus, then adapts a fresh policy independently for each objective. After every accepted batch, it trains on the best-scoring half of the current molecules and a uniformly sampled group of historical elites. Each original accepted SMILES is fitted toward the frozen prior log probability plus sixty times its observed score, with equal weight for every training sequence. Only current elites enter memory after that update; the thirty-two highest-scoring identities survive. Complete molecules are then sampled directly from the policy, validated and filtered for canonical novelty.
approach.novelty: Change only which historical elites survive in memory. Retain the best member of each molecular core before retaining second members of those cores, proceeding in score order within each round until the existing memory is full. The original uniform replay then gives every surviving family access to the same learning rule. This differs from the sibling that always replays the strongest records: it changes future availability while keeping replay sampling intact. An earlier graph-evolution experiment used similar retention, but its protected molecules never entered the narrow score bands used for breeding. Uniform replay supplies a different route from protected memory to actual learning, which this experiment will measure directly. Broader core counts alone will not establish better chemistry or scores.

nodes.hypothesis: Retain accepted historical elites by successive score-ordered rounds across Murcko cores, taking each core's best record before any core's next record, then restore descending-score/canonical order for the inherited uniform replay while preserving original accepted records and the existing memory capacity.

finding_summary.headline: Protected cores reached learning and duplicate draws fell, with little net score gain
finding_summary.insights: The earlier core-retention experiment in graph evolution failed to expose protected records to its restricted breeding sampler. Uniform neural replay opens that route: retained alternatives now enter the real loss and affect learning before later proposals. Access remains sparse, however. Only 74 of 302 protected records with a later nonterminal opportunity were drawn, and protection lasted a median of one retained snapshot after its first event. The same accepted-stream greedy comparison gives a replay reward of 0.31539, so weaker replay reward is a direct retention tradeoff rather than only a difference between generated trajectories. Broader core access and fewer duplicates did not meet the expected 0.002 mean score improvement; useful transfer from those lower-reward alternatives remains unresolved. The generated chemistry remains conventional, ring-rich aromatic amine/carbonyl chemistry with familiar leading families and no specified stereochemistry, so more core counts do not establish the precise chemical coverage the objectives need. Twenty-two protected training targets were positive and unattainable as log probabilities, another inherited limitation. The gradient evidence also has a numerical boundary: two mathematically equivalent groupings differed in combined norm by up to 0.045% under the inherited floating computation. Protected-removal signals exceeded the registered threshold by at least 86,620 times, but full vectors were not retained to establish exact numerical equivalence.
finding_summary.results: Core protection changed 216 of 435 retention decisions that preceded further proposals. Every changed local contest retained more ring cores than greedy selection. Across all 435 local contests, mean ring-core coverage was 28.71 versus 27.50. Seventy-four protected accepted records subsequently entered learning in 83 exposures across 70 updates. All seventy updates showed a measurable protected gradient contribution, and protected target mean-square error fell from 165.10 to 100.63. Summed within sessions, actual replay covered 862 distinct ring cores versus 750 in the Parent, while its mean accepted reward fell from 0.31637 to 0.27659. Duplicate raw draws fell from 30.11% to 25.51%, and batch-level novel-valid yield rose from 60.31% to 64.76%; both runs still submitted exactly 4,350 valid novel proposals. Mean final score was 0.508476 versus 0.507554, a paired gain of 0.000922. The three seed changes were -0.013399, +0.007440 and +0.008726. Median_2 improved by 0.019383 on average, while sitagliptin_mpo fell by 0.015668; the smaller remaining task changes did not produce a clear overall score gain.

Independent audit: audit.py/audit.json verifies 121586 conditions; retention.py/retention.json verifies 43687, totaling 165273 passing registered reconstruction checks with zero errors. The coverage includes all 900 child/Parent updates, 8,700 emitted proposal joins, full local accepted-record memory continuity, every actual replay random index, float32 target and equal-row loss reconstruction, scalar diagnostic tolerances/geometry, protection ancestry and caches, and source/checkpoint/dependency invariance. metrics.py/metrics.json independently aggregates those records and reproduces all six asserted quantities of the pre-registered Parent-stream core-round counterfactual. lifetime.py/lifetime.json separately measures the duration after first protection, retaining complete original-record provenance, opportunity windows, evictions and right censoring. No optimizer, preparation, suggestion, model-training, oracle evaluation or scored counterfactual was executed by Analyze.

Supplementary numerical limitation: comparing the inherited current/history regrouping with the new protected/remaining regrouping of the same mathematical equal-row gradient gives different combined-gradient norms beyond the 1e-8 + 1e-6 relative scale in 72 of 73 protected updates, including terminal updates. Maximum relative norm disagreement is 0.0004466193353211453 (0.0446619%); maximum absolute disagreement is 0.46589479479871443. This extra equality test was not registered as the activation falsifier; its mismatches are retained explicitly, and no registered removal tolerance was widened. The inherited source enables TF32 and uses floating backward computations, a plausible numerical explanation that has not been separately established. The protected-removal difference exceeds its unchanged registered tolerance by at least 86,620.89 times on all 70 qualifying nonterminal updates. A difference of norms is not an upper bound on vector error. Full gradient tensors and intermediate policy checkpoints were not retained, so this audit cannot independently rerun exact pre-update gradient vectors or establish bitwise equivalence to the real backward gradient. It verifies actual row membership, fixed inputs, mathematical source grouping, recorded finite norms/tolerances and actual optimizer use; it does not claim the two regroupings agree to 1e-6.

molecular.headline: Conventional ring-rich medicinal chemistry has useful amine and carbonyl families, but limited precise coverage and no specified stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: The supplied output covers all five objectives and all three seeds, with 900 evaluated molecules and 870 optimizer proposals per task. All 4,350 optimizer proposals parse with RDKit. These are predominantly conventional aromatic and heteroaromatic molecules containing amides, sulfonamides, cyclic amines, ethers, carboxylic acids and hydrazones. Median proposal heavy-atom counts are 23, 28, 26, 23 and 24 in task order, and median ring counts are three, three, four, three and three. Digest aromatic-token rates range from 0.9586 to 0.9954 and ring-closure rates from 0.9885 to 0.9966, so rings and aromaticity are abundant. No proposal contains a detected N-, O- or S-halogen bond, carbon allene or acid halide; two contain an O-O single bond and ten contain an azide. Dominant connectivity is synthetically plausible, although that is a structural reading rather than demonstrated synthesis or stability. Individual tasks contain 490-771 distinct nonchiral Murcko scaffolds, yet leading examples often concentrate in related indole amides, arylpiperazine/indole structures, hydrazones or methylenedioxyaryl/piperazine combinations. Relative to the parent, recognizable aromatic carbonyl and cyclic-amine chemistry persists, with changed local arrangements and some shared leading chemotypes. No optimizer proposal has an assigned stereocentre, while 208, 156, 378, 219 and 263 proposals have an unassigned centre in task order. Chemical coverage and three-dimensional specification, rather than missing ring construction, are the main limitations visible here.

per_task.generated_character: The highest molecule combines an N-acetic-acid-substituted pyrazole, a cyclopentene and an indole: 23 heavy atoms, four rings and three aromatic rings, with one unspecified stereocentre on the partially saturated ring. Another leading family comprises substituted indole carboxamides whose amide nitrogen belongs to an isoindoline- or tetrahydroisoquinoline-like ring; formamido, methoxy, ethoxy and acetyl substituents appear. A nitrile-bearing tertiary arylsulfonamide supplies a different three-phenyl-ring example. These are generally recognizable synthetic chemotypes. The parent also led with indole carboxamides, including a methoxy indole coupled to a cyanobenzyl-substituted amide; the current digest therefore retains aromatic/carbonyl chemistry while giving more prominence to constrained cyclic amide substituents and the pyrazole-acid alternative.
liabilities: Long alkyl linkers and bulky polycyclic appendages create severe low-score outliers even though the resulting bonds remain chemically recognizable.
The acid-bearing leader, neutral amides and tertiary sulfonamide have different ionization and hydrogen-bonding behavior; their objective values do not establish interchangeable physical properties.
No synthesis, conformational or stability measurements are supplied for the new cyclic arrangements.
missing_features: The high-score set supplies several useful compact polar ring arrangements but relatively few chemically distinct alternatives beyond nearby indole amide substitutions; no unique missing target-like group is established.
The highest cyclopentene-containing molecule and the arylpyrrolidine amide alternative have unassigned stereogenic centres, leaving the proposed configurations unspecified.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The pyrazole-acid/indole structure scores 0.465254, and compact indole carboxamides reach 0.441237 and 0.437370. A formamido indole carboxamide at 0.441237 and its displayed methoxy counterpart at 0.415644 support sensitivity to local polar substitution in that family; they do not establish a universal formamide requirement. The tertiary arylsulfonamide reaches 0.416563, so an amide-linked indole is not the only productive architecture. Very long alkyl ethers and larger polycyclic amide assemblies fall to approximately 4.40e-32 and 7.97e-38. A terminal N-methyl-N-benzylaniline scores 0.015410, showing that an aromatic amine alone does not reproduce the more organized multi-ring/polar arrangements.

per_task.generated_character: The leaders are highly aromatic sulfonylhydrazones and acylhydrazones, plus fluorinated multi-heteroaryl amides and sulfonamides. The highest structure joins an amino-substituted pyridine sulfonylhydrazone to a fused azaaromatic ring, with a trifluoromethoxy aryl arm; it has 34 heavy atoms, four aromatic rings and molecular mass 487.463. Other leaders contain four to six aromatic rings with very little saturated carbon. The whole proposal set is smaller on average, with median 28 heavy atoms and three aromatic rings; its digest halogen rate is 0.7103. The parent also produced aromatic hydrazones and fluorinated heteroaryl systems. Current N-N=C proposals number 144 compared with 181 in the parent, so hydrazone chemistry persists without being the sole available functional-group family.
liabilities: Four- to six-ring aromatic leaders and extensive fluorination can produce high molecular mass and limited saturated shape; their solubility and exposure are not measured.
Sulfonylhydrazone and acylhydrazone connections introduce configurational and potential stability questions that do not arise in exactly the same way for ordinary amides.
Six proposals exceed 50 heavy atoms, although the displayed higher-score examples already show that larger aryl appendages are not uniformly beneficial.
missing_features: Broader stable architectures reproducing the productive polar and aromatic arrangement are less visible among the leaders than repeated sulfonylhydrazone or polyaryl variants.
The hydrazone leaders do not specify C=N geometry, and their tautomeric and stability behavior is uncharacterized; the displayed scores cannot identify a preferred realizable form.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The fused azaaromatic sulfonylhydrazone scores 0.601810 and the displayed naphthalene counterpart 0.591495, providing a close example in which ring nitrogen placement accompanies a modest score difference. Replacing the trifluoromethoxy aryl arm with a phenoxy-substituted arm gives 0.589330, and fluorinated heteroaryl amides reach about 0.587-0.591. In contrast, benzyl sulfones and other differently connected sulfones score about 0.266-0.301 despite substantial aromatic and sulfur content. Thus sulfur, aromaticity and halogen counts alone do not specify the productive arrangement. Thiophene scores 0.5, while terminal aminoalkyl heteroaryl structures reach roughly 0.56-0.57; intermediate score is not itself evidence of a fully developed multi-ring chemotype.

per_task.generated_character: The highest displayed family is an arylpiperazine carrying an alkyl-linked bromo- or iodoindole. The aryl ring bears alkyl, alkenyl, acyl or aminoalkyl substitutions, while two- and three-carbon indole linkers both appear. The top example has 28 heavy atoms, four rings, three aromatic rings and molecular mass 440.429. These are conventional basic-amine/aromatic medicinal-chemistry structures. The parent also had an arylpiperazine with a propyl-linked haloindole among its strongest molecules, so the leading chemistry is substantially shared. Other current seeds produce arylpiperidines and more fused polycyclic amines; the terminal digest particularly shows the latter, including additional secondary or tertiary amino substituents.
liabilities: Long alkyl substituents and heavy aryl halogens raise conformational freedom or molecular mass without a clear practical score advantage among the displayed near-ceiling analogues.
The iodo/butyl example has molecular mass 501.456 compared with 440.429 for the bromo/propyl leader; neither value establishes favorable physical properties.
Some terminal fused amines contain multiple stereogenic centres and elaborate ring junctions, so their geometry cannot be interpreted from unspecified SMILES alone.
missing_features: No additional required functional group can be inferred from these near-ceiling values; economical alternatives within the demonstrated amine/aromatic arrangements remain more justified than prescribing extra decoration.
The achiral leading arylpiperazine family does not need assigned centres, but many fused-amine alternatives do: 378 proposals contain an unassigned stereocentre and no proposal assigns one.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Numerous arylpiperazine/haloindole variants reach near-ceiling scores, including smaller methyl or ethyl substituents and longer alkyl alternatives. This supports the shared amine/linker/aromatic arrangement, while the nearly saturated scores provide little basis for claiming that added alkyl length or iodine is chemically necessary. The low end includes nitro/acid heteroaromatic amides, sulfonamides and an acylhydrazone at approximately 1.86e-05 to 4.11e-05; their nitrogen atoms often occupy less basic environments than the leading tertiary amines. A terminal hydrocarbon-rich fused aromatic molecule without nitrogen scores 0.069077, whereas fused amine-containing alternatives remain approximately 0.976-0.999992. These are molecular associations in the trajectory, not measurements of receptor activity.

per_task.generated_character: The highest molecule combines a methoxy benzimidazole-like aromatic system, a methylenedioxyphenyl group and an N-methylpiperazine: 27 heavy atoms and five rings, three of them aromatic. Other leading examples join methylenedioxyaryl groups to piperazines through sulfonyl, carbonyl or aromatic linkers, sometimes adding a benzoic-acid group. A more fused lactam/sulfone/indole example is also present and is the same displayed chemotype as a parent seed leader. The parent already contained arylsulfonylpiperazine and carbonyl heterocycle families; the current digest makes the methylenedioxyaryl/piperazine combination particularly visible. Dominant structures are conventional and synthetically plausible. Full proposals have median 23 heavy atoms and three rings, with 766 nonchiral Murcko scaffolds.
liabilities: Sulfonylation, acylation and direct aryl attachment change piperazine nitrogen electronics; treating every ring nitrogen as an equivalent basic centre would misdescribe the chemistry.
Acidic, neutral and basic examples coexist, without measured ionization, permeability or solubility to establish their practical balance.
Rare organic azides and long-chain unusual nitrogen/oxygen species occur at the low end, although fragmented or exotic bonding is not the dominant output character.
missing_features: The output needs more precise coverage of how its aromatic, oxygen-containing and piperazine regions are connected; all those building-block features exist, but simple presence does not explain the gradient.
Stereochemical specification is absent in the chiral fused lactam/sulfone alternative and in 219 proposals overall, despite many other leading piperazine structures being achiral.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The methoxy heteroaromatic/methylenedioxyaryl piperazine scores 0.238153 and a carboxyphenylsulfonyl methylenedioxyarylpiperazine 0.228086. A smaller methylenedioxyarylsulfonylpiperazine still reaches 0.214834 with only 18 heavy atoms, so increased size or extra rings are not mandatory across the useful examples. Allyl azide scores zero, small unusual or acyclic polar structures lie near 0.008-0.029, and a terminal chlorophenol-piperazine is only 0.106030. Piperazine presence or abundant polar groups alone therefore does not recover the combined arrangement in the leaders. The visible scores do not isolate a single absent substituent that would resolve the remaining gap.

per_task.generated_character: The leading molecules are several distinct compact polar chemotypes: a fused N-rich dicarbonyl bicycle bearing aryl and hydroxybenzyl groups; a dimethylaminoacetamide/furan carboxamide attached to an aniline; and amino azaheteroaromatic carbonyl systems. Additional leaders include acylated nitrogen-chain hydrazones, a pyridine N-oxide urea and a nitropyridylmethyl phenolic piperazine. The highest fused dicarbonyl has 27 heavy atoms and four rings, whereas the aminoacetamide/furan example has 21 heavy atoms and two aromatic rings. Most have plausible conventional connectivity, with specific qualification for extended N-N-N chains, nitro groups and hydrazone geometry. The parent already produced the same dimethylaminoacetamide/furan chemotype and other fused carbonyl heterocycles. Current full proposals have median 24 heavy atoms and three rings, with 771 distinct nonchiral Murcko scaffolds.
liabilities: Nitro, N-oxide and extended N-N-containing examples have different electronic and potential reactivity profiles from ordinary amides; their objective values do not establish practical chemical quality.
Overgrown polycyclic, peptide-like and extended aromatic structures can have negligible score despite abundant nitrogen and oxygen; four proposals exceed 50 heavy atoms.
Late large or fused structures include unspecified stereochemistry and long conjugated appendages, limiting chemical interpretation beyond their displayed graph and score.
missing_features: Chemically distinct compact polar families are already reachable, but their useful functional-group arrangements are not broadly represented in the higher-score part of the output.
Hydrazone and extended nitrogen-chain examples lack specified C=N geometry and demonstrated stability; no observed score establishes that extending the N-N chain is necessary.

No proposal assigns stereocentres even though 263 contain an unassigned centre. The leading examples themselves are mostly achiral, so this is a conditional coverage gap rather than an inferred mandatory chiral group.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The fused dicarbonyl structure scores 0.291745, the dimethylaminoacetamide/furan carboxamide 0.287703 and its positional isomer 0.283073. Other compact heteroaromatic or hydrazone structures reach approximately 0.22-0.27. These support compact, organized polar functionality in several architectures rather than one mandatory scaffold or one basic-amine motif. Oversized polycycles, long linked peptides and highly elaborated aromatic molecules produce zero or vanishing scores even though they contain many familiar groups. The digest median of 1e-06 is rounded: the full 900-row median is 6.776037459724324e-07 and only two rows are exactly zero. The higher-score chemistry is therefore sparsely represented within a structurally diverse, predominantly very-low-score distribution.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A fused azaaromatic sulfonylhydrazone scores 0.601810 while its displayed naphthalene counterpart scores 0.591495; differently connected benzyl sulfones are near 0.27. A methoxy heteroaromatic/methylenedioxyaryl piperazine scores 0.238153 while a simple chlorophenol-piperazine scores 0.106030. Elsewhere, basic arylpiperazine/indole systems reach near-ceiling values while amide and sulfonamide nitrogen environments are among the low-score examples. These observations concern arrangements and nitrogen or sulfur electronic environments, not missing heteroatom vocabulary.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve useful functional-group placement and electronic context across its conventional chemotypes.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The missing chemical capability is reliable exploration of alternative attachment positions and linker environments while retaining useful polar and aromatic relationships. Preserve distinctions between basic amines, amides, sulfonamides, hydrazones and oxidized nitrogen groups, and let observed feedback establish where each context is useful.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The five proposal sets contain 546, 490, 517, 766 and 771 nonchiral Murcko scaffolds. Their displayed leaders nevertheless cluster into several closely related indole amides, sulfonylhydrazones, arylpiperazine/indole analogues or oxygenated aryl/piperazine combinations. The session with 771 scaffolds has a full-trajectory median score of about 6.78e-07, yet its leaders include distinct compact dicarbonyl, aminoacetamide and hydrazone families. The necessary structural vocabulary exists but is sparsely realized in higher-score arrangements.
transferable_gaps.gap: Broad graph-scaffold coverage does not consistently yield broad coverage of productive compact chemical architectures.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support chemically distinct core and linker alternatives that preserve an observed useful arrangement, alongside local positional and substituent changes. Chemical coverage should reflect access to productive families and their meaningful alternatives, rather than unique strings or new ring closures alone.

transferable_gaps.evidence: None of the 4,350 optimizer proposals has an assigned stereocentre. In fixed session order, 208, 156, 378, 219 and 263 proposals contain at least one unassigned centre. Cited higher-score molecules include a cyclopentene-linked heteroaromatic acid, an arylpyrrolidine amide and fused amine or lactam systems. Hydrazone leaders also omit explicit C=N geometry. Many strong arylpiperazine and amide examples are achiral, so stereochemistry matters conditionally.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator leaves stereogenic structures and relevant imine configurations unspecified.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide configurationally explicit alternatives when a chemical structure supports stereocentres or imine geometry, while maintaining chemically consistent representations and access to achiral families. The observed data do not authorize prescribing any particular unobserved stereoisomer.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Proposal sizes are usually moderate, but the five sessions contain zero, six, seven, zero and four proposals above 50 heavy atoms. Very long alkyl ethers and oversized polycyclic amides occur among vanishing-score examples even below that size threshold. Compact 18-heavy-atom sulfonylpiperazine chemistry remains competitive within its observed neighborhood, and small alkyl-substituted arylpiperazines share near-ceiling values with variants with heavier aryl halogens and longer alkyl groups. Large linked aromatic or peptide-like structures can instead have exactly zero or extremely small scores.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator still expands useful structures into excessive linkers or appendages without consistently retaining their chemical arrangement.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Maintain alternatives with controlled linker length, substituent mass and ring elaboration while preserving useful polar-group placement. The need is context-sensitive chemical growth, not a universal size limit: both compact and more extended conventional chemotypes are demonstrated, and added complexity should remain chemically purposeful.

nodes.method_name: Augmented Hill-Climb with a corpus-trained SMILES policy
nodes.method_thesis: Train a compact autoregressive SMILES prior solely on the supplied unlabeled corpus, then initialize a fresh policy from that prior for each objective. Use the initial observations and each subsequent scored batch to update only its highest-reward sequences with the Augmented Hill-Climb loss: fit policy log likelihood to frozen-prior log likelihood plus scaled observed reward. Sample complete molecules token by token from the updated policy, canonicalize them, and refill invalid or duplicate proposals by further generation. The corpus supplies language training, never a ranked molecular pool. Elite-conditioned policy updates should shift generation toward new high-scoring molecular combinations quickly enough to improve the benchmark's mean final Top-1. This is a small-budget transfer hypothesis, not a claim that published larger-budget gains carry over. The root uses the current scored batch; randomized historical replay is reserved for the first improvement. The anchor's elite augmented-likelihood mechanism is described by [Thomas et al.](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13321-022-00646-z).

approach.method_basis: ChemTS runs Monte Carlo tree search over the prefixes of a SMILES string. Each node in the tree is a partial molecule, and the search picks which prefix to extend using an upper confidence bound that balances how well that branch has scored against how rarely it has been tried. A frozen language model completes the chosen prefix into a whole molecule by stochastic rollout, and the score that comes back is propagated up the path that produced it, so the tree accumulates a value estimate for every prefix.
approach.novelty: This root commits to keeping the rollout prior completely frozen and putting all task adaptation into the tree statistics, so nothing about the generative model changes during an objective. It initializes each fresh tree's statistics from the supplied initial observations rather than from an empty tree, and uses an explicit exploration constant of one half against the completed visit counts, which is the specific balance the method statement leaves open.

nodes.hypothesis: Search an expanding SMILES prefix tree with UCT using task-local observed returns, expand prefixes from a frozen corpus-trained autoregressive RNN, complete molecules by stochastic RNN rollouts, and backpropagate accepted oracle scores through their generating paths.

finding_summary.headline: Frozen-prior tree search reproduced across three seeds; strong docking scores and concentrated batches persisted
finding_summary.insights:
The search behavior and strong docking outcomes now recur across independently prepared priors, so the original result was not confined to one trained checkpoint or rollout seed. This replication does not isolate a score benefit from UCT over unguided sampling: all runs use both the corpus prior and tree adaptation, and preparation randomness changes along with search randomness. The substantial sitagliptin spread also shows that similar mechanism activation can yield materially different best molecules.

The search remains shallow at this budget. New rollout-start prefixes averaged about 3.38 tokens while completed strings averaged 38.53, and almost half the batches used a single prefix. Yet the molecular assessment finds broad ring and functional-group diversity, so concentrated short SMILES prefixes do not by themselves demonstrate chemical collapse. They may group molecules with weakly related returns. These observations make pending-rollout accounting and more chemically meaningful reward sharing plausible questions to test, without establishing that either improves final scores. Unspecified stereochemistry, size extremes and occasional awkward functional groups also persist despite the generally recognizable medicinal chemistry.
finding_summary.results:
Both added replicas confirmed the intended search mechanism. Prior weights stayed fixed throughout each task, all 2,900 accepted generated scores updated their recorded tree paths, and all 19,580 traversal choices matched the declared UCT rule. Later accepted scores entered 11,960 chosen value estimates; in 2,120 selections the empirical-mean term made the chosen branch outrank a branch with a larger exploration bonus. The new replicas added 590 prefix nodes across ten task trees and completed every ten-molecule batch without an invalid or duplicate submission.

The two new macro final Top-1 scores were 0.508151 and 0.481129, alongside the original 0.479189. The three-seed mean is 0.489490 with population standard deviation 0.013219. Task means are 0.433514 for zaleplon, 0.612739 for decoration hopping, 0.964212 for docking, 0.177507 for median_2 and 0.259477 for sitagliptin. Docking remained between 0.938221 and 0.977922 across the three seeds; sitagliptin varied more, from 0.206406 to 0.334869. Prefix concentration persisted: 141 of the 290 new batches emitted all ten molecules from one prefix, versus 76 of 145 originally.

molecular.headline: Broad aromatic scaffolds and accessible amines, with unassigned stereochemistry and a tail of oversized or chemically awkward structures
molecular.overall_character: This assessment covers the supplied seed-1 and seed-2 trajectories. The comparison baseline is seed 0 of the same Algorithm Node, not a different parent implementation. All five tasks have trajectories, each with 600 evaluated records including 580 optimizer proposals. The output spans linked and fused azaarenes, indoles, sulfur heterocycles, saturated nitrogen rings, cyclic carbonyl compounds, sulfonamides, ethers and occasional peptide-like or nucleotide-like structures. Structural variety is broad; the chemistry has not collapsed to one ring family. The digest reports ring-closure indicators in 98.79–99.66% of proposals and aromatic-atom indicators in 96.72–97.93%. These are fractions of SMILES containing those features, not aromatic atom fractions or measurements of molecular shape. Mean SMILES lengths are 38.1–40.2 characters, but the full trajectories also contain much larger structures. Conventional medicinal-chemistry frameworks predominate, supporting plausible apparent makeability, while highly extended structures and reactive or unusual functional groups make overall drug-likeness moderate. Makeability, stability and biological selectivity have not been experimentally established. Explicit stereocentre markers are absent from every proposal set, even though several high-scoring saturated-ring structures have stereogenic carbons. This is missing stereochemical specification, not absence of saturated or three-dimensional ring systems. Formal-charge counters likewise do not measure how many neutral SMILES contain protonatable amines. The recurring gaps concern chemical specification, size and polarity balance, and the arrangement of functional groups, rather than an inability to generate rings or aromatic heteroatoms.

per_task.generated_character: The higher-scoring output consists of medium-sized phenyl/azaaryl assemblies: an N-ethyl triazole with a cyanophenyl group and a carboxybenzyl thioether, a methylsulfone-substituted linked heteroaromatic system, a chroman carboxylic acid attached to an aminopyrimidine, and morpholine-substituted fused azaarenes. Indole, benzimidazolone, ether, amide and hydroxamic-acid chemistry also appears. These are mostly recognizable, apparently makeable small-molecule frameworks. The proposal set has mean SMILES length 39.6, ring-closure rate 0.9966 and aromatic-atom rate 0.9759; its extremes include very large peptide-like, phosphorous-containing and multiply fused structures.
liabilities: The best molecule contains a thioether, and another high-scoring example contains a hydroxamic acid; these introduce oxidation-state or metal-binding questions that the supplied score does not resolve.

The final sulfur-rich example combines a thioester with an unusual hydrogen-bearing, multiply bonded sulfur linkage. Its chemical form and synthetic route are less straightforward than the conventional heteroaryl examples.
Long peptide-like chains and heavily decorated phosphorous-containing structures introduce large size, flexibility or dense polar functionality without retaining favorable scores.
missing_features: Consistent retention of the moderate size and aromatic/polar balance present in the high-scoring structures; both oversized extensions and underdecorated saturated frameworks remain in the evaluated output.
Stereochemical specification at the substituted chroman carbon is absent. The trajectories do not establish whether resolving that configuration would change this objective.

A uniquely missing target motif cannot be identified from these chemically different high scorers; their scores support more precise control of attachment patterns, not a claim that an entire ring or functional-group class is absent.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The triazole/carboxybenzyl thioether scores 0.4588223100704468 and the linked heteroaryl methylsulfone scores 0.4467986735542579. Their distinct polar groups show that no single terminal group explains the high end. The initial indole carboxamide already scores 0.3051048083696145. The seed-0 baseline best was a compact aryl/pyridyl thiourea at 0.3949199041196016; the new higher-scoring structures retain an aromatic, moderately sized character while changing the central connectivity. At the low end, both a very large peptide-like chain and the small fully saturated bridged aminoalcohol score 0.0. Thus the observed preference is for a bounded combination of size, aromatic connectivity and polar functionality, rather than simply smaller molecules or more rings. The reported median is 0.011662. A high-scoring proposal at evaluation 297 is followed by a large final phosphoramidate at 1.274785543572214e-22; the last proposals are not a uniformly favorable chemical family.

per_task.generated_character: The high end is rich in linked nitrogen heteroarenes and fused azaarenes, with amino or ether connections, thiophene/thiadiazole rings, and occasional morpholine. The best structure combines an acrylamide, methylthio-substituted pyrimidine, pyridyl ether and benzothiadiazole. Other high-scoring molecules use an aminoethylamino connection to a quinazoline-like core, or hydrazones and sulfonamides. The mean SMILES length is 39.5, ring-closure rate 0.9931 and aromatic-atom rate 0.9759. These generally resemble accessible heteroaromatic screening compounds, although some highly conjugated and extensively linked structures are chemically more demanding.
liabilities: The best molecule carries an electrophilic acrylamide and a thioether. A favorable score does not establish that either reactivity or oxidative stability is acceptable.
Hydrazones and imines among the higher-scoring and late structures leave questions of hydrolytic stability, tautomerism and double-bond geometry.
Some extensively linked aromatic structures provide substantial conjugated surface and limited saturated character; their solubility and conformational behavior are not given.
missing_features: The generator does not consistently preserve the connected azaaryl and amino/ether architecture visible at the high end when varying substituents and ring systems.

More controlled alternatives to the carbon-bonded sulfone arrangements seen at the low end are missing as an interpretable local series. The favorable sulfonamide example prevents a blanket claim that oxidized sulfur should be removed.
No particular missing target decoration or required geometry can be established from these unpaired examples alone.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The acrylamide-containing heteroaryl assembly scores 0.6206976589959546, and the aminoethylamino-linked azaarenes score 0.6115153965366216. The seed-0 best at 0.6060034997980885 was also an amino-linked fused azaarene, bearing a benzoic acid and a fused cyclic ketone. The recurring high-end feature is a connected, nitrogen-rich aromatic architecture with appropriately placed linkers. All six digest worst examples contain carbon-bonded sulfone linkages, including the brominated acrylamide/methylsulfone at 0.2579134792930625 and the methylsulfone indole at 0.2629377264102122. A sulfonamide-containing hydrazone scores 0.5803755601394125, so sulfur oxidation alone is not a sufficient explanation. The initial small alkyl bromide scores 0.5, the median is 0.530123, and the final sulfonylguanidine scores 0.5069001207521131. Those observations also show that a middling score is not evidence of elaborate or desirable chemistry. These are unmatched molecular contrasts, not isolated substituent effects.

per_task.generated_character: The high-scoring structures are medium-sized aromatic compounds with exposed aliphatic amines: arylpiperazines, substituted piperidines and an indanyl secondary amine connected to a fused sulfur/nitrogen heteroarene. Indanone, benzothiazole, indole-like fused systems and flexible alkyl or benzyl spacers provide varied aromatic surroundings. The proposal set remains predominantly ring-containing and aromatic, with rates 0.9966 and 0.9793 and mean SMILES length 38.1. These amine/aryl frameworks are generally synthetically recognizable, but the full output also includes neutral carbonyl-rich heterocycles and heavily halogenated phenols.
liabilities: The high-scoring chlorinated arylpiperazine includes a benzylic chloride, an electrophilic handle that warrants separate chemical assessment despite its score of 0.9375158755153281.

Several late structures accumulate bromine or iodine on phenolic aromatic systems, and one carries an azo linkage; these add substantial halogenation or chemically consequential functionality without approaching the favorable amine-containing examples.
missing_features: Consistent coverage of the exposed aliphatic amine plus aromatic-spacer arrangement is missing from much of the proposal distribution, although the generator clearly can produce it.

Controlled variation of the distance and attachment geometry between the amine and aromatic surfaces is needed to distinguish useful arrangements from the low-scoring basic imidazoline and aminoalcohol examples; basic nitrogen alone is not a sufficient observed feature.
The indanyl secondary amine and more complicated saturated polycycles have unspecified stereochemistry. No stereoisomer comparison is available.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The bromophenyl piperazine joined through a benzyl group to an indanone scores 0.9764936974373054. The indanyl secondary amine scores 0.9382214313583629, and the phenylpropyl-substituted benzothiazolyl piperidine scores 0.9351873161919285. The seed-0 best at 0.9779218035868983 used an indole-linked piperidine and a lactam, retaining an exposed aliphatic amine in a different surrounding scaffold. At the low end, the pyrrolidine nitrogen in a urea-containing sulfonamide is carbonyl-bound and scores 3.086197932883512e-05; an N-acyl piperidine scores 3.408357355512484e-05. These support a distinction between an available basic amine and simply containing nitrogen or a nitrogen ring. Availability is not sufficient: the late imidazoline-substituted phenol scores 0.008098003998695502, and an aromatic aminoalcohol scores 0.06735006158434823. The median is 0.005833, and a final halogenated naphthol scores 0.008710857097960593, showing that much of the evaluated chemistry lacks the favorable combination of basicity, spacing and aromatic environment.

per_task.generated_character: The high-scoring output combines aromatic heterocycles with cyclic carbonyl or sulfonamide chemistry: a benzofused nitrogen-containing dione bearing an N-sulfonyl azepane, a cyanoimidazole linked through an acylpiperazine to benzodioxole, sulfonylpiperazines, xanthine-like polycarbonyl rings and morpholine-containing structures. This is broader than a single fused-ring series. Mean SMILES length is 40.2, with ring-closure rate 0.9879 and aromatic-atom rate 0.9672. Most examples are conventional small-molecule combinations with plausible synthetic building blocks; the low end also contains acyclic sulfur-rich fragments, amino-acid-like structures and long flexible chains.
liabilities: The higher-scoring hydrazone example introduces an unspecified C=N geometry and a hydrolytic-stability question.

The low-scoring long-chain guanidino/phosphonic-acid structure combines a long flexible hydrophobic segment with strongly polar termini, a very different size and polarity distribution from the favorable compact ring systems.

Carbonyl- or sulfonyl-bound piperazine nitrogens should not be assumed to provide the basicity of unsubstituted aliphatic amines; those groups occur among favorable molecules here, so attenuated basicity is not itself evidence of failure.
missing_features: The output does not show a consistently favorable, precisely arranged combination of aromatic rings, cyclic carbonyl or sulfonyl groups and saturated heterocycles; those ingredients are already present separately and in varied combinations.

No specific missing reference-like scaffold or attachment pattern can be inferred from these scores alone. The evidence supports studying related arrangements of existing functional groups rather than asserting that a ring family is unavailable.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The benzofused dione/N-sulfonyl azepane scores 0.1814990197188793 and the acylpiperazine/cyanoimidazole scores 0.17716466781757798. The initial polycarbonyl fused heteroarene already scores 0.1678386594791329. The seed-0 best, an oxazolidinone-linked fused lactam/phenol assembly, scored 0.17994167047030216. The new and baseline high ends therefore contain different scaffolds with overlapping aromatic and cyclic polar features, without a large separation from ordinary starting chemistry. At the low end, a small acyclic N-hydroxythiourea scores 0.0, a long guanidino/phosphonic-acid chain scores 0.015193428136569091, and sulfamide scores 0.02668612498071339. Aromatic ring architecture combined with carbonyl/sulfonyl and saturated-ring functionality separates these examples more clearly than heteroatom abundance alone. However, the reported median of 0.109136 and the broad range of high-end scaffolds do not reveal a unique missing substructure.

per_task.generated_character: The higher-scoring molecules are compact to medium-sized, phenyl-bearing nitrogen heterocycles with carbonyl, hydroxy or amino functionality. They include a fluorinated fused N-heterocycle with an aminotetrahydrofuran substituent, a triazolone/thioacetamide, a benzyl-substituted polycarbonyl fused heterocycle, and a hydroxyquinolone carboxamide. Other proposals include piperidines, piperazines, amidines and guanidines. Mean SMILES length is 40.1, ring-closure rate 0.9948 and aromatic-atom rate 0.9724. The ordinary heteroaromatic examples are apparently makeable, while large peptide-like chains and nucleotide polyphosphates occupy a very different part of the output.
liabilities: The best aminotetrahydrofuran structure has an N,O-acetal-like attachment and a hydroxy/carbonyl-rich heterocycle, raising chemical-form and stability questions that a SMILES score does not settle.

The high-scoring triazolone/thioacetamide contains a thioether, while late amidines introduce protonation and tautomer questions; these are properties to characterize rather than evidence of measured toxicity.
Large peptide-like and polyphosphate structures combine many polar groups and flexible connections and fall far outside the compact structures associated with the favorable scores.
missing_features: Consistent control of compact size together with the placement and number of polar groups is missing; the output repeatedly reaches both highly extended aromatic structures and peptide/polyphosphate extremes.

The tetrahydrofuran attachment carbon in the best molecule is stereogenic but unspecified. The absence of explicit stereochemistry is observable, whereas an objective benefit from resolving it has not been tested.

A particular missing fluorinated fragment, amine class or target-like connection is not established by the shown scores. Both fluorinated and unhalogenated compounds, and different nitrogen functional states, occur among the favorable examples.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The fluorinated fused heterocycle with hydroxy, carbonyl and aminotetrahydrofuran groups scores 0.3348688435749572. An unhalogenated triazolone/thioacetamide scores 0.25193522359670406, and the fluorobenzyl polycarbonyl heterocycle scores 0.2444857272022064. Thus neither fluorine nor an exposed basic amine is a uniquely supported requirement. The seed-0 best was a tertiary benzylamine bearing azoles at 0.23715698113688108; the seed-2 best is a hydroxyquinolone carboxamide at 0.20640632511413345. These differing favorable chemotypes suggest a restrictive combination of size and polar/aromatic features rather than a single observed motif. The large peptide-like structure and polyphosphate nucleotide score 0.0, while a very extended largely aromatic structure scores 8.786833153590336e-69. Both excessive polar complexity and excessive aromatic extension occur at the low end. Conversely, the small fluorochlorobenzamidine at the end scores only 8.674707650435866e-06, so compactness, halogenation and a basic group are not enough. The digest reports median 0.0, including many extremely small positive scores in the full trajectories.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every task digest reports stereocentre_rate 0.0 over 580 optimizer proposals. Digest examples include a substituted chroman carboxylic acid, an indanyl secondary amine and an aminotetrahydrofuran-containing high scorer, each with a stereogenic carbon left unspecified. Saturated and fused ring systems are present, so the gap is specification of their configuration.
transferable_gaps.gap: Stereogenic saturated structures are emitted without explicit stereochemical specification.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide the ability to specify and preserve stereochemistry at eligible centers and to compare those chemical identities using current task-local observations. These trajectories do not establish whether the absence originates in vocabulary, preprocessing or sampling, and they do not prove that the observed objectives distinguish stereoisomers.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Mean proposal SMILES lengths stay between 38.1 and 40.2, but task maxima range from 93 to 123 characters. The digest includes zero-scoring extended peptide-like and polyphosphate structures and extremely low-scoring large aromatic assemblies alongside compact high-scoring heterocycles. A small saturated bridged aminoalcohol also scores zero, so reducing size indiscriminately is not supported.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently control size and polarity while retaining an otherwise useful aromatic scaffold.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Enable controlled changes to scaffold extension, linker length and the number of appended polar groups around observed favorable molecules. Let local feedback determine the useful size and polarity range; a universal preference for the smallest or least polar molecules would contradict the output.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A benzyl/arylpiperazine scores 0.9764936974373054, whereas a urea-bound pyrrolidine scores 3.086197932883512e-05 and a basic imidazoline-containing aromatic compound scores 0.008098003998695502. Elsewhere, N-acyl and N-sulfonyl cyclic amines occur among the digest high scorers. The generator already supplies these functional states, but the examples do not form controlled comparisons of basicity and spacing.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output lacks systematic local variation of amine availability and its geometric relation to neighboring aromatic groups.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support related molecular variants that change amine acylation or sulfonylation, spacer length or attachment position while preserving the surrounding core. Use task-local scores to learn which functional relationship is useful; neither universal amine addition nor universal removal of carbonyl/sulfonyl groups is justified.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Digest high scorers include an acrylamide/thioether structure at 0.6206976589959546 and a benzylic-chloride-containing arylpiperazine at 0.9375158755153281. A late proposal contains an unusual hydrogen-bearing, multiply bonded sulfur linkage and scores 5.7691712191843035e-08. Hydrazones, imines and complex phosphorous-containing structures also occur. These are observed reactivity or chemical-form questions, not measured toxicity outcomes.
transferable_gaps.gap: Favorable scaffold chemistry is not consistently accompanied by tractable, chemically well-specified functional groups.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make conservative functional-group and linkage alternatives available within related scaffold families, and retain explicit chemical-form information where meaningful. Evaluate alternatives using local observations and separate chemical tractability from the numerical objective; do not assume every electrophile, sulfur group or ionizable center requires exclusion.

nodes.method_name: ChemTS: UCT-guided SMILES prefix search with a frozen rollout prior
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in [ChemTS](https://arxiv.org/html/1710.00616v1): train a compact autoregressive SMILES model solely on the supplied unlabeled corpus during preparation, then freeze it. For each independent objective, maintain a fresh prefix tree whose nodes hold visit counts and observed returns. Initialize its statistics from the supplied observations. Select prefixes through upper-confidence tree search, expand them using the frozen model's next-token distribution, and generate complete molecules by stochastic continuation. Backpropagate accepted oracle scores through the corresponding paths after feedback. Generate further continuations until the evaluator-announced batch contains distinct canonical structures. This is an expanding generative tree, with no corpus ranking or fixed molecular candidate set. The hypothesis is that sharing each scarce reward across its visited prefixes directs subsequent continuations toward promising molecular families quickly enough to improve the mean of independent final Top-1 scores. The root adapts tree statistics; it does not update neural parameters with rewards. The paper supports this search mechanism, but its larger, time-limited experiments do not establish performance under this benchmark's scarce feedback. Learning a useful rollout prior within permitted preparation remains an empirical prerequisite.

approach.method_basis: The Parent learns a recurrent SMILES prior from an unlabeled corpus, then starts a fresh policy for each objective. After each accepted batch it trains on the current best-scoring half plus a uniform sample of older elites from a memory of the thirty-two highest-scoring accepted identities. It preserves each molecule's original accepted SMILES and score. The policy log probability for each training sequence is fitted toward that sequence's frozen prior log probability plus sixty times its observed reward, with equal row weights. Novel molecules are then sampled directly from the adapted policy and checked for chemical validity and canonical duplicates.
approach.novelty: Replay a historical molecule through an equivalent SMILES traversal instead of always repeating its original string. The same accepted molecule and score remain the training example, while the traversal changes which token contexts carry that feedback. Current elites still use their original strings, and memory membership and sampling stay intact. This tests a different route to transfer from the siblings that changed replay selection or core retention. It also differs from alternative-string prior preparation: the prior stays unchanged, and views receive only the historical molecule's actual accepted reward during online adaptation. One deterministic equivalent view is reserved from training for each molecule so that transfer can be checked beyond the strings fitted.

nodes.hypothesis: Replace the original serialization of each uniformly selected historical elite with a deterministic accepted-identity-equivalent atom-rooted SMILES training view, preserving its original accepted record and score, while reserving one distinct equivalent view from training and keeping current elites, memory membership, the frozen prior and the inherited online loss unchanged.

finding_summary.headline: Equivalent replay improves unseen spellings while weakening original support and final scores
finding_summary.insights: The new spellings entered the loss and transferred some fitting benefit to excluded spellings, so absence of exposure or complete failure of sequence transfer cannot explain the score loss. That transfer came with weaker support for the originally accepted strings, rather than better fitting across all representations. Keeping the prior fixed did not prevent this tradeoff. The original reward is preserved, but the inherited target depends on the spelling: the new views lower its value by about 47.86 log-likelihood units on average, and reduce positive, unattainable targets from 461 to 64 on the same accepted examples. Thus improved view fit combines different token contexts with different numeric targets; it does not establish representation-independent reward learning. Fewer duplicate samples and somewhat broader core coverage also fail to establish useful molecular transfer. The generated molecules still include recognizable carbonyl and cyclic-amine families, but changed leading arrangements do not consistently improve objectives, and the chemistry assessment retains stereochemical and reactive-group gaps. The experiment confirms a working view-replay and held-out-transfer mechanism while rejecting its overall utility under this panel.
finding_summary.results: All 2100 historical replay exposures before subsequent sampling used verified new spellings of the same accepted molecules. Their gradients differed measurably from original-string replay in all 420 eligible updates. Reserved equivalent strings, never used for training, improved their mean squared target error from 202.59 to 169.07; every task and seed showed this improvement. However, original historical strings worsened from 144.14 to 152.33, and their average likelihood fell in every session. Duplicate draws dropped from 30.11% to 14.07%, but raw chemical validity fell from 90.43% to 87.24%. The three-seed macro mean declined from 0.507554 to 0.493167, a paired loss of 0.014387 against the required gain of 0.002. Deco_hop improved in all seeds; sitagliptin declined in all seeds.
