molecular.headline: Conventional amide and cyclic-amine families coexist with polyfluorinated amidoximes, polynitro aromatics and incomplete stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: All five tasks have complete supplied trajectories for three seeds, with 900 evaluated molecules and 870 optimizer proposals per task. All 4,350 optimizer-proposal SMILES parse with RDKit. The dominant chemistry is ring-rich and recognizable: aryl/heteroaryl amides, pyrazole carboxamides, sulfonamides, cyclic amines, hydrazone or azine connections, and heteroaromatic carbonyl systems. Median proposal heavy-atom counts are 23, 26, 26, 23 and 24 in fixed task order; median ring count is three throughout. Digest aromatic-token rates are 0.9437-0.9920 and ring-closure rates 0.9747-0.9966. The main limitations are therefore not absent rings or aromatic atoms. There are 460-762 distinct nonchiral Murcko scaffolds per task, but leading molecules concentrate in several local chemical families. Most connectivity is synthetically plausible, with specific qualification for repeated nitro substitution, amidoxime/hydrazone geometry, occasional isocyanides and chloroalkyl appendages. In the most nitro-rich session, the digest charged rate of 0.2586 includes nitro and other internally charge-separated groups: 216 proposals contain nitro groups, but only five have nonzero net formal charge. Relative to the parent, familiar carbonyl and cyclic-amine chemistry persists, while different positional arrangements and nitrogen-linker families dominate individual high-score sets. No proposal contains assigned stereocentres; 184, 62, 414, 231 and 308 proposals contain an unassigned centre in task order. These structural observations do not establish synthesis, physical properties, stability or experimental activity.

per_task.generated_character: The two highest molecules are compact alpha-aryl, alpha-pyridyl acetamides with an N-pyridyl amide substituent. They have three aromatic six-membered rings, 23 or 24 heavy atoms and an unassigned central stereocentre. Another family is an N-aryl pyrazole carboxamide, while much of the remaining leading digest consists of azine-linked thiazolidinone-like carbonyl rings carrying two haloaryl regions. Those latter examples contain a C=N-N=C connection whose configuration is not specified. The parent led with substituted indole carboxamides; the current highest family rearranges its aromatic and carbonyl groups around a stereogenic acyclic carbon instead. N-N=C proposals number 101 versus 34 in the parent, consistent with the greater visibility of nitrogen-linked imine chemistry in the current output.
liabilities: C=N-N=C and related imine connections introduce E/Z and tautomeric questions not resolved by the displayed scores.
Several equal-score haloaryl variants increase mass without demonstrating a benefit in the visible gradient.
Four proposals exceed 50 heavy atoms, and bulky multiply linked structures dominate the very low-score tail despite familiar individual functional groups.
missing_features: The highest acetamides do not specify their stereogenic central carbon, so the useful three-ring/polar arrangement has not been proposed as distinct configurations.

The leading region has limited chemically distinct alternatives beyond acetamide, pyrazole and azine-linked analogue families; repeated halogen substitutions do not address the missing precise placement of polar groups.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The methylphenyl/pyridyl acetamide scores 0.454082 and the methoxyphenyl counterpart 0.453163. In the latter framework, replacing the alpha-pyridyl ring with phenyl gives 0.375059 in the terminal digest, supporting the value of that ring-nitrogen placement within this local arrangement. The pyrazole carboxamide reaches 0.436818. Numerous halo-substitution variants of the azine/thiazolidinone family all score 0.413359, so their extra chlorine or fluorine changes do not establish a useful gradient. By contrast, very large peptide-like, polycyclic or extended aromatic assemblies are as low as approximately 2.93e-67, while a simple arylsulfonamide terminal molecule is about 3.66e-08. The useful association is organized moderate-size aromatic/carbonyl chemistry, not either maximal size or an isolated polar group.

per_task.generated_character: The highest structure is a compact hydroxy aza-fused aromatic sulfonamide bearing a difluoroanilino group: 24 heavy atoms, three aromatic rings and molecular mass 353.310. Other leaders include polyfluorinated aryl amidines, amidoximes and aminoheteroaryl systems. One high example is an isocyanide-bearing multi-heteroaryl molecule, and another has four nitro groups across an aromatic ether assembly. The whole proposal set has median 26 heavy atoms, three aromatic rings and a very low median sp3-carbon fraction of about 0.0833. There are 216 nitro-containing proposals and 102 O-N=C matches, the latter reflecting abundant oxime/amidoxime chemistry. Parent leaders included aromatic acylhydrazones and fluorinated heteroaryl systems; current N-N=C proposals fall from 181 to eight while the displayed imine chemistry shifts toward amidines and amidoximes. These motifs are synthetically recognizable, but repeated nitro and fluorine decoration narrows their apparent medicinal-chemistry quality.
liabilities: Polynitro aromatic systems and the isocyanide example introduce reactivity or stability questions that differ from ordinary amides and sulfonamides; valid graph representations do not resolve them.
The charged-string rate should not be interpreted as a population of ionic molecules: only five proposals have nonzero net formal charge, while 216 contain nitro groups.
Strong aromatic bias and extensive aryl fluorination provide little saturated shape in many leaders, and seven proposals exceed 50 heavy atoms.
missing_features: The leading output lacks broad stable alternatives that reproduce the useful polar/aromatic arrangement without relying so heavily on dense fluorination, amidoxime variants or repeated nitro substitution.
Amidine and amidoxime C=N configurations are unspecified, and their tautomeric or ionization behavior is not established by the supplied scores.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The compact difluoroanilino sulfonamide scores 0.612372, a more heavily fluorinated aryl amidine 0.606725 and an aminoheteroaryl compound 0.606682. These show that maximal fluorination or aromatic expansion is not necessary for the highest displayed score. Within a specific amidoxime pair, a more fluorinated aryl region scores 0.602841 versus 0.571754 for its less fluorinated terminal counterpart, supporting a local substituent effect without a universal fluorine rule. The polynitro aromatic ether scores 0.598691 and the isocyanide-bearing example 0.604700, so these liabilities are tolerated. Low-score benzyl, alkyl or cyclic sulfones lie near 0.262-0.302 despite sulfur, oxygen and aromatic rings; their different attachment context matters.

per_task.generated_character: The highest molecule joins an amino-oxazole-like aromatic ring to a substituted cyclohexane, an ethyl linker and an arylpiperazine. It has 27 heavy atoms, four rings, two aromatic rings and molecular mass 372.488, with unspecified stereochemistry in the substituted saturated ring. Most other leaders are arylpiperazines or seven-membered diazepanes linked to diarylmethyl or aryl/cyclohexyl regions, often bearing bromine or multiple chlorines. These are recognizable basic-amine medicinal-chemistry families. Parent leaders also had arylpiperazine and fused-amine architectures, including indole-linked examples; the current leading neighborhood emphasizes saturated cyclohexyl and diarylalkyl arms. Full proposals have median 26 heavy atoms and three rings, but their median score is only 0.027500: the near-ceiling structures do not describe the typical score or all of the generated chemistry.
liabilities: Diarylmethyl arms, long linkers and multiple bromine or chlorine substituents raise mass and conformational freedom without demonstrating a general need in the highest structure.
Several leaders approach or exceed molecular mass 500, while the highest displayed molecule is 372.488.
Eleven proposals exceed 50 heavy atoms and the largest has 88, so otherwise familiar amine chemistry can expand into much less economical whole molecules.
missing_features: The output already reaches useful cyclic-amine arrangements, but those arrangements are inadequately represented across a population whose median score remains 0.027500.

Relative configuration on the substituted cyclohexane and configuration at diaryl/aryl-cyclohexyl centres are unspecified; 414 proposals contain an unassigned stereocentre and no proposal assigns one.
No additional required pharmacophoric group can be inferred from the near-ceiling examples; precise alternative arrangements are better supported than prescribed extra substituents.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The aminoheteroaryl/cyclohexyl piperazine scores 0.999994 and a diarylalkyl diazepane 0.999984. Haloaryl piperazine analogues lie around 0.99, indicating that a basic ring nitrogen positioned between aromatic and saturated hydrophobic regions is productive across several topologies. The top molecule does not require the extensive heavy-halogen decoration of many nearby leaders. Low examples are rich in amide, sulfonamide, nitro or hydrazone functionality, approximately 3.80e-05 to 6.08e-05, with different nitrogen electronics and spatial arrangements. This supports contextual amine presentation rather than nitrogen or ring counts alone. The comparison describes supplied molecular scores and does not establish receptor activity or a universal ring-amine requirement.

per_task.generated_character: Leading molecules include arylsulfonylpiperazines, methylenedioxybenzyl piperazines and fused lactam/indole structures. The highest example is a piperazine bearing an ethoxy/methoxy arylsulfonyl group and a bis-amide side chain, with 33 heavy atoms, three rings and molecular mass 479.530. A much simpler methylphenylsulfonyl N-methylpiperazine has only 17 heavy atoms and two rings. A methylenedioxybenzyl N-methylpiperazine also has 17 heavy atoms. These are plausible conventional chemotypes. The parent already had a simple N-methyl arylsulfonylpiperazine and fused carbonyl alternatives among its leaders, so the principal chemistry is shared while the attachment patterns vary. Full proposals have median 23 heavy atoms and three rings, with 736 distinct nonchiral Murcko scaffolds.
liabilities: Acylated and sulfonylated piperazine nitrogens are electronically different from free tertiary amines; the leading family cannot be summarized as simply adding more basic centres.
Large bis-amide or fused-ring appendages increase synthetic and physical-property burdens while remaining close in score to compact examples.
Five proposals exceed 50 heavy atoms, and exceptionally long alkyl chains appear at the low end of the observed distribution.
missing_features: The leading repertoire needs more precise alternatives in aromatic/piperazine attachment and polar-linker placement; larger elaborations provide little visible separation from simple structures.
Configuration remains unspecified in chiral fused carbonyl alternatives and in 231 proposals overall, although the simplest piperazines are achiral.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The larger bis-amide/sulfonylpiperazine scores 0.208126, the simple arylsulfonyl N-methylpiperazine 0.207671 and the methylenedioxybenzyl N-methylpiperazine 0.204569. Their close scores show that the added aromatic ring, amides and size of the largest example are not clearly necessary. These structures associate organized aromatic, cyclic-nitrogen and polar-linker regions with the higher visible scores, but not a unique ionization pattern: the highest piperazine has both nitrogens sulfonylated or acylated, unlike the basic N-methyl alternatives. Small polar species or simple cycloalkyl amines score approximately 0.008-0.029, and very long-chain molecules remain near 0.018-0.020. Adding polarity, basic nitrogen or size alone therefore does not reproduce the useful arrangement.

per_task.generated_character: The highest molecule is a tert-butyl-substituted nitrogen-rich heteroaromatic carbonyl ring attached to a benzamide with a 2-chloroethyl substituent: 23 heavy atoms and two aromatic rings. Other leaders include a benzimidazole/pyrazole-like heteroaryl system bearing an ethyl methylsulfone side chain, a trimethoxyaryl pyridyl acylhydrazone, compact aminoheteroaromatics and nitroaryl thiosemicarbazone-like structures. These are mostly recognizable synthetic families, with specific concerns for the chloroethyl arm, imine geometry and sulfur/nitrogen-chain chemistry. Parent leaders also included fused nitrogen/carbonyl structures and compact polar amides, but the current digest supplies different combinations and sparse moderate-score examples. Full proposals have median 24 heavy atoms and three rings, with 762 nonchiral Murcko scaffolds. The worst displayed molecules include oversized peptide-like, polyfunctional or heavily chlorinated multiaryl assemblies.
liabilities: The primary chloroethyl arm is a possible electrophilic side-chain liability, while nitroaryl and thiosemicarbazone-like examples introduce separate reactivity or stability questions.
Large peptide-like and heavily elaborated aromatic structures can contain many familiar polar groups while giving exactly zero score; eight proposals exceed 50 heavy atoms.
Terminal sulfur/disulfide or highly substituted fused structures add chemistry whose practical stability and physical properties are not established by the trajectories.
missing_features: More precise and broader coverage of compact polar heteroaromatic/carbonyl arrangements is missing even though several viable-looking families are already produced.
Stable alternatives to the chloroethyl and thiosemicarbazone-like features are not demonstrated as matched high-score analogues; the visible data do not establish those liabilities as required.
Hydrazone C=N geometry is unspecified, and no proposal assigns stereocentres despite 308 containing an unassigned centre; many of the displayed leaders themselves are achiral.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The benzamide/heteroaromatic-carbonyl molecule scores 0.268815, the sulfone-substituted heteroaryl molecule 0.233604 and the trimethoxyaryl acylhydrazone 0.229727. Compact aminoheteroaromatic and sulfur-containing alternatives reach roughly 0.18-0.23. Those examples suggest a preference for particular compact polar arrangements without establishing any one mandatory group; the highest chloroethyl substituent is not shown in a matched pair proving its necessity. The large peptide-like and multiaryl molecules are zero or vanishing. The digest median is rounded to 0.0: the full 900-row median is 1.766839397052908e-07 and seven rows are exactly zero. Thus the higher-score chemistry occupies a sparse part of a predominantly very-low-score population, not a population of literal zeros.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A methoxyphenyl/pyridyl acetamide scores 0.453163 while its displayed phenyl-for-pyridyl counterpart scores 0.375059. In another set, conventional cyclic-amine leaders reach near-ceiling scores while typical output has a median of 0.027500 and low examples place nitrogen in amides, sulfonamides or hydrazones. A further leading set includes both a piperazine with acylated/sulfonylated nitrogens and basic N-methylpiperazines at nearly equal scores, showing that useful nitrogen chemistry depends on the surrounding arrangement.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently reproduce the precise placement and electronic context of useful polar groups.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support meaningful alternatives in ring-nitrogen position, amide orientation and linker attachment while preserving the useful structural relationships suggested by feedback. Treat free amines, amide nitrogens, sulfonamide nitrogens, amidines and hydrazones as distinct chemical environments rather than interchangeable nitrogen content.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Per-session nonchiral Murcko scaffold counts range from 460 to 762, yet digest leaders repeat acetamide, azine/thiazolidinone, fluorinated amidoxime or cyclic-amine families. Several haloaryl azine variants have the same score of 0.413359. One structurally diverse session has 762 scaffolds but a full-trajectory median score near 1.77e-07. Meanwhile, 33- and 17-heavy-atom piperazine structures in another session score 0.208126 and 0.207671, illustrating that added size is not necessarily useful coverage.
transferable_gaps.gap: Broad scaffold counts do not provide sufficiently broad coverage of productive, economical chemical families.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide chemically distinct core and linker alternatives that preserve an observed useful arrangement, alongside controlled local variation. Measure chemical breadth through access to productive families and alternatives, rather than more unique graphs, repetitive halogen changes or larger appendages alone.

transferable_gaps.evidence: No assigned stereocentres occur in 4,350 optimizer proposals. The five sessions contain 184, 62, 414, 231 and 308 proposals with unassigned centres. Higher-score examples include alpha-aryl/heteroaryl acetamides, substituted cyclohexyl cyclic amines, diarylalkyl centres and fused lactams. Amidoxime, hydrazone and azine leaders also omit explicit C=N configuration; one session contains 102 O-N=C matches.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator leaves stereogenic centres and configurationally variable nitrogen double bonds unspecified.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Enable chemically consistent, explicitly configured alternatives when a proposed structure has stereocentres or relevant imine geometry, while retaining achiral chemistry. The supplied observations do not identify a preferred unobserved stereoisomer or tautomer, so those possibilities must remain empirically distinguishable.

transferable_gaps.evidence: One session contains 216 nitro-bearing proposals and displays a four-nitro aromatic ether at 0.598691, while its highest structure is a smaller difluoroanilino sulfonamide at 0.612372. An isocyanide and dense fluorinated amidoximes also appear among leaders. Elsewhere, the highest compact benzamide carries a primary chloroethyl arm without a matched example proving that arm necessary. Across sessions, four, seven, eleven, five and eight proposals exceed 50 heavy atoms, and long-chain or peptide-like structures recur among very low or zero scores.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator needs stable and less burdensome alternatives to repeated reactive-group decoration and excessive molecular growth.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Retain access to conventional stable linkers and substituents that realize useful polar arrangements with controlled mass and appendage size. Distinguish potentially reactive nitro-rich, isocyanide, imine-chain and haloalkyl motifs from ordinary aromatic substitution, and avoid treating tolerated chemical burden as evidence that more of it is required.

nodes.method_name: Augmented Hill-Climb with a corpus-trained SMILES policy
nodes.method_thesis: Train a compact autoregressive SMILES prior solely on the supplied unlabeled corpus, then initialize a fresh policy from that prior for each objective. Use the initial observations and each subsequent scored batch to update only its highest-reward sequences with the Augmented Hill-Climb loss: fit policy log likelihood to frozen-prior log likelihood plus scaled observed reward. Sample complete molecules token by token from the updated policy, canonicalize them, and refill invalid or duplicate proposals by further generation. The corpus supplies language training, never a ranked molecular pool. Elite-conditioned policy updates should shift generation toward new high-scoring molecular combinations quickly enough to improve the benchmark's mean final Top-1. This is a small-budget transfer hypothesis, not a claim that published larger-budget gains carry over. The root uses the current scored batch; randomized historical replay is reserved for the first improvement. The anchor's elite augmented-likelihood mechanism is described by [Thomas et al.](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13321-022-00646-z).

approach.method_basis: CMA-ES samples candidate points from a multivariate Gaussian, ranks the ones that come back, and moves the distribution itself rather than any individual point. The mean shifts toward a weighted average of the better samples, the covariance matrix adapts so the Gaussian stretches along directions that have been paying off, and a separate cumulative path controls the overall step size. Applied to molecules, the sampled points are latent vectors and each one is turned into a molecule by a frozen autoencoder decoder before scoring.
approach.novelty: This root commits to a 24-dimensional latent with full covariance adaptation rather than a diagonal approximation, so the Gaussian can learn correlated directions in the latent space. It attaches every observed score to the exact latent sample that generated the molecule, uses descending score rank with logarithmic recombination weights, and carries cumulative evolution paths for both covariance and step size across all fourteen generations of an objective.

nodes.hypothesis: Sample de novo molecules through a frozen deterministic SELFIES VAE decoder from an adaptive multivariate Gaussian, attach observed scores to the exact generating latent samples, and update the Gaussian mean, full covariance, and global step size using descending score ranks, weighted recombination, and cumulative evolution paths.

finding_summary.headline: Full covariance adaptation ran exactly and finished eleventh at 0.303, undone by one objective
finding_summary.insights: The optimizer is correct and its budget is the problem. Fourteen generations of twenty scored offspring is a very short run for an algorithm that spends its early generations learning a covariance, so the distribution barely finishes adapting before the budget ends. Its collapse on drd2_docking is informative in a different way: that objective rewards a compact basic amine, and this node's proposals there average eighty characters, nearly double every other objective on the same node. The Gaussian drifted into a region of latent space that decodes to large lipophilic molecules and covariance adaptation then reinforced that direction. A smaller population with more generations is the obvious change. One seed only.
finding_summary.results: The macro mean of 0.303 places this eleventh of thirteen. The result is bimodal: 0.611 on deco_hop, which is the third best in the round, and 0.443 on zaleplon_mpo, against 0.064 on drd2_docking, which is the second worst any root recorded there. median_2 reached 0.208 and sitagliptin_mpo 0.187. Every mechanism check was exact. All 70 generations used full 24 by 24 covariance matrices with reconstructed rank-one and rank-mu terms, the recomputed learning constants matched, the cumulative path and step-size control were independently reproduced through eigendecomposition of each covariance, and every one of the accepted offspring joined its exact generating latent and score.

molecular.headline: Latent drift into large lipophilic molecules, with aromatic content collapsing on the objectives it loses
molecular.overall_character: The population varies more by objective than any other root, which is what covariance adaptation in a latent space would be expected to produce. Where it does well, aromatic content reaches 86 to 95 percent with molecules around forty to fifty-nine characters. Where it fails, aromatic content drops to 36 and 49 percent and molecules balloon to eighty characters of fluorinated ethers and alkyl chains. Ring closure stays high throughout at 87 to 99 percent, so the decoder is producing closed structures; what changes is whether those rings are aromatic and whether the molecule stays a reasonable size.

liabilities: cyclic imine bridges hydrolyse under physiological conditions
enol ether termini appear throughout and are acid labile
missing_features: halogen substitution, present in under a tenth of proposals
stable ring fusions rather than the imine bridges in the top scorers
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best at 0.443 is a diarylamine fused through an imine into a tricyclic, and it is the node's second strongest objective. The zero scorers are large open chains carrying multiple amide and ester groups, so the latent region here stayed compact where on other objectives it did not.

per_task.generated_character: The node's best objective and third best in the round. Halogenated benzamides linked to fused polyaza aromatics, averaging fifty-nine characters with 94 percent aromatic content and near-total ring closure.

per_task.score_gradient_reading: The top four cluster between 0.595 and 0.611 and all share a substituted benzoate amide joined to a nitrogen-rich fused ring. The bottom of the range drops the fused aromatic for sulfone-bridged enones. Where the latent Gaussian stayed in aromatic territory, this method performs well.

Not one proposal carries the basic amine on a compact aromatic that other roots used to reach above 0.9. The top scorers are large spirocyclic ethers with pendant fluorophenyl chains, which is the wrong region entirely.

liabilities: cross-conjugated ketoamides among the low scorers are reactive
missing_features: molecules positioned between the two similarity targets rather than near one
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best at 0.208 is the third highest on this objective in the round, and it is also the smallest molecule in its own top four, a simple ethoxyphenyl benzodioxole. Scores fall away into open conjugated amides, so compactness and ring content are what the objective is rewarding here.

per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best reaches 0.187 against a median of 0.0001. The top entries are small partially saturated pyridines and acrylamides, while the zero scorers are large terpenoid and steroid-like polycycles with long alkyl chains, which is the same latent drift toward lipophilic bulk seen on the objective it lost.

transferable_gaps.evidence: On the objective it loses worst, proposals average eighty characters against thirty-six to fifty-nine on the same node's other objectives, with aromatic content falling to 49 percent and long perfluoroalkyl chains dominating the top of the range.
transferable_gaps.gap: the sampling distribution drifts into large lipophilic regions and then reinforces the drift
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Adapting a covariance on ranked samples amplifies whatever direction the early generations happened to favour, so a bad early drift becomes self-reinforcing rather than self-correcting. A bound on the sampled region, or a restart when the population's character shifts, is what this asks for.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Each objective completed exactly fourteen generations of twenty scored offspring, while a full 24 by 24 covariance with rank-one and rank-mu updates needs far more to become informative.
transferable_gaps.gap: the search has too few generations to finish adapting its covariance
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Spending a fixed budget on twenty samples per generation buys covariance estimates that never converge. Fewer samples per generation and more generations would let the adaptation mechanism actually do its work within the same number of evaluations.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The second and third highest-scoring molecules on one objective each carry three or four consecutive N=C linkages in a single chain, and similar chains appear throughout that population.
transferable_gaps.gap: the generator writes chains of consecutive imine bonds
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The decoder can repeat an imine token indefinitely because nothing checks that the resulting chain is a real functional group. Capping consecutive heteroatom double bonds at emission removes these without constraining the latent search.

nodes.method_name: CMA-ES: covariance adaptation through a frozen molecular decoder
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the optimizer in CMA-ES: sample a multivariate Gaussian, rank evaluated samples, move its mean by weighted recombination, and adapt covariance and step size using selected displacements and cumulative evolution paths. [Hansen, Sections 1-4](https://arxiv.org/html/1604.00772v2) describes this mechanism. For the molecular transfer, train a compact SELFIES VAE solely on the permitted unlabeled corpus and freeze its encoder and deterministic decoder. Each objective starts with fresh Gaussian and path state. Encodings of high-scoring supplied molecules may initialize geometric search locations, but their scores must not be assigned to nonidentical reconstructions. Generate latent samples, decode them into new molecules, and attach accepted oracle feedback to the exact latent sample that produced each submitted structure. Assemble scored generations while respecting the evaluator-announced batching, then update the Gaussian from descending observed-score ranks. Reject invalid or duplicate structures locally and continue de novo decoding. The corpus trains a generator and never supplies a ranked molecular library. The hypothesis is that learning correlated latent displacements directly from successful generations can uncover improving combinations without first estimating an objective surrogate, increasing the mean of independent final Top-1 scores. Useful decoder support and covariance adaptation within scarce feedback are empirical prerequisites; continuous-domain performance is not evidence that decoded molecular landscapes will behave similarly.

approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from accepted high-scoring molecules. It selects breeding parents by score band, then either makes a local mutation walk or joins connected fragments from two parents. Crossover independently cuts non-ring single bonds, usually retaining the larger first fragment and the smaller donor fragment; an optional finishing mutation can follow. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled, while ordinary mutation continuation remains active. Stable canonical identity and duplicate checks form fresh surplus pools. A Gaussian process trained on accepted scores uses counts of local molecular environments and generalized Tanimoto similarity; correlated posterior draws select which pool members receive evaluations. Accepted offspring update both the archive and breeding population. This Parent retains the original unconditioned donor rule.
approach.novelty: Construct donors with reciprocal local attachment correspondence, excluding a cut from that conditional distribution when its valid immediate product exactly reproduces either generating parent. Keep the original relative cut weights, retain invalid alternatives under the existing failure rules, and fall back to the original donor draw when no conditional support remains. The preceding compatible-donor sibling often rebuilt a parent and relied on finishing mutation for novelty; it exposed some useful distinct recombinants but lowered final scores. This follow-up starts again from the unchanged Parent and revises that one construction law. It differs from selecting similar whole parents, preserving every first-parent ring, rejecting constructed mismatches, or changing posterior allocation or mutation continuation. It tests whether removing immediate parent copies exposes useful recombination, with no assumption that distinctness itself improves chemistry or endpoints.

nodes.hypothesis: Within reciprocal-compatible donor support, exclude cuts whose valid immediate product equals either generating parent, renormalize the inherited physical-cut and orientation masses, and use the original unconditioned donor law when revised support is empty or inapplicable.

finding_summary.headline: Copy exclusion exposes more distinct recombinants, but every seed mean falls
finding_summary.insights:
Removing immediate parent copies did expose a real, useful recombination channel, but solving that allocation obstacle did not make this donor refinement beneficial. Most crossover attempts still used inherited fallback, and more distinct evaluations did not preserve the complete search quality. This complete panel therefore supports a negative contribution from the revised donor law under the tested composition. It preserves the earlier negative compatibility-only result and the separate evidence that crossover itself contributes positively; it cannot isolate the incremental exclusion effect by treating the earlier sibling as the code Parent.

The chemical assessment makes clear why string distinctness is an incomplete target: evaluated descendants include very large repeated assemblies and difficult heterocycles, alongside useful compact amines and amides. A 110-heavy-atom repeated leader and a poorly scoring halogen-rich size tail coexist with stronger compact alternatives. These are observed limitations of selected chemistry, not proof that size or any one bond caused the loss. Local correspondence omits stereochemistry and remote functional relationships, and later mutations can change the matched environment.

The remaining attribution gap is which changed ancestors, pool competition and accepted feedback led to the lower endpoints; unselected previews supply no counterfactual scores. Invalid-only and whole-fragment/exception branches must also remain distinct: atom-limit failures were naturally observed, while other failure controls were synthetic or source-only. The bounded follow-up has now returned another endpoint loss, so its registered review condition is met without turning the result into a broad anti-crossover, validity or safety conclusion.
finding_summary.results:
The registered exclusion worked on 747 states with both removable parent-copy mass and remaining support. On those same states, the earlier compatible-donor law would allocate an average 47.20% probability to a valid parent copy; the revised conditional law allocated zero. Independent reconstruction found no weight, predicate, sampling or preview/actual discrepancy. Compatible atom-limit products kept their probability mass: 139 were actually selected and failed through the inherited checks. Empty support remained common: 11,911 attempts had no compatible orientation and 18,031 were emptied by removing copies, so both used the original donor fallback.

The conditioned channel produced 4,459 valid immediate products distinct from both parents, 3,408 pooled descendants, 356 evaluations and 134 final survivors. Of the 356 evaluated descendants, 280 were pure crossovers and 76 had finishing mutation; 80 beat their best generating parent, 32 improved the incumbent and 264 later served as parents. Across all branches, distinct-immediate crossover evaluations increased from 1,368 to 1,610 and pure crossover from 961 to 1,122. Fallback still supplied 70 evaluated products made novel only after copying a parent and then mutating it. Coverage remained uneven: median seed 0 pooled 23 distinct conditioned products but evaluated none; seeds 1 and 2 evaluated 13 and 14.

All 15 task runs completed. Mean final score fell from 0.595670 to 0.493017, a paired change of -0.102653 against the required +0.002. Seed changes were -0.066514, -0.030336 and -0.211109; ten of fifteen task-seed endpoints declined and five improved. Seed population SD rose from 0.026593 to 0.074022. More local parent beats, 695 versus 629, accompanied fewer incumbent gains, 249 versus 258, and weaker endpoints.

molecular.headline: Distinct recombinants include large repeated assemblies and strained heterocycles; compact amine and amide counterexamples remain
molecular.overall_character: The complete Child n-bddb1dbe8e32 panel is paired with code Parent n-62daf219c70a on Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2 under the supplied frozen profile: child_complete=true and paired_complete=true, with no profile mismatches. All thirty supplied trajectory files and corresponding Search logs were read; no trajectory or task is missing. Each node has 4,500 recorded evaluations, including 4,350 optimizer proposals, with 900 records and 870 optimizer proposals per task. The protocol reports means 0.49301691876777937 and 0.5956696497334577 for Child and Parent. These supplied outcomes and the differing runtimes do not establish activation or identify a chemical cause of the change. The evaluated output spans indole/azaindole carboxamides, very large repeated aza-aromatic dione assemblies, crowded oxygen/nitrogen polycycles, cyclic and flexible aryl amines, heavily halogenated ester/ketone assemblies, bridged nitrogen-carbonyl systems and fluorinated imino/carbonyl heterocycles. Optimizer median heavy-atom counts in fixed task order are 25, 33, 38, 32 and 27, versus Parent 25, 33, 31, 30 and 27. The common median of 33 in the second task hides a large tail: Child mean is 46 heavy atoms versus Parent 33.277011494252875, and one seed leader has 110 heavy atoms. Child ring-closure-string rates span 0.9655 to 0.9805 and aromatic-string rates 0.9598 to 0.9736. These count molecules bearing text features, not fractions of aromatic atoms or perceived ring counts. Ring and aromatic content are rich, with moderate diversity across seeds but recurring local families. Synthetic plausibility remains questionable and drug-likeness weak overall: conventional amines and amides coexist with N-halogen/O-halogen bonds, peroxides, crowded bridges, unusual aromatic-labelled rings and excessive assembly size. No task has explicit charge or stereocentre markers in the digest. Protonatable amines and potentially stereogenic centres are nevertheless present; neutral notation does not prove absent basicity. Read-only RDKit 2023.09.6 size and ring readings in .slots/r0017-01-improve-L01/molecular/trajectory_chemistry_audit.json do not establish synthesis, conformation, stability or biological activity. The full trajectories, rather than only digest final_molecules from the last seed, support the seed-level comparisons below. Actual output provenance is separately joined in .slots/r0017-01-improve-L01/molecular/donor_exposure_audit.json. Across 34,540 Child crossover requests, 4,598 use conditioned support; 4,459 yield a valid immediate product distinct from both generating parents, 3,408 reach the temporary pool, 356 are emitted and evaluated, and 134 remain in the final populations. Of those 356 evaluated descendants, 280 have only crossover in their recorded operator list; the others include finishing mutation. Across all crossover branches, 1,610 evaluated products have distinct immediate identities and 70 start as a parent copy and become novel after finishing mutation, compared with 1,368 and 124 in the Parent. Parent immediate identities are reconstructed from the first finishing-mutation source or the unchanged raw checker identity; Parent cut/support receipts are absent, so its conditional, support-empty and whole-fragment exposures cannot be reconstructed from these logs. Child support is empty before exclusion on 11,911 attempts and emptied by copy exclusion on 18,031 attempts; these invoke inherited donor construction. No Child whole-fragment path was observed. Compatible preview entries include 24,600 confirmed valid parent copies excluded from conditional support and 753 atom-limit entries retained in support. Invalid-product and preview-exception statuses were not observed; their retained-support rule remains outside observed exposure. Thus the declared exclusion is only of confirmed valid immediate parent copies, not a general validity, global-novelty, scaffold-distance or chemical-quality guarantee. Unchosen previews have no scores and are not pool or evaluated molecules. All retained statements use observed feedback plus a score/serial retention replay checked against every batch receipt; ancestry is not endpoint attribution. The prior compatible-donor variant n-eb61315a5619 remains negative evidence: its supplied paired mean change was -0.020270634588430703, with ten task/seed decreases and five increases, despite real distinct recombinants and later useful descendants. Its absent informative evaluations in one objective did not establish absent unchosen support. The reused n-7ba291681388 predicate compares source-graph endpoint atom types and non-cut heavy-neighbor bond/type context, excluding hydrogen, isotope and stereochemical information. It supplies no complete functional-group or geometry preservation guarantee. That L07 gate evidence is incomplete, and the n-32ac3137615b continuation-composition mapping remains partial; neither establishes full-composition equivalence or transferable efficacy here. The gaps below preserve these conditions and counterexamples rather than assigning a descendant score to an individual cut.

nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from accepted, scored survivors. It keeps the highest-scoring molecules in score and admission order, chooses breeding parents from high-ranked score bands, and builds fresh structures through connected-fragment crossover and local atom and bond mutations. The first parent supplies the ordinary mutation source or the usually larger crossover core; a separately drawn partner supplies the usually smaller graft. Ordinary multistep mutation and optional crossover finishing remain active, while direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled. Canonical identity checks form a fresh surplus pool. A Gaussian process fitted to the complete task-local accepted-score archive uses counts of molecular environments and generalized Tanimoto similarity; correlated posterior draws choose pool members for evaluation. Accepted offspring update both the model and the live breeding population.
approach.novelty: Remove unequal rank probabilities only from the first-parent draw, while preserving exactly the molecules that this draw can already select. The partner keeps its original score-band rule and exclusion of the chosen first molecule. The earlier control made both roles uniform on their original supports, and another also admitted previously unsupported survivors; neither identifies the first role separately. A balanced first-parent scheduler preserved rank preferences but changed dependence between draws, so it addresses a different question. This control keeps independent requests and changes only first-parent rank preference. The prediction is weaker average source quality and possibly lower final scores; the experiment will determine that role's conditional contribution, including any null or beneficial removal result.

nodes.hypothesis: Remove nonuniform rank weighting only from each actual first-parent request by sampling uniformly over its exact original positive support after the inherited passive band draw, while retaining the original active score-quantile law and identity exclusion for every crossover-partner request.

finding_summary.headline: First-parent rank preference contributes: its removal lowers mean final Top-1 by 0.072496
finding_summary.insights:
The result localizes useful rank preference to the first-parent role while the crossover partner keeps its original law. Earlier removal from both roles could not establish that distinction. This is positive conditional contribution of first-parent rank weights in the tested composition and three-seed panel; it does not determine the partner’s contribution or permit subtraction of the shared-baseline controls into independent effects. The first parent supplies both ordinary mutation and crossover cores, so their separate values remain open.

More local wins did not mean better search. Strict best-parent beats rose from 629 to 819 and distinct accepted offspring later reused rose from 2,401 to 2,511, but mean best-parent score fell from 0.470456 to 0.372509 and mean offspring score from 0.385256 to 0.303045. Sequential incumbent gains fell from 258 to 237, with mean positive gain falling from 0.022510 to 0.019917. The easier parent reference explains why win counts alone would misread the outcome. Molecular inspection finds abundant rings, aromaticity and recognizable amine/carbonyl arrangements alongside reactive attachments and unresolved geometry and stereochemistry. Larger, decorated families did not consistently reproduce the Parent’s useful compact arrangements, but conventional-bond high-scoring counterexamples remain. Those associations narrow the search-quality problem without establishing a chemical cause of the loss. The fixed first-parent control now has an informative answer; support-only value, chemical mediation, the partner-only control and whole-foundation contribution remain open.
finding_summary.results:
Every one of 74,353 first-parent requests preserved the original eligible molecules while changing their probabilities; 71,068 actual identities differed from the inherited choice on the same random state. All 33,811 partner requests retained their original conditional law. Expected first-parent score on the actual populations fell from 0.359600 to 0.334474, and expected topness fell from 0.884224 to 0.755392. Changed first choices reached 3,926 of 4,350 accepted offspring; 2,211 of those offspring later bred. Full accepted-score learning, bounded greedy survival, ordinary graph transformations and all 435 complete candidate-pool selections remained active.

Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.595670 to 0.523174, a paired change of -0.072496 against the registered 0.002 scale. Seed macro changes were -0.156631, -0.029176 and -0.031680. Eleven of fifteen endpoints declined. Four improved: zaleplon seeds 0 and 2 (+0.075655 and +0.010925), median similarity seed 1 (+0.013577), and sitagliptin seed 1 (+0.124636). Four task means declined; zaleplon rose by 0.001980. Macro population SD increased from 0.026593 to 0.041376. All task runs completed with their full oracle budgets and no posterior fallback.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic families retain reactive attachments and unspecified stereochemistry; larger structures do not ensure better scores
molecular.overall_character: Algorithm Node n-be83d2b1a4bd produces substituted indole amides and imines, linked nitrogen heterocycles, aryl/cyclic amines, medium-ring carbonyl systems, and fluorinated imino/dione heterocycles. Rings and aromaticity are abundant: the digest ring-closure incidences range from 0.9460 to 0.9782 and aromatic-text incidences from 0.9425 to 0.9736. These count proposal strings containing a feature, not perceived ring counts or aromatic-atom fractions. Every task has 900 records, including 870 optimizer proposals. All recorded evaluated optimizer proposal strings parse with the available RDKit; graph parsing does not establish synthesis or stability. Halogen-text incidence ranges from 0.2448 to 0.9897, while explicit charge and stereocentre-text incidence are 0.0 throughout. Clearly protonatable amine candidates are present despite neutral notation. Many saturated and bridged centres have unspecified configuration. The overall chemistry is synthetically questionable and weak in drug-likeness because conventional aromatic, amide and amine regions coexist with N-halogen/O-halogen bonds, peroxides, highly decorated structures and difficult ring junctions. This is not universal: the high-scoring aryl/azetidine family lacks N-halogen, O-halogen and peroxide bonds, and ordinary N-H indole amides also occur. Diversity is moderate across tasks and seeds but leading examples often belong to close local families; different strings are not evidence of independent scaffold coverage. All 15 Child trajectories and all 15 published Parent trajectories were read in full; no supplied path is missing and no task is omitted. Every digest excerpt was reconciled with its Child trajectory. Parent n-62daf219c70a paths match the published-path template in context.evidence_index. The immutable request reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true, matched Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2, and no profile-mismatched seeds. Comparisons below use those published Parent records, not the changing worktree as Parent authority. Conditions are Research in Depth epoch 1, batch size 10 and 300 observations per task/seed. The Parent baseline reproduced historical n-c55c3d520a2c chemistry under its new profile; the original gap reports in both indexed nodes were read, and their source is retained in the transferable gaps. Historical identity is not an additional independent current comparison. Digest final_molecules are late seed-2 proposals rather than all seeds' retained best molecules; full trajectories supply the other seeds and best-score pairs. Scores below are observed values rounded to six decimal places unless scientific notation is needed. Heavy-atom and ring counts are RDKit readings of the cited records. Chemistry associations describe output only; they do not establish a missing target pharmacophore, component attribution, activation, biological activity or contribution. The audit and complete path/hash inventory are in .slots/round-0023-slot-2/molecular/trajectory_audit.json.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-0 leader is a 25-heavy-atom, three-aromatic-ring indole carboxanilide carrying methylamino, methoxymethyl, aryl fluorine and N-chloro-amide groups. Seed 1 instead favors a similarly sized N-amino indole/aryl ketimine with methoxy and fluoromethyl substituents. Seed 2 reaches a 25-heavy-atom partially unsaturated six-membered N-chloro heterocycle linked to an anilide and an O-linked cyanate side chain; its leading structure has two rings, only one aromatic. Thus not every leader is a fully aromatic indole. Mean proposal SMILES length is 43.1, ring-closure incidence 0.9609 and aromatic-text incidence 0.9425. Published Parent leaders are also compact aromatic frameworks, but include an N-hydroxy pyridyl amide, an indole-linked diketone, and a cumulene/imine family rather than these exact Child seed families.
liabilities: The highest seed-0 molecule has chlorine on the amide nitrogen, chemically distinct from its ordinary carbon-bound aryl fluorine.
The seed-2 family contains N-Cl and O-linked cyanate groups, while other leaders have N-N substitution or imines. Their scores are not stability or synthetic-route evidence.
Tiny late proposals lose almost all functional context; extensive unsaturated substituent changes can also reduce the score while leaving a recognizable scaffold.

The Parent also contains questionable reactive groups and is not a chemical-quality standard.
liabilities: The annulated three-membered carbocycle shares an edge with the aromatic framework and merits a geometry assessment; ring closure and aromatic notation alone do not establish feasibility.
N-F, O-F, peroxide, chloromethyl-ether and acyl-fluoride environments appear in high or late examples. Carbon-bound fluorine should not be conflated with those attachments.

A methoxy-to-peroxide relative still scores 0.601476 beside its 0.603470 methoxy structural counterpart. In contrast, the 0.989715 aryl/azetidine molecule lacks N-halogen, O-halogen and peroxide bonds, and ordinary N-H amides also occur. The recurring gap is local bond environment, not absence of useful heterocycles or a universal problem with carbon-bound halogens.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve conventional bond environments while retaining useful aromatic and polar-group relationships.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator needs chemically contextual alternatives that can retain favorable scaffold relationships without automatically inheriting reactive attachments. Preserve ordinary aryl halogens and useful amine centres when supported by local feedback. This suggests testing environmental plausibility, not a blanket halogen filter; these associations neither establish a score benefit for replacement nor attribute the chemistry to one component.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Original gap source: n-c55c3d520a2c, reproduced in baseline n-62daf219c70a; re-observed here in n-be83d2b1a4bd under Research in Depth epoch 1, Search Seeds 0/1/2, batch size 10 and 300 observations per task/seed. The historical source includes a severe cyclic-cumulene example; that exact geometry is not the current leader. Current leaders instead include a cyclopropane-annulated aromatic edge, a fused cyclobutene and several medium-ring bridged carbonyl frameworks. Conventional cyclic amines also attain high scores, and extra ring connections can accompany lower scores. Thus rich ring content survives while geometric feasibility remains unestablished.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not consistently distinguish a valid ring graph from a geometrically credible unsaturation pattern and ring junction.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring transformations need awareness of bond geometry, ring size and bridge connectivity, alongside plausible alternative topologies preserving learned functional relationships. Ordinary azetidines, fused systems and small rings should be distinguished from unsupported strained arrangements. Parsing and aromatic labels cannot substitute for this information, and no endpoint advantage or component-specific source of the issue is established.

The digest stereocentre-string rate is 0.0 in every current task. Substituted azetidines, fluorinated ring centres and bridged carbonyl frameworks nevertheless contain potential stereogenic environments. Neutral-charge notation is also universal, while ordinary protonatable amine candidates are clearly present; charge absence is a separate issue.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator leaves stereochemical identity unspecified after creating potentially stereogenic saturated and bridged centres.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Representation and graph transformations need to preserve or explicitly resolve stereochemistry where chemically meaningful, accounting for achiral and configurationally unstable cases. Protonation and tautomerism require separate assessment rather than an assumption from neutral SMILES. The evidence establishes unspecified identity, not a measured stereochemical penalty or a demonstrated gain from enumeration.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Original gap source: n-c55c3d520a2c, reproduced in baseline n-62daf219c70a; re-observed here in n-be83d2b1a4bd under Research in Depth epoch 1, Search Seeds 0/1/2, batch size 10 and 300 observations per task/seed. Tiny late hydrocarbon and halogen proposals reach recorded floors, while some linked heterocyclic families expand to heavily decorated large structures. Current 47- and 53-heavy-atom leaders are not intrinsically better than compact alternatives; a smaller related amide/heterocycle scores 0.593733 beside a 0.597187 larger leader. A separate 48-heavy-atom proposal scores 6.593933252035046e-30, while a compact 28-heavy-atom dione reaches 0.611642. These are context-dependent comparisons, not isolated effects of atom count.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently retain useful connected molecular context while avoiding excessive elaboration.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Task-local feedback can guide transformations that preserve relevant connected functional groups while allowing simplification or replacement of dispensable regions. The missing capability is consistent chemical context control; neither a fixed minimum size nor a preference for larger molecules follows. More plausible or compact proposals still require observed score evidence, and this report assigns no causal responsibility to a component.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Original gap source: n-c55c3d520a2c, reproduced in baseline n-62daf219c70a; re-observed here in n-be83d2b1a4bd under Research in Depth epoch 1, Search Seeds 0/1/2, batch size 10 and 300 observations per task/seed. Current high-scoring examples repeatedly modify indole amides, linked nitrogen heterocycles, aryl/cyclic amines or bridged carbonyl systems by changing peripheral halogens, short linkers and local ring connections. Distinct seeds do produce substantially different families, including both flexible and cyclic amines, and some Child families exceed their matched Parent examples. This supports limited within-family alternatives, not global structural collapse, inability to make rings or a universal failure of the current chemistry.

transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator would need feasible scaffold reorganizations that preserve favorable functional relationships learned from accepted observations. Distinct SMILES, extra ring closures or broad coverage alone are insufficient evidence of useful alternatives. Assess resulting chemistry and its own observed reward; these associations neither show that more diversity improves endpoints nor identify the responsible search component.

nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

approach.method_basis: The Parent learns a recurrent SMILES language prior from an unlabeled molecular corpus and initializes a fresh policy from that frozen prior for each objective. It trains on the highest-scoring half of the new accepted batch together with the strongest eligible examples from a memory of thirty-two earlier elites. Each example retains its original accepted string and reward. Historical examples used more often receive smaller relative coefficients, while current and historical groups keep their count-based shares. The target is frozen-prior sequence log likelihood plus sixty times accepted reward, capped individually at zero. Bounded clipped Adam updates fit squared target residuals and retain the final iterate. The policy directly samples complete SMILES, and validation and canonical novelty checks refill the announced batch.
approach.novelty: Remove repeated historical examples from the active loss and train only on the current batch elites, with their original target ceilings and a plain mean reduction. Retain the historical selection and forwarding work as passive diagnostics so the removed contribution can be measured under the same tensor shapes and random draws. Earlier siblings changed which history was replayed, its relative influence, or its target construction. The recent score-priority removal kept replay active and lowered the final score in every seed. The original current-only root used uncapped targets and supplies only one paired screening seed. This probe directly tests replay learning in the developed learner. Its activation claim is zero historical loss contribution and a changed learning direction; its utility prediction is that removing repeated access to stronger accepted history lowers the final endpoint.

nodes.hypothesis: Remove historical replay from the active optimization loss, fitting only the unchanged current accepted elites to their individually ceiling-projected targets with a plain mean squared residual, while retaining historical memory, selection and exposure bookkeeping solely as passive comparison state.

finding_summary.headline: Replay removal lowered final scores despite higher recorded AUC and fewer duplicate draws.
finding_summary.insights:
The developed learner still benefits from repeatedly fitting accepted history at the final endpoint. The parent's small historical gradients were not evidence that history was redundant: the records were already well fitted under continued replay. Once replay stopped, previously accepted examples often became much worse fitted even though current elites remained easy to fit. Matched initialization, exact loss isolation and the complete paired score panel support a contribution from replay in this composition. They do not show universal protection against forgetting, and the improved seed plus higher AUC leave the timing and task dependence of that contribution open.

The result separates useful search from generic novelty. Deco-hop explored more distinct nonempty molecular cores, 438 versus 355, yet finished worse. The supplied chemistry assessment finds familiar aromatic amide, sulfonamide and cyclic-amine families on both sides; generally smaller molecules and broad ring coverage did not reliably recover the stronger parent's fragment arrangements. New molecules shared a core with the selected historical set in 320 of 4,200 subsequent emissions, versus 685 with active replay, but that association cannot identify which remembered molecule caused a score change. Unspecified stereochemistry, oversized outliers and unstable-looking linker alternatives remain unresolved.

This removes historical loss contributions, not learned historical information: policy parameters and persistent Adam moments retain earlier current learning. Passive memory selection, exposure counts and union forwarding also remain, so fewer duplicate draws do not establish a replay runtime saving. Individual target ceilings remain active but do not make the joint current target set attainable: 177 of 420 nonterminal current sets still demand total sequence probability above one. Further contribution tests must keep those residual target constraints and the difference between early AUC and final quality explicit.
finding_summary.results:
Historical examples received exactly zero loss weight and zero likelihood derivatives in all 5,220 real optimizer steps containing history. All 420 history-bearing updates followed by proposals changed the gradient direction after clipping; every real first backward matched the current-only objective exactly. All fifteen matched initialization controls reproduced the same first twenty accepted records, and every session completed its budget.

Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.522705 to 0.495640, a paired decrease of 0.027066, exceeding the registered 0.002 effect. Seed changes were +0.008523, -0.023353 and -0.066368; population score dispersion fell from 0.020072 to 0.011865. Every task mean fell, led by sitagliptin (-0.072443) and deco-hop (-0.041088), then median (-0.015291), zaleplon (-0.006499) and docking (-0.0000068). Recorded mean AUC nevertheless rose from 0.405593 to 0.430068, with docking reaching strong scores earlier. The final-score loss therefore coexists with better discovery earlier in the recorded budget.

Current projected fitting error fell from 60.166 to 3.804 within updates. On the same actual updates, weighted error on passively observed history rose from 69.678 to 86.195; under active replay in the parent it fell from 3.366 to 2.436. Those are fitting measurements on each run's own states. Raw duplicate draws fell from 32.21% to 25.99%, and batches needing extra sampling fell from sixteen to three, while raw validity fell from 91.79% to 87.35%.

molecular.headline: Aromatic amides, sulfonamides and cyclic amines dominate, with oversized outliers and undefined stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: All supplied child and parent trajectories were read, and every requested task is covered. Each task contains 900 recorded molecules, including 870 optimizer proposals. Ring-closure-token rates range from 0.9759 to 0.9966, aromatic-token rates from 0.9368 to 0.9943, and mean SMILES lengths from 37.8 to 47.6. These counters measure presence in molecular strings, not fractions of aromatic atoms or practical feasibility. The output spans ordinary aromatic amides, sulfonamides, aza-heterocycles, indoles, piperazines, piperidines, hydrazones and some larger natural-product-like or lipid-like structures. Leading families are generally recognizable synthetic chemistry, with ordinary sulfur functional groups and carbon-bound halogens. Structural diversity is broad across and within seeds, though local high-score excerpts often concentrate on related cores. Typical molecular sizes are comparable to or smaller than parent n-c2ef5c1d5a78, while occasional very long chains and large ring systems remain. The charged-token rates of 0.0391-0.0989 include nitro, azide and N-oxide representations; they do not by themselves demonstrate alternative protonation states of basic amines. Every stereocentre-token rate is 0.0. Plausible synthesis here means that most leading structures use familiar fragments and linkages, not that routes or stable stereoisomers were demonstrated. Size and configuration counts below are passive RDKit readings of supplied SMILES. Score comparisons are confined to observed molecules and do not establish target binding, an unseen required scaffold or a causal effect for changes that alter several features.

per_task.generated_character: The proposal median is 23 heavy atoms, with a range of 7-48. Leading molecules are compact fused aza-aromatics or indoles attached to an amide or ketone and another aryl group. The highest observed molecule has 24 heavy atoms: a fused diaza-aromatic carboxamide acylates an aryl-substituted pyrrolidine, whose phenyl group carries a phenol. Its cyclic amide nitrogen is not a free aliphatic amine. Other leaders include quinoline-like carboxanilides, a dimethylamino benzofused diazinone with a benzoyl group, and indole amides containing small imine/N-N rings. These are mostly conventional medicinal fragments, although the small imine rings need closer feasibility scrutiny. Low molecules include extremely long alkyl-linked polyamines, bulky multiaryl structures and enlarged heterocycles with several appended amides; size and flexibility become much less controlled.
liabilities: Long hydrocarbon segments, repeated aryl groups and multiple appended amides produce excessive size or flexibility in the low-score tail.
Small imine-containing N-N rings and unsaturated linkers are less routine than the ordinary amide series.
The leading arylpyrrolidine has an unassigned tetrahedral centre.
missing_features: The oversized low-score products lack the compact heteroaromatic/carbonyl organization retained by the stronger structures.

The hydroxyl-free analogue lacks the phenolic group associated with the strongest local example; positional changes show that simply adding a heteroatom is not equivalent to reproducing its arrangement.
The substituted pyrrolidine configuration is unspecified, and the small imine/N-N ring alternatives do not establish a complete set of stable, geometrically defined linkers.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The phenolic arylpyrrolidine amide scores 0.5 versus 0.4519753205796759 for its corresponding phenyl analogue without the hydroxyl group. A different hydroxyl-regioisomer bearing fluorine scores 0.4603736522870685; both position and substitution differ, so this is not a fluorine-only comparison. The dimethylamino benzofused diazinone/ketone scores 0.471981152610369, while converting that dimethylamino substituent into a dimethylamide gives 0.44989726212142783. By contrast, the long polyamine reaches 0.0, and a large, highly aromatic branched derivative scores 3.23625721744337e-34. The observed preference is for compact and specifically positioned aromatic/polar functionality rather than extra rings or appended amines. Relative to the parent, seed 0 changes from an indole amide maximum of 0.43351949803907636 to the phenolic cyclic amide at 0.5. Seeds 1 and 2 move to different leading families with maxima 0.4187728703049131 and 0.471981152610369, versus parental 0.4767312946227961 and 0.5.

per_task.generated_character: The proposal median is 28 heavy atoms, compared with 33 in the parent, although current outliers span 4-99. Leading examples are substituted heteroaryl assemblies: an anilino fused diazine joined to thiazole and malondiamide, an anilino pyridine relative, and a substituted triazine carrying pyridyl nitrile and aryl groups. Other families contain polyaryl ethers, N-N aza-heterocycles, or fused N-H heterocycles bearing aryl carboxamides. Most are synthetically recognizable, but aromatic surface and substitution can be extensive: a polyaryl-ether leader has 42 heavy atoms, and another strong example has 53 heavy atoms with a long amide/polyamine side chain. Nitro groups, a pyridine N-oxide and a heterocyclic thione occur in later molecules. Low examples include tiny halocarbons and an aromatic nitrile-substituted alkenyl sulfone/thione compound.
liabilities: Many aromatic rings and long appended amide/polyamine chains can complicate solubility, conformation and synthesis even with ordinary valence.
Nitro, N-oxide and thione chemistry introduces distinct redox or tautomeric considerations; these charged representations should not be confused with protonated amines.
The low-score alkenyl sulfone bearing a nitrile has an electrophilic unsaturated motif.
missing_features: The small low-score fragments lack the connected heteroaryl/aryl and donor-acceptor architecture of stronger molecules; the low aromatic sulfone also shows that possessing those atom types without the right connectivity is insufficient.

A compact, complete set of matched linker and substituent alternatives around the stronger heteroaryl assemblies is not demonstrated. The tied peripheral variants do not show a requirement for their particular fluorinated side chains.
The large polyaryl and polyamine examples do not supply evidence that their extra size or conformational freedom is necessary.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The anilino fused-diazine/thiazole/malondiamide structure scores 0.5970617559087443, its pyridine-containing relative 0.5930306905370843, and the decorated triazine 0.5904510410975536. The nitrile-bearing alkenyl sulfone/thione structure scores only 0.29576032540675845 despite substantial aromatic and nitrogen content, while tiny halocarbons remain near 0.5. Thus neither ring count nor generic chemical complexity explains the gradient. Three nitro/aza-heterocyclic analogues share exactly 0.5845887135341942 with quite different fluoroalkoxy or carbamate appendages, showing that those peripheral changes are not distinguished here. The parent retains more substituted azine-rich leading families. Current per-seed maxima are 0.586764705882353, 0.5970617559087443 and 0.5860900982273908, versus parental 0.5998615059406662, 0.6263699396108253 and 0.6669492630755185. The generally smaller current molecules do not reproduce the parent best fragment arrangements.

per_task.generated_character: The proposal median is 26 heavy atoms, and the displayed leaders contain 23-29. They combine substantial aryl surface with accessible aliphatic amines. One family is a propyl-substituted indole bearing a dichlorophenyl group and a bridged bicyclic diamine. Another is a methyl/aryl-substituted piperidine with a long arylalkyl N-substituent. Other leaders combine aminotetralin/thiazole/pyrrolidine fragments, or phenolic benzylamine, piperidine and a fused aryl ether. These are plausible medicinal scaffolds with ordinary bonding, although the chlorinated aryl groups, long chains and several basic centres can make physicochemical behavior demanding. The lowest molecules instead contain aromatic imides, amides, sulfonamides or acylhydrazones, often with nitro substituents and without the same accessible aliphatic-amine arrangement.
liabilities: Long arylalkyl chains and multiple chlorinated aromatic groups add hydrophobic surface and flexibility.
Several potentially basic centres coexist without explicit protonation-state comparisons.
The leading bridged diamine and arylpiperidine each have two unassigned tetrahedral centres in passive RDKit readings.
missing_features: The low amide/imide/sulfonamide compounds lack the freely available aliphatic-amine and aryl-linker organization common to stronger products.
The high-scoring set does not establish a need for its longest chains or heaviest aromatic halogenation; more compact matched relatives are not systematically resolved by the near-saturated score.
The substituted piperidines, tetralin systems and bridged diamines lack specified configurations. Their neutral strings also leave actual amine protonation unresolved.

Matched terminal aryl fluorine/chlorine variants share 0.9999872465278599, and extending propyl to butyl on the indole changes 0.9999968787724475 to 0.9999963450040522. The near-saturated scores do not establish a benefit from greater chain length or heavier halogenation. The parent also has aryl/cyclic-amine and flexible diamine leaders with scores close to 1, but different structures. per_task.generated_character: The proposal median is 23 heavy atoms, with a range of 6-54. The stronger families are ordinary substituted piperazines, piperazinones and aryl sulfonamides, often with amide, carbamate or benzodioxole groups. The highest observed molecule has 27 heavy atoms and a piperazine capped by an aryl sulfonyl group and an aryl carbonyl group; both ring nitrogens are acylated or sulfonylated rather than freely basic. Another strong family contains a benzodioxole-benzyl substituent on a piperazinone. Simple N-methyl arylsulfonyl piperazines are already close in score. A separate seed reaches a compact fused indole/lactam framework. Low products include allyl isothiocyanate, allyl azide, long-chain charged nitrogen derivatives and simple aliphatic acid/amide fragments. A much simpler arylsulfonyl N-methylpiperazine has 16 heavy atoms and scores 0.20718664161756667. Adding chlorine to that simple arylsulfonyl analogue gives 0.20444464181057284, so halogenation is not uniformly rewarded. Allyl isothiocyanate and allyl azide both score 0.0, while the long-chain nitrogen/acid compound scores 0.019641313778463534. The gradient favors an assembled aromatic/cyclic-nitrogen/polar-linker pattern over isolated reactive fragments or long aliphatic chains; it does not require every ring nitrogen to remain basic. The parent already has this piperazine/sulfonamide theme. Current seed 0 and seed 1 maxima are 0.2146585422450621 and 0.2125118592516207, versus parental 0.2125118592516207 and 0.20428349275442803. per_task.generated_character: The proposal median is 24 heavy atoms, with a range of 7-53. The strongest current family is a readily recognizable acylhydrazone: a methoxyphenyl imine connects through N-N and carbonyl/methylene groups to an aniline bearing a benzodioxole ring. The leading molecule has 24 heavy atoms. Other relatively strong molecules include a nitrogen-rich fused dione with thiol and trifluoromethylphenyl groups, a compact N/O ring system with an aryl sulfone, a sulfonylpiperidine/imidazole, a sulfonamidoethyl aryl ester, and acetanilide-thioether aza-heterocycles. The low-score excerpt instead contains very long lipid-like chains, large lactones, extended mixed-function chains and bulky polycyclic structures. These need not be impossible to synthesize, but they differ sharply in size and topology from the compact stronger families. transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make bounded linker, branch and ring-size alternatives available around intact useful fragment arrangements. Include coherent contractions and expansions rather than relying on either severe fragmentation or long-chain extension to explore new structures.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Matched aryl fluorine/chlorine variants share 0.9999872465278599. Extending an indole propyl group to butyl changes 0.9999968787724475 to 0.9999963450040522. transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide matched simpler and less heavily substituted alternatives that preserve the main ring and polar-group arrangement. transferable_gaps.evidence: Every stereocentre-token rate is 0.0. transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not define stereochemistry and relevant molecular states for otherwise plausible medicinal scaffolds.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve and specify feasible stereochemical relationships and double-bond geometry when constructing substituted rings or imine linkers. nodes.method_name: Augmented Hill-Climb with a corpus-trained SMILES policy
nodes.method_thesis: Train a compact autoregressive SMILES prior solely on the supplied unlabeled corpus, then initialize a fresh policy from that prior for each objective. Use the initial observations and each subsequent scored batch to update only its highest-reward sequences with the Augmented Hill-Climb loss: fit policy log likelihood to frozen-prior log likelihood plus scaled observed reward. Sample complete molecules token by token from the updated policy, canonicalize them, and refill invalid or duplicate proposals by further generation. The corpus supplies language training, never a ranked molecular pool. Elite-conditioned policy updates should shift generation toward new high-scoring molecular combinations quickly enough to improve the benchmark's mean final Top-1. This is a small-budget transfer hypothesis, not a claim that published larger-budget gains carry over. The root uses the current scored batch; randomized historical replay is reserved for the first improvement. The anchor's elite augmented-likelihood mechanism is described by [Thomas et al.](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13321-022-00646-z).
