Fresh independent objective policy and Adam state initialized from a checkpoint-verified frozen prior.

Current accepted-batch top-half elites fitted to frozen-prior sequence log likelihood plus sixty times original accepted reward, with individual positive targets capped at zero and nonpositive targets preserved.
Active current-only mean squared residual with five equal current coefficients, exactly zero historical coefficients and original accepted serialization provenance.
Persistent bounded Adam, norm-one gradient clipping, inherited stopping threshold and final-iterate retention.
Direct complete autoregressive policy sampling, RDKit validation, canonical novelty filtering and bounded direct-policy refill.
Task-local canonical top-32 accepted-elite memory and descending-score historical selection retained only for passive comparison and unchanged union tensor context.
Inherited passive uniform history draw and once-per-executed-update passive replay-selection ledger; inverse-one-plus-count historical weights belong only to the passive Parent objective.

Active current target projection plus explicitly passive historical/union target diagnostics, direct current-only/Parent and raw/projected gradients with private clipping, real-first-backward agreement and per-step zero-history/scalar receipts.

approach.method_basis: The Parent learns a recurrent SMILES language model from an unlabeled molecular corpus and begins each objective with a fresh policy copied from that frozen prior. Each accepted batch contributes its highest-scoring half. A memory keeps the thirty-two strongest earlier elites, and its strongest eligible records join the current examples with their original accepted strings and scores. Historical examples receive diminishing weights based on how many earlier fitting batches used them, while the total current and historical loss shares stay fixed. The policy minimizes weighted squared error toward frozen-prior sequence log likelihood plus sixty times accepted reward, using up to twelve clipped Adam steps and retaining the final policy. It directly samples complete SMILES, with chemical validation and canonical duplicate rejection refilling each batch.
approach.novelty: Add an individual log-probability ceiling to the fitting targets: replace only positive targets with zero. This removes the positive excess that a normalized sequence model cannot reach while keeping every nonpositive target and the Parent's exposure weights. The earlier shared-normalization sibling shifted every target in an affected batch, reversed some learning directions and lost sequence completion in two replicas. Ceiling projection never turns a capped row toward lower likelihood. The two Huber siblings bounded residual influence symmetrically; this change acts only on targets above the probability ceiling. Same-state target and gradient comparisons will test execution, and later molecular proposals will test utility. Multiple zero targets are still jointly incompatible, and collapsing distinctions among saturated targets can weaken useful exploitation.

nodes.hypothesis: Project each selected sequence's augmented likelihood target independently onto the nonpositive log-probability half-line, t_i = min(frozen_prior_log_likelihood_i + 60 * accepted_score_i, 0), while preserving the Parent's inverse-exposure historical coefficients, selected membership and squared-residual Adam update.

finding_summary.headline: Ceiling projection changed real learning and reduced duplicate draws, with an uneven gain in final score.
finding_summary.insights:
Removing individually impossible demands can alter the direction of a clipped, exposure-weighted update without reversing any capped sequence's scalar learning direction. The matched controls make this attribution unusually clear: all six sessions without a positive target reproduced the parent's complete molecular records and scores exactly, and every changed session retained its matched proposal prefix until the first positive-target intervention. This narrows the effect to active target projection under the existing replay and optimizer rules.

The mechanism satisfies only the individual probability ceiling. Two hundred of the 420 historical updates still had combined projected target probability above one. Thirty-six batches set all ten selected targets to zero, erasing their raw target distinctions. Positive raw-target appearances actually increased from 977 to 1,067 as search changed; the mechanism removes their excess when fitting, rather than preventing such opportunities. Lower projected loss also does not protect every remembered row: 905 of 2,100 historical residuals worsened, almost the parent's 906, and 1,006 historical likelihoods decreased. Every repeated training appearance was consecutive, so these records cannot establish forgetting between skipped updates.

The chemical assessment places the main gain in a more concentrated decorated quinazoline family, while overall medicinal scaffolds remain ring-rich and attachment chemistry and stereochemical definition remain unresolved. Distinct observed cores increased for zaleplon despite its slightly lower endpoint and decreased for deco-hop despite its gain. That combination rules out treating broader core counts or lower duplication as a sufficient explanation for useful search. The open question is whether the endpoint benefit persists across seeds while retaining distinctions among saturated targets and preserving useful progress earlier in the budget.
finding_summary.results:
All positive target excess was removed, and the change reached actual learning. Among 420 historical updates followed by proposals, 195 contained positive targets: 465 current and 602 historical row appearances were capped, removing 13,705.38 nats of unattainable target excess. Every affected update changed gradient direction after clipping. The three affected initialization updates did too. All 244 no-positive updates retained exactly the same local raw and projected gradient, and every one of the 450 real first backward passes matched the projected objective exactly. No capped row reversed from upward to downward likelihood pressure.

On the child's own historical training states, projection reduced the mean sum of absolute scalar learning factors from 12.795 to 6.305. Projected weighted squared error fell from 26.936 before learning to 2.984 afterward; error against the original raw targets on those same states fell from 135.072 to 97.457. Those are fitting measurements under different target definitions, not score gains. All fifteen tasks completed their budgets. Raw duplicate draws fell from 36.22% to 32.21%, and batches needing extra sampling fell from 29 to 16.

Mean final Top-1 rose from 0.517655 to 0.522705, a paired gain of 0.005050. Seed changes were -0.008594, +0.007415 and +0.016329. The gain was concentrated in deco-hop, whose task mean increased by 0.025328; docking rose by 0.001300 near its ceiling, zaleplon fell by 0.001379, and the other two tasks were unchanged. Mean recorded AUC fell from 0.406769 to 0.405593, so the endpoint gain did not produce faster useful discovery overall. Terminal updates establish execution only and contribute no later proposals.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich medicinal scaffolds with uneven attachment chemistry, concentrated analogue families and no specified stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character: Node n-c2ef5c1d5a78 produces substantial organic structures, dominated by aromatic amides, decorated nitrogen heterocycles, aryl sulfonamides and cyclic amines. The digest reports 870 optimizer proposals per task; ring-closure rates range from 0.9805 to 0.9966 and aromatic-atom-presence rates from 0.946 to 0.9931. These are fractions of SMILES strings containing the indicated features, not atom fractions or perceived ring counts. The passive RDKit audit finds median heavy-atom counts of 24, 33, 28, 24 and 24 in the fixed task order, with median perceived ring counts of 3, 4, 3, 3 and 3. All 4,350 accepted optimizer appearances parse, but parsing is not a synthetic-route or stability assessment. Constitutional exploration is broad: the respective distinct atom-typed Murcko scaffold counts are 540, 356, 588, 733 and 775; these counts also distinguish linker and ring-atom changes and do not establish useful diversity. The strongest subsets can nevertheless concentrate on a single decorated core. Most leading structures have recognizable medicinal chemistry, alongside very flexible, highly aromatic, reactive-handle and unusually assembled outliers. The entire panel has stereocentre_rate 0.0; RDKit identifies 832 optimizer appearances with an unassigned tetrahedral centre and none with an assigned centre. Against Parent n-3462511d7ff0, two tasks have identical chemical records, while the others mainly change families or their substitution and linkage patterns. Score-gradient interpretations below are associations within recorded structures, not hidden-objective definitions, activity measurements, causal matched-pair experiments unless stated, or mechanism-activation judgements. All five task trajectories were supplied and read; tasks_without_trajectories is empty in the brief. Descriptor definitions, exact input hashes, Parent comparisons and structural receipts are saved in runs/SPIRAL2/policy/responses/r0011-06-improve-L03-molecular.audit.json.

per_task.generated_character: Predominantly medium-sized, aromatic amides: anilides, benzylamides, pyridyl ethers, pyridones and indole carboxamides. The leading seed-2 ether-linked bis-pyridyl anilide has 24 heavy atoms and three aromatic rings; its molecular weight is 319.364. The next benzyl-pyridone/pyridylmethyl benzamide and methylamino diaryl-ether analogue have the same heavy-atom count and molecular weight. These ordinary amide and aryl-ether connections appear makeable, while the low tail includes small inorganic/ionic fragments and elaborate polycycles. The Parent also led with aromatic amides; the node changes their heteroaromatic and linker arrangements. For example, the seed-0 leading family changes from a substituted pyrrole tertiary carboxamide at recorded 0.4902347642636414 to an acetamidoindole benzylamide at 0.43351949803907636. Seed 2 instead reaches the cited ether-linked anilide at 0.5, versus the Parent aromatic amide at 0.4767312946227961.
liabilities: The low tail contains overbuilt fused/bridged polycycles with unspecified stereochemistry; their valid SMILES do not supply a practical synthesis.

A high-scoring O-benzyl hydroxamate-like amide and a sulfinamide illustrate less routine N-O and sulfur attachment chemistry; the latter has an unassigned sulfur centre. These groups require individual assessment and are not inherently invalid.
The final expanded multi-anilide retains substantial aromatic surface and extra amide burden despite its very low score.
missing_features: Reliable preservation of the moderate-sized, organized aromatic amide/ether combination during late exploration: expanded amide assemblies and fragmented outputs lose that organization.
Controlled heteroatom placement and linker topology within that composition range remain unresolved; abundant rings do not imply the required arrangement has been found.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The leading 24-heavy-atom aromatic amides score 0.5 or 0.4767312946227961; the isolated thiocyanate representation scores 5.670115669739515e-23, and the enlarged 44-heavy-atom multi-amide scores 3.2151129360788796e-21. Late growth to the related 35-heavy-atom multi-anilide at seed-2 evaluation 296 gives only 0.00015241757289843227. A moderate size/composition window and specific aromatic nitrogen/amide organization are therefore supported better than indiscriminate ring or amide addition. The differently connected leaders sharing molecular weight still differ in score, so size alone is not sufficient; the records do not identify a unique absent target scaffold.

per_task.generated_character: The digest leaders are all seed-2 variants of a butoxy/dimethoxy 4-anilino-2-phenylquinazoline, with fluorine/chlorine substitutions and related alkoxy changes. The leading molecule has 35 heavy atoms, four aromatic rings, molecular weight 483.490 and nine rotatable bonds. The aryl-amino and aryl-ether connections are recognizable synthetic chemistry, although heavy decoration increases size and route complexity. Full trajectories also contain other families: a dinitrophenylhydrazone in seed 0 and a nitrogen-rich fused heteroaromatic family in seed 1. Compared with the Parent seed-2 sulfonamide/imine-decorated quinoline leader at 0.6085883514313919, the node reaches the cited quinazoline at 0.6669492630755185. The largest Murcko family grows from 71 Parent proposals to 160 node proposals; this local concentration coexists with 356 distinct node scaffolds.
liabilities: The leading family combines extensive aromatic surface, multiple halogens and flexible alkoxy substituents; solubility, conformation and synthesis remain unmeasured.
The broader stream still includes heavily nitrated hydrazones and large aliphatic ionic outliers. Their presence should not be confused with useful scaffold coverage.
No stereochemistry is specified even in branched alkoxy variants that can carry a stereocentre.
missing_features: The leading excerpt lacks alternative core architectures that retain the successful substituent arrangement: its apparent variety largely comes from decoration of one quinazoline framework.

The local score differences support more precise substituent positioning and ether connectivity, but do not identify any particular unobserved scaffold or missing functional group as the objective answer.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The strongest decorated quinazoline scores 0.6669492630755185. A difluoroaniline member scores 0.6666996765035981, whereas its same-fluorine-count positional isomer at final evaluation 298 scores 0.6362655153804642. Removing the butoxy oxygen in the cited final analogue gives 0.6316114681166585; these local comparisons support sensitivity to substitution position and linkage. Ring-rich sulfones in the worst excerpt score 0.28535067873303166 and 0.28799019607843135, while a long-chain quaternary ammonium compound scores 0.5. Thus the score is not a general measure of aromatic richness, size, or chemical plausibility.

per_task.generated_character: The leading molecules have accessible non-acylated amines combined with aromatic groups: benzyl/aryl piperazines, benzene-fused azepines connected through aminoalkyl chains, and aryl ketones bearing propoxy-piperidine substituents. The first digest leader has 30 heavy atoms, three aromatic rings and a saturated piperazine, with molecular weight 463.463 and calculated TPSA 6.48. The next fused-azepine leader is smaller, at 26 heavy atoms and molecular weight 360.448, but retains a flexible linker. These are recognizable medicinal scaffolds, with conventional amine/aryl chemistry in many examples. The Parent also produced cyclic amines, but its seed-2 near-ceiling leader carried an N-hydroxyaminal connection; the node supplies ketone-linked examples instead. Parent seed-0 recorded best 0.9961294199375436 becomes 0.9999997933663268 for the cited piperazine family; this is chemical comparison at an already compressed score ceiling.
liabilities: The highly aromatic first leader has little calculated polar surface, while other leaders carry long flexible linkers and multiple potentially protonatable amines; neither actual protonation nor solubility was measured.
The chloromethyl ether in a leader scoring 0.9999994163676008 is a reactive attachment requiring scrutiny even though the recorded score is high.
The final polyether-linked amide has 17 rotatable bonds and score 0.5728095677025575, showing that extensive flexible growth is still admitted.
missing_features: Some low and final proposals lose the combination of a non-acylated cyclic amine and the larger aromatic/linker arrangement; the generator can emit these features but does not preserve their chemical roles consistently.
Several high-scoring aminoalkyl families lack linker restraint. More constrained counterparts are a chemical coverage gap, with no demonstrated score benefit from the records supplied.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Free cyclic amines with suitably connected aromatic groups occur repeatedly near the score ceiling. By contrast, the N-sulfonyl piperidine example scores 1.9828327575562915e-05 and the N-acyl piperidine example 2.6715842904959654e-05: a nitrogen ring whose nitrogen is sulfonylated or acylated is chemically different from a free amine. Late seed-2 ketones retaining the propoxy-piperidine appendage score 0.9999937368364026 and 0.999988872643426, whereas the smaller amino-ketone lacking that appendage scores 0.0035116287191461495. Those are not single-change matched pairs, but support the importance of amine/aryl spacing beyond mere nitrogen presence. The many nearly identical high scores cannot establish a preferred linker length or experimental binding affinity.

per_task.generated_character: The stronger molecules combine aryl sulfonyl groups with piperazine, quinoline or benzodioxole units. The leading molecule is an unsymmetrical bis-sulfonyl piperazine linking a methylquinoline and benzodioxole: 32 heavy atoms, five perceived rings, three aromatic rings and molecular weight 475.548. Other strong examples retain N-methyl or N-aryl piperazines; the broader stream also contains amides and assorted heterocycles. Aryl sulfonamide assembly is recognizable makeable chemistry, whereas the seed-1 N-rich unsaturated ring is less routine. Every supplied node and Parent record agrees in evaluation, source, SMILES and score across all seeds for this task, so there is no molecular-output change to describe.
liabilities: Repeated sulfonyl and piperazine additions can produce large, acceptor-rich molecules without improving on the more compact leader.
The leading bis-sulfonyl piperazine has no free basic piperazine nitrogen; any intended ionization property must follow its actual substitution, not the ring name.
The low tail includes a trichloromethyl N-hydroxyformamide and an organic azide; these are chemically distinct reactive or specialized compounds, not evidence of routine medicinal plausibility.
missing_features: Many lower-scoring proposals lack the combined aromatic/sulfonyl/piperazine organization; isolated amine or sulfonyl motifs do not reproduce the leading arrangement.

A more effective topology beyond the observed bis-sulfonamide is not identifiable from these scores. The enlarged example shows that duplicating recognizable fragments does not resolve that uncertainty.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The bis-sulfonyl piperazine scores 0.2588686674995393. The smaller quinoline sulfonyl N-methylpiperazine scores 0.2272296156064184, and the expanded structure carrying additional sulfonyl-piperazine material scores 0.2301209791058402 despite reaching 41 heavy atoms and molecular weight 628.795. Small acyclic compounds, including the cited organic azide at 0.0 and thiodiacetic acid at 0.02095188685475281, lack the combined ring/linker architecture. A late simple pyrrolylmethyl piperazine scores 0.10826206026353223, so piperazine alone is insufficient. Both nitrogens of the leading piperazine are sulfonylated: a missing free basic nitrogen is not supported as this objective's general deficit.

per_task.generated_character: The stronger excerpt remains chemically heterogeneous. It includes a butylamino-acetyl N-acylsulfonamide on a fluoro/trifluoromethyl phenyl ring, a branched oxalamide/anilide, sulfonylated cyclic amidines bearing an aromatic ester, a guanidino benzofused amine, and an acylthiourea quinolinone. The first three leaders have 23, 26 and 25 heavy atoms and molecular weights 356.341, 377.338 and 362.382; the first two each have only one aromatic ring, whereas the cyclic-amidine ester has three rings overall. Several fragments are synthetically familiar, but the varied N-acylsulfonamide, amidine, hydrazone and acylthiourea connections need individual chemical assessment. All supplied node/Parent chemical records and scores are identical across the seeds; this chemistry is inherited unchanged in the observed output.
liabilities: The high-scoring amino-acylsulfonamide combines a potentially basic amine with a potentially acidic N-acylsulfonamide; a neutral SMILES does not establish its solution microstate.
The acylthiourea and sulfonylhydrazone families introduce tautomeric or configurational questions, while the branched oxalamide is explicitly stereochemically undefined.
Large peptide-like and lipid-like outliers carry substantial size or flexibility burdens. The final stream still contains densely carbonylated or imino structures at very low recorded scores.
missing_features: Reliable compact assembly with the local polarity and substituent arrangement seen in the better examples is missing from many proposals; late carbonyl-rich and bulky structures still depart from those arrangements.

The branched oxalamide, guanidino benzofused amine and other chiral proposals lack specified tetrahedral configurations. This is a molecular-definition gap; these trajectories do not test whether stereochemical assignment changes the objective score.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The compact amino-acylsulfonamide scores 0.32609684308650033 and the branched oxalamide 0.3085499097640706. Within the sulfonylated cyclic-amidine ester family, adding the cited aryl fluorine changes the recorded score from 0.24905607529893223 to 0.3034617343186778. Replacing the methyl ester in the unfluorinated family with an ethyl carboxamide gives 0.20841151065209942. Thus substituent identity and polar-group arrangement matter locally. The large peptide-like structures, extended lipid-like chain and heavily substituted polyaromatic examples in the worst excerpt have zero or extremely small scores. However, unfluorinated guanidino and acylthiourea leaders also score 0.2711448282680827 and 0.26424211308214746. Neither more fluorine nor more rings is a supported universal requirement, and the diverse leaders do not reveal a unique missing target pharmacophore.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Free cyclic amines recur among near-ceiling molecules, while cited N-acyl and N-sulfonyl versions of nitrogen rings occur at very low scores. Elsewhere the strongest bis-sulfonyl piperazine deliberately has both nitrogens blocked, so no universal free-amine preference is justified. Same-fluorine-count positional isomers on a decorated quinazoline score 0.6666996765035981 and 0.6362655153804642. These examples show why ring names and element counts do not determine chemical function or useful attachment geometry.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator varies atom identities and attachments without consistently preserving the chemical role of the resulting functional group.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Represent and explore functional-group roles, atom neighborhoods and substituent positions coherently, including alternatives that preserve a useful arrangement while changing one local connection. Let task-local observed feedback determine which roles matter; impose no universal amine, halogen or scaffold requirement.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A 24-heavy-atom aromatic amide scores 0.5, while a related 35-heavy-atom expanded multi-anilide scores 0.00015241757289843227. A 32-heavy-atom bis-sulfonyl piperazine scores 0.2588686674995393, while a 41-heavy-atom expanded sulfonyl/piperazine structure scores 0.2301209791058402. Large peptide-like and long-chain outliers also appear at zero or negligible scores. These are observed associations, not universal molecular-size cutoffs.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably control size and polar-group growth while retaining the organization of a useful molecular family.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support compact additions, removals and replacements that vary size, flexibility and donor/acceptor organization separately enough for feedback to resolve them. Avoid assuming that duplicating a recognized group or increasing ring count preserves the useful whole-molecule arrangement.

transferable_gaps.evidence: All 12 digest leaders in the decorated anilino-phenylquinazoline basin share that framework, despite extensive fluorine/chlorine and alkoxy variation. Its largest atom-typed Murcko family contains 160 optimizer proposals, versus 71 in the Parent. Across the panel ring-closure rates are already 0.9805 to 0.9966, and many distinct scaffolds occur, so the gap is not an inability to close rings or explore constitutional structures.
transferable_gaps.gap: High-scoring local exploration can become concentrated on peripheral decorations without demonstrating equivalent access to alternative core arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide chemically coherent core and attachment rearrangements alongside decoration changes, retaining substituent roles where possible. Assess resulting molecules through ordinary feedback rather than treating scaffold counts or enforced diversity as evidence of utility.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every digest reports stereocentre_rate 0.0. The passive structural audit finds 832 accepted optimizer appearances with an unassigned tetrahedral centre and none with an assigned centre. The branched oxalamide scoring 0.3085499097640706 and the sulfinamide scoring 0.4531317717091581 provide digest witnesses. This absence concerns molecular identity, not proven stereochemical sensitivity of the recorded scores.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator has no demonstrated ability to specify the stereochemical identities of the chiral molecules it emits.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support explicit stereochemical alternatives when a proposed graph admits them, and preserve assigned configuration through subsequent changes. Keep any usefulness claim conditional on observed feedback; do not assume that stereochemical specification itself improves the objective.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A chloromethyl-ether arylpiperazine has recorded score 0.9999994163676008. The same panel includes an organic azide, a trichloromethyl N-hydroxyformamide, stereochemically unspecified polycycles and amino-acylsulfonamides with competing ionizable groups. All accepted optimizer structures parse, which verifies a narrower property than stability, route feasibility or a defined solution microstate.
transferable_gaps.gap: Score-compatible generation still admits reactive attachments and structures whose practical synthesis or solution form is unresolved.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Maintain chemically coherent connection types and the ability to distinguish ordinary end-product functionality from reactive handles or unresolved microstates using general chemical context. Treat unusual N-N, N-O and sulfur chemistry individually rather than banning entire bond classes; the observed scores do not substitute for synthetic or physicochemical evidence.

nodes.method_name: Augmented Hill-Climb with a corpus-trained SMILES policy
nodes.method_thesis: Train a compact autoregressive SMILES prior solely on the supplied unlabeled corpus, then initialize a fresh policy from that prior for each objective. Use the initial observations and each subsequent scored batch to update only its highest-reward sequences with the Augmented Hill-Climb loss: fit policy log likelihood to frozen-prior log likelihood plus scaled observed reward. Sample complete molecules token by token from the updated policy, canonicalize them, and refill invalid or duplicate proposals by further generation. The corpus supplies language training, never a ranked molecular pool. Elite-conditioned policy updates should shift generation toward new high-scoring molecular combinations quickly enough to improve the benchmark's mean final Top-1. This is a small-budget transfer hypothesis, not a claim that published larger-budget gains carry over. The root uses the current scored batch; randomized historical replay is reserved for the first improvement. The anchor's elite augmented-likelihood mechanism is described by [Thomas et al.](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13321-022-00646-z).

approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves fresh molecular graphs from accepted scored molecules. It keeps a bounded score-greedy breeding population, draws parents from high-ranked score bands, and uses connected-fragment crossover and local graph mutations with ordinary continuation. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled. Stable canonical admission and duplicate rejection form a surplus pool. A Gaussian process using counts of local molecular environments and generalized Tanimoto similarity fits every accepted observation; the same current archive supplies the score mean and scale. Correlated function draws select the evaluated batch. Each real accepted offspring immediately updates the full archive, survivors and subsequent breeding.
approach.novelty: Remove generated records only from the GP conditioning matrix while continuing to compute normalization from every current accepted raw score. The training cohort becomes immutable copies of the usable initial records, but its standardized targets, raw predictions and uncertainty can still respond to the current normalizer. One earlier sibling froze membership and normalization together; another froze normalization with full membership. This is their missing consumer split. It tests whether generated conditioning rows contribute when adaptive normalization and live genetic feedback remain present, without repeating either earlier control.

nodes.hypothesis: Remove generated accepted records only from active GP conditioning by fitting immutable copies of the original usable initial accepted cohort, while recomputing the inherited score mean and scale from the full current accepted archive at every original fit call and retaining immediate live genetic feedback.

finding_summary.headline: Generated conditioning rows contribute: removing them lowers the mean by 0.22566
finding_summary.insights:
Generated conditioning records have positive conditional value even when adaptive normalization, score-based survival and recursive breeding remain available. This answers the missing membership question without treating the intervention as removal of all online learning. The same-input reference had lower prediction error on the actual scored molecules, but it supplies no rewards for omitted alternatives and no alternative future history; prediction error, reuse and uncertainty changes do not identify the route to the endpoint loss.

The earlier joint freeze and normalization-only findings remain intact. With complete matched outcomes and source boundaries checked, the four-treatment arithmetic interaction is +0.108156. Initial-only conditioning with current normalization scored 0.073800 below the jointly frozen version, while the historical full-conditioning comparison supported current normalization. The sign therefore depends on the conditioning context in these observations. This descriptive comparison shares one control, retains mixed task-level interaction signs, and establishes neither independent replication nor additive or mediated effects.

The molecular assessment finds persistent sulfur-rich, heavily halogenated docking families where the Parent reached more conventional aryl/amine arrangements, and more tiny fragments on every task. Useful aromatic amides and alternative ring arrangements still occur. These chemical associations help describe the weaker search outcomes but do not attribute them to one motif or prove a chemical mediator. Bond plausibility, ring geometry, stereochemical identity and the broader graph-evolution contribution remain open.
finding_summary.results:
All 435 fits kept the same ten initial records in exact order while normalization used the growing accepted archive. The 4,200 generated records with a later fit never entered conditioning, but all entered normalization; 150 final records had no later opportunity. Every first batch matched the Parent exactly. After feedback, all 420 later sets differed from a full-conditioning reference on the same saved pools and normal draws. Of 3,608 actual accepted choices absent from those reference sets, 3,475 later entered normalization and 1,146 later bred. Across all offspring, 1,626 identities served as later parents, so feedback remained active outside conditioning.

All fifteen task runs completed. Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.595670 to 0.370013, a paired change of -0.225656 against the registered 0.002 loss scale. Seed changes were -0.245204, -0.221990 and -0.209774. Fourteen endpoints and all five task means declined; zaleplon in seed 2 increased by 0.001361. Docking had the largest mean decrease, from 0.998989 to 0.298274. The Child still made 511 strict generating-parent wins and 118 incumbent advances, versus 629 and 258 for the Parent. These local successes did not preserve its endpoint.

The same-input reference had lower prediction error on the actual scored molecules, but it supplies no rewards for omitted alternatives and no alternative future history; prediction error, reuse and uncertainty changes do not identify the route to the endpoint loss.

The earlier joint freeze and normalization-only findings remain intact. With complete matched outcomes and source boundaries checked, the four-treatment arithmetic interaction is +0.108156. Initial-only conditioning with current normalization scored 0.073800 below the jointly frozen version, while the historical full-conditioning comparison supported current normalization. The sign therefore depends on the conditioning context in these observations. This descriptive comparison shares one control, retains mixed task-level interaction signs, and establishes neither independent replication nor additive or mediated effects.

The molecular assessment finds persistent sulfur-rich, heavily halogenated docking families where the Parent reached more conventional aryl/amine arrangements, and more tiny fragments on every task. Useful aromatic amides and alternative ring arrangements still occur. These chemical associations help describe the weaker search outcomes but do not attribute them to one motif or prove a chemical mediator. Bond plausibility, ring geometry, stereochemical identity and the broader graph-evolution contribution remain open.

molecular.overall_character: Node n-c2f46c40bbba produces substituted indole amides and open diaryl enamides, linked aza-aromatic carbonyl systems, halogenated sulfur-rich aryl structures, dense nitrogen/carbonyl polycycles, and smaller unsaturated polar fragments. The immutable brief explicitly reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true with all issued seeds matched and no profile mismatch. Initial molecule/score records match within each task/seed. Each Child task contains 900 observations, including 870 optimizer proposals. Structural diversity is moderate across seeds, while leaders repeatedly occupy a narrower family within a seed. Unique SMILES do not establish independent plausible scaffolds. The clearest paired chemical difference is persistent sulfur-rich, often highly halogenated Child chemistry versus more conventional aryl/aliphatic-amine Parent leaders on one task; other tasks show different departures rather than a single universal missing group. nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from a bounded population of accepted high-scoring molecules. It samples breeding parents by score band, recombines connected fragments and applies local graph mutations. Its retained special move exchanges a nitrogen and a carbon within one aromatic six-member ring, preserving formula and connectivity while changing nitrogen placement. Stable identity admission forms a fresh surplus pool. A Gaussian process trained on all earlier accepted scores uses counts of local molecular environments and generalized Tanimoto similarity; correlated score draws choose which pool members receive evaluations. Accepted offspring update both the prediction archive and the breeding population.
approach.novelty: Remove only the direct aromatic nitrogen-position exchange from the atom-replacement menu and measure its contribution to the complete feedback loop. The ordinary element substitutions, crossover, other mutations and count-based posterior remain. Earlier evidence established useful positional edits before the posterior learned environment counts, and a later integration sibling removed crossover. None of the supplied siblings isolates whether this particular two-atom move still adds useful search paths under the retained count-based selector. Because some current exchange products improve incumbents and later breed, the registered prediction is a score decrease when the move is removed. The experiment tests that contribution rather than assuming sparse use makes the move dispensable.

nodes.hypothesis: Remove the direct formula-preserving aromatic C/N positional-exchange options from the inherited atom-replacement menu, leaving only its original single-atom element substitutions while retaining all other graph, feedback and posterior mechanisms.

finding_summary.headline: Direct nitrogen exchanges were removed, and all three seed macro scores improved
finding_summary.insights: The Parent had real local successes from direct exchanges: thirty-five clean exchange offspring included nine parent beats and four incumbent improvements, and thirty later bred. Those successes did not establish that allocating menu probability to this route helped the full count-posterior search. Removing it improved the final mean while barely changing total parent beats, from 624 to 629. The largest decoration gain accompanied a shift from a 71-heavy-atom leader to a 30-heavy-atom heterocyclic family. This supports a contribution test at the level of the complete search process rather than judging an operator from selected success stories. It does not show that every exchange is harmful or isolate the value of an omitted isomer: smaller menus also change later random draws, pools and feedback. The chemistry remains mixed. Large assemblies became less common, but reactive nitrogen-halogen bonds, unspecified stereochemistry and difficult ring geometry persisted, including a high-scoring cyclic cumulene.
finding_summary.results: Exchange selection fell to zero despite 904 eligible selected-site menus; all withheld partners and unchanged legacy choices were verified. Crossover, ordinary mutations, accepted-only learning and correlated posterior selection remained active. All fifteen runs completed. Mean final Top-1 rose from 0.574344 to 0.595670, a paired gain of 0.021326, reversing the predicted decrease of at least 0.002. All three seed macro scores improved; nine task–seed scores rose, four fell and two tied. Gains were largest for decoration hopping and sitagliptin, while mean zaleplon and median-task scores declined. Population SD rose from 0.012317 to 0.026593. Mean recorded AUC increased slightly, from 0.482560 to 0.483817.

molecular.headline: Compact aromatic families and aryl amines coexist with reactive halogen bonds, difficult bridges and cyclic cumulenes
molecular.overall_character: The output is rich in aromatic and heterocyclic scaffolds: substituted indole amides and diketones, linked fused nitrogen heterocycles, aryl-containing basic amines, medium-ring nitrogen-carbonyl systems and fluorinated imino/carbonyl heterocycles. Ring-closure-string rates range from 0.9632 to 0.9828 and aromatic-string rates from 0.954 to 0.9736. These counters measure the presence of a feature in a SMILES, not ring diversity or the fraction of aromatic atoms. Formal-charge and stereocentre-string rates are 0.0 throughout; neutral records nevertheless contain obvious protonatable amines. Some leaders are recognizable medicinal-chemistry frameworks, especially the aryl amines, but N-halogen and O-F bonds, peroxides, unusual small-ring unsaturation and dense bridges remain serious limitations. Within-seed leaders are often close variants of a retained family. Compared with Parent n-559d25e9c9c7, some output is smaller, especially the leading decoration-task family, while the strongest fluorinated family includes a more difficult cyclic cumulene. Thus chemical changes accompany score changes without establishing uniformly improved feasibility. All five tasks have complete supplied trajectories, each with 900 molecules and 870 optimizer proposals; no task lacks trajectory evidence. Heavy-atom counts, weights and ring descriptions below were derived with RDKit from supplied trajectory SMILES. A perceived aromatic ring or potential stereogenic centre does not establish accessible geometry or configurational stability. Digest final excerpts are late seed-2 proposals rather than the incumbents of every seed.

per_task.generated_character: The best molecule has 25 heavy atoms and an ethyl/dimethyl/chloro-substituted indole linked through an N-hydroxy amide to pyridyl; the indole nitrogen bears fluorine. Other leaders retain the same fused aromatic/pyridyl-amide arrangement with N-halogen, N-S or halomethyl substitutions. Seed 2 also reaches an indole-aryl vicinal diketone family with aminomethyl groups. Mean proposal SMILES length is 42.1, and halogen-string incidence is 0.8805. These are compact, mostly planar frameworks whose local nitrogen and halogen chemistry is more concerning than their overall size. Parent leaders also contained N-halogen or N-S amides. Child seed-1 best is 0.47411701813450596 versus Parent 0.4423126980074005, while the other seeds reach different structures with lower best scores than their Parent counterparts. The chemistry remains concentrated in related aromatic families.
liabilities: N-fluoro, N-chloro and N-bromo indole variants, N-S substitution and halomethyl ethers occur among the leaders. These should not be summarized simply as ordinary aryl halogenation.
N-hydroxy amides are a recognizable chemical class, but do not resolve the separate N-halogen liability elsewhere in the same molecule.
The late vicinal-dicarbonyl series introduces a potentially reactive carbonyl pattern and remains strongly concentrated on the original aromatic framework.
missing_features: Conventional stable nitrogen substitution retaining the favorable fused-aromatic/carbonyl/pyridyl arrangement is poorly represented among the leading examples.
The leading excerpt explores substituent changes more than chemically independent compact frameworks with the same functional-group arrangement.
The scores do not identify an absent exact target pharmacophore; their clearest positive evidence concerns the observed compact aromatic organization.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxyindole anilide scores 0.3051048083696145. The substituted indole/pyridyl N-hydroxy amide reaches 0.47411701813450596, with related N-S and halomethyl variants at 0.4509940583060807 and 0.4478476056206344. Tiny chlorine, sulfur-chloride and hydrocarbon molecules score 0.0. Several different N-halogen or halomethyl placements share 0.4478476056206344, supporting a favorable compact aromatic/carbonyl organization without showing that a specific reactive halogen bond is required. The seed-2 diketone leader scores 0.438972502037081, while more substituted late members can score only 0.2537139094300773; extra polar groups are not uniformly beneficial.

per_task.generated_character: The best seed-0 family is a compact linked system of fused nitrogen heterocycles: a quinazoline-like bicyclic aromatic region is attached to a bridged nitrogen-rich carbonyl/thione system. The leader has 30 heavy atoms and calculated molecular weight 473.25, with O-F, aryl chlorine and fluorinated/chloromethyl-ether substituents. A 28-heavy-atom difluoromethyl analogue has the same score. Seed 1 favors linked aza-aromatic/lactone-like rings bearing carbon-linked nitrile and O-linked cyanate groups. Seed 2 retains aryl/heteroaryl assemblies containing peroxide links, halogenated methine centres and, in a late example, nitrite and N=S functionality. Mean proposal SMILES length is 59.1. The Parent seed-0 leader had 71 heavy atoms and score 0.6092799188640974, whereas the Child seed-0 leader has 30 and scores 0.8561477222467935. This is a substantial shift toward a smaller heterocyclic family, without eliminating reactive bonds.
liabilities: The leading aryl O-F bond is chemically different from an ordinary aryl C-F bond and is a prominent reactivity concern.
The leaders combine a thione and dense nitrogen-ring connectivity with unspecified potential stereogenic centres; graph validity does not establish a practical route or conformation.
Other cited output contains O-linked cyanates, peroxides, nitrite or N=S bonds. These remain despite the smaller leading family.
The maximum proposal SMILES length is 191, so smaller leaders do not imply that all large assemblies disappeared.
missing_features: Stable replacements for O-F and other reactive peripheral groups, preserving the successful compact heterocyclic arrangement, are not demonstrated among the best examples.
The compact high-scoring arrangement is concentrated in one seed; other seeds remain in different families with cyanate, peroxide or halogenated-methine liabilities.
Geometry and stereochemical identity of the bridged core and substituted methine centres are unresolved; no absent target-specific decoration can be inferred from scores alone.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted fused dione scores 0.548381482770623; the new linked nitrogen-rich family reaches 0.8561477222467935. Several different peripheral fluorinated substituents share that score, while a nearby ring-connectivity variant scores 0.8467276542724114. The improvement therefore accompanies a particular combined heterocyclic organization, rather than indiscriminate growth or a single small substituent. Small molecules including ethene, cyanide and cyanogen remain at the 0.5 floor. Other seeds reach 0.6248206599713055 and 0.6178024026512013 with different heteroaromatic arrangements. The records do not isolate whether the leader's O-F group is required, and they do not demonstrate chemical stability.

per_task.generated_character: The best molecule is a relatively conventional flexible tertiary amine linking two aromatic regions, with phenol, methoxy, ethyl and propyl substituents, a benzylic chloride and two aromatic bromines. It has 30 heavy atoms but calculated molecular weight 561.79 because of its heavy halogens. Other leaders include pyrrolidine attached to a substituted dihydrobenzothiophene/biaryl system, or an aminoethyl-substituted pyrrolidine joined to a fluorinated benzylic and cyclic aryl-ether region. Thus basic amines and hydrophobic aromatic groups are already abundant. Mean proposal SMILES length is 53.8. The Parent seed-0 leader combined an aryl amine with unusual sulfur-oxo connectivity at 0.9959491085611949; the Child leader reaches 0.9999989177995104 with a more conventional amine skeleton but heavy halogenation. Parent and Child seed-2 leaders also retain closely related aryl/cyclic-amine organizations.
liabilities: The flexible leader has a benzylic chloride, substantial bromine/chlorine mass and a long hydrophobic chain; high score alone does not characterize stability, solubility or selectivity.
Some close high-scoring variants close large rings or introduce a cyclic cumulated-double-bond segment.
Pyrrolidine/thioether frameworks are more recognizable synthetic targets, but their stereochemistry is unspecified.
missing_features: Stereochemically specified versions of the successful aryl/cyclic-amine arrangements are absent, despite potential centres in the benzylic and saturated-ring regions.
Stable alternatives to benzylic chloride and excessive heavy-halogen loading are not established at the leading score; the basic-amine motif itself is already present.
The neutral records leave relevant protonation states unresolved, without establishing that the generator lacks protonatable centres.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The low-scoring N-sulfonyl cyclic amine scores 0.00021169315013374197, whereas the flexible tertiary amine scores 0.9999989177995104 and the cyclic thioether/pyrrolidine analogue scores 0.9999934235240012. The consistent visible association is the presentation of accessible aliphatic amines with aromatic hydrophobic regions; nitrogen count or an isolated aromatic ring is insufficient. A much smaller final fused-thioether amine still scores 0.9947190867301007, showing that maximal size and every aromatic appendage are not required in this sample. Near-ceiling scores occur for both flexible and cyclic forms, including a cyclic cumulene variant, so no claim of geometric validation or measured binding follows.

per_task.generated_character: The leading seed-2 family links a propyl-substituted quinoline to a partially unsaturated, bridged nitrogen/oxygen ring system bearing N-methyl groups and two carbonyls. The leader has 29 heavy atoms, calculated molecular weight 394.48 and perceived eight-membered cycles alongside the quinoline rings. Other seeds use related quinoline-linked amino/ether rings or a densely bridged diaryl lactam with an N-O bridge. Mean proposal SMILES length is 52.6 and halogen-string incidence is relatively low at 0.1241. The chemistry is recognizable at the functional-group level, but medium-ring closures and stereochemical definition remain uncertain. Parent seed 2 had a related quinoline/dicarbonyl nitrogen-ring leader at 0.23035161967494103; the Child reaches 0.22600312875247064. Its slightly smaller family remains within the same broad chemical territory.
liabilities: Medium-ring bridges and ring-bound unsaturation create synthesis and geometry questions that atom-count compactness does not resolve.
Some near-leading or late structures introduce N-O or N-N bonds while retaining the same family.
No proposal has a stereocentre marker despite potential centres in the leading cyclic structures.
missing_features: Chemically independent frameworks presenting the favorable aromatic and nitrogen-carbonyl functions are scarce among the leaders.
The bridged medium rings lack assigned stereochemical and conformational identity.
Simpler accessible connectivities reproducing the combined favorable arrangement are not demonstrated by the leading excerpt; isolated low-scoring fragments cannot answer that question.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted fused dione scores 0.1678386594791329, while the leading quinoline-linked bridged dicarbonyl structure reaches 0.22600312875247064. Extending one oxygen-containing ring segment gives 0.2243673789386108; replacing the corresponding oxygen-containing segment with carbon gives 0.22237557923837944. The narrow interval supports the combined aromatic/nitrogen-carbonyl organization more strongly than any unique local atom choice. Tiny methane, acetylene and ethene proposals score 0.0. Related final medium-ring variants remain around the supplied 0.20735848908965118 to 0.2219442706159798 values, without exposing a missing exact pharmacophore.

per_task.generated_character: The best seed-2 molecule has 26 heavy atoms and calculated molecular weight 372.32. It combines an aromatic-labelled nine-membered nitrogen heterocycle bearing imino and carbonyl groups with a fluorinated five-membered ring containing a cumulated sequence of double bonds and an enolic hydroxyl. Fluoroethyl and fluoromethyl substituents decorate the nitrogen-rich region. This leader does not require an N-F bond, but its small cyclic cumulene is a major geometric concern. Other high scorers retain N-fluorinated fused carbonyl/imino heterocycles with small unsaturated nitrogen rings. Mean proposal SMILES length is 46.6, and cumulated-double-bond-string incidence is 0.0517. Parent seed-0 and seed-1 best molecules and scores recur; seed 2 changes from a conventional-sized fused heterocycle at 0.6025252354500499 to the cyclic-cumulene family at 0.7208853668418119. The increased score does not imply improved chemical feasibility.
liabilities: A cumulated double-bond sequence forced into a five-membered ring raises severe strain and accessibility concerns.
Aromatic SMILES perception for the nine-membered heterocycle does not establish a stable aromatic conformation.
Other high-scoring families still use N-F bonds and small unsaturated rings, so removal of N-F from the top molecule does not establish general reactivity control.
Fluorinated substitution can change score sharply while leaving the difficult core intact.
missing_features: Geometrically credible noncumulated frameworks preserving the favorable compact fluorinated/polar arrangement are not established at the leading score.
The large aromatic-labelled nitrogen ring, enolic representation and potential stereogenic centre lack demonstrated conformational, tautomeric and stereochemical definition.
A chemically independent stable alternative to the leading family is not demonstrated; the score does not identify an absent exact target motif.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted dione scores 0.0020944534688323298. The new cyclic-cumulene leader reaches 0.7208853668418119; a related noncumulated five-membered-ring analogue with different nitrogen fluorination scores 0.6725143757617169. Thus high reward is not shown to require the cumulene itself. A particularly informative close pair replaces the leader's fluoromethyl substituent with hydroxymethyl and falls to 0.006653135242129762, with the rest of the cited framework unchanged. This shows strong sensitivity to local substituent composition in that scaffold, without revealing the hidden scoring rule. Isolated fluorine, fluorine gas and fluoromethane have extremely low scores, so fluorination alone is insufficient.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Leading molecules contain O-F, N-F, N-Cl or N-Br bonds, halomethyl ethers and benzylic chlorides. Other supplied molecules retain peroxide and cyanate groups. Familiar aromatic and carbonyl frameworks therefore coexist with local reactivity concerns.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently distinguish stable halogen placement from reactive bonds to heteroatoms or benzylic centres.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Task-agnostic generation needs bond-environment awareness and conventional substituent alternatives that preserve learned favorable scaffold relationships. A universal halogen ban would ignore ordinary aryl fluorination, while the present scores do not prove that replacing every reactive group improves reward.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The highest-scoring fluorinated leader contains a five-membered cyclic cumulene attached to an aromatic-labelled nine-membered nitrogen ring. Other leaders include medium-ring bridges, and a high-scoring aryl-amine variant contains another cyclic cumulated-double-bond segment.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring construction can preserve graph validity while creating unsaturation and bridges of doubtful geometric feasibility.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator would need ring-size-aware unsaturation and conformational constraints, alongside topology-aware alternatives. Ring counts and aromatic labels alone cannot certify a realizable structure; ordinary small rings should remain distinguishable from unsupported bond geometry.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every task has stereocentre-string rate 0.0. Leading aryl/cyclic amines, bridged nitrogen heterocycles and fluorinated ring systems have unassigned potential stereogenic centres in their parsed structures.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output lacks explicit stereochemical identity after creating saturated or bridged centres.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Representation and transformations need to preserve or deliberately resolve stereochemistry when the chemistry requires it. Protonation and tautomeric state are separate questions; neutral strings and unspecified centres do not by themselves establish a score penalty.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The digest contains isolated halogens, simple hydrocarbons and other small reagents at the score floors, while successful molecules combine several ring and functional-group regions. A leading compact heterocycle is much smaller than its Parent counterpart, and several peripheral variants share exactly the same score; large proposals nevertheless remain.
transferable_gaps.gap: Useful structural context is not consistently retained: output includes tiny floor-scoring fragments as well as unnecessarily elaborate relatives.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Task-agnostic proposals need to preserve enough molecular context to test learned functional-group arrangements and support structural simplification within those arrangements. The evidence motivates feedback-informed control of fragment loss and redundant elaboration, not a universal molecular-size cutoff.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The leading excerpts repeatedly change halogen location, short side chains, ring atoms or carbonyl-adjacent groups on retained aromatic amide, fused heterocycle, aryl-amine or bridged dicarbonyl families. High identity counts and ring presence therefore do not demonstrate broad useful scaffold coverage.
transferable_gaps.gap: Leading chemistry is often confined to close variants of a single framework within a seed.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator needs scaffold-level transformations that reorganize learned favorable functional-group relationships into chemically independent plausible frameworks. Scored descendants and chemical feasibility should distinguish meaningful diversity from new SMILES alone.

nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves a bounded population of molecular graphs that have real accepted scores. Greedy score and arrival-order survival immediately admits useful offspring; score-band draws then choose first parents and distinct crossover partners from those current survivors. Connected-fragment crossover, optional finishing and ordinary graph-edit walks make a complete fresh surplus pool. Stable canonical admission rejects duplicates. A Gaussian process learns from the full chronological accepted archive using counts of local molecular environments and generalized Tanimoto similarity, and correlated posterior draws allocate the next evaluations. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is already disabled. Every real accepted label immediately updates both ordinary survivors and the predictor archive.
approach.novelty: Test the aggregate contribution of adaptive breeder support and rank allocation by replacing their shared consumer with uniform draws from one immutable copy of the retained initial population. Generated offspring can still improve live survivors and train the predictor, but cannot become starting breeding sources. Earlier siblings fixed initial sources while retaining ranked draws, made current live draws uniform while retaining recursion, or delayed newly accepted sources by one feedback cohort. This control removes dynamic source membership and rank allocation together at one boundary. It measures that scoped aggregate; graph primitives, initial score-dependent retention and learned evaluation allocation remain, so the complete foundation contribution stays unresolved.

nodes.hypothesis: Remove ongoing scored-adaptive source support and rank allocation jointly at the breeder consumer by using uniform eligible first-parent and distinct-identity partner draws from one immutable serial-ordered snapshot of the original retained usable initial LIVE population, including that snapshot in the inherited crossover-availability guard, while ordinary current greedy survivors and full accepted-label count-GP learning remain immediate.

finding_summary.headline: Adaptive breeder feedback remains valuable: fixed uniform initial sources lose 0.24468 in mean Top-1
finding_summary.insights: The experiment supports positive conditional value of adaptive source membership and score-ranked allocation together at the breeder boundary, even when every generated score still trains the predictor. It rules out a broken or starved learning archive as the explanation for this panel’s loss, and shows why parent-beat counts and easier selected-stream prediction can mislead when source quality and reward range fall. Chemistry agrees with this pattern: small fragments and acyclic emissions became more frequent, and compact free-amine/aromatic combinations were recovered inconsistently, despite many new cores and continued access to rich ring systems. Fewer questionable reactive bonds did not rescue the endpoints. These are observed chemical associations, not a demonstrated mediator. The earlier fixed ranked-source and live-uniform controls are compatible with this result but share its Parent; their losses cannot be added or used to infer an interaction. The experiment does not divide the value between membership, weights, survivor selection or subsequent learned allocation, and it does not remove retained graph primitives or initial score-dependent retention. The whole graph-foundation contribution gap therefore remains open.
finding_summary.results: Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.59567 to 0.35099 across the five tasks and three matched seeds, a loss of 0.24468 against the registered 0.002 scale. Fourteen of fifteen endpoints fell; zaleplon’s third seed improved by 0.00046. Every breeding draw used an unchanged initial molecule, and 1,309 generated molecules that naturally had positive original breeding support were blocked. All 4,200 nonterminal generated labels still entered later GP fits; the final 150 labels had no later suggestion. Local best-parent beats rose from 629 to 2,033, while incumbent gains fell from 258 to 79: beating weaker fixed sources did not sustain improvement. Prospective selected-stream pair ordering rose from 71.1% to 76.1%, and prediction MSE fell from 0.01272 to 0.00197, yet endpoint quality deteriorated. Seed macro dispersion widened from 0.02659 to 0.07699.

molecular.headline: Aromatic starting-scaffold families persist, with more tiny fragments and inconsistent recovery of compact amine-rich or reorganized heterocycles
molecular.overall_character: Assessed n-c8e2f3c42535 against accepted code Parent n-62daf219c70a. The immutable request reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true, matched Search seeds 0/1/2 and no profile mismatch. All 15 Child and 15 published Parent trajectory paths were present and read: each has 300 accepted observations, ten initial and 290 optimizer emissions. No task is omitted and no smoke record is included. The evidence-index published template and original Parent policy node were used; historical gaps retain origin n-c55c3d520a2c as reproduced by n-62daf219c70a. All 30 files have the same ordered ten initial molecular identities. Thus cross-seed recurrence and shared initial chemical families are dependent evidence; structural resemblance is not an ancestry join. All 4350 Child and 4350 Parent optimizer SMILES parse and sanitize with the installed RDKit, which establishes graph representability, not route feasibility, stability, binding, toxicity or clinical usefulness. No new labels were obtained. The Child produces indole arylamides, diaryl pyrazoline thiocarboxamide derivatives, quinoline-linked phenoxy systems, aryl pyrrolopyrimidinediones, polyaryl oxo O/N heterocycles and large acid/amide/sulfonamide hybrids. Both saturated and aromatic rings are abundant. Child median heavy-atom counts in task order are 25/31/39/32/22; Parent medians are 25/33/31/30/27. Child has 341 emissions of at most five heavy atoms and 542 acyclic emissions versus Parent 123 and 129, respectively. These are emission counts with repeated molecular identities across seeds, not independent discoveries. Child displays 128 emissions with a covalent N/O/S–halogen bond and 81 with O–O bonds versus Parent 1329 and 273 under explicit substructure definitions; lower reactive-bond incidence does not explain or negate the endpoint changes. Conventional amides, ethers, phenols and amines coexist with O-halogen fragments, thiocarbonyl/hydrazine combinations, crowded fused/bridged topologies and very large aromatic conjugates. Medicinally recognizable chemistry supports moderate drug-likeness, but the mixture makes synthetic plausibility questionable. Child raw unique typed/generic Murcko core counts by task are 266/143, 445/346, 554/488, 388/272 and 343/235, with every acyclic structure assigned one shared <acyclic> core. Parent counts are 295/124, 404/277, 391/259, 584/406 and 208/93. These raw counts are not productive novelty, endpoint gain or chemically credible independent scaffold coverage. Leaders often resemble the initial scaffold families, and two central-task seed leaders are exactly the same molecular identity. No genealogy, new-core mediation or separate source-support/rank contribution is inferred. Digest stereocentre and formal-charge string incidences are zero throughout; RDKit identifies potential tetrahedral stereocentres in 1841 Child emissions but no specified atom chirality. Neutral SMILES do not establish absence of protonatable amines. Parent leaders can be higher-scoring while chemically more doubtful. Reported score associations therefore do not justify imitating reactive halogen bonds or cyclic cumulenes, identify an objective optimum, or clear the unresolved whole-foundation contribution gap.

nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves scored molecular graphs within each task. It breeds from high-score quantiles of a bounded, greedily retained population, uses connected-fragment crossover and local mutations with ordinary continuation, and admits fresh candidates under stable canonical identities. Its direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled. Before each allocation it fits a Gaussian process to every usable accepted observation, including offspring no longer in the breeding population. Folded Morgan counts and generalized Tanimoto covariance support correlated function draws over the complete fresh offspring pool. The current accepted-score mean and population standard deviation set both the training normalization and the raw units of predictions and draws; masked sampled maxima choose the announced batch.
approach.novelty: Remove only the repeated updating of that score normalizer: retain the mean, population standard deviation and floored scale from the first ordinary fit, while continuing to train on every newly accepted raw score. This tests the conditional contribution of adaptive normalization. The earlier initial-cohort control froze both training membership and normalization; this control keeps online data conditioning active. Other siblings changed target ranks, added residual-amplitude feedback or reserved a variance-seeking position. None isolated this existing normalizer while retaining the original full-archive correlated selector.

nodes.hypothesis: Remove only ongoing recomputation of the GP score-normalization mean and scale by retaining the exact initial accepted-label normalization constants, while continuing full-archive raw-label conditioning and the inherited correlated posterior selector at every original fit.

finding_summary.headline: Adaptive normalization contributes: freezing it lowers mean final score by 0.03436
finding_summary.insights:
Updating the score mean and scale has positive conditional value even when the GP continues to learn from every new accepted label. The earlier control froze training membership and normalization together; this result narrows the answer to normalization without undoing that joint finding. It still does not separate centering from scaling, the associated change in raw observation noise, or their interaction with online training. The fixed scale becomes especially small relative to later score spread in docking and sitagliptin, whereas it exceeds the contemporaneous scale in median_2. These measured differences explain why raw uncertainty changes in different directions; they do not identify which consequence caused the endpoint loss.

More local parent wins, more reused breeders and slightly better same-stream prediction error are therefore insufficient evidence for useful search. The molecular assessment likewise finds fewer perceived scaffold families on every objective, but preserves useful aromatic amides, amines and alternative ring arrangements alongside reactive substituents, questionable ring geometry and unresolved stereochemistry. That combination does not support a universal size, ring or heteroatom explanation, nor does it assign the score loss to one chemical motif. The passive reference has no rewards for omitted choices and no alternative future history, so mediation remains open. This complete exposed panel answers the registered normalization-only control under the current budget and composition; it supplies neither a broader claim that uncertainty should always increase nor a reason to retune this fixed control.
finding_summary.results:
The intended control executed while online learning remained active. All 435 fits retained every currently accepted raw label in order, with 4,200 generated labels entering their next fit and 150 final observations correctly censored. The first fit and selected batch matched the Parent in every task and seed. Fixed initial constants then differed from current-archive normalization in all 420 later fits. On the actual Child pools, the passive adaptive-normalization reference selected different sets in 401 of 435 batches; five additional batches differed only in order. Of 1,710 actually evaluated molecules absent from the reference sets, 1,641 entered a later fit and 1,016 later served as breeding parents. All evaluations completed.

Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.595670 to 0.561314, a paired change of -0.034355 against the predicted loss scale of 0.002. Seed changes were -0.098249, +0.017166 and -0.021983; ten of fifteen task–seed endpoints declined and five improved. The Child had more generating-parent wins, 691 versus 629, but fewer sequential incumbent advances, 242 versus 258. Lower local prediction error also failed to translate into a better endpoint: on the same scored Child molecules, fixed-normalizer MSE was 0.005729 versus 0.005867 for the passive adaptive reference, while nominal 95% latent-interval coverage fell from 77.43% to 55.49%.
