molecular.headline: Aromatic scaffolds and cyclic amines coexist with reactive heteroatom bonds, sulfur-rich cages, and undefined stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: Node n-ccfeef46a581 produces compact to relatively large, extensively branched ring-containing molecules. All supplied tasks have trajectories; the brief tasks_without_trajectories list is empty. Each task digest covers 900 evaluations, including 870 optimizer proposals. The optimizer-proposal ring_closure_rate and branch_rate are 1.0 on every task. In the fixed task order, aromatic_atom_rate is 0.9517, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0, and 0.7184; these are string-presence rates, not fractions of atoms or perceived aromatic rings. Mean SMILES lengths are 45.9, 69.6, 68.8, 61.0, and 62.8, respectively; text length is only a rough indication of molecular elaboration. Recognizable indole carboxamides, aryl ketones, cyclic amines, ureas, and lactams are present. They coexist with peroxide and nitrogen-halogen bonds, unconventional sulfur valences, nonbenzenoid small-ring unsaturation, and densely bridged polycycles. Charged_rate and stereocentre_rate are 0.0 throughout. This describes the submitted representations: many molecules contain potentially ionizable groups or stereogenic structures despite having no charge or tetrahedral stereochemical annotations. Across tasks and seeds there are distinct scaffold families, so diversity has not collapsed globally; within several best-molecule panels, closely related members of one seed-specific family dominate. Synthetic plausibility is mixed, with ordinary medicinal fragments embedded in structures whose stability, geometry, and practical assembly are doubtful. These are structural judgments, not synthesis predictions or activity measurements. All child and Parent trajectory records were read. Parent comparison shows exact molecular-history preservation for median_2 and sitagliptin_mpo, with changed families on the other tasks. The digest final_molecules excerpts contain the last proposals from seed 2; they are not all-seed final incumbents. The gradients below describe associations and occasional direct structural comparisons in the observed scores. They do not reveal hidden objective definitions or establish a specific missing target pharmacophore.

per_task.generated_character: The relatively compact output is dominated by fused aromatic or partly aromatic heterocycles bearing aryl carboxamides or aryl ketones, with alkoxy, alkyl, amino, halogen, and sulfur substituents. The ethoxy/methyl/thiol-substituted indole carboxanilide at 0.399050 is recognizable synthetic chemistry, though the free thiol adds reactivity. The maximum at 0.402997 instead combines an aminomethyl substituent, a thiocarboxylic acid, an S-bound nitrile, an unsaturated fused oxygen/sulfur ring system, and a bridged tertiary nitrogen group. The lowest optimizer excerpt at 0.021533 has an expanded, partly saturated ring and an N-fluoro hydroxylamine substituent. Late seed-2 proposals retain the unusual sulfur/bridged-amine framework. Relative to Parent n-abcd951ab7cc, the seed-0 and seed-1 best molecules and scores are identical; the seed-2 best changes from a substituted benzofuran aryl carboxamide at 0.410039 to the sulfur-containing bridged-amine structure at 0.402997. That structural change does not demonstrate improved makeability.
liabilities: Expanded-valence sulfur, a thiocarboxylic acid, and the bridged unsaturated nitrogen group make the maximum less straightforward to synthesize than its near-scoring indole carboxamide comparator.
N-fluoro hydroxylamine, nitrogen-bromine, and cyclic cumulated-double-bond motifs occur in the trajectory excerpts. The digest cumulated_double_bond_rate is 0.1149.
The new bridged structures have no stereochemical assignments, so the scored strings do not define a single stereochemical product.
missing_features: Compact aromatic-carbonyl organization and the productive aminomethyl spacing are not consistently retained in the low-score and late edited molecules, even though higher-scoring examples show them.

A well-defined, ordinary-valence series preserving the newly favored nitrogen placement while avoiding the bridged sulfur framework is not established by these excerpts; its score benefit remains unmeasured.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial methoxy-rich indole carboxamide scores 0.305105, while the ethoxy/methyl/thiol analogue scores 0.399050. A carbonyl-disrupted aminoalkyl analogue in the low excerpt scores 0.033430, and the expanded partly saturated structure scores 0.021533; the observed contrast is consistent with preserving a compact aromatic/carbonyl arrangement. There is also a more specific comparison: replacing the maximum molecule's aminomethyl group with fluoromethyl gives 0.329946, and shortening it to a directly attached amino group gives 0.330107. The placement and spacing of this nitrogen therefore matter in this observed scaffold. Neither conventional valence nor an entirely aromatic framework is sufficient to explain the ranking: the expanded-valence sulfur maximum slightly exceeds the ordinary indole carboxamide, and cyclic cumulated-double-bond analogues appear at 0.386646.

per_task.generated_character: These are comparatively large, heavily substituted aromatic molecules; mean SMILES length is 69.6, and every proposal has both ring-closure and aromatic-atom text. The 0.617463 maximum contains a phenyl-pyridyl diarylamine assembly, a furan carrying a substituted urea, an aryl imine, a methylthio group, an O-O-N substituent bearing bromine on nitrogen, and a terminal thiocarbonyl chain. The seed-2 final excerpt instead contains fused nitrogen heterocyclic diones, a fused aza ring system, a flexible polyene side chain, and alkoxy-rich branches. The low 0.518907 excerpt is a crowded bridged heterocycle retaining an ester and amide-type carbonyls but disrupting much of the ordinary aromatic organization. Compared with the Parent, the seed-0 maximum changes from 0.616171 to 0.617463 and the seed-1 maximum from 0.605140 to 0.609136, while the seed-2 trajectory is molecularly identical. The changed branches continue to produce extensively decorated aromatic and nitrogen/sulfur-rich structures; they do not establish a consistently simple synthetic series.
liabilities: The best series combines peroxide, nitrogen-halogen, and terminal thiocarbonyl functionality, raising stability and practical synthesis concerns despite high scores.

The large polyene/alkoxy branches and heavily bridged alternatives create conformational and assembly complexity; double-bond and tetrahedral configurations are not explicitly defined in the cited examples.
Halogen_rate is 0.7425, but some halogens are bonded to nitrogen rather than residing only in conventional carbon-halogen substituents.
missing_features: Stable, ordinary-linkage realizations of the highly decorated aromatic/carbonyl arrangement are not represented as a coherent high-scoring comparison series; the leading family repeatedly carries peroxide-linked nitrogen and thiocarbonyl appendages.

Controlled comparisons that preserve the useful aromatic attachment pattern while simplifying flexible branches and bridges are missing. The score ties do not justify inventing a specific hidden decoration or binding geometry.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted fused dione scores 0.548381. Higher values accompany elaborated aromatic/aza-aromatic connectivity retaining urea or dione carbonyls, while the disrupted bridged low excerpt scores 0.518907. This is a multifeature association, not proof that adding bulk or a particular functional group causes improvement. The digest contains an exact 0.617402 tie between an open diarylamine derivative, a bridged derivative, and a derivative with chlorine replacing a methyl group on the peroxide-linked nitrogen. Those equal scores show that the observed high region does not reliably distinguish these changes in geometry or chemical liability. The separate dione/polyene family also reaches 0.609218, so a unique required terminal decoration cannot be identified from these trajectories.

per_task.generated_character: The output spans bulky acid/amide/sulfonamide polyaryls, more compact polycyclic amines, and sulfur-rich bridged structures. The 0.999999 maximum is an N-methyl tetrahydroisoquinoline-like scaffold bearing an amino-substituted azetidine through a methylene linker, together with an ethyl group, aryl fluorine, methoxy, and a thioether-linked nonbenzenoid fused small-ring group. It contains recognizable potentially basic cyclic amines and an exocyclic primary amine, all encoded neutrally. The 0.006990 low excerpt retains carboxylic acid, amide, and N-sulfonylated cyclic nitrogen functionality in a larger polyaryl molecule. The final seed-2 excerpt instead has dense sulfur-containing bridges, multiple nitrogen/oxygen linkages, and sulfur-carbon triple bonding; it is chemically very different from the seed-0 maximum. Parent comparison is heterogeneous: the seed-0 maximum changes from 0.885624 to 0.999999 with a less sulfur-heavy amine scaffold, while the other seed maxima change from 0.868020 to 0.806462 and from 0.914814 to 0.471973. The single near-unity maximum therefore does not characterize every trajectory.
liabilities: The high series combines ordinary saturated nitrogen rings with an unusual fused unsaturated small-ring group; recognizing the amine scaffold does not validate the appended ring geometry.
A high-scoring hydroperoxide analogue and late expanded-valence sulfur, sulfur-carbon triple bonds, and nitrogen-oxygen/nitrogen-nitrogen linkages raise distinct stability concerns.
Halogen_rate is 0.9977. The molecules also have unassigned stereogenic structures despite the universal absence of stereocentre annotations.
missing_features: The compact cyclic-amine/aryl organization seen in the high seed-0 series is not reproduced cleanly in the other trajectories, which retain heavily bridged and sulfur-rich structures.
Chemically interpretable alternatives to the nonbenzenoid small-ring appendage, with the same amine presentation and defined stereochemistry, are not established as a scored series.
Explicit protonation alternatives are absent despite potentially ionizable amines. The trajectories provide no direct charge-state comparison, so a charge-related score benefit cannot be asserted.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The high seed-0 series replaces much of the low series's acid, amide, and sulfonamide burden with compact cyclic amines and differently positioned hydrophobic ring groups. That supports an association with amine presentation and molecular organization, not a conclusion about a particular receptor interaction. Amine presence alone is insufficient: the initial N-methylpiperidine-containing molecule scores 0.000379. A hydroperoxide-containing analogue remains at 0.999994, close to the 0.999999 maximum, showing that this high-score region tolerates a conspicuous chemical liability. The final seed-2 sulfur-rich example scores 0.210570, while a related example replacing one sulfur centre with carbon scores 0.343373. This local contrast supports sensitivity to the represented sulfur framework, without explaining the whole between-seed difference.

per_task.generated_character: The molecules are medium to large aromatic heterocycles with substantial ring bridging and amide-derived functionality; mean SMILES length is 61.0 and aromatic_atom_rate is 1.0. The 0.211969 maximum contains pyridyl and tolyl groups, alkyl substituents, an alkene, an N-methyl lactam, and an N-O bridge in a densely connected polycyclic framework. The high excerpt mainly varies the alkyl groups and bridge composition around this family. The low 0.124680 example is a more open aryl/pyrrole ester-phenol scaffold with a flexible ketone/urea/hydrazine-bearing branch. Another low example carries organic hypobromite and brominated side-chain functionality. The final seed-2 excerpt has a bridged sulfur/nitrogen dicarbonyl system with aromatic and hydroxymethyl/alkoxy substituents. Every molecular record and score in the child trajectories matches the Parent for this task, including the 0.211969 best structure. Ordinary lactam and aromatic fragments are present, but the recurring bridge networks and N-O chemistry make the whole structures synthetically questionable.
liabilities: The leading series contains N-O bridges, and a nearly scoring analogue contains an O-O bond within that bridge; these linkages complicate stability and synthetic interpretation.
Dense overlapping ring closures and unspecified stereogenic centres make a single practical three-dimensional product difficult to infer from the strings.
Other branches add organic hypobromites and unconventional sulfur bonding; the observed ring richness is not evidence that those assemblies are readily makeable.
missing_features: A broader set of chemically ordinary arrangements that retain the leading aromatic/lactam relationships without the crowded N-O bridge network is not established by the high-molecule panel.
The constrained structures lack stereochemical definition. Whether resolving those configurations would change this score is not observable here.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl fused-dione molecule scores 0.167839, the open ketone/urea/hydrazine example 0.124680, and the constrained lactam/N-O-bridged maximum 0.211969. Within the leading family, extending the carbon substituent at the ring bridge from methyl to ethyl changes 0.208747 to 0.211969. The observed gradient therefore contains both a preference for this particular constrained aromatic/lactam organization over the shown open analogues and only modest local sensitivity to alkyl elaboration. An additional oxygen in the N-O bridge gives a peroxide-containing analogue at 0.206478, so nearly retaining the score does not establish chemical stability. These structures and scores do not identify an absent reference scaffold or prove that more bridges generally improve the objective.

per_task.generated_character: The leading molecules are densely cyclized, sulfur-rich, fluorinated heterocycles rather than a simple amine/amide series. Mean SMILES length is 62.8; ring_closure_rate is 1.0, while aromatic_atom_rate is 0.7184, consistent with the substantial nonaromatic cage chemistry in the trajectories. The 0.590353 maximum combines a nitrogen heterocyclic dione, carbon-fluorine substituents, an alcohol-bearing fluoro carbon attached to sulfur, sulfur-sulfur connectivity, and expanded-valence sulfur embedded in multiple fused and bridged rings. A high seed-0 example at 0.481186 has a still more sulfur-heavy framework, an acyl fluoride, and sulfur-nitrogen functionality. The seed-2 final family contains a cyclic thioester/carbonyl framework, aldehyde or sulfur-containing acyl branches, an imidoyl nitrogen group with N-F connectivity, and dense bridges; it includes the 0.448455 seed-2 best. All child molecular records and scores for this task reproduce the Parent exactly. The sulfur valences, reactive appendages, and unspecified stereochemical relationships make these among the least synthetically convincing structures in the panel.
liabilities: Repeated expanded-valence sulfur and sulfur-sulfur bonds are incorporated directly into constrained unsaturated cages; graph readability does not establish stable bonding or feasible geometry.
The cited examples contain an acyl fluoride, N-F bonds, an aldehyde, and a sulfur-chlorine acyl substituent. These are reactive functionality concerns, not measured toxicity claims.
Extensive fused and bridged ring construction leaves stereogenic relationships unspecified; the neutral strings do not define single stereochemical synthetic products.
missing_features: The trajectories do not establish ordinary-valence, synthetically interpretable analogues that preserve the favorable local fluorinated carbonyl/nitrogen arrangement; the observed higher scores remain tied to highly unusual cage chemistry.
The densely fused structures have no assigned stereochemistry or demonstrated spatial feasibility. No score comparison establishes an advantage for a particular configuration.

A clean matched series separating fluorine placement, carbonyl spacing, and sulfur substitution is absent from the leading examples, so a specific missing functional group cannot be justified from this evidence alone.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aromatic ester/phenol fused dione scores 0.002094, and an expanded-ring derivative retaining that general decoration scores only 7.590554525032884e-10. Higher scores occur after major reorganization into compact fluorinated sulfur-containing frameworks while carbonyl/nitrogen functionality remains in altered arrangements. Fluorination or sulfur enrichment alone cannot explain the gradient: the low digest also contains already sulfur-rich, fluorinated polycycles. Within the late seed-2 family, related carbonyl/linker variants score 0.253662 and 0.448455, while the sulfur-containing acyl-branch variant scores 0.004200. This shows strong sensitivity to the particular composition and connectivity around the cage and carbonyl groups. It does not demonstrate that unusual sulfur chemistry is itself desirable or that a known target pharmacophore is missing.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Across the supplied best, low, and late excerpts, recognizable amides, ureas, lactams, and amines coexist with O-O bonds, nitrogen-halogen bonds, terminal thiocarbonyls, and expanded-valence sulfur. A peroxide-bearing cyclic-amine analogue scores 0.999994, and an O-O-N-linked aromatic urea series reaches 0.617463, demonstrating that these liabilities can survive into high-scoring output. The limitation is therefore not a complete absence of useful functional groups; their chemically ordinary context is not maintained.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably preserve chemically ordinary, stable functional-group connectivity during elaboration.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator needs accessible edits that preserve complete functional-group contexts and produce ordinary-valence analogues of the existing favorable arrangements. Bond proposals and heteroatom substitutions can use the local molecular environment to distinguish conventional amide, ether, amine, and thioether chemistry from reactive or unusual combinations. Any effect on the observed objective scores requires a separate evaluation; these structural concerns do not justify assuming a universal score gain from filtering.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every optimizer proposal set has ring_closure_rate 1.0. The cited high and final structures include densely overlapping bridges, nonbenzenoid fused small-ring unsaturation, cyclic cumulated double bonds, and sulfur-centred multiple bonding. Ordinary indole, saturated cyclic-amine, and lactam fragments are also present, so the missing capability is controlled ring architecture rather than ring creation itself.
transferable_gaps.gap: Abundant ring construction is not accompanied by consistent control over chemically credible ring geometry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The generator would need to propose and retain more interpretable ring and linker arrangements at comparable functionality, using molecule-local topology and geometry plausibility to distinguish ordinary saturated/fused systems from strained unsaturated closures. Conventional small saturated rings should remain accessible; the evidence supports examining the particular bonding and bridge context, not banning every small ring or assuming a particular ring family must score better.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The digest stereocentre_rate is 0.0 in every proposal set. The cited substituted cyclic amines and sulfur-rich bridged frameworks contain stereogenic arrangements whose configurations are left unspecified. The gap concerns representation of the produced molecules; the supplied scores provide no comparison between assigned configurations.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generated structures do not include explicit tetrahedral stereochemical definition despite recurring stereogenic polycycles.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator would need to recognize stereogenic elements and make chemically valid configuration assignment or variation available while preserving explicit isomeric identity. Configuration choices should follow the actual molecular graph and observed feedback, without assuming a preferred configuration or inventing task-specific stereochemical requirements.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Charged_rate is 0.0 on every task despite cited primary and tertiary cyclic amines, carboxylic acids, and thiocarboxylic acids. High-scoring amine-bearing structures are therefore represented only in neutral form in these trajectories; the digest contains no evidence that a different charge state would improve a score.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ionizable functional groups are produced without an observed set of explicit charge or protonation alternatives.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The generator would need molecule-local support for chemically valid protonation and formal-charge alternatives, with the chosen representation kept explicit and consistent. This would address missing chemical-state coverage; its usefulness must be tested through allowed feedback rather than inferred from an objective name or from unmeasured pKa values.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The full panel contains distinct aromatic amide, cyclic-amine, lactam, and sulfur-cage families, supporting moderate overall diversity. Several best-molecule excerpts nevertheless repeat a single seed-specific scaffold through alkyl, halogen, or bridge changes, and the final excerpts can retain the same unusual heteroatom framework. The numerous unique strings do not by themselves establish broad coverage of ordinary alternative scaffolds around the useful functional groups.
transferable_gaps.gap: High-scoring output has limited scaffold variety at a preserved, interpretable functional-group arrangement.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator would need scaffold and linker rearrangements that preserve recognizable functional groups and their relative attachment pattern while offering different, chemically ordinary ring architectures. Such proposals should be driven by the currently observed molecules and scores; the trajectories do not supply a universal desired scaffold or justify choosing a benchmark-specific motif.

nodes.method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
nodes.method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.

approach.method_basis: The Parent searches from one scored current molecule by drawing local atom, bond, path and ring edits, rejecting invalid or previously proposed identities, and submitting the first full batch permitted by short-lived inverse-motif memory. It moves to the highest-scoring accepted neighbor even after a worsening step and keeps a separate best archive. Its retained neighborhood extension also lets an aromatic nitrogen exchange positions with a hydrogen-bearing carbon in the same six-member ring, preserving composition and the attachment framework. Those paired exchanges are extra options in the ordinary atom-change menu; the repaired identity join, same-transition two-sign memory gate and latest-transition overlap refresh remain part of the method.
approach.novelty: Remove the optional aromatic nitrogen-exchange menu extension and test whether the resulting simpler proposal path retains the Parent's score within the supplied margin. The intervention removes both the direct exchange opportunities and their competition with single-element substitutions at participating sites. Earlier integration siblings removed tabu enforcement or overlap refresh; this ablation leaves those mechanisms operative and removes only the paired-exchange proposal channel. It is an explicit contribution and repeatability check: the remaining proposal policy is expected to reproduce the already recorded repaired ancestor, so a matching result will not count as a newly discovered optimization method or independent evidence from new seeds.

nodes.hypothesis: Ablate the retained aromatic C/N relocation menu augmentation so each change_atom draw chooses only its inherited single-element substitution options, removing direct formula-preserving nitrogen exchanges and their allocation competition while retaining the complete inverse-memory and accepted-walk rules.

finding_summary.headline: Exchange removal reproduces the ancestor and stays within the mean loss margin
finding_summary.insights: The result confirms the expected reversion and repeatability; it adds no independent seed evidence beyond the historical ancestor. This sparse exchange allocation is not needed to stay within the supplied mean margin on this panel, although individual paths benefit and one replica loses more than the margin. The experiment also shows why the exchange chemistry cannot be credited or blamed alone: in one shared-source batch, the Parent exchange was not selected, but the changed random-draw progression altered a later ordinary carbon extension into an oxygen extension and changed the winner. Removal measures the whole menu allocation policy. Nitrogen-containing molecules remain reachable, and the resulting families retain reactive bonds, unusual sulfur, dense rings and unassigned stereochemistry. The evidence supports a narrower proposal path in this particular walk, without demonstrating better chemistry or general dispensability of nitrogen relocation.
finding_summary.results: Direct nitrogen exchanges fell from 13 proposals, 10 accepted molecules and 3 selected states to zero, despite eligible pairs appearing in 92 child batches. Removing their menu entries changed 65 of 435 submitted batches and 54 selected states, while the retained tabu gate, overlap refresh, graph validation and accepted-maximum walk passed reconstruction. All fifteen tasks completed. Mean final score fell from 0.521759 to 0.520918, a paired change of -0.000841 within the specified 0.002 margin. Seed changes were +0.000374, -0.002898 and zero; the largest task loss was deco_hop seed 1 at -0.014491. Twelve of fifteen final task scores were unchanged. Every complete child trajectory exactly reproduced the historical repaired ancestor. Live exchange enumeration disappeared, but unmatched wall timings do not establish a speedup.

molecular.headline: Aromatic carbonyls, aryl amines and dense sulfur cages persist; stable linkers and defined stereochemistry remain incomplete
molecular.overall_character: All supplied child and parent trajectories were read; every requested task is covered. Each task contains 900 recorded molecules, including 870 optimizer proposals. The proposal ring-closure-token rate is 1.0 throughout, aromatic-token rates span 0.7184 to 1.0, and mean SMILES lengths span 46.7 to 70.1. The ring and aromatic counters measure presence in molecular SMILES, not fractions of atoms or aromatic stability. The output ranges from moderately sized indole/benzofuran carbonyl compounds to large decorated aza-heterocycles, aryl polyamines and compact but densely bridged sulfur cages. Different seeds explore recognizable different families, but the strongest excerpts are concentrated in closely related frameworks. Parent n-abcd951ab7cc has the same dominant families; entire trajectories are identical for 11 of the 15 task/seed pairs, and the changed pairs retain similar overall size and ring character. Ordinary amides, amines, phenols and thioethers coexist with N-halogen and O-halogen bonds, peroxides, N-N/N-O bridges and unusually substituted multiply bonded sulfur. The charged-token and stereocentre-token rates are 0.0 on every task. Neutral strings do not imply absence of ionizable groups, and unassigned configurations do not imply achiral molecules. Heavy-atom sizes and structural observations below are passive RDKit readings of the supplied SMILES; no synthetic-accessibility score, new oracle evaluation or conformational feasibility calculation was made. Score associations and exact local ties describe only the evaluated molecules, and do not reveal an unseen target structure or establish that chemically questionable groups are necessary.

per_task.generated_character: The proposals contain 21-29 heavy atoms. Leading molecules are substituted fused aromatic heterocycles attached to aryl amides or aryl ketones. The highest observed example is a benzofuran-like N-chloro carboxanilide bearing methyl groups, a thiol and an amino-chloromethyl group. A nearby strong indole carboxanilide instead has an ordinary N-H amide, ethoxy group, methyl and thiol. Other leaders include a benzothiophene-like aryl ketone and partially saturated bridged O/N/S frameworks. The changed seed-0 maximum retains a pyridyl ketone but adds a multiply bonded substituted sulfur centre and an N,N-difluoroaminomethyl group. Aromatic nitrogen therefore remains represented. The low examples retain substantial molecular size but disrupt ring conjugation, enlarge a ring or replace the carbonyl connection. The simpler aromatic amides are plausible synthetic motifs; the reactive and bridged derivatives are much less convincing as stable compounds.
liabilities: N-Cl amide, N-F and N-O groups are distinct chemical concerns from ordinary carbon-bound halogens; the amino-chloromethyl group is also reactive-looking.
Thiols, multiply bonded substituted sulfur and increasingly bridged ring systems complicate stability and synthesis.
Later molecules retain dense rings and introduce N-N bonds without resolving configuration.
missing_features: The weaker carbonyl-replaced or ring-expanded derivatives lack the compact carbonyl-linked aromatic organization present in stronger molecules.
The leading reactive series does not provide a complete set of conventional N-H amide and stable linker counterparts, although an ordinary indole amide already gives a nearby score.
Configurations at substituted saturated carbon sites and bridged junctions remain unspecified.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The N-chloro benzofuran derivative scores 0.41003927643747895, while the more conventional indole amide scores 0.39905049777278273. A carbonyl-replaced indole derivative scores 0.03343008011310944 and an expanded sulfur-containing ring system scores 0.023463222457063. Thus the observed gradient is consistent with maintaining the compact aromatic/carbonyl arrangement; the low carbonyl-replaced molecule remains aromatic, so aromatic content alone is insufficient. Bridged N-H amide relatives bearing carbon-bound chlorine or bromine both score 0.3900523103411983, and their dehalogenated relative scores 0.385823971421255. Current seed 0 reaches 0.3966634883331815 with the unusual pyridyl-ketone/sulfur framework, versus the parent maximum 0.393567030299894 with the benzothiophene-like ketone. Seeds 1 and 2 are unchanged. The small score movement does not resolve the reactive-bond liabilities.

per_task.generated_character: These are the largest proposal families, with 30-53 heavy atoms. The leading molecule has 51 heavy atoms and combines an extensively substituted phenyl ring with a fused nitrogen heterocycle, carbonyl and thiocarbonyl groups, imines and an amino-fluoroalkyl connection. A long mixed ether/thioether chain and a multiply bonded, additionally substituted sulfur centre add substantial flexibility and chemical complexity; N-bromo and terminal S-Cl relatives occur. The final seed-2 family contains a heteroaromatic dione, an unsaturated carbon chain and a fused aza/ether ring with acetal-like branching. The changed seed-1 family instead contains highly unsaturated side chains and an aza-carbonyl/arylamino-ester arrangement. Low examples have more compact ester/phenol/aza-carbonyl structures with altered heterocyclic conjugation. Familiar fragments are abundant, but the assembled high-score molecules have weak practical simplicity and questionable stability.
liabilities: N-Br and S-Cl bonds, imines and multiply bonded sulfur carrying additional substituents raise stability and synthetic concerns.
Long mixed ether/thioether chains and extensively branched substituents increase flexibility and assembly complexity.
Several sizeable changes to peripheral chemistry are indistinguishable in the observed score.
missing_features: The weaker altered-ring compounds lack the retained heteroaromatic/carbonyl organization of stronger decorated molecules.

The leading family lacks a systematic set of compact, stable-linker analogues preserving its main ring arrangement; equal scores do not establish a need for N-bromination or additional flexible appendages.
Configuration at fluorinated and acetal-like carbon centres and geometry of unsaturated substituents remain unassigned.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The leading decorated molecule scores 0.6161710037174721. Multiple relatives share exactly 0.6155070237050044 despite alkyl extension, sulfur-side-chain extension, additional branching or replacement of N-methyl by N-bromo. Two final aza/ether-ring relatives likewise share 0.6092182584436399 with different oxygen/sulfur-containing appendages. These ties do not demonstrate a benefit from the added reactive bond or greater side-chain complexity. Early altered-ring examples score 0.526081691583997 and 0.5286081645773063, below the initial aromatic dione at 0.548381482770623. The larger, decorated heterocyclic arrangement associates with stronger scores, but its individual peripheral requirements are poorly distinguished. Seeds 0 and 2 exactly reproduce the parent trajectories. The changed seed-1 maximum is 0.5906482326855353 versus parental 0.605139548855754, accompanying a different unsaturated ester-containing family in place of the parent amidine/thioester family. The change does not produce an obviously simple or chemically settled series.

per_task.generated_character: The proposals contain 32-43 heavy atoms and retain aromatic and halogenated groups almost throughout. Stronger molecules combine phenol or other aryl surfaces with saturated or partly unsaturated nitrogen rings, primary aminomethyl groups and other potentially basic aliphatic amines. They are also sulfur-rich: the highest observed molecule has 32 heavy atoms, sulfur-containing rings and a sulfur-sulfur multiple bond. Other leaders contain small nitrogen rings or heavily fused aryl/heteroatom frameworks. The low molecules are larger acid/amide/sulfonamide derivatives of the initial biaryl family; their nitrogens are less available as basic aliphatic centres. The aryl/amine fragments are familiar medicinal chemistry, but their unusual sulfur bonding and constrained, unassigned ring relationships make the complete molecules questionable.

nodes.method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
nodes.method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.

approach.method_basis: The Parent searches from one scored current molecule by sampling local graph edits, including direct aromatic nitrogen relocation that preserves molecular formula. It normalizes molecular identities, rejects duplicates and evaluates the first full batch allowed by short-term structural memory. The highest-scoring accepted neighbor becomes the next state even after a worsening move, while a separate archive retains the best observations. Memory records a bounded, sign-balanced set of inverse local-motif changes from every selected transition. A neighbor is vetoed when both signs match one selected-transition origin. Each restriction currently expires after four completed moves, and a newer installation replaces an overlapping key.
approach.novelty: Give a restriction one additional lifetime only when that specific entry actually helped veto a neighbor during its original lifetime. This tests whether exercised structural avoidance is being forgotten too soon. The extension preserves the original transition identity and can happen only once. Earlier siblings changed which motifs receive credit, refined matching, gated credit by score or preserved overlapping origins until their original expiry. This intervention changes the lifetime of used restrictions while retaining the Parent's credit, matching and overlap rules.

nodes.hypothesis: Renew an inverse-motif restriction for exactly one additional inherited tenure when that specific live entry has actually participated in a same-transition bidirectional veto during its initial tenure, retaining its original selected-transition provenance and allowing no further renewal.

finding_summary.headline: Renewed memory replaced 62 evaluated neighbors but lowered the panel score
finding_summary.insights: This rules out a merely larger memory table or a lack of later recurrence as the explanation for the result: renewed restrictions changed both evaluated membership and selected states. Recurrence remains a weak guide to value. Of 343 renewals, 240 never participated in another qualifying veto during their observed extension, and partial matches alone accounted for 103 of those cases. More concretely, at the first DRD2 divergence in seed 1, the renewed memory excluded a neighbor that the actual Parent had scored from the identical source and selected as its winner, improving that source by 0.059783. The Child instead made a worsening move. This is direct evidence that extending an exercised restriction can remove a useful opportunity; the later endpoint loss cannot be assigned to that one veto because subsequent draws and walks diverge. The molecular assessment also finds reactive heteroatom bonds and complex sulfur cages among strongly scored structures, so this recurrence signal provides no demonstrated improvement in chemical stability or makeability. The open question is whether a task-independent signal can distinguish harmful revisits from productive reuse; actual veto participation alone did not supply that distinction in this panel.
finding_summary.results: The intended lifetime and evaluation changes both happened. All 343 used restrictions that survived to their original deadline renewed once, adding 1206 completed restriction-steps; none exceeded the eight-step limit. Renewed entries caused 65 additional vetoes in 53 batches and displaced 62 candidates from complete, reconstructed ten-member comparator batches. All 62 replacements were evaluated, seven became walk states, eight beat their source and two improved the best archive. Renewal changed at least one batch in every task/seed session, while credit selection, overlap replacement and provenance remained intact. All fifteen sessions completed their full budgets. The three-seed macro mean fell from 0.521759 to 0.513767, a paired change of -0.007992 against the required +0.002. Seeds 0 and 2 improved by 0.018110 and 0.028962, but seed 1 fell by 0.071049. Mean DRD2 score fell by 0.068863 and deco_hop by 0.008789; gains in zaleplon (+0.022797), sitagliptin (+0.013894) and median_2 (+0.000999) did not offset those losses. The renewal mechanism is confirmed; its preregistered score benefit failed.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic scaffolds coexist with reactive heteroatom bonds and sulfur cages; high scores do not establish makeability
molecular.overall_character: Read all supplied node and Parent trajectories across seeds 0, 1 and 2 and all five objectives. Each task digest covers 900 scored records, including 870 optimizer proposals; no task lacks trajectories. All optimizer proposals carry ring-closure tokens. Aromatic-token presence rates in the fixed task order are 0.9598, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0 and 0.8287; these measure the presence of aromatic text, not the fraction of aromatic atoms. Every task has charged-token and stereocentre-token rates of 0.0. These are ring-rich, frequently aromatic, branched molecules with carbonyls, nitrogen heterocycles, amines, halogens and conspicuous sulfur chemistry. Some families resemble ordinary medicinal scaffolds, but the stronger observations also include large flexible decorated heteroaromatics, small strained heterocycles and densely bridged sulfur cages. The seed-specific families support moderate overall structural diversity; the 879 unique strings per task do not by themselves establish broad scaffold diversity. The same broad liabilities occur in Parent n-abcd951ab7cc. All saved optimizer molecules in both panels parse with the supplied RDKit, which establishes graph acceptance and does not establish isolation, stability, feasible conformations or a synthetic route. Quantitative molecular sizes, perceived rings and bond counts below are passive readings of the saved molecules, documented with file hashes and per-seed records in .slots/SPIRAL2.r0011-10-improve-L16.molecular-audit.json. All scores below were already present in the supplied trajectories. Score associations are descriptive; no excluded candidate was scored and no mechanism activation or causal efficacy is inferred.

per_task.generated_character: The optimizer molecules have 21-29 heavy atoms, median 25, and 2-7 perceived rings, median 3. The strongest displayed family is a compact unsaturated O/S fused system bearing a nitrile, alkyl substituents and an aminopyridyl ketone; its best member has formula C18H17N3O2S and score 0.4619578459378901. Seed 1 retains a more conventional ethoxy/methyl/thiol-substituted indole carboxanilide as its best observation, 0.39905049777278273. Seed 2 peaks at 0.41003927643747895 with a benzofuran carboxanilide carrying N-chlorination and a chlorinated aminomethyl substituent. Those seed 1 and 2 best molecules and scores also occur in the Parent; the Parent seed 0 best is a thiophene-fused aryl ketone at 0.393567030299894. Thus the new strongest seed contains substantially different nitrile-bearing sulfur chemistry, while the other seeds retain their earlier best families. Late seed 2 proposals are more densely bridged sulfur/aryl-amide structures; the displayed final molecule scores only 0.12143963082287383. The ordinary indole and aryl-carbonyl portions are synthetically recognizable, but the higher-scoring sulfur valences and late bridges make the full structures questionable.
liabilities: Several strong structures contain nonstandard sulfur-carbon multiple bonding or hydrogen-bearing hypervalent sulfur. The late bridged systems add conformational and synthetic uncertainty.
The lower-scoring set includes N-O, N-S and hydroperoxide attachments; the seed 2 peak also contains an N-Cl bond. These liabilities are more specific than a generic objection to sulfur or halogens.
The digest reports no stereochemical annotation, despite the substituted saturated sites and bridges visible in this stream.
missing_features: Consistent retention of the compact nitrile, directly attached carbonyl and intact aminopyridyl aromatic ring is missing from the weaker local variants; rings and heteroatoms themselves are plentiful.

The stronger nitrile arrangement lacks a displayed set of chemically ordinary sulfur-free or conventional-sulfur analogues with established score retention. Such alternatives are a missing comparison, not a demonstrated objective requirement.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxyindole carboxanilide scores 0.3051048083696145. Within the displayed nitrile family, changing the aminophenyl ketone ring to an aminopyridyl ring accompanies a change from 0.4229793555098886 to 0.4394278959350887; replacing the other ring sulfur with oxygen accompanies 0.4619578459378901. A particularly informative comparison is the hydroxy nitrile compound at 0.41930905650182426: its aminoethyl replacement scores 0.029336319454260972, and the analogue with the aminopyridyl ring expanded and dearomatized scores 0.021622380167913884. These observations support a compact nitrile/aryl-carbonyl/heteroaromatic arrangement in this sampled family. They do not show that unusual sulfur bonding is required, or identify an unseen reference structure.

It combines an aza-arene fused to an oxygen ring, a branched acetal-like site, an aminal, an enamine/acylurea chain, phenethyl substitution, thioethers and a sulfenyl chloride. Seed 1 instead reaches a heavily halogenated pyrazole/pyridyl amidine family; its best member at 0.5995615637559372 contains both a carbon-sulfur triple bond and a peroxide. The strongest seed 2 molecule is large and highly flexible; the seed 1 peak is heavy through extensive halogenation. Both add synthetic complexity beyond the recognizable heteroaromatic core.

nodes.method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
nodes.method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.

approach.method_basis: The Parent begins each objective with a recurrent SMILES policy copied from a frozen model trained on an unlabeled molecular corpus. It learns from the best-scoring half of each accepted batch together with the strongest eligible earlier elites from a memory of thirty-two molecules. Those historical records keep their original accepted strings and scores. Within history, an identity's weight decreases with the number of earlier fitting updates that used it, while the total current and historical coefficient shares stay fixed. The policy fits frozen-prior log likelihood plus sixty times accepted reward with a weighted squared-error loss, taking up to twelve clipped Adam steps and retaining the last iterate. It then samples complete SMILES directly and fills the announced batch through chemical validation and canonical duplicate rejection.
approach.novelty: Add a Huber residual loss whose transition scale is the starting weighted root-mean-square residual of that update. Large residuals then have capped influence before their sequence gradients combine; residuals inside the transition keep the Parent's exact squared-error expression. The threshold stays fixed throughout the update. This addresses concentration of fitting pressure that the inherited exposure counter does not measure. Earlier siblings changed training membership or views, normalized target probabilities, restored an earlier optimizer checkpoint, or projected a proposed step to protect historical loss. None bounded individual residual influence while retaining the Parent's current targets and exposure weights. The experiment will establish coefficient suppression and actual gradient-direction changes on identical policy states, then test whether subsequent useful discoveries improve.

nodes.hypothesis: Replace the Parent's exposure-weighted squared residual with an exposure-weighted Huber residual whose transition is the detached starting weighted root-mean-square residual of each update, floored at the square root of the inherited stopping tolerance and held fixed through that update, thereby capping individual residual influence while preserving selected members, augmented targets and exposure coefficients.

finding_summary.headline: Residual caps changed learning direction and improved AUC, but lowered final score and increased duplication
finding_summary.insights: Global gradient clipping did not make the row-level cap redundant: relative learning direction changed measurably in every prospective fitting opportunity. That establishes a real learning intervention, but more balanced residual influence did not provide the proposed final-score benefit. Faster discovery and the final endpoint separated: much of the AUC gain came from reaching strong DRD2 molecules earlier, where the parent already finished near the score ceiling, while sitagliptin lost substantial endpoint value. The molecular assessment found its stronger compact lactam–sulfonamide family in only one seed; broad core coverage in the other seeds did not supply equally useful structures. The cap also left target feasibility unresolved: historical exposures with positive, unattainable log-probability targets increased from 489 to 752 on the resulting trajectories. Starting caps affected current elites much more often than history, yet accepted-score averages and AUC increased, so the prediction of uniformly weaker early exploitation is not supported either. What remains open is how to preserve these early gains while reducing later repetition and avoiding the task-dependent loss of useful molecular families. The evidence does not isolate a particular suppressed row, token change or chemical feature as the cause of the endpoint loss.
finding_summary.results: The cap executed in all 450 updates. In the 420 historical updates followed by new proposals, it reduced influence on 1,465 of 4,200 selected row exposures at update start, including 1,092 current elites and 373 historical elites. The capped rows' mean share of absolute scalar influence fell from 69.22% to 59.37% on those same inputs. Every one of these updates changed the combined gradient direction even after global norm clipping, and every real first backward matched the Huber diagnostic exactly. Huber loss fell in 419 of the 420 updates, although 928 of 2,100 individual historical row exposures ended with larger residuals. All replicas completed. The three-seed final mean fell from 0.517655 to 0.508373, a paired change of -0.009283, with seed changes -0.026055, +0.032442 and -0.034235. The endpoint gain expected by the intent was not observed. Recorded mean AUC nevertheless rose from 0.406769 to 0.458439 and improved in every seed. The largest endpoint changes were a sitagliptin decrease of 0.080247 and a zaleplon increase of 0.035486. Raw duplicates rose from 36.22% to 48.80%, and batches needing additional sampling doubled from 29 to 58, while all 4,350 submitted proposals remained valid and novel.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich medicinal chemistry with concentrated peak families, unspecified stereochemistry and recurring nitroso chemistry in one seed.
molecular.overall_character: All five objectives are covered: the digest contains 900 accepted rows per task, including 870 optimizer proposals, and no tasks without trajectories. I read all child and Parent trajectory files. These are predominantly aromatic medicinal-chemistry structures with amides, sulfonamides, ethers, nitriles, heteroaromatics and saturated nitrogen rings. The digest's ring-closure rates span 0.9805 to 0.9966 and aromatic-token presence rates span 0.9448 to 0.9943; these indicate presence in strings, not fractions of aromatic atoms or measured three-dimensional shape. Every proposal pool has a stereocentre-marker rate of 0.0. Global connectivity diversity is substantial, while the highest-scoring subsets concentrate into particular series. The passive RDKit audit finds child Murcko-core counts of 414, 431, 403, 741 and 754 in task order, versus Parent counts of 472, 372, 537, 733 and 775. Those counts describe chemistry and do not establish utility or mechanism activation. Ordinary high-scoring amides, sulfonamides and cyclic amines appear synthetically plausible from connectivity, but the full output also includes excessive molecular growth, unresolved stereochemistry, unusual heteroatom states and recurrent N-nitroso linkages. No synthesis, stability, solubility, affinity or toxicity was measured here. All descriptor and substructure counts are passive readings of the supplied molecules, documented with exact input hashes and digest-to-trajectory checks in /projects/standard/adeshwal/shared/zhou2577/SPIRAL/runs/SPIRAL2/policy/responses/r0011-03-improve-L03-molecular.audit.json; its adjacent .audit.py reproduces the reading without candidate execution or objective calls. Scores below are recorded values, rounded for readability; associations are descriptive rather than proof of an objective's hidden chemical requirements.

per_task.generated_character: The upper end is compact, largely planar aromatic amide chemistry. The best methoxy/cyanoquinoline bearing an N-methyl-N-pyridylmethyl carboxamide scores 0.532652 and has 25 heavy atoms, three aromatic six-membered rings and molecular weight 332.363. Its benzyl and pyridyl positional analogues recur among the best molecules. Another strong family contains alkoxy- or ethyl-substituted quinoline carboxamides attached to a cyanophenyl group. These are recognizable amide, ether and nitrile combinations with plausible synthetic disconnections, although no route is supplied. The broad pool has median 24 heavy atoms and three rings. Compared with Parent n-3462511d7ff0, whose seed peaks include pyrrole carboxamides and linked aromatic amides, the child high end emphasizes fused cyanoquinolines; it retains the same broad aromatic-amide character. Child seed peaks are 0.467099, 0.532652 and 0.521093, so the new family is not the high-scoring chemistry in every seed.
liabilities: Large peptide-like, polyhydroxylated and long-chain excursions add substantial size and flexibility without the favorable compact arrangement; the cited zero-score polycycle has molecular weight about 866.1 and many unassigned potential stereocentres.

The high-scoring aromatic cores are relatively flat, and some alpha-substituted amide analogues introduce stereogenic connectivity without specifying configuration. These are chemical-quality limitations, not demonstrated causes of their scores.
missing_features: Lower-scoring proposals often fail to combine the compact azaaromatic scaffold, correctly placed nitrile and amide linkage seen together in the stronger series; individual aromatic rings or nitrogen atoms are already plentiful.

The best excerpt gives limited evidence for alternative fused-ring and amide-attachment arrangements outside its recurring quinoline families. It does not identify an unseen mandatory scaffold or establish that greater nitrogen content would help.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every proposal pool has digest stereocentre-marker rate 0.0. Passive graph perception finds 605 of 870 proposals with potential unassigned atom stereocentres in one pool, versus 218 for its Parent. The cited best substituted azepane has two potential unassigned atom centres. Complex low-score polycycles and simpler substituted amide/lactam examples show the same omission.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator produces stereogenic connectivity without specifying stereochemical identity.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator needs to preserve or deliberately explore stereochemical states when its existing connectivity creates stereocentres, and distinguish a specified compound from unresolved stereoisomers. Whether that affects utility must come from ordinary feedback; these trajectories do not establish a universally favorable configuration.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A compact cyanoazaaryl amide at molecular weight 332.363 scores 0.532652 while a polyoxygenated structure near 866.1 scores 0. A compact lactam-sulfonamide near 334.4 scores 0.298922 while an elaborate ester near 837.1 scores 0. Very small fragments and unstructured long chains also score poorly. Conversely, a larger cyclic-amine molecule near 482.9 reaches a near-ceiling recorded score, so small size is not a universal answer.
transferable_gaps.gap: Molecular extent is not consistently coupled to a coherent arrangement of functional groups.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Generation should support complete, compact functional-group combinations and meaningful larger architectures without routinely drifting into fragment-sized endpoints or extended chains and polycycles. The chemical requirement is context-sensitive control of extent and connectivity, using available feedback rather than a universal molecular-size target.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The cited near-ceiling azepanes and diazepanes contain unconjugated aliphatic amines, whereas a very low-scoring acylated sulfonamide contains nitrogen in strongly different bonding contexts. Elsewhere, a bis-sulfonylated diazepane is the strongest observed molecule despite both ring nitrogens being capped, and lactam/sulfonamide combinations lead another upper series. All these motifs already occur in the output.
transferable_gaps.gap: Nitrogen-rich output does not consistently retain the functional context that distinguishes free amines from resonance-deactivated nitrogen.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Chemical variation needs to preserve and explore nitrogen's neighboring atoms, conjugation, ring position and linker role as a connected motif. Generic nitrogen enrichment, universal amine addition or universal deprotection would discard the conflicting chemistry visible in the generator's own feedback.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The recorded upper excerpts concentrate on cyanoazaaryl amides, linked azaaromatic ether systems, aromatic cyclic amines and lactam-sulfonamides. Some methoxy/ethoxy analogues tie at 0.614046, and paired sulfonamide positions on a fused lactam give effectively equal 0.298922 scores. These repeated decorations coexist with hundreds of distinct cores elsewhere and with weaker seeds that do not reproduce the stronger composite motif.
transferable_gaps.gap: Broad global scaffold coverage coexists with limited productive exploration of attachment and linker alternatives around the strongest composite motifs.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator needs ways to explore ring topology, attachment position and linker arrangement while retaining useful combinations already supported by its observations. Distinct strings, more peripheral substituents and larger global scaffold counts alone do not demonstrate this chemical capability.

transferable_gaps.evidence: One full proposal pool contains 110 N-nitroso-amine structural matches, with 107 in one seed, compared with five in the Parent. Digest examples also include an unusual N-H/two-O-minus arrangement at 0.576675 and simultaneous sulfur-oxo/sulfur-thioxo bonds at 0.565662. These are observable structures with recorded scores, not demonstrated stability, synthetic feasibility or toxicity results.
transferable_gaps.gap: Accepted molecular strings do not consistently retain conventional or well-supported heteroatom functional-group states.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The generator needs chemical-context handling that distinguishes conventional charge-separated groups and deliberately represented uncommon functions from incidental heteroatom rearrangements. Positive feedback and successful SMILES parsing should not be treated as evidence that every represented functional-group state is chemically suitable.

nodes.method_name: Augmented Hill-Climb with a corpus-trained SMILES policy
nodes.method_thesis: Train a compact autoregressive SMILES prior solely on the supplied unlabeled corpus, then initialize a fresh policy from that prior for each objective. Use the initial observations and each subsequent scored batch to update only its highest-reward sequences with the Augmented Hill-Climb loss: fit policy log likelihood to frozen-prior log likelihood plus scaled observed reward. Sample complete molecules token by token from the updated policy, canonicalize them, and refill invalid or duplicate proposals by further generation. The corpus supplies language training, never a ranked molecular pool. Elite-conditioned policy updates should shift generation toward new high-scoring molecular combinations quickly enough to improve the benchmark's mean final Top-1. This is a small-budget transfer hypothesis, not a claim that published larger-budget gains carry over. The root uses the current scored batch; randomized historical replay is reserved for the first improvement. The anchor's elite augmented-likelihood mechanism is described by [Thomas et al.](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13321-022-00646-z).

approach.method_basis: The Parent samples local molecular graph edits from one scored current state, normalizes identities, rejects duplicates and sends the first full tabu-admissible batch for evaluation. It then walks to the best accepted neighbor, including worsening moves, while retaining an independent best archive. Bond changes alter bond order; deletions remove atoms or leaves. Neither directly relocates an intact side group along an aromatic ring. The Parent already includes the repaired identity join and its established inverse-motif memory.
approach.novelty: Add one intact-substituent relocation along an existing aromatic ring edge. Detach an acyclic pendant group from an aromatic carbon and reconnect the same group to an adjacent aromatic carbon bearing a hydrogen. This changes substitution position while retaining the whole group, the ring framework and molecular formula. The move becomes an extra choice when the existing bond-change operator selects that attachment bond. Earlier branch deletion discarded groups; nitrogen exchange moved ring elements. This experiment instead reconnects an existing side group and incorporates neither earlier extension.

nodes.hypothesis: Extend the existing change_bond neighborhood with relocation of an intact single-attachment acyclic branch from an aromatic carbon to its adjacent hydrogen-bearing aromatic carbon, directly exposing substitution-position isomers while preserving the branch, ring framework and molecular formula.

finding_summary.headline: Ten intact-group position changes were evaluated, but none carried the improved panel score
finding_summary.insights: Direct positional accessibility is established: none of the ten scored products is reachable by a single original bond-order change, and each changes local motifs and measured score. Intact-group retention therefore avoids the necessary atom loss of branch deletion, but it does not reliably make a stronger neighbor. All four evaluated larger-branch relocations lose to their sources, including the methoxy and carboxyl shifts. The distinction between a successful panel and useful new molecules matters here: since no relocation is selected, the panel gain cannot be credited to descendants carrying a moved group. The expanded menu also changes proposal choices and batch competition among the original operators. The evidence supports a working positional channel and one local thiol-position gain, while leaving a reproducible score benefit from retaining a new position unresolved. The stronger sulfur-free aryl-amine series identified by the molecular assessment is an original-operator outcome and still contains strained nitrogen rings; other populations retain unusual sulfur and reactive heteroatom bonds. Conserving the existing group and ring has not established better stability or synthetic accessibility.
finding_summary.results: Ten fresh positional isomers reached evaluation from thirteen sampled branch relocations, with all atoms, the complete branch, molecular formula and aromatic ring framework retained. Six moved one-heavy-atom groups and four moved larger groups. One thiol position change improved its source score; the other nine lost. None won its batch, updated the best archive or produced a later walk descendant. The three-seed macro mean nevertheless rose from 0.520918 to 0.525257, a paired gain of 0.004339 that exceeds the 0.002 target. One seed improved and two declined; the largest endpoint gain was in one DRD2 seed, while median_2 and sitagliptin endpoints were unchanged throughout.

molecular.headline: Sulfur-rich cages persist; a stronger aryl-amine family removes sulfur but retains strained nitrogen rings
molecular.overall_character: All supplied current and parent trajectories were inspected. Every objective has 900 entries, including 870 optimizer proposals, and none lacks trajectories. These are consistently substantial ring-containing molecules: ring-closure and branch presence rates are 1.0 throughout. Aromatic-token presence is also 1.0 on several populations, 0.9345 on the arylamide population, and 0.7184 on the sulfur-cage population. These are molecule-level text counters, not aromatic atom fractions, ring feasibility, or molecular conformations. The outputs range from recognizable indole carboxamides and aryl cyclic amines to heavily bridged N/O frameworks, long sulfur/oxygen side chains, and multiply bonded sulfur cages. Mean SMILES lengths range from 46.9 to 69.0; the main problem is not a population of trivial fragments or universally giant repeated assemblies. Rather, much of the visible variety changes decoration or connectivity within seed-specific complex families. Explicit charge and tetrahedral stereolabel rates are zero, despite potentially basic amines and stereogenic carbon or sulfur connectivity. Some current chemistry differs meaningfully from the parent, especially the sulfur-free aryl-amine leader, while other leading structures and entire chemical trajectories are unchanged. Apparent synthetic plausibility remains questionable and overall drug likeness weak because useful recognizable groups coexist with strained rings, unusual sulfur valence, reactive heteroatom-halogen bonds, and undefined stereochemistry.

per_task.generated_character: The compact leaders carry aromatic rings and amide or ketone carbonyls, but they separate into chemically different families. The best combines an alkyl-substituted unsaturated sulfur/nitrogen ring system, a primary carboxamide, and an acylated nitrogen bridging adjacent benzene carbons. That last unit is a strained benzene-fused small nitrogen ring, not an ordinary anilide. Related leaders retain the same constrained amide nitrogen with benzothiophene, aminomethoxy, or chloromethyl substitution. A more conventional ethoxy/methyl/thiol-substituted indole carboxanilide is also near the top. The final seed instead favors pyridylmethyl ketones attached to unusual sulfur-containing unsaturated rings and a cyclobutadiene-like small ring. Ring presence is 1.0 and aromatic presence 0.9345, with mean SMILES length 46.9; ring abundance coexists with substantial chemical strain.
liabilities: The acylated nitrogen bridging adjacent aromatic carbons creates severe small-ring geometry concerns.
Multiply bonded ring sulfur with additional substituents should not be read as ordinary thiophene or terminal thiocarbonyl chemistry.
Late cyclobutadiene-like rings are highly strained, and several related products also contain N-N or N-O bonds.
Thiol and chloromethyl decorations add reactivity concerns without a consistent local score advantage.
missing_features: Ordinary amide-nitrogen and ring alternatives retaining the leading carbonyl and aromatic arrangement are not established within the strongest strained-amide series.
Stable sulfur bonding and less strained fusion patterns are underrepresented around the late pyridyl ketones.

nodes.method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
nodes.method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.
