molecular.headline: Rich aromatic and fused-ring chemistry persists, with reactive nitrogen substitutions, difficult bridges and undefined stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: Child n-dd2b25d32925 was assessed against the accepted published code Parent n-62daf219c70a. All supplied Child and Parent Search trajectories were read in full; every task and seed is covered and no supplied trajectory path is missing. context.comparison reports both child_complete=true and paired_complete=true for seeds 0, 1 and 2, with no profile mismatch. This is a complete matched comparison on the exchange-disabled L01 graph/count-GP Parent at 300 observations per task, including ten initial, batch ten and the frozen Research in Depth profile. The supplied macro means are 0.547424387911938 for Child and 0.5956696497334577 for Parent; signed seed macro differences are -0.08364553981417, -0.01809049406612706 and -0.04299975158426195. These numbers describe the supplied comparison, not a molecular activation or selection decision. The output contains indole-like aryl amides, linked nitrogen-rich aromatic carbonyl systems, bridged/cyclic basic amines with aromatic appendages, fused nitrogen-dicarbonyl frameworks, and fluorinated nitrogen-carbonyl/enamine chains. Each task digest covers 900 observations and 870 optimizer proposals. Ring-closure-text incidence is 0.9598 to 0.9931 and aromatic-text incidence 0.923 to 0.9828. These are molecule-level incidences of SMILES features, not perceived ring counts or aromatic-atom fractions. Potentially useful ring and amine chemistry is present, but local N-halogen/N-S environments, small-ring unsaturation, crowded bridges and very large recombined structures make overall plausibility questionable. Diversity is moderate across tasks and seeds; leaders within seeds often retain close scaffold families. Formal charge is nearly absent, but neutral aliphatic amines are visibly present; neutral strings do not establish nonbasic molecules. Stereocentre-text incidence is 0.0 for every task despite potentially stereogenic saturated and bridged centres. Missing stereochemical identity is observable; a reward penalty, accessible conformation, stability, route or biological activity is not established. The digest final_molecules are the last seed-2 proposals, not all seed endpoints. Published Parent trajectories are authoritative for comparisons but are absent from context.citation_trajectory_paths, so Parent-only SMILES are deliberately excluded from cited_smiles. Historical gap ancestry was read through context.evidence_index from n-c55c3d520a2c and n-62daf219c70a; the same-code baseline carries those original gaps and conditions. Current re-observation does not attribute them to the covariance replacement or any retained component. The read-only support audit is .slots/round-0026-slot-0/molecular-evidence-audit.json. Actual logged parent draws and accepted direct descendant identities distinguish realized use from mere graph novelty, but overlapping generating parents do not identify donated atoms or causal chemical inheritance. Nonuse does not distinguish lack of survivor support from supported-but-undrawn records; terminal proposals have no later breeding opportunity. No unscored pool member has a known reward, and this report does not claim kernel mediation, calibration or a component contribution. The actual accepted-emission join records 623 strict best-parent beats and 232 incumbent gains for Child, versus 629 and 258 for Parent, among 4350 offspring per panel. Actual later parent draws occur for 2349 Child records and 2401 Parent records; 1851 and 1799 nonterminal records respectively are never drawn later. Each panel has 150 terminal records, with 92 Child and 97 Parent immediate survivor admissions; these are censored opportunities, not measured useful continuations. Child has 261 parent-beating records with a later direct accepted parent-beating child and 112 incumbent-gain records with a later direct incumbent-gain child; Parent has 282 and 122. These overlapping identity-based categories demonstrate some productive continuation without establishing independent discoveries or chemical causation. All current seed leaders beat their logged best generating parent and the pre-feedback incumbent, but later direct accepted children of those final leaders do not exceed the leader. Five Child leaders arise in the last observed batch and have no future-use opportunity. These event counts are derived from trajectory-matched real observed scores and logged source identities in the support audit; they are not molecular quality scores.

per_task.generated_character: Mostly compact to medium fused aromatic frameworks connected through an amide to phenyl or pyridyl rings. Seed 2's leader is a methoxy/amino/methyl fused nitrogen system bearing an N-S-substituted aryl amide; seed 1 retains a substituted indole and pyridyl amide but attaches chlorine directly to the amide nitrogen. Seed 0 develops a bridged indole-like core with a hydroxyl centre and a cyclic hydrazine-containing amide region. Thus ring chemistry is abundant, including nonaromatic bridges, rather than just isolated aromatic fragments. Mean proposal SMILES length is 44.6, with halogen-text incidence 0.7655. Conventional aryl amides coexist with N-S, N-N and N-Cl chemistry and topology that is not routinely supported by a synthetic route. Parent leaders instead include N-halogen indole derivatives, a diketone and a cumulene family; neither panel demonstrates consistently conventional local chemistry.
liabilities: Amide N-Cl and N-S bonds are distinct from ordinary aromatic carbon-bound halogens and require local reactivity assessment.
Hydrazine-containing and bridged relatives raise stability and geometry questions that graph validity cannot answer.
Late proposals still include single atoms, small reactive fragments and an unusual charged diazene-like amide representation.
missing_features: Stable, conventional nitrogen substitution retaining the favorable aromatic/amide arrangement is not demonstrated consistently among the leaders; an ordinary N-H indole amide is already present initially.
The bridged saturated core lacks specified stereochemistry and demonstrated feasible geometry.
Independent plausible frameworks expressing the same useful functional arrangement are scarce among within-seed leaders; the observed scores identify no exact absent target pharmacophore.

nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

approach.method_basis: The Parent learns a recurrent SMILES prior from the original unlabeled corpus strings and retains the checkpoint with the lowest heldout token loss. Each objective clones that prior into an adaptable flow policy and keeps the reference prior frozen. The online loop alternates a neural batch with two graph batches; accepted neural molecules refresh the breeding population and provide a protected parent at the first graph handoff. Accepted-score fingerprint posterior samples choose the other offspring from temporary pools, and accepted graph trajectories feed trajectory-balance learning of the neural policy. The same reciprocal loop is retained here. The preparation choice being questioned is its use of string likelihood alone to decide which learned prior all those components receive.
approach.novelty: Choose the prepared checkpoint by its observed yield of valid, connected, distinct molecules under a fixed ancestral sampling probe, with heldout token loss breaking ties. A separate diagnostic probe then compares that choice with the ordinary loss-minimizing checkpoint from the same training trajectory. This sibling changes checkpoint selection, whereas the previous preparation sibling changed the strings used for training. It neither combines the two interventions nor changes neural learning, graph construction or posterior allocation during an objective.

nodes.hypothesis: Select the reusable prior checkpoint by fixed-noise ancestral valid-connected-unique molecular emission yield among unlabeled checkpoints that improve the initial holdout loss, breaking ties by lower original-string holdout NLL while preserving the Parent training and stopping rules.

finding_summary.headline: Checkpoint selection raises endpoint scores, while molecular-yield gains transfer unevenly
finding_summary.insights:
The minimum token-loss checkpoint is not the only useful prior along the same unchanged learning trajectory. This experiment cleanly separates checkpoint choice from changes to training representations, gradients or the online search algorithm. It also exposes the limitation of the selection criterion: choosing among 60 checkpoints with one fixed 256-draw sample creates a selection-sample advantage that mostly disappears on fresh diagnostic randomness in two seeds. That pattern is compatible with selection noise and supports only limited generalization of the measured yield gain. The lower online raw validity shows that valid prior sampling and useful adaptation should remain separate measurements; even the first online batch follows accepted-score policy updates.

The molecular assessment gives the same distinction a chemical interpretation. Useful aromatic, amine and carbonyl arrangements coexist with unusual sulfur bonding, nitroso groups, peroxide bonds and unresolved stereochemistry. Valid connected uniqueness does not distinguish those liabilities, and higher endpoint scores do not establish better synthetic plausibility. The campaign now has evidence that an earlier checkpoint can improve the reciprocal search without a reliably better valid-emission rate. Whether a more representative unlabeled diagnostic can predict that downstream usefulness remains open.
finding_summary.results:
The rule selected different prior weights in all three preparations. On the fixed selection samples, the chosen checkpoints produced 243, 245 and 238 valid, distinct molecules out of 256, compared with 232, 236 and 229 for the lowest-loss checkpoints from the same training trajectories. The independent diagnostic changed those counts by -1, +10 and 0; its pooled gain was only 9 of 768 draws, compared with 29 of 768 on the selection samples. Thus checkpoint choice and its selection-sample advantage are established, while an independent yield advantage appeared in only one seed. All training runs completed the same 29,742 updates, and the ordinary lowest-loss weights exactly matched the published parent weights, so no training-length difference explains the choice. The selected checkpoints incurred small token-loss increases of 0.001852, 0.002624 and 0.003124.

During optimization, valid terminated neural draws fell from 8,441 of 12,000 to 8,156 of 12,000, or 70.34% to 67.97%. Nevertheless, the complete three-seed endpoint mean rose from 0.520669 to 0.550198, with paired gains of 0.026285, 0.051553 and 0.010747. The mean gain, 0.029528, exceeds the registered 0.002 target. Deco hop, median and sitagliptin task means improved; zaleplon was nearly unchanged and DRD2 declined slightly. Every task completed the supplied evaluation panel. The new checkpoints therefore changed useful downstream search outcomes, but the score increase cannot be explained as a consistent increase in valid molecular emission.

molecular.headline: Rich aryl, amine and carbonyl rings coexist with triple-bonded sulfur, nitroso groups, peroxides and unspecified stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character: All 4,500 child trajectory rows and 4,500 corresponding Parent rows were read, including 4,350 optimizer proposals in each node. Each task supplies 900 evaluated molecules, of which 870 are optimizer proposals. The child has abundant fused heteroaromatics, saturated amine rings, aryl amides, sulfonamides and carbonyl heterocycles. Its ring-closure marker rates are 0.9816–0.9943; aromatic-marker rates are 0.7736–0.9747, with the lower value reflecting substantial unsaturated nonaromatic ring chemistry in one output set. These digest counters measure string-level presence, not atom fractions or perceived ring quality. Read-only RDKit inspection parses all 4,350 emitted child SMILES and gives median heavy-atom counts of 25, 36, 30, 32 and 24 in the supplied task order. Recognizable medicinal-chemistry architectures coexist with unusually bonded sulfur, N-nitroso substituents, peroxide bonds, highly contracted unsaturated rings and oversized assemblies. All task digests have stereocentre_rate 0.0; RDKit identifies at least one unassigned tetrahedral centre in 392, 225, 563, 348 and 353 optimizer rows respectively, with assigned centres in none. The repertoire varies across seeds, while the upper tails repeatedly revisit a few related families. Chemistry quality is therefore mixed: ring and aromatic content are rich, but neither parseability nor high observed scores establish synthetic accessibility, stability or well-defined geometry. This assessment describes the output without attributing it to an algorithmic mechanism.

per_task.generated_character: The digest leaders are medium-sized heteroaryl structures. Seed 0 links a quinoline-like ring system to a fused five/five-membered aza-ring framework; its leading variants carry N–O or N–O–N attachments and an oxygen-linked carbon triply bonded to hydrogen-bearing sulfur. The leading molecule has 25 heavy atoms and four perceived rings, three aromatic. Seed 2 also provides a more conventional methoxy/cyano-substituted partially saturated quinoline-like carboxamide and a different hydroxy-nitrile/amidine series with unsaturated carbocyclic or oxygen-containing rings. Across the full optimizer output the median is 25 heavy atoms and three rings, as in the Parent. Nonchiral Murcko scaffold counts are 577 for the child and 529 for the Parent; this counts local ring edits as distinct and is not a count of useful synthetic series. The Parent leaders included biaryl pyrazole/acetanilide, indole-amide and quinoline/urea families. Rings, nitrogen and carbonyl groups are thus not missing, but the new leading families include more problematic connectivity.
liabilities: Fifty-one of 870 child proposals contain a carbon–sulfur triple bond, versus none in the corresponding Parent task. The leading C≡S–H environment and N–O–N or O–S attachments are not ordinary medicinal functional groups, and parsing supplies no stability or synthetic evidence.

The hydroxy-nitrile and unsaturated ring families include potentially sensitive local connectivity and unassigned stereocentres. Relative stability and geometry of those proposed forms are not established by the trajectory.
Ten optimizer proposals have at most three heavy atoms. Such fragments, as well as the cited large polyfunctional assembly, lose the connected arrangement seen in the favorable examples.
missing_features: Chemically ordinary alternatives that preserve the favorable local aryl/nitrogen/substituent arrangement are not consistently established within the sulfur-rich leading family. A separate conventional nitrile/amide family is present, so the limitation is not an inability to make amides or nitriles.
Defined configurations are absent for substituted fused-ring and hydroxy-nitrile centres. The data do not establish which stereoisomer, if any, would be preferred.
Controlled core replacements preserving useful local functionality remain incomplete: some changes retain the core but sharply lose the score, while fragmentation removes it entirely.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The oxygen-linked C≡S–H structure with an N–O–N substituent scores 0.49151859442707624; the corresponding O–S substituent gives 0.46889981462810426, while the N–O version retaining C≡S–H gives 0.4509940583060807. A methoxy/N-hydroxy relative scores 0.4524187090179798. These observations show that questionable bonding is accepted among the favorable local variants, not that the sulfur motif is chemically necessary. The cyano/carboxamide alternative scores 0.46457806514522626; replacing its nitrile by methyl gives 0.31305283559478153, N-methylating its amide gives 0.4098058836024565, and replacing a methyl substituent by amino gives 0.3487840659540038. Those close-family comparisons associate the score with specific nitrile, amide and substitution relationships. The hydroxy-nitrile/amidine family reaches 0.4572645941803378. Sulfur, hydrazine, methane, a saturated sulfur-rich bicyclic structure and a large polyol/amide assembly all appear at 0.0. The pooled median is 0.177987. No uniquely required absent heterocycle follows from these whole-molecule observations.

nodes.method_name: Genetic GFN: reciprocal learning between a flow policy and graph search
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Genetic GFN: alternately generate molecules with a GFlowNet policy, refine the resulting scored population through graph crossover and mutation, and distill scored descendants back into the policy using rank-weighted off-policy replay. The policy uses trajectory balance with a learned log normalizer and regularization toward a frozen prior. [Kim et al., Section 3](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.05961v4) describe this mechanism. Train the prior only on the permitted unlabeled corpus. Each objective starts with clean policy adaptation, replay and population state initialized from its supplied observations. Use a positive terminal reward increasing with the observed maximization score. Schedule policy and genetic phases around the evaluator's announced feedback; both produce new molecules, and all reward-bearing training records come from accepted observations. Later policy samples must enter genetic populations, and accepted graph descendants must affect subsequent policy updates. Generate further valid, canonical-unique structures to fill announced batches, without corpus ranking or a fixed molecular library. The hypothesis is that learned global proposals propagate local discoveries into new promising regions and then support further graph refinement, raising the mean of five independent final Top-1 scores. Published larger-budget gains do not establish that this reciprocal learning becomes useful quickly enough here.

approach.method_basis: GenMol generates by remasking rather than by building from scratch. A bidirectional masked diffusion model is trained to fill in deleted spans of a molecular fragment sequence, so at generation time you take an existing molecule, blank out one fragment, and let the model iteratively denoise the gap while every surrounding fragment stays fixed. Because the model sees context on both sides, the replacement it writes has to fit what remains, which keeps the output chemically coherent in a way left-to-right generation does not guarantee.
approach.novelty: This root commits to a fragment representation with explicit attachment labels that are round-trip checked during preparation, so the retained context keeps its exact connection points and the replacement block must satisfy them. It freezes the denoiser entirely and adapts per objective only by changing which observed molecules are selected to supply future contexts, ranked by their accepted scores. All learning is therefore in the choice of what to remask, not in the model that fills the gap.

nodes.hypothesis: Freeze a corpus-trained bidirectional masked discrete denoiser over SAFE fragment sequences, then repeatedly select high-ranked task-local observed molecules, replace one fragment with a variable-length mask chunk, iteratively denoise the missing tokens while preserving the surrounding context, and use accepted scores to update which whole molecules supply future contexts.

finding_summary.headline: Second highest at 0.495, and the most consistent root across all five objectives
finding_summary.insights: Consistency, not peak performance, is what this node contributes. Its sitagliptin_mpo score of 0.344 is the best in the round and its drd2_docking of 0.908 is third, which no other method combines. The negative context-beating delta is the interesting result: the search improves by keeping the rare good completion and discarding the rest, rather than by proposing better molecules on average. That means throughput of attempts matters more here than proposal quality, which is a different tuning direction from every other lineage. One seed, and the fragment vocabulary itself has not been varied.
finding_summary.results: The macro mean of 0.495 is second of thirteen. It is the only root above 0.20 on every single objective: 0.908 on drd2_docking, 0.591 on deco_hop, 0.424 on zaleplon_mpo, 0.344 on sitagliptin_mpo and 0.207 on median_2. Context selection enrichment was positive on every objective and held under a tie-midrank sensitivity check. Every remasking attempt decoded with an unchanged prefix and suffix, a nonempty retained subgraph, exactly one replacement block and fixed outside attachment labels. One registered measurement came back against expectation: the mean score of a completion minus its generating context is negative in aggregate and on every task, so individual completions usually score worse than the molecule they came from.

molecular.headline: The cleanest and most consistent chemistry in the round, anchored on one xanthine-like core
molecular.overall_character: Ring closure and aromatic content both reach 100 percent on two objectives and never fall below 98 percent, and cumulated double bonds are effectively absent throughout. The molecules read as coherent medicinal chemistry with correct attachment: pyrazolines, sulfonyl pyrrolidines, halogenated benzoates. Fragment remasking preserves whatever was already there, which shows as a strong shared core across objectives, a dimethyl pyrimidinedione appearing in the top molecules of three of them. Halogen content is high at 48 to 95 percent, and molecule size stays moderate at forty-three to seventy characters.

transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The generator is not a proposal improver; it is a lottery whose winners are kept. That makes attempt throughput and context ranking the levers that matter, and makes any change aimed at raising average proposal quality the wrong place to spend effort.

transferable_gaps.gap: the generator preserves so much context that one core dominates every objective
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Remasking a single fragment while fixing every attachment label cannot leave the neighbourhood of the starting molecule. Reaching a different core needs either multi-fragment remasking or occasional context resets that discard the current archive.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The highest-scoring molecule on one objective carries both an N-chloro thiourea and a chloroacetyl group, and thiourea appears in all four top scorers there.
transferable_gaps.gap: the generator writes reactive and toxic functional groups into completions
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The denoiser learned these tokens from the corpus and the reward has no way to object, so they persist wherever they happen to score. A toxicophore screen at emission removes them without touching the denoiser or the selection rule.

nodes.method_name: GenMol fragment remasking with a corpus-trained discrete denoiser
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the method in GenMol's fragment-remasking mechanism: a bidirectional masked discrete diffusion model generates replacement fragments while retaining the surrounding molecular context. The anchor is described in [GenMol, Sections 4.1-4.2](https://arxiv.org/html/2501.06158v3). For this benchmark adaptation, train a compact denoiser solely on the permitted unlabeled corpus, then freeze it. Start each objective with a fresh archive of its supplied scored molecules. Select high-ranked observed whole molecules as contexts, replace a randomly chosen fragment with a variable-length mask chunk, iteratively sample the missing SAFE tokens, and decode the resulting complete molecule. Generate further completions until the evaluator-announced batch contains distinct canonical structures. Accepted feedback updates context selection and allows improving completions to become future contexts. This root uses the remasking core with observed whole-molecule contexts; the paper's corpus-derived fragment-vocabulary initialization and fragment-attaching stage are not required. The corpus trains the denoiser and supplies unlabeled length statistics, never a molecule pool for ranking or retrieval. The hypothesis is that contextual fragment replacement preserves useful structure while generating improving alternatives, raising the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Task-local selection can respond immediately to feedback without reward-dependent neural training, but useful conditional generation from the permitted preparation remains an empirical prerequisite.

approach.method_basis: The Parent samples local graph edits from one scored molecule, sanitizes and normalizes each result, rejects prior identities and directly evaluates a full batch allowed by inverse-motif memory. It selects the best accepted neighbor even when that move lowers score and separately retains its best archive. Its atom and attachment menus are governed by graph valence and available hydrogens, so a halogen can attach directly to nitrogen, oxygen or sulfur as well as carbon. The repaired identity join and the established memory lifecycle are part of this Parent.
approach.novelty: Add one source-relative attachment gate: a new neighbor may not increase the number of halogen bonds to non-carbon heavy atoms. Carbon-bound halogens remain eligible under the existing rules. The gate changes which fresh neighbors proceed to tabu testing and evaluation while keeping every edit draw unchanged. The earlier sulfur filter targeted a sulfur valence envelope, and the positional experiments changed local molecular construction; this experiment isolates the remaining halogen attachment pattern and combines none of those mechanisms.

nodes.hypothesis: Reject a graph-valid canonically novel neighbor before tabu testing when it increases the source-relative count of bonds between F, Cl, Br or I and a non-carbon heavy atom, redirecting the existing edit stream away from new non-carbon halogen attachment while preserving carbon-halogen eligibility and the Parent walk.

finding_summary.headline: Non-carbon halogen attachments disappear, but the gate fails score non-inferiority
finding_summary.insights: The attachment criterion has a distinct effect beyond existing tabu memory: every measured rejection changes which fresh neighbor can reach evaluation. It also separates carbon-bound halogens from direct nitrogen-, oxygen- and sulfur-halogen bonds, rather than simply eliminating all halogen-containing molecules. The chemistry cleanup therefore happened, but its score cost is real in this panel. The Parent had obtained six immediate archive improvements from count-increasing moves, so this was never a uniformly unhelpful channel; those historical scores do not label the different rejected products. The rule is source-relative and would permit equal or lower counts on a molecule with pre-existing counted bonds. Its complete absence here depends on the zero-count starting states. Other liabilities remain outside the mechanism: the molecular assessment still finds unusual sulfur coordination, dense bridges, small unsaturated rings and undefined stereochemistry. Removing one attachment class neither establishes generally plausible chemistry nor preserves objective performance.
finding_summary.results: The gate rejected 130 valid, novel attachment increases; all 130 would otherwise pass the contemporaneous tabu rule, and each was followed by another actual neighbor from the same source. Starting from zero-count molecules, the complete panel emitted no targeted bonds, compared with 974 affected Parent emissions. Carbon-halogen chemistry remained active in 2670 evaluated molecules versus 2596 before, including 265 source improvements and 153 archive gains. Generation attempts per batch rose from 12.15 to 12.63. The macro mean fell from 0.520918 to 0.513044, a paired loss of 0.007874 exceeding the permitted 0.002. Gains in DRD2 and some other endpoints did not offset the larger sitagliptin losses.

molecular.headline: Tightly sized ring-rich molecules retain unusual sulfur centres, dense bridges and undefined stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: The complete panel contains 900 evaluated molecules per task across three seeds, including 870 optimizer proposals each. All 4,350 optimizer proposals parse with RDKit. Every proposal contains a ring-closure digit, and digest aromatic-token rates range from 0.8667 to 1.0; rings are abundant. Proposal heavy-atom ranges are tightly concentrated at 21-29, 30-48, 29-43, 28-45 and 26-34 in fixed task order, with no proposal above 50 heavy atoms. Nevertheless, these are not uniformly simple molecules: median ring counts are three, four, four, five and six, and the last task reaches 17 perceived rings within its limited atom range. Recognizable ketones, thioesters, lactams, ethers, phenols and amines coexist with unusual sulfur coordination, highly fused or bridged graphs and small unsaturated rings. Proposals with explicit-H sulfur atoms bonded to at least two heavy atoms number 50, 138, 747, 192 and 554. These [SH] sites should not be read as ordinary terminal thiols. Direct N-halogen and O-halogen bonds are absent from current proposals, whereas they occurred in the parent, but unusual sulfur and ring chemistry remains pervasive. All proposals have zero charged-string markers; neutrality does not establish ordinary valence chemistry or stable solution species. Per-task nonchiral Murcko scaffold counts are 430, 418, 452, 442 and 521, while leaders remain concentrated in a few related families. No proposal assigns a stereocentre; 624, 396, 870, 668 and 780 contain unassigned centres. I read the dominant sulfur-rich high-score families as implausible practical synthetic targets without substantial chemical validation, while some ketone, thioester and lactam alternatives are more recognizable. The assessment concerns chemical appearance, not demonstrated synthesis or activity.

per_task.generated_character: The highest structure combines an unsaturated sulfur/nitrogen bicycle with a carboxamide and an N-acyl nitrogen closing a three-membered ring across adjacent aromatic carbons. It has 24 heavy atoms and four perceived rings, but only one aromatic ring. The next family is more recognizable: substituted indene-like ketones or heteroaryl thioesters, often with amino, alkoxy or bromoethyl groups. Several carry an O/N/S-substituted carbon connected to a bromomethyl group, a chemically different motif from a simple ether. Parent leaders included N-halogenated amide or sulfur-containing fused frameworks. Current direct N-halogen proposals fall from 172 to zero, but sulfur and ring-bond alterations persist. Full proposals have median 25 heavy atoms and three rings.
liabilities: The highest N-acyl substituent contains a three-membered ring fused to an aromatic bond, a substantial geometry concern despite successful parsing.
Bromomethyl or bromoethyl arms and O/N/S-substituted carbons introduce potential reactivity and stability questions.
Sulfur double-bond and coordination changes must be assessed in context; ordinary thioesters should not be equated with unusual cyclic sulfur centres.
missing_features: Stable, conventional alternatives preserving the useful fused-ring/carbonyl placement are underrepresented among leaders relative to sulfur-valence and ring-closure variants.
The leading three-membered N-ring and heteroatom-rich side-chain structures lack established geometry or synthetic access, and 624 proposals have unassigned centres.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The sulfur/strained-N-ring structure scores 0.425403 and an indene-like heteroaryl thioester 0.424583, so the unusual first topology is not the only visible route to a similar value. A bromoethyl ether ketone scores 0.412377, while O/N/S-substituted analogues lie around 0.39-0.42. These examples associate a compact fused aromatic/carbonyl arrangement with appreciable score, without isolating a benefit from unusual sulfur or reactive side chains. Low optimizer proposals, approximately 0.008-0.035, already have many rings and polar groups but alter the connecting topology, aromatic region or cyclic carbonyl context. Terminal ring-contracted or heavily altered sulfur structures fall around 0.13-0.34. The overall score minimum includes initial molecules; the cited optimizer minimum is 0.008082.

per_task.generated_character: The leading family contains two substituted aromatic rings connected through a benzyl-bound neutral [SH] centre also bonded to nitrogen, with imine, urea-like and thiocarbonyl substituents. One aromatic region is fused to an eight-membered carbonyl/O/N ring. The highest molecule has 39 heavy atoms, three rings, two aromatic rings and molecular mass 641.564. Many displayed variants retain almost the entire framework while changing carbonyl versus sulfur groups, alkyl length or terminal unsaturation. This is chemically much less straightforward than an ordinary sulfide or sulfonamide. Relative to the parent, explicit-H sulfur with multiple heavy-atom neighbours increases from 46 to 138 proposals, while direct N-halogen bonds fall from 29 to zero. Full proposal median size is 38 heavy atoms and median mass 565.1945.
liabilities: A neutral sulfur atom bearing explicit hydrogen and several heavy-atom bonds is not an ordinary thiol; its stability cannot be inferred from neutral SMILES syntax.
Displayed leaders have molecular masses around 640-720 despite fewer than 50 heavy atoms, showing that atom-count moderation does not remove substantial mass burden.
Thiocarbonyl, imine and sulfur-rich side chains create unresolved reactivity and tautomeric issues in a largely repeated framework.
missing_features: The high-score neighborhood lacks demonstrated ordinary-linker alternatives preserving its aromatic and polar arrangement without a multiply connected [SH] centre.
Imine geometry and synthetic access to the eight-membered O/N carbonyl ring and elaborate side chain are not established.
Many near-identical scores provide little evidence for choosing among the observed carbonyl, thiocarbonyl and sulfur-coordination substitutions.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The highest scores 0.608802 and many chemically different peripheral variants all score 0.608402, despite swapping carbonyl/sulfur environments, alkyl groups and oxygen/sulfur ring atoms. That flat local response does not establish those unusual groups as useful or stable. Lower optimizer examples around 0.526-0.531 contain aromatic carbonyl/urea-like frameworks but lack the same extended arrangement. Terminal sulfur-rich heteroaryl assemblies reach about 0.57-0.59. Thus the visible gradient distinguishes whole chemical neighborhoods more clearly than particular sulfur edits. The overall minimum of 0.5 includes initial molecules; the lowest cited optimizer proposal is 0.526082.

per_task.generated_character: The highest molecules are densely bridged amine/sulfur cages combining several aromatic rings, a tertiary nitrogen, hydroxylated sulfur connectivity, a phenylthio group and often a bromoethyl arm. The top has 36 heavy atoms, eight perceived rings, three aromatic rings, mass 604.676 and four unassigned stereocentres. Another family is a less fused phenolic amino/pyrrolidine framework bearing a C-[SH]=C-S side chain. Both retain accessible amine and aromatic regions, but neither is ordinary conventional drug-like chemistry as a whole. Parent output was also sulfur-rich and stereochemically complex. Current multi-neighbour explicit-H sulfur proposals rise from 535 to 747, and every one of the 870 current optimizer proposals contains at least one unassigned centre. The full median mass is 613.6855 and halogen-string rate 0.9989.
liabilities: The [SH] sites have multiple heavy-atom bonds, and 185 proposals contain S=S connections; these are not interchangeable with routine thioethers or sulfonamides.
High ring density and multiple bridges impose substantial geometric and synthetic constraints without adding many atoms.
Near-universal halogenation, occasional primary bromoalkyl groups and high molecular mass create additional burdens uncharacterized by the scores.
missing_features: Stable, less sulfur-dependent realizations of the useful amine/aromatic relationships are not demonstrated in the displayed high-score neighborhood.
All 870 proposals contain unassigned stereocentres and none assigns them; ring-junction configuration and feasible cage geometry remain undefined.
More economical alternatives are missing despite similar values for eight-ring and less-fused amine architectures.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The bridged cage scores 0.978423, a phenolic amino/pyrrolidine structure 0.971579 and a less cyclic related phenolic amine 0.966607. These associate accessible amine functionality and aromatic regions with higher scores across several topologies, without proving that the sulfur cage or bromoethyl arm is necessary. Low optimizer examples around 0.007-0.015 are more acid/amide/sulfonamide-rich, with different nitrogen electronics, even when sulfur is introduced. Thus adding sulfur or rings alone does not reproduce the high-score arrangement. Terminal cages retain values around 0.72-0.90 despite extensive topology changes. These are observations about molecular scores, not experimental binding or a mechanism-activation judgment.

per_task.generated_character: The highest family is a propyl-substituted aromatic nitrogen/oxygen ring system joined to another aryl group and a cyclic N-methyl amide through a partially unsaturated, bridged arrangement. The top has 31 heavy atoms, four rings and two aromatic rings; perceived nonaromatic cycles include nine- and seven-membered rings. Close variants expand the larger cycle to eleven atoms, add N-N connectivity or alter aryl alkoxy groups. These leaders are more recognizable than the sulfur-rich terminal cages, but still require conformational and synthetic qualification. The parent also led with related large-ring carbonyl/N/O arrangements. Direct O-halogen proposals fall from 214 in the parent to zero; current OCF substituents are O-CH2-F, not O-F. Full median size is 34 heavy atoms and five rings.
liabilities: Nine- to eleven-membered perceived cycles, N-O or N-N connections and bridged carbonyl arrangements introduce synthetic and conformational questions.
OCF is a fluoromethyl ether, so its presence should not be misclassified as the direct O-halogen liability absent from current proposals.
There are 192 multi-neighbour explicit-H sulfur proposals, largely outside the most straightforward leading N/O frameworks.
missing_features: The leading medium/large-ring carbonyl architecture lacks broad simpler alternatives retaining its polar/aromatic arrangement.
Configuration and ring conformations remain unspecified: the highest has an unassigned centre and 668 proposals have at least one.
Stable alternatives to the sulfur-rich terminal bridge systems are not demonstrated by the supplied molecular evidence.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The fluoromethoxy leader scores 0.210745 and its methoxy counterpart 0.208804, a small local difference. Related carbon-for-nitrogen ring and alkoxy variants share 0.207549, giving little support for further peripheral decoration. Lower optimizer examples around 0.125-0.141 retain aromatic ester/carbonyl/urea-like fragments but have different connections or more open arrangements. Terminal sulfur-rich bridged carbonyl compounds lie around 0.17-0.19; a version replacing an explicit-H sulfur ring site with nitrogen reaches 0.193197, without establishing a general substitution rule. Useful spatial/polar arrangement appears more important than adding ring complexity or sulfur. The overall lower score span includes initial molecules, below the cited optimizer minimum of 0.124680.

per_task.generated_character: The highest molecules are exceptionally dense sulfur/nitrogen polycycles bearing brominated cyclopropene or cyclopropane groups, fluoromethyl nitrogen substituents, cyclic carbonyls and multiple unusual sulfur connections including [SH]=S. The top has 30 heavy atoms, six perceived rings, no aromatic rings, mass 572.554 and six unassigned stereocentres. Another displayed analogue has ten perceived rings and eleven unassigned centres within 30 heavy atoms. Some related leaders retain two aromatic rings, so the zero aromaticity of the highest structures does not describe the full task; its digest aromatic-token rate is 0.8667 and median perceived aromatic-ring count two. Parent leaders were similarly unusual. Current direct N-halogen proposals fall from 288 to zero and acid halides from 66 to two, but S=S proposals rise from 13 to 225 and multi-neighbour explicit-H sulfur from 439 to 554. This is not a demonstrated stable medicinal-chemistry family.
liabilities: S=S bonds occur in 225 proposals and multi-neighbour explicit-H sulfur in 554; these patterns are chemically distinct from ordinary thioethers or thiols.
Dense small-ring fusion and bridge closure can create six to ten perceived rings in displayed 30-heavy-atom leaders, with severe configurational and geometric uncertainty.
N(CF) represents N-CH2-F rather than direct N-F; removal of direct heteroatom-halogen bonds does not validate the remaining sulfur-rich topology.
missing_features: Ordinary, geometrically credible core alternatives preserving the useful polar and ring arrangement are absent from the displayed leading neighborhood.
Configurations are not defined despite six unassigned centres in the highest molecule and eleven in a cited analogue; 780 proposals contain unassigned centres overall.
Stable sulfur electronic structures and accessible syntheses are not established for the [SH]=S, N-S and multiply bridged motifs.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The highest imino-sulfur version scores 0.460396; close carbonyl- or carbon-imino-containing versions score 0.408074 and 0.407696, while another sulfur/carbonyl rearrangement reaches 0.442354. The score tolerates or favors particular unusual local connectivities without validating their stability. In a close saturated-ring comparison, an N-fluoromethyl version scores 0.439194 while adding an intervening aminomethylene unit in the terminal N-substituent gives 0.073509. Replacing a carbonyl-containing element also produces terminal values near 0.055-0.062. Low optimizer examples include both conventional aromatic dicarbonyl systems and differently connected sulfur polycycles, down to 7.84e-11. Sulfur abundance alone therefore is insufficient; local arrangement matters within a chemically questionable family. No full-trajectory row is exactly zero.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Counts of proposals with explicit-H sulfur bonded to at least two heavy atoms are 50, 138, 747, 192 and 554 across the five sessions. Leading molecules include multi-substituted neutral [SH], [SH]=S, N-S and unusual ring-bound sulfur arrangements. One session contains 225 S=S proposals. Direct N-halogen and O-halogen bonds are absent, but these remaining motifs dominate several high-score families. Ordinary thioesters and other recognizable sulfur functional groups also occur and should be distinguished from the unusual centres.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator lacks reliable support for ordinary stable sulfur environments rather than merely graph-valid sulfur coordination.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide stable bonding and electronic environments that preserve useful observed polar relationships, with chemical distinctions among thioesters, thioethers, sulfonamides and unusual neutral sulfur centres. Neutral syntax and parser acceptance cannot serve as substitutes for credible molecular chemistry.

transferable_gaps.evidence: All proposal heavy-atom ranges remain between 21 and 48, with none above 50. Yet a leading 36-heavy-atom molecule has eight perceived rings and mass 604.676, while a 30-heavy-atom leader has six rings and another has ten. Medium and large N/O cycles also occur among leaders. The highest molecules in one session have masses around 640-720 despite only 39-42 heavy atoms.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator controls atom counts without consistently controlling feasible ring topology, mass or synthetic complexity.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support chemically credible ring closures and lower-burden core alternatives within the observed size range. Atom count alone does not capture bridge strain, accessible conformations, elemental mass or synthetic difficulty; these properties need distinct representation in the generated chemistry.

transferable_gaps.evidence: No stereocentres are assigned in 4,350 optimizer proposals. The five sessions contain 624, 396, 870, 668 and 780 proposals with unassigned centres. Every proposal in one session is stereogenic by RDKit perception, and a displayed high-score 30-heavy-atom cage has eleven unassigned centres. Another highest molecule has six. Ring richness and saturated complexity therefore do not establish defined three-dimensional proposals.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator proposes complex stereogenic molecules without specifying any of their configurations.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Represent chemically consistent configurations and relevant bond geometries where they exist, retaining simpler achiral alternatives when appropriate. The supplied evidence does not choose an unobserved stereoisomer, and adding stereogenic ring junctions without specification does not provide interpretable molecular geometry.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Per-session nonchiral Murcko scaffold counts are 430, 418, 452, 442 and 521, but displayed leaders repeatedly occupy the same sulfur-linked aromatic, bridged amine or polycyclic carbonyl neighborhoods. Many carbonyl/sulfur/alkyl variants share score 0.608402, and several alkoxy or ring-atom alternatives share 0.207549. Low and high examples can both contain abundant sulfur or rings, showing that raw counts do not specify useful polar and aromatic relationships.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator has limited chemically distinct productive alternatives beyond repeated modifications within unusual core families.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Broaden distinct stable core and linker arrangements that preserve useful functionality, beyond peripheral substitutions and alternate ring closures. Treat functional-group electronic context and spatial placement as chemical properties, with usefulness determined by observed feedback rather than a prescribed objective-specific scaffold.

nodes.method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
nodes.method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.

approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from accepted, scored molecules. It samples high-ranked breeding parents, recombines connected fragments and applies local mutations and occasional successive mutations; direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is already disabled. Stable identity checks form a fresh surplus pool. An accepted-only Gaussian process represents molecules by counts of local Morgan environments and uses generalized Tanimoto similarity. Its correlated posterior score draws allocate the next evaluations, and accepted offspring update the full prediction archive and the bounded breeding population.
approach.novelty: Remove environment multiplicity from the predictor by replacing each cached count vector with binary presence in exactly the same molecular vocabulary. Keep the shared kernel equation, fitting settings and correlated allocation rule. This is a reverse control on the current exchange-free Parent: earlier count variants improved the mean on an exchange-enabled search, while narrowing intervals and worsening coverage, and they repeated the same trajectories. No evaluated same-Parent child in this brief has tested the representation removal. The pending correlation and mean-only controls retain count features and change allocation instead. This experiment asks whether count information still supports endpoint search, with a predicted loss when it is removed; any replay of an older binary search will be identified explicitly.

nodes.hypothesis: Remove Morgan environment multiplicity from the shared posterior representation by replacing each inherited count vector c with binary presence 1[c > 0] for every training, pool and next-fit feature use, while retaining the generalized Tanimoto implementation and all fitting, graph-generation and correlated-allocation rules.

finding_summary.headline: Removing environment counts lowers the matched mean by 0.051296 and reproduces the earlier binary search
finding_summary.insights: The isolated reverse control supports a positive contribution of environment multiplicity in the current exchange-free composition. It changes both fitted means and covariance, so the experiment does not assign the gain specifically to calibrated uncertainty. More structural variety is also insufficient: binary selection yields 2,267 typed and 1,546 generic cores versus 1,851 and 1,118 under counts, yet strict local parent beats fall from 629 to 565 and incumbent gains from 258 to 218. Molecular evidence preserves the useful conventional ketone and aminoaryl-dione gains alongside reactive environments, repeated large assemblies and destructive fragments; no universal size or chemistry rule explains the score loss. The fifteen trajectories and all shared non-timing decisions exactly reproduce the earlier binary ancestor. That establishes provenance and rules out treating the replay as new independent evidence; the current matched Parent comparison remains the contribution test. Which changes in similarity, means and covariance mediate the useful search behavior remains open.
finding_summary.results: Every active feature is binary under extensive repeated-environment exposure, and all 435 fitted pools change their posterior relative to counts on the same inputs. The retained correlated draws, graph operations and accepted feedback reconstruct correctly. Mean final score falls from 0.595670 to 0.544374, a paired loss of 0.051296 against the registered 0.002 scale. All seed macros decline: 0.077877, 0.002003 and 0.074008. Twelve task-seed endpoints decline; zaleplon_mpo improves on seed 0, while deco_hop and sitagliptin_mpo improve on seed 1. On the actual binary stream, latent 1.96-SD coverage is 79.75% versus 73.52% for a passive count model using the same earlier labels and scored molecules. Their MSEs are 0.016600/0.009873. Binary error is higher in all fifteen task-seed cells, while its coverage is lower for median_2 on every seed despite the aggregate increase. These diagnostics answer a different question from endpoint search utility.

molecular.headline: Compact ketone and aminoaryl-dione leaders coexist with reactive heterocycles, repeated large assemblies and low-scoring fragments
molecular.overall_character: All fifteen Child and fifteen published Parent trajectory files were present and read. Every task has 900 records and 870 optimizer proposals across Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2; tasks_without_trajectories is empty. The brief reports complete Child evaluation and complete profile-matched pairing with code Parent n-62daf219c70a, with no profile-mismatched seeds. The Parent comparisons below therefore use the complete published current-profile panel. This report describes chemistry and its observed score associations; it does not judge activation or attribute individual structural changes to the feature-representation intervention. The output remains rich in rings and aromatic frameworks: ring-closure-string incidence spans 0.9736 to 0.9943, and aromatic-string incidence 0.9414 to 0.9885. These counters measure presence in a molecule, not perceived ring count, aromatic-atom fraction or useful scaffold diversity. The molecules include compact annulated ketones, nitrogen/sulfur-containing spiro and bridged systems, linked heteroaromatic carbonyl assemblies, aryl-containing basic amines, medium/large nitrogen-carbonyl rings and fluorinated fused diones. Families differ across seeds, but leaders often remain close relatives within a seed, supporting moderate overall structural diversity. Some conspicuous leaders have comparatively conventional local chemistry: the ketone/fluoropyridyl family and an aminomethyl/fluoroalkyl aryl-dione family improve their matched Parent scores without N-F bonds. The strongest aryl-amine examples also use ordinary carbon-bound halogens. These counterexamples prevent a claim that reactive heteroatom-halogen chemistry is unavoidable. Nevertheless, other leaders contain N-F/N-Cl, peroxide-halogen chains, cyanates, aldehydes, chloromethyl ethers or crowded nitrogen/sulfur bridges. Large repeated aryl/dione assemblies and tiny poor-scoring fragments occur alongside the compact families. Synthetic plausibility remains questionable and overall drug-likeness weak; the visible conventional examples do not validate the complete set. Formal-charge and stereocentre-string incidences are 0.0 for all tasks, despite protonatable amines and potentially stereogenic saturated centres. Heavy-atom sizes below were counted from the cited trajectory SMILES tokens; geometry, synthesis and physical properties were not validated. The digest final excerpts are late seed-2 proposals, and some final proposals are poor fragments or truncated analogues despite a better retained incumbent. Parent statements use its published trajectories; cited_smiles contains only current molecules allowed by the digest or trusted citation paths.

The seed-2 fluorocyclopropyl leader becomes a lower-scoring 0.3862488109868912 relative after a ring-unsaturation/topology change; neither that nor the Parent's cyclic-cumulene leader establishes that strained unsaturation is required. The best local score gain therefore accompanies a plausible alternative family, while other seeds remain below the Parent.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Observed in n-e00db808bbb4 on Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2 at 300 observations per task, with complete current-profile Parent n-62daf219c70a. The environment gap previously recorded in n-c55c3d520a2c persists through N-halogen, oxygen-oxygen-halogen, cyanate, aldehyde and chloromethyl-ether chemistry. Counterexamples are especially important here: a compact ketone family and a conventional aminoaryl-dione family improve matched Parent scores without N-F, and the strongest aryl-amine examples use carbon-bound halogens. Thus reactivity is conditional on local environment and is not unavoidable for useful output.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently retain conventional bond environments while exploring useful aromatic and polar arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Task-agnostic transformations need plausible local alternatives preserving feedback-supported functional-group relationships, while distinguishing ordinary carbon-bound halogens, amides, ethers and amines from reactive bond patterns. Preserve and explore the demonstrated conventional alternatives. The evidence does not prove that a blanket filter improves score or attribute any specific liability to the feature representation.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-e00db808bbb4 under complete paired Search conditions with n-62daf219c70a, continuing the context/coverage gap first recorded in n-c55c3d520a2c. Current output contains a 65-heavy-atom repeated aryl/dione leader below its matched 30-heavy-atom Parent, a 60-heavy-atom assembly at an extremely low score, and a 41-heavy-atom doubled aromatic variant below its 28-heavy-atom relative. Tiny late fragments and truncated aryl-amine analogues also score poorly. Counterexamples include compact conventional families that improve their matched endpoints and substantial rings that retain useful scores; neither growth nor simplification is uniformly beneficial.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably preserve useful molecular context while controlling repeated elaboration and destructive simplification.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Use task-local feedback to test independent connectivities and simplifications that preserve useful aromatic, carbonyl and basic-region relationships, rather than treating repeated motifs or fewer atoms as sufficient. The missing capability is consistent preservation of functional context, not an inability to form rings or large molecules. No fixed size cutoff, repetition ban or component-level causal claim follows from this chemistry.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-e00db808bbb4 on the supplied complete Search panel and profile, compared with n-62daf219c70a. Leaders contain nitrogen/sulfur bridges, spirocycles, carbon centres attached to several nitrogens, larger nitrogen-carbonyl rings and compact fused diones. Ring text remains prevalent throughout. The earlier geometry concern from n-c55c3d520a2c persists in changed structures, while a conventional aminoaryl-dione and a recognizable diazaspirocycle are counterexamples to a uniformly implausible output. The Parent's particular cyclic-cumulene leader is not a property of the current best family.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not consistently establish geometric and synthetic feasibility for crowded annulations, aminal centres and larger nitrogen rings.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Topology changes need environment-sensitive assessment of ring connectivity, unsaturation, aminal stability and accessible conformations, with alternative structures preserving learned useful arrangements. Ring counts and aromatic text cannot establish feasibility. Preserve conventional small and spiro rings where appropriate; this evidence does not establish that all unusual topology is impossible or that geometric filtering necessarily raises reward.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-e00db808bbb4 across all supplied Search Seeds at 300 observations per task, continuing the identity gap recorded in n-c55c3d520a2c and Parent n-62daf219c70a. Every task has stereocentre-string and formal-charge-string incidence 0.0, although substituted saturated rings, spiro/bridged structures and aminoalkyl centres can have stereochemical distinctions. Clear primary, secondary and tertiary amines remain present, so neutral strings do not establish a lack of protonatable chemistry. The comparatively conventional leading dione does not remove the issue from the other generated families.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator leaves relevant stereochemical and molecular-state identity unspecified after producing saturated and heteroatom-rich structures.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Representations and transformations need to preserve or deliberately resolve relevant stereochemistry, with separate assessment of protonation, tautomerism and imine/alkene configuration. Distinguish achiral or configurationally labile structures from those needing stable stereoisomer assignment. These observations establish incomplete chemical identity, not a measured state-dependent score penalty or proof that adding charge or enumeration improves the objective.

nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

retained_mechanisms: Accepted-only task-local GP archive, bounded greedy survivors and score-quantile breeding parents.
Connected-fragment crossover and optional post-crossover mutation; ordinary one-/two-/three-call mutation continuation with the complete saturation/retry law.
All seven ordinary atom/bond/ring mutation families, fixed weights and atom bounds; aromatic C/N exchanges remain disabled with passive opportunity tracing.
Sanitization, stable canonical identity and original-graph reuse, initial/emitted and temporary-pool duplicate rejection, bounded attempts and fixed surplus pools.
The same hashed Morgan vocabulary and shared cache, now active binary presence; shared generalized Tanimoto equation, normalization, fixed noise, finite checks and jitter schedule.
Full posterior covariance, nonzero correlated residuals, inherited random-array call and masks/ties, identity-bound predictions, pending joins and next-fit probes.
Fresh objective-local state, prepared CONFIG and fixed batches/budgets/resources; numerical fallback and generation recovery remain source-preserved but unexercised.

approach.method_basis: The root follows the basic procedure in Section 2 of [Fred Glover's Tabu Search—Part I (1989)](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf). Tabu search keeps one current solution and a separate record of the best solution found. It selects the best available move allowed by temporary restrictions, including a worsening move when improvement is unavailable. Short-term memory stores attributes of recent transitions and temporarily forbids their reversal; partial attributes can apply to several different solutions. Restrictions expire as the walk advances, and older restrictions can be released when they prevent further movement. This molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation, generates chemically valid graph-edit neighbors, directly evaluates an admissible batch, and moves unconditionally to its highest-scoring accepted neighbor. Only that selected transition updates the inverse-attribute memory. The proposal is that this combination can carry the walk through useful intermediate structures while preserving the best observed score.
approach.novelty: The molecular implementation commits to signed changes in occurrence counts of canonical rooted local subgraphs as its move attributes. Counting occurrences keeps an addition or removal visible when the same motif also occurs elsewhere; describing local chemistry lets a restriction affect fresh molecular identities. A fixed stochastic mixture of atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and checked ring changes generates every neighbor from the current graph. A reproducible rule retains a small bounded subset of the selected transition's inverse attributes, with a fixed positive tenure measured only in completed walk steps. Recorded generation obstruction permits the oldest restrictions to be released as needed. These choices test whether shared local memory can change available chemistry without suppressing nearly every move. Selection uses only the actual accepted scores, with a reproducible tie rule and a separate best-observed archive. Preparation publishes reusable configuration and needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. A passive comparison records the first valid novel neighbors before tabu filtering from the same generation stream, exposing changes in batch membership and selected states without additional evaluations. Source-relative and incumbent score gains remain separate evidence from memory activation.

nodes.hypothesis: Walk from the best supplied molecular observation by directly evaluating fresh graph-edit neighbors that pass expiring inverse local-subgraph restrictions, move to the highest-scoring accepted neighbor even when it worsens the current score, and install bounded inverse attributes of that selected transition while retaining a separate best-observed archive.

finding_summary.headline: Tabu memory changed almost every later batch across replicas, while only 10% of accepted neighbors beat their source
finding_summary.insights: The replication rules out memory acting only as whole-molecule duplicate rejection or as a passive record: its restrictions repeatedly removed unseen molecules and changed actual state selection. Worsening moves can be followed by recovery and later incumbent gains, but the episodes overlap and do not establish distinct successful escapes. The separate best archive matters: on sitagliptin the final current scores were only 0.16887 and 0.20350 while the preserved best scores were 0.41959 and 0.46369. Following the current walk alone would therefore conceal much of what the search had found. Broad structural vetoing still coexists with weak average local proposals: accepted neighbors scored 0.06743 below their current source on average, despite positive average winner transitions. The passive reference has no scores for omitted molecules, so changed batches and incumbent-gain provenance cannot establish an advantage over an unrestricted walk. The molecular assessment further shows that graph sanitization and numerical gains coexist with N-halogen bonds, unusual sulfur valence and strained ring arrangements in tightly related high-scoring families. Correct tabu operation does not make those products chemically plausible or demonstrate broader useful scaffold exploration. A scored comparative walk and chemically meaningful evaluation remain necessary to separate useful memory from redirection toward permissively scored chemistry.
finding_summary.results: Both new replicas reproduced the intended graph walk and structural memory. All 2,900 accepted proposals were valid novel edits of the actual current graph. Temporary inverse-motif restrictions vetoed 7,503 otherwise valid novel draws (72.12% of such tests), changed 279 of the 280 batches after initialization, and led to 176 selected next states absent from the first ten unfiltered valid novel neighbors. Every one of 89 required worsening moves occurred; 62 later recovered above their own pre-move score, 24 did not recover despite later opportunities, and three occurred at the terminal step. Memory installation, refresh and four-step expiry reconstructed correctly, and neither new replica needed a forced release. Accepted neighbors beat their generating current score 292 times out of 2,900 (10.07%), with 167 strict improvements to the best-observed score. The new macro final-best scores were 0.49531 and 0.50903, alongside 0.51081 in seed 0. The three-seed mean was 0.50505 with population standard deviation 0.00693. Task means were 0.40256 for zaleplon, 0.60530 for scaffold hopping, 0.83839 for DRD2 docking, 0.18975 for median similarity and 0.48924 for sitagliptin. Every task finished all 300 oracle evaluations, and every final best score exceeded its supplied initial best.
