molecular.headline: Aromatic templates decorated with N-halogen bonds, unusual sulfur valence and strained rings; favorable scores mask poor chemical plausibility
molecular.overall_character: The supplied evidence covers seeds 1 and 2, compared with seed 0 of the same Algorithm Node. All five tasks have trajectories, each with 600 evaluated records including 580 optimizer proposals. The output consists of locally related, heavily decorated aromatic templates: indole-like carbonyl compounds, nitrogen-rich carbonyl/thione rings, aryl-linked amines and large cyclic polyamines or hydrazides. Across those families, unusual sulfur valence patterns, N-halogenation, N–S/N–O bonds and strained ring connections recur in the high-scoring products. All task digests report ring_closure_rate and aromatic_atom_rate of 1.0, alongside charged_rate and stereocentre_rate of 0.0. These are text indicators. They establish that every proposed string contains a ring and aromatic atoms, but not that every ring is aromatic, every nitrogen is nonbasic, or a formally neutral molecule is chemically stable. Mean SMILES lengths range from 47.7 to 75.3, with maxima from 59 to 91. The upper groups are tightly related within each seed rather than a broad range of conventional medicinal scaffolds. The dominant elaborated products are synthetically implausible as specified, and overall drug-likeness is weak. This assessment concerns the full combinations of multiply bonded hydrogen-bearing sulfur, N-halogenated functional groups, unusual heteroatom links and constrained ring geometry; individual familiar substructures can of course be made. The main missing chemistry is a plausible, configurationally defined realization of the favorable feature arrangements. The trajectories do not establish that any particular reactive group is necessary for the objective.

per_task.generated_character: The upper structures retain moderately sized, methyl-substituted indole-like or partially saturated fused aromatic cores linked to aryl/pyridyl carbonyl or imine groups. Their substituents are chemically unusual: N-brominated hydrazides, O-acyl hydroxylamines, ring-N–S(H) or N–S–Br groups, thiols and brominated N,O-acetal-like units. Mean SMILES length is 47.7; ring and aromatic indicators are both 1.0, halogen_rate is 0.819 and no charges or stereocentres are explicitly marked. Graph inspection of the full seed-2 trajectory finds N–halogen bonds in 177 of 290 optimizer molecules, so this is a recurring chemical family, not an isolated alert.
liabilities: N-bromination of a hydrazide and O-acylation of an arylhydroxylamine introduce reactivity beyond that of a normal carboxamide.
N–S–Br, N–S(H), thiols and brominated N,O-acetal-like units create oxidation, hydrolysis or halogen-transfer questions.
Late sulfinamide-like connections combine N–F, N–O and thiol functionality without defined sulfur or carbon configuration.
missing_features: The favorable compact aromatic/linker arrangement is present, but chemically conservative counterparts to the N-brominated hydrazides, N–S groups and brominated acetals are not demonstrated as a sustained series.
Configurations and chemical forms of the substituted saturated, sulfur-containing and imine-bearing structures are unspecified.
No unseen target motif can be identified as missing; the observed score preference for some reactive substitutions does not establish their chemical necessity.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The N-brominated hydrazide scores 0.3978246797147542, versus 0.3713987617652478 for its unbrominated hydrazide counterpart. Replacing that hydrazide connection with an O-acyl hydroxylamine gives 0.3953519239480604. These are useful local contrasts: the score favors or tolerates changes that substantially alter chemical reactivity. A different thiol/aminomethoxy fused-ring ketone also scores 0.3953519239480604. The initial conventional indole carboxamide scores 0.3051048083696145. The seed-0 best at 0.4145039882261785 already used an N-brominated indole-like imine with bromomethoxy substitution, so the baseline also lacks a clearly conventional chemical realization. The lowest optimizer proposal, at 0.01944116589877781, replaces an aryl carbonyl partner with a larger nonaromatic unsaturated ring; ring-expanded and open-chain variants score 0.05477203059248125 and 0.05668571231341881. This supports retention of a compact aromatic connection, but not a unique required reactive group. The median is 0.263721. The digest span minimum belongs to the initial alkyl bromide, not an optimizer proposal. Late N-fluoro sulfinamide/thiol structures remain moderate or low, including 0.2406047033036551.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-1 upper family combines substituted fluoropyridines, thioethers and an enlarged nitrogen-rich conjugated ring carrying carbonyl and thiocarbonyl groups. A hydrogen-bearing S=N–N link joins these regions, while brominated alkyl or thione side chains add further sulfur and halogen chemistry. The central conjugated ring is nine-membered by graph perception, not a routine pyrimidinedione. Seed 2 instead retains a fused carbonyl/thione heterocycle linked to heavily decorated azaarenes and methylthiomethyl groups. Mean SMILES length is 67.2, with ring/aromatic indicators both 1.0 and halogen_rate 0.6069. These are substantial, highly elaborated structures with poorly supported synthetic plausibility.
liabilities: Multiply bonded hydrogen-bearing sulfur, S=S-containing side chains and thioketones introduce chemical-form and stability questions beyond an ordinary thioether.
N-brominated thiocarbonyl derivatives and brominated alkyl chains provide additional reactive handles.
Some lower and intermediate structures contain cumulated double bonds, distorted rings or peroxide links; retaining aromatic atoms elsewhere does not make those complete structures conventional.
missing_features: Conventional, stable connections between the favorable azaaryl and carbonyl-containing regions are insufficiently demonstrated in place of the hydrogen-bearing S=N–N and S=S-rich links.
The output lacks defined configurations at brominated side-chain carbons and sulfur-containing centres, and does not establish a plausible geometry for the enlarged conjugated ring.
A unique missing decoration cannot be inferred from a high group that assigns identical scores to chemically different side chains.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The sulfur-imino-linked fluoropyridine/aza-thione structure scores 0.6137646155929755, unchanged when a methyl is added next to the sulfur linkage. A brominated thioketone side chain scores 0.6132067176646443; replacing its central carbon by sulfur to make an S=S-containing connection retains exactly that score. In seed 2, a decorated azaaryl/fused-thione molecule and chlorinated or brominated side-chain variants all score 0.6027037832975162 in the full trajectory. Thus close numerical values or exact ties coexist with substantial chemical changes. The seed-0 best at 0.5994428608447784 also had an expanded nitrogen-rich thione ring and a highly strained carbon-triple-bond-containing aromatic fragment. Both baseline and replication retain the same chemical-form problem. The initial fused-dione ester scores 0.548381482770623; the lowest optimizer proposal, with a sulfur-containing distorted ring, scores 0.5253369553860621, while the new median is 0.578899. Connected azaaryl/carbonyl/thione architecture distinguishes the upper family, but these scores do not show that its unusual sulfur linkages or brominated side chains are required.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-2 high family joins brominated/propyl-substituted aromatic rings to an unusual four-membered sulfur-containing unsaturated ring and an amino-substituted aziridine. Vinylamino or aminoalkyl arms and phenolic groups provide nitrogen and oxygen functionality. Seed 1 instead makes aryl-linked polyamines containing hydrogen-bearing imino sulfur and aryl S–Cl groups. These are large, heavily decorated amine-containing structures: mean SMILES length is 75.3, and every proposal has a ring, aromatic atoms and a halogen. Full-trajectory graph inspection finds multiply bonded hydrogen-bearing sulfur in 250 of 290 seed-1 and 278 of 290 seed-2 optimizer molecules. The problematic sulfur chemistry is therefore central to the generated population.
liabilities: Amino-substituted aziridines and four-membered unsaturated sulfur rings combine ring strain with chemically unusual valence patterns.
Aryl O–S(H), S–Cl and hydrogen-bearing imino-sulfur groups are not ordinary ether, chloride or amine substitutions.
The combination of large size, extensive halogenation, multiple reactive groups and undefined configurations makes a plausible synthesis and stable product substantially less evident than the score.
missing_features: The generator shows aromatic/amine combinations, but does not demonstrate chemically conventional saturated nitrogen rings and linkers that realize the same arrangement without aminoaziridine and multiply bonded sulfur complications.
Configurations of the amino-substituted small rings, branched side chains and sulfur-containing centres are unspecified throughout the favorable families.
No additional obligatory target interaction can be inferred from the numerical scores, especially where chemically disparate triple-bond linkages receive the same value.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The aryl/aminoaziridine structure scores 0.8858698958644818, and its aminoalkyl-arm relative scores 0.8840303912861983. Replacing the terminal phenolic aromatic group with an open conjugated chain in a late proposal lowers the score to 0.1179862719373953 while retaining much of the unusual sulfur/amine scaffold. The visible preference therefore includes the placement of aromatic surface around accessible nitrogen functionality. The baseline best at 0.773935927884237 also combined amines, halogenated aromatic regions and unusual sulfur/small-ring geometry. The lowest current optimizer proposals remain close to the initial amide/sulfonamide/acid framework, with scores such as 0.007468397818197266 and 0.01174587710699566, rather than the freer amino functionality of the upper structures. Many changes occur together, so this does not isolate an amine-only effect. A particularly revealing pair in seed 1 retains score 0.8214401673399405 when an ethynyl linkage is changed to a carbon–sulfur triple-bond linkage. The median is 0.219919. These score associations do not establish that the strained rings or exotic sulfur states are plausible binding structures.

per_task.generated_character: The main seed-2 family consists of aryl-linked, fused or bridged cyclic polyamine/hydrazide systems with multiple carbonyls, a phenol and a multiply bonded ring sulfur. The principal core contains seven- and nine-membered rings; it is not an ordinary piperazine or simple cyclic urea. Seed 1 explores a different large cyclic polyamine joined to an N–N aromatic ring and thioaryl/methylthio substituents. Mean SMILES length is 60.3; every proposal has ring and aromatic indicators, with no explicit charge or stereochemistry. The local families are densely sampled but chemically complex and stereochemically unresolved.
liabilities: The upper templates combine N–N-containing carbonyl groups, multiple amines and multiply bonded ring sulfur, complicating chemical form, oxidation and synthetic route planning.
A peroxide linkage is tolerated near the high end, and late structures add aryl O–N functionality or strongly distorted fused rings.
The score-tied fluoro and thiol variants have materially different chemical behavior despite identical reported values.
missing_features: A chemically tractable, simpler realization of the favorable aromatic/cyclic-polar relationship is not demonstrated beyond elaborate polyamine/hydrazide templates.
Defined carbon and sulfur configurations are absent, although the high-scoring fused/bridged systems contain stereogenic centres.
The narrow score band and exact ties do not identify a uniquely missing target-like scaffold or justify the added peroxide and sulfur complexity.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The fluorinated aryl/polycyclic hydrazide and its thiol-substituted aryl counterpart both score 0.19506328689370275. A related carbon-based ring connection scores 0.19423482736613115, while insertion of an O–O link into the complex ring system still gives 0.19340483308724274. In seed 1, changing an aryl amino group to chlorine, and then a sulfur bridge to a methylene bridge, retains 0.19245008972987526. These ties show that the upper numerical band does not resolve substantial differences in chemical reactivity or connectivity. The seed-0 best at 0.18173088254689942 was also a large carbonyl-rich heterocycle with an unusual hydrogen-bearing sulfur substituent. The initial conventional fused-dione ester scores 0.1678386594791329 and the new median is 0.177211. Lower proposals, including polyene-decorated or ring-opened relatives, score 0.12627394888184854 and 0.14217551071713674. The supplied initial alkyl bromide accounts for the overall span minimum. The visible preference is for particular ring-connected aromatic/polar arrangements, not evidence that thiols, peroxide links or large ring sulfur are necessary.

per_task.generated_character: The favorable structures are compact-to-medium but exceptionally sulfur-rich fused nitrogen/carbonyl systems. They combine N-fluorinated carbonyl heterocycles, multiply bonded hydrogen-bearing ring sulfur, thiol-substituted unsaturated arms and a benzofused four-membered sulfoxide ring. The seed-1 family instead includes N–S(H) substitution and sulfinyl fluoride groups on highly connected fused sulfur/carbonyl frameworks. Mean SMILES length is 61.0, with ring/aromatic indicators both 1.0, halogen_rate 0.8362 and cumulated_double_bond_rate 0.0397. Graph inspection finds N–halogen bonds in 233 of 290 seed-2 optimizer molecules. These are systematically unusual chemical forms, not ordinary fluorinated aromatic candidates.
liabilities: N–F or N–Br bonds on carbonyl heterocycles are chemically different from aryl fluorides or bromides and raise halogen-transfer and stability questions.
Hydrogen-bearing multiply bonded sulfur, thiol/thione combinations, strained sulfoxide or small sulfur rings and sulfinyl fluorides create demanding chemical-form and synthetic problems.
Late molecules add cumulated multiple bonds and a hydroperoxide. None of these structures has a validated stability or synthesis result in the supplied evidence.
missing_features: The output does not demonstrate a plausible stable version of the favorable carbonyl/imino and ring arrangement without N-halogenation, unusual ring sulfur and strained sulfur heterocycles.
Stereochemistry at saturated junctions and sulfoxide centres, and geometry of the unsaturated arms, are unspecified.
No missing conventional target pharmacophore can be inferred from these observations; the primary gap is chemical realizability of the structures receiving favorable scores.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The imino-substituted sulfur-rich fused system scores 0.463686320747673; its otherwise related carbonyl variant scores 0.4273912466002992. Changing a side-chain carbon into sulfur in the latter family gives 0.45108661991979854. Thus the score differentiates atom identity and polar-group placement within this unusual template, without establishing that its sulfur valence states or N–F bond are chemically desirable. The seed-0 best at 0.5844507853133432 was an even more densely bridged sulfur/N-fluoro structure, so the baseline also offers no conventional stable comparator. Early ring-altered relatives of the initial fused-dione ester score 7.590554525032884e-10 or 5.3704200337573903e-08; the overall span minimum instead belongs to an initial molecule. The median is 0.048093. Later migration to N-brominated, cumulene/sulfur-rich templates loses the favorable arrangement: one terminal structure scores 4.961705474958894e-06, while an analogue with an unsaturated three-membered ring containing two sulfur atoms scores 0.20349897544099319. transferable_gaps.evidence: The digest high groups repeatedly contain N-brominated hydrazides, N-fluorinated carbonyl heterocycles, N–S(H), S–Cl, hydrogen-bearing S=N or S=C groups, S=S connections and peroxide links. Full-trajectory graph inspection finds multiply bonded hydrogen-bearing sulfur in 250 of 290 proposals in one seed and 278 of 290 in its companion. Every task nevertheless has charged_rate 0.0, showing that formally neutral strings do not establish chemical plausibility.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably produce chemically defensible functional-group and sulfur-valence states around its favorable templates.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide chemically defensible hydrogen, valence and oxidation-state control, and conventional functional-group alternatives around the same ring/heteroatom arrangement. Judge explicit chemical forms rather than treating neutral charge or sanitization as sufficient. This does not require excluding all sulfur, halogens or ionizable groups.

transferable_gaps.evidence: All ring-closure indicators equal 1.0, yet digest examples include aminoaziridines linked to unsaturated four-membered sulfur rings, expanded nine-membered conjugated aza-rings, seven-/nine-membered polyamine-hydrazide cores, peroxide-containing closures and small multiply sulfur-containing rings. Favorable scores occur inside these families rather than demonstrating simpler conventional counterparts.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring-rich output is not consistently realized as geometrically and synthetically plausible ring architecture.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make bounded, chemically credible alternatives to ring size, ring junctions and linkers available while preserving useful aromatic and polar-group relationships. Let task-local feedback compare those alternatives; the presence of ring digits alone should not stand in for a feasible scaffold.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The digest records 0.6132067176646443 for both a thiocarbonyl side chain and its S=S-containing analogue, 0.8214401673399405 for ethynyl and carbon–sulfur triple-bond variants, and 0.19506328689370275 for fluoro and thiol aryl variants. A peroxide-containing ring variant remains at 0.19340483308724274. These ties or close values do not establish equivalent chemistry.
transferable_gaps.gap: Chemically very different substitutions often receive equal scores, while interpretable conservative alternatives remain underrepresented.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support local series defined by complete, chemically meaningful functional-group and connectivity changes, including simpler stable counterparts to favorable templates. Use task-local scores as objective evidence without interpreting a tie as evidence of comparable reactivity, stability or makeability.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every task reports stereocentre_rate 0.0 over 580 optimizer proposals. The digest contains brominated side-chain stereocentres, amino-substituted aziridines, fused polyamine junctions and sulfoxide or other stereogenic sulfur centres, while the cited alkenes and imines also lack geometry markers.
transferable_gaps.gap: The dominant substituted and fused structures lack configuration and geometric specification.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Enable explicit configurations and geometric alternatives for chemically plausible structures, preserving those identities during generation. The evidence establishes omitted specification, not a preferred stereoisomer or proof that the hidden objectives are stereosensitive.

nodes.method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
nodes.method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.

approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds molecular graphs from accepted high-scoring molecules using connected-fragment crossover and local atom or bond edits. It also retains stable canonical-identity admission and a direct, formula-preserving exchange of aromatic nitrogen positions. Each fresh surplus pool is evaluated by a binary-fingerprint Gaussian process trained on all accepted scores, and correlated posterior draws choose the oracle submissions. Accepted offspring can then enter the breeding population. The posterior currently uses the same small observation-noise level at every fit, even when its prediction errors differ substantially across the molecular neighborhoods encountered.
approach.novelty: Learn that single observation-noise level from the current accepted archive by comparing exact Gaussian marginal likelihoods over a fixed five-level menu. Larger selected noise represents mismatch between fingerprint similarity and accepted scores, reducing how tightly the posterior must interpolate them. Earlier posterior siblings changed binary environment presence into occurrence counts; this experiment retains the Parent's binary representation and instead tests whether task-local noise learning changes conditional uncertainty and improves prospective predictions. The graph, population and correlated-draw selection mechanisms remain inherited.

nodes.hypothesis: Choose the fingerprint Gaussian process's standardized observation-noise standard deviation at each fit by minimum exact negative log marginal likelihood over five fixed multiples of the inherited noise level, using only the current accepted archive.

finding_summary.headline: Noise learning changed 255 fits and improved matched coverage, but mean score fell 0.017540
finding_summary.insights:
Archive likelihood can identify and propagate substantial surrogate mismatch without improving the search endpoint. The matched measurements show better average coverage and predictive loss, but wider intervals still cover fewer than the nominal 95% of observed scores, and ranking gets weaker. Better uncertainty accounting is therefore insufficient evidence that the unchanged posterior-draw selector allocates evaluations more productively. The unchanged decoration and median trajectories also show that a measurable posterior change need not alter an emitted choice.

The remaining uncertainty problem includes score scaling. In an early sitagliptin batch, even the maximum standardized noise is multiplied by an archive scale of 0.001: a predicted mean of 0.00111 and total SD of 0.00118 precede a score of 0.18595, more than 157 SDs away. This narrows the next modeling question toward anticipating score-unit changes from a nearly flat accepted archive; expanding the menu alone is not established as a remedy. Frequent upper-endpoint selection leaves the appropriate noise range unresolved, while unchanged binary-fingerprint ties leave representational limitations intact.

The chemistry assessment also finds the existing structural liabilities intact, including unusually large repeated scaffolds, reactive heteroatom bonds, undefined stereochemistry and a new sulfur-radical branch. These observations limit what improved statistical coverage or occasional high scores mean chemically; they do not identify the cause of the aggregate score loss. The evidence establishes noise-learning activation and a failed score-benefit expectation on this panel, without isolating the causal value of any individual changed selection.
finding_summary.results:
The learned noise reached the actual posterior in 255 of 435 fits; 180 retained the reference level and 116 selected the largest allowed value. All five likelihood trials, final conditioning, accepted-label provenance and recorded posterior draws reconstructed correctly. After feedback, mean uncertainty on the admitted molecules remained 0.02821 score units, compared with 0.00405 under the fixed-noise rule on those same current archives.

On the 4,350 molecules actually submitted, the matched fixed-noise comparison shows latent 1.96-SD coverage rising from 79.68% to 82.44%. Including fitted observation noise raises observed-score coverage from 79.72% to 89.84%, with average interval width increasing from 0.1901 to 0.2604. Mean predictive negative log density improves from 6.3965 to 1.9102, and prediction MSE falls from 0.012180 to 0.011625 against an archive-mean baseline of 0.024654. Within-batch rank association weakens from 0.4146 to 0.3943. These are comparisons on identical accepted data and actual emissions.

Search utility declines: mean final-best score falls from 0.551771 to 0.534231, a paired loss of 0.017540 that misses the registered +0.002 benefit criterion. One seed improves and two decline; population standard deviation rises from 0.008223 to 0.023491. DRD2 and zaleplon task means fall, sitagliptin rises, and decoration and median retain exactly the same trajectories in every seed. Actual best-parent beats are essentially unchanged at 592 versus 593. All tasks and pools complete, with no numerical fallback; the additional 2,175 noise-trial factorizations consume 3.745 seconds of recorded unsynchronized host search time.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic families with size extremes, labile heteroatom bonds, sulfur radicals and unresolved stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: Read all 15 Child and 15 Parent trajectory files, covering seeds 0, 1 and 2 on every supplied task; no task lacks trajectories. Each Child task contains 900 records, including 870 optimizer proposals. All 4,350 Child proposal records parse with the supplied RDKit 2023.09.6; this establishes graph readability, not synthesis or stability. The digest's molecule-level string indicators give ring-closure rates of 0.9609 to 0.9908 and aromatic-token rates of 0.9460 to 0.9874. These indicate the presence of those features in SMILES, not aromatic atom fractions. The output is dominated by indole/pyrazole amides and thiocarbonyls, repeated heteroaromatic carbonyl units, halogenated aryl/polyamine systems, and fused or bridged ureides. Saturated rings and three-dimensional connectivity are present; their stereochemistry is unspecified. Passive graph counts find unassigned tetrahedral centres in 2,274 proposals, with no assigned centres and no explicitly charged proposals. They also identify 73 radical-containing proposals, all in one sulfur-rich seed, 874 proposals with N-halogen bonds, 381 with O-halogen bonds and 163 with O-O bonds; these categories overlap and flag structures for chemical review, not measured reactivity. Graph variation is substantial, but high-score neighborhoods repeatedly elaborate a few functional-group families. Overall drug-likeness is weak because familiar medicinal fragments coexist with excessive molecular size, difficult ring connectivity and unusual electronic or functional-group states. Parent comparison is molecular and descriptive: the complete ordered evaluation/source/SMILES/score records are identical on deco_hop and median_2 for every seed. The other tasks change their molecular neighborhoods; none of these observations judges mechanism activation. All sizes, ring counts and structural flags below are passive descriptors of recorded molecules. Score readings are associations within the supplied trajectories; they do not reveal an absent reference structure or establish a binding mode, pKa, synthetic route or measured stability. Reproducible provenance and descriptor calculations are in .slots/SPIRAL2.r0011-11-improve-L01.molecular-audit.json.

per_task.generated_character: Proposals have a median of 25 heavy atoms. Seed 0 concentrates on phenol-substituted pyrazoles with thiocarbonyl/thiourea linkages and unsaturated small carbocycles; seeds 1 and 2 favor alkyl/alkoxy indoles bearing aryl or pyridyl carboxamides. The seed-2 leader at evaluation 298 has 25 heavy atoms, three aromatic rings, an indole NH, ethoxy and methyl groups, a fluoropyridyl group and an N-fluoroamide. Seed 1 reaches an ordinary secondary-amide analogue, whereas the seed-0 leader has four rings, two aromatic, and a hydroxylated cyclobutene substituent. These are recognizable medium-sized heteroaromatic molecules, but the N-fluoroamide and strained/unsaturated ring substitutions make the panel only conditionally plausible as synthetic chemistry. Compared with the Parent, seed 0 shifts from a fused indole-related endpoint into the pyrazole/thiocarbonyl family; seeds 1 and 2 retain the indole/azaaryl-carbonyl neighborhood. Recorded best scores by seed change from 0.442313/0.460926/0.451975 to 0.420196/0.416350/0.438799, with similar molecular scale.
liabilities: The highest observed molecule contains an N-F bond in an amide; a late low-scoring structure combines N-F and O-F bonds with a thiocarbonyl. These are chemically sensitive connectivities, even though the SMILES sanitize.

Cyclobutene/cyclopentadiene substitutions and additional fused closures introduce strain or reactivity concerns; they cannot be treated as routine synthetic analogues solely because they retain the parent functional groups.
missing_features: The upper end does not demonstrate broad alternative ring/linker arrangements that preserve the favorable compact heteroaromatic and polar-group pattern beyond the recurring indole and pyrazole families. A specific absent target motif cannot be inferred from these scores.
Stereodefined forms of the newly substituted nonaromatic rings are not represented; this is a coverage gap, with no score evidence that a particular configuration would help.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxy indole carboxamide scores 0.305105; the compact substituted indole and pyrazole endpoints reach 0.416350 to 0.438799. The low and high score quartiles have median heavy-atom counts of 28 and 25, respectively, so retaining a compact heteroaromatic core matters more here than indiscriminate enlargement. The seed-2 evaluation-298 leader scores 0.438799, whereas evaluation 295, which has methoxy and aminomethyl substitutions, scores 0.304901. These are multiple simultaneous differences, not an isolated amine penalty. A Br/F substitution pair in the seed-1 leaders ties at 0.416350, while the elaborate thione/O-fluoro terminal proposal scores 0.091681. Very small proposals such as the cited halogen and hydrocarbon fragments score zero. The observed preference is for a particular compact arrangement of aromatic rings and polar carbonyl/thiocarbonyl groups, with substantial tolerance for chemically unusual substitutions; it does not establish that those unusual bonds cause the gain.

per_task.generated_character: This panel grows large, mostly aromatic assemblies: the proposal median is 69 heavy atoms and nine perceived rings. Seed 0 builds extended azaaryl/aryl carbonyl and ether assemblies; seed 1 repeats aryl and nitrogen/oxygen heteroaromatic carbonyl units with alkoxy, imine, nitrile/cyanate and chloromethyl-ether substituents. The seed-1 evaluation-295 leader has 91 heavy atoms, nine aromatic rings and calculated molecular weight about 1,303.5; evaluation 296 has 113 heavy atoms and 13 aromatic rings. Seed 2 is smaller, with a proposal median of 39 heavy atoms, but commonly joins two fused ureide systems through an amino-heteroaryl unit and introduces N-F, N-Cl or O-Cl bonds. The large repeated products are far outside ordinary small-molecule scale and would require substantial synthetic justification; even the smaller seed-2 series contains unusual reactive functionality. All ordered molecular records and scores match the Parent in all seeds.
liabilities: Very high molecular size, many linked aromatic rings and numerous acceptors create substantial solubility, conformational and synthesis concerns. These are structural concerns, not measured exposure or permeability results.

Chloromethyl ethers, imine/enol-ether segments and the smaller series' N-F/N-Cl/O-Cl bonds require stability and synthetic scrutiny; high scores do not establish that these are isolable, useful compounds.
missing_features: Compact, nonrepeated scaffolds retaining the heteroaromatic/carbonyl/aryl-ether arrangement seen at the upper end are not demonstrated at comparable scores. The missing coverage concerns economical placement of these features, not a shortage of rings or aromatic atoms.

The trajectories do not identify which unseen decoration or reference feature is absent; they show repeated functional-group assemblies rather than evidence for a particular target-specific replacement.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The tiny cited fragments all sit at 0.5. Initial indole and fused ureide-containing molecules already score 0.546402 and 0.548381; elaborated aromatic assemblies reach 0.611413. The low and high score quartiles have median heavy-atom counts of 38 and 85 and median aromatic-ring counts of four and ten. This is an association between the sampled favorable motifs and extensive aromatic elaboration, not evidence that adding arbitrary mass helps. The 91-heavy-atom leader scores 0.611413 and the 113-heavy-atom analogue scores 0.611206, showing that greater size is not monotonically rewarded. Seed 0 reaches 0.609808, seed 1 0.611413 and seed 2 0.597688. The cited compact seed-2 terminal analogue scores 0.577517, while the linked/fused larger terminal structures score around 0.588 to 0.597. High scalar scores therefore tolerate both repeated large architectures and N-/O-halogenated chemistry; no synthesis benefit follows from this gradient.

per_task.generated_character: The high end consists of medium-sized halogenated diaryl molecules with substantial saturated ring/linker content and several nitrogen centres. The proposal median is 36 heavy atoms; the high-score quartile is narrower, at 30 to 37 heavy atoms. Seed 2 builds amidine-containing, amino-substituted pyrrolidines connected through an NCN aminal segment to another aryl-bearing carbon. Its leading phenol has 31 heavy atoms, two aromatic rings plus a pyrrolidine, several potential protonation sites and three unassigned tetrahedral centres. Seed 0 instead retains small nitrogen rings attached to an aryl-substituted [SH](=N) sulfur centre; the supplied RDKit assigns one radical electron to that sulfur in the cited leaders. There are 73 radical-containing proposals in that seed, versus none in the Parent panel. Seed 1 favors polycyclic amine/sulfoxide structures. The Parent already produced compact diaryl/basic-nitrogen structures. Its recorded seed maxima of 0.979377/0.951235/0.991404 become 0.938121/0.829081/0.946088 here, alongside the new sulfur-radical branch and the amidine/polyamine branch.
liabilities: The [SH](=N) leaders carry a sulfur-centred radical by the matching RDKit's electron assignment. This is a stronger issue than merely uncommon sulfur nomenclature and is not detected by SMILES parse success alone.

Neutral SMILES for amidines/polyamines leave important solution-state charge possibilities unresolved. Multiple donors/basic sites, brominated aromatic groups and unspecified stereocentres complicate interpretation as a defined medicinal compound; no pKa, permeability or synthetic route is supplied.
Small strained nitrogen rings and NCN aminal connections warrant chemical stability and synthetic review even when the rest of the scaffold uses familiar fragments.
missing_features: Basic nitrogen centres are abundant. What is absent from the submitted representations is explicit protonation and defined stereochemistry for these existing centres and substituted saturated rings; downstream oracle protonation handling is not established by these trajectories.

The favorable compact diaryl/basic-group arrangement has not been broadly reproduced through simpler linkers and routinely closed-shell ring systems. The sulfur branch lacks a demonstrated closed-shell counterpart retaining its high-end arrangement, while the polyamine branch relies on an aminal and many polar/basic sites.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial large acidic sulfonamide scores 0.019041, and a truncated N-chloroamide/sulfonamide scores 0.000347. The leading diaryl/amidine/polyamine phenol scores 0.946088; replacing that phenol with an aniline gives 0.936709. Cited terminal molecules show that nitrogen abundance alone is insufficient: the analogue lacking the second aryl group scores 0.236533, an additional-amidine analogue scores 0.627986, and an enlarged three-aryl analogue scores 0.403056. These are not isolated edits, but together they favor a compact two-aryl/basic-nitrogen arrangement over extra size or indiscriminate polar-group addition. The low and high score quartiles have median heavy-atom counts of 43 and 33. The two sulfur-radical leaders tie at 0.938121 despite changing one aryl Cl to F. This demonstrates that a high recorded docking objective can coexist with an electronically unusual submitted graph; it does not establish how the oracle treated that state or identify a receptor contact.

per_task.generated_character: These are mostly medium-sized, densely connected N/O heterocycles: the proposal median is 30 heavy atoms, five rings and two aromatic rings. Seed 0 develops constrained nitrogen-rich carbonyl systems attached to alkylated azaaryl groups; seed 1 favors phenyl/ethoxy-substituted fused or bridged ureide/enamine/ether architectures; seed 2 retains azaaryl-linked fused imide-like systems. The seed-1 evaluation-218 leader has 33 heavy atoms, five rings, two aromatic rings, cyclic carbonyl/urea functionality, an N-methyl group and an N,O-acetal carbon carrying an unassigned stereocentre. Its elemental functional groups are familiar, but its ring connectivity and medium-ring closures demand a specific synthetic route. This is genuine saturated and aromatic ring chemistry, not an aromatic-only string collection. All ordered molecular records and scores are identical to the Parent across all seeds.
liabilities: Dense annulation, medium-ring carbonyl systems and enamine/acetal connections make synthetic feasibility and conformational accessibility uncertain without a route or structural analysis.

Duplicating the heterocyclic framework adds size and rings while producing a lower-scoring cited terminal molecule; chemical complexity alone should not be read as meaningful new pharmacophore coverage.
missing_features: The upper end does not show a broad set of simpler alternative ring/linker topologies preserving the favorable aromatic/carbonyl/nitrogen arrangement; the recorded gain remains concentrated in densely fused or bridged ureide-related chemistry. The trajectory does not identify a particular absent reference scaffold.

Explicit configurations are missing where new ring junctions or N,O-acetal substitutions create tetrahedral centres. The missing information is stereochemical definition, not the capacity to generate saturated or three-dimensional graphs.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial fused ureide-containing molecule scores 0.167839. Later constrained carbonyl/amine systems reach seed maxima of 0.204784, 0.213610 and 0.207878. The seed-1 leaders at evaluations 218 and 203 score 0.213610 and 0.213010 with closely related 33-heavy-atom polycycles. The cited seed-2 terminal 28-heavy-atom, six-ring product scores 0.201130, while the larger duplicated 41-heavy-atom, eight-ring product scores 0.165558. The low and high score quartiles have median heavy-atom counts of 32 and 31 and median aromatic-ring counts of three and two. The observed gradient favors particular compact, partly saturated arrangements of aromatic and carbonyl/nitrogen features, not simply more rings or larger molecules. Hydrocarbon and hydroxylamine fragments at the low end score zero or 0.012461. The terminal excerpt still varies substantially within the same functional-group families.

per_task.generated_character: The proposal median is 27 heavy atoms. Seed 0 reaches compact fluorinated fused ureide-like heterocycles bearing several carbonyls, fluoroalkyl substituents, a fluorinated alkenyl chain and an N-SH substituent. The tied leaders have 28 heavy atoms, two aromatic rings and molecular weight about 426.4. Seed 1 favors fluorinated conjugated carbocyclic ketones attached to imino/carbonyl heterocycles with an N-F bond. Seed 2 instead develops more fused ring systems with peroxyester and N-halogen functionality. The seed-0 leaders therefore look more compact than many early aryl-rich products, but their N-SH chemistry is still unusual. The other seeds' N-F and peroxyester chemistry makes synthetic plausibility questionable. Relative to the Parent's compact fluorinated nitrogen/carbonyl systems, seed 0 changes toward the N-SH/fluoroalkyl ureide series and the other seeds toward different labile ring families. Recorded maxima change from 0.475978/0.575091/0.503080 to 0.663627/0.504586/0.411429.
liabilities: The leading n(S) substitution is an N-SH connection with a terminal sulfur hydrogen in the supplied RDKit, not an ordinary carbon thioether. Its persistence and synthetic handling are not established.

N-halogen bonds, conjugated unsaturated ketones and peroxyesters appear in the other seeds; these can be reactive motifs and require chemical review. The panel contains 79 peroxide-bearing proposals compared with five in the Parent, despite both panels having a median of 27 heavy atoms.
Large duplicated heterocycles and tiny fragments continue to appear late, so compact high-scoring chemistry is not maintained in every subsequent proposal.
missing_features: The high-end size and fluorinated/carbonyl balance is not demonstrated across a broad set of conventional stable functional-group arrangements: the best branch uses N-SH, while other upper-end branches contain N-F or peroxyester groups. The gap is reliable access to chemically ordinary alternatives, not missing fluorine, amides or rings.

Geometric specification of the unsaturated side chains and defined configurations in the more fused products are missing from the cited SMILES. No trajectory comparison establishes whether assigning those states changes the objective.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-rich fused ureide ester scores 0.002094. A duplicated 60-heavy-atom, nine-ring ureide/aryl product scores 1.6758614448245604e-53, whereas the compact 28-heavy-atom leaders score 0.663627. The low and high score quartiles have median heavy-atom counts of 31 and 27. Within the cited seed-0 series, lengthening one fluoromethyl substituent to fluoroethyl accompanies a change from 0.536196 to 0.663627. Moving which of the two nitrogen substituents carries that additional carbon leaves the two leaders tied at 0.663627. A related chloroethyl member scores 0.520929. These comparisons support sensitivity to the sampled size/composition and polar/fluorinated balance, without proving a unique required connectivity. Both extreme enlargement and the terminal acetylene fragment are poor: the latter scores 3.716764234274643e-25. A late seed-2 peroxyester-containing molecule scores 0.277703, while its enlarged peroxide-linked relative scores 1.5627949162950568e-19. The gradient clearly does not establish stability or justify peroxide chemistry.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Passive parsing finds 73 radical-containing optimizer proposals. The cited aryl/small-nitrogen-ring [SH](=N) leaders at score 0.938121 have one sulfur-centred radical electron in the matching RDKit. Every proposal still passes parsing, and the Parent trajectories contain no such radicals.
transferable_gaps.gap: The emitted structures do not consistently preserve closed-shell electronic states.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make electronic-state consistency explicit in generic molecular construction and admission, and support closed-shell alternatives to unusual sulfur connectivity. Parse success alone cannot serve as evidence of an ordinary stable molecular product; no objective identity is needed to address this gap.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Across 4,350 proposal records, passive bond inspection finds N-halogen bonds in 874, O-halogen bonds in 381 and O-O bonds in 163. The cited high-scoring compact indole contains an N-fluoroamide; compact fluorinated ureides carry N-SH; later fused products carry peroxyesters. These are structural flags, not a measured instability count.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ordinary functional-group connectivity is not reliably retained during molecular variation.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide chemically informed ways to vary substituents and heteroatom placement while preserving recognizable functional groups, including stable alternatives to heteroatom-halogen, terminal N-SH and peroxide connections. Apply the same chemical rules and accepted-feedback learning to every objective, without treating an alert as proof that every occurrence is unusable.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Cited aromatic assemblies contain 91 and 113 heavy atoms with very similar scores, while a different cited duplicated 60-heavy-atom framework has a near-zero score. The complete proposal panel also contains 55 molecules with at most three heavy atoms. High-scoring neighborhoods elsewhere are compact ring-bearing molecules, so there is no universal larger-is-better rule.
transferable_gaps.gap: Molecular scale is variable but insufficiently controlled against repeated-framework growth and collapse to tiny fragments.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support local growth and contraction that retain useful ring/linker context and can remove duplicated substructures. Let already accepted score feedback determine where molecular elaboration matters, while preserving chemically meaningful intermediate sizes; the evidence does not justify one objective-specific size rule or a blanket ban on larger molecules.

transferable_gaps.evidence: All digest stereocentre-marker rates are zero. Passive nonlegacy tetrahedral perception finds unassigned centres in 2,274 proposal records and assigned centres in none. The cited amino-substituted pyrrolidine leader has three unassigned centres, and the leading fused N,O-acetal has an unassigned centre as well.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator produces stereogenic graphs without producing explicitly defined stereoisomers.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve and represent stereochemistry when edits create or modify stereogenic environments, and make alternative configurations available as chemically defined candidates under ordinary identity handling. This adds molecular-state coverage; the supplied scores do not establish which configurations would be favored.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every task's digest charged-marker rate is zero and passive parsing finds no charged proposal. Nevertheless the cited leaders include amidines and multiple aliphatic amines, while supplied low and initial molecules include carboxylic acids. Neutral SMILES do not imply that those compounds stay neutral in solution.
transferable_gaps.gap: Explicit acid/base charge states are absent despite frequent potentially ionizable functional groups.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support chemically consistent representations of ionizable centres and relevant protonation alternatives using a universal state policy. Preserve the distinction between the submitted representation and any downstream preparation; these trajectories alone neither reveal that preparation nor prove a score benefit from charge enumeration.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The panel contains many distinct graphs, but the cited high-end families repeatedly elaborate fused ureides, indole/pyrazole carbonyl compounds or diaryl/basic-nitrogen systems. Some upper-end ureides have five interconnected rings and an N,O-acetal, while more elaborate duplicated terminal frameworks score below compact related examples. Rich ring counts therefore coexist with uncertain ring-closure feasibility.
transferable_gaps.gap: Dense ring rearrangements outpace evidence for simpler, synthetically interpretable alternative scaffolds.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Expand alternative ring and linker constructions that preserve useful functional-group arrangements with interpretable bond-forming relationships, rather than counting every added closure or duplicated framework as equivalent chemical coverage. Synthetic plausibility must be assessed as a property of the proposed structure, with no task name or hidden reference scaffold supplied.

nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves scored molecular graphs through score-band parent selection, connected-fragment crossover and local mutation. Stable canonical admission creates a surplus pool. A Gaussian process learns from every earlier accepted raw score using folded counts of radius-two molecular environments and generalized Tanimoto similarity. It chooses evaluations through correlated posterior draws, then updates the archive, breeding population and incumbent using real raw scores.
approach.novelty: Add a fixed topological atom-pair count channel alongside the retained local counts, and average their separately normalized similarity kernels equally. Atom types separated by graph distances up to thirty bonds can provide relational information missing from local environment counts. Earlier unfolding kept the same local environments, while ordinal targets changed label spacing; both lost mean endpoint score. This tests additional molecular information through one fixed covariance composition, with raw-score targets and the search rules retained. Added information may also dilute useful locality, so alias splitting or better prediction alone will not establish benefit.

nodes.hypothesis: Retain the Parent's local Morgan occurrence-count covariance and add sparse topological atom-pair occurrence-count covariance, using the fixed equal-weight average of their separate generalized Tanimoto kernels for every GP block while preserving raw-score learning and the inherited search rules.

finding_summary.headline: Atom-pair information changed search and split six local aliases, but the mean endpoint fell by 0.033408
finding_summary.insights: More descriptor distinctions and better predictions on selected molecules did not yield better endpoint search in this fixed mixture. On the actual accepted stream, raw MSE improved from 0.009475 for the passive local model to 0.009335, and mean batch ordering correlation rose from 0.545819 to 0.571243, despite the endpoint loss. These improvements were uneven: MSE worsened in seven task/seed cells, including all median_2 cells. Ordinary similarity and regularization changes were broadly exposed, whereas alias-mediated benefit was not: ten members of five split pool pairs remained unscored, and only one member of the cross pair was evaluated. Thirteen other pairs shared atom-pair counts but remained distinguishable through local counts; the channels still do not establish complete molecular identity. The negative result belongs to this one equal-weight composition and does not undo the earlier evidence for retaining local occurrence counts or isolate atom-pair information from mixture weighting. Molecular evidence still shows reactive heteroatom-halogen and sulfur motifs, large linked assemblies and destructive fragments alongside conventional high-scoring chemistry. Added topological information does not enforce chemical feasibility, and neither a universal size explanation nor an alias-resolution explanation is established.
finding_summary.results: All 435 batches changed their raw posterior means, uncertainties and conditional covariance. Against the same-input local-only reference, 432 selected sets and 433 orders changed; three sets and two orders remained unchanged. All six distinct local-count alias pairs split, but none had both members scored. All three matched replicas completed. Mean final score fell from 0.595670 to 0.562261, a loss of 0.033408 against the required gain of 0.002. Seed deltas were −0.072325, +0.009185 and −0.037084. Six of fifteen task/seed endpoints improved: all three zaleplon results and the seed-1 deco_hop, drd2 and sitagliptin results. Every median_2 result declined. Seed dispersion decreased from 0.026593 to 0.006995 around the lower mean. The mechanism ran correctly; its registered endpoint-benefit prediction was falsified.

molecular.headline: Aromatic amides, aza heterocycles and aryl amines persist; reactive bonds and unresolved ring geometry remain
molecular.overall_character: All fifteen Child and fifteen published Parent trajectory files were read: Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2, 300 observations per task/seed, with 900 records and 870 optimizer proposals per task. No task or Parent path is missing. The fresh brief marks both Child completion and matched Parent pairing complete, with no profile mismatches; the comparison is to n-62daf219c70a. The evaluated output contains compact fused aromatic carboxamides, linked nitrogen-rich carbonyl/thione heterocycles, polycyclic aryl amines, aromatic lactam/urea assemblies and fluorinated unsaturated nitrogen-carbonyl rings. Ring-closure text incidence is 0.9529 to 0.9805 and aromatic-text incidence 0.9276 to 0.977. These are molecule-level text incidences, not ring counts or aromatic-atom fractions. All stereocentre-text rates are zero. Charge-text incidence is zero except for one charge-separated nitrogen motif in the aromatic-amide task, rate 0.0011; neutral representations still contain basic amines. The chemical reading is rich rings/aromaticity, questionable synthetic plausibility, weak overall drug-likeness and moderate structural diversity across seeds, with narrower families among leaders within a seed. Conventional functional groups coexist with N-halogen and O-F bonds, unusual sulfur-H oxo environments and difficult bridges. No synthesis, stability, protonation, conformation or biological activity has been established. Sizes below are heavy-atom-token counts from the actual SMILES, not geometric measurements. The trajectory/offspring audit joins all 4,350 accepted offspring to their raw score, actual selected pool position and earlier evaluated parents. All fifteen raw-score leaders were evaluated and immediately admitted as survivors, and their scores agree with final best_so_far records. Immediate admission does not establish that every other evaluated molecule survives later replacement. The digest's final excerpt is a late seed-2 proposal list, not the retained leader of each seed. Full pool logs, rather than evaluated-only trajectories, support the pool observations below. Logged descriptors preserve the distinction between retained folded local Morgan counts and the added native sparse atom-pair counts. The receipts specify chirality-aware two-dimensional distances 1 through 30 and a fixed equal average of separately normalized count-Tanimoto kernels. Six distinct local-count-equal pairs occur in core training/cross/pool operands: five within-pool pairs and one archive-to-pool pair seen twice, hence seven occurrences; training contributes none. All six have unequal atom-pair rows and mixed similarity below one. Five additional pool_equivalence records repeat the five pool pairs and are not new pairs or independent observations. No distinct pair remains equal in both channels in these logged operands. This absence is conditional on the actual panel, not proof of molecular uniqueness. None of the ten members of the five within-pool pairs was evaluated in its task/seed. The cross pair has only one evaluated member: the 80-heavy-atom nitrogen-dione assembly in seed 2/evaluation 239 of the linked-heterocycle task, score 0.5910185045885361, immediately admitted but not an incumbent improvement. Its other member has no raw label. The six splits therefore supply no paired scored comparison. Conversely, thirteen distinct pairs remain equal in the atom-pair component alone while local counts distinguish them. Ten involve different single atoms with empty atom-pair rows; three involve sulfur-H or ring-bond variants. Their mixed similarities are below one, so component equality must not be called mixed-kernel equality. Finite identifiers, equal descriptor multisets, unspecified stereochemistry and restricted two-dimensional distances still limit identity and feasibility claims. The 435 passive local-only records explicitly have no alternative labels. Their predictions and choices are not another scored search, and a component or mixed similarity change does not demonstrate chemical benefit or mediation. Active posterior means are reported in raw-score units, covariance/noise in standardized raw-score units; the accepted labels and endpoint scores used here remain raw. Nothing here establishes global calibration. nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

approach.method_basis: The reference is RACOS, introduced by Yu, Qian and Hu in their 2016 paper, Derivative-Free Optimization via Classification. It uses observed objective values to label promising examples as positive and poorer examples as negative. In its categorical form, it selects a positive exemplar and randomly fixes coordinates to that exemplar's values until every observed negative example lies outside the remaining region. It then fixes more coordinates as needed to limit how many remain free. New proposals sample the free coordinates uniformly while preserving the fixed values. A broader uniform sampling component maintains exploration, and fresh randomized classifiers can define different regions around the same exemplar. Feedback updates the examples that guide subsequent regions.
approach.novelty: This root applies categorical RACOS directly to molecular SELFIES token frames, using removable padding to permit length changes and a construction alphabet extracted from the unlabeled corpus. Initial molecules enter classification only after a verified molecular identity round trip. Each accepted generated molecule retains its actual sampled frame and returned score, with one record per canonical molecule. Ranked labels include all ties at the positive cutoff and stay fixed throughout each announced batch. Decoding, chemical validation and novelty filtering connect raw frame sampling to oracle submissions; exhausted regions trigger reconstruction or the declared broad sampling component. The implementation also compares each final region with the same-coordinate-order restriction from the free-coordinate limit alone, so any additional restriction caused by negatives is visible. These choices test whether exact exclusion in token coordinates produces useful molecular proposals while keeping representation identity, decoded duplication and the contribution of negative examples separately measurable.

nodes.hypothesis: Rank real task-local molecular observations into positive and negative examples, build fresh categorical regions by randomly fixing a positive exemplar's SELFIES-frame coordinates until every observed negative frame is excluded and the remaining free-coordinate count is bounded, then sample uniform token assignments inside those regions with a broader uniform construction-space component.

finding_summary.headline: RACOS ran correctly; negative exclusion added no restrictions beyond the uncertainty limit
finding_summary.insights:
Negative examples were consulted and newly admitted negatives prolonged the exclusion phase in 330 regions, so the classifier was active. Yet exclusion always finished after at most 70 fixed coordinates, while the uncertainty limit required 75. The limit therefore determined every final mask, and perfect exclusion supplies no evidence for an additional contribution of negative labels to proposal geometry or score. The observed procedure supports direct molecular score provenance and feedback-guided sampling around positively ranked exemplars; whether making negatives influence the final region improves search remains open.

Distinct token restrictions also did not imply distinct molecular neighborhoods: 48 raw decodes overlapped an earlier different region, and ten draws recovered a currently negative molecular identity through another encoding. Filtering caught these cases, but it cannot repair weak molecular geometry. The molecular assessment finds frequent radicals, unusual charges and reactive linkages among high scorers, with only an uneven subset of conventional scaffold chemistry. Together with the low exemplar-beating rate and the unchanged median_2 incumbent, this identifies useful, chemically credible token neighborhoods as an unresolved bottleneck. Neither reliable performance across seeds nor a benefit from alternative serialization views is established.
finding_summary.results:
All five objectives completed on the screening seed, with 300 evaluations each and all 1,450 generated submissions accepted. Every initial molecule preserved its identity through token encoding, every returned score stayed attached to its actual sampled frame, and all 150 rank-label snapshots included the required cutoff ties. All 1,355 constructed regions retained their positive exemplar and reduced the number of included observed negatives to zero, while leaving exactly four of 79 token positions free. Real feedback was reused: all 1,400 generated observations with a later opportunity participated in subsequent region construction. However, the final restrictions in every region were identical to those obtained from the four-free-coordinate limit alone.

The five-task final Top-1 mean was 0.315539, compared with 0.208492 for the supplied initial observations. Initial-to-final Top-1 scores were 0.305105 to 0.345581 for zaleplon_mpo, 0.548381 to 0.579123 for deco_hop, 0.019041 to 0.120104 for drd2_docking, 0.167839 to 0.167839 for median_2, and 0.002094 to 0.365051 for sitagliptin_mpo. All 18 incumbent improvements came from regional submissions. Only 67 of 1,304 accepted regional proposals (5.14%) beat their selected exemplar; mean child-minus-exemplar score was -0.096376. There is no Parent comparison or additional seed in this root experiment, so these within-run gains do not establish a comparative score advantage.

All five objectives completed on the screening seed, with 300 evaluations each and all 1,450 generated submissions accepted. Every initial molecule preserved its identity through token encoding, every returned score stayed attached to its actual sampled frame, and all 150 rank-label snapshots included the required cutoff ties. All 1,355 constructed regions retained their positive exemplar and reduced the number of included observed negatives to zero, while leaving exactly four of 79 token positions free. Real feedback was reused: all 1,400 generated observations with a later opportunity participated in subsequent region construction. However, the final restrictions in every region were identical to those obtained from the four-free-coordinate limit alone.

The five-task final Top-1 mean was 0.315539, compared with 0.208492 for the supplied initial observations. Initial-to-final Top-1 scores were 0.305105 to 0.345581 for zaleplon_mpo, 0.548381 to 0.579123 for deco_hop, 0.019041 to 0.120104 for drd2_docking, 0.167839 to 0.167839 for median_2, and 0.002094 to 0.365051 for sitagliptin_mpo. All 18 incumbent improvements came from regional submissions. Only 67 of 1,304 accepted regional proposals (5.14%) beat their selected exemplar; mean child-minus-exemplar score was -0.096376. There is no Parent comparison or additional seed in this root experiment, so these within-run gains do not establish a comparative score advantage.

Negative examples were consulted and newly admitted negatives prolonged the exclusion phase in 330 regions, so the classifier was active. Yet exclusion always finished after at most 70 fixed coordinates, while the uncertainty limit required 75. The limit therefore determined every final mask, and perfect exclusion supplies no evidence for an additional contribution of negative labels to proposal geometry or score. The observed procedure supports direct molecular score provenance and feedback-guided sampling around positively ranked exemplars; whether making negatives influence the final region improves search remains open.

Distinct token restrictions also did not imply distinct molecular neighborhoods: 48 raw decodes overlapped an earlier different region, and ten draws recovered a currently negative molecular identity through another encoding. Filtering caught these cases, but it cannot repair weak molecular geometry. The molecular assessment finds frequent radicals, unusual charges and reactive linkages among high scorers, with only an uneven subset of conventional scaffold chemistry. Together with the low exemplar-beating rate and the unchanged median_2 incumbent, this identifies useful, chemically credible token neighborhoods as an unresolved bottleneck. Neither reliable performance across seeds nor a benefit from alternative serialization views is established.
