molecular.headline: Frequent rings, but high scorers often carry radicals, unusual charges and reactive linkages; conventional scaffold chemistry is uneven.
molecular.overall_character: All five supplied seed-0 trajectories were read, each containing 300 observations and 290 optimizer proposals. There is no Parent node or Parent trajectory, so comparisons use the supplied initial molecules and the within-task score contrasts. The output ranges from tiny heteroatom fragments to medium and larger multiring frameworks. Rings are common: the per-task ring_closure_rate spans 0.6241 to 0.8207. Aromatic content is uneven, with aromatic_atom_rate spanning 0.1517 to 0.6207; those rates describe the presence of SMILES text features, not fractions of atoms or perceived aromatic rings. Some recognizable neutral indole carboxamides, aryl aminals and fused nitrogen/carbonyl frameworks survive. However, charged_rate spans 0.6862 to 0.9448, and reparsing the supplied trajectory graphs confirms widespread radical centres as well as formal charges. Oxonium-containing unsaturated rings, low-coordinate charged atoms, atypical sulfur/phosphorus environments, peroxides and highly unsaturated chains recur among the high scorers. The ring and aromaticity judgements therefore reflect real but inconsistent coverage; they do not imply chemically credible ring geometry. Formal atom and bond diversity is substantial, while high-scoring chemistry within a task repeatedly returns to related scaffold families. Synthetic plausibility is poor overall, with a more conventional subset particularly visible in the aryl-aminal and fused-dicarbonyl families. Every proposal set has stereocentre_rate 0.0, which establishes absent stereochemical specification rather than absence of potentially stereogenic structures. The score observations establish local structural associations. They do not identify an unseen target pharmacophore or show that a chemically cleaner analogue would necessarily score better.

per_task.generated_character: Mostly medium-sized unsaturated organic frameworks, interspersed with very small fragments; mean SMILES length is 42.1 and maximum length 84. The ring_closure_rate is 0.8207 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.6207. The high-scoring proposals combine benzene or other aromatic fragments with nitrogen-rich thione/thioamide linkages, N-N or N=N connectivity, and oxygen-containing unsaturated rings. Evaluation 135 adds an exocyclic boron double bond, oxonium and a low-coordinate carbon cation to a densely connected multiring framework. Evaluation 21 retains aryl thiourea-like connectivity but embeds an alkyne in an oxonium-containing ring system. These are substantially less convincing synthetic targets than the supplied neutral methoxyindole carboxamide at evaluation 9. The generated set has charged_rate 0.9241 and cumulated_double_bond_rate 0.2069.
liabilities: Persistent oxonium centres, a radical-bearing low-coordinate carbon cation in evaluation 135, and additional radical nitrogen/oxygen environments elsewhere in the digest.
Cyclic alkynes, cumulated unsaturation, exocyclic boron double bonds and unusually connected N-N/thione systems make stability and feasible synthesis doubtful.
missing_features: Reliable preservation and variation of compact aromatic frameworks with intact nitrogen/carbonyl or nitrogen/thione linkages; these features coexist in the stronger supplied examples but are frequently disrupted in the lower-scoring generated structures.

Chemically ordinary, closed-shell versions of the high-scoring aromatic/polar architectures. The initial neutral indole carboxamide demonstrates relevant coverage, but the leading proposals largely explore oxonium-rich alternatives; the data do not establish a score benefit from neutrality itself.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Evaluation 135 scores 0.3455806835841063, evaluation 21 scores 0.3430778750697882, and the aryl/N=N/thioamide-containing evaluation 195 scores 0.34169169616841205. The neutral initial indole carboxamide at evaluation 9 already scores 0.3051048083696145, whereas the initial aryl-rich nitrogen/thione compound at evaluation 3 scores 0.1501184006136499. The tiny imidate-like anion at evaluation 289 scores 0.0. In the final excerpt, evaluation 295 retains an unsaturated oxonium ring but replaces the thione/aromatic arrangement with a thiol-bearing branched chain and scores 0.07284283327394388. The visible preference is for particular assembled aromatic/nitrogen-containing frameworks and their linker arrangements over fragments or damaged arrangements. Neither aromatic ring presence alone nor an unusual charge establishes a favourable contribution.

per_task.generated_character: Medium-sized aryl-rich molecules and smaller chain fragments; mean SMILES length is 41.9 and maximum length 85. The ring_closure_rate is 0.7724 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.5655. The upper tail includes methoxyindole carboxamide/amidine derivatives with a fluoropyridyl group, and linked diaryl cyclic aminals carrying methoxy, fluoroethoxy, methyl and sometimes hydroxyl groups. The neutral cyclic-aminal members at evaluations 138 and 253 have recognizable organic functionality, although ring construction and hydroxyaminal stability remain unestablished. Other close members replace ordinary substituents with peroxide/alkoxide chains, an aryl-bound nitrogen anion or an O-Cl group. The full proposal set has charged_rate 0.6862 and halogen_rate 0.6828.
liabilities: Peroxide bonds combined with terminal alkoxide groups in the highest-scoring indole series, and reactive O-Cl functionality in a high-scoring aminal analogue.

The aryl-bound nitrogen anion in evaluation 296 is a deprotonated amine environment, not a conventional neutral amine. Hydroxylated aminal centres and complex cyclizations also warrant caution even in otherwise neutral members.
missing_features: Broader stable substitution chemistry around the retained aryl/nitrogen frameworks. Near-leading neutral examples are present, but other leading decorations introduce chemically labile bonds or strongly basic anions without demonstrating that those features are necessary.

Additional coherent scaffold families that preserve the aromatic and polar-group relationships visible in the stronger molecules; the high-scoring excerpt mainly recycles indole and diaryl-aminal arrangements. Exact hidden decoration requirements cannot be inferred from these scores.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The indole amidine with a peroxide-containing alkoxide substituent at evaluation 272 scores 0.5791225581141548; its corresponding carboxamide at evaluation 187 scores 0.5711425931629196. This pair supports a local preference for the amidine change within that particular scaffold. The neutral diaryl hydroxyaminal at evaluation 138 scores 0.5766980825479363, exactly the score of the related O-Cl-containing evaluation 205. The aryl nitrogen anion at evaluation 296 scores 0.5782514840798705, while the neutral gem-dimethyl aminal at evaluation 253 scores 0.5749037932930181. Tiny formaldehyde at evaluation 244 and the short chlorinated ether at evaluation 270 both score 0.5. The final, partly de-aromatized evaluation 299 scores 0.5387550321456468. The observed gradient favours coherent multiaryl nitrogen-containing architecture over small fragments, with modest changes among the high-scoring substituent variants; it does not show that peroxide, O-Cl or anionic functionality is required.

per_task.generated_character: The upper tail consists of relatively large, densely connected polycyclic frameworks with chlorinated and fluorinated aryl regions, unsaturated bridges, and sulfur/nitrogen-rich linkages. Mean SMILES length is 57.7 and maximum length 108. The ring_closure_rate is 0.7, but aromatic_atom_rate is only 0.2586: the many rings and double bonds across the trajectory do not generally correspond to intact aromatic systems. The best examples recover aromatic regions within heavily modified scaffolds. Evaluations 213, 273 and 260 contain small-ring nitrilium/triple-bond segments, unusual sulfur environments and radical centres. Cationic nitrogen can also carry covalently bound chlorine. These are poor candidates for straightforward synthesis despite being parseable graphs. The proposal set has charged_rate 0.9034 and halogen_rate 0.8552.
liabilities: Small-ring triple-bond/nitrilium geometry, radical nitrogen centres and covalent N-Cl functionality in the leading polycycles.

Atypical sulfur/phosphorus coordination, extensive halogenation and unresolved stereochemical/conformational possibilities make the apparent rigid frameworks chemically doubtful. No binding poses or experimental stability evidence are supplied.
missing_features: Chemically credible realization of the combined aryl surface, constrained shape and polar/ionizable functionality represented in the upper tail. The leading molecules express much of their nitrogen chemistry through nitrilium or low-coordinate charged/radical environments.

Well-defined saturated nitrogen heterocycles and specified stereochemistry within otherwise intact aryl frameworks are poorly represented among the leading generated examples. This is a chemistry-coverage gap; the low score of the initial tertiary-amine molecule prevents claiming that a particular amine centre would solve the objective.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The elaborate halogenated polycycle at evaluation 213 scores 0.12010438063540518, the phosphorus-containing relative at evaluation 273 scores 0.118818265142154, and the boron/ammonium-containing evaluation 260 scores 0.11451910258577357. The initial conventional aryl/sulfonamide/carboxamide framework at evaluation 10 scores 0.01904115112334333. A short neutral ether/formamide at evaluation 86 scores 0.001217586292651792. The initial aromatic hydroxamate/amide bearing a saturated tertiary amine at evaluation 6 scores still lower, 0.0003786988088202195, so a basic amine plus aromatic rings is not sufficient in the supplied observations. The truncated final charged sulfur/nitrogen structure at evaluation 296 scores 0.007096085062148271. The visible preference is associated with the fuller halogenated, conformationally constrained, heteroatom-bearing architecture. These examples do not isolate a causal benefit from charge, radical character or any specific binding interaction.

per_task.generated_character: The stronger proposals are medium-to-large, aromatic and carbonyl-rich frameworks related to the initial phenolic aryl ethyl ester linked to an N-methylated fused dicarbonyl heterocycle and a phenyl group. Mean SMILES length is 48.6 and maximum length 87; ring_closure_rate is 0.7966 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.5276. Evaluation 252 makes a further methylene-linked annulation while retaining ordinary ester, phenol and cyclic carbonyl functionality. Evaluation 144 retains the fused dicarbonyl portion but has a nonaromatic cyclopentadienone region. These neutral examples are more synthetically recognizable than the boron/sulfur ring insertion at evaluation 161 or the many charged and partly opened variants elsewhere. The full generated set still has charged_rate 0.7483 and cumulated_double_bond_rate 0.1448; synthetic plausibility is mixed and scaffold-dependent.
liabilities: Boron/sulfur and phosphorus insertions, charged substitutions and partial destruction of aromatic or cyclic carbonyl systems throughout the generated set.

The most conventional generated annulation still creates a more demanding fused architecture, while cyclopentadienone and cumulated-unsaturation variants raise reactivity and geometric concerns. Parseability does not supply a synthetic route.
missing_features: Controlled, chemically ordinary variation that retains the combined aromatic/ester/carbonyl topology while changing its arrangement; the strongest generated examples remain close to an initially supplied family.

Broader coverage of distinct intact aromatic amide-rich scaffolds alongside the dominant fused-dicarbonyl series. The separate initial amide/hydroxamate is also relatively strong, but it is absent from the best-generated digest excerpt; no unseen reference structure can be deduced from that contrast.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl ester/fused dicarbonyl compound at evaluation 7 remains the observed maximum at 0.1678386594791329. The strongest generated annulated relative at evaluation 252 scores 0.16526725762745997, the boron/sulfur-containing relative at evaluation 161 scores 0.16482878931282252, and evaluation 144 scores 0.15842507656543134. The chemically distinct initial aromatic amide/hydroxamate at evaluation 6 also scores 0.1569767171139282. At the end, the short ether/aldehyde at evaluation 299 scores 0.031008683647302127, and the tiny boron/phosphorus/silicon/iodine fragment at evaluation 300 scores 0.0. Retention of assembled aromatic and carbonyl-containing motifs is associated with higher scores than fragmentary chemistry. Extra annulation or unusual element insertion does not improve on the supplied initial maximum in these observations.

per_task.generated_character: The high-scoring output is predominantly nonaromatic: medium-sized branched polyenes, imine/azine chains and cumulated C=C=N-type linkages, with fluorinated termini and thiol-containing ether or silicon appendages. Some members have a small unsaturated nitrogen/boron or nitrogen/oxygen ring; the high-scoring evaluation 177 is acyclic. Mean SMILES length is 45.3 and maximum length 84. The overall ring_closure_rate is 0.6241, but aromatic_atom_rate is only 0.1517, cumulated_double_bond_rate 0.531 and charged_rate 0.9448. Evaluations 277, 177, 147 and 210 contain low-coordinate charged/radical nitrogen, phosphorus, boron or silicon environments. Their chemical identities are much closer to highly reactive heteroatom-rich unsaturated graphs than conventional isolable medicinal compounds.
liabilities: Multiple radical or low-coordinate charged centres within individual structures, including silicon and phosphorus environments that are unlike ordinary saturated silanes or phosphate/phosphonate groups.

Cumulated unsaturation, N-O bonds, long imine/azine or polyene sequences, thiol termini and unspecified stereochemistry give substantial stability and synthesis concerns. The upper scores do not establish medicinal plausibility.
missing_features: Chemically credible, closed-shell alternatives spanning the medium-sized mixed-heteroatom chain/ring arrangements sampled in the stronger molecules; the demonstrated high-score region is populated by radical-rich structures.

Stable, well-specified versions of the observed polar and unsaturated frameworks, with conventional ionization and stereochemical definition. Their score effect remains unmeasured; absent aromatic rings cannot honestly be called a score-supported deficiency here.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Evaluation 277 scores 0.36505100258606615; the acyclic polyene/azine at evaluation 177 scores 0.3436199762843053. The boron-ring/silicon relative at evaluation 147 scores 0.3354265133232108 and its oxygen-ring relative at evaluation 210 scores 0.3251031345422294. Thus neither aromaticity nor ring closure is necessary for the high-score family visible here. The conventional initial aromatic ester/dicarbonyl compound at evaluation 7 scores only 0.0020944534688323298. The final modified relative at evaluation 296 scores 6.214769695340417e-08, and the truncated nitrile-containing chain at evaluation 298 scores 4.7513256368956235e-07. A heteroatom-dense charged chain at evaluation 300 scores 0.0. The gradient is sensitive to the assembled chain/ring and heteroatom arrangement; neither mere complexity nor charge density explains it. The observed median is 0.000102. The trajectory supplies no basis for prescribing a missing aromatic pharmacophore or a drug-specific amine pattern.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Across the supplied proposal sets, charged_rate ranges from 0.6862 to 0.9448. Reading and reparsing the same graphs reveals low-coordinate carbon/nitrogen radical centres and unusual radical-bearing silicon/phosphorus environments, including in upper-tail molecules. The charges are frequently oxonium, nitrilium, strongly basic anions or other atypical states rather than ordinary protonatable amines and carboxylates. The neutral indole carboxamide, neutral aryl aminal and neutral fused-dicarbonyl examples show that conventional electronic structures are also present in chemically relevant score regions.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably produce chemically credible electronic states while varying polar and ionizable functionality.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make closed-shell polar structures and controlled, chemically credible ionization states routinely accessible. Construction constraints should distinguish ordinary ionic functional groups from unsupported radicals and low-coordinate charged atoms, while feedback determines which polar architectures matter. Element identity or a net-charge ban alone would not capture this gap.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The upper-tail indole series contains peroxide/alkoxide substituents. A neutral methoxy/fluoroethoxy aryl hydroxyaminal and an O-Cl-containing relative both score 0.5766980825479363. Other high-scoring examples contain cyclic alkynes, cumulated bonds or unusually connected sulfur groups. These liabilities are not resolved by successful parsing or by removing formal charge, and the score contrasts do not demonstrate that reactive decorations are necessary.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator lacks consistent functional-group stability even when its proposed graph is neutral and closed-shell.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Expand ordinary stable ether, amide, amine and related substitution chemistry around the frameworks supported by current feedback. Chemical construction should account for labile bond combinations and ring strain as well as valence, allowing stable alternatives to be explored without encoding a particular objective or target structure.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The stronger aromatic families retain assembled nitrogen/thione, aryl-aminal or fused-dicarbonyl patterns, while the low-scoring excerpts repeatedly contain small fragments or opened/de-aromatized versions. An initial intact aromatic ester/dicarbonyl scaffold scores 0.1678386594791329; its strongest generated annulated relative scores 0.16526725762745997, whereas a late short ether/aldehyde scores 0.031008683647302127. The high-score nonaromatic family also loses score after substantial changes to its assembled heteroatom chain. Frequent ring closures therefore do not establish reliable preservation of useful topology.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator cannot consistently vary useful scaffolds without disrupting aromatic rings and the linker or carbonyl groups that organize them.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support scaffold-preserving changes to substituents and attachment relationships while retaining explicit ring edges and complete functional-group bond patterns. Let the observed feedback identify which structures to preserve, and keep alternative coherent scaffolds accessible so preservation does not become fixation on an initial molecule.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Ring_closure_rate spans 0.6241 to 0.8207, yet leading examples include highly unsaturated oxonium loops, small-ring nitrilium segments and complex heteroatom-rich bridges. Every proposal set has stereocentre_rate 0.0. Saturated amine-containing rings are visible in supplied initial molecules, but the leading generated cationic ring examples often express charge through more problematic bonding. This establishes a coverage gap, not a measured preference for saturation or stereochemistry.
transferable_gaps.gap: Conventional saturated and stereochemically specified ring architectures are poorly covered among the stronger generated structures.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make feasible saturated and partly saturated heterocycles, controlled basic centres and explicitly specified stereochemical variants available as general construction options. Ring geometry and stereochemical identity should remain coherent during variation, with task-local feedback deciding where these chemical dimensions help.

nodes.method_name: RACOS: negative-exclusion sampling of de novo SELFIES regions
nodes.method_thesis: The anchor is RACOS, selected before locating the primary source. Its categorical form chooses a positively labeled exemplar, randomly fixes coordinates to that exemplar until negative examples are excluded, further restricts the number of free coordinates, and samples the resulting region; a broader uniform component preserves exploration. Each proposal can use a newly randomized classifier. These are the mechanisms described by Yu, Qian and Hu in [Derivative-Free Optimization via Classification](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/10289/10148). My molecular adaptation applies this process directly to bounded categorical SELFIES frames, with removable padding that permits changes in molecular length. Preparation extracts only a construction-token alphabet from the permitted unlabeled corpus. There is no trained molecular encoder or decoder. Initial labeled molecules become exemplars only after encoding and decoding reproduce their canonical identity. For generated molecules, retain the actual sampled frame, its decoded canonical molecule, and the score actually returned for that molecule. Rank the current objective's observed molecules into a high-score positive group and a lower-score negative group; use these labels to construct exclusion regions. Free token positions are newly sampled and decoded into complete molecules, checked, canonicalized, and deduplicated. Rebuild a region or use the broad generation component when a region cannot provide a fresh molecule. These are online constructions from token primitives, not retrieval or enumeration of complete molecules. After each announced batch receives real feedback, refresh the labeled sets and incumbent; all pending proposals use only previously observed scores. Each objective starts with clean task-specific state and follows the protocol's supplied batch and resource limits. The hypothesis is that explicitly excluding observed poor token configurations will concentrate new molecular proposals around combinations that improve the incumbent with few labels. Success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Region exclusion, validity, or classification accuracy alone cannot establish that hypothesis. Positional token restrictions may have weak structural meaning, and multiple frames can decode to the same molecule; exact representation checks address score provenance but do not establish useful search geometry.

method_tags.acquisition_mechanism: stochastic region generation with a broader construction-space sampling component
method_tags.learning_mechanism: objective-rank positive/negative labeling followed by randomized coordinate shrinking
method_tags.proposal_mechanism: uniform de novo token sampling inside randomized positive-exemplar regions that exclude observed negatives
method_tags.representation: direct categorical SELFIES frames with removable padding and verified molecular identity

retained_mechanisms: Corpus-only SELFIES construction alphabet with frozen categorical frames and removable PAD
Verified initial molecular identity round trips and one retained actual scored frame per canonical molecule
Task-local score ranking with positive-cutoff ties and labels frozen through each unresolved batch
Uniform positive-exemplar selection and randomized negative-exclusion coordinate shrinking followed by the four-free-coordinate uncertainty limit
Uniform regional token sampling mixed with broad uniform construction, plus local molecular validity and novelty filtering
Exact pending-frame score attachment, complete-batch feedback refresh, task-local incumbent tracking and later reuse of accepted positive and negative records
Matched-order uncertainty-only masks and decoded-region overlap diagnostics; bounded region-rebuild and broad-refill recovery retained in source but exhaustion/refill paths unexercised

approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from real accepted scores. It selects breeding parents across high-scoring population quantiles, applies connected-fragment crossover and ordinary successive atom and bond edits, and fills a fresh surplus pool after graph validation and canonical duplicate rejection. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled. A Gaussian process uses the complete task-local accepted archive, folded integer Morgan environment counts and fixed dot-product Tanimoto covariance. Correlated sampled functions select distinct offspring for evaluation; accepted scores then update the archive and a bounded greedy population.
approach.novelty: Substitute one fixed Matérn-3/2 covariance on normalized count composition for the current Tanimoto law. Euclidean distance between unit-length count rows changes similarity and roughness while retaining the same extracted fingerprints and all other search operations. This differs from siblings that unfolded the count coordinates, added an atom-pair channel, replaced the model by trees or removed predictive selection. Normalization deliberately loses overall count scale and aliases proportional count rows; these are risks of this single recipe, not separately identified effects. The hypothesis is that its changed geometry improves prospective ordering and delivery of useful scored offspring, which may improve the complete endpoint mean.

nodes.hypothesis: Replace dot-product count Tanimoto covariance with fixed Matérn-3/2 covariance on L2-normalized unchanged folded Morgan count rows: z(x)=x/||x||2 for nonzero x and z(0)=0; r=||z(x)-z(y)||2; K(x,y)=(1+sqrt(3)*r)*exp(-sqrt(3)*r), with lengthscale one and unit amplitude.

finding_summary.headline: Changed allocations and more local gains, but mean Top-1 falls by 0.02751
finding_summary.insights: The failure is informative because the new predictor had real allocation exposure, complete accepted feedback and intact numerical controls: an inactive implementation or unseen changed choices cannot explain the negative endpoint result. More parent-beating offspring and incumbent events did not translate into better final best molecules. Average best-generating-parent score fell from 0.470456 to 0.416185, and offspring score from 0.385256 to 0.338080: beating weaker sources more often is not independent evidence of stronger exploration. The original predictor also ranks the very same scored Child selections better, narrowing the predictive hypothesis without requiring unscored pool labels. Local event counts and selected-stream errors cannot stand in for the benchmark objective. Normalizing count rows deliberately loses overall count scale and introduces proportional-coordinate aliases by construction, although no proportional-only pairs or zero rows were naturally exposed in this panel; those effects belong to the complete tested covariance recipe and were not separately randomized or attributed. Productive-event reuse, later conditioning and descendant cores remain conditional associations with overlapping ancestry and censored final-batch sources. The chemistry assessment also shows familiar useful carbonyl/aromatic and amine frameworks alongside reactive heteroatom-halogen arrangements, unresolved stereochemistry and occasional large elaborations; compact leaders and useful deletions show that blanket growth, fluorination or fragmentation rules are not justified. No evidence identifies that chemistry as a mediated consequence of covariance geometry. End this exact exposed complete law under the registered rule. A future materially different law needs a sourced distinguishing hypothesis; transferable kernel-family benefit and independent plausible descendant coverage remain open.
finding_summary.results: The replacement changed 434 of 435 accepted candidate sets and 435 selection orders when compared with the original predictor on exactly the same pools, earlier observations and random draws. All 4,350 Child offspring reached real feedback with their original pre-label predictions; no formal numerical fallback or rejection occurred. On those actual Child selections, unequal-label pair-order accuracy was 0.646947, versus 0.731356 for passive original predictions; average defined within-batch Spearman was 0.380506, versus 0.579077. Raw-unit selected-stream MSE was 0.012160, versus 0.007080 for the passive original and 0.032088 for the archive mean. The actual Parent stream had pair accuracy 0.711063, Spearman 0.532208 and MSE 0.012718; those adaptive streams differ after the first batch. Strict best-generating-parent beats increased from 629 to 682, and sequential incumbent advances from 258 to 269. Batch-frozen incumbent beats were 373 versus 346. Despite those local events, mean final Top-1 fell from 0.595669649733 to 0.568161409345, a signed change of -0.027508240389. Seed macro changes were -0.062538302981, +0.001846540890, -0.021832959074; 4 of 15 task/seed endpoints improved. Population seed dispersion was 0.007592488960 versus 0.026592870628. The complete +0.002 gain criterion failed.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic families persist, with reactive N/O-halogen bonds, occasional oligomer growth and unspecified stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: Complete Child evaluation and complete matched Parent pairing are explicitly true in context.comparison; all fifteen Child and fifteen published Parent trajectory paths and their task logs were present and read. All five digest objectives are covered, with no tasks_without_trajectories. Each objective has 900 trajectory rows including 870 optimizer proposals. The parent-only molecules used for chemistry comparisons are not included in cited_smiles because the trusted allowlist contains Child trajectories only. Signed endpoint evidence for every task/seed appears below, including all losses. The Child and Parent are separate three-seed panels sharing one baseline; chemical associations and exact generating provenance do not identify Matérn mediation, activation, independent replication, or component-specific effects. Chemistry spans indole amides, linked azaaromatic heterocycles, small/medium-ring aryl amines, dense dicarbonyl systems and fluorinated imino/dione families. Ring and aromaticity are rich, consistent with digest ring-closure-string incidences 0.9874 to 0.9989 and aromatic-string incidences 0.9839 to 0.9977. These incidences are SMILES-text molecule indicators, not perceived ring counts. Synthetic plausibility is questionable and overall drug-likeness weak because reactive heteroatom-halogen bonds, unresolved tautomer/stability questions, dense topology and occasional large oligomers accompany familiar medicinal groups. Diversity is moderate across seeds and objectives but narrower within leading families; no independent core diversity claim follows from distinct strings. Heavy-atom sizes and perceived rings mentioned in this report come from RDKit parsing the actual cited trajectory molecules in the read-only support audit, never oracle evaluation. No synthesis, stability, affinity or conformational feasibility measurement is available. Initial rows are fixed starting observations; best retained endpoints, last proposals and digest final_molecules are distinguished: the digest final excerpt is late seed-2 proposals, not all three final retained leaders. Actual generating-parent/emission/accepted joins are recorded for every leader below and fully retained in .slots/round-0026-slot-1/molecular_audit.json. Chronological delivery audit: child: 4350 accepted offspring; 682 strict best-parent beats and 269 logged incumbent-improvement flags during sequential accepted-feedback processing; among parent beats 667 had later actual generating-parent draws, 569 had accepted direct descendants, 15 had no later draw, and 13 occurred in the final batch; parent: 4350 accepted offspring; 629 strict best-parent beats and 258 logged incumbent-improvement flags during sequential accepted-feedback processing; among parent beats 614 had later actual generating-parent draws, 536 had accepted direct descendants, 15 had no later draw, and 12 occurred in the final batch. Later generating-parent draws include unsuccessful/unselected breeding, so they are not accepted-descendant counts; accepted direct descendants can overlap in ancestry, and terminal unused events are censored rather than failures. Incumbent-improvement flags are logged during sequential processing of each accepted batch and must not be mistaken for the preregistered batch pre-feedback incumbent statistic. All accepted offspring labels and joins came from existing trajectories/logs. Inherited gaps retain original source n-c55c3d520a2c, the same-code baseline n-62daf219c70a, and current source n-ea03f38e7e10 with their profile conditions; the full original policy-node molecular reports were read through the evidence index. No missing paths or absent matched comparisons were found.

per_task.generated_character: The three seed leaders have 24, 25 and 25 heavy atoms. They retain fused indole-like rings attached through an amide or N-hydroxy amide to phenyl/pyridyl rings. Seed 0 adds a partially unsaturated nitrogen ring and hydroxymethyl group while retaining an N-fluoro amide; seed 1 has a conventional secondary amide and N-fluoromethyl indole; seed 2 carries an aryl N-methyl-N-chloro group and N-hydroxy amide. The recognizable aromatic/carbonyl framework is medicinal-chemistry-like, but N-F/N-Cl environments make several leading examples questionable synthesis or stability targets. Published Parent leaders use a cumulene/azaaryl family, N-fluoroindole N-hydroxy amide, and N-chloroindole vicinal diketone respectively; the Child changes leading families without consistently resolving local reactive chemistry. The digest reads 870 optimizer proposals across seeds: ring-closure-string incidence 0.9908, aromatic-string incidence 0.9885, mean SMILES length 45.6, maximum 94, halogen-string incidence 0.9724. These are molecule-level SMILES text incidences, not ring counts or aromatic-atom fractions.
liabilities: N-fluoro amides and aryl N-methyl-N-chloro groups are distinct from conventional carbon-bound aromatic fluorine or chlorine and raise reactivity/stability concerns.

N-hydroxy amides are recognizable functionality but do not establish that the separate N-halogen bond is synthetically useful. Nearby leaders introduce N-O-F, N-Cl or more elaborate fused-ring substitutions.
missing_features: The high-scoring record does not consistently supply conventional nitrogen substitution while preserving the compact aromatic/amide arrangement; a conventional amide leader is present in one seed, so this is inconsistent coverage rather than inability to form amides.
Chemically independent plausible compact frameworks are limited among leaders within each seed. The trajectories cannot identify an exact absent target pharmacophore.

per_task.generated_character: Seed 0 grows into an oligomeric 93-heavy-atom leader with multiple azaaryl branches, thienyl regions, imines, enol ethers and carbonyls. This is much larger than its published Parent 30-heavy-atom, densely fused/bridged carbonyl-thione heterocycle; graph size and aromatic labels do not establish a plausible synthesis. Seed 1 instead produces a 38-heavy-atom four-ring azaaryl/benzoxazinone-like assembly bearing two alkynes, thioether, an acetal-like carbon, and a chloroalkoxy group. Its Parent used a smaller linked heteroaryl/nitrile/cyanate family. Seed 2 reaches a 34-heavy-atom substituted indole thioamide linked to a fluorinated diazine, with N-O-Cl and haloalkyl ether chemistry; its Parent leader carried a peroxide/nitrite/N=S family. Rich ring chemistry therefore coexists with size overgrowth and reactive attachments, not uniform ring scarcity. The digest reads 870 optimizer proposals across seeds: ring-closure-string incidence 0.9989, aromatic-string incidence 0.9977, mean SMILES length 91.8, maximum 230, halogen-string incidence 0.6931. These are molecule-level SMILES text incidences, not ring counts or aromatic-atom fractions.
liabilities: The large oligomer combines extensive aromatic/imine/enol-ether regions and a difficult synthesis burden; many proposed graphs approach the permitted size ceiling.

Seed-2 N-O-Cl and haloalkyl ethers raise local reactivity concerns. The seed-1 O-alkynyl ether and acetal-like substitutions require environment-specific assessment; terminal alkynes or ordinary thioethers should not be treated as categorically implausible.
missing_features: The output does not reliably retain compact useful ring/functional-group context while exploring alternatives: one seed elaborates a large oligomeric family with little endpoint advantage over its own nearby precursors. Other seeds already produce compact alternatives.

Conventional stable peripheral replacements and geometrically accessible ring arrangements at comparable scores are not consistently demonstrated; neither the floor nor this panel identifies an exact absent objective-specific motif.
Stereochemical identity is absent at potentially stereogenic acetal/haloalkoxy carbons.

nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

retained_mechanisms: Score-quantile parent allocation, previously accepted scored parents, bounded greedy survival and the full accepted-score archive.
Connected-fragment crossover with unchanged post-crossover mutation probability and multi-parent opportunities.
Ordinary single-atom replacement plus append, delete, insert, bond-change, ring-open and ring-close mutations, with inherited walk and saturation laws.
Sanitization, stable canonical identity admission, initial/emitted and temporary-pool duplicate rejection, bounded retries and fixed surplus pools.

approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds a fresh surplus of molecular graphs from its highest-scoring accepted survivors, using fragment crossover and local atom or bond edits. A fingerprint Gaussian process learns from all accepted observations, and correlated posterior draws select each evaluation batch. Accepted offspring compete for later breeding. Before pool admission, the Parent confirms that each canonical molecular identity is stable, normalizing verified aliases and rejecting unresolved representations. Its bond-change operator alters one existing bond order; it has no direct move that changes a ketone position while retaining the surrounding carbon skeleton.
approach.novelty: Add a ketone-position move that transfers a terminal carbonyl oxygen to an adjacent methylene carbon. Both the old and new carbonyl must have carbon neighbors, so the move retains the molecular formula, carbon skeleton and ketone class while changing the oxygen position. It becomes an alternative within the existing bond-change operator. Earlier siblings protected carbonyl atoms, exchanged aromatic nitrogen positions or moved branches around aromatic rings. This experiment instead offers a coordinated positional change within a saturated carbon framework.

nodes.hypothesis: Offer direct transfer of a ketone carbonyl oxygen to an adjacent methylene as an alternative within change_bond, preserving molecular formula, the carbon skeleton and ketone class while exposing a new carbonyl position to the inherited fresh-pool selector.

finding_summary.headline: Ketone shifts reached evaluation: four direct tests gave one gain, two ties and one loss
finding_summary.insights:
A ketone can move within these observed ring and acyclic carbon frameworks without destroying its class or changing the molecule's composition. That establishes a usable positional neighborhood, while the direct score results show that utility depends on the particular position and molecular family. Exposure is narrow: only 140 of 7,723 bond-change calls had an eligible source, and only four of 4,290 scored proposals isolate the transfer itself. The available evidence therefore supports access to this neighborhood more strongly than a reliable optimization benefit.

The largest whole-search improvement, a 0.083867 gain in one sitagliptin run, occurred with no selected ketone transfer at all. Two eligible calls instead chose the original bond-order mode, changing subsequent random consumption. This rules out interpreting that gain as an observed benefit of the shifted oxygen; selected molecules and later search history changed together. The four direct comparisons are the evidence for local positional utility. Their unchanged composition also explains why they do not establish repair of the chemical liabilities identified by the molecular assessment. Broader useful exposure, consistent improvement and completion of the full score panel remain open.
finding_summary.results:
The oxygen-position mechanism happened. All 70 executed shifts retained the molecular formula, carbon skeleton and ketone class and produced a different, stable molecular identity. Forty-eight pool entries retained the exact immediate shifted graph, covering 39 distinct identities. Four reached evaluation as sole changes to accepted scored molecules: a DRD2 transfer improved its source by 0.003265, a median_2 transfer lost 0.003475, and two ring transfers tied. A fifth evaluated history included an additional atom replacement and lost 0.002890 against its generating parent. All five entered the survivor population; none improved the incumbent.

Every generated pool and batch was full, but deco_hop in seed 2 timed out after 240 of 300 evaluations, leaving 14 of 15 task sessions complete. The two complete seed macros average 0.553584 versus their matched parent's 0.553199, a paired gain of only 0.000385, with one seed lower and one higher. This is below the registered 0.002 target on the available complete seeds; the full three-seed effect cannot be evaluated. The parent completed the entire panel. The changed whole-search chemistry still contains reactive bonds, large repeated assemblies and unspecified stereochemistry.

molecular.headline: Aromatic polycycles and crowded amines retain reactive bonds, oversized repeats and unspecified stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character: The observed output contains substantial aromatic and heterocyclic chemistry: compact bridged aryl carbonyls, linked carbonyl heteroaromatics, halogenated polyamines, larger aza rings, and fluorinated aryl dicarbonyl heterocycles. Ring-closure text rates span 0.9782–0.9966 and aromatic-presence rates span 0.9471–0.9897; these are proportions of proposal strings containing the corresponding feature, not atom fractions or perceived ring counts. Functional-group diversity and differing core families justify moderate overall structural diversity, but the highest-scoring excerpts repeatedly modify related cores. Familiar medicinal-chemistry fragments coexist with N–halogen, O–halogen and peroxide bonds, crowded aminals, unusual bridges, and very large repeated assemblies, making overall synthetic plausibility questionable and drug-likeness weak. No proposal string specifies an atom stereocentre or formal charge. Neutral strings do not imply absence of potentially basic amines. All five objectives have supplied trajectories; tasks_without_trajectories is empty. The observed deco_hop seed-2 trajectory stops at evaluation 240, so its chemistry and comparisons with a parent trajectory reaching 300 describe partial coverage. Other supplied child task/seed trajectories reach 300. All child and parent trajectory files were read. Structural counts were derived passively with RDKit from those recorded molecules and are reproducible in /projects/standard/adeshwal/shared/zhou2577/SPIRAL/runs/SPIRAL2/policy/responses/r0010-15-improve-L01-molecular.audit.json. No new molecule, score, objective requirement or mechanism-activation judgment is introduced. Score gradients below are associations within the observed search histories, not isolated causal effects or claims of experimental activity.

per_task.generated_character: Mostly compact aromatic carbonyl assemblies with densely bridged nitrogen-containing cores, small alkyl/alkoxy groups and fluorinated aromatic appendages. Proposal median size is 25 heavy atoms, the same as the parent; mean SMILES length is 45.0, ring-closure presence 0.9805 and aromatic presence 0.9793. The leading molecule has 25 heavy atoms, a bridged aza core and an N-fluoro carboxanilide. Other high excerpts retain an aroyl ketone or thioester; later products include fused N–N and N–O rings. The conventional methoxy-substituted indole carboxanilide in the initial set gives way to more demanding bridged structures. The parent leading family was also a compact bridged aryl/heteroaryl ketone, with recorded best 0.4463521672202675; the child leading N-fluoro amide reaches 0.4478476056206344. This is a change within a similar chemical region, with additional N–halogen occurrences: 243 of 870 proposals versus 187 of 870 in the parent.
liabilities: The leading amide has an N–F bond rather than an ordinary N–H or N–alkyl substituent. High numerical score does not establish its stability or suitability as a medicinal compound.

Thioesters, late N–N/N–O rings and short bridged connections need specific synthesis and stability assessment. The generated series does not specify configurations where potential atom stereocentres arise.
missing_features: The smallest low-scoring fragments omit the connected aromatic, nitrogen-containing core and carbonyl-bearing appendage shared by the stronger examples.

The stronger excerpts provide limited ordinary alternative core geometries that preserve this compact functional arrangement. Broader comparable amide/ketone structures without unusual N–F or bridged heteroatom connections remain underrepresented; an exact unseen preferred topology cannot be inferred.

The compact bridged N-fluoro amide CCc1cc2c3c(C)c1CN2C(C(=O)N(F)c1ccc(F)cc1)=CN3 scores 0.4478476056206344, the aroyl ketone CCc1cc2c3c(C)c1OCN2C(C(=O)c1ccc(F)cc1)=CN3 0.4349635367667153, and the thioester CCc1cc2c3c(C)c1OCN2C(C(=O)Sc1ccc(F)cc1)=CN3 0.4238198477630873. per_task.generated_character: The best excerpts join carbonyl-bearing O/N heteroaromatics through an NH linkage, with short annulated carbon bridges, aryl halogens, an aryl cyanate group and peroxide–halogen appendages. The best molecule has 32 heavy atoms, but the entire observed proposal stream has median 52 and maximum 119 heavy atoms. Repeated polyaromatic/dicarbonyl assemblies carry a large synthetic burden and unmeasured solubility or conformational liabilities. Their continuing evaluation at substantial scores does not establish useful medicinal properties.

High-scoring output gives few clearly tractable alternate implementations of that arrangement without unusual short annulations, cyanate or peroxide–halogen chemistry. nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from a bounded population of accepted high-scoring molecules. It selects parents by score band and either makes a local mutation walk or combines connected fragments from two parents. Crossover cuts one non-ring single bond in each source, usually retains the larger first fragment and smaller donor fragment, and joins their endpoints with a single bond; an optional finishing mutation can follow. Ordinary mutation continuation remains active, while the direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled. Stable canonical identity and novelty checks form fresh surplus pools. A Gaussian process trained on all accepted scores uses counts of local molecular environments and generalized Tanimoto similarity; correlated posterior draws choose the pool members that receive evaluations. Accepted offspring update the archive and breeding population. The crossover currently draws its donor without checking whether the two local attachment environments correspond.
approach.novelty: Construct a compatible donor fragment while keeping the already selected parent pair and first fragment. Enumerate the donor cuts, retain those whose endpoint contexts reciprocally match the two sides of the first cut, and sample them with their original relative probabilities. If there is no compatible choice, keep the original donor behavior. This targets actual attachment correspondence. The completed siblings removed retained components; earlier crossover experiments instead favored similar whole parents, retained the complete first-parent ring core, or rejected already constructed mismatches. The last approach nearly eliminated evaluated crossover, often leaving parent reproduction followed by mutation. This experiment keeps crossover opportunities and measures whether distinct compatible recombinants reach evaluation, without assuming that a matching rate or more local wins will improve final scores.

nodes.hypothesis: Condition the retained connected-fragment crossover donor-cut distribution on reciprocal endpoint-context compatibility with the unchanged first-parent cut whenever compatible support exists, preserving the inherited donor behavior otherwise.

finding_summary.headline: Compatible donor sampling activated, but parent reproduction rose and mean score fell 0.020271
finding_summary.insights:
Constructing compatible donors avoided the earlier hard gate’s near-elimination of evaluated crossover, but retaining the route count did not retain its composition. Exact local correspondence often selected a fragment that rebuilt an existing parent; subsequent mutation then supplied novelty. This separates three claims that a matching percentage conceals: correct donor allocation, exposure to genuinely new recombination, and improvement of the complete search. The first is established, the second survives in a smaller channel with a clear task boundary, and the endpoint improvement prediction is contradicted. The experiment supports a negative mean contribution from this particular refinement under the tested composition; it does not overturn the separate evidence that crossover itself is useful.

Local correspondence also fails to certify chemistry. The output remains rich in aromatic, carbonyl and amine families, with conventional alternatives alongside reactive halogen bonds, doubtful ring geometry and unspecified stereochemistry. In the fluorinated family, fewer nitrogen-halogen molecules accompany more oxygen-halogen molecules, so one reduced alert would hide a changed liability. Finishing mutations can also remove the matched attachment environment. The useful next distinction is whether donor choices preserve favorable complete molecular relationships while producing a distinct, chemically credible product. Neither excluding reproduced parents nor filtering unusual bonds has been tested here. Which change in ancestry, pool competition or later feedback caused the endpoint loss remains open; the scored cohorts do not provide labels for unchosen donors.
finding_summary.results:
The conditional donor law worked exactly on 26,727 informative crossover attempts. On those same states, the inherited chance of a reciprocal context match averaged 9.55%; the applied law made it 100%. Independent reconstruction found no key, weighting, support, sampling or product-identity discrepancy. The resulting channel was usable: 354 compatible products that differed from both parents reached evaluation, including 257 pure crossovers. They produced 70 strict best-parent beats and 32 incumbent gains; 268 later served as parents. However, 22,117 of the 26,727 conditioned immediate products reproduced a parent. Of 850 evaluated conditioned descendants, 496 became novel only through finishing mutation. No informative nonidentical product reached evaluation in any of the three median-task runs.

Total crossover evaluations rose slightly from 1,492 to 1,549, but novel crossover pool entries fell from 29,730 to 22,962. Evaluations following genuinely nonidentical immediate crossover fell from 1,368 to 1,023, and pure crossovers fell from 961 to 725. All fifteen task runs completed, with every announced batch valid and unique. The complete matched endpoint mean fell from 0.595670 to 0.575399, a change of -0.020271 against the required +0.002. Seed changes were -0.061941, +0.019643 and -0.018514; ten of fifteen task-seed endpoints declined. Seed population SD fell from 0.026593 to 0.008463. Overall local parent beats nevertheless increased from 629 to 654, and incumbent gains from 258 to 277.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic families retain unusual halogen bonds, difficult ring geometry and unspecified stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: Node n-eb61315a5619 produces compact indole-derived amides and aryl ketones, linked nitrogen-rich heterocycles, aryl-substituted aliphatic amines, diaryl macrocyclic amides and other connected nitrogen/carbonyl rings, and fluorinated fused imino/carbonyl heterocycles. This is substantial ring chemistry, with narrower leading families within individual seeds. It is neither ring-deficient nor globally scaffold-collapsed. The digest ring-closure-string incidence ranges from 0.9759 to 0.9920 and aromatic-string incidence from 0.9736 to 0.9862; these are molecule-level text incidences, not ring counts or fractions of aromatic atoms. Stereocentre-string incidence is 0.0 on every task. Formal-charge-string incidence is 0.0011 for median_2 and 0.0 elsewhere, although recognizable protonatable aliphatic amines occur. All 15 Child and 15 published Parent trajectory paths were present and read. Each objective has 900 records, including 870 optimizer observations, in each node. No objective, issued Search seed or Parent path is missing: context.comparison reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true, matched seeds 0, 1 and 2, and no profile-mismatched seeds. The comparison is against the published n-62daf219c70a seed directories, not a historical profile or a partial panel. Initial rows are excluded from the descriptor counts below. Read-only RDKit 2023.09.6 perception of the trajectory SMILES gives Child median heavy-atom counts of 25, 35, 36, 32 and 27 in the fixed objective order, versus Parent medians of 25, 33, 31, 30 and 27. Rich rings and ordinary amide, ether and amine groups coexist with N-halogen/O-halogen bonds, reactive peripheral groups, cyclic alkynes or cumulenes and difficult bridges. The aggregate judgment is questionable synthetic plausibility and weak drug-likeness, with real counterexamples of more conventional chemistry. Scores and SMILES alone do not establish stability, synthesis, conformations, protonation or biological activity. The task gradients below are descriptive associations and explicitly do not attribute a chemical feature to donor conditioning, mutation or any component. The digest final_molecules are late seed-2 proposals; the full trajectories supplied the other seed endpoints and show that the final proposal need not be the incumbent. Exact record provenance, descriptors and path hashes are in .slots/r0016-01-improve-L01/molecular/trajectory_chemistry_audit.json. Quoted SMILES come only from the Child digest or trusted Child citation paths; Parent comparisons cite published seed/evaluation records descriptively. The recurring gaps retain provenance in n-c55c3d520a2c through the published n-62daf219c70a assessment. That historical provenance is not an additional matched replica.

transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve conventional local bond chemistry while retaining favorable complete molecular arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator needs transformations that distinguish bond environment and intact functional-group context, while offering conventional alternatives to reactive attachments without erasing useful aromatic, carbonyl or amine arrangements. Assess the full set of emitted environments so that one liability is not merely replaced by another. These output associations do not attribute the chemistry to a component or establish that a blanket filter improves scores.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Original source n-c55c3d520a2c via the published n-62daf219c70a assessment; independently present in n-eb61315a5619 on the complete current-profile Search panel at 300 observations per objective. transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring transformations need ring-size, bond-geometry and bridge-connectivity awareness, with feasible alternate topologies that preserve functional relationships supported by current feedback. A successful molecular graph check or aromatic label is insufficient. Do not infer a universal prohibition of small rings, fused rings or macrocycles; the observed counterexamples and absence of geometry measurements limit this to a feasibility gap, with no demonstrated component-specific or causal score benefit.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Originally reported for n-c55c3d520a2c and carried by n-62daf219c70a, this persists in n-eb61315a5619 on Search seeds 0, 1 and 2 under the current profile and 300 observations per objective. transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Representations and transformations should preserve or resolve stereochemical identity where chemically meaningful, while treating achiral and configurationally unstable cases appropriately. Charge state and tautomerism require separate handling: neutral notation does not mean a basic centre is absent. The trajectories establish an identity gap, not a measured stereochemical score penalty or evidence that any particular retained component caused it.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Original source n-c55c3d520a2c through the published n-62daf219c70a assessment; re-observed in n-eb61315a5619 on the matched current-profile Search panel at 300 observations per objective. Child still emits 47 molecules with at most three heavy atoms among 4350 optimizer observations, although Parent emitted 99. transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Use accepted task-local feedback to preserve useful combinations of chemical regions when shrinking, expanding or reconnecting a molecule. Allow meaningful simplification and growth; neither a fixed minimum size nor a preference for larger structures follows from these examples. The evidence describes residual context control under this Parent and profile, not attribution to crossover or a proven gain from a size rule.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Originally recorded for n-c55c3d520a2c and reproduced by n-62daf219c70a, this remains conditional evidence in n-eb61315a5619 under the supplied current profile, Search seeds 0, 1 and 2, and 300 observations per objective. Leading series repeatedly change short substituents, halogen attachment, ring size or carbonyl/imino identity while retaining the same aromatic/carbonyl organization. Different seeds nevertheless reach distinct fused, flexible-amine and macrocyclic families, and the Child supplies genuinely different ring connectivities. Thus the observation is narrow useful alternatives within local families, not global collapse or inability to generate rings.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator has limited consistent access to chemically independent plausible alternatives within a successful local scaffold family.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide alternative scaffold connectivities that preserve favorable functional relationships learned from the current observations, and examine their chemical credibility as well as their labels. Distinct SMILES and higher ring counts do not alone demonstrate useful coverage. This is a conditional generator capability gap; no objective identity, preselected target scaffold, specific component attribution or guaranteed benefit from more diversity is supported.

nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

retained_mechanisms: Score-quantile allocation of previously accepted parents, bounded greedy survival and the full accepted-score archive.

Connected-fragment two-parent crossover, with reciprocal-context conditional donor construction as the tested implementation variant; inherited first-fragment law, no-support donor fallback and optional finishing mutation remain.

All seven ordinary mutation families and the inherited multi-step continuation/saturation law; direct aromatic C/N exchange remains disabled, with its unreachable implementation and passive enumeration retained.
Sanitization, stable canonical identity admission, initial/emitted and temporary-pool duplicate rejection, bounded retries and fixed fresh surplus pools.
Integer-count Morgan features, generalized Tanimoto GP on every accepted observation, unchanged normalization/noise/jitter and full posterior covariance.
Correlated posterior draws, actual masked pool selection, pending identity joins and next-fit accepted-feedback probes.
Passive source-index, donor probability, immediate identity, mutation and accepted-descendant provenance; diagnostic copies do not enter candidate identities.
Fresh objective-local state, deterministic prepared configuration, announced ten-member batches and protocol-owned budgets/resources.

approach.method_basis: The reference is Zhu and colleagues' 2022 paper, An Inverse QSAR Method Based on Linear Regression and Integer Programming. The method learns a linear relationship between molecular descriptors and a measured property, then places that predictor and the descriptor equations inside an integer program describing a chemical graph. Atom identities, bonds and structural restrictions are represented by discrete variables and constraints. Solving the combined program constructs a graph whose descriptors satisfy the predictor's requested property range and the structural specifications. Because the descriptors and graph share one constrained assignment, the representation used to predict the property is tied directly to the molecule being constructed.
approach.novelty: This root adapts the published construction framework to online score maximization with limited accepted observations. It refits a regularized linear predictor of whole-molecule atom, degree and typed-bond counts after each accepted batch, then maximizes that prediction while replacing a small, singly attached acyclic peripheral region of a scored molecule. The surrounding context stays fixed; the program chooses replacement size, atom identities, bond orders and a chemically eligible attachment site together. Source selection favors higher observed scores while retaining alternatives. Bounded solves may use feasible incumbents, with repeated assignments excluded and additional construction attempts used to obtain novel molecules. Independent checks require the submitted graph's count descriptors to match the integer model exactly. These choices make exact prediction realization testable within the resource budget, while leaving the usefulness of the linear predictor and construction throughput as separate empirical questions.

nodes.hypothesis: Fit a task-local regularized linear score model on exact molecular count descriptors, then construct new bounded peripheral regions of scored molecules by maximizing that predictor in a mixed-integer graph program whose atom, bond, attachment, valence, connectivity and descriptor constraints jointly define the submitted molecular graph.

finding_summary.headline: Exact integer realization held for all 1,450 proposals; only 41% of predicted local gains became observed gains
finding_summary.insights: The construction and adaptive feedback mechanisms happened. This result establishes that exact count realization and sufficient integer-construction throughput are attainable in this bounded peripheral-edit domain; the remaining predictive errors cannot be attributed to a mismatch between optimized descriptors and submitted graphs. The representational limit is visible in the accepted data: different molecules with identical full descriptor vectors received different scores on every task. In the docking trajectory, the two fluorine-position variants highlighted by the chemistry assessment share all 384 counts but score 0.124071 and 0.189601. No refit of this descriptor-only linear predictor can distinguish that pair. The chemistry assessment also finds familiar inherited rings carrying many reactive or unconventional appendages, alongside simpler high-scoring alternatives. Together, these observations make richer chemical-environment representation and constraints on functional-group compatibility worth testing while keeping exact realization as a control. They do not establish that either change will improve scores. Current evidence covers neutral, unspecified-stereochemistry peripheral trees and retained ring frameworks; new ring construction, broader chemistry and reliable advantage across replicas remain open.
finding_summary.results: All five tasks completed on the screening seed. The optimizer supplied 145 full batches and 1,450 novel accepted molecules from feasible integer assignments, with zero discrepancies across their 384 count descriptors. All 150 ridge fits reconstructed from accepted task-local scores, and the 140 feedback refits with later opportunities changed subsequent construction objectives. Accepted constructions were selected again as sources 525 times. Of 1,450 proposals, 1,400 had positive predicted gains over their source; 578 of those predictions became actual gains. Overall, 598 proposals beat their source and 36 improved the running best, although mean child-minus-source score was negative on three of the five tasks. The final five-task Top-1 mean was 0.286518. Initial to final Top-1 changed from 0.305105 to 0.395373 for zaleplon_mpo, 0.548381 to 0.583606 for deco_hop, 0.019041 to 0.189601 for drd2_docking, 0.167839 to 0.175888 for median_2, and 0.002094 to 0.088123 for sitagliptin_mpo. This root has no Parent, and one screening seed does not establish comparative advantage.

Initial to final Top-1 changed from 0.305105 to 0.395373 for zaleplon_mpo, 0.548381 to 0.583606 for deco_hop, 0.019041 to 0.189601 for drd2_docking, 0.167839 to 0.175888 for median_2, and 0.002094 to 0.088123 for sitagliptin_mpo. This root has no Parent, and one screening seed does not establish comparative advantage.

The construction and adaptive feedback mechanisms happened. This result establishes that exact count realization and sufficient integer-construction throughput are attainable in this bounded peripheral-edit domain; the remaining predictive errors cannot be attributed to a mismatch between optimized descriptors and submitted graphs. The representational limit is visible in the accepted data: different molecules with identical full descriptor vectors received different scores on every task. In the docking trajectory, the two fluorine-position variants highlighted by the chemistry assessment share all 384 counts but score 0.124071 and 0.189601. No refit of this descriptor-only linear predictor can distinguish that pair. The chemistry assessment also finds familiar inherited rings carrying many reactive or unconventional appendages, alongside simpler high-scoring alternatives. Together, these observations make richer chemical-environment representation and constraints on functional-group compatibility worth testing while keeping exact realization as a control. They do not establish that either change will improve scores. Current evidence covers neutral, unspecified-stereochemistry peripheral trees and retained ring frameworks; new ring construction, broader chemistry and reliable advantage across replicas remain open.
