molecular.headline: Ring-rich inherited scaffolds acquire unusual reactive appendages; conventional amides and amines coexist with azo, N-F and thiocarbonyl chemistry.
molecular.overall_character: All supplied trajectories were read, covering every task in the brief. Each contains 300 molecules, including 290 optimizer proposals, on seed 0. There is no Parent or Parent trajectory, so the comparison is with the supplied initial molecules and the observed within-task score gradient. Scores quoted below are rounded recorded values, not new evaluations. The output contains substantial ring chemistry: ring_closure_rate is 1.0 throughout. The recurrent frameworks are indoles, diaryl fused dione heterocycles, quinoline/phenoxy/piperidine assemblies, biphenyl/arylsulfonyl/pyrrolidine assemblies, and oxygen-rich polyacetals. These are recognizable in the initial molecules; much of the subsequent variety changes their substituents while retaining their ring frameworks. Aromatic_atom_rate, which measures the fraction of proposal strings containing aromatic atoms rather than the fraction of atoms that are aromatic, is 0.9586, 0.9897, 0.9966, 1.0 and 0.331 in the fixed task order. The last trajectory develops a predominantly nonaromatic polyacetal series. Thus structural diversity is moderate across the supplied outputs, but the chemically favored series within a task are narrower than the 300 unique identities suggest. Synthetic plausibility is mixed. Familiar amides, ethers, esters, alkylated amines and heterocycles remain available, while many proposals combine N-F, repeated N-O or N-N linkages, sulfur-halogen bonds, unstabilized thiocarbonyls or cumulated double bonds. The recognizable cores do not make these appendages ordinary medicinal chemistry. Every proposal set has charged_rate and stereocentre_rate of 0.0: explicit ions and assigned tetrahedral stereochemistry are absent from the submitted strings, although ionizable atoms and potential stereocentres are present. No synthesis, stability, affinity or protonation-state measurement was supplied.

per_task.generated_character: The better molecules are medium-sized, aromatic indole derivatives carrying a fluorophenyl group through a carboxamide or an aminomethyl linker. Methoxy/other ether substituents and the indole NH are recurrent. Evaluation 153 is a comparatively conventional dimethoxyindole carboxamide with an N-methyl-N-fluorophenyl amide; its amide nitrogen is not an ordinary basic amine. Other upper-score examples add N-fluoroaminomethyl ethers, N-ethynyl groups or vinylamine motifs. Lower-score families include elaborate saturated polyacetals and bulkier diaryl fused diones. The optimizer strings have mean length 48.6, aromatic_atom_rate 0.9586 and halogen_rate 0.9483. The best conventional amide looks synthetically plausible in outline; many surrounding analogues are substantially less convincing.
liabilities: N-F-bearing amines, sulfur-fluoride/chloride appendages and heteroatom-substituted alkynes raise stability and route-planning concerns. The aryl C-F bond in the best molecule should not be conflated with these heteroatom-halogen bonds.
Cumulated_double_bond_rate is 0.1345. Several high-score analogues retain unsaturated or N-F-bearing appendages even though the observed maximum needs neither.
missing_features: The later output does not consistently retain the favorable combination of a small N-alkyl carboxamide and uncomplicated aryl ethers: final analogues frequently replace it with N-F, ethynyl-ether or sulfur-halogen chemistry. The clean combination exists at the maximum, so this is a coverage gap rather than complete inability to make it.

Alternative ring-nitrogen placements and reorganized ring frameworks are not represented among the cited high-score molecules. Their benefit cannot be established from this trajectory, which does not identify a unique missing target pharmacophore.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxyindole secondary amide at evaluation 9 scores 0.305105, whereas the dimethoxy N-methyl amide at 153 scores 0.395373. This supports a local preference for that combined substitution change, without separating the effects of losing a methoxy group, its position and amide methylation. The N-F-containing analogue at 160 is nearly equal at 0.394920, so the score tolerates unusual chemistry rather than demonstrating its necessity. The oxygen-rich polycycle at 13 scores 0.0000369102 and the larger fused-dione compound at 95 scores 0.0000487084. Final ethynyl-ether/sulfur-fluoride indoles at 299 and 300 both score 0.0153241. The observed favorable feature is the particular compact indole/aryl/linker combination, not aromaticity or halogenation alone.

per_task.generated_character: The output is dominated by fairly large diaryl fused dione heterocycles with N-methylated ring nitrogens. Their aromatic substituents acquire primary or alkylated amino groups, methylthio groups, fluorinated aminoalkyl branches and azo/diazene substituents. The maximum at 284 combines a fused dione core with densely substituted phenyl rings, dimethylamino functionality, an alpha-fluoroamine branch and repeated azo functionality. A distinct high-score example at 169 instead has amino/methylamino groups, a phenol and an aldehyde, without azo or fluorinated appendages. Indole carboxamides also recur late. Mean SMILES length is 65.4, aromatic_atom_rate is 0.9897 and halogen_rate is 0.6621. Familiar cores are present, but the densely decorated azo/aminal-rich periphery often makes the complete molecules questionable synthetic targets.
liabilities: Aryl/alkyl azo groups and terminal diazenes introduce unassigned geometric isomerism and potential redox or decomposition liabilities; repeated N-N units and highly substituted aminal/hemiaminal-like branches are especially unconventional.
Aldehydes, amino-substituted aromatics and methylthio groups still need chemical scrutiny in the simpler series; a high scalar score is not evidence of stability or an executable synthesis.
Fluorinated aminoalkyl branches can introduce stereocentres, but no tetrahedral configuration is specified in these proposal strings.
missing_features: Relatively simple amino/phenol/carbonyl combinations are underrepresented among the heavily decorated upper-score examples, despite evaluation 169 demonstrating a competitive conventional alternative. What is missing is sustained exploration of that chemistry without repeatedly coupling it to azo chains or mixed heteroatom-rich branches.

The cited upper-score set supplies little evidence of alternative cyclic linkers or new ring heteroatom arrangements. Their contribution to this objective remains untested rather than known to be beneficial.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial diaryl dione at 7 scores 0.548381; its extensively decorated relatives at 284 and 286 score 0.583606 and 0.582950. Amino, thioether and azo substitutions on those aromatic surfaces accompany the higher values. However, the amino/phenol/aldehyde analogue at 169 scores 0.575221 without azo groups, showing that they are not required for the upper observed range. The saturated polyacetal at 47 scores 0.506214, while the quinoline/piperidine analogue with an N-O-rich chain at 24 scores 0.530764. The late indole amide at 297 reaches 0.574024 with a methylthio/azo/amino decoration. These comparisons support locally useful aromatic polar substitution on more than one core; they do not establish that indiscriminately adding heteroatoms improves the objective.

per_task.generated_character: Most proposals are large, heavily decorated biphenyl compounds joined to an arylsulfonyl pyrrolidine through amide, amine, enamine or aminothiol-containing linkers. The recurring pyrrolidine nitrogen is sulfonylated; it should not be described as an unmasked basic cyclic amine. Extra aniline or aliphatic amino groups appear on the periphery. The best molecule at 273 has a dimethylamino-substituted dichlorophenyl sulfonamide, a difluorobiphenyl group and a chlorinated enamine linker. Evaluation 218 instead supplies an accessible dimethylaminomethyl branch. Mean SMILES length is 84.2, the longest mean in the digest; aromatic_atom_rate is 0.9966 and halogen_rate is 0.9862. The underlying sulfonamide/aryl chemistry is recognizable, but many proposed complete structures are encumbered by polyhalogenated appendages and reactive linkers.
liabilities: Chlorinated enamines, sulfenamide/aminothiol motifs and extensively brominated or chlorinated branches complicate stability and synthesis. Fluoroalkyl cumulenes occur late; cumulated_double_bond_rate is 0.1414.

Large aromatic surfaces and heavy halogen decoration coexist with several flexible bonds and unspecified stereochemistry. These are liabilities for a tractable series even when the recorded scalar increases.
Neutral input notation must not be mistaken for proof that the molecules are nonionizable, and a docking-task scalar must not be equated with measured receptor affinity.
missing_features: The dominant series does not provide a conventional, independently varied basic cyclic nitrogen: its ring nitrogen remains sulfonylated while additional amines are appended elsewhere. The useful peripheral amine examples motivate a gap in independent control of nitrogen placement and electronic state, not a claim that any cyclic amine would help.

Defined stereoisomers of the substituted pyrrolidine and benzylic/linker centres are absent. Explicitly charged representations are also absent from the submitted strings; whether the evaluation prepared protonated forms internally is not shown.

Chemically ordinary alternatives to the chlorinated enamine and aminothiol linkers, retaining comparable attachment geometry, are missing from the cited upper-score series. Their score effect would require observation.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial arylsulfonyl/pyrrolidine amide bearing a carboxylic acid at 10 scores 0.0190412. The amine/enamine-bearing analogues at 218 and 273 reach 0.187076 and 0.189601, respectively. Several changes occur together, so the trajectory does not isolate an amine, acid-removal or linker effect. A particularly informative pair is 272 versus 273: relocating fluorines on the distal phenyl ring changes 0.124071 to 0.189601 without changing the main framework or elemental composition. This makes substituent placement an observed distinction beyond simply adding nitrogen or halogens. The quinoline/phenoxy/piperidine compound at 275 scores only 0.00334580 despite a tertiary cyclic amine. Final polyhalogenated/cumulene-containing analogues such as 300 score 0.0677295. The evidence favors particular spatially organized combinations; it supplies no binding pose or interaction assignment.

per_task.generated_character: This trajectory contains the most conventional upper-score chemistry in the supplied set. Better molecules include alkyl-substituted quinolines connected through a methylene ether and phenyl amide to N-alkyl piperidines, alongside diaryl fused diones bearing esters, ethers and alkyl substituents. Evaluation 237 combines a propyl/methyl quinoline, an aryl ether, an amide, an N-methyl piperidine and an aldehyde. Evaluation 102 is an ethyl-substituted diaryl fused dione with an ethyl ester. Elsewhere the trajectory still proposes N-O and N-S chains and branched alkyl growth. These are medium-to-large molecules with mean SMILES length 65.9; aromatic_atom_rate is 1.0, halogen_rate 0.5586 and cumulated_double_bond_rate 0.0. The main high-score motifs are plausible medicinal-chemistry starting points in outline, with route and stereochemical details unresolved.
liabilities: The highest quinoline example retains an aldehyde, introducing an electrophilic and potentially metabolically sensitive group; its score does not establish acceptable stability.
Long alkyl branches enlarge flexible hydrophobic regions. Early N-O/N-S-rich variants are chemically less ordinary than the upper-score ester/amide series.
Substituted saturated rings and branched chains contain potential stereochemical distinctions that are unspecified in every optimizer string.
missing_features: Many later molecules do not preserve the modest alkyl substitution and simple polar-group balance seen in the better examples; long or branched alkyl additions and further N-alkylation often accompany lower scores. The gap is reliable exploration around chemically economical combinations already demonstrated by the output.

Alternative ring arrangements and defined piperidine/substituent stereochemistry are not represented in the cited upper-score set. The observed modest score differences do not identify a specific absent target motif.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial diaryl dione at 7 scores 0.167839. Loss of its phenolic OH together with ethyl substitution on an aromatic ring gives 0.175839 at 102 and 0.174613 at 103. The quinoline/piperidine initial molecule at 6 scores 0.156977; the propyl-substituted aldehyde analogue at 237 scores 0.175888. Conventional alkyl/ether/carbonyl patterns therefore characterize the upper observed values. Alkyl extension is not monotonically favorable: the otherwise closely related pentyl quinoline at 282 scores 0.166260, below the propyl compound at 237. N-O-rich derivatives at 18-20 score 0.110506, and the modified flavone at 14 scores 0.112923. The useful distinction is a particular balance and placement of hydrocarbon substituents and conventional polar groups, not unlimited growth or heteroatom-chain elaboration.

per_task.generated_character: The best molecules are nonaromatic oxygen-rich polyacetals resembling heavily protected carbohydrate frameworks, decorated with terminal thioaldehydes, other thiocarbonyl groups, aldehydes and chlorinated carbon branches. Evaluation 243 retains the elaborate polyacetal framework while adding repeated terminal thiocarbonyls, an aldehyde and a trichloromethyl substituent. Its near-equal-score relative at 242 redistributes the appendages around the same kind of framework. Other proposals explore hydrazones, N-O chains, sulfur/nitrogen chains and thioketene or longer cumulene appendages; aromatic starting families persist at lower values. Mean SMILES length is 57.6, aromatic_atom_rate is 0.331, halogen_rate 0.5345 and cumulated_double_bond_rate 0.1931. The polyacetal skeleton is recognizable chemistry, but the multiply reactive sulfur-rich products look poor as isolable medicinal compounds without substantial stabilization and synthesis evidence.
liabilities: Repeated terminal thioaldehydes, thioketenes and adjacent thiocarbonyl motifs present substantial chemical-reactivity and isolation concerns. These differ materially from ordinary stable thioamides or sulfones.
The crowded polyacetal framework and multiple oxygen-bearing stereocentres would demand controlled synthesis; no stereochemical assignments or synthetic route are supplied.
Hydrazone/N-O-rich side chains and long cumulated unsaturation recur even among very low-scoring analogues. Rich ring content here does not imply conventional drug-like chemistry.
missing_features: The upper-score series lacks chemically stable alternatives that preserve its favorable balance of ring oxygen, sulfur-containing substituents and chlorinated branches without exposed terminal thioaldehydes or cumulated bonds. Whether a stable replacement preserves the score is unknown.

Conventional basic amines and aromatic nitrogen acceptors are absent from the highest polyacetals, while the earlier aromatic/amine-containing molecules are generally poorer. Their absence can be described, but this trajectory does not support prescribing their addition as this objective's answer.
The stereochemical configurations needed to specify these highly substituted polyacetals are absent from the proposal strings. There is no evidence here of a stereochemically resolved series.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial polyacetal at 4 scores 0.0000254690; the extensively sulfur/chlorine-decorated polyacetals at 242 and 243 each score approximately 0.0881235. In contrast, the same broad polyacetal family with hydrazone and O-N appendages at 56 scores 1.23960e-32, and the nitrogen/sulfur-decorated biphenyl amide at 130 scores 1.06523e-33. This supports a narrow favorable combination on the oxygen-rich scaffold, not a general reward for sulfur, heteroatoms or chlorination. The final trichloromethyl/thioketene-containing polyacetal at 296 falls to 1.03025e-09 despite retaining many ostensibly favorable ingredients; the final thiocarbonyl/aldehyde variant at 300 scores 0.00937443. The nearly equal scores for 242 and 243 show tolerance of those particular positional alternatives. No reference molecule or component scores were shown, so the large gradient cannot be assigned to a specific desired pharmacophore or physicochemical term.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Its output repeatedly combines N-F bonds, N-O/N-N chains, sulfur-halogen groups, terminal thioaldehydes and cumulated bonds with otherwise familiar ring frameworks. Cumulated-double-bond rates reach 0.1345, 0.1414 and 0.1931 in the affected proposal sets. A conventional dimethoxy N-methyl indole amide has recorded score 0.395373, while a closely related N-F-bearing analogue scores 0.394920; unusual appendages are therefore not required to reach that observed neighborhood. Conventional amino/phenol/carbonyl and ester/amide examples also coexist with reactive variants.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably keep new substituents within chemically stable functional-group environments.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Add task-independent sensitivity to local bond environments and functional-group compatibility so ordinary amines, ethers, amides and appropriately stabilized sulfur groups remain available without automatically turning into heteroatom chains or reactive endpoints. Preserve structurally comparable stable alternatives and let accepted scalar feedback determine their usefulness.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Ring_closure_rate is 1.0 for every proposal set, but the repeated indole, fused dione, quinoline/piperidine, arylsulfonyl/pyrrolidine and polyacetal frameworks are recognizable in the supplied initial molecules. The cited maxima remain variations on those frameworks. Across the trajectories, much of the visible novelty lies in pendant chains, exocyclic functionality and substitution positions rather than new cyclic connectivity.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring abundance does not translate into demonstrated exploration of substantially different ring frameworks.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A generator seeking broader chemical coverage would need a way to vary cyclic connectivity, ring heteroatom placement and the connections between ring units, while retaining chemically plausible scaffolds as alternatives. This is a chemical capability gap, not evidence that any particular unseen ring system will improve the score.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The dominant sulfonylated pyrrolidine series keeps a deactivated ring nitrogen while introducing separate aniline or aliphatic amine centres. Upper-score analogues mix those changes with chlorinated enamine or aminothiol linkers. Relocating distal phenyl fluorines on an otherwise matching framework changes the recorded score from 0.124071 to 0.189601. Conversely, a tertiary cyclic amine on another scaffold has a low recorded score, so nitrogen presence alone does not explain the observed chemistry.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output offers limited independent control of functional-group position, basicity and linkage geometry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support matched changes in attachment position, nitrogen bonding environment and linker type so the search can vary accessible basic centres and molecular geometry independently of adding reactive appendages. Distinguish amines, anilines, amides and sulfonamides as different chemical environments using only the observed scalar feedback.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Stereocentre_rate and charged_rate are both 0.0 in every proposal set. Nevertheless, the submitted molecules include substituted piperidines and pyrrolidines, benzylic amino centres, fluorinated aminoalkyl branches and complex polyacetals. Several structures contain ionizable amines or acids. These counters establish absent input annotations, not absent molecular stereochemistry or neutral behavior in solution; evaluation-side preparation was not supplied.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not express stereochemically resolved or explicitly charged candidate alternatives in these outputs.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Where the candidate contract supports them, provide chemically justified stereoisomer and ionization-state alternatives and track their identities explicitly. Base the choices on generic chemical rules and accepted observations, without assuming that added stereochemical or charge annotation is itself rewarded.

nodes.method_name: Inverse-QSAR: mixed-integer de novo molecular construction
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the method in inverse-QSAR through coupled linear regression and mixed-integer graph construction. [Zhu et al., Sections 1, 3 and 4](https://www.imrpress.com/journal/FBL/27/6/10.31083/j.fbl2706188) encode both a molecular descriptor function and a learned predictor in a program that constructs a graph satisfying structural specifications. Our benchmark adaptation fits a regularized linear score model only to the current objective's accepted observations, using atom-type, degree and typed-bond counts that can be represented exactly by integer constraints. For each proposal, take a scored molecule, choose a bounded editable peripheral region and retain its connected surrounding context. Represent replacement atom identities, bond orders and attachment choices as discrete variables, with connectivity, valence and descriptor-consistency constraints. Maximize the fitted scalar prediction over these variables instead of solving the paper's fixed target-interval problem. A feasible integer assignment supplies the new molecular graph directly. Validate the actual graph and recompute its descriptors before submission; exclude repeated assignments and retry construction when canonical identity is duplicate or invalid. Vary contexts and editable regions as feedback accumulates, and continue construction until the announced batch is filled. Use bounded subproblems and feasible solver incumbents rather than requiring a proof of global optimality for every proposal. The root needs no generative checkpoint or external labels. It constructs atom and bond combinations, without a corpus molecule pool, stored-fragment retrieval or the paper's subsequent isomer-enumeration stage. Each objective starts with clean scored and fitted state. The hypothesis is that jointly enforcing realizable structure while optimizing a task-local prediction concentrates evaluations on improving molecules and raises the mean of independent final Top-1 scores. Exact descriptor realization cannot compensate for an inaccurate predictor; both predictive usefulness and sufficient construction throughput remain unproven.

retained_mechanisms: Task-local accepted-only centered/scaled ridge with an unpenalized intercept and raw-count prediction coefficients
Exact whole-molecule atom, heavy-degree and typed-bond count equations including retained context and attachment-degree changes
Positive observed-score rank preference over eligible accepted source contexts with alternative sources retained
Bounded mixed-integer construction of neutral singly attached peripheral trees with variable atom identities, sizes, bonds and attachment sites
Feasible incumbent decoding with independent sanitization, connectedness, valence, immutable-context, descriptor and prediction checks
Active-prefix/earlier-parent tree conventions, assignment no-good exclusions and canonical novelty rejection to fill exact announced batches

approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from a bounded, score-ranked population of accepted molecules. It draws a first parent from weighted score bands and either mutates that molecule or crosses it with a separately drawn, distinct partner. Crossover usually keeps the larger fragment of the first parent and the smaller fragment of the partner, with an optional finishing mutation. Ordinary mutation can continue for several steps; direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled. Stable canonical identity and duplicate checks form a fresh proposal pool. A Gaussian process fitted to all accepted scores uses counts of local molecular environments and correlated posterior draws to select evaluations. Accepted offspring update both the predictive archive and the score-greedy breeding population.
approach.novelty: Remove rank preference only when choosing the crossover partner. Keep precisely the partners the original law could select, but choose uniformly among them; every first-parent request keeps its original weighted rule. Earlier siblings removed weights in both roles, expanded eligibility to all live survivors, balanced first-parent schedules, or favored chemically similar partners. None isolated this partner-only weight contribution on the current Parent. The hypothesis is that flattening partner probabilities weakens the scored graft-source distribution and may lower final best scores despite broader partner use. This is a conditional contribution control, with the first-parent law and graph construction preserved.

finding_summary.headline: Crossover-partner rank weights contribute: their removal lowers mean final Top-1 by 0.051808
finding_summary.insights:
The score-ranked crossover partner has positive conditional value even when the first-parent rule and eligible partner set are preserved. Earlier removal in both roles could not localize that value; this control answers the partner question. It leaves first-parent contribution, support-only value and the value of the complete graph-evolution system open. Shared-baseline results cannot be added or subtracted into those answers.

More local success did not mean better search. Strict best-parent wins rose from 629 to 702, accepted offspring later reused rose from 2,401 to 2,619, and incumbent advances rose from 258 to 265. But the generating reference weakened: mean best-parent score fell from 0.470456 to 0.386162, mean offspring score fell from 0.385256 to 0.325006, and the average positive incumbent increment fell from 0.022510 to 0.018983. These results rule out treating local win counts, reuse or lower dispersion as sufficient evidence of productive exploration.

The molecular assessment describes substantial aromatic, amine and carbonyl chemistry, including a comparatively conventional nitrile ketone in the improved zaleplon run. The largest losses include failure to recover the Parent’s compact high-scoring decoration-hopping arrangement, while much larger decorated structures, reactive nitrogen/oxygen–halogen bonds, difficult ring geometry and unspecified stereochemistry persist. Those associations suggest a gap in useful feasible alternatives, but neither the cleaner counterexample nor the liabilities identify the chemical cause of the loss. Partner identities, subsequent graph randomness and adaptive feedback remain inseparable parts of this measured total effect.

Greedy survival, complete accepted-score learning and all 435 full candidate-pool selections remained active.

Eleven of fifteen task/seed endpoints declined; zaleplon seed 0, median similarity seeds 1 and 2, and sitagliptin seed 1 improved. Task means rose for zaleplon and median similarity but fell for decoration hopping, docking and sitagliptin. Seed-average population deviation fell from 0.026593 to 0.008407. Every task completed its full oracle budget.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic output mixes a plausible nitrile ketone and aryl amines with reactive halogen bonds and difficult polycycles
molecular.overall_character: This assessment names n-ee95752352ec and compares its actual output with code Parent n-62daf219c70a. All 15 Child Search trajectories and all 15 published Parent trajectories were present and read in full. Each task has 900 records, including 870 optimizer proposals, across seeds 0, 1 and 2; no task lacks trajectories. The request reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true, with matched seeds 0, 1 and 2 and no profile mismatches. The current comparison is therefore complete under the supplied epoch-1 profile, batch size 10 and 300 observations per task/seed. The historical gap source n-c55c3d520a2c and its carried-forward n-62daf219c70a report were read through context.evidence_index; that earlier same-code baseline reproduction had profile-mismatched pairing and is retained only as gap provenance, not another matched replicate. The output comprises nitrile-substituted fused heteroaromatic ketones and amides, extended nitrogen-rich diones, aryl/aliphatic amines, bridged nitrogen-carbonyl systems, and fluorinated diones with unusual nitrogen substitution. Child ring-closure-string incidence is 0.9644 to 0.9862 and aromatic-string incidence is 0.9586 to 0.9816. Those are molecule-level text-feature rates, not fractions of aromatic atoms or independent scaffolds. Formal-charge and stereocentre-string incidence are 0.0 on every task; protonatable amines and potentially stereogenic centres nevertheless occur. All optimizer records in both panels parsed with the locally available RDKit. Heavy-atom counts, ring sizes and bond counts below were derived from those supplied strings; graph perception does not establish realizable geometry, a synthesis, configurational stability or activity. The inventory and file hashes are recorded in .slots/round-0023-slot-3/molecular/trajectory_inventory.json. There is substantial chemistry across tasks and seeds, but leading examples within a seed repeatedly retain the same families. The cleaner ketone leader and recognizable cyclic amines are counterexamples to universal chemical implausibility; O-halogen and N-halogen bonds, difficult small-ring fusions, large decorated frameworks and unspecified stereochemistry justify the weaker overall quality judgement. Digest final_molecules are late seed-2 proposals, not each seed's best retained molecule. Parent structures are described by their authoritative seed/evaluation positions; cited_smiles contains only Child molecules admitted by the trusted request. These are conditional chemistry associations, with no attribution to a search component, mechanism-activation decision or eligibility judgement.

per_task.generated_character: Optimizer proposals have median 25 heavy atoms and median 3 perceived rings; mean SMILES length is 42.5. The seed-0 leader at evaluation 129 has 24 heavy atoms: a methoxy/methyl/nitrile-substituted benzimidazole with a ketone linking it to a methylphenylmethyl group. Its ordinary N-H, nitrile, ether and ketone bonding makes it a more recognizable synthetic target than many nearby alternatives. Seed 1 evaluation 119 instead has 23 heavy atoms and a carbonyl-linked aza-aromatic unit attached to a partly unsaturated NH ring system; perceived cycles include a seven-membered ring. Seed 2 evaluation 203 has 26 heavy atoms, a methyl thioether, an N-N-containing fused four-membered thione ring and an aryl urea-like carbonyl linkage. Thus neither the pooled leading family nor its comparatively conventional bonding represents all seeds. The Parent leaders at evaluations 289, 293 and 294 retain indole-like aromatic frameworks but carry N-Cl or N-F substitution, with cumulene, N-hydroxy amide or vicinal-diketone functionality. Child N-halogen incidence is 81 of 870 optimizer molecules, versus 445 of 870 for the Parent; this is a local bond-inventory change, not proof of generally improved chemistry.
liabilities: Near-leading amides contain N-Cl or N-F, and other high variants combine nitrogen-sulfur attachments with aromatic carbonyl frameworks. These bonds differ chemically from ordinary aryl C-halogen substitution.
The seed-2 four-membered N-N/thione fusion and seed-1 unusual ring junctions require geometry and synthesis scrutiny; parsing and score do not establish their accessibility.
Much larger aromatic dimers and very small fragments remain in the scored output despite poor scores.
missing_features: Consistently plausible alternatives to the fused N-N/thione and unusual aza-ring families are not demonstrated at the cleaner seed-0 leader's score. Conventional N-H heteroaromatic chemistry is already attainable, so it is not a missing capability in absolute terms.

Leading alternatives usually preserve a seed-specific fused aromatic/carbonyl organization. The record does not demonstrate broad coverage of independent, feasible connectivities that retain that favorable arrangement.
Potential saturated-ring stereochemistry in the seed-1 family remains unspecified; the achiral-looking seed-0 leader is an explicit exception to a universal stereochemical deficiency.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxyindole anilide scores 0.3051048083696145, while the seed-0 nitrile/benzyl-ketone leader reaches 0.5188745216627708. A larger coupled aromatic-amide proposal at seed 0 evaluation 24 scores only 3.5758235031768006e-16, and ethene at seed 1 evaluation 196 scores 0.0. The visible reward therefore concerns a compact combined aromatic/polar arrangement, not aromatic content or size alone. A neighboring N-chloro amide at seed 0 evaluation 195 scores 0.5108921546316982, so high scores tolerate a reactive nitrogen environment but the best Child example does not require it. The late seed-2 thione/azaaryl-urea variant at evaluation 300 scores 0.37081201154324345, below that seed's best. Child best observed scores on seeds 0, 1 and 2 are 0.5188745216627708, 0.4239904333396317, 0.4254027310763201; the published Parent values in the same order are 0.39405142067435733, 0.47411701813450596, 0.438972502037081. The opposite seed-level directions and different skeletons do not identify a unique missing pharmacophore or a causal chemical mediator.

per_task.generated_character: This is the largest typical Child output: median 41 heavy atoms versus the Parent's 33, with mean SMILES length 78.2 and maximum length 206. Child leaders on seeds 0, 1 and 2 have 57, 48 and 50 heavy atoms, whereas the corresponding Parent leaders have 30, 32 and 37. The seed-0 leader at evaluation 215 is a heavily decorated nitrogen-rich aromatic dione with polyene chains, ethers and fluorinated ester-bearing substituents. nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from accepted high-scoring molecules. It samples breeding parents from score quantiles, combines connected fragments and applies ordinary atom, bond and ring edits with its retained continuation rules; direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled. Stable canonical identities and duplicate rejection admit a fresh surplus pool. A narrow sulfur rule rejects new or multiplied disallowed signatures relative to the maximum count in the original scored generating parents. A Gaussian process fitted to the complete earlier accepted archive represents molecules by counts of local environments and uses generalized Tanimoto covariance. Correlated posterior function draws choose each successive batch member while masking previously chosen identities. Actual accepted scores update the greedy survivor population and chronological prediction archive.
approach.novelty: Remove only sampled residual influence from successful allocation: select the highest original posterior mean at each available-mask step, keeping the original model, covariance, factorization and function draws as passive computations. This isolates whether sampled departures from the mean still contribute after sulfur admission changes the pool and ancestry. Current siblings replaced a mean path or residual law, removed multiplicity, or removed the entire successful selector; none isolates original residual presence on this gated Parent. Earlier mean-only controls on ungated Parents lost endpoint score and remain prior evidence. This is a changed-applicability contribution test, not a claim of a new performance gain.

nodes.hypothesis: Remove only original sampled residual influence on successful pool allocation by choosing the maximum original count-GP posterior mean on each inherited available mask, resolving exact ties by the first pool index, while retaining full original covariance, Cholesky, normal-array consumption and correlated sampled arrays as passive computations with unchanged failure routing.

finding_summary.headline: Mean-only allocation loses 0.11632; sampled residuals contribute under the sulfur gate
finding_summary.insights: The loss cannot be explained by a missing intervention, absent natural choice exposure, altered original model arithmetic, broken accepted-feedback joins or a changed sulfur admission rule: those checks passed. Higher predicted means and lower error on the acquired stream did not preserve the best observed outcome. Selected-stream MSE was lower than Parent in all 15 cells, yet pair ordering and Spearman were worse in 14; the only favorable ranking cell was zaleplon seed 2. Those comparisons describe different adaptively acquired streams. On identical Child identities and labels, active and passive original-mean prediction/ranking contrasts are exactly zero. The narrower selected cores and the Molecular assessment's repetitive connected families are consistent with restricted exposure, while reactive attachments remain in both methods; they do not identify why residual sampling helped or establish chemical mediation. Lack of later breeding is also insufficient as a general explanation: 657 of 659 nonterminal parent-winning Child sources were actually drawn, versus 636 of 639 in Parent. However, 390 drawn Child winners had no productive direct accepted descendant, versus 343 in Parent. Each panel's 150 final-batch offspring remain censored. This answers the current gated residual-presence criterion as one total adaptive removal contrast. It does not establish constituent additivity, sulfur interaction, the value of covariance dependence, independent validation, a complete optimizer foundation or transfer from older ungated Parents; those questions remain open.
finding_summary.results: Every mean-only choice followed the original model mean, with no non-tied mean-loss decisions. The original sampled rule preferred a different identity at 3,958 of 4,350 actual mask positions. A separately masked replay changed all 435 batch orders and 434 selected sets; 2,731 actual accepted molecules were outside its sets. On these same Child pools, mean-only selection raised the average sum of ten predicted means from 3.16569 to 3.42482, lowered selected latent SD from 0.03059 to 0.01583, and raised count-Tanimoto redundancy from 0.58199 to 0.82801. The model uncertainty and original draws remained intact. All 15 task/seed evaluations completed. Macro score fell from 0.59645311 to 0.48013623, a loss of 0.11631688. Paired seed changes were −0.22680180, −0.03988971 and −0.08225913. Twelve task cells lost; median-2 seeds 0 and 2 and sitagliptin seed 1 improved. Local parent wins rose from 648 to 668, but mean best-generating-parent score fell from 0.45530 to 0.37127 and mean offspring score from 0.37205 to 0.33081. Total incumbent gain fell from 5.81942 to 4.07466; new nonempty generic cores with a strict parent-beating member fell from 168 to 101. These complete, exposed results support positive conditional contribution of original sampled residual presence at the registered 0.002 scale.

nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from accepted, scored survivors. It keeps the highest-scoring survivors in score and admission order, chooses breeding parents from several high-ranked score bands, and generates fresh structures through connected-fragment crossover and local atom and bond mutations with ordinary multistep continuation. Its direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange move is disabled. Canonical identity checks form a fresh surplus pool. A Gaussian process fitted to the complete task-local accepted-score archive uses counts of molecular environments and generalized Tanimoto similarity; correlated posterior draws allocate evaluations among the pool members. Accepted offspring update both this model and the live breeding population, allowing repeated productive descendants to breed again.
approach.novelty: Remove only the unequal rank probabilities among parents that the existing breeding rule can already choose. For each request, keep exactly the original eligible support after partner exclusion and its existing fallback, then choose uniformly from that support. The earlier uniform-live sibling also made previously unsupported survivors eligible, so its score loss cannot distinguish support restriction from rank weighting. Frozen-parent and survivor-retention siblings changed other parts of the feedback loop; earlier core-balancing and success-credit experiments added different within-band preferences. This control supplies the missing weight-only contrast while recursive feedback, greedy retention and posterior allocation remain active. The preregistered prediction is that weaker preference for the highest supported ranks will reduce generating-parent quality and may lower final scores; either contribution sign or no material effect is informative.

nodes.hypothesis: Remove nonuniform score-rank weighting conditional on the original same-state positive breeding support: choose uniformly from the increasing-rank union of the inherited positive-probability eligible quantile groups after original partner exclusion and empty-group fallback, retaining the original band-choice call as passive and the original member-choice call as the sole active parent allocation.

finding_summary.headline: Within-support rank weights contribute: uniform sampling lowers mean final Top-1 by 0.057003.
finding_summary.insights:
Nonuniform weighting has positive conditional value even when the set of eligible parents is held fixed. This separates the weight question from the earlier uniform-live control, which also admitted previously unsupported survivors. It does not identify support-only value or the value of the whole graph-evolution foundation, and the two shared-baseline controls cannot be subtracted into independent component effects.

The extra local wins used a weaker reference. Strict best-parent beats rose from 629 to 936, and distinct offspring later reused rose from 2,401 to 2,521. Yet mean best-generating-parent score fell from 0.470456 to 0.383214 and mean offspring score from 0.385256 to 0.321688; sequential incumbent gains fell from 258 to 238 and their average size also fell. Broader use therefore did not preserve absolute search quality. Founder ancestry, chemical core coverage and later use are distinct descriptions, and none establishes the causal route to the score loss.

The molecular assessment finds more generic core identities on four tasks but fewer on median similarity, alongside recognizable aromatic/carbonyl and amine chemistry. Useful-looking structural variety still includes reactive local bonds, demanding bridges and unresolved stereochemistry, with conventional-bond and less-bridged counterexamples. The high-scoring Parent decoration-hopping arrangement was not recovered in the most affected seed. These observations narrow plausible explanations but do not show that a specific chemical defect caused the loss or that a universal chemical restriction would help. The registered weight-only question is answered for this composition, budget and three-seed panel; support-only effects, chemical mediation and broader foundation value remain open.
finding_summary.results:
The control preserved the exact original positive breeding support in all 108,254 parent requests. Every request offered a nonuniform-law comparison, and 103,018 actual parent identities differed from the inherited choice made from the same saved post-band random state. Mean selected topness was 0.756082 versus the original same-state expectation of 0.883924, and mean parent score was 0.348279 versus 0.373596. Changed choices reached 4,020 of 4,350 accepted offspring; 2,269 of those offspring later bred. Greedy recursion, complete accepted-score learning and all 435 full candidate-pool selections remained active.

Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.595670 to 0.538667, a paired change of -0.057003, beyond the registered 0.002 scale. Seed macro changes were -0.113955, -0.012930 and -0.044124. All five task means declined, but four of fifteen task-seed endpoints improved: zaleplon seed 0 (+0.031351), decoration hopping seed 1 (+0.003856), sitagliptin seed 1 (+0.008015) and median similarity seed 2 (+0.006814). The other eleven declined. Seed-macro population deviation fell from 0.026593 to 0.019563. Every formal session completed with its full oracle budget and no fallback.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic amides, aza-diones and aryl amines retain reactive bonds, difficult bridges and unresolved stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: Node n-f30747ffdbf8 produces substituted indole/partly hydrogenated quinoline amides, linked aza-aromatic and lactone/dione systems, aryl-bearing saturated amines, polycyclic lactams with sulfones, and fluorinated nitrogen-carbonyl frameworks. Every supplied Child and published code-Parent n-62daf219c70a trajectory was read: all five objectives and Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2 are covered on both sides. No supplied trajectory path is missing and no objective is omitted. context.comparison separately reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true, matched seeds 0, 1 and 2, and no profile-mismatched seeds. These are complete chemistry comparisons under the supplied batch-size-10, 300-evaluation conditions; they do not establish activation, component contribution, chemical mediation or an independent replication. Each task has 900 Child trajectory records, including 870 accepted optimizer proposal instances. Initial molecules and repeated identities across seeds must not be counted as new chemistry. The digest final_molecules excerpt contains late seed-2 proposals, not every seed incumbent; the full trajectories supplied the seed-level comparisons below. The accepted trajectories do not expose invalid, duplicate-rejected or unscored proposal-pool structures. The digest ring-closure-string incidences are 0.9632, 0.977, 0.9816, 0.9862 and 0.9667 in fixed task order; aromatic-string incidences are 0.9563, 0.9747, 0.9736, 0.9793 and 0.8517. These measure whether a SMILES contains the specified text feature, not perceived ring counts or fractions of aromatic atoms. Charge- and stereocentre-string incidences are 0.0 throughout. Neutral strings nevertheless contain many potentially basic aliphatic amines. Read-only RDKit 2023.09.6 descriptors were computed on one CPU from these accepted records: all 9,000 Child-plus-Parent records parse, but parsing is not a synthesis, geometry, stability or activity test. The 4,350 Child optimizer rows include 2,491 rows with RDKit-flagged unassigned tetrahedral centres, and none has assigned atom or bond stereochemistry. Small rings, bridges and sulfoxides therefore often lack a specified stereochemical identity. The Child/Parent nonempty generic Murcko-core counts, in fixed task order, are 134/123, 347/276, 268/258, 393/405 and 156/92. These deterministic topology descriptors show substantial generated structural variation, including a counterexample to any claim of uniformly increased coverage. They do not measure generating-parent ancestry, independent founder reachability, synthetic plausibility or useful pharmacophore coverage. Within-seed leading molecules often remain related even when atom substitutions and ring edits produce different core keys. Overall diversity is therefore moderate rather than globally collapsed; neither unique SMILES nor multiple ancestral paths would establish useful scaffold diversity. Familiar medicinal-chemistry motifs coexist with N-halogen/O-halogen bonds, acyl halides, peroxides, imines and difficult ring junctions, supporting questionable synthetic plausibility and weak overall drug-likeness. There are important conventional-bond counterexamples, so this is not a claim that every molecule is implausible. nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

approach.method_basis: The Parent walks from one scored current molecule by sampling local graph edits, including a direct formula-preserving exchange of aromatic nitrogen and carbon. It sanitizes and normalizes each identity, rejects duplicates and submits the first full batch permitted by inverse-motif memory. The highest-scoring accepted neighbor becomes the next state even when its score worsens, while a separate archive retains the best observation. After each selected transition, memory keeps at most four inverse changes to rooted local motifs, balancing the two signs and favoring larger occurrence-count changes. Restrictions expire after four completed steps, overlapping keys receive the latest transition's provenance, and a veto requires both signs from one live transition. The repaired identity join is part of this Parent.
approach.novelty: Prioritize the fraction of a motif's occurrences changed by the selected transition when choosing its limited inverse-memory attributes. A motif that disappears entirely or appears entirely new receives priority over a partly changed motif that also remains elsewhere in the molecule. This reallocates the same memory capacity toward more complete local-environment turnover; it does not assert that count turnover identifies a physical edit site. Earlier siblings withheld credit from nonimproving transitions, required every retained attribute to match, or preserved older overlapping origins. This experiment changes only which attributes receive credit within each selected transition, while retaining the Parent's credit eligibility, matching rule and memory lifecycle.

nodes.hypothesis: Rank each selected transition's changed motifs first by absolute occurrence-count change divided by the larger of its before and after counts, then by the Parent's existing rank, so the unchanged bounded sign-balanced inverse installation prioritizes complete motif turnover over partial changes to recurring motifs.

finding_summary.headline: Turnover-based memory redirected 26 scored batches, but the panel mean fell by 0.002456
finding_summary.insights: This rules out absent exposure, mere reordering and failure to change evaluated allocation as explanations for the missed score target. More complete turnover demonstrably changes which local attributes receive memory and which fresh molecules are tested. It also changes admissibility in both directions, so it is not a general relaxation of tabu. The full stream produced slightly more source improvements and archive improvements than the Parent, but their average positive gains were smaller; those event counts did not translate into better final search. The largest loss is not explained by rejecting the best immediate neighbor at the first divergence: in the affected sitagliptin seed, both runs chose the same next molecule after replacing a losing proposal, and their later histories separated. Nine of eleven first batch divergences similarly preserved the next state. Later archive gains are therefore evidence of actual descendants, not isolated causal rewards for particular retained motifs or missing alternatives. Turnover measures how much of a motif multiset changed, without identifying a physical edit site. The molecular assessment still finds reactive heteroatom bonds and dense sulfur cages alongside more conventional aromatic families; the improved memory proxy has not established better chemical plausibility. The unresolved question is which local environments deserve exclusion for useful search, rather than whether fractional ranking can redirect it.
finding_summary.results: The new ranking changed the retained key set at 104 of 435 installations and replaced 114 attributes. On those same recorded transitions, mean selected occurrence turnover rose from 0.931289 under the old ranking to 0.965876, without reducing it at any installation or changing the number of slots assigned to either sign. Partly changed motifs occupied 110 of 1,707 slots, down from 221 under the old ranking. Separate memory histories on the recorded candidate stream yielded 28 newly admitted evaluated molecules and four new vetoes. Three vetoes caused evaluated replacements; one occurred beyond the alternative batch cutoff. This establishes changes to 26 complete scored batches. The recorded stream resolves all ten alternative legacy members in three of those batches; the other 23 alternatives remain incomplete. Among the 31 affected evaluated molecules, seven improved their source, one tied and 23 worsened it; six became next states and three immediately improved the archive. The complete three-seed macro mean fell from 0.521759 to 0.519304, a paired change of -0.002456 against the required +0.002. One seed improved and two declined. Mean DRD2 performance increased by 0.034439, while sitagliptin decreased by 0.048248.

Mean DRD2 performance increased by 0.034439, while sitagliptin decreased by 0.048248.

This rules out absent exposure, mere reordering and failure to change evaluated allocation as explanations for the missed score target. More complete turnover demonstrably changes which local attributes receive memory and which fresh molecules are tested. It also changes admissibility in both directions, so it is not a general relaxation of tabu. The full stream produced slightly more source improvements and archive improvements than the Parent, but their average positive gains were smaller; those event counts did not translate into better final search. The largest loss is not explained by rejecting the best immediate neighbor at the first divergence: in the affected sitagliptin seed, both runs chose the same next molecule after replacing a losing proposal, and their later histories separated. Nine of eleven first batch divergences similarly preserved the next state. Later archive gains are therefore evidence of actual descendants, not isolated causal rewards for particular retained motifs or missing alternatives. Turnover measures how much of a motif multiset changed, without identifying a physical edit site. The molecular assessment still finds reactive heteroatom bonds and dense sulfur cages alongside more conventional aromatic families; the improved memory proxy has not established better chemical plausibility. The unresolved question is which local environments deserve exclusion for useful search, rather than whether fractional ranking can redirect it.
