molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic families and dense sulfur cages, with reactive bonds and unresolved stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: Assessment of the complete saved three-seed panels for this node and Parent n-abcd951ab7cc. Each objective contributes 900 recorded molecules, including 870 optimizer proposals; no objective lacks trajectories. The products range from compact fused aromatic carbonyl compounds to larger decorated heteroaromatics, bridged amine/lactam frameworks and densely interconnected sulfur cages. Offline graph reading of the saved SMILES informs the size and ring descriptions; no new objective, drug-likeness or synthesis scores were calculated. The digest reports ring_closure_rate 1.0 for every proposal set. Aromatic-token presence rates in task order are 0.9586, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0 and 0.7299; these are fractions of strings containing aromatic atoms, not aromatic atom fractions or proof of aromaticity throughout a molecule. All sets have charged_rate 0.0 and stereocentre_rate 0.0. There are recognizable indole carboxamides and aromatic amines, but also benzene-fused unsaturated four-member rings, peroxides, heteroatom-bound halogens and unusual multiple-bonded sulfur. The Parent comparison shows local changes within these broad families, including a sulfur-free bridged aromatic amine among the Child high scorers; it does not show uniform improvement in chemical plausibility. Structural diversity is moderate across the panel but much narrower within late seed trajectories: numerous distinct strings decorate related frameworks. Synthetic plausibility is therefore questionable overall, with plausible-looking subsets and especially doubtful cage/sulfur subsets. All score-gradient statements below describe recorded associations. The available molecules do not establish a unique missing target scaffold or a causal contribution from an individual substituent.

per_task.generated_character: The optimizer emits compact carbonyl-linked ring systems, with 20-29 heavy atoms on graph reading. Seed 1 retains an indole carboxanilide family with ethoxy, methyl and thiol substituents; its recorded best at evaluation 61 is 0.39905049777278273 and is comparatively recognizable synthetic chemistry. Seeds 0 and 2 also reach benzene-fused unsaturated four-member carbocycles. The seed-0 best at evaluation 176, 0.4254027310763201, is an ester joining that strained fused framework to a methylpyridine, with a terminal enamine and fluoromethyl substituent. It is not an indene. Later seed-0 products include unusual sulfur-containing ring variants; seed-1 products acquire N-O bonds and awkward oxygen heterocycles; the final seed-2 cited amide carries an aryl hydroperoxide. The aromatic-token presence rate is 0.9586 and the cumulated-double-bond string rate is 0.1218, so this is ring-rich chemistry with appreciable unusual unsaturation.
liabilities: The best ester contains a benzene-fused unsaturated four-member ring and an enamine; ring strain and chemical stability are concerns even though the graph parses.

Other high entries use unusual sulfur multiple bonding, while low and late entries include N-O linkages, heteroatom-bound halogens or hydroperoxides. Their presence should not be equated with ordinary medicinal substituents.
The aryl thiol in the comparatively plausible indole example remains a reactive functional group; its good recorded score is not a synthesis or stability measurement.
missing_features: Consistent retention of ordinary fused aromatic carbonyl frameworks during later diversification is missing: the relatively conventional indole carboxamide is present, but later proposals frequently substitute strained annulation or disruptive heteroatom bonding.

The favorable compact carbonyl/aromatic pattern is not developed into a broad set of stable alternative attachment geometries. The trajectory cannot identify a particular absent heterocycle as the objective solution.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial methoxy-rich indole carboxamide scores 0.3051048083696145; its simpler ethoxy/methyl/thiol relative reaches 0.39905049777278273. By comparison, the cited seed-0 carbonyl-disrupted, hydroxylamine-bearing analogue scores 0.03343008011310944, and the seed-1 N-hydroxy, extended oxygen-heterocycle amide scores 0.030639811858172862. Compact aromatic frameworks with a retained carbonyl connection fare better in these observations than those particular expanded or disrupted structures. This does not establish a universal benefit for sulfur or halogen substitution. Against the Parent, the seed-0 maximum changes from 0.393567030299894 in a benzothiophene ketone family to 0.4254027310763201 in the four-member-ring ester family; the seed-1 best molecule and score are unchanged, while seed 2 changes from 0.41003927643747895 to 0.3819619698458151. The higher seed-0 score therefore accompanies a more strained ring topology, rather than demonstrating easier synthesis.

per_task.generated_character: These are the largest and most heavily decorated products in this panel: 30-53 heavy atoms in optimizer proposals, with aromatic atoms and ring-closure digits in every string. Seed 0 develops a fused pyrrole/pyrimidine carbonyl-thione system bearing imines and a long oxygen/sulfur-rich side chain. Its best cited molecule at evaluation 232 scores 0.6154582763337894 and includes a sulfur-chlorine terminus and unusual multiple-bonded sulfur. Seed 1 reaches an anilino aza-bicyclic aromatic family with an N-methyl diacyl nitrogen, a dimethylamino O,N-acetal side chain, a peroxide and an oxygen-chlorine group. Its maximum is 0.6165764586926783. Seed 2 retains a fused dicarbonyl heterocycle and oxygen/nitrogen ring decoration while acquiring thioethers, a thioacetal-like carbon and an allene-containing unsaturated chain; its maximum is 0.5933446875409407. The ordinary aromatic and carbonyl substructures are embedded in increasingly doubtful combinations of reactive groups.
liabilities: The leading seed-1 series combines a peroxide with an organic hypochlorite group; its O,N-acetal and activated diacyl nitrogen add further stability questions. An unsaturated acyl group is an electrophilic motif, not a demonstration of selective reactivity.
Seed-0 structures include sulfur-chlorine bonding, imines and unusual sulfur valence environments. Seed-2 structures add allene/polyene and sulfur-rich side chains.

The large number of substituents and unspecified configurations complicate synthetic interpretation. Equal recorded scores across reactive-group changes do not establish equivalence in real chemical behavior.
missing_features: The high-scoring aromatic/carbonyl framework lacks a well-developed set of chemically conservative peripheral variants. A recorded oxygen-chlorine replacement preserves the score, but peroxide-free and otherwise stable analogues of that same family are not established by the cited high-scoring set.

The output does not demonstrate control over side-chain complexity while retaining favorable ring and polar-group arrangements; the late products remain heavily decorated and chemically heterogeneous.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial fused dicarbonyl heteroaromatic ester scores 0.548381482770623, whereas the cited early exocyclic-methylene/carbonyl-modified analogue scores 0.5286081645773063. Larger heteroaromatic structures with elaborated polar and alkyl decoration reach the higher recorded band, but the gradient is tolerant of chemically substantial peripheral changes. The cited seed-1 ethyl and methyl variants, and the analogue replacing oxygen-bound chlorine with a chloroethoxy chain, all score 0.6165764586926783. Thus the oxygen-chlorine bond is not required to retain that observed value in this family. Parent maxima for seeds 0, 1 and 2 are 0.6161710037174721, 0.605139548855754 and 0.6092182584436399, respectively. The Child substitutes a peroxide-bearing aza-bicyclic family for the Parent seed-1 imine-rich aza-aromatic family and ends seed 2 in a more sulfur-decorated allene family. The score changes do not indicate a consistent move toward stable functionality.

per_task.generated_character: The proposals are medium-to-large aromatic amine frameworks, with 30-43 heavy atoms on graph reading, aromatic-token presence 1.0 and halogen presence 0.9989. Early low scorers are oxygen-rich biaryl carboxylic acids carrying amide and N-sulfonyl pyrrolidine groups. Later seed-0 products contain small nitrogen rings, free amines and unusual sulfur linkages. Seed 1 reaches a sulfur-free bridged polyaromatic nitrogen framework with an aminoalkyl secondary amine, an aryl amino group, a phenol and chlorinated aryl/benzylic substitution; its best cited molecule scores 0.9420019982182398. Seed 2 instead reaches a chlorophenyl/fluoropyrrolidine amine assembly attached to a sulfur-rich fused ring system with an aminomethyl group and sulfur-sulfur multiple bonds; its maximum is 0.9441493227693659. Basic amine functionality is clearly available to the generator, although no formal charged state is encoded.
liabilities: The sulfur-rich leaders contain unusual neutral sulfur-sulfur multiple bonds and hydrogen-bearing sulfur environments; sanitization does not demonstrate isolable, conformationally feasible compounds.
The sulfur-free bridged leader still contains a benzylic chloride and an aryl amine, and its ring-junction configurations are unassigned.

Almost universal halogenation and the extensive aromatic surface make these hydrophobic frameworks rather than broadly balanced polar chemotypes; actual solubility or ionization cannot be read from the objective score.
missing_features: Explicit protonation-state and stereochemical alternatives for the amine-containing ring assemblies are absent from the supplied representation; the evidence does not show whether such alternatives would change the objective.

Chemically simpler ways of presenting the observed aromatic/amine arrangement are underdeveloped. The sulfur-free family is an existing foothold, while many other high entries keep unusual sulfur bonding or highly bridged topology.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The cited early acid/amide/sulfonamide structure scores 0.007468397818197266, compared with 0.9420019982182398 for the bridged aromatic aminoalkyl structure and 0.9441493227693659 for the sulfur-rich aminomethyl structure. The visible association favors aromatic hydrophobic surface arranged with non-amide amines and fewer acidic/carbonyl-rich appendages; atom count alone does not explain it. The two cited seed-2 leaders differ by a ring sulfur versus carbon and have the same 0.9441493227693659 score, so that particular extra sulfur is not required for the observed maximum. The Parent-to-Child seed maxima are unchanged at 0.8856242185485628 for seed 0, change from 0.868020189804352 to 0.9420019982182398 for seed 1, and from 0.9148143511682032 to 0.9441493227693659 for seed 2. Seed 1 supplies a real sulfur-free high-scoring family, but the persistent bridged topology and reactive substituents still limit synthetic confidence. These scores alone do not establish a binding pose or interaction mechanism.

per_task.generated_character: The products combine aromatic groups with lactam/urea-derived and bridged heterocyclic frameworks, spanning 27-43 heavy atoms in optimizer proposals. Ring-closure and aromatic-token presence are both 1.0. Seed 0 develops a compact, densely bridged pyridine/phenyl system with a tertiary lactam and an N-O bridge; the best cited molecule at evaluation 196 scores 0.21196904390980506. Seed 1 retains a brominated aromatic/thioester family and later oxygen-bromine and sulfur-rich ring derivatives; its maximum is 0.19092251395438758. Seed 2 develops larger oxygen/nitrogen-containing ring assemblies with lactam and ketone functionality, then unusual sulfur junctions; its maximum is 0.20784255919268485. The late cited seed-2 molecules additionally carry an aryl hydroperoxide. Some components are ordinary medicinal chemistry, but the complete bridge networks and heteroatom combinations have questionable synthetic plausibility.
liabilities: N-O bridges, multiple shared ring junctions and larger heterocyclic loops leave substantial conformational and stereochemical uncertainty.

Oxygen-bromine groups, hydroperoxides, hydrazine-like connections and unusual sulfur environments appear in the cited output. These are real features of the proposed chemistry, not evidence of synthetic accessibility.
The high number of distinct strings includes close variations of recurring bridged families; it does not establish broad coverage of practical scaffolds.
missing_features: The favorable aromatic/lactam arrangement is not explored as a broad family of ordinary, stereochemically defined ring frameworks; late variation largely elaborates dense bridges and unusual heteroatom connections.

The data do not demonstrate a clean structural compromise that raises the recorded band while simplifying the bridge network. More rings or more sulfur cannot be identified as a generally missing objective requirement.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial fused dicarbonyl heteroaromatic ester scores 0.1678386594791329. The cited ring-opened, extended urea/hydrazine analogue scores 0.12467972074136988, while the constrained seed-0 lactam/N-O-bridged system reaches 0.21196904390980506. This supports an association with particular constrained aromatic/polar arrangements, not a general preference for maximum ring count. The seed-1 oxygen-bromine/sulfur compound with an opened polar chain scores 0.12870267321446027. Reactive groups also survive in high entries: the cited seed-0 peroxide-bridge variant scores 0.20647766243219587 and the seed-2 aryl-hydroperoxide variant scores 0.20769510081357428. Parent best molecules and maxima are retained in seeds 0 and 1; seed 2 changes from 0.20185639717998205 in an oxygen/nitrogen-rich ring assembly to 0.20784255919268485 in a sulfur-containing derivative. The recorded improvement is therefore compatible with persistent chemical liabilities.

per_task.generated_character: These are compact but densely interconnected sulfur-rich cages, with 25-33 heavy atoms in optimizer proposals. Aromatic-token presence is 0.7299, yet the cited best molecules from seeds 0 and 2 have no aromatic atoms on graph reading; ring density must not be confused with aromaticity. The seed-0 best at evaluation 260 scores 0.48118636011729826 and combines small unsaturated rings, repeated hydrogen-bearing sulfur junctions, a carbonyl, fluoromethyl and acyl fluoride groups, and a sulfur-oxygen/nitrogen substituent. The seed-1 best at evaluation 294 scores 0.4456072955728387 and contains a thio-ring network, a residual aromatic nitrogen/carbonyl ring, N-chlorine and sulfur-fluorine bonding. The seed-2 best at evaluation 297 scores 0.4484554129767839 and combines sulfur bridges, small rings, a carbonyl, aldehyde and N-fluoro amidine-like group. These high-scoring structures are among the least convincing synthetic products in the panel.
liabilities: Small unsaturated rings, heavily shared junctions and unusual neutral sulfur valence environments make conformational feasibility and practical synthesis especially doubtful.
Acyl fluorides, N-fluorinated or N-chlorinated nitrogen, sulfur-fluorine groups and aldehydes create reactive chemistry in combinations whose stability is unestablished.

Configurations at substituted cage junctions and possible stereogenic heteroatom environments are unspecified. A graph-valid string and a positive objective score do not resolve those structures into experimentally characterized molecules.
missing_features: The high-scoring set does not supply chemically ordinary, stereochemically resolved scaffolds that test the compact polar/carbonyl arrangements without the dense sulfur framework.

Stable placement of fluorine and nitrogen functionality is underdeveloped: much of the shown variation binds halogens to nitrogen or sulfur, or uses acyl fluorides, rather than establishing a coherent family with conventional carbon-bound substituents. The trajectory does not identify a specific absent target pharmacophore.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial fused dicarbonyl heteroaromatic ester scores 0.0020944534688323298, and its cited early ring-expanded carbonyl analogue scores 7.590554525032884e-10. Much higher values occur after dense sulfur-ring restructuring and changes in carbonyl/fluorine placement. This is not a smooth reward for sulfur or ring count: the cited sulfur-rich seed-1 molecule at evaluation 248 still scores only 3.04809716642635e-09, and the final seed-2 ring/linker-expanded variant at evaluation 298 scores 0.01685401516576383 beside the evaluation-297 maximum of 0.4484554129767839. These compounds differ in connectivity, so an isolated substituent effect cannot be assigned. The Parent and Child retain the same best molecules and scores in seeds 0 and 2; seed 1 changes from a different sulfur-rich cage scoring 0.5903526424693334 to the N-chlorinated cage scoring 0.4456072955728387. The chemical family remains highly unconventional even where scores differ substantially.

transferable_gaps.evidence: High and late digest molecules include peroxides, oxygen-bound chlorine or bromine, nitrogen-bound fluorine or chlorine, and sulfur-chlorine groups alongside ordinary amides, ethers and amines. In one cited high-scoring aromatic series, replacing oxygen-bound chlorine with a chloroethoxy chain retains exactly the same recorded score. Reactive functionality is therefore sometimes tolerated without being necessary for that observed value.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve chemically stable functional-group identities while diversifying otherwise recognizable scaffolds.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator needs chemically coherent alternatives for local functional-group changes, including stable replacements that preserve the surrounding attachment geometry. Apply any chemical plausibility treatment through general local chemistry, and let observed feedback determine which variants matter.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every digest proposal set has ring_closure_rate 1.0. The cited compact ester leaders contain a benzene-fused unsaturated four-member ring; other high entries are densely bridged lactam frameworks or sulfur cages with small unsaturated rings. Their favorable recorded scores coexist with substantial uncertainty about conformational feasibility.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator explores ring closure abundantly but does not demonstrate reliable control of realistic ring strain and junction geometry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring proposals need access to chemically credible attachment topologies and junction arrangements, with strain-sensitive structural checks or coherent ring replacements. This is a need for control over which ring systems are produced, rather than for more ring-closure events.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The stereocentre_rate is 0.0 in every digest proposal set, including the amine-containing saturated rings, multiply substituted cage junctions and bridged lactam structures. The cited high scorers likewise carry no explicit tetrahedral configuration tags.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator has no demonstrated stereochemical resolution of the substituted and bridged structures it emits.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: To represent chemically distinct products fully, the generator would need to recognize genuinely stereogenic environments and preserve or enumerate compatible configurations without changing scaffold connectivity. The current observations establish missing representation, not an objective-score benefit from adding it.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The cited output includes primary aminomethyl groups, secondary aminoalkyl linkers, tertiary amines and aza-aromatic nitrogens, yet charged_rate is 0.0 in every proposal set. Neutral notation alone does not establish the solution protonation state, nor does it mean the generator lacks basic centers.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ionizable amine functionality is available, but explicit chemical-state coverage is not demonstrated.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic representation could distinguish relevant charge and protonation states while preserving chemical identity and avoiding redundant state proposals. Any usefulness would have to be checked against the actual scoring interface; it cannot be inferred from the absence of charge marks.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The digest contains 879 unique molecules in most proposal-plus-initial task pools and 877 in the remaining pool, but late seed trajectories repeatedly decorate related carbonyl-linked aromatics, bridged amine/lactam frameworks or sulfur cages. Comparatively conventional indole carboxamides and a sulfur-free bridged aromatic amine are present, showing that ordinary chemistry is accessible but not consistently developed.
transferable_gaps.gap: Many distinct output strings do not yet amount to broad coverage of chemically credible scaffold families around favorable motifs.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Broader exploration would require coherent alternatives to the recurring ring and linker frameworks while retaining useful functional-group arrangements. Scaffold and attachment diversity should be assessed chemically, rather than treating every new graph string as evidence of a new practical chemotype.

nodes.method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
nodes.method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.

approach.method_basis: The Parent trains a recurrent SMILES language model on an unlabeled molecular corpus and starts each objective with an independent policy copied from that frozen prior. Each accepted batch supplies its highest-scoring half. The strongest eligible records from a memory of thirty-two accepted elites join them with their original strings and scores. Historical records receive decreasing weights as they accumulate fitting exposures, while current and historical loss shares retain their inherited totals. The policy fits weighted squared error toward frozen-prior sequence log likelihood plus sixty times accepted reward, with each positive target individually capped at zero. Up to twelve clipped Adam steps retain the final policy. It generates complete SMILES directly from that policy and fills each batch in draw order using chemical validation and canonical duplicate rejection.
approach.novelty: Add one attachment-specific admission rule: withhold a newly sampled molecule when a saturated carbon bonded to chlorine, bromine or iodine is also bonded to a neutral oxygen connecting two carbons. Continue drawing from the same policy to fill the batch. This addresses the observed chloromethyl-ether and related bromoether forms without assigning a general preference to fewer halogens, smaller molecules or different ring cores. The earlier scaffold quotas broadened batches but lost final score; this gate has no scaffold quota. Earlier halogen constraints excluded direct heteroatom-halogen bonds while allowing carbon-bound halogens, so they would permit the attachment targeted here. The claim is removal of this precisely defined form with score non-inferiority, not a claim that every admitted molecule is stable or that removing the form improves reward.

nodes.hypothesis: Reject a complete, RDKit-valid, canonically novel policy draw before emission when it contains a neutral divalent C-O-C linkage whose adjacent neutral tetrahedral carbon has a single bond to terminal neutral Cl, Br or I; continue the inherited bounded direct-policy refill with all learning and token sampling unchanged.

finding_summary.headline: Two late attachment rejections removed the targeted forms while preserving every score-progress trace.
finding_summary.insights:
The evidence distinguishes direct admission changes from later search changes. Only two molecules were directly rejected; the other three matching parent appearances disappeared after accepted feedback and learning changed. Positive raw draws and the two same-stream replacements show that exclusion was exercised, while exact no-action sessions and pre-rejection prefixes locate the intervention at admission. This narrows the earlier attachment question: a carbon-bound halogen can still require a specific oxygen/carbon neighborhood test, while ordinary aryl halides, carbon-fluorine bonds and oxygen linkages continue to be admitted.

Preserved scores have a limited but clear explanation. Both interventions were late, the removed parent examples had not improved their incumbents, and neither replacement nor any of the 48 identities appearing only in the child's affected sessions produced a new incumbent. The test establishes delivery of the specified chemistry without losing observed progress. It does not establish a reward gain or show that earlier, more frequent exclusions would be equally inexpensive. Iodine and haloalkyl-ester contexts had no observed opportunities.

The molecular assessment still describes ring-rich medicinal scaffolds with unresolved size, linker and reactive-form variation, and 843 generated appearances with unassigned perceived tetrahedral centres. Eliminating this attachment leaves those gaps open. The useful next question is whether precise form control can preserve incumbent progress when opportunities occur more often. Reduced raw motif prevalence, greater stability and practical synthesis remain separate claims requiring their own evidence.
finding_summary.results:
Across 435 completed batches, the raw policy stream contained four molecules with the specified oxygen-adjacent saturated carbon–heavy-halogen attachment. Two arrived after the batch was full and were discarded anyway. The other two—a chloromethyl ether and a cyclic oxygen-adjacent carbon bearing fluorine and bromine—were actively withheld and replaced by nonmatching samples from the same draw stream. No targeted form reached any of the 4,350 optimizer evaluations, compared with five matching appearances in the parent. Both replacements entered the next training update with their original sampled strings and real accepted scores.

All fifteen task sessions finished. Mean final Top-1 remained 0.522705, with population seed deviation 0.020072; the paired change was exactly zero in each seed and task. Mean recorded AUC remained 0.405593, and every recorded best-so-far trace was unchanged. This meets the registered 0.002 endpoint non-inferiority allowance on the complete panel. Thirteen sessions reproduced the parent's entire molecular records; the affected sessions retained identical prefixes through evaluations 248 and 286 before diverging.

Both active batches filled without another sampling call. Overall raw generation stayed at 35,568 draws, including 32,647 valid strings; extra calls remained 23 across sixteen batches. Duplicates rose by seven, so exclusion did not improve raw generation quality. Measured batch-generation time totaled 32.164 seconds versus 24.745 for the parent, including 6.324 seconds in the structural predicate and 0.471 seconds in recorded receipt regions. These measurements describe the runs, rather than isolating a causal overhead.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich medicinal scaffolds retain undefined stereochemistry and uneven control of size, linkers and reactive forms.
molecular.overall_character: Node n-f5484e31d41d produces phenyl/pyridyl carboxamides, decorated quinazolines, aromatic molecules bearing cyclic amines, sulfonyl-linked piperazines, and varied amide, amidine and sulfur-containing structures. All five objectives and all three seeds were inspected: 4,350 optimizer appearances and 150 fixed-initial appearances for this node, with the same complete Parent panel. Passive RDKit readings of optimizer appearances give medians of 26 heavy atoms, 368.41 Da, three rings and three aromatic rings; the heavy-atom range is 3 to 90. The digest ring-closure rates are 0.9805 to 0.9966 and aromatic-presence rates 0.9460 to 0.9931; these are string-presence rates, not fractions of atoms or RDKit ring counts. Saturated-ring chemistry is present in 1,294 appearances, so the output is neither ring-deficient nor exclusively aromatic. There are 2,806 distinct nonempty exact Murcko scaffolds, versus 2,813 in Parent n-c2ef5c1d5a78. This supports broad whole-panel exploration, while several successful families concentrate strongly on one core. Exact Murcko differences can also reflect linker or ring-substitution topology and do not establish useful pharmacological diversity. Many leading structures have ordinary, apparently makeable medicinal-chemistry motifs. The questionable synthesis assessment concerns the mixture as a whole: unusual attachment states, activated functional handles, and very large or elaborate outliers remain, without demonstrated routes or stability. The structures do not establish experimental activity, solution microstates or developability. The stereochemical gap is concrete: 843 optimizer appearances contain RDKit-perceived unassigned tetrahedral centres, totaling 1,428 centres, while none has an assigned tetrahedral centre, an @ marker or a directional alkene marker. These are representation observations, not evidence that assigning stereochemistry would improve any score. Compared with the Parent, the specified neutral C-O-C/adjacent saturated-carbon/terminal Cl, Br or I form occurs in zero Child optimizer appearances versus five Parent appearances; initial appearances contain none in either panel. Thirteen complete paired sessions retain identical molecule/score records. The differing records are confined to seed-1 drd2_docking and seed-1 sitagliptin_mpo, and all fifteen recorded final-best values are unchanged. This is a narrow observed output difference, not a general chemical-stability finding or an activation judgment. One sulfonyl fluoride elsewhere in the panel remains a distinct functional handle, illustrating why non-carbon halogen bonding alone is not a makeability verdict. No objective lacks trajectories. Numerical structural readings and every digest-to-trajectory join are recorded in runs/SPIRAL2/policy/responses/r0012-11-improve-L03-molecular.audit.json, produced by the adjacent passive audit script after reading all 9,000 Child/Parent records. The report uses existing oracle scores only; it does not rescore molecules or infer unobserved target structures.

per_task.generated_character: Across 870 optimizer appearances the median molecule has 24 heavy atoms, molecular weight 333.37 Da and three rings. The twelve digest leaders are much more consistent than the full set: 23 to 25 heavy atoms, three aromatic rings each, and an amide in every structure. Seed 0 contributes an acetylamino indole bearing a benzyl carboxamide; seed 1 contributes pyridylmethyl benzamides with anilino or pyridone-containing appendages; seed 2 contributes pyridyl ethers bearing an anilide. These are largely conventional connected aromatic amide structures with modest appendages. The whole set also includes tiny charged fragments, large polycyclic structures and repeated amide/aryl expansions. All 900 molecule/score records, including initial observations, match the Parent across the three seeds.
liabilities: Large repeated amide/aryl assemblies add size and conformational burden without the observed reward of the smaller leaders.

The final alpha-bromoacrylamide at seed-2 evaluation 295 contains an activated unsaturated acyl group and scores 0.06933217991151693. Its absence from the screened oxygen-adjacent saturated-halide class does not establish benign reactivity.

The high N-O-linked acyl compound and sulfinamide show that unusual heteroatom attachment can coexist with useful scores. The latter has an unassigned perceived stereocentre; neither should be labeled unmakeable solely from the bond type.
missing_features: Many proposals lack the compact aromatic-ring/amide/short-linker balance shared by the leaders; adding more amides or retaining only a small fragment loses that arrangement.

The leading structures lack saturated ring alternatives to their aromatic frameworks. The data do not establish that such alternatives are rewarded or identify a unique missing target core; the supported gap is reliable preservation of the useful attachment pattern while changing the surrounding framework.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxyindole anilide at evaluation 9 scores 0.3051048083696145; the seed-0 acetylamino-indole benzylamide at evaluation 152 scores 0.43351949803907636. The seed-1 pyridylmethyl benzamide/pyridone at evaluation 273 scores 0.4767312946227961, and the seed-2 ethylpyridyl ether/anilide at evaluation 271 scores 0.5. These examples associate higher reward with a compact aromatic amide arrangement, rather than a unique ring identity. Both extremes fail: the tiny anionic N=C=S fragment scores 5.670115669739515e-23, while the large repeated amide/bicyclic-amine structure at seed-0 evaluation 211 scores 3.2151129360788796e-21. A late four-ring, 35-heavy-atom amide expansion at seed-2 evaluation 296 scores only 0.00015241757289843227. The trifluoromethyl-containing ether/anilide at evaluation 299 scores 0.18573410909422844, so aromaticity, an amide and halogen substitution alone do not reproduce the leading arrangement. These are observed associations, not isolated substitution experiments.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 optimizer appearances have medians of 33 heavy atoms, 450.43 Da and four aromatic rings. Every one of the twelve digest leaders is a seed-2 substituted arylamino/phenyl quinazoline with butoxy and methoxy groups: 34 to 41 heavy atoms, four aromatic rings and one shared exact Murcko scaffold. The full trajectories are broader, with 355 distinct nonempty Murcko scaffolds. Seed 0 ends with a substituted pyridyl/dinitrophenyl hydrazone as its recorded leader, whereas seed 1 favors an imino, anilino and cyano-substituted fused aza-ring system. Thus the seed-2 family should not be mistaken for the whole panel. The leading quinazolines are plausible aromatic medicinal scaffolds, but their aromatic area, alkoxy appendages and halogen content give substantial hydrophobic bulk. All three trajectories are identical to the Parent.
liabilities: Four aromatic rings, multiple alkoxy groups and extensive halogenation can produce bulky hydrophobic structures; measured solubility and useful exposure are not supplied.

The secondary ether appendage in the 590.04-Da cited leader at seed-2 evaluation 268 has an unassigned tetrahedral centre. The full task contains 99 optimizer appearances with unassigned perceived centres and no explicit stereochemical tags.

The low-tail long-chain quaternary ammonium is structurally closer to a surfactant than to the leading heteroaromatic family. Other seeds also expose hydrazone/imine-form questions, so the highest-score family does not describe every proposed chemical form.
missing_features: Alternative cores retaining the successful arylamino/aza-aromatic/ether attachment relationships are absent from the twelve leading examples, despite broader exploration elsewhere in the trajectories.

Successful exploration of nonplanar ring architectures is not shown by this leading family. Its reward pattern supplies no basis for prescribing one unseen reference scaffold or assuming that more halogens would close the remaining gap.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Recorded final-best scores are 0.5998615059406662, 0.6263699396108253 and 0.6669492630755185 for seeds 0, 1 and 2. Within the cited seed-2 family, the trifluorophenyl leader scores 0.6669492630755185 and the difluorophenyl analogue 0.6666996765035981. Increasing to the cited tetrafluorophenyl form yields 0.6534013806124255, and a different difluoro placement yields 0.6362655153804642. The butyl-linked final analogue scores 0.6316114681166585, below the butoxy-linked leader. Reward therefore tracks the arrangement of the arylamino, aza-aromatic and ether-linked decorations more closely than a simple preference for more fluorine or carbon. Plausible sulfone-containing quinoline and indole structures score 0.28535067873303166 and 0.28799019607843135. The long-chain quaternary ammonium scores 0.5 and hexanol 0.5008612522607871; that relatively high floor cannot be interpreted as comparable medicinal chemistry.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 optimizer appearances have medians of 28 heavy atoms, 389.20 Da, three rings and two aromatic rings. The twelve leaders contain 25 to 30 heavy atoms and three to five rings; eight contain a piperazine. Seed 0 supplies lipophilic biaryl/benzyl piperazines, including the brominated propyl-substituted leader. Seed 1 supplies phenolic or methoxybenzyl secondary amines connected by alkyl chains to difluorobenzazepine or arylpiperazine units. Seed 2 supplies aromatic ketones or amides bearing a phenoxypropylpiperidine arm and a second aromatic appendage. These are recognizable medicinal-chemistry architectures containing potentially basic saturated nitrogens, rather than a shortage of cyclic amines. Compared with Parent n-c2ef5c1d5a78, the four oxygen-adjacent chloromethyl forms are absent, while methoxy, phenoxy and aryl-halide chemistry remains. Only the seed-1 trajectory differs, beginning at evaluation 249; all recorded endpoint best scores remain identical.
liabilities: Lipophilic biaryl/halogen substituents and several potentially ionizable nitrogens create unresolved solubility and solution-microstate questions; neutral SMILES do not demonstrate a single neutral species.
Long alkyl and ether-rich chains add conformational freedom, illustrated by the lower-scoring final long-linker amide.

The twelve cited leaders have no RDKit-perceived unassigned tetrahedral centres, so their lack of @ tags is not itself a stereochemical defect. The broader task contains 190 appearances with unassigned centres. Absence of the Parent chloromethyl forms is a narrower observation than general chemical stability.
missing_features: The low-scoring structures often lack the exposed saturated amine/aromatic attachment relationship already present in the leaders. The generator can produce that relationship but does not consistently retain it while changing ring systems or linkers.

The high-scoring set already contains basic cyclic amines and multiple aromatic contacts; these observations do not justify prescribing another amine, a particular unseen receptor interaction or one uniquely missing pharmacophore.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The brominated biaryl/benzyl piperazine scores 0.9999997933663268 and the phenol-linked difluorobenzazepine diamine scores 0.9999997851052089. Lower examples retain aromatic rings but put nitrogen in amide or sulfonamide environments: the amide/sulfonyl-piperidine structure scores 1.9828327575562915e-05 and the acylated piperidine carboxamide scores 2.6715842904959654e-05. The observed separation is consistent with accessible basic amine placement combined with aromatic bulk, not nitrogen count alone. In the final seed-2 examples, the smaller amino ketone lacking the phenoxypropylpiperidine arm scores 0.0035116287191461495, while the arm-bearing amino ketone scores 0.999988872643426. A longer ether-rich amide with 17 RDKit rotatable bonds scores 0.5728095677025575, whereas the shorter ketone with nine scores 0.9999937368364026. Thus adding flexible polar linker material does not uniformly help. Scores near their observed ceiling cannot resolve a missing binding interaction or establish experimental binding.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 optimizer appearances have medians of 24 heavy atoms, 340.03 Da and three rings, with broad exact-core coverage: 732 nonempty Murcko scaffolds. The leaders nevertheless show a recurring chemical arrangement: ten of the twelve have a sulfonamide and eleven contain a piperazine. The best is a 32-heavy-atom, 475.55-Da bis-sulfonyl piperazine connecting a methylquinoline and a benzodioxole, with five perceived rings in total. Both piperazine nitrogens are sulfonylated, so this leading example must not be described as a freely basic piperazine. Other leaders use an N-methyl piperazine, an aryl sulfonamide, or benzodioxole-linked alkyl chains. Most of these scaffolds have plausible conventional synthetic connections, while a partially unsaturated N-rich ring and much larger repeated sulfonyl assemblies make the whole output more mixed. All 900 molecule/score records match the Parent.
liabilities: The 628.80-Da two-piperazine leader illustrates repeated sulfonyl and ring accumulation, which increases molecular and polar-group burden without surpassing the more compact leading arrangement.

The ringless azide and N-hydroxy trichloromethyl form are chemically distinct from ordinary stable medicinal scaffolds and merit attachment-specific scrutiny; their low reward alone is not a synthesis assay.

A sulfonyl fluoride persists at seed-0 evaluation 289 with observed score 0.15884700241362154. This is a recognizable reactive functional handle, not proof of invalid chemistry or a reason to ban all heteroatom-halogen bonds. It is outside the removed oxygen-adjacent carbon-halide form.
missing_features: Many proposals lack the connected sulfonyl/cyclic-diamine/aromatic arrangement seen in the leaders; isolated small polar fragments or a lone piperazine-bearing ring do not reproduce it.

Useful recombination of that arrangement remains inconsistent despite extensive scaffold exploration. The trajectories do not identify an unseen reference pair or prove that increasing basicity, adding another sulfonyl group or maximizing raw scaffold count would improve the objective.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The methylquinoline/bis-sulfonyl-piperazine/benzodioxole leader scores 0.2588686674995393. The smaller methylquinoline sulfonyl-N-methylpiperazine scores 0.2272296156064184, whereas the more elaborate two-piperazine, 41-heavy-atom assembly scores 0.2301209791058402. A compact sulfonamide-linked benzodioxole/piperazine example scores 0.2229480268629566. These examples favor a combined cyclic-diamine, sulfonyl and aromatic arrangement, but do not support indefinite multiplication of those groups or a requirement for a free basic nitrogen. The six low-tail digest examples are all ringless: allyl azide scores 0.0, the sulfur-linked diacid 0.02095188685475281, and the small sulfur-oxo acid 0.02668612498071339. A final small pyrrole/piperazine structure scores 0.10826206026353223. Ring presence and piperazine alone therefore do not recover the fuller leading arrangement.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 optimizer appearances have medians of 24 heavy atoms, 347.09 Da and three rings, but the twelve leaders range from one to four rings and 20 to 26 heavy atoms. The seed-2 leader is a secondary-amino acylsulfonamide attached to a fluoro/trifluoromethyl phenyl group. Other strong examples include a branched amino-amide/oxalamide, arylsulfonyl cyclic amidines bearing ester or imidate substituents, a guanidine-bearing benzofused amine, a sulfonyl pyrrolidinone and a quinolone acylthiourea. The leaders occupy eight exact nonempty Murcko scaffolds; the full proposals occupy 774. This is broad but chemically uneven exploration, including large peptide-like chains and densely decorated aromatic or polycyclic outliers. Ordinary amide and sulfonamide chemistry is plentiful, while some leading imidate, hydrazone, thiourea and amidine forms have additional state and attachment questions. Parent comparison changes only five seed-1 molecule/score records; the oxygen-adjacent bromo-ring form is absent and all three endpoint-best scores remain the same.
liabilities: Large peptide-like chains and polycyclic expansions combine size, conformational complexity and frequently undefined stereochemistry. The complete task has 273 optimizer appearances with unassigned centres.

The acylsulfonamide, imidate, sulfonyl hydrazone, guanidine and acylthiourea examples have different acid/base, tautomer and attachment chemistry. Their SMILES and rewards do not establish a shared solution state or validated stability.

The fluorinated branched amino-amide is a credible compact chemotype, but its potentially stereogenic centre is unspecified. Merely omitting the oxygen-adjacent bromo attachment seen in the Parent does not resolve this broader representation gap.
missing_features: Consistent delivery of moderate-sized molecules with the useful amino/amide/sulfonyl attachment relationships is missing across much of the trajectory; both large repeated polar chains and small poorly arranged polar structures score weakly.

Four of the twelve leaders have RDKit-perceived unassigned tetrahedral centres, including the branched amino-amide and guanidine-bearing fused ring. No stereochemical configurations are explored explicitly, although these trajectories do not establish a score benefit for doing so.
The available high-scoring examples span several distinct chemotypes. No unique absent target heterocycle, substitution pattern or pharmacophore can be inferred from these scores alone.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The compact amino-acylsulfonamide scores 0.32609684308650033 and the branched amino-amide/oxalamide 0.3085499097640706. The fluoroaryl cyclic-amidine ester scores 0.3034617343186778, its cited imidate counterpart 0.2795168707513844, and the corresponding nonfluorinated aryl ester 0.24905607529893223. A nonfluorinated guanidine-bearing fused ring still scores 0.2711448282680827, and the quinolone acylthiourea scores 0.26424211308214746. The common signal is an appropriate combination of moderate size and polar-group arrangement across several scaffolds, not an obligatory fluorinated core. The six low-tail examples have 40 to 61 heavy atoms and molecular weights from 572.56 to 863.92 Da, including peptide-like and long-chain structures with zero or extremely small reward. Size reduction alone also fails: the final 18-heavy-atom carbonyl-rich heterocycle at evaluation 297 scores 2.6445959326166367e-17. The digest median is reported as 0.0; the examples do not identify which hidden objective component limits reward.

transferable_gaps.evidence: All 4,350 optimizer strings lack @ and directional alkene markers. Passive perception finds 843 appearances containing 1,428 unassigned tetrahedral centres. Cited high-scoring examples include a branched amino-amide at 0.3085499097640706, a guanidine-bearing fused ring at 0.2711448282680827, a sulfinamide at 0.4531317717091581 and a secondary ether appendage at 0.6546458319881191. Some leading families are achiral, so the gap applies to eligible structures rather than every molecule.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator produces potentially stereogenic structures without expressing their configurations.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Represent eligible configurations during de novo generation while retaining coherent connectivity and canonical identity. Distinguish genuinely stereogenic centres and configurationally meaningful bonds from achiral structures, and let observed feedback establish where configuration matters; no universal stereochemical score gain follows from the present data.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The full proposal panel contains 2,806 distinct nonempty exact Murcko scaffolds, yet twelve leading decorated aza-aromatic examples share one scaffold and differ mainly in aryl halogen and alkoxy decorations. Other leading groups repeatedly reuse aromatic amides or sulfonyl-linked cyclic diamines. Thus missing ring chemistry is not the issue; useful relationships between rings, linkers and polar centres become concentrated in a few families.
transferable_gaps.gap: Broad scaffold exploration does not reliably extend the attachment arrangements of successful families into alternative cores.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support changes to ring architecture and linker topology while preserving the useful chemical attachment relationships found in accepted observations. Assess whether the resulting evaluated families retain those relationships and useful reward; increasing an exact scaffold count by itself is insufficient, and no fixed reference core or objective identity is required.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A compact three-aromatic-ring amide scores 0.5 while a later 35-heavy-atom repeated-amide expansion scores 0.00015241757289843227. A long ether-rich amide with 17 rotatable bonds scores 0.5728095677025575 while a shorter arm-bearing ketone with nine scores 0.9999937368364026. A 41-heavy-atom repeated sulfonyl/piperazine assembly scores 0.2301209791058402 versus 0.2588686674995393 for a smaller connected arrangement. Conversely, small ringless fragments and a small carbonyl-rich heterocycle also score poorly, so these observations do not support a universal small-molecule preference.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator lacks consistent control of appendage growth, linker length and polar-group repetition within otherwise promising structures.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make appendage size, linker spacing and polar-group density adjustable without losing productive ring/amine/amide or sulfonyl connections. Use the generator's own task-local feedback to learn appropriate combinations rather than applying an unconditional size cap, removing all polar groups or repeating a favorable fragment indefinitely.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The specified oxygen-adjacent saturated carbon bearing Cl, Br or I is absent from 4,350 Child optimizer appearances versus five in the Parent, but the digest still contains an alpha-bromoacrylamide, an azide, an N-hydroxy trichloromethyl form, sulfonyl hydrazones, an imidate and an acylthiourea. A trajectory also retains one sulfonyl fluoride. Several unusual heteroatom-containing leaders have substantial reward, and ordinary amides, sulfonamides, ethers and aryl halides are widespread. These are distinguishable chemical contexts, not a single class of invalid or unstable molecules.
transferable_gaps.gap: Excluding one narrowly defined attachment form leaves heterogeneous reactive handles and unresolved chemical states in the generated output.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Develop attachment-aware representation of complete chemical forms, including plausible valence, local functional-group context and explicit state or configuration where relevant. Preserve conventional heteroatom and halogen chemistry, and distinguish intentional reactive handles from accidental attachment combinations. Any further form constraint needs evaluated evidence; the current narrow absence does not establish improved synthesis, stability or reward.

nodes.method_name: Augmented Hill-Climb with a corpus-trained SMILES policy
nodes.method_thesis: Train a compact autoregressive SMILES prior solely on the supplied unlabeled corpus, then initialize a fresh policy from that prior for each objective. Use the initial observations and each subsequent scored batch to update only its highest-reward sequences with the Augmented Hill-Climb loss: fit policy log likelihood to frozen-prior log likelihood plus scaled observed reward. Sample complete molecules token by token from the updated policy, canonicalize them, and refill invalid or duplicate proposals by further generation. The corpus supplies language training, never a ranked molecular pool. Elite-conditioned policy updates should shift generation toward new high-scoring molecular combinations quickly enough to improve the benchmark's mean final Top-1. This is a small-budget transfer hypothesis, not a claim that published larger-budget gains carry over. The root uses the current scored batch; randomized historical replay is reserved for the first improvement. The anchor's elite augmented-likelihood mechanism is described by [Thomas et al.](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13321-022-00646-z).

approach.method_basis: The Parent alternates direct neural molecular proposals with two graph refinement phases. It learns from a full archive of real accepted scores and exact molecular token trajectories sampled by score rank. Joint trajectory-balance updates adapt the policy and a learned normalizer, while policy-to-prior categorical KL keeps a reference to frozen corpus-trained weights. A fingerprint Gaussian posterior allocates graph-offspring evaluations and protects the initial fresh-policy handoff. The frozen prior was selected along unchanged unlabeled training by valid, connected, unique generation yield, with original holdout loss breaking ties. In its current update, both trajectory-specific score mismatch and the common normalizer mismatch contribute to policy credit.
approach.novelty: Center the trajectory-balance policy credit within each actual replay minibatch and assign the common mismatch to the existing normalizer alone. Each trajectory still receives relative credit from its exact accepted score and likelihood, and every pairwise difference in those coefficients is retained. Unlike the earlier scaffold mixture or reversed KL penalty, this changes neither which records are learned from nor the reference distribution. It tests whether separating shared normalization error from relative policy learning makes accepted-score adaptation more useful; it does not assume that zero mean credit or lower loss guarantees better molecules.

nodes.hypothesis: Center accepted trajectory-balance policy coefficients within each replay minibatch while routing the detached common residual exclusively to the learned normalizer, preserving score-ranked replay and the original categorical prior penalty.

finding_summary.headline: Centering activated, but common error grew and useful neural emission fell
finding_summary.insights:
The common policy-credit component was not merely an expendable normalization error in this setting. Removing it left the scalar objective unchanged at a given state, yet shifted much more unresolved error onto the normalizer and weakened later transfer of graph feedback into neural proposals. This happened while graph-origin replay share increased from 73.54% to 75.43%, so dilution of graph records is not the explanation. Greater emitted scaffold variety and the disappearance of duplicate raw draws also failed to compensate for lower valid yield and policy-origin scores.

The early-versus-late reversal narrows the problem to continuing accepted-score adaptation rather than a different prepared prior: the checkpoint identities and preparation were unchanged. Preserving the direct normalizer derivative was insufficient to preserve its trajectory, because the policy state and shared clipping changed. The improved sitagliptin endpoint must also be read alongside the molecular assessment, which found prominent peroxide-linked, stereochemically undefined structures; broader graph coverage does not establish better chemical quality. Mechanism execution is confirmed, while the registered search-advantage condition is unsupported. The remaining question is how to control common and relative learning jointly without discarding the useful molecular transfer observed in the parent.
finding_summary.results:
All 7,200 replay updates used the intended centered policy credit. Independent differentiation verified that the common term had no policy gradient and that the normalizer retained its original direct derivative. The change reversed 99,068 of 230,400 policy-credit signs while preserving pairwise differences and the scalar loss value within numerical precision. Nevertheless, the common mismatch became much larger in the resulting histories: its mean squared contribution was 44.130, compared with 4.418 in the parent, accounting for 62.59% rather than 14.95% of trajectory-balance loss.

Raw valid novel yield fell from 7,991/12,000 draws (66.59%) to 6,861/12,280 (55.87%). The first adapted policy batches improved in validity, but later yield fell from 64.00% to 51.82%. Mean accepted policy-origin score fell from 0.204941 to 0.172874, and later emitted molecules matching previously trained graph scaffolds fell from 53 to 15. The three-seed mean final score fell from 0.550198 to 0.542654, a decrease of 0.007543; paired changes were -0.009239, -0.029845 and +0.016454. All fifteen task replicas completed their 300 evaluations.

molecular.headline: Recognizable amide and piperazine chemistry is mixed with acid chlorides, N-O-O chains and stereochemically undefined polycycles
molecular.overall_character: The supplied panel is complete: each of five tasks has 900 evaluated molecules across three seeds, including 870 optimizer proposals. All 4,350 optimizer-proposal SMILES parse with RDKit. Rings and aromatic atoms are plentiful: digest ring-closure rates are 0.9851-0.9931 and aromatic-token rates 0.9402-0.9828. In fixed task order, proposal median heavy-atom counts are 25, 37, 25, 30 and 26, and median ring counts are three, five, three, four and four. Conventional aryl propionamides, aminoheteroaryls, cyclic tertiary amines, arylsulfonylpiperazines and aromatic dicarbonyl systems coexist with O-fluoro groups, O-acyl hydroxylamines, acid chlorides, bridged sulfur/nitrogen ring systems and unusual N-O-O-C substituents. These liabilities occur in leading families: one task contains 139 acid-halide proposals; another contains 211 proposals with O-O single bonds, including 201 with N-O-O chains, and its highest structure has seven RDKit-perceived unassigned stereocentres. No proposal assigns a stereocentre, while counts containing an unassigned centre are 492, 198, 389, 350 and 538. Each task has 553-679 nonchiral Murcko scaffolds, but leading molecules repeat close families rather than establish broad accessible synthetic diversity. The parent already generated elaborate ring systems and unusual bonds; current acid-halide and peroxide-rich families make those limitations prominent. Overall drug-likeness is weak because major leading families carry reactive or physically burdensome features, despite conventional amide and piperazine subsets. The trajectories do not establish synthesis or stable experimental compounds.

per_task.generated_character: The highest molecule is an alpha-aryl propionamide whose amide nitrogen carries a methylene-linked N-arylpyrrole; the attached aryl group is a fluoropyridine. It has 25 heavy atoms, three aromatic rings and an unassigned alpha-carbon stereocentre. Related leaders use pyrazoles, an O-acyl hydroxylamine connection instead of the amide, or ring-contracted unsaturated nitrogen heterocycles. The ordinary amides are recognizable medicinal chemistry; aryl O-F, acyl-O-N and four-membered unsaturated nitrogen-ring variants need separate qualification. Parent leaders included indole-amide and fused heterocyclic structures, whereas this digest concentrates around a three-ring propionamide/heteroarylmethyl architecture.
liabilities: An O-acyl hydroxylamine is an acyl-O-N connection, chemically distinct from an ordinary amide or hydroxamic acid; the score does not establish its stability.
Sixteen proposals contain O-halogen bonds and 23 N-halogen bonds, although the highest displayed molecule requires neither.
Eleven proposals have at most three heavy atoms and 18 exceed 50, so fragmentation and overgrowth coexist with the leading ring-rich chemistry.
missing_features: The leading alpha-aryl acyl family does not specify its central stereocentre, leaving the proposed configurations undefined.
Broad stable alternatives retaining the useful amide/heteroaromatic relationship are less visible than O-F, N-O and small-ring variants.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The conventional amide scores 0.445826 and its displayed aryl O-F counterpart 0.445454, showing tolerance rather than a demonstrated need for O-fluorination. In another local pair, an O-acyl hydroxylamine scores 0.442718 and the direct amide 0.432360; that extra oxygen changes bond chemistry, not just polarity. A related three-ring amide remains at 0.417399, whereas truncated two-ring amide or heteroaryl structures score 0.007181 and 0.004449. Very large assemblies and tiny halogen or hydrazine species reach zero. The visible association is a particular moderate-size ring/linker/carbonyl arrangement.

per_task.generated_character: The highest family is a three-ring aminoheteroaryl assembly with methoxy, dimethylamino, bromo or fluoro substituents and a vinyl-ether-containing N-substituent. Its top member has 34 heavy atoms, three aromatic rings and molecular mass 534.390. A second leading family has arylsulfonamide/anilino frameworks bearing two acid chlorides, often with methylenedioxy and sulfur/nitrogen fused rings. These are recognizable reactive intermediates rather than demonstrated stable final medicinal compounds. Some variants add aromatic bridges or unusual sulfur double-bond arrangements. Full proposals have median 37 heavy atoms, five rings and molecular mass 573.860; 201 exceed 50 heavy atoms. Acid-halide proposals increase from 15 in the parent to 139 here.
liabilities: There are 139 acid-halide proposals, and several leaders contain two acid chlorides, providing reactive acylating sites rather than demonstrated persistent drug-like substituents.
Thirty-three proposals contain O-halogen bonds and 41 have O-O single bonds, distinct concerns from ordinary aryl halogenation.
The proposal range reaches 111 heavy atoms and molecular mass 2035.098, limiting the practical meaning of graph validity.
missing_features: Stable functional-group alternatives retaining the useful polar/aromatic arrangement are not demonstrated across the high-score acid-chloride neighborhood.
The output lacks consistently economical whole-molecule coverage around the aminoheteroaryl family, often extending into larger repeated or fused structures.
Synthetic access and stable geometry are unestablished for the aromatic bridges and unusual sulfur-bond variants.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The aminoheteroaryl leader scores 0.615282, a close analogue 0.614174 and a methoxy-for-bromo variant 0.613310, so bromine is not required for a nearby score. The bis-acid-chloride sulfonamide scores 0.613582; ring-bridged or sulfur-bond variants remain near 0.61. Those values tolerate reactive groups without establishing chemical persistence. Replacing methoxy with O-F in a local aminoheteroaryl pair gives 0.609781 versus 0.614174, providing no benefit from O-F. Low sulfone-rich or heavily elaborated structures lie around 0.285-0.299 despite many rings and heteroatoms.

per_task.generated_character: The highest molecule combines a nine-membered tertiary-amine ring with indole and phenol regions, an ethyl substituent and a fluoromethylamino arm. It has 32 heavy atoms, four rings and two unassigned stereocentres. The fluoromethylamino arm is N-CH2-F, not a direct N-F bond. Eight-membered analogues, bridged amines, dimethylaminoethyl aromatic frameworks and aldehyde-bearing arylpiperidines also lead. These include familiar medicinal motifs, but medium or bridged rings raise synthetic and conformational questions. Parent leaders likewise combined cyclic amines with aromatic, indole or phenolic regions; the current digest emphasizes medium-size rings and unusual junctions. Full proposals have median 25 heavy atoms and three rings.
liabilities: Eight- and nine-membered rings and multiple bridges impose conformational and synthetic questions that the graphs do not resolve.
Some leaders contain aldehydes, and 32 proposals have direct N-halogen bonds; the highest N-CH2-F structure must not be confused with those direct N-F species.
Sixteen proposals exceed 50 heavy atoms, with a maximum of 95, showing excessive elaboration around otherwise useful amine chemistry.
missing_features: Leading medium-ring and bridged amines lack explicit relative configurations and established conformations; 389 proposals contain unassigned stereocentres.
No additional mandatory group follows from near-ceiling scores; economical stable alternatives preserving the observed amine/aromatic relationships are the supported need.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The nine-membered amine scores 0.999991, an eight-membered analogue 0.997059, a less elaborate dimethylaminoethyl aromatic structure 0.993803 and an aldehyde-bearing arylpiperidine 0.993765. Their shared feature is accessible amine functionality positioned with aromatic regions; the nine-membered ring and fluoromethylamino arm are not universal requirements. Low acylhydrazone, carbamate, thiosemicarbazone and amide examples lie near 4.11e-05 to 1.11e-04 despite nitrogen and rings. A terminal direct N-F cyclic amine scores 0.247498 while other terminal amines remain above 0.91, but those are different structures and do not isolate an N-F substituent effect.

per_task.generated_character: The strongest family is conventional arylsulfonylpiperazine chemistry with the second piperazine nitrogen attached to a substituted quinoline-like or diazaaromatic fused ring. The highest has 29 heavy atoms, four rings, three aromatic rings and molecular mass 409.555. Methyl, fluoromethyl, chlorine, hydroxyl and amino substitutions supply close alternatives. Another leader is a fused aromatic dicarbonyl nitrogen heterocycle attached to an ethoxy-substituted N/O ring system. These leaders are more chemically straightforward than many terminal structures. The parent also produced sulfonamide and fused cyclic-carbonyl architectures. Current proposals have median 30 heavy atoms and four rings versus parent medians of 32 and four, with 666 nonchiral Murcko scaffolds.
liabilities: Sulfonylated and aryl-attached piperazine nitrogens are electronically different from interchangeable free aliphatic amines.
Terminal proposals include O-O-containing rings, dense sulfur/nitrogen fusion and duplicated carbonyl frameworks without established stability or synthetic access.
Sixty-eight proposals exceed 50 heavy atoms, substantially larger than the leading conventional piperazines.
missing_features: Useful sulfonylpiperazine and dicarbonyl arrangements have limited distinct alternatives beyond local substitutions with identical or nearly identical scores.
The wider output lacks consistent ring-fusion and configurational control: 350 proposals have unassigned centres, although the highest piperazine family is achiral.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The arylsulfonylpiperazine scores 0.232655, the alternative dicarbonyl compound 0.231883 and the fluoromethyl variant 0.231824. Several amino, hydroxyl, fluoro or aryl-halogen variants share 0.225523, giving little evidence that more peripheral decoration resolves the remaining gap. Small ethane, ether, carbonate or guanidine-like species score approximately 0.012-0.029 and lack the combined aromatic/polar-ring architecture. Terminal examples repeating carbonyl heterocycles or adding complex rings remain around 0.139-0.203. More ring closure or heteroatoms alone therefore does not explain the useful arrangement.

per_task.generated_character: The highest family combines a five-membered lactone or cyclic carbamate with a multiply fluorinated fused sulfur/nitrogen system and a fluorinated cyclopropyl group. Most displayed members also carry an unusual N-O-O-C connection. The highest has 29 heavy atoms, five rings, only one aromatic ring and seven RDKit-perceived unassigned stereocentres. This is detailed connectivity without configurational specification, and the N-O-O chain combines N-O and peroxide bonds. Another high family contains an N-fluoro sulfur-containing fused system; terminal molecules show nitrogen-rich dicarbonyl cores linked to unsaturated sulfur rings bearing carbon allenes. Parent leaders also included unusual fluorinated heterocycles, but current O-O proposals rise from 48 to 211, including 201 with N-O-O chains. These structures need strong chemical qualification as stable compounds.
liabilities: N-O-O chains occur in 201 proposals and any O-O single bond in 211; these are chemically different from ordinary ethers or amino substituents.
Twenty-five proposals contain N-halogen bonds and 29 carbon allenes; 19 place an allene in a perceived ring of at most seven atoms, leaving local reactivity and ring geometry unresolved.
Several cited lactone/carbamate leaders have five to seven unassigned centres, so saturated complexity does not establish a coherent specified stereoisomer.
missing_features: Stable alternatives preserving the useful carbonyl, fluorinated-ring and nitrogen arrangement without N-O-O chains or other unusual bonds are not demonstrated across the leading neighborhood.
The highest structure has seven unassigned centres, and 538 proposals contain unassigned centres with none assigning any; defined three-dimensional molecules are missing.
Stable geometry and synthetic access are unestablished for fused sulfur/nitrogen cores, fluorinated small rings and cyclic-allene alternatives.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The lactone/N-O-O structure scores 0.519276 and a ring-connectivity analogue 0.501405. In a close cyclic-carbamate pair, the N-O-O version scores 0.492253 and its shorter N-O counterpart 0.463156. That numerically favors peroxide insertion in this pair without establishing stability. A different N-fluoro fused structure scores 0.475223. Several terminal carbon-allene sulfur-ring compounds reach approximately 0.302-0.403. Very polar glycosylated, multiply hydroxylated or oversized structures are as low as 1.13e-128. The full median is 0.0028918204 and there are no exact-zero rows, so this is a wide score distribution rather than a zero-score population.

transferable_gaps.evidence: One set contains 139 acid halides and leaders with two acid chlorides near score 0.613. Another has 211 O-O proposals, 201 with N-O-O chains; a cyclic-carbamate pair scores 0.492253 with N-O-O versus 0.463156 with N-O. Elsewhere, ordinary amide and aryl O-F variants score 0.445826 and 0.445454, showing that the reactive bond is not numerically needed in that pair. All structures pass RDKit parsing, which does not establish chemical persistence.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably distinguish stable functional-group alternatives from reactive connections tolerated by scores.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide stable bonds and functional groups that preserve useful observed arrangements. Distinguish amides from O-acyl hydroxylamines, ethers from peroxide or N-O-O chains, aryl halogens from O-halogen bonds, and stable carbonyl groups from acid halides independently of objective identity.

transferable_gaps.evidence: No assigned stereocentres occur in 4,350 optimizer proposals. The five sessions contain 492, 198, 389, 350 and 538 proposals with unassigned centres. The highest peroxide-bearing lactone has seven RDKit-perceived unassigned centres, and leading propionamides and medium-ring amines also omit configuration. Several strong piperazines are achiral, so the issue is conditional.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator adds stereogenic complexity without defining the configurations of its proposed molecules.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support explicit chemically consistent configurations and relevant bond geometries when the structure permits them, while retaining achiral alternatives. Complex connectivity must not substitute for specified three-dimensional molecules, and the data do not prescribe an unobserved preferred stereoisomer.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The five sessions contain 18, 201, 16, 68 and eleven proposals above 50 heavy atoms; the largest has 111 heavy atoms and molecular mass 2035.098. High-score aminoheteroaryls also include simpler three-ring structures, and conventional four-ring sulfonylpiperazines score above more elaborate terminal carbonyl assemblies. Other proposals contract aromatic heterocycles into small unsaturated rings or create medium and bridged amine rings without defining geometry.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator lacks consistent control of molecular growth and ring elaboration around useful chemical arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Maintain economical alternatives with controlled linker length, topology, appendage count and mass while preserving useful polar relationships. Overgrowth and indiscriminate ring contraction can both lose valuable chemistry; the missing capability is contextual control of accessible whole molecules.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Each task has 553-679 nonchiral Murcko scaffolds, yet leaders cluster around propionamides, aminoheteroaryls, bis-acid-chloride sulfonamides, medium-ring amines, sulfonylpiperazines or fluorinated peroxide-bearing polycycles. Several piperazine amino, hydroxyl, fluoro and aryl-halogen variants share 0.225523. In an aminoheteroaryl family, bromo and methoxy alternatives remain near 0.614 while O-F substitution is lower than its methoxy counterpart.
transferable_gaps.gap: Substantial graph diversity still produces narrow leading families and repetitive peripheral-substitution alternatives.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Broaden meaningful core and linker alternatives preserving useful functionality, beyond repeated halogen swaps and ring closures. Functional-group position, electronic environment and stable geometry need representation alongside scaffold identity, with their usefulness determined by observed feedback.

nodes.method_name: Genetic GFN: reciprocal learning between a flow policy and graph search
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Genetic GFN: alternately generate molecules with a GFlowNet policy, refine the resulting scored population through graph crossover and mutation, and distill scored descendants back into the policy using rank-weighted off-policy replay. The policy uses trajectory balance with a learned log normalizer and regularization toward a frozen prior. [Kim et al., Section 3](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.05961v4) describe this mechanism. Train the prior only on the permitted unlabeled corpus. Each objective starts with clean policy adaptation, replay and population state initialized from its supplied observations. Use a positive terminal reward increasing with the observed maximization score. Schedule policy and genetic phases around the evaluator's announced feedback; both produce new molecules, and all reward-bearing training records come from accepted observations. Later policy samples must enter genetic populations, and accepted graph descendants must affect subsequent policy updates. Generate further valid, canonical-unique structures to fill announced batches, without corpus ranking or a fixed molecular library. The hypothesis is that learned global proposals propagate local discoveries into new promising regions and then support further graph refinement, raising the mean of five independent final Top-1 scores. Published larger-budget gains do not establish that this reciprocal learning becomes useful quickly enough here.
