approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves a task-local population of accepted molecular graphs. It keeps up to 64 survivors ordered by observed score and insertion order, independently chooses breeding parents through three preferred score bands, and generates fresh molecules by connected-fragment crossover and local atom/bond edits, including short mutation walks. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen positional exchange is disabled. A Gaussian process trained on the complete accepted-score archive uses counts of local molecular environments and generalized Tanimoto similarity; correlated posterior draws select the next announced batch from a full surplus pool. Accepted offspring update both the model archive and the breeding population.
approach.novelty: Introduce randomly permuted systematic blocks for first-parent requests. Each prospective block keeps the Parent's exact rank preference and positive support, but its counts stay close to their expected allocation before the records are consumed in random order. Block length is the existing fresh-pool target. Earlier siblings changed the eligible support, marginal parent weights, survivor retention or proposal lifetime; this experiment changes only dependence among first-parent draws and keeps crossover-partner selection inherited. The hypothesis is that limiting accidental allocation clumps can improve the supply of useful offspring while retaining strong parents. The guarantee concerns prospective complete blocks; validity-dependent stopping can bias consumed prefixes, and improved endpoints remain an untested prediction.

nodes.hypothesis: Replace independent first-parent requests within each suggestion by uniformly permuted systematic blocks of length equal to the inherited fresh-pool target, preserving the exact inherited prospective categorical rank probabilities and positive support while leaving every second-parent request on the original quantile law.

finding_summary.headline: Balanced first-parent use activated, but final scores fell across all three seeds
finding_summary.insights: Balanced prospective allocations transmitted into real accepted descendants and more complete breeder coverage. That exposure makes this a useful negative result: coverage and local parent-win counts are insufficient evidence of endpoint benefit for this fixed scheduler. The Child’s generating parents had lower absolute scores, so its extra local wins were measured against weaker references; more incumbent advances also came in smaller steps. The largest losses involved decoration hopping and sitagliptin, while median-2 and zaleplon task means improved. The chemistry assessment found substantial formal scaffold variety and useful aromatic, amine and carbonyl arrangements, alongside reactive bonds, strained closures and unspecified stereochemistry. Plausible alternative leading families remain limited even where graph counts are broad. Those descriptions do not establish which chemical feature caused the score loss. The fixed scheduling approach has a complete adverse result under this profile. The respective roles of changed parent sequences and their associated graph-RNG paths in producing those losses remain unresolved, as does contribution of the broader graph-evolution foundation.
finding_summary.results: The scheduler preserved the original prospective rank preference and balanced all 870 preallocated blocks. It consumed 75,411 of 139,200 records; the other 63,789 were unused. Each suggestion actually used every supported first parent, raising mean distinct first-parent coverage from 24.32 to 29.00. More accepted offspring beat their generating parents (720 versus 629), and more accepted records were later used for breeding (2,636 versus 2,401). Yet average offspring score fell from 0.385256 to 0.352623, and the average positive incumbent increment fell from 0.022510 to 0.018417. All fifteen task/seed runs completed on each side. Macro mean fell from 0.595670 to 0.553508, a paired change of -0.042161 against the required +0.002 gain. Every seed macro declined; eleven task/seed endpoints declined and four improved. The improved cells were zaleplon seeds 0 and 2 and median-2 seeds 1 and 2. Macro dispersion also decreased, from 0.026593 to 0.018224, without meeting the performance prediction.

molecular.headline: Aromatic and ring-rich molecules retain useful amines and carbonyls alongside reactive bonds, strained rings and unspecified stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: All fifteen Child and fifteen published Parent Search trajectory paths, and all six frozen summaries, were present and read. The immutable context reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true for seeds 0, 1 and 2; no objective or comparison is absent. Each side has 900 records per task, including 870 accepted optimizer molecules. Trajectory maxima agree with every supplied summary. This assessment describes those evaluated outputs, not unselected internal graph pools. The molecules include substituted indole carboxamides and unsaturated four-membered fused rings, linked aza-aromatic thioamides, aryl-containing aliphatic amines, bridged nitrogen/carbonyl systems, and fluorinated imino/dione heterocycles. The Child digest ring-closure incidences are 0.969, 0.9782, 0.9805, 0.9782 and 0.9678; aromatic-string incidences are 0.9655, 0.9782, 0.977, 0.9736 and 0.9621 in the fixed task order. These are molecule-level text-feature incidences, not ring counts or aromatic-atom fractions. Offline RDKit inspection gives Child median heavy-atom counts 25, 40, 32, 33 and 29, versus Parent 25, 33, 31, 30 and 27. Typed/generic Murcko graph counts among accepted optimizer outputs, counting the empty acyclic scaffold, are Child 267/112, 465/352, 365/252, 507/340 and 319/195; Parent 295/124, 404/277, 391/259, 584/406 and 208/93. Generic graphs erase atom and bond types. These counts show substantial formal graph variety, while leading molecules within individual seeds often share a much narrower chemical family. Neither distinct strings nor these scaffold counts establish plausible independent chemical coverage. Scaffold similarity, recorded founder reachability and demonstrated atom retention are separate observations. The evaluated trajectories contain no atom-mapped genealogy; this report neither reconstructs founder ancestry nor claims that recognizable initial motifs prove retained atoms. Every Child task has stereocentre-string incidence 0.0; neutral strings nevertheless contain available aliphatic amines. Questionable synthesis and weak overall drug-likeness reflect local heteroatom-halogen bonds, peroxide links and problematic ring geometry alongside familiar functional groups, not a computed feasibility score. Graph parsing and oracle labels establish neither synthesis nor stability, conformation or biological activity. The digest final excerpts are late seed-2 evaluations, not all seed incumbents. All cited_smiles below are exact task-scoped Child strings in the trusted request paths; Parent descriptions refer to its authoritative published trajectories and seed/evaluation locations. The transferable gaps preserve their historical source in n-c55c3d520a2c under its Development profile and their later baseline observation in n-62daf219c70a; historical evidence is not pooled into the current matched comparison. No chemical association here identifies mechanism activation, component contribution or an Anchor decision.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-0 leader (evaluation 256) is a 23-heavy-atom, three-ring N-brominated indole carboxamide with an N-hydroxy-N-phenyl amide. Seed 2 (279) has a 24-heavy-atom indole carboxamide with an N-amino substituent, chlorophenyl, methyl and fluoromethyl groups. Seed 1 (262) instead has 25 heavy atoms: a methoxy/vinyl-substituted benzene fused to an unsaturated four-membered carbon ring, joined through a thioamide/hydrazone group to pyridine. The three leaders therefore share aromatic surface and a polar carbonyl/thione region but do not share the same ring topology. The ordinary indole and amide motifs are recognizable synthetic starting points; the four-membered unsaturation, N-Br and N-N/O environments need separate feasibility assessment. The published Parent likewise has indole-derived amide/dicarbonyl families and an unsaturated linker family. Its seed-1 leader (293) is a pyridyl N-hydroxy carboxamide with N-F; its seed-2 leader (294) is an aryl diketone. This Child does not lack rings or aromatic groups.
liabilities: N-bromination and other N-halogen variants are distinct from ordinary carbon-bound halogens and bring local reactivity concerns.
The unsaturated four-membered fused carbon ring raises geometry and stability concerns; high score and valid aromatic notation do not resolve them.
N-amino, N-hydroxy and hydrazone derivatives require environment-specific assessment, and overgrown aromatic duplicates can have extremely low scores.
missing_features: High-scoring examples do not establish a comparably useful, geometrically credible replacement for the unsaturated four-membered ring while preserving its linker arrangement; the indole leader is an alternative topology but not an isolated replacement experiment.

Conventional local alternatives to the leading N-Br, N-O and N-N substitutions are not consistently demonstrated at the same scores. These records do not identify an exact absent target pharmacophore.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial indole anilide scores 0.3051048083696145. Child leaders for seeds 0/1/2 score 0.44024381449798056, 0.4475341963854715 and 0.4394278959350887; published Parent leaders score 0.39405142067435733, 0.47411701813450596 and 0.438972502037081. Within the seed-1 fused-ring family, the N-amino thioamide scores 0.4369542269692598; its terminal methylene-imine derivative scores 0.4475341963854715, while the chloromethylene-imine derivative scores 0.4201182934804424. These local comparisons suggest sensitivity to the polar linker and substituent pattern, not a general benefit of adding halogen. A much larger linked indole-amide structure at seed 2/evaluation 31 scores 1.7997013645006645e-14, and N=S scores 0.0. The visible reward is for a particular compact aromatic/polar organization; both fragmentation and extensive duplication can lose it. The seed-2 leader lacks an N-halogen bond, so that liability is not necessary for the observed high-score region.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-0 leader (289) has 43 heavy atoms and four six-membered aromatic rings linked by carbonyl, carbon-carbon and thioether connections, with methoxy, fluoro and tertiary aryl-amino substituents. The seed-1 leaders have 34 heavy atoms and connect a substituted pyridine to a fused nitrogen heterocycle through a thioamide; the appended oxygen-containing ring includes an O-O bond. The seed-2 leader (295) is a 39-heavy-atom, densely cross-linked O/N polycycle with ten RDKit-perceived rings, an N-O connection, exocyclic unsaturation and a chloroethyl imine substituent. Across accepted output, median size is 40 heavy atoms, versus Parent 33; the Child also emits much larger graphs. The Parent seed-0 leader (297), at 31 heavy atoms, combines linked nitrogen-rich carbonyl/thione heterocycles rather than the Child seed-2 dense polycycle. Familiar heteroaryl and thioamide pieces coexist with peroxide chemistry and challenging cross-links, so synthesis is questionable despite abundant rings.
liabilities: The seed-1 leaders contain a cyclic O-O link, which must be assessed as peroxide chemistry rather than an ordinary ether.
The seed-2 dense polycycles contain N-O connectivity and multiple constrained unsaturated ring junctions; perceived ring count does not demonstrate accessible conformation or synthesis.
Very large elaborations and floor-scoring fragments coexist with medium-sized leaders, without evidence that either extreme supplies useful structural context.
missing_features: The Child does not demonstrate reliable access to the particular compact linked heterocyclic organization seen in the stronger-scoring published Parent seed-0 family; this is a coverage observation, not proof of retained founder atoms or a component cause.

High-scoring families lack established geometrically accessible, locally stable alternatives to the peroxide and dense cross-linked arrangements. The near-scoring nonperoxide relative shows that O-O is not universally required.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-fused dione scores 0.548381482770623, the smaller oxygen-containing aromatic carbonyl structure at seed 0/evaluation 13 scores 0.5252566400521428, and methane scores 0.5. Child seed leaders score 0.6041124414367517, 0.6120582590041774 and 0.6112056392805056; published Parent leaders score 0.8561477222467935, 0.6248206599713055 and 0.6178024026512013. The Child seed-1 peroxide thioamide has several peripheral variants tied at 0.6120582590041774. A related ether-ring thioamide without O-O at evaluation 243 scores 0.6106181943884312; other substituents also differ, so this is a counterexample to a necessary peroxide rather than a measured peroxide effect. A still more elaborate seed-2 polycycle at evaluation 291 scores 0.5830654842582195. These examples associate useful scores with connected heteroaromatic/polar arrangements, but do not support more atoms or more ring closures as a sufficient improvement.

per_task.generated_character: The Child leaders combine aromatic surfaces with available aliphatic amines. Seed 2/evaluation 261 has 27 heavy atoms, two substituted benzene rings, a dimethylamino alkyl linker, methoxy and aniline groups, carbon-bound fluorine, and a three-membered carbon ring fused across adjacent aromatic atoms. Seed 0/evaluation 278 has 28 heavy atoms, a secondary ethylamino side chain and two four-membered rings in its fused aryl/amine region. Seed 1/evaluation 270 has 32 heavy atoms, a saturated diazacycle, substituted cyclopentane, phenolic/aniline groups and an O-Cl substituent. The published Parent leaders instead include a flexible tertiary diarylalkylamine (seed 0/evaluation 284), an aminoalkyl pyrrolidine/aryl ether (1/261), and a pyrrolidine-substituted fused thioether/biaryl structure (2/285). nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

approach.method_basis: The Parent makes local graph edits from one scored current molecule, sanitizes and normalizes each identity, rejects duplicates and directly evaluates the first full batch allowed by inverse-motif memory. It moves to the highest-scoring accepted neighbor even after a worsening score and separately retains its best observation. Ring closure samples hydrogen-bearing attachment pairs within the existing graph-distance range and adds a bond; it can connect sites across already extensive ring frameworks. Same-transition bidirectional tabu matching, the repaired identity join and the established memory lifecycle remain in place.
approach.novelty: Add one topology gate specifically to new ring closures. A proposed closure may form a cycle whose chosen existing shortest path contains no old ring atom, one old ring atom, or two adjacent old ring atoms joined by an existing ring bond. These cases retain access to separate, spiro-like and single-edge fused additions while excluding more extensive overlap under this narrow rule. All edit sampling stays unchanged; an otherwise valid fresh rejected closure is replaced by continued sampling from the same source. This differs from the earlier sulfur filter, branch-removal menu and configuration assignment, and incorporates none of them.

nodes.hypothesis: Reject an otherwise valid canonically novel close_ring neighbor before tabu testing unless its source shortest path overlaps the existing ring graph in zero atoms, one atom, or exactly one existing ring edge, thereby redirecting new-cycle proposals away from extended or separated ring overlap while retaining the Parent's edit sampling and accepted-score walk.

finding_summary.headline: Targeted ring closures disappear, while the mean score falls by 0.003396
finding_summary.insights:
The experiment establishes that a narrow source-path rule can strongly control ring-junction growth without disabling all closures or disturbing identity, memory and feedback. Most evaluated rings remain, and the admitted closure repertoire still produces improvements. The score cost is nevertheless real on this panel: the parent had 37 source-improving and 19 selected closures in the now-excluded class. Those historical observations explain why score retention required a test, but they do not provide scores for the newly rejected structures or identify which missing transition caused a later loss.

The chemical assessment shows what the topology restriction leaves unresolved. Less elaborate ring cages still contain unusual sulfur coordination, reactive heteroatom-halogen bonds and unspecified configurations. The permitted classes do not establish accessible three-dimensional geometry or synthetic plausibility, and the rule neither removes complexity already present in a source nor constrains other edit types. The campaign now has evidence that extensive ring overlap can be suppressed selectively, alongside evidence that this degree of suppression did not retain the registered mean-score margin. Ring topology and local chemical bonding remain separate limitations.
finding_summary.results:
The gate rejected 275 valid, fresh ring-closure attempts. Independent reconstruction of the current tabu table shows that 257 of these would otherwise have been admitted; each was replaced by a different neighbor from the same scored source before feedback. Emitted closures with extended or separated overlap fell from 241 to zero. Ring growth remained active through 40 permitted closures: six paths outside existing rings, three with a single old ring atom and 31 sharing one old ring edge. Nine permitted closures beat their source score and seven improved the best archive.

The overall molecules also lost much of the targeted complexity. Among 4,350 emitted neighbors, the number with a pair of RDKit-perceived rings sharing at least three atoms fell from 1,867 to 10, while mean ring-atom participation changed only from 62.89% to 61.70%. This preserved substantial ring content while removing most extensive ring overlap. All batches completed, requiring 12.83 attempts per ten submitted molecules versus 12.15 for the parent. The complete three-seed mean fell from 0.520918 to 0.517522, a paired change of -0.003396 that exceeds the allowed 0.002 loss. Seed changes were +0.004044, -0.024305 and +0.010073. DRD2 improved on average; the other four task means declined.

molecular.headline: Aromatic carbonyl and amine frameworks retain reactive halogens, unusual sulfur bonding and undefined stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: Every supplied current and parent trajectory was read. Each task has 900 recorded molecules and 870 optimizer proposals. The current output remains entirely ring-bearing by the digest's string counter, with aromatic-token rates from 0.9103 to 1.0 and mean SMILES lengths from 46.6 to 73.2. Molecules range from compact fused heterocycles to bulky aryl amines and expanded carbonyl-containing heterocycles. The leading structures generally have fewer elaborate cage connections than several parent families, but that does not make their bonding uniformly conventional. Ordinary thioethers, sulfoxides, amides and amines coexist with substituted S-H centres, multiply bonded sulfur carrying additional substituents, N-halogen groups, O-F groups and reactive sulfur-halogen connections. All charged-token and stereocentre-token rates are 0.0. Neutral SMILES do not establish neutral solution species for the amines, and the many potentially stereogenic ring and sulfur centres remain unspecified. Structural diversity is moderate across seeds and families, with the displayed leaders often concentrated in one closely related series. Synthetic plausibility and drug-likeness are limited primarily by unusual local bonding and reactive functionality, rather than by a lack of rings or heteroatoms.

per_task.generated_character: The leading seed-2 molecules are compact fused furan/unsaturated sulfur-ring systems bearing an aryl amide or pyridyl ketone. Alkyl, aminomethyl, imine and chlorinated amino substituents decorate the larger ring; the main ring sulfur itself is an ordinary divalent sulfide. The best molecule contains both an amino-chloromethyl substituent and an N-chloro amide. A close-scoring pyridyl-ketone relative has methylamino and imine groups without an N-halogen bond. Seed 1 retains a comparatively straightforward ethoxy/methyl/thiol indole carboxanilide. The low examples disrupt the attached aromatic ring, expand or open a heterocycle, or replace the compact carbonyl-containing connection with a more flexible heteroatom chain.
liabilities: N-chloro amides, N-chloro amines and amino-chloromethyl groups introduce reactive bonds beyond ordinary aryl chlorination.
Some alternatives contain labile imines, free thiols, sulfur-halogen groups or cumulated unsaturation.
Partly saturated fused rings and multiple unsaturated connections are not accompanied by defined stereochemistry or alkene geometry.
missing_features: The lowest ring-expanded and chain-like derivatives lack the intact aromatic carbonyl organization present in the stronger structures.

The high-scoring set lacks a systematic series that preserves the fused aromatic carbonyl framework while replacing reactive N-chloro and amino-chloromethyl groups with stable alternatives; a chlorine-free relative already shows that such chemistry can score closely.
Ring substituents with possible stereogenic relationships remain unassigned, and no configuration preference can be inferred from these strings.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The fused furan/sulfur-ring N-chloro amide scores 0.41700086027236194; a pyridyl-ketone relative with methylamino and imine substituents but no N-halogen group scores 0.4137456434408254. The ordinary indole carboxanilide reaches 0.39905049777278273. Thus the observed high-scoring family does not require every reactive chlorine substituent. A compact aryl-amide example scores 0.3957609793331631, while replacing its attached aromatic nitrogen-containing ring by an expanded unsaturated ring gives 0.01654726774958358. A pyridyl ketone at 0.40650757542526167 becomes 0.3305825215461728 when its carbonyl connection is replaced by a sulfoxide. The gradient favors retention of a compact aromatic carbonyl arrangement more clearly than sulfur enrichment. Current seed 2 reaches 0.41700086027236194 versus parental 0.41003927643747895 with a related but differently fused framework; seed 1 retains the same best indole amide, while seed 0 reaches 0.3504977161693128 versus 0.3966634883331815.

per_task.generated_character: The highest-scoring family is a bulky substituted phenyl group connected through an amino/exocyclic unsaturated arrangement to a nitrogen-containing carbonyl/imino ring. It carries branched conjugated carbon chains, fluoromethyl or difluoromethyl substituents, direct N-chlorination and an ester or imidate side chain ending in an aldehyde. Some side chains include an oxygen-linked alkyne, and some close relatives replace part of the carbon chain with additionally substituted, multiply bonded sulfur. The final seed-2 family instead contains an expanded nitrogen-rich dicarbonyl ring, imine and nitrile side chains, alkyl groups, methoxy groups and a bromoalkyl substituent. Early low examples retain more compact ester/phenol/dicarbonyl frameworks with disrupted ring connections. The assembled leading molecules have recognizable fragments but a high density of reactive or unusually conjugated connections.
liabilities: Direct N-Cl bonds, aldehydes and oxygen-linked alkynes introduce reactive functionality; the imidate alternative adds another hydrolysis-sensitive connection.
Extensive conjugated unsaturation and branching create configurational ambiguity and synthetic complexity.
Multiply bonded, additionally substituted sulfur and bromoalkyl groups appear in alternatives even where their local score advantage is not demonstrated.
missing_features: The low ring-altered compounds do not retain the same decorated aromatic and exocyclic heterocycle organization as the higher-scoring family.

Matched chemically simpler versions retaining that organization are underrepresented among the displayed leaders. Equal scores across several appendage changes do not demonstrate that the reactive or flexible embellishments are needed.
Imine and alkene geometry, and the configurations of branched side chains, are unspecified throughout the proposal set.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The leading imidate/alkyne/aldehyde derivative scores 0.6005008990495762, compared with 0.5976915588930607 for its carbonyl ester relative. Multiple variants share exactly 0.5976915588930607 despite changes in side-chain branching, alkene substitution, aminoalkyl substitution, aldehyde versus ketone termination, or introduction of an unusual sulfur-containing carbon-chain replacement. This supports the broader decorated aryl/heterocycle arrangement more strongly than those individual embellishments. nodes.method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
nodes.method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.

approach.method_basis: The Parent is a genetic algorithm that breeds molecular graphs from a population of up to sixty-four scored molecules. It draws parents from three high-ranking score bands, makes connected-fragment crossovers and local atom or bond edits, and sends each valid, novel offspring directly for evaluation. Accepted scores immediately update a greedy survivor population, so useful offspring can become parents of the next batch. This feedback loop worked, but most evaluated offspring scored below their generating parents.
approach.novelty: Add posterior-sampling selection before offspring reach the oracle. The same graph operators first generate a fresh pool; a fingerprint Gaussian process learned only from this task's accepted scores draws plausible score functions, and each batch position takes a different sampled function's best available offspring. This concentrates evaluations on promising generated structures while allowing uncertainty to change the choices. The lineage has only its root so far: no sibling has tested learned offspring selection, and the supplied mechanism-cluster history is empty. The new mechanism changes which generated offspring are evaluated; its training archive and diagnostics support that single selection mechanism.

nodes.hypothesis: Select oracle-bound offspring by maximizing independent joint posterior function draws from a task-local fingerprint Gaussian process over a fresh pool generated by the Parent's unchanged graph evolution operators.

finding_summary.headline: Posterior selection reproduces across seeds, but offspring yield stays below the historical parent-beating rate
finding_summary.insights: The experiment now separates reliable selector execution from the hoped-for improvement in offspring yield. The new runs' posterior means contain useful predictive information on the selected molecules: pooled prediction MSE is 0.017182 versus 0.036613 for the same-fit archive mean, with average within-batch rank correlation 0.412. Yet this information and widespread uncertainty-driven choice do not produce a higher parent-beating fraction. The remaining question is how to turn predictive information into more productive evaluations relative to already strong parents. Prediction quality is also uneven: on sitagliptin_mpo it is worse than the archive-mean predictor in two of three seeds, and that objective has the largest final-score variation. The chemistry assessment shows ample aromatic amides, cyclic amines and carbonyl-containing rings, alongside reactive substitutions and destructive edits; access to recognizable molecular families is established, while reliable discrimination among useful, chemically credible alternatives remains open. The unused pool members have no scores, so these runs cannot identify which rejected alternatives would have been better. Matched Parent replicas and same-pool comparisons with mean-only and generation-order selection are needed to isolate score benefit, efficiency, and uncertainty's contribution.
finding_summary.results: The two additional runs reproduce posterior selection and feedback. All 2,900 selected offspring maximize their reconstructed correlated function draws, uncertainty changes 2,693 choices (92.86%) compared with choosing the highest posterior mean, and all 2,800 eligible predictions on the same molecules change after accepted feedback. All 290 fits use only earlier accepted observations. Mean final-best score across the five objectives is 0.558863 in the first additional run and 0.526723 in the second, compared with 0.547535 in the original run of this selector. Across all three seeds, mean score is 0.544374 with population standard deviation 0.013310. The intended offspring-efficiency improvement does not appear: only 371 of 2,900 new offspring beat their best generating parent (12.79%), and their mean child-minus-parent score is -0.100465. The original direct-submission Parent's single-seed references are 13.86% and -0.084154. Across all three selector runs, 565 of 4,350 offspring beat their best parent (12.99%). The original paired screening-score gain of 0.055880 remains a one-seed comparison because matched additional runs of the direct-submission Parent are unavailable.

molecular.headline: Aromatic amides, cyclic amines and dicarbonyl heterocycles are abundant, but reactive halogen and peroxide substitutions persist.
molecular.overall_character: Every task has 600 observed molecules across seeds 1 and 2, including 580 optimizer proposals. Ring_closure_rate ranges from 0.9724 to 0.9966 and aromatic_atom_rate from 0.969 to 0.9897, supporting a predominantly ring-rich aromatic repertoire. These counters measure SMILES-text presence, not ring counts or fractions of aromatic atoms. The molecules include benzofused nitrogen heterocycles with aryl amides, bridged lactams, carbonyl-rich fused heteroaromatics, saturated cyclic aminals, macrocyclic nitrogen/carbonyl systems and fluorinated aryl primary amines. Thus useful rings, amines, carbonyls and heteroaromatic chemistry are demonstrably available. Mean SMILES lengths range from 45.0 to 85.3 and the maximum reaches 248; moderately sized leaders coexist with bulky assembled structures and occasional tiny fragments. Charged_rate is 0.0 throughout, which does not mean that neutral SMILES lack protonatable amines. Stereocentre_rate is also 0.0 despite several asymmetric saturated centres, ring junctions and constrained frameworks. The main chemical-quality issue is the persistence of nitrogen-halogen, oxygen-halogen and peroxide functionality, including among high-scoring structures. Some leading molecules are much more conventional, especially the primary-amine-bearing fluorinated aryl dicarbonyl family and ordinary carbon-linked cyclic amines. Synthetic plausibility is therefore mixed, and drug-likeness moderate overall. Core diversity is greater across runs than within their concentrated upper families; numerous local ring and substituent variants should not be mistaken for uniformly broad useful chemistry. The supplied parent_trajectories are seed 0 of n-fc2c108a5253 itself. Comparisons below describe those different runs and do not judge algorithm activation. Missing chemistry denotes gaps in the observed output, not established benefits for unobserved replacements.

per_task.generated_character: Seed 2 favours moderately sized benzofused unsaturated nitrogen-nitrogen rings bearing a carboxanilide, methoxy and methyl groups. The leading carboxanilide nitrogen is fluorinated, and other variants halogenate the ring nitrogen or add bromomethyl/chloromethyl groups. Seed 1 instead produces bridged or spiro-like lactam/imine frameworks containing an aromatic nitrogen ring and vinyl ether or vinyl sulfide decoration; some introduce sulfur-nitrogen bridges. Ring_closure_rate is 0.9724, aromatic_atom_rate 0.9707 and halogen_rate 0.8224. Recognizable amide and heterocycle chemistry is retained, but neither the N-fluoro amides nor all of the bridged sulfur variants are routine medicinal substitutions. Prior seed 0 reached 0.4463521672202675 with a bridged aromatic nitrogen/oxygen system bearing an aryl-containing ketone side chain. The new high families change core chemistry but remain below that observed best.
liabilities: N-fluoro amides, N-halogenated hydrazine-like rings and halomethyl substituents introduce reactive functionality into the high tail.
Nitrogen-nitrogen, sulfur-nitrogen and oxime-ether-like linkages add stability or configurational questions to already constrained structures.
Tiny late fragments discard the useful molecule rather than providing a coherent small analogue; bridged stereochemistry remains unspecified.
missing_features: Stable local alternatives to N-fluoro amides, ring-nitrogen halogenation and sulfur-nitrogen bridges are incompletely represented in the leading series, although a more conventional bridged lactam already reaches the upper neighbourhood.
Broader independent cores preserving the useful aromatic and carbonyl relationships are not established beyond the concentrated fused-nitrogen and bridged-lactam families.
Explicit configuration at asymmetric bridged centres and credible core-preserving contractions are absent from parts of the output.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial methoxyindole carboxamide scores 0.3051048083696145. The N-fluoro carboxanilide on the benzofused hydrazine-like ring reaches 0.4163503402962837, while the vinyl-sulfide, sulfur-nitrogen-bridged lactam/imine reaches 0.4126819838532174. A related vinyl-ether bridged lactam without that sulfur bridge scores 0.4005670758913022, showing a relatively conventional alternative in the same broad upper range. Adding chlorine or fluorine to the hydrazine-ring nitrogen gives 0.40314990987966176; changing the ring nitrogen pair to an oxygen/nitrogen connection gives 0.36286362320121707. A related imidamide-containing fused ring scores 0.40497388700123543. These observations favour coherent aromatic/polar cyclic arrangements over indiscriminate halogen addition. Ethene, methane, molecular fluorine and small sulfur or imine fragments appear at 0.0, and the seed-2 trajectory ends with ethene at 0.0. The useful cores are therefore not consistently preserved in all emissions.

per_task.generated_character: The leading seed-1 molecules join carbonyl-containing oxygen/nitrogen heteroaromatic ring systems through an amino linkage. They are heavily decorated with halogens, short ring bridges and, often, oxygen-oxygen-halogen chains. Several also carry an O-cyanate substituent, which is chemically different from a carbon-bound nitrile. Seed 2 develops a related but distinct family of coupled and bridged nitrogen dicarbonyl heterocycles with N-halogenation and halomethyl substitution. Ring_closure_rate and aromatic_atom_rate are both 0.9862; halogen_rate is 0.9552. Mean_smiles_length 85.3 and max_smiles_length 248 show a substantial bulky-assembly tail, although the supplied leaders are more compact than the most extended proposals. The prior seed-0 best, 0.6004556752278376, was a much more extensively assembled nitrogen/carbonyl heteroaromatic structure with conjugated appendages. The new upper structures are more compact connected heterocycles but introduce pronounced reactive-group liabilities.
liabilities: Oxygen-oxygen-halogen chains, oxygen-halogen bonds and O-cyanate groups make the leading chemistry substantially more reactive than an ordinary halogenated heteroaryl series.
Seed-2 late structures repeatedly carry nitrogen-fluorine or nitrogen-chlorine bonds, adding a separate stability concern.
Short bridges across aromatic frameworks and very large connected assemblies create geometric and synthetic demands that the score alone does not resolve.
missing_features: Chemically robust substituents that preserve the useful heteroaromatic arrangement are underrepresented relative to peroxide and heteroatom-halogen variants. The fluoromethyl analogue demonstrates that a less reactive alternative can retain a similar score.
Independent stable scaffold and linker alternatives are incompletely represented within the leading coupled-heterocycle families.
Reliable control of short ring bridges and avoidance of unnecessary multi-core concatenation are missing from parts of the broader output.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The leading amino-linked heterocycle with an oxygen-oxygen-chlorine substituent scores 0.6324703199409752. A closely related aza-ring version scores 0.6300605077662029, whereas replacing its oxygen-oxygen-chlorine group with fluoromethyl gives 0.6293992623616929. Chlorinated and brominated oxygen-containing side-chain alternatives also score 0.6293992623616929. Thus a nearly comparable upper value is observed with an ordinary carbon-bound fluorine substituent; the peroxide/oxygen-halogen motif is not demonstrably essential. A less bridged analogue scores 0.6309644029285534. The initial dicarbonyl heterocycle scores 0.548381482770623, and tiny chlorine, fluoromethane, enol-ether or cyanogen-halide fragments occupy the 0.5 floor. Late seed-2 nitrogen-halogen-rich dicarbonyl assemblies remain around 0.6058710298363812 and 0.6012872454997692. The gradient supports a specific connected heteroaromatic/carbonyl arrangement over isolated fragments or arbitrary size, while being relatively insensitive to some chemically consequential peripheral substitutions.

per_task.generated_character: The best seed-2 molecules combine halogenated aromatic rings with a saturated imidazolidine-type aminal ring, secondary or tertiary amines, and short aminoalkyl or enamine-containing connections to another substituted aromatic group. The leading central aminal carbon also bears an amino substituent. These are moderately large, recognizable amine-rich medicinal architectures, although aminal stability and some reactive substitutions remain concerns. Seed 1 reaches a different, more bridged amine/aryl family. Ring_closure_rate is 0.9828, aromatic_atom_rate 0.9724, halogen_rate 0.9828 and mean_smiles_length 58.7. Formal charge markers are absent, but accessible basic centres are abundant in the leading SMILES. The prior seed-0 leader scored 0.9908331648929692 and used a more rigid spiro saturated-amine framework between halogenated and thiol-substituted aromatic groups. Both old and new upper families clearly contain cyclic amines and substantial aromatic surface.
liabilities: Amino-substituted aminal centres, enamine functionality and multiple basic nitrogens require stability and physicochemical scrutiny beyond their high scores.
Chloromethyl, bromomethyl and thiol-containing side chains occur among near-leading variants.
The structures combine substantial aromatic/halogen content with basic centres, and some late variants disturb the aromatic or amine environment instead of preserving a coherent analogue.
missing_features: No absence of basic cyclic amines is supported; the missing coverage is stable, well-defined alternatives to the aminoaminal/enamine architecture that preserve its useful amine and aromatic relationships.
Control of nitrogen acylation, aromaticity and linker attachment is inconsistent, with some local changes losing much of the observed score.
Defined stereochemistry at the substituted aminoalkyl and aminal centres is missing; the trajectory does not establish a preferred configuration.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The amino-substituted imidazolidine with a carbon-linked secondary amine reaches 0.9914038363125457. The otherwise related example without that central amino substituent scores 0.9725868595115974. The enamine-connected counterpart scores 0.981088217863691, and its N-formyl analogue scores 0.48797702544581545, supporting a role for the local electronic state of the ring nitrogen. A halomethyl-substituted relative remains high at 0.989167131859766, whereas dearomatizing its terminal halogenated ring in a related family gives 0.08210159005746291. Removing the second aryl-containing amine side chain and retaining a hydroxylamine-like fragment yields 0.011495655106721757. The visible preference is for the connected amine/aryl arrangement, not aromatic surface, amine count or halogenation alone.

per_task.generated_character: Seed 1 favours aryl-substituted bridged or fused nitrogen rings carrying multiple carbonyls, with an ethoxy benzofuran-like region and an N-fluoro centre in its leading structures. Seed 2 instead develops quinoline-linked macrocyclic nitrogen/carbonyl systems containing tertiary amines, amide-like carbonyls, and hydroxyl, methyl or thiol substitutions. These molecules range from medium-sized macrocycles to bulkier fused systems and have recognizable synthetic building blocks, although their full ring topology and some substitutions are demanding. Ring_closure_rate is 0.9966, aromatic_atom_rate 0.9897 and mean_smiles_length 56.6. The prior seed-0 best, 0.22405709718343647, was another nitrogen/carbonyl ring system combining aromatic and saturated regions. The new leaders change ring layout but remain in a similar chemical class and below that score.
liabilities: The leading seed-1 structures contain nitrogen-fluorine bonds, whereas a near-leading seed-2 macrocycle demonstrates a conventional alternative without that functionality.
Multiple carbonyls, tertiary amines and constrained ring systems create conformational and synthetic complexity; thiol-containing analogues add oxidation concerns.
Small cyclic peroxide fragments and overgrown multi-aryl variants occur at lower scores, showing that ring presence alone is not sufficient chemical organization.
missing_features: A broader set of stable cores that retain the useful macrocyclic or bridged nitrogen/carbonyl arrangement is not established beyond closely related upper families.
Coherent simplification and linker changes are incompletely explored: useful medium-sized macrocycles exist, but both fragmentation and further core duplication can lose the favourable arrangement.
Defined configuration at bridged saturated centres and adequate specification of constrained-ring geometry are missing.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial diaryl dicarbonyl heterocycle scores 0.1678386594791329. The N-fluoro bridged carbonyl structure reaches 0.2133697489012744, while the more conventionally bonded hydroxyquinoline-linked macrocycle scores 0.21037674112349405 and a related azaaryl/carbonyl macrocycle scores 0.20917089553667287. Hydroxyl-, methyl- and thiol-containing relatives share 0.20736246951923798, so those particular peripheral changes do not distinguish their recorded scores. Phenol alone scores 0.06793662204867576, the small aryl amide acid scores 0.07504633196017493, and ethane and a small cyclic peroxide score 0.012461119656980673 and 0.0239774717598468. A late structure adding a second quinoline-containing region scores only 0.1754730092490373. The apparent preference is for organized aromatic/nitrogen/carbonyl relationships and suitable ring size, not maximal molecular growth or N-fluorination as a universal requirement.

per_task.generated_character: The leading seed-1 family is a moderately sized, fluorinated aryl primary-amine series attached to a bicyclic nitrogen dicarbonyl heterocycle. The best molecule carries aminomethyl, aryl fluorine and fluoromethyl groups with ordinary carbon-bound fluorination; its core nitrogens are alkylated rather than directly fluorinated. Other high relatives use aminoethyl groups, fused small carbocycles or N-fluorination. This leading chemistry is more recognizable and plausibly makeable than the much larger linked dicarbonyl assemblies in the low tail. Seed 2 reaches a different fused heteroaromatic family with small fluorinated carbocycles, hydroxyl and thiomethyl groups. Ring_closure_rate is 0.9724, aromatic_atom_rate 0.969, halogen_rate 0.781 and mean_smiles_length 56.5. The prior seed-0 best, 0.4759777345546235, used an acylated nitrogen-rich fluorinated heterocycle with an unsaturated oxygen ring. The new highest family brings a clear primary-amine/aryl/dicarbonyl arrangement into the upper output.
liabilities: Direct nitrogen-fluorine bonds occur in several high relatives even though the leading molecule demonstrates ordinary carbon-bound fluorination and N-alkylation.
Other variants contain strained small unsaturated carbocycles, thiols or thiomethyl groups; their stability and stereochemical accessibility are not established.

Large duplicated or fused dicarbonyl assemblies produce substantial bulk with extremely poor recorded scores, indicating a need for coherent size and core organization rather than further concatenation.
missing_features: The useful primary amine is present in the leading family, but stable alternative cores and linkers preserving its placement relative to the aryl dicarbonyl system remain incompletely represented.
Consistent retention of the favourable local amino group is missing in some substitutions and in the alternative fused heteroaromatic trajectory.
Stereochemically specified small-ring variants are absent where configuration becomes relevant; the leading acyclic side-chain example itself does not require an assigned tetrahedral stereocentre.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The aminomethyl, fluoromethyl-substituted aryl dicarbonyl leader scores 0.5845583988949146. Replacing a peripheral fluoromethyl group with chlorine in the otherwise corresponding structure gives 0.5064928497454653. An aminoethyl analogue scores 0.5180292619150341; the full trajectory shows its closely matched terminal-amine-to-fluorine replacement at 0.0007365197806377691, supporting the importance of that local primary-amine functionality in this family. N-fluorinated aminoethyl relatives score 0.5652209810580261 and 0.5615749101173619, below the conventionally N-alkylated leader. Very large linked dicarbonyl molecules score 1.6758614448245604e-53 and 5.4391203474237023e-42. Seed 2 reaches 0.4071395189354175 with a small fluorinated carbocycle attached to its fused aromatic core, but ends at 0.0038179150668162477 after losing that substituent and changing nearby sulfur decoration. The gradient supports compact, correctly placed amine/aryl/carbonyl relationships; neither total fluorination nor accumulating more copies of the core is a sufficient rule.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The cited upper families contain N-fluoro amides and amines, oxygen-oxygen-halogen chains, oxygen-halogen bonds and O-cyanate substituents. Yet a fluoromethyl alternative scores 0.6293992623616929 near its peroxide-bearing relative at 0.6300605077662029, a conventional macrocycle scores 0.21037674112349405 near an N-fluorinated leader, and an ordinarily N-alkylated aryl primary amine leads another family at 0.5845583988949146. The data show usable conventional chemistry alongside reactive edits.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently prefer chemically robust local alternatives over reactive heteroatom-halogen and peroxide substitutions.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make stable functional-group replacements available while preserving the useful core and polar-group relationships. Treat carbon-bound halogens, nitrogen-halogen bonds and oxygen/peroxide-halogen chains as distinct chemistry, and use accepted molecular feedback to compare coherent alternatives instead of treating all halogen substitutions alike.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A connected cyclic-aminal/amine structure scores 0.9914038363125457, whereas deleting its second aryl-containing amine region gives 0.011495655106721757. In a related family, nitrogen formylation changes a 0.981088217863691 structure to one scoring 0.48797702544581545. The fluorinated aryl primary-amine family also shows a sharp loss when an aminoethyl terminus is replaced by fluorine. These observations establish local arrangement, not merely nitrogen or halogen abundance, as useful visible chemistry.
transferable_gaps.gap: Useful amine and carbonyl attachment context is not reliably preserved during local substitution, acylation or linker changes.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve and deliberately vary the spacing, attachment and electronic environment of amines, aromatic groups and carbonyls. Distinguish free or cyclic amines from acylated, oxygen-linked or sulfur-linked nitrogen so feedback can assess chemically meaningful local changes.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Tiny ethene, methane and halogen fragments occupy zero or floor-score tails, while large duplicated dicarbonyl assemblies score 1.6758614448245604e-53 and 5.4391203474237023e-42. A late macrocycle acquiring an additional quinoline region scores 0.1754730092490373, below simpler relatives near 0.21037674112349405. Conversely, some useful molecules are themselves moderately large and cyclic, so the evidence does not support a universal size minimum or maximum.
transferable_gaps.gap: Size changes can discard useful cores or duplicate them into bulky assemblies instead of producing coherent analogues.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide core-preserving growth, contraction and linker moves that maintain complete functional groups. Let accepted observations determine useful size locally while maintaining alternatives to both fragmentation and repeated assembly of the same core.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every digest reports stereocentre_rate 0.0. The cited molecules include asymmetric aminoalkyl centres, substituted aminal carbons, bridged lactams and fluorinated small carbocycles. Such structures can have configurational alternatives even though all supplied strings omit stereocentre annotations. Short bridges and constrained rings also need more than a valid ring-closure string to define plausible geometry.
transferable_gaps.gap: Explicit stereochemistry and controlled geometric interpretation are missing from asymmetric cyclic and bridged structures.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Represent relevant stereochemical and geometric alternatives when changing saturated centres, constrained alkenes or ring junctions. Preserve chemically credible connectivity and let accepted feedback determine useful configurations; their present absence does not establish a score benefit for any one choice.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The high tails repeatedly revisit benzofused aryl amides or bridged lactams, coupled carbonyl heteroaromatics, imidazolidine-type amine architectures, quinoline-linked macrocycles and aryl primary-amine dicarbonyl systems. Different seeds reach distinct cores, so scaffold change is possible, but many leading examples differ only by local halogen, heteroatom or ring edits and some receive identical scores.
transferable_gaps.gap: Coverage of independent useful chemical cores remains narrower than the number of local analogues and peripheral edits suggests.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Maintain several chemically distinct accepted core families and support scaffold replacements that preserve useful donor, acceptor, amine and aromatic relationships. Evaluate coverage through credible core chemistry and attachment geometry alongside molecular identity, rather than relying on a new substituent or ring closure alone.

nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

De novo connected-fragment graph crossover

approach.method_basis: The Parent moves persistent particles through a fixed molecular autoencoder. Each particle retains its current position and velocity, remembers its best actually scored generating position, and is pulled toward that personal best and the best resolved position found by the swarm. A frozen deterministic decoder turns each proposed position into a molecule. Accepted scores update memories only at the exact position that produced their molecular identity. Initially, the encoder supplies particle locations, but an initial molecule can supply a scored attractor only when decoding its encoding reproduces that molecule. In the observed run this worked for just one of the ten supplied molecules.
approach.novelty: Add bounded latent inversion at initialization: move only the input coordinates of each initially mismatched molecule to make its known token sequence preferred by the frozen decoder. Install a refined position only after an exact canonical reconstruction check succeeds, so additional known scores can become usable swarm attractors. Failed refinements retain the original initialization. This is the first Child in the lineage; the Parent tried direct encoder placement but never corrected its coordinates through the decoder. The experiment tests recovery of scored starting positions before proposing any change to the subsequent swarm motion.

nodes.hypothesis: At objective initialization, refine each identity-mismatched initial encoding by bounded gradient descent on frozen-decoder target-token margin loss, and replace its particle starting position and admit its real initial score only when unchanged deterministic decoding exactly recovers that initial canonical molecule.

finding_summary.headline: One initial molecule became a working swarm attractor, but the macro score fell from 0.451 to 0.348
finding_summary.insights: At least one missing starting identity was already representable by the frozen decoder: correcting its coordinates recovered that identity without changing neural weights or transferring a score to a different molecule. The causal path from recovery to installation, motion and scored attraction is therefore established. That repairs a real coverage defect, but this run does not support the expectation that doubling the initially scored particles improves overall search quality. On drd2_docking and sitagliptin, both recovered personal memories were replaced after their first proposals, before they could supply a nonzero personal pull; their shared memory still influenced other particles. On deco_hop, the recovered shared attractor was referenced in 210 motions and both recovered personal memories survived to the end, yet the task score was lower. The amount of attractor reuse alone is therefore insufficient evidence of useful search guidance. All nine optimization attempts lowered their best visited mean loss, but only one recovered its molecule, so the token-margin proxy cannot replace the production identity check. The eight failures do not establish that those molecules lack an inverse: the bounded local optimizer may simply have failed to find one. Mean decoded fingerprint distance from the source remained large, increasing from 0.854 to 0.864. The molecular assessment likewise finds abundant rings alongside long unsaturated chains, labile polar linkers and irregular ring arrangements. Exact initialization does not control those downstream structural changes. Broader inversion coverage and the usefulness of moves around a recovered position remain separate open questions; this single seed establishes activation and an observed score loss, without establishing a reproducible score effect.
finding_summary.results: Exact starting coverage increased from one to two of the ten supplied molecules. The same additional molecule was recovered in all five objective sessions after 168 latent updates: its mean target-margin loss fell from 0.168312 to 0.019830, and its checked position was installed in two particles per session. This doubled scored initial particle memories from two to four out of twenty. All ten recovered particle copies supplied actual motion sources; their memories produced 44 nonzero personal-attraction terms and 252 nonzero attractions from other particles. Eight other mismatched molecules reached the 256-step limit and retained their original positions, while the original exact match stayed unchanged. These five sessions reuse one fixed ten-molecule set and are not five independent reconstruction tests. The frozen model and exact score-position provenance remained intact. On the supplied seed, the mean final Top-1 score fell from 0.450789 to 0.347733. Zaleplon improved from 0.374833 to 0.390441 and median_2 from 0.167839 to 0.202143; deco_hop fell from 0.592706 to 0.553113, drd2_docking from 0.859171 to 0.412549, and sitagliptin from 0.259395 to 0.180421. Every task completed all 300 evaluations with no invalid or duplicate evaluator submissions.
